title: A C^1 Counterexample to the Entropy Conjecture
abstract: We disprove the general C1 self-map formulation of Shub's entropy conjecture. We construct a noninvertible C1 self-map of a compact smooth manifold without boundary whose topological entropy is zero, while its action on second real homology has eigenvalue 2. Thus the topological entropy is strictly smaller than the logarithm of the homological spectral radius.

tex.abstract:
We disprove the general \(C^1\) self-map formulation of Shub's entropy
conjecture. We construct a noninvertible \(C^1\) self-map of a compact
smooth manifold without boundary whose topological entropy is zero,
while its action on second real homology has eigenvalue \(2\). Thus the
topological entropy is strictly smaller than the logarithm of the
homological spectral radius.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There are a positive integer \(q\) and a \(C^1\) self-map \(f\) of the
compact smooth manifold
\[
 M=(\R/100\Z)\times(S^2)^{q+1}
\]
such that \(\htop(f)=0\) and \(f_*:H_2(M;\R)\to H_2(M;\R)\) has
eigenvalue \(2\). In particular,
\[
 \htop(f)=0<\log 2\le \log\rho(f_*).
\]

statements.label: prop:regularity
statements.text:
For the choices above, with $q$ finite and $L>\max\{B,2\}$, the series
\eqref{eq:input} defines $C^1$ maps
$U_\ell\colon(\mathbb R/100\mathbb Z)\times\Sigma\to\mathbb C$.
Consequently, \eqref{eq:map} defines a $C^1$ self-map of the nonempty
compact smooth manifold $M$.

statements.label: prop:attraction
statements.text:
For the map $f:M\to M$ constructed in Section~\ref{sec:construction}, every
$x\in M$ satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{dist}\bigl(f^n(x),Z_0\cup Z_\infty\bigr)\longrightarrow0
 \qquad(n\longrightarrow\infty)
\]
in every compatible metric on $M$.
More precisely, if the lifted clock of the orbit is bounded above, then
the clock converges to $50$ modulo $100$ and $z_n\to0$.
If that lift is unbounded above, then $z_n\to\infty$ in $\Sigma$ and all
registers are identically zero from some time onward.

statements.label: prop:zero-entropy
statements.text:
The map $f$ defined in~\eqref{eq:map} has
$h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)=0$.

statements.label: prop:homology
statements.text:
For the map \(f\) in \eqref{eq:map}, the action
\(f_*:H_2(M;\R)\to H_2(M;\R)\) has eigenvalue \(2\).

title: A CH obstruction to a prescribed categoricity threshold
abstract: Assuming the continuum hypothesis, we construct an abstract elementary class with Löwenheim–Skolem number ℵ<sub>0</sub> that is categorical in every sufficiently large cardinal but has at least two nonisomorphic models of cardinality \(\beth_{\omega_2}\). Thus categoricity does not transfer down to the proposed bound \(\beth_{(2^{\aleph_0})^+}\), which equals \(\beth_{\omega_2}\) under CH. Consequently, if ZFC is consistent, the prescribed-threshold form of Shelah's categoricity conjecture is not provable in ZFC.

tex.abstract:
Assuming the continuum hypothesis, we construct an abstract elementary
class with L\"owenheim--Skolem number \(\aleph_0\) that is categorical in
every sufficiently large cardinal but has at least two nonisomorphic
models of cardinality \(\beth_{\omega_2}\).
Thus categoricity does not transfer down to the proposed bound
\(\beth_{(2^{\aleph_0})^+}\), which equals \(\beth_{\omega_2}\) under CH.
Consequently, if ZFC is consistent, the prescribed-threshold
form of Shelah's categoricity conjecture is not provable in ZFC.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Assume the continuum hypothesis. There is an abstract elementary class
\(K\) in a countable finitary relational language such that
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item \(\LS(K)=\aleph_0\);
 \item \(K\) has at least two nonisomorphic models of cardinality
       \(\beth_{\omega_2}=H(K)\);
 \item putting \(\Lambda=\beth_{(2^{\aleph_1})^+}\),
       the class \(K\) is categorical in every cardinal
       \(\mu\ge\Lambda\).
\end{enumerate}
In particular, \(\lambda=\Lambda^+>H(K)\) is a categoricity cardinal
from which downward transfer to \(H(K)\) fails.

statements.label: aec:class
statements.text:
The pair \(K=(\mathcal C,\le_K)\) of
Definition~\ref{aec:objects} is an abstract
elementary class in a fixed countable finitary
relational language, with
\[
 \LS(K)=\aleph_0.
\]
It has the union and common-upper-bound
properties for every nonempty set-indexed
directed family of strong substructures.

statements.label: end:two-models
statements.text:
The class \(K\) has two nonisomorphic models of
cardinality \(\beth_\eta\).  One has an order sort
of cardinality \(\aleph_1\), and the other has a
countable order sort.

statements.label: cor:consistency
statements.text:
ZFC proves \(\mathrm{CH}\Rightarrow\Theta\).
For each fixed \(\Phi\) as above, it also proves
\(\mathrm{CH}\Rightarrow\neg\Phi\), and
\[
 \Con(\mathrm{ZFC})
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \Con(\mathrm{ZFC}+\Theta)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \Con(\mathrm{ZFC}+\neg\Phi).
\]
If ZFC is consistent, no such \(\Phi\) is a theorem of ZFC.

statements.text:
The class \(K\) has neither joint embedding nor amalgamation.
The failure of amalgamation can be witnessed over a countable model.

This applies, in particular, to every model on the categoricity tail
\(\|H\|\ge\Lambda\).

title: A Capacity Criterion for Four-State Potts Reconstruction on Trees
abstract: For the ferromagnetic four-state broadcast model with \(0\lt \lambda\lt 1\), we prove that reconstruction on a bounded-degree deterministic rooted tree occurs exactly when its L3 capacity with edge resistances \(\lambda^{-2|e|}\) is positive. This gives an exact criterion without regularity or growth-rate assumptions on the tree, including at the exponential critical boundary.

tex.abstract:
For the ferromagnetic four-state broadcast model with $0<\lambda<1$,
we prove that reconstruction on a bounded-degree deterministic rooted
tree occurs exactly when its $L^3$ capacity with edge resistances
$\lambda^{-2|e|}$ is positive. This gives an exact criterion without
regularity or growth-rate assumptions on the tree, including at the
exponential critical boundary.

title: A Charged Reduction of the Spacetime Penrose Inequality in Spatial Dimensions at Least Four
abstract: Using the companion neutral spacetime Penrose theorem exactly at its stated strong-decay, future-trapped, positive-area, and future-timelike scope, we prove the sharp purely electric upper-area inequality in every spatial dimension n ≥ 4 for one-ended charged data satisfying the charged dominant energy condition and \(\mathop{\mathrm{div}}\nolimits _g E=0\), with the specified decay, integrability, and finite-flux assumptions. The data may have arbitrary interior topology and ADM momentum, with a future or past trapping sign chosen independently on each boundary component. Positive enclosing area and strict ADM timelikeness are conclusions. The polynomial mass rearrangement is asserted only when the \((n-2)\)nd power of the enclosing-area radius exceeds \(|Q|\). When \(m\gt |Q|\), equality under the stated connected, outermost, outer-area-minimizing future-horizon hypotheses recovers the original metric, second fundamental form, and electric field as a global spacelike slice of a Reissner–Nordström–Tangherlini exterior. The equality classification includes only slices whose induced magnetic two-form vanishes.

tex.abstract:
Using the companion neutral spacetime Penrose theorem exactly at its
stated strong-decay, future-trapped, positive-area, and future-timelike
scope, we prove the sharp purely electric upper-area inequality in every
spatial dimension $n\ge4$ for one-ended charged data satisfying the charged
dominant energy condition and $\Div_g E=0$, with the specified decay,
integrability, and finite-flux assumptions. The data may have arbitrary interior
topology and ADM momentum, with a future or past trapping sign chosen
independently on each boundary component. Positive enclosing area and
strict ADM timelikeness are conclusions. The polynomial mass rearrangement
is asserted only when the $(n-2)$nd power of the enclosing-area radius
exceeds $|Q|$. When $m>|Q|$, equality under the stated connected,
outermost, outer-area-minimizing future-horizon hypotheses recovers the
original metric, second fundamental form, and electric field as a global
spacelike slice of a Reissner--Nordstr\"om--Tangherlini exterior. The
equality classification includes only slices whose induced magnetic
two-form vanishes.

statements.title: Neutral numerical input
statements.label: thm:neutral-input
statements.text:
Let $d\ge3$ and let $(U^d,h,L)$ be a connected oriented smooth initial-data exterior with nonempty compact smooth boundary $T$, complete with $T$ included, with compact complement of exactly one Euclidean coordinate end. Write
\[
 2\mu=R_h+(\tr_hL)^2-|L|_h^2,
 \qquad J=\Div_h(L-(\tr_hL)h).
\]
Suppose $\mu\ge|J|_h$, $\mu,|J|_h\in L^1$, and for some
\[
 \frac{d-2}{2}<q_0<d-2
\]
assume
\[
 h-\delta=O_6(r^{-q_0}),\qquad L=O_5(r^{-1-q_0}).
\]
Assume that the ADM limits exist, with energy factor
$[2(d-1)\omega_{d-1}]^{-1}$ and momentum factor
$[(d-1)\omega_{d-1}]^{-1}$ applied to the Euclidean fluxes in
\eqref{eq:adm-energy}--\eqref{eq:adm-momentum}, with $g,K,\tau$ replaced by $h,L,\tr_hL$.
Assume $\mathcal E_{\mathrm{ADM}}>|\mathbf P_{\mathrm{ADM}}|$, and suppose every component of $T$ satisfies
\[
 H_T+\tr_TL\le0
\]
with normal toward the end. Let $A_*>0$ be the infimum of the areas of full cuts in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:full-cut}, now in $(U,h)$, with all components and contact with $T$ counted. Then
\begin{equation}
 \sqrt{\mathcal E_{\mathrm{ADM}}^2-|\mathbf P_{\mathrm{ADM}}|^2}
 \ge\frac12\left(\frac{A_*}{\omega_{d-1}}\right)^{(d-2)/(d-1)}.
\end{equation}
No minimizing cut is required to be smooth or attained. No spin, symmetry, maximality, vacuum or stationary-development hypothesis is imposed.

statements.title: Strict direction for compact variations
statements.label: prep:strict-direction
statements.text:
On the original weakly asymptotically flat exterior, choose a smooth
majorant $B\geq|K|$ equal to $Cr^{-1-q}$ far out and apply
Lemma~\ref{prep:strictification}.  Consider the tangent direction
\[
 (g',K',\alpha',D_m')=(2\phi g,\phi K,0,0)
\]
at purely electric data, transporting $v$ by the metric square root.
On an active ray $\mu_m+J_m(v)=0$, the derivative
$\mathfrak C'=2(\mu_m+J_m(v))'$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 
 \mathfrak C'
 =2k\bigl(-\Delta\phi+K(\nabla\phi,v)\bigr)
       +4(n-2)c_n^2\phi|E|^2
 \geq2k\rho_0,
 \qquad \mathfrak C'/\rho_0\longrightarrow2k.
\end{equation}
At a marginal boundary $\theta_+'=-k$.  The energy derivative is finite,
the momentum derivative is zero, and $\phi=O_2(r^{2-n})$.
statements.section_title: Area positivity and preparation of the asymptotic end

statements.title: Preparation at rest
statements.label: prep:rest-preparation
statements.text:
Suppose the original data have a future-timelike ADM vector, and set
$m=(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{ADM}}^2-|\mathbf P_{\mathrm{ADM}}|^2)^{1/2}>0$.
Choose once and for all
\[
 \frac{n-2}{2}<q<n-2,
 \qquad 0<\beta<\min\{1,q\},
\]
weakening the original decay exponent if necessary.  There is a sequence
of smooth data on the same exterior, with the same electric flux form
and charge, satisfying
\begin{align}
 
 &K_j\text{ is compactly supported},\qquad
   g_j-\delta=O_l(r^{2-n})\quad\text{for every }l,\\
 &R_{g_j}=O(r^{-n-\beta}),\qquad
   \mu_{m,j}-|J_{m,j}|_{g_j}\geq c_jr^{-n-\beta},\qquad
   H_j+\epsilon_a\tr_{S_a,g_j}K_j<0,
 \nonumber
\end{align}
where $c_j>0$.  Its momentum vanishes and
\begin{equation}
 
 \mathcal E_{\mathrm{ADM}}(g_j,K_j)\longrightarrow m,
 \qquad \liminf_{j\to\infty}a(g_j)\geq a(g).
\end{equation}
The same conclusion holds with a fixed compactly supported closed
$D_m$, provided the original data are already future-timelike, have
strict trapping, and satisfy a strict charged margin
$\mu_m-|J_m|\geq c r^{-n-\beta}$ for some $c>0$.
The constants and support radii in
\eqref{prep:prepared-properties} need not be uniform in $j$.

statements.title: Distortion bound
statements.label: alg:distortion-proposition
statements.text:
With the choices above, every smooth homotopy solution on
$\mathcal M_{N,R}$ with $\min t> -\varepsilon$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 -\varepsilon<t\leq Z\leq\mathcal P_N,\qquad
 \ell\leq l\leq e,\qquad
 |f|+|\nabla f|\leq\exp(\mathcal P_N).
 
\end{equation}
The constants are independent of $R\geq R_{\min}(N)$ and of the
homotopy parameter.
statements.section_title: The filled scalar system and its a priori bounds

statements.title: A filled solution
statements.label: pde:filled-solve
statements.text:
For fixed prepared data and \(\varepsilon>0\), all sufficiently large
\(N\) admit a smooth solution of \eqref{alg:system} on the entire
one-ended filled manifold \(\mathcal M_N\), with
\[
 t>-\varepsilon,\qquad
 t\le Z\le\mathcal P_N,\qquad
 \ell\le l\le e,\qquad
 |f|+|\nabla f|\le e^{\mathcal P_N}.
\]
The functions \(f\) and all their derivatives decay exponentially on
the end, with constants depending on fixed \(N\).  Moreover
\begin{equation}
 t,Z=O_j(r^{2-n})\quad\hbox{for every }j,\qquad
 \Delta_gt=O(r^{-n-\beta}).
 
\end{equation}
The uniform height bound and the radial height estimate of
Lemma~\ref{alg:trace-height} hold on the limiting solution.
statements.section_title: The coupled elliptic construction and its limiting geometry

statements.title: The mass cost of the filled construction
statements.label: pde:mass-cost
statements.text:
Let \(\widehat g=e^{2t}(g+l^2df^2)\) be obtained from
Proposition~\ref{pde:filled-solve}, and let \(E_*\) be the ADM energy
of the prepared metric \(g\).  Then
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak F
 :=\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S_r}g(V,\nu)\,\dd A_g
 =\int_{\mathcal M_N}u\Xi\,\dd V_g,\qquad
 \mathcal E_{\mathrm{ADM}}(\widehat g)
 =E_*-\frac{\mathfrak F}{k\omega}.
 
\end{equation}
For fixed \(\varepsilon\),
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak F\ge
 -\mathcal P_N(\ell+\ell^2/\eta)
 =-\mathcal P_N(\ell+\ell^{1/2})=-o_N(1).
 
\end{equation}
The metric \(g_b=e^{2\varepsilon}\widehat g\), written in its
dilated asymptotic coordinates, consequently has
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal E_{\mathrm{ADM}}(g_b)
 \le e^{(n-2)\varepsilon}(E_*+o_N(1)).
 
\end{equation}
It has all-order metric decay \(O_j(r^{2-n})\), a finite ADM energy,
and scalar curvature \(O(r^{-n-\beta})\).

statements.title: Separation of the original boundary by height
statements.label: pde:height-separation
statements.text:
There are \(b_2>0\) and \(N_2\), depending on the fixed prepared data
and \(\varepsilon\), such that the solutions of
Proposition~\ref{pde:filled-solve} satisfy, for \(N\ge N_2\),
\[
 h<-b_2\quad\hbox{on every plus component of }S,\qquad
 h>b_2\quad\hbox{on every minus component of }S.
\]
The constants are independent of \(N\).
For every fixed \(b>0\), the portion of the original exterior on which
\(|h|\ge b\) is contained in a fixed compact set, independent of \(N\).

statements.title: The charged low-height region
statements.label: pde:charged-region
statements.text:
Choose \(b_3>0\) sufficiently small relative to \(b_2\) and the
strict prepared matter margin.  For every sufficiently large \(N\),
put
\[
 \bar g=g+l^2df^2,\qquad
 g_b=e^{2(t+\varepsilon)}\bar g.
\]
On the original exterior \(g_b\ge g\) as quadratic forms, and
\[
 |dh|_{\bar g}\le\eta/l\le\ell^{1/2}.
\]
If \(\alpha=\iota_EdV_g\) is the retained electric flux form, then
on the original region \(\{|h|\le b_3\}\),
\begin{equation}
 \frac{R_{g_b}}2\ge c_n^2|\alpha|_{g_b}^2.
 
\end{equation}
There is \(c_*>0\), independent of \(N\), such that on the original
band \(b_3/4\le|h|\le b_3\),
\begin{equation}
 e^{2(t+\varepsilon)}\frac{R_{g_b}}2
 \ge I_g(w)+c_*+(1-\delta_0)\mathcal T.
 
\end{equation}
The band lies in a fixed compact portion of the original exterior.
Here \(I_g(w)\) is the electromagnetic expression defined with the
prepared data; it also permits the compactly supported magnetic form
used in the strict numerical extension.

statements.title: Prepared numerical bound
statements.label: flux:prepared-bound
statements.text:
For the prepared data, for every $0<s<1$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal E_*\geq s|Q|+\frac{1-s^2}{2}X_*.
 
\end{equation}
The conclusion also holds for prepared data carrying a smooth compactly
supported closed magnetic two-form, with the charged energy convention
used in the filled scalar construction.
statements.section_title: Conversion of electric flux into an energy decrease

statements.title: Strict compact-magnetic numerical extension
statements.label: flux:magnetic-extension
statements.text:
Let the original exterior satisfy the numerical geometric and asymptotic
hypotheses, and let $D_m$ be an arbitrary smooth compactly supported closed
two-form.  With $\alpha=i_E\vol_g$ closed, use the electromagnetic convention
\begin{equation}
 I_g(v)=c_n^2\bigl(|E|_g^2+|D_m|_g^2+2D_m(v,E)\bigr),
 \qquad
 \mu_m+J_m(v)=\mu+J(v)-I_g(v).
 
\end{equation}
Assume also that $\mu_m,|J_m|_g$ are integrable and that the ADM and
charge flux limits exist with the stated normalizations.  Assume the ADM
vector is future timelike, the fixed componentwise trapping
inequalities are strict, and for some $c>0$ and
$0<\beta<\min(1,q)$,
\begin{equation}
 \mu_m-|J_m|_g\geq c r^{-n-\beta}.
 
\end{equation}
Then, with the original full-cut infimum $a$ and the original normalized
electric charge $Q$,
\begin{equation}
 m\geq s|Q|+\frac{1-s^2}{2}X_A\quad(0<s<1).
 
\end{equation}
Equivalently, $m\geq|Q|$, and when $X_A>|Q|$ one also has
$m\geq(X_A+Q^2/X_A)/2$.  No magnetic equality classification or
non-timelike extension is asserted here.
statements.section_title: Conversion of electric flux into an energy decrease

statements.title: Area envelope and regular patches
statements.label: var:area-envelope
statements.text:
The least perimeter of filled competitors equals the full smooth-cut
infimum $a$.  The family $\mathcal F_*$ of minimizing filled sets,
considered modulo null sets, is compact in local $L^1$, and all its
members are supported in a common compact set.  Their exterior end
components have the full-boundary convention of
Definition~\ref{def:full-cut}.

Each minimizing frontier is smooth and minimal at its free regular
points.  Its possible singular set has Hausdorff dimension at most
$n-8$.  All contact points with $S$ are regular of class $C^{1,\gamma}$
for some $\gamma>0$, and their graph representations belong to
$W^{2,p}$ for every finite $p$.  At an interior regular point of one
frontier, any other minimizing frontier through the point coincides
with it locally.  On a smaller neighborhood the minimizing frontiers
that meet that neighborhood are disjoint single graphs, with uniform
smooth interior estimates.

For a differentiable metric path with $g'_0=h$, the right derivative
of its enclosing-area infimum is
\begin{equation}
 a'_+(h)=\min_{F\in\mathcal F_*} a'_F(h),\qquad
 a'_F(h)=\frac12\int_{\partial^*F}
                       \operatorname{tr}_{T\partial^*F}h\,\dd A_g.
 
\end{equation}
Here and below $\partial^*F$ is used for integration, while
``frontier'' means the support of its perimeter measure.

statements.title: Multiplier identity
statements.label: var:multiplier-identity
statements.text:
There are a probability measure $\pi$ on $\mathcal F_*$, a
nonnegative locally finite measure $\Lambda$ on the active rays,
and a nonnegative finite measure $\zeta$ on $S$, such that
\begin{equation}
 2k\omega\mathcal B'-c\int_{\mathcal F_*}a'_F(h)\,\dd\pi(F)
 =\int\mathfrak C'\,\dd\Lambda-\int_S\theta'_+\,\dd\zeta
 
\end{equation}
for every compact test and every end prototype above.  No
surjectivity of a constraint map is required.

statements.title: Regularity of the measure moments
statements.label: var:moment-regularity
statements.text:
In the open exterior the moments are functions satisfying the first Killing initial data (KID) equation
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{sym}\nabla X=-uK,
 
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Hess}u
  =\mathcal L(u,X,\nabla X)
    +\frac c2\int_{\mathcal F_*}
       \nu_F^\flat\otimes\nu_F^\flat\,
                       \dd A_F\,\dd\pi(F).
 
\end{equation}
The equations are distributional, and surface measures in the
second equation are expressed relative to ambient volume.
The operator $\mathcal L$ has smooth linear coefficients.
It is specifically the lower-order operator from the metric
adjoint in \eqref{var:separation}, with the flux form fixed
and the unit-ball rays transported as specified above.
In particular, it is not an arbitrary operator with smooth
coefficients.  Locally $u$ is Lipschitz and $X$ is $C^{1,1}$.
The complementarity relations
\eqref{var:moment-complementarity} hold pointwise.

statements.title: Elimination of the interior area multiplier
statements.label: var:area-elimination
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses above and the exclusion of a smooth interior
enclosing frontier with zero future expansion in
Definition~\ref{def:rigidity-class}, the measure $\pi$ is
concentrated on the given boundary:
\begin{equation}
 \pi=\delta_S,
 \qquad
 \int_{\mathcal F_*}a'_D(h)\,d\pi(D)=a'_S(h).
\end{equation}
Here $\delta_S$ denotes the point mass at the filled minimizer
whose frontier is $S$.

statements.title: Stationary data supplied by equality
statements.label: var:stationary-data
statements.text:
There are smooth fields $u,X$ on $\Omega$, including $S$, with
$u\ge |X|$, $u>0$ in the open exterior and
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{sym}\nabla X=-uK,\qquad
 u\mu_m+J_m(X)=0.
 
\end{equation}
For any sufficiently small decrease $q_0<q$ with
$q_0>(n-2)/2$, their end behavior is
\begin{equation}
 (u,X)=(b^0,b^i)+O_2(r^{-q_0}).
 
\end{equation}
On $\R_z\times\operatorname{int}\Omega$ set
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf g=-u^2\dd z^2+
             g_{ij}(\dd x^i+X^i\dd z)(\dd x^j+X^j\dd z),
 \qquad \xi=\partial_z,\qquad
 \mathbf F=c_n\dd z\wedge uE^\flat.
 
\end{equation}
The stationary fields satisfy Maxwell's equations and
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Ein}_{\mathbf g}-\mathsf S
       =\mu_m u^{-2}\xi^\flat\otimes\xi^\flat,
 \qquad
 \mathsf S_{ab}=2\left(\mathbf F_{ac}\mathbf F_b{}^c
           -\tfrac14\mathbf F_{cd}\mathbf F^{cd}\mathbf g_{ab}\right).
 
\end{equation}
The extra term is zero unless $\xi$ is null.  The original slice
has future normal $N=(\partial_z-X)/u$ and induces exactly
$(g,K,E)$, with $\mathbf F$ restricting to zero on it.
There is a global smooth function $p$, including up to $S$, with
\begin{equation}
 \dd p=(k-1)uE^\flat,
 \qquad p(\infty)=0,
 \qquad p=O_2(r^{2-n}),
 \qquad \dd(i_X\alpha)=0.
 
\end{equation}

Let $\kappa=c/2>0$.  On $S$ the boundary laws are
\begin{equation}
 X=u\nu,\qquad
 \partial_\nu u+K(X,\nu)=\kappa,\qquad
 cH=2L_+^*u,
 
\end{equation}
where $L_+$ is the outward normal linearization of
$H+\operatorname{tr}_S K$, and its adjoint uses $\dd A_g$.
Either $u>0$ on all of $S$, or $u=0$ on all of $S$.
The nonnegative function $W=u^2-|X|^2$ tends to one at
infinity, vanishes on $S$, and is strictly positive in a
deleted collar of $S$.  If $u>0$ on $S$, then
\begin{equation}
 \dd W=2\kappa X^\flat\quad\hbox{on }S.
 
\end{equation}
If $u=0$ on $S$, writing $s$ for exterior distance from $S$,
there are smooth fields $a_*,Y_*$ such that
\begin{equation}
 u=s a_*,\qquad X=s^2Y_*,\qquad a_*|_S=\kappa.
 
\end{equation}
No assertion of a Lorentzian extension across the zero-lapse
boundary is made at this stage.

statements.title: Charged reduction to vacuum
statements.label: stat:charged-vacuum
statements.section_title: Electric transport and the complete vacuum static base

statements.title: Global positivity when the charge vanishes
statements.label: stat:zero-charge-positivity
statements.text:
If $Q=0$, then $E=0$, $p=0$, and $W>0$ on all of
$\Omega^\circ$.  The attached pair $(h_s,\lambda)$ is a complete
vacuum static pair with $0<\lambda<1$, connected compact boundary,
and boundary derivative $\kappa$.
statements.section_title: Electric transport and the complete vacuum static base

statements.title: Complete vacuum reduction
statements.label: stat:vacuum-reduction
statements.text:
Under the stationary interface stated at the start of this section,
the Killing field is timelike on the whole open exterior:
$W>0$ on $\Omega^\circ$.  The original matter densities vanish
there, $X\wedge E=0$, and $dA_s=0$.  The orbit pair
$(h_s,\lambda)$ has the regular attachment in
Lemma~\ref{stat:base-attachment}.

If $Q\ne0$, define $(h_0,\lambda_0)$ by
\eqref{stat:explicit-vacuum-transform}; if $Q=0$, take
$(h_0,\lambda_0)=(h_s,\lambda)$.  In either case this is a smooth
vacuum static pair satisfying~\eqref{stat:vacuum-equations} on a
connected orientable exterior, complete including its connected
compact boundary, with compact complement of exactly one Euclidean
coordinate end.  Its lapse is zero at the boundary, lies strictly
between zero and one in the interior, and tends to one at infinity.
The inward boundary derivative is a positive constant, equal to
\eqref{stat:vacuum-boundary-gradient} in the charged case and to
$\kappa$ in the uncharged case.  The boundary is totally geodesic
and $\operatorname{Hess}_{h_0}\lambda_0=0$ there.  Gaussian
reflection of $h_0$ with odd reflection of $\lambda_0$ is at least
$C^{2,\alpha}$ for $0<\alpha<1$.

After a fixed linear change of end coordinates,
\begin{equation}
 h_0-\delta=O_2(r^{-q_0}),\qquad
 \lambda_0-1=O_2(r^{-q_0})
 
\end{equation}
for $q_0$ as in~\eqref{stat:end-exponent}.  No simple-connectivity
claim or global primitive of $A_s$ is needed for this reduction.
statements.section_title: Electric transport and the complete vacuum static base

statements.title: Vacuum uniqueness
statements.label: uniq:vacuum-uniqueness
statements.text:
Let $n\geq4$ and let $(B,h_0,\lambda_0)$ be a smooth oriented vacuum static
exterior, complete including its connected compact boundary $S$,
with a compact complement of one Euclidean coordinate end. Suppose
\begin{equation}
 \Hess_{h_0}\lambda_0=\lambda_0\Ric_{h_0},\qquad
 \Delta_{h_0}\lambda_0=0,\qquad
 \lambda_0|_S=0,\qquad \lambda_0\longrightarrow1,
\end{equation}
and $\partial_\nu\lambda_0=\kappa_0>0$ on $S$, with $\nu$ pointing
toward the end. Assume, after a constant linear normalization of end
coordinates,
\begin{equation}
 h_0-\delta=O_2(r^{-q_0}),\qquad
 \lambda_0-1=O_2(r^{-q_0}),\qquad
 \frac{n-2}{2}<q_0<n-2.
\end{equation}
Then $B$ is globally the exterior of a round sphere in isotropic
coordinates. For some $R>0$, writing $\rho=|x|\geq R$,
\begin{equation}
 h_0=\left(1+\frac{R^{n-2}}{\rho^{n-2}}\right)^{4/(n-2)}\delta,
 \qquad
 \lambda_0=
 \frac{1-R^{n-2}/\rho^{n-2}}{1+R^{n-2}/\rho^{n-2}}.
\end{equation}
The identification extends smoothly to $S$.
statements.section_title: Vacuum doubling with a weak asymptotic tail

statements.title: Global recovery of the original exterior
statements.label: rec:original-embedding
statements.text:
Under the connected nonextremal equality hypotheses, the original
$(\Omega,g,K,E)$ admits a global orientation-preserving smooth
spacelike embedding, including its boundary, into the regular future
horizon extension of the Reissner--Nordstr\"om--Tangherlini exterior
\begin{equation}
 G_{m,Q}=-f(r)\,\dd T^2+f(r)^{-1}\,\dd r^2+r^2\sigma_k,
 \qquad
 f(r)=1-\frac{2m}{r^{k-1}}+\frac{Q^2}{r^{2k-2}},
\end{equation}
with Faraday form
\begin{equation}
 F_{m,Q}=c_n Qr^{-k}\,\dd T\wedge\dd r,
 \qquad c_n=\sqrt{\frac{k(k-1)}2}.
\end{equation}
It induces exactly $g,K,E$ with
$K(U,V)=G_{m,Q}(\nabla_U N,V)$ and
$E^\flat=c_n^{-1}\iota^*(i_NF_{m,Q})$, and
$\iota^*F_{m,Q}=0$. Its boundary is a full smooth future horizon
section if $u|_S>0$, and is the bifurcation sphere if $u|_S=0$.
The future normal and all induced data extend smoothly to the
boundary; the end approaches the corresponding spatial infinity.
Moreover $\mu_m=J_m=0$ on the original exterior.
statements.section_title: Recovery of the original data and sharp examples

statements.title: Converse and sharpness
statements.label: rec:sharpness
statements.text:
Every model slice in the stated converse class, with parameters
$M>|q_0|$ and actual invariant ADM mass and signed flux equal to
$M,q_0$, attains equality. For every such parameter pair and every
$n\geq4$, this class contains the static exterior slice and smooth
compact radial time perturbations of it with $K\not\equiv0$.

title: A Codimension-One Bound for the Singular Set of a Stationary Integral Varifold
abstract: The singular set of every stationary integral m-varifold in an open Euclidean set has Hausdorff dimension at most \(m-1\), in every positive dimension and codimension. This sharp bound proves the Euclidean singular-set conjecture recorded by Brena, Decio, and De Lellis.

tex.abstract:
The singular set of every stationary integral $m$-varifold in an open
Euclidean set has Hausdorff dimension at most $m-1$, in every positive
dimension and codimension. This sharp bound proves the Euclidean
singular-set conjecture recorded by Brena, Decio, and De Lellis.
sections: Flat scales carrying many singular centers
Density centers survive the height blow-up
Dimension reduction for the limiting measures

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every stationary integral $m$-varifold $V$ in an open set
$U\subset\R^{m+n}$, where $m,n\ge1$,
\[
 \dim_{\Hh}\Sing V\le m-1.
\]

statements.title: Flat scales and a measure of centers
statements.label: prop:flat-scales
statements.text:
Suppose that $V$ is a stationary integral $m$-varifold in an open
subset of $\R^{m+n}$ and that
\[
 m-1<s<\dim_{\Hh}\Sing(V).
\]
After a translation there exist a fixed point $0\in\Sing(V)$, an
integer $Q\ge1$, an $m$-plane $\Pi$ through zero, radii $L_i\downarrow0$,
and positive Radon measures $\sigma_i$ such that
\begin{equation}
 
 \Theta_V(0)=Q,\qquad V_{L_i}\rightharpoonup Q|\Pi|
 \quad\hbox{locally in }\R^{m+n}.
\end{equation}
Each $\sigma_i$ is supported in $\overline{\mathbf B}_1$ on singular
points of $V_{L_i}$ having density exactly $Q$. There are constants
$c,C>0$, independent of $i$, for which
\begin{equation}
 
 \sigma_i(\mathbf B_u(X))\le C u^s
 \quad(X\in\R^{m+n},\ u>0),\qquad
 c\le\sigma_i(\overline{\mathbf B}_1)\le C.
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Flat scales carrying many singular centers

statements.title: Signed excess
statements.label: thm:signed-input
statements.text:
Fix an integer $Q\ge1$ and $\kappa>0$. In the normal-cylinder setting above, scale a
physical base radius $l$ to one and suppose $B_4$ is available. Set
$\tau=|M|+D+\Lambda$. If
\begin{equation}
 \tau(B_4)\le d=e^{-T},\qquad
 l+\sup|z_{\mathrm{phys}}|\le d^\kappa,
\end{equation}
where the supremum is over the restricted support above the available
chart, then, for $T$ sufficiently large,
\begin{equation}
 \int w\,\dd(2M-D-C_Q\Lambda)
       \le d\exp[-F_Q(T)]
\end{equation}
whenever $w$ is supported in $B_1$, $0\le w\le1$, and $\Lip w\le1$.
The finite derivative order $J$, threshold, and constants depend only
on the stated fixed data. For a subchart in inherited frames, the second
condition is imposed on $\gamma$ in Equation~\eqref{eq:physical-gamma}.
For a flat reference, take $\Lambda=0$ and omit the second condition.

statements.title: Uniform comparison at the targets
statements.label: prop:target-frequency
statements.text:
All sufficiently late $L_i$ belong to intervals
\eqref{eq:target-interval}. After passing to a subsequence, either one
interval extends to zero and contains all these targets, or the indices
of their covering intervals tend to infinity. In the latter case,
on each sufficiently late covering interval,
\begin{equation}
 |P(r)|\le C\qquad(B_*b\le r\le r_*),
\end{equation}
and \eqref{eq:height-doubling} holds there with uniform constants.
In the former case the same conclusions hold on the sufficiently
small-radius part of the fixed interval.

statements.title: Centered blow-up at the target scales
statements.label: prop:centered-blowup
statements.text:
Let the stationary integral varifold, singular origin, integer $Q$,
plane $\Pi$, and sequence $L_i\downarrow0$ be as in
Proposition~\ref{prop:flat-scales}. After taking a subsequence and
identifying $\Pi$ with the horizontal plane, there are positive
$a_i\to0$ and $C^J$ graph disks $S_i$ over a fixed enlargement of
$B_8\subset\Pi$, converging to $\Pi$ through all derivative orders
needed below, with the following properties. In target units let
$\mu_i$ be the weight of $V_{L_i}$, let $\pi_i$ be nearest projection
to $S_i$, and set
\[
 z_i=X-\pi_iX,\qquad
 M_i=(\pi_i)_\#\mu_i-Q\vol_{S_i},\qquad
 D_i=(\pi_i)_\#(e_i\mu_i).
\]
All measures are restricted to one fixed interior normal cylinder
containing the support in question, with a support-free gap at its
vertical boundary. On the part over $B_8$,
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
 D_i+|M_i|=O(a_i^2)\quad\hbox{in total mass},
 \qquad |z_i|\le Ca_i\quad\hbox{on the support},\\
 \sup\bigl(|\mathcal H_{S_i}|+
                  |\nabla^\perp\mathcal H_{S_i}|\bigr)=o(a_i),
 \qquad
 a_i^{-1}(\pi_i)_\#(z_i\mu_i)\rightharpoonup0.
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
Moreover the normalized height-square measures have uniformly bounded
mass there and are quantitatively nonzero on a fixed compact subset
of $B_4$; in particular, for all sufficiently large $i$,
\begin{equation}
 c\le a_i^{-2}\int_{\pi_iX\in B_3}|z_i|^2\,\dd\mu_i
 \le a_i^{-2}\int_{\pi_iX\in B_8}|z_i|^2\,\dd\mu_i\le C.
\end{equation}
Balls in this statement are understood through the graph coordinates
over $\Pi$. The weak convergence in \eqref{eq:centered-interface}
holds against compactly supported tests in $B_8$.

statements.title: The limiting measure equations
statements.label: prop:linearized
statements.text:
Let $V_i$ be stationary integral $m$-varifolds converging locally to
$Q|\Pi|$, where $Q$ is a positive integer and $\Pi$ is an $m$-plane.
Let $S_i$ be reference graphs converging to $\Pi$ in every fixed finite
derivative order used below, on a normal cylinder with fixed interior
room over a connected disk $\Omega\subset\Pi$. The cylinders contain all
support used below and have a support-free gap at their artificial vertical
boundaries above each compact base subset. Let $\mu_i$ denote the weight
of $V_i$ restricted to this cylinder, $\pi_i$ nearest projection onto
$S_i$, and $z_i=X-\pi_iX$. All pushforwards below use this restriction.
Use the horizontal and vertical tangent blocks relative to $S_i$ to set
$B_i=I-(P_T)_{hh}$, $e_i=\tr B_i$,
$D_i=(\pi_i)_\#(e_i\mu_i)$, and
$M_i=(\pi_i)_\#\mu_i-Q\vol_{S_i}$.
Suppose $a_i\downarrow0$ and, on each compact subdisk with interior room,
\begin{gather*}
 |M_i|+D_i=O(a_i^2),\qquad |z_i|\le Ca_i\quad\hbox{on the support},\\
 |\mathcal H_{S_i}|+|\nabla^\perp\mathcal H_{S_i}|=o(a_i),
 \qquad a_i^{-1}(\pi_i)_\#(z_i\mu_i)\rightharpoonup0.
\end{gather*}
Assume also that $a_i^{-2}(\pi_i)_\#(|z_i|^2\mu_i)$ has a positive
uniform lower mass bound on a fixed compact subset of $\Omega$.
Identify the bases by their converging graph coordinates. After passage
to a subsequence there are Radon measures satisfying
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 a_i^{-2}(\pi_i)_\#(|z_i|^2\mu_i)&\rightharpoonup\nu,&
 a_i^{-2}(\pi_i)_\#(B_i\mu_i)&\rightharpoonup\beta,\\
 a_i^{-2}D_i&\rightharpoonup d_0=\tr\beta,&
 a_i^{-2}M_i&\rightharpoonup\mathfrak m,\\
 a_i^{-2}(\pi_i)_\#\bigl(z_i\cdot(P_T)_{vh}\,\mu_i\bigr)
   &\rightharpoonup f.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Here $\nu\ne0$ and $d_0$ are nonnegative measures, $f$ is vector-valued,
$\beta$ is symmetric matrix-valued, and $\mathfrak m$ is signed. They obey
\begin{equation}
 \begin{pmatrix}\nu&f^{\mathsf t}\\ f&\beta\end{pmatrix}\ge0
\end{equation}
as a matrix-valued measure, and
\begin{equation}
 \nabla\nu=2f,\qquad \diver f=d_0,\qquad
 \int_\Omega\diver X\,\dd\mathfrak m
   =\int_\Omega DX:\dd\beta
 \quad (X\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\R^m)).
\end{equation}
Finally, locally on $\Omega$,
\begin{equation}
             2\mathfrak m\le d_0,\qquad
             |\mathfrak m|\le C d_0.
\end{equation}
The data supplied by Proposition~\ref{prop:centered-blowup} satisfy these
hypotheses, with a fixed disk containing the closed unit ball of density
centers.

statements.title: Comparison at the density centers
statements.label: prop:density-comparison
statements.text:
In the setting of Proposition~\ref{prop:linearized}, suppose that
$\Omega$ contains a fixed neighborhood of $\overline B_1\subset\Pi$.
Let $\sigma_i$ be positive measures supported on density-$Q$ points of
$V_i$ in the ambient closed unit ball, with
\[
 c\le\sigma_i(\overline{\mathbf B}_1)\le C,
 \qquad \sigma_i(\mathbf B_r(X))\le Cr^s
 \quad(X\in\R^{m+n},\ r>0),\qquad s>m-1.
\]
Pass to a weak limit $\sigma$ along the subsequence defining the
linearized measures. Then $\sigma\ne0$, its support lies in
$\overline B_1\subset\Pi$, and it has the same upper ball bound.
There is $l_*>0$ such that
\begin{equation}
 2l^2\int\phi_{x,l}\,\dd\mathfrak m
       \ge\int\psi_{x,l}\,\dd\nu
 \qquad(x\in\spt\sigma, 0<l<l_*).
\end{equation}

prop:surface

surface $X$ with an ample globally generated divisor $H$ such that

statements.label: cor:affine-local
statements.text:
Let $X$ and $H$ be the surface and polarization constructed in

\[
 T=T(X,H),\qquad \mathfrak n=T_{>0}.

Then $T$ is a finitely generated graded three-dimensional $\C$-domain,
$\mathfrak n$ is maximal with $T/\mathfrak n=\C$, and the
three-dimensional local domain $T_{\mathfrak n}$ has no nonzero finitely
generated maximal Cohen--Macaulay module.

title: A Conditional Reduction for Algebraic Kuga–Satake Correspondences
abstract: For a polarized K3 surface whose primitive cohomology has full orthogonal Hodge group, one algebraic correspondence inducing a nonzero map from that cohomology to the second cohomology of an abelian variety suffices to recover the prescribed full Kuga–Satake correspondence. We give an equivalent condition using holomorphic one-forms on a generically finite surface cover. If this input holds very generally in a polarized component, the prescribed correspondence is algebraic throughout that component, for every choice of standard data on the transcendental part. The existence of the initial correspondence remains a hypothesis.

tex.abstract: For a polarized K3 surface whose primitive cohomology has full orthogonal Hodge group, one algebraic correspondence inducing a nonzero map from that cohomology to the second cohomology of an abelian variety suffices to recover the prescribed full Kuga--Satake correspondence. We give an equivalent condition using holomorphic one-forms on a generically finite surface cover. If this input holds very generally in a polarized component, the prescribed correspondence is algebraic throughout that component, for every choice of standard data on the transcendental part. The existence of the initial correspondence remains a hypothesis.
sections: Cycle operations and the two inputs
Full Clifford structures and their tensor maps
Recovering the full Clifford correspondence at a general point
Specialization of an actual algebraic class
Restriction and the prescribed data at a special fiber

statements.title: Recovery at a point with full Hodge group
statements.label: main:generic
statements.text:
Suppose $\operatorname{Hg}(V)=\operatorname{SO}(V,q)$. The following conditions are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
\item There are an abelian variety $B$ and a cycle $\alpha\in\operatorname{CH}^2(S\times B)_{\mathbb Q}$ such that
\[
 \alpha_*:V\longrightarrow H^2(B,\mathbb Q)
\]
is nonzero.
\item There are a smooth connected projective surface $Y$ and a dominant generically finite morphism $f:Y\to S$ such that
\begin{equation}
 f_*\!\left(\operatorname{im}\!\left[
 \bigwedge\nolimits^2 H^0(Y,\Omega_Y^1)
 \longrightarrow H^0(Y,\Omega_Y^2)\right]\right)\ne0.
\end{equation}
\item The prescribed full Kuga--Satake map is realized as in \eqref{eq:cycle-target}, for any stipulated standard data on $T$.
\end{enumerate}
In this situation $T=V$. The same input realizes the standard map for the full primitive Clifford construction with the cup form.

statements.title: Specialization in a polarized component
statements.label: main:specialization
statements.text:
Fix a component of the moduli space of primitively amply polarized K3 surfaces of degree $2d$. Assume that condition \textup{(i)} or condition \textup{(ii)} of Theorem~\ref{main:generic} holds very generally in that component. Then every $(S,h)$ in the component satisfies \eqref{eq:cycle-target}, with all the stipulated standard data on $T(S)$.

Here it suffices that, about each desired point, the input holds outside a countable union of proper closed analytic subsets of a full polarized period chart. In particular an input outside countably many proper algebraic subsets of the moduli component suffices. The witness cycles, abelian varieties, or surface covers need not vary in a family.

statements.label: main:all-degrees
statements.text: If the hypothesis of Theorem~\ref{main:specialization} holds in the required polarized components in every degree, then \eqref{eq:cycle-target} holds for every projective K3 surface.

statements.title: Correspondences and surface covers
statements.label: cyc:equivalence
statements.text: Conditions \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} of Theorem~\ref{main:generic} are equivalent. The implication from the surface condition to a nonzero correspondence on $V$ does not require the full Hodge-group hypothesis.
statements.section_title: Cycle operations and the two inputs

statements.label: cliff:construction
statements.text:
The Hodge structures $P_H^\pm$ are polarizable, and
\begin{equation}
 m^Q:H(1)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(P_H^+,P_H^-),
 \qquad x\longmapsto L_x
\end{equation}
is a rational Hodge embedding. The parity spaces are rationally
Hodge-isomorphic by right multiplication by any fixed invertible odd
Clifford element. On a sufficiently small period chart, their Hodge
filtrations vary holomorphically and admit fixed rational polarizations.
statements.section_title: Full Clifford structures and their tensor maps

statements.label: gen:genericity
statements.text:
In any sufficiently small, full-dimensional marked polarized period chart,
Equation~\eqref{gen:full-group} holds outside a countable union of proper
closed analytic subsets.  At every point satisfying
Equation~\eqref{gen:full-group}, the Hodge structure $V$ is irreducible and
$T(S)=V$.
statements.section_title: Recovering the full Clifford correspondence at a general point

statements.label: gen:generation
statements.text:
Assume Equation~\eqref{gen:full-group}.  Suppose that
$\alpha\in\operatorname{CH}^2(S\times B)_{\mathbb Q}$ induces a
nonzero map $V\to H^2(B,\mathbb Q)$ for some complex abelian variety
$B$.  Let $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\in\{+,-\}$, and let $A_1,A_2$ be
abelian varieties realizing $W^{\epsilon_1},W^{\epsilon_2}$ as their
first rational cohomology.  Every rational Hodge map
\[
 \beta:V\longrightarrow W^{\epsilon_1}\otimes W^{\epsilon_2}
 \subset H^2(A_1\times A_2,\mathbb Q)
\]
is the restriction of the action of a cycle
$\Gamma\in\operatorname{CH}^2(S\times A_1\times A_2)_{\mathbb Q}$.
In particular, this recovers the full primitive Clifford
multiplication tensor and its prescribed even-Clifford realization.
statements.section_title: Recovering the full Clifford correspondence at a general point

statements.title: Specialization from very general algebraicity
statements.label: spec:specialization
statements.text:
Let $D$ be a connected polydisc, and let
$p:\mathcal X\to D$ be a smooth proper holomorphic family of
$n$-dimensional varieties, $n\geq2$, with a relative embedding in
$D\times\mathbb P^N$.  Let
\[
 \theta\in H^0(D,R^4p_*\mathbb Q)
\]
be a flat rational class.  If $\theta_t$ is the class of a rational
codimension-two algebraic cycle for very general $t\in D$, then the same
holds for every $t\in D$.
statements.section_title: Specialization of an actual algebraic class

statements.title: The primitive map at every polarized fiber
statements.label: spec:primitive
statements.text:
Fix a polarized moduli component, and assume that at very general
points the nonzero algebraic input of Theorem~\ref{main:generic} holds.
Then at every $(S_0,h)$ in that component the standard full primitive
Clifford tensor is induced by a rational codimension-two algebraic
cycle.  The same conclusion holds if the hypothesis is made outside
countably many proper closed analytic subsets in a full-dimensional
polarized period chart about each desired point.
statements.section_title: Specialization of an actual algebraic class

statements.title: Restriction to the transcendental part
statements.label: data:restriction
statements.text:
Set $q_0=q|_T$. Algebraic realization of $m^q$ on $V$ implies
algebraic realization of $m^{q_0}$ on $T$.
statements.section_title: Restriction and the prescribed data at a special fiber

statements.title: Change of quadratic polarization
statements.label: data:polarization
statements.text:
Let $q_0$ and $q_1$ be rational quadratic Hodge polarizations on
the same K3-type Hodge structure $T$, allowing either overall sign
as in Section~\ref{cliff:section}. If $T\subset H^2(S,\mathbb Q)$
and $m^{q_0}$ is algebraically realized, then so is $m^{q_1}$.
statements.section_title: Restriction and the prescribed data at a special fiber

title: A Coulomb ground-state density without Kohn-Sham ensemble representation
abstract: We construct a finite three-electron Coulomb molecule whose spin-summed ground-state density cannot be reproduced by any ground-state ensemble of noninteracting electrons in a single real, spin-independent local potential in \(L^{3/2}(\mathbf R^3)+L^\infty(\mathbf R^3)\). The molecule has two equal positive integer nuclear charges, specified by an exact finite nonnumerical formula.

tex.abstract:
We construct a finite three-electron Coulomb molecule whose spin-summed
ground-state density cannot be reproduced by any ground-state ensemble
of noninteracting electrons in a single real, spin-independent local
potential in \(L^{3/2}(\R^3)+L^\infty(\R^3)\).
The molecule has two equal positive integer nuclear charges,
specified by an exact finite nonnumerical formula.
sections: The Coulomb system and its small-coupling limit
Exterior channels and the density near the median plane
An angle minimum and its spectral gap
Certification of the ensemble kinetic minimum
The obstruction from the median plane
An exact choice of the charges and nuclear positions
A functional consequence for the physical density

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Set \(D=10^{200}\) and \(e_z=(0,0,1)\).
There is a finite positive integer \(Z\), specified by
\Cref{eq:explicit-charge}, for which the Coulomb Hamiltonian
\[
H_C=\sum_{i=1}^3
\left(-\frac12\Delta_i
-\frac{Z}{|r_i-(D/Z)e_z|}
-\frac{Z}{|r_i+(D/Z)e_z|}\right)
+\sum_{1\le i<j\le3}\frac1{|r_i-r_j|}
\]
has a normalizable absolute ground state \(\Psi\) in the sector
\(S_z=1/2\), normalized by \(\|\Psi\|_2=1\), but there is no
\(v\in\mathcal V\) and no ground-state
ensemble \(\Gamma\) of \(H_s(v)\) such that
\[
n_\Gamma=n_\Psi\qquad\text{almost everywhere on }\R^3.
\]

statements.title: Dilation to integer nuclear charges
statements.label: prop:scaling
statements.text:
Suppose that the density of a ground state of \(H_{3,1/Z}\), for a
positive integer \(Z\), has no noninteracting ground-state ensemble
representation with a real spin-independent potential in
\(L^{3/2}(\R^3)+L^\infty(\R^3)\).
The physical Coulomb system with three electrons and charges \(Z,Z\)
at
\[
 (0,0,D/Z),\qquad (0,0,-D/Z)
\]
then has a ground-state density with the same obstruction.
statements.section_title: The Coulomb system and its small-coupling limit

statements.title: Two-centre spectrum
statements.label: prop:two-centre-spectrum
statements.text:
For \(D\ge100\), the two lowest eigenvalues of \(h_D\) are simple.
They have normalized real, axisymmetric eigenfunctions \(b,e\), where
\(b>0\) is even and \(e\) is odd and strictly positive on \(z>0\).
Write
\[
 \epsilon_b=-\frac{\gamma^2}{2},\qquad
 \epsilon_e=-\frac{k_0^2}{2},\qquad
 d_*=\epsilon_e-\epsilon_b .
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 0<d_*<\frac{100}{D},\qquad
 |\gamma-1|+|k_0-1|<\frac{200}{D}.
 
\end{equation}
The spectrum on \(\{b,e\}^{\perp}\) lies more than \(0.2\) above
\(\epsilon_e\).  In particular, the spectral gap above \(b\) in the
even subspace is greater than \(0.2\).
statements.section_title: The Coulomb system and its small-coupling limit

statements.title: Small repulsive coupling
statements.label: prop:small-coupling
statements.text:
Fix \(D\ge100\).  For all sufficiently small \(\lambda\ge0\), the
ionic operator \(H_{2,\lambda}\) has a simple isolated ground state,
and \(H_{3,\lambda}\) has a simple isolated ground state
\(\Psi_\lambda\) in the sector \(S_z=1/2\).  Its energy is an absolute
ground energy of \(H_{3,\lambda}\).

The ionic ground state is a spin singlet, is even under simultaneous
reflection of its two spatial coordinates, and is axisymmetric.
The state \(\Psi_\lambda\) is real, axisymmetric, and odd under
simultaneous reflection of its three spatial coordinates.
The states and energies can be chosen analytic near zero; in
particular, their state vectors converge with error \(O(\lambda)\)
in \(H^2\).  At zero coupling,
\begin{equation}
 \Psi_0=b\uparrow\wedge b\downarrow\wedge e\uparrow,\qquad
 E_2(0)=2\epsilon_b,\qquad
 E_3(0)=2\epsilon_b+\epsilon_e .
 
\end{equation}
The ionic state has spatial factor \(b(x_1)b(x_2)\) and the normalized
singlet spin factor.
statements.section_title: The Coulomb system and its small-coupling limit

statements.title: Density estimates
statements.label: prop:density-properties
statements.section_title: Exterior channels and the density near the median plane

statements.title: Channels at a fixed coupling
statements.label: prop:fixed-parameter-channels
statements.text:
Suppose \(D\) satisfies \Cref{prop:two-centre-spectrum} and
\[
 k_0>\sqrt{0.98},\qquad \gamma<\sqrt{49/45}.
 \]
Fix \(t\in(0,1]\).  Assume the two-electron ground level is isolated
and simple with an even ionic singlet, and the three-electron
ground level in \(S_z=1/2\) is isolated and simple, is an absolute
ground level, and has a real axisymmetric odd ground state.
Assume \(n_t>0\), and set
\[
 k=\sqrt{2(E_2(t)-E_3(t))},\qquad
 A_t(r)=e^{-kr}r^{(2-2t)/k-1}.
 \]
Suppose
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
 2\epsilon_b-E_3(t)>0.49,\qquad 0.99<k<\gamma,\\
 \inf_{\omega_z>0}\liminf_{r\to\infty}
 \frac{\|P_tF_{\mathrm{true},t}(r\omega)\|}
      {\omega_z A_t(r)}>0.
 \end{gathered}
 
\end{equation}
Then \(n_t\) has the local regularity in
\Cref{lem:density-regularity}, is smooth away from the nuclei,
and satisfies \Cref{eq:plane-tail,eq:plane-translate,eq:bulk-translate}
at this fixed coupling, with \(A=A_t\) and suitable positive constants.
Membership of \(t\) in the preceding perturbative interval is
not required.
statements.section_title: Exterior channels and the density near the median plane

statements.title: Existence and regularity of the angle
statements.label: prop:angle-minimizer
statements.text:
Let \(n\) be a positive, continuous, even density with
\(\int n=3\), \(n\in H^2_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R^3)\), and
\(\sqrt n\in H^1(\R^3)\).  The problem
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 &\min_{\vartheta\in H^1(n;\R)}
       \int_{\R^3}n|\nabla\vartheta|^2,\\
 &\text{subject to }\quad
       \vartheta\text{ odd},\qquad
       \int_{\R^3}n\sin^2\vartheta=1
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
has a minimizer \(\theta\) satisfying
\(0\le\theta\le\pi/2\) on \(\Omega_+\).
Every such folded minimizer has a multiplier \(d>0\) and satisfies
\begin{equation}
 L_n\theta:=n^{-1}\operatorname{div}(n\nabla\theta)
       =-d\sin(2\theta)
 \quad\hbox{on }\R^3.
\end{equation}
It belongs locally to \(W^{2,p}\) for every \(p<6\), and
\[
 0<\theta<\pi/2\quad\hbox{on }\Omega_+.
\]
In particular, it is locally \(C^{1,\alpha}\) for every
\(0<\alpha<1/2\).  Axial symmetry of \(n\) is not required for this
proposition, and axial symmetry of \(\theta\) is not asserted.
statements.section_title: An angle minimum and its spectral gap

statements.title: Convergence of every folded minimum
statements.label: prop:angle-convergence
statements.text:
For every choice of folded minimizing angles for \(n_\lambda\),
\begin{equation}
 \theta_\lambda\longrightarrow
 \theta_*=\arctan\!\left(\frac{e}{\sqrt2\,b}\right),
 \qquad
 d_\lambda\longrightarrow d_*=\epsilon_e-\epsilon_b.
\end{equation}
The angle convergence is weak in local \(H^1\), strong in local
\(L^2\), and in \(C^1\) on every fixed compact set.  In particular,
all these conclusions hold uniformly over the set of folded
minimizers in the sequential sense.
statements.section_title: An angle minimum and its spectral gap

statements.title: The two orbital equations
statements.label: prop:orbital-equations
statements.section_title: An angle minimum and its spectral gap

statements.title: Uniform exterior gap
statements.label: prop:exterior-gap
statements.text:
For sufficiently large \(D\), there are \(\lambda_0>0\) and \(R_0<\infty\)
such that every folded minimizing angle for
\(0\le\lambda<\lambda_0\) satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \frac12\int_{\Omega_+}g^2|\nabla\xi|^2
       \ge0.03\int_{\Omega_+}g^2|\xi|^2
\end{equation}
for tests supported in \(\{|x|>R_0\}\).
No zero trace on \(z=0\) is required.
The inequality holds throughout the corresponding weighted form domain.

statements.title: An ensemble kinetic certificate
statements.label: prop:ensemble-certificate
statements.text:
Assume the density regularity of \Cref{lem:density-regularity}, the
orbital hypotheses of \Cref{prop:orbital-equations}, and the weighted
gap \Cref{eq:weighted-gap}.  Then the formal potential $V$ satisfies
$\int_{\R^3}n|V|<\infty$.  Every ensemble with density $n$ and finite
kinetic energy obeys
\begin{equation}
 T[\Gamma]+\int_{\R^3}Vn\ge d.
 
\end{equation}
The determinant $\Phi_\theta$ attains equality.  Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 T_{\mathrm{ens}}[n]
 =T[|\Phi_\theta\rangle\langle\Phi_\theta|]
 =d-\int_{\R^3}Vn.
 
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Certification of the ensemble kinetic minimum

statements.title: Transfer to a representing Hamiltonian
statements.label: prop:potential-identification
statements.text:
Assume the hypotheses of \Cref{prop:ensemble-certificate}.  Let
$v\in L^{3/2}(\R^3)+L^\infty(\R^3)$ be real and spin independent,
and let $h_v=-\Delta/2+v$ be its spatial one-particle operator, defined
by the closed form on $H^1(\R^3)$.  Suppose
$H_v=\sum_{i=1}^3(h_v\otimes\id_{\C^2})_i$ on $\mathfrak H_3$
has a ground eigenspace supporting an ensemble $\Gamma_s$ with
$n_{\Gamma_s}=n$.  Then $\Phi_\theta$ belongs to that ground eigenspace,
and there is a real constant $e_g$ such that
\begin{equation}
 h_v g=e_g g,
 \qquad v=V+e_g\quad\text{almost everywhere}.
 
\end{equation}
In particular, $V\in L^{3/2}(\R^3)+L^\infty(\R^3)$.
statements.section_title: Certification of the ensemble kinetic minimum

statements.title: The unique potential limit at infinity
statements.label: prop:potential-limits
statements.text:
Assume \Cref{eq:admissible-formal-potential} and the density translation
limits \Cref{eq:plane-translate,eq:bulk-translate}.  For every sequence
\(|y_j|\to\infty\), every local weak-star subsequential limit of
\(V_{\mathrm b}(y_j+\cdot)\) is the constant
\begin{equation}
 c_\infty=d+\frac{k^2}{2}.
 
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: The obstruction from the median plane

statements.title: A fixed-density obstruction
statements.label: thm:obstruction
statements.text:
Let \(n,\theta,g,h,V,d\) have the analytic properties stated at the
beginning of this section, with \(d>0\).  Suppose that
\Cref{eq:plane-tail,eq:plane-translate,eq:bulk-translate} hold with fixed
\(k>0\) and \(\beta\), and that the weighted gap
\Cref{eq:weighted-gap} holds.  Then
\[
 V\notin L^{3/2}(\R^3)+L^\infty(\R^3).
\]
Moreover, \(n\) is not the density of a ground-state ensemble of any
three-electron noninteracting Hamiltonian with a single real,
spin-independent potential in this class.  These hypotheses are all
fixed-parameter hypotheses; no perturbative neighborhood is required.

statements.title: A family of finite Coulombic counterexamples
statements.label: thm:qualitative-counterexample
statements.text:
For every sufficiently large fixed \(D\), there is an integer
\(Z_0(D)\) such that, for every integer \(Z\ge Z_0(D)\), the
three-electron Coulomb Hamiltonian with nuclear charges \(Z,Z\) at
\((0,0,\pm D/Z)\) has an absolute ground state whose density is not
representable by a ground-state ensemble of a single real,
spin-independent noninteracting potential in
\(L^{3/2}(\R^3)+L^\infty(\R^3)\).

title: A Counterexample to Kaplansky's Direct-Finiteness Conjecture in Characteristic Two
abstract: We disprove Kaplansky's direct-finiteness conjecture by constructing a finite field K of characteristic two, a finitely presented group G, and finite sums \(a,b\in K[G]\) with \(ab=1\) but \(ba\ne1\). The group G is nonsofic. The same elements define a cellular automaton on KG that is injective but not surjective, disproving Gottschalk's surjunctivity conjecture.

tex.abstract: We disprove Kaplansky's direct-finiteness conjecture by constructing a finite field $K$ of characteristic two, a finitely presented group $G$, and finite sums $a,b\in K[G]$ with $ab=1$ but $ba\ne1$. The group $G$ is nonsofic. The same elements define a cellular automaton on $K^G$ that is injective but not surjective, disproving Gottschalk's surjunctivity conjecture.

An incidence criterion and its embedded local groups
From subgroup averages to the scalar defect

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There exist a finite field $K$ of characteristic two, a finitely presented group $G$ containing an element of odd prime order, and elements $a_{\mathrm{out}},b_{\mathrm{out}}\in K[G]$ such that
\[
a_{\mathrm{out}}b_{\mathrm{out}}=1,
\qquad b_{\mathrm{out}}a_{\mathrm{out}}\ne1.
\]
The field, group, and finite sums are specified by a terminating prescription involving finite sets and finite-field arithmetic.

statements.title: The pairing supplied by holes
statements.label: prop:pairing
statements.text:
Let $q\ge4$ be a power of two, let $Q$ be a field of order $q$, fix an enumeration of $Q$, and let $n\ge1$. Put $d_0=(q-2)/2$, $S=S_{d_0}\subset\mathcal A=Q^n$, and $N_{\rm pt}=q^n$. Let $\ell$ be an odd prime and $D=\ell+1$. Suppose that $O\subset S$ and that $\mathcal F$ is a family of full affine $Q$-lines contained in $V=\mathcal A\setminus O$, with
\begin{equation}

\frac{2N_{\rm pt}}{D^2}\le |O|\le\frac{7N_{\rm pt}}{D^2}.
\end{equation}
Suppose also that every point of $V$ lies on $D$ members of $\mathcal F$ and that the incidence graph has girth at least $12$. If $K$ is a finite extension of $Q$ containing a primitive $\ell$th root of unity, then, with $m=|O|$ and $t=|V|$, there are columns $x_v\in K^m$, $v\in V$, such that
\[
0<m<t\le m\ell^2,\qquad
\sum_{v\in V}x_vx_v^{\mathsf T}=-I_m,\qquad
\sum_{v\in f}x_vx_v^{\mathsf T}=0\quad(f\in\mathcal F).
\]
statements.section_title: Polynomial pairings on a punctured affine space

statements.title: Incidence criterion
statements.label: thm:criterion
statements.text:
Let $\ell$ be an odd prime, let $K$ be a finite field of characteristic two
containing a primitive $\ell$th root of unity $\zeta$, and put
$\kappa=\ell^2$. Let $V$ be a finite set of cardinality $t$, and let
$\mathcal F$ be a finite family of nonempty subsets of $V$. Assume that
every $v\in V$ belongs to exactly $\ell+1$ members of $\mathcal F$ and
that the bipartite incidence graph of $V$ and $\mathcal F$ has girth at
least $12$.

Suppose that an integer $m$ and column vectors $x_v\in K^m$, $v\in V$,
satisfy
\begin{equation}

0<m<t\le m\kappa
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}

\sum_{v\in V}x_vx_v^{\mathsf T}=-I_m,
\qquad
\sum_{v\in f}x_vx_v^{\mathsf T}=0
\quad\text{for every }f\in\mathcal F.
\end{equation}
Then there are a finitely presented group $G$ containing an element of order $\ell$ and finite sums
$a_{\mathrm{out}},b_{\mathrm{out}}\in K[G]$ such that
\[
a_{\mathrm{out}}b_{\mathrm{out}}=1,
\qquad
b_{\mathrm{out}}a_{\mathrm{out}}\ne1.
\]
They are given by the constructions and formulas below.
statements.section_title: An incidence criterion and its embedded local groups

statements.label: thm:hypergraph
statements.text:
For all sufficiently large $h$, for every $Q$ and enumeration as above,
there are a set $O\subset S$ and a set $\mathcal F$ of affine lines
contained in $V=\mathcal A\setminus O$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \frac{2N_{\rm pt}}{D^2}\le |O|\le\frac{7N_{\rm pt}}{D^2},
\end{equation}
every point of $V$ lies on exactly $D$ members of $\mathcal F$, and
the bipartite incidence graph of $V$ and $\mathcal F$ has girth at
least $12$.
statements.section_title: A regular hypergraph of affine lines

statements.label: prop:ca-transfer
cor:nonsurjunctive
statements.text:
For the field $K$, group $G$, and outputs of
Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, the cellular automaton
$T_{b_{\mathrm{out}}}:K^G\to K^G$ is injective and not surjective.
Its image is the fixed set of $T_{b_{\mathrm{out}}a_{\mathrm{out}}}$.
In particular, $G$ is not surjunctive.

statements.label: cor:finfty-counterexample
statements.text:
For the finite characteristic-two field $K$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:main},
there are a group $U$ of type $F_\infty$ and scalar elements
$A,B\in K[U]$ such that $AB=1$ and $BA\ne1$.
The group $U$ is nonsofic and nonsurjunctive.

statements.label: op:main
statements.text:
Put
\[
 m=\binom{1200}{600},\qquad
 p=\min\{h\in\mathbb Z:h>1,\ h\mid(m!)^2+1\}.
\]
Then $p$ is an odd prime. There are a specified field $K$ of order $p^4$,
a specified finitely generated group $G$ containing torsion, and specified
finite sums $a,b\in K[G]$ satisfying $ab=1$ and $ba\ne1$.

statements.label: op:graph

statements.label: op:modular
statements.text:
There is a specified idempotent $e\in K[H]$ satisfying, for every $s\in P$,
\[
 (u(s)-1)^\ell e=0,\qquad e(v(s)-1)^\ell=0.
\]

statements.label: op:edge-zero
statements.text: For every edge $i<j$ of $\Gamma$, $e_i e_j=0$ in $K[G_0]$.

statements.label: prop:first-gluing-injective
statements.text:
Every natural map $H_i\to G_0$ is injective.  In particular, the maps

statements.label: prop:sector-ranks
statements.text:
Under these assumptions, there is a group $G_1$ containing $G_0$ and a
central element $z\in G_1$ of order $M$ with the following property.  Set
\[
 R=K[G_1],\qquad
 f=\frac1M\sum_{k=0}^{M-1}\zeta^{-k}z^k,\qquad
 S=fR,\qquad P_i=fe_i.
\]
Then $f$ is a nonzero central idempotent.  There are explicitly
specified matrices
\[
 J_i\in\operatorname{Mat}_{w\times d}(S),\qquad
 Y_i\in\operatorname{Mat}_{d\times w}(S)
\]
satisfying
\begin{equation}
 Y_iJ_i=fI_d,\qquad J_iY_i=P_iI_w.
\end{equation}
The entries of $J_i$ and $Y_i$ lie in the group algebra of a finite
subgroup of $G_1$, multiplied by $f$.  Their construction uses only
finite group operations and linear algebra over $K$.
statements.section_title: Realizing the local ranks in a common central sector

statements.label: op:heisenberg
statements.text:
Let $K$ be a field, let $M\ge2$ be invertible in $K$, and let
$\zeta\in K$ have order $M$. For an integer $q\ge0$ put
$Z_q=(\mathbb Z/M\mathbb Z)^q$ and $n=M^q$. There is a finite group
$\Lambda$ of order $Mn^2$ and a nonzero central idempotent
$f'\in K[\Lambda]$ for which explicitly specified elements
$\Omega_{uv}$, $u,v\in Z_q$, form a basis of $f'K[\Lambda]$ and obey
\[
 \Omega_{uv}\Omega_{st}=\delta_{vs}\Omega_{ut},\qquad
 \sum_u\Omega_{uu}=f'.
\]
Thus $\Mat_n(K)\cong f'K[\Lambda]$ by its standard matrix units.

statements.label: op:scalar
statements.text:
Under the field hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{op:heisenberg}, suppose
$A,B\in\Mat_r(K[L])$ for a group $L$ and an integer $r\ge1$, with
$AB=I_r$ and $BA\ne I_r$. Finite formulas give a finite group $\Lambda$
and $a,b\in K[L\times\Lambda]$ with $ab=1$ and $ba\ne1$.
In particular, over any fixed finite field with at least three elements,
a failure of stable finiteness transfers to a scalar failure after a
finite direct factor, without changing the field.

statements.label: op:cellular
statements.text:
Let $k$ be a finite field, $L$ a group, and $a,b\in k[L]$ with $ab=1$.
Then $T_b:k^L\to k^L$ is an injective cellular automaton, with
\[
 \im T_b=\{y\in k^L:T_{ba}y=y\}.
\]
For every $h$ with $(ba-1)_h\ne0$, the configuration $\delta_h$ is
absent from its image.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is a countable division ring $D$ of characteristic zero, with
center $F=Z(D)$, and elements $x,y\in D$ such that
\[
 D=F[x,y]=F(x,y),\qquad [D:F]=\infty,
\]
while every element of $D$ is algebraic over $F$.

statements.title: Algebraic lifting
statements.label: thm:lifting
statements.text:
Let $k$ be a countable field of characteristic zero containing every root
of unity, and let $A$ be a finite-dimensional central division algebra
over $k$. Suppose
$X\in A\langle\!\langle z_1,z_2\rangle\!\rangle^u$ satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $X_0$ generates $A$ as a $k$-algebra;
\item $X_1,X_2$ have linearly independent classes in $A^u/J_A(X_0)$.
\end{enumerate}
For every $w\in A\langle\!\langle z_1,z_2\rangle\!\rangle$, there exist
a countable field extension $k'/k$, a central division algebra $A'/k'$ of
strictly larger degree, and series
\[
 X'\in A'\langle\!\langle s_1,s_2\rangle\!\rangle^u,
 \qquad w'\in A'\langle\!\langle s_1,s_2\rangle\!\rangle
\]
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item Every noncommutative polynomial identity over $k$ satisfied by the
tuple $(X,w)$ is satisfied by $(X',w')$ as an identity of formal series.
\item The constant tuple $X'_0$ generates $A'$ over $k'$, and the classes
of $X'_1,X'_2$ in $(A')^u/J_{A'}(X'_0)$ are linearly independent.
\item There is a monic nonzero polynomial $q\in k'[t]$ such that $q(w')=0$.
\end{enumerate}
Here the degree of a central division algebra $B/F$ is $\sqrt{[B:F]}$.

statements.label: prop:active-partition
statements.text:
For the direction $v$ chosen in \eqref{eq:nonzero-direction}, there
is a partition of $\{1,\ldots,e_n\}$ such that
\[
 \mathcal T_P=
 \left\{c\in\Omega_P^{e_n}:
 \frac{c_h}{D_h(P;v)}\text{ is constant on each part}\right\}.
\]

statements.title: Transfer of a leading coefficient
statements.label: prop:word-transfer
statements.text:
Let $R=\operatorname{diag}(P,C_0)$ be a small matrix input of total size $N\in
\mathcal S$;
the block $C_0$ may be absent.  Let $I$ be a set of labels at
$P$ such that $W(C_0)-\lambda_h$ is invertible for every $h\in I$.
Work over a field $E$ containing the labeled spectral data at $P$ and the
entries of $C_0$, with the formal evaluations allowed by
Lemma~\ref{lem:admissible-evaluation}.  Let
\[
 Z(s_1,s_2)\in M_N(E)\langle\!\langle s_1,s_2\rangle\!\rangle^2
\]
have constant term $R$.  These are input matrices: their scalar entries
act on the input factor and commute with the old coefficient algebra.

For $h\in I$, embed $\pi_h$ at the $P$ block, put $\bar\pi_h=1-\pi_h$,
and form
\[
 S_h(Z)=\pi_h(W(Z)-\lambda_h)\pi_h
 -\pi_hW(Z)\bar\pi_h
 \bigl(\bar\pi_h(W(Z)-\lambda_h)\bar\pi_h\bigr)^{-1}
 \bar\pi_hW(Z)\pi_h.
\]
Suppose that every $S_h(Z)$ vanishes in degrees less than $\ell$, where
$\ell\ge1$.  For each word $\omega$ of length $\ell$, there are scalars
$c_{h,\omega}\in E$ such that
\[
 [S_h(Z)]_\omega=c_{h,\omega}\pi_h,
 \qquad (c_{h,\omega})_{h\in I}\in
        (\mathcal T_P|_I)\otimes E.
\]
The same conclusion holds for homogeneous degree-$\ell$ coefficients of
perturbations in finitely many ordinary commuting parameters.
statements.section_title: Transfer of the first unsolved word coefficient

statements.title: Functional linkage
statements.label: prop:functional-linkage
statements.text:
Let $P$ be a small generic input of size $p$, and let $h,h'$ be linked
labels at $P$.  Let $C_1,\ldots,C_s$ be small generic inputs of sizes in
$\mathcal S$, jointly independent with $P$, where $s=0$ is allowed.
Put $R=\operatorname{diag}(P,C_1,\ldots,C_s)$.
Over a common spectral splitting field $E$, denote by
$\Lambda_j^R(\Delta)$ the scalar eigenvalue branch of $W(R+\Delta)$
whose value at zero is $\lambda_j(P)$, for $j=h,h'$.

Define
\[
 g_j(\eta)=\lambda_j(P+\eta v)-\lambda_j(P)
 \in\Omega_P[[\eta]],\qquad j=h,h'.
\]
Then $g_{h'}'(0)\neq 0$, and
\begin{equation}
 \Lambda_h^R(\Delta)-\lambda_h(P)
 =\bigl(g_h\circ g_{h'}^{-1}\bigr)
       \bigl(\Lambda_{h'}^R(\Delta)-\lambda_{h'}(P)\bigr).
 
\end{equation}
Here $g_{h'}^{-1}$ denotes the inverse for composition.  In particular,
the univariate series in this identity depends only on $P,h,h'$ and $v$,
and is unchanged when auxiliary blocks are adjoined.

statements.title: Replication of active dimensions
statements.label: prop:active-replication
statements.text:
For every positive integer $N$,
\[
 a_{pN}=N a_p.
\]

statements.title: Equal-size partners
statements.label: cor:equal-size-partners
statements.text:
There are $r\in\mathcal S$ and a positive integer $K_0$ with the
following property.  Let $P,Q_1,\ldots,Q_{K_0}$ be independent small
generic inputs of size $r$.  For generic fixed input arrows
$U_j:P\leftarrow Q_j$, the loop columns and the images of
\[
 V\longmapsto m(P,Q_j;U_j,V),
 \qquad V:Q_j\leftarrow P,\quad 1\leq j\leq K_0,
\]
span $\mathcal T_P$ after extension to the joint field of the data.
The analogous assertion holds with the other arrow fixed.  The same
$r$ and $K_0$ may be used for both assertions.

statements.title: Compatible dual relations
statements.label: prop:compatible-relations
statements.text:
For any finite nonempty collection of independent generic size-\(b\)
points \(P_i\), there is a \(g\)-dimensional space
\[
 \mathcal G_{\{P_i\}}\subseteq\bigoplus_i H_{P_i}^*
\]
with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Projection to each \(H_{P_i}^*\) is an isomorphism.
\item It annihilates all joint paired responses, with both arrows
arbitrary.
\item For a fixed generic arrow between \(P_i,P_j\), the
annihilator in \(H_{P_i}^*\oplus H_{P_j}^*\) of the variable
reverse-arrow image is exactly the restriction of
\(\mathcal G_{\{P_i\}}\).
\item On adjoining independent blocks, restriction of the larger
space is the original space after scalar extension.
\end{enumerate}
For one block this space is \(H_P^*\). These statements include
\(g=0\).
statements.section_title: The common space of spectral relations

statements.title: Cyclic compatibility of the error
statements.label: thm:cyclic-compatibility
statements.text:
Let \(Z(s_1,s_2)\) be a pair of formal series in two free letters,
with constant term \(\operatorname{diag}(P_1,\ldots,P_m)\).
Suppose that the fixed-root Schur expressions \(S_{i,h}\), for
every block \(i\) and every root label \(h\), vanish in every
degree below \(\ell\), where \(\ell\geq1\).
By transfer, their degree-\(\ell\) coefficients are scalar on
their root spaces; write
\[
 [s^\omega]S_{i,h}=e_{i,h,\omega}\pi_{i,h},
 \qquad |\omega|=\ell.
\]
For each word the scalar tuple at block \(i\) belongs to its
active space. For every cyclic orbit \(\mathcal O\) of words of
length \(\ell\) and every \(c\in\mathcal G\),
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{\omega\in\mathcal O}
 \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{h\in I_i}
 c_{i,h}e_{i,h,\omega}=0.
 
\end{equation}
The orbit sum runs over distinct words, including when a word has
a nontrivial rotational stabilizer.
statements.section_title: Cyclic relations on the leading free-word errors

statements.label: prop:eleven-block-correction
statements.text:
Prescribe generic input-arrow pairs on the edges
\[
 \begin{array}{c|c}
 \text{letter}&\text{offsets }i-j\text{ of edges }i\leftarrow j\\ \hline
 s_1&1,2\\
 s_2&3,4.
 \end{array}
\]
Under the response and cyclic-sum hypotheses above, there is a pair
$Z(s_1,s_2)\in M_{mb}(E)\langle\!\langle s_1,s_2\rangle\!\rangle^2$
with constant term $R$ and exactly these prescribed linear coefficients,
for which
\[
 S_{i,h}(Z)=0\qquad\text{for every }i,h.
\]
It can be constructed by finite linear systems.  At step $\ell\ge3$ the
new unknowns are coefficients of degree $\ell-1$ on the reverse edges
and coefficients of degree $\ell$ on the diagonal blocks.

title: A counterexample to Ryser's covering conjecture
abstract: For every sufficiently large prime \(s\equiv2\pmod3\) and every sufficiently large odd integer n, with the threshold depending on s, we construct an intersecting \((s^n+1)\)-partite \((s^n+1)\)-uniform hypergraph with covering number \(s^n+1\). This disproves Ryser's covering conjecture in its intersecting case.

tex.abstract:
For every sufficiently large prime $s\equiv2\pmod3$ and every sufficiently
large odd integer $n$, with the threshold depending on $s$, we construct
an intersecting $(s^n+1)$-partite $(s^n+1)$-uniform hypergraph with covering
number $s^n+1$. This disproves Ryser's covering conjecture in its
intersecting case.
sections: The hypergraph and its covering number

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There exists $s_0$ such that, for every prime $s\ge s_0$ with
$s\equiv2\pmod3$, there is an integer $n_0(s)\ge3$ with the following
property. For every odd integer $n\ge n_0(s)$, put $q=s^n$.
There is a finite intersecting $(q+1)$-partite $(q+1)$-uniform
hypergraph $H$ satisfying
\[
 \tau(H)=q+1.
\]
In particular, the intersecting case of~\eqref{eq:ryser} is false.

statements.label: cor:tree-cover
statements.text:
Let $s_0$ and $n_0(s)$ be as in Theorem~\ref{thm:main}. For every prime
$s\ge s_0$ with $s\equiv2\pmod3$ and every odd integer $n\ge n_0(s)$,
put $r=s^n+1$. There is a finite simple complete graph with an
$r$-edge-coloring for which the minimum number of monochromatic trees
needed to cover its vertices is exactly $r$. The same minimum holds with
connected monochromatic subgraphs or maximal monochromatic components in
place of trees.

statements.label: thm:incidence

statements.title: Compatible translates from independent pools
statements.label: thm:selection
statements.text:
For every positive integer $D$ there is a positive integer $K=K(D)$
with the following property.  Let $q$ tend to infinity through prime
powers.  For each $q$, let $n\le Dq$, and for $1\le i\le n$ let
$W_i\subseteq\F_q^2$ and let $D_i$ be a set of directions, with
\[
 |W_i|\le D,\qquad |D_i|\le D.
\]
Assume that each direction belongs to $D_i$ for at most $D$ indices $i$.
For distinct indices $i,j$, declare the translates $b+W_i$ and
$b'+W_j$ to conflict if there are $u\in W_i$, $v\in W_j$, and
$d\in D_i\cup D_j$ such that
\[
 (b+u)-(b'+v)\in d.
\]
For each $i$, draw $K$ independent uniform shifts
$b_{i,1},\ldots,b_{i,K}\in\F_q^2$, independently for all indices.
With probability tending to one, one can choose $k_i\in\{1,\ldots,K\}$
for every $i$ so that the translates $b_{i,k_i}+W_i$ have no conflicts.
The convergence is uniform over all data satisfying the stated bounds.

title: A Counterexample to Wall's D(2) Problem
abstract: We give a negative answer to Wall's finite \(D(2)\) problem. We construct a finite connected three-dimensional CW complex satisfying the \(D(2)\) finiteness condition but not homotopy equivalent to any finite CW complex of dimension at most two. The example has infinite fundamental group.

tex.abstract:
We give a negative answer to Wall's finite $D(2)$ problem. We construct
a finite connected three-dimensional CW complex satisfying the $D(2)$
finiteness condition but not homotopy equivalent to any finite CW complex
of dimension at most two. The example has infinite fundamental group.
sections: A tower obstruction in dimension two

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is a finite connected three-dimensional CW complex $X$ such that
\[
 H_i(\widetilde X;\Z)=0\quad(i>2),\qquad
 H^3(X;M)=0\quad\text{for every }\Z[\pi_1(X)]\text{-module }M,
\]
but $X$ is not homotopy equivalent to any finite CW complex of
dimension at most two.

statements.title: Tower obstruction
statements.label: thm:tower
statements.text:
Let $Y$ be a finite connected CW complex of dimension at most two, and
let $L$ be a rank-one complex local system on $Y$ with $H_2(Y;L)=0$.
There is no map $f:F\to Y$ from a finite connected simplicial complex
satisfying $b_1(F;\Q)=0$ for which $f^*L$ has nontrivial monodromy.

statements.title: Characters and torsion
statements.label: cor:torsion
statements.text:
Let $Y$ be a finite connected CW complex of dimension at most two.
If a character $\rho:\pi_1(Y)\to\C^\times$ satisfies
$H_2(Y;\C_\rho)=0$, then $\rho(g)=1$ for every finite-order
element $g\in\pi_1(Y)$.

title: A Counterexample to the Group-Ring Determinant Conjecture
abstract: We disprove the unrestricted group-ring Determinant Conjecture. We construct a finitely generated group G and a square matrix over \(\mathbb Z[G]\) that is invertible over \(\mathbb Q[G]\) and has Fuglede–Kadison determinant strictly between zero and one. The logarithmic integral defining the determinant is finite.

tex.abstract: We disprove the unrestricted group-ring Determinant Conjecture. We construct a finitely generated group $G$ and a square matrix over $\mathbb Z[G]$ that is invertible over $\mathbb Q[G]$ and has Fuglede--Kadison determinant strictly between zero and one. The logarithmic integral defining the determinant is finite.
sections: From the scalar defect to a projection
Lifting the factorization and preserving integrality

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There are a finitely generated discrete group $G_D$, an integer
$n\ge1$, and $A\in\Mat_n(\Z[G_D])$ invertible over $\Q[G_D]$ such
that
\[
 0<\det_{\N(G_D)}(T_A)<1.
\]
The integral in Equation~\eqref{eq:conjecture} is finite and strictly
negative. Thus the unrestricted group-ring Determinant Conjecture
has a negative resolution.

statements.title: {\cite[Theorem 1.1]{CharacteristicTwo}}
statements.label: thm:input
statements.text:
There exist a finite field $K_2$ of characteristic two, a finitely
generated group $H_2$, and finite sums $a_2,b_2\in K_2[H_2]$ with
$a_2b_2=1$ and $b_2a_2\ne1$.

statements.label: prop:separation
statements.text:
Let $X,Y\in\Mat_d(\F_2[H_2])$, $d\ge1$, satisfy
$XY=I_d\ne YX$. In the group
$G_D=(\bigoplus_{h\in H_2}C_3)\rtimes H_2$, where $H_2$ acts
by left translation on coordinate labels, there is an orthogonal
projection $P\in\Mat_{d+1}(\Z[1/3][G_D])$ and a finite set
$S\subseteq H_2\setminus\{1\}$ such that
\[
 \tau_{d+1}(P)=d+\theta,\qquad
 \theta=\frac13\left(\frac23\right)^{|S|}>0,
 \qquad \bar P=uv,
\]
where $u$ has size $(d+1)\times d$ and $v$ has size $d\times(d+1)$
over $\F_2[G_D]$. The integer $D=3^{1+|S|}$ clears all coefficients
of $P$.
statements.section_title: From the scalar defect to a projection

statements.label: prop:criterion
statements.text:
Let $G$ be a discrete group, $m,r\ge1$, and let
$P=P^*=P^2\in\Mat_m(\Q[G])$. Suppose an odd $D>0$ clears its
denominators and $\bar P=uv$ with
$u\in\Mat_{m,r}(\F_2[G])$ and
$v\in\Mat_{r,m}(\F_2[G])$. For every $q=2^k>1$ congruent to one
modulo $D$, the matrix $A$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:integral} satisfies
\begin{align}
 \tau_{r+m}(\log(T_A^*T_A))
   &=2(r-\tau_m(P))\log q,\\
 \log\det_{\N(G)}(T_A)&=(r-\tau_m(P))\log q.
 
\end{align}
It is integral and rationally invertible, and its positive-square
spectral measure has support in a compact subinterval of $(0,\infty)$.
