title: A classification of finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations
abstract: We classify finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations by a necessary and sufficient tensor condition over their coordinate fields. The Ramsey property here concerns monochromatic congruent copies at the original scale under arbitrary finite colorings. The criterion shows that every nonempty subtransitive set and every nonempty set of at most five points on a circle is Ramsey. In particular, some Ramsey cyclic quadrilaterals are not subtransitive, disproving the necessity direction of the Leader–Russell–Walters conjectured characterization.

tex.abstract:
We classify finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations by a necessary and
sufficient tensor condition over their coordinate fields. The Ramsey
property here concerns monochromatic congruent copies at the original
scale under arbitrary finite colorings. The criterion shows that every
nonempty subtransitive set and every nonempty set of at most five points
on a circle is Ramsey. In particular, some Ramsey cyclic quadrilaterals
are not subtransitive, disproving the necessity direction of the
Leader--Russell--Walters conjectured characterization.
sections: Rational tensors and the coloring obstruction
Exact coordinate permutations at two scales
From coordinate permutations to equal path endpoints

statements.title: Classification
statements.label: thm:classification
statements.text:
Let $A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_s\}\subset\R^d$ be a finite set of at least two
points with affine span $\R^d$, and define $p_i,F,B,m_F$ as above.
Then $A$ is Ramsey if and only if there is a matrix
$P\in\operatorname{Mat}_{d+1}(B)$ such that
\begin{align}
 (p_i\otimes1)^T P(1\otimes p_i)&=0
       &&(1\le i\le s),\\
 m_F(P_{\alpha\beta})&=\delta_{\alpha\beta}
       &&(1\le\alpha,\beta\le d).
\end{align}
Here the entries of $p_i\otimes1$ and $1\otimes p_i$ are formed
componentwise. There are no separate conditions on the multiplied
constant row or constant column of $P$.

statements.label: alg:equivalence
statements.text:
The matrix condition in Theorem~\ref{thm:classification} is equivalent
to~\eqref{alg:tensor}.
statements.section_title: Rational tensors and the coloring obstruction

statements.label: alg:necessity
statements.text:
If~\eqref{alg:tensor} has no solution, then there is an integer $r_0\geq2$
such that every $\R^D$ admits an $r_0$-coloring with no monochromatic
congruent copy of $A$.  In particular, every Euclidean Ramsey set
satisfies the matrix condition of Theorem~\ref{thm:classification}.
statements.section_title: Rational tensors and the coloring obstruction

statements.title: A path criterion
statements.label: paths:criterion
statements.text:
Suppose that for every integer $n\ge1$ there are two paths with the
same endpoint and weights $\lambda>0$ and $\mu\ge0$ satisfying
$\mu/\lambda<1/n$. Then $A$ is Euclidean Ramsey.

statements.label: groups:endpoints
statements.text:
Suppose $q>0$ and $f_i,g_i\in\R^\ell$ satisfy
\[
 \|f_i-f_j\|^2=\|a_i-a_j\|^2,\qquad
 \|g_i-g_j\|^2=q\|a_i-a_j\|^2
 \quad(1\le i,j\le s),
\]
and each $g_i$ is a coordinate permutation of $f_i$.
For every $\delta>0$ there exist two paths with the same endpoint and
weights $\lambda>0$ and $\mu\ge0$ such that
\[
 \frac{\mu}{\lambda}\le q+s\delta.
\]
statements.section_title: From coordinate permutations to equal path endpoints

statements.label: cons:spherical
statements.text: Every finite Euclidean Ramsey set is spherical.

statements.label: cons:transitive
statements.text: Every nonempty subset of a finite transitive Euclidean set is Ramsey.

statements.label: cons:quadratic
statements.text:
Let $A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_s\}\subset\R^d$ be spherical and affinely
span $\R^d$. Put $p_i=(1,a_i)^{\mathsf T}$ and let $F$ be its
coordinate field. If the $s$ row vectors
\[
 (p_{i\alpha}p_{i\beta})_{0\le\alpha,\beta\le d}
 \quad(1\le i\le s)
\]
are linearly independent over $F$, then $A$ is Ramsey.

statements.label: cons:quadrilateral
statements.text:
Every nonempty set of at most five distinct points on a circle is Ramsey.
In particular, every cyclic quadrilateral is Ramsey.

statements.label: cons:kites
statements.text:
For every transcendental $a\in(-1,1)$, the cyclic quadrilateral
\[
 K_a=\bigl\{(-1,0),(1,0),
             (a,\sqrt{1-a^2}),(a,-\sqrt{1-a^2})\bigr\}
\]
is Ramsey and is not subtransitive.

statements.label: cons:nine
statements.text:
Let $t_1,\ldots,t_9$ be algebraically independent real numbers over
$\Q$. The nine points
\[
 a_i=\left(\frac{1-t_i^2}{1+t_i^2},
                \frac{2t_i}{1+t_i^2}\right),\qquad 1\le i\le9,
\]
form a spherical set that is not Ramsey.

statements.label: cons:twelve
statements.text:
Set
\[
 t=\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}10^{-m!},\qquad
 u=\frac{1-t^2}{1+t^2},\qquad v=\frac{2t}{1+t^2},
 \qquad Q_0=\{(\pm1,0),(0,\pm1)\},
\]
and define
\[
 R_+=\begin{pmatrix}u&-v\\v&u\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 R_-=\begin{pmatrix}u&v\\-v&u\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 X=R_+Q_0\cup R_-Q_0\cup Q_0.
\]
Then $X$ is a twelve-point subset of the unit circle that is not Ramsey.

title: A closed Ricci flow with bounded scalar curvature and finite-time curvature blowup
abstract: We disprove the scalar-curvature extension conjecture in its unrestricted all-dimensions form. In sufficiently high dimension, we construct a Ricci flow on a closed manifold whose scalar curvature remains uniformly bounded while full curvature diverges at a finite maximal time. In one fixed sufficiently high dimension, the examples have two-sided power-law curvature blowup with arbitrarily large exponents.

tex.abstract:
We disprove the scalar-curvature extension conjecture in its unrestricted
all-dimensions form. In sufficiently high dimension, we construct a Ricci
flow on a closed manifold whose scalar curvature remains uniformly bounded
while full curvature diverges at a finite maximal time. In one fixed
sufficiently high dimension, the examples have two-sided power-law curvature
blowup with arbitrarily large exponents.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There are an integer \(q\ge10\), a time \(T>0\), and a smooth Ricci flow
\(g(t)\), \(0\le t<T\), on the closed connected manifold
\(M=\Sp^2\times\Sp^{q+1}\), with smooth initial metric, such that
\[
\sup_{M\times[0,T)}|R_{g(t)}|<\infty,
\qquad
\lim_{t\uparrow T}\max_M|\Rm_{g(t)}|=\infty.
\]
In particular, \(T\) is the finite maximal existence time of this flow.

statements.title: Construction input
statements.label: prop:input
statements.text:
For the parameters above, Stolarski's construction supplies a smooth Ricci
flow up to a finite time \(T\) on \(\Sp^p\times\Sp^{q+1}\) with the
following properties, after translating its starting time to zero.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item Off the two pole orbits it has the form
\[
g=ds^2+\phi^2g_{\Sp^p}+r^2g_{\Sp^q}.
\]
Here \(s\) is radial arclength at each time. The metric is invariant under
reflection exchanging the poles. On each open hemisphere, oriented from
its pole toward the equator, \(r_s>0\). At a pole, \(r=0\), \(r_s=1\),
and \(\phi_s=0\); the usual odd and even polar expansions hold for \(r\)
and \(\phi\), respectively, and \(\phi>0\) for every \(t<T\).

\item Write \(u=\log\phi\), \(z=r_s^2\), and
\[
\Ut=\log\frac{\phi}{(A/B)r},\qquad \Zt=z-B^2.
\]
There are positive tolerances \(\eta_j^U,\eta_j^Z\), large fixed numbers
\(1<Y_1\le Y_2\), and constants \(M_0>0\), \(0<\beta<1/2\), such that
for \(j=0,1,2\),
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\left|\partial_\gamma^j(\Ut-\delta^\nu U_k)\right|
&\le\eta_j^U\delta^\nu
       \bigl(\gamma^{-d-j}+\gamma^{2k-d}\bigr),\\
\left|\partial_\gamma^j(\Zt-\delta^\nu Z_k)\right|
&\le\eta_j^Z\delta^\nu
       \bigl(\gamma^{-d-j}+\gamma^{2k-d}\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The first estimate holds from \(Y_1\delta^{\nu/d}\) to
\(M_0e^{\beta\tau}\), and the second from \(Y_2\delta^{\nu/d}\) to that
upper endpoint, within the hemisphere. The profiles are smooth on
\(\gamma>0\). The function \(U_k\) is \(\gamma^{-d}\) times a polynomial
of degree \(k\) in \(\gamma^2\), with positive leading coefficients at
zero and infinity:
\[
U_k(\gamma)\sim c_1\gamma^{-d}\quad(\gamma\downarrow0),\qquad
U_k(\gamma)\sim c_2\gamma^{2k-d}\quad(\gamma\to\infty),\qquad c_1,c_2>0.
\]
Also \(Z_k(\gamma)=O_{q,k}(\gamma^{-d})\) as \(\gamma\downarrow0\).

\item For all sufficiently late times, putting \(f=ru_r\), one has
\begin{equation}
\begin{gathered}
\phi/r\ge A/B,\qquad 0\le f\le1,\qquad f_r\ge0
       \quad(0<r\le Y_1\theta),\\
B^2\le z\le1\quad(0<r\le Y_2\theta).
\end{gathered}
\end{equation}
These inner intervals lie strictly below the equator.

\item At the initial time \(\tau_0=-\log T\), the same weighted profile
bounds hold up to an initial outer cutoff
\(G_{\mathrm{init}}=M_0e^{\beta_{\mathrm{init}}\tau_0}\),
where \(0<\beta_{\mathrm{init}}<1/2\), and \(\Ut\ge0\) beyond that
cutoff. The exponents are chosen in the ranges permitted by the
construction; in particular, one may take
\[
0<\beta<\frac{\nu}{2\nu+1}\le\beta_{\mathrm{init}}<\frac12.
\]
They are therefore distinct choices, not two arbitrary exponents.
The tolerances can be
chosen sufficiently small depending on \(q,k\). The inner cutoffs can then
be increased in order, first \(Y_1\) and then \(Y_2\); the initial
rescaled time can subsequently be increased. Each such increase is
subject only to lower-size requirements from the construction.
\end{enumerate}

statements.label: prop:reaction
statements.text:
At late times on \(0<r\le\frac18\sqrt\delta\), the reaction quotient
\[
c(x,t)=\frac{2\langle\Rm(\Ric),\Ric\rangle}{|\Ric|^2}
\quad\text{where }|\Ric|>0
\]
satisfies both bounds
\begin{equation}
c\le\frac{2(q-1)+C\sqrt q}{r^2},\qquad
c\le\frac{C_*}{\theta^2}.
\end{equation}
Here \(C\) is independent of \(q,k\); \(C_*\) may depend on the entire
chosen flow. The second bound holds at the pole orbits as well.
Globally at positive \(r\), one also has \(c\le D_1/r^2\) for some
flow-dependent \(D_1>0\).

statements.label: prop:ricci-barrier
prop:scalar-inner
statements.text:
The scalar curvature is uniformly bounded above on
\(0\le r\le\xi\sqrt\delta\) at late times.

statements.label: prop:exterior
statements.text:
There is a constant \(C\) such that
\(|\Ric|\le C\) on \(r\ge\xi\sqrt\delta\) at late times.

statements.title: Curvature rates in a fixed dimension
statements.label: cor:rates
statements.text:
For every sufficiently large integer \(q\), set
\[
d_q=\frac{q+1-\sqrt{(q+1)(q-7)}}2.
\]
For every sufficiently large even integer \(k\), with the threshold
allowed to depend on \(q\), there is a smooth Ricci flow on
\(\Sp^2\times\Sp^{q+1}\) with finite maximal time \(T\), uniformly
bounded scalar curvature, and constants \(0<c\le C<\infty\) such that
\[
c(T-t)^{-2k/d_q}\le\max_M|\Rm|(\cdot,t)
\le C(T-t)^{-2k/d_q}
\]
for all sufficiently late times. In particular, one fixed dimension
admits such flows with an unbounded discrete set of power-law Type-II
curvature exponents. The flow, \(T\), and the constants may depend on
\(q\) and \(k\).

title: A conditional abelianity theorem for special fourfold pairs with a half-weight divisor
abstract: Using the abelianity theorem for special compact Kähler manifolds in every dimension, we prove virtual abelianity of the entire orbifold fundamental group of the special order-two root orbifold associated with a pair \((X,\tfrac12D)\), where X is a smooth projective fourfold and D is a nonempty smooth connected divisor. We construct a special smooth projective eightfold whose fundamental group surjects onto the required group.

We construct a special smooth projective eightfold whose fundamental group surjects onto the required group.

statements.label: prop:branched-model
statements.text:
There is a connected smooth projective variety $Y$ of dimension

properties.

\item Over

 U=X\setminus\bigl(D\cup B_1\cup\cdots\cup B_5\bigr),

title: A continuum temperature singularity for a radial pair potential
abstract: We construct a stable radial pair potential in three dimensions whose canonical free energy has a strict downward derivative jump at one common finite positive inverse temperature throughout an open interval of positive densities. The potential has a divergent repulsive core, a nontrivial attractive interval, and an integrable tail satisfying \(\phi(r)=o(r^{-3})\). Its free-cube canonical free energy is finite at every positive inverse temperature and density.

tex.abstract:
We construct a stable radial pair potential in three dimensions whose canonical
free energy has a strict downward derivative jump at one common finite positive
inverse temperature throughout an open interval of positive densities. The
potential has a divergent repulsive core, a nontrivial attractive interval,
and an integrable tail satisfying $\phi(r)=o(r^{-3})$. Its free-cube canonical
free energy is finite at every positive inverse temperature and density.
sections: A stable class with four-particle clusters
Uniform estimates and the Kac approximation

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There exist an admissible radial difference-only pair potential
$\Phi(x)=\phi(|x|)$ on $\R^3$, a nonempty open interval
$I\subset(0,\infty)$, and one $\beta_c\in(1/2,3/2)$ with the following
properties. The potential satisfies $\phi(r)=o(r^{-3})$ as $r\to\infty$.
The free-cube limit \eqref{eq:free-energy-definition} exists and is finite
for every $\beta>0$ and every density $\rho>0$. For every $\rho\in I$,
the finite one-sided derivatives at the same critical point satisfy
\[
 D_\beta^- f_\Phi(\beta_c,\rho)
 >D_\beta^+ f_\Phi(\beta_c,\rho).
\]
Thus one potential and one critical inverse temperature give a strict
canonical temperature singularity throughout $I$.

statements.title: Uniform stability
statements.label: prop:stability
statements.text:
Put $A_0=E/8$ and $B_0=E/2$. Every potential in
\eqref{eq:physical-class} satisfies, for every finite configuration,
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{\ell<k}\psi_t(x_\ell-x_k)
 \ge A_0\sum_i n_i^2-B_0N,
 \qquad
 U_N^\varphi\ge (A_0-M/2)\sum_i n_i^2-B_0N.
 
\end{equation}
These inequalities remain valid if positive core interactions between
members of a partition into unions of whole cells are deleted, or if
any negative interactions are multiplied by factors in $[0,1]$.

statements.title: Bounds for the density transform
statements.label: prop:transform
statements.text:
Let $t$ satisfy \eqref{eq:t-choice}. For every physical pressure
$Q_\varphi$ in \eqref{eq:physical-class} and every
$\sigma\in[0,A+1]$, the function $T_\sigma Q_\varphi$ is finite
and convex on $\Omega$, nonnegative, and nondecreasing in $h$.
The supremum in \eqref{eq:transform} is attained. For every compact
$W\subset\Omega$, there is $D_W<\infty$, depending only on
$W,t,b,w,A$, such that every maximizing density belongs to
$[0,D_W]$, uniformly over all potentials in the class and all these
values of $\sigma$. The transformed pressures are also uniformly
bounded on $W$.
statements.section_title: A stable class with four-particle clusters

statements.title: Uniform local moments
statements.label: prop:moments
statements.text:
Fix a compact set \(\mathcal K\subset\Omega\).
For all potentials in \eqref{eq:physical-class}, all finite cubes, and all
the modified systems just described, there is a constant \(C_{\mathcal K}\)
such that
\[
 \mathbb E_{\beta,h}[n_i n_j]\le C_{\mathcal K}
 \qquad ((\beta,h)\in\mathcal K)
\]
for every pair of cells meeting the cube.  The constant is independent of
the number and ranges of the attractive summands.
statements.section_title: Uniform estimates and the Kac approximation

statements.title: Attractive perturbations
statements.label: prop:tail
statements.text:
Fix a compact set \(\mathcal K\subset\Omega\).
For two of the preceding finite-volume systems differing by a negative
interaction, let \(J^{\mathrm{diff}}_{ij}\) be cellwise suprema of its
absolute value.  If the linear interpolation stays within the same
attractive mass bound, then
\begin{equation}
 |\log\Xi(1)-\log\Xi(0)|
 \le \frac{\beta C_{\mathcal K}}2\sum_{i,j}J^{\mathrm{diff}}_{ij}
 \qquad ((\beta,h)\in\mathcal K).
\end{equation}
In particular, for
\[
 \varphi=\psi_t-t\sum_{j\ge1}\sigma_jw_{R_j},
 \qquad
 \varphi_n=\psi_t-t\sum_{j\le n}\sigma_jw_{R_j},
\]
there is a range-independent constant \(C'_{\mathcal K}\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \|Q_\varphi-Q_{\varphi_n}\|_{\mathcal K}
 \le C'_{\mathcal K}\sum_{j>n}\sigma_j .
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Uniform estimates and the Kac approximation

statements.title: Physical Kac approximation
statements.label: prop:kac
statements.text:
Let
\[
 \varphi=\psi_t-t\sum_{j=1}^k\sigma_jw_{R_j}
\]
have finitely many attractive summands, with the empty sum allowed.
Fix \(\sigma\ge0\) such that \(\sum_{j=1}^k\sigma_j+\sigma\le A+1\).
Then
\begin{equation}
 Q_{\varphi-t\sigma w_R}\longrightarrow\T_\sigma Q_\varphi
 \quad\text{as }R\to\infty
\end{equation}
uniformly on compact subsets of \(\Omega\).
statements.section_title: Uniform estimates and the Kac approximation

statements.title: Initial supporting triple
statements.label: prop:initial-triple
statements.text:
For all sufficiently large \(t\), there are
\(\lambda_1\in B(\lambda_*,r_0/16)\) and nonempty compact convex sets
\(K_i^1\subset\overline B(v_i,\tau/2)\), \(i=1,2,3\), such that

All vectors in the \(K_i^1\) have nonnegative density coordinate.
In particular \(\partial P_1^t(\lambda_1)\) contains
\(\overline B(g,\gamma)\).

title: A counterexample to Hadwiger's conjecture
abstract: We disprove Hadwiger's conjecture by constructing arbitrarily large graphs whose chromatic number exceeds their Hadwiger number. The examples have independence number at most two, and even their ordinary fractional chromatic number exceeds their Hadwiger number. Thus they also disprove the fractional-coloring weakening discussed by Reed and Seymour.

tex.abstract:
We disprove Hadwiger's conjecture by constructing arbitrarily large
graphs whose chromatic number exceeds their Hadwiger number. The examples
have independence number at most two, and even their ordinary fractional
chromatic number exceeds their Hadwiger number. Thus they also disprove
the fractional-coloring weakening discussed by Reed and Seymour.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There are arbitrarily large integers \(m\) for which an \(m\)-vertex
finite simple graph \(G\) satisfies
\[
             \alpha(G)\le2
             \qquad\text{and}\qquad
             \cm(G)<\frac{m}{100}.
\]

statements.label: cor:hadwiger
statements.text:
There are finite nonempty simple graphs \(G\) of arbitrarily large
order \(m\) for which
\[
 h(G)<\frac{26m}{75}+\frac23
 <\frac m2\le\chi_f(G)\le\chi(G).
\]
Thus Hadwiger's conjecture and its fractional-coloring weakening
\(\chi_f(G)\le h(G)\) are false.

statements.title: Raw supersaturation
statements.label: thm:raw-supersaturation
statements.text:
For the construction parameters specified in \Cref{sec:geometry,sec:parameters}, for all sufficiently large \(n\), every probability law \(\sigma\) on units satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \sigma_1\le M\mu,\qquad \sigma_2\le M\mu,\qquad
 \sigma\le 2^{DN}\mu^2
\end{equation}
has the following property: two independent units drawn from \(\sigma\) have all four cross holes with probability at least \(2^{-100gN}\).
The inequalities in \Cref{eq:raw-law-caps} are pointwise inequalities of measures on the finite raw spaces.
statements.section_title: From supersaturation to a finite graph

statements.label: prop:raw-to-graph
statements.text:
Assume the conclusion of \Cref{thm:raw-supersaturation} at a given sufficiently large \(n\).
For \(m=2^{C_0gN}\), the sampled graph defined in \Cref{sec:geometry} satisfies
\[
 \alpha(G)\le2,\qquad \cm(G)<m/100
\]
with probability \(1-\exp(-\Omega(m))\).
The implied positive constant is independent of \(n\).
statements.section_title: From supersaturation to a finite graph

statements.label: prop:matching-minor
statements.text:
For every finite nonempty graph \(G\) of order \(m\),
\[
 \had(G)\le\frac{m+4\cm(G)+2}{3}.
\]
In particular, if \(\alpha(G)\le2\) and \(\cm(G)<m/100\), then
\[
 \had(G)<\frac{26m}{75}+\frac23<\frac m2\le\chi(G)
 \qquad(m\ge5).
\]

statements.title: Gradient realization
statements.label: thm:gradient-realization
statements.text:
Suppose two units in fixed leaves have lists satisfying
\eqref{eq:recipe-scalars}, the binary prescriptions yielding
\eqref{eq:recipe-gradients}, equal matched keys, and an
admissible injecting small table.  Freeze their actual cross
Gram entries whenever either argument is a pin or a key
direction.  Then there are abstract cross bilinear forms on
the full nominal spaces, extending all these frozen entries,
whose primal-versus-channel entries satisfy
\begin{equation}
 u_zU_i=r(v_{iz})\quad\text{on }\cX
 \qquad(i\text{ and }z\text{ in opposite units}).
\end{equation}
Only the primal-versus-channel entries need be prescribed in
the final test.  Their number is at most
$16|\cE|h\dim\cB=O(n)$, with its coefficient fixed before
$M_0$.  Agreement of the actual cross Grams with these entries
produces all four cross holes, with witnesses $(v_{iz},v_{zi})$.
statements.section_title: Recipes and realization of the gradients

statements.title: Collision criterion
statements.label: prop:collision
statements.text:
Let $\sigma$ be a unit law in \Cref{thm:raw-supersaturation},
and let $\widetilde\sigma$ be a restriction of it of relative
mass at least $2^{-o(N)}$, decomposed into leaves satisfying
\eqref{eq:final-leaf-minentropy}.  Mix the leaves with their
actual masses in $\widetilde\sigma$.
Suppose accepted numerical queries as above, with their
leaf-pair choices of table and separate filters, satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \E_{\text{independent leaf pair}}
       \int d_A d_B\,d\nu_n\ge 2^{-o(N)}.
\end{equation}
Then two independent units from the original $\sigma$ have
all four cross holes with probability at least
\begin{equation}
 2^{-(k_{\max}+.03)N-o(N)}.
\end{equation}
It suffices to obtain \eqref{eq:overlap-criterion} after skipping
some leaf pairs, or after summing over a bounded number of
numerical options.  Positive subsequential constants and
inverse-polynomial overlap bounds both suffice.  In particular,
this conclusion contradicts a sequence violating
\Cref{thm:raw-supersaturation}.
statements.section_title: From overlapping key distributions to four holes

statements.title: Phase alternative
statements.label: thm:phase-alternative
statements.text:
Suppose a marked-unit law is obtained by restricting an admissible
law in \Cref{thm:raw-supersaturation} to mass at least \(10^{-12}\),
and \(\Delta_O\ne0\) throughout. For all sufficiently large \(n\),
one can retain a sublaw of fixed positive relative mass, bounded below
using only the early parameters, such that one of the following holds
for independent draws \(A,B\):
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item every nontrivial phase mean
\[
 \E(-1)^{u_{B,S}(\Delta_A)+u_{A,R}(\Delta_B)},
 \qquad(S,R)\ne(\varnothing,\varnothing),
\]
has absolute value less than \(.005\);
\item a componentwise cover of total dimension at most \(d_0\)
covers every \(\Delta_O\), and every displayed mean for which
\(|S|=1\) or \(|R|=1\) is \(2^{-\Omega(N)}\).
\end{enumerate}
The cover may depend on the law and on \(n\). The constants in its
dimension bound and in the relative mass bound do not depend on the
later selector or channel sizes.

statements.title: Status preparation
statements.label: prop:status-preparation
statements.text:
Along a subsequence, the unit law can be prepared with final
pin dimension at most \(K\) and the final per-leaf bounds of
\Cref{lem:peeling}, at relative mass cost \(2^{-o(N)}\), so
that one of the following descriptions applies.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item There is no prediction as in \Cref{def:prediction}
on the first-peeled law. The effective spaces are still the
first ones. For independent units, the mass admitting an
admissible injecting small table is greater than \(.99\).
\item A prediction with fixed \(\alpha_i,c\) and common
classes \(e_i\) is retained. The old marks and exceptions
are preserved, and \Cref{eq:prediction} has uniform \(o(1)\)
error on every retained unit. The mass admitting an
admissible injecting table satisfying
\Cref{eq:phase-compatibility} is bounded below by a positive
constant.
\item Both prediction classes are zero, and every retained
unit satisfies the exact identities
\[
 p_i=T(\lambda_i,\cdot)+a
 \quad\text{on all of }\cX,\qquad i=1,2.
\]
There is a set of leaf pairs of mass at least
\(c_2N^{-4}\) under the final leaf mixture, for a fixed
\(c_2>0\), with phase compatibility determined by the
two leaves. For each such pair one can choose a specific
injecting compatible table whose two separate orientation
admissibility filters have masses at least \(a_0>0\).
The constants \(c_2,a_0\) are independent of \(n\).
\end{enumerate}
In every case the mixed joint density is at most
\(2^{(D+o(1))N}\mu^2\), and its individual marginals are at
most \(M2^{o(N)}\mu\).
Relative to the stored leaf bases and pin images, all numerical
table formats, unary statuses, old-mark coordinates and exception-set
descriptions have bounded length in \(n\). The extra exact pins
are used only in case \textup{(iii)}.

statements.title: Weak product comparison
statements.label: thm:weak-product
statements.text:
Let $W_n$ be any sequence of real functions on $\cK_n$ with
$\norm{W_n}_\infty\le B$, where $B$ is fixed. Extend it to the product
of the single-key spaces with the same bound. For every $\eps>0$
there are constants $L,C<\infty$, independent of $n$, and functions
\begin{equation}
 S_n(k_1,\ldots,k_r)
   =\sum_{a=1}^{L}c_{a,n}\prod_{j=1}^{r}f_{a,j,n}(k_j),
 \qquad
 \abs{c_{a,n}}\le C,\quad \abs{f_{a,j,n}}\le1,
\end{equation}
with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item For arbitrary global unary functions $g_{j,n}$ of bound one,
\begin{equation}
 \abs{\int(W_n-S_n)\prod_jg_{j,n}(k_j)\,d\nu_n}\le\eps
\end{equation}
for all sufficiently large $n$.
\item Under any mixed unit law satisfying
\eqref{eq:histogram-mixed-caps}, outside an exponentially small
exceptional set of orientations,
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{\abs{w_j}\le1}
 \abs{\E_z\mathcal A_n(O,z)
       (W_n-S_n)(K(O,z))\prod_jw_j(O,z_j)}\le\eps.
\end{equation}
The unary input weights may depend on the entire fixed orientation
and on any additional marks fixed with it. The exceptional set is
independent of these weights.
\end{enumerate}
The functions $f_{a,j,n}$ are global key functions; they can be chosen
to be indicators of sets, or finite linear combinations of such
indicators with uniformly bounded complexity. They do not depend on
the sampled orientation. The constants may depend on $B,\eps$ and
the fixed template and construction parameters, but not on $n$.

An additional orientation-only filter of bound one may multiply
\eqref{eq:weak-product-actual} without changing it. In particular,
after averaging normalized leaves, the same error control applies to
unnormalized admissibility-filtered query measures, even when the
filter is chosen using the opposite leaf. No assertion is made for
an arbitrary additional joint input filter.

statements.title: Positive-mass overlap
statements.label: prop:positive-overlap
statements.text:
For every positive-mass alternative of
\Cref{prop:status-preparation}, some fixed numerical option has expected
unnormalized successful-query overlap bounded below by a positive
constant along a subsequence. Consequently it satisfies
\eqref{eq:overlap-criterion}. This conclusion includes the prepared
restrictions of reciprocal mass $2^{o(N)}$ permitted there.

statements.label: prop:rare-overlap
statements.text:
In the inverse-polynomial alternative of
\Cref{prop:status-preparation}, the overlap criterion
\eqref{eq:overlap-criterion} holds with a lower bound
\(\Omega(N^{-4})\), along the prepared sequence.

title: A counterexample to Kaplansky's quasitrace conjecture and failure of tensor-product stable finiteness
abstract: We refute Kaplansky's quasitrace conjecture by constructing a separable unital complex C∗-algebra that admits normalized 2-quasitraces but has no tracial state. As a consequence, we show that the minimal tensor product of two unital simple stably finite complex C∗-algebras can be properly infinite, even when one factor is the reduced free-group algebra \(C_r^*(\mathbb F_2)\).

tex.abstract:
We refute Kaplansky's quasitrace conjecture by constructing a separable
unital complex \(C^*\)-algebra that admits normalized \(2\)-quasitraces
but has no tracial state. As a consequence, we show that the minimal tensor
product of two unital simple stably finite complex \(C^*\)-algebras can be
properly infinite, even when one factor is the reduced free-group algebra
\(C_r^*(\mathbb F_2)\).
sections: The algebra and a uniform additivity defect

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There exist a separable unital complex \(C^*\)-algebra \(A\), admitting
a normalized \(2\)-quasitrace, and positive contractions \(a,b\in A\)
such that every normalized \(2\)-quasitrace \(\tau\) on \(A\) satisfies
\[
 \tau(a+b)-\tau(a)-\tau(b)\ge\frac1{144}.
\]

statements.title: Tensor products and stable finiteness
statements.label: cor:stable-finiteness
statements.text:
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item There are two unital simple stably finite complex \(C^*\)-algebras
whose minimal tensor product is properly infinite. One factor can be
taken to be \(C_r^*(\mathbb F_2)\).
\item There is a separable unital complex \(C^*\)-algebra \(B\) admitting
a normalized \(2\)-quasitrace such that
\(B\otimes_{\min}C_r^*(\mathbb F_2)\) is properly infinite and admits no
normalized \(2\)-quasitrace.
\item There is a separable unital stably finite complex \(C^*\)-algebra
with no tracial state.
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Quasitrace existence
statements.label: thm:existence
statements.text:
A unital \(C^*\)-algebra \(C\) admits a normalized \(2\)-quasitrace
if and only if \(M_m(C)\) is not properly infinite for every
positive integer \(m\).

statements.label: prop:bundle-test
thm:construction
statements.text:
There is a separable unital complex $C^*$-algebra
$B=C^*(1,x_1,\ldots,x_{24})$ such that
\begin{equation}
  \sum_{i=1}^{24}x_i^*x_i=1,
  \qquad
  \sum_{i=1}^{24}x_ix_i^*\le\frac23\,1,
  
\end{equation}
and $M_m(B)$ is not properly infinite for every integer $m\ge1$.

title: A counterexample to Naimark's problem in ZFC
abstract: We construct in ZFC a unital infinite-dimensional simple complex C∗-algebra with a faithful tracial state whose nonzero irreducible representations are all unitarily equivalent. This gives a negative answer to Naimark's problem without additional set-theoretic assumptions.

tex.abstract:
We construct in ZFC a unital infinite-dimensional simple complex
$C^*$-algebra with a faithful tracial state whose nonzero irreducible
representations are all unitarily equivalent. This gives a negative answer
to Naimark's problem without additional set-theoretic assumptions.
sections: Pure states, excision, and peaking projections
Joining two classes while preserving unique extensions

statements.label: na:main
statements.text:
There exists a unital infinite-dimensional simple complex $C^*$-algebra
$A$ with a faithful tracial state such that all its nonzero irreducible
representations are unitarily equivalent. In particular, $A$ is not
isomorphic to $K(H)$ for any complex Hilbert space $H$.

statements.label: na:hnn
statements.text:
Let $(A,\tau)$ be a unital $C^*$-algebra with faithful tracial state,
let $D_1,D_2\subset A$ be unital subalgebras with trace-preserving
conditional expectations $E_i:A\to D_i$, and let
$\theta:D_1\to D_2$ be a trace-preserving isomorphism.  There is a
unital extension with a faithful tracial state extending $\tau$,
\[
 H(A)=C^*(A,v),\qquad vdv^*=\theta(d)\quad(d\in D_1),
\]
where $v$ is called the \emph{stable unitary}, and a trace-preserving
conditional expectation $E_A:H(A)\to A$
annihilating every nonempty reduced word
\eqref{na:hnn-word}.  Among faithfully tracial extensions generated by
$A$ and such a unitary, the relation and vanishing of the trace on
nonempty reduced words determine $H(A)$ uniquely, by an isomorphism
fixing $A$ and $v$.

statements.label: na:hnn-restriction
statements.text:
With the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{na:hnn}, let $A'\subset A$
be a unital subalgebra containing $D_1$ and $D_2$.  Then
$C^*(A',v)\subset H(A)$ is the reduced adjunction $H(A')$ formed with
the restricted trace and expectations $E_i|_{A'}$.  The expectation
$E_A$ restricts to the expectation $H(A')\to A'$.

statements.label: na:reorder
statements.text:
Let $O$ be a unital faithfully tracial $C^*$-algebra.  For each
$t\in\{j,k\}$, let $D_1^t,D_2^t\subset O$, $E_i^t:O\to D_i^t$
and $\theta_t:D_1^t\to D_2^t$ satisfy the hypotheses of
Proposition~\ref{na:hnn}.  When forming an adjunction over $H_j(O)$
or $H_k(O)$, extend the other data expectations by composition with
the expectation onto $O$.  There is a trace-preserving isomorphism
\begin{equation}
 H_k(H_j(O))\ \cong\ H_j(H_k(O))
\end{equation}
fixing $O$ and the named stable unitaries $v_j,v_k$.

statements.title: The bridge
statements.label: na:bridge
statements.text:
Let $A$ be a unital $C^*$-algebra with a faithful tracial state $\tau$
and no finite-dimensional irreducible representations. For $i=1,2$,
let $(p_n^i)_{n\geq0}$ be a decreasing sequence of projections, with
$p_0^i=1$, peaking to a pure state $f_i$. Suppose that $f_1\not\sim f_2$
and
\[
 \tau(p_n^1)=\tau(p_n^2)=t_n,
 \qquad 1=t_0>t_1>\cdots>0,
 \qquad t_n\longrightarrow0.
\]
Put $D_i=C^*(p_n^i:n\geq0)$ and let
$\theta:D_1\to D_2$ be determined by $\theta(p_n^1)=p_n^2$.
Form the reduced HNN extension $H(A)$ of Proposition~\ref{na:hnn}
using these data and their trace-preserving conditional expectations.
Then every pure state $h$ of $A$ has a unique state extension
$\widetilde h$ to $H(A)$. These extensions are pure, and for all pure
states $h,k$ of $A$,
\[
 \widetilde h\sim\widetilde k
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 h\sim k
 \quad\text{or}\quad
 \{[h],[k]\}=\{[f_1],[f_2]\}.
\]
The extension has a faithful tracial state extending $\tau$ and a
faithful trace-preserving conditional expectation onto $A$. If $A$ is
simple, then $H(A)$ is simple.
statements.section_title: Joining two classes while preserving unique extensions

statements.label: na:closed-extension
statements.text:
For every dependency-closed $S\subset\delta$, the inclusion
$A[S]\subset X_\delta$ has property \textup{(U)}.

statements.label: na:state-count
statements.text:
Put $\mathfrak c=2^{\aleph_0}$. If $|\delta|\le\mathfrak c$, then
$X_\delta$ has at most $\mathfrak c$ pure states.

statements.title: Kishimoto--Ozawa--Sakai
statements.label: na:homogeneity
statements.text:
Let $B$ be a separable $C^*$-algebra. If pure states $h,k$ of $B$
have GNS representations with the same kernel, there is an
automorphism $\gamma$ of $B$ such that $h\circ\gamma=k$.
In particular, this holds for every pair of pure states of a
separable simple $C^*$-algebra.

title: A counterexample to Sidorenko's conjecture
abstract: We disprove Sidorenko's conjecture with a bipartite graph on 35 vertices and 66 edges: its homomorphism density in some finite simple graph is smaller than the conjectured lower bound. The same connected graph also disproves the forcing conjecture: at one fixed density, asymptotically matching the edge and pattern densities does not imply quasirandomness.

tex.abstract:
We disprove Sidorenko's conjecture with a bipartite graph on \(35\) vertices
and \(66\) edges: its homomorphism density in some finite simple graph is
smaller than the conjectured lower bound. The same connected graph also
disproves the forcing conjecture: at one fixed density, asymptotically
matching the edge and pattern densities does not imply quasirandomness.
sections: Lagrangian counts and ordered triple orbits
Local bounds from the planted law

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let \(H\) be the incidence graph of the \(22\) triples on \(13\) points
in Table~\ref{tab:complex}. This bipartite graph has \(35\) vertices
and \(66\) edges. There is a finite simple undirected graph \(G\)
with at least one edge such that
\[
t(H,G)<p(G)^{66}.
\]

statements.title: Amplification and injective supersaturation
statements.label: cor:amplification
statements.text:
For the same graph \(H\) as in Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, the following
hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item For every \(c>0\), there is a finite simple undirected graph
\(F\) with \(p(F)>0\) such that
\[
t(H,F)<c\,p(F)^{66}.
\]
\item There are \(p_*\in(0,1)\), \(\delta_*>0\), and finite simple
undirected graphs \(F_s\) of orders \(n_s\to\infty\) for which
\(d_s=|E(F_s)|/\binom{n_s}{2}\to p_*\) and, for all sufficiently
large \(s\),
\[
\operatorname{Inj}(H,F_s)
\le(1-\delta_*)(n_s)_{35}d_s^{66}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Failure of the forcing conjecture
statements.label: cor:forcing
statements.text:
For the same connected bipartite graph \(H\) of
Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, there are \(p\in(0,1)\) and a nonconstant
graphon \(W\) such that
\[
t(K_2,W)=p,\qquad t(H,W)=p^{66}.
\]
Consequently, \(H\) is not \(p\)-forcing at this density and hence is
not forcing, despite being bipartite and containing a cycle.

statements.label: prop:complex
statements.text:
The complex has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Every pair in $E$ lies in exactly two faces, $|E|=33$, and the
face-neighbor graph is connected.
\item For each bit position, each of its two classes consists of
$11$ faces covering all $13$ points. Each class has an ordering in
which every face after the first shares a pair with an earlier face
and introduces exactly one new point.
\item Every $a_e$ is at least $1/3$, and some $a_e$ is greater than
$1/3$.
\item Color refinement of $H$, starting with a separate color for each
part, eventually gives distinct colors to all vertices within either
part.
\end{enumerate}

statements.label: prop:triple-orbits

statements.title: Three active incidences
statements.label: prop:planted-gain
statements.text:
For a local profile $(h_1,h_2,h_3,c)$, we choose one pointwise gain
exponent independent of \(q\) as follows. Let \(\mathcal U\) be the
union, over all odd prime fields and all ordered orbits of this profile,
of the parameter tuples arising from actual quadruples
$(L_1,L_2,L_3,Y)$ with the stated point profile and
$\dim(L_i\cap Y)=r$, using
Equations~\eqref{eq:planted-reduced-parameters} and
\eqref{eq:planted-subspace-parameters}. Their integer entries are bounded
at fixed \(D\), so \(\mathcal U\) is finite. If \(\mathcal U\) is empty,
the face factor is zero over every odd prime field. Otherwise the face
factor with three active incidences is
$O(q^g)$ uniformly over all triples in the profile, where
\begin{equation}
 g=\max_{\text{tuple}\in\mathcal U}\left\{
 g_C+\sum_i b(s_i)-\delta P-\sum_i p_i^2-vw
                   -\sum_i b(t_i)+b(v)\right\},
\end{equation}
so the selected exponent is independent of \(q\).

Every tuple in \(\mathcal U\) satisfies the following necessary
constraints:
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
 0\le u\le\min(c,r),\quad 0\le r'=r-u\le d,
 \quad |\delta|\le c,\quad d-\delta=2r',\\
 P+T=\sum_i s_i\le d,\qquad
 0\le t_i\le p_i+\delta,\qquad
 0\le v\le p_i+\delta\quad(1\le i\le3),\qquad w\ge0.
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
In particular $T\le P+3\delta$ and $d+3\delta\ge0$.
These conditions are not claimed sufficient for realizability.

title: A counterexample to Tachikawa's second conjecture
abstract: We disprove Tachikawa's second conjecture by constructing a finite-dimensional symmetric algebra over \(k=\mathbb F_2(q,H_1,H_2)\) with a finite-dimensional nonprojective module whose self-extension groups vanish in every positive degree. The associated endomorphism algebra also gives counterexamples to the classical, generalized, and strong Nakayama conjectures, the Auslander–Gorenstein conjecture, and the Wakamatsu tilting conjecture. These conclusions persist after every extension of k.

tex.abstract:
We disprove Tachikawa's second conjecture by constructing a
finite-dimensional symmetric algebra over $k=\mathbb F_2(q,H_1,H_2)$
with a finite-dimensional nonprojective module whose self-extension
groups vanish in every positive degree. The associated endomorphism
algebra also gives
counterexamples to the classical, generalized, and strong Nakayama
conjectures, the Auslander--Gorenstein conjecture, and the Wakamatsu
tilting conjecture. These conclusions persist after every extension of $k$.
sections: Derived induction and the trace obstruction
The triangular module and the counterexample
The endomorphism algebra and homological consequences

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let
\[
 k=\mathbb F_2(q,H_1,H_2),
\]
where $q,H_1,H_2$ are algebraically independent.
There exist a finite-dimensional associative unital symmetric
$k$-algebra $A$ and a finite-dimensional unital left $A$-module $M$
such that $M$ is nonprojective and
\[
 \Ext_A^i(M,M)=0\qquad\text{for every integer }i>0.
\]
In particular, Tachikawa's second conjecture is false.

statements.title: Homological conjectures
statements.label: cor:homological
statements.text:
Let $A,M$ be as in Theorem~\ref{thm:main}. For every field extension
$K/k$, put $A_K=K\otimes_k A$, $M_K=K\otimes_k M$, and
\[
 \Gamma_K=\End_{A_K}(A_K\oplus M_K)^{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Then $\Gamma_K$ is a finite-dimensional $K$-algebra with the following
properties, in the category of finite left $\Gamma_K$-modules.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Every term of the minimal injective resolution of $\Gamma_K$
is projective, but $\idim_{\Gamma_K}\Gamma_K=\infty$.
\item There is a nonzero simple module $S$ such that
$\Ext_{\Gamma_K}^i(S,\Gamma_K)=0$ for every $i\geq0$.
\item There is a projective-injective Wakamatsu tilting module $W$
which is not tilting.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the classical, generalized, and strong Nakayama conjectures,
the Auslander--Gorenstein conjecture, and the Wakamatsu tilting conjecture
are false for finite-dimensional algebras over $K$.

statements.title: Finitistic dimensions
statements.label: cor:finitistic
statements.text:
Let $k$ be the field in Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, let $K/k$ be any field
extension, and let $\Gamma_K$ be the algebra in
Corollary~\ref{cor:homological}. For every integer $n\geq1$, there is a
finite-dimensional left $\Gamma_K$-module $C_n$ such that
\[
 \pd_{\Gamma_K}C_n=n.
\]
Consequently $\Gamma_K$ has infinite little left finitistic dimension
and infinite big left finitistic dimension.

statements.title: Transfer through the trivial extension
statements.label: tr:transfer
statements.text:
Let $P$ be a totally acyclic complex of finite projective left
$R$-modules, and put $Z=c_0P$.  Suppose that $Z$ is nonprojective and
\begin{equation}
 H^a\Hom_R(P,Z)=0
 \qquad\text{for }a>0\text{ and for }a\leq -2.
\end{equation}
Then
\[
 A=R\ltimes DR,\qquad M=A\otimes_R Z
\]
are a finite-dimensional symmetric algebra and a finite-dimensional
nonprojective left $A$-module satisfying
\[
 \Ext_A^a(M,M)=0\qquad(a>0).
\]

statements.label: a:dual-dimensions
statements.text:
The dual regular module \(DC\) has projective dimension at most two
on both sides.  More precisely,
\[
D(eC)\cong Ce,\qquad D(Ce)\cong eC,
\]
and there are exact sequences
\begin{align}
0\longrightarrow Cf\xrightarrow{\rho_t}Ce
 \xrightarrow{\rho_{\ell_{-2}}}Ce
 \xrightarrow{e\mapsto j^*}D(fC)\longrightarrow0,
\\
0\longrightarrow fC\xrightarrow{\lambda_u}eC
 \xrightarrow{\lambda_{\ell_0}}eC
 \xrightarrow{e\mapsto v^*}D(Cf)\longrightarrow0.

\end{align}
Consequently
\begin{equation}
\pd_B({}_B E)\le4,\qquad
\pd_{B^{\mathrm{op}}}(E_B)\le4,\qquad
\idim_B({}_B B)\le4.

\end{equation}

statements.label: a:resolution
e:polynomial
e:all-degrees
e:twists
statements.text:
For every \(H\in k^\times\) and every \(m\ge0\), the action of
\(U_H(-)\) on the groups in \eqref{e:profile} is
\begin{equation}
\left.U_H\right|_{\cH^{3m}}=H^{-m}\,1_{\mathcal P_m},
\qquad
\left.U_H\right|_{\cH^{-3m-1}}=H^{m+2}\,1_{D\mathcal P_m}.

\end{equation}
In particular, the negative action is the stated scalar on the entire
\((m+1)\)-dimensional space.

statements.label: b:bimodule
statements.text:
There is a finite \(E\)-bimodule \(Y\), projective separately as a left and
as a right \(E\)-module, such that
\begin{equation}
 W^a:=\sHom_E(X,(YX)[a])
 \cong
 \begin{cases}
 k,&a=-3,0,\\
 0,&a\notin\{-3,0\}.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
For every \(H\in k^\times\), there is an ordinary bimodule map
\(g_H:U_H\to Y\) whose evaluation, under \(U_HX=X\), represents a nonzero
element of \(W^0\).  The same \(Y\) works for all \(H\), and all modules and
maps are defined over \(k\).
statements.section_title: Derived induction and the trace obstruction

statements.label: t:vanishing
statements.text:
The module and resolution in \eqref{t:cone} satisfy
\[
 H^a\Hom_\Lambda(P_Z,Z)=0
 \qquad(a>0\ \text{or}\ a\leq-2).
\]
statements.section_title: The triangular module and the counterexample

statements.label: prop:endomorphism
statements.text:
Let $B$ be a finite-dimensional symmetric algebra over a field and let
$N$ be a finite-dimensional nonprojective left $B$-module satisfying
$\Ext_B^i(N,N)=0$ for all $i>0$. Put
\[
 G=B\oplus N,\qquad \Gamma=\End_B(G)^{\mathrm{op}},
\]
where endomorphisms compose in the ordinary order. Then
\[
 \domdim({}_\Gamma\Gamma)=\infty,
 \qquad \idim_\Gamma\Gamma=\infty.
\]
In particular, $\Gamma$ is not self-injective.
statements.section_title: The endomorphism algebra and homological consequences

statements.title: Infinitely many tilting complements
statements.label: cor:tilting-complements
statements.text:
For every field extension $K/k$, let $\Gamma_K$ be the algebra in
Corollary~\ref{cor:homological}. There is a finite-dimensional projective
almost complete tilting left $\Gamma_K^{\mathrm{op}}$-module $P_K$ with
infinitely many pairwise nonisomorphic indecomposable complements.
statements.section_title: The endomorphism algebra and homological consequences

statements.title: Idempotent stratifications
statements.label: cor:stratifying
statements.text:
For every field extension $K/k$ and every integer $L\geq1$, there is an
auxiliary finite-dimensional indecomposable symmetric $K$-algebra $T_L$
admitting an idempotent stratification of length at least $L$ in the sense
of Chen, Fang and Xi. In particular, $T_L$ has a nonzero proper
stratifying ideal, and $\mathcal D(T_L\text{-}\mathrm{Mod})$ admits a
chain of at least $L$ nontrivial standard recollements through successive
corner algebras. Here $\mathrm{Mod}$ denotes all left modules and
$\mathcal D$ is the unbounded derived category.

title: A counterexample to integer-degree harmonic dimension comparison
abstract: For some even n ≥ 8 and integer k ≥ 2, we construct a complete smooth metric on ℝn with nonnegative Ricci curvature whose space of real harmonic functions of pointwise polynomial growth at most k has dimension larger than the Euclidean harmonic-polynomial dimension. The metric is Euclidean near the origin, has asymptotic volume ratio strictly between zero and one, and has nonunique tangent cones at infinity. This answers the integer-degree form of Yau's dimension comparison question in the negative.

tex.abstract:
For some even $n\ge8$ and integer $k\ge2$, we construct a complete smooth
metric on $\mathbb R^n$ with nonnegative Ricci curvature whose space of real
harmonic functions of pointwise polynomial growth at most $k$ has dimension
larger than the Euclidean harmonic-polynomial dimension. The metric is
Euclidean near the origin, has asymptotic volume ratio strictly between zero
and one, and has nonunique tangent cones at infinity. This answers the integer-degree form of Yau's dimension comparison
question in the negative.
sections: A complete metric with nonnegative Ricci curvature
Exact transmission on the regular harmonic subspaces

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There are an even integer $n\geq8$, an integer $k\geq2$, and a complete
smooth metric $g$ on $\mathbb R^n$ such that $\operatorname{Ric}_g\geq0$
and
\[
 h_k(\mathbb R^n,g)>h_k(\mathbb R^n,g_{\mathrm E}).
\]
The metric is Euclidean near the origin, and its asymptotic volume ratio
satisfies
\[
 0<\lim_{R\to\infty}
 \frac{\operatorname{vol}_g B_g(0,R)}{\omega_nR^n}<1,
\]
where $\omega_n$ is the volume of the Euclidean unit ball.

statements.title: Simultaneous control
statements.label: prop:control
statements.text:
Fix positive numbers \(\kappa_l\), \(2\leq l\leq L\).  As \(J\) ranges
over all orthogonal complex structures on \(\mathbb R^{2s}\), the tuples
\begin{equation}
 X_J=\bigl(\kappa_l(D_J^2|_{V_l})_{\mathrm{tf}}\bigr)_{l=2}^L
 
\end{equation}
generate, under real linear combinations and brackets, the full Lie
algebra
\[
 \bigoplus_{l=2}^L\mathfrak{sl}(V_l).
\]

statements.title: A finite word with invertible differential
statements.label: prop:word
statements.text:
Let \(d=\sum_{l=2}^L(N_l^2-1)\).
There exist finitely many orthogonal complex structures
\(J_1,\ldots,J_R\), an open neighborhood \(U\) of zero in
\(\mathbb R^d\), and smooth real functions \(c_1,\ldots,c_R\) on
\(U\) such that
\[
 \mathcal W(h)=
   \exp(c_R(h)X_{J_R})\cdots\exp(c_1(h)X_{J_1})
\]
satisfies \(\mathcal W(0)=\Pi\), and
\[
 D\mathcal W(0):\mathbb R^d\longrightarrow T_\Pi\mathcal G
\]
is an isomorphism.  The same assertion holds for any prescribed
target in \(\mathcal G\).

statements.label: prop:metric
statements.text:
For the fixed spectral data above, there are a smooth function
\(a:\R\to(0,1]\) and an index \(j_{\rm geom}\) such that, for every
\(j_0\geq j_{\rm geom}\), every sequence
\((h_j)_{j\geq j_0}\) in \(K\), used in the preceding scheme, defines
a smooth complete metric on \(\R^{m+1}\) with nonnegative Ricci
curvature:
\[
 g=dr^2+r^2\gamma(\log r),\qquad
 \gamma(t)=G(a(t),q(t),J(t)).
\]
The function \(a\) is identically \(1\) for \(t\leq2\), decreases to
\(a_*\), and, for some \(\mu>0\), satisfies
\begin{equation}
 b(t):=\frac{a'(t)}{a(t)}
       =-\mu(1+t)^{-5/4}\quad(t\geq4),
 \qquad
 \log\frac{a(t)}{a_*}=4\mu(1+t)^{-1/4}\quad(t\geq4).
\end{equation}
The metric is Euclidean near the origin, and its distance from the
origin is exactly \(r\).
Its volume form is
\[
 d\operatorname{vol}_g
   =r^m a(\log r)^m\,dr\,d\operatorname{vol}_{g_0}.
\]
The function \(a\) and the starting index \(j_0\) can be chosen
independently of the sequence of control parameters.
statements.section_title: A complete metric with nonnegative Ricci curvature

statements.title: Exact full-period transmission
statements.label: prop:transmission
statements.text:
For finite spectral data as specified at the end of Section~\ref{sec:counting},
choose the word and compact pulse family above. There are a starting
index \(j_0\) and parameters \(h_j\in K\), for every \(j\geq j_0\),
such that the center-regular value transmissions of the resulting metric
satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal T_{l,j}=s_{l,j}D_{l,j}\Pi_l,\qquad
 s_{l,j}>0,\qquad |\log s_{l,j}|\leq C T_j
 \quad(2\leq l\leq L,\ j\geq j_0).
 
\end{equation}
The positive diagonal matrices \(D_{l,j}\) propagate the reference
Cauchy data \((I,\theta_l I)\) over the entire leg following the pulse;
they satisfy \eqref{eq:diagonal-growth}. The regular value equation has the
bounds \eqref{eq:riccati-barriers}. All estimates used to choose \(j_0\)
are uniform over preceding admitted controls for this fixed finite family.
statements.section_title: Exact transmission on the regular harmonic subspaces

statements.title: Cone geometry and the union of degrees
statements.label: prop:cone-consequences
statements.text:
Let \(g\) be the metric constructed in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:main},
with link parameters \(a_*,q_*\) and comparison integer \(k\).
Every cone with link \(G(a_*,q,J_0)\), \(1\leq q\leq q_*\), occurs
as a pointed tangent cone at infinity. In particular the tangent cone is
not unique. The metric \(g\) is not locally conformally flat. If
\(\mathcal D(M)\) denotes the union of nonnegative homogeneous harmonic
degrees over all its tangent cones, then \(\mathcal D(M)\) contains a
half-line and a neighborhood of \(k\).

title: A counterexample to the Colin de Verdière chromatic conjecture
abstract: We disprove the Colin de Verdière chromatic conjecture by constructing graphs whose chromatic number exceeds their Colin de Verdière invariant by more than one. The examples have independence number at most two. In fact, their ordinary fractional chromatic number also exceeds their Colin de Verdière invariant by more than one.

tex.abstract:
We disprove the Colin de Verdière chromatic conjecture by constructing
graphs whose chromatic number exceeds their Colin de Verdière invariant
by more than one. The examples have independence number at most two.
In fact, their ordinary fractional chromatic number also exceeds their
Colin de Verdière invariant by more than one.
sections: The tensor geometry and the hole relation
The distribution problem and its preliminary tools
Recipes and realization of the gradients
From overlapping key distributions to four holes
A common limit for successful queries
Conflicts between a unit and an independent point
From distribution tests to finite graphs
Compact measure constructions used in the proof

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There are finite graphs \(G\) of arbitrarily large order for which
\[
 \alpha(G)\le2,\qquad
 \mu(G)+1<\frac{|V(G)|}{2}\le\chi(G).
\]
In particular, the Colin de Verdière chromatic conjecture is false.

statements.title: Base graphs
statements.label: thm:base-graphs
statements.text:
There is a constant \(a>0\) such that, for every \(\beta>0\),
there are arbitrarily large integers \(m\) and graphs \(H\) on
\(m\) vertices with \(\alpha(H)\le2\) and the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(G\arabic*)},ref=G\arabic*]
\item
Every matching of size at least \(m/20\), partitioned into classes
of size at most \(am\), contains two conflicting edges in different
classes.
\item
Every matching of size at least \(\beta m\) and every vertex set
of size at least \(\beta m\) contain an edge and a vertex in conflict.
\item
Every two vertex sets of size at least \(\beta m\) contain a cross
hole.
\end{enumerate}
The two vertex sets in \ref{item:base-holes} may overlap.

statements.title: Fractional-colouring obstruction
statements.label: cor:fractional-spectral
statements.text:
There are finite nonempty simple graphs \(G\) of arbitrarily large
order for which
\[
 \chi_f(G)\ge \frac{|V(G)|}{\alpha(G)}
 \ge \frac{|V(G)|}{2}
 >\kappa(G)+1\ge\mu(G)+1\ge h(G).
\]

statements.title: A linear list-colouring bound
statements.label: cor:list-spectral
statements.text:
Let \(C\) be the absolute integer in
\citet[Theorem~1.1]{OpenAILinearListHadwiger2026}. Every finite nonempty
simple graph \(G\) satisfies
\[
 \chi_{\mathrm{list}}(G)\le C\bigl(\mu(G)+1\bigr).
\]

statements.title: Finite tree principle
statements.label: mt:finite-tree
statements.text:
For each index \(s\), let \(P_{1,s},\ldots,P_{k,s}\) be positive
subspaces in a Lorentz space, whose dimension may depend on \(s\).
Fix a set \(\mathcal D\) of pairs of distinct labels, and assume
\[
 \sup_s d_{\mathbb H}(F_{P_{i,s}},F_{P_{j,s}})\le D<\infty
 \qquad (\{i,j\}\in\mathcal D).
\]
After passing to a subsequence, there are a finite combinatorial tree
\(T\) and a nonempty connected vertex set \(S_i\subseteq V(T)\)
for every label, with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item \(S_i\cap S_j\ne\varnothing\) for every
\(\{i,j\}\in\mathcal D\).
\item For every vertex \(x\), called a \emph{bag}, choose any
Lorentz-orthonormal basis in every \(P_{i,s}\) with \(x\in S_i\).
The Gram matrix of the concatenated list has operator norm bounded
uniformly in \(s\).  The bound depends only on \(k,D\), and not on
the dimensions or on the bases.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, mutually orthogonal blocks can always be required to
have intersecting subtrees.

statements.title: A common bag
statements.label: mt:common-bag
statements.text:
Suppose the hypotheses of \Cref{mt:single-bag,mt:weighted-bag}
hold in the same tree.  Suppose additionally that
\(S_e\cap S_v\ne\varnothing\) whenever the edge \(e\) and the
vertex \(v\in V_0\) conflict.  If
\(q\le cm/4\), there is a vertex \(x\) such that
\begin{equation}
 |\{v\in V_0:x\notin S_v\}|<5q,
 \qquad \sum_{e:\,x\in S_e}w_e\ge\frac{cm}{2}.
\end{equation}
If all edges of \(\mathcal E\) have both endpoints in \(V_0\) and
\(q\le cm/30\), deleting every edge incident with a missing vertex
leaves bag weight at least \(cm/3\).

statements.title: Matrix obstruction
statements.label: thm:matrix-obstruction
statements.text:
For every $a\in(0,1]$ there are constants $\beta_0(a)>0$ and
$m_0(a)\in\mathbb N$ with the following property.  Let
$0<\beta\le\beta_0(a)$, let $m\ge m_0(a)$, and let $G$ be an
$m$-vertex graph satisfying the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item Every matching of size at least $m/20$, partitioned into classes
of size at most $am$, contains two conflicting edges in different
classes.
\item Every matching of size at least $\beta m$ and every vertex set of
size at least $\beta m$ contain a conflicting edge--point pair.
\item Every two vertex sets of size at least $\beta m$ have a cross hole.
\end{enumerate}
Then there is $s_0=s_0(G,a,\beta)$ such that, for every integer
$s\ge s_0$, every real symmetric well-signed matrix $M$ for the clique
blow-up $G[K_s]$ with exactly one negative eigenvalue satisfies
\[
  \rank M>\frac{ms}{2}+1.
\]
Consequently $\mu(G[K_s])+1<ms/2$ for all these $s$.

statements.title: Distribution tests
statements.label: thm:distribution-tests
statements.text:
There is a constant \(\eta_{\rm col}>0\), depending only on the early
parameters and \(M\), with the following property.  Fix any \(L<\infty\)
after \(\eta_{\rm col}\) and before the selector and channel parameters;
choose all remaining parameters in the order of
\Cref{eq:parameter-order,sec:parameters}.  For every sufficiently large
\(n\), the law \(\pi\) constructed above satisfies both conclusions.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item Let \((A,c)\) have a probability law on units marked by a colour in
any fixed finite palette.  The colour may be randomized conditional on
\(A\).  Write \(\sigma_1,\sigma_2\) for the endpoint
marginals of its projected unit law \(\sigma\), and suppose
\begin{equation}
 \sigma_1\le M\pi,\qquad \sigma_2\le M\pi,\qquad
 \sigma\le2^{3000gN}\pi^2,
 \qquad \Pr(c=j)\le\eta_{\rm col}\quad\text{for every }j.
\end{equation}
For two independent draws \((A,c),(B,c')\),
\[
 \Pr(A\bowtie B, c\ne c')\ge2^{-100gN}.
\]
\item Let \(A\) have a unit law \(\sigma\) and let \(z\) be an independent
point with law \(\theta\), where
\begin{equation}
 \sigma_1\le L\pi,\qquad \sigma_2\le L\pi,\qquad
 \sigma\le2^{3000gN}\pi^2,
 \qquad \theta\le L\pi.
\end{equation}
Then \(\Pr(A\bowtie z)\ge2^{-100gN}\).
\end{enumerate}
The threshold for \(n\) may depend on the fixed palette and on \(L\).
All inequalities between measures are pointwise on their finite spaces.
statements.section_title: The distribution problem and its preliminary tools

statements.title: Colours and actual leaf weights
statements.label: cor:coloured-peeling
statements.text:
For a law satisfying \Cref{eq:coloured-law-caps}, discard colours whose
mass is below \(2^{-\zeta N}\), and apply \Cref{lem:peeling}(a) to each
remaining conditional colour law.  The total discarded mass tends to
zero exponentially, the leaves have at most \(K_1\) pins and satisfy
\Cref{eq:leaf-minentropy}, and each leaf has an absolute density bound
\(2^{(D+K_1+1)N}\rawlaw^2\).  With their actual retained masses these
leaves form a mixed law whose endpoint marginals are bounded by
\((1+o(1))M\pi\).  Any subsequent combined restriction of mass
\(2^{-o(N)}\) has the first-pin freshness in
\Cref{eq:final-leaf-minentropy}, after the trimming in
\Cref{lem:peeling}(b).
statements.section_title: The distribution problem and its preliminary tools

statements.title: An independent pair as an unpinned leaf
statements.label: cor:independent-point-leaf
statements.text:
Let \(\theta\le L\pi\), and draw two independent \(\theta\)-points.
The probability that they form an internal hole is \(2^{-\Omega(N)}\).
Their law conditioned on being a unit is a single leaf with no pins,
with endpoint marginals at most \((1+o(1))L\pi\), and it satisfies
\Cref{eq:leaf-minentropy} for every rank \(t\ge1\).  Its effective spaces
\(C_1,C_2\), defined in \Cref{sec:moments}, are consequently zero.
statements.section_title: The distribution problem and its preliminary tools

statements.title: Gradient realization
statements.label: thm:gradient-realization
statements.text:
Suppose two units in fixed leaves have lists satisfying
\eqref{eq:recipe-scalars}, the binary prescriptions yielding
\eqref{eq:recipe-gradients}, equal matched keys, and an
admissible injecting small table.  Freeze their actual cross
Gram entries whenever either argument is a pin or a key
direction.  Then there are abstract cross bilinear forms on
the full nominal spaces, extending all these frozen entries,
whose primal-versus-channel entries satisfy
\begin{equation}
 u_zU_i=r(v_{iz})\quad\text{on }\cX
 \qquad(i\text{ and }z\text{ in opposite units}).
\end{equation}
Only the primal-versus-channel entries need be prescribed in
the final test.  Their number is at most
$16|\cE|h\dim\cB=O(n)$, with its coefficient fixed before
$M_0$.  Agreement of the actual cross Grams with these entries
produces all four cross holes, with witnesses $(v_{iz},v_{zi})$.
statements.section_title: Recipes and realization of the gradients

statements.title: Filtered collision criterion
statements.label: prop:collision
statements.text:
Let $\sigma_A,\sigma_B$ be two laws on units, possibly carrying
finitely many colour or type marks.  After forgetting these
marks, suppose each law has density at most $2^{3000gN}$
relative to $\pi\otimes\pi$.
For $O\in\{A,B\}$, let $\widetilde\sigma_O$ be a normalized
restriction of $\sigma_O$ of relative mass at least $2^{-o(N)}$,
decomposed into leaves satisfying
\eqref{eq:final-leaf-minentropy}.  On each side mix the leaves
with their actual masses in $\widetilde\sigma_O$.

Fix a required predicate $\Psi(A,B)$ on the marked units and
an allowed leaf-pair indicator $J_n$.
Use only numerical query options whose joint acceptance on
an allowed leaf pair, including their separate orientation
filters, implies $\Psi(A,B)$.  Suppose these accepted queries satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \E_{\text{independent leaf pair}}
       J_n(\ell_A,\ell_B)\int d_A d_B\,d\nu_n\ge 2^{-o(N)}.
\end{equation}
Then independent draws $A\sim\sigma_A$, $B\sim\sigma_B$ satisfy
$\Psi(A,B)$ and have all four cross holes with probability at least
\begin{equation}
 2^{-(k_{\max}+.03)N-o(N)}.
\end{equation}
It suffices to obtain \eqref{eq:overlap-criterion} after skipping
some leaf pairs, or after summing over a bounded number of
numerical options.  In particular, a positive subsequential
overlap lower bound yields \eqref{eq:collision-conclusion} along
that subsequence.  With $\sigma_A=\sigma_B$ and
$\Psi$ the distinct-colour test, the conclusion retains that
test.  The statement also applies when the two sides have
different prescribed law types.
statements.section_title: From overlapping key distributions to four holes

statements.title: Phase alternative
statements.label: thm:phase-alternative
statements.text:
Suppose a marked-unit law \(\sigma\) satisfies
\[
 \sigma_i\le\Lambda\pi\quad(i=1,2),\qquad
 \sigma\le2^{(D+.01)N}\rawlaw^2,
\]
where \(\Lambda\) is fixed before the channel size, and suppose
\(\Delta_O\ne0\) throughout.  For all sufficiently large \(n\),
one can retain a sublaw of relative mass at least
\(\delta_{\rm ph}>0\), depending only on the early parameters,
such that one of the following holds for independent draws \(A,B\):
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item every nontrivial phase mean
\[
 \E(-1)^{u_{B,S}(\Delta_A)+u_{A,R}(\Delta_B)},
 \qquad(S,R)\ne(\varnothing,\varnothing),
\]
has absolute value less than \(.005\);
\item writing \(F(A,B)=u_{B,\{1,2\}}(\Delta_A)\), one has
\(F(A,B)=0\) for every pair of retained units, and every displayed
mean for which \(|S|=1\) or \(|R|=1\) is \(2^{-\Omega(N)}\).
\end{enumerate}
All marks remain in their first effective spaces.  No additional
image directions are pinned.  Neither the retained-mass bound nor
the tiny-cover dimension used in the proof depends on selector or
channel sizes; the lower bound required of \(h\) may depend on
\(\Lambda\).

statements.title: A uniform phase compatibility margin
statements.label: tp:phase-compatibility
statements.text:
On either retained law of \Cref{thm:phase-alternative}, for each
fixed \(c\in\F\) and all sufficiently large \(n\),
\begin{equation}
 \PP\{u_{B,1}(\Delta_A)=u_{B,2}(\Delta_A)
       =u_{A,1}(\Delta_B)=u_{A,2}(\Delta_B)=c\}\ge1/32.
 
\end{equation}
Also \(\PP\{F(A,B)+F(B,A)=0\}\ge .49\), and each single
prescribed phase bit has probability at least \(.49\).

statements.title: Status preparation
statements.label: prop:status-preparation
statements.text:
There are constants \(\delta_*,c_*>0\), fixed before the selector
and channel sizes, with the following property.  Along a subsequence,
the original pooled unit law has a restriction of mass at least
\(\delta_*\) whose first pin dimension is at most \(K_1\) and whose
normalized leaves satisfy \Cref{eq:final-leaf-minentropy}.  One of
the following descriptions applies.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item There is no prediction as in \Cref{def:prediction} on the
first pooled law before the final negligible leaf trimming.  For
independent draws from the prepared law, the probability of an
admissible injecting actual small table is greater than \(.99\).
\item A prediction with fixed \(\alpha_i,c\) and common classes
\(e_i\) is retained.  Its marks and exceptions are preserved, and
\Cref{eq:prediction} has uniform \(o(1)\) error on every retained
unit.  If both classes vanish, \Cref{eq:exact-prediction} is exact
on every unit.  For independent draws from the prepared law,
the probability of an admissible injecting actual table satisfying
\Cref{eq:phase-compatibility} is at least \(1/64\).
\end{enumerate}
In particular the corresponding successful pair event, measured
in two draws from the original pooled law, has mass at least
\(c_*\).  One may take
\begin{equation}
 \delta_* = \frac{10^{-6}\delta_{\mathrm{ph}}}{64},
 \qquad c_* = \frac{\delta_*^2}{64},
 \qquad 0<\eta_{\mathrm{col}}<\frac{c_*}{4},
 
\end{equation}
where \(0<\delta_{\mathrm{ph}}\le1\) is the early retained-mass
constant in \Cref{thm:phase-alternative}.  The colour bound in
\Cref{eq:preparation-early-margins} can be chosen using the initial
\(M\) and early geometric constants only; the marginal constant
\(L\) of the second distribution test does not enter it.

After forgetting colour and other marks, the prepared law
\(\sigma'\) satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \sigma'_i\le\frac{M}{\delta_*}\pi\quad(i=1,2),
 \qquad
 \sigma'\le 2^{(D+o(1))N}\rawlaw^2.
 
\end{equation}
The endpoint primal marginals consequently have the same constant
bound relative to \(\operatorname{pr}_*\rawlaw\).  Every normalized
leaf has joint density at most \(2^{O(N)}\rawlaw^2\).  The successful
table event is detected by a finite list of numerical tables and
separate unary orientation flags, together with leaf-pair tests.
The size of this list is fixed in \(n\), but need not be early.

statements.title: Removing equal colours
statements.label: tp:preparation-colours
statements.text:
Suppose the original colour masses are \(p_\gamma\le
\eta_{\mathrm{col}}\).  The successful prepared pair event of
\Cref{prop:status-preparation}, with the further requirement that
its two colours differ, has mass at least
\(c_*-\eta_{\mathrm{col}}>3c_*/4\) in the original pooled law.

statements.title: Weak product comparison
statements.label: thm:weak-product
statements.text:
Let $W_n$ be any sequence of real functions on $\cK_n$ with
$\norm{W_n}_\infty\le B$, where $B$ is fixed. Extend it to the product
of the single-key spaces with the same bound. For every $\eps>0$
there are constants $L,C<\infty$, independent of $n$, and functions
\begin{equation}
 S_n(k_1,\ldots,k_r)
   =\sum_{a=1}^{L}c_{a,n}\prod_{j=1}^{r}f_{a,j,n}(k_j),
 \qquad
 \abs{c_{a,n}}\le C,\quad \abs{f_{a,j,n}}\le1,
\end{equation}
with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item For arbitrary global unary functions $g_{j,n}$ of bound one,
\begin{equation}
 \abs{\int(W_n-S_n)\prod_jg_{j,n}(k_j)\,d\nu_n}\le\eps
\end{equation}
for all sufficiently large $n$.
\item Under any mixed unit law satisfying
\eqref{eq:histogram-mixed-caps}, outside an exponentially small
exceptional set of orientations,
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{\abs{w_j}\le1}
 \abs{\E_z\mathcal A_n(O,z)
       (W_n-S_n)(K(O,z))\prod_jw_j(O,z_j)}\le\eps.
\end{equation}
The unary input weights may depend on the entire fixed orientation
and on any additional marks fixed with it. The exceptional set is
independent of these weights. Thus one may prescribe channel flags
such as $p_i$ in a unary weight without making them common key tests
or asserting positivity for their individual values.
\end{enumerate}
The functions $f_{a,j,n}$ are global key functions; they can be chosen
to be indicators of sets, or finite linear combinations of such
indicators with uniformly bounded complexity. They do not depend on
the sampled orientation. The constants may depend on $B,\eps$ and
the fixed template and construction parameters, but not on $n$.

An additional orientation-only filter of bound one may multiply
\eqref{eq:weak-product-actual} without changing it. In particular,
after averaging normalized leaves, the same error control applies to
unnormalized admissibility-filtered query measures, even when the
filter is chosen using the opposite leaf. No assertion is made for
an arbitrary additional joint input filter.
For distinct marked laws, use their fixed-weight mixture, with caps
checked after forgetting the marks. A retained ordered type pair or
different-colour condition is an orientation/leaf-pair filter, so the
same conclusion applies before normalization. All leaf averages use
their actual weights; no marginal hypothesis on a separately
normalized colour class is needed.

statements.title: Factorized integration of the approximant
statements.label: cor:weak-product-factorized-integration
statements.text:
For the structured sum in \eqref{eq:weak-product-approximant} and
arbitrary bounded unary input weights, outside exponentially small
mixed mass,
\begin{align}
 &\E_z\mathcal A_n(O,z)S_n(K(O,z))\prod_jw_j(O,z_j)\notag\\
 &\qquad=
 \kappa\sum_{a=1}^{L}c_{a,n}
       \prod_j\E_{z_j}
        \bigl[f_{a,j,n}(K_j(O,z_j))w_j(O,z_j)\bigr]+o(1).
\end{align}
The error is uniform over the unary weights. An orientation-only
filter may be included before averaging this identity over leaves.
In particular the same statement applies to marked mixtures and
retained type/colour pairs as in \Cref{thm:weak-product}.

statements.title: The limiting overlap obstruction
statements.label: prop:limit-overlap
statements.section_title: A common limit for successful queries

statements.title: Positive-mass overlap
statements.label: prop:positive-overlap
statements.text:
Consider two independent unit laws with actual leaf weights, the mixed
caps \eqref{eq:histogram-mixed-caps}, the final per-leaf image bounds,
and a permitted-pair indicator $J_n$ as in \Cref{sec:common-limit}.
Suppose their common model has positive mass of pairs with $J=1$
admitting a passed injecting table whose scalar system is soluble after
every bounded exclusion used by \Cref{lem:fresh-lists}. Then some fixed
numerical option has expected unnormalized, permitted-pair overlap
bounded below by a positive constant along a subsequence. Consequently
it satisfies \eqref{eq:overlap-criterion}, with the same permitted-pair
predicate. The two laws need not coincide. If the original laws
additionally satisfy the hypotheses of \Cref{prop:collision}, its
probability bound holds along the same subsequence, with any initial
restrictions of reciprocal mass $2^{o(N)}$ charged to that probability.

statements.title: Different-colour conflicts
statements.label: prop:coloured-distribution
statements.text:
Let the early constant $\eta_{\mathrm{col}}>0$ satisfy
\[
 \eta_{\mathrm{col}}<\frac14c_* ,\qquad
 c_*:=\frac{\delta_*^2}{64},
\]
where $\delta_*$ is the retained-mass margin in
\eqref{eq:preparation-early-margins}. This choice depends on the original
endpoint bound $M$ and the early geometric constants, and precedes the
selector and channel dimensions. For every fixed finite palette and all
sufficiently large $n$, a unit law with both endpoint marginals bounded
by $M\pi$, pair law after forgetting colour bounded by $2^{3000gN}\pi^2$, and each
colour of mass at most $\eta_{\mathrm{col}}$ satisfies
\[
 \Pr\{A\text{ and }B\text{ have four cross holes and different colours}\}
 \ge 2^{-100gN},
\]
where $A,B$ are independent draws from that law. In particular,
\Cref{thm:distribution-tests}\textup{(i)} holds.

statements.title: The asymmetric distribution test
statements.label: prop:asymmetric-distribution
statements.text:
For every fixed \(L\), with the late parameters chosen as above,
all sufficiently large \(n\) and all laws satisfying
\eqref{eq:asym-caps} obey
\[
 \PP_{A\sim\sigma,\ Z\sim\nu}
       \{A\text{ and }Z\text{ conflict}\}\ge2^{-100gN}.
\]
Thus \Cref{thm:distribution-tests}\textup{(ii)} holds.

title: A counterexample to the Monge ansatz for the three-marginal Coulomb cost
abstract: We construct a smooth compactly supported probability density on ℝ3, with a smooth compactly supported square root, for which the three-marginal Coulomb transport minimum is not attained by any pair of measure-preserving Borel maps. Nevertheless, the Monge and Kantorovich infima agree: we construct preserving maps whose costs approach the Kantorovich minimum. For every d ≥ 2 and s > 0, we also construct a smooth identical marginal with the same nonattainment and equality-of-infima properties for the inverse-power interaction \(\sum_{i\lt j}|x_i-x_j|^{-s}\) on ℝd.

tex.abstract:
We construct a smooth compactly supported probability density on
\(\R^3\), with a smooth compactly supported square root, for which the
three-marginal Coulomb transport minimum is not attained by any pair of
measure-preserving Borel maps. Nevertheless, the Monge and Kantorovich
infima agree: we construct preserving maps whose costs approach the
Kantorovich minimum. For every \(d\ge2\) and \(s>0\), we also construct a
smooth identical marginal with the same nonattainment and equality-of-infima
properties for the inverse-power interaction
\(\sum_{i<j}|x_i-x_j|^{-s}\) on \(\R^d\).
sections: A supporting inequality on five components
The marginal and exclusion of every Monge optimizer

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is a nonnegative density \(\rho\) on \(\R^3\) such that
\[
 \int_{\R^3}\rho(x)\dd x=1,\qquad
 \rho\in C_c^\infty(\R^3),\qquad
 \sqrt{\rho}\in C_c^\infty(\R^3),
\]
with the following properties. For \(\mu=\rho\dd x\), the value
\(\E(\mu)\) is finite and is attained by a coupling in
\(\Pi(\mu,\mu,\mu)\), but every pair of Borel maps
\(T_2,T_3:\R^3\to\R^3\) satisfying
\((T_2)_\#\mu=(T_3)_\#\mu=\mu\) obeys
\[
 \int_{\R^3}c\bigl(x,T_2(x),T_3(x)\bigr)\dd\mu(x)>\E(\mu).
\]
The inequality permits the left-hand side to be infinite.

statements.label: prop:certificate
statements.text:
There are pairwise disjoint open balls \(U_0,U_k^+,U_k^-\) centered
at \(0,a_k,-a_k\), respectively, and a bounded continuous function
\(u:U\to\R\), where
\[
 U=U_0\cup U_1^+\cup U_1^-\cup U_2^+\cup U_2^-,
\]
such that
\begin{equation}
 c(x_1,x_2,x_3)\ge\sum_{i=1}^3u(x_i)
 \quad\text{on }U^3.
\end{equation}
Equality holds precisely at the triples in \(U^3\) which, after a
permutation, have the form
\begin{equation}
 (X_k(y),y,Z_k(y))\in U_0\times U_k^+\times U_k^-,
 \qquad y\in U_k^+,\quad k\in\{1,2\}.
\end{equation}
The maps \(X_k,Z_k\) are diffeomorphisms on \(U_k^+\), with
\[
 X_k(U_k^+)\subset U_0,\qquad Z_k(U_k^+)\subset U_k^-.
\]
statements.section_title: A supporting inequality on five components

statements.label: prop:equal-infima
statements.text:
For the probability measure \(\mu\) of Theorem~\ref{thm:main},
\[
 \inf_{\substack{T_2,T_3:\R^3\to\R^3\ \mathrm{Borel}\\
                 (T_2)_\#\mu=(T_3)_\#\mu=\mu}}
 \int c(x,T_2(x),T_3(x))\dd\mu(x)=\E(\mu).
\]
Every pair in this infimum has cost strictly greater than the common
infimum, but pairs with finite cost approach it.

statements.label: thm:riesz
statements.text:
For every integer \(d\ge2\) and every real \(s>0\), there is a
nonnegative density \(\rho\) on \(\R^d\) such that
\[
 \int_{\R^d}\rho(x)\dd x=1,\qquad
 \rho\in C_c^\infty(\R^d),\qquad
 \sqrt{\rho}\in C_c^\infty(\R^d),
\]
with the following properties. For \(\mu=\rho\dd x\), the value
\(E_s(\mu)\) is finite and attained by a coupling, but every pair of
Borel maps \(T_2,T_3:\R^d\to\R^d\) with
\((T_2)_\#\mu=(T_3)_\#\mu=\mu\) satisfies
\[
 \int_{\R^d}c_s\bigl(x,T_2(x),T_3(x)\bigr)\dd\mu(x)>E_s(\mu).
\]
The left-hand side may be infinite.
Nevertheless,
\[
 \inf_{\substack{T_2,T_3:\R^d\to\R^d\ \mathrm{Borel}\\
                 (T_2)_\#\mu=(T_3)_\#\mu=\mu}}
 \int c_s(x,T_2(x),T_3(x))\dd\mu(x)=E_s(\mu),
\]
and pairs with finite cost approach this infimum.
