title: A counterexample to the coarse Novikov conjecture
abstract: We disprove the coarse Novikov conjecture: ordinary coarse assembly need not be rationally injective for uniformly discrete spaces of bounded geometry. We construct a coarse disjoint union of finite graphs of uniformly bounded degree and an infinite-order class in its degree-one coarse K-homology whose image under ordinary coarse assembly in the K-theory of the reduced, locally compact Roe algebra vanishes.

tex.abstract:
We disprove the coarse Novikov conjecture: ordinary coarse assembly need not
be rationally injective for uniformly discrete spaces of bounded geometry.
We construct a coarse disjoint union of finite graphs of uniformly bounded
degree and an infinite-order class in its degree-one coarse K-homology whose
image under ordinary coarse assembly in the K-theory of the reduced, locally
compact Roe algebra vanishes.
sections: Coarse assembly and locally finite classes

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is a uniformly discrete bounded-geometry metric space $X$, which is a
coarse disjoint union of finite connected graphs of uniformly bounded degree,
and an infinite-order element $\alpha\in KX_1(X)$ such that
\[
 \mu_X(\alpha)=0\quad\text{in }K_1(C^*(X)).
\]
Consequently, ordinary coarse assembly for $X$ fails to be injective both
integrally and after tensoring its domain and target with $\Q$.

statements.label: prop:persistence
statements.text:
For every integer $r\ge1$ there is a homomorphism
\[
 \lambda_r:K_1^{\lf}(P_r(X))\longrightarrow\Z
 \quad\text{such that}\quad \lambda_r(\alpha_r)=1.
\]
Consequently, every nonzero integer multiple of $\alpha$ is nonzero in
$KX_1(X)$.

statements.title: Transfer through finite fibers
statements.label: prop:transfer
statements.text:
Let $D$ and $X$ be countable uniformly discrete bounded-geometry spaces.
Suppose $X=\coprod_{u\in D}F_u$ is a partition into nonempty finite sets.
Write $\xi_u=\abs{F_u}^{-1/2}\sum_{x\in F_u}\delta_x$ and let $P$ be the
orthogonal projection on $\ell^2(X)$ onto the span of the $\xi_u$.
Assume:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $P$ is an operator-norm limit of finite-propagation contractions $P_n$
on $\ell^2(X)$;
\item for every $R<\infty$ there is $s_R<\infty$ such that, whenever
$d_D(u,v)\le R$, there is a contraction
$O_{uv}:\ell^2(F_v)\to\ell^2(F_u)$ of propagation at most $s_R$ with
$O_{uv}\xi_v=\xi_u$.
\end{enumerate}
For the isometry
\[
 V:\ell^2(D)\otimes\HH_0\longrightarrow\ell^2(X)\otimes\HH_0,
 \qquad V(\delta_u\otimes h)=\xi_u\otimes h,
\]
conjugation defines a $*$-homomorphism
$\Ad V:C^*(D)\to C^*(X)$ between the reduced, locally compact Roe algebras.

tex.abstract:
We disprove the unrestricted nearby Lagrangian conjecture. For some
sufficiently large even integer $N$, we construct a closed exact smoothly
embedded Lagrangian in $T^*(S^9\times S^{N-1})$ that is diffeomorphic to
the base but is not Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For some sufficiently large even integer $N$, the manifold
$Q=S^9\times S^{N-1}$ admits a closed exact smoothly embedded Lagrangian
$L\subset T^*Q$ such that $L$ is diffeomorphic to $Q$ and no compactly
supported Hamiltonian isotopy carries the zero section to $L$.

statements.title: Waldhausen's tube fibration
statements.label: thm:tube-fibration
statements.text:
For the stable smooth tube space \eqref{eq:stable-tubes} there is a
homotopy fiber sequence
\begin{equation}
 \Hs(*)\longrightarrow\T\xrightarrow{\gamma}BG.
\end{equation}
The rigid tube map $\iota:BO\to\T$, defined by nondegenerate quadratic
forms, satisfies $\gamma\circ\iota\simeq BJ$, where
$BJ:BO\to BG$ is the stable spherical fibration map.

statements.label: prop:one-critical
prop:hcob-injectivity
statements.text:
Let $k,l\geq20$, and put
\[
 Y=S^{k+l-1},\qquad
 \Sigma=\{q_{k,l}=0\}\cap Y\cong S^{k-1}\times S^{l-1}.
\]
For a closed collar embedding $e:\Sigma\times J\hookrightarrow Y$, the
composite
\begin{equation}
 H(\Sigma)\xrightarrow{\sigma}H(\Sigma\times J)
 \xrightarrow{e_!}H(Y)\longrightarrow\Hs(Y)
\end{equation}
induces an isomorphism on $\pi_9$ in the product component. Consequently,
if a sphere family in $H(\Sigma)$ has null image under this composite,
the family is itself null.

statements.label: prop:embedded-realization
statements.text: On $Q=B\times S^{N-1}$ there is a smooth Morse family $F:Q\times\R^N\to\R$ which equals $g_b(w)$ outside a uniform vertical ball and whose generating map is a diffeomorphism from its critical locus onto a closed exact embedded Lagrangian $L\subset T^*Q$. Its critical locus, and hence $L$, is diffeomorphic to $Q$. The infinity class on each slice $B\times\{v_0\}$ is the chosen class $a$.

statements.title: One transport step with controlled infinity data
statements.label: prop:transport-step
statements.text:
Suppose $F_o:U\times\R^r\to\R$ is a smooth Morse family, with
$\Gamma_{F_o}$ a diffeomorphism onto its generated Lagrangian
$\mathcal L_o\subset T^*U$.  Suppose that it is smooth up to
$\overline U$, with uniform bounds on compact vertical sets, and
equals a homogeneous function $g_o(x,w)$ for $\norm{w}\ge R_o$, where
$g_o$ is smooth for $w\ne0$ and
\begin{equation}
 \norm{\nabla_wg_o(x,w)}\ge c_o\norm{w},
 \qquad \norm{d_xg_o(x,w)}\le C_o\norm{w}^2,
 \qquad c_o>0.
 
\end{equation}
For a small step $\psi$ as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:transport-mixed-generator}, there is a smooth Morse
family on $U\times\R^{r+2d}$ generating $\psi(\mathcal L_o)$ with
the same properties.  Its critical locus corresponds
diffeomorphically to $\Crit(F_o)$.  On every fixed compact parameter
slice in $U$, its homogeneous data represent the split quadratic
stabilization of the preceding tube class.

title: A cubic lower bound for border determinantal complexity of the permanent
abstract: We prove that the complex border determinantal complexity of the \(m\times m\) permanent is \(\Omega(m^3)\), allowing arbitrary affine-linear determinant representations and coefficientwise limits. It also gives cubic lower bounds for exact determinantal complexity and for the numbers of vertices and edges in affine-linear algebraic branching programs, including coefficientwise limits with a fixed vertex or edge budget.

tex.abstract:
We prove that the complex border determinantal complexity of the $m\times m$
permanent is $\Omega(m^3)$, allowing arbitrary affine-linear determinant
representations and coefficientwise limits. It also gives cubic lower bounds
for exact determinantal complexity and for the numbers of vertices and edges
in affine-linear algebraic branching programs, including coefficientwise
limits with a fixed vertex or edge budget.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There exist absolute constants $c>0$ and $m_0$ such that, for every integer
$m\ge m_0$,
\[
 \bdc(\per_m)\ge c m^3.
\]
One may take $c=1/(5\,529\,600e)$ and $m_0=1408$.

statements.title: Equivalence of the two border models
statements.label: prop:model-equivalence
statements.text:
For every $n\ge m\ge1$,
\[
 \bdc(\per_m)\le n
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 [P_{n,m}]\in\mathcal D_n.
\]
statements.section_title: Border models and smooth homogeneous forms

statements.title: Lower bound for smooth homogeneous forms
statements.label: thm:smooth-border
statements.text:
Let $G\in\C[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$ be a nonzero homogeneous polynomial of degree
$r\ge2$, where $d\ge2$. If its zero set in $\PP^{d-1}$ is smooth, then
\[
 \bdc(G)\ge \frac{(r-1)(d-1)}{4e}.
\]
statements.section_title: Border models and smooth homogeneous forms

statements.title: Coefficient projection
statements.label: prop:selector
statements.text:
Let $k\ge1$ and $0\le q\le\lfloor k/2\rfloor$ be integers, put $r=k-2q$,
and let $D=\operatorname{diag}(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_k)$ with
$\theta_i\in\C$.  For every integer $m\ge11k-2q$, there is an $m\times m$
matrix $A(X)$ of complex affine-linear forms such that
\begin{equation}
 \per_m(A(X))=a_0G_D(X),
 \qquad a_0=(-2)^{2k}\big((k-q)!\big)^4\ne0.
 
\end{equation}
Its entrywise homogenization $B(X,z)$ is a matrix of homogeneous linear
forms whose permanent is the degree-$m$ homogenization of $a_0G_D$:
\begin{equation}
 \per_m(B(X,z))=a_0z^{m-r}G_D(X).
 
\end{equation}
The construction requires no distinctness or nonvanishing assumption on
the entries of $D$.
statements.section_title: Selecting a coefficient by a permanent projection

statements.label: cor:selector-border
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:selector}, let $d\ge1$ be an
integer and let
$\Lambda:\C^d\to\Mat_k(\C)$ be any fixed affine map.  Then
\[
 \bdc(G_D\circ\Lambda)\le\bdc(\per_m).
\]
In particular, this holds for every fixed linear restriction of $G_D$.
statements.section_title: Selecting a coefficient by a permanent projection

statements.title: Length forced by the gradient
statements.label: prop:adjugate-length
statements.text:
With the parameters in \eqref{eq:adjugate-parameters}, let
\(X\in\Mat_k(K)\) satisfy \(\nabla G_D(X)=0\).
Then its adjugate zero scheme \(Z\) satisfies
\[
 \length Z\ge T=\binom{q+2}{2}.
\]

statements.section_title: The conductor and the normalization defect

statements.title: Gradient codimension
statements.label: prop:gradient-codimension
statements.text:
Let $K=\overline{\mathbb F}_2$, let $k\geq2$, and set
\[
 q=\left\lfloor\frac{k-1}{3}\right\rfloor,
 \qquad T=\binom{q+2}{2}.
\]
For pairwise distinct $\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_k\in K$, put
$D=\operatorname{diag}(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_k)$ and
\[
 G_D(X)=[s^qt^q]\per_k(X+sI+tD),
 \qquad X\in\Mat_k(K).
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \dim\{X\in\Mat_k(K):\nabla G_D(X)=0\}
 \leq k^2+k-T.
 
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: From curve defects to matrix codimension

statements.title: Dimension of a matrix fiber
statements.label: prop:matrix-fiber
statements.text:
For the morphism $f_D$ in \eqref{eq:determinant-curve-map}, every fiber
has dimension at most $N=k(k-1)/2$.
statements.section_title: From curve defects to matrix codimension

statements.title: Smooth linear section
statements.label: prop:smooth-slice
statements.text:
Let \(F\) be a nonzero homogeneous complex polynomial of degree \(r\ge2\)
on a vector space \(V\) of dimension \(v\).  Set
\(Y=V_{\PP(V)}(F)\), and suppose
\[
 \dim\operatorname{Sing}Y\le v-1-\delta
\]
for an integer \(\delta\ge1\).  If \(2\le d<v\) and
\(d-1<\delta\), then a nonempty Zariski open subset of
\(\operatorname{Gr}(d,V)\) consists of subspaces \(H\) for which
\(F|_H\) is nonzero and defines a smooth degree-\(r\) hypersurface
in \(\PP(H)\).
statements.section_title: Characteristic transfer and smooth linear sections

statements.title: A smooth form obtained from the permanent
statements.label: prop:smooth-projection
statements.text:
Let \(k\ge128\) be an integer, and put
\[
 q=\left\lfloor\frac{k-1}{3}\right\rfloor,\qquad
 r=k-2q,\qquad d=\left\lfloor\frac{k^2}{100}\right\rfloor.
\]
There is a nonzero homogeneous polynomial
\(G\in\C[x_1,\ldots,x_d]\) of degree \(r\) such that its zero set in
\(\PP^{d-1}_{\C}\) is smooth and, for every integer \(m\ge11k-2q\),
there is an affine map \(\Phi_m:\C^d\to\Mat_m(\C)\) satisfying
\[
 G=\per_m\circ\Phi_m.
\]
The parameters also satisfy
\[
 r-1\ge\frac{k}{4},\qquad d-1\ge\frac{k^2}{200}.
\]
statements.section_title: Characteristic transfer and smooth linear sections

statements.label: polar:ambient-bound
statements.text:
Let $N,n,\mu\ge1$ and $h\ge0$ be integers. Suppose that
$P\in\C[x_1,\ldots,x_N]$ is a coefficientwise limit of determinants of
$n\times n$ matrices of affine-linear forms. Let
$\Psi:\C^{h+1}\to\C^N$ be an affine map and
$w_1,\ldots,w_h\in\C^N$ constant directions. If
\begin{equation}
 P(\Psi(\xi))=0,\qquad
 (\partial_{w_i}P)(\Psi(\xi))=0\quad(1\le i\le h)
\end{equation}
has at least $\mu$ distinct simple zeros, then
\begin{align}
 \mu&\le [H^{h+1}U^{n-1}V^{n-1}]
            (H+U)^n(H+V)^{n-1}(U+V)^h\\
  &\le 2^h\binom{2n-1}{h+1},\notag\\
 n&\ge\frac{h+1}{4e}\mu^{1/(h+1)}.
\end{align}
The binomial coefficient is zero if $h+1>2n-1$.
statements.section_title: Counting polars of a smooth hypersurface

statements.title: Exact determinantal complexity
statements.label: cor:exact-complexity
statements.text:
For every integer $m\ge1408$,
\[
 \dc(\per_m)\ge \frac{m^3}{5\,529\,600e}.
\]
statements.section_title: The permanent lower bound and its consequences

statements.title: Affine-linear algebraic branching programs
statements.label: cor:abp-complexity
statements.text:
Over $\C$, an algebraic branching program is a finite directed acyclic
graph with distinct designated source $s$ and sink $t$, whose edges carry
affine-linear forms; its output is the sum of the commutative products of
labels along all directed $s$-to-$t$ paths. Such a program computing
$\per_m$ requires $\Omega(m^3)$ vertices and $\Omega(m^3)$ edges, even after
trimming to the vertices and edges on source-to-sink paths. The same
bounds hold if $\per_m$ is a coefficientwise (equivalently, Zariski)
limit of outputs with a fixed vertex budget, respectively a fixed edge
budget, along the approximation.
statements.section_title: The permanent lower bound and its consequences

statements.title: Smooth initial form
statements.label: cor:smooth-initial-form
statements.text:
Let $g\in\C[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$, where $d\ge2$, and let $a\in\C^d$.
Suppose that the lowest nonzero homogeneous term $G_r(x)$ of $g(a+x)$
has degree $r\ge2$ and defines a smooth hypersurface in $\PP^{d-1}$.
Then
\[
 \bdc(g)\ge\frac{(r-1)(d-1)}{4e}.
\]
The same lower bound holds for $\dc(g)$.

title: Three fixed points on the symplectic quadric threefold
abstract: We construct a smooth Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of the complex quadric threefold with exactly three fixed points, at least one of which is degenerate. The critical number and the unit-inclusive rational cup length of this manifold are both four. Thus the example disproves the unrestricted critical-number and rational cup-length forms of the Arnold conjecture.

tex.abstract:
We construct a smooth Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of the complex quadric
threefold with exactly three fixed points, at least one of which is
degenerate. The critical number and the unit-inclusive rational cup length
of this manifold are both four. Thus the example disproves the unrestricted
critical-number and rational cup-length forms of the Arnold conjecture.

statements.label: thm:counterexample
statements.text:
There is a smooth Hamiltonian diffeomorphism $\phi$ of the closed connected
symplectic six-manifold $Q^3$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \#\Fix(\phi)=3<4=\Crit(Q^3)
                  =\operatorname{cuplength}(Q^3;\mathbb Q).
\end{equation}
At least one fixed point of $\phi$ is degenerate.

statements.label: prop:reduction
statements.text:
Let \((M,\omega)\) be a closed symplectic manifold, and let
\(A\in\Ham(M,\omega)\) satisfy \(A^m=\id\) for some positive integer
\(m\). Suppose that \(F=\Fix(A)\) is a closed embedded submanifold and
that
\[
  T_qF=\ker(dA_q-\id)
  \qquad\text{for every }q\in F.
\]
For every smooth function \(f:F\to\R\), there is a smooth
\(A\)-invariant extension \(K:M\to\R\) such that, if \(B_s\) is its
Hamiltonian flow, then for every sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\)
the map
\[
  \phi_\varepsilon=A\circ B_\varepsilon
\]
is Hamiltonian and satisfies
\[
  \Fix(\phi_\varepsilon)=\CritSet(f),
\]
where the critical set on the right is viewed as a subset of \(M\).

statements.label: prop:quadric
statements.text:
The manifold $M$ is closed, connected, and of real dimension six. For
the restricted Fubini--Study form $\omega$, normalized below, the map
\[
 A[z_0:z_1:z_2:z_3:z_4]
   =[z_0:-z_1:-z_2:-z_3:-z_4]
\]
is a Hamiltonian involution.  Its fixed set is the smooth submanifold
\[
 F=M\cap\{z_0=0\}\cong S^2\times S^2.
\]
For every $q\in F$, the differential $dA_q$ acts as $+\id$ on $T_qF$
and as $-\id$ on a complementary real two-dimensional subspace of
$T_qM$.

title: A density-uniform condensate bound for dilute Bose gases
abstract: For each fixed bounded measurable, nonnegative, radial interaction of finite range in three dimensions that is not zero almost everywhere, we prove a positive lower bound on the constant-orbital condensate fraction that is uniform over all sufficiently small densities and all temperatures between zero and the square of the density. The interaction and density remain fixed in the thermodynamic limit.

tex.abstract:
For each fixed bounded measurable, nonnegative, radial interaction of finite
range in three dimensions that is not zero almost everywhere, we prove
a positive lower bound on the constant-orbital
condensate fraction that is uniform over all sufficiently small densities
and all temperatures between zero and the square of the density.
The interaction and density remain fixed in the thermodynamic limit.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every potential $v$ as above there are constants
$\rho_*(v)>0$ and $c_*(v)>0$ with the following property.
For every $0<\rho<\rho_*(v)$ there is $L_0(\rho,v)<\infty$ such that,
for every $L\ge L_0(\rho,v)$, every integer $N\ge1$ satisfying
$\rho/2\le N/L^3\le2\rho$, and every $0\le T\le\rho^2$,
\[
 \frac{\langle u_0,\gamma^{(1)}_{N,L,T}u_0\rangle}{N}
 \ge c_*(v).
\]
Consequently, for each such fixed density $\rho$ and fixed
$0\le T\le\rho^2$, every sequence with $L\to\infty$ and
$N/L^3\to\rho$ has lower limiting condensate fraction at least $c_*(v)$.

statements.label: prop:atypical-moment
statements.text:
Fix $K$ as in the cell construction.  There exist $D_{\min}$, $C_v$, and
$\kappa>0$, depending on the fixed potential and on $K$, such that the
following holds.  Fix $D\ge D_{\min}$ and $0<\zeta\le1$.  For sufficiently
small $\rho>0$ and sufficiently large volume at that density, uniformly
for $\rho/2\le N/V\le2\rho$ and $0<T\le\rho^2$, every nonempty coarse
cell union $U$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \log\mathbb E_{\mathrm{cl}}\exp(J_U^{\mathrm{fail}})
 \le
 \left[C_v\sum_{j\ge0}D_j^3e^{-\kappa D_j^2}
       +o_\rho(1)\right]\rho|U|,
 \qquad D_j=2^jD.
 \tag{17}
\end{equation}
The constants $C_v,\kappa$ do not depend on $D$ or $\zeta$.  The term
$o_\rho(1)$ is at fixed $v,K,D,\zeta$ and is uniform in the stated
particle numbers, volumes, and temperatures.

Choose $D$ and $\varepsilon$ so that
$C_v\sum_{j\geq0}D_j^3e^{-\kappa D_j^2}
\leq10^{-4}b_-\varepsilon$ in (17). Then choose $\zeta>0$
sufficiently small in terms of these fixed constants, followed
by $C_0>\Delta_A$ sufficiently large. For small enough density,
there is $q_{\mathrm{cl}}=q_{\mathrm{cl}}(\rho)\to0$ as
$\rho\downarrow0$ such that every collection $\mathcal U$
of specified cells satisfies
\begin{equation}
 P_{\mathrm{cl}}(\text{every cell of }\mathcal U
                         \text{ is defective})
 \leq q_{\mathrm{cl}}^{|\mathcal U|}.
 \tag{22}
\end{equation}
The bound and the convergence of $q_{\mathrm{cl}}$ are uniform
in the allowed temperatures and sufficiently large volumes.
Increasing $C_0$ preserves the statement.

title: A dimension-free logarithmic Sobolev inequality for subgaussian log-concave measures
abstract: We prove that every centered log-concave probability measure with a Lebesgue density on ℝn and linear subgaussian parameter a satisfies \(\mathop{\mathrm{Ent}}\nolimits _\mu(f^2)\le Ca^2\int|Df|^2\,d\mu\) for compactly supported smooth f, with one universal constant C. This resolves positively the dimension-free logarithmic Sobolev conjecture for subgaussian log-concave measures.

tex.abstract:
We prove that every centered log-concave probability measure with a
Lebesgue density on $\mathbb R^n$ and linear subgaussian parameter $a$
satisfies $\operatorname{Ent}_\mu(f^2)\le Ca^2\int|Df|^2\,d\mu$
for compactly supported smooth $f$, with one universal constant $C$.
This resolves positively the dimension-free logarithmic Sobolev conjecture
for subgaussian log-concave measures.
sections: Efficient probes and the prediction curve
A symmetric hierarchy of nearly first eigenfunctions
The reduced square root and a frozen matrix algebra

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is an absolute constant \(C<\infty\) with the following property.
For every \(n\ge1\), every centered log-concave probability measure
\(\mu\) with a Lebesgue density on \(\R^n\), and every \(a>0\)
satisfying \eqref{eq:intro-subgaussian} for \(X\sim\mu\),
\[
 \Ent_\mu(f^2)\le C a^2\int_{\R^n}|Df|^2\,d\mu
 \qquad\text{for every }f\in C_c^\infty(\R^n).
\]
The same constant works in every dimension.

statements.title: Quadratic transport--entropy inequality
statements.label: cor:intro-transport
statements.text:
Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, every
$\nu\in\mathcal P_2(\R^n)$ satisfies
\[
 W_2(\nu,\mu)^2\le Ca^2 H(\nu\mid\mu),
\]
with the same absolute constant $C$ as in that theorem.

statements.title: The critical sequence
statements.label: prop:critical-sequence
statements.text:
If Theorem~\ref{thm:main} fails, there is a sequence of dimensions
and centered compactly supported log-concave laws $\mu$ satisfying
Equation~\eqref{eq:critical-normalization}. Fix $s=1/8$, form
$\mu_s,b_s,M_s,K_s$ as in Equation~\eqref{eq:critical-posterior},
and put $\lambda=R_s^{-1}$. After passage to a subsequence there
are smooth positive probabilities $\eta$ and smooth vector fields
$w$ such that, with $A=A_\eta$ and $I=\E_\eta|w|^2$,
\begin{gather}
 \lambda\longrightarrow1,\qquad R(\eta)\le\lambda^{-1},
 \qquad 0<I<\infty,\qquad w\in\Dom(A)^n,
 \\
 A w=(\lambda\Id-K_s)w,\qquad
 \|(A-1)w\|_{L^2(\eta)}+|\E_\eta w|=o(\sqrt I),
 \\
 \E_\eta|K_sw|^2=o(I),\qquad
 \E_\eta|Dw|^2=(1+o(1))I.
 
\end{gather}
The spectral gap of $A$ is at least $\lambda$. Each coordinate
function belongs to $\Dom(A)$. Exactly one of the following
constructions can be used throughout the subsequence:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $R_s>R_s^P$, $\eta=f^2\mu_s$ for the positive unit-norm
optimizer, $w=D\log f^2$, and
$I=2\lambda H(\eta\mid\mu_s)$. The exact deficit identity in
Equation~\eqref{eq:critical-exact-deficit} holds for compact square-root
tests relative to $\eta$, and
$A Y=(Y-b_s)/s-w$.
\item $R_s=R_s^P$, $\eta=\mu_s$,
$A\varphi=\lambda\varphi$, $\E_\eta\varphi=0$,
$w=D\varphi$, and $I=\lambda\E_\eta\varphi^2$.
One may rescale $\varphi$ so that $I\to0$.
\end{enumerate}
All $o$-terms refer to the counterexample sequence with fixed
finite parameters. In particular no relation between dimension,
$I$, and the rate of convergence is asserted or needed here.

statements.title: Symmetric tensor hierarchy
statements.label: prop:hierarchy
statements.text:
Consider a sequence of smooth positive probability densities $\eta$ on
finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces, with finite second moments.  Let
$A=-\Delta-D\log\eta\cdot D$, and suppose that $\eta$ satisfies Poincar\'e
with constant at most $\lambda^{-1}$, where $\lambda\to1$.  Fix $s=1/8$.
Suppose smooth vector fields $b,w$ and a symmetric matrix field $K$ satisfy
\[
 D\log\eta=-\frac{y-b(y)}s+\omega(y),\qquad
 Db=\Id-sK,\qquad 0\le K\le s^{-1}\Id,
\]
where either $\omega=w$ throughout the sequence or $\omega=0$ throughout
the sequence.  Assume $b,w\in L^2(\eta)$, $w$ is a gradient, and, with
$I=\|w\|_2^2>0$,
\begin{equation}
 w\in\Dom A,\qquad
 \|(A-1)w\|_2=o(\sqrt I),\qquad
 |\E_\eta w|=o(\sqrt I),\qquad
 \langle w,Kw\rangle_2=o(I).
\end{equation}
Assume also the following prediction and projection properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item For $Y\sim\eta$ and an independent standard Gaussian $G$, set
\[
 U_r=Y+\sqrt r\,G,\quad h_r(u)=\E[w(Y)\mid U_r=u],\quad
 m(r)=I^{-1}\E|h_r(U_r)|^2.
\]
For every fixed $0<r<1/4$, one has $m(r)\to e^{-r}$.
\item For every fixed $c<\infty$,
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{\substack{\Pi^2=\Pi=\Pi^*\ \mathrm{deterministic}\\
                   \rank\Pi\le cI}}
       \|\Pi w\|_2^2=o(I).
\end{equation}
For every $\epsilon>0$ there is a deterministic projection $\Pi_\epsilon$
of rank at most $C_\epsilon I$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \left\|\E[(1-\Pi_\epsilon)bb^*(1-\Pi_\epsilon)]\right\|_{\op}
 +\left\|\E[(1-\Pi_\epsilon)\omega\omega^*
                  (1-\Pi_\epsilon)]\right\|_{\op}\le\epsilon
\end{equation}
eventually along the sequence.
\item If $\omega=w$, the conditional covariance
$C_r=\Cov(w(Y)\mid U_r)$ satisfies, for every fixed $r\in(0,1/4)$ and
$a>0$,
\begin{equation}
 \E\tr\bigl(C_r\1_{\{C_r>a\}}\bigr)=o(I).
\end{equation}
No conditional covariance-tail assumption is made when $\omega=0$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there are totally symmetric tensor fields $T_l$ of order $l+1$, for
every fixed integer $l\ge0$, with $T_0=w$, such that
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
 \|T_l\|_2^2=(1+o(1))I,\qquad
 \|(A-1)T_l\|_2=o(\sqrt I),\\
 \|DT_l-T_{l+1}\|_2=o(\sqrt I).
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \langle T_l,K_1T_l\rangle_2=o(I).
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{\substack{\Pi^2=\Pi=\Pi^*\ \mathrm{deterministic}\\
                   \rank\Pi\le cI}}
      \|\Pi_1T_l\|_2^2=o(I)
 \qquad\text{for every fixed }c<\infty.
\end{equation}
Every $T_l$ belongs componentwise to $\Dom A$.  For $l\ge1$ it can be
chosen in $\bigcap_{p\ge1}\Dom A^p$.  By symmetry, the specified slot in
Equations~\eqref{eq:hierarchy-curvature} and
\eqref{eq:hierarchy-projection} may be any slot.  All assertions can be
made simultaneous for any fixed finite collection of levels and parameters.

statements.title: Frozen diffusion law
statements.label: prop:frozen-law
statements.text:
Let $Y_u$ be the stationary diffusion with invariant law $\eta$ and driving
Brownian motion $B_u$, and fix $t>0$.  Make the matrix construction of
Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-blocks} at $Y_0$, using an independent random block
offset.  In its orthonormal frame put $N=B_t/\sqrt t$; conditionally on the
initial data and block offset, $N$ is a standard Gaussian vector.  Define,
in the initial spatial coordinates,
\begin{equation}
 \sigma=\bigoplus_\beta\beta^2
       \exp\bigl(\sqrt{8t}\,H[N]-4t\Id_\beta\bigr),
\end{equation}
and set $\sigma=0$ on the omitted kernel.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \E\|R(Y_t)-\sigma^{1/2}\|_{\HS}^2\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
The matrices defining $\sigma$ obey the bounded-column and input-map
bounds \eqref{eq:matrix-column-bound} and \eqref{eq:flattening-bound},
the weighted defects \eqref{eq:matrix-tracial-defects}, and the mixed
moment law of Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-gaussian-moments}.

We give a direct proof of the sharp constant-two numerical-range inequality
for matrix-valued polynomials in all finite base and coefficient dimensions.
This resolves the complete Crouzeix conjecture in its matrix formulation,
including matrices whose numerical ranges are points or line segments.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every pair of positive integers $n,m$, every $A\in M_n(\C)$,
every nonnegative integer $d$, and every polynomial
$P(z)=\sum_{k=0}^d B_kz^k$ with $B_k\in M_m(\C)$,
\begin{equation}
 \|P[A]\|\le2\max_{z\in W(A)}\|P(z)\|.
\end{equation}
The constant two cannot be decreased uniformly over $n,m$, and $d$.

statements.title: The resolvent expansion and double-layer positivity
statements.label: lem:resolvent
statements.text:
Let $\Omega,h,q$, and $(b_k)$ satisfy the hypotheses and conclusions of Theorem~\ref{lem:faber}. For any positive integer $n$ and $A\in M_n(\C)$ with $W(A)\subset\Omega$, on $\T$ let
\begin{equation}
 R(\lambda)=q(\lambda)(h(\lambda)I-A)^{-1}.
\end{equation}
Then
\[
 R(\lambda)=\sum_{k\ge0}b_k(A)\lambda^{-k},\qquad R(\lambda)+R(\lambda)^*\succeq0.
\]
For the fixed $A,h$, there are constants $C<\infty$ and $0<\theta<1$
such that $\|b_k(A)\|\le C\theta^k$ for all $k\ge0$. Thus the series
converges absolutely and uniformly on $\T$. In particular,
$\int_\T R\,d\tau=I$ and $\int_\T(R+R^*)\,d\tau=2I$.

title: A directional zero–one law for finite-range-dependent random environments
abstract: We prove a directional zero–one law for uniformly elliptic nearest-neighbor random walks in stationary, ergodic, finite-range-dependent environments on ℤd, d ≥ 3. For every fixed nonzero real direction, the probability of escape in that direction, averaged over the environment, is either zero or one. Finite-range dependence is imposed on the full transition rows: collections of rows at distance greater than a fixed range are independent, including collections indexed by infinite deterministic sets.

tex.abstract:
We prove a directional zero--one law for uniformly elliptic nearest-neighbor
random walks in stationary, ergodic, finite-range-dependent environments on
$\ZZ^d$, $d\ge3$. For every fixed nonzero real direction, the probability
of escape in that direction, averaged over the environment, is either zero
or one. Finite-range dependence is imposed on the full transition rows:
collections of rows at distance greater than a fixed range are independent,
including collections indexed by infinite deterministic sets.

statements.title: Directional zero--one law
statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Under assumptions \textup{(i)--(iii)}, for every fixed
$\ell\in\RR^d\setminus\{0\}$,
\[
 P_0(A_\ell)\in\{0,1\}.
\]

statements.title: Regeneration law
statements.label: prop:cut-law
statements.text:
Fix a normalized real direction \(v\) and suppose \(p_v>0\).
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=*]
 \item Under the raw law \(P_0\), on
       \(\{\sup_n h(X_n)=\infty\}\) there is a cut almost surely.
 \item Under \(\widehat P_v\), there are infinitely many cuts.  With
       time zero counted as an initial boundary, the relative marked
       words between successive boundaries are independent and
       identically distributed.  Their common law \(\nu_v\) assigns
       mass
       \begin{equation}
        \nu_v(\{\gamma\})=W(\gamma)
       \end{equation}
       to each regeneration word \(\gamma\).  These finite words
       concatenate to the entire conditioned walk.
 \item Under the raw law, conditional on any realized prefix through
       the first cut, the translated suffix has law
       \(\widehat P_v\).  This assertion is restricted to the event
       that a cut exists.
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Directional sign union
statements.label: prop:sign-union
statements.text:
For every fixed \(v\ne0\),
\begin{equation}
 P_0(A_v)>0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 p_v>0\ \text{ and }\ P_0(A_v\cup A_{-v})=1.
\end{equation}
More precisely, when \(p_v>0\), infinite height supremum implies
\(A_v\) almost surely, and finite height supremum implies \(A_{-v}\)
almost surely.

statements.title: Reduction to a coordinate direction
statements.label: prop:coordinate-reduction
statements.text:
If $0<P_0(A_v)<1$ for some fixed nonzero real direction $v$, then there
is a coordinate $i\in\{1,\ldots,d\}$ such that
\[
  P_0(A_{e_i})>0\qquad\text{and}\qquad P_0(A_{-e_i})>0.
\]

statements.title: Exact-cut bridges
statements.label: prop:exact-cut-bridges
statements.text:
The renewal masses satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \bar u_0^\sigma=1,\qquad
 \bar u_j^\sigma=0\quad(1\le j<M),\qquad
 \bar u_H^\sigma=\xi u_{H-M}^\sigma\quad(H\ge M).
 
\end{equation}
For a list of slabs $(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_m)$ with total width $H$, its
mass under $\mathcal B_H^\sigma$ is
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal B_H^\sigma(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_m)
   =\frac{\prod_{i=1}^m W(\gamma_i)}{\bar u_H^\sigma}.
 
\end{equation}
In particular, reversing the list order preserves this law; the steps
within each word retain their original order.

For $H\ge M$, concatenating the list gives the raw marked path through its
first hit of $H$, conditioned on $\mathcal D_H^\sigma$. Each such path has
a unique parsing into slabs. Concatenating any prescribed slab words, or
successive bridges of prescribed widths, gives a raw path weight equal to
the product of the constituent raw weights.

statements.title: Common blocks
statements.label: prop:common-blocks
statements.text:
The common blocks exist indefinitely, and their pairs of slab lists are
iid. Their widths $K_i$ have a common law satisfying
\[
                  M\le K_i<\infty\quad\text{a.s.},
             \qquad \mu:=\mathbf E K_i<\infty.
\]
The expected sum of the radii of all slabs on both sides of one common
block is finite. In particular, if
\begin{equation}
 W'_0=0,\qquad W'_i=\sum_{j=1}^iK_j,
 
\end{equation}
then $W'_i/i\to\mu$ almost surely.

statements.title: First contact above a scripted prefix
statements.label: prop:first-contact
statements.text:
Assume \(p_+p_->0\), and let \(M\le k<r<N\) be integers with
\(r-k\ge R\).  Start a positive bridge \(Y\) with law
\(\mathcal B_N^+\) at the origin, and put
\(E_{\mathrm{lat}}=\pi Y_{T_N}\).
Independently of \(Y\), sample a relative marked path with law
\(\widehat P_-\), and translate it to start at
\((N-1,E_{\mathrm{lat}})\); denote the resulting path by \(\beta\).
Define
\[
 \tau=\inf\{i:T_k(Y)\le i<T_N(Y),\quad
       \|Y_i-\beta_j\|_\infty\le R\text{ for some }j\ge0\},
\]
with \(\inf\varnothing=\infty\).  Let
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal C_{k,r,N}=
 \left\{
 \begin{gathered}
  \mathcal D_k^+(Y),\quad \tau<T_N(Y),\quad (Y_\tau)_1\ge r,\\
  \min_{T_k(Y)\le i\le\tau}(Y_i)_1\ge k,
  \quad |E_{\mathrm{lat}}|\le N^2
 \end{gathered}
 \right\}.
\end{equation}
Here \(\mathcal D_k^+(Y)\) is a condition on the prefix through the
first hit of \(k\).  There is a constant \(C\), independent of
\(k,r,N\), such that, with
\(\Delta=u_{r-k}^+-u_{N-k}^+\),
\begin{equation}
 P(\mathcal C_{k,r,N})
 \le C\log(2N)\,\Delta\log^2(\mathrm e/\Delta).
\end{equation}
The right-hand side is defined to be zero when \(\Delta=0\).

statements.title: Contact lower bound
statements.label: prop:contact-lower
statements.text:
Suppose that $P_0(A_{e_1})>0$ and $P_0(A_{-e_1})>0$, and let $m(J)$ be the
contact statistic of the opposed tapes defined in \eqref{eq:contact-count}.
There are constants $c>0$ and an integer $c_1\ge0$ such that, for all sufficiently
large integers $J$,
\begin{equation}
 m(J+c_1)\ge \frac{cJ}{1+\log\log J}.
\end{equation}

title: A directional zero–one law under strict ellipticity
abstract: We prove the directional zero–one conjecture for nearest-neighbor random walks in independent and identically distributed strictly elliptic environments on ℤd, d ≥ 3: the probability of escape in each fixed nonzero real direction is zero or one. Only strict positivity of the transition probabilities is required; no uniform lower bound or moment assumption is imposed.

tex.abstract:
We prove the directional zero--one conjecture for nearest-neighbor random
walks in independent and identically distributed strictly elliptic environments
on $\ZZ^d$, $d\ge3$: the probability of escape in each fixed nonzero real
direction is zero or one. Only strict positivity of the transition probabilities
is required; no uniform lower bound or moment assumption is imposed.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $d\ge3$, let $\PP$ be an independent and identically distributed
law of nearest-neighbor transition rows on $\ZZ^d$ satisfying
\eqref{eq:ellipticity}, and let $\ell\in\RR^d\setminus\{0\}$.
Then
\[
 P_0(A_\ell)\in\{0,1\}.
\]

statements.title: Spatial radius under coexistence
statements.label: prop:radius
statements.text:
Let the environment consist of iid strictly positive transition rows,
and let
\(v\in\RR^d\setminus\{0\}\).  Suppose
\(P_0(A_v)>0\) and \(P_0(A_{-v})>0\).  For each sign
\(\sigma\in\{+,-\}\), let \(\nu_{\sigma v}\) be the slab law from
Lemma~\ref{lem:slabs}.  If \(R\) is the maximum Euclidean distance from
a slab's initial site, including its terminal site, then
\[
 \int R\,d\nu_v+\int R\,d\nu_{-v}<\infty.
\]

 P_0(A_{e_i})>0\qquad\text{and}\qquad P_0(A_{-e_i})>0.

statements.text:
Suppose that both coordinate signs have positive directional-transience
probability. In the opposed arrangement of Section~\ref{sec:arrangement},

$(2^j,2^{j+1}]$, $1\le j\le J$, containing a departure-site contact,

\[
 m(J)=O\!\left(\frac{J}{\log J}\right)\qquad(J\longrightarrow\infty).

 P\left(T_r\le\tau<T_N,\

title: A doubling Hilbert subset with no finite-dimensional bi-Lipschitz embedding
abstract: Every infinite-dimensional real Banach space contains a compact doubling subset that admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any finite-dimensional real normed space. The doubling constant has a universal bound, independent of the ambient Banach space. This answers the Lang–Plaut problem negatively, even for compact subsets of Hilbert space.

tex.abstract: Every infinite-dimensional real Banach space contains a compact doubling subset that admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any finite-dimensional real normed space. The doubling constant has a universal bound, independent of the ambient Banach space. This answers the Lang--Plaut problem negatively, even for compact subsets of Hilbert space.

statements.title: Finite-$p$ function-space obstruction
statements.label: cor:lp
statements.text: For every real $1\le p<\infty$, the fixed metric space $S$ of Theorem~\ref{thm:main} is isometric to a subset $S_p$ of $L_p([0,1];\R)$, where $[0,1]$ carries Lebesgue measure. With its induced $L_p$ metric, $S_p$ has doubling constant at most $76800$ and admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any finite-dimensional real normed space at any finite distortion.

statements.title: Compact Banach-space obstruction
statements.label: cor:banach
statements.text: There is a universal constant $\Lambda$ such that every infinite-dimensional real Banach space $B$ contains a compact subset $K_B$ whose doubling constant is at most $\Lambda$ and which admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any finite-dimensional real normed space at any finite distortion. The subset $K_B$ may depend on $B$, but is chosen independently of the target dimension and distortion.

title: A finite Smith–Toda complex V(4) at the prime 1009
abstract: We construct a Smith–Toda complex \(V(4)\) at the prime 1009. It is an ordinary finite 1009-local spectrum whose Brown–Peterson homology is \(BP_*/(1009,v_1,v_2,v_3,v_4)\), with its canonical comodule structure and generator in degree zero.

tex.abstract:
We construct a Smith--Toda complex $V(4)$ at the prime $1009$. It is an
ordinary finite $1009$-local spectrum whose Brown--Peterson homology is
$BP_*/(1009,v_1,v_2,v_3,v_4)$, with its canonical comodule structure and
generator in degree zero.

statements.label: intro:main
statements.text:
At $p=1009$ there is a finite $p$-local spectrum $X$ and an isomorphism
\[
 BP_*X\ \cong\ BP_*/(p,v_1,v_2,v_3,v_4)
\]
of graded $BP_*BP$-comodules, with the canonical quotient comodule on the
right and its generator in degree zero.

statements.label: fw:anss
statements.text:
For every bounded-below $p$-local spectrum $Z$, the sphere-source
Adams--Novikov spectral sequence has
\[
 E_2^{s,t}(Z)=H^{s,t}\bigl(C^\bullet_\Gamma(BP_*Z)\bigr)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \pi_{t-s}Z.
\]
It converges strongly, and the induced filtration in each stem is finite.
The differential $d_r$ changes $(s,t)$ by $(r,r-1)$.  The filtration-zero
edge identifies $E_\infty^{0,*}$ with the image of the $BP$-Hurewicz map
$\pi_*Z\longrightarrow BP_*Z$.
statements.section_title: Brown--Peterson coordinates and the Adams--Novikov resolution

statements.title: Binary pairings of the resolution
statements.label: fw:anss-pairing
statements.text:
For bounded-below $p$-local spectra $Z_1,Z_2,Z_3$, an actual map
$f:Z_1\wedge Z_2\to Z_3$ induces pairings of the
Adams--Novikov spectral sequences, with the Leibniz rule on every page.
The $E_2$ pairing is the cobar cup pairing induced by the exterior
$BP$-homology pairing, and the $E_\infty$ pairing is the associated-graded
pairing of the actual homotopy map $f$.  No associativity of $f$ is needed.
If $Z_1=Z_2=Z_3=Z$ has a binary two-sided unital multiplication and
$BP_*Z=R/I$ is cyclic on its unit, the $E_2$ pairing is the ordinary
multiplication on cobar cohomology with quotient-ring coefficients.
statements.section_title: Brown--Peterson coordinates and the Adams--Novikov resolution

statements.title: Sparsity
statements.label: fw:sparsity
statements.text:
If $BP_*Z$ is concentrated in internal degrees divisible by $q$, then all
pages of its Adams--Novikov spectral sequence have that same internal
sparsity.  Every possibly nonzero positive differential has length
$r=qk+1$ for an integer $k\geq1$.  In weight notation it changes
$(s,w)$ to $(s+qk+1,w+k)$.  In particular, a primitive coefficient of
weight $u_n$ in filtration zero can have only targets
\begin{equation}
 (s,w)=(qk+1,u_n+k),\qquad k\geq1.
 
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Brown--Peterson coordinates and the Adams--Novikov resolution

statements.title: Construction through $V(3)$
statements.label: low:V3
statements.text:
For $0\leq n\leq3$ there is a finite $p$-local cell spectrum $V(n)$ with
a bottom-cell unit $\eta_n:S_{(p)}\to V(n)$ and a binary multiplication
\[
 \mu_n:V(n)\wedge V(n)\longrightarrow V(n)
\]
whose two unit identities hold.  Its cells are indexed by subsets of
$\{0,\ldots,n\}$, in dimensions
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{i\in S}(qu_i+1),
 
\end{equation}
and its $BP$-homology is the canonical quotient comodule $R/I_{n+1}$,
generated in degree zero by the bottom unit.  In particular, we may fix
\begin{equation}
 Y=V(3),\qquad BP_*Y=R/I_4,
 
\end{equation}
with such a binary two-sided unital multiplication.
statements.section_title: The unital complexes through height three

statements.title: The action of $p$ on $Y$
statements.label: low:p-null
statements.text:
For the spectrum $Y$ of Proposition~\ref{low:V3}, $\pi_0Y=\mathbb F_p$ and
$p\operatorname{id}_Y$ is nullhomotopic.
statements.section_title: The unital complexes through height three

statements.title: An injective multiplication
statements.label: may:injectivity
statements.text:
Multiplication by the primitive class $h_{1,4}$ is injective on actual
cobar cohomology in bidegree $(q+1,u_4+1)$:
\[
 H^{q+1,u_4+1}(P)\xrightarrow{\ h_{1,4}\ }
 H^{q+2,u_5+1}(P).
\]

statements.title: The first Adams--Novikov differential
statements.label: may:first-differential
statements.text:
In the Adams--Novikov spectral sequence for $Y$, one has
$d_{q+1}(v_4)=0$.

statements.title: All later obstruction candidates
statements.label: may:remaining-list
statements.text:
For $k\geq2$ the complete initial May page in
\eqref{may:obstruction-degrees} is Table~\ref{may:remaining-table}; all
other values of $k$ give an empty page.  Put
$N_0=(p-1)^2$ and $N=p(p-1)-2$.
\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering
\begin{tabular}{c l}
\toprule
$k$ & Initial May monomials\\
\midrule
$2$ & $xac B A^{p-2}C^{p-2}$,
       $\quad xacyz A^{p-2}C^{p-2}$\\[2pt]
$p-1$ & $y B^3 A^{N_0-3}$,
         $\quad b B^2 A^{N_0-2}$,
         $\quad ybz B A^{N_0-2}$\\[2pt]
$p$ & $cyb A^{N+1}$,
       $\quad ayb B A^N$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Every initial May monomial for the later $v_4$ obstruction
bidegrees.}

\end{table}

statements.title: The row $k=2$
statements.label: frob:k2
statements.text:
At $s=4p-3$ and $w=u_4+2$, the cobar cohomology group in
Table~\ref{may:remaining-table} is zero.
statements.section_title: Eliminating two obstruction degrees by Frobenius

statements.title: The row $k=p-1$
statements.label: frob:kpminus1
statements.text:
Put $N_0=(p-1)^2$.  At $s=2N_0+1$ and
$w=u_4+p-1$, the cobar cohomology group in
Table~\ref{may:remaining-table} is zero.
statements.section_title: Eliminating two obstruction degrees by Frobenius

statements.label: frob:vanishing
statements.text:
The obstruction groups in bidegrees
\[
 (s,w)=(2q+1,u_4+2),\qquad
 (s,w)=(q(p-1)+1,u_4+p-1)
\]
vanish in the additive cobar calculation of
Table~\ref{may:remaining-table}.  Among its rows with $k\geq2$,
only the row $k=p$ remains to be addressed.
statements.section_title: Eliminating two obstruction degrees by Frobenius

statements.title: The extended-power relation
statements.label: top:extended-power-relation
statements.text: The image of $\alpha\beta^p$ in $\pi_*Y$ is zero.
statements.section_title: The final obstruction and the finite cofiber

statements.title: The symmetric null map
statements.label: top:symmetric-null-map
statements.text:
For $d=|\beta|=pq-2$, the actual stable map
\begin{equation}

 f:\Sigma^dT\xrightarrow{\ \Sigma^d\varepsilon_T\ }S^d
       \xrightarrow{\ \beta\ }S^0
       \xrightarrow{\ \eta\ }Y
\end{equation}
is nullhomotopic.

statements.title: Averaging and annihilation
statements.label: top:annihilation
statements.section_title: The final obstruction and the finite cofiber

statements.title: Disappearance before the last differential
statements.label: top:early-disappearance
statements.text:
Every class in $E_2^{qp+1,u_4+p}(Y)$ is zero on the
Adams--Novikov page $E_{qp+1}$.

title: A finite-entropy separation of microstates and nonmicrostates free entropy
abstract: We answer the finite-entropy equality question for microstates and nonmicrostates free entropy negatively. We construct a bounded self-adjoint tuple X in a von Neumann algebra with faithful normal tracial state such that \(-\infty\lt \chi(X)\leq\chi^*(X)-\tfrac12\lt \infty\). Here χ is the original microstates entropy with an operator-norm cutoff and a limsup over matrix sizes. The counterexample uses a large but fixed number of variables.

tex.abstract:
We answer the finite-entropy equality question for microstates and
nonmicrostates free entropy negatively. We construct a bounded self-adjoint
tuple $X$ in a von Neumann algebra with faithful normal tracial state such that
$-\infty<\chi(X)\leq\chi^*(X)-\tfrac12<\infty$.
Here $\chi$ is the original microstates entropy with an operator-norm
cutoff and a limsup over matrix sizes. The counterexample uses a large but
fixed number of variables.
sections: A cumulant bound for the Fisher deficit
The signal and its two noise scales
Entropy production for specified matrix ensembles

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There exist an integer $n\geq2$ and a bounded self-adjoint tuple
$X=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ in a von Neumann algebra with faithful normal
tracial state such that
\[
 -\infty<\chi(X)\leq\chi^*(X)-\tfrac12<\infty.
\]
Here $\chi$ is the original microstates entropy using an operator-norm
cutoff and a limsup over matrix sizes.

statements.title: Squared-cumulant Fisher bound
statements.label: prop:fisher
statements.text:
Let $C$ be a centered bounded self-adjoint $n$-tuple with diagonal
covariance $\tau(C_iC_j)=\delta_{ij}c_i$, where $c_i\geq0$, and let $S$ be a standard
semicircular family free from $C$. Put $V_u=C+\sqrt u S$ and
$v_i(u)=u+c_i$ for $u>0$. For every $u>0$,
\[
 \sum_i\frac1{v_i(u)}\leq\Phi^*(V_u)\leq\frac n u.
\]
Whenever
$\sum_{r\geq2}u^{-r}\|\kappa_{r+1}(C)\|_2^2<\infty$,
\begin{equation}
 0\leq\Phi^*(V_u)-\sum_i\frac1{v_i(u)}
 \leq\frac1{u^2}\sum_{r\geq2}u^{-r}\|\kappa_{r+1}(C)\|_2^2.
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: A cumulant bound for the Fisher deficit

title: A zero-entropy system without a smooth positive-volume model
abstract: We construct an ergodic invertible transformation of a standard nonatomic probability space with zero Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy that has no smooth positive-volume model. More precisely, it is not measurably conjugate to any C∞ diffeomorphism preserving a strictly positive smooth probability density on a compact finite-dimensional manifold. A single example excludes every finite dimension, including models on nonorientable manifolds and manifolds with smooth boundary.

tex.abstract:
We construct an ergodic invertible transformation of a standard nonatomic
probability space with zero Kolmogorov--Sinai entropy that has no smooth
positive-volume model. More precisely, it is not measurably conjugate to any
$C^\infty$ diffeomorphism preserving a strictly positive smooth probability
density on a compact finite-dimensional manifold. A single example excludes
every finite dimension, including models on nonorientable manifolds and
manifolds with smooth boundary.
sections: Linear estimates on finite orbit segments
Switching a past and a future with controlled volume
Words with prescribed relations and recognizable boundaries
An invariant process and its window laws
The obstruction to a smooth volume model

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There exists an ergodic invertible measure-preserving transformation
$(X,\mu,T)$ of a standard nonatomic probability space such that
$h_\mu(T)=0$ and $(X,\mu,T)$ is not measurably conjugate, on invariant conull sets, to
any $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism of a compact finite-dimensional manifold
preserving a strictly positive smooth probability density. The manifold
may have smooth boundary and need not be orientable.

statements.title: Good finite orbit segments
statements.label: prop:good-frames
statements.text:
For each $\eta>0$ there is a positive sequence $(b_k)_{k\geq1}$ with
\begin{equation}
 b_k\geq 2^{-k/10},
 \qquad
 \sum_{k\geq1}b_k^2<\infty,
\end{equation}
and compact sets $\widetilde{\mathcal G}_k\subset\mathcal F M$ and
$\mathcal G_k=\pi(\widetilde{\mathcal G}_k)\subset M$ such that
\[
 \widetilde\nu(\widetilde{\mathcal G}_k)\geq1-\eta/100,
 \qquad \nu(\mathcal G_k)\geq1-\eta/100.
\]
For $n=2^k$, $b=b_k$, and $e\in\widetilde{\mathcal G}_k$, define
\[
 A_t=R(\widetilde S^t e)\quad(-n\leq t<n),
 \qquad
 \lambda_j=\frac1{2n}\sum_{t=-n}^{n-1}\ln(A_t)_{jj}.
\]
Then for every $j$ and every integer $-n\leq u\leq n$,
\begin{equation}
 \left|\sum_{t=-n}^{u-1}\ln(A_t)_{jj}
          -(u+n)\lambda_j\right|\leq bn.
\end{equation}
Consequently, on every subinterval $-n\leq u\leq v\leq n$,
\begin{equation}
 \left|\sum_{t=u}^{v-1}\ln(A_t)_{jj}
          -(v-u)\lambda_j\right|\leq2bn.
\end{equation}

statements.title: Finite-interval splitting
statements.label: prop:finite-splitting
statements.text:
Fix $d\geq1$ and $A_*>1$.  There is a constant $C$, depending only on
these two quantities, with the following properties.
Let $n\geq2$, $b>0$, and $\ln(2n+1)\leq bn$.
Suppose that $A_t$, $-n\leq t<n$, are upper triangular with positive
diagonal and
\[
 \|A_t\|,\ \|A_t^{-1}\|\leq A_*,
 \qquad
 \left|\sum_{t=-n}^{u-1}\ln(A_t)_{jj}
                  -(u+n)\lambda_j\right|\leq bn
\]
for $-n\leq u\leq n$ and $1\leq j\leq d$, where
$\lambda_j=(2n)^{-1}\sum_{t=-n}^{n-1}\ln(A_t)_{jj}$.

First, order the rates as
$\lambda_{(1)}\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_{(d)}$.
For every $0\leq q\leq d$ and every $-n\leq s\leq t\leq n$,
\begin{equation}
 \left|\ln\|\mathord{\bigwedge}^q A(t,s)\|
       -(t-s)\sum_{j=1}^q\lambda_{(j)}\right|\leq Cbn.
\end{equation}
The analogous estimate for $A(s,t)$ uses the $q$ largest members of
$\{-\lambda_1,\ldots,-\lambda_d\}$.

Next, suppose that real $\gamma$ and $g>0$ separate all the rates:
each $\lambda_j$ is at most $\gamma-g$ or at least $\gamma+g$.
Let $F$ be the set of indices in the second group, let
$p=|F|$, and put
\[
 \Lambda=\sum_{j\in F}\lambda_j,\qquad
 \Omega=-\sum_{j\notin F}\lambda_j.
\]
There are decompositions
$\R^d=E_t^s\oplus E_t^f$, $-n\leq t\leq n$, invariant under each
$A_t$, with $\dim E_t^f=p$, whose two projections have norm at most
$e^{Cbn}$.  For $s\leq t$ and $l=t-s$ they satisfy
\begin{align}
 \|A(t,s)|E_s^s\|&\leq e^{(\gamma-g)l+Cbn},
 &
 \|A(s,t)|E_t^f\|&\leq e^{-(\gamma+g)l+Cbn},
 \\
 \|\mathord{\bigwedge}^p A(t,s)\|&\leq e^{\Lambda l+Cbn},
 &
 e^{\Lambda l-Cbn}\leq
 J_p(A(t,s)|E_s^f)&\leq e^{\Lambda l+Cbn},
 \\
 \|\mathord{\bigwedge}^{d-p} A(s,t)\|&\leq e^{\Omega l+Cbn},
 &
 e^{\Omega l-Cbn}\leq
 J_{d-p}(A(s,t)|E_t^s)&\leq e^{\Omega l+Cbn}.
 
\end{align}
If $0<p<d$ and at least one of $v_1,\ldots,v_p$ belongs to $E_s^s$,
then
\begin{equation}
 \|A(t,s)v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge A(t,s)v_p\|
 \leq e^{(\Lambda-2g)l+Cbn}\prod_{j=1}^p\|v_j\|.
\end{equation}
The backward analogue has exterior degree $d-p$, exponent
$(\Omega-2g)l+Cbn$, and at least one factor in $E_t^f$.
When a group is empty its space is $\{0\}$, all statements on that
space are vacuous, and the exterior-degree-zero conventions apply.
statements.section_title: Linear estimates on finite orbit segments

statements.title: Smooth switching
statements.label: thm:switching
statements.text:
Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold of positive finite dimension, let
$\nu$ be a smooth positive probability volume in the density sense of
\Cref{sec:introduction}, and let $S:M\to M$
be a smooth diffeomorphism preserving $\nu$.  Fix a Riemannian distance
$d_M$ and $\eta>0$.  There exist positive numbers $B_k$ with
$\sum_k B_k^{16}<\infty$ and a constant $C$ such that the following
holds for all sufficiently large $k$, with $n=2^k$.

There is a finite measurable partition $\mathcal D_k$ of $M$ with
$\#\mathcal D_k\le \exp(CB_kn)$.  Define the probability measure
\begin{equation}
 \rho_k=\sum_{\substack{Q\in\mathcal D_k\\\nu(Q)>0}}
       \frac{(\nu|_Q)\otimes(\nu|_Q)}{\nu(Q)}.
\end{equation}
Thus one first samples a cell with its $\nu$-weight and then samples
two independent points in that cell.  There are a measurable set
$G_k\subset M\times M$, with $\rho_k(G_k)\ge1-\eta$, and a measurable
map $z_k:G_k\to M$ such that
\begin{equation}
 (z_k)_*(\rho_k|_{G_k})\le 2\nu
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{(x,y)\in G_k}\left[
 \max_{0\le t\le n}d_M(S^t z_k(x,y),S^t x)
 +\max_{-n\le t\le0}d_M(S^t z_k(x,y),S^t y)
 \right]\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
The measure on the left of \eqref{eq:switch-law} is not normalized
after restriction to $G_k$.  The same conclusions hold if $M$ has a
smooth boundary.
statements.section_title: Switching a past and a future with controlled volume

statements.title: Finite word families
statements.label: prop:words
statements.text:
Choose $s_1$ so that $K_1\ge256$, and define the parameters by
\eqref{eq:word-parameters}--\eqref{eq:word-recursion}.
There are families $\mathcal W_i\subset\mathcal A^{m_i}$ of cardinality
$L_i$, with $\mathcal W_1=\mathcal A$, such that every
$w\in\mathcal W_{i+1}$ is a concatenation of $N_i$ members of
$\mathcal W_i$ and the following properties hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(W\arabic*)},ref=W\arabic*,leftmargin=*]
\item\textbf{Relations within groups.}
Write $c_i(w)=(u_0,\ldots,u_{N_i-1})$.
For every $0\le b<N_i/H_i$, every
$0\le k\le\lfloor K_i/8\rfloor$, and every
$0\le r<r+2^k<H_i$,
\[
  [u_{bH_i+r},u_{bH_i+r+2^k}]_i=0.
\]
\item\textbf{Distance between words and shifted words.}
If $v,w\in\mathcal W_{i+1}$ are distinct, then
\[
  d_{\mathrm H}\bigl(c_i(v),c_i(w)\bigr)
     \ge(1-\varepsilon_i)N_i.
\]
For all $v,w,z\in\mathcal W_{i+1}$, with repetitions allowed, and all
$1\le t<N_i$,
\[
  d_{\mathrm H}\bigl((c_i(v)c_i(w))[t,t+N_i),c_i(z)\bigr)
     \ge(1-\varepsilon_i)N_i.
\]
\item\textbf{Distributions of short windows.}
Let $U$ be uniform on $\mathcal W_{i+1}$.
For each $0\le t\le N_i-D_i^*$ there is a probability $Q_{i,t}$ on
$\mathcal W_i^{D_i^*}$ such that
\[
  \TV\bigl(\mathcal L(c_i(U)[t,t+D_i^*)),Q_{i,t}\bigr)
     \le\vartheta.
\]
Moreover, for $1\le d'\le D_i^*$, any distinct positions
$0\le r_1<\cdots<r_{d'}<D_i^*$, and any prescribed labels
$v_1,\ldots,v_{d'}\in\mathcal W_i$,
\begin{equation}
  Q_{i,t}\{u:u_{r_j}=v_j\text{ for }1\le j\le d'\}
       \le 2\left(\frac{2^{2K_i}}{L_i}\right)^{d'}.
\end{equation}
\item\textbf{Approximation in each individual word.}
Suppose $i\ge2$.  For every fixed $w\in\mathcal W_{i+1}$, write
$c_i(w)=(u_0,\ldots,u_{N_i-1})$ and let $J$ be uniform on
$\{0,\ldots,N_i-1\}$.  If $U$ is uniform on $\mathcal W_i$, then for
each $0\le t\le N_{i-1}-D_{i-1}^*$,
\[
 \TV\left(
   \mathcal L\bigl(c_{i-1}(u_J)[t,t+D_{i-1}^*)\bigr),
   \mathcal L\bigl(c_{i-1}(U)[t,t+D_{i-1}^*)\bigr)
 \right)\le\vartheta.
\]
The first law averages the constituents of the single fixed word $w$;
it does not average over $\mathcal W_{i+1}$.
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: Words with prescribed relations and recognizable boundaries

statements.label: prop:system
statements.text:
There is a $T$-invariant ergodic Borel probability $\mu$ on $X$.
Every $T$-invariant Borel probability on $X$ is nonatomic, is standard
modulo null sets, and has zero Kolmogorov--Sinai entropy.

title: A finite-time singularity of Calabi flow on projective space
abstract: We construct a smooth Kähler metric in the Fubini–Study class of \(\mathbb{CP}^{10}\) whose Calabi flow develops unbounded scalar curvature in finite time. This disproves Chen's smooth long-time existence conjecture, even in a class containing a constant-scalar-curvature metric.

tex.abstract:
We construct a smooth K\"ahler metric in the Fubini--Study class of
\(\CP^{10}\) whose Calabi flow develops unbounded scalar curvature in finite time.
This disproves Chen's smooth long-time existence conjecture, even in a class
containing a constant-scalar-curvature metric.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is a smooth \(U(10)\)-invariant K\"ahler form \(\omega_0\) on
\(\CP^{10}\), in the class \([\omega_{\mathrm{FS}}]\), whose maximal smooth
Calabi flow has existence interval \([0,T_*)\) with \(0<T_*<\infty\).
There are a point \(p\in\CP^{10}\) and a constant \(a>0\) such that
\[
 S(\omega(t))(p)\sim a(T_*-t)^{-1/2}\qquad\text{as }t\uparrow T_*.
\]

statements.title: Products with stationary factors
statements.label: cor:product-singularities
statements.text:
Let \(\omega(t)\), \(T_*\), \(p\), and \(a\) be as in
Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, and let \((Y,\eta)\) be a compact connected
K\"ahler manifold with \(\eta\) of constant scalar curvature.  With
\(\pi_X\) and \(\pi_Y\) the projections from \(\CP^{10}\times Y\),
the maximal smooth Calabi flow from
\(\Omega_0=\pi_X^*\omega_0+\pi_Y^*\eta\) is
\[
 \Omega(t)=\pi_X^*\omega(t)+\pi_Y^*\eta,
 \qquad 0\leq t<T_*.
\]
For every \(y\in Y\),
\(S(\Omega(t))(p,y)\sim a(T_*-t)^{-1/2}\).
In particular, finite-time smooth Calabi-flow singularities occur in
every complex dimension \(n\geq10\), on
\(\CP^{10}\times\CP^{n-10}\), in a class containing a
K\"ahler--Einstein metric.

statements.title: Shrinking profile
statements.label: prof:profile
statements.text:
There exist a constant $c>0$ and a function $G\in C^\infty([0,\infty))$
such that
\begin{equation}
 Q(y\partial_y)(G-1)=\frac{y^2}{2}\left(\frac1G-\frac1c\right),
 \qquad Q(D)=(D-1)(D+9)(D+10).
\end{equation}
The function $G$ is bounded above and bounded away from zero, satisfies
$G(0)=1$ and $G'(0)<0$, and is analytic near zero.  There are real
coefficients $g_j$, $j\ge1$, such that, for every $J,\ell\ge0$,
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\dd^\ell}{\dd y^\ell}
 \left(G(y)-c-\sum_{j=1}^{J}g_jy^{-2j}\right)
 =O\bigl(y^{-2(J+1)-\ell}\bigr)\qquad(y\longrightarrow\infty).
\end{equation}
In particular, $u\mapsto G(u^{-1/2})$ extends smoothly to $u=0$ from
the right, with value $c$.

Set $h(y)=(G(y)-1)/y$, with its smooth value at zero.  For $t<0$, the
function
\begin{equation}
 F(t,x)=\rho^{-1}h(x/\rho),\qquad \rho=\sqrt{-t},
\end{equation}
solves
\[
 F_t+(1+xF)^2\widehat{\A}F=0,
 \qquad \widehat{\A}=(x\partial_x^2+12\partial_x)^2.
\]

statements.title: Ancient flat right inverse
statements.label: flat:inverse
statements.text:
There is a number $\delta\in(0,1)$ such that, for every fixed
$\alpha\in(0,1)$, the operator \eqref{flat:operator} has a bounded real
linear right inverse
\[
 \widehat D:Y\longrightarrow X,\qquad
 \widehat{\Pcal}\widehat D f=f,\qquad
 \|\widehat D f\|_X\le C\|f\|_Y,
 \qquad p_0=-2+2\delta.
\]
Here $Y$ has weight $p_0-4$ and parabolic exponent $\alpha$, and $X$
has weight $p_0$ and includes the parabolic $\alpha$ norms of all
spatial derivatives through order four and of the first time
derivative. The solution is radial and classical on $t<0$.
Its initial values are selected by the construction. The constant
depends only on the fixed profile, $\delta$, $\alpha$, and the fixed
choices in the local norms.
statements.section_title: An ancient inverse for the flat linearization

statements.title: Compact realization
statements.label: glue:solution
statements.text:
Let $G$ be the profile of Theorem~\ref{prof:profile}, put
\[
 h(y)=\frac{G(y)-1}{y},\qquad
 F(t,x)=\rho^{-1}h(x/\rho),
\]
and fix $0<\alpha<\alpha'<1$.  Choose $\delta\in(0,1)$ and the ancient
right inverse supplied by Theorem~\ref{flat:inverse}.  For every
sufficiently small $\eps>0$, there are $T>0$ and a real invariant
function $V\in X_\alpha$ on $\Sigma\times[-T,0)$ such that
$\norm{V}_{X'_\alpha}\le\eps$ and $H=F+V$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 H_t+(1+v_*H)^2\A H=0,\qquad v_*=x(1-x).
\end{equation}
The function $H$ is smooth on $\Sigma\times(-T,0)$, and there are
constants $0<c_1<c_2<\infty$, independent of $t$, such that
\begin{equation}
 c_1\le 1+v_*H\le c_2.
\end{equation}
In particular, $H(t,\cdot)$ is smooth as a function of $x\in[0,1]$, and
\begin{equation}
 V(t,0)=O(\rho^{-1+\delta})\qquad(t\uparrow0).
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: A concentrating solution on the compact manifold

statements.title: Uniform compact right inverse
statements.label: glue:inverse
statements.text:
There are $\beta_0,\eta_0,C_D>0$ such that, for
$0<\beta\le\beta_0$ and $0<T\le\eta_0\beta^4$, the operator
$\Pcal$ has a real invariant right inverse
$D:Y_\alpha\to X_\alpha$ with $\norm D\le C_D$.
No initial value is prescribed for $Df$.

statements.title: Finite shooting bounds
statements.label: cert:shoot
statements.text:
For every parameter \(z_*\in[-R,R]^2\), where \(R=5\cdot10^{-10}\), let
\((k,d)\) be given by \eqref{prof:parameters}, and let \(p\) be the origin
solution of \eqref{prof:ode} supplied by Lemma~\ref{prof:origin}.
This solution extends to \(0\le s\le S_0=56\) and satisfies
\[
 1+p(s)>0.
\]
For the coordinates of its jet relative to \(p_{\rm a}\), defined in
\eqref{prof:coordinates}, one has
\begin{equation}
 |q|\le .25R,\qquad
 \big\|(\Re\xi,\Im\xi)-z_*\big\|_\infty\le .13R.
\end{equation}

title: A finitely generated counterexample to the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture
abstract: We construct a finitely generated residually finite group of integral cohomological dimension two and geometric dimension three, disproving the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is a finitely generated residually finite group $G$ such that
\[
 \cdim G=2,\qquad \gdim G=3.
\]
One may take $G$ to be the height kernel in the right-angled Artin group associated to a finite acyclic flag triangulation of the presentation complex
\begin{equation}

 \langle x,y\mid x^2=y^5,\ x^2=(xy^{-1})^3\rangle.
\end{equation}
No two-dimensional classifying space for this $G$ exists, regardless of the number of its cells.

statements.title: The presentation comparison theorem
statements.label: thm:presentation
statements.text:
Suppose that $\Gamma$ is residually finite and that $\mathcal D$ is a
finite indexed list of words on $S$, trivial in $\Gamma$, whose chains
form a free $\Lambda$-basis of $\ker\partial_1$.  Thus the canonical map
\begin{equation}
 \Lambda^{(\mathcal D)}\longrightarrow\ker\partial_1,
 \qquad e_z\longmapsto[z],
\end{equation}
is an isomorphism.
If $\Gamma$ admits a $K(\Gamma,1)$ of dimension at most two, there is an
$\eta>0$ with the following property.  Assign a label in $H=\SU(2)$ to
every oriented generator edge, assign the inverse label to its reverse,
and assume that every label has distance less than $\eta$ from $1$.
If the product along every translate of every $z\in\mathcal D$ is $1$,
then the product along every closed edge path is $1$.
statements.section_title: Comparison with an arbitrary aspherical presentation

statements.label: prop:model
statements.text:
The finite flag complex $L$, its nontrivial representation
$\alpha:\pi_1(L)\to H$, and the group $G$ of
\eqref{eq:height-kernel} have the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $G$ is countable, finitely generated, and residually finite,
      with $\cdim(G)=2$ and $\gdim(G)\le3$.
\item $G$ acts freely on the integrally acyclic two-dimensional
      simplicial complex $X$ of \eqref{eq:zero-level}.  The action
      has finitely many cell orbits and one vertex orbit, identified
      with $G$ acting on itself on the left.
\item There is a finite generating alphabet $S$ for $G$ and a
      finite indexed list $\mathcal D$ of words trivial in $G$ such
      that, for $\Lambda=\Z[G]$, the graph of $X$ has edges
      $g\to gs$ and
      \begin{equation}
       0\longrightarrow\Lambda^{(\mathcal D)}
       \xrightarrow{\ \partial_2\ }\Lambda^{(S)}
       \xrightarrow{\ \partial_1\ }\Lambda
       \xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{aug}\ }\Z\longrightarrow0
      \end{equation}
      is exact, with $\partial_1(e_s)=s-1$ and
      $\partial_2(e_z)=[z]$.  Here $[z]$ is the oriented edge chain
      of the triangular boundary word $z$ based at $1$.
      In particular, the chains $[z]$, $z\in\mathcal D$, are a
      free $\Lambda$-basis of $\ker\partial_1$.
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: An acyclic level model for a height kernel

statements.label: prop:small-labels
statements.text:
For every $\epsilon>0$, the oriented edges of $X$ admit labels
$h_e\in H$ such that
\[
 h_{\bar e}=h_e^{-1},\qquad |h_e-1|<\epsilon,
\]
the product around every triangular two-cell is $1$, and the product
around some closed edge path is different from $1$.

title: A group without fixed price
abstract: We construct a finitely generated group with two essentially free probability-measure-preserving actions of different costs. This gives a negative answer to Gaboriau's general fixed-price problem. The group is an amalgam of a free group of rank 100 with a direct product. Its Bernoulli action has cost bounded away from one, whereas finite height extensions have costs tending to one.

tex.abstract:
We construct a finitely generated group with two essentially free
probability-measure-preserving actions of different costs. This gives
a negative answer to Gaboriau's general fixed-price problem. The group is an
amalgam of a free group of rank $100$ with a direct product. Its
Bernoulli action has cost bounded away from one, whereas finite height
extensions have costs tending to one.

statements.label: intro:main
statements.text:
Put $K=e^{96}96^{99}/95^{95}$, choose
\[
 0<\alpha<1/200,\qquad K\alpha^3<1/2,
 \qquad \eta=\alpha/100.
\]
For the group and actions just defined,
\[
 \operatorname{Cost}(\mathcal R_{\Gamma\curvearrowright X})
      \ge1+\eta,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Cost}(\mathcal R_{\Gamma\curvearrowright Y_M})
      \le1+\frac{99}{M}\quad(M>100).
\]
In particular, choosing an integer $M>\max\{100,99/\eta\}$ gives
two essentially free p.m.p. actions of the same finitely generated
group with strictly different costs. Thus the general fixed-price
assertion is false.

statements.label: actions:low
statements.text:
For every integer $M>100$, the free p.m.p. action
$\Gamma\curvearrowright(Y_M,\nu_M)$ of
\eqref{actions:product-action} satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{Cost}(\mathcal R_{\Gamma\curvearrowright Y_M})
 \leq1+\frac{99}{M}.
\]

statements.label: compression:cost-one
statements.text:

space, all of whose classes are infinite, has cost at least one.

statements.label: deployment:main
statements.text:
Let $\Gamma=A*_J B$ be finitely generated, let $J$ be infinite, and
let $\Gamma$ act essentially freely and p.m.p. on a standard probability
space $(X,\mu)$. If $\delta_X$ is the infimum cost of graphings that
generate $\mathcal R_A$ together with the supplied relation
$\mathcal R_J$, then
\[
 \operatorname{Cost}(\mathcal R_\Gamma)\geq 1+\delta_X.
\]

statements.label: models:transfer
statements.text:
Let $V_k$ be finite exact right $A$-sets, with $n_k=|V_k|\to\infty$,
such that for every fixed $g\in A\setminus\{1\}$,
\begin{equation}
 \frac{|\{v\in V_k:vg=v\}|}{n_k}\longrightarrow0.
 
\end{equation}
For the free Bernoulli action on $X$ from
Section~\ref{actions:section}, whose cost agrees with the full product
action on $X_0=[0,1]^\Gamma$, one has
\[
 \delta_X\ge\limsup_{k\to\infty}
 \frac{\operatorname{rk}(D_{V_k})}{n_k}.
\]

statements.label: models:sequence
statements.text:
Put $K=e^{96}96^{99}/95^{95}$. Fix
\[
 0<\alpha<1/200,\qquad K\alpha^3<1/2.
\]
There exists a sequence of finite exact right $A$-sets $V_k$, with
$n_k=|V_k|\to\infty$, satisfying \eqref{models:fixed-points} and
\begin{align}
 |N(T)|&>96|T|
 &&(T\subseteq V_k,\ 1\le |T|\le\alpha n_k),
 \\
 b(V_k)&=o(n_k).
 
\end{align}

statements.label: rank:main
statements.text:
Let $V$ and $\mathcal T$ be sets of cardinality $n$.  For each
$t\in\mathcal T$, let
\[
 r_t=x_{c(t,0)}x_{c(t,1)}\cdots x_{c(t,99)},\qquad c(t,i)\in V,
 \qquad
 D=\langle x_v\ (v\in V)\mid r_t=1\ (t\in\mathcal T)\rangle.
\]
For $T\subseteq\mathcal T$, put
$N(T)=\{c(t,i):t\in T,\ 0\le i\le99\}$.
Call a row $t$ bad if it has a repeated column, or if it shares at least
two distinct columns with another row, and let $b$ be the number of bad
rows.  Suppose that
\[
 0<\alpha<\frac1{200},\qquad \alpha n\ge1,
 \qquad 100b\le\alpha n,
\]
and that
\begin{equation}
 |N(T)|>96|T|\qquad
 \text{whenever }1\le |T|\le\alpha n.
\end{equation}
Then the minimum size of a generating set of $D$ satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{rk}(D)>\frac{\alpha n}{100}.
\]

statements.label: rank:asymptotic
statements.text:
Suppose that a sequence of length-$100$ row systems satisfies
\eqref{rank:expansion} for a fixed $0<\alpha<1/200$, their sizes
$n$ tend to infinity, and their bad-row counts satisfy $b=o(n)$.
Then their presented groups satisfy
\[
 \operatorname{rk}(D)>\frac{\alpha n}{100}
 \quad\text{for all sufficiently large }n,
 \qquad
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{rk}(D)}n
 \ge\frac\alpha{100}.
\]

tex.abstract:
We disprove the Chow and rational-cohomological forms of Pixton's completeness
conjecture for his original relation system. We construct a formal tautological
class outside the original Pixton relation span whose image is zero in the Chow
ring and in rational cohomology. The example has genus \(10^{60}\) and

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Set
\[
g=10^{60},\qquad D_*=\binom g3,\qquad n=3D_*.
\]
The explicitly defined class \(Y\in \Salg_{g,n}^{2D_*}\) of
Definition~\ref{def:candidate} satisfies
\[
q_{g,n}(Y)=0,\qquad Y\notin\Pspan_{g,n}.
\]
Consequently Pixton's original relation span does not exhaust the
tautological Chow relations: the equality
\(\ker q_{g,n}=\Pspan_{g,n}\) fails for this stable pair.

statements.title: Rational-cohomological incompleteness
statements.label: cor:cohomological-incompleteness
statements.text:
For the stable pair and class \(Y\) of Theorem~\ref{thm:main},
\[
q^H_{g,n}(Y)=0
\quad\text{in }H^{4D_*}\!\left(\Mbar_{g,n}(\C);\Q\right),
\qquad
Y\notin\Pspan_{g,n}.
\]
In particular, \(\Pspan_{g,n}\subsetneq\ker q^H_{g,n}\).

statements.title: Known validity and stability
statements.label: prop:known-relations
statements.text:
The span in Definition~\ref{def:pixton-span} is an ideal and is stable
under tautological gluing and forgetting pushforwards and pullbacks.
For gluing pullback to a product, the target relation space is the sum
of the spaces with a relation in one factor.
Moreover
\[
\Pspan_{g,n}\subseteq\ker q_{g,n}.
\]

statements.label: prop:detector
statements.text:
There are a supercommutative \(\Q\)-algebra \(R\), a finite free
supermodule \(V\) over \(R\), and \(\Q\)-linear maps
\[
 t_m:\Salg_{g,m}\longrightarrow V^{\otimes_R m}
 \qquad(m\geq 0)
\]
such that \(t_m(\Pspan_{g,m})=0\) for every \(m\), whereas
\(t_n(Y)\neq0\).  In particular \(Y\notin\Pspan_{g,n}\).

statements.title: Faithful Chow tensor test
statements.label: prop:tensor-test
statements.text:
In the setup above, either in relative rational Chow or in the indicated
quotient by base support, there is a supercommutative rational algebra
\(\mathfrak B\) with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item
The curve correspondence algebra has a faithful tensor model on
\[
 \mathfrak B\otimes
 \bigl(\Q 1\oplus W_b\oplus\Q e\bigr),
\]
where \(1,e\) are even and \(W_b\) is an odd symplectic space of dimension
\(2b\).  The classes \(1_C,e'_C\) correspond to \(1,e\), and \(\eta\)
projects onto \(W_b\).  Integration gives the hyperbolic pairing
\(\langle1,e\rangle=1\), \(\langle1,1\rangle=\langle e,e\rangle=0\)
on the two even summands and the symplectic pairing on \(W_b\).
All actual Chow correspondences between curve powers, not only pairing
diagrams, are included faithfully in this model.
\item
The projected small diagonal is an alternating three-form
\[
 \varphi\colon W_b^3\longrightarrow\mathfrak B_{\mathrm{odd}}.
\]
Cup product, integration, tensor products, permutations, and contractions
are computed in the model with the Koszul signs.
\item
Let \(U\) be a finite-dimensional ordinary rational color space.  A pure
colored tensor in
\begin{equation}
 
 \left(
   \eta^{\otimes k}\CH^*(C^k)
   \otimes U^{\otimes k}\otimes\mathrm{sgn}_k
 \right)_{\mathfrak S_k}
\end{equation}
is zero if and only if all its evaluations using the same ordinary
linear map \(z\colon U\to W_b\) in every slot are zero in \(\mathfrak B\).
Finitely many rational maps \(z\) suffice for each fixed \(U,k\).
The assertion holds in the base-support quotient as well.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, a product of projected cubic entries is tested by
products of
\(\varphi(z(i),z(j),z(k))\), with the fixed Koszul sign coming from the
ordering of the factors.  A vanishing established by these tests is a
vanishing in Chow, with the stated base-support bound.
statements.section_title: Faithful tensor tests in relative Chow

statements.title: Surface bound
statements.label: thm:surface
statements.text:
Suppose \(b\geq5\) and \(\dim S<\chi-1\).
Let \((w_\alpha)_{\alpha\in I}\) be any finite collection of vectors in the
odd symplectic standard space \(W_b\) whose span is isotropic. For any
matrix of scalars \(\gamma=(\gamma_{\alpha\beta})_{\alpha,\beta\in I}\),
put
\begin{equation}

 T_\gamma=
 \sum_{\substack{\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3\in I\\
                  \beta_1,\beta_2,\beta_3\in I}}
 \left(\prod_{j=1}^3\gamma_{\alpha_j\beta_j}\right)
 \varphi(w_{\alpha_1},w_{\alpha_2},w_{\alpha_3})
 \varphi(w_{\beta_1},w_{\beta_2},w_{\beta_3}).
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}

 T_\gamma^{\,t_0}=0\qquad\text{in }\mathfrak B.
\end{equation}
The assertion remains valid after any characteristic-zero scalar
extension of the tensor formalism.
statements.section_title: A surface relation from determinant-fixed Quot schemes

statements.title: Localization relation
statements.label: prop:localization
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:surface}, the scalar
\(a_{N,t_0}\) satisfies
\[
 a_{N,t_0}\,T_\gamma^{\,t_0}=0
 \qquad\text{in }\mathfrak B_{S,b-1}.
\]
statements.section_title: A surface relation from determinant-fixed Quot schemes

statements.label: prop:scalar
statements.text:
The bare-triple scalar \(a_{N,t_0}\) in
Proposition~\ref{prop:localization} is nonzero.
Consequently Theorem~\ref{thm:surface} holds.

statements.title: Controlled pure lifts
statements.label: prop:controlled-lifts
statements.text:
For every stable heavy type $(h,B)$ one can choose a symmetric class
$G_{h,B}\in\CH^2(X_{h,B}(3))$ with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item
Over the smooth heavy base, $G_{h,B}$ is exactly the pullback of
$\Delta_C^{\mathrm{pure}}$ by the coarse-position map.
\item
Pull a raw cubic $F^0$, or one of these chosen pure lifts $G$, from any
ancestor chart to a compact descendant cut chart.  Its operation is
a sum of the chosen pure lifts at the relevant descendant vertices,
with all three labels assigned to that vertex, together with
pair-times-singleton operations and a residual cubic operation.
\item
The singleton operations in \textup{(ii)}, and all their further
pullbacks through cuts and light forgetting, are controlled as
follows.  Over fixed smooth core data their restrictions lie
componentwise in the span of the unit, the canonical class, and the
flag points.  On any smooth test family the same statement holds
modulo classes supported over positive base codimension.
\item
On the current smooth-core open the residual operation in
\textup{(ii)} is a finite sum of classes containing a pulled base
divisor factor.  The base divisor may come from the current heavy
base or from a compact ancestor base.  Consequently its pullback to
every smooth test family is zero operationally after removing a
positive-codimension subset of that test base.
\end{enumerate}
All expansions preserve the color multiset.  They may always use one
and the same chosen $G$ and centering at a given current vertex,
regardless of which ancestor supplied the operation.

statements.text:

 \quad\text{in }\CH^*(\Mbar_{g,n};\Q).
