title: A hyperbolic group with no geometric CAT(0) action
abstract: We construct a hyperbolic group with a finite classifying space that admits no geometric action on a proper complete CAT(0) space. Consequently, a finite aspherical simplicial complex with a linear combinatorial disk-filling inequality need not have a finite locally CAT(0) homotopy model, and hence need not have a finite locally CAT(−1) model. Here metric models carry geodesic length metrics inducing the given complex topology.

tex.abstract: We construct a hyperbolic group with a finite classifying space that admits no geometric action on a proper complete CAT(0) space. Consequently, a finite aspherical simplicial complex with a linear combinatorial disk-filling inequality need not have a finite locally CAT(0) homotopy model, and hence need not have a finite locally CAT($-1$) model. Here metric models carry geodesic length metrics inducing the given complex topology.
sections: The incidence template and the nested tables
Conditional sampling from the nested tables

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There exist a finite connected two-dimensional aspherical simplicial complex $K$ and a constant $C<\infty$ with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item Every combinatorial edge loop of length $\ell$ in the universal cover of $K$ bounds a disk diagram with at most $C\ell$ triangular faces.
\item The group $\pi_1K$ admits no geometric action on a proper complete $\CAT(0)$ space.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, $\pi_1K$ is word-hyperbolic, and no finite simplicial complex homotopy equivalent to $K$ admits a locally $\CAT(0)$ geodesic length metric inducing its given topology. Consequently, no such model admits a compatible locally $\CAT(-1)$ geodesic length metric.

statements.label: thm:diagram
statements.text:
Fix sufficiently small positive $\alpha,\beta,\delta$ with
$\beta>7\alpha$, and put $f=2-\alpha$ and $p=3-\beta$.
As $n\longrightarrow\infty$, the probability tends to one that $P$ is
aspherical and its letter presentation satisfies a linear disk
isoperimetric inequality.

statements.label: prop:sampling
statements.text:
For any finite family $\mathcal T$ of conditional tests, there is a
neighborhood of the critical parameters such that every sufficiently
small fixed positive $(\alpha,\beta,\delta)$ in that neighborhood
with $\beta>7\alpha$ has the following properties as $N\to\infty$.
With probability tending to one, the master pattern has a nonempty
set of matches, its count is
\[
|\Omega_n|=(1+o(1))N^{3-\beta-90\delta},
\]
every single-field marginal of its uniform law $\mu_N$ is $o(1)$
in total variation from the uniform law on $S_n$, and every test in
$\mathcal T$ has the coupling of Lemma~\ref{sample:lem-coupling}.
The six-letter counts also satisfy Equation~\eqref{sample:eq-six-pair}.
All these properties concern only the tables and are independent of
any choice of action or metric space.
statements.section_title: Conditional sampling from the nested tables

statements.label: prop:configuration
statements.text:
Let $P_\nu$ be a sequence of aspherical instances whose master-match
statistics and six-letter relative counts satisfy the conclusions
of Proposition~\ref{prop:sampling}, with errors tending to zero for
every fixed test and every fixed $t$.  If every $\pi_1(P_\nu)$ has
a proper cocompact isometric action on a proper complete $\CAT(0)$
space, then there are a complete $\CAT(0)$ space $Z$, a
configuration indexed by the core vertices of $\Gamma$, and a
point $c\in Z$ with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Every core edge has length one.  Every nonbacktracking
two-edge core path has squared endpoint distance two.  Every
three-edge core path with distinct admissible fields has squared
endpoint distance at least three.
\item Every core hexagon has its three opposite-pair midpoints
equal to $c$.  All core vertices have distance $r=\sqrt3/2$ from
$c$.  For any two vertices occurring in one core hexagon, their
central triangle with $c$ is flat and their tangent scalar
product is given by Equation~\eqref{energy:hexagon-products}.
\item With $H_0=CD$ and $J=\operatorname{mid}(X_C,Y_C)$, one has
\[
 d(H_0,J)^2=\frac12,\qquad d(H_0,X_D)=1,
 \qquad \angle_{H_0}(J,X_D)\ge\frac\pi2.
\]
More precisely, all the fractional-point inequalities in
Equation~\eqref{energy:fractional-angle} hold.
\end{enumerate}

statements.label: prop:no-configuration
statements.text:
No complete $\CAT(0)$ space contains the configuration asserted in
Proposition~\ref{prop:configuration}.

statements.label: prop:completion-no-action
statements.text: For all sufficiently large $j$, the group $G_j$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:completion-diagonal} admits no geometric action on any proper complete $\CAT(0)$ space.

title: A latest-anchor induction with spectrally compact masks for worst-case trace reconstruction
abstract: We give an improved worst-case sample bound for reconstructing a string from independent deletion traces, with its length and retention probability known. For each fixed retention probability, the number of traces is quasipolynomial: the logarithm of the sample budget is \(O((\log n)^3(1+\log\log(2n))^6)\). If the deletion probability is at most \(n^{-\varepsilon}\) for fixed ε > 0, polynomially many traces suffice. These bounds apply to binary strings and to strings of general symbols observed exactly. They concern sample complexity and do not assert an efficient reconstruction algorithm or matching optimality.

title: A linear cycle-and-edge decomposition of every graph
abstract: We prove that every finite simple undirected graph on n vertices has an edge partition into at most \(Cn\) simple cycles and single edges, for an absolute constant C. This resolves the Erdős–Gallai cycle decomposition conjecture positively.

tex.abstract:
We prove that every finite simple undirected graph on \(n\) vertices
has an edge partition into at most \(Cn\) simple cycles and single
edges, for an absolute constant \(C\). This resolves the
Erd\H{o}s--Gallai cycle decomposition conjecture positively.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is an absolute constant \(C>0\) such that, for every finite
simple undirected graph \(G\) with \(n\) vertices, \(E(G)\) has a
partition into at most \(Cn\) parts, each of which is the edge set of
a cycle or consists of a single edge.

statements.label: cor:eulerian-cycles
statements.text:
Every finite simple undirected Eulerian graph on \(n\) vertices has an
edge partition into at most \(Cn\) cycles, with \(C\) from \Cref{thm:main}.

For every fixed \(\delta,p>0\), there exist \(\eps>0\) and an integer
\(n_0\ge1\) such that every finite simple undirected Eulerian graph \(G\)
on \(n\ge n_0\) vertices has an edge partition into at most
\(\Delta(G)/2+\delta n\) cycles, provided that every partition
\(V(G)=A\mathbin{\dot\cup}B\) with \(|A|,|B|\ge\eps n\) satisfies
\[
 e_G(A,B)\ge p|A||B|.
\]
Here \(\Delta(G)\) denotes the maximum degree, and \(e_G(A,B)\)
is the number of edges joining \(A\) to \(B\).

statements.title: Lov\'asz
statements.label: thm:lovasz
statements.text:
The edges of a finite simple graph on \(n\) vertices can be
partitioned into at most \(\floor{n/2}\) paths and cycles.

statements.label: cor:endpoint-paths
statements.text:
Every finite simple graph on \(n\) vertices has an edge
partition into paths such that each vertex is an endpoint of at
most two paths. In particular, the partition has at most \(n\)
paths.

statements.title: Aharoni--Haxell
statements.label: thm:aharoni-haxell
statements.text:
Let \(s\) be a positive integer and let
\((\mathcal H_i)_{i\in J}\) be a finite indexed family of
hypergraphs on a common ground set. Suppose every edge is
nonempty and has size at most \(s\). If, for every nonempty
\(I\subseteq J\), the union
\(\bigcup_{i\in I}\mathcal H_i\) has a matching of size
strictly greater than \(s(|I|-1)\), then there are edges
\(E_i\in\mathcal H_i\), one for each \(i\in J\), that are
pairwise disjoint.

statements.label: prop:induction-bound
statements.text:
There is an absolute constant \(C\) such that every finite simple
graph on \(n\ge1\) vertices has an edge partition into at most
\(C\phi(n)n\) simple cycles and single edges.

abstract: We prove that every finite nonempty graph G satisfies \(\chi_{\mathrm{list}}(G)\le C h(G)\) for an absolute integer C, where \(h(G)\) is the largest order of a clique minor. This resolves the Linear List Hadwiger conjecture affirmatively.

tex.abstract:
We prove that every finite nonempty graph $G$ satisfies
$\chi_{\mathrm{list}}(G)\le C h(G)$ for an absolute integer $C$, where
$h(G)$ is the largest order of a clique minor. This resolves the Linear
List Hadwiger conjecture affirmatively.

statements.title: Grouping terminals
statements.label: thm:grouping
statements.text:
There is an absolute integer $\gamma\ge1$ such that the following holds.
In a $\gamma m$-connected graph, every partition of $m\ge1$ distinct
terminals into nonempty groups can be realized by pairwise disjoint
connected vertex sets, one containing each group.

statements.label: prop:small-list
statements.text:
There are an absolute positive integer $L$ and an absolute integer $t_0$
such that, for every integer $t\ge t_0$ and every graph $G$,
\[
 h(G)<t,\qquad |V(G)|\le t^{11/10}
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \ell(G)\le Lt.
\]

statements.label: density:list-district
statements.text:
Fix \(K\) and \(D_K\) as in Lemma~\ref{lem:district}.
For all sufficiently large integers \(t\), if
\[
 h(P)<t,\qquad \ell(P)>2D_Kt+2,
\]
then \(P\) contains an induced \((Kt)\)-connected subgraph of order
at most \(t^{1.06}\).

statements.label: thm:recursive-woven
statements.text:
There are absolute positive integers $K,Q$ such that, for every integer
$a\ge1$, every $Ka$-connected graph $P$ with $\ell(P)\ge Qa$ is
$(a,3a)$-woven.

title: A local Penrose inequality for conformal perturbations of Schwarzschild–anti-de Sitter data
abstract: We prove the asymptotically hyperbolic Penrose inequality for sufficiently small maximal vacuum conformal perturbations of a positive-mass Schwarzschild–anti-de Sitter exterior, for every fixed decaying transverse-traceless seed and every solution branch satisfying the stated decay and mass assumptions. The bound uses the area of the marginally outer trapped boundary itself; it requires neither outermostness nor outer area-minimization, and no bulk-versus-boundary domination condition. For sufficiently small positive parameters, equality holds for radial seeds and the inequality is strict otherwise.

tex.abstract:
We prove the asymptotically hyperbolic Penrose inequality for sufficiently
small maximal vacuum conformal perturbations of a positive-mass
Schwarzschild--anti-de Sitter exterior, for every fixed decaying
transverse-traceless seed and every solution branch satisfying the stated
decay and mass assumptions. The bound uses the area of the marginally
outer trapped boundary itself; it requires neither outermostness nor
outer area-minimization, and no bulk-versus-boundary domination condition.
For sufficiently small positive parameters, equality holds for radial
seeds and the inequality is strict otherwise.
sections: CMC sphere jets and their Hawking mass
The quadratic estimate and its complete kernel
Fourth order in the quadratic kernel
Radial equality and the nonlinear conclusion

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every background, fixed TT seed, and solution branch satisfying
\eqref{eq:background}--\eqref{eq:branch} and the mass assumptions
above, there is $0<\eps_0\leq\eps_*$ such that
\[
 m_{\AH}(\eps)\geq
 \sqrt{\frac{A_\eps}{16\pi}}\left(1+\frac{A_\eps}{4\pi}\right)
 \qquad(0\leq\eps<\eps_0).
\]
For all sufficiently small positive $\eps$, equality holds if the
seed is radial, and the inequality is strict otherwise.

statements.label: cor:penrose
statements.text:
In addition to the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, suppose
$q_{ss}\geq0$ on $S$. Assume, for every sufficiently small positive
$\eps$, that no compact smooth embedded two-sided surface in the
interior enclosing $S$ has $\theta_+\leq0$ everywhere, and that
every smooth enclosing surface has area at least $A_\eps$.
Disconnected enclosing competitors are allowed, and $S$ itself is
allowed in the area infimum. Then the exact local Penrose inequality
holds with $A_{\min}(S)=A_\eps$.

statements.title: Expansions of the given branch
statements.label: prop:expansions
statements.text:
For every prescribed seed and branch in the theorem, set $p=2$ and
take $u_j,F_j,B_j$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:rotation}.  If the seed has the
form \eqref{ana:kernel-seed}, we may instead take $p=4$ with the
finite coefficient construction.  In both cases,
\begin{align}
 \left\|\psi-\sum_{j=1}^p\eps^ju_j\right\|_\beta
     &=O(\eps^{p+1}),\notag\\
 \left\|L\psi-\sum_{j=1}^p\eps^jF_j\right\|_{2\beta}
     &=O(\eps^{p+1}),\notag\\
 \left\|\partial_s\psi|_S-\sum_{j=1}^p\eps^jB_j\right\|_{C^0(S)}
     &=O(\eps^{p+1}).
 
\end{align}
The area and all four mass components have actual expansions to the
same order.  Their mass coefficients are
\begin{equation}
 a_{\mu j}[q]=\mathcal G_\mu(u_j,F_j,B_j),\qquad
 p_\mu(\eps)=p_\mu(0)+\sum_{j=1}^p\eps^j a_{\mu j}[q]
                      +O(\eps^{p+1}).
 
\end{equation}

In particular, the actual deficit satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak D_q(\eps)=c_2[q]\eps^2+O(\eps^3)
 
\end{equation}
for every seed under consideration.  The coefficient $c_2$ is a
continuous quadratic form on $\mathscr T_{\tau,\alpha}$ in the
$\|\cdot\|_\beta$ topology, invariant under rotations.  For seeds
of the form \eqref{ana:kernel-seed} there is additionally the actual
expansion
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak D_q(\eps)
     =c_2[q]\eps^2+c_3[q]\eps^3+c_4[q]\eps^4+O(\eps^5).
 
\end{equation}
The subsequent geometric arguments determine the signs and the
vanishing of these coefficients.

statements.title: CMC sphere jets
statements.label: prop:cmc-jets
statements.text:
Let \(p\geq1\), and let \(G\) be a smooth Riemannian metric jet of order
\(p\), with base \(G_0=g_0\), whose coefficients have finite angular type.
Suppose that there are angular scalar jets \(C,E\), with
\(C_0=2m_0\) and \(E_0=0\), such that
\begin{equation}
 G-b=r^{-3}\bigl(C\,\dd\eta^2+E r^2\sigma\bigr)+o(r^{-3}).
\end{equation}
For the coefficient of degree \(j\), \(1\leq j\leq p\), suppose that
the remainder satisfies this estimate after every mixed radial and
angular derivative of total order at most \(p-j+1\).

There is a smooth family of sphere jets
\(\Sigma_s\), \(0\leq s<\infty\), given by graphs over
\(\{s\}\times S^2\), with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
 \item \(\Sigma_s\) has constant outward mean curvature through order
 \(p\), and \(\Sigma_0\) is minimal through that order.
 \item The graph coefficients have finite angular type.  The normal
 lapse \(f\) for variation in \(s\) has base value \(f_0=1\).
 \item If \(A(s)\) and \(H(s)\) are the area and mean curvature jets,
 then the CMC Hawking mass
 \begin{equation}
 m_H(\Sigma_s)=
 \sqrt{\frac{A(s)}{16\pi}}
 \left(1-\frac{(H(s)^2-4)A(s)}{16\pi}\right)
 \end{equation}
 satisfies, coefficientwise,
 \begin{equation}
 \lim_{s\to\infty}m_H(\Sigma_s)
 =m_{\AH}(G)
 :=\sqrt{p_0(G)^2-\sum_{i=1}^3p_i(G)^2}.
 \end{equation}
 Here \(p_\mu(G)\) is the coefficientwise flux \eqref{eq:mass-flux},
 and the square root is its formal branch with base value
 \(m_0>0\).
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: CMC sphere jets and their Hawking mass

statements.title: Leading coefficient as a positive integral
statements.label: prop:leading-energy
statements.text:
Use the construction of Proposition~\ref{prop:cmc-jets} through order
\(2l\), where \(l\ge1\), and let \(A_{\mathrm{leaf}}=A(0)\) be the area
jet of its minimal first leaf.
Suppose, as ambient and leafwise coefficient identities, respectively,
that
\begin{equation}
 \scal_G+6=\eps^{2l}|k|_{g_0}^2+O(\eps^{2l+1}),
 \qquad
 \II^\circ=\eps^lU+O(\eps^{l+1}),
 \qquad
 \delta f=\eps^lF+O(\eps^{l+1}).
\end{equation}
Here \(k\) is a smooth tensor on \(M\); the fields \(U,F\) on the
background spheres are identified with fields on \(M\).
Then every coefficient below degree \(2l\) of
\(m_{\AH}(G)-b_*(A_{\mathrm{leaf}})\) vanishes, and
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 &\bigl[m_{\AH}(G)-b_*(A_{\mathrm{leaf}})\bigr]_{2l}\\
 &\quad=\frac1{16\pi}\int_0^\infty N(s)
   \int_{\{s\}\times S^2}
    \left(|k|^2+|U|^2+2FJ_s^0F\right)\dd A_{g_0}\,\dd s
 \ge0.
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
All norms in this formula use the background metrics.
The displayed iterated integral is finite.
If it vanishes, then \(k,U,F\) vanish for \(s>0\), and also at the
boundary by continuity.

statements.title: The quadratic deficit
statements.label: prop:quadratic
statements.section_title: The quadratic estimate and its complete kernel

statements.title: The complete quadratic kernel
statements.label: cor:kernel
statements.text:
The kernel of $c_2$ is exactly $\mathcal K$, a four-dimensional real
vector space.  In particular, the nonzero degree-one directions are
genuine quadratic null directions.
statements.section_title: The quadratic estimate and its complete kernel

statements.title: The quartic coefficient
statements.label: prop:quartic
statements.text:
Suppose that \(c_2[q]=0\).  Write the representation furnished by
Corollary~\ref{cor:kernel} as
\[
 q=Q(v):=\Hess_{g_0}v-Bv,\qquad Lv=0,
 \qquad v=v_0(s)+v_1(s,x),
\]
where \(v_1\) has only degree-one spherical modes and \(v\) decays at
infinity.  Then
\[
 c_0[q]=c_1[q]=c_2[q]=c_3[q]=0,
 \qquad c_4[q]\geq 0.
\]
If \(v_1\not\equiv0\), then \(c_4[q]>0\).  In particular, in that
case the actual deficit \(\mathfrak D_q(\eps)\) is strictly positive
for all sufficiently small positive \(\eps\).
statements.section_title: Fourth order in the quadratic kernel

statements.title: Exact radial equality
statements.label: prop:radial
statements.text:
Suppose the fixed TT seed $q$ is invariant under rotations of $S^2$.
Every branch in Theorem~\ref{thm:main} is radial for all sufficiently
small $\eps$, and on that parameter interval
\[
 m_{\AH}(\eps)=b_*(A_\eps).
\]
This includes the zero seed, and requires no sign for $q_{ss}|_S$.

title: A marked tensor obstruction to four-dimensional disk embedding
abstract: We disprove the unrestricted four-dimensional disk-embedding conjecture. We construct immersed disks in a compact oriented smooth four-manifold with framed algebraic dual spheres satisfying the usual equivariant intersection and reduced self-intersection conditions, but with no pairwise disjoint locally flat replacements that preserve the boundary maps and induced normal framings. The obstruction holds even when the replacement disks' relative homotopy classes are not prescribed.

tex.abstract:
We disprove the unrestricted four-dimensional disk-embedding conjecture.
We construct immersed disks in a compact oriented smooth four-manifold with
framed algebraic dual spheres satisfying the usual equivariant intersection
and reduced self-intersection conditions, but with no pairwise disjoint locally
flat replacements that preserve the boundary maps and induced normal framings.
The obstruction holds even when the replacement disks' relative homotopy classes
are not prescribed.
sections: Formal potentials for a single edge
Matching the edge potentials at the vertices

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There exist a compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold \(M\) with boundary,
an integer \(k\geq1\), generically immersed proper disks
\[
 f_1,\ldots,f_k:(D^2,S^1)\longrightarrow(M,\partial M)
\]
with disjoint embedded boundary circles, and generically immersed framed spheres
\(g_1,\ldots,g_k:S^2\longrightarrow M\), such that
\[
 \lambda(f_i,g_j)=\delta_{ij},\qquad
 \lambda(g_i,g_j)=0\quad\text{for all }i,j,\qquad
 \widetilde\mu(g_i)=0\quad\text{for all }i,
\]
but there are no pairwise disjoint locally flat embedded disks in \(M\)
with the same boundary maps and the boundary normal framings induced by the
\(f_i\).

statements.title: Universal framed disk replacement
statements.label: ass:disk
statements.text:
Let \(M\) be a compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold with boundary.
Suppose that a finite collection of proper generic immersions
\[
 f_i\colon(D^2,S^1)\longrightarrow(M,\partial M),\qquad 1\leq i\leq k,
\]
has pairwise disjoint embedded boundary circles, and admits generically immersed
framed spheres \(g_1,\ldots,g_k\) such that
\[
 \lambda(f_i,g_j)=\delta_{ij},\qquad
 \lambda(g_i,g_j)=0,\qquad
 \widetilde\mu(g_i)=0
 \quad\text{for all }i,j.
\]
Here intersections are counted in \(\mathbb Z[\pi_1M]\), with fixed whiskers,
the diagonal equations are included, and
\[
 \widetilde\mu(g_i)\in
 \mathbb Z[\pi_1M]\big/
 \big\langle h-h^{-1},\,\mathbb Z\cdot1\big\rangle
\]
uses the additive quotient. Then the \(f_i\) can be replaced by pairwise disjoint
locally flat embedded disks with the same boundary maps and the same induced
normal framings on those boundary circles.

statements.title: Geometric reduction
statements.label: prop:geometric-reduction
statements.text:
For the integers \(m,p\) and the finite list just specified, there is a
compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold \(X\), constructed without
Assumption~\ref{ass:disk}, with the following properties.

It has a regular cover with deck group \(F_m\), whose block graph is the
Cayley tree of \(F_m\). Each block is a four-dimensional one-handlebody on
the \(p\) extra letters. Its exposed boundary piece is
\[
 K_v\cong
 \bigl(\#^p(S^1\times S^2)\bigr)
 \setminus\operatorname{int}\nu(L_{2m}),
\]
where \(L_{2m}\) is a \(2m\)-component unlink in a ball. The port meridians
and the extra letters freely generate \(\pi_1K_v\).
At every join, the meridian on one side is the longitude on the other.
There is a finite family of framed grope bodies with boundary in these
pieces, equivariant in the cover, realizing the list
\eqref{eq:three-slot-inputs}.

If Assumption~\ref{ass:disk} holds, there are equivariant cuts, with compact
quotient, having connected vertex pieces \(V_v\) and connected edge
three-manifolds \(Y_e\). Each \(Y_e\) has as its entire boundary the prescribed
join torus. Every corresponding three-slot grope word is trivial in
\(\pi_1V_v\).

In the index-two parity quotient, these cuts give two connected vertex
pieces \(A,B\) and \(2m\) connected oriented edge pieces \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_{2m}\).
Their ambient manifold \(X_2\) is homotopy equivalent to the graph with two
vertices and \(2m\) edges, with \(p\) additional circles at each vertex.
For any characteristic-zero field \(k\), difference of restrictions gives
\begin{equation}

 H^2(A;k)\oplus H^2(B;k)
       \xrightarrow{\;\cong\;}
       \bigoplus_{i=1}^{2m}H^2(Y_i;k).
\end{equation}
In degree one it is surjective, and restricts to an isomorphism on the
kernel of evaluation on the \(p\) extra loops at each vertex.

At each boundary torus choose the two original coordinate loops
\(\alpha_i,\beta_i\) so that \(\alpha_i\) has nonzero image in
\(H_1(Y_i;k)\) and \(\beta_i\) has zero image. Such a choice is possible:
one of the original coordinate directions, not just an arbitrary slope,
is killed. Call the endpoint where \(\beta_i\) is a longitude the
\emph{plus endpoint}; there \(\alpha_i\) is the port meridian.
There are exactly \(m\) edges with plus endpoint \(A\).
After numbering these as \(1,\ldots,m\), the finite relation list includes,
at \(A\), all the required three-slot relations on any three distinct
\(\alpha_i\), and, at \(B\), those on the corresponding \(\beta_i\),
with independent conjugations by \(\mathcal C\).

statements.title: Finite tensor obstruction
statements.label: thm:tensor-obstruction
statements.text:
Let \(h=(h_1,\ldots,h_n)\) be a finite list of coordinate blocks over a
characteristic-zero field \(K\), of total dimension \(N\).  Let
\(I\subset\{1,\ldots,n\}\) have cardinality \(m\geq5\), and let
\[
 F_i\in K\langle h_i\rangle\quad(1\leq i\leq n),
 \qquad b_i\in K\langle h_i\rangle\quad(i\in I).
\]
Put
\[
 T=K[t_i:i\in I]/(t_i^2:i\in I),\qquad
 S_0(h)=\sum_{i=1}^nF_i(h_i),\qquad
 S_t(h)=S_0(h)+\sum_{i\in I}t_i b_i(h_i).
\]
Suppose there are formal parametrizations
\[
 H_L(x,t)\in (x,t)\,T[[x]]^N,\qquad
 H_R(y)\in (y)\,K[[y]]^N,
\]
where \(x\) has \(a\) coordinates and \(y\) has \(N-a\) coordinates, with
the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item The central tangent maps
 \[
  \partial_xH_L(0,0):K^a\longrightarrow K^N,\qquad
  \partial_yH_R(0):K^{N-a}\longrightarrow K^N
 \]
 are injective and have complementary images.
 \item The identities
 \[
     S_t(H_L(x,t))=0,\qquad S_0(H_R(y))=0
 \]
 hold in \(T[[x]]\) and \(K[[y]]\), respectively.
 \item For every three distinct \(i,j,k\in I\),
 \begin{align}
 t_i t_j t_k
 &\in\bigl((\partial_{h_\nu}S_t)(H_L(x,t)):
                    1\leq\nu\leq N\bigr)\subset T[[x]],
       \\
 (b_i b_j b_k)(H_R(y))
 &\in\bigl((\partial_{h_\nu}S_0)(H_R(y)):
                    1\leq\nu\leq N\bigr)\subset K[[y]].
       
 \end{align}
\end{enumerate}
Then these data do not exist.

statements.title: The marked edge potential
statements.label: prop:edge-potential
statements.text:
With the boundary polarization fixed above, there is a formal potential
$f\in\mathbb C[[h_1,\ldots,h_N]]$, where
$N=3(b_1(Y)-1)$, and a slice $s(h)$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item $f=\mathcal C(s)$ has order at least three.  Its full Jacobian
 ideal equals the curvature ideal of $s$.  The formal critical scheme
 $\Crit(f)=\Spf(S/\Jac(f))$ is the based flat-representation scheme
 with $G_\alpha=1$, and carries its marked based matrix $G_\beta$.
 \item For each fixed $T_0\in\g$ there is an affine slice with boundary
 $\tau T_0\zeta+v(h,\tau)\xi$ and adjusted potential
 \[
  f_\tau=f+\tau b
    =\mathcal C(s(h,\tau))
             +\tfrac{\epsilon}{2}\tr(\tau T_0v(h,\tau)),
  \qquad \tau^2=0.
 \]
 Its internal Jacobian ideal equals its full curvature ideal.
 Accordingly $\Crit_h(f_\tau)$ is the based flat-representation scheme
 with $G_\alpha=\exp(-\tau T_0)$.  No derivative with respect to
 $\tau$ is imposed in this relative critical scheme.
 \item On the entire, possibly nonreduced, central critical scheme,
 \begin{equation}
 
  b=\epsilon\tr(T_0v(h,0))
      =-\epsilon\tr\bigl(T_0\log G_\beta\bigr)
       \quad\bmod\Jac(f).
 \end{equation}
 The function $b$ has order at least two.  Every flat connection with
 the indicated normalized boundary value is carried uniquely to the
 corresponding slice by gauge transformations equal to the identity
 on $T$.
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: Formal potentials for a single edge

statements.title: Algebraic edge potential with markings
statements.label: thm:edge-algebraicity
statements.text:
Put \(N=\dim(H^1(C)\otimes\mathfrak{sl}_2)\),
\(R=\mathbb C[[h_1,\ldots,h_N]]\), and \(J=\Jac(f)\).
There are an invertible formal coordinate change \(x=\varphi(h)\) and an
algebraic power series \(F(x)\in(x)^3\) such that
\[
                         f(h)=F(\varphi(h)).
\]
Fix a torus basepoint and any finite collection of based loops in \(Y\).
For every matrix entry of their holonomies on the central critical scheme
\(\Spf(R/J)\), there is an algebraic power series in the \(x\)-coordinates
whose pullback is that entry.  In particular this holds for the based
\(\beta\)-holonomy.  The coordinate change can be chosen to identify these
markings on the entire, possibly nonreduced, critical scheme.

statements.title: Vertex data
statements.label: prop:vertex-data
statements.text:
Suppose that the data of Proposition~\ref{prop:geometric-reduction} exist,
with $m\geq 5$, $p\geq9$ extra letters, and the finite family of
independently conjugated boundary laws described there.  Their Brunnian
property means that omitting any slot makes the law the identity, as in
Equation~\eqref{eq:grope-word-properties}.
There are a characteristic-zero field $K$, internal coordinate blocks $h_i$
for the $2m$ edges, and algebraic power-series germs $F_i(h_i)$ and $b_i(h_i)$,
the latter for the $m$ active edges, with the following properties.
Put
\[
 T=K[t_i:i\text{ active}]/(t_i^2:i\text{ active}),\qquad
 S_0=\sum_i F_i,
 \qquad S_t=S_0+\sum_{i\text{ active}}t_i b_i.
\]
There are formal parametrizations $H_L(x,t)$ over $T$ and $H_R(y)$ over $K$
whose central tangent maps are injective and have complementary images in
the full internal coordinate space.  They are smooth graph germs over $T$
and $K$, respectively, and
\begin{equation}

 S_t(H_L)=0,\qquad S_0(H_R)=0.
\end{equation}
For every three distinct active indices $i,j,k$,
\begin{align}
 t_i t_j t_k
 &\in\left((\partial_{h_a}S_t)(H_L):a=1,\ldots,N\right)
       \subset T[[x]],                                      \\
 (b_i b_j b_k)(H_R)
 &\in\left((\partial_{h_a}S_0)(H_R):a=1,\ldots,N\right)
       \subset K[[y]],                                      
\end{align}
where $N$ is the total number of internal coordinates.  The field can be
taken to be $K=\mathbb C((\sigma))$.  The individual functions can be
normalized so that $F_i(0)=b_i(0)=0$.

statements.label: cor:vertex-tensor-interface
statements.text:
The cut data of Proposition~\ref{prop:geometric-reduction}, with
$m\geq5$ and the indicated finite law list, supply all the hypotheses
of Theorem~\ref{thm:tensor-obstruction}.

title: A negatively pinched Kähler threefold without bounded holomorphic coordinates
abstract: We construct a contractible domain in complex dimension three with a complete Kähler metric whose real sectional curvatures lie between two finite negative constants. It admits no bounded holomorphic map to ℂ<sup>3</sup> with nowhere-vanishing Jacobian and is therefore not biholomorphic to a bounded domain. This gives a negative answer to the negatively pinched Kähler uniformization question.

tex.abstract:
We construct a contractible domain in complex dimension three with a
complete K\"ahler metric whose real sectional curvatures lie between two
finite negative constants. It admits no bounded holomorphic map to
$\mathbb C^3$ with nowhere-vanishing Jacobian and is therefore not
biholomorphic to a bounded domain. This gives a negative answer to the
negatively pinched K\"ahler uniformization question.
sections: Two inputs and the bounded-map obstruction

statements.label: main:theorem
statements.text:
There exist a contractible domain $M\subset\C^3$, a smooth complete
K\"ahler metric $g$ on $M$, and finite constants $0<A\le B$ such that
\[
 -B\le K_g(\sigma)\le -A<0
\]
for every real two-plane $\sigma\subset T_pM$ and every $p\in M$.
No bounded holomorphic map $F:M\to\C^3$ has a nowhere-vanishing Jacobian
determinant. In particular, $M$ is not biholomorphic to a bounded domain
in $\C^3$.

statements.title: A controlled potential
statements.label: base:existence
statements.text:
There exist $\phi\in C^\infty(\B,\R)$ and a finite constant $C$ for
which \eqref{base:control} and \eqref{base:jets} hold with $c=1$, and
such that no $H\in\mathcal O(\B)$ and $C_H\in\R$ satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Re}H(z)
 \le C_H+4\log\frac1{1-|z|}+\phi(z)
 \qquad(z\in\B).
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Two inputs and the bounded-map obstruction

statements.title: Hartogs metric transfer
statements.label: metric:transfer
statements.text:
Let $\phi\in C^\infty(\B,\R)$ satisfy \eqref{base:control} and
\eqref{base:jets} for fixed $0<c\le C<\infty$.  There is a finite
$\lambda_0=\lambda_0(c,C)>0$ such that, for every
$\lambda\ge\lambda_0$, the domain $M_\phi$ in
\eqref{metric:domain} is contractible and the tensor
$g_\lambda=2\operatorname{Re}\widehat g_\lambda$ defined by
\eqref{metric:potential} is a smooth geodesically complete K\"ahler
metric.  For this fixed $\lambda$ there are constants
$0<A_\lambda\le B_\lambda<\infty$ such that
\[
 -B_\lambda\le K_{g_\lambda}(\sigma)\le-A_\lambda<0
\]
for every point of $M_\phi$ and every real two-plane $\sigma$ in its
tangent space.
statements.section_title: Two inputs and the bounded-map obstruction

statements.title: Uniform representing densities
statements.label: density:main
statements.text:
There is a constant $K_*>0$, depending only on the fixed profiles
$f,b$ and $R_0$, with the following property.  For every fixed
$D_0>\max\{1,2\sqrt{2R_0}\}$ there is an integer threshold $Q_0$
such that, for every integer $Q\ge Q_0$ and every choice of the
separated sets above, the recursion \eqref{density:recursion}
has the following properties for all $j\ge1$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $W_j$ is smooth and strictly positive, and $W_j\,d\sigma$
represents holomorphic evaluation at zero.  In particular it is
a probability measure.
\item Under global phase rotation, $W_j$ has frequencies only
between $-\ell_j$ and $\ell_j$, and its mean on every phase orbit
is exactly one.
\item At every point of $S$,
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
 c_0W_{j-1}\le W_j\le2W_{j-1},\\
 |ZW_j|\le K_*\sqrt{k_j}\,W_j,
 \qquad |TW_j|\le K_*k_jW_j
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
for every unit horizontal vector $Z$.
\end{enumerate}
The threshold $Q_0$ may also be enlarged to impose any fixed lower
threshold on the degrees $k_j$.

statements.title: Negative averages at one scale
statements.label: tests:negative
statements.text:
There exist $\epsilon>0$, $\eta\in(0,1/2)$ and $D_*\ge1$, depending
only on the fixed profile data, with the following property.
For every $D_0\ge D_*$ there are $k_*>0$ and $d_2>0$ such that, for
every integer $Q$ satisfying the density theorem and $Q\ge k_*$,
\begin{equation}
 \int_S U_{k_j}(r\xi)W_j(\xi)\,d\sigma\le-d_2
 \qquad
 \bigl(j\ge1,\quad 1-\eta\le r^{k_j}\le1\bigr).
\end{equation}
The constants $k_*,d_2$ may depend on $D_0$, but are independent of
$j$ and of further increases in $Q$.

title: A nine-dimensional counterexample to Borsuk's covering assertion
abstract: The compact set of rank-one orthogonal projectors on ℝ<sup>4</sup>, with the Frobenius metric, cannot be covered by ten sets of strictly smaller diameter. It therefore gives a counterexample to Borsuk's conjecture in dimension nine.

tex.abstract:
The compact set of rank-one orthogonal projectors on $\mathbb R^4$,
with the Frobenius metric, cannot be covered by ten sets of strictly
smaller diameter. It therefore gives a counterexample to Borsuk's
conjecture in dimension nine.
sections: From diameter covers to projective maps
The equality case gives a simplicial cycle

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
The compact set
\[
 X=\{uu^{\mathsf T}:u\in\mathbb R^4,\ \|u\|=1\}
 \subset\{A\in\operatorname{Sym}_4(\mathbb R):\operatorname{tr}A=1\},
\]
with the Frobenius metric, has diameter $\sqrt2$ and cannot be covered
by ten subsets of diameter strictly less than $\sqrt2$.

statements.title: The number of labels
statements.label: thm:label-bound
statements.text:
If $k\ge2$, every smooth admissible map
$f:\mathbb P(\mathbb R^k)\to\Delta^{m-1}$ satisfies $m\ge N_k$.
If $m=N_k$, its extension $F$ has mod-two degree one and is
surjective.  In this equality case, every pair of labels is an edge
of the support complex of $f$.
statements.section_title: The equality case gives a simplicial cycle

statements.title: Supports at equality
statements.label: thm:equality-complex
statements.text:
Let $k\ge3$ and $m=N_k$.  Suppose
$f:\mathbb P(\mathbb R^k)\to\Delta^{m-1}$ is a smooth admissible map.
Its support complex $K$ has every pair of labels as an edge, every
facet has $k$ vertices, and
\[
 \sum_{I\text{ a facet of }K} I
\]
is a simplicial cycle over $\mathbb F_2$.  Consequently every
$(k-2)$-dimensional face lies in a positive even number of facets.
statements.section_title: The equality case gives a simplicial cycle

statements.label: thm:no-ten-labels
statements.text: There is no admissible map $\mathbb{RP}^3\to\Delta^9$.

statements.label: cor:higher-dimensions
statements.text:
For every integer $d\geq9$, there is a compact subset of $\mathbb R^d$
of diameter $\sqrt2$ that cannot be covered by $d+1$ subsets of
strictly smaller diameter.

title: A nondegenerate counterexample to the Morse-number Arnold bound
abstract: We construct a smooth one-periodic Hamiltonian on a closed symplectic twelve-manifold whose time-one map has fewer fixed points than the manifold's ordinary Morse number. Every fixed point is nondegenerate and has a contractible Hamiltonian trajectory. This disproves the Morse-number form of the Arnold conjecture. The deficit can be arbitrarily large among twelve-dimensional examples.

tex.abstract:
We construct a smooth one-periodic Hamiltonian on a closed symplectic
twelve-manifold whose time-one map has fewer fixed points than the
manifold's ordinary Morse number. Every fixed point is nondegenerate and
has a contractible Hamiltonian trajectory. This disproves the Morse-number
form of the Arnold conjecture. The deficit can be arbitrarily large among
twelve-dimensional examples.
sections: A relative Morse model in twelve dimensions
The Morse lower bound and the deficit

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There exist a closed connected symplectic manifold $(M,\omega)$ of real
dimension twelve and a smooth one-periodic Hamiltonian $H$ such that every
fixed point of $\phi_H^1$ is nondegenerate and
\[
\#\Fix_0(\phi_H^1;H)=\#\Fix(\phi_H^1)
                   =\chi(M)+128<\Morse(M).
\]

statements.label: cor:deficit
statements.text:
For every real number $D>0$, there is an example as in
Theorem~\ref{thm:main} satisfying
\[
 \Morse(M)-\#\Fix(\phi_H^1)>D.
\]
The manifold is allowed to depend on $D$.

statements.label: prop:relative-morse
statements.text:
Let $G$ be a finite group whose right augmentation ideal in $\Z[G]$
has a generating list of length $b\geq2$.
Let $X$ be a closed connected oriented smooth four-manifold with
$\pi_1(X)\cong G$.
There is a smooth Morse function $F:X\times\R^8\to\R$ such that
\[
 F=Q\quad\text{for }r\geq 3,
 \qquad
 \#\Crit(F)=\chi(X)+4b.
\]
Its critical points have indices between four and eight.
statements.section_title: A relative Morse model in twelve dimensions

statements.label: prop:cap-transfer
statements.text:
Let $(X,\omega_X)$ be a closed connected symplectic four-manifold. Write
$(u,v)\in\R^4\times\R^4$ and set
\[
 Q(u,v)=\frac{|v|^2-|u|^2}{2},
 \qquad r^2=|u|^2+|v|^2.
\]
Suppose that $F\colon X\times\R^8\to\R$ is a smooth Morse function
such that $F=Q$ whenever $r\ge3$, and let $N=\#\Crit(F)$.
Let $\sigma$ be the standard area form of total area $4\pi$ on the unit
sphere. For every $\lambda>25/2$, the closed symplectic manifold
\[
 (M,\omega_M)=
 \left(X\times(S^2)^4,
 \omega_X+\lambda\sum_{j=1}^4\sigma_j\right)
\]
admits a Hamiltonian $H\in C^\infty((\R/\mathbb Z)\times M,\R)$ such
that every fixed point of $\phi_H^1$ is nondegenerate, every loop
$t\mapsto\phi_H^t(p)$ based at a fixed point $p$ is contractible in
$M$, and
\[
 \#\Fix_0(\phi_H^1;H)=\#\Fix(\phi_H^1)=16N.
\]
Here $\sigma_j$ denotes the pullback of $\sigma$ from the $j$th sphere,
and Hamiltonian vector fields satisfy $\omega_M(X_H,\cdot)=dH$.

title: A pointwise 2-converse for elliptic curves with rational two-torsion
abstract: We prove a pointwise 2-converse for elliptic curves over \(\mathbf Q\) with nonzero rational two-torsion: if the \(2^\infty\)-Selmer corank is zero or one, then the analytic rank and Mordell–Weil rank equal that corank, and the Shafarevich–Tate group is finite. The result allows arbitrary reduction at 2.
version_note: This version updates a citation to a revised manuscript in this collection; see the [previous version](../A-pointwise-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-with-rational-two-torsion-September-24-2026/paper.pdf).

tex.abstract:
We prove a pointwise $2$-converse for elliptic curves over $\mathbf Q$
with nonzero rational two-torsion: if the $2^\infty$-Selmer corank is
zero or one, then the analytic rank and Mordell--Weil rank equal that
corank, and the Shafarevich--Tate group is finite. The result allows
arbitrary reduction at $2$.
sections: Selmer coranks and fixed local data
Cyclotomic interpolation for extensions of trivial residual modules
Ring-class switches, determinant lattices, and transfer
Auxiliary twists with prescribed local behavior
Coefficient systems and their contraction identities

statements.title: The rational-two-torsion $2$-converse
statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $E/\Q$ be an elliptic curve with $E(\Q)[2]\ne0$ and
$s_2(E)\in\{0,1\}$. Then
\[
\ord_{s=1}L(E,s)=\rank_{\Z}E(\Q)=s_2(E),
\qquad
\Sha(E/\Q)\text{ is finite}.
\]

statements.title: Cyclotomic lower bound
statements.label: cy:lower-bound
statements.text:
There is a constant $C_E$ such that, for every allowed $h$ with
$L(E^{(h)},1)\ne0$,
\[
 v_2(\mathcal L(h))\ \geq\ 2w(h)+s(h)-C_E.
\]
The constant is independent of the number and sizes of the primes dividing
$h$.
statements.section_title: Cyclotomic interpolation for extensions of trivial residual modules

statements.title: Transfer to the missing vertex
statements.label: cy:missing-vertex
statements.text:
Let $h_0$ be an allowed discriminant with $s_2(E^{(h_0)})=0$.  Suppose that
for arbitrarily large $b$ there are a finite set $Q$ of distinct primes
$q\nmid 2Nh_0$ and linear forms
$\lambda_q:\mathbb F _2^b\longrightarrow\mathbb F _2$ giving
\[
 h_x=h_0\prod_{q\in Q}(q^*)^{\lambda_q(x)},\qquad x\in\mathbb F _2^b,
\]
all in the fixed local and sign classes.  Suppose that a number $B$,
independent of the family, satisfies
\[
 L(E^{(h_x)},1)\ne0,\qquad D(h_x)\leq B\qquad(x\ne0).
\]
Then $L(E^{(h_0)},1)\ne0$ and $D(h_0)\leq B+C_E$.
Here $C_E$ is independent of $h_0$, $Q$, and $b$; the dimension needed in
the proof is allowed to depend on the fixed precision being tested.
statements.section_title: Cyclotomic interpolation for extensions of trivial residual modules

statements.title: Central determinant formula
statements.label: cy:central
statements.text:
There is a constant $C_{\mathrm{loc}}$, depending only on the fixed curve
and local classes, with the following property.  If $s_2(E^{(h_x)})=0$,
then $u_x(0)=0$ when $L(E^{(h_x)},1)=0$.  Otherwise
\begin{equation}
 \bigl|v_2(u_x(0))-D(h_x)\bigr|\leq C_{\mathrm{loc}}.
\end{equation}
The rational positive complex at $t=0$ has cohomology only in degree one,
of dimension two, so these are specializations of the same determinant.
statements.section_title: Cyclotomic interpolation for extensions of trivial residual modules

statements.title: Ring-class lower bound
statements.label: rd:ring-lower

statements.title: The fixed-\(K\) missing-vertex implication
statements.label: rd:missing-vertex

statements.title: Finite-precision ring-class characters
statements.label: rl:characters
statements.text:
Fix finitely many split primes of $K$ above odd rational primes, outside
$2N$, and orient one prime in each conjugate pair.  There are distinct
split rational primes $r_i$ avoiding all the fixed data and characters
\[
 \xi_i:\operatorname{Gal}(H_{r_i}/K)\longrightarrow
                 \mathbf Z/2^{n_i}\mathbf Z,
 \qquad n_i\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
such that $\xi_i$ is surjective on the inertia quotient at $r_i$, is zero
at the primes above $2N$, and has odd value at each prescribed oriented
prime.  We can require $r_i\to1$ in $\mathbf Z_2$ and
\begin{equation}
 v_2(2+a_{r_i}(E)),\quad v_2(2-a_{r_i}(E)),\quad
 v_2\det(1\pm\operatorname{Fr}_{r_i}\mid T)\ \leq c_E.
\end{equation}
The constant $c_E$ is independent of the list and of $K$.

statements.title: Integral evaluation through the outer limit
statements.label: rl:outer-evaluation
statements.text:
Let $C_j$ be any family of the preceding limiting complexes, completed
over $\mathcal O_j=\widehat{\Lambda_{(2)}}$, possibly for different
quadratic fields $K_j$.  Suppose their minimal ranks are bounded.
Keep their actual evaluation matrices, and transport them through the
integral contractions to these minimal models.  For a nonprincipal
ultrafilter $\mathcal U$, put
\[
 \mathcal O_\infty=
 \left(\prod_{\mathcal U}\mathcal O_j\right)/\mathfrak a,
 \qquad
 \mathfrak a=\{(x_j):
    \{j:v_2(x_j)\geq n\}\in\mathcal U\text{ for every }n\}.
\]
Then $\mathcal O_\infty$ is a DVR with uniformizer $2$ and a
characteristic-zero fraction field $L_\infty$.  The outer complex has
an injection of its $H^1$ over $L_\infty$ into crossed classes on the
product of the inner sequence groups.  Its restriction to the product
of their exact common kernels is injective.  All arbitrary-sequence
degree-two evaluation identities survive.  These conclusions also
hold after retaining any fixed finite collection of additional
integral diagrams.

statements.title: The limit and evaluation interface
statements.label: rl:limit-evaluation-package
statements.text:
For the ring data fixed at the start of this section, retain the finite
target-side arithmetic diagrams with their maps to original cochains, homotopies,
and dualities as in Lemma~\ref{rl:finite-limits}.  The moving characters,
local conditions, and evaluation constructions then have the following
simultaneous properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Every specified finite target-side arithmetic diagram admits a bounded free
model together with maps to its original cochains; the specified
maps, homotopies and dualities survive the inner limit.
\item At the stated height-one tests the relaxed active local
complexes are acyclic, and the Selmer duality pairs degrees one
and two.  Integral Kummer conditions at $2N$ include their full
derived degree-zero invariants.
\item The residual sizes needed for the outer construction are
bounded independently of the active conductor support, with
dependence only on $E$, the bound on $\omega(\operatorname{disc}K)$,
and the number of retained derivative primes.
\item Inner and outer $H^1$ are detected by actual crossed
cocycles, including on the exact common kernel.  The evaluations
and their degree-two identities can be realized by finite
Chebotarev conditions without disturbing earlier finite data.
\end{enumerate}
These assertions do not assert an Euler-system reciprocity law or
an integral derivative class that has not first been constructed
at finite level.  Once those finite arithmetic diagrams are
constructed, this Theorem supplies their limit compatibility.

statements.title: Nonnegative valuations away from \((2)\)
statements.label: rd:away-two
statements.text:
Assume the simultaneous diagrams, derivative classes, and exact-kernel
evaluation maps of Lemmas~\ref{rl:evaluation}, \ref{rl:kernel},
\ref{rd:local-model}, and \ref{rd:derivative}.  For a primitive
constituent whose generic cohomology has rank at most one in degrees
one and two and zero elsewhere, its class-dual determinant
coordinate belongs to \(\Lambda[1/2]\).
This includes a simple-zero constituent and a base with
\(2^\infty\)-Selmer corank one.
statements.section_title: Ring-class switches, determinant lattices, and transfer

statements.title: Uniform residual valuation from outer rank reduction
statements.label: rd:outer-bound
statements.text:
Assume all of the following properties of a collection of primitive
ring instances:
\begin{enumerate}
\item after any fixed number of switches, minimal \(\mathcal O\)-models
have size bounded independently of \(h\) and of \(K\) with
\(\omega(k)\le A\);
\item the all-sequence evaluation and exact-kernel restriction of
Proposition~\ref{rl:outer-evaluation}, and the finite Chebotarev
realization of Lemma~\ref{rl:chebotarev-evaluation}, hold for these
models, retaining their degree-two cocycle identities;
\item the integral localization and duality diagrams and the
derivative classes of Lemma~\ref{rd:derivative} survive this same
outer limit; the class and its closed dual functional have a common
bounded clearing exponent.
\end{enumerate}
Then there is \(C(E,A)\) such that
\begin{equation}
 v_{(2)}(u)\ge-C(E,A)
 
\end{equation}
for every simple-zero ring instance.  The hypotheses refer to a
single simultaneous construction.  In particular, separate
abstract models realizing its individual cohomology groups do
not establish this proposition's arithmetic applicability.
statements.section_title: Ring-class switches, determinant lattices, and transfer

statements.title: The central determinant formula
statements.label: rd:central-formula
statements.text:
Suppose the product
\[
 L(E^{(h)},s)L(E^{(hk)},s)
\]
has a simple zero at \(s=1\).
Use the primitive Heegner sum \(P_h\) and its free-line index
\(j_h\) defined at the start of Section~\ref{rl:section}, and put
\[
 s(h)=\operatorname{length}_{\mathbb Z_2}
             \Sha(E^{(h)}/\mathbb Q)[2^\infty].
 \]
Use the primitive Selmer determinant coordinate \(u_h\)
with the fixed class multiplier of Lemma~\ref{rd:derivative}.
For the primitive Selmer diagrams constructed above, we have
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 v(u_h(0))
  &=2j_h-
    \operatorname{length}_{\mathbb Z_2}
                  \Sha(E^{(h)}/K)[2^\infty]
    -2\sum_{p\mid h}t_p+O_E(1)\\
  &=2j_h-s(h)-s(hk)-4w(h)+O_{E,A}(1),
       \qquad \omega(k)\le A .
 \end{split}
 
\end{equation}
The first error includes the auxiliary prime and the fixed
parametrization multiplier.  The second has no dependence
on the number of primes dividing \(h\).
statements.section_title: Ring-class switches, determinant lattices, and transfer

statements.title: The bounded clearing factor for the family
statements.label: rd:family-clearing
statements.text:
Assume the compatible universal Selmer and Heegner
diagrams and their primitive specializations.
Suppose every character constituent of the universal Selmer complex
is generically acyclic or has generic
cohomology of dimension one in degrees one and two and zero
elsewhere.  If the fixed base has \(2^\infty\)-Selmer corank
one over \(K\), the corrected coordinates of
Lemma~\ref{rd:unused} admit the factorization
\eqref{rd:clearing-equations}, with central
valuation and fixed-precision pole bounds
independent of \(b\) and \(\#Q\).
statements.section_title: Ring-class switches, determinant lattices, and transfer

statements.title: Assembly of the arithmetic diagrams
statements.label: rd:assembly
statements.text:
For the ring data stated at the start of this section, the actual
finite Heegner and Selmer constructions satisfy the simultaneous
diagram hypotheses of Propositions~\ref{rd:away-two},
\ref{rd:outer-bound}, and \ref{rd:central-formula}.
The bounds needed for the lower-bound argument depend only on
\(E\), the fixed local data, and a bound \(A\) on \(\omega(k)\).
For the binary data \eqref{rd:binary-data} with fixed \(E,K\)
and base Selmer corank one, assume in addition that every
character constituent of the universal Selmer complex is generically acyclic
or has generic cohomology of
dimension one in degrees one and two and zero elsewhere.
Then the constructions satisfy all the hypotheses of
Proposition~\ref{rd:family-clearing}, with
bounds independent of the cube dimension and of its
new-prime support.
statements.section_title: Ring-class switches, determinant lattices, and transfer

statements.title: Local witnesses
statements.label: nv:local-witness
statements.text:
Fix an elliptic curve $A/\Q$ and a nonempty filter of fundamental
discriminants prime to $2N_A$, with specified real sign and unit
squareclasses at finitely many primes. If the root number in the filter
is $+1$, it contains $d$ of arbitrarily large absolute value with
$L(A^{(d)},1)\ne0$.
If the root number is $-1$, it contains such $d$ with
$L'(A^{(d)},1)\ne0$. Any additional finite set of primes may be excluded.
statements.section_title: Auxiliary twists with prescribed local behavior

statements.title: Bounded-factor completion
statements.label: nv:rough
statements.text:
There is an absolute integer $A_0$ with the following property.
In the positive-root-number case of Proposition~\ref{nv:local-witness},
one can require $\omega(d)\le A_0$ and require every prime divisor of
$d$ to exceed any fixed bound.
The size threshold for the resulting $d$ may depend on the curve, the
filter, and the excluded primes; $A_0$ does not.
statements.section_title: Auxiliary twists with prescribed local behavior

statements.title: Even coefficient system
statements.label: co:even
statements.text:
Fix an even-sign filter and a nonvanishing index $D_0$ in it.
There is a holomorphic cuspidal form $g=\sum_{n\geq1}a(n)q^n$ of weight
$3/2$, orthogonal to unary theta series, of level supported on a fixed
enlargement of $S$, and characters $\eta,\psi$ of $2$-power order such that
$\psi/\eta=\chi_{-\sigma}$ and
\begin{equation}
 a(p^2n)=\bigl(\eta(p)a_p(E)-\psi(p)(-n/p)\bigr)a(n)
              -p\eta(p)^2a(n/p^2)\qquad(p\notin S).
\end{equation}
Its coefficients are zero off the unit-squareclass filter.  After
normalization at $D_0$, every squarefree coefficient is rational up to a
$2$-power root of unity.  For two nonzero squarefree coefficients,
\begin{equation}
 2v\!\left(\frac{a(D)}{a(D_0)}\right)
   =v\!\left(\frac{L_*(\sigma D)}{L_*(\sigma D_0)}\right).
\end{equation}
Moreover $a(D)\neq0$ exactly when $L(E^{(\sigma D)},1)\neq0$.
Consequently any previously established bound
$v(L_*(\sigma D))\geq2w(D)+s(\sigma D)-C$ gives
\begin{equation}
 v(a(D))\geq w(D)+\tfrac12s(\sigma D)-C_g
\end{equation}
with $C_g$ fixed independently of $D$.
statements.section_title: Coefficient systems and their contraction identities

statements.title: Odd coefficient detection
statements.label: co:odd
statements.text:
The forms in Lemma~\ref{co:theta-bridge}, after a fixed adjustment of
precision, satisfy
\[
 v(a_M(D))\geq\min\{M,j(P_D)-C\},\qquad
 v(a_M(D))<M\ \Longrightarrow\ j(P_D)\leq v(a_M(D))+C.
\]
A visible coefficient detects $a(E^{(D)})=1$, and a fixed positive
witness has bounded coefficient valuation as $M\to\infty$.
All constants are independent of $M,\ell,D$.
statements.section_title: Coefficient systems and their contraction identities

statements.title: Symbol interface
statements.label: co:symbol-interface
statements.text:
Under the arithmetic lower bounds in Lemma~\ref{co:minimum}, the
symbols of either coefficient source have the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For matching $U$, the trace on split elements factors through
the maximal elementary $2$-extension of $F$ unramified outside
$S\cup U$.  For opposite $U$, traces factor through the corresponding
rational elementary extension.  Adding a split vertex $q$ is read
by coefficient $1$ of $t(\operatorname{Fr}_q)H_U$; adding a simple
vertex is read on the opposite $B_U$.
\item Let $p\in U$ and $g=\operatorname{Fr}_q$.  Changing one
oriented ramification bit at $p$ changes the symbol by
\begin{equation}
 A\bigl((U\setminus\{p\})\cup\{q'\}\bigr),\qquad
 \operatorname{Fr}_{q'}\sim g\phi_p,
\end{equation}
unless $p,q$ are both simple, in which case the change is zero.
The replacement has the product labels at all retained places.
Its coefficient system has support $S\cup(U\setminus\{p\})$:
the entire rational prime $p$, including both places above it when
it splits in $F$, is omitted.
\item A split vertex with trivial label in the elementary extension
for the other vertices has zero symbol.
\item In matching parity, insertion of two simple primes with equal
rational labels on the fixed support and at the existing split
vertices preserves the symbol if
$\#E(\mathbb F_q)/2$ is odd for that label.  Their mutual simple
bits and their incidences with other simple vertices do not affect
this statement.
\end{enumerate}
These are coefficient identities.  Simultaneous realization of
their labels by primes is a separate arithmetic construction.
statements.section_title: Coefficient systems and their contraction identities

statements.title: Address lemma
statements.label: gr:address
statements.text:
Suppose the binary symbols under consideration depend only on the
arithmetic graph data and satisfy the contraction, whole-rational-prime
omission, and primary-isolation rules of
Proposition~\ref{co:symbol-interface}, with the realization freedoms
of Lemma~\ref{gr:realization}.  Contraction includes the product labels
and external incidences, and the zero rule for two simple vertices.
These identities are required only on nonempty configurations and for
contractions with nonempty output.
Fix $b\ge1$ and either of the following terminal arrangements.
\begin{enumerate}
\item One symbol, a nonempty set of always active terminals, and a
nonzero polynomial in their independent pair bits.
\item One or two symbols on terminals with nonzero linear activations,
including at least one terminal for every nonzero linear form.  At each
$x\ne0$ each symbol separately is a nonzero polynomial in the active
terminal bits.  The symbols may read different compatible projections
of a common graph alphabet and may have fixed stationary external data.
\end{enumerate}
Suppose also that at each nonzero address the total active terminal data,
together with any stationary external data, obey the required filter.
Starting from any fixed realization of the terminal and stationary
vertices, one can adjoin finitely many fresh primary auxiliary vertices,
activated by nonzero linear forms, and choose only incidences involving
these new vertices so that every symbol equals $1$ at every $x\ne0$.
All data on the original vertices remain unchanged.  No auxiliary is
present at $0$.  All auxiliaries may satisfy the fixed splitting and
neutral external-incidence conditions incorporated into the primary type.

It is enough that a terminal polynomial have a nonzero evaluation or
a nonzero iterated edge difference.  In particular a partitionability
certificate suffices for the stationary hypothesis.

statements.title: Collected interfaces
statements.label: pw:interfaces
statements.text:
The following statements hold for the fixed curve and fixed local data.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The cyclotomic missing-vertex statement of
Theorem~\ref{cy:missing-vertex} applies to any fixed base $h_0$ of Selmer
corank zero.  If arbitrarily large binary cubes based at $h_0$, with no old
prime removed, have nonzero central values at every other address and satisfy
\[
 v(L_*(h_x))-2w(h_x)-s(h_x)\le B\quad(x\ne0),
\]
then the base central value is nonzero and satisfies the same inequality
with $B$ replaced by $B+C$.  The constant $C$ depends only on the fixed curve
and local data, not on $h_0$, its number of prime factors, or the cube
dimension.  The dimension required for the argument may depend on the base.
The cyclotomic lower bound at an analytically nonvanishing parameter is also
available.
\item Corollary~\ref{rd:ring-lower} has the following uniform form.  If
$k<0$ is an odd fundamental discriminant with at most $A$ prime factors,
$K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{k})$ is neither an extra-unit field nor the CM field,
$k$ is a square at $2Nh$, and the twists $h,hk$ have respective analytic
orders one and zero, then their ring-class Heegner sum has free-line index
$j_h(k)$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
 2j_h(k)\ge 4w(h)+s(h)+s(hk)-C_{E,A}.
\end{equation}
For a fixed such $k$, Theorem~\ref{rd:missing-vertex} applies to
cubes based at $h=1$ whose new primes all split in $K$.  If
$s_2(E/K)=1$ and the nonzero addresses have product analytic order one and
uniformly bounded
$2j_h(k)-4w(h)-s(h)-s(hk)$, the base product has analytic order one.
\item The even coefficient system, exact same-filter square comparison,
divided operators, and trace identities of
Proposition~\ref{co:even} and Lemmas~\ref{co:operators},
\ref{co:traces}, and \ref{co:inertia} are available.
After a uniform lower bound for the relevant point indices has been proved,
the moving odd coefficient system and its stabilized minimum are available
as in Proposition~\ref{co:odd} and Lemma~\ref{co:minimum}.  The resulting unit symbols
satisfy the contraction, good-twin, and primary-isolation rules of
Proposition~\ref{co:symbol-interface}.  An even unit gives
\begin{equation}
 L_*(h)\ne0,\qquad v(L_*(h))\le 2w(h)+C;
\end{equation}
an odd unit gives analytic order one and
\begin{equation}
 j(P_h)\le w(h)+C.
\end{equation}
The constants are independent of the number and sizes of the variable
primes.  The fixed genus partner used to define $P_h$ is denoted $h_*$.
\item Arithmetic realization and the forest and address statements of
Lemmas~\ref{gr:realization} and \ref{gr:forest} and
Theorem~\ref{gr:address} hold.
In particular, separate nonzero terminal polynomials may be addressed
simultaneously.  Primary auxiliaries preserve all fixed local classes,
have neutral incidence to specified stationary external vertices, and may
be required to split in any compatible fixed fields.  They contribute no
prime at address zero.
\end{enumerate}

A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for Three-Machine Unit-Job Scheduling
abstract: We give a uniform deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for scheduling unit-length jobs with arbitrary precedence constraints on three identical parallel machines. The algorithm constructs a schedule of minimum makespan and decides exactly whether all jobs can finish by a specified deadline. The proof reorganizes feasible schedules into intervals whose job sets have descriptions of bounded size. A dynamic program searches a family containing polynomially many such descriptions. Global boundary conditions and simplification of inherited information keep the descriptions bounded throughout the decomposition.

tex.abstract:
We give a uniform deterministic polynomial-time algorithm for scheduling
unit-length jobs with arbitrary precedence constraints on three identical
parallel machines. The algorithm constructs a schedule of minimum makespan
and decides exactly whether all jobs can finish by a specified deadline.
The proof reorganizes feasible schedules
into intervals whose job sets have descriptions of bounded size.
A dynamic program searches a family containing polynomially many such
descriptions. Global boundary conditions and simplification of inherited
information keep the descriptions bounded throughout the decomposition.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let an explicitly listed finite directed acyclic graph specify the
precedence constraints on \(n\ge1\) nonpreemptive unit-length jobs
on three identical machines. There is a uniform deterministic algorithm
that constructs a feasible schedule of minimum makespan.
Given also an integer deadline \(1\le T\le n\), it decides feasibility
exactly and returns a schedule whenever the answer is affirmative.
Both tasks can be performed in
\(O((L+2)^{150020})\) steps on a deterministic multitape Turing machine,
where \(L\) is the total binary input length.

statements.label: prop:algorithm
statements.text:
This is a uniform deterministic polynomial-time algorithm. Every set it
accepts has a full schedule, which the algorithm can explicitly return.
With \(K=10000\), its deadline decision and schedule construction take
\(O((L+2)^{150020})\) deterministic multitape steps.

statements.title: Hierarchy bound for the metric test cone
statements.label: thm:tg-hierarchy
statements.text:
There is an absolute integer $h_0$ such that, for every integer
$h\ge h_0$, every locally $h$-connected hierarchy of $G$, and every
collection $\mathcal M$ of nonroot nodes satisfying
$|O(A)|\ge |P(A)|/h$, there is a matrix $D\succ0$ on $\mathsf E$ with
\begin{align}
 \ip{D}{Z}&\le\ip{L_G}{Z} &&(Z\in\mathcal N),\\
 \frac1{|O(A)|}\sum_{e\in O(A)}b_e^TD^{-1}b_e
 &\le h^{-31/40} &&(A\in\mathcal M).
\end{align}
The cutoff is independent of the graph and the hierarchy depth.

statements.title: Simultaneous response
statements.label: prop:tg-response
statements.text:
Let $H$ be connected and let $G\subseteq H$ be a spanning subgraph.
Let $r$ be a sufficiently large integer, put $h=\lfloor r/2\rfloor$,
and suppose $G$ and the subgraphs induced by all parts of a nested
sequence of partitions are $h$-edge-connected, with the singleton
condition vacuous.  If $0<s\le r^{1/4}$, there is $Y\in\mathcal K_H$
such that, at every partition $\mathcal P$ in the sequence, all but
at most $r^{-1/3}|E_G(\mathcal P)|$ crossing edges satisfy
\begin{equation}
 Y\succeq6s\,b_eb_e^T.
\end{equation}
Here $E_G(\mathcal P)$ denotes the edges whose endpoints lie in
different parts of $\mathcal P$.

statements.title: Constructive shortcut extraction
statements.label: prop:ta-extraction
statements.text:
There are absolute constants $A$ and $r_0$ such that the following holds.
If an explicit multigraph $H$ on at least two vertices contains $r\ge r_0$
edge-disjoint spanning trees, one can deterministically compute a rational
$X\in\mathcal K_H$ and at least
\[
                 (1-Ar^{-1/16})r
\]
edge-disjoint spanning trees, every edge $e$ of which satisfies
$b_e^TX^{-1}b_e\le r^{-1/4}$. The running time and output encoding length
are polynomial in $|V(H)|+|E(H)|$.

statements.title: Thin and cheap rounding of fractional cuts
statements.label: cor:ta-fractional-rounding
statements.text:
Fix once and for all an integer $B\ge\max\{1,C\}$, where $C$ is the
constant in Theorem~\ref{thm:tt-algorithm}. Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite undirected
graph on $n\ge2$ vertices, given by an explicit list of edge records;
in this corollary, loops and parallel records are allowed. Given
nonnegative rational numbers $x_e,c_e$ in binary, suppose that
\[
 x(\delta_G(S)):=\sum_{e\in\delta_G(S)}x_e\ge1
       \qquad(\varnothing\ne S\subsetneq V).
\]
There is a deterministic algorithm, polynomial in the total binary
input length, that returns a spanning tree
$T\subseteq\{e\in E:x_e>0\}$ satisfying simultaneously
\begin{align}
 |\delta_T(S)|&\le24B\,x(\delta_G(S))
       &&(\varnothing\ne S\subsetneq V),
       \\
 c(T):=\sum_{e\in T}c_e&\le24B\sum_{e\in E}c_ex_e.
       
\end{align}
The cut inequalities are a promise on the input; no metric assumption
on the costs is required.

statements.title: Rational rank-one signing
statements.label: thm:rational-signing
statements.text:
Given rational Hermitian matrices $H_1,\ldots,H_N$ of rank at most one,
a deterministic algorithm returns signs $\sigma_i\in\{-1,1\}$ such that
\[
 \left\|\sum_i\sigma_iH_i\right\|
 \le40\left\|\sum_iH_i^2\right\|^{1/2}.
\]
Its running time is polynomial in the total binary encoding length.
Consequently, for rational columns $v_i$ with $\sum_i v_iv_i^*=I$,
the same algorithm gives discrepancy at most
$40\sqrt{\max_i\|v_i\|^2}$.

title: A positive solution to Tingley’s problem
abstract: Every surjective isometry between the unit spheres of real Banach spaces extends uniquely to a surjective real-linear isometry, giving an affirmative solution to Tingley's problem. If distances between different radii are not preserved, we realize the positive maximal defect in a possibly enlarged pair of Banach spaces. We then align extremal chords using common supports and Darbo's fixed-point theorem and obtain a contradiction from support and convexity estimates.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $X,Y$ be nonzero real Banach spaces and let $f:S_X\to S_Y$ be a surjective isometry. Then
\[
T(0)=0,\qquad T(x)=\norm{x}f\left(\frac{x}{\norm{x}}\right)\quad(x\ne0)
\]
is a surjective real-linear isometry. It is the unique linear extension of $f$.

\[
\chi(g(H))\le\gamma\chi(H)\qquad(H\subset C),
\]
then $g$ has a fixed point.

title: A power improvement in the Heilbronn triangle lower bound
abstract: There are absolute constants \(\eta,c_1\gt 0\) such that, for every sufficiently large integer n, one can choose n points in the unit square so that every triangle they determine has area at least \(c_1n^{-2+\eta}\). Thus the almost n−2 upper-bound formulation of Heilbronn's triangle problem is false. The exponent η is fixed but extremely small.

tex.abstract:
There are absolute constants $\eta,c_1>0$ such that, for every sufficiently
large integer $n$, one can choose $n$ points in the unit square so that every
triangle they determine has area at least $c_1n^{-2+\eta}$.
Thus the almost $n^{-2}$ upper-bound formulation of Heilbronn's triangle
problem is false. The exponent $\eta$ is fixed but extremely small.

statements.label: lat:fixed-det
statements.text:
Let $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb Z^3$ have index $I$, let $X\ge2$, and
suppose its third successive length satisfies $\lambda_3\le X$.
For every $t\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$, the number of $3$ by $3$
matrices with rows in $\Lambda$, row lengths at most $X$, and
determinant $t$ is at most
\[
 C\bigl(\log(2X)\bigr)^2\frac{X^6}{I^2}.
\]
The constant is absolute.

statements.label: aux:weights
statements.text:
For the distribution in \eqref{aux:set-definition}, with
$s=|S|\ge1$, the following bounds hold with absolute constants:
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 W(A)&\ll1
   &&\text{if the columns of }A\bmod q\text{ are affinely independent},\\
 W(A)&\ll q^3/s
   &&\text{if }\operatorname{rank}(A\bmod q)\ge2,\\
 W(A)&\ll(q^3/s)^2
   &&\text{for every }A.
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
If $W(A)>0$, no column of $A\bmod q$ is zero, and its columns are
either affinely independent or include two equal columns.  For an
affinely independent triple with $W(A)>0$, there is no nonzero
$x\in\mathbb Z^3$ with $|x|\le H$ and $Ax=0\bmod q$.

columns lie in $\mathcal B$, whose projected columns are pairwise
distinct, and which satisfy $A\bmod h\in\mathcal O$ and $\det A=t$.
Then
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{A\in\mathcal A_t}W(A)
 \ll (\log(2N))^2\frac{N^6}{I^2}.

title: A power saving for intersective polynomial differences with an exponent depending only on the degree
abstract: An integer polynomial is intersective if it has a root modulo every positive integer. For each degree k ≥ 2, we prove that there is an exponent \(c_k\gt 0\) such that every set \(A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}\) whose differences avoid all nonzero values \(h(1),h(2),\ldots\), where h is an intersective polynomial of degree k with positive leading coefficient, satisfies \(|A|=O_h(N^{1-c_k})\). The implied constant may depend on h, but the power-saving exponent depends only on its degree.

tex.abstract:
An integer polynomial is intersective if it has a root modulo every positive
integer. For each degree $k\ge2$, we prove that there is an exponent $c_k>0$
such that every set $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ whose differences avoid all nonzero values $h(1),h(2),\ldots$,
where $h$ is an intersective polynomial of degree $k$ with positive leading
coefficient, satisfies
$|A|=O_h(N^{1-c_k})$. The implied constant may depend on $h$, but the
power-saving exponent depends only on its degree.
sections: A signed kernel for polynomial differences
Exceptional terms and the power-saving induction

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every integer $k\ge2$, there is a constant $c_k\in(0,1)$ with the
following property. For every intersective polynomial $h\in\Z[x]$ of degree
$k$ with positive leading coefficient, there are a constant $C_h\ge1$ and an
integer $N_h\ge1$ such that, whenever $N\ge N_h$ and $A\subseteq[N]$ satisfy
\[
 (A-A)\cap h(\N_+)\subseteq\{0\},
\]
one has
\[
 |A|\le C_h N^{1-c_k}.
\]

statements.label: tuple:laws
statements.text:
For all sufficiently large primes $p$, uniformly in $l\ge1$, define
\begin{align*}
 M_{l,p}&=\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq[w]\\|S|\le t+1}}
                 p^{-|S|\delta/2}\nu_{l,p,S},\\
 \mu_{l,p}&=\frac{M_{l,p}}{M_{l,p}(1)},\\
 \eps_{l,p}&=\frac{1}{M_{l,p}(1)}
       \sum_{|S|=t+1}p^{-(t+1)\delta/2}\nu_{l,p,S}.
\end{align*}
Then $\mu_{l,p}$ is a reflection-positive probability law and
$0\le\eps_{l,p}\le\mu_{l,p}$.  Its exceptional mass satisfies
\[
 \eta_{l,p}:=\eps_{l,p}(1)\le p^{-4}.
\]
The probability law
\[
 \mu_{l,p}^{\circ}
       =\frac{\mu_{l,p}-\eps_{l,p}}{1-\eta_{l,p}}
\]
has only admissible increments $z_{v_{j+1}}-z_{v_j}$ along the
designated cycle.  Every component and both measures $\mu_{l,p}$,
$\eps_{l,p}$ are invariant under simultaneous translation of all
labels.  Every positive-mass component or subsum therefore has uniform
single-slot marginals after normalization.  In either $\mu_{l,p}$ or
$\mu_{l,p}^{\circ}$, the total probability of components with
$S\ne\varnothing$ is $O(p^{-\delta/2})$.

statements.title: Dependence of the prime threshold
statements.label: tuple:threshold-dependence
statements.text:
For the auxiliary family and local choices above, the threshold $P$ can
be chosen as a function of $k,P_1,L,t$ alone so that
Proposition~\ref{tuple:laws}, Lemmas~\ref{tuple:covariance}
and~\ref{tuple:conditional-mixing}, and \eqref{eq:9} hold uniformly in
$l$.  For general fixed data, $P_1$ may depend on $h$, and $L$ may depend
on $h$ and its chosen roots.  If $h$ satisfies Condition~\eqref{local:unit-condition}
and the degree-dependent choices of $P_1$, $E_p$, and $L$ from
Section~\ref{sec:local} are used, then $P$ and $M_0$ depend only on $k$.

statements.title: Signed H\"older inequality
statements.label: lift:signed-holder
statements.text:
For every positive integer \(l\), finite set \(\mathcal P\) of primes
at least \(P\), and real functions \(g,g_v:X_{\mathcal P}\to\R\),
\begin{equation}
 Z_{l,\mathcal P}(g)\ge0,
 \qquad
 \left|\mathcal Z_{l,\mathcal P}((g_v)_{v\in V})\right|
 \le\prod_{v\in V} Z_{l,\mathcal P}(g_v)^{1/d}.
 
\end{equation}

statements.title: Uniform lift moments
statements.label: lift:moments
statements.text:
Let \(\mathcal P\) be any finite set of primes, \(Q\ge1\), and let
\(I\) be a consecutive integer interval with \(|I|\ge10Q^6\).
For every integer \(r\ge1\), every \(\epsilon>0\), every function
\(f:I\to\C\), and every subfamily
\(\mathcal F\subseteq\{B\subseteq\mathcal P:q_B\le Q\}\),
\begin{equation}
 \left\|\sum_{B\in\mathcal F}f_B\right\|_{2r}
 \le C_{r,\epsilon}\|f\|_\infty Q^\epsilon.
 
\end{equation}
The constant is independent of the prime set, the interval and its
location, the function, and the subfamily.

statements.title: Density domination and a uniform upper bound
statements.label: lift:density
statements.text:
For all positive integers \(l,N\) and all \(A\subseteq[N]\),
\[
 Y_l(N,A)\ge\left(\frac{|A|}{N}\right)^d\ge0.
\]
For every \(\epsilon>0\), there is a constant \(C_\epsilon\),
independent of \(l,N,A\), such that
\[
 Y_l(N,A)\le C_\epsilon N^\epsilon.
\]

statements.title: Ordered polynomial-kernel estimate
statements.label: kernel:estimate
statements.text:
Use the fixed parameters in~\eqref{eq:14}, and let $N$ be a sufficiently
large integer. Suppose $1\le l\le N^\zeta$ and
\[
 D=M_0\prod_{p\in B}p\le N^\beta,
\]
where $B$ is a finite set of primes at least $P$. Let
$J_1,J_2:[N]\to\C$ satisfy $|J_1|,|J_2|\le1$ and be supported in
residue classes $a_1,a_2$ modulo $D$, respectively. Suppose that
$r=a_2-a_1$ is admissible for $l$ modulo $D$, that $x<y$ whenever
$x\in\operatorname{supp}J_1$ and $y\in\operatorname{supp}J_2$, and
that no such difference $y-x$ belongs to $F(\N_+)$.
Put $H=N^{\beta/2}$ and
\[
 \Xi=\{\xi\in\Q/\Z:q(\xi)\le H,\quad q(\xi)\text{ squarefree},
                         \quad(q(\xi),D)=1\}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 D\left|\sum_{\xi\in\Xi}\Gamma(\xi)
          \widehat{J_1}_{[N]}(-\xi)\widehat{J_2}_{[N]}(\xi)\right|
 \ll H^{-\gamma/2}.
 
\end{equation}
The implied constant and the threshold for $N$ depend only on the fixed
polynomial and the fixed parameters, not on $l,D,r,J_1,J_2$.
statements.section_title: A signed kernel for polynomial differences

statements.title: Shorter-scale comparison
statements.label: transfer:shorter-scale
statements.text:
Let $N$ be sufficiently large, let $l\ge1$, and let $A\subseteq[N]$
satisfy \eqref{eq:24}.  Suppose that $B\subseteq\mathcal P_N$ and
$q_B\le N^\tau$.  Set
\begin{gather*}
 \mathcal S=\mathcal P_N\setminus B,
 \qquad D=M_0q_B,
 \qquad L_D=\lambda(D),\\
 n_B=\left\lceil\frac{N}{L_D}\right\rceil,
 \qquad \Lambda_B=\frac{L_Dn_B}{N}.
\end{gather*}
For each $v\in V$, choose $s_v\in\Z/M_0\Z$ and specialize $G_{s_v}$
at an arbitrary vector of coordinates on $B$, obtaining a function $g_v$
on $X_{\mathcal S}$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \bigl|\mathcal Z_{l,\mathcal S}((g_v)_{v\in V})\bigr|
 \le \Lambda_B^d\mathcal Y_{lD}(n_B)+O(N^{-\sigma}).
\end{equation}
The scale and the rounding factor satisfy $1\le n_B<N$ and
\begin{equation}
 1\le\Lambda_B\le1+M_0^kN^{k\tau-1}.
\end{equation}
The implied constant and the threshold for $N$ are independent of
$l,A,B$ and all specializations.

statements.title: Cancellation on good assignments
statements.label: transfer:cancellation
statements.text:
Let $N$ be sufficiently large, let $l\le N^\zeta$, and let
$A\subseteq[N]$ satisfy \eqref{eq:24}.  If $(s_v)_{v\in V}$ is good
for $l$, then
\begin{equation}
 \left|
  \int\prod_{v\in V}G_{s_v}(z_v)\,
    d\bigotimes_{p\in\mathcal P_N}
       (\mu_{l,p}-\eps_{l,p})
 \right|\ll N^{-\sigma}.
\end{equation}
The bound is uniform in $l,A$ and the good assignment.

statements.title: Recurrence for the maximal functional
statements.label: induction:recurrence
statements.section_title: Exceptional terms and the power-saving induction

statements.title: Decay throughout the auxiliary family
statements.label: induction:decay
statements.text:
There are constants $a_0,b_0>0$ and $C_0\ge1$, depending only on the fixed
polynomial $h$, its chosen roots, and the fixed structural choices, such that
for all positive integers $l,N$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal Y_l(N)\le C_0l^{b_0}N^{-a_0}.
 
\end{equation}
The exponents $a_0,b_0$ can be chosen as functions only of the structural
parameters $k,\zeta,\sigma,M_0,\rho_*$.  If the chosen roots of $h$
satisfy Condition~\eqref{local:unit-condition} and the choices depending
only on $k$ from Sections~\ref{sec:local} and~\ref{sec:tuples} are used, then
$a_0,b_0,d$ depend only on $k$, while $C_0$ may still depend on the fixed data.
