title: A spectral gap throughout the high-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick phase
abstract: For every fixed inverse temperature \(0\lt \beta\lt 1\), we prove that the unscaled spectral gap of single-site heat-bath dynamics for the zero-field Gaussian Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model is bounded away from zero with probability tending to one over the disorder. Equivalently, the Gibbs law satisfies a dimension-free Poincaré inequality for all functions.

tex.abstract:
For every fixed inverse temperature $0<\beta<1$, we prove that the unscaled
spectral gap of single-site heat-bath dynamics for the zero-field Gaussian
Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model is bounded away from zero with probability
tending to one over the disorder. Equivalently, the Gibbs law satisfies a
dimension-free Poincar\'e inequality for all functions.
sections: The theorem and the structure of the proof
From posterior estimates to a spectral gap
Weak residual identities and discrete differentiation
Posterior estimates at a stable field
The spectral gap at a large observation time

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is a finite constant $C_\beta$, depending only on $\beta$, such that
\[
 \Prob_J\left\{\Var_{\mu_0}(f)\le C_\beta\D_0(f)
       \text{ for every }f:\{-1,1\}^n\longrightarrow\R\right\}
 \longrightarrow1.
\]
Consequently, the discrete-time heat-bath chain that chooses a uniform site
has spectral gap at least $1/(C_\beta n)$ with probability tending to one.
statements.section_title: The theorem and the structure of the proof

statements.title: Stability along observations
statements.label: prop:stable-fields
statements.text:
Fix $j\in(0,1)$ and $0<T<\infty$.  There are constants
$\eta,c,\epsilon_A,\rho_0,a>0$, depending only on $j,T$, and events
$\mathcal J_n$ for the zero-diagonal Gaussian matrix $J$, such that
$\Prob(J\in\mathcal J_n)\longrightarrow1$ and the following assertion
holds for every $J\in\mathcal J_n$.  Let $X\sim\mu_0$, let $B_0$ be an
independent standard $n$-dimensional Brownian motion, and put
$Y(t)=tX+B_0(t)$.  With conditional probability at least $1-e^{-an}$,
simultaneously for $0\le t\le T$, $y\in\R^n$, and all diagonal $A$,
\begin{equation}
 \left.
 \begin{gathered}
 \norm{F_{J,Y(t)}(y)}\le2\rho_0\sqrt n,\\
 0\le A\le(1+\eta)I,\qquad
 \norm{A-V_y}_{\Frob}\le\epsilon_A\sqrt n
 \end{gathered}
 \right\}
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \mathsf H_J(y,A)\succ cI.
 
\end{equation}
We may require $j(1+\eta)^2<1$ and
$\norm J\le2\sqrt j+\theta$ on $\mathcal J_n$, for any sufficiently
small fixed $\theta>0$ chosen in the proof.

statements.title: Stopping formulation
statements.label: cor:stopping
statements.text:
For every $J\in\mathcal J_n$ there is an observation stopping time $\tau_0$
such that
\[
 \Prob(\tau_0\le T\mid J)\le e^{-an},
\]
and, for every $t\in[0,T]$ with $t<\tau_0$, the implication \eqref{eq:stable-field} holds
at $Y(t)$ with residual threshold $\rho_0\sqrt n$ in place of
$2\rho_0\sqrt n$. The stopping rule depends on $J$ and the observations,
and is independent of any test function.

statements.title: Terminal observation gap
statements.label: prop:terminal-gap
statements.text:
Fix $j\in(0,1)$.  There are finite $T>0$, $c>0$, and events
$\mathcal E_n^{\mathrm{term}}$ depending only on $J$, with
$\Prob_J(\mathcal E_n^{\mathrm{term}})\to1$, such that the following holds
for every sufficiently large $n$ and every $J\in\mathcal E_n^{\mathrm{term}}$.
Let $X$ have any probability law on $\{-1,1\}^n$, possibly depending on
$J$, and let $Z$ be an independent standard Gaussian vector.  Set
$Y=TX+\sqrt T\,Z$.  Then, conditionally on $J$, except on an event of
probability at most $e^{-cn}$, the inequality
\begin{equation}
 \Var_{\mu_Y}(f)\le 2\D_Y(f)
 
\end{equation}
holds simultaneously for every real function $f$ on the cube.
All constants and matrix events are independent of the law of $X$.

title: A stable coordinate that is not a coordinate in four variables
abstract: We construct an explicit degree-five polynomial over \(\mathbf C\) that is not a coordinate in four variables but becomes one after adjoining a single variable. This gives a counterexample to the stable coordinate conjecture in four variables. Every fiber is isomorphic to affine three-space, yet its embedding in affine four-space is not rectifiable. Thus the example also disproves the Abhyankar–Sathaye embedding conjecture in ambient dimension four.

tex.abstract:
We construct an explicit degree-five polynomial over $\C$ that is not a
coordinate in four variables but becomes one after adjoining a single variable.
This gives a counterexample to the stable coordinate conjecture in four
variables. Every fiber is isomorphic to affine three-space, yet its embedding
in affine four-space is not rectifiable. Thus the example also disproves the
Abhyankar--Sathaye embedding conjecture in ambient dimension four.
sections: Lifting the obstruction to a line bundle

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
In $R=\C[x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4]$, put
\begin{equation}
 Q=x_2^2-x_4^2+x_1x_3,
 \qquad
 f=x_1-2Q\bigl(Q(x_2+x_4)+x_1x_4\bigr).
\end{equation}
There is a $\C$-algebra automorphism of $R[w]$ sending $f$ to $x_1$, but there is no such automorphism of $R$.

statements.label: cor:fibers
statements.text: For every $\lambda\in\C$, the hypersurface $f^{-1}(\lambda)\subset\A^4$ is isomorphic to $\A^3$ and its embedding in $\A^4$ is not rectifiable.

statements.label: prop:polynomial
statements.text:
There are polynomial coordinates $p',s',F',J$ on $A$ such that
\begin{equation}
 x=(s')^2-J^2+p'F',\qquad
 p=p'-2x\bigl(x(s'+J)+p'J\bigr).
\end{equation}
Thus, under the identification $(p',s',F',J)=(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)$,
the element $p$ is the polynomial $f$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.

statements.label: prop:stable
statements.text:
For an independent variable $w$, the ring $A[w]$ is a polynomial ring in
five variables with $p$ as one of its coordinates.

statements.label: prop:fibers
statements.text:
For every $\lambda\in k$, the quotient $A/(p-\lambda)$ is a polynomial
ring in three variables over $k$.

statements.label: prop:graded
statements.text:
The filtration on $A$ is exhaustive and separated.  Its associated
graded ring is the domain
\begin{equation}

 G:=\gr A
 \simeq k[p,s,u,F,J]/(H_*),
 \qquad
 H_*=x^2F-(1+2sx)J-pJ^2,
 \quad x=s^2-u^2+pF,
\end{equation}
with the grading induced by \eqref{gr:weights}.
The filtration degrees of $p,s,u,F,J$ in $A$ are respectively
$-1,0,0,1,1$.

statements.label: prop:coordinate-obstruction
statements.text:
If $p$ is a coordinate of $A$, then there exist a nonzero locally
nilpotent derivation $E$ of the ring $B$ in \eqref{gr:quadric} and
an element $0\ne h\in I$ such that $E(h)=0$.

statements.label: prop:lift
statements.text:
Let $E$ be a nonzero locally nilpotent derivation of $B$ such that
$I\cap\ker E\ne0$.  There is a nonzero locally nilpotent derivation
$\widetilde E$ of $C$ that extends $E$, preserves fiber weights, and satisfies
$\widetilde E(v)=0$.
statements.section_title: Lifting the obstruction to a line bundle

statements.label: prop:rigidity
statements.text:
There is no nonzero locally nilpotent derivation of
$C=k[a,d,b,c,u]/(ac-bd-1)$ that preserves the fiber weights
\eqref{bun:fiber-weights} and annihilates
$v=a^3b+a^2u^2-d^2$.

title: A strict four-row permanent inequality and permutation moments
abstract: We prove a permanent inequality with exponent strictly below two for laws on S4 sufficiently close to uniform and with exactly uniform coordinate marginals. Applied to a four-row recursion, it shows that an absolute number of coordinate sweeps brings the full permutation of the Thorp shuffle on \(N=2^d\) cards to total-variation distance tending to zero from uniform as \(N\to\infty\). Thus the mixing time has the optimal order \(O(\log N)\) in physical shuffles.

Applied to a four-row recursion, it shows that an absolute number of coordinate sweeps brings the full permutation of the Thorp shuffle on $N=2^d$ cards to total-variation distance tending to zero from uniform as $N\to\infty$. Thus the mixing time has the optimal order $O(\log N)$ in physical shuffles.

statements.label: thm:main

There is a smooth connected projective complex surface $X$ containing a connected nodal curve $Z_0$ with smooth rational irreducible components such that
\[
 \im\bigl(\pi_1(Z_0)\longrightarrow\pi_1(X)\bigr)

statements.label: prop:involution
statements.text:
Let \(L\) be the free pro-\(2\) group on \(a_{h,j}\), with
\(h\in(\Z/4)^2\) and \(0\le j\le2\), and let
\(\sigma(a_{h,j})=a_{b_j-h,j}^{-1}\), where \(b_j\bmod2\ne0\).
Equip \(L\) with the basis and weights of \Cref{lem:shift-basis}.
There are 24 elements \(g\in L\), with assigned positive weights
\(w_g\), such that
\[
 \nu_L(g)\ge w_g,\qquad
 \nu_L(r_g)\ge w_g+1,
 \qquad r_g=\sigma(g)g^{-1},
\]
and the closed normal subgroup generated by the \(r_g\) imposes
\(\sigma=\id\) on all of \(L\).  The basis polynomial and the
polynomial of the chosen weights are
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 P(t)&=\sum_{i,\ell,j}t^{i+\ell+1}
       =3t(1+t+t^2+t^3)^2,\\
 G(t)&=\sum_g t^{w_g}
       =3t(1+t)(1+t^2)^2.
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
In particular, \(P=(1+t)G\), and these involution relations have
degree cost at most \(tG(t)\).

title: A two-dimensional area law from a global spectral gap
abstract: We prove an entropy area law for the unique ground state of a finite-range Hamiltonian on any finite induced subgraph of the square lattice. A lower bound on the spectral gap of the full Hamiltonian and fixed bounds on the local dimension, interaction range, and interaction strength suffice. For every set of sites, its entanglement entropy is bounded by a constant times the number of edges crossing its boundary, independently of the size and shape of the domain.

tex.abstract:
We prove an entropy area law for the unique ground state of a finite-range
Hamiltonian on any finite induced subgraph of the square lattice. A lower bound
on the spectral gap of the full Hamiltonian and fixed bounds on the local
dimension, interaction range, and interaction strength suffice. For every set
of sites, its entanglement entropy is bounded by a constant times the number of
edges crossing its boundary, independently of the size and shape of the domain.

statements.title: Area law
statements.label: thm:area
statements.text:
For every $q,R,J$ as above and every $\Delta>0$, there is a finite constant
$C=C(q,R,J,\Delta)$ with the following property. Suppose that $\Lambda$ is a
finite induced square-lattice domain and that the Hamiltonian
\eqref{eq:hamiltonian} has a unique normalized ground vector $\Omega$, up to
phase, with ground energy $E_0$, and satisfies
\[
 H-E_0\id\ \ge\ \Delta\bigl(\id-\ket{\Omega}\bra{\Omega}\bigr).
\]
Then for every $A\subseteq\Lambda$,
\begin{equation}
 S_\Omega(A)\le C\,|\partial_\Lambda A|.
\end{equation}
The same constant applies to all such domains, sets, and Hamiltonians.

statements.label: cor:rectangles
statements.text:
The conclusion of Theorem~\ref{thm:area} holds for every subset of a finite
rectangular square lattice with bounded on-site and nearest-neighbor
interactions and a unique ground state separated by a fixed global gap.
For every domain covered by that theorem it also implies
\[
 S_\Omega(A)\le4C|\partial_{\rm in}A|,
 \qquad S_\Omega(A)\le2C|Z_A|.
\]

statements.title: Positive replacement of the Hamiltonian
statements.label: prop:positive
statements.text:
Suppose $H\Omega=E_0\Omega$, $\|\Omega\|=1$, and
\[
 H-E_0I\ge\Delta(I-P_\Omega),\qquad
 P_\Omega=|\Omega\rangle\langle\Omega|.
\]
For each integer $p\ge1$ and $\alpha=p/(p+1)$, there are operators
$k_i$, indexed by the original supports and retaining their anchors, and a
constant $c_*>0$ such that
\begin{equation}
 0\le k_i\le I,\qquad k_i\Omega=0,\qquad
 H_F:=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}k_i
       \ge c_*^{-1}(H-E_0I)\ge g(I-P_\Omega),
 \qquad g:=\Delta/c_*.
 
\end{equation}
Thus $H_F$ has the unique ground vector $\Omega$, ground energy zero, and
gap at least $g$.  Furthermore,
\begin{equation}
 k_{i,l}:=E_{i,l}(k_i)\in[0,I],\qquad
 \|k_i-k_{i,l}\|\le Ce^{-cl^\alpha}
 \quad(l\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}).
 
\end{equation}
Each $k_i$ is supported in the connected component containing $a_i$.
statements.section_title: Positive constraints and truncation near a finite set

statements.title: Truncation near a finite set
statements.label: prop:truncation
statements.text:
Use Proposition~\ref{prop:positive} with $p=1$, so $\alpha=1/2$.
Fix $C_0>0$.  There is a constant $C_1$, depending only on
$q,R,J,\Delta,C_0$, with the following property for every real $n\ge2$
and every nonempty $S_0\subseteq\Lambda$ with $|S_0|\le C_0n^2$.
Put $r_0=\lceil C_1(\log n)^2\rceil$.  If
$d_i^0:=d_\Lambda(a_i,S_0)<\infty$, define
\begin{equation}
 r_i=\max\{r_0,\lfloor d_i^0/2\rfloor\},\qquad
 \widetilde h_i=k_{i,r_i},\qquad \widetilde X_i=N_{r_i}(a_i).
 
\end{equation}
If $d_i^0=\infty$, set $\widetilde h_i=k_i$ and designate its anchor's
entire component as $\widetilde X_i$.  Then
$\widetilde H=\sum_i\widetilde h_i$ is a sum of positive contractions and
\begin{equation}
 \|\widetilde H-H_F\|\le\epsilon_n,
 \qquad \epsilon_n:=\min\{n^{-1000},g/4\}.
 
\end{equation}
Its ground energy $\widetilde E_0$ lies in $[0,\epsilon_n]$, its ground
vector $\widetilde\Omega$ is unique, and its gap is at least $g/2$.
After a choice of phase,
\begin{equation}
 \|\widetilde\Omega-\Omega\|\le2\sqrt{\epsilon_n/g},\qquad
 \frac12\big\||\widetilde\Omega\rangle\langle\widetilde\Omega|
                 -P_\Omega\big\|_1\le\sqrt{2\epsilon_n/g}.
 
\end{equation}

For a set $X\subseteq S_0$, let $b_X=|\partial_\Lambda X|$ and let
$\mathcal C_X$ be the labels whose designated supports
$\widetilde X_i$ meet both $X$ and $\Lambda\setminus X$.
Every such support has radius exactly $r_0$, and
\begin{equation}
 |\mathcal C_X|\le Cb_X(r_0+1)^2,\qquad
 \log d_i\le C(r_0+1)^2\quad(i\in\mathcal C_X),\qquad
 d_i:=q^{|\widetilde X_i|}.
 
\end{equation}
Consequently the cut parameter
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal B_X:=1+\sum_{i\in\mathcal C_X}\log^2(e d_i)
       \le C(1+b_X)(r_0+1)^6.
 
\end{equation}
In particular, $b_X\le C_2nD$ and $D\ge1$ imply
$\mathcal B_X\le CnD(\log n)^{12}$, with the constant also depending
on $C_2$.

statements.title: Entropy and energy transport
statements.label: prop:transport
statements.text:
Fix a finite one-copy space, history and conditional choice trees,
partitions, cross-band commutation, positive parameter $a$, and positive
contractions with designated supports as specified above.  Let $\ell$
bound the logarithmic dimensions of every transferred subsystem and
every designated support $D_i$ for which $\mathcal J_i\ne\varnothing$,
with the stipulated smallness of $a\ell$.
For every $k$ and nonzero $\mathrm{pre}\in\mathcal S_k$, set
\begin{equation}
 s=\frac14,\qquad
 N(p)=\norm{\mathcal M(p)^{-s}\mathrm{pre}},\qquad
 v(p)=\frac{\mathcal M(p)^{-s}\mathrm{pre}}{N(p)}.
\end{equation}
For every $0<p<1$, let $\Phi_j$ be the normalized map from terminal
leaf $j$ to $\mathcal M(p)$ and define density matrices
\begin{equation}
 \sigma_{j,u}=\Phi_j^*\bigl(
 |\mathcal M(p)^{-iu}v(p)\rangle
 \langle\mathcal M(p)^{-iu}v(p)|\bigr),\qquad u\in\R.
\end{equation}
The adjoint here is for the trace pairing:
$\Tr(\Phi_j^*(\sigma)Z)=\Tr(\sigma\Phi_j(Z))$.
Write $\sigma_{h,u}$ for the state at $j=(h,\mathrm{old})$, and put
$C_h=A_h^{-1/2}B_hA_h^{-1/2}$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 -\partial_p\log N(p)^2
 =\sum_h w_h\int_{\R}m_s(u)\Tr(\sigma_{h,u}\log C_h)\,du.
\end{equation}
There is $\beta_k=O_{\mathrm{fixed}}(\log(k+1))$, independent of $p$
and $\mathrm{pre}$, such that
\begin{align}
 -\partial_p\log N(p)^2
 \geq{}&ka\sum_{h,g}w_h\int_{\R}m_s(u)
    \int\sum_{c\in\mathcal C_h}q_{c\mid h}
          \eta_{h,c,g}(\theta)\,d\mu_{\sigma_{h,u}}(\theta)\,du
 \notag\\[-2pt]
 &{}-CkaK a^{1/4}\ell^C-\beta_k.
\end{align}
If in addition $\bar H\,\mathrm{pre}=E_0\mathrm{pre}$, then
\begin{equation}
 \langle v,\bar Hv\rangle
 \leq 2E_0+C a^2\ell^C
 \sum_i W_i(p)\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_i}\pi_j
 \int_{\R}m_s(u)\int\eta_{i,j}(\theta)^{1/8}
                 \,d\mu_{\sigma_{j,u}}(\theta)\,du+o_k(1).
\end{equation}
The remainder in \eqref{transport:energy} is uniform in $p\in(0,1)$,
in nonzero $\mathrm{pre}$ satisfying the eigenvector assumption, and in
all replica states.  The constants $C$ and the exponents denoted by $C$
in \eqref{transport:entropy-gain} and \eqref{transport:energy} are
universal; support dimensions enter those coefficients only through
$\ell$.  Only the implicit constant in
$\beta_k=O_{\mathrm{fixed}}(\log(k+1))$ and the convergence rate of
$o_k(1)$ may depend on the entire fixed finite data.  Neither depends
on $p$ or the replica state.  The entropy estimate can be integrated
over a closed subinterval
of $[0,1]$ using the continuous endpoint values of $N$.

statements.title: Upper and lower norm comparisons
statements.label: prop:comparators
statements.text:
Fix the positive gapped Hamiltonian and physical target $X$ above,
a finite collection of status partitions satisfying
\eqref{comparator:nesting}, a typical Schmidt set satisfying
\eqref{comparator:typical-set}, and a mean tree with metrics
\eqref{comparator:metrics}. There is a sequence of common auxiliary
labels $\lambda_k$ and nonzero vectors
\begin{equation}
 \mathrm{pre}_k=\pi_R^{\lambda_k}
  (\widetilde\Omega\otimes\mathrm{Bell}_{CR})^{\otimes k}
       \in\mathcal S_k,
 \qquad \|\mathrm{pre}_k\|\le1,
 
\end{equation}
Here $\pi_R^{\lambda_k}$ is the Schur-label projection on the $R$ copies.
These vectors are physical mean-energy eigenvectors of eigenvalue
$\widetilde E_0$ and have label $\lambda_k$ on both $C$ and $R$.
For every tree above, set
\[
 N=\|\mathcal M^{-s}\mathrm{pre}_k\|,
 \qquad v=\mathcal M^{-s}\mathrm{pre}_k/N,
 \qquad
 E_{\mathrm{def}}=
 \frac{\langle v,\overline{\widetilde H}v\rangle-\widetilde E_0}
      {\widetilde g},
 \qquad
 \overline{\widetilde H}=\frac1k\sum_{i=1}^k\widetilde H^{(i)}.
\]
\emph{Rough comparisons.} For $0<\tau<1/2$, the upper bound below
uses the prefix data \eqref{comparator:prefix-data}:
\begin{align}
 -\frac{\log N^2}{k}
 &\le 2\log d_*-\log z+
       2sW\left(\frac{2B_{\mathrm{sh}}}{z}+2B_{\mathrm{exc}}\right)
       +o_k(1),
 \\
 -\frac{\log N^2}{k}
 &\ge 2sW\left[
       2S'-C\left(\tau\log d_*+\frac{h(\tau)}a\right)
       -C\frac{E_{\mathrm{def}}}{\tau}S'\right]-o_k(1).
 
\end{align}
Here $h$ is binary entropy.  The lower bound does not require
\eqref{comparator:prefix-data} or \eqref{comparator:mgf-data}.

\emph{Sharp comparisons.} If \eqref{comparator:mgf-data} holds and
$a\le c/\sqrt{\mathcal B}$, with $c$ sufficiently small in terms of
$c_0$, define
\begin{align*}
 g_{j,g}^{\mathrm{pre}}
   &=S(XU_{j,g})+S(V_{j,g})-S(Y_{j,g}),\\
 g_{j,g}^{\mathrm{post}}
   &=S(U_{j,g})+S(U_{j,g}Y_{j,g})-S(Y_{j,g}),
 \qquad g_{\max}=\max_{j,g}g_{j,g}^{\mathrm{pre}}.
\end{align*}
Then $g_{j,g}^{\mathrm{pre}}\ge0$, and the sharp comparisons are
\begin{align}
 -\frac{\log N^2}{k}
 &\le 2\log d_*-\log z+
  2sW\left[\langle g^{\mathrm{post}}\rangle_{\mathrm{av}}
          +C\left(a\mathcal B+\frac{|\log z|}{a}\right)\right]
          +o_k(1),
 \\
 -\frac{\log N^2}{k}
 &\ge 2sW\left[2S'+(1-\tau)
                  \langle g^{\mathrm{pre}}\rangle_{\mathrm{av}}
       -C\left(\tau\log d_*+\frac{h(\tau)}a+a\mathcal B\right)
       -C\frac{E_{\mathrm{def}}}{\tau}(S'+g_{\max})\right]
       -o_k(1).
 
\end{align}
The upper sharp bound does not require \eqref{comparator:prefix-data}.
For every physical partition there is the exact identity
\begin{equation}
 2S_X+g_{j,g}^{\mathrm{pre}}-g_{j,g}^{\mathrm{post}}
       =I(X:V_{j,g})+I(X:Y_{j,g}V_{j,g}).
 
\end{equation}

All replica limits are taken with the physical system, auxiliary dimensions,
finite status collection and tree, $a$, and $\tau$ fixed.  The errors are
uniform over terminal probabilities, including their dependence on $k$,
and over the symmetric vectors to which the lower comparison is applied.
Constants or degrees in intermediate polynomial factors in $k$ may depend
on the fixed entire system.  They disappear in $o_k(1)$.  The displayed
constants in the rough bounds are universal; those in the sharp bounds
may also depend on $C_0,c_0$.  None has additional dependence on the
system dimensions.
statements.section_title: Norm comparisons from an auxiliary pair

statements.title: The scanner estimate
statements.label: prop:scanner
statements.text:
Assume \eqref{scanner:scales} and \eqref{scanner:test-geometry}, and let
\(0<e<1\) satisfy \(\kappa\le e\).  Suppose
\begin{equation}
 S_\Omega(X)\le C_e n^{1+e},\qquad
 S_\Omega(Q_j)\le C_e(nL^e+n)\quad(0\le j\le L).
 
\end{equation}
Let \(\epsilon=n^{-\nu}\), where \(\nu>0\) is fixed, and suppose
\(a r_0^2\) is sufficiently small.  Construct the auxiliary systems,
the fixed label sector, and the unnormalized vector \(\mathrm{pre}\)
as in Proposition~\ref{prop:comparators}, using typical width
\(w=n^{3/5}\).  For each sufficiently large replica count \(k\),
there are a charge round and a common parameter
\(p_k\in[\epsilon/2,\epsilon]\) at which the normalized vector
\(v_k=\mathcal M^{-s}\mathrm{pre}/N\), \(s=1/4\), has defect energy
\[
 E_{{\rm def},k}
 =\frac{\langle v_k,\overline{\widetilde H}v_k\rangle
                         -\widetilde E_0}{\widetilde g}
\]
bounded by
\begin{equation}
 E_{{\rm def},k}
 \le Cn^\ell D^2W^2(\log n)^C
        \bigl(\delta_n^{1/8}+\epsilon+n^{-100}\bigr)
        +Cn^{-1000}+o_k(1),
 
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
 \delta_n=C_e\epsilon^{-1}
        \bigl(n^{e-\mu}+a^{1/4}(\log n)^C\bigr).
 
\end{equation}
Here \(\overline{\widetilde H}\) is the mean of the physical
Hamiltonian over the copies.  All norm comparisons of
Proposition~\ref{prop:comparators} apply at the selected points, with
shell entropy bound \(B_{\rm sh}\le C_e(nL^e+n)\), mismatch
\(B_{\rm exc}\le CnD\), and marginal parameter
\(\mathcal B\le CnD(\log n)^C\).  The sharp comparisons additionally
require their stated condition on \(a\sqrt{\mathcal B}\).

The entire finite physical system, \(n\), the scan, and all auxiliary
dimensions are fixed before \(k\to\infty\).  The remainder is uniform
over the selected round and parameter, although these may depend on \(k\).
Constants may depend on the fixed exponents and the input constant \(C_e\).
statements.section_title: Scanning collars and improving the entropy bound

statements.title: Improved safe-box estimate
statements.label: prop:small-box
statements.text:
There is a constant \(C\), depending only on the Hamiltonian parameters,
such that
\[
 F_{\rm box}(r)\le Cr^{1+e_*}\quad(r\ge1),
 \qquad e_*=2\cdot10^{-6}.
\]
statements.section_title: Scanning collars and improving the entropy bound

statements.title: A sublinear collar bound
statements.label: prop:collar
statements.text:
Let \(T\) be a template separated from the cut, with parameters
\((n,s_0)\) as in Definition~\ref{scanner:template}.  Set
\[
 L=\lfloor n^{1-10^{-5}}\rfloor,
 \qquad X=A\cap T,
 \qquad S_0=A\cap T_L,
\]
and suppose \(L\le s_0\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\),
\begin{equation}
 I_\Omega(X:\Lambda\setminus S_0)
       \le C n^{1-\varepsilon},\qquad \varepsilon=10^{-5}.
 
\end{equation}
The constant and threshold are independent of \(T,s_0,n,\Lambda\),
and \(A\).  The cuts of \(X,S_0\), and \(S_0\setminus X\) have
\(O(n)\) edges, and \(|S_0|=O(n^2)\).
statements.section_title: Scanning collars and improving the entropy bound

statements.title: Amplification
statements.label: prop:amplification
statements.text:
Fix $C_0>0$ and let $\varepsilon,\beta,\alpha$ be as in
\eqref{eq:amplification-exponents}.  Suppose $n\ge2$,
$L=\lfloor n^{1-\varepsilon}\rfloor$, and
\[
 X=A\cap T,\qquad S_0=A\cap T_L,\qquad Y=S_0\setminus X,
 \qquad Z'=\Lambda\setminus S_0.
\]
Assume that $|S_0|\le C_0n^2$, that each of the three cuts
$X,Y,S_0$ has at most $C_0n$ crossing edges, and that
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal I:=I_\Omega(X:Z')\le C_0n^{1-\varepsilon}.
\end{equation}
For every integer $M\ge1$, at all sufficiently large $n$, there is
an integer radius $r$ such that
\begin{equation}
 r\le C_M n^{(1-\varepsilon)/\alpha},\qquad
 L+2r=o(n^\beta),
\end{equation}
and, simultaneously for every physical set
$J\subseteq\Lambda\setminus N_{2r}(S_0)$,
\begin{equation}
 I_\Omega(X:J)\le C_M n^{-M}.
\end{equation}
The same bound holds with any subset of $X$ in place of $X$.
The constants and the threshold may depend on $C_0$ and $M$, but are
independent of $\Lambda,A,T$ subject to the stated assumptions.

If in addition
\begin{equation}
 \dist_\infty(T,Z)>L+n^\beta,
\end{equation}
where $Z$ is the set of endpoints of the original cut, then
$N_{2r}(S_0)\subseteq A$.  In particular the remote set $J$ may
include all of $\Lambda\setminus A$.

statements.title: Two families with separated birth templates
statements.label: prop:two-families
statements.text:
Fix the constants $D_0$ and $C_{\mathrm{tpl}}$ in
Definition~\ref{scanner:template}, and a lower scale threshold $n_*\ge1$.
There is a constant $C$ with the following property.  Let $\Lambda$ be a
finite induced subgraph of the square lattice, let $A\subseteq\Lambda$,
and suppose that $b=|\partial_\Lambda A|>0$.  Let $Z$ be the set of
endpoints of those cut edges.

There are a set $D\subseteq A$, a finite ordered collection of disjoint
nonempty sets $X_i\subseteq A$, labels $f_i\in\{0,1\}$, ambient templates
$T_i\subset\Z^2$, and integers $n_i\ge n_*$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item
$A=D\mathbin{\dot\cup}\bigcup_iX_i$ and $|D|\le Cb$.
\item
$X_i\subseteq A\cap T_i$.  Each $T_i$ is a template of
Definition~\ref{scanner:template}: it is a union of $N_i$ lattice samples
of closed convex rectangles or triangles with side slopes
$0,\infty,1,-1$, each of sup-norm diameter at most $s_i$, where
\[
 \diam_\infty T_i\le n_i,\qquad
 n_i\ge C_{\mathrm{tpl}}N_i(s_i+1),\qquad
 \dist_\infty(T_i,Z)>4D_0s_i.
\]
Moreover $L_i=\lfloor n_i^{1-\ell}\rfloor\le s_i$.
\item
The templates satisfy
\begin{align}
 \dist_\infty(T_i,Z)&>2n_i^\beta,\\
 \dist_\infty\left(T_i,
       \bigcup_{\substack{j<i\\f_j=f_i}}X_j\right)
       &>2n_i^\beta.
\end{align}
As usual, the distance to the empty set is infinite.
\item
The scale losses are summable:
\[
 \sum_i n_i^{-100}\le Cb.
\]
\end{enumerate}
The constant $C$ may depend on the fixed template constants and on $n_*$,
but not on the domain or cut.

title: A typical-start upper bound for low-temperature SK Glauber dynamics
abstract: For every fixed inverse temperature β > 1, we prove subexponential mixing for rate-one-per-site heat-bath dynamics in the zero-field Gaussian Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model from a typical equilibrium configuration. If one Gibbs-sampled configuration is held fixed as the initial state, its total-variation distance from equilibrium is at most 1/4 by time \(\exp(n^{1-1/40000000})\), with joint probability tending to one over the disorder and the sampled state.

tex.abstract:
For every fixed inverse temperature $\beta>1$, we prove subexponential
mixing for rate-one-per-site heat-bath dynamics in the zero-field Gaussian
Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model from a typical equilibrium configuration.
If one Gibbs-sampled configuration is held fixed as the initial state,
its total-variation distance from equilibrium is at most $1/4$ by time
$\exp(n^{1-1/40000000})$, with joint probability tending to one over
the disorder and the sampled state.
sections: Scalar inputs and the entropy--energy identity
From balanced flows to typical-state mixing

statements.title: Mixing from a typical Gibbs state
statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every fixed $\beta>1$, there is $c_\beta\in(0,1)$ such that
\[
 \mathbb P_{J,\,\sigma_0\sim\pi_{n,\beta}^J}
 \left\{T_{n,\beta}^J(\sigma_0)
       \le\exp\bigl(n^{1-c_\beta}\bigr)\right\}
 \longrightarrow1
 \qquad\text{as }n\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
The exponent is independent of $n$ and of the realized disorder.
The proof permits $c_\beta=1/40000000$ for every fixed $\beta>1$.

statements.title: Two-sided typical-start bounds
statements.label: cor:typical-two-sided
statements.text:
For every fixed $\beta>1$, in the model and continuous-time convention
above,
\[
 \mathbb P_{J,\,\sigma_0\sim\pi_{n,\beta}^J}
 \left\{
 \begin{aligned}
  \exp\bigl(n^{1/10000}\bigr)&<T_{n,\beta}^J(\sigma_0)\\
  &\le\exp\bigl(n^{1-1/40000000}\bigr)
 \end{aligned}
 \right\}\longrightarrow1
 \qquad\text{as }n\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
The Gibbs state $\sigma_0$ is held fixed before the total variation in
\eqref{eq:intro-state-mixing-time} is evaluated.

statements.title: Proposal comparison
statements.label: prop:proposal
statements.text:
For every fixed $0<l\le1/100$ and all sufficiently large $n$,
\[
 {\rm KL}(Q_l\Vert P)\le2n^{1-l/2}.
 \tag{5}
\]
There is an event in the proposal experiment of probability at least
$1-\exp(-n^{1-10l})$ such that the output subprobability restricted to
this event is dominated, on the space of $(G,x)$, by
\[
 \exp(n^{1-l/2})P.
 \tag{6}
\]
The empirical Gram matrix of the $T_k$ is within $n^{-l}$ of the
identity in operator norm, except with probability at most
$\exp(-n^{1-10l})$. The dimension required for these estimates may
depend on the fixed $l$.

statements.title: Coverage at a target disorder
statements.label: prop:coverage
statements.text:
Let $G,\bar G$ be independent standard Gaussian disorder vectors, set
$G^\circ=\sqrt{1-\delta}\,G+\sqrt\delta\,\bar G$, and let
$\nu(\cdot\mid G^\circ)$ be the conditional spin kernel of
$\mathcal SQ_f$ defined above. Then
\[
 \mathbb E\,{\rm KL}\bigl(\pi_G\Vert\nu(\cdot\mid G^\circ)\bigr)
 \le O_\beta(n\sqrt\delta)+2n^{1-f/2}/\delta.
 \tag{9}
\]
With probability tending to one over this target/base pair,
\[
 {\rm KL}\bigl(\pi_G\Vert\nu(\cdot\mid G^\circ)\bigr)
 \le n^{1-4d}.
 \tag{10}
\]
On the same event, simultaneously for every set
$A\subseteq\{-1,1\}^n$ with $\pi_G(A)\ge n^{-d}$,
\[
 \nu(A\mid G^\circ)\ge\exp(-n^{1-2d}).
\]
The set $A$ may be chosen after the target and base are realized.

statements.title: Balanced-cut flow
statements.label: prop:cuts
statements.text:
With probability tending to one in the target disorder,
\[
 Q_G^{\rm edge}(S,S^c)>B_{\min}:=\exp(-n^{1-b/20})
 \quad\text{for every }S\text{ such that }
 \min(\pi_G(S),\pi_G(S^c))\ge n^{-d}.
 \tag{11}
\]

title: A uniform Hilbert transform estimate for Lipschitz directions
abstract: We prove a uniform L2 bound for the Hilbert transform along a Lipschitz unit vector field in the plane, with integration restricted to a fixed absolute multiple of the reciprocal Lipschitz seminorm. The bound is uniform in the inner truncation and holds for fields depending on both coordinates. This gives an affirmative answer to Stein's weak-\((2,2)\) conjecture.

tex.abstract:
We prove a uniform \(L^2\) bound for the Hilbert transform along a
Lipschitz unit vector field in the plane, with integration restricted
to a fixed absolute multiple of the reciprocal Lipschitz seminorm.
The bound is uniform in the inner truncation and holds for fields
depending on both coordinates. This gives an affirmative answer to
Stein's weak-\((2,2)\) conjecture.
sections: Ordinary tiles and the popular forest
A strict finite Fourier inequality with constant one
Residual terms and integration along paths

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There are absolute constants \(a_*\in(0,1/2)\) and \(C_*<\infty\)
such that every Lipschitz field \(v:\R^2\to S^1\) with
\(\Lip(v)\le1\) satisfies
\[
 \sup_{0<\epsilon<a_*}
 \norm{H_{v,a_*}^{\epsilon}f}_{L^2(\R^2)}
 \le C_*\norm{f}_{L^2(\R^2)}
 \qquad(f\in\mathcal S(\R^2)).
\]
Its symmetric principal value therefore satisfies
\[
 \norm{H_{v,a_*}f}_2\le C_*\norm f_2,
 \qquad
 \big|\{x:|H_{v,a_*}f(x)|>\lambda\}\big|
 \le C_*^2\lambda^{-2}\norm f_2^2
 \quad(\lambda>0).
\]

statements.title: Lacey--Li
statements.label: red:kakeya
statements.text:
Let \(v:\R^2\to S^1\) be Lipschitz and \(0<\delta<1\). Restrict to
rectangles satisfying
\[
 L(R)\le \frac1{100\Lip(v)},\qquad
 \abs{R\cap v^{-1}(\operatorname{EX}(R))}\ge\delta\abs R,
\]
where the first restriction is void when \(\Lip(v)=0\). Then
\[
 \mathcal M_{v,\delta}h(z)
   =\sup_R\frac{\one_R(z)}{\abs R}\int_R\abs h
 \quad\text{satisfies}\quad
 \norm{\mathcal M_{v,\delta}h}_{L^{2,\infty}}
       \le C\delta^{-1/2}\norm h_2.
\]
Here the supremum is tested at every point of \(R\), and the constant
is independent of \(v\) and \(\delta\).

statements.title: Restricted estimate on a vertical band
statements.label: thm:band-restricted
red:composition-commutator
statements.text:
For \(\abs t\le b_0\) and \(T\) as in \Cref{red:commutator},
\begin{equation}
 \norm{TC_t h-C_tTh}_2
      \le C A(\mathfrak m)\abs t\,\norm h_2.
\end{equation}
The constant is uniform over \(\abs u\le1\),
\(\Lip(u)\le C_{\rm Lip}\).

statements.label: red:band-implies-main
statements.text:
The uniform restricted estimate in \Cref{thm:band-restricted} implies
\Cref{thm:main}.

statements.title: Packet representation
statements.label: red:packet-representation
statements.text:
The diagonal form
\[
 \sum_j\langle\mathcal A_{u,\mathcal L}
                         \widetilde Q_j f_j,g_j\rangle
\]
is a sum, with absolutely summable scalar coefficients, of averages
of forms \eqref{eq:src-3}. Each form satisfies
\Cref{red:packets}, uniformly in \(w,m,\mathcal L\), and has one
common angular grid and common spatial lattices across components.
The same assertion holds for \(m=1\) with the original
positive-frequency band cutoff in place of \(\widetilde Q_1\).
The sums can be obtained as limits of finite packet collections.

statements.label: red:model-suffices
statements.text:
Suppose that the following bounds hold, uniformly for every admissible
finite form \(\Lambda_{\mathcal S}\) in
\Cref{red:packets}, with the fixed packet constants there.
The field \(u:\R^2\to\R\) is bounded and measurable, the sets
\(F,E\subset\R^2\) are measurable with positive finite measure,
and the input and test satisfy
\(\norm{f(z)}_{\mathcal H}\le\one_F(z)\),
\(\norm{g(z)}_{\mathcal H}\le\one_E(z)\).
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item For \(m\ge1\), there is a fixed exponent \(C_1\) such that
\begin{equation}
 |\Lambda_{\mathcal S}(f,g)|
     \le C(1+\log(2m))^{C_1}\sqrt{|F||E|}.
\end{equation}
\item For \(L\ge L_0\), with \(\tau,m,W\) as in
\eqref{red:small-time-parameters}, assume in addition that
\(\abs u\le1\), \(\Lip(u)\le C_{\rm Lip}\), and
\(F,E\subset I\times\R\) for an interval \(I\) with
\(\abs I\le b_0\). Whenever
\(L/2\le\log\sqrt{|E|/|F|}\le2L\),
\begin{equation}
 |\Lambda_{\mathcal S}(f,g)|
       \le C L^{-20}\sqrt{|F||E|}.
\end{equation}
\item For \(m=1\), one scalar component, and \(|E|\le|F|\),
there is a fixed \(c>0\) such that
\begin{equation}
 |\Lambda_{\mathcal S}(f,g)|
       \le C\sqrt{|F||E|}(|E|/|F|)^c.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
Then \Cref{thm:band-restricted} holds. The constants remain uniform
in \(w\), \(\epsilon\), and the number of retained scales.

statements.title: Ordinary model estimates
statements.label: tile:prop-model
statements.section_title: Ordinary tiles and the popular forest

statements.label: forest:prop-count
statements.text:
For the tops in \eqref{forest:eq-witnesses},
\begin{equation}
 \norm{n}_{L^{2,\infty}(\mathcal D)}
       \le C L^C\sqrt S.
\end{equation}
More precisely, if
\[
 D_*\ge\max(2K_0,\,2L^{C_{\mathrm{as}}},\,2),
\]
then one may take the right-hand side to be
\(C L^{C_{\mathrm{as}}}D_*^3\sqrt S\), provided \(D_*\)
is chosen within an absolute factor of the displayed maximum.
In particular, when \(K_0=L^k\), a permissible exponent in
\eqref{eq:src-6} is
\begin{equation}
 c_{\mathrm{cnt}}(k)
     =C_{\mathrm{as}}+3\max(k,C_{\mathrm{as}}).
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Ordinary tiles and the popular forest

statements.label: conc:line-moments
statements.text:
For every slope $t$, every collection satisfying \eqref{eq:src-9},
every line $Y_t=y_0$, every horizontal interval $I$ of length $l$ on
that line, and every $b\geq2$, the normalized $L^b(I)$ norms of
$\mathcal E_t$, $\mathcal S_t$, and
\[
 \mathcal V_3\left(\sum_{\ell_s=2^k}\phi_s\right),
 \qquad
 \mathcal V_3\left(\sum_{\ell_s=2^k}q_{T(s)}\phi_s\right)
\]
are at most $C b^C(1+\log B)^C$.
The constants are uniform in the line, interval, finite collection,
dimension, and number of scales.  In particular the assertion holds
for every fixed deterministic subcollection with the same constants.

statements.label: conc:top-good
conc:mask-removal
statements.text:
Given any fixed $H>0$, choose $A$ sufficiently large after $K_1$ and
$C_{\mathrm{top}}$, and then choose a sufficiently large fixed count
threshold exponent $C_n$.  There is a measurable set
$F_{\rm conc}\subset F$ such that
\[
 \abs{F\setminus F_{\rm conc}}\leq L^{-H}\abs F,
 \qquad
 \int_{F_{\rm conc}}\norm{P-P_q}_{\mathcal H}
       \leq L^{-H}N\abs F,
 \qquad P_q=\sum_sq_{T(s)}\phi_s,
\]
and \eqref{eq:src-11} holds there for every top.  On this set,
\begin{equation}
 n(z)=\sum_T h_T(z)\leq NL^{C_n}.
\end{equation}
One has $K_0=L^{A+2}>K_1$, so both
\eqref{eq:src-11} and \eqref{conc:top-horizontal-derivative} also hold
with $h_T$ in place of $h_T^{(1)}$.

statements.label: count:simultaneous

statements.title: Finite Fourier gain
statements.label: phase:finite-fourier
statements.text:
Let \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d\in\R\), where \(d\le D\), satisfy
\(\abs{\lambda_i-\lambda_j}\ge\Delta>0\) for \(i\ne j\).
Let \(\nu\) be any positive probability measure on \(\R\) such that
\(\supp\widehat\nu\subset(-\epsilon_0\Delta,\epsilon_0\Delta)\).
Then, for every finite \(p\ge4\) and every complex coefficient sequence,
\begin{equation}
 \left(\int_\R
       \left|\sum_{i=1}^d a_i e^{i\lambda_i t}\right|^p
       \,\dd\nu(t)\right)^{1/p}
 \le \left(\sum_{i=1}^d |a_i|^{r_*}\right)^{1/r_*}.
 
\end{equation}
The same estimate holds for coefficients in a finite-dimensional Hilbert
space \(\mathcal H\) when the exponentials act diagonally: in an
orthonormal basis, the \(\xi\)-th component may use frequencies
\(\lambda_{i,\xi}\), provided they are \(\Delta\)-separated as \(i\)
varies, for each fixed \(\xi\).  The right side is then
\( (\sum_i\norm{a_i}_{\mathcal H}^{r_*})^{1/r_*}\).
All these estimates have constant one.
statements.section_title: A strict finite Fourier inequality with constant one

statements.title: Averaging factors on marked cells
statements.label: pred:marked-comparison
statements.text:
There is an absolute \(c_{\rm av}>0\) with the following property, for
all sufficiently large \(L\). On a fixed line of slope \(s_R\), each
marked \(H_j\)-cell \(I\) meeting \(Z\) admits a nonnegative function
\(\Gamma_j\) which is constant on the \(H_{j-1}\)-subcells of \(I\),
satisfies \( |I|^{-1}\int_I\Gamma_j\le1\), and obeys
\begin{equation}
 \beta_J^0(z)\le
       \exp\bigl(G^{-c_{\rm av}}u_j(z)\bigr)\Gamma_j(z)
       \qquad (z\in I).
 
\end{equation}
Set \(\Gamma_j=1\) on unmarked cells and on cells not meeting \(Z\).
The functions can be chosen measurably on each fixed line. No choice
jointly measurable in the family of parallel lines is needed.

statements.title: Integrated path product
statements.label: res:path-product
statements.text:
With $M$ chosen by \eqref{res:choice-M}, the estimate
\eqref{eq:src-22} holds for every path top $R$, every shift, and
every vertex parameter with $\norm{\Im\zeta}_2\le L^2$.
Its constants are independent of the tile collection, angular
depth, and Hilbert-space dimension.
statements.section_title: Residual terms and integration along paths

statements.title: Vertex estimate
statements.label: assembly:vertices
statements.text:
For every nonempty root \(v\), every shift \(\sigma\), and every
parameter with
\[
 \Re\zeta=\mu e_\sigma,
 \qquad \|\Im\zeta\|_2\le L^2,
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
 \big\|n_v^{\alpha/p-1}A_v(\zeta)\big\|_{L^p(Z;\mathcal H)}
       \le L^C S^{1/p}.
\end{equation}
The constant and exponent are independent of the shift and the grid
translation.

statements.title: Improvement for the popular model
statements.label: assembly:improved-model
statements.text:
The popular adjoint sum satisfies Equation~\eqref{eq:src-7}; namely,
\[
 \int_F\|P\|\lesssim L^{-20}N|F|.
\]

statements.title: The three model estimates
statements.label: assembly:all-model-estimates
statements.text:
For the packet forms in \eqref{eq:src-3}, let \(u\) be a bounded
measurable real slope, let \(F,E\subset\R^2\) be measurable sets of
positive finite measure, and suppose
\(\|f\|_{\mathcal H}\le\one_F\) and
\(\|g\|_{\mathcal H}\le\one_E\) pointwise.  The following estimates
hold uniformly over every finite subcollection.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item For \(m\ge1\),
\[
 |\Lambda(f,g)|\lesssim(1+\log(2m))^C\sqrt{|F||E|}.
\]
\item Suppose \(L\ge L_0\), with \(\tau,m,W\) chosen by
\eqref{red:small-time-parameters}, and
\(L/2\le\log\sqrt{|E|/|F|}\le2L\).  If
\(\abs u\le1\), \(\Lip(u)\le C_{\rm Lip}\), and
\(F,E\subset I\times\R\) for an interval \(I\) of length at most
\(b_0\), then
\[
 |\Lambda(f,g)|\lesssim L^{-20}\sqrt{|F||E|}.
\]
\item For the scalar model with \(m=1\) and \(|E|\le|F|\), there is an absolute
\(c>0\) such that
\[
 |\Lambda(f,g)|\lesssim
       \sqrt{|F||E|}\left(\frac{|E|}{|F|}\right)^c.
\]
\end{enumerate}

title: A uniform influence bound for hypergraph properties
abstract: For every fixed integer r ≥ 3, we prove that every relabeling-invariant Boolean property of simple r-uniform hypergraphs on n vertices satisfies \(\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}\nolimits _p(f)\le C_r I_p(f)/(\log n)^{r/(r-1)}\). The constant depends only on r, and the bound holds uniformly for all \(0\lt p\lt 1\) without a monotonicity assumption. For increasing properties, it gives the corresponding threshold-width bound with exponent \(r/(r-1)\), proving the hypergraph threshold-width conjecture of Friedgut and Kalai.

tex.abstract:
For every fixed integer $r\ge3$, we prove that every relabeling-invariant
Boolean property of simple $r$-uniform hypergraphs on $n$ vertices
satisfies
$\Var_p(f)\le C_r I_p(f)/(\log n)^{r/(r-1)}$.
The constant depends only on $r$, and the bound holds uniformly for all
$0<p<1$ without a monotonicity assumption. For increasing properties,
it gives the corresponding threshold-width bound with exponent
$r/(r-1)$, proving the hypergraph threshold-width conjecture of
Friedgut and Kalai.
sections: A Fourier estimate for small individual influences
The uniform bound and its threshold consequence

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every integer $r\ge3$ there is a finite constant $C_r$ such that,
for every integer $n\ge r$, every $0<p<1$, and every hypergraph property
$f:\{0,1\}^{E_{n,r}}\to\{0,1\}$,
\begin{equation}
 \Var_p(f)\le \frac{C_r}{(\log n)^{r/(r-1)}}I_p(f).
\end{equation}
No monotonicity assumption is required.

statements.label: cor:threshold
statements.text:
For a nontrivial increasing property of $r$-uniform hypergraphs on
$n\ge r$ vertices, where $r\ge3$, and every $0<\varepsilon<1/2$,
\[
 p_{1-\varepsilon}-p_\varepsilon
 \le\frac{2C_r}{(\log n)^{r/(r-1)}}
                  \log\frac{1-\varepsilon}{\varepsilon}.
\]

title: A universal group of type F∞
abstract: We construct a single group of type F∞ containing every finitely presented group. Its finitely generated subgroups, up to isomorphism, are exactly the finitely generated recursively presented groups. This answers the F∞ form of the higher-dimensional Higman embedding question.

tex.abstract:
We construct a single group of type $\Finfty$ containing every finitely
presented group. Its finitely generated subgroups, up to isomorphism, are
exactly the finitely generated recursively presented groups. This answers
the $\Finfty$ form of the higher-dimensional Higman embedding question.
sections: Uniform fillings with finitely many simplex types
From controlled fillings to finite skeleta

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There exists a group $H$ of type $\Finfty$ such that every finitely
presented group admits an injective homomorphism into $H$.

statements.label: cor:recursive
statements.text:
A finitely generated group embeds in $H$ if and only if it is
recursively presented.

statements.label: prop:finite-envelope
statements.text:
For every finitely presented group $U$ there are a finitely presented
group $\widehat W$ and homomorphisms
\[
 k_{\ell,E}:U\longrightarrow\widehat W
 \qquad(\ell\in\{2,3\},\ E\in\mathcal P_\ell)
\]
such that $k_{2,I}=k_{3,I}$ is injective.  For each $\ell$, whenever
$E,E',E+E'\in\mathcal P_\ell$ and $EE'=E'E=0$, the subgroups
$k_{\ell,E}(U)$ and $k_{\ell,E'}(U)$ commute elementwise, and
\[
 k_{\ell,E+E'}(u)=k_{\ell,E}(u)k_{\ell,E'}(u)
 \qquad(u\in U).
\]

statements.label: prop:self-map
statements.text:
Let $U$ be a finitely presented group containing an isomorphic copy of
every finitely presented group.  There are an injective endomorphism
$f:U\to U$ and homomorphisms
$h_{\ell,E}:U\to U$ for $\ell\in\{2,3\}$ and
$E\in\mathcal P_\ell$, with $h_{2,I}=h_{3,I}=f$, satisfying all the
orthogonal commutation and sum identities of
Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-envelope}.

statements.title: Ascending-torus theorem
statements.label: thm:torus
statements.text:
Let $U$ be a group and $f:U\to U$ an injective endomorphism.  Suppose
that the following conditions hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item There are a finitely presented group $P$ and homomorphisms
      $a:U\to P$ and $b:P\to U$ such that $f=ba$.
\item For each $\ell\in\{2,3\}$ there are homomorphisms
      $h_{\ell,E}:U\to U$, indexed by the finite set
      $E\in\mathcal P_\ell$ defined above, with $h_{\ell,I}=f$.
      Whenever $E,E',E+E'\in\mathcal P_\ell$ and
      $EE'=E'E=0$, the subgroups $h_{\ell,E}(U)$ and
      $h_{\ell,E'}(U)$ commute elementwise, and
      \[
       h_{\ell,E+E'}(u)
          =h_{\ell,E}(u)h_{\ell,E'}(u)
          \qquad(u\in U).
      \]
\end{enumerate}
Then $U$ embeds naturally in $T(U,f)$, and $T(U,f)$ is of type
$\Finfty$.

statements.label: prop:uniform-fillings
statements.text:
Assume the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:torus}.  For every finite
bound $A\subseteq U$ and every integer $n\ge0$, there are an integer
$k\ge0$ and a finite bound $B\subseteq U$ such that, for every
reduced integral $n$-cycle $z\in C_n^A(U)$, there is a finite chain
$y\in C_{n+1}^B(U)$ satisfying
\[
 \partial y=(f^k)_*z.
\]
The chain $y$ may depend on $z$, with no uniform restriction on its
length or coefficients.

title: Abelian covers, Gale correspondences, and the Hodge conjecture for powers
abstract: We prove the rational Hodge conjecture on every self-power of the Jacobian at each tensor Hodge-generic point of the full marked variation of a connected abelian cover of curves. This holds in every base genus and for every compatible branching pattern. For any CM abelian variety, the conclusion also holds for every self-power of its product with the Jacobian, on the same Hodge-generic locus. We also prove the conjecture on every self-power of a very general member of the full smooth labelled family of diagonal complete intersections cut out by at most two equations of a common degree, in every dimension and every degree at least two.
version_note: This version updates citations to revised manuscripts in this collection; see the [previous version](../Abelian-covers-Gale-correspondences-and-the-Hodge-conjecture-for-powers-September-30-2026/paper.pdf).

tex.abstract:
We prove the rational Hodge conjecture on every self-power of the
Jacobian at each tensor Hodge-generic point of the full marked variation
of a connected abelian cover of curves.  This holds in every base genus
and for every compatible branching pattern.  For any CM abelian variety,
the conclusion also holds for every self-power of its product with the
Jacobian, on the same Hodge-generic locus.
We also prove the conjecture on every self-power of a very general
member of the full smooth labelled family of diagonal complete
intersections cut out by at most two equations of a common degree, in
every dimension and every degree at least two.
sections: Abelian covers with full marked variation

statements.title: Powers of abelian-cover Jacobians
statements.label: p4:abelian-covers
statements.text:
For each fixed connected topological abelian cover as above, every
\(s\in\mathcal T_\phi^{\mathrm{Hg}}\), every complex CM abelian variety
\(M\), and every integer \(N\geq1\), the rational Hodge conjecture holds
in every codimension of
\[
 \bigl(\Jac(C_s)\times M\bigr)^N.
\]
It also holds for \(C_s^a\times M^b\) for all integers \(a,b\geq0\),
where a zeroth power means a point.  The point \(s\) is chosen before
\(M\): the same Hodge-generic locus works for every CM companion.

statements.title: Powers of diagonal complete intersections
statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Fix \(n\geq2\),
\(d\geq0\), \(c\in\{0,1,2\}\), and put \(m=d+c+1\).
Outside a countable union of proper closed algebraic subsets of
\(\D_{c,m}\), the rational Hodge conjecture holds in every codimension
on \(X_A^u\) for every \(u\geq1\).  For \(c\leq1\), or for \(d=0\),
no exceptional subset is needed.

statements.title: Fermat supply
statements.label: p4:fermat-supply
statements.text:
For integers $n\ge2$ and $a\ge0$, let
\[
 F_n^a=\{x_0^n+\cdots+x_{a+1}^n=0\}
       \subset\mathbb P^{a+1}_\C.
\]
For every degree $q$, there are finitely many CM abelian varieties
$B_\nu$, integers $j_\nu$, and rational algebraic correspondences
$\Gamma_\nu\in\CH^{\dim B_\nu+j_\nu}(B_\nu\times F_n^a)_\Q$
such that the sum of their maps
\[
 \bigoplus_\nu H^{q-2j_\nu}(B_\nu,\Q)(-j_\nu)
 \xrightarrow{\;\sum_\nu(\Gamma_\nu)_*\;}
 H^q(F_n^a,\Q)
\]
is surjective.  One may take every $B_\nu$ to be a power of the
CM abelian variety $\operatorname{Jac}(F_n^1)$, allowing its
zeroth power, a point.  In dimension zero the finite reduced
scheme $F_n^0$ is supplied component by component by points.

statements.title: Determinants for abelian covers
statements.label: p4:abelian-determinants
statements.text:
Let a finite abelian group $P$ act faithfully on a smooth connected
projective complex curve $C$, and put $B=C/P$.  For every
character $\chi:P\to k^\times$, the line
$D(H^1(C,k)_\chi)$ is CM-supplied.  This includes the zero
character spaces.  For the trivial character the line is
generated by a rational algebraic cycle class.

For $\chi\ne1$, let $r_\chi$ be the number of branch points of
$C/\ker\chi\to B$.  Then
\[
 \dim_k H^1(C,k)_\chi=2g(B)+r_\chi-2.
\]
The number $r_\chi$ counts precisely the original branch points
whose inertia is not killed by $\chi$.

For a fixed $P$, the CM sources for all these lines can be taken
to be powers of one fixed product of Fermat-curve Jacobians
depending only on $P$, not on the complex structure of $C$.

statements.title: Saturated data for the marked cover family
statements.label: p4:cover-saturation
statements.text:
For every connected topological abelian cover and full marked family
defined above, and every \(s\in\mathcal T_\phi^{\mathrm{Hg}}\), the
Jacobian \(\operatorname{Jac}(C_s)\) admits saturated data in
Companion results~\ref{comp:saturated}.
statements.section_title: Abelian covers with full marked variation

statements.title: Positive-genus character projections
statements.label: p4:positive-projections
statements.text:
For $h\ge1$, every nonzero nontrivial character space is mixed in Hodge
type at every scalar conjugate.  At every
$s\in\mathcal T_\phi^{\mathrm{Hg}}$ the image
of the derived Hodge group on that space is the full standard special
linear or full standard symplectic group.  The invariant character space,
when nonzero, has Hodge dimensions $(h,h)$ and full standard symplectic
derived action.
statements.section_title: Abelian covers with full marked variation

statements.title: Sphere projections
statements.label: p4:sphere-projections
statements.text:
At every $s\in\mathcal T_\phi^{\mathrm{Hg}}$ the following assertions hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If $n\ge3$, then either $M_\chi$ is finite and the Hodge
action on its rational scalar orbit is toric, or
\[
 M_\chi^\circ=
 \begin{cases}
  \operatorname{Sp}(W_\chi),&\chi^2=1,\\
  \operatorname{SL}(W_\chi),&\chi^2\ne1.
 \end{cases}
\]
In the infinite case the derived Hodge projection is the same
standard group.
\item In dimensions at most two every non-toric character space
has dimension two and has standard derived Hodge projection
$\operatorname{SL}_2$.
\end{enumerate}
Here the symplectic group is for the restricted polarization on
the order-two character space.  Each non-toric character space
is supported by a single simple ideal of $\operatorname{Lie}(J^{\mathrm{der}})_k$.
statements.section_title: Abelian covers with full marked variation

statements.title: Links within one sphere cover
statements.label: p4:sphere-links
statements.text:
Suppose two non-toric character spaces $W_\chi,W_{\chi'}$
are supported by the same simple Hodge Lie ideal.
They have the same dimension $n$ and standard derived
representations equivalent up to duality.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If $n\ge3$, then $\chi'=\chi$ or $\chi^{-1}$.
The inverse character is identified by the polarization with the
polarized dual.  If the standard group is symplectic, the
character has order two and the space is mixed at every
scalar translate.
\item If $n=2$, one can choose either $W_\chi$ or its polarized
dual as model so that an equivalence of its derived
representation with $W_{\chi'}$ respects the Hodge circle at
every scalar translate.
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Exact smooth locus
statements.label: prop:smooth-locus
statements.text:
Let \(n\geq2\), \(1\leq c\leq m-1\), and let \(A\) be a rank-\(c\)
matrix with \(m\) columns.  Then \(X_A\) is a complete intersection
of dimension \(m-c-1\).  It is smooth if and only if every
\(c\)-column minor of \(A\) is nonzero.  This condition is equivalent
to coordinate generality of \(P=\ker A\).

statements.title: Character cohomology and support
statements.label: prop:characters
statements.text:
For \(P\in\U_{d,m}\), invariant cohomology is the pullback of
\(H^*(\PP(P),\kk)\) and is spanned by algebraic hyperplane
classes.  Every nontrivial character occurs only in degree \(d\),
and
\[
 \dim_{\kk} W_{P,b}=\binom{s(b)-2}{d}\quad(b\ne0),
\]
where the value is zero if \(s(b)-2<d\).

If \(S=S(b)\) has \(s\geq d+2\) elements, projection identifies
\(P\) with a coordinate-general plane \(P_S\subset\C^S\)
and defines a finite quotient \(p_S:X_P\to X_{P_S}\).
Its pullback is an isomorphism
\(H^d(X_{P_S},\kk)_{b|_S}\simeq W_{P,b}\).
These descriptions commute with smooth parameter pullback.

statements.title: Perfect Gale tensor
statements.label: thm:gale
statements.text:
Let \(P\in\U_{d,m}\), set
\[
 Q=P^\perp\quad\text{for }\sum_i u_i v_i,\qquad d'=m-d-2.
\]
Then \(Q\in\U_{d',m}\), and
\[
 f_P:X_P\times X_Q\longrightarrow F_n^{m-2},\qquad
 ([x_i],[y_i])\longmapsto[x_i y_i]
\]
is an algebraic morphism.  For every full-support character \(b\),
\(L_b=H^{m-2}(F_n^{m-2},\kk)_b\) is a line, and pullback maps it
to \(W_{P,b}\otimes W_{Q,b}\).  For every \(0\ne\ell\in L_b\), the
tensor \(f_P^*\ell\) has full pairing rank: the associated map
\(W_{P,b}^*\to W_{Q,b}\) is an isomorphism.  This includes \(d=0\)
and \(d'=0\).

statements.title: Gale cohomology supply
statements.label: prop:supply
statements.text:
Let \(P\in\U_{d,m}\).  For each \(S\subset\{1,\ldots,m\}\)
with \(s=|S|\geq d+2\), put
\[
 P_S=\pr_S P,\quad Q_S=P_S^\perp,\quad Y_S=X_{Q_S},
 \quad h_S=s-d-2.
\]
There is a rational algebraic correspondence from
\(F_n^{s-2}\times Y_S\) to \(X_P\), with degree shift
\(-2h_S\), whose image after scalar extension contains
\(W_{P,b}\) for every character with support \(S\).

Together with hyperplane cycles from a point, these finitely many
maps span the full rational cohomology of \(X_P\).  In the middle
degree the source maps may be taken on the entire groups
\[
 H^{d+2h_S}(F_n^{s-2}\times Y_S,\Q)(h_S).
\]

statements.title: The branch map
statements.label: prop:parameter
statements.text:
The normalized branch configuration is the regular morphism
\[
 \lambda:\D_{2,m}\to M_m,\qquad
 z_i=\frac{\Delta_{2i}\Delta_{13}}{\Delta_{1i}\Delta_{23}}
 \quad(i\geq4).
\]
There is a global product isomorphism
\(\D_{2,m}\simeq M_m\times(\Gm)^{m-1}\) under which \(\lambda\)
is projection.  It is smooth and surjective, and the quotient by
the effective coefficient torus \((\Gm)^m/\Gm\) is \(M_m\).

statements.title: The normalized root family and its fixed deck datum
statements.label: prop:cover-family
statements.text:
The map
\[
 \rho:\widetilde\D_{2,m,n}:=M_m\times(\Gm)^{m-1}\to\D_{2,m},
 \qquad (z,h_2,\ldots,h_m)\mapsto(z,h_2^n,\ldots,h_m^n)
\]
is a connected finite \'{e}tale cover of degree \(n^{m-1}\).
Set \(h_1=1\).  Over it, the algebraic maps
\([y_i]\mapsto[h_i y_i]\) and \([x_i]\mapsto[h_i^{-1}x_i]\)
identify the normalized dual and original root families with
the families for \(Q(t,z)\) and \(P(t,z)\), respectively.
They commute with \(G_{m,n}\).

Every \(q_z\) is a connected \(G_{m,n}\)-cover of \(\PP^1\),
with ordered branch points
\((\infty,0,1,z_4,\ldots,z_m)\).  Identify
\[
 G_{m,n}\simeq(\Z/n)^m/\langle(1,\ldots,1)\rangle
\]
using \(\zeta_n=\exp(2\pi i/n)\).  Its ordered positive local
monodromies are the images \((\bar e_1,\ldots,\bar e_m)\) of
the standard basis.  The family runs over all ordered branch
configurations with this fixed deck datum.

statements.label: cor:good-curves
statements.text:
There is a countable union \(Z\) of proper closed algebraic subsets
of \(M_m\) such that
for \(z\notin Z\), every CM abelian \(B\), and every \(N\geq1\),
the rational Hodge conjecture holds on
\((\Jac(X_{Q_0(z)})\times B)^N\).  The same holds for the dual
curve at every point of \(\D_{2,m}\setminus\lambda^{-1}(Z)\).

Absolutely Continuous Spectrum for Weak-Disorder Anderson Models in Dimensions at Least Three
abstract: For each fixed dimension d ≥ 3 and each fixed sufficiently small positive disorder strength, we prove that the Anderson operator on ℤd with independent uniform site potentials almost surely has purely absolutely continuous spectrum with nonzero weight on an open energy interval. The interval may depend on d but is independent of the disorder strength. This settles the purely absolutely continuous energy-range question in Simon's Problem 1 for this model.

tex.abstract:
For each fixed dimension $d\ge3$ and each fixed sufficiently small positive
disorder strength, we prove that the Anderson operator on $\mathbb Z^d$ with
independent uniform site potentials almost surely has purely absolutely
continuous spectrum with nonzero weight on an open energy interval. The
interval may depend on $d$ but is independent of the disorder strength.
This settles the purely absolutely continuous energy-range question in
Simon's Problem~1 for this model.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is a fixed sufficiently small number $e_2\in(0,1/100)$ such that,
for every fixed integer $d\ge3$, there is a number $\lambda_d>0$
with the following property. Set
\begin{equation}
 I_d=
 \begin{cases}
   (-6+e_2/2,-6+e_2),&d=3,\\
   -2d+(1/200,1/100),&d\ge4.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
Then
for every fixed $0<\lambda<\lambda_d$, almost surely
\[
 I_d\subset\sigma(H_{\lambda,\omega}),\qquad
 \chi_{I_d}(H_{\lambda,\omega})\ell^2(\ZZ^d)
       \subset\mathcal H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H_{\lambda,\omega}).
\]
In particular, the spectral restriction to $I_d$ is purely absolutely
continuous and $\chi_{I_d}(H_{\lambda,\omega})\ne0$.
For $d\ge4$, one may take $\lambda_d=\sqrt3\,2^{-n_*(d)}$, where the finite-matrix
specification of $n_*(d)$ is given in Definition~\ref{def:threshold}.
For $d=3$, the proof supplies an existential positive threshold.

statements.title: Spectral coexistence
statements.label: cor:coexistence
statements.text:
For every fixed $d\ge3$ and every fixed $0<\lambda<\lambda_d$,
there is a deterministic number $\delta_{d,\lambda}\in(0,\lambda/2]$
such that the open interval
\[
 J_{d,\lambda}
 =(-2d-\lambda,-2d-\lambda+\delta_{d,\lambda})
\]
is disjoint from $I_d$ and, almost surely, both
$\chi_{I_d}(H_{\lambda,\omega})$ and
$\chi_{J_{d,\lambda}}(H_{\lambda,\omega})$ are nonzero.
The restriction to $I_d$ is purely absolutely continuous, whereas the
restriction to $J_{d,\lambda}$ is pure point with exponentially decaying
eigenfunctions. The probability-one event may depend on $d$ and $\lambda$.

statements.title: Finite-volume certificate
statements.label: prop:certificate
statements.text:
For each fixed $d\ge3$ there exist $\lambda_0(d)>0$ and constants $c,C>0$
with the following property. For every fixed $0<\lambda<\lambda_0(d)$,
every $E\in I_d$, and every $m\ge4n_0$, one
can use auxiliary independent randomness to construct an event
$\mathcal S_m$, depending on the fixed $E,\lambda$, such that
$\PP(\mathcal S_m)\to1$ as $m\to\infty$.
On $\mathcal S_m$ there are a set $A\subset\mathbb T_L$, $|A|\ge N/2$,
and complex numbers $r_i$, $i\in A$, satisfying
\[
 |r_i|\le C,\qquad c\le\Im r_i\le C,
\]
such that
\[
 \widehat G=(H_m-E-\eta\diag_A r)^{-1}
 \quad\text{exists},\qquad
 \Im\widehat G_{ii}\ge c\quad(i\in A).
\]
For fixed $d$ the constants are independent of $E,\lambda,m$, and
the convergence in probability is uniform in $E\in I_d$ for each
fixed $\lambda$. The failure estimates are also uniformly small for
all $m\ge4n_0$ and $u\in(1/4,1]$ once $n_0$ is sufficiently large.
The potential in $H_m$ consists entirely of the original true variables.
statements.section_title: A finite-volume certificate and the matrix state

statements.title: Initialization
statements.label: prop:initialization
statements.text:
For each fixed $d\ge3$ there are $\lambda_0(d)>0$ and positive
constants $a_0,B,c,C,C_0$, depending only on the fixed dimension and
window, with the following
property.  For
$0<\lambda<\lambda_0(d)$, the scales in \eqref{eq:scales},
$m\ge4n_0$, $L=4^{20m}$, and every $E\in I_d$,
write $t=t_{n_0}$.  There is a scalar $r$ with
\[
 |\Re r|\le B,\qquad a_0\le p:=\Im r\le B,
 \qquad
 r=N^{-1}\sum_k\frac1{a(k)-E-tr}.
\]
It is the unique solution in the displayed rectangle and depends
continuously on $E$.

Take all sites active, all partial potentials zero, and
$g=(H_0-E-tr)^{-1}$, where $H_0$ is the free hopping matrix on
$\mathbb T_L$.  With $h,K,F,D,X$ as in
Section~\ref{sec:state}, one has $g_{ii}=r$, $\|K\|\le1/10$, and
\[
 \max_i\sum_j|h_{ij}|^4\le\tfrac1{10}t^{1+\delta}.
\]
The kernel of $D$ is exactly the constants, and on neutral charges,
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 X&\ge ct^2\Lambda^+,\qquad X\ge c\Id,\\
 X&\le C_0\Id+Ct^2\Lambda^+,\\
 X&\le(1+t^\kappa)p^{-2}\Id+Ct\Lambda^+.
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
Thus this state satisfies \eqref{eq:comparators}, with startup
$b=t_{n_0}t=t^2$ and constants independent of $E,\lambda,m$.

statements.title: Ordinary-sweep increment estimates
statements.label: prop:sweep-increments
statements.text:
Consider a current numerical prefix of a sweep whose initial physical
state satisfies the bounds at a stage boundary in Section~\ref{sec:state},
including self-consistency, and is duplicated as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:duplication}. Assume that this prestate satisfies
\eqref{eq:sweep-global-caps}--\eqref{eq:sweep-row-lag-caps},
the broad bounds on $r,p$, and the active-site count.
For the lag estimates also assume
$\|(\Id-K)^{-1}\|_{\infty\to\infty}\le C\ell$.
Let $\mathcal B$ be any subset of the remaining bit ports and use
fresh scalars satisfying \eqref{eq:sweep-digit-moments}.
Then the estimates of Lemmas~\ref{lem:sweep-j},
\ref{lem:sweep-laplacian}, \ref{lem:sweep-lag}, and
\ref{lem:sweep-fourth} hold before division by the number of remaining
permutation slots.

More precisely, let $\mathcal H$ be a finite-dimensional real Hilbert
space and let $B:\mathcal H\to$ initial-port potentials be a fixed
linear extension map with
\[
 W(Bv)\le C\|v\|_{\mathcal H}^2,\qquad
 \|B^*y\|_{\mathcal H^*}^2\le CW^*(y).
\]
The dual estimate is required for neutral charges $y$.
Interpret $B^*L_xB$ as a self-adjoint operator by the Riesz
identification. The following table gives a bound for the summed
conditional mean, the pathwise square stack, and a single jump:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
 \text{increment}&\text{summed mean}&\text{square stack}&\text{jump}\\ \hline
 J_x&t^\beta&t^{\delta/2}&t^{\delta/4}\\
 B^*L_xB&t^\beta&t^{\delta/2}&t^{\delta/4}\\
 \Delta\widetilde U_i^x&
 \ell(t^{2\beta}+\sqrt t)+\ell^2t^{\delta/2}&
 \ell^2t^\delta&\ell t^{\delta/2}\\
 R_i^x/H_*&t^\kappa&t^\kappa&t^{\kappa/2}
\end{array}
\]
All entries are upper bounds up to a fixed multiplicative constant.
For $J_x$ the square stack includes both orders, as required by
Hermitian dilation.
statements.section_title: The algebra and estimates of an ordinary sweep

statements.title: Ordinary sweep
statements.label: prop:ordinary-sweep
statements.text:
Suppose a committed stage state satisfies the complete stage-boundary
bounds of Section~\ref{sec:state}, including the broad bounds and
comparators \eqref{eq:comparators}, the self-consistency relation
\(r_i=g_{ii}\), the fourth-power bound \(H_*=t^{1+\delta}\), the boundary
cap \(\|K_{\rm old}\|\le1/3\), and
\eqref{eq:local-metric-input}.  Assume also that at least \(N/2\)
physical sites are active, where \(N\) is the torus volume, and assume
the conditional slot and scalar interface above.
Let \(\theta\in[.25,.625]\) be the reserve fraction, so the new
damping scale is \(t'=\theta t\).  This includes
\(\theta=t_{n+1}/t_n\) at ordinary stages and \(\theta=1/2\) in the
final residual sweep.  Set \(w=1-\theta\) and use port weights
\(k_{\rm bit}=w^{1/4}\), \(k_{\rm reserve}=\theta^{1/4}\) in
Lemma~\ref{lem:duplication}.  Queried variables in port normalization
are real variables satisfying the conditional moment and size
assumptions above.  If every failed trial is followed by a retry supplied
with a new independent permutation and fresh inputs satisfying this
interface, the trial process terminates almost surely.  The indexed
auxiliary signs supply these retries for digit sweeps; the actual final
sweep instead aborts at its first failure.  Every completed sweep leaves
the terminal set unchanged and has the following endpoint bounds, with \(r,p\) frozen
in physical normalization:
\begin{align*}
 X_{\rm new}
  &=(1+O(t^{.10\delta}))
       \big[\theta X_{\rm old}
               +(1-\theta)\diag(p^{-2})\big],\\
 \|K_{\rm new}\|&\le\|K_{\rm old}\|+t^{.10\delta},\\
 \sup_i|g^{\rm new}_{ii}-r_i|&\le Ct^\beta,\\
 \sup_i\sum_j|h^{\rm new}_{ij}|^4
   &\le\big(\theta^2+Ct^{.0005\delta}\big)t^{1+\delta}
     <.7(\theta t)^{1+\delta}.
\end{align*}
The first line denotes two-sided quadratic-form bounds on neutral
charges.  A first trial at any tile fails conditionally with probability
at most \(e^{-t^{-c}}\).

In particular, with \(b'=\theta b\), the lower and low-frequency
constants in \eqref{eq:comparators} change by relative
\(1+O(t^{.10\delta})\); the rough diagonal upper constant becomes at
most \((1+O(t^{.10\delta}))(\theta C_0+C)\); and the sharp diagonal
upper coefficient becomes
\(1+\theta t^\kappa+O(t^{.10\delta})\).
statements.section_title: Local trials and the ordinary sweep

statements.title: Spatial decay of a core completion
statements.label: cor:core-decay

statements.title: Preparation of a small component
statements.label: prop:clearing-trial
statements.text:
Assume \eqref{eq:clearing-broad}, the geometry and conditional residual
inputs just stated, and $1\le |B|\le r_*$.  At trial start suppose
\begin{equation}
 \max_i\sum_k|h^0_{ik}|^4\le .8H_*,\qquad
 \max_i|g^0_{ii}-r_i|=o(t^{\beta_w}),
\end{equation}
uniformly over the input states under consideration.  Assume also that every
true terminal principal matrix at the fixed energy is invertible.
For all sufficiently small $t$, the stopped trial is measurable and satisfies
\[
 \PP(\mathrm{FAIL}\mid\mathcal F_0)\le\exp(-t^{-c_2})
\]
for a fixed $c_2>0$.  The constants are independent of the torus volume and of
the component.  On DONE, fewer than $n_h$ exterior sites carry their true values and
are provisionally removed, the budgets \eqref{eq:clearing-budgets} hold, and
\begin{equation}
 \max_{i\in R}(\Pi_{\Ran\mathcal C})_{ii}\le2l_*.
\end{equation}
Here $\mathcal C=S_{RB}$ is formed from the final active inverse before
completion of $B$. Thus DONE is the successful preparation outcome. The
subsequent deterministic core completion and the single successful commit
are specified with the clearing schedule in Section~\ref{sec:assembly}.

statements.title: Deterministic assembly of committed changes
statements.label: prop:committed-assembly
statements.text:
Fix a clearing stage with parameter $t$. Consider the finite sequence of
its committed numerical states: the initial post-sweep state, indexed by
$0$, and the states after successive successful clearings, indexed by
$a=1,\ldots,k_{\max}$. Failed trials leave this numerical sequence
unchanged. Let $A_a\subset A_{a-1}$ be the active sites after operation
$a$, put $O_a=A_{a-1}\setminus A_a$, and let $T_a$ be the complement of
$A_a$ in the physical torus.

At each index use the physical state of Section~\ref{sec:state}: the
sites in $T_a$ have their exact true potentials, the sites in $A_a$ have
their current partial potentials, and $M^{(a)}$ is the real terminal-Schur
matrix. The relevant true terminal principal matrices are invertible at
the fixed energy. Use the restriction of one frozen vector $r$ at every
index, with $p=\Im r$ bounded above and below by positive constants, and
write
\[
 g^{(a)}=(M^{(a)}-t\diag(r|_{A_a}))^{-1},\qquad
 h^{(a)}=\sqrt t\,g^{(a)},\qquad
 K^{(a)}_{ij}=(h^{(a)}_{ij})^2,\qquad
 F^{(a)}_{ij}=|h^{(a)}_{ij}|^2.
\]
Let $D_a$ be the Ward Laplacian of this state, so
\[
 D_a(f)=\frac12\sum_{i,j\in A_a}p_ip_jF^{(a)}_{ij}|f_i-f_j|^2.
\]
With $q_i^{(a)}=\Im g^{(a)}_{ii}$, the Ward identity gives
$F^{(a)}p=q^{(a)}$.
The word committed here identifies the numerical endpoints. The comparison
at the initial endpoint is an input; its transport to later endpoints is
the conclusion below.

Assume at the initial state that, on potentials modulo constants,
\begin{equation}
 cW\le D_0\le CW,\qquad
 \max_{i\in A_0}\sum_{j\in A_0}|h^{(0)}_{ij}|^4
 \le .7H_*,\qquad
 \max_{i\in A_0}|g^{(0)}_{ii}-r_i|\le Ct^{.42\delta}.
 
\end{equation}
Here $H_*=t^{1+\delta}$ and
$W(f)=\inf_{f=\alpha+v|_{A_0}}
 (\|\alpha\|_2^2+b^{-1}\|\nabla v\|_2^2)$, with $b=t_{n_0}t$.

Assume also the geometric bounds supplied by
Lemma~\ref{lem:clearing-locality}. For $D_s\asymp t^{-8-\nu}$, each
$O_a$ lies in the ball of radius $D_s$ about its anchor $z_a$ and has
size at most $Cn_h$, where $n_h=\lfloor t^{-1-.46\delta}\rfloor$.
The anchors are distinct. The cube halos $Q_a,Q'_a$
of radii $100D_s,200D_s$ are embedded lattice cubes in the torus, and
each family has overlap at most $Ct^{-d\nu}$. At every indexed state,
$|A_a|\ge N/2$ and
\[
 d_{T_a}(u,v)\ge\tfrac12\dist(u,v)-m',\qquad m'\le t^{-1.03}.
\]

For each operation set
\[
 a^{(a)}=h^{(a)}-h^{(a-1)}|_{A_a\times A_a}.
\]
Assume these actual survivor differences satisfy
\begin{align}
 \max_{i,j\in A_a}|a^{(a)}_{ij}|
 &\le C\sqrt t\,t^{.42\delta},\notag\\
 \max_{i\in A_a}\sum_{j\in A_a}|a^{(a)}_{ij}|^2
 &\le Ct^{.25\delta},\qquad
 \sum_{i,j\in A_a}|a^{(a)}_{ij}|^2
 \le Ct^{-1-.47\delta}.
 
\end{align}
Assume further that, with constants $c,C>0$ and a fixed $P$,
\begin{equation}
 |a^{(a)}_{ij}|
 \le t^{-P}\exp\!\left\{-ct\left[
 (\dist(i,O_a)-Cm')_++(\dist(j,O_a)-Cm')_+
 \right]\right\}.
 
\end{equation}
Then, for all sufficiently small $t$, every prefix $0\le k\le k_{\max}$
satisfies
\begin{align}
 \|K^{(k)}\|&\le\|K^{(0)}\|+t^{.10\delta},
 \\
 \max_{i\in A_k}|g^{(k)}_{ii}-r_i|
 &\le Ct^{.42\delta-d\nu}=o(t^{.36\delta}),
 \\
 \max_{i\in A_k}\left(\sum_{j\in A_k}|h^{(k)}_{ij}|^4\right)^{1/4}
 &\le\left(.7^{1/4}+Ct^{.0225\delta-d\nu}\right)H_*^{1/4}
 <(.8H_*)^{1/4}.
 
\end{align}
All Schur complements in the successive definition
\[
 L_a=D_a-\Schur_{O_a}D_{a-1}\quad\hbox{on }A_a
\]
exist, and each $D_a$ has precisely the constant kernel. Extend each
$L_a$ by zero to $A_0$. Then
\begin{equation}
 \left|\sum_{a=1}^k L_a\right|
 \le t^{.10\delta}D_0
 
\end{equation}
in quadratic forms.  In particular, writing $X_k=D_k^+$, every neutral
charge $y$ supported in $A_k$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 (1+t^{.10\delta})^{-1}X_0(y)
 \le X_k(y)\le
 (1-t^{.10\delta})^{-1}X_0(y),
 
\end{equation}
where $y$ is extended by zero in $X_0(y)$.  All constants are uniform
in the number of components and the torus volume.

statements.title: Diagonal reset
statements.label: prop:reset
statements.text:
Let $g=(M-t\diag r)^{-1}$ on a nonempty active set, where $M$ is real
symmetric, $r$ is bounded, and $0<c\le p_i=\Im r_i\le C$.
Assume $\ker D=\CC\mathbf1$. Suppose $q_i=\Im g_{ii}\le C$, the lag
$e'=\diag(g)-r$ satisfies $\|e'\|_\infty=o(t^{.36\delta})$ uniformly in
the construction parameters, and
\[
 \|K\|<\tfrac12,\qquad
 \|(\Id-K)^{-1}\|_{\infty\to\infty}\le C\log(1/t).
\]
For small $t$ there is a measurable vector $\zeta$, with
$\|\zeta\|_\infty\le t^{.35\delta}$, such that for $r'=r+\zeta$ and
$g'=(M-t\diag r')^{-1}$ one has $g'_{ii}=r'_i$.
Writing $\rho=\|\zeta\|_\infty$, the changes satisfy
\begin{align}
 \max_i\|\Delta h_i\|_2&\le C\rho,
 &\max_{i,j}|\Delta h_{ij}|&\le C\sqrt t\,\rho,
 &\max_i\|\Delta h_i\|_4&\le Ct^{1/4}\rho,
 \\
 \|K'-K\|&\le C\rho,
 &(1-C\rho)D&\le D'\le(1+C\rho)D.
 
\end{align}
Here $D'$ uses $p'=\Im r'$, which remains in a fixed positive bounded
range. The corresponding inverse forms on neutral charges change by
a factor $1+O(\rho)$.
statements.section_title: Committing clearings and restoring the stage bounds

statements.title: Uniform stage bounds
statements.label: prop:deterministic-induction
statements.text:
Choose the fixed energy window and the initialization constants as in
Proposition~\ref{prop:initialization}. For sufficiently large $n_0$,
uniformly in $m\ge4n_0$ and in the fixed energy in that window, the
following statements hold along every finite history produced by the
ordinary-sweep and clearing rules, with failed trials rolled back.
At each completed stage start the diagonal fixed-point relation,
the three comparisons \eqref{eq:comparators}, the fourth-row bound
$\max_i\sum_j|h_{ij}|^4\le t^{1+\delta}$, and $\|K\|\le1/3$ hold.
The vectors $r$ remain bounded with their imaginary parts in one fixed
positive bounded range. The low comparison constants remain in fixed
positive bounded ranges, and the rough high constant $C_0$ can be
chosen independently of the stage. The kernel of $D$ consists of the
constants, at least $N/2$ sites remain active, and the terminal metric
satisfies \eqref{eq:assembly-terminal-metric}.

During a clearing stage, every committed prestate has lag
$o(t^{.36\delta})$, fourth-row sums below $.8t^{1+\delta}$, and the
comparison bounds furnished by Proposition~\ref{prop:committed-assembly}.
No comparison for $D$ or bound on $K$ is asserted at a provisional heat
prefix. All constants and smallness thresholds are independent of the
history and of the torus volume.
statements.section_title: Committing clearings and restoring the stage bounds

statements.title: Pending-site bound
statements.label: prop:witness-bound
statements.text:
There is a constant $c_{\rm h}>0$ such that, after increasing the fixed lower
cutoff $n_0$ if necessary, for every $n_0\le j\le\lfloor m/2\rfloor$ and
every torus site $x$,
\[
 \PP(x\text{ is pending at the end of stage }j)
 \le\exp(-4^{c_{\rm h}j}).
\]
All constants are uniform in $m,E,\lambda$ in the stated ranges.
statements.section_title: Failure histories and removal of pending sites

statements.title: Existence and measurability of the threshold
statements.label: prop:threshold
statements.text:
The feasibility event in \eqref{eq:threshold-criterion} is Borel, and
the set of integers in Definition~\ref{def:threshold} is nonempty.
Consequently $\lambda_d>0$. For every fixed $0<\lambda<\lambda_d$,
every $m\ge4n_0$, and every $E\in I_d$, the true operator at coupling
$\lambda$ satisfies \eqref{eq:threshold-criterion} with
$k=n_*(d)$ and certificate probability at least $1/2$.
statements.section_title: Failure histories and removal of pending sites

statements.title: Spectral readout
statements.label: prop:certificate-readout
statements.text:
Fix $d\ge3$, $\lambda>0$ and a nonempty bounded open interval $I$.
Let $H_m$ be the true Anderson operator on
$\mathbb T_m=(\ZZ/L_m\ZZ)^d$, $L_m=4^{20m}$, with independent
uniform diagonal values in $[-\lambda,\lambda]$ at every site,
and let $\eta_m\asymp4^{-m}$.
Suppose that for every fixed $E\in I$ and all sufficiently large
$m$, with probability at least $1/2$ there exist
$A\subset\mathbb T_m$ and numbers $r_i$, $i\in A$, such that
\[
 |A|\ge N_m/2,\qquad |r_i|\le B,\qquad
 0<p_-\le\Im r_i\le p_+,
\]
where $N_m=L_m^d$ and the displayed constants do not depend on
$m$ or $E$, and such that $(H_m-E-\eta_m\diag_A r)^{-1}$ exists
and its active block $\widehat G_A$, acting on $\ell^2(A)$, satisfies
\[
 \Im(\widehat G_A)_{ii}\ge q_*>0\qquad(i\in A),
\]
with $q_*$ independent of $m,E$. Every diagonal value of $H_m$, on
$A$ and on $A^c$, is already a true site value; here $A$ records the
sites retaining artificial damping. The certificate may depend on
all true variables and auxiliary randomness; no measurable
selection of $A,r$ is required. Then almost surely
\[
 I\subset\sigma(H_{\lambda,\omega}),\qquad
 \chi_I(H_{\lambda,\omega})\ell^2(\ZZ^d)
       \subset\mathcal H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H_{\lambda,\omega}).
\]
In particular, this spectral restriction is purely absolutely
continuous and $\langle e_0,\chi_I(H_{\lambda,\omega})e_0\rangle>0$.
