statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is a finite integer $N>3$, divisible by eight, and there are reduced
polynomials $f_1,f_2\in\R[z_1,\ldots,z_N]$, weighted homogeneous for
positive rational weights, such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item each $f_j$ has an isolated critical point at the origin;
\item $\ord_0f_1=2$ and $\ord_0f_2=3$;
\item there is a homeomorphism germ of ambient pairs
\[
 (\C^N,V(f_1),0)\ \cong\ (\C^N,V(f_2),0).
\]
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Milnor
statements.label: bg:milnor
statements.text:
Let $s\geq2$, and let $f:(\mathbb C^s,0)\to(\mathbb C,0)$ be a holomorphic germ with an isolated
critical point at $0$, with $f(0)=0$.  For sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, the link
$K_f=f^{-1}(0)\cap S^{2s-1}_\varepsilon$ is a smooth closed manifold of
dimension $2s-3$, and
\[
 f/|f|:S^{2s-1}_\varepsilon\setminus K_f\longrightarrow S^1
\]
is a locally trivial fibration.  Each fiber is the interior of its closure
$F_f$, a compact manifold with boundary $K_f$.  Both $F_f$ and its interior
are homotopy equivalent to a finite bouquet of $(s-1)$-spheres.
The link is $(s-3)$-connected.

statements.title: Thom--Sebastiani--Sakamoto
statements.label: bg:ts
statements.text:
Suppose $f$ and $g$ have isolated critical points in $a$ and $b$ variables,
respectively.  There is an isomorphism of integral lattices
\[
 L_{f+g}\cong L_f\otimes_{\mathbb Z}L_g
\]
under which
\[
 M_{f+g}\cong M_f\otimes M_g,
 \qquad
 S_{f+g}\cong(-1)^{ab}S_f\otimes S_g.
\]
The assertion includes one-variable powers, with reduced zeroth homology.

statements.title: Weighted homogeneous spectrum
statements.label: bg:spectrum
statements.text:
If $f$ is weighted homogeneous of normalized degree $1$ and has an isolated
critical point, its spectral polynomial is
\begin{equation}
 P_f(t)=\sum_{\beta\in\operatorname{Sp}^{+}(f)}t^\beta
       =\prod_{j=1}^s\frac{t^{w_j}-t}{1-t^{w_j}}.
\end{equation}
Exponents are counted with multiplicity.  Their classes modulo $\mathbb Z$
determine the eigenvalues of $M_f$ by exponentiation, with a fixed choice
of sign in the exponent.  The operator $M_f$ has finite order.

statements.title: Real Seifert forms from the spectrum
statements.label: bg:real
statements.text:
Let $f$ and $g$ be isolated weighted homogeneous singularities in the same
number of variables.  If their multisets of positive spectral exponents
agree modulo $2\mathbb Z$, their real Seifert forms are isomorphic.

statements.title: Hertling--Mase
statements.label: bg:orlik
statements.text:
Suppose $f$ is a sum of chains
\[
 x_1^{a_1}x_2+\cdots+x_{r-1}^{a_{r-1}}x_r+x_r^{a_r},
 \qquad a_i\geq2,
\]
including chains with $r=1$.  Write the characteristic polynomial of
$M_f$ as $\prod_d\Phi_d(t)^{c_d}$, where $\Phi_d$ is cyclotomic.
Then, as an integral module with operator $t=M_f$,
\begin{equation}
 (L_f,M_f)\cong
 \bigoplus_{j=1}^{\max c_d}\mathbb Z[t]/\bigl(p_j(t)\bigr),
 \qquad p_j(t)=\prod_{c_d\geq j}\Phi_d(t).
\end{equation}
In particular, the eigenvalues with multiplicity determine this integral
monodromy module within the indicated class of singularities.

statements.title: Hasse--Minkowski
statements.label: bg:hasse
statements.text:
Two nondegenerate quadratic forms over a number field $F$ are isometric
over $F$ if and only if they are isometric over $F_v$ for every place
$v$, including the archimedean places.

statements.title: Strong approximation
statements.label: bg:approximation
statements.text:
Let $G$ be a connected, simply connected, absolutely almost simple
algebraic group over a number field $F$.  If
$\prod_{v\mid\infty}G(F_v)$ is noncompact, then $G(F)$ is dense in
$G(\mathbb A_{F,f})$, the group of finite adelic points.

statements.title: Smale and Levine
statements.label: bg:classification
statements.text:
A smooth closed manifold of dimension $d\geq5$ that is homotopy
equivalent to $S^d$ is homeomorphic to $S^d$.

Let $q\geq3$, and let $K_1,K_2\subset S^{2q+1}$ be smooth oriented
submanifolds homeomorphic to $S^{2q-1}$.  Suppose the knots are
\emph{simple}, meaning
\[
 \pi_1(S^{2q+1}\setminus K_j)\cong\mathbb Z,
 \qquad
 \pi_i(S^{2q+1}\setminus K_j)=0\quad(2\leq i\leq q-1).
\]
If their integral Seifert matrices are congruent, then they are
ambiently isotopic.  In particular their embedded sphere pairs are
homeomorphic.

statements.title: The seeds
statements.label: seed:seeds

statements.title: Removing eigenvalue one
statements.label: seed:prepared
statements.text:
In two new variables on each side, put
\begin{equation}
 q_j=p_j+x^5+y^7,\qquad j=1,2,
 \qquad s=s_0+2.
\end{equation}
These are real-coefficient isolated sums of chains in the same even
number $s$ of variables, with orders $2$ and $3$.  Their real Seifert
forms are isomorphic, and their integral monodromy modules are
isomorphic.  Both monodromies have odd order dividing
\[
 m=3^{12}\cdot5\cdot7,
\]
and neither has eigenvalue $1$.

statements.title: Odd-prime tensor squares
statements.label: local:odd-primes
statements.text:
Let $L$ be a finite free $\Z_\ell$-module, with $\ell$ odd, and let
$T$ be an automorphism of $L$.  If $B_1,B_2$ are unimodular symmetric
forms preserved by $T$, then
\[
 (L\otimes L,T\otimes T,B_1\otimes B_1)
 \cong
 (L\otimes L,T\otimes T,B_2\otimes B_2)
\]
by an equivariant integral isometry.
statements.section_title: Local and rational isometries of tensor squares

statements.title: Dyadic uniqueness
statements.label: local:dyadic
statements.text:
Let $L$ be a finite free $\Z_2$-module, and let $T$ satisfy $T^m=1$
for an odd $m$.  Suppose $1$ is not an eigenvalue of $T$ on
$L\otimes\Q_2$.  Any two $T$-invariant unimodular symmetric forms
on $L$ are equivariantly isometric over $\Z_2$.
statements.section_title: Local and rational isometries of tensor squares

statements.title: Local and rational square isometries
statements.label: local:rational
statements.text:
Set
\[
 A_j=(L_j,T_j,B_j)^{\otimes2}.
\]
There are an equivariant rational isometry
$R:A_1\otimes\Q\longrightarrow A_2\otimes\Q$ and, for every prime
$\ell$, an equivariant isometry
$D_\ell:A_1\otimes\Z_\ell\longrightarrow A_2\otimes\Z_\ell$.
These can be chosen so that $D_\ell=R$ after extension to $\Q_\ell$
for all but finitely many primes.
statements.section_title: Local and rational isometries of tensor squares

statements.title: Integral equivariant isometry
statements.label: global:integral
statements.text:
The triples $H_1$ and $H_2$ in \eqref{global:final-data} are
isometric over $\Z$: there is a lattice isomorphism
$U:\Lambda_1\longrightarrow\Lambda_2$ satisfying
\[
 U\Theta_1=\Theta_2U,
 \qquad U^{\mathsf t}\beta_2U=\beta_1.
\]
statements.section_title: From local isometries to an integral isometry

statements.title: Negative answer to Arnold's corank problem
statements.label: topo:arnold-corank
statements.text:
In the finite ambient dimension $N>3$ divisible by eight
in~\eqref{topo:dimension}, the polynomials $f_1,f_2$
in~\eqref{topo:polynomials} have different Hessian coranks, although
their reduced complex hypersurface germs are ambiently homeomorphic.
Both polynomials have real coefficients, are weighted homogeneous with
positive rational weights, and have isolated critical points at the origin.
statements.section_title: From the integral forms to the ambient germs

statements.title: Right-topological multiplicity and parity counterexamples
statements.label: topo:right-equivalence
statements.text:
For the same polynomials $f_1,f_2$ and the single finite ambient dimension
$N>3$ divisible by eight in Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, there is a homeomorphism
germ
\[
 \varphi:(\C^N,0)\longrightarrow(\C^N,0)
 \qquad\text{such that}\qquad
 f_1=f_2\circ\varphi.
\]
Nevertheless, their multiplicities are respectively $2$ and $3$. Thus
neither multiplicity nor multiplicity modulo two is invariant under
topological right equivalence, even for reduced real-coefficient weighted
homogeneous holomorphic germs with positive rational weights and isolated
critical points at the origin.
statements.section_title: From the integral forms to the ambient germs

statements.title: Initial-form Milnor-fibre counterexamples
statements.label: topo:tangent-milnor
statements.text:
In the single ambient dimension $N+1$, put
\[
 \widetilde f_j(z,t)=f_j(z)+t^2,\qquad j=1,2.
\]
The germs $\widetilde f_1,\widetilde f_2:(\C^{N+1},0)\to(\C,0)$ are
topologically right equivalent and have isolated critical points at the
origin, but
\[
 H_0\bigl((\widetilde f_1)_*^{-1}(1);\Z\bigr)\cong\Z,
 \qquad
 H_0\bigl((\widetilde f_2)_*^{-1}(1);\Z\bigr)\cong\Z^2.
\]
Thus integral homology of the initial-form Milnor fibre is not invariant
under topological right equivalence, already in degree zero. In particular,
the initial-form Milnor-fibre homotopy conjecture of Budur, Fern\'andez de
Bobadilla, L\^e, and Nguyen
\cite[Conjecture~1.7 in arXiv v3]{BudurEtAl2022ContactLoci} fails.

title: An Almost-Linear Approximation Scheme for Edit Distance
abstract: We give a uniform randomized approximation scheme for unit-cost edit distance. For every fixed rational \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), it estimates the distance between arbitrary explicitly stored strings of total length N within a factor \(1+\varepsilon\) with probability at least 2/3, in worst-case expected time \(N^{1+o(1)}\) on a logarithmic-word RAM. The algorithm supports polynomially bounded integer alphabets and returns zero deterministically on equal strings.

tex.abstract:
We give a uniform randomized approximation scheme for unit-cost edit distance.
For every fixed rational $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, it estimates the distance
between arbitrary explicitly stored strings of total length $N$ within a
factor $1+\varepsilon$ with probability at least $2/3$, in worst-case expected
time $N^{1+o(1)}$ on a logarithmic-word RAM.
The algorithm supports polynomially bounded integer alphabets and returns zero
deterministically on equal strings.
sections: Predicted bands and the refined tables
A comparison tree and cost-weighted curvature
Conditional regret and the first crossing
Accuracy and the sequence of seed passes
Lazy evaluation and the expected work bound

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is one uniform randomized algorithm that, given $x,y$ and a rational
$\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, returns a nonnegative integer $\widehat D$ such that
\[
 \Pr\bigl[\ED(x,y)\le \widehat D\le(1+\varepsilon)\ED(x,y)\bigr]
 \ge \frac23.
\]
For every fixed rational $\varepsilon$, its worst-case expected running time
on strings of total length $N$ is $N^{1+o(1)}$ as $N\to\infty$ on the
logarithmic-word RAM. The expectation is over internal randomness only,
and the bound includes input processing, preprocessing, numerical work,
random sampling and all data-structure operations. Equal strings return zero
deterministically.

statements.title: Initial estimates
statements.label: thm:seed
statements.text:
With the parameters and labeled interval tree of Section~\ref{sec:geometry},
there is a lazily evaluated random table $U^{(0)}(I,q)$ of integers in $[0,N]$
such that, with probability at least $0.99$, simultaneously at every state,
\begin{equation}
 c(I,q)\le U^{(0)}(I,q)\le A_{\mathrm{init}}c(I,q).
\end{equation}
Every zero-cost state has value zero on every execution.  Conditional on any
first request for an entry and the previously exposed randomness, its expected
evaluation cost is at most $(1+|I|)2^{o(H)}$, uniformly in the state.  This cost
bound includes arithmetic and random sampling and does not require
\eqref{eq:seed-guarantee} to hold.

statements.title: Refinement
statements.label: thm:refinement
statements.text:
Use the parameters and interval tree of Section~\ref{sec:geometry} in the
large-input branch.  Let $A$ be a power of two with
$1\le A\le A_{\rm init}$, and let $U$ be an integer table on every labeled
tree node and every valid target state, with
\[
 0\le U(I,q)\le N,\qquad c(I,q)\le U(I,q)\le A c(I,q).
\]
Set $a=\max\{1,A/F\}$.  There is a randomized, finitely executable
refinement table $d_S$ such that, for every state $(I,q)$,
\begin{equation}
 d_S(I,q)\ge c(I,q)/a,\qquad
 \E\bigl[\pos{d_S(I,q)-c(I,q)}\bigr]\le c(I,q)/\ell.
\end{equation}
The first inequality holds for every outcome of the refinement randomness;
the expectation in the second is conditional on the fixed table $U$.
At zero-cost states the returned value is zero for every outcome.

statements.title: Local cost of the online rule
statements.label: cor:online-local-cost
statements.text:
For a band in the edit-distance algorithm, the numerical mixture in
Section~\ref{sec:bands} can be constructed and sampled with local
expected bit cost $2^{o(H)}$, using only already gathered child values
of earlier indices.  The storage used by this calculation is
$2^{o(H)}$ words.

statements.title: Charged expected running time
statements.label: thm:work
statements.text:
The large-input algorithm has worst-case expected running time
$N^{1+o(1)}$ on the logarithmic-word RAM, over its internal
randomness.  This includes input processing, preprocessing, initial
and refined table calculations, all rational arithmetic, sampling,
and data-structure operations.  Its workspace on every execution
is bounded by a fixed polynomial in $N$.  Together with the exact
fallbacks, the same program has the claimed expected asymptotic
bound for each fixed rational $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$.

title: An Artin group with no geometric CAT(0) action
abstract: We construct an Artin group on 116 generators that admits no proper, cocompact isometric action on a nonempty proper CAT(0) space. This refutes the CAT(0) conjecture for Artin groups.

tex.abstract:
We construct an Artin group on 116 generators that admits no proper,
cocompact isometric action on a nonempty proper CAT(0) space.
This refutes the CAT(0) conjecture for Artin groups.
sections: A quantitative constraint from braid groups

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is an Artin matrix \(M\) on 116 generators, with every
off-diagonal label in \(\{2,3,\infty\}\), such that \(A_M\) admits no
geometric action.  One explicit matrix is given in
Definition~\ref{def:matrix}.

statements.label: prop:braid-angle
statements.text:
Suppose a group acting geometrically on a CAT(0) space contains elements
$s_1,\ldots,s_{39}$ satisfying the $B_{40}$ relations, with
$\ell(s_1^2)>0$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \left(\frac{\ell((s_1s_2)^3)}{3\ell(s_1^2)}\right)^2
 \ge\frac{143}{513}>\frac14,
\end{equation}
and in particular
\[
 \frac{\ell((s_1s_2)^3)}{3\ell(s_1^2)}
 =\frac{\ell((s_1s_2)^3)}{3\ell(s_2^2)}>\frac12.
\]
statements.section_title: A quantitative constraint from braid groups

statements.label: prop:triangle-obstruction
prop:sphere-counts
statements.text:
For every combinatorial map from a finite triangulated oriented
two-sphere to $\mathcal K$, and every individual target triangle
$\tau$, the sum of the signs of all occurrences of $\tau$ is zero.
Collapsed triangles are allowed in the map and contribute zero.

title: An Endpoint Gradient Bound for the Centered Disk Maximal Operator
abstract: We prove the endpoint gradient bound \(\|\nabla Mf\|_1\le C\|\nabla f\|_1\) for every real-valued \(f\in W^{1,1}(\mathbb R^2)\), where \(Mf(x)\) is the supremum of the averages of \(|f|\) over disks centered at x, and C is an absolute constant. The maximal function belongs to \(W^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^2)\) and has a globally integrable weak gradient. This gives a positive resolution of the planar centered-disk case of the endpoint question of Hajłasz and Onninen.

tex.abstract:
We prove the endpoint gradient bound $\|\nabla Mf\|_1\le C\|\nabla f\|_1$
for every real-valued $f\in W^{1,1}(\R^2)$, where $Mf(x)$ is the supremum
of the averages of $|f|$ over disks centered at $x$, and $C$ is an absolute
constant. The maximal function belongs to $W^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R^2)$
and has a globally integrable weak gradient. This gives a positive resolution
of the planar centered-disk case of the endpoint question of Haj{\l}asz and
Onninen.
sections: Cancellation at disks and three local bounds
Dyadic vector masses and common prices
Directions that change slowly in scale and position
Analytic facts used in the limiting argument

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is an absolute constant $C<\infty$ such that, for every
real-valued $f\in W^{1,1}(\R^2)$, the function $Mf$ is locally
integrable, belongs to $W^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R^2)$, and satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \int_{\R^2}|\nabla Mf|\,\dd x
 \le C\int_{\R^2}|\nabla f|\,\dd x.
\end{equation}
In particular, its distributional derivatives are represented by
globally integrable functions.

statements.title: Signed finite-band estimate
statements.label: prop:finite-band
statements.text:
There is an absolute constant $C$ such that, for every real
$g\in C_c^\infty(\R^2)$ and $0<a\le b$ with $b/a$ a power of two, including one,
\begin{equation}
 \int_{\R^2}|\nabla S_{a,b}g|\,\dd x
 \le C\int_{\R^2}|\nabla g|\,\dd x.
\end{equation}
The constant is independent of $a$, $b$, and the number of dyadic
radius scales between them.

distributional derivatives have finite total variation. For every

\[

with the constant from Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.
Writing $P(F)=|D\1_F|(\R^2)$ for perimeter, every measurable
set $E$ with $|E|<\infty$ and $P(E)<\infty$ satisfies
\[

title: An Exact Semidefinite Lift of a Nonspectrahedral Hyperbolicity Cone
abstract: We construct an exact semidefinite lift of the explicit nonspectrahedral hyperbolicity cone in twenty-three variables defined in the companion paper. The lift is a homogeneous real symmetric pencil of size 100 with 307 auxiliary variables and represents the entire closed cone, including every point with singular X. Thus, although this cone has no semidefinite representation in its original coordinates, it admits one when auxiliary variables are allowed. The stated sizes are not claimed to be minimal.

tex.abstract:
We construct an exact semidefinite lift of the explicit nonspectrahedral
hyperbolicity cone in twenty-three variables defined in the companion
paper. The lift is a homogeneous real symmetric pencil of size $100$
with $307$ auxiliary variables and represents the entire closed cone,
including every point with singular $X$. Thus, although this cone has no
semidefinite representation in its original coordinates, it admits one
when auxiliary variables are allowed. The stated sizes are not claimed
to be minimal.

Fix a box-valid small-count profile $(x,y)$ with total $p$, an integer
$0\le j\le H$, and rational parameters
$0<\xi_{\mathrm{in}},\theta<1/4$.  There is a randomized procedure
returning a positive rational $\widehat h$ such that
\[
 \mathbb P\left[
  (1-\xi_{\mathrm{in}})h_j(x,y)\le\widehat h
       \le(1+\xi_{\mathrm{in}})h_j(x,y)
 \right]\ge1-\theta.
\]
On every execution its bit cost is bounded by a fixed polynomial in
$L,\epsilon^{-1},\xi_{\mathrm{in}}^{-1},\theta^{-1}$ and the encoding
lengths of the parameters.  If

\begin{equation}

\end{equation}

depend on the statistical success event.

statements.label: cor:integral-flows
statements.text:
For the network data above, there are algorithms with these guarantees.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item Given rational $\varepsilon,\delta\in(0,1)$, the counting algorithm
outputs a nonnegative rational $\widehat Z_{\mathrm{flow}}$ satisfying
\[
 \P\bigl((1-\varepsilon)|\mathcal F|\le\widehat Z_{\mathrm{flow}}
             \le(1+\varepsilon)|\mathcal F|\bigr)\ge1-\delta.
\]
If $\mathcal F$ is empty, it outputs zero on every execution.
\item Given rational $\tau\in(0,1)$, the sampling algorithm reports
infeasibility exactly when $\mathcal F$ is empty. Otherwise it outputs
$\widehat f\in\mathcal F$ on every execution, with
\[
 \TV\bigl(\mathcal L(\widehat f),\operatorname{Unif}(\mathcal F)\bigr)
 =\frac12\sum_{f\in\mathcal F}
   \left|\P(\widehat f=f)-\frac1{|\mathcal F|}\right|\le\tau.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Both algorithms use independent unbiased bits. Let $L$ denote the total
binary input length, including the corresponding accuracy parameters.
Fixed polynomials in $L,\varepsilon^{-1},\log(\delta^{-1})$ for counting
and in $L,\tau^{-1}$ for sampling bound the total bit operations on
every execution.

title: An FPRAS for Common Integer Polymatroid Bases with Binary Capacities
abstract: We give a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting common integer bases of two polymatroids with the same total rank, supplied by exact rank-value oracles. The total rank and capacities are encoded in binary, and each integer vector is counted once. On every execution, the number of oracle calls and the bit work outside the oracles are bounded by a fixed polynomial in the ground-set size, the binary input length, the inverse relative-error tolerance, and the logarithm of the inverse failure probability. The algorithm handles binary capacities directly, without expanding them into labelled copies.

tex.abstract:
We give a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting
common integer bases of two polymatroids with the same total rank, supplied
by exact rank-value oracles. The total rank and capacities are encoded in
binary, and each integer vector is counted once. On every execution, the
number of oracle calls and the bit work outside the oracles are bounded
by a fixed polynomial in the ground-set size, the binary input length,
the inverse relative-error tolerance, and the logarithm of the inverse
failure probability. The algorithm handles binary capacities directly,
without expanding them into labelled copies.

There is a single uniform randomized algorithm which, for every input
described above, outputs a nonnegative rational $\widehat Z$ satisfying
\[
 \PP\bigl((1-\eps)Z\le\widehat Z\le(1+\eps)Z\bigr)
 \ge1-\delta.
\]
If $Z=0$, the algorithm outputs zero on every execution. On every

statements.title: Oracle algorithms
statements.label: prop:oracle-tools
statements.text:
The following operations have deterministic oracle and bit complexity
bounded by fixed polynomials in the indicated input sizes.
\begin{enumerate}
 \item An integer-valued submodular function on a finite ground set can
 be minimized, with a minimizing set returned, from an exact value oracle
 and a bound on the binary lengths of its values.  The size parameters are
 the ground-set cardinality and that value-length bound.
 \item Let $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded rational polytope, supplied
 by strong separation, a coordinate bound, and a bound on the binary
 encoding length of each individual defining inequality.  The separator
 returns inequalities of length polynomial in the query length and
 the supplied description bounds.  Exact rational
 linear optimization, including an emptiness decision and the production
 of an optimal vertex when $Q$ is nonempty, is polynomial in $d$, these
 bounds, and the objective length.  This assertion includes
 lower-dimensional polytopes.  All separation queries have polynomial
 encoding length.
\end{enumerate}
The first operation also applies to an integer submodular function with
a rational modular term added, and with prescribed elements required to
belong or not to belong to the minimizing set.

statements.label: prop:shift-logconcavity
statements.text:
Let $f_1,f_2$ be integral normalized submodular functions on $E$,
not necessarily nondecreasing, and define
\[
 Y(d)=\#\{(x_1,x_2)\in(B(f_1)\cap\Z^E)\times
                         (B(f_2)\cap\Z^E):x_1-x_2=d\}.
\]
For $d_0\in\Z^E$ and distinct $j,k\in E$, put
$y(t)=Y(d_0+t(e_j-e_k))$, $t\in\Z$.
The positive support of $y$ is an integer interval, possibly
empty or a singleton.  For integers $a<t<b$ with
$y(a),y(b)>0$,
\begin{equation}
 y(t)\ge y(a)^{(b-t)/(b-a)}y(b)^{(t-a)/(b-a)}.
 
\end{equation}

statements.title: A bounded weight evaluator
statements.label: prop:weight-evaluator
statements.text:
Given a profile in the entire slice $\mathcal S$, rational
$0<\rho,\beta<1$, and a rational power $s\in[0,1]$ with denominator
$q_s$, there is an evaluator using fresh random bits and returning a strictly positive rational
$\widehat h_s$ such that
\[
 \PP\bigl[(1-\rho)h^s\le\widehat h_s\le(1+\rho)h^s\bigr]
       \ge1-\beta.
\]
Its output length, number of rank queries, and other bit operations
are bounded on every execution by fixed polynomials in $N$, the
input encoding lengths, $\rho^{-1}$, $\log(\beta^{-1})$, and $q_s$.
In particular an equally spaced schedule with a polynomial number of
phases has polynomially bounded denominators. Moreover $J$ admits
a deterministic positive rational approximation $\widehat J$ with
$|\log(\widehat J/J)|\le N^{-7}$ in polynomial work.

statements.label: prop:counting-transport
statements.text:
Suppose $f$ is positive on all $p$-subsets and has the omission property,
$\widetilde f$ is positive on that domain and has the addition property,
the weights agree on $\mathcal A$, and
\eqref{eq:counting-comparison} holds with $q\geq1$.
For good multipliers put
\begin{equation}
 C_{\rm p}=p(1+8pq^2),\qquad
 C_{\rm d}=8+32pq^3,\qquad
 K_{\rm obs}=10p^4(9C_{\rm p}+2C_{\rm d}).
 
\end{equation}
Then for every real function $g$ on $\mathcal X$,
\begin{equation}
 C\operatorname{Var}_\mu(g)\leq C_{\rm p}\mathfrak D(g),\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_\pi(\mathcal Qg)
 \leq(9C_{\rm p}+2C_{\rm d})\frac{\mathfrak D(g)}C
 \leq K_{\rm obs}\mathcal E_P(g).
 
\end{equation}
If $\mathcal QG=G$ and an initial law satisfies $\nu\leq D\pi$
pointwise, then $m\geq1$ consecutive observations satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E_\nu\left[
  \left(m^{-1}\sum_{t=0}^{m-1}G(S_t)-\mathbb E_\pi G\right)^2\right]
 \leq\frac{2D K_{\rm obs}}m\operatorname{Var}_\pi(G).
 
\end{equation}
The trace on $\mathcal A$, counting every strictly positive return as
one step, is lazy and reversible with stationary law $\mu$ and inverse
spectral gap at most $2p^2C_{\rm p}\leq K_{\rm obs}$.  In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \left|\frac{P_{\rm tr}^t(x,y)}{\mu(y)}-1\right|
 \leq\mu_{\min}^{-1}\exp(-t/K_{\rm obs}).
 
\end{equation}
If a trace starts from $\nu\leq D\mu$, the expected cost of $t$ trace
steps in underlying transitions is at most $tD/\pi(\mathcal A)$;
at each deterministic trace index its law is still at most $D\mu$.

statements.label: thm:simplicity
statements.text:

and simple, and
\[
 [F_m,F_m]=A_m.

statements.label: thm:amenability
statements.text:
For every positive integer $m$, the discrete group $F_m$ is amenable.  Every
subgroup of $F_m$, in particular $A_m$, satisfies the finite-set F\o lner
condition.

statements.label: prop:am-field-covariance
statements.text:
For any finite list of smooth signals constant outside compact sets, and any
finite list of flag types, the laws of the independent fields
in~\eqref{eq:am-field} can be chosen so that, for every $g\in\mathcal K$,
the total variation distance between their joint law and its image under
$g$ is arbitrarily small on all sites at once.  With probability tending
to one as $N\to\infty$, every bit is one wherever its signal is at least
two, and zero wherever its signal is at most minus two.

statements.title: All rectangular laws
statements.label: prop:rectangular-law
statements.text:
For a sufficiently large fixed initial window $n_0$, its true table
and the finite geometric tables described above imply
$\mathcal R(n)$ for every $n$.  In particular every finite family
of aligned rectangular tests has its actual central law in

statements.title: The polygon law
statements.label: thm:polygon-law
statements.text:
There is one finite choice of true initial relations in
$\widehat G$, for sufficiently large fixed finite $m$, such
that every finite family of aligned polygon tests has its
actual central law.  The assertion holds simultaneously on
subalphabets.  Its canonical representations
\[
 \rho_{U,I}:\Alt(I)^\ast\longrightarrow\widehat G
\]
are compatible with restriction of the alphabet, split
exactly over finite disjoint polygon refinements, and are
covariant under common translations on proper supports.

statements.title: A finitely presented central cover

statements.text:

presented group $\widehat G$ and a surjective homomorphism
$\pi:\widehat G\to A_m$ whose kernel is central.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $V$ be the ring of integers in the unramified extension of $\Q_5$ of
degree eight, and put
\[
 A=\bigl(V[x,y]/(5+x^4+y^4)\bigr)_{(5,x,y)}.
\]
Then $A$ is a Noetherian regular local domain of dimension two and
\[
 \ker\bigl(K_5(A)\longrightarrow K_5(\Frac A)\bigr)\ne0.
\]
Consequently the unrestricted integral Gersten conjecture has a negative
answer.

statements.title: Integral lift and conjugates
statements.label: prop:integral-lift
statements.text:
Let $u=\zeta-1\in S^\times$, and let $b$ be multiplication by the
class $\beta$ in \eqref{eq:equivariant-bott}.  There exists
$c\in K_5(S)$ such that
\begin{equation}
 
 c\bmod5=b^2[u]_5\quad\text{in }K_5(S;5).
\end{equation}
For every $\delta\in\Delta$,
\begin{equation}
 
 (\delta c)\bmod5=\chi(\delta)^2b^2[\delta u]_5
       \quad\text{in }K_5(S;5).
\end{equation}
For any fixed homomorphism $\iota:S\to H$ to a field, let
$\operatorname{res}_\iota$ denote extension of scalars.  Restriction of
these equalities gives the corresponding identities in $K_5(H;5)$.
In the second identity this means
\[
 \operatorname{res}_\iota(\delta c)\bmod5
 =\chi(\delta)^2 b_\iota^2[\iota(\delta u)]_5,
\]
where $b_\iota$ is multiplication by $\operatorname{res}_\iota(\beta)$; no action of
$\delta$ on $H$ is required.

statements.title: Picard specialization
statements.label: prop:specialization
statements.text:
Let $L$ be a finite extension of $\Q_5$ containing $\mu_5$, with valuation
ring $R$ and residue field $k$.  Let $\mathcal X\to\Spec R$ be a smooth
projective morphism of relative dimension one with geometrically integral
fibers
\[
 C=\mathcal X_L,\qquad D=\mathcal X_k.
\]
For a closed point $q$ of $C$, let $r(q)$ be its specialization on $D$:
it is the image of the closed point under the unique extension of
$\Spec\kappa(q)\to\mathcal X$ to the valuation ring of $\kappa(q)$.
For a closed point $r$ of $D$, write $[r]\in\Pic(D)$ for the class of the
divisor $(r)$.  Let $m\geq0$ be an integer, and suppose that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $U$ is the spectrum of an arbitrary localization of the coordinate
ring of a nonempty affine open of $C$, and $p_1,\ldots,p_m$ are distinct
$L$-rational closed points of $U$;
\item $Z$ is a finite set of closed points of $D$, and every closed point
$q$ of $C$ with $r(q)\notin Z$ belongs to $U$;
\item $B$ is an abelian group killed by $5$, and
$\psi:\Pic(D)\to B$ is a homomorphism satisfying $\psi([r])=0$ for every
$r\in Z$.
\end{enumerate}
Put $r_i=r(p_i)\in D(k)$.  Choose $\beta_L\in K_2(L;5)$ with
$\partial_{\mathrm{coef}}\beta_L=[\zeta]$ for a primitive fifth root of
unity $\zeta$, and let $b$ be multiplication by its restrictions, with
$b^2=b\circ b$.  Let $v_L$ be the normalized valuation of $L$.
For $a_i\in L^\times$ and $e_i\in\F_5$, the condition
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{i=1}^m e_i v_L(a_i)\,\psi([r_i])\ne0\quad\text{in }B
\end{equation}
implies
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{i=1}^m (p_i)_*\bigl(e_i b^2[a_i]_5\bigr)
       \ne0\quad\text{in }G_5(U;5).
\end{equation}
Here $[a_i]_5$ is the class of $a_i$ in
$K_1(L;5)=L^\times/L^{\times5}$, and the scalars in
\eqref{eq:specialization-test} act through the natural $\F_5$-module
structure on $B$.

tex.abstract:
We construct a two-dimensional ramified regular local ring $A$ in mixed

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
The ring $A$ is a two-dimensional Noetherian regular local domain
of mixed characteristic $(0,5)$, with $\pi\in\mathfrak m_A^2$.
There is an integral class $c\in K_3(A)$ such that
\[
 c|_{\Frac A}=0,
 \qquad
 c|_{A[1/\pi]}\bmod5\ne0
 \quad\text{in }G_3(A[1/\pi];\Z/5).
\]
In particular, $K_3(A)\to K_3(\Frac A)$ is not injective.

statements.label: prop:integral
statements.text:
There exists $b\in K_3(S)$ whose restriction to $D$, followed
by coefficient reduction, is $a_D$. If
$j:\Spec S\hookrightarrow\Spec A$ and $c=j_*b\in G_3(A)=K_3(A)$,
then $c|_{\Frac A}=0$. Moreover, for
$T=\Spec A[1/\pi]$ and $i:\Spec D\hookrightarrow T$,
\[
 c|_T\bmod5=i_*a_D\quad\text{in }G_3(T;\Z/5).
\]

title: An irrational-trace counterexample to reduced Baum–Connes
abstract: We construct a finitely generated discrete group whose reduced group C∗-algebra contains a projection of irrational canonical trace. Its K0-class lies outside the image of the coefficient-free reduced Baum–Connes assembly map. This disproves the coefficient-free reduced Baum–Connes conjecture for countable discrete groups.

tex.abstract:
We construct a finitely generated discrete group whose reduced group
\(C^*\)-algebra contains a projection of irrational canonical trace. Its
\(K_0\)-class lies outside the image of the coefficient-free reduced
Baum--Connes assembly map. This disproves the coefficient-free reduced
Baum--Connes conjecture for countable discrete groups.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There exist a finitely generated discrete group \(\Gsur\) and a projection
\(b_0\in C_r^*(\Gsur)\) with irrational canonical trace. Moreover,
\[
[b_0]\notin\mu_0^{\Gsur}\bigl(K_0^{\Gsur}(\underline E\Gsur)\bigr).
\]
In particular, the coefficient-free reduced Baum--Connes conjecture for
countable discrete groups is false.

statements.label: prop:cone-geometry
statements.text:
There is an integer \(D_0\), independent of all the above data, such that
every vertex on a geodesic triangle in \(\widehat X\) is within \(D_0\) of
a vertex on another side. Moreover:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item
If an edge path of length \(L\) joins \(x,a\in P\) while avoiding

d_P(x,a)\le12(L+1)\lambda\sigma(P).

statements.title: Choice of data
statements.label: prop:data
statements.text:
There are labelled graphs \((\Theta_i)_{i\ge1}\) satisfying all the
hypotheses of Section~\ref{sec:geometry}, with the following additional
properties. Write \(n_i=|\operatorname{Vert}(\Theta_i)|\),
\(k_i=\lfloor n_i/2\rfloor\), and let \(\sigma_i\) be the girth.
There are constants \(\rho,\kappa>0\), independent of \(i\), such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item On the orthogonal complement of constants in
\(\ell^2(\operatorname{Vert}(\Theta_i))\),
\(dI-\Adj_{\Theta_i}\ge\rho I\), and for every vertex subset \(W\),
\begin{equation}
|\partial W|\ge\kappa\min\{|W|,n_i-|W|\}.
\end{equation}
Here \(\partial W\) is the unoriented edge boundary in \(\Theta_i\).
\item With
\begin{equation}
c=\frac\eta2\min\{\kappa,1\},
\end{equation}
we have \(n_i>100\), \(\sigma_i>\max\{16,20/c\}\),
\(\lambda\sigma_i>3\), and
\(1<\lfloor\lambda\sigma_i\rfloor<\lfloor\lambda\sigma_{i+1}\rfloor\).
\item Every induced intrinsic ball of radius at most \(\sigma_i/16\)
is a tree with fewer than \(\eta n_i\) vertices.
\item The integers \(k_i\) strictly increase and
\(k_{i+1}-k_i\to\infty\).
\end{enumerate}
Consequently every ball \(B_P\) in Lemma~\ref{lem:overlap}, for every
permitted root and chosen root geodesic, is an induced tree satisfying
\begin{equation}
r_P\le\sigma(P)/16,\qquad |B_P|<\eta|P|.
\end{equation}

title: An Isolated Particle Pole for the Two-Dimensional O(3) Spin Field
abstract: We consider the continuum spin field constructed from the nearest-neighbor two-dimensional \(O(3)\) model by the fixed prescription of the companion paper. We prove that its vector two-point spectral measure has a positive atom corresponding to the lowest mass, separated by a positive gap from all remaining mass support.

tex.abstract:
We consider the continuum spin field constructed from the nearest-neighbor
two-dimensional $O(3)$ model by the fixed prescription of the companion
paper. We prove that its vector two-point spectral measure has a positive
atom corresponding to the lowest mass, separated by a positive gap from
all remaining mass support.
sections: The continuum field and the uniform lattice inputs
Visibility of the lowest transfer energy
A linear bound on the low-energy state count
From the state count to an isolated mass

statements.title: An isolated lowest mass
statements.label: intro:main
statements.text:
For the field $\phi$ just specified, there exist $m_1,Z,\delta>0$ and a
positive measure $\rho_{\mathrm{rest}}$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \rho=Z\delta_{m_1^2}+\rho_{\mathrm{rest}},
 \qquad
 \supp\rho_{\mathrm{rest}}\subset[(m_1+\delta)^2,\infty).
 
\end{equation}
In particular, $m_1$ is the smallest mass in the support of the spin-field
two-point function.

statements.title: Inputs from the continuum construction
statements.label: inp:contracts
statements.text:
There are integers $K_0,M_0>0$ and constants $c,C>0$ with the following
properties.  Write $w_k=M_0 2^k$, and let $Z_N(t,w)$ be the partition
function on a torus of time length $t$ and spatial circumference $w$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item In the cutoff plane, all joint moments of the variables
\eqref{inp:field} converge to those of the Euclidean field $\phi$.
The limiting Schwinger distributions are tempered, Euclidean invariant,
and $O(3)$ covariant.  Their Osterwalder--Schrader reconstruction is the
Wightman field of Theorem~\ref{intro:main}, with unique vacuum $\Omega$
and
\[
 H_{\mathrm{phys}}|_{\Omega^\perp}\ge m>0.
\]
For some real test $f$ supported strictly in positive time, the
one-field reflection norm
$\E[\phi^1(\theta f)\phi^1(f)]$ is strictly positive.
\item For all $N\ge K_0$ and $k\ge0$,
\begin{equation}
 0\le \Delta_N(w_k)
 :=4\log Z_N(w_k,w_k)-\log Z_N(2w_k,2w_k)
 \le C e^{-c w_k}.
 
\end{equation}
\item On these square tori and on the cutoff plane, the component
moment measures
\[
 S_{r,N}^{\boldsymbol i}
 =(B_Na^2)^r\sum_{x_1,\ldots,x_r}
     \E\!\left[\prod_{j=1}^r q_{x_j}^{i_j}\right]
     \delta_{(x_1,\ldots,x_r)}
\]
are nonnegative.  For arbitrary translated unit boxes $Q_1,\ldots,Q_r$,
\begin{equation}
 S_{r,N}^{\boldsymbol i}(Q_1\times\cdots\times Q_r)
 \le C^r r!,
 
\end{equation}
uniformly in $N\ge K_0$, the square torus, the box positions, and the
component indices.
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: A positive physical gap at every large width
statements.label: tra:gap
statements.text:
There are $c_0>0$ and $w_0<\infty$ such that
\[
 e_N(w)\ge c_0\qquad(N\ge K_0,\ w\ge w_0,\ w\in a_N\N).
\]

statements.title: Comparison for three-quarter supports
statements.label: tra:comparison
statements.text:
Let $w=w_k$ be sufficiently large.  If the support of a bounded
observable $F$ has a lift contained in a rectangle of extent at most
$3w/4$ in each coordinate, then
\begin{equation}
 \left|\E_{\mathrm{tor},N;w,w}F-\E_{\mathrm{plane},N}F\right|
       \le C\|F\|_\infty e^{-cw},
 
\end{equation}
uniformly in $N\ge K_0$.  The assertion holds for bounded measurable
observables.  Comparison of this square with its infinite-time
cylinder requires only the time extent bound.

statements.title: Comparison of field moments
statements.label: tra:moments
statements.text:
Fix a number of component tests, chosen from families with uniformly
bounded suprema and support diameters.  If their translated supports
together satisfy the extent condition of
Proposition~\ref{tra:comparison}, then the square-torus and cutoff-plane
expectations of their product differ by at most $Ce^{-cw}$.
The constants may depend on the number and shapes of the tests but
not on their separate translations, the cutoff, or $w$.

statements.title: Quadratic covariance bound
statements.label: par:covariance
statements.text:
Let $P$ and $Q$ be monomials in spin components for the law
\eqref{par:graph-law}, of even total degrees $r$ and $s$, with nonempty
site lists $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$. Put
\[
 G=\max_{x\in\mathcal A,\ y\in\mathcal B}\E(q_x^3q_y^3).
\]
There is a constant $C_{r,s}$, depending only on the two degrees, such that
\begin{equation}
             |\Cov(P,Q)|\le C_{r,s}G^2.
\end{equation}
If either monomial is constant, its covariance is zero.

title: An L² Einstein Gap for Nonnegatively Curved Four-Manifolds
abstract: We prove a universal, scale-invariant L2 gap for the trace-free Ricci tensor on simply connected closed four-manifolds with nonnegative sectional curvature. If the trace-free Ricci energy is sufficiently small, the manifold is diffeomorphic to S4, \(\mathbb{CP}^2\), or \(S^2\times S^2\). The proof uses the classification of positive-Einstein, nonnegatively curved four-manifolds supplied by the companion zero-plane rigidity theorem, stated explicitly as the classification premise of our result. No auxiliary curvature, volume, diameter, injectivity-radius, or Sobolev bound is required. The conclusion concerns the smooth manifold, not an isometry of the original metric.

tex.abstract:
We prove a universal, scale-invariant $L^2$ gap for the trace-free Ricci
tensor on simply connected closed four-manifolds with nonnegative
sectional curvature. If the trace-free Ricci energy is sufficiently
small, the manifold is diffeomorphic to $S^4$, $\CP^2$, or
$S^2\times S^2$. The proof uses the classification of positive-Einstein,
nonnegatively curved four-manifolds supplied by the companion
zero-plane rigidity theorem, stated explicitly as the classification
premise of our result. No auxiliary curvature, volume, diameter,
injectivity-radius, or Sobolev bound is required. The conclusion concerns
the smooth manifold, not an isometry of the original metric.
sections: The compact Einstein limit and the gap

statements.label: ass:classification
statements.text:
Every connected smooth closed Riemannian four-manifold $(N,h)$ satisfying
\[
 \Ric_h=3h,\qquad \sec_h\ge0
\]
has universal Riemannian cover isometric to one of the following:
the round $S^4$ of sectional curvature $1$; Fubini--Study $\CP^2$ normalized
by $\Ric=3g$; or
$S^2(1/\sqrt3)\times S^2(1/\sqrt3)$ with its product metric.

statements.label: thm:gap
statements.text:
Assume Classification Assumption~\ref{ass:classification}. There is a
universal constant $\varepsilon_0>0$ with the following property.
If $(M,g)$ is a connected, simply connected, smooth closed Riemannian
four-manifold with $\sec_g\ge0$ and
\[
 \int_M\left|\Ric_g-\frac{\Scal_g}{4}g\right|_g^2\,d\mu_g
 <\varepsilon_0,
\]
then $M$ is diffeomorphic, without a prescribed orientation, to the
standard smooth $S^4$, $\CP^2$, or $S^2\times S^2$.

statements.label: prop:initial
prop:initial-sobolev
prop:weighted
prop:tail
statements.text:
After discarding finitely many indices, there are uniform constants
$S_2,C$ such that, for $0\le t<\min\{T,\mathcal T_j\}$,
\begin{align}
 \norm f_4^2&\le S_2\int_M(|\nabla f|^2+f^2)\dd,
       \\
 \int_M w_j(t)^2\dd&\le e^{Ct}\int_M w_j(0)^2\,d\mu_{g_j},
       \\
 \int_M|\Rm_{g_j(t)}|^2\dd&\le C.
       
\end{align}
The Sobolev estimate holds for every Lipschitz function $f$.
In particular, the supremum of $\norm{w_j(t)}_2$ over these existing
times tends to zero.

statements.text:

There are a subsequence, a connected simply connected closed smooth
four-manifold $N$, a metric $h$ on $N$, and diffeomorphisms
$\Phi_j:N\to M_j$ such that
\[
 \Ric_h=3h,\qquad \sec_h\ge0,
\]

\begin{equation}
 \Phi_j^*g_j(t)\longrightarrow (1-6t)h
\end{equation}

title: An L³ bound for the dyadic triangular Hilbert form
abstract: We prove a uniform \(L^3\times L^3\times L^3\) estimate for the dyadic triangular Hilbert form with unrestricted real inputs. The sum of the absolute local contributions over any finite set of scales is bounded by forty times the product of the input norms. In particular, the bound allows coefficients of modulus at most one to vary independently among admissible interval triples.

tex.abstract:
We prove a uniform \(L^3\times L^3\times L^3\) estimate for the dyadic
triangular Hilbert form with unrestricted real inputs. The sum of the
absolute local contributions over any finite set of scales is bounded
by forty times the product of the input norms. In particular, the bound
allows coefficients of modulus at most one to vary independently among
admissible interval triples.

title: An L3 bound for the trilinear Hilbert transform
abstract: We prove that the trilinear Hilbert transform with fixed slopes 1, 2, 3 maps \(L^3(\mathbb R)\times L^3(\mathbb R)\times L^3(\mathbb R)\) to \(L^1(\mathbb R)\), resolving this case of the trilinear Hilbert transform conjecture.

tex.abstract:
We prove that the trilinear Hilbert transform with fixed slopes $1,2,3$ maps
$L^3(\R)\times L^3(\R)\times L^3(\R)$ to $L^1(\R)$, resolving this case of
the trilinear Hilbert transform conjecture.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is a finite constant $C$ such that
\[
 \norm{T(f_1,f_2,f_3)}_{L^1(\R)}
 \le C\prod_{j=1}^3\norm{f_j}_{L^3(\R)}
 \qquad(f_1,f_2,f_3\in\mathcal S(\R)).
\]
Consequently $T$ has a unique bounded trilinear extension from
$L^3(\R)\times L^3(\R)\times L^3(\R)$ to $L^1(\R)$.

statements.title: Uniform local estimate
statements.label: thm:local
statements.text:
For some $q\in(2,3)$, the constants $C_N(q)$ are bounded independently
of $N$.
statements.section_title: Local forms and the outer reduction

statements.title: Normalized absorption estimate
statements.label: prop:normalized
statements.text:
For a suitable fixed $q\in(2,3)$ and every sufficiently small fixed
$c>0$, there is an $A<\infty$, independent of $N$, with the following
property.  Suppose a finite rooted subtree has root $I_*$, all summation
cells lie in at most $N$ consecutive depths, and
\[
 \norm{f_j}_{q,I}\le1
 \qquad(0\le j\le3, I\text{ in the subtree}).
\]
Then
\[
 \sum_{I\text{ a summation cell}}|I|\,|H_I(f)|
 \le (A+cC_N)|I_*|.
\]
statements.section_title: Local forms and the outer reduction

statements.title: Leng--Sah--Sawhney
statements.label: thm:lss
statements.text:
For a \(1\)-bounded function \(f:[L]\to\C\) with
\(\|f\|_{U^3[L]}\ge\delta\), there are a degree-two filtered
nilmanifold \(G/\Gamma\), a polynomial sequence \(g:\Z\to G\)
adapted to its filtration, and a function \(F:G/\Gamma\to\C\) such that
\[
 \left|\frac1L\sum_{n=1}^L
        f(n)\overline{F(g(n)\Gamma)}\right|\ge\varepsilon.
\]
The dimension is at most \(C(1+\log(1/\delta))^{C}\), and the complexity
of \(G/\Gamma\), the Lipschitz norm of \(F\), and
\(\varepsilon^{-1}\) are at most
\(\exp(C(1+\log(1/\delta))^C)\).
The nilmanifold has a rational Malcev basis adapted to the filtration,
with integer second-kind coordinates for \(\Gamma\).
The Lipschitz norm includes the supremum norm.

statements.title: A finite predictor list
statements.label: cor:predictor-list
statements.text:
Fix the two low atoms on $J$, with complexity at most $H_{\rm low}$.
For every $B\ge1$, their product in the form can be replaced, with
absolute length-weighted scale-sum error at most
\[
 e^{-B}\operatorname{poly}\bigl(\log(2D_{\mathrm h}),1+L\bigr)
 \|\1_JF_a\|_2\|\1_JF_b\|_2,
\]
by a finite list of terms
\begin{equation*}
 \psi_a(y_a)\psi_b(y_b)w_I(x,t)e(\lambda_*t^2),
 \qquad |\lambda_*||I|^2\le D_{\rm pred}.
\tag{6}
\end{equation*}
The scalar coefficients may depend on the scale.  The list of triples
$(\psi_a,\psi_b,\lambda_*)$ is fixed on $J$.  Its size, the absolute
coefficient bounds, and all atom complexities satisfy
\[
 \log D_{\rm pred}
 \le\operatorname{poly}\bigl(1+B,\log(2H_{\rm low})\bigr).
\]
The multipliers $\psi_a,\psi_b$ may be normalized to have supremum norm
at most one by incorporating their sizes into the coefficients.
statements.section_title: Two accuracies, delayed projections, and the base reduction

statements.title: Truncating the two high positions
statements.label: prop:high-truncation
statements.text:
For the tuple above, put $k=k_t$.  There are an integer
$K_0\le k^{O(1)}$, further bounded-packing segments, and nested
projection families $P^{\rm new}_a,P^{\rm new}_b$ on those
segments, for which
\begin{equation*}
 Y_i=X_i,\qquad Y_j=X_j,\qquad
 Y_e=P^{\rm new}_{e,s+K_0}F_e-g_{e,\mathrm{prev}}\quad(e=a,b),
 \qquad s=\operatorname{depth}(I).
\tag{9}
\end{equation*}
The absolute length-weighted replacement error in $H_I$, summed
over the original normalized root, is at most $Ce^{-k}$ times
its length.  Path counts, inverse private weights, atom
complexities, and the physical supremum bounds on coarse
evaluation cells are all at most $\exp(k^{O(1)})$.
For $t\ge12$, after decreasing an absolute $\theta>0$ if necessary,
every pair of full $Y$ arguments has form norm at most
$\eta=e^{-k^\theta}$ against normalized $L^2$ opponents.
All $Y$ arguments have bounded normalized $L^2$ size.
statements.section_title: Two accuracies, delayed projections, and the base reduction

statements.title: Reduction to the active cell minimum
statements.label: prop:base-reduction
statements.text:
The remaining patterns, with at least three $B$
arguments and optionally one $U$ argument, can
be restricted, with total absolute error at
most $e^{-k}|R|$, to a common active collection
whose path multiplicity satisfies
\begin{equation*}
 M\le D_{\rm base}^{C}.
\tag{10}
\end{equation*}
The finitely many leading update levels have
a bound independent of the number of depths.
For $t\ge12$, it suffices on each segment and
for each retained pattern $z$ to estimate
\begin{equation*}
 \sum_{I\ \mathrm{active}}|I|
                       \min\bigl(\eta,|H_I(z)|\bigr).
\tag{11}
\end{equation*}
The two nonside arguments complementary to a
pair of later side arguments are the whole
$B$ arguments of this tuple before further
filters.  Restoring them to their full $Y$
arguments recovers the pair-smallness above.
Further attempts may restart on normalized
subroots with these basic arguments and their
inherited lists unchanged.
statements.section_title: Two accuracies, delayed projections, and the base reduction

statements.title: Localization into current groups
statements.label: prop:localization
statements.text:
For an active pattern in \eqref{eq:src-11}, there are
$\operatorname{poly}(k)$ fixed search leaves such that, up to total
absolute length-weighted error at most $Ce^{-k}|R|$, each leaf contributes
\begin{equation*}
 \sum_{G\ \mathrm{current}}
 H_I(Z_{0,G,s},Z_{1,G,s},Z_{2,G,s},Z_{3,G,s}),\qquad
 Z_{l,G,s}=\overline L_{l,G,s}\mathcal B_{l,s}z_l.
 \tag{14}
\end{equation*}
Here $\overline L_{l,G,s}$ is one positive smeared ball filter, and
$\mathcal B_{l,s}$ is a product of cumulative filters or complements
of length $O(\log\mathcal L)$, independent of $G$.  The product and
slot choices are fixed by the search leaf, uniformly over cells.  A
group is summed only at an actual current central use.  The minimum
with $\eta$ in \eqref{eq:src-11} may be applied separately per leaf.

statements.title: Side estimate
statements.label: prop:side-estimate
statements.text:
Assume the base and localization hypotheses above, the helper
conclusions of Lemma~\ref{lem:transfer}, and the linear-side square
bound \eqref{eq:src-17}.  Fix $p\in(2/3,1)$.  After common
first-crossing cuts of arbitrarily small fixed total relative
length, terms having at least three side factors have total
length-weighted $p$th-power cost at most $P^C|R|$, provided the
fourth factor has retained normalized $L^2$ size at most $P^C$.
This includes a fourth side, a bounded current argument, or a
bounded current argument minus side factors.

Terms having exactly two side factors and whole current coarse
complements admit the following estimates.  Their freeze errors,
large-complement terms, and restoration errors have total
length-weighted $p$th-power cost at most $P^C|R|$.  Their transferred
main terms cost at most $\eta P^C|R|$ absolutely.  Their numerical
errors are negligible after the stated choice of the main
precision.  Their remaining coupled near-band terms obey
Equation~\eqref{eq:src-19} without taking a power less than one.

All statements are uniform on normalized subroots with the same
basic data.  Subsequent common cuts may remove original summands
without changing the fixed functions used in these estimates.
statements.section_title: Short depth blocks and side terms

statements.title: Square energy of the linear side
statements.label: prop:linear-side
statements.text:
For each basic-\(B\) role, on every retained \(v_b\)-cell let
\(V_{l,G,b}\) be the exact subtotal of the linear-side modes in
\(\widetilde Z_{l,G,b}\), including their private coordinates.
Set it to zero on branches without a needed output or certificate.
Then
\[
 \sum_{G,b}\|V_{l,G,b}\|^2\le G_0|R|.
\]
In particular these functions satisfy Equation~\eqref{eq:src-17},
uniformly in the branch offsets.

statements.title: Top count
statements.label: prop:top-count
statements.text:
After removing summands on first stopping cells of arbitrarily
small fixed total relative length, the following holds on every
retained path.  Fix a core role \(j\), a height
\(h\in\mathcal H_{\mathrm{up}}\), a type, and a dyadic amplitude bin
\(\sigma_j\le\sigma_{\mathcal F}<2\sigma_j\).
Let \(\mathcal A_j^G\) be the distinct representatives of
successful components of this type actually used in that bin
along the path.  Then
\begin{equation*}
 \sum_G|\mathcal A_j^G|
      \le \min(D_*,P^C\sigma_j^{-2}).
 \tag{28}
\end{equation*}
The exponent \(C\) is fixed.  Enlarging \(D_*\) by a fixed power is
harmless in this statement.  On retained uses, all component sizes
and full local side sizes are at most \(P^C\), and for a side role
\[
 \sum_{s,G}\|S_{l,G,s}\|_{2,I_s}^2\le P^C.
\]

statements.title: Counts for the tested core tuples
statements.label: prop:thin-count
statements.section_title: Successful heights and concentration across scales

statements.title: Powered estimate for the core terms
statements.label: prop:core-estimate
statements.text:
There are absolute $\varepsilon>0$ and $C_4<\infty$, with
$1-\varepsilon>2/3$, such that the terms containing at least three
core roles in the localized expansion of \eqref{eq:src-11} have
total contribution at most
\begin{equation*}
 C_q\eta^\varepsilon P^{C_4}|R|+O(e^{-k}|R|).
 \tag{37}
\end{equation*}
Here the original cell minimum is applied before the subadditive
estimates, and all numerical errors are estimated absolutely.
The constants are uniform in the finite depth range and the
retained attempt.  In particular $\varepsilon$ and $C_4$ can be
fixed before choosing how close $q$ is to $2$.

title: An algebra of infinite little finitistic dimension
abstract: We construct a finite-dimensional complex algebra whose finite-dimensional modules have unbounded finite projective dimensions. This disproves the little finitistic-dimension conjecture.

tex.abstract:
We construct a finite-dimensional complex algebra whose finite-dimensional
modules have unbounded finite projective dimensions. This disproves the little
finitistic-dimension conjecture.
sections: A selection process with unbounded extinction
Localization and a fixed lifted diagram
A square-zero extension and projective dimension

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is a finite-dimensional unital complex algebra \(A\) such that,
for every integer \(m\ge1\), there is a finite-dimensional left
\(A\)-module \(N_m\) with
\[
2m-2\le\pd_A N_m<\infty.
\]
In particular, \(\findim A=\infty\).

statements.title: Extreme left--right asymmetry
statements.label: cor:left-right-asymmetry
statements.text:
There is a finite-dimensional unital complex algebra \(\Lambda\) such that
\[
\findim \Lambda=\Findim \Lambda=\infty,
\qquad
\findim(\Lambda^{\mathrm{op}})=\Findim(\Lambda^{\mathrm{op}})=0.
\]
All four dimensions here use left modules. Thus the little and big
finitistic dimensions of \(\Lambda\) are infinite on the left and zero
on the right. Injective left \(\Lambda\)-modules do not generate the
unbounded derived category of all left \(\Lambda\)-modules, whereas
injective right \(\Lambda\)-modules generate the unbounded derived
category of all right \(\Lambda\)-modules.

statements.label: prop:selection
statements.text:
There exist a finitely presented unital complex algebra $R$, a central
idempotent $e\in R$, and an automorphism $\alpha$ of $R$ such that, for
every integer $m\geq 1$, a finite-dimensional left $R$-module $Y_m$
satisfies
\begin{equation}
  H^{\circ j}(Y_m)\neq 0\quad(0\leq j<m),
  \qquad H^{\circ m}(Y_m)=0.
  
\end{equation}
The algebra, idempotent, and automorphism are independent of $m$.
statements.section_title: A selection process with unbounded extinction

statements.title: Fixed lifted diagram
statements.label: prop:lifted-diagram
statements.text:
For the fixed data $R,e,\alpha$ and the algebra $B$ above, there are
bounded complexes $D_0,D_1,D_2$ of finitely generated projective
right $B$-modules, chain maps
\[
  f_a:D_i\longrightarrow D_j\qquad(a:i\to j),
\]
and right-$B$-linear maps $h_\rho:D_0\to D_2$ of degree $-1$
for $\rho\in\mathcal R$, such that
\begin{equation}
  d_{D_2}h_\rho+h_\rho d_{D_0}
      =\sum_{b,a}\rho_{ba}f_bf_a.
\end{equation}
For every finite-dimensional left $R$-module $Y$, the diagram
whose objects and arrows in $\D^b(k)$ are
\begin{equation}
  D_i\otimes_B M(Y),\qquad f_a\otimes_B\id_{M(Y)}
\end{equation}
is isomorphic to the diagram having $eY\oplus(eY)[3]$ at all three
vertices, identities on $s,s'$, and the action of $\alpha(x_h)$
on both summands for $a_h,a'_h$.
All the complexes, maps, and homotopies in this statement are fixed
before $Y$ is chosen.
statements.section_title: Localization and a fixed lifted diagram

statements.label: thm:realization
statements.text:
Let \(k\) be a field, let \(R\) be a finitely presented \(k\)-algebra,
let \(e\in R\) be a central idempotent, and let
\(\alpha:R\to R\) be a unital endomorphism.
Use the finite-dimensional algebra \(B\) and the modules \(M(Y)\)
constructed in the preceding section, and put
\(H(Y)={}_{\alpha}(eY)\).
There is a single bounded complex \(P\) of finite-dimensional
\(B\)-bimodules, termwise projective on the right, such that for
every finite-dimensional left \(R\)-module \(Y\) one has
\begin{equation}
 P\otL_B M(Y)
 \simeq M(H(Y))\oplus M(H(Y))[3]
 \qquad\text{in }\D^b(B\text{-}\modu).
\end{equation}
All choices defining \(P\) are made independently of \(Y\).

Put \(\Phi=P\otL_B-\).  For every integer \(j\geq0\) and every
finite-dimensional left \(R\)-module \(Y\), there is an isomorphism
\[
 \Phi^j(M(Y))
 \simeq
 \bigoplus_{q=0}^j
   \bigl(M(H^{\circ j}(Y))[3q]\bigr)^{\oplus\binom{j}{q}} .
\]

statements.label: prop:ordinary-simulation
statements.text:
The algebra \(D\) has finite global dimension on both sides.
Let \(F=X\otL_D-\).  For every complex \(Z\) of left
\(B\)-modules, regarded as a complex on the first factor of
\(D\), there is an isomorphism
\begin{equation}

F^2(Z)\simeq P[b_*]\otL_B Z,
\qquad
T\otL_{B\otimes_k C}O\simeq P[b_*].
\end{equation}
The second isomorphism is an isomorphism of complexes of
\(B\)-bimodules, and the first is supported on the first
factor of \(D\).

statements.label: prop:bar-splitting
statements.text:
Let \(D\) be a finite-dimensional \(k\)-algebra, let \(X\) be
a finite-dimensional \(D\)-bimodule, and let
\(A=D\ltimes X\) be the algebra with multiplication
\[
(d,x)(d',x')=(dd',dx'+xd').
\]
Let \(N\) be a left \(D\)-module, inflated to \(A\) through
the projection \(A\to D\), and put \(F=X\otL_D-\).
In the derived category of left \(D\)-modules there is an
isomorphism
\begin{equation}

D\otL_A N
\simeq
\bigoplus_{r\ge0}(F^rN)[r].
\end{equation}
Here \(F^0N=N\), and every \(F^r\) denotes an iteration
of the derived tensor functor.
statements.section_title: A square-zero extension and projective dimension

statements.label: cor:pd-detection
statements.text:
In the setting of \Cref{prop:bar-splitting}, suppose that
\(D\) has finite global dimension on both sides and that
\(N\) is finite-dimensional.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If \(F^tN\simeq0\) for some \(t\ge1\), then
      \(\pd_A N<\infty\).
\item If \(F^rN\not\simeq0\), then \(\pd_A N\ge r\),
      with infinite projective dimension allowed.
\end{enumerate}

title: An asymptotic formula for the number of totients
abstract: Let \(V(x)\) count the distinct values of Euler's totient function up to x. We give an explicit asymptotic equivalent for \(V(x)\). Its coefficient is a uniform limit of functions defined from finite arithmetic data. We also prove that \(V(cx)/V(x)\to c\) as \(x\to\infty\) for every fixed c > 0, answering a question of Erdős and Hall.

tex.abstract: Let $V(x)$ count the distinct values of Euler's totient function up to~$x$. We give an explicit asymptotic equivalent for $V(x)$. Its coefficient is a uniform limit of functions defined from finite arithmetic data. We also prove that $V(cx)/V(x)\to c$ as $x\to\infty$ for every fixed $c>0$, answering a question of Erd\H{o}s and Hall.
sections: The arithmetic coefficient and the limiting formula

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For sufficiently large positive integers $H$, there are nonnegative
functions $A_H(1;\cdot):[0,1)\to\mathbb R$, given by the finite
arithmetic formula \eqref{eq:AH} below,
which converge uniformly as $H\to\infty$ to a function $A(1;\cdot)$
satisfying
\[
 0<\inf_{0\le s<1}A(1;s)
   \le\sup_{0\le s<1}A(1;s)<\infty.
\]
With the parameters \eqref{eq:renewal}--\eqref{eq:Gj},
\[
 V(x)\sim\frac{x}{\log x}\,G_m A(1;\theta).
\]
Moreover, for every fixed real $c>0$,
\[
 \frac{V(cx)}{V(x)}\longrightarrow c.
\]

statements.label: thm:companion
statements.text:
For each fixed positive integer $k$, the functions $A_H(f_k;s)$ converge uniformly for $0\le s<1$, and
\[
 N_k(x)=\frac{x}{\log x}\,G_m\bigl(A(f_k;\theta)+o(1)\bigr).
\]
There are two possibilities.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item If some $d\in\mathcal V$ satisfies $\ell(d)>kd$, then
 \[
  \inf_{0\le s<1}A(f_k;s)>0,\qquad
  N_k(x)\sim\frac{x}{\log x}\,G_m A(f_k;\theta)
       \asymp_k V(x).
 \]
 \item If no such $d$ exists, then $N_k(x)=0$ for every $x>0$, and $A(f_k;s)=0$ for every $s\in[0,1)$.
\end{enumerate}
The first alternative holds for $k=1,2$.

statements.label: prop:basic
statements.text:
There is a set \(E_x\subseteq\mathcal V\cap[1,x]\) with
\[
 |E_x|\le\{\varepsilon_H+o_{x;H}(1)\}V(x)
\]
such that every preimage of every
\(v\in(\mathcal V\cap[1,x])\setminus E_x\) is
\(p_0\cdots p_La\) for a basic witness.  One may take
\[
 \varepsilon_H\ll
 \e^{-cP}+K_H\exp\{-\exp(cP\rho^{-P})\}.
\]
For every basic witness, putting \(w=p_{R+1}\cdots p_La\), we have
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
 p_1\cdots p_La\le\exp((\log x)^{0.8}),\\
 \log w\le H\exp(0.62b_R)+\exp(2\widetilde b_L),
 \qquad w<p_R.
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
In particular \(w\) is bounded in terms of \(H\) alone, uniformly
in the phase.

statements.label: prop:discard
statements.text:
For \(t=x\) and \(t=x/c\), with the same \(x\)-dependent parameters,
\[
 |\mathcal D(t)|
 \le\{\varepsilon_H+o_{x;H}(1)\}\frac{xG_m}{\log x}.
\]
One may take \(\varepsilon_H\ll K_HH^{-2}\).
For all the witnesses in \eqref{eq:good-conditions} we also have
\begin{equation}
 P^+(D_i)<z_i,\qquad S_i<z_i,\qquad
 c h_i^{-20}\le b_{i+J_i}/b_i\le C h_i^{-18}.
\end{equation}

statements.label: prop:comparison
statements.text:
There are absolute constants $C$ and $y_0$ such that the following
holds.  Let $y\ge y_0$, put $B_y=\log_2 y$, and let $b$ be an integer
with $1\le b\le B_y$.  Suppose that real cutoffs satisfy
\[
 Y_0=y,\qquad \e^\e\le S\le Y_b,
 \qquad Y_{j+1}<U_j<Y_j\quad(0\le j<b).
\]
Put
\[
 \nu_j=\frac{\log_2 Y_j}{B_y}\quad(0\le j\le b),
 \qquad
 \mu_j=\frac{\log_2 U_j}{B_y}\quad(0\le j<b),
 \qquad
 \delta=\sqrt{\frac{\log_2 S}{B_y}}.
\]
Fix a positive integer $D$ with $P^+(D)\le Y_b$ and a real $r\ge1$.
Let $N$ count the ordered tuples
\[
 (p_0,\ldots,p_{b-1},q_0,\ldots,q_{b-1},D')
\]
in which $D'$ is a positive integer and the following conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item The $p_j,q_j$ are $S$-normal primes, $p_j\ne q_j$, and
 \[
  U_j\le P^+(p_j-1),P^+(q_j-1)\le Y_j
  \qquad(0\le j<b).
 \]
 \item $P^+(D')\le Y_b$ and
 \[
  D\prod_{j=0}^{b-1}(p_j-1)
  =D'\prod_{j=0}^{b-1}(q_j-1)\le\frac yr.
 \]
 \item The common product in \textup{(ii)} is squarefree on primes
 greater than $Y_b$.
 \item The part of $p_0-1$ supported above $Y_1$ exceeds $\sqrt y$.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 N\le{}&\frac{y}{rD}(CB_y^6)^b(b+1)^{\Omega(D)}
       (\log Y_b)^{1+3b\log(b(b+1))}\\
 &\quad\times
 (\log y)^{-2+\sum_{j=1}^{b-1}a_j\nu_j+E_b},
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
 E_b=2\sum_{j=1}^{b-1}(\nu_j-\mu_j)
      +\delta\sum_{i=2}^b(i\log i+i).
\end{equation}
Here $a_j$ is as defined in \eqref{eq:aj}.  Empty sums are zero;
in particular, when $b=1$ the cutoff in
\textup{(iv)} is $Y_1=Y_b$.

statements.title: Prefix collisions
statements.label: prop:collisions
statements.text:
Fix $c>1$, and form all parameters from $x$, with $H$ fixed before $x$
tends to infinity.  For $t=x$ or $t=x/c$, let
\[
 K(t)=\#\{(\tau,\sigma)\in\mathcal G(t)^2:
             \tau\ne\sigma,\ F(\tau)=F(\sigma)\}.
\]
There is a quantity $\epsilon_H\to0$, independent of the phase, such that
\[
 K(t)\le\bigl(\epsilon_H+o_{x;H}(1)\bigr)
                   \frac{xG_m}{\log x}.
\]
The pairs counted here are ordered pairs of distinct tuples.

statements.title: A common prefix for all preimages
statements.label: prop:unique-prefix
statements.text:
For $t=x$ or $t=x/c$, with the same parameters formed from $x$,
\begin{equation}
 \bigl|\,|\mathcal T(t)|-V(t)\,\bigr|
       \le\bigl(\epsilon_H+o_{x;H}(1)\bigr)\frac{xG_m}{\log x},
 \qquad\epsilon_H\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
There is a set $E^*(t)\subset\mathcal V\cap[1,t]$ for which both
$|E^*(t)|$ and the number of tuples in $\mathcal T(t)$ with values in
$E^*(t)$ are at most
$(\epsilon_H+o_{x;H}(1))xG_m/\log x$, after enlarging $\epsilon_H$.
For every $v\in(\mathcal V\cap[1,t])\setminus E^*(t)$ there is a unique tuple
$(p_0,\ldots,p_R,d)\in\mathcal T(t)$ of value $v$, and every preimage
of $v$ has this prefix and a remaining factor of totient $d$.
In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \ell(v)=p_0\cdots p_R\ell(d).
\end{equation}

title: An atomic certificate for triangular-lattice universal optimality
abstract: We prove that the density-one triangular lattice minimizes the lower energy per particle for every nonnegative completely monotone function of squared distance, among all locally finite planar configurations of centered disk density one. The comparison includes infinite energies. The proof constructs sharp Gaussian Fourier minorants using an atomic interpolation certificate.

tex.abstract:
We prove that the density-one triangular lattice minimizes the lower energy
per particle for every nonnegative completely monotone function of squared
distance, among all locally finite planar configurations of centered disk
density one. The comparison includes infinite energies. The proof constructs
sharp Gaussian Fourier minorants using an atomic interpolation certificate.
sections: Exact evaluation of the finite certificate

statements.title: Universal energy minimum
statements.label: thm:universal
statements.text:
For every smooth nonnegative completely monotone function $g$ on
$(0,\infty)$ and every locally finite planar set $\mathcal C$ of centered
disk density one,
\[
 E_g(\mathcal C)\ge
 \sum_{a\in A\setminus\{0\}}g(|a|^2)=E_g(A).
\]
The comparison and the equality are in the extended nonnegative reals.

statements.title: Sharp Gaussian minorants
statements.label: thm:gaussian
statements.text:
For every $\alpha>0$ there is a real radial Schwartz function
$f_\alpha:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ such that
\[
 f_\alpha(x)\le k_\alpha(x),\qquad
 \widehat f_\alpha(\xi)\ge0
 \quad(x,\xi\in\mathbb R^2),
\]
and
\[
 f_\alpha(a)=k_\alpha(a)\quad(a\in A\setminus\{0\}),\qquad
 \widehat f_\alpha(w)=0\quad(w\in A^*\setminus\{0\}).
\]
For $\alpha\ge1$, the construction uses two finite $20$-by-$20$ interpolation
blocks and an absolutely summable infinite correction.

statements.title: Exact interpolation and approximation
statements.label: prop:exact-interpolation
statements.text:
For every $\alpha\ge1$, let $z$ and $e$ be its Gaussian parameter and
data vector defined in Sections~\ref{sec:construction}
and~\ref{sec:finite-certificate}. Retain the fixed coefficients
$c_{i,0},d_{i,0},C_i$ in \eqref{analytic:input-functions}.
There are unique real coefficient lists
\[
 u_i\in\mathbb R^{20},\qquad
 w_i\in\ell^1(T;\mathbb R^2)\qquad(i=1,2),
\]
indexed respectively by the pairs $(c_{i,n},d_{i,n})$ on $f$ and $T$,
for which the functions $J_i=e^{\pi hs}F_i$ from that construction
satisfy
\[
 J_1(n)=G_z(n),\quad J_1'(n)=G_z'(n),\qquad
 J_2(n)=J_2'(n)=0\qquad(n\in\mathcal N).
\]
Relative to the finite coefficient lists $A_i e$, they obey
\begin{equation}
 \|w_i\|_1<3\cdot10^{-9},\qquad
 \|u_i-(A_i e)_f\|_1<10^{-5}\qquad(i=1,2).
 
\end{equation}
The resulting $F_i$ are real radial Schwartz functions with
$\widehat F_1=F_2$. Uniqueness concerns these coefficient lists with
the prescribed fixed columns, not all radial Schwartz functions with
the same interpolation data.

statements.title: Global signs
statements.label: prop:global-signs
statements.text:
The exact interpolation functions satisfy
\[
 J_1(s)\le G(s),\qquad J_2(s)\ge0\qquad(s\ge0).
\]

title: An exact Hausdorff gauge for SLE
abstract: For each \(0\lt \kappa\lt 8\), we construct a deterministic Hausdorff gauge that almost surely assigns positive finite measure to every nontrivial compact positive-time segment of chordal Schramm–Loewner evolution. This answers Schramm's Hausdorff-measure existence problem in this parameter range. The entire trace has finite expected gauge measure in each bounded box.

tex.abstract:
For each \(0<\kappa<8\), we construct a deterministic Hausdorff gauge
that almost surely assigns positive finite measure to every nontrivial
compact positive-time segment of chordal Schramm--Loewner evolution.
This answers Schramm's Hausdorff-measure existence problem in this
parameter range. The entire trace has finite expected gauge measure
in each bounded box.

statements.title: An exact moment gauge
statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Fix $0<\kappa<8$, and let $\gamma$ be chordal $\SLE_\kappa$ from
$0$ to $\infty$ in the upper half-plane $\HH$, parametrized by half-plane capacity $2t$.
There is a deterministic Hausdorff gauge $h_\kappa$, depending only on
$\kappa$, such that almost surely, simultaneously for every real
$0<s<t<\infty$,
\[
 0<\Haus^{h_\kappa}(\gamma([s,t]))<\infty.
\]

statements.label: op:potential
statements.section_title: Conformal radius and the law centered at one point

statements.title: Multipoint radius estimate
statements.label: mp:estimate
statements.text:
Let $D=J(\HH)$ as in Section~\ref{op:section}, and let
$x_1,\ldots,x_m\in D$ be distinct. Suppose
\[
 0<b_i\le R_D(x_i),\qquad b_i\le |x_i-x_j|\quad(j\ne i).
\]
For targets $0<e_i\le b_i$, let $E$ be the event that each $x_i$
reaches conformal radius $e_i$ while alive. Then
\begin{equation}
 \PP(E)\le C_{m,a}\prod_{i=1}^m(e_i/b_i)^\alpha.
 
\end{equation}
The constant depends only on $m$ and $a$, independently of $D$, $J$,
the initial angles, the radii, and the order and times of the hits.
A point need not remain alive after reaching its own target.
For targets exceeding some caps, the corresponding constraints may be
dropped, giving, after enlarging $C_{m,a}$,
\begin{equation}
 \PP(E)\le C_{m,a}
                \prod_{i=1}^m\min\{1,(e_i/b_i)^\alpha\}.
 
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: A uniform estimate for several radius hits

statements.title: Integrated level weights
statements.label: mp:level-moments
statements.text:
Let $f\ge0$ be bounded and supported in a compact $K\Subset D$.
Then, for every integer $m\ge1$,
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{l>0}\EE[A_l(f)^m]<\infty.
 
\end{equation}
Fix also $x_0\in D$ and $0<e_0\le R_D(x_0)$, and let $E_0$ be the
event that $x_0$ reaches radius $e_0$ while alive. Then
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{l>0}\EE[\ind_{E_0} A_l(f)^m]\le C e_0^\alpha.
 
\end{equation}
Here $C$ can be chosen using only $m,a$, the size and support of $f$,
the bounded location of $x_0$, and a positive lower bound for
$R_D$ on $K\cup\{x_0\}$. In particular, in a fixed disk these bounds
are uniform over all initial boundary angles.
statements.section_title: A uniform estimate for several radius hits

statements.title: Construction and conditional kernel
statements.label: mass:construction
statements.text:
There is an adapted increasing family $(\mu_t)_{0\le t\le\infty}$ of
locally finite measures on $\HH$, starting at zero, with the following
properties.  Its terminal measure is nonatomic and has moments of every
integer order on compact sets.  Almost surely, simultaneously for all
$0\le v<t<\infty$, the increment $\mu_t-\mu_v$ is carried by
$\gamma([v,t])\cap\HH$.  The process is locally continuous in total
variation, and $\mu_t\uparrow\mu_\infty$ as $t\to\infty$.
For every stopping time $S$, possibly infinite,
\begin{equation}
 \EE\bigl[\mu_\infty(\dd x)-\mu_S(\dd x)\mid\mathcal F_S\bigr]
   =G_S(x)\,\dd A(x),
 \qquad G_\infty:=0.
 
\end{equation}
This is an equality of conditional measure kernels; in particular it
allows nonnegative tests known at time $S$.  Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \EE\mu_\infty(\dd x)=G_0(x)\,\dd A(x).
 
\end{equation}

statements.label: mass:first-visit

statements.title: Pathwise interior restart
statements.label: mass:restart
statements.text:
Fix a stopping time $S$.  On $\{S<\infty\}$ put
$J_S=(g_S-B_S)^{-1}:\HH\to H_S$, and let $\widetilde\mu$ be the canonical
mass functional of the fresh Brownian motion $B_{S+t}-B_S$.
Almost surely, as measures on $H_S$, simultaneously for all
$0\le t\le\infty$,
\begin{equation}
 (\mu_{S+t}-\mu_S)|_{H_S}
       =(J_S)_*\bigl(|J_S'|^d\widetilde\mu_t\bigr).
 
\end{equation}
The same assertion holds when the initial domain is a fixed conformal
image of $\HH$.  Once this equality of measures has been obtained,
one may integrate any random nonnegative Borel weight on the restart
domain and evaluate at any later random time.
statements.section_title: A canonical mass on the trace

statements.title: Positive mass on every interval
statements.label: mass:positive
statements.text:
Almost surely, for every \mbox{$0\le v<t<\infty$},
\[
 (\mu_t-\mu_v)(\HH)>0.
\]
The positive mass can always be detected on an interior compact.  The
same statement holds in every fixed conformal image, in its associated
half-plane time.

statements.title: Gauge properties and finite exclusions
statements.label: gauge:admissible
statements.text:
The function \(h_\kappa\) is a Hausdorff gauge and satisfies
\begin{equation}
h_\kappa(Cr)\le C^2h_\kappa(r)
\qquad(C\ge1,\ r\ge0).
\end{equation}
The radii from distinct batches may interleave. Set
\[
H_{ni}(r)=b_{ni}r_{ni}^{\,d}\max\{1,(r/r_{ni})^2\}.
\]
If \(0\le F(r)\le M<\infty\) and
\(F(r)\le C H_{ni}(r)\) for every \(n\ge n_0\), every
\(1\le i\le I_n\), and every \(r>0\), then
\(F(r)\le C' h_\kappa(r)\) for all \(r>0\), for some finite
\(C'\).

statements.title: The lower Hausdorff bound
statements.label: hd:lower
statements.text:

\[
 \Haus^h(\gamma([s,t]))>0
 \qquad\text{for every real }0<s<t<\infty.
\]

statements.title: The upper Hausdorff bound
statements.label: hd:upper
statements.text:
For every integer $m\ge1$, the random variable
$\Haus^h(\Gamma\cap B_m)$, where $B_m=[-m,m]+i[0,m]$, is measurable
and satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \EE\,\Haus^h(\Gamma\cap B_m)<\infty.
 
\end{equation}
In particular, these whole-trace bounded-box measures are almost
surely finite simultaneously for all $m$.

title: An explicit counterexample to the Auslander-Reiten conjecture
abstract: We disprove the Auslander–Reiten conjecture for Artin algebras. We construct a finite-dimensional algebra Λ over \(k=\mathbb F_2(q,H_1,H_2)\) and a finite-dimensional nonprojective left module Z such that \(\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}\nolimits ^i_\Lambda(Z,Z)=\mathop{\mathrm{Ext}}\nolimits ^i_\Lambda(Z,\Lambda)=0\) for every i > 0. The module is Gorenstein-projective, so the same example also disproves the Gorenstein-projective conjecture. Both counterexamples persist after every extension of k.

tex.abstract:
We disprove the Auslander--Reiten conjecture for Artin algebras.
We construct a finite-dimensional algebra $\Lambda$ over
$k=\mathbb F_2(q,H_1,H_2)$ and a finite-dimensional nonprojective left module
$Z$ such that $\Ext^i_\Lambda(Z,Z)=\Ext^i_\Lambda(Z,\Lambda)=0$ for every
$i>0$. The module is Gorenstein-projective, so the same example also
disproves the Gorenstein-projective conjecture. Both counterexamples
persist after every extension of $k$.
