statements.title: Order and one-sided regularity of the coefficient
statements.label: an:coefficient-regularity
statements.text:
The function $a:(0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ is nondecreasing,
upper semicontinuous, and bounded above by $k$.  It is strictly
increasing on its positive set.  More precisely, if $k_2>k_1$
and $a(k_1)>0$, then
\begin{equation}
 \frac1{a(k_2)}\le\frac1{a(k_1)}+
                                    \frac1{k_2}-\frac1{k_1}.
 
\end{equation}
If its positive set is nonempty, it equals $[k_c,\infty)$
for some $k_c\ge8\pi$, and the physical critical temperature
is $\bc(J)=v_J^2k_c$.  In particular the endpoint is rough.
statements.section_title: Annular comparison, the physical criterion, and mixed pins

statements.title: Mixed-boundary height scaling
statements.label: an:mixed-scaling
statements.text:
On a fixed permitted component meeting a nonempty
positive-area pin region, the centered massless height
law at $k_h$ has the full Gaussian Laplace and moment
limits with covariance $a_h$ times the mixed inverse:
zero on that entire region and free on the other
walls.  This includes bounded piecewise continuous
smears and energy-approximable shifts.  Adding an admitted finite
observation penalty gives the corresponding Gaussian limit, also
for components without hard pins when translations are summed.
The limits are uniform over the fixed compact coefficient and center
sets just specified.
statements.section_title: Annular comparison, the physical criterion, and mixed pins

statements.title: Gaussian pin determinant and locality
statements.label: an:gaussian-localization
statements.text:
All assertions in this proposition are for real Gaussians.
The discrete limits allow every integer sequence $s\to\infty$
satisfying the bounded lattice rounding and retained-route assumptions
above.  The gradient coefficient may be any fixed
$a_{\mathrm g}>0$, independently of the height input $k_h$:
for unit-cell mass replace $\mathcal T_U$ by
\[
 \mathcal T_{U,a_{\mathrm g}}(v,w)
 =a_{\mathrm g}^{-1}\int_U\nabla v\cdot\nabla w
       +\sum_{d\subset U}(Bv)_d(Bw)_d .
\]
At $a_{\mathrm g}=a_h$ this is \eqref{an:continuum-high-form}.
Let $\mathcal E_U$ be the Hilbert space with inner product
$\mathcal T_{U,a_{\mathrm g}}$.  Set
\[
 V_p=\{v\in\mathcal E_U:v=0\text{ a.e. on }p\}^{\perp},
 \qquad V_H=\{v\in\mathcal E_U:v=0\text{ a.e. on }H\}^{\perp},
\]
and denote the orthogonal projections by $\Pi_p,\Pi_H$.
Then $C=\Pi_H|_{V_p}$ is Hilbert--Schmidt and $\|C\|<1$.
The finite interaction is
\begin{equation}
 D_U^{\mathrm{cg}}(H,p)
   =-\frac12\log\det\bigl(\Id-C^*C\bigr)
   =-\frac12\log\det\bigl(\Id-\Pi_p\Pi_H\Pi_p|_{V_p}\bigr).
 
\end{equation}
The full-pin interactions for the corresponding discrete
real Gaussians converge to \eqref{an:pin-determinant} as
$s\to\infty$; for real Gaussians the interaction is the logarithm
of the corresponding density ratio at zero.

The same Hilbert--Schmidt property, norm gap, determinant formula,
full discrete pin limit, and exhaustion by finite smooth pin-density
probes hold for the modified energy space with form
\[
 a_{\mathrm g}^{-1}\int_U\nabla v\cdot\nabla w
       +(\mathcal Ov)^TQ(\mathcal Ow),\qquad Q\ge0,
\]
where $\mathcal O$ is a fixed finite family of box averages or bounded
piecewise continuous density smears, each supported in one pre-pin
component, and $Q$ has no entries coupling different components.
The fixed penalty is coercive on the whole released component-constant
subspace.  The rank, coefficients, geometry, and separated positive-area
pin regions remain fixed through the mesh limit.  This includes each
fixed confining band partition and strength.  It also applies to the
fixed face-connected rectangular-piece geometries described after
Definition~\ref{an:geometry}, with the same pre-pin energy space.

For the locality assertions below, the mass cells may also be
axis-parallel rectangles whose side lengths lie in a fixed interval
$[c_0,C_0]\subset(0,\infty)$ and whose aspect ratios are bounded.
Here $(Bv)_d=|d|^{-1}\int_d v$, $B_s$ takes the corresponding
discrete uniform averages, and every cell has the squared-average
mass with coefficient one.  These bounds include any fixed finite
normalized shape list and its bounded lattice rounding.
For this local cell mass, harmonic extension and inverse-form
sources have energy tails bounded by $Ce^{-cr}$ at
distance $r$ from their supports.  Cross-projection
Hilbert--Schmidt norms satisfy the same decay up to a
polynomial factor in the number of relevant cells, with a fixed
positive lower bound on the pin clearance for the two restrictions.
Consequently $D_U^{\mathrm{cg}}(H,p)\le Ce^{-cr}$ up to
such a factor when their separation is $r$ and their
volumes are polynomial in $r$.

For this local cell mass let $T_{U,a'}$ be the operator of
$\mathcal T_{U,a'}$ and write
$\mathsf E_{U,a'}=\Id-BT_{U,a'}^{-1}B^*$ for the matrix of
\eqref{an:comparison-energy}, with its discrete analogue
using $B_s$.  Its off-diagonal entries decay exponentially.
If bonds at a core are cut, the change of this matrix
decays exponentially as either observation index recedes
from the core.  Computing this change in an open patch
whose guard has width $r$ makes an error bounded by
\begin{equation}
 C e^{-cr-c\dist(i,j)}
 
\end{equation}
in cell entries, after local differences are extended by
zero.  All the preceding locality constants, including
the tail and cross-projection bounds, are uniform when $a'$ ranges over
a fixed compact interval in $(0,\infty)$ and on the permitted
cell ensembles with the stated uniform shape bounds and uniform
polynomial ball volumes in the cell graph.  The compared topologies use
the same $a'$.  Patch boundaries follow
cell faces and the guard width is measured in the common inclusion
cell graph.  The discrete locality estimates also hold on finite
periodic identifications satisfying the same cell and retained-route
assumptions and polynomial ball-volume bounds.  Distances are then
measured in the quotient inclusion graph, and the guard width is
the distance to the bonds actually cut to form the patch.  The patch
is a union of intact cells with all crossing bonds cut; an opened
periodic seam counts as part of its boundary.  A patch equal to the
whole component with its periodic bonds retained has zero proxy error.
Without hard pins these
change and error forms have zero row sum on each
underlying component.  Thus an entry bound with prefactor
$\delta$ and exponential distance decay bounds their
quadratic forms by
\begin{equation}
 C\delta\sum_{\{i,j\}\text{ neighboring cells in the region}}
                       (y_i-y_j)^2.
 
\end{equation}
For hard-wall changes one instead retains the entry
bounds on $y_i y_j$, with decay from the walls.

statements.title: Full hard-pin comparison
statements.label: an:pin-interaction
statements.text:
For every fixed geometry and separated box regions $H,p$
as above, at $k=k_h$,
\begin{equation}
 D_U(H,p)\longrightarrow D_U^{\mathrm{cg}}(H,p)
 \qquad(s\to\infty).
 
\end{equation}
The baseline on both sides has unit-cell observation mass,
free exterior walls, and no other hard pins.
statements.section_title: Annular comparison, the physical criterion, and mixed pins

statements.title: Conditional convergence and pin ratios
statements.label: an:conditional-pins
statements.text:
In the centered high law on a fixed permitted geometry,
for every fixed finite list of real linear cell or bounded
piecewise continuous density smears $X$ with their sampled
profiles, the conditional expectations
$\E(e^X\mid h_p)$ converge in probability in the
finite-observation approximation sense to their
Gaussian conditional values.  The same holds jointly
for conditional weak laws on fixed finite lists.
Define
\begin{equation}
 r_H(b)=\frac{P_U(h_H=0\mid h_p=b)}
                   {P_U(h_H=0\mid h_p=0)}.
 
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 0<r_H(b)\le1,\qquad \E r_H=e^{-D_U(H,p)},
 
\end{equation}
and $r_H$ converges in the same approximation sense
to the Gaussian ratio $r_H^{\mathrm{cg}}$, which is
strictly positive almost surely.  The expectation identity in
Equation~\eqref{an:pin-ratio-mean} is for the centered high law.
The convergence assertions persist under a real exponential tilt
$T_s=\sum_jt_jX_{j,s}$ from a fixed finite list of such observations,
or energy-approximable observations with the same joint full and
hard-pinned Laplace and moment limits together with the pin probes.
The chosen list must have uniformly bounded bare covariance.
The coefficients $t_j$ may range over a
fixed compact set.  The limit is the corresponding tilted Gaussian
conditional law.  When the centered ratio $r_H$ is evaluated at
tilted random pin data its pointwise bounds remain valid, but its
expectation need not remain $e^{-D_U(H,p)}$.

If restoring bonds supported inside $H$ changes
the centered high law from $\mu$ to $\nu$, and
$Q_\Delta(h)=\exp(-(h,\Delta h)/2)$ is their
positive quadratic penalty, set
\begin{equation}
 r_\Delta(b)=
 \frac{\E_\mu(Q_\Delta\mid h_p=b)}
      {\E_\mu(Q_\Delta\mid h_p=0)}.
 
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 r_H\le r_\Delta\le1,\qquad
 \frac{\dd\nu_p}{\dd\mu_p}
      =\frac{r_\Delta}{\E_\mu r_\Delta},\qquad
 r_H\le\frac{\dd\nu_p}{\dd\mu_p}\le e^{D_U(H,p)}.
 
\end{equation}
Consequently events about the pin data whose probabilities
tend to zero can be transferred in both directions between
these cut and restored topologies with identical exterior.
All assertions concern fixed domains and fixed finite
lists; they do not assert convergence uniformly at
arbitrarily prescribed microscopic pin values.

statements.title: Placement factors
statements.label: rg:restricted-localization
statements.text:
For small linear terms at a prescribed coarse block the number of fine placements is at most $CL^2$.  For terms whose fine support is within a fixed number of fine blocks of a specified straight side it is at most $CL$, and for terms within a fixed number of fine blocks of one of a fixed number $k$ of marked points it is at most $Ck$.  Thus the neutral bulk, even wall, and unrestricted marked remainders of Lemma~\ref{rg:localization}, after summing placements, are bounded respectively by
\[
 C L^{-1}\eps,\qquad C L^{-1}\eps,\qquad C kL^{-1}\eps
\]
in output activity norm, apart from large polymers and nonlinear terms.  A bulk term whose fluctuation neighborhood touches a wall can always be bounded without subtraction by $C_{L,A}\eps$ and used as forcing.
statements.section_title: Finite-range integration and local partition algebra

statements.title: Exact local partition map
statements.label: rg:partition-map
statements.text:
Under the locality, finite-range, and norm hypotheses already specified, shell integration, localizations on small linear inputs, and extraction of their designated field-independent coefficients define activities $K'$ and numbers $a_b$, one at each coarse block, satisfying the exact identity
\begin{equation}
 \E\mathcal Z_m(K;\phi+\zeta)
 =\prod_{b\in\mathcal B_S}(1+a_b)\mathcal Z_S(K';\phi).
\end{equation}
The map preserves the period, locality, and every symmetry respected by the designated localizations.  To first order, $K'$ is the sum of the subtracted small expectations, the unchanged large expectations, and the nonconstant parts assigned to coarse singletons.  When singleton polynomials are measured separately, write
\[
 K(X)=K_{\rm reg}(X)+\ind_{X=\{B\}}\sum_{\nu\in I}t_{B,\nu}P^\nu_{m,B},
 \qquad
 |P^\nu_{m,B}|_{m,\{B\},\phi}\le C_{\rm pol}W_m^\kappa(\{B\},\phi).
\]
Here $I$ is fixed and finite, and the $P^\nu_{m,B}$ form a fixed family of local polynomials, independent of the activity inputs, with the prescribed collar and period.  The displayed point-norm bound is uniform in $\nu$, the retained scale, the block, and the finite volume.  Suppose
\[
 \|K_{\rm reg}\|_{m,A,\kappa}
       +\sup_B\sum_{\nu\in I}|t_{B,\nu}|\le\eps.
\]
If a fixed scalar representation retains $K_{\rm reg}=\sum_\mu K_{\rm reg}^\mu$ as separate components, replace $\|K_{\rm reg}\|_{m,A,\kappa}$ in this bound by $\sum_\mu\|K_{\rm reg}^\mu\|_{m,A,\kappa}$, and include every separately retained coefficient occurrence in the absolute coefficient sum.  With external parameters fixed, all designated localization and scalar extraction maps are fixed complex-linear maps of this measured input vector.  Let $F_{Y,b}$ be the complete singleton piece assigned from the small linear inputs with original closure $Y$ to $b\in Y$, retaining $Y$ as its exclusion label, and let $a_b$ be the sum of the designated field-independent scalar contributions from these same local $Y\to b$ inputs.  Each assigned piece has the prescribed target collar and period.  For every complex input vector obeying the displayed bound, require
\[
 \sup_b\left\{
 \sum_{Y\ni b}\sup_\phi
 \frac{|F_{Y,b}|_{S,\{b\},\phi}}{W_S^\kappa(\{b\},\phi)}
       +|a_b|\right\}\le C_{L,A}\eps,
\]
uniformly in retained scales and finite volumes.
Then on a sufficiently small ball
\begin{equation}
 \|K'-K'_{\rm lin}\|_{S,A,\kappa}\le C_{L,A}\eps^2.
\end{equation}
This is a complex analytic map of its activity inputs, with the corresponding convergent Taylor series and derivative bounds.  The assertion is not analyticity in the frequency convention $\alpha$.

The same finite algebra and spatial enumeration apply to a separately specified representation under the same locality, finite-range, and exclusion hypotheses, with fixed complex-linear designated maps, provided its input size includes every retained component and it supplies the corresponding bounds for compatible-family products, Gaussian integration, complete assigned singleton pieces, and scalars in its normalized size.  The point-norm and complex analyticity assertions above are statements about the scalar representation.

After $L$ has been fixed, taking $A$ sufficiently large makes the contribution from large linear inputs an arbitrarily small multiple of their norm.  The small linear estimates are those of Lemmas~\ref{rg:localization}, \ref{rg:charged} and Corollary~\ref{rg:restricted-localization}.  All constants and smallness radii are uniform in finite volumes.  For the terminal assertion, separately assume that the retained activity grid at scale $m_*$ satisfies the grid conditions above and $M/m_*\le D_0L$; its block count is then at most $C(D_0L)^2$.  The spectral decomposition and terminal estimates retain their own stated domains.
statements.section_title: Finite-range integration and local partition algebra

statements.title: Microscopic initialization
statements.label: vi:initialization
statements.text:
After this first convolution and extraction of identical scalar factors
in twisted and untwisted volumes, the plane activities have the form
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal K_0^b(X,\phi)
 =\ind_{X=\{B\}}\frac s2 e_B(\phi)+\mathcal P_0(X,\phi),\qquad
 \norm{\mathcal P_0}\le C(s^2+z),\quad z=e^{-cb}.
 
\end{equation}
Here $e_B$ is the gradient energy on the sites of the block, with the
orientation average used in Lemma~\ref{rg:localization}.  Finite free or
periodic grids have full initial norm at most $C(|s|+z)$.  For each fixed
$C_\eta<\infty$, the same bound holds for twists with
$\sup|\eta|\le C_\eta$, with $C$ allowed to depend on $C_\eta$.
In an unchanged interior neighborhood the untwisted activities are the plane activities.
In every neighborhood with a common lift $\lambda$ of the twist, the
twisted activities equal the corresponding untwisted activities evaluated
at $\phi+\lambda$.

statements.title: Scalar tuning
statements.label: vi:bulk-tuning
statements.section_title: The ordinary Villain model and transfer to a full spin field

statements.title: Walls and arbitrary integer side lengths
statements.label: vi:walls
statements.text:
On each free square of side $M=2n$, for every integer $n$, and on each
periodic square of side $L^N$, the untwisted activities are exact copies
of the tuned plane activities wherever the required local neighborhoods
miss the walls or unwrap on the torus.  If $w_j$ is their full norm on
the remaining supports, then for some $\rho<\rho_1<1$,
\begin{equation}
 w_j\le Cz\rho_1^j.
\end{equation}
After the scalar factors of the local maps have been extracted, the
terminal partition average tends to one as $M\to\infty$.
statements.section_title: The ordinary Villain model and transfer to a full spin field

statements.title: Identification with the height coefficient
statements.label: vi:height-bridge
statements.text:
For all sufficiently large $b$, the parameter tuned in
Proposition~\ref{vi:bulk-tuning} satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \beff(J_{\nn},\pi^2b)=\frac{\pi^2b}{1+s(b)},\qquad
 K_{\mathrm V}(b)=\frac{\beff(J_{\nn},\pi^2b)}{\pi^2}.
 
\end{equation}
The first identity is obtained from the same bulk map as the spin-source
estimates below.
statements.section_title: The ordinary Villain model and transfer to a full spin field

statements.title: Translated copies and defect flow
statements.label: vi:marked-flow
statements.text:
There is a choice of exact twisted maps with the following properties.
On every shift-good support the twisted activity is exactly the
untwisted activity at the local lifted translate.  For $k\le2$ at every
scale, or for arbitrary fixed $k$ with source separations at least
$\epsilon M$ at scales
\begin{equation}
 S=Lm\le c\epsilon M/(k+1),                              
\end{equation}
the full defect norm $v_j$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 v_{j+1}\le\theta v_j+C(u_j+w_j)
                         +C(u_j+w_j+v_j)^2,\qquad
 v_j\le Cz\rho_2^j,\quad \rho_1<\rho_2<1.              
\end{equation}
The constants in the decaying regime are independent of $k$ under
\eqref{vi:early-scale}.  For each fixed $k,\epsilon$, the remaining
bounded number of scales preserve an $o(1)$ bound as $M\to\infty$.
Consequently, after extracting the designated scalar factors, the
twisted terminal partition average tends to one uniformly for separated
interior configurations.
statements.section_title: The ordinary Villain model and transfer to a full spin field

statements.title: A location-independent amplitude
statements.label: vi:amplitude
statements.text:
For the single parameter $s(b)$ chosen in
Proposition~\ref{vi:bulk-tuning}, there is $c(b)\in(0,\infty)$ such that
for every fixed $k$ and every sequence of signed unit sources tending to
distinct interior points,
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal R_{n,b}\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^k\varsigma_i\delta_{x_i}\right)
             \longrightarrow c(b)^k.                    
\end{equation}
The limit is uniform on separated compact configurations.  For $k\le2$
the ratios are bounded above and below by positive constants uniformly
in the locations, signs, coincidences, and sufficiently large $n$.
Moreover $|\log c(b)|\le Cz$.

statements.title: Normalized correlations
statements.label: vi:correlations
statements.section_title: The ordinary Villain model and transfer to a full spin field

statements.title: Transfer from signed correlations to the full spin field
statements.label: vi:field-transfer
statements.text:
Fix one of the ordinary nearest-neighbor XY or Villain models on $D_n$,
at a fixed positive inverse temperature, with zero boundary angles.
Suppose there are constants $K>1/(4\pi)$ and $A>0$, independent of $n$,
with the following properties.  Put
\[
 a_n(x)=A\exp\{G_n(x,x)/(2K)\},\qquad
 U_n^\sigma(x)=a_n(x)e^{i\sigma\theta_x},\qquad
 S_n^\sigma(f)=n^{-2}\sum_{x\in D_n^\circ}f(x)U_n^\sigma(x).
\]
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item For every $m\geq1$, every signs $\sigma_i\in\{-1,1\}$,
every $E\Subset D$, and every $\delta>0$, uniformly for
$x_i\in E\cap D_n^\circ$ with $|x_i-x_j|\geq\delta$ for $i\ne j$,
\begin{equation}
 \E\prod_{i=1}^m U_n^{\sigma_i}(x_i)
 -\exp\left\{-\frac1K\sum_{i<j}\sigma_i\sigma_j
                          G_D(x_i,x_j)\right\}\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
\item There is $Q\in[0,2)$ such that, for every $E\Subset D$, some
$C_E<\infty$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 0\leq\E[U_n^\sigma(x)U_n^\tau(y)]
       \leq C_E(|x-y|+n^{-1})^{-Q}
\end{equation}
for all $n$, all $x,y\in E\cap D_n^\circ$, including $x=y$, and
all $\sigma,\tau\in\{-1,1\}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\[
 S_n^+\ \Longrightarrow\ V_{K,D}
           \quad\hbox{in }H^{-3}_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)
\]
along the full sequence of integers $n$.
All finite collections of complex smeared fields converge jointly, and
every mixed moment of such a collection converges to
\eqref{vi:continuum-moments}.
statements.section_title: The ordinary Villain model and transfer to a full spin field

statements.title: Low-temperature Villain field
statements.label: vi:villain-spin
statements.text:
There is $b_0(\mathrm V)<\infty$ such that for every $b\ge b_0(\mathrm V)$
the ordinary Villain model with zero boundary angles satisfies
\[
 n^{-2}\sum_{x\in D_n^\circ}
 A_{\mathrm V}(b)\exp\{G_n(x,x)/(2K_{\mathrm V}(b))\}
       e^{i\theta_x}\delta_x
 \ \Longrightarrow\ V_{K_{\mathrm V}(b),D}
       \quad\hbox{in }H^{-3}_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)
\]
along all integers $n\to\infty$, with joint convergence of every finite
collection of complex smears and convergence of all their mixed moments.
Here
\[
 A_{\mathrm V}(b)=c(b)^{-1}>0,\qquad
 K_{\mathrm V}(b)=\frac b{1+s(b)}
  =\frac{\beff(J_{\nn},\pi^2b)}{\pi^2},\qquad
 \frac{K_{\mathrm V}(b)}b\longrightarrow1.
\]
The lower bound can be chosen so that $K_{\mathrm V}(b)>1/(4\pi)$ and
$\pi^2b\ge\bc(J_{\nn})$ for every such $b$.
statements.section_title: The ordinary Villain model and transfer to a full spin field

statements.title: Unwrapping and sources
statements.label: xyh:branch
statements.text:
Up to a positive source-independent constant, the XY partition function is
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{\substack{q\in\Z^{\mathrm{dual}}\\\sum q=0}}
 e^{-\|V_q\|^2/2}\,
 \E_{X\sim N(0,P_T)}\prod_e f_b((X+V_q)_e),
 \qquad V_q=\mathfrak p\partial Gq.
\end{equation}
For an integral source $l$ on primal vertices, choose an integral current
$dG_n l+\mathcal R\partial a$ of divergence $l$, and set
\[
 \vartheta=a/\sqrt b,\qquad
 \eta=-\mathcal R^{-1}dG_n l/\sqrt b.
\]
The numerator for $\E e^{i(l,\theta)}$ is the same sum with insertion
\begin{equation}
 e^{-i(X,\eta)+i\mathfrak p(q,\vartheta)}.
\end{equation}
In particular $\partial^*\eta=0$ and
$\|\eta\|^2=(l,G_nl)/b$.
statements.section_title: The ordinary XY model: mixed Gaussian histories

statements.title: Exact compensation and spin offsets
statements.label: xyh:compensation
statements.text:
The normalized integral with inverse covariance
Equation~\eqref{xyh:inverse-pair}, vertex factors, edge factors $f_b(w)$,
and factor $e^{U(w,p)}$ equals
Equation~\eqref{xyh:positive-ensemble} up to one source-independent
determinant normalization. If in the interaction one replaces
\begin{equation}
 p\mapsto p+\eta,\quad \psi\mapsto\psi+\vartheta,
 \quad w\mapsto w-i d_c\eta/\mu,
\end{equation}
including this last replacement in $f_b$, the integral is the physical
inserted partition function multiplied by
\begin{equation}
 \exp\{(s+d_c^2/\mu)\|\eta\|^2/2\}.
\end{equation}
These identities have the finite-dimensional limiting interpretation
specified in the proof, including at $s=0$.
statements.section_title: The ordinary XY model: mixed Gaussian histories

statements.title: The exact XY activity calculus
statements.label: xyh:calculus
statements.text:
Fix the covariance construction and the local partition map above.
Choose the fixed support and collar clearances, small-support threshold,
and $K_0$ first; then choose sufficiently large dyadic $L$, the polymer
weight as in Proposition~\ref{rg:partition-map}, a sufficiently small
parameter neighborhood, and finally sufficiently large $b$. Within
Equation~\eqref{xyh:permitted-parameters} the original XY integrals admit
positive representation sizes with all the following properties. Write
$\mathsf s_X(\mathcal R)$ for the size of a specified representation on
$X$, and $\|\mathcal R\|_A=\sup_X A^{|X|}\mathsf s_X(\mathcal R)$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item An $F_b$ leaf costs $C/b$; a nonzero charge $q$ costs
$C e^{-cbq^2}$, summable over $q\ne0$; the linear microscopic
compensation costs $C|s_\bullet|$, and its nonlinear remainder costs
$C|s_\bullet|^2$. A full-block tensor costs $C|t|$, and a localized
polynomial costs a constant times its coefficient on normalized
$m$-scale directions.
\item Convolving a compatible product multiplies its input sizes, up to
a fixed factor per input. Temporary exclusions, relocation, scalar
normalizer decorations, and separation into a singleton tensor and
remainder are exact. The animal and placement sums obey
Proposition~\ref{rg:partition-map}; hence all multiple-input and
normalizer corrections are quadratic in the input sizes.
\item For a small single neutral linear input of size $u$, localization
has normalized coefficients at most $Cu$ and remainder size
$CL^{-3}u$ in the even bulk after constant and quadratic subtraction,
$CL^{-2}u$ at an even wall after constant subtraction, and $CL^{-1}u$
at a defect after constant subtraction. Each small charged single-input
step has size at most $CL^{-4}u$. Constants in these local gains do not
grow with sufficiently large $L$.
\item Sizes bound terminated evaluations and fixed-order Cauchy
derivatives with bounded smooth normalized backgrounds. In finitely many
normalized source directions the evaluated expressions are jointly
holomorphic on fixed bounded polydiscs, with the corresponding Cauchy
bounds after adding their finitely many probe events. They apply to
copied good pieces, their one-time translations to defects, and the
intrinsic offsets of Equation~\eqref{xyh:offsets}. For fixed separated
sources, the lower bound on $b$ is independent of their number; only the
boundedly many late numerical event costs may depend on the fixed source
configuration. If $T_\Lambda$ is an admissible early transport of an
untagged representation, then for any $A_U\ge A_D>0$, before support relocation
\[
 \mathsf s_X(T_\Lambda\mathcal R)=\mathsf s_X(\mathcal R),\qquad
 A_D^{|X|}\mathsf s_X(T_\Lambda\mathcal R)
 \le (A_D/A_U)^{|X|}\|\mathcal R\|_{A_U}.
\]
The transport leaves every opaque completed coefficient occurrence
unchanged and is not defined on an already tagged live root.
\item Every finite-depth activity, assigned coefficient, and normalized
partition identity is continuous in the permitted parameters, including
at $s=d_*s_{12}^2$ and at $s=0$, as long as its scalar normalizers are
nonzero. The statement holds on the plane at finite support, on finite
reflected grids, and on auxiliary tori with terminal transverse harmonic
directions. The bulk tensor and its local recursion are the same in all
these settings wherever the calculation has the required clearance.
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: The ordinary XY model: mixed Gaussian histories

statements.title: Bulk recurrence
statements.label: xyf:recurrence
statements.text:
For every sufficiently small fixed \(\theta>0\), the geometric
parameters, then \(L\), and then \(A\) can be chosen so that the exact
bulk activities have the decomposition
\[
 K_j(X)=\ind_{X=\{B\}}\mathcal E_B(t_j)+\mathcal P_j(X),
 \qquad t_0=(s_{11},s_{12},s_{22}).
\]
If \(r_j\) is their remainder size, then, while the quantities on the
right are small,
\begin{align}
 |t_{j+1}-t_j|_\infty&\le C r_j,\\
 r_{j+1}&\le\theta r_j+C_{L,A}(|t_j|_\infty+r_j)^2,
       \\
 r_0&\le C_{L,A}\bigl(b^{-1}+|t_0|_\infty^2\bigr).
       
\end{align}
At every fixed depth these coefficients and the needed fixed field
derivatives are continuous on the set where the preceding bounds are
retained.  The recurrence also holds, with the same bulk tensors,
on an auxiliary torus of side \(F L^j\), through scale \(L^j\), if
the fixed integer \(F\) is sufficiently large.
statements.section_title: The XY flow, admissible tuning, and spin-field limit

statements.title: Admissible infinite trajectory
statements.label: xyf:shooting
statements.text:
For all sufficiently large \(b\), there is a choice
\[
 |s_{11}|+|s_{12}|+s_{22}=O(b^{-1}),\qquad
 s_{22}\ge d_*s_{12}^2,
\]
for which the exact bulk flow satisfies
\begin{equation}
 |t_j|_\infty\le T\eps\rho^j,
 \qquad r_j\le2\eps\rho^j,
 \qquad \eps=C_*/b,
 \quad 0<\theta<\rho<1.
 
\end{equation}
The constants and the lower bound on \(b\) do not depend on a
correlation order or a finite-volume cutoff.
statements.section_title: The XY flow, admissible tuning, and spin-field limit

statements.title: Forced recurrences
statements.label: xyf:forced
statements.text:
For untwisted wall activities let \(w_j\) denote their full size.
For twisted defect activities let \(v_j\) denote their full size.
There are fixed \(\rho<\rho_1<\rho_2<1\) such that
\begin{align}
 w_{j+1}&\le\theta w_j+C u_j+C(u_j+w_j)^2,
             &w_j&\le C\eps\rho_1^j,
             \\
 v_{j+1}&\le\theta v_j+C(u_j+w_j)+C(u_j+w_j+v_j)^2,
             &v_j&\le C\eps\rho_2^j.
             
\end{align}
The defect statements hold at all scales for at most two unit signed
sources, including coincident sources.  For \(k\) fixed sources
separated by at least \(\epsilon_0 n\) in lattice units, they hold
through scales \(L^{j+1}\le c\epsilon_0 n/(k+1)\).
The constants in these decaying recurrences and the required lower
bound on \(b\) are independent of \(k\).  The subsequent bounded
number of steps preserve an \(o(1)\) activity bound as \(n\to\infty\),
with constants allowed to depend on the fixed configuration and \(k\).
statements.section_title: The XY flow, admissible tuning, and spin-field limit

statements.title: A universal spatial amplitude
statements.label: xyf:amplitude
statements.text:
There is \(c_b\in(0,\infty)\), depending only on \(b\) and the
fixed surviving parameters, such that, for each fixed \(k\) and
every convergent configuration of distinct interior continuum
locations,
\begin{equation}
 R_n\!\left(\sum_{r=1}^k\varsigma_r\delta_{x_{r,n}}\right)
       \longrightarrow c_b^k.
 
\end{equation}
The same \(c_b\) works for both signs, every interior position,
every integer sequence \(n\to\infty\), and every choice of nested
cuts.  The ratios for at most two sources are bounded uniformly
without a separation condition.

statements.title: Low-temperature XY field
statements.label: xyf:spin
statements.section_title: The XY flow, admissible tuning, and spin-field limit

statements.title: Microscopic smallness
statements.label: wh:uv
statements.text:
For $a'$ in a fixed compact interval containing $k_0$ or lying above it,
the two ultraviolet integrations have the exact block representation
\begin{equation}
 K_0(X)=\ind_{X=\{B\}}\{s e_B^0/2+z_0c_B^\alpha\}
          +\mathcal R_0(X),\qquad
 z_0=2m_0^2e^{-a'D_{\rm uv}/2}.
\end{equation}
For spread-out $J_\rho$, choose $1/2<\gamma'<\gamma$ and put
$\delta_0=e^{-\gamma'a'v^2/2}$.  For exponentially small $s$,
\begin{equation}
 \|\mathcal R_0\|\le C\rho^C(|s|+\delta_0)^2,
 \qquad
 \|\partial_s\mathcal R_0\|\le C\rho^C(|s|+\delta_0).
\end{equation}
Thus, uniformly on $|s|\le C'z_0$, these bounds are $o(z_0)$ and
$o(1)$, respectively.  Uniformly towards unbounded $a'$, it suffices
to use the weaker bounds $C\rho^C(s^2+\delta_0)$ and
$C\rho^C(|s|+\delta_0)$, and the designated cosine may be absorbed in
the remainder.  For fixed $J$ these weaker bounds hold with $C_J$ and
any fixed $0<\gamma'<\gamma$ when $a'$ is sufficiently large.

statements.title: Weak local maps
statements.label: wh:map
statements.text:
Choose the regulator parameters and $h_0$ first, then $L$ sufficiently
large, and then $A$ sufficiently large depending on $L$.  On a fixed
small activity ball the exact partition algebra induces analytic maps
\begin{equation}
 \begin{pmatrix}t_+\\z_+\\R_+\end{pmatrix}
 =\begin{pmatrix}t+P_j^tR\\\lambda_jz+P_j^zR\\C_jR\end{pmatrix}
     +\mathcal N_j(t,z,R),
 \quad
 \|C_j\|\le\theta<1,\quad
 \|P_j^t\|+\|P_j^z\|\le C_{L,A},
\end{equation}
where $\theta$ can be chosen arbitrarily small and
\begin{equation}
 \|\mathcal N_j(t,z,R)\|
       \le C_{L,A}(|t|+|z|+\|R\|)^2.
\end{equation}
The same ball has uniform analytic Taylor coefficient and differentiated
estimates at fixed $a'$.  These assertions hold on a fixed one-sided
reference interval $k_0\le a'\le k_0+\delta_{\rm ref}$,
uniformly in sufficiently spread-out $J_\rho$ for the first kernel
family.  For every fixed $J$, they hold at a sufficiently large
starting scale for either the first family or the entry family of
Lemma~\ref{wh:kernels}.

On a compact subinterval of $a'>k_0$, one may omit the cosine
coordinate and leave every charged activity in the remainder.  Choose
$L$ depending on the gap from $k_0$; then the corresponding map has
the same assertions with its $z$ row deleted.  For $a'\ge4k_0$ there
is also such a map with a charged contraction uniform in $a'$.

The scalar coefficients obtained on the plane are exactly the torus
coefficients through the stopping scale.  Torus remainders and their
activity derivatives obey the same estimates.  Each fixed-support
finite recursion and each finite scalar projection is continuous in
the parameters while its preceding activities remain in the small
ball.  This last assertion does not assert norm analyticity under
variation of $\alpha$.

statements.title: Balanced map
statements.label: wh:balanced-map
statements.text:
On a fixed small norm ball the maps in these coordinates have the form
\begin{align}
 T_+&=T+b_j^{tt}T^2+b_j^{zz}Z^2+E_{1,j},\notag\\
 Z_+&=(1-\mu)Z+b_j^{tz}TZ+E_{2,j},\\
 R_+&=C_jR+O((|T|+|Z|+\|R\|)^2),\notag\\
 |E_{i,j}|&\le C\{(|T|+|Z|)^3+(|T|+|Z|)\|R\|+\|R\|^2\}.
 \notag
\end{align}
All errors are analytic in the activity coordinates with the
corresponding Taylor and derivative estimates.  Under half-period
translation the scalar coordinates have parities $T\mapsto T$ and
$Z\mapsto-Z$; this accounts for all displayed quadratic monomials
on pure scalar inputs.

statements.title: The secular quadratic terms
statements.label: wh:quadratic-coefficients
statements.text:
In the continuum limit at $a'=k_0$, the balanced coefficients are
independent of the scale and satisfy
\begin{equation}
 b^{tt}=0,\qquad b^{tz}=-b<0,\qquad b^{zz}=-H<0.
\end{equation}
The positive numbers $b,H$ stay in compact subintervals of
$(0,\infty)$ as $u$ ranges over the compact interval in
Lemma~\ref{wh:kernels}.  Consequently, given $\varepsilon>0$, one
can first take $\mu_0$ small and then $\rho$ large so that, uniformly
in $j$, $|b_j^{tt}|\le\varepsilon$ and $-b_j^{tz},-b_j^{zz}$ lie in
fixed compact positive intervals.  For every fixed $J$ the same
conclusion follows by making the starting scale sufficiently large.
At that fixed $J$ the coefficients converge to their continuum
limits as $j\to\infty$ when $a'=k_0$.

For the fixed-$J$ entry family, use its own multipliers
$\lambda_j^{\rm en}$ and its own projection operators in the same
balanced coordinates.  Its critical continuum coefficients are
\[
\begin{gathered}
 b_{\rm en}^{tt}=0,\qquad b_{\rm en}^{tz}=-b_{\rm en},
 \qquad b_{\rm en}^{zz}=-H_{\rm en},\\
 b_{\rm en}=2\log L,\qquad
 H_{\rm en}=\frac{8\pi\cdot\pi}{4}
       e^{8\pi c_{\upsilon_{\rm en}}}\log L>0,\\
 \upsilon_{\rm en}=\frac{v}{\sqrt{32}}.
\end{gathered}
\]
At this fixed $J$, the corresponding discrete coefficients converge
to these limits at criticality and have the stated positive bounds
on a sufficiently small one-sided reference interval once $m$ is
large.  If $d$ is the largest power of two not exceeding the sup
range of $J$, then $u_{\rm wh}=v/(d\sqrt{32})$ is the width of
the first fixed-$J$ family at the same block ratio, and
$H_{\rm en}=d^4H_{\rm wh}$, whereas $b_{\rm en}=b_{\rm wh}$.
These entry-family bounds are not uniform in a varying $J$.

statements.title: A vanishing-activity shot
statements.label: wh:gapped-shooting
statements.text:
In each of the following regimes there is a choice of the input
$s$ in Equation~\eqref{wh:compensation} for which all interaction
activities tend to zero exponentially in scale:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
 \item $J=J_\rho$, a prescribed fixed $a'>k_0$, and $\rho$
       sufficiently large;
 \item an arbitrary fixed admissible $J$ and $a'$ sufficiently large.
\end{enumerate}
The shot satisfies $|s|\le Cx_*$, where $x_*$ is exponentially
small in $a'v^2$ in (i), and $x_*\le C_Je^{-c_Ja'}$ in (ii).
At the input $k=a'/(1-s)$ its actual structural coefficient is
exactly $a'$.

statements.title: Every sufficiently high input
statements.label: wh:high-temperature
statements.text:
For every admissible fixed $J$, the positive-coefficient regime is
nonempty and its physical onset is finite.  Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 a(k)=k+O_J(e^{-c_Jk}),\qquad
 \beff(J,\beta)=\beta+O_J(e^{-c_J'\beta})
       \quad(k,\beta\to\infty).
\end{equation}

statements.title: Spread-out onset
statements.label: wh:spread-out
statements.text:
For the spread-out family,
\[
 \frac{\bc(J_\rho)}{8\pi v_{J_\rho}^2}\longrightarrow1.
\]

statements.title: Local entry at every positive coefficient
statements.label: en:entry
statements.text:
Fix $J,k_h,a_h$ as above.  Fix admissible parameters for the small-activity
maps of Proposition~\ref{wh:map}, including their block factor $L$, activity
weights $A$, and analytic radius $h_0$, with the regulator choices allowed
by Lemma~\ref{en:regulator}.  For every $\epsilon>0$ there are a fixed
dyadic integer $q$, an arbitrarily large dyadic $R$, $P=R^5$, a dyadic
$s$, and a neighborhood
$\mathcal U\subset(0,\infty)\times\operatorname{int}I$ of $(k_h,a_h)$,
such that the following assertions hold at $m=qRs$.

On the plane there are real, even, square-covariant local activities
$K_m(X;k,a')$, invariant under translations of the block grids and
under common field translation by $2\pi/\alpha$, with
\begin{equation}
                 \|K_m(k,a')\|_{m,A,V}\leq\epsilon
                 \quad ((k,a')\in\mathcal U).
\end{equation}
Their subset expansion on every dyadic torus fitting the hierarchy and
with side $n\geq sP$ is an exact representation of
Equation~\eqref{en:exact-density}, after integrating the observation
noise and the Gaussian covariance below side $m$, up to a
field-independent factor that cancels upon normalization.  The torus
activities obey the same estimate.  A support whose padded neighborhood
unwraps has exactly its plane activity.  This copying property persists
under the local maps up to their specified stopping scale.
Here fitting means that $n/s$ is a multiple of $qR$, the torus uses
the same grid origin, and $n/(mL^j)$ is an integer for every retained
coarse grid.

On a smaller neighborhood the activities are analytic in $k$ at fixed
$a'$.  For every integer $r\geq0$ there is $C_r<\infty$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \|\partial_k^rK_m(k,a')\|_{m,A,V}\leq C_r\epsilon.
\end{equation}
The constants may depend on $s,R,J,k_h$ and the chosen neighborhoods.
Finite-support evaluations, their field derivatives, and scalar
localization projections are continuous in $a'$.

The choices are made in the following order: the downstream norm
parameters and the imaginary field strip widths are fixed first;
then $R$ and $P$; then a finite large-field threshold; then $s$; and
finally $\mathcal U$.  No uniform scaling assertion at temperatures
other than $k_h$ is part of either the hypotheses or the proof.
statements.section_title: Entry from a positive Gaussian coefficient

statements.title: No exit and vanishing at true references
statements.label: ep:no-exit
statements.text:
For every sufficiently small prescribed tube radius $\rho>0$,
the entry choices can be made so that the true-reference plane
trajectory stays in this tube at every step and tends to zero.
The stopped torus remainders also tend to zero.  If
$a(k_c)=8\pi$, the same entry choices keep all true-reference
trajectories $(k,a(k))$, $k\in[k_c,k_c+\delta)$, in that tube for
some $\delta>0$.  Each of these trajectories tends to zero;
uniform convergence in $k$ is not asserted here.

statements.title: Completion of the height assertions
statements.label: ep:height-conclusion
statements.text:
For every admissible finite-range $J$, the uniquely determined
effective temperature is
\[
 \beff(J,\beta)=v_J^2a(\beta/v_J^2),\qquad
 \beta\ge\bc(J).
\]
It has the field, Laplace-functional, and tightness conclusions
in Theorem~\ref{main:heights}, is differentiable for $\beta>\bc(J)$, and satisfies
\[
 \beff(J,\bc(J))=8\pi v_J^2,\qquad
 \lim_{\beta\downarrow\bc(J)}
 \frac{\beff(J,\beta)-\beff(J,\bc(J))}
      {\beta-\bc(J)}=+\infty .
\]
Its high-temperature normalization and spread-out onset are
\[
 \beff(J,\beta)=\beta+O_J(e^{-c_J\beta}),\qquad
 \frac{\bc(J_\rho)}{8\pi v_{J_\rho}^2}\longrightarrow1 .
\]
For nearest neighbors the endpoint value is $2\pi$.

title: Backward intertwiners and a transitive commutant
abstract: We give a negative answer to the hyperinvariant-subspace problem by constructing, on every infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space, a nonzero bounded norm-quasinilpotent operator with no nonzero proper closed hyperinvariant subspace. Its commutant is a proper strongly closed unital transitive complex operator algebra.

tex.abstract:
We give a negative answer to the hyperinvariant-subspace problem by
constructing, on every infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space,
a nonzero bounded norm-quasinilpotent operator with no nonzero proper closed
hyperinvariant subspace. Its commutant is a proper strongly closed unital
transitive complex operator algebra.

statements.label: thm:direct-model
statements.text:
There are measurable positive weights $\beta_j:X\to(0,\infty)$,
$j\in\Z$, and a contraction $V\in\B(H_0)$ with the following properties.
The shifts
\[
 S_xe_j=\beta_j(x)e_{j+1},\qquad (Sf)(x)=S_xf(x),
\]
define a bounded operator $S$ on $H_0$, and:
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $x\in X$, the closed invariant subspaces of $S_x$ are
exactly $\Ktail{h}$, $h\in\Z\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\}$.
\item The operator $S$ is nonzero, $\|S\|=e^{-10}$, and for every
integer $n\ge1$,
\begin{equation}
 \|S^n\|\le
 \exp\left(-10\left\lfloor\frac{(n+1)^2}{4}\right\rfloor\right).
\end{equation}
\item The operator $V$ commutes with $S$ and has the form
\[
 (Vf)(\theta x)=V_xf(x),\qquad V_xe_j=b_j(x)e_{j-1},
\]
where $0\le b_j(x)\le1$ are measurable and are positive on a common
conull set. On that set,
\[
 \overline{V_x\Ktail{h}}=\Ktail{h-1}\quad(h\in\Z),
 \qquad \overline{V_xK}=K.
\]
\item The unital complex algebra generated by $S$, $V$, and all
scalar multipliers $M_g$ is transitive.
\end{enumerate}

statements.label: cor:direct-algebra
statements.text:
Every infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space admits a
nonzero bounded norm-quasinilpotent operator with no nonzero proper
closed hyperinvariant subspace. Its commutant is a proper strongly
closed unital transitive complex operator algebra.

statements.label: prop:fibers
statements.text: For every $x\in X$, the operator $S_xe_j=\beta_j(x)e_{j+1}$ is bounded, has norm $e^{-c}$, and has precisely the standard tails as its closed invariant subspaces. For each $v\in K$, the map $x\mapsto S_xv$ is measurable.

statements.label: prop:normquasi
statements.text:
The operator $S$ is nonzero and norm-quasinilpotent. More precisely, for
all integers $n\ge1$,
\[
 \|S^n\|\le \exp\left(-c\left\lfloor\frac{(n+1)^2}{4}\right\rfloor\right).
\]

statements.label: prop:V
statements.text:
The contraction $V$ commutes with $S$. For every $x\in X_*$ and $h\in\Z$,
\[
 \overline{V_x\Ktail{h}}=\Ktail{h-1},\qquad
 \overline{V_xK}=K.
\]

title: Balanced counterexamples to Ryser's conjecture at prime orders
abstract: For every sufficiently large prime q, we construct a finite intersecting \((q+1)\)-partite \((q+1)\)-uniform hypergraph with covering number \(q+1\) and exactly \(q+1\) nonisolated vertices in each part. This disproves Ryser's covering conjecture, even for intersecting hypergraphs with equally sized parts.

tex.abstract:
For every sufficiently large prime $q$, we construct a finite intersecting
$(q+1)$-partite $(q+1)$-uniform hypergraph with covering number $q+1$
and exactly $q+1$ nonisolated vertices in each part. This disproves
Ryser's covering conjecture, even for intersecting hypergraphs with
equally sized parts.
sections: From modified line partitions to a hypergraph
Deletion lines and concentration of core covers
Random merged pairs and their candidate graph
Excluding small covers at affine pencils

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There exists $q_0$ such that, for every prime $q\ge q_0$, there is a
finite intersecting $(q+1)$-partite $(q+1)$-uniform hypergraph $H$ with
\[
 |V_1|=\cdots=|V_{q+1}|=q+1,
 \qquad \tau(H)=q+1.
\]
Every vertex belongs to an edge.

statements.label: cor:tree-cover
statements.text:
For every sufficiently large prime $q$, there is a finite complete
graph with a $(q+1)$-edge-coloring whose vertices require exactly
$q+1$ monochromatic trees to cover. The same minimum holds for
connected monochromatic subgraphs.

statements.title: Deterministic reduction
statements.label: prop:deterministic-reduction
statements.text:
Let $q\geq4$ be a prime power.  Suppose a compatible collection of valid
tuples in $\mathbb F_q^2$ satisfies occupancy, concentration of core
covers, and the local condition with parameters $0<\rho<1$ and
$B\geq0$.  If
\begin{equation}
 \rho q>2(1+B),
 
\end{equation}
then there is an intersecting $(q+1)$-partite $(q+1)$-uniform hypergraph
with exactly $q+1$ nonisolated vertices in each part and cover number
$q+1$.  Its edges are in bijection with the set $X$ in
\eqref{eq:det-core}.
statements.section_title: From modified line partitions to a hypergraph

statements.title: Robust deletion estimates
statements.label: thm:deletion
statements.text:
Fix $k\ge1$ and $K\ge0$.  For each $q$, let $\mathsf Q_q$ be a probability
law on the same sets as $\mathsf U_{q,k}$ such that
\[
 \mathsf Q_q(D)\le e^{Kq}\mathsf U_{q,k}(D)
 \quad\text{for every }D.
\]
Then the following assertions hold as $q\to\infty$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item The empirical probability measure
$q^{-2}\sum_{x\in A}\delta_{i_D(x)}$ converges in probability, in total
variation, to the Poisson distribution with mean $k$.
\item Write $\mu=e^{-k}$.  For every fixed $\lambda,\eta>0$, the probability
that at least $\eta q$ lines $\ell\in\mathcal L\setminus D$ satisfy
\[
 \left|\frac{|\ell\cap R_D|}{q}-\mu\right|\ge\lambda
\]
tends to zero.
\item For every fixed $\delta>0$, the probability that there is a set
$C\subseteq\mathcal L\setminus D$ with $|C|\le q$ which covers $R_D$ and
leaves at least $\delta q^2$ points of $A$ uncovered tends to zero.
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: Deletion lines and concentration of core covers

statements.title: Concentration of core covers
statements.label: cor:core-pencil
statements.text:
Assume the laws of Theorem~\ref{thm:deletion}, and let $q$ tend to infinity
through primes.  For each fixed $\zeta>0$, with probability tending to one,
every set $C\subseteq\mathcal L\setminus D$ of at most $q$ lines covering
$R_D$ has at least $(1-\zeta)q$ members through a common projective point.
statements.section_title: Deletion lines and concentration of core covers

statements.label: prop:candidate-graph
statements.text:
There are constants $c_*>0$ and $C_*<\infty$ such that, with probability
$1-o(1)$, the following assertions hold simultaneously, with
$\beta=1/8$ and $c_0=1/5$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $c_*q\le |Q_g|\le q$ for every direction $g$.
\item Every vertex has degree at most $C_*q$, and has at most $q^\beta$
neighbors in each slot.
\item For every $v$ there is a set $J(v)$ of at most $q^\beta$ vertices
such that $|N(v)\cap N(w)|\le q^\beta$ for $w\notin J(v)$.
Every member of $J(v)$ is adjacent to $v$ or is in its slot.
\item At most $\lceil\log q\rceil$ constituents pass through any affine
point, counting multiplicity. Every line other than one of the $M_g^1$
has at least $c_0q$ points outside $\bigcup_gM_g^1$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently the event that these assertions hold and that
$M_g^0\ne M_g^1$ for every $g$ has probability $e^{-1}+o(1)$.
statements.section_title: Random merged pairs and their candidate graph

statements.title: Selection with bounded cylinder probabilities
statements.label: sel:selection
statements.text:
Fix constants $c_*,C_*>0$ and $0<c_0\le1$, and put $\beta=1/8$.
For each sufficiently large integer $q$, let a finite graph have its
vertex set partitioned into $n=2(q+1)$ slots $Q_i$, with no edge within
a slot.  Write $N(v)$ for the neighborhood of a vertex.  Suppose that
\begin{align}
 c_*q\le |Q_i|\le q,&\qquad |N(v)|\le C_*q,
 \qquad |N(v)\cap Q_i|\le q^\beta,\\
 |J(v)|\le q^\beta,&\qquad
 |N(v)\cap N(w)|\le q^\beta\quad(w\notin J(v)),
\end{align}
where every $w\in J(v)$ is either adjacent to $v$ or in its slot.
There are constants $K_*,\rho>0$, depending only on $c_*,C_*,c_0$,
and a random procedure which either fails or returns an independent
transversal $(V_i)_{i\in I_0}$, where $I_0$ is the set of slots and
$V_i\in Q_i$.  If $\mathcal A$ denotes its event of returning a
transversal, then
\begin{equation}
 \Prb(\mathcal A)=1-o(1).
\end{equation}
For any $s$ distinct slots $i_1,\ldots,i_s$ and any prescribed vertices
$v_j\in Q_{i_j}$,
\begin{equation}
 \Prb\bigl(\mathcal A, V_{i_j}=v_j\ (1\le j\le s)\bigr)
 \le (K_*/q)^s.
\end{equation}

Suppose also that the slots are indexed by $(g,k)$, with two slots for
each direction $g$ of an affine plane of order $q$.  Associate to each
vertex in slot $(g,k)$ a line of direction $g$, injectively within
that slot.  For every affine line $\ell$, let $T_\ell\subseteq\ell$
be a fixed set of at least $c_0q$ points.  From $T_\ell$ remove every
point on a selected line different from $\ell$, and call the remaining
set $T_\ell^{\rm fin}$.  Then the same procedure satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \Prb\bigl(\mathcal A, \min_\ell |T_\ell^{\rm fin}|<\rho q\bigr)
 =o(1).
\end{equation}
The errors in \eqref{sel:success} and
\eqref{sel:occupancy-conclusion} are uniform in all the stated input
data.  By the injectivity within a slot, \eqref{sel:cylinder} also
holds for prescribed candidate lines.

statements.title: Domination of the deletion-line law
statements.label: sel:deletion-domination
statements.text:
Let $D$ consist of the selected split lines and the lines $M_g^1$
in the preceding experiment.  Conditional on $\mathcal A$, the law
of $D$ is dominated pointwise by $\exp(O(q))$ times the uniform
law on sets containing three distinct lines in each direction.

statements.label: prop:pencil-local
statements.text:
In the independent offset experiment with the selection procedure above,
\[
 \mathbb P\bigl(\mathcal A\text{ and the local condition fails at some }
 p\in A\bigr)=o(1).
\]
Here the local condition, required whenever $b(p)\ge3$, is the prohibition
on covers of $F(p)$ by $Z(p)$ and at most $b(p)-1$ additional sets stated in
Section~\ref{sec:deterministic-construction}.

title: Baumslag-Solitar-free one-relator groups are hyperbolic
abstract: We prove Gersten's conjecture: every finitely generated one-relator group containing no subgroup isomorphic to a Baumslag–Solitar group \(\mathop{\mathrm{BS}}\nolimits (m,n)\), for nonzero integers m, n, is word-hyperbolic.

tex.abstract:
We prove Gersten's conjecture: every finitely generated one-relator group
containing no subgroup isomorphic to a Baumslag--Solitar group
$\operatorname{BS}(m,n)$, for nonzero integers $m,n$, is word-hyperbolic.
sections: Intersections, cyclic commensurators, and rank bounds
Annuli and currents for a restricted HNN extension
A stationary current and its line trajectories
Finite carriers for a stationary current
Expansion and periodic lines in the support
Special rays and the end of the combination proof

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $X$ be a finite set and let $r\in F(X)$. If the one-relator group
$G=\langle X\mid r\rangle$ contains no subgroup isomorphic to
$\operatorname{BS}(m,n)$ for any nonzero integers $m,n$, then $G$ is
word-hyperbolic.

statements.label: thm:magnus
statements.text:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite connected graph, and let
$\lambda:S^1\to\Gamma$ be a nontrivial immersed circuit representing a
non-power in $\pi_1\Gamma$. Attach a $2$-cell along $\lambda$, obtaining
$Y$. If $\pi_1Y$ is Baumslag--Solitar-free, then, for every connected
subgraph $S\subseteq\Gamma$ with $\lambda(S^1)\nsubseteq S$, the map
\[
 \pi_1S\longrightarrow\pi_1Y
\]
is injective and its image is quasiconvex.

statements.label: pre:cyclic-off-diagonal
statements.text:
Let \(P\) be a finitely generated free group and \(E\leq P\) a strongly
inert subgroup. If \(g\in P\setminus E\), then
\(E\cap gEg^{-1}\) is trivial or cyclic.
statements.section_title: Intersections, cyclic commensurators, and rank bounds

statements.title: Restricted combination theorem
statements.label: ann:combination
statements.text:
Let $H$ be a torsion-free word-hyperbolic group, let $A,B\leq H$ be
finitely generated free quasiconvex subgroups, and let $\phi\colon A\to B$
be an isomorphism.  Set
\[
 G=\langle H,t\mid tat^{-1}=\phi(a)\ (a\in A)\rangle,
 \qquad P=A,\qquad I=A\cap B,\qquad J=t^{-1}It\leq P.
\]
Assume the following two conditions.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item For $M,N\in\{A,B\}$ and $g\in H$, the intersection
      $M\cap gNg^{-1}$ is at most cyclic unless $g\in MN$.
\item The groups $I,J$ are finitely generated, and each $E\in\{I,J\}$
      satisfies
      \begin{equation}
      \sum_{SpE\in S\backslash P/E}
        \bar r(E\cap p^{-1}Sp)\leq\bar r(S)
      \qquad\text{for every finitely generated }S\leq P.
      
      \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
If $G$ contains no subgroup isomorphic to $BS(m,n)$ for any nonzero
integers $m,n$, then $G$ is word-hyperbolic.
statements.section_title: Annuli and currents for a restricted HNN extension

statements.title: Algebraic annular flaring
statements.label: ann:external-flaring
statements.text:
Let $H$ be word-hyperbolic, let $A,B\leq H$ be finitely generated,
and let $\phi:A\to B$ be an isomorphism such that both attaching
maps $A\to H$ are quasi-isometric embeddings. Set
$G=\langle H,t\mid tat^{-1}=\phi(a),\ a\in A\rangle$.
Then $G$ is word-hyperbolic if there exist $\lambda>1$ and an integer
$m\geq1$ such that, for every $\rho>0$, there is $h(\rho)$ for which
every essential algebraic annulus as defined above, with $2m+1$ rows,
width at most $\rho$, and girth at least $h(\rho)$, is
$\lambda$-hyperbolic.
statements.section_title: Annuli and currents for a restricted HNN extension

statements.title: The current trajectory forced by nonflaring
statements.label: ann:trajectory
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{ann:combination}, if $G$ is not
hyperbolic, there exist currents
$\mu_s\in\operatorname{Curr}(P)$ for $s\in\mathbb Z$, signs
$\epsilon_s\in\{+,-\}$, and transition types $\tau_s$ with signs
$(\epsilon_s,\epsilon_{s+1})$, such that
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $\|\mu_0\|=1$, every $\mu_s$ is nonzero, and
      $\sup_{s\in\mathbb Z}\|\mu_s\|<\infty$;
\item for every $s$ there is a current
      $\nu_s\in\operatorname{Curr}(K_{\tau_s})$ with
      \[
      \mu_s=(\theta_{\tau_s,0})_*\nu_s,
      \qquad
      \mu_{s+1}=(\theta_{\tau_s,1})_*\nu_s;
      \]
\item all types are essential: any reversing type uses a double
      coset outside the common side subgroup.
\end{enumerate}
The constants in~\eqref{ann:uniform-transition-bounds} apply to this
trajectory.  In particular, $\|\mu_s\|\geq C^{-|s|}$ for all $s$.
statements.section_title: Annuli and currents for a restricted HNN extension

statements.label: stat:no-atoms
statements.text:
Let $(\mu_s)_{s\in\mathbb Z}$ be a bounded sequence of nonzero
$P$-currents with transition currents and compatible essential types
as in Proposition~\ref{ann:trajectory}.  If $G$ is Baumslag--Solitar
free, every $\mu_s$ is atomless.
statements.section_title: A stationary current and its line trajectories

statements.label: stat:stationary
statements.text:
Under the assumptions of Proposition~\ref{stat:no-atoms}, there exist
a nonzero current $\nu$ on $I$ and a nonzero atomless current $\mu$ on
$P$ such that
\begin{equation}
                         i_*\nu=j_*\nu=\mu.
\end{equation}
In particular, if the restricted HNN extension is not hyperbolic,
Proposition~\ref{ann:trajectory} supplies such a stationary current.
statements.section_title: A stationary current and its line trajectories

statements.label: stat:transfers
statements.text:
There is a translation- and flip-invariant conull Borel set
$\mathcal U\subset\Omega$ with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item Every line of $\mathcal U$ has two irrational endpoints and is
carried by a unique $I$ coset and a unique $J$ coset.
\item On lines carried by $p\Lambda I$, translate by $p^{-1}$ and
apply the boundary isomorphism from $I$ to $J$.  This forward
transfer, and the analogous backward transfer from $q\Lambda J$,
preserve $\mu$ on their domains.
\item Every defined transfer, its inverse, and every output frame
translation take lines of $\mathcal U$ to lines of $\mathcal U$.
Consequently all successive forward and backward transfers exist on
$\mathcal U$.
\end{enumerate}
Measure preservation in~\textup{(ii)} holds on the full Borel domain
of lines with irrational endpoints, not only after restriction to
$\mathcal U$.
statements.section_title: A stationary current and its line trajectories

statements.label: stat:windows
statements.text:
Every line $L\in\mathcal U$ determines an actual aligned bilateral
path of positively traversed edges
\[
                     \cdots,E_{-1},E_0=e,E_1,\cdots
\]
in $\mathcal T$, with transferred lines in its successive edge frames.
The following properties hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item The path is independent of coset representatives and of
compatible changes of frames and line coordinates.
\item For every finite window containing $E_0$, its stabilizer
$K\le P$ is finitely generated and noncyclic, and the endpoints of
$L$ lie in $\Lambda K$.
\item Two distinct actual aligned windows of the same shape about
$e$ have at most cyclic common stabilizer.  In particular, an
irrational point can belong to the limit sets of at most one such
window stabilizer.
\item If an aligned one-sided window joins $e$ to $he$, its
stabilizer is $S=P\cap hPh^{-1}$.  The boundary map of
\[
                  S\longrightarrow h^{-1}Sh,
                         \qquad x\longmapsto h^{-1}xh,
\]
implements its line transfer.  On the irrational-endpoint domain it
preserves $\mu$; it takes its domain in $\mathcal U$ into
$\mathcal U$.
\end{enumerate}
In~\textup{(iii)}, a shape specifies the numbers of edges before and
after the central edge, all traversed positively.
statements.section_title: A stationary current and its line trajectories

statements.title: Finite cofinal carriers
statements.label: car:finite-carriers
statements.text:
The noncyclic component subgroup classes of
$\Gamma^{\mathrm{sm}}$ belong to $\mathcal C$ and form a finite
cofinal subset: every $[Q]\in\mathcal C$ is contained, up to
$P$-conjugacy, in one of them.  In particular $\mathcal C$ has only
finitely many maximal elements, and they are exactly the maximal
members of this finite family.
statements.section_title: Finite carriers for a stationary current

statements.title: Atoroidal return
statements.label: car:return
statements.text:
The map $F$ is an order-preserving bijection with order-preserving
inverse.  It permutes the finite set of maximal classes of
$\mathcal C$.  For every representative $M$ of such a class, there
are an integer $p\ge1$ and an element $v\in G$ of height $p$ such
that
\[
 v^{-1}Mv=M.
\]
The automorphism $\alpha:M\to M$, $\alpha(m)=v^{-1}mv$, is
atoroidal: no nontrivial conjugacy class in $M$ is periodic under
$\alpha$.
statements.section_title: Finite carriers for a stationary current

statements.title: Zero mass on a maximal carrier
statements.label: car:zero-mass
statements.text:
For every maximal carrier $M$ supplied by
Proposition~\ref{car:finite-carriers},
\[
 \mu(\partial^2\Lambda M)=0.
\]
The same holds for every $P$-translate of this line set.
statements.section_title: Finite carriers for a stationary current

statements.label: exp:carrier-periodic
statements.text:
If $\Omega$ contains a line carried, up to translation, by a maximal
noncyclic carrier $M$, then $\Omega$ contains a periodic line.
statements.section_title: Expansion and periodic lines in the support

statements.label: exp:no-periodic
statements.text: The support $\Omega$ contains no periodic line.
statements.section_title: Expansion and periodic lines in the support

statements.label: exp:support
statements.text:
The following assertions hold for the closed support $\Omega$.
\begin{enumerate}
 \item No line of $\Omega$ is carried by the small subgraph.
 There is an integer $B_0$ such that every segment of a lift of
 an $\Omega$-line to any of the selected subsequence cores
 $\Gamma_n$, if contained entirely in the small subgraph, has
 length at most $B_0$.
 \item Every endpoint of every line of $\Omega$ is irrational.
 \item Every line of $\Omega$ lifts to each centered core union $\Gamma_n$
 and has a unique compatible bilateral trajectory. On each
 fixed window, the partial boundary transfer takes every
 support line in its domain to a line of $\Omega$.
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: Expansion and periodic lines in the support

statements.label: mag:nonpower-hyperbolicity
statements.text:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite connected graph, and let
$\lambda\colon S^1\to\Gamma$ be a nontrivial immersed circuit
representing a non-power in $\pi_1\Gamma$.
If $\pi_1(\Gamma\cup_\lambda D^2)$ is $BS$-free, then it is
word-hyperbolic.

statements.label: cor:free-by-cyclic
statements.text:
Let $X$ be finite, let $r\in F(X)$, and suppose that
$G=F(X)/\langle\!\langle r\rangle\!\rangle$ contains no subgroup
isomorphic to $\operatorname{BS}(m,n)$ for any nonzero integers $m,n$.
There are a finite-index subgroup $H\leq G$, an integer $d\geq0$, an
automorphism $\alpha$ of the rank-$d$ free group $F_d$, and an embedding
\[
H\hookrightarrow F_d\rtimes_\alpha\mathbb Z.
\]
Consequently the same $H$ fits into an exact sequence
\[
1\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow H\longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow1,
\qquad K\text{ free},\quad Q\leq\mathbb Z.
\]
Thus $G$ is virtually free-by-cyclic, with the rank of $K$ allowed to be
infinite and $Q$ allowed to be trivial.

title: Beyond the Square-Root Exponent for Depth-Three Boolean Circuits
abstract: We construct a language in deterministic polynomial time whose n-bit membership function requires \(2^{\omega(\sqrt n)}\) gates in an unbounded-fan-in OR–AND–OR circuit. The bound holds at every sufficiently large input length and counts all gates, including the bottom layer.

tex.abstract:
We construct a language in deterministic polynomial time whose \(n\)-bit
membership function requires \(2^{\omega(\sqrt n)}\) gates in an
unbounded-fan-in OR--AND--OR circuit.  The bound holds at every
sufficiently large input length and counts all gates, including the
bottom layer.
sections: A restriction bound independent of clause count
A disjoint sparse partition of bounded-width CNFs
One explicit language and its hard slices

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is a language \(L\subseteq\bits^*\), a deterministic Turing machine
deciding \(L\), and fixed positive integers \(C,a\) such that the machine
runs in time at most \(C(n+1)^a\) on every input of length \(n\).
If \(f_n\) is the membership function of \(L\) on \(\bits^n\), then
\[
 \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log_2 S_3(f_n)}{\sqrt n}=\infty.
\]
Equivalently, for every real \(A>0\), there is an integer \(N_A\)
such that
\[
 S_3(f_n)>2^{A\sqrt n}\qquad\text{for every }n\ge N_A.
\]
No uniformity or bottom fan-in restriction is imposed on the circuits.

statements.label: prop:polytime
statements.text:
The language $L$ is decided on every input of length $n$ by one
deterministic Turing machine in time $C(n+1)^a$, for some fixed positive
integers $C,a$.
statements.section_title: One explicit language and its hard slices

statements.label: prop:good-slices
statements.text:
For each fixed integer $b\ge1$ and real $B>0$, all sufficiently large
lengths $n$ admit fixed settings of the non-data bits such that, with
\[
 p=\frac{B}{\sqrt d},\qquad m_0=pd=B\sqrt d,
\]
the resulting sign $g$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \Pr_{T,\rho}\left[
 |T|\notin[m_0/2,2m_0]
 \ \text{or}\ 
 \corr_b(g_{T,\rho})>2^{-|T|/8}
 \right]
 \le4\cdot2^{-m_0/16}.
\end{equation}
Here $T$ includes each of the $d$ data coordinates independently with
probability $p$, and $\rho$ is an independent uniform assignment outside
$T$.  In particular, the correlation bound on a good restriction holds
simultaneously for all members of $\mathcal C_b(T)$.

title: Bi-Lipschitz Absorption of c0 Without a Linear Copy of c0
abstract: We construct a separable real Banach space Z that contains no linear copy of c0, yet is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to \(Z\oplus_\infty c_0\). The same space contains a bi-Lipschitz image of every separable metric space.

tex.abstract:
We construct a separable real Banach space \(Z\) that contains no linear
copy of \(c_0\), yet is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to
\(Z\oplus_\infty c_0\). The same space contains a bi-Lipschitz image
of every separable metric space.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is a separable real Banach space \(Z\) containing no closed linear
subspace isomorphic to \(c_0\), and an onto bi-Lipschitz map
\[
                 F:Z\oplus_\infty c_0\longrightarrow Z.
\]

statements.title: Global distance bounds
statements.label: prop:global
statements.text:
For every \(x,x'\in D\),
\begin{equation}
 \left(\frac15-24\eta\right)\|x-x'\|_D
 \leq\|g(x)-g(x')\|_U
 \leq(5+24\eta)\|x-x'\|_D.                                  
\end{equation}
In particular, \(g\) is injective and continuous.

statements.title: Onto-ness of the nonlinear shift
statements.label: prop:onto
statements.text:
The map \(g:D\to U\) in \eqref{eq:g-definition} is onto. Together with
Proposition~\ref{prop:global}, it is a bi-Lipschitz bijection.

statements.title: Selection of compatible detectors
statements.label: prop:compatible-detectors
statements.text:
Let \((m_i)\subset Z\) be weakly null, meaning
\(u(m_i)\to0\) for every \(u\in Z^*\). Suppose \(F_i\) belong to one
listed class \(\mathcal L\) and
\begin{equation}
                  |\langle F_i,m_i\rangle|\geq\delta>0
                  \qquad(i\geq1).
                  
\end{equation}
There are a subsequence \((m_{i_k})\), a listed class
\(\mathcal L_1\), tests \(\widetilde F_k\in\mathcal L_1\),
\(\delta_1>0\), and an integer \(C_1\geq1\) such that
\[
 |\langle\widetilde F_k,m_{i_k}\rangle|\geq\delta_1,
 \qquad
 \Lip\!\left(\sum_{k\in H}\epsilon_k\widetilde F_k\right)\leq C_1
\]
for every \(k\), every finite \(H\), and all signs \(\epsilon_k\).

statements.label: prop:no-c0
statements.text: The Banach space \(Z\) contains no linearly isomorphic copy of \(c_0\).

statements.label: cor:same-space
statements.text:
For this same separable real Banach space \(Z\):
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(Z\oplus_\infty c_0\) and \(Z\) are bi-Lipschitz equivalent
but not linearly isomorphic.
\item \(c_0\) embeds bi-Lipschitzly into \(Z\), although \(Z\)
contains no linear copy of \(c_0\).
\item Every separable metric space embeds bi-Lipschitzly into \(Z\).
\end{enumerate}

title: Bi-Lipschitz Coordinates at Regular Points of Noncollapsed RCD Spaces
abstract: We resolve the regular-point bi-Lipschitz conjecture in the noncollapsed setting. For every integer n ≥ 2 and every real K, every regular point of a noncollapsed \(\mathrm{RCD}(K,n)\) space has an open neighborhood bi-Lipschitz homeomorphic to an open subset of ℝn. The bi-Lipschitz constant depends only on n, and the neighborhood uses the restricted ambient distance.

tex.abstract:
We resolve the regular-point bi-Lipschitz conjecture in the noncollapsed
setting. For every integer \(n\ge2\) and every real \(K\), every regular
point of a noncollapsed \(\RCD(K,n)\) space has an open neighborhood
bi-Lipschitz homeomorphic to an open subset of \(\R^n\). The bi-Lipschitz
constant depends only on \(n\), and the neighborhood uses the restricted
ambient distance.
sections: Heat averages and cumulative matrix control
Renormalization in the space of coordinate values

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every integer \(n\ge2\) there is a constant \(L_n\ge1\) with
the following property. Let \(K\in\R\), and let
\((X,d,\mathcal H_d^n)\) be a noncollapsed \(\RCD(K,n)\) space.
Let \(p\in X\).
If every pointed Gromov--Hausdorff tangent of \(X\) at \(p\) is
pointed-isometric to \((\R^n,|\cdot|,0)\), then there exist an open
neighborhood \(U\) of \(p\), an open set \(V\subset\R^n\), and a
homeomorphism \(F:U\to V\) such that
\[
 L_n^{-1}d(x,z)\le |F(x)-F(z)|\le L_nd(x,z)
 \qquad (x,z\in U).
\]
The distance on the left and right is the original distance \(d\)
restricted to \(U\).

statements.label: cor:full-measure-atlas
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, there is an open set
\(\mathcal U\subset X\) containing every \(n\)-regular point, with
\(\mathcal H_d^n(X\setminus\mathcal U)=0\), and a countable atlas
of \(L_n\)-bi-Lipschitz charts from ambient-open subsets of
\(\mathcal U\) onto open subsets of \(\R^n\). Each chart uses the
restricted ambient distance, and its transition maps are
\(L_n^2\)-bi-Lipschitz.

statements.title: Summable directional pinching
statements.label: pi:directional-pinching
statements.text:
For every fixed $L,C_{\mathrm{sep}}>1$, the functions $E_i$ may be chosen
as in \eqref{pi:definition-E}, with the uniform summability and
positive floors in \eqref{pi:pinching-summability}, so that the
following holds for all sufficiently late spaces.  Define
\[
 D_{i,y}=R_i(y)^{-1}
       \bigl[r_i^{2-n}M(u)(B_{Lr_i}(y))\bigr]R_i(y)^{-1}.
\]
For every configuration \eqref{pi:center-configuration},
\begin{equation}
 D_{i,y}[u(x)-u(z)]
 \le Cr_i^2\bigl(E_i(x)+E_i(z)\bigr).
 
\end{equation}
The same functions work simultaneously for all such centers and
all dyadic scales.  All enlargement constants are fixed before
choosing the late-space threshold.

statements.title: Uniform metric and jet bounds
statements.label: re:metric-iteration
statements.text:
There are fixed $A,B$ and a sufficiently small flatness threshold
such that the maps~\eqref{re:iteration} are smooth on all of $\Omega$
for every finite $i$, their Jacobians are invertible there, and
\eqref{re:metric-bootstrap}--\eqref{re:jet-bootstrap} hold for all
$x\in B_1(p)$ and every $i$.
statements.section_title: Renormalization in the space of coordinate values

statements.title: The limiting chart
statements.label: re:limit-chart
statements.text:
For sufficiently flat data in the preceding construction, there is
$\rho>0$ such that the uniform limit
\[
 F(x)=\lim_{i\to\infty}h_i(u(x)),\qquad x\in B_1(p),
\]
restricts to a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism from $B_\rho(p)$ onto an
open subset of $\R^n$.  Its distance comparisons use the ambient
distance $d$ restricted to $B_\rho(p)$.

title: Bloch’s conjecture for surfaces with p_g=0
abstract: We prove Bloch's conjecture for smooth connected projective complex surfaces with \(p_g=0\): the Albanese homomorphism on integral degree-zero zero-cycles is an isomorphism.

tex.abstract:
We prove Bloch's conjecture for smooth connected projective complex
surfaces with \(p_g=0\): the Albanese homomorphism on integral
degree-zero zero-cycles is an isomorphism.
sections: Fixed virtual classes and the divisor cosection
A Chow relation and its universal diagonal coefficient
Nonvanishing when the minimal intersection lattice has rank at least two
The integral conclusion and motivic consequences

statements.label: thm:bloch
statements.text:
Let \(S\) be a smooth connected projective surface over \(\mathbb C\)
with \(p_g(S)=q(S)=0\). Then
\[
\deg:\CH_0(S)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z
\]
is an isomorphism, where \(\CH_0(S)\) has integral coefficients.

statements.title: Bloch's conjecture for surfaces with \(p_g=0\)
statements.label: cor:bloch-pg-zero
statements.text:
Let \(S\) be a smooth connected projective surface over \(\mathbb C\)
with \(p_g(S)=0\). Then the Albanese homomorphism
\[
\operatorname{alb}_S:\CH_0(S)^0\longrightarrow\Alb(S)(\mathbb C)
\]
is an isomorphism of abelian groups, where \(\CH_0(S)\) has integral
coefficients.

statements.title: Motivic consequences
statements.label: cor:tate-motives
statements.text:
Let \(S\) be a smooth connected projective surface over \(\mathbb C\)
with \(p_g(S)=0\). Then \(h(S)_{\mathbb Q}\) is finite-dimensional in
the sense of Kimura and \(t_2(S)=0\).

If, in addition, \(q(S)=0\), then
\[
h(S)_{\mathbb Q}\simeq
\mathbf 1\oplus\mathbb L^{\oplus b_2(S)}\oplus\mathbb L^2.
\]
In this case, for every \(m,n\ge0\), the rational Chow motives of the
power \(S^m\) and the Hilbert scheme \(S^{[n]}\) of length-\(n\)
zero-dimensional subschemes are pure Tate, with
\(S^0=S^{[0]}=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C\).
For \(Y=S^m\) or \(Y=S^{[n]}\), the rational cycle-class maps satisfy
\[
\operatorname{cl}_Y^i:\CH^i(Y)_{\mathbb Q}
 \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}H^{2i}(Y,\mathbb Q),
\qquad H^{2i+1}(Y,\mathbb Q)=0
\quad\text{for every }i\ge0.
\]

statements.label: prop:reduction
statements.text:
To prove Theorem~\ref{thm:bloch} with rational coefficients, it is
enough to prove it for smooth minimal surfaces \(X_0\) of general
type with \(p_g=q=0\). For such a surface, putting
\(k_0=K_{X_0}^2\), one has
\begin{equation}
1\le k_0\le9,\qquad
\chi(\mathcal O_{X_0})=1,\qquad
\int_{X_0}c_2(X_0)=12-k_0,\qquad b_2(X_0)=10-k_0.
\end{equation}
It is also enough to prove the assertion on any chosen sequence of
point blowups of each such \(X_0\).

statements.title: The determinant-fixed Quot theory
statements.label: prop:quot-pot

statements.title: The actual fixed obstruction theory
statements.label: prop:fixed-pot
prop:fixed-pg0
statements.text:
Assume \(p_g=q=0\).  A nonempty fixed part with lines \(T,H\)
and lengths satisfying \eqref{eq:length} is the smooth product
\[
 W=|T|\times|H|\times X^{[n_1]}\times X^{[n_2]}.
\]
Let \(x_i=c_1(\mathcal O_{|D_i|}(1))\), with \(D_1=T,D_2=H\).
The fixed virtual class is
\begin{equation}
 [W]^\vir=
 \prod_{i=1}^2\bigl(x_i^{h^1(D_i)}\eu(F_i)\bigr)\cap[W],
 \qquad
 F_i=\bigl((K-D_i)^{[n_i]}\bigr)^\vee\otimes\mathcal O(1_i).
\end{equation}
A part with either \(m_T<0\) or \(m_H<0\) contributes zero.
For the other parts, after including \(\eu(F_1)\eu(F_2)\),
pushforward over the linear systems is coefficient extraction at
\([x_1^{m_T}x_2^{m_H}]\).
statements.section_title: Fixed virtual classes and the divisor cosection

statements.label: prop:fixed-auxiliary
statements.text:
Assume \(p_g=q=1\), \(K\) ample, and \(D=3K\).
Every fixed contribution vanishes except those obtained
from a low divisor equal to the empty divisor or to the
canonical divisor.  In either surviving case the
contribution is computed on the actual fiber
\[
 |D_a|\times X^{[n_a]}\times X^{[n_b]},
\]
with the factors \(\eu(F_a)\eu(F_b)\).
The low hyperplane is \(x_b=0\) and \(m_{D_b}=0\);
pushforward over \(|D_a|\) is extraction at
\(x_a^{m_{D_a}}\).
The overall multiplier is \(1\) for the empty divisor and
\(-s\), with the same \(s>0\) as in
\eqref{eq:canonical-cycle}, for the canonical divisor.
The statement applies to operational insertions in
universal perfect complexes, also after adjoining marked
surface factors.
statements.section_title: Fixed virtual classes and the divisor cosection

statements.title: Chow universality of a fiber contribution
statements.label: prop:universal
statements.text:
The class in~\eqref{rel:fiber-contribution} admits a decomposition
\begin{equation}
 C_*(T,H;n_1,n_2)=c_*[\Delta_X]+\Gamma_*,
 \qquad
 \Gamma_*\in\sum_{a+b=2}R_X^a\boxtimes R_X^b.
 
\end{equation}
One can choose $c_*$ by a fixed universal rule.  Besides the integer
parameters and the chosen weights, this rule depends only on
\begin{equation}
 \int_X c_2(T_X),\qquad
 \int_X UV\quad
 (U,V\in\{K,L_1,L_2,T,H\}).
 
\end{equation}
It gives $c_*=0$ when $n_1=n_2=0$.  The same rule applies on every
smooth projective surface with the same data and $\chi(\mathcal O_X)=1$,
whether or not the lines $T,H$ are effective; effectivity is needed
only for realizing the formula as a fixed contribution.
statements.section_title: A Chow relation and its universal diagonal coefficient

statements.title: Chow relation
statements.label: thm:chow-relation
statements.text:
For either surface setting, and any $p\geq0$ with $v>p+2$, sum the
classes~\eqref{rel:fiber-contribution} with the following multiplicities:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item If $p_g=q=0$, sum over the effective ordered line pairs $T+H=D$
 and nonnegative point lengths satisfying~\eqref{eq:length}, with
 $m_T,m_H\geq0$.  Each fixed part has multiplier $1$.
 \item In the auxiliary setting, $D=3K$.  Sum over the ordered pairs
 $(3K,0),(0,3K)$ with multiplier $1$, and $(2K,K),(K,2K)$ with
 multiplier $-s$, with the admissible point lengths.  Here $s>0$ is
 the canonical-divisor coefficient of~\eqref{eq:canonical-cycle}.
\end{enumerate}
All sums are finite.  Writing $c$ for the same weighted sum of the
coefficients chosen in Proposition~\ref{prop:universal}, one obtains
\begin{equation}
 0=c[\Delta_X]+\Gamma
 \qquad\text{in }\CH^2(X\times X),
 
\end{equation}
where $\Gamma$ is a sum of external products of total codimension two.
statements.section_title: A Chow relation and its universal diagonal coefficient

statements.label: rel:correspondence
statements.text:
If $p_g=q=0$ and the coefficient $c$ in
\eqref{rel:chow-identity} is nonzero, then
$\CH_0(X)^0\otimes\mathbb Q=0$.
statements.section_title: A Chow relation and its universal diagonal coefficient

statements.label: prop:nonrank
statements.text:
Suppose $1\leq k_0\leq8$.  Blow up
\[
 e=\max\{k_0-5,0\}
\]
distinct points of $X_0$, and call the resulting surface $X$.
There are choices of $L_1,L_2,D,n,p$ on $X$ for which
Theorem~\ref{thm:chow-relation} gives a relation with $c>0$.
Consequently the degree map on $\CH_0(X_0)_{\mathbb Q}$ is an isomorphism.
statements.section_title: Nonvanishing when the minimal intersection lattice has rank at least two

statements.label: prop:rankone
statements.text:
Let $X$ be a smooth minimal projective complex surface of general type
with $p_g(X)=q(X)=0$ and $K_X^2=9$.  Take
\begin{equation}
 L_1=L_2=0,\qquad D=3K_X,\qquad n=20,\qquad p=7.
\end{equation}
The coefficient $c$ in the Chow relation of
Theorem~\ref{thm:chow-relation} is strictly positive.

title: Bloch's Law for Finite-Range Heisenberg Ferromagnets in Three Dimensions
abstract: We prove Bloch's T3/2 law for the spontaneous magnetization of three-dimensional quantum Heisenberg ferromagnets at every fixed positive quantum spin. The result holds for every nonnegative symmetric finite-range interaction whose support generates ℤ3, including spatially anisotropic couplings. The leading magnetization deficit has the exact coefficient determined by the determinant of the quadratic one-magnon dispersion. The thermodynamic limit is taken before the right field derivative at zero, and the low-temperature limit is taken last.

tex.abstract:
We prove Bloch's $T^{3/2}$ law for the spontaneous magnetization of
three-dimensional quantum Heisenberg ferromagnets at every fixed positive
quantum spin. The result holds for every nonnegative symmetric finite-range
interaction whose support generates $\Z^3$, including spatially anisotropic
couplings. The leading magnetization deficit has the exact coefficient
determined by the determinant of the quadratic one-magnon dispersion.
The thermodynamic limit is taken before the right field derivative at zero,
and the low-temperature limit is taken last.
