title: Finite congruence lattices: characterization and undecidability
abstract: We give an explicit colored-graph characterization of the finite nonempty lattices that occur as full congruence lattices of finite algebras, and prove that deciding this representation property is undecidable. In particular, the finite lattice representation problem has a negative answer. We also prove that recognition of full subgroup intervals in finite groups is undecidable.

tex.abstract:
We give an explicit colored-graph characterization of the finite nonempty lattices
that occur as full congruence lattices of finite algebras, and prove that
deciding this representation property is undecidable. In particular, the
finite lattice representation problem has a negative answer. We also prove
that recognition of full subgroup intervals in finite groups is undecidable.
sections: Affine test lattices and almost simple intervals
Simultaneous path pruning and affine witness patterns
Pruning inside a high-rank classical ancestor
Protections and the length of high-type paths
Completion of the forward marker theorem
Weighted templates and simultaneous size readings
A uniform computable bound for weighted templates
A finite description of a minimum lattice

statements.label: m:main
statements.text:
The following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item A finite nonempty lattice is representable if and only if it satisfies
the finite colored-graph criterion in \Cref{f:criterion}.
For each candidate graph size the criterion is decidable by a finite test.
\item There is no deterministic Turing machine that, given the order table
of a finite nonempty lattice, always halts and decides \(\mathcal R(L)\).
\item There is a nonrepresentable finite lattice \(L_0\) of minimum
cardinality, specified by the finite formulas in \Cref{sec:minimum}.
Every finite lattice of smaller cardinality is representable, and
\(\lvert L_0\rvert>7\).
\item Given the order table of a finite nonempty lattice \(L\), it is
undecidable whether \(L\cong[H,G]\) for some finite group \(G\) and
subgroup \(H\le G\), where \([H,G]\) is the full subgroup interval.
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Graph criterion
statements.label: f:criterion
statements.text:
The lattice $L$ is the full congruence lattice of a finite algebra if and only
if there is an $L$-colored complete graph $(A,d)$ satisfying all three
conditions below.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If $p\ne q$, then $d(p,q)\ne0$, and
\[
 d(p,q)\le d(p,u)\vee d(u,q)\qquad(p,q,u\in A).
\]
\item Whenever $a\not\le b$ in $L$, there are vertices
$p,q$ with $d(p,q)\le a$ and $d(p,q)\not\le b$.
\item For every nonempty edge set $S$, vertices
$p,q$ satisfying $d(p,q)\le a_S$ lie in the same connected component of
$\Gamma_S$.
\end{enumerate}
For each fixed $|A|$, these conditions involve only lattice inequalities,
finite vertex labelings, and paths.

statements.title: Enumeration and bounds
statements.label: f:cor-witness-bound
statements.text:
Representability is semidecidable. Moreover, a total algorithm deciding
representability of finite lattice order tables exists if and only if there
is a total computable function $b:\mathbb N_{>0}\to\mathbb N_{>0}$ such that
every representable lattice $L$ has a graph witness in \Cref{f:criterion} with
at most $b(|L|)$ vertices.

statements.label: f:prop-l7-interval
statements.text:
With their usual subfield inclusion, the groups
\[
 H=\operatorname{PGL}_2(\mathbb F_2)
 \le G=\operatorname{PGL}_2(\mathbb F_{64})
\]
have subgroup interval $[H,G]\cong L_7$.

statements.label: f:small-lattices
statements.text: Every finite nonempty lattice of at most seven elements is representable.

statements.label: f:negative-family
statements.text:
There are choices of the finite parameters in \Cref{f:def-test-lattice} for
which the resulting finite lattice is not the congruence lattice of any
finite algebra.
statements.section_title: Affine test lattices and almost simple intervals

statements.title: Geometry of the test lattice
statements.label: f:prop-chart-properties
statements.text:
The construction in \Cref{f:def-test-lattice} gives a finite self-dual
lattice $L$. It is graded of length $n+2$, atomistic, coatomistic, and simple.
Any two charts intersect in a flat of each, of rank at most $m$, with the
same affine structure on the intersection. Within one chart the primal
join of two flats is their affine span if that span has dimension at most
$n$. Attachment preserves all old meets and joins. In particular, flats in
two distinct private charts attached at the same $W$, neither contained in
$W$, have no common proper primal upper bound. There are at least three
horizontal comparability components in the interior of $L$, each containing
a chain of distinct comparable interior elements.
statements.section_title: Affine test lattices and almost simple intervals

statements.title: Prepared reverse links
statements.label: f:prop-prepared-links
statements.text:
If $X$ is a nonempty flat of rank at most $m$ in a trunk chart, the reverse
ideal with top $X$, denoted $[0,X]$, is graded, atomistic, and coatomistic.
Its strict interior has at least two horizontal comparability components,
each containing comparable distinct elements. The following additional
properties hold for $L$ and for every such prepared link.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item Every bottom interval of length two is a diamond
$M_b$ with $b\ge3$ atoms, where $b-1\ge2$ is not a prime power.
\item In every interior component there is an
element $y$ two ranks below the interval's top whose upper interval is a
diamond with at least two middle elements.
\end{enumerate}
In addition, $L$ has the following separation property:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},resume]
\item For any atom $u$ and any proper upper bound
$\omega\ge u$, there is a rank-two element $z\ge u$ with
$z\not\le\omega$.
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: Affine test lattices and almost simple intervals

statements.label: f:prop-ordinary-interval
statements.text:
If the test lattice $L$ is representable by a finite algebra, it is
isomorphic to an ordinary subgroup interval of a finite group.
statements.section_title: Affine test lattices and almost simple intervals

statements.title: Normal supplements
statements.label: f:prop-monolith
statements.text:
Suppose $[H,G]$ is isomorphic either to $L$ or to a prepared reverse link.
After quotienting by $\operatorname{core}_G(H)$, every nontrivial normal
subgroup is supplemented by $H$. The quotient has a unique minimal normal
subgroup $M=S^s$, with $S$ nonabelian simple, and $H$ acts transitively on
its simple factors. Moreover $C_G(M)=1$ in the core quotient. In that
quotient the subgroup interval identifies with
\begin{equation}
 [P,S^s]^H,\qquad P=H\cap S^s,
\end{equation}
the $H$-invariant subgroups in this range, by intersection with $S^s$;
the inverse sends $Y$ to $HY$.
statements.section_title: Affine test lattices and almost simple intervals

statements.title: Cases for a prepared interval
statements.label: f:prop-interval-cases
statements.text:
Use the notation of \Cref{f:prop-monolith}, in the core quotient. Let
$\Lambda\le\operatorname{Aut}(S)$ be the image of a coordinate stabilizer
in $H$, and put $I=\Lambda\cap S$, identifying $S$ with its inner
automorphisms. The following are the only possibilities.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $c(P)=S^s$. All labels are subdirect. If the
interval represents the whole $L$, its opposite has an ordinary subgroup
representation with top-group order at most $|H|<|G|$.
\item $P=c(P)\ne1$. The interval is isomorphic to the
ordinary almost simple interval $[\Lambda,S\Lambda]$.
\item $P=1$ and $I=S$. Every nonbottom label is
subdirect, and the dual interval is the extension poset of
\Cref{f:lem-extension-description} with one artificial top adjoined.
\end{enumerate}
In particular the cases $P<c(P)<S^s$, $P=1$ with $I=1$, and $P=1$ with
$1<I<S$ are impossible.
statements.section_title: Affine test lattices and almost simple intervals

statements.title: Ordinary almost simple starting interval
statements.label: f:thm-almost-simple-reduction
statements.text:
If the test lattice $L$ is representable, then either the whole $L$ or a
prepared reverse link with top an initial trunk point has an ordinary
almost simple subgroup-interval representation. On the reverse side,
there are at least $D-1$ further generations of prepared stages starting
at that top. This conclusion uses only the field condition and
\eqref{f:eq-parameters}, independently of later choices of larger
parameters.
statements.section_title: Affine test lattices and almost simple intervals

statements.title: Finite schedule of simultaneous exclusions
statements.label: c:pruning-schedule
statements.text: Suppose that the local exclusions below prohibit their prescribed failed patterns with absolute case and chart-loss bounds. For a bounded path length, finitely many rounds then produce a flat of final increment \(r\) such that the subgroup label of every proper extension in it is contained in none of the prescribed proper full stabilizers relative to any high-type ancestor. The next local simple has the corresponding transitivity or full-spanning properties relative to all those ancestors.
statements.section_title: Simultaneous path pruning and affine witness patterns

statements.title: Order of the finite parameter choices
statements.label: c:parameter-order
statements.text: The test-lattice parameters can be chosen in an order that meets all the pattern requirements and all the later path requirements. In particular the initial height-dependent pattern requirement does not create a circular dependence between \(m,n,N\). Once the local group results are applied, these choices force either the bounded-type contradiction or a path longer than the protected-path bound.
statements.section_title: Simultaneous path pruning and affine witness patterns

statements.title: Linear subspaces, signed flags and idempotents
statements.label: c:linear-subspaces
statements.text: In linear type, the initial round excludes stabilizers of proper nonzero subspaces when there are no anti-actions. In the presence of anti-actions it excludes signed flags \(0<I\le J<V\) and individual proper nontrivial idempotents. These exclusions require no prior anchor and make the collineation part of every subsequent good group irreducible.
statements.section_title: Pruning inside a high-rank classical ancestor

statements.title: Singular and nondegenerate subspaces
statements.label: c:isometry-subspaces
statements.text: In isometry type, the initial round excludes stabilizers of nonzero totally singular subspaces, proper nonzero nondegenerate subspaces, and nonsingular radical lines in orthogonal characteristic two. It requires no prior anchor. The resulting good groups act irreducibly by semilinear transformations.
statements.section_title: Pruning inside a high-rank classical ancestor

statements.title: Completion of direct-system pruning
statements.label: c:direct-pruning
statements.text: The remaining direct systems are excluded, both when their supported normal product is retained and when it is missing. The bounds are absolute, independently of the ground field and natural degree.
statements.section_title: Pruning inside a high-rank classical ancestor

statements.title: Prime-degree field algebras in linear type
statements.label: c:linear-fields
statements.text: After the direct-system exclusions, the full normalizers of field algebras \(D/F\) of prime relative degree are excluded in linear type, including when the ambient group contains anti-actions.
statements.section_title: Pruning inside a high-rank classical ancestor

statements.title: Ordered factors in linear type
statements.label: c:linear-factors
statements.text: After \Cref{c:linear-fields}, the full stabilizers of proper nonscalar ordered central simple factors are excluded in linear type.
statements.section_title: Pruning inside a high-rank classical ancestor

statements.title: Ordered factors apart from two retained plane types
statements.label: c:partial-isometry-factors
statements.text: In isometry type, after the direct-system exclusions, the full stabilizers of ordered proper nonscalar selfadjoint central simple factors are excluded except possibly when the retained support is an odd-characteristic bilinear orthogonal plane or a symplectic plane over \(\mathbb F_2\). These exceptions concern the retained side of the ordered factorization.
statements.section_title: Pruning inside a high-rank classical ancestor

statements.title: Prime-degree selfadjoint fields
statements.label: c:isometry-fields
statements.text: After direct-system pruning and the partial ordered-factor exclusion of \Cref{c:partial-isometry-factors}, the full stabilizers of selfadjoint field algebras of prime relative degree are excluded. The pattern is colored by whether the adjoint restriction on the field is the identity.
statements.section_title: Pruning inside a high-rank classical ancestor

statements.title: Completion of the algebra exclusions
statements.label: c:remaining-factors
statements.text: After \Cref{c:isometry-fields}, the full stabilizers of unordered proper idempotent pairs \(e,e^*=1-e\) are excluded. The two remaining retained-plane types in \Cref{c:partial-isometry-factors} are then impossible, completing the ordered-factor exclusions.
statements.section_title: Pruning inside a high-rank classical ancestor

statements.title: Elementary abelian normalizers
statements.label: c:elementary-normalizers
statements.text: Under the full-spanning conclusion of \Cref{c:full-spanning}, full normalizers of nontrivial elementary abelian subgroups of \(S\) are excluded.
statements.section_title: Pruning inside a high-rank classical ancestor

statements.title: Completion of tensor-system pruning
statements.label: c:tensor-pruning
statements.text: The missing tensor systems of \Cref{c:tensor-products} are excluded by an absolute bound on the possible invariant partitions of their common fine slots. Hence all tensor systems are excluded.
statements.section_title: Pruning inside a high-rank classical ancestor

statements.title: The next classical-ancestor socle
statements.label: c:classical-conclusion
statements.text:
Let \(K\) be a tested descendant with a prepared interval, good for all the exclusions in this section, or containing the final good anchor. There is an actual nonabelian simple subgroup \(B\trianglelefteq K\) inside the ancestor socle \(S\), with full natural spanning, such that
\[
 HB=K,\qquad C_K(B)\le\operatorname{core}_K H,
\]
and \(C_K(B)\) is soluble. The quotient by this centralizer is almost simple with socle \(B\), and the exact subgroup interval is preserved.
statements.section_title: Pruning inside a high-rank classical ancestor

statements.title: Subsets and equal-block partitions
statements.label: c:alternating-primitivity
statements.text: In the prepared alternating configuration, full stabilizers of proper nonempty subsets and nontrivial equal-block-size partitions are excluded. Subsequent good anchors are primitive.

statements.title: Elementary abelian regular groups
statements.label: c:alternating-affine
statements.text: For a primitive previously good anchor, normalizers of elementary abelian regular groups are excluded.

statements.title: Completion of Cartesian pruning
statements.label: c:cartesian-pruning
statements.text: Missing Cartesian labels are excluded. Together with \Cref{c:cartesian-retained}, this excludes all nontrivial Cartesian decompositions.

statements.title: Diagonal normalizers
statements.label: c:diagonal-pruning
statements.text: Under the successively primitive, non-affine and non-Cartesian anchor hypotheses, the full normalizers of the groups \(Y\) in \Cref{c:primitive-diagonal} are excluded. Both retained and missing normal powers are covered.

statements.title: The next alternating-ancestor socle
statements.label: c:alternating-conclusion
statements.text: After the exclusions, every tested descendant with its prepared interval is primitive almost simple. Its actual simple socle is transitive, lies in \(A_v\), and is supplemented by \(H\).

statements.title: Sufficiently general finite subgroups
statements.label: w:lp
statements.text:
For the fixed finite list of simple adjoint types, there is a uniform degree bound $d_0$ with the following property. If a finite subgroup $\Gamma\le G(k)$, where $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_p$, is contained in no proper closed subset of equation complexity at most $d_0$, then there is a Steinberg map $\Psi$ such that
\[
 (G^\Psi)'\le\Gamma\le G^\Psi.
\]
Here the degree bound follows from the uniform constructible-family
formulation of the sufficiently-general subgroup theorem of
Larsen--Pink \citep[Theorem~0.5 and Metadefinition~2.2]{LarsenPink2011}:
the exceptional family has uniformly bounded defining equations in
the fixed affine models.

statements.title: No bounded-type parent with a stage remaining
statements.label: w:bounded-exclusion
statements.text: Fix the finite list of bounded root systems. There is a fixed trial increment $t$ such that a prepared current parent with a remaining private-chart stage cannot have socle of one of these types, provided the residual interval length is sufficiently large. All choices are uniform in the characteristic and parameter.

statements.title: Counting prime tensor coarsenings
statements.label: w:coarsening-count
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses of \Cref{w:atom-cycle}, each prime $s\mid t(B)$ defines a canonical congruence coarsening $\mathcal P_s$ into $s$ matrix factors, normalized by the candidate label. Its full stabilizer in the ancestor is proper. There is an absolute constant $c_1$ such that
\[
 \#\{s:s\text{ is prime and }s\mid t(B)\}
 \le \operatorname{ht}[K_{\rm cand},K_{W_i}]+c_1.
\]
The height is taken in the actual subgroup interval, or equivalently in its prepared ancestor quotient.
statements.section_title: Protections and the length of high-type paths

statements.title: Counting fixing prime roots
statements.label: w:root-count
statements.text:
Let $B$ be as in \Cref{w:atom-cycle}, in the high classical ancestor with adjoint group $G_i$ and ordinary Steinberg map $\Phi_i$ of height $f_i$. Consider pairs $(s,\Theta)$ where $s$ is prime,
\[
 \Theta^s=\Phi_i,
 \qquad \Theta|_B=1,
\]
and $\Theta$ belongs to the inner--diagram--Frobenius point-map group. The full normalizer labels of $S(\Theta)=(G_i^\Theta)'$ are proper, contain the candidate label, and number at most
\[
 2\operatorname{ht}[K_{\rm cand},K_{W_i}].
\]
There are at most two maps at each possible height, one for each diagram choice, and all such roots commute.
statements.section_title: Protections and the length of high-type paths

statements.title: Equal natural modules force a fixing root
statements.label: w:natural-root
statements.text: Suppose $B<S_i$ is a same-series high classical candidate of the same natural dimension as $S_i$, and its projective action on $V_i$ is its own natural module, allowing a Frobenius twist and, in type A, a diagram natural/dual twist. Then some prime root of $\Phi_i$ fixes $B$ pointwise. Thus the absence of such fixing roots excludes this case.
statements.section_title: Protections and the length of high-type paths

statements.title: Selecting all ancestor protections
statements.label: w:selection
statements.text: Assume that the current same-characteristic classical run is already protected through its current node $W$. Fix an upper bound $D$ on the number of path steps and a fixed number $c$ of continuation colors. There is a finite extension rank $r$, depending only on $D,c$ and earlier fixed requirements, such that from every suitably pruned private chart at a current high classical node one can select a next proper extension. If that extension continues the current same-characteristic run, it has both protections relative to every ancestor in that run, including the current node. Earlier structural exclusions are preserved.
statements.section_title: Protections and the length of high-type paths

statements.title: Composing the rational highest-weight actions
statements.label: w:rational-composition
statements.text:
Let $i<j<l$ lie in one protected run, and suppose these three nodes have the same series A, B, C, or D. Use consistent natural realizations and simply connected covers of the actual nested simple subgroups. Write $G_s=\widehat G_j$ and $J=\widehat G_l$. The lifted edge representations $ij$ and $jl$ have highest weights
\[
 p^x\lambda,\qquad p^y\eta,
\]
where $\lambda,\eta\ne0$ are $p$-restricted. The latter representation induces an algebraic homomorphism $J\to (G_s)_{\rm ad}$ which lifts to $J\to G_s$. The resulting rational composition of $L_{G_s}(p^x\lambda)$ is irreducible. Its highest weight $\mu$ is one nonzero $p$-digit times a power of $p$, and that digit has the shape, up to diagram, of the direct edge $il$.
statements.section_title: Protections and the length of high-type paths

statements.title: No homogeneous type A configuration
statements.label: w:a-obstruction
statements.text: Four nodes of a protected run of type A cannot have all pair edges of one color in the preceding palette.
statements.section_title: Protections and the length of high-type paths

statements.title: No homogeneous signed configuration
statements.label: w:signed-obstruction
statements.text: Four nodes of a protected run having one fixed series B, C, or D cannot have all pair edges of one color in the preceding palette.
statements.section_title: Protections and the length of high-type paths

statements.title: Bound on protected high-type paths
statements.label: w:path-bound
statements.text: There is an absolute constant $D_0$ such that a prepared path all of whose socles are of high alternating or high classical type, and whose consecutive same-characteristic classical runs are protected, has fewer than $D_0$ nodes. This constant is independent of all chart dimensions, finite fields, and path-construction parameters.
statements.section_title: Protections and the length of high-type paths

statements.title: Reverse alternating exclusion
statements.label: r:reverse-exclusion
statements.text:
For all sufficiently large integers $v$, the lattice
$\operatorname{Sub}(A_v)^{\mathrm{op}}$ has no exact realization as
\[
 [P,S^b]^\Delta,
\]
where $S$ is nonabelian simple, $\Delta$ acts by automorphisms transitively
on the $b$ simple factors, $P$ is a $\Delta$-invariant coordinate product,
and either $P\ne1$ or $b=1$.

statements.title: Forward marker theorem
statements.label: r:forward-marker
statements.text:
For every nonnegative integer $m$, there are integers $a(m)$ and
$t_0(m)$ such that the following holds whenever $|T|\ge t_0(m)$.
Every exact forward realization
\[
 F_T=[P,S^b]^\Delta
\]
with $S$ nonabelian simple, $\Delta$ transitive on the factors,
and invariant coordinate product $P\ne1$ (or $b=1$), has the
following configuration in the ordinary site interval of
\Cref{r:marker-site}.  There is $A\subset T$ with $|A|\le a(m)$
such that $K_{M_A}$ has an actual high-degree alternating simple
normal subgroup $B_A\le S$ satisfying
\[
 HB_A=K_{M_A},\qquad
 C_{K_{M_A}}(B_A)\le H,
 \qquad C_{K_{M_A}}(B_A)\text{ is soluble}.
\]
In the almost simple quotient
$K_{M_A}/C_{K_{M_A}}(B_A)$, at least $m$ distinct labels
$M_{A\cup\{i\}}$, with fresh indices $i\in T\setminus A$,
are full stabilizers of individual points in the natural
alternating action.  The constants $a(m)$ and $t_0(m)$ are independent
of $S,b,\Delta,P$ and the realization; the high-degree threshold is
the fixed one used in the structural exclusions.

statements.title: Subset stabilizers produce points
statements.label: fa:subset-points
statements.text:
If a tested descendant is contained in a proper subset stabilizer, then, after the finite selections of
\Cref{fa:all-ancestors}, there are arbitrarily many distinct relative labels \(M_{\{i\}}\) that are full
stabilizers of individual natural points.  In absolute notation these are \(M_{A\cup\{i\}}\).
Consequently, in the absence of the conclusion of \Cref{r:forward-marker}, the required descendants and
their bounded intersections are transitive.

statements.title: Exclusion of affine and Cartesian structures
statements.label: fa:cartesian-exclusion
statements.text:
After \Cref{fa:imprimitive-exclusion}, the tested descendants are primitive.  They cannot lie in full
normalizers of elementary abelian regular groups or in proper Cartesian-system stabilizers.

statements.title: Maximality of an unbalanced ordered splitting
statements.label: fa:projector-maximal
statements.text:
Let \(V=W\oplus U\), with \(0<\dim U<\dim W\), be a nondegenerate splitting in an isometry type, or an
image--kernel splitting in linear type with anti-actions.  Let \(M\) be a group of the corresponding
classical actions containing the natural special group, and let \(K\) be the full ordered splitting
stabilizer, equivalently the idempotent stabilizer for the ring action.  Assume that \(K\) supplements
the special group in \(M\), that its collineations act semilinearly irreducibly on \(U\), and that the
supported special group on \(W\) is available, as is that on \(U\) when \(\dim U\) is large.  In the
linear case assume also that \(K\) contains an anti-action fixing the projector, hence carrying its
image--kernel data into the dual annihilator data.  For sufficiently large \(\dim W\), the subgroup \(K\)
is maximal in \(M\).

statements.title: Exclusion of proper projectors
statements.label: fa:projector-exclusion
statements.text:
Under the preceding classical rounds, the tested descendants cannot lie in any of the proper stabilizers
considered in \Cref{fa:projector-orthogonal}.  The remaining descendants and the required bounded
intersections therefore have irreducible anchors; in linear type their collineation parts are also
irreducible.

statements.title: Exclusion of the remaining direct systems
statements.label: fa:direct-exclusion
statements.text:
After the preceding classical rounds, a homogeneous family of proper full direct-system stabilizers
cannot occur at the tested descendants.

statements.title: Maximality of an unequal ordered tensor factor
statements.label: fa:ordered-factor-maximal
statements.text:
Let \(S\) be a high-rank classical simple group on \(V\), and let an ordered proper matrix tensor factor
give natural dimensions \(x<y\), both sufficiently large.  In isometry type assume that the factor is
selfadjoint.  In characteristic two assume that the bilateral factor forms are alternating, and in
orthogonal type use the canonical tensor quadratic form.  Exclude symplectic type in characteristic two.
Then the full stabilizer in \(S\) of the ordered factor is maximal.

statements.title: Field and paired overgroups in the prepared configuration
statements.label: fb:field-pair-overgroups
statements.text:
Use the transferred forms of \Cref{sec:classical}.
Let \(D\subseteq\mathcal A\) be a field containing \(F\), with \([D:F]=n\), where \(n\) is prime or a
product of two distinct primes, and let \(m=v/n\) be sufficiently large.
In an isometry type assume that \(D\) is selfadjoint; in orthogonal
characteristic two assume the irreducible normalization already obtained in the
preceding rounds.  Omit symplectic characteristic two with nontrivial adjoint
on \(D\).

Alternatively, in an isometry type other than symplectic characteristic two,
let \(e,e^*=1-e\) be exchanged complementary idempotents, with totally
singular images when a quadratic form is present, and let \(m=v/2\) be
sufficiently large.  Suppose that the collineation action of each overgroup
under consideration is semilinearly irreducible, as ensured here by the
previous-good axis.

Every proper overgroup in \(M\) of the full field stabilizer preserves a
nontrivial subfield algebra of \(D\) over \(F\).  Every proper overgroup of
the full paired stabilizer preserves that pair.  Consequently a prime-degree
field stabilizer and an exchanged-pair stabilizer are maximal; for a
compositum of two prime degrees its maximal overgroups can only be the
stabilizers of its prime-degree subfields.
statements.section_title: Completion of the forward marker theorem

statements.title: Exclusion of two large ordered factors
statements.label: fb:both-high-factors
statements.text:
At the present forward-test stage, a homogeneous family of failures preserving
proper ordered matrix tensor factorizations cannot have both factor degrees
above the fixed large-degree threshold.  In isometry types the factors are
selfadjoint and have the normalized factor forms.
statements.section_title: Completion of the forward marker theorem

statements.title: Exclusion of fields, pairs, and nuisance planes
statements.label: fb:field-pair-exclusion
statements.section_title: Completion of the forward marker theorem

statements.title: Exclusion of permuted tensor systems
statements.label: fb:permuted-tensors
statements.text:
After the preceding rounds, neither a full-algebra elementary abelian
normalizer nor a nontrivial permuted tensor-system stabilizer can be a failure
label in the forward test.
statements.section_title: Completion of the forward marker theorem

statements.title: Grounding at bounded omissions
statements.label: fb:grounding
statements.text:
After the prescribed rounds, every tested descendant has an actual nested
normal simple supplement with soluble centralizer in the base.  Relative to a
high classical ancestor it is absolutely irreducible and avoids all the
excluded tensor structures.  Relative to an alternating ancestor it is
primitive and transitive unless the desired point configuration has already
been obtained.  Its simple type can be required to exceed any fixed bounded
order or bounded-rank threshold.

The same actual normal simplicity and full spanning apply to a label above a
previous-good axis and below the ancestor when it has the indicated
nonabelian part: either a contained perfect simple group as used here, or its
own pure link satisfying the normal test.  In the first case that perfect
group lies in the resulting normal simple.
statements.section_title: Completion of the forward marker theorem

statements.title: Singleton tensor failures
statements.label: fb:singleton-tensors
statements.text:
The singleton coatom witnesses in \Cref{fb:protection-count} cannot be
prime tensor-coarsening stabilizers.
statements.section_title: Completion of the forward marker theorem

statements.title: Completion of the forward marker argument
statements.label: fb:forward-completion
statements.text:
The forward marker assertion of \Cref{r:forward-marker} holds.  In the
prepared configuration, the assumption of no point success at all the
prescribed bounded prefixes is impossible once the initial marker set is
sufficiently large.
statements.section_title: Completion of the forward marker theorem

statements.title: From algebras to ordinary intervals
statements.label: t:weighted-algebra
statements.text:
Every nilpotent join-preserving deflation of \(\bar F\) is zero.
If some nontrivial image of \(F\) is the congruence lattice of a finite algebra
of size \(m\), there is an ordinary finite-group interval representing the
dual of a nontrivial image of \(F\), whose top group has order at most
\(60^m m!\).  The full lattice \(F\) itself has a finite algebra representation.
statements.section_title: Weighted templates and simultaneous size readings

statements.title: Normal endpoint property for weighted images
statements.label: t:weighted-normal
statements.text:
For sufficiently large absolute cohort stock, every ordinary interval
representing a nontrivial weighted image, in either orientation, satisfies
\((*)\).  Its base acts transitively on the simple factors of its monolith
modulo the base core.  The same assertion holds for the bounded axis deletions
used here, provided the remaining stock is sufficient.
statements.section_title: Weighted templates and simultaneous size readings

statements.title: Forward proper projections
statements.label: t:weighted-forward-projections
statements.text:
In a forward realization \([P,\mathcal W]^H\), suppose \(P>1\) and
\(c(P)<\mathcal W\).  Every cut coatom is a product label.  If
\(P<c(P)\), its closure label has empty footprint and lies below \(J^*\).
statements.section_title: Weighted templates and simultaneous size readings

statements.title: Reverse projections and the trivial-base cases
statements.label: t:weighted-reverse-projections
statements.text:
In reverse orientation, if \(P>1\), then \(c(P)=\mathcal W\).
If \(P=1\), every nonidentity actual label is subdirect and the site-action
image \(\Lambda\) contains the inner automorphisms of \(S\).
In forward orientation with \(P=1\), either a marker axis filter gives
product success, or the same subdirectness and inner-action conclusions hold.
statements.section_title: Weighted templates and simultaneous size readings

statements.title: Product success with absolute stock
statements.label: t:weighted-product-success
statements.text:
There are absolute stock and marker-loss bounds with the following
property.  Any ordinary realization, in either orientation, of a nontrivial
weighted image yields a forward realization of a nontrivial image of the
weighted template with at most boundedly many markers deleted, in which
product success holds.  The stock bound is independent of all numerical
unit sizes and of the number of cohorts.  The simple group at a site has
order at most the original top-group order.  A larger prescribed fixed
stock can be retained by increasing the initial absolute stock.
statements.section_title: Weighted templates and simultaneous size readings

statements.title: Common alignment of all cuts
statements.label: t:weighted-alignment
statements.text:
There is a single bijection from the formal units together with the
foundation position to the \(\Theta\)-orbits on \(\Omega\), under which
every cut and every intersection of cuts is the corresponding stabilizer
of unions of those orbits.  Write \(u_j>0\) for the size of the cell of unit
\(j\).  The specified genuine point markers have size one.
statements.section_title: Weighted templates and simultaneous size readings

statements.title: Equal totals and equal copies
statements.label: t:weighted-equal-totals
statements.text:
Let \(D,E\) be disjoint bounded collections of nonfoundation units with
equal formal total size, with ample spare markers outside them.  If at least
one of \(D,E\) contains more than one unit, then
\[
 \sum_{j\in D}u_j=\sum_{j\in E}u_j.
\]
In a sufficiently numerous cohort, all copies have the same actual cell
size.  In particular, all surviving markers have size one.
statements.section_title: Weighted templates and simultaneous size readings

statements.title: Reading a primary square
statements.label: t:weighted-square
statements.text:
For a primary square \(O\) and its full side reference \(R\), let
\(r=u_R\) in the alignment of \Cref{t:weighted-alignment}.  If \(r\) is even
and \(r\ge8\), then \(u_O=r^2\).
statements.section_title: Weighted templates and simultaneous size readings

statements.title: Weighted realization and simultaneous numerical readings
statements.label: t:weighted-realization
statements.text:
Fix any bounded support size for the comparisons and any desired fixed
number of spare copies.  There are absolute initial cohort-stock and
marker-loss bounds, independent of the numerical unit sizes and the number
of cohorts, with the following property.  The bounds may depend on the
fixed support and spare-copy requirements.  An ordinary realization of a
nontrivial weighted image, in either orientation and with top order \(M\),
gives a forward realization after at most that many marker deletions, with
all cuts product in an actual alternating power.  A single common cell
alignment gives positive sizes \(u_j\le M\), equal on each cohort and one
on all surviving markers.  In this same alignment the equal-total reading
of \Cref{t:weighted-equal-totals} and the square reading of
\Cref{t:weighted-square} hold.

If the input is a finite algebra of size \(m\) representing a nontrivial
image, the same conclusion holds with \(M=60^m m!\), for a possibly
different nontrivial image of the original template.  The full template
itself is finitely representable.
statements.section_title: Weighted templates and simultaneous size readings

statements.title: Rank-one overgroups
statements.label: n:rank-one
statements.text:
There are computable functions of $s$ that bound, for every rank-one
control $X$ of complexity at most $s$ on a finite nonempty set $I$,
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item the number of transitive groups $U$ with $X\le U\le S_I$ and
      the index $[U:\langle X^U\rangle]$;
\item the length of a generating list for $U$ over $X$, chosen so
      that every generator $g$ has a rank-one control of computably
      bounded complexity inside $X\cap gXg^{-1}$.
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: A uniform computable bound for weighted templates

statements.title: Overgroups of controls with private squares
statements.label: n:private-squares
statements.text:
There are computable functions $B(s),C(s)$ such that every control
$X$ with private squares of complexity at most $s$ on a finite
nonempty set $I$ has at most $B(s)$ transitive overgroups in $S_I$,
and every such overgroup $U$ satisfies
\[
 [U:\langle X^U\rangle]\le C(s).
\]
The functions can be taken nondecreasing and at least one.
statements.section_title: A uniform computable bound for weighted templates

statements.title: Uniform computable template bound
statements.label: n:template-bound
statements.text:
There is a total computable nondecreasing function
$\Phi:\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\to\mathbb Z_{\ge1}$ such that every weighted
template
\[
 F=[S_Z\times Y,S_{Z\sqcup(\bigcup T)}]
\]
of \Cref{sec:weighted}, with at most $t$ units, excluding
the foundation $Z$ from this count, and
$|Z|>|\bigcup T|$, satisfies $|F|\le\Phi(t)$.
The bound is independent of all full-unit sizes, square sides,
auxiliary axis lengths, offset sizes, and the size of $Z$.
No stock-size hypothesis is required for this counting assertion.
statements.section_title: A uniform computable bound for weighted templates

statements.title: Undecidability of finite representability
statements.label: n:undecidable
statements.text:
There is no algorithm which, given the tables of a finite
lattice, decides whether it is isomorphic to the congruence
lattice of a finite algebra.  Equivalently, there is no
total computable bound, in terms of lattice cardinality,
for the minimum carrier size among all representable
finite lattices.

statements.title: Undecidability of finite subgroup-interval recognition
statements.label: n:interval-undecidable
statements.text:
There is no deterministic Turing machine which, given the order table
of a finite nonempty lattice $L$, always halts and decides whether
$L\cong[H,G]$ for some finite group $G$ and subgroup $H\le G$, where
$[H,G]$ consists of every subgroup $K$ with $H\le K\le G$, ordered by
inclusion.  Equivalently, there is no total computable bound, in terms
of lattice cardinality, on the least possible order of the top group
$G$ among lattices admitting such a realization.

statements.title: Quantitative genericity
statements.label: q:genericity
statements.text:
Let $x\ge10^9$, and let $G$ be adjoint simple of rank at most $x$ over an
algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$.  If a finite subgroup
$\Gamma\le G$ is not contained in any proper closed subset of affine ring
format at most $J^{1000}(x)$, then there is a positive-height standard point
map $\Psi$ such that
\begin{equation}
                   (G^\Psi)'\le\Gamma\le G^\Psi.
\end{equation}
Proper closed subsets in this hypothesis need not be irreducible.

statements.title: Size ceiling
statements.label: q:size-ceiling
statements.text:
The negative affine-chart construction has a choice of finite parameters
for which its lattice $L$ is nonrepresentable and
\[
                              |L|<M_*.
\]
In particular a nonrepresentable lattice exists among the tables of
cardinality at most the ordinary computable integer $M_*$.

statements.title: Finite description of a minimum example
statements.label: q:minimum
statements.text:
The bounded formulas \eqref{q:selection-z}--\eqref{q:minimum-order},
with the ordinary unevaluated Busy Beaver constant
\eqref{q:BB-bound}, specify the full finite order table of a
nonrepresentable lattice $L_0$ of minimum cardinality.  Its cardinality
is the integer $a_0$ in \eqref{q:a0t0}, and
\[
                              7<a_0\le M_*.
\]
This is a finite order description and a proof of minimum cardinality;
it does not supply a numerically evaluated value of that cardinality.
statements.section_title: A finite description of a minimum lattice

title: Finite Instructions and Solenoidal Shear Flows
abstract: We realize finite reciprocal affine instruction maps by smooth incompressible shear flows on a flat three-torus. Applied to a reversible one-head recorder with a finite transition table, this gives a complete machine-to-fluid construction: a fixed particle enters a fixed open strip exactly when a given machine halts, with zero initial velocity, zero pressure, and a solenoidal mean-zero force that is periodic after initialization. The construction acts on full closed rectangles and controls every intermediate trajectory. Separate heights resolve overlap between sources and targets, and an endpoint-size estimate controls all excursions independently of the reciprocal scaling factor.

tex.abstract:
We realize finite reciprocal affine instruction maps by smooth incompressible
shear flows on a flat three-torus. Applied to a reversible one-head recorder
with a finite transition table, this gives a complete machine-to-fluid construction:
a fixed particle enters a fixed open strip exactly when a given machine halts,
with zero initial velocity, zero pressure, and a solenoidal mean-zero force
that is periodic after initialization. The construction acts on full closed
rectangles and controls every intermediate trajectory. Separate heights
resolve overlap between sources and targets, and an endpoint-size estimate
controls all excursions independently of the reciprocal scaling factor.

statements.title: Initialized computation by a solenoidal force
statements.label: thm:initialized
statements.text:
Fix a positive computable viscosity $\nu$ on the unit flat torus $\T^3$.
There is an algorithm taking a deterministic one-tape machine $M$ with head
moves in $\{-1,0,1\}$ and a finite input word $w$ to an effective smooth force
$f_{M,w}$ with these properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),itemsep=2pt]
\item The force is divergence free and has zero spatial mean. Equation
\eqref{eq:NS} has a global smooth solution $(u,p)=(U,0)$, unique in the
classical class just specified on every finite time interval.
\item All mixed derivatives of $U$ and $f_{M,w}$ are globally bounded, and
the kinetic energy is uniformly bounded. Both fields have period one for
$t\ge1$ and vanish on a neighborhood of every integer time. The period-one
mechanism after initialization depends on $M$ alone.
\item With fixed label $a_*=(1/8,3/8,1/2)$ and fixed open strip
$O=\{(x,y,z):1/2<x<1\}$, the trajectory enters $O$ at a finite time if and
only if $M$ halts on $w$, including an initially halted machine.
\end{enumerate}
For arbitrary fixed real $\nu>0$, the same formulas and conclusions hold;
the evaluation algorithm is then relative to that parameter.
statements.section_title: From finite instructions to a fluid experiment

statements.title: Reciprocal affine maps by shears
statements.label: thm:shears
statements.text:
For $1\le i\le N$, let $P_i,Q_i$ be closed axis-parallel rectangles with
rational endpoints and positive side lengths in the planar chart of
$\T_L^3$. Let their centers be $p_i,q_i$, and suppose
\[
 F_i(X)=q_i+\diag(\lambda_i,\lambda_i^{-1})(X-p_i),
 \quad F_i(P_i)=Q_i,
 \quad\lambda_i\in\Q_{>0}.
\]
Assume the following:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),nosep]
\item The $P_i$ are pairwise positively separated, and the $Q_i$ are
pairwise positively separated.
\item Every coordinate half-width of every $P_i$ and $Q_i$ is at most a
given rational $h>0$.
\item All $p_i,q_i$ belong to a closed rectangle $K$ with rational
endpoints, and $K+[-2h,2h]^2$ is compactly contained in the planar chart.
\item The coding height $z_0$ is rational and lies inside the vertical chart.
\end{enumerate}
There is an effectively constructed smooth velocity $V$ on
$\R\times\T_L^3$ with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*),itemsep=2pt]
\item It is one-periodic in time and vanishes near every integer time.
Every mixed space and time derivative has an effective uniform bound.
\item $\divg V=0$, $\int_{\T_L^3}V=0$, and $(V\cdot\nabla)V=0$.
\item Its period map is $(X,z)\mapsto(F_i(X),z)$ on an effectively
specified positive neighborhood of each $P_i\times\{z_0\}$.
\item Starting from $(X,z_0)$ with $X\in P_i$, the four scaling stages
stay within horizontal sup distance $2h$ of $p_i$. The next stage follows
$((1-\theta)p_i+\theta q_i)+d$, where $0\le\theta\le1$ and
$|d|_\infty\le h$. The lifting and lowering stages leave $X$ unchanged.
\item For each fixed positive computable $\nu$, the force
$f=\partial_tV-\nu\Delta V$ is smooth, mean zero, and solenoidal, with
period one and bounded mixed derivatives. Equation~\eqref{eq:NS} from
zero initial velocity has the solution $(u,p)=(V,0)$, with uniformly
bounded kinetic energy. This solution is unique among spatially periodic
classical solutions for which $u$, its spatial derivatives through order
two, $u_t$, $p$, and $\nabla p$ are continuous on each finite closed time
cylinder, and $p$ has zero spatial mean at each time.
\end{enumerate}
No separation between a source and a target is required. For $N=0$ the
zero velocity has all the asserted properties, with no branch conditions.

statements.label: cor:observer
statements.text:
Under Theorem~\ref{thm:shears}, suppose a branch satisfies
$p_{i,1},q_{i,1}\le a$. Every point starting in $P_i\times\{z_0\}$
has first coordinate at most $a+2h$ throughout the period. If instead
both centers are at least $a$, its first coordinate is at least $a-2h$.
If $\mathcal O\subseteq\T_L^3$ is open and
$Q_i\times\{z_0\}\subseteq\mathcal O$, every point starting in
$P_i\times\{z_0\}$ reaches $\mathcal O$ at the integer sample and
remains there for a time interval.

title: Finite Monoid Computations and a Uniform Generalized Star-Height Bound
abstract: Every regular language over a finite alphabet has a generalized regular expression of star height at most thirteen over that same alphabet. We prove this uniform bound by representing finite monoid computations as affine updates and recovering them through twelve successive split constructions.

tex.abstract:
Every regular language over a finite alphabet has a generalized regular
expression of star height at most thirteen over that same alphabet.
We prove this uniform bound by representing finite monoid computations as
affine updates and recovering them through twelve successive split
constructions.
sections: Two outer splits and five residual witnesses
Aligned splits for the residual witnesses
Expressions, the final suffix, and the uniform bound

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every finite alphabet \(\Sigma\) and every regular language
\(L\subseteq\Sigma^*\),
\[
                         h_\Sigma(L)\le 13.
\]

statements.label: prop:parameters
statements.text:
For every fixed nonempty finite alphabet, finite monoid \(M\), and
finite representation space \(V\), all parameters in the two outer
splits and the five aligned stages can be chosen to satisfy their
stated hypotheses. More precisely, the stencils are nonempty, have
more than \(C_i\) copies of each required kind, and satisfy
\[
 \#\{(p,p')\in\mathcal P_i^2:p\ne p',\
       A_i^{\Gamma_i}(t+p-p',q)\}\le C_i
       \qquad(0\le i\le4)
\]
on every complete episode. Write \(N_i=|\mathcal P_i|\).
In order, these bounds concern first-clock or prediction failure,
inner-search instability, second-clock failure, a right-margin marker,
and end-search instability. The constants can be taken to be
\begin{align}
 C_0&=K+c_{\rm cl}\log(2m_1),\\
 C_1&=10|\mathcal Z|N_0^4(2R_1+3),\\
 C_2&=N_0^4N_1^4c_{\rm cl}\log(2m_2),\\
 C_3&=10|\mathcal Z|(2R_2+3)\prod_{j<3}N_j^4,
       \\
 C_4&=10(2w_E+3)\prod_{j<4}N_j^4.
       
\end{align}
Here \(K=|M|^{|V|^2+1}\), \(m_1,m_2\) are the respective full tag
alphabet sizes, and \(c_{\rm cl}\) is the absolute constant of
Lemma~\ref{lem:clock}; logarithms are natural. Also,
\(\operatorname{diam}\mathcal P_i<w_E\) for \(i<4\).
All measurements, trials, and inspections have the chronological and
reading-side access required in Lemmas~\ref{lem:main-split},
\ref{lem:periodic-split}, and~\ref{lem:aligned-stage}. Every bounded
control, including every control at a false candidate origin, lies
inside the true first episode. The same choices satisfy the end
margins of Section~\ref{sec:geometry}.

statements.title: Component expressions
statements.label: prop:component-cost
statements.text:
Every single-episode domain used in the construction, including \(E\),
\(S_1,S_2,D_i,D_i'\) and the full sets, has height at most one.
Every prefix component \(P_x\) has height zero and every suffix component
\(Q_y\) has height at most one. These are expressions over the original
alphabet, including when a standalone suffix's guessed metadata or origin
is false.

title: Finite Smith–Toda Complexes at Varying Primes
abstract: For every nonnegative integer n, we construct a Smith–Toda complex \(V(n)\) at some prime p depending on n. It is a finite p-local spectrum whose Brown–Peterson homology is \(\mathrm{BP}_*/(p,v_1,\ldots,v_n)\) with its canonical comodule structure and generator in degree zero. Each listed generator is killed to its first power.

tex.abstract:
For every nonnegative integer $n$, we construct a Smith--Toda complex
$V(n)$ at some prime $p$ depending on $n$. It is a finite $p$-local
spectrum whose Brown--Peterson homology is
$\BP_*/(p,v_1,\ldots,v_n)$ with its canonical comodule structure and
generator in degree zero. Each listed generator is killed to its first
power.
sections: The Euler layer and ordinary reduction
Connectivity at weights growing with the prime

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every integer $n\geq0$, there exist a prime $p$ and a finite
$p$-local spectrum $X$ such that
\[
 \BP_*X\cong\BP_*/(p,v_1,\ldots,v_n)
\]
as graded $\BP_*\BP$-comodules, with the canonical quotient coaction
and generator in degree zero.

statements.label: found:ultraproduct
statements.text:
The category $\cC$ is stable and symmetric monoidal, with finite
stable constructions and tensor products computed primewise.  If
$X=[(X_p)]$ and $Y=[(Y_p)]$, then
\begin{equation}
 \map_{\cC}(X,Y)
  \simeq\colim_{U\in\U}\prod_{p\in U}
                   \map_{\Sp_{(p)}}(X_p,Y_p).
\end{equation}
Every mapping spectrum is rational, and the endomorphism algebra of
the tensor unit is $HD$.  The ring $D$ contains $\Q$, and $\varpi$ is
a nonzerodivisor.

Objects, arrows, and homotopies forming a diagram indexed by a finite
simplicial set can be represented simultaneously on a large set of
primes.  The same holds for specified finite cofiber diagrams.  Sequence
objects become compact in $\Ind(\cC)$.

statements.label: found:finite-cell-morita
statements.text:
The functor $h_\Omega$ induces a symmetric monoidal equivalence
between $\cC_{\mathrm{cell}}$ and the category of finite-cell graded
$A$-modules.  For $X,Y\in\cC$, the natural comparison
\begin{equation}
 h_\Omega(X)\otimes_A h_\Omega(Y)
       \longrightarrow h_\Omega(X\otimes Y)
\end{equation}
is an equivalence whenever either input is in $\cC_{\mathrm{cell}}$.
These comparisons preserve units, compositions, and symmetric
multi-input products.  In particular, a commutative $A$-algebra whose
underlying module is finite-cell determines a commutative algebra
in $\cC$.

statements.label: found:koszul-realization

statements.title: The unnormalized power
statements.label: power:operation
statements.text:
For a sequence of actual primewise $\Lambda$-graded commutative
algebras, there is a natural map of graded commutative algebras over
rational spectra
\begin{equation}
 
 P_X:h_\Lambda(X)\longrightarrow B(X)[t^{-1}]_{*,0,0}.
\end{equation}
On a represented degree-zero class, its value is obtained by taking
the permuted $p$-fold smash and then multiplying the $p$ factors. In
particular, that value has this represented class in $B(X)$ before
Euler inversion. No $D$-linearity is asserted for $P_X$.

statements.title: The multiplicative Euler layer
statements.label: layer:comparison
statements.text:
For every sequence of graded commutative algebras $X$, there are
natural product-compatible equivalences
\begin{equation}
 
 B(X)//t\xrightarrow{\simeq}\Phi(X)
 \xleftarrow{\simeq}Q(X)\otimes_D(D//\varpi).
\end{equation}
The right-hand comparison applies to arbitrary spectrum inputs as
well. The scalar action in the $\delta$ direction agrees with
ordinary evaluation on $Q(X)$ followed by reduction. The
comparisons are compatible with algebra units and maps of inputs.
The first map uses the tautological Euler null on $S(2V)$, restricted
to $S(V)$.
statements.section_title: The Euler layer and ordinary reduction

statements.title: The first Koszul layer
statements.label: layer:first-koszul
statements.text:
For constant input $\one$, the comparison identifies
\[
 B(\one)//t\simeq F^*h_\Omega(Y_1)
\]
as graded algebras. For $M=(\MU_{(p)})_p$ there is a compatible
identification
\[
 B(M)//t\simeq F^*h_\Omega(M\otimes Y_1).
\]
These identifications preserve the algebra maps induced by the
unit and the scalar action in the $\delta$ direction.
statements.section_title: The Euler layer and ordinary reduction

statements.label: universal:primewise-models
statements.text:
For the chosen cycles through $b_a$, there exist the following data
as germs along $\U$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Filtered $\Lambda$-graded commutative ring spectra $R_p^a$,
with an equivalence
$R^a\simeq h_\Lambda(R_p^a)$ at every filtration order, compatible
with the filtered algebra structures.
\item Maps of whole unfiltered graded commutative algebras
$R_p^a\to S_{(p)}$, where the sphere is constant in the weight
grading, together with a homotopy identifying their normalized
evaluation with Equation~\eqref{universal:evaluation}.
\item Filtered finite-cell $R_p^a$-modules $K_p^a$, with an
equivalence $K^a\simeq h_\Lambda(K_p^a)$ of filtered modules.
\end{enumerate}
The algebra models, their comparisons, and the evaluation
homotopies may be chosen relative to the preceding stage.
Thus the maps $R^{a-1}\to R^a$ and $R_p^{a-1}\to R_p^a$
and their evaluations form compatible diagrams of algebras.
No algebra structure is required on $K_p^a$.

statements.label: universal:whole-module
conn:symmetric
statements.text:
Fix a positive integer $C$. For every odd prime $p>C$, every
$0\leq k\leq Cp$, and every integer $d$, one has
\[
 \Sym^k(S^d)\in\Sp_{\geq kd}.
\]
If $d$ is odd, there is the additional bound
\begin{equation}
 \Sym^k(S^d)\in\Sp_{\geq kd+k-(2C+1)}.
\end{equation}
If $d$ is even, the objects in
Equation~\eqref{conn:cofiber-definition} satisfy
\begin{equation}
 T_{p,k}(d)\in\Sp_{\geq kd+2k-3C}.
\end{equation}
More precisely, writing $k=lp+b$ with $0\leq b<p$, an odd-degree
extended power is contractible if $b\geq2$, and otherwise its
cohomology above its rank begins no earlier than $l(p-2)$.
For even $d$ and $k>0$, the multiplication cofiber is contractible
if $b>0$, and if $b=0$ its cohomology above its rank begins no
earlier than $l(2p-3)$.
statements.section_title: Connectivity at weights growing with the prime

statements.label: conn:estimate
statements.text:
Fix $0\leq a<n$ and $\lambda,\delta\in\Lambda$,
and set
\begin{equation}
 C=\max\{0,\sigma(\lambda)\}+|\sigma(\delta)|+1,
 \qquad N_a=2^{a+1}-1,
 \qquad E=N_a(5C+1).
\end{equation}
On a set of primes in $\U$, and for all its sufficiently large
members, the underlying unfiltered module satisfies
\begin{equation}
 K_p^a(p\lambda+\delta)
 \in\Sp_{\geq d(p\lambda+\delta)
                  +2\nu(p\lambda+\delta)-E}.
\end{equation}
The constants are independent of the individual multiplicities
occurring at this weight and of the prime.
statements.section_title: Connectivity at weights growing with the prime

statements.label: conn:k-test
statements.section_title: Connectivity at weights growing with the prime

statements.title: The compatible towers
statements.label: norm:construction
statements.text:
There exist cycles $b_0,\ldots,b_n$ and their realizations
$Y_0,\ldots,Y_{n+1}$, together with the algebras $L_a,L_a^M$ for
$0\leq a\leq n$, satisfying Equation~\eqref{eq:target-layer} and
its sphere-to-$M$, initial-layer, tower-map, and ordinary
$\delta$-scalar compatibilities. Each $b_j$ has chain degree zero
and weight $w_j$. For each $0\leq a<n$
there are rational algebra maps $P^a$ and $f^a$ as constructed above,
and $g_a=f^a(b_a^u)$ has chain degree zero and weight $i_a$.
It defines the next tower attachment and reduces modulo $t$ to
$b_{a+1}$ under Equation~\eqref{eq:target-layer}.

statements.title: Recovery on the preceding Koszul object
statements.label: norm:recovery
statements.text:
For $0\leq a<n$ there is a map of $\Lambda$-graded rational algebras
\begin{equation}

 h_\Lambda(M\otimes Y_a)
 \simeq h_\Lambda(M)\otimes_{R^a}K_-^a
 \longrightarrow \bigl(L_a^M[t^{-1}]\bigr)^\flat.
\end{equation}
On $h_\Lambda(M)$ it is the unnormalized power $P_M$ followed by
the map to the completed tower and inversion.  The $M$-Hurewicz
image of $b_a$ maps to $t g_a^M$, where $g_a^M$ is the image of
$g_a$ in $L_a^M$.

statements.label: cob:coefficient-relation
real:hurewicz
statements.text:
There is a \(\U\)-large set of primes on which the unit maps
induce, simultaneously for \(0\leq j\leq n+1\),
\begin{equation}
 (M_p)_*Y_{j,p}\cong (M_p)_*/I_j,
 \qquad
 \BP_*Y_{j,p}\cong\BP_*/\overline I_j.
 
\end{equation}
For every \(0\leq j\leq n\), there is a scalar
\(u^{(j)}\in D^\times\) such that the \(M\)-Hurewicz
image of \(b_j\) equals \(u^{(j)}x_j\) in
\(\pi_0h_\Omega(M\otimes Y_j)_{w_j}\).

title: Finite algebraic envelopes and the Boone–Higman conjecture
abstract: We prove the Boone–Higman conjecture. A finitely generated group has decidable word problem if and only if it embeds in a finitely presented simple group.

tex.abstract:
We prove the Boone--Higman conjecture. A finitely generated group has
decidable word problem if and only if it embeds in a finitely presented
simple group.
sections: The group input and the algebraic data
Coding with a decreasing dependency bound

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every finitely generated group \(G\), the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item \(G\) has decidable word problem.
\item \(G\) embeds in a finitely presented simple group.
\end{enumerate}

statements.label: thm:envelope
statements.text:
Every finitely generated group with decidable word problem embeds in a
finitely presented group \(\Gamma\) admitting a faithful two-transitive
action on a countably infinite set. Every point stabilizer of this action
is finitely generated.

statements.label: thm:algebra-package
statements.text:
For every finitely generated group \(L\) with decidable word problem,
there are the following data over \(k=\F_2\):
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item A nonzero finitely presented unital algebra \(B\), a simple
subalgebra \(A\subseteq B\) with identity \(e\), and an embedding
\(L\hookrightarrow A^\times\).
\item An injective nonunital algebra homomorphism \(\phi:B\to B\) with
\(\phi(B)\subseteq A\) and \({p=\phi(1_B)\ne1_B}\).
\item Elements \(s_0,s_1,t_0,t_1\in pBp\) commuting with \(\phi(B)\)
and satisfying
\[
 t_i s_j=\delta_{ij}p,\qquad s_0t_0+s_1t_1=p
 \quad(i,j\in\{0,1\}).
\]
\item An element \(b_*\in B\) with the following property. Put
\[
 R=B\otimes_k B^{\op},\qquad
 \psi=\phi\otimes\phi^{\op},
 \qquad (a\otimes b^{\op})\cdot m=amb.
\]
Then
\[
 r\ne0\ \Longrightarrow\ \psi(r)\cdot b_*\ne0
 \qquad(r\in R).
\]
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Zaremsky
statements.label: thm:zaremsky
statements.text:
Suppose a finitely presented group \(\Lambda\) acts faithfully on a
nonempty countable set \(X\). If the point stabilizers are finitely
generated and there are finitely many orbits on the unordered
two-element subsets of \(X\), then \(\Lambda\) embeds in a nontrivial
finitely presented simple group.
statements.section_title: The group input and the algebraic data

statements.label: prop:affine
statements.text:
For the algebra $B$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:algebra-package}, the group
\[
 \Gamma_0=B^6\rtimes\St_6(R),\qquad R=B\otimes_kB^{\op},
\]
is finitely presented.

statements.label: thm:kernel
statements.text:
Let $R$ be a unital associative ring, let $\psi:R\to R$ be an additive
multiplicative map, and put $P=\psi(1)$.  Suppose that
$U_0,U_1,V_0,V_1\in PRP$ commute with $\psi(R)$ and satisfy
\[
 V_iU_j=\delta_{ij}P,\qquad U_0V_0+U_1V_1=P.
\]
Then the homomorphism
\[
 \theta:\operatorname{St}_6(R)\longrightarrow\operatorname{St}_6(R),
 \qquad x_{ij}(a)\longmapsto x_{ij}(\psi(a)),
\]
satisfies $\theta(\ker\pi)=1$.

statements.label: prop:two-transitive-action
statements.text:
The set $X$ is countably infinite.  The action of $\Gamma$ on $X$ is
faithful and two-transitive, and all its point stabilizers are finitely
generated.

statements.label: thm:monoids
statements.text:
Let \(\widehat G\) be a finitely generated group with decidable word
problem.  There exist a finitely presented monoid \(K\) with zero
\(\Omega\ne1_K\), and a finitely generated monoid \(H\) with decidable
word problem and zero \(\zeta\ne1_H\), with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item There is an injective group homomorphism
\(\widehat G\longrightarrow H^\times\).
\item For the monoid \(T\) defined above, there is an injective unital
monoid homomorphism \(\kappa:T\longrightarrow H\) with
\(\kappa(0_T)=\zeta\).
\item For every finite ordered tuple \(h_1,\ldots,h_d\) of distinct
nonzero elements of \(H\), with \(d\ge1\), there are \(L,R\in H\)
such that
\[
 Lh_1R=1_H,\qquad Lh_iR=\zeta\quad(2\le i\le d).
\]
\item There is an injective multiplicative map \(c:H\longrightarrow K\)
whose image is disjoint from \(\{1_K,\Omega\}\).  We write
\(c_h=c(h)\); this map is not required to preserve identities or zeros.
\item There is an element \(z\in H\) such that the map
\[
 (\tau,\tau')\longmapsto\kappa(\tau)z\kappa(\tau')
\]
is an injection from \((T\setminus\{0_T\})^2\) into
\(H\setminus\{\zeta\}\).
\end{enumerate}

title: Finite angular cylinder covers below the half-area bound
abstract: A regular tetrahedron admits a finite cylinder covering with compact triangular perpendicular bases whose total area is less than half its minimum orthogonal projection area. This disproves the half-area cylinder-covering conjecture. By affine invariance, the same construction gives a counterexample to the directionwise normalized half-bound for every nondegenerate tetrahedron.

tex.abstract:
A regular tetrahedron admits a finite cylinder covering with compact triangular
perpendicular bases whose total area is less than half its minimum orthogonal
projection area. This disproves the half-area cylinder-covering conjecture.
By affine invariance, the same construction gives a counterexample to the
directionwise normalized half-bound for every nondegenerate tetrahedron.
sections: Counts and formulas under changes of scale

statements.label: thm:counterexample
statements.text:
The tetrahedron \eqref{eq:tetrahedron} has $A_{\min}(K)=\sqrt2$.
For every $0<\eps\le1/2000$, it admits a covering by
$m=2\lceil2/\eps^2\rceil$ cylinders with compact triangular perpendicular
bases such that
\begin{equation}
 \frac1{\sqrt2}\sum_{i=1}^m|B_i|
 =\frac12-\frac{13}{6000}\eps^2+O(\eps^4).
\end{equation}
The remainder has absolute value at most $2\eps^4$, and the total base
area is strictly less than $A_{\min}(K)/2$.

statements.label: cor:normalized-covering
statements.text:
Every nondegenerate tetrahedron $T\subset\R^3$ admits a finite cylinder
covering with compact triangular perpendicular bases for which
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^m\frac{|B_i|}{|\pi_{u_i^\perp}T|}<\frac12.
\]
Thus the 1-Codimensional Cylinder Covering Conjecture is false.

statements.label: prop:coverage
statements.text:
For every $0<\eps\le\eta/2$, the $2n$ cylinders
\eqref{eq:first-family}--\eqref{eq:second-family}, with parameters
\eqref{eq:parameters}--\eqref{eq:cutoffs}, cover the closed tetrahedron $K$.

statements.title: Quantitative coverage criterion
statements.label: cor:quantitative-coverage
statements.text:
Let $0<\tau<1$ and $\eta\ge0$. Choose an integer $n$ with
$\Delta=2/n\le\tau^2$, put $q_j=-1+j\Delta$, and define
$\alpha_j,\beta_j$ by \eqref{eq:axis-coefficients}. Use the triangles and
directions \eqref{eq:first-family}--\eqref{eq:second-family}, with
$\eps$ replaced by $\tau$ and with cutoffs
\[
 T_j=\frac12+\tau^2\left(\eta+\max_{q_j\le q\le q_{j+1}}d(q)\right).
\]
These $2n$ cylinders cover $K$ whenever
\begin{equation}
 2\eta-(2+2\eta)\tau-\frac{\tau^2}{4}\ge0.
\end{equation}

statements.label: prop:area-expansion
statements.text:
For the construction \eqref{eq:parameters}--\eqref{eq:second-family} and
$0<\eps\le1$,
\[
 \left|\frac{S(\eps)}H-\frac12-
       \left(2\eta-\frac1{240}\right)\eps^2\right|
 \le 2\eps^4.
\]

statements.title: Area estimate with a variable margin
statements.label: cor:variable-margin-area
statements.text:
Let $0<\tau\le1$ and $0\le\eta\le1/8$. Choose an integer $n$ with
$\Delta=2/n\le\tau^2$, put $q_j=-1+j\Delta$, and use the secant
coefficients \eqref{eq:axis-coefficients} and cutoffs
\[
 T_j=\frac12+\tau^2\left(\eta+\max_{q_j\le q\le q_{j+1}}d(q)\right).
\]
For the two families \eqref{eq:first-family}--\eqref{eq:second-family},
with $\eps$ replaced by $\tau$, their total perpendicular base area $C$
satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \left|\frac CH-\frac12-
       \left(2\eta-\frac1{240}\right)\tau^2\right|
 \le\frac{59}{64}\tau^4+\tau^2\Delta
 \le2\tau^4.
\end{equation}
The estimate is uniform over all these choices; it does not assume
that the cylinders cover $K$.

statements.title: Compatible boundaries and radial caps
statements.label: ext:general-cap
statements.text:
Let $\tau>0$ tend to zero through any set accumulating at zero.
For each $\tau$, choose a finite partition
$-1=q_0<\cdots<q_m=1$, constants $\alpha_j,\beta_j$, and positive
continuous functions $R_j$ on $I_j=[q_{j-1},q_j]$.
Suppose that $L(q)=\alpha_j-q\beta_j$ is continuous on $[-1,1]$
and $L(-1)=L(1)=0$.  Suppose also, uniformly for every $j$ and
$q\in I_j$, that
\begin{align}
 \beta_j&=q/2+O(\tau^2),&
 \alpha_j&=(1+q^2)/4+O(\tau^2),\\
 R_j(q)&=\tfrac12+\tau^2\bigl(d(q)+\eta\bigr)+O(\tau^4),
 &&0<\eta<1/480.
\end{align}
Here $\eta$ is fixed, and all error constants and their common range of
validity are independent of $\tau,j,q$.
Define
\begin{align*}
 P_j^-&=\{(0,qS,HS):q\in I_j,\ 0\le S\le R_j(q)\},&
 v_j^-&=(1,\tau\alpha_j,H\tau\beta_j),\\
 P_j^+&=\{(qT,0,H(1-T)):q\in I_j,\ 0\le T\le R_j(q)\},&
 v_j^+&=(-\tau\alpha_j,1,H\tau\beta_j).
\end{align*}
For every sufficiently small admissible $\tau$, the $2m$ cylinders
$P_j^-+\mathbb Rv_j^-$ and $P_j^++\mathbb Rv_j^+$ cover the closed
tetrahedron $K$.  Their bases are compact, and their total area $C_\tau$
satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \frac{C_\tau}{H}
 =\frac12+\left(2\eta-\frac1{240}\right)\tau^2+O(\tau^4).
\end{equation}
If each $R_j$ is constant, every base is a triangle.
The threshold and error constant may depend on $\eta$ and the uniform
constants in the hypotheses, but not on $m$.

statements.label: prop:angular-cubic
statements.text:
For every $0<\tau\le1$, the tetrahedron $K$ admits a cover by
$2\lceil8/\tau^2\rceil$ cylinders with compact, nondegenerate triangular
perpendicular bases. Their total base area $C_\tau$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \left|\frac{C_\tau}{H}-\frac12+\frac{\tau^2}{240}
                   -\frac{25}{2}\tau^3\right|
 \le2\tau^4\qquad(0<\tau\le1/50).
\end{equation}
In particular, $C_\tau<A_{\min}(K)/2$ for $0<\tau\le1/4000$, and
\[
 \frac{C_\tau}{A_{\min}(K)}
 =\frac12-\frac{\tau^2}{240}+O(\tau^3)
 \qquad(\tau\downarrow0).
\]

title: Finite cylinder approximation of ruled sets
abstract: We approximate compact ruled families of segments by finitely many cylinders with square intercept tiles and perpendicular-base area at most their integral projection cost plus any positive error. The velocity field is C1, and its differential has opposite real eigenvalues whose magnitudes are strictly below the inverse segment half-length; both eigenvalues may vanish. The result includes square-zero differentials with unrestricted shear and fields that pass between the two regimes. It holds for arbitrary compact label sets.

tex.abstract:
We approximate compact ruled families of segments by finitely many
cylinders with square intercept tiles and perpendicular-base area at
most their integral projection cost plus any positive error. The
velocity field is $C^1$, and its differential has opposite real
eigenvalues whose magnitudes are strictly below the inverse segment
half-length; both eigenvalues may vanish. The result includes
square-zero differentials with unrestricted shear and fields that
pass between the two regimes. It holds for arbitrary compact label
sets.
sections: From affine coverings to a finite family

statements.title: Perpendicular base area
statements.label: b:projection
statements.text:
Let $h>0$, let $T\subset\R^2$ be bounded and measurable, and let
$g\in\R^2$. The image $F_h(\Cyl(T,g))$ is a cylinder whose perpendicular
base has area $h|T|J_h(g)$. A compact nondegenerate parallelogram tile
has a compact nondegenerate parallelogram base. An open tile gives an
open base. The formula is unchanged after a Euclidean isometry.

statements.title: Finite approximation by square tiles
statements.label: b:approximation
statements.text:
Let $D\subset\R^2$ be compact, let $V$ be $C^1$ on an open
neighborhood of $D$, and let $L,h>0$. Suppose that
\begin{equation}
 \tr DV(p)=0,\qquad -L^{-2}<\det DV(p)\le0
 \quad(p\in D).
\end{equation}
For every $\varepsilon>0$, there are finitely many compact
nondegenerate square tiles $T_i\subset\R^2$, with possibly different
orientations, and velocities $g_i\in\R^2$ such that
\begin{equation}
 E(D,V,L)\subset\bigcup_i\Cyl(T_i,g_i),\qquad
 \sum_i |T_i|J_h(g_i)
 \le\int_D J_h(V(p))\,dp+\varepsilon.
\end{equation}
Under $F_h$, the perpendicular bases are compact nondegenerate
parallelograms and have total area $h\sum_i|T_i|J_h(g_i)$.
No condition on the area of $\partial D$ or smallness of $\|DV\|$
is required.

statements.title: Approximation by product cells
statements.label: b:product
statements.text:
Let $h,M>0$, let $D\subset\mathbb R^2$ be compact with
$|\partial D|=0$, and let $V$ be $C^1$ on an open neighborhood of $D$.
Suppose that $DV(p)$ has eigenvalues $\lambda_p,-\lambda_p$, where
$0<M\lambda_p<1$ for every $p\in D$.  For every $e>0$, the set
\[
 \mathcal S_h(D,V,M)=
 \{(x,p_1+xV_1(p),h(p_2+xV_2(p))):p\in D,\ |x|\le M\}
\]
has a finite cylinder cover with bounded open measurable perpendicular
bases whose total area is at most
\[
 h\int_D J_h(V(p))\,dp+e,
 \qquad J_h(w)=(1+w_1^2+h^2w_2^2)^{-1/2}.
\]

statements.title: Approximation by logarithmic cells
statements.label: b:logarithmic
statements.text:
Let $X,k>0$, let $U\subset\mathbb R^2$ be compact with
$|\partial U|=0$, and let $v$ be $C^2$ on an open rectangle containing
$U$.  Suppose that, for every $p\in U$,
\[
 \operatorname{tr}Dv(p)=0,\qquad \det Dv(p)<0,\qquad
 kX\sqrt{-\det Dv(p)}<1.
\]
In orthonormal coordinates $(x,p)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^2$,
the set
\[
 \{(x,p+xkv(p)):p\in U,\ |x|\le X\}
\]
has, for every $e>0$, a finite cylinder cover with bounded open
measurable perpendicular bases and total base area at most
\[
 \int_U(1+k^2|v(p)|^2)^{-1/2}\,dp+e.
\]

title: Finite generation for the K(n)-local sphere
abstract: We prove that the homotopy groups of the \(K(n)\)-local sphere are finitely generated ℤp-modules in every integer degree, for every prime p and positive height n. Equivalently, the same conclusion holds after \(K(n)\)-localizing any finite p-local spectrum. This answers the degreewise finiteness question of Hovey and Hovey–Strickland.

tex.abstract:
We prove that the homotopy groups of the $K(n)$-local sphere are finitely
generated $\mathbb Z_p$-modules in every integer degree, for every prime $p$
and positive height $n$. Equivalently, the same conclusion holds after
$K(n)$-localizing any finite $p$-local spectrum. This answers the degreewise
finiteness question of Hovey and Hovey--Strickland.
