title: Fontaine–Mazur modularity at the prime 2
abstract: We prove that every continuous, irreducible, odd two-dimensional 2-adic representation of \(G_{\mathbb Q}\), unramified outside finitely many primes and de Rham at 2 with distinct Hodge–Tate weights, is modular up to Tate twist. This resolves the odd, regular two-dimensional Fontaine–Mazur conjecture over ℚ at 2, including all residual representations.
version_note: This version updates citations to revised manuscripts in this collection; see the [previous version](../Fontaine-Mazur-modularity-at-the-prime-2-September-23-2026/paper.pdf).

tex.abstract:
We prove that every continuous, irreducible, odd two-dimensional
\(2\)-adic representation of \(G_{\mathbb Q}\), unramified outside
finitely many primes and de Rham at \(2\) with distinct Hodge--Tate
weights, is modular up to Tate twist. This resolves the odd, regular
two-dimensional Fontaine--Mazur conjecture over \(\mathbb Q\) at \(2\),
including all residual representations.
sections: Completed forms and their local parameters

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let
\[
 r:G_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow\GL_2(\overline{\mathbb Q}_2)
\]
be continuous and irreducible. Suppose that \(r\) is odd, is
unramified outside finitely many primes, and is de Rham at \(2\)
with distinct Hodge--Tate weights. Then \(r\) is isomorphic to
a Tate twist of the \(2\)-adic Galois representation associated
with a classical cuspidal eigenform.

statements.title: Representation spaces
statements.label: prop:rep-space
statements.text:
Let $G$ satisfy $\Phi_2$, let $\overline D$ be a continuous
two-dimensional determinant over the finite field $\kk$, and fix a
continuous lift $\chi$ of its determinant character.  The following
statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The determinant deformation functor is represented by a complete
Noetherian local $\OO$-algebra $R^{\mathrm{ps}}$.  There is a finite
$R^{\mathrm{ps}}$-algebra $\mathscr E$ carrying its universal Cayley--Hamilton
representation.  Matrix representations of $\mathscr E$ compatible with the
universal determinant form an affine scheme of finite type over
$R^{\mathrm{ps}}$.  Its completion at a closed residual matrix
representation is that representation's framed deformation space.
\item Invariant lines at finitely many closed subgroups can be imposed
by closed incidence conditions in products of projective lines.  On the
absolutely irreducible global locus, existence of such a line with a
specified character is closed in the trace and character parameters.
\item Suppose the subgroups' abelianizations have finitely generated
maximal pro-$2$ quotients.  Adjoining the characters on the specified
lines gives a finite extension of the completed trace-and-determinant
image.
\item At an absolutely irreducible representation over a coefficient
field, determinants classify unframed deformations.  After a splitting
extension, the framed fiber is a conjugacy orbit of dimension three.
\end{enumerate}
These assertions do not require the residual determinant to be
multiplicity-free.

statements.title: Relative relation bounds
statements.label: prop:relative-presentation
statements.text:
Let $F$ be totally real of degree $d$, let $S$ contain the real and
dyadic places, and let $\rho$ be a representation over a finite
residue field, a curve field as above, or a finite $2$-adic field.
Use one global frame and a fixed determinant.  Let $T\subset S$
consist of all real places and $m$ dyadic places, each isomorphic to
$\QQ_2$.  Over the completed product of the unrestricted local framed
deformation rings at $T$, the global framed ring has a power-series
presentation with $g$ relative variables and $r$ relations satisfying
\begin{equation}
g-r\ge 3-6m-h^0\bigl(D^\vee(1)\bigr).
\end{equation}
Local quotient conditions and local line charts may then be imposed
by base change without changing this bound.  This includes replacing
the local base by its reduction.

For the variable-determinant problem with independent frames at the
places of $S$, the relative tangent dimension over the local framed
base is
\begin{equation}
h^1_{\mathrm{Sel}}(\ad\rho)
 +\sum_{v\in S}h^0_v(\ad\rho)-h^0(\ad\rho),
\end{equation}
where the Selmer condition is zero at $S$ and any other prescribed
conditions are included in the Selmer group.  On the absolutely
irreducible locus, forgetting these independent frames has smooth
fiber dimension $4|S|-1$.

statements.title: A characteristic-zero line chart
statements.label: cor:charzero-line-dimension
statements.text:
For a two-dimensional representation of $G_{\QQ_2}$ over a finite
$2$-adic field with a chosen invariant line and fixed determinant,
every component of its framed line-deformation chart has dimension
at least five.  The odd fixed-determinant real chart has dimension
two.  In particular, over $\QQ$, the relative bound for these two
local charts is $-3$ whenever $h^0(D^\vee(1))=0$.

statements.title: Local component geometry
statements.label: prop:local-geometry
statements.text:
The ring $A^{\mathrm{rd}}$ is a flat complete-intersection normal
domain over $\mathcal L$, of dimension $1+8d$, and its special fiber
is a normal domain of dimension $8d$.  Set
\[
e=1+8d+4u+g.
\]
Then the following statements hold for the model
\eqref{eq:tame-model}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Spec B_i$ is irreducible of dimension $e$, and its unique
irreducible component is horizontal.
\item The two rings have a canonical common special fiber, compatible
with their universal matrices and the variables $X_1,\ldots,X_g$.
Its irreducible components have dimension $e-1$ and are indexed by a
choice, at each tame place, of the unramified component or the closure
of the nontrivial-unipotent component.
\item The irreducible components of $\Spec B_1$ are horizontal and
have dimension $e$.  They are indexed by the same choices.  The
specialization of each has precisely its corresponding special-fiber
component as underlying support.  In particular the generic point
of a special-fiber component lies on exactly one component of
$\Spec B_1$.
\end{enumerate}
The assertions remain valid after finite extension of the constants
and curve field and the resulting enhanced completion.  No condition
on the dyadic curve representations is required.

statements.label: prop:completed-forms
statements.text:
For the tame level \(U^2\), central character \(\psi=\chi\eps\),
and full compact forms module \(M\) just defined, the following
properties hold. In the second assertion weights and local parameters
use the normalization of Section~\ref{sec:preliminaries}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For a sufficiently small product \(K\) of uniform open
subgroups of \(\SL_2(F_v)\), the full compact module \(M\)
is finite free over \(\OO[[K]]\). The integral and torsion
function spaces are admissible and commute with reduction
of coefficients.
\item Locally algebraic vectors are classical definite
quaternionic forms of the corresponding algebraic weight.
Their regular noncharacter eigenpackets transfer to Hilbert
cuspidal eigenforms. They have Galois representations of
determinant \(\chi\), with the local compatibility described
below.
\item The regular classical vectors are dense in the Banach
space. They remain dense if, at each \(v\mid2\), one fixes a
smooth principal-series type with two distinct inertial
characters and varies the algebraic factor with the
prescribed central degree.
\item Every residual local factor \(\mathbb T\) of the
completed Hecke algebra away from \(S\) is a complete quotient
of \(R_F^{\mathrm{ps},\chi}\). It is reduced and
\(\OO\)-torsion-free, and its spectrum is the closure of its
classical coefficient points.
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: Completed forms and their local parameters

statements.label: prop:block-comparison
statements.text:
The residual Hecke summand belongs to the product block
just specified. The exact projective-generator functor gives
\[
 L=\Hom_{\mathrm{cts},G_2}(P,M),
\]
taken in the compact dual category of the specified product block,
with the right \(E_{\mathrm{loc}}\)-action by precomposition. It is
faithful over \(\mathbb T\), finite over
\(R_{\mathrm{loc}}^{\mathrm{ps}}\), and finite over
\(\mathbb T\). The local pseudodeformation action on \(L\)
is the restriction of the global Galois action, with the
stated cyclotomic twist. In particular,
\(\mathbb T\) is finite over \(R_{\mathrm{loc}}^{\mathrm{ps}}\).

At a coefficient point \(x:\mathbb T\to E'\), after finite
extension of \(E'\), its Banach Hecke eigenspace contains
\[
 \widehat\bigotimes_{v\mid2}\Pi_v,
\]
where \(\Pi_v\) is an irreducible unitary Banach
representation with local parameter
\((r_x|_{G_{F_v}}\otimes\eps)^{\mathrm{ss}}\), of determinant
\(\chi_v\eps^2\), in the block normalization of
Section~\ref{sec:preliminaries}. If every local parameter is absolutely
irreducible, de Rham, and regular, the eigenspace has a
nonzero locally algebraic vector. If the untwisted
parameter at \(v\) is
\(\gamma_{1,v}\oplus\gamma_{2,v}\), with ratio outside
\(\{1,\eps,\eps^{-1}\}\), the possibilities are the
continuous unnormalized upper-Borel inductions
\[
 \Ind_B^{\GL_2(\mathbb Q_2)}
       (\gamma_{i,v}\eps\otimes\gamma_{j,v}),
 \qquad \{i,j\}=\{1,2\}.
\]
statements.section_title: Completed forms and their local parameters

statements.label: prop:hecke-dimension
statements.text:
For every irreducible component \(C\) of
\(\Spec\mathbb T\),
\[
 \dim C\ge1+2d.
\]
statements.section_title: Completed forms and their local parameters

statements.title: Localized propagation
statements.label: thm:localized-propagation
statements.text:
Let \(F\) be a totally real solvable field of even degree, completely
split at~\(2\), and let \(S\) contain its real and dyadic places and
the allowed finite ramification. Fix the determinant
\(\chi=\det r=\chi_{\mathrm{fin}}\eps^w\) of a target \(r\) as in
Section~\ref{sec:preliminaries}, a semisimple residual representation
with determinant \(\bar\chi\), and let
\(R_F^{\mathrm{ps},\chi}\) be the corresponding complete local global
pseudodeformation ring. Let $C$ be a characteristic-two curve in
\(\Spec R_F^{\mathrm{ps},\chi}\).  Suppose that $C$ is potentially pro-modular,
that its generic representation is not virtually solvable, and that its
local images at the non-dyadic finite places in $S$ are finite.  Every
irreducible closed locus of \(\Spec R_F^{\mathrm{ps},\chi}\)
containing $C$ is potentially pro-modular, with ramification allowed
only at the specified set \(S\) before base change.

statements.title: The patched regular sequence
statements.label: prop:patched-regular-sequence

statements.title: Full support after patching
statements.label: prop:patched-support
statements.text:
The untwisted patched module satisfies
\[
 \Supp_{R_{1,\infty}}N_{1,\infty}
       \supseteq\Spec R_{1,\infty}^f.
\]
Consequently the old module has full support:
$\Supp_{R_1^f}N_1=\Spec R_1^f$.

statements.title: Field preparation
statements.label: prop:field-preparation
statements.text:
There is a constant $U$, depending only on the fixed residual data and
$\Sigma$, with the following property.  One can construct abelian,
totally real $2$-extensions
\[
                 \QQ\subset A\subset F
\]
in which $2$ splits completely, together with allowed sets $S_A,S_F$,
such that the following assertions hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The allowed sets contain the real and dyadic places and all places
above $\Sigma$.  Their numbers $u_A,u_F$ of non-dyadic finite places
are at most $U$.  The degrees $d_A=[A:\QQ]$ and $[F:A]$ can be
made arbitrarily large, with $d=[F:\QQ]=[F:A]d_A$.
\item If $\bar r$ is absolutely irreducible, its restriction to $G_F$
is absolutely irreducible.  In this case there are no marked places.
\item In the reducible case, the characters remain distinct on $G_F$
if they were distinct on $G_{\QQ}$.  If $\alpha_2\ne1$, there are
again no marked places.  If $\alpha_2=1$, there is a dyadic place
$v_0$ of $A$ and the marked set $M$ consists of all its extensions
to $F$.  Set $m=|M|$; thus $m=[F:A]$ and $m/d=1/d_A$ in the
marked case, whereas $m=0$ otherwise.
\item In the reducible case, for $\beta=\alpha,\alpha^{-1}$ the
following group is zero:
\begin{equation}
 \left\{c\in H^1(G_{F,S_F},k(\beta)):
       \operatorname{loc}_v(c)=0\text{ for every }v\in S_F\setminus M
 \right\}=0.
\end{equation}
Here the zero conditions include all real places.  The condition at a
marked place is unrestricted.
\item In the reducible case, restriction preserves residual extension
classes: for either ratio
$\beta$, the map
\[
 H^1(G_{A,S_A},k(\beta))\longrightarrow H^1(G_{F,S_F},k(\beta))
\]
is injective.
\end{enumerate}
In the reducible case let $H^1_{\mathrm{str}}(F,k(\beta))$ denote the
Selmer group with zero condition at $M$, full condition at
$S_F\setminus M$ (including the real places), and unramified condition
elsewhere.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \dim_k H^1_{\mathrm{str}}(F,k(\beta))\le
 \begin{cases}
 d+u_F,&\alpha_2\ne1,\\
 2d-3m+u_F,&\alpha_2=1.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}

statements.label: thm:potential-promodularity
statements.text:
Let \(r\) satisfy the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:main} and be not
virtually solvable. Then \(r\) is pro-modular over
some solvable totally real Galois extension of
\(\mathbb Q\), of even degree and split completely
at \(2\).

More generally, fix a complete integral framed deformation family over
\(\mathbb Q\), with determinant \(\chi=\det r\), containing the
coefficient point defined by \(r\), and with ramification confined
to a finite set. The closed trace image of this family is pro-modular
after restriction to one common extension of the stated kind, at
one fixed tame level.

statements.title: Ordinary weight finiteness
statements.label: prop:ordinary-weight-finiteness
statements.text:
The space $W$ is an $\OO$-submodule stable under $T_1$, the tame Hecke
operators, and $U^{\pm1}$, and these actions commute.  Its dual $M$ is
finite over~$\Omega$.  The closed commutative algebra generated by these
actions on~$M$ is finite over~$\Omega$.

tex.abstract:
We prove the sixth-symmetric-power case of Foulkes' conjecture. For every
integer \(b\ge6\) and every finite-dimensional complex vector space \(V\),
there is a \(\GL(V)\)-equivariant injection
\(\Sym^6(\Sym^b V)\hookrightarrow\Sym^b(\Sym^6 V)\).
sections: The large-degree range and finite reductions
An upper bound and two exact recurrences
A power bound from leading monomials
Exact differences in the small-tail band

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every integer \(b\ge6\) and every finite-dimensional complex vector
space \(V\), there is a \(\GL(V)\)-equivariant injection
\[
                 \Sym^6(\Sym^b V)\ \hookrightarrow\ \Sym^b(\Sym^6 V).
\]
Equivalently, \(h_b[h_6]-h_6[h_b]\) is Schur-positive for every \(b\ge6\).

is a \(\GL(V)\)-equivariant injection
\(\Sym^6(\Sym^b V)\hookrightarrow\Sym^b(\Sym^6 V)\).

statements.label: prop:power
statements.text:
Suppose \(Q(x)\ge C>0\), where \(C\) is an integer and
\(w(x)=6d_0\) with \(d_0>0\). Put
\[
 z=\min\left(18,\ \min\left\{h\ge0:
                              \binom{d_0+h}{h}\ge C\right\}\right).
\]
Then for all \(k\ge1\),
\begin{equation}
                Q(kx)\ge f(C,z,k).
\end{equation}

tex.abstract:
We prove canonical nonvanishing for smooth connected projective complex
fourfolds: if \(K_X\) is pseudo-effective, then
\(H^0(X,mK_X)\ne0\) for some positive integer \(m\).
sections: A fixed minimal model of full nef dimension
The analytic inputs and the lifting problem
Signed representatives and logarithmic general type
Moving jets on a two-slot bundle
Fixed finite data and the final contradiction
A section on the original normal variety

statements.label: thm:nonvanishing
statements.text:
Let $X$ be a smooth connected projective complex fourfold. If $K_X$ is
pseudo-effective, then $H^0(X,mK_X)\ne0$ for some positive integer $m$.

\label[corollary]{cor:lc-nonvanishing}
Let $(X,\Delta)$ be a connected normal projective log canonical complex
pair of dimension at most four. Suppose that $\Delta\geq0$ is rational
and $D=K_X+\Delta$ is $\mathbb Q$-Cartier and nef. For every positive
integer $r$ such that $rD$ is Cartier, there is a positive integer $m$
with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(mrD))\ne0$.

statements.text:
\label[proposition]{prop:subvarieties}
For $Y$ as in \Cref{prop:reduction}, every proper positive-dimensional
subvariety through a point of a suitable fixed very general locus is
of general type.

statements.title: Scalar orders
statements.label: eq:scalar-orders

statements.title: Zero Lelong numbers for nef klt adjoints
statements.label: thm:adjoint-metric
statements.text:
Let $(H,\Theta)$ be a normal connected projective complex klt pair,
where $\Theta\ge0$ is rational and $D_H=K_H+\Theta$ is nef and
$\Q$-Cartier. Let $\pi:V\to H$ be any projective log resolution.
The rational line bundle $\pi^*D_H$ admits a semipositive metric
with minimal singularities, and every such metric has zero Lelong
number at every point of $V$. Its multiplier ideal is trivial for
every positive exponent. Neither $K_H$ nor $\Theta$ is required
to be separately $\Q$-Cartier.
statements.section_title: The analytic inputs and the lifting problem

statements.title: Ordinary interior injectivity
statements.label: thm:interior-injectivity
statements.text:
Let $V$ be a smooth projective complex variety and $L$ an integral
divisor. Let $0\le C_0\le C_2$ be effective rational divisors whose
combined support has simple normal crossings. Suppose the actual
rational line bundles $L-C_0$ and $L-C_2$ have semipositive singular
Hermitian metrics with zero Lelong numbers at every point. For a
rational number $0<\lambda<1$ put $C_1=(1-\lambda)C_0+\lambda C_2$.
The natural inclusion of sheaves induces an injection
\[
 H^1(V,\cO_V(K_V+L-\lfloor C_1\rfloor))
 \longrightarrow H^1(V,\cO_V(K_V+L-\lfloor C_0\rfloor)).
\]
statements.section_title: The analytic inputs and the lifting problem

statements.title: Signed representative alternative
statements.text:
\label[proposition]{prop:signed-alternative}
Let $Y$ be a projective $\Q$-factorial terminal fourfold such that $K_Y$ is
nef and $\kappa(Y,K_Y)=-\infty$. Suppose that there is a very general locus
of $Y$ through whose points every proper positive-dimensional subvariety
is of general type on resolution. Let $J$ be a rational Weil divisor,
with coefficients of either sign, satisfying $J\sim_{\Q}K_Y$.
Let $p:W\to Y$ be a projective log resolution, and let $D_W$ be a reduced
simple normal crossings divisor containing the strict support of $J$
and every $p$-exceptional divisor. Then $K_W+D_W$ is big.
statements.section_title: Signed representatives and logarithmic general type

statements.title: Two-slot jets
statements.label: eq:two-slot-seshadri
statements.text:
\label[proposition]{prop:two-slot-jets}
Let \(Z\) and \(P\) be defined by
\Crefrange{eq:two-slot-bundle}{eq:two-slot-polarization}.
Fix \(\epsilon>0\), choose \(\delta\) satisfying
\Cref{eq:two-slot-gap-choice}, and then fix \(q\) large enough
for \Cref{eq:two-slot-jet-volume}. For all sufficiently small
positive rational \(t\), one has
\begin{equation}
 \varepsilon(P;z)>2n+2=10
\end{equation}
at a very general smooth point of the torus open of \(Z\).
statements.section_title: Moving jets on a two-slot bundle

statements.title: Bounded correspondences cannot sweep the bundle
statements.text:
\label[proposition]{prop:two-slot-correspondences}
Fix \(\epsilon>0\), an integer \(q>0\), and positive constants
\(B_0,B_1\). Keep \(Y,K,A,L_t\) and \(P=L_1+L_2+q\xi\) as above.
For all sufficiently small positive rational \(t\), there is no
irreducible finite-type parameter space \(T\) and integral closed
subvariety \(\Gamma\subset T\times Z\), dominant over \(T\), with
the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item The evaluation \(\Gamma\to Z\) is dominant, and a general
fiber \(V\) over \(T\) is an integral subvariety of dimension \(n\).
\item On a smooth projective resolution \(V^*\to V\), both
projections \(g_i:V^*\to Y\), \(i=1,2\), are dominant and
generically finite.
\item Writing \(P\) also for its pullback to \(V^*\), one has
\[
 0<P^n\cdot V\le B_0,\qquad
 K_{V^*}P^{n-1}\le B_1(P^n\cdot V).
\]
\end{enumerate}
The restriction on \(t\) depends only on the fixed geometry and
\(\epsilon,q,B_0,B_1\), not on the parameter space or family.
statements.section_title: Moving jets on a two-slot bundle

statements.label: eq:fixed-two-slot-jet-map
statements.text:
\label[corollary]{cor:fixed-two-slot-jets}
Fix sufficiently small \(t\) as in
\Cref{prop:scalar-orders,prop:two-slot-jets}, and let
\(p:W\to Y\) be any fixed smooth projective resolution. Continue
to denote pullbacks by \(L\) and \(S_0\). On
\[
 Z_W=\PP\bigl(\cO_W(S_0)_1\oplus\cO_W(S_0)_2\bigr)
       \longrightarrow W\times W,\qquad
 M=L_1+L_2+q\xi ,
\]
there are a smooth torus point \(z_*\), over the isomorphism opens
of \(p\) in both slots, and a sufficiently divisible integer
\(k_0>0\) such that \(k_0L\) is Cartier and
\begin{equation}
 H^0(Z_W,\cO_{Z_W}(k_0M))
 \longrightarrow
 \cO_{Z_W}(k_0M)\otimes
 \bigl(\cO_{Z_W,z_*}/\mathfrak m_{z_*}^{\,10k_0+1}\bigr)
\end{equation}
is surjective. In particular, finitely many sections can be fixed
whose jets span its target.
statements.section_title: Moving jets on a two-slot bundle

statements.title: Finite-data Frobenius incompatibility
statements.label: thm:finite-data
statements.text:
Let $W$ be a smooth connected projective complex variety of dimension
$n\ge2$. Fix rational Cartier divisors $L,H$, with $H$ ample, an
integral Cartier divisor $S$, an integer $q>0$, and real numbers
$r>1$, $\epsilon>0$. Suppose
\begin{gather*}
 H^n\le(2\epsilon)^n,\qquad
 K_WH^{n-1}\le 2H^n/r,\qquad
 (2L+qS)H^{n-1}\le4H^n,\\
 (14\epsilon)^n<1/4,\qquad80\epsilon<3/4.
\end{gather*}
The following three kinds of fixed data cannot all exist.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item A smooth integral complete-intersection flag ending in a curve
$C$, of successive divisor classes $l_iH$ for positive integers $l_i$,
with $\mu_{\min}(\Omega_W^1|_C)\ge0$.
\item On $Z_W=\PP(\cO(S)_1\oplus\cO(S)_2)\to W\times W$,
in the symmetric-power convention, put $M=L_1+L_2+q\xi$.
For some integer $k_0>0$ with $k_0L$ Cartier, finitely many sections of
$k_0M$ surject onto
$\cO_{Z_W,z_*}/\mathfrak m_{z_*}^{(2n+2)k_0+1}$ after
trivialization at a smooth torus point $z_*$.
\item A point $x\in W$, the blowup $\pi_x:\widehat W\to W$
with exceptional divisor $J_x$, and a curve class
$\gamma=f_*(A_1\cdots A_{n-1})$, where
$f:V\to\widehat W$ is a fixed birational morphism from a smooth
integral projective variety and the $A_i$ are ample Cartier divisors,
such that $J_x\gamma>0$ and
\[
 \pi_x^*(L+K_W/2+\lambda S)\gamma
 \le40\epsilon J_x\gamma\qquad(0\le\lambda\le q).
\]
It suffices to check the two endpoint inequalities.
\end{enumerate}
No nefness of $L,S,K_W$ is assumed, and $z_*$ need not lie over $x$.
All divisors, the flag, the point, the curve representative, and the
finite jet sections are fixed over $\C$ before the residual
characteristic varies.

title: Frobenius Structures on Tame Hecke Eigensheaves
abstract: We construct nonzero perverse Weil Hecke eigensheaves for SLn with Borel level at one marked point, after a finite extension of the field of constants. The parameter is a geometrically dense arithmetic PGLn-local system with tame regular-unipotent monodromy on a once-punctured curve of genus at least two over a finite field of characteristic p > n. The full multi-leg eigenstructure is Frobenius compatible with the prescribed arithmetic eigenvalue, and the geometric sheaf has parabolic nilpotent singular support.

tex.abstract:
We construct nonzero perverse Weil Hecke eigensheaves for $\SL_n$ with Borel
level at one marked point, after a finite extension of the field of constants.
The parameter is a geometrically dense arithmetic $\PGL_n$-local system with
tame regular-unipotent monodromy on a once-punctured curve of genus at least
two over a finite field of characteristic $p>n$. The full multi-leg
eigenstructure is Frobenius compatible with the prescribed arithmetic
eigenvalue, and the geometric sheaf has parabolic nilpotent singular support.
sections: Arithmetic towers and equivariant gluing at a node
From the separating node to an equivariant flag eigensheaf

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $n\geq2$, let $\F_q$ have characteristic $p>n$, let $\ell\ne p$,
and put $E=\E$. Let $X_0/\F_q$ be a smooth projective geometrically
connected curve of genus at least two, with $x_0\in X_0(\F_q)$, and
put $U_0=X_0\setminus\{x_0\}$. Suppose
\[
 \rho:\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(U_0)\longrightarrow\PGL_n(L)
\]
is continuous for a finite extension $L/\Q_\ell$, its geometric
restriction is Zariski dense, and its inertia at $x_0$ kills wild inertia
and has the form
\begin{equation}
 \rho(\gamma)=\exp\bigl(t_\ell(\gamma)N\bigr)
\end{equation}
for a regular nilpotent $N$. Here a choice of compatible
$\ell$-power roots of unity identifies the tame quotient
$\Z_\ell(1)$ with $\Z_\ell$ and defines $t_\ell$.

There are an integer $m\geq1$ and a nonzero $E$-adic Weil sheaf $M_0$ on
\[
 \Bun_{\SL_n,B,x_0}(X_0)_{\F_{q^m}}
\]
whose geometric pullback $M$ is locally constructible perverse and has
singular support in $\Lambda_{\mathrm{par}}$. If $\rho_m$ denotes the
restriction of $\rho$ to $\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(U_{0,\F_{q^m}})$, then
for every finite set $I$ and every family
$V_i\in\Rep_E(\PGL_n)$ there are isomorphisms of Weil sheaves
\begin{equation}
 \Hecke_{I,\boldsymbol V}(M_0)
   \simeq M_0\boxtimes\bigboxtimes_{i\in I}(V_i)_{\rho_m}.
\end{equation}
They are natural in the representations and coherent for the unit,
convolution, permutations, and all fusion diagonals.

statements.title: Geometric specialization and transport
statements.label: prop:equivariant-specialization
statements.text:
In this setup, geometric nearby cycles preserve local bounded
constructibility and are perverse exact. They admit natural isomorphisms
\begin{equation}
 \Hecke^s_{I,\boldsymbol V}(\Psi F)
  \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
  \Psi\bigl(\Hecke^{\bar\eta}_{I,\boldsymbol V}(F)\bigr)
\end{equation}
compatible with the unit, convolution, permutations, and every fusion
diagonal. Suppose $F$ has a coherent eigenstructure with parameter
$\vartheta_{\bar\eta}$. For each representation, suppose its evaluation
sheaf has a lisse lattice whose finite reductions extend lisse after
finite trait extensions, compatibly on further extensions and with the
reductions of a special-fiber tensor system $\vartheta_s$. Then $\Psi F$
has a coherent eigenstructure with eigenvalue $\vartheta_s$.

If the models, $F$ with its given coherent eigenstructure, and these
tensor-specialization data carry a semilinear generator, with a
compatible lift to $\bar\eta$, all the
comparisons and the resulting eigenstructure are equivariant. For the
finite-stage lattice models one may use compatible invariant trait
extensions. No single finite extension is required for all reductions.

statements.label: prop:equivariant-unramified
statements.text:
Let $C$ be a smooth projective connected curve of genus at least two over
an algebraically closed field $K$ of characteristic zero.  Let $f$ be a
semilinear automorphism of $C$ with an ample line bundle $\mathcal L$
and an isomorphism $f^*\mathcal L\simeq\mathcal L$.  Let $G=\SL_n$
and $\Gd=\PGL_n$.  Suppose that $\tau$ is a continuous $\Gd$-local system
on $C$, defined over a finite extension of $\Q_\ell$, with Zariski-dense
image and an isomorphism $u:f^*\tau\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau$.

There is a nonzero locally bounded constructible complex $D_\tau$ on
$\Bun_G(C)$, with nilpotent singular support, a full coherent Hecke
eigenstructure of eigenvalue $\tau$, and an isomorphism
\[
                 b:f^*D_\tau\xrightarrow{\sim}D_\tau
\]
compatible with that eigenstructure and $u$.  The object $D_\tau$ is compact
in the automorphic nilpotent category.  The eigenstructure uses the
relative Satake normalization of Section~\ref{sec:conventions} and is
compatible with unit, convolution, permutations, and every fusion
diagonal.  The isomorphisms $b$ and $u$ define compatible actions of
$\Z$ on the eigencomplex and its eigenvalue.

statements.label: prop:lifted-parameter
statements.text:
The arithmetic representation $\rho$ determines a continuous
parameter
\[
 \sigma_1:\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}((U_1)_{\Dbar})
             \longrightarrow\PGL_n(L')
\]
for a finite coefficient extension $L'/L$, together with equivariance
under $\varphi$, with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item Its geometric image is Zariski dense.  After compatible choices
of frames it is the same compact subgroup as
$\rho(\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(U_{0,k}))$.
\item Its boundary homomorphism is
\begin{equation}
 \gamma\longmapsto\exp(t_\ell(\gamma)N_1),
\end{equation}
where $N_1$ is regular nilpotent.  Every prime factor of
characteristic-zero inertia other than $\ell$ acts trivially.
\item In compatible frames at the coordinate-neutralized root gerbes
of $x_1$, the equivariance has a single value
$A\in H_0$, where $H_0=\rho(\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(U_0))$, and
\begin{equation}
                    \Ad(A)N_1=qN_1.
\end{equation}
\item For every algebraic representation of $\PGL_n$, the associated
local system over $(U_1)_K$ admits an invariant lattice whose finite
reductions extend lisse over $\mathscr U_R$, equivariantly under
$\varphi$.  Their specializations recover the tensor local system of
$\rho$, including its given arithmetic action.
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: Arithmetic towers and equivariant gluing at a node

statements.label: prop:nodal-parameter
statements.text:
There exists a continuous Zariski-dense parameter
\[
              \tau:\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(C)\longrightarrow J
                      \subset\PGL_n(L')
\]
with equivariance under $\varphi$.  For every algebraic representation
of $\PGL_n$, an invariant lattice in its evaluation local system has
finite reductions extending lisse over
$\mathcal V\times_{S_{b_*}}S_{b_r}$ for sufficiently large $r$.
These extensions are equivariant and specialize on the two punctured
components to $\sigma_1$ and $\sigma_2$, with their given actions,
compatibly with the entire tensor system.
statements.section_title: Arithmetic towers and equivariant gluing at a node

statements.label: prop:charzero-equivariant
statements.text:
Let $(C_1,x_1)/D$, $\sigma_1$, and $\varphi$ be the pointed curve,
dense lifted parameter, and semilinear automorphism of
Proposition~\ref{prop:lifted-parameter}.  There exist an integer
$m\geq 1$ and a nonzero locally constructible perverse geometric
$\E$-adic sheaf
\[
 M_{\Dbar}\quad\text{on}\quad
 \mathcal A_1=\Bun_{G,B,x_1}((C_1)_{\Dbar})
\]
with a $\varphi^m$-structure and the full coherent Hecke eigenstructure
for $\sigma_1$.  Every eigenisomorphism is compatible with this
structure and with the given $\varphi^m$-structure on $\sigma_1$.
Moreover, $\SS(M_{\Dbar})\subset\Lambda_{\mathrm{par}}$.

title: From critical crossings to quenched near-critical universality in Voronoi percolation
abstract: Taking Cardy's crossing formula for critical Poisson–Voronoi percolation as an input, we prove a universal joint limit for the near-critical crossing thresholds of rational polygonal quadrilaterals under the monotone coupling. Conditional on the Poisson tessellation, the threshold law converges in probability over tessellations to the same law as on the triangular lattice. Each model is normalized by its own expected number of color-pivotal sites for a unit-square crossing.

tex.abstract:
Taking Cardy's crossing formula for critical Poisson--Voronoi
percolation as an input, we prove a universal joint limit for the
near-critical crossing thresholds of rational polygonal quadrilaterals
under the monotone coupling. Conditional on the Poisson tessellation,
the threshold law converges in probability over tessellations to the same
law as on the triangular lattice. Each model is normalized by its own
expected number of color-pivotal sites for a unit-square crossing.

statements.title: Scalar critical Cardy formula
statements.label: hyp:cardy

statements.title: Quenched near-critical universality
statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Assume Hypothesis~\ref{hyp:cardy}. The expectations in
\eqref{eq:requested-scales} are finite and strictly positive for every
mesh, and both scales tend to zero as their mesh tends to zero.
There is a probability measure $\nu_\triangle$ on $\mathcal K$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \Law(\tau_\delta^\triangle)\Longrightarrow\nu_\triangle
 \qquad(\delta\downarrow0).
 
\end{equation}
For the independently normalized Voronoi model,
\begin{equation}
 d_{\mathrm{BL}}\bigl(\Law(\tau_\varepsilon^V\mid\eta_\varepsilon),
                 \nu_\triangle\bigr)
 \xrightarrow[\varepsilon\downarrow0]{\PP}0.
 
\end{equation}
The conditional law averages all color marks and no geometry.

statements.title: Quenched scalar Cardy convergence
statements.label: prop:quenched-cardy
statements.text:
For every fixed polygon quad $Q$,
\[
 \PP^{\eta_e}(C_Q)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Cardy}(Q)
 \quad\text{in probability over the Poisson geometry}.
\]
The assertion holds simultaneously for every member of any fixed
finite collection of polygon quads.
statements.section_title: Critical estimates and their geometric consequences

statements.title: Chordal exploration convergence
statements.label: prop:chordal
statements.text:
Let graph disks on a deterministic sequence as above approximate a
bounded Jordan domain $D$, with switches converging to distinct boundary
points $a,b$.  Give their interiors independent fair colors and their
two boundary arcs the prescribed opposite colors.  The exploration from
$a$ to $b$ converges in law, in the curve metric, to chordal
$\mathrm{SLE}_6$ in $D$ from $a$ to $b$.  This conclusion holds for every
such converging sequence of disks and marks.

statements.title: Oriented loop convergence
statements.label: prop:loops
statements.text:
In a Jordan disk with monochromatic boundary, along every
deterministic sequence of tilings under consideration, the
critical interface loops converge to the Camia--Newman
$\mathrm{SLE}_6$ loop construction.  For each positive cutoff
chosen outside the atoms of limiting loop diameters, the loops
above that cutoff can be matched in the curve metric, including
their orientation, multiplicity, and order of excursions.
There are no surplus macroscopic loops.  The convergence holds
jointly for any finite number of independent color replicas
on the same fixed geometry.

statements.title: Joint critical tests with prescribed squares
statements.label: prop:critical-tests
statements.text:
Fix finitely many polygon quads and finitely many closed squares of positive
side length, with the squares mutually separated and separated from every
quad boundary. For any finite collection of test specifications, the joint
law of their exact closed-cell crossing indicators has a common limit along
every deterministic good sequence of either model. The limit is continuous
in the centers and positive side lengths of the squares throughout the open
range where the stated separations hold, and under sufficiently small marked
polygonal deformations of the quads. The conclusion remains valid when the
centers and side lengths converge to such an admissible fixed configuration
as the mesh tends to zero.

For Poisson--Voronoi percolation the conditional law given $\eta_e$ converges
in probability, in total variation on this finite Boolean space, to the
same deterministic limiting law. With any fixed number of conditionally
independent fair-color replicas on one Poisson geometry, the limiting law
is that of independent copies of the same critical configuration, with all
the prescribed tests performed in their specified replicas. In particular,
two replicas sharing their geometry have the same joint critical limit as
two independent triangular replicas.

statements.title: Uniform bound for the site expansion
statements.label: prop:expansion-bound
statements.text:
Fix a box $B$, finitely many polygonal crossing tests, and $R\leq2$
replica labels.  Let $g\in(1,2)$ be an exponent in the lower four-arm
bound of Lemma~\ref{lem:arm-inputs}.  There is a constant $C$, depending
only on this data, such that, for every $k\geq1$, every choice of
nonempty $I_i$, and centered weights $w_{i,r}$,
\begin{equation}
 \frac{(m_eq_e)^k}{k!}
   \int_{B^k_{\ne}}
       |K_e(F;\mathbf x,\mathbf I,\mathbf w)|
                    \,d\sigma_e^{\otimes k}(\mathbf x)
 \leq C^k k^{-(1-g/2)k}
             \prod_{i,r\in I_i}\|w_{i,r}\|_{\TV},
 
\end{equation}
uniformly for all sufficiently small meshes and all $|F|\leq1$ of the
specified crossing indicators.  Consequently the absolute sum in
\eqref{eq:site-expansion} is bounded by
$\sum_{k\geq1}C_T^k k^{-(1-g/2)k}<\infty$ when all times have absolute
value at most $T$.  For two replicas, the total absolute contribution
of terms with $|I_i|=2$ for at least one $i$ is $O_T(q_e)$.
statements.section_title: An absolutely convergent expansion in sites

statements.title: Signed relative replacement
statements.label: prop:replacement
statements.text:
Under the preceding assumptions, fix the types $t_2,\ldots,t_k$ and put
\[
 K_s=K_e^{(s,t_2,\ldots,t_k)}(F;\boldsymbol x,\boldsymbol w),\qquad
 K_d=K_e^{(d,t_2,\ldots,t_k)}(F;\boldsymbol x,\boldsymbol w),\qquad
 P_e=\prod_{i=2}^k \gamma_e(t_i).
\]
The empty product is $1$.  In either model,
\begin{equation}
 \lim_{h\downarrow0}\limsup_{e\downarrow0}
 \sup_{\boldsymbol x}
 \frac{|K_sD_e(h)-K_dS_e|}{P_e a_e a_{e,h}}=0.
 
\end{equation}
The supremum is over the fixed compact separated range, restricted to
lattice sites in the triangular model; in Poisson insertion integrals,
null general-position exceptions are omitted.  The assertion is uniform
for bounded total variations of the centered weights.
statements.section_title: Replacing a site by a mesoscopic square

statements.title: Common finite-time crossing limits
statements.label: prop:nearcritical-tests
statements.text:
Choose finitely many quads in $\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{rat}}$ and finitely
many real parameters. Their jointly coupled crossing indicators,
with the prescribed scales $r_e$, have a limiting law common to the
two models. The assertion holds for one color replica and for two
independent color replicas conditional on the same geometry.
Every such limiting probability is continuous in the real parameter
vector, and the convergence remains valid for convergent parameter
vectors.

title: From partial permutation information to Fourier bounds
abstract: We show how information about partial permutations controls full permutation laws. Let n tend to infinity through multiples of eight. If the images of a uniformly chosen \(7n/8\) labels approach the uniform injection law in average total variation, and the sign mean tends to zero, then the product of two independent permutations with the given law converges to uniform on Sn.

tex.abstract: We show how information about partial permutations controls full permutation laws. Let $n$ tend to infinity through multiples of eight. If the images of a uniformly chosen $7n/8$ labels approach the uniform injection law in average total variation, and the sign mean tends to zero, then the product of two independent permutations with the given law converges to uniform on $S_n$.

statements.title: Complementary cosets control Fourier matrices
statements.label: l:main

statements.title: Fourier amplification
statements.label: l:amplification
statements.text:
Let $\mu_n$ be probabilities on $S_n$ with $\widehat\mu_n(\sgn)=o(1)$. Suppose either $f_n$ is a nonnegative subprobability with $f_n\le\mu_n$ and mass tending to one, or $f_n$ is a probability with $\|f_n-\mu_n\|_{\TV}=o(1)$. If, uniformly for every irreducible of degree $D>1$,
\[
 \|\widehat f_n\|_{\op}\le A D^{-\beta},
\]
where $A,\beta>0$ are fixed, then $\|\mu_n^{*r}-U\|_{\TV}\to0$ for every fixed integer $r$ with $2-2r\beta<0$.
If instead $\|\widehat f_n\|_{\HS}^2\le A D^{-\gamma}$, the sufficient condition is $1-r\gamma<0$.
statements.section_title: Degree sums, common trimming, and normalization

statements.title: Orbit-span transfer
statements.label: l:orbit-span
statements.text:
Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{l:main}, for every $u>0$,
\[
 \|\widehat f(\rho)\|_{\op}\le\sqrt{bBC_u}\,D^{-1/2+(u+2)/(2b)}.
\]
statements.section_title: The complete transfer from disjoint coset systems

statements.title: Four convolutions by the orbit argument
statements.label: l:orbit-completion
statements.text:
Let $n\to\infty$ through multiples of eight. Suppose probabilities $\mu_n$ on $S_n$ have sign mean $o(1)$ and
\[
 \E_{|M|=n/8}\|\mu_{n,H_M}-U_{G/H_M}\|_{\TV}=o(1).
\]
Then $\|\mu_n^{*4}-U_G\|_{\TV}\to0$.
statements.section_title: The complete transfer from disjoint coset systems

statements.title: Isotypic transfer
statements.label: l:isotypic
statements.text:
Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{l:main},
\[
 \|\widehat f(\rho)\|_{\HS}^2\le bBC_uD^{-1+(u+2)/b}.
\]
In fact the right side can be multiplied by $f(G)$.
statements.section_title: The complete transfer from disjoint coset systems

statements.title: Two convolutions from eight complements
statements.label: l:isotypic-completion
statements.text: Under the hypotheses of Corollary~\ref{l:orbit-completion}, $\|\mu_n^{*2}-U_G\|_{\TV}\to0$.
statements.section_title: The complete transfer from disjoint coset systems

statements.title: Coefficient-evaluation transfer
statements.label: l:coefficient-operator
statements.text:
For every $u>0$ and irreducible $\rho$ of degree $D$,
\[
 \|\widehat f(\rho)\|_{\op}\le\sqrt{bBC_u}\,D^{-1/2+(u+2)/(2b)}.
\]
statements.section_title: Coefficient spaces and finer fixed-partition estimates

statements.title: Coefficient and character Hilbert--Schmidt transfers
statements.label: l:coefficient-lift
statements.section_title: Coefficient spaces and finer fixed-partition estimates

statements.title: Low-type central-projector estimates
statements.label: l:central-projector-operator
statements.text:
Let $\eta$ be a probability satisfying the coset caps of this section. Let $P_i$ select its $H_i$-types of degree at most $D^{1/b}$ and put $R_i=\sum_{\dim\tau\le D^{1/b}}(\dim\tau)^2$. Then
\[
 \|\widehat\eta(\rho)P_i\|_{\op}\le BD^{-1/2}R_i,
 \qquad D\|\widehat\eta(\rho)P_i\|_{\HS}^2\le B^2R_i.
\]
Consequently
\begin{align*}
 \|\widehat\eta(\rho)\|_{\op}&\le BC_u\sqrt b\,D^{-1/2+(u+2)/b},\\
 \|\widehat\eta(\rho)\|_{\op}&\le B\sqrt{bC_u}\,D^{-1/2+(u+2)/(2b)}.
\end{align*}
statements.section_title: Coefficient spaces and finer fixed-partition estimates

statements.title: Branching refinement
statements.label: l:branching-hs
statements.text:
For an irreducible $\rho_\lambda$ of degree $D$, the disjoint-block caps give
\[
 \|\widehat f(\rho_\lambda)\|_{\HS}^2\le BbM(k_\lambda)D^{-1+2/b}.
\]
The blocks may have unequal sizes.
statements.section_title: Coefficient spaces and finer fixed-partition estimates

statements.title: Random-partition lift
statements.label: l:random-partition
statements.text:
Let $n$ tend to infinity through multiples of a fixed integer $q>3$,
and let $\mu$ be probability laws on $S_n$.  For a uniform
$n/q$-subset $C$, put $H_C=\Sym(C)$, fixing its complement pointwise.
Suppose
\[
 \mathbb E_C\|\mu_{H_C}-(U_G)_{H_C}\|_{\TV}=o(1),
 \qquad \widehat\mu(\sgn)=0.
\]
There is a conditional probability law $\nu$ with
$\|\nu-\mu\|_{\TV}=o(1)$ such that, for every irreducible $\rho$
of degree $D$,
\begin{equation}
 \|\widehat\nu(\rho)\|_{\op}
 \le \frac2M\sqrt{2qC_1}\,D^{-(1-3/q)/2},
\end{equation}
where $M=1-o(1)$ is the retained mass and $C_1$ is from
Lemma~\ref{l:degree-basic}.  In particular for $q=8$,
$\|\mu^{*8}-U_G\|_{\TV}=o(1)$.

statements.title: Every positive inverse power
statements.label: l:degree-all-powers

statements.title: Character-projection transfer
statements.label: l:character-lift
statements.text:
Let $H_i=\Sym(M_i)\le S_n$, $1\le i\le b$, for disjoint nonempty
sets $M_i$.  Let $f\ge0$ have mass $z\le1$ and suppose
\[
 f(gH_i)\le\frac B{[S_n:H_i]}
       \quad(g\in S_n,\ 1\le i\le b).
\]
For every irreducible $\rho$ of degree $D$,
\begin{equation}
 \|\widehat f(\rho)\|_{\HS}^2
 \le BzbC_1D^{-1+1026/b},
\end{equation}
where $C_1=\sup_{m\ge1}\sum_{\tau\in\Irr(S_m)}d_\tau^{-1}$.
More generally, if $a\ge0$ and every type of every $H_i$ has a one-dimensional
subcharacter of index at most $d_\tau^a$, the exponent $1026/b$
in \eqref{l:character-lift-bound} may be replaced by $(a+2)/b$.
statements.section_title: One-dimensional characters in subgroups of controlled index

statements.title: Joint-type orbit transfer
statements.label: l:joint-type-operator
statements.section_title: Joint restriction types and multiplication on two sides

statements.title: Four-block transfer
statements.label: l:four-block-reservoir
statements.text:
Partition $n$ points into four sets of size $n/4$, and let $H_i$
permute those sets.  For all sufficiently large such $n$, every
subprobability $f$ with $f(gH_i)\le2/[S_n:H_i]$ satisfies
\[
 \|\widehat f(\lambda)\|_{\op}\le D_\lambda^{-1/8}
       \qquad(D_\lambda>1).
\]
statements.section_title: Joint restriction types and multiplication on two sides

statements.title: Eight-block transfer
statements.label: l:eight-block-probe
statements.text:
Partition $n$ points into eight sets of size $n/8$, and let $H_i$
permute those sets.  For all sufficiently large such $n$, every
subprobability $f$ with $f(gH_i)\le2/[S_n:H_i]$ satisfies
\[
 \|\widehat f(\lambda)\|_{\op}\le D_\lambda^{-1/4}
       \qquad(D_\lambda>1).
\]
statements.section_title: Joint restriction types and multiplication on two sides

statements.title: Two-sided Fourier multiplication
statements.label: l:two-sided
statements.section_title: Joint restriction types and multiplication on two sides

statements.title: Two-factor completion
statements.label: l:two-sided-completion
statements.text:
Fix $b>4$ and finite constants $B_L,B_R$.  Suppose probabilities
$\mu_n,\nu_n$ on $S_n$ dominate subprobabilities
$\alpha_n,\beta_n$, respectively, whose masses tend to one and
which satisfy \eqref{l:two-sided-caps} for $b$ disjoint nonempty
blocks.  If
$\widehat\nu_n(\sgn)\widehat\mu_n(\sgn)\to0$, then
\[
 \|\nu_n*\mu_n-U_{S_n}\|_{\TV}\longrightarrow0.
\]
In particular this applies to a single law with small sign mean
when separate subprobabilities supply its two cap orientations.
statements.section_title: Joint restriction types and multiplication on two sides

statements.title: Sixteen equivariant subkernels
statements.label: l:equivariant-sixteen
statements.text:
Consider a sequence of the preceding state spaces and partitions with
$\min_i m_i\to\infty$.  Let $K$ be a doubly stochastic,
$H$-equivariant kernel.  Suppose that, for every $i$,
\begin{equation}
 \frac1{L_i}\sum_{a\in X_i}
 \frac12\sum_{b\in X_i}|q_i(a,b)-L_i^{-1}|\le\delta,
 
\end{equation}
where $\delta\to0$.  Choose $\varepsilon\to0$ with
$\delta/\varepsilon\to0$, form the kernels
\eqref{l:sixteen-cutoff}, and assume also that
\begin{equation}
 \beta_i:=\|T_i^{\mathrm{sgn}}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2\longrightarrow0
 \qquad(1\le i\le16).
 
\end{equation}
Then
\[
 \frac1{|\Omega|}\sum_{x\in\Omega}
       \|K^{16}(x,\cdot)-U_\Omega(x,\cdot)\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
If $K$ is equivariant under a transitive group of permutations of
$\Omega$, the same conclusion holds for the maximum over starting
states.

More precisely, put $T=T_1\cdots T_{16}$.  For a product type
$\boldsymbol\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_{16})$, set
$f_i=\dim\alpha_i$ and $D=\prod_i f_i$.  If
$T_{i,\boldsymbol\alpha}$ is the operator on its full
$H$-multiplicity space, then
\begin{equation}
 \|T_{i,\boldsymbol\alpha}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2
       \le(1+\varepsilon)\frac{f_i^2}{D},\qquad
 D\|T_{1,\boldsymbol\alpha}\cdots
             T_{16,\boldsymbol\alpha}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2
       \le(1+\varepsilon)^{16}D^{-13}.
 
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Equivariant kernels and their multiplicity spaces

statements.title: Three-group two-sided truncation
statements.label: l:three-group
statements.text:
Consider a sequence of kernels \eqref{l:three-convolution-kernel}
satisfying \eqref{l:three-bistochastic}, with
$\min_i m_i\to\infty$.  Suppose $\delta\to0$ and, for every $i$,
\begin{align}
 \sum_{s',h_{-i}}|q_i(s,s',h_{-i})-M_i^{-1}|&\le2\delta
                                      &&(s\in\mathcal S),\\
 \sum_{s,h_{-i}}|q_i(s,s',h_{-i})-M_i^{-1}|&\le2\delta
                                      &&(s'\in\mathcal S).
\end{align}
Let $\chi(h)=\prod_{i=1}^3\mathrm{sgn}(h_i)$, and assume that the
untrimmed all-sign matrix
\[
 A_\chi(s,s')=\sum_{h\in H}p_{s,s'}(h)\chi(h^{-1})
\]
has absolute row and column sums at most $a$, where $a\to0$.
Then $K^{15}$ mixes in average row total variation:
\[
 \frac1{|\Omega|}\sum_x
       \|K^{15}(x,\cdot)-U_\Omega(x,\cdot)\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
The maximum row distance also tends to zero if $K$ is equivariant
under a transitive group of permutations of $\Omega$.

Specifically, retain the fibers
\begin{equation}
 \widetilde p_{s,s'}(h)=p_{s,s'}(h)
     \prod_{i=1}^3\mathbf1\{q_i(s,s',h_{-i})\le2/M_i\},
 
\end{equation}
and let $\widetilde K$ be the corresponding kernel.  At most
$6\delta$ mass is removed from every row and column.  For an
irreducible product type $\rho=\rho_1\otimes\rho_2\otimes\rho_3$,
put $D_i=\dim\rho_i$ and $D=\prod_iD_i$.  Its multiplicity matrix
is the $M$ by $M$ block matrix
\begin{equation}
 B_\rho(s,s')=\sum_{h\in H}\widetilde p_{s,s'}(h)\rho(h^{-1}),
 
\end{equation}
with blocks of size $D$ by $D$, and it satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \|B_\rho\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2
       \le4\frac{D_i}{\prod_{j\ne i}D_j}\quad(1\le i\le3),
 \qquad
 D\|B_\rho^{15}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2\le2^{30}D^{-4}.
 
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Equivariant kernels and their multiplicity spaces

statements.title: Spectral pruning
statements.label: l:spectral-pruning
statements.text:
Let $n\to\infty$ through multiples of $16$. For each $n$, partition
$[n]$ into $b=16$ equal blocks $R_i$, and let $\mu_n$ be a probability
on $S_n$ satisfying
\[
 \|(\mu_n)_{-R_i}-U_{-R_i}\|_{\TV}\le\delta_n
 \quad(1\le i\le16),\qquad \delta_n\longrightarrow0.
\]
There is a nonnegative measure $0\le\nu_n\le\mu_n$ of mass
$1-\gamma_n$, with $\gamma_n\to0$, such that
\[
 \|\widehat\nu_n(\rho)\|_{\op}\le D^{-1/8}
 \quad\text{for every irreducible $\rho$ of degree $D>1$}.
\]
The operator bound has constant one, and $\nu_n$ is not normalized.
statements.section_title: Selecting coefficient tests and omitted sets

statements.title: Omitted-set transfer
statements.label: l:omitted-set-transfer
statements.text:
Let $n\to\infty$ through multiples of $1024$, and let $\mu_n$ be
probabilities on $S_n$ such that
\[
 \delta_n=\E_{|R|=n/1024}
       \|(\mu_n)_{-R}-U_{-R}\|_{\TV}\longrightarrow0.
\]
For all sufficiently large $n$, condition $\mu_n$ on the event $E$
of Lemma~\ref{l:adaptive-domain-preparation}, obtaining $\nu_n$.
Then $\|\nu_n-\mu_n\|_{\TV}\le16\delta_n$, and there is an absolute
$C$ such that every irreducible representation $\rho$ of degree $D>1$
satisfies
\[
 \|\widehat\nu_n(\rho)\|_{\op}\le CD^{-1/4}.
\]
If in addition $\E_{\mu_n}\sgn(g)=o(1)$, then
$\|\mu_n^{*8}-U_n\|_{\TV}\to0$.
statements.section_title: Selecting coefficient tests and omitted sets

statements.title: Random-domain transfer
statements.label: l:domain-transfer
statements.text:
Let $n\to\infty$ through multiples of $256$, and let $\mu_n$ be
probabilities on $S_n$ satisfying
\[
 \delta_n=\E_{|R|=n/256}
       \|(\mu_n)_{-R}-U_{-R}\|_{\TV}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Condition on the event that at least $7/8$ of the sets $R$ satisfy
$\mu_n(gH_R)\le2/[S_n:H_R]$, and call the resulting law $\nu_n$.
For all sufficiently large $n$ it is defined, satisfies
$\|\nu_n-\mu_n\|_{\TV}\le16\delta_n$, and obeys
\[
 \|\widehat\nu_n(\rho)\|_{\op}\le CD^{-1/8}
 \qquad(D=\dim\rho>1)
\]
with an absolute $C$. If $\E_{\mu_n}\sgn(g)=o(1)$, then
$\|\mu_n^{*32}-U_n\|_{\TV}\to0$.
The averaged relative-entropy hypothesis
\[
 \E_{|R|=n/256}D((\mu_n)_{-R}\|U_{-R})=o(1)
\]
is sufficient for these conclusions.
statements.section_title: Selecting coefficient tests and omitted sets

statements.title: Arbitrary-tilt entropy transfer
statements.label: l:tilted-entropy
statements.section_title: Entropy comparisons for every change of measure

statements.title: Signed-palette transfer
statements.label: l:palette-transfer
statements.text:
Let $n$ tend to infinity through even integers.  For each $n$, partition
$[n]=A\sqcup B$ into equal halves and let $\mu$ be a probability on
$S_n$.  Suppose that $\varepsilon_n\to0$ and that, for every palette
on either half, every placement of its classes, its subgroup $H$, and
every $x\in S_n$,
\begin{equation}
 \mu(xH)\le [S_n:H]^{-1}
            \exp\{v\mathcal H(p)+\varepsilon_n\}.
 
\end{equation}
Here $\delta$ and $v$ satisfy \eqref{l:palette-delta}.  For all
sufficiently large $n$, uniformly over
$\lambda\notin\{(n),(1^n)\}$,
\begin{align}
 \|\widehat\mu(\lambda)\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2
 &\le D_\lambda^{-1/3},\\
 \|\widehat\mu(\lambda)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 &\le D_\lambda^{-1/6}.
 
\end{align}
If in addition $|\widehat\mu(\mathrm{sgn})|=o(1)$, then
$\|\mu^{*4}-U_{S_n}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=o(1)$, and consequently
$\|\mu^{*30}-U_{S_n}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=o(1)$ as well.
Both conclusions also hold with $\mu$ replaced in every factor
by a probability $\mu_0$ satisfying
$\|\mu_0-\mu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=o(1)$.

statements.title: Entropy clipping and isotypic transfer
statements.label: l:replica-clipping
statements.text:
Partition $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ into $q\ge1$ nonempty blocks, and let
$H_i$ be the subgroup supported on block $i$.  Suppose a probability
$w$ on $S_n$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{i=1}^qD(w_{H_i}\Vert U_{G/H_i})\le K.
\end{equation}
For every $t>0$ there is a subprobability $v\le w$, of mass $m$,
such that
\begin{align}
 1-m&\le\frac{K+q/e}{t},\\
 v(gH_i)&\le e^t\frac{|H_i|}{|G|}\quad(g\in G,\ 1\le i\le q),
 \\
 \sum_{h\in H_i}(\check v*v)(h)
 &\le e^t\frac{|H_i|}{|G|},\\
 \|\widehat v(\lambda)\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2
 &\le qC_u e^tD_\lambda^{-1+(u+2)/q}
        \quad(\lambda\vdash n, u>0).
 
\end{align}
Here $\check v(g)=v(g^{-1})$, $C_u$ is the constant in
Theorem~\ref{l:degree-all-powers}, the Fourier transform is the mass
transform $\widehat v(\lambda)=\sum_gv(g)\rho_\lambda(g)$, and
the Hilbert--Schmidt norm is unnormalized.
statements.section_title: Entropy clipping and large representation dimensions

statements.title: Selecting complementary lists by averaging
statements.label: l:replica-partition-selection
statements.text:
Let $q$ divide $n$, put $r=n/q$, and suppose the image law $w_I$ of
a uniformly chosen ordered list $I$ of $n-r$ distinct inputs satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E_I D(w_I\Vert U_I)\le K_0,
\]
where $U_I$ is uniform on ordered distinct output lists of that length.
There is a partition into $q$ blocks of size $r$ for which
\eqref{l:replica-entropy-assumption} holds with $K=qK_0$.
statements.section_title: Entropy clipping and large representation dimensions

statements.title: The logarithmic cutoff with 256 blocks
statements.label: l:replica-large-dimension
statements.text:
Let $n=2^d$ and suppose, for each sufficiently large integer $d$, that
a probability $w$ has an equal partition into $q=256$ blocks with
total complement entropy $O(d^4)$.  There is $v\le w$ of mass
$1-O(d^{-2})$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \|\widehat v(\lambda)\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2
 \le256 C_{32}e^{d^6}D_\lambda^{-1+34/256}.
\end{equation}
In particular, whenever $\log D_\lambda>d^8$, this is at most
$D_\lambda^{-1/2}$ for all sufficiently large $d$, uniformly in
$\lambda$.
statements.section_title: Entropy clipping and large representation dimensions

statements.title: Sixteen groups in the large-degree range
statements.label: l:forest-bulk
statements.section_title: Weak entropy and an independent sparse estimate

statements.title: Entropy and sparse-degree hybrid
statements.label: l:forest-hybrid
statements.text:
Let $n\to\infty$ through multiples of $16$.
For each $n$, let $\mu$ and $K$ be probabilities on $S_n$.
Suppose a fixed equal sixteen-block partition satisfies
\eqref{l:forest-entropy-hyp} for $\mu$.  Suppose also that $K$ satisfies
\begin{align}
 \|\widehat K(\lambda)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 &\le n^{-k/10}
 &&\left(1\le k=n-\lambda_1\le n^{1/20}\right),
 \\
 \widehat K(\lambda)&=0
 &&\left(\lambda'_1>n/2\right).
 
\end{align}
Then the retained probability $\nu$ from
Lemma~\ref{l:forest-clipping} satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \|\nu^{*12}*K^{*40}-U_{S_n}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=o(1),
 \qquad
 \|\mu^{*12}*K^{*40}-U_{S_n}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=o(1).
 
\end{equation}
All factors in these convolutions are independent.  There is no assumed
identity between $K$ and a convolution root or power of $\mu$.
statements.section_title: Weak entropy and an independent sparse estimate

statements.title: Conditional-product transfer
statements.label: l:tabloid-product
statements.text:
Put $C_0=2{,}000{,}000$, and fix an integer $L\ge 2C_0$.
Let $V=A\sqcup C$, where $|A|=|C|=h$ and $L$ divides $h$.
Partition each half into $L$ buffers of size $h/L$, and put
$H=S_A\times S_C\subseteq S_V$.
Let $\xi$ be a subprobability on $S_V$ such that, for $J=A,C$ and
every ordered injection $\mathbf v:J\longrightarrow V$,
\begin{equation}
 \xi\{x:x^{-1}|_J=\mathbf v\}
 \le 2U_V\{x:x^{-1}|_J=\mathbf v\}.
 
\end{equation}
Let $Z$ have any probability distribution.  Measurably in $z$, let
$t_z\in S_V$ and let $\nu_A^z,\nu_C^z$ be subprobabilities on
$S_A,S_C$, respectively.  Suppose that for almost every $z$, each
$J=A,C$, each of its
buffers $B$, and every ordered injection
$\mathbf w:J\setminus B\longrightarrow J$,
\begin{equation}
 \nu_J^z\{y:y|_{J\setminus B}=\mathbf w\}
 \le 2U_J\{y:y|_{J\setminus B}=\mathbf w\}.
 
\end{equation}
Regard the product $\nu_A^z\otimes\nu_C^z$ as a measure on $H$ and set
\[
 \omega=\mathbb E_Z\bigl[\delta_{t_Z}*
                (\nu_A^Z\otimes\nu_C^Z)\bigr],
 \qquad \theta=\omega*\xi.
\]
Then, for all sufficiently large $h$, every irreducible representation
of $S_V$ with $D_\lambda>1$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \|\widehat\theta(\lambda)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le K_0D_\lambda^{-1/40},\qquad K_0=\sqrt{22}.
 
\end{equation}
The threshold on $h$ and the constant $K_0$ are independent of the
environment, the transporters and all the measures.

statements.title: Completion of the conditional-product bound
statements.label: l:tabloid-completion
statements.text:
Identify $V$ with $\{1,\ldots,2h\}$, and consider a sequence of
the data of Theorem~\ref{l:tabloid-product} with $h\to\infty$
and fixed $L$.
Suppose that $\mu$ is a probability on $S_{2h}$ satisfying
$\theta\le\mu$ pointwise,
\[
 \theta(S_{2h})=1-o(1),\qquad
 \left|\widehat\mu(\mathrm{sgn})\right|=o(1).
\]
Then
\[
 \|\mu^{*100}-U_{\{1,\ldots,2h\}}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
In particular the sign hypothesis holds if $\mu$ has exactly
zero expected sign.

statements.title: Coefficient-space average
statements.label: l:coefficient-average
statements.text:
For $b=32$ and cap $B=4$,
\[
 \|\widehat f(\rho)\|_{\op}\le\frac83\sqrt{C_1}\,D^{-5/16}.
\]

statements.title: Orbit-space average
statements.label: l:orbit-average
statements.text:
For $b=256$ and cap $B=4$,
\[
 \|\widehat f(\rho)\|_{\op}\le4\sqrt{C_{32}}D^{-1/4}.
\]

statements.title: Four-factor coefficient decomposition
statements.label: l:four-coefficient
statements.text:
If there are four blocks and the subprobability cap is $B=2$, then
\[
 \|\widehat f(\rho)\|_{\op}\le2C_{1/4}^2D^{-1/8}.
\]

statements.title: The peeling character transfer
statements.label: l:peeling-lift
statements.text:
Let $b=2^{22}$ and partition $n=bm$ points into $b$ sets of size
$m$.  Let $H_i$ permute the $i$th set.  If $f\ge0$ has mass at
most one and $f(gH_i)\le2/[S_n:H_i]$ for every $g,i$, then for
all sufficiently large $m$ and every irreducible of degree $D$,
\begin{equation}
 \|\widehat f(\rho)\|_{\HS}^2
 \le6bD^{-1+(C_{\rm peel}+2)/b}.
\end{equation}

title: Fujita's freeness conjecture
abstract: We prove Fujita's freeness conjecture. If X is a smooth complex projective variety of dimension n and L is an ample line bundle, then \(K_X+mL\) is globally generated for every integer \(m\geq n+1\).

tex.abstract:
We prove Fujita's freeness conjecture. If $X$ is a smooth complex
projective variety of dimension $n$ and $L$ is an ample line bundle,
then $K_X+mL$ is globally generated for every integer $m\geq n+1$.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $X$ be a smooth connected projective variety over $\C$ of dimension
$n\geq 1$, and let $L$ be an ample line bundle on $X$. Then
\[
                    K_X+(n+1)L
\]
is generated by its global sections.

statements.title: Kawamata--Viehweg vanishing
statements.label: thm:kv
statements.text:
Let $T$ be smooth and projective over $\C$. Let $\Delta$ be an
effective rational SNC divisor with coefficients in $[0,1)$, and
let $D$ be an integral divisor. If $D-(K_T+\Delta)$ is nef and big,
then $H^i(T,\cO_T(D))=0$ for every $i>0$.

statements.title: Ordinary-order alternative
statements.label: prop:ordinary-gap

statements.title: Existence and uniform bounds for minimizers
statements.label: prop:minimizers
statements.text:
Suppose that $P$ is not generated at $x$. For the constants and ranges
in Lemma~\ref{lem:min-coercivity}, $f_{m,t}(x)$ satisfies
\eqref{eq:min-uniform-bounds} and is attained by an ordered basis
of $R_m$ and a nonzero real-weight monomial test on a projective log
resolution of the divisors of that basis. Every minimizing test has
\[
 a_*\leq\A(v)\leq a^*.
\]
More generally the same bounds hold eventually along every minimizing
sequence. In particular, the positive lower bound $a_*$ is independent
of $m\geq m_0$ and $t\in[t_0,n+1]$.

statements.label: prop:point-center
statements.text:
Suppose that $P$ is not generated at $x$. There is a real number
$0<t<n+1$ such that, for arbitrarily large integers $m$, the infimum
$f_{m,t}(x)$ is attained and every minimizing monomial pair has center
exactly $\{x\}$.

statements.label: cor:all-powers
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, $K_X+mL$ is globally
generated for every integer $m\geq n+1$.

title: Full support of the zero-temperature Sherrington-Kirkpatrick order parameter
abstract: We prove that every admissible integrable minimizer of the zero-temperature Parisi functional for the pure, zero-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model has full relative Stieltjes support on \([0,1)\). Thus its support has no gaps at any overlap scale below one. We use the covariance normalization \(\xi(t)=t^2/2\).

tex.abstract:
We prove that every admissible integrable minimizer of the zero-temperature
Parisi functional for the pure, zero-field Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model
has full relative Stieltjes support on $[0,1)$. Thus its support has no
gaps at any overlap scale below one. We use the covariance normalization
$\xi(t)=t^2/2$.

statements.title: Full support at zero temperature
statements.label: thm:full-support
statements.text:
If $\gamma\in\mathcal U$ minimizes $\mathcal P$, then
\[
 \supp\mu_\gamma=[0,1).
\]
In particular $\gamma(b)>\gamma(a)$ whenever $0\leq a<b<1$.
For the solution of~\eqref{eq:model-diffusion},
\begin{equation}
 \E[u_\gamma(t,X_t)^2]=t,\qquad
 \E[\Phi_{\gamma,xx}(t,X_t)^2]=1,
 \qquad 0\leq t<1.
\end{equation}

statements.title: Integrated coercivity
statements.label: cert:coercivity
statements.text:
Suppose $r,v,w,z,s$ and the variables $R,K,b,j,L,B,S$ are related as in
Lemma~\ref{shape:ibp}, with the derivative rules~\eqref{shape:D-rules}
and signs~\eqref{cert:signs}.  Assume their quotients extend across zero.
Let $f$ be a probability density satisfying $f_x/f=r-s$ such that every
term of~\eqref{cert:identity} is integrable and $rfF_2$ tends to zero at both
spatial infinities.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \E_f[z^2-12vw^2+6v^4]
 \geq\frac{1661507}{1521000000}\E_fv^4
 \geq\frac1{1000}\E_fv^4.
\end{equation}

statements.title: Constant-interval curvature
statements.label: prop:gap-curvature
statements.text:
Let $\gamma\in\mathcal U$ and suppose $\gamma=c$ on an open interval
$I\subset(0,1)$. For its controlled diffusion, put
$q(t)=\E\Phi_{\gamma,x}(t,X_t)^2$.
If $c>0$, then $q'$ is strictly convex on $I$; more precisely, with
$v=c\Phi_{\gamma,xx}$,
\begin{equation}
 q'''(t)\geq\frac{1}{1000c^2}\E v(t,X_t)^4>0,
 \qquad t\in I.
\end{equation}
If $c=0$, then $q'$ is strictly increasing on $I$.

statements.title: Finite Gaussian coefficients
statements.label: prop:gaussian
statements.text:
Fix $0<T<1$, a minimizer $\gamma$, and $u,a$ as above. For an integer
$N\geq1$ put $\Delta=T/N$ and $t_j=j\Delta$. On independent standard
normal variables $Z_1,\ldots,Z_{N+1}$, define
\begin{align}
 Y_0&=0,\qquad
 Y_j=Y_{j-1}+\sqrt\Delta Z_j
      +\Delta\gamma(t_{j-1})u(t_{j-1},Y_{j-1}),
       &&1\leq j\leq N,\\
 c_j&=\bigl(\E a(t_{j-1},Y_{j-1})^2\bigr)^{-1/2}>0,
 \qquad g_j=c_j a(t_{j-1},Y_{j-1})Z_j.
       
\end{align}
For all sufficiently large $N$ these constants are finite and positive.
For these mesh counts, let $F_{\rm G}$ denote the standard normal
distribution function and set
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 F_N=\operatorname{sgn}\bigl(u(T,Y_N)+2F_{\rm G}(Z_{N+1})-1\bigr),\\
 A_j=\E[F_Ng_j],\qquad B_i=\E[F_NZ_i],\qquad A_0=0.
 \end{gathered}
\]
Here $1\leq j\leq N$ and $1\leq i\leq N+1$ in the definitions of
$A_j$ and $B_i$.
The value of the sign at zero is immaterial. Then
\begin{equation}
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\sum_{j=0}^N A_jB_{j+1}
       =\int_0^T\E a(t,X_t)\,\dd t.
\end{equation}
Letting $T\uparrow1$ on the right gives $P_*$.

statements.title: Asymptotically optimal SK optimization
statements.label: cor:algorithm
statements.text:
For every fixed $\epsilon>0$, there is a randomized algorithm with
operation count at most $C(\epsilon)n^2$ in the model just described,
where $C(\epsilon)$ is independent of $n$, that takes the Gaussian
couplings of $H_n$ as input and returns
$\sigma^{\rm alg}\in\{-1,1\}^n$ such that
\[
 \Pr\left\{
 H_n(\sigma^{\rm alg})\geq
 \max_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^n}H_n(\sigma)-\epsilon n
 \right\}\longrightarrow1
 \qquad(n\to\infty).
\]
The probability includes the couplings and the algorithm's randomness.

title: Functional universality of critical SK autocorrelations
abstract: We prove that the stationary spin autocorrelation of the zero-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model at inverse temperature β = 1 has a common functional scaling limit for Gaussian and Rademacher couplings. With rate-one heat-bath clocks at every site, time is scaled by n2/3 and the mean spin autocorrelation is multiplied by n1/3. The functions converge in law uniformly on compact positive-time intervals. Their limiting law is not a point mass: it retains sample-to-sample randomness, and its functions decay to zero at large times.

tex.abstract:
We prove that the stationary spin autocorrelation of the zero-field
Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model at inverse temperature $\beta=1$ has a common
functional scaling limit for Gaussian and Rademacher couplings. With
rate-one heat-bath clocks at every site, time is scaled by $n^{2/3}$ and the
mean spin autocorrelation is multiplied by $n^{1/3}$. The functions converge
in law uniformly on compact positive-time intervals. Their limiting law
is not a point mass: it retains sample-to-sample randomness, and its
functions decay to zero at large times.

statements.title: Functional universality
statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is a Borel probability law $Q_{\mathrm{crit}}$ on
$C_{\mathrm{loc}}((0,\infty))$ such that, for each of the two choices of $D$,
\[
 \Law_D(A_{n,J})\Longrightarrow Q_{\mathrm{crit}}
 \qquad(n\to\infty).
\]
The law $Q_{\mathrm{crit}}$ is not a point mass. It assigns probability one
to nonzero, nonnegative, nonincreasing functions $f$ satisfying
$\lim_{s\to\infty}f(s)=0$. The Gaussian and Rademacher models use exactly
the normalization in \eqref{eq:intro-rescaling}.

statements.title: The conditioned edge measure
statements.label: prop:edge-conditioned-law
statements.text:
Formula~\eqref{eq:source-1} defines a finite random variable, and
\[
 D_n(b_n):=n^{1/3}-\sum_{a=1}^n l_{a,n}
       \ \Longrightarrow\ D(b)
\]
jointly with the edge coordinates.  Almost surely $\sum_a l_a=\infty$.
The law of $(Z_a)_{a\ge1}$ conditioned on $S=D(b)$ has a version
$\Pi=\Pi_g$ characterized by continuous conditional densities.  It is
independent of the admissible choice of $b$.

Let $\mu^{\rm sp}$ denote normalized surface measure on the sphere of
radius $\sqrt n$, tilted by $\exp(X^{\mathsf T}WX/2)$.  The fixed-coordinate marginals of $n^{-1/3}U^{\mathsf T}X$ under
$\mu^{\rm sp}$ converge jointly in distribution with the eigenvalues to
the random marginals of $\Pi$.  On the spectral representations of
Remark~\ref{rem:edge-tight-convergence}, this is ordinary weak convergence
of measures, including convergence of every fixed polynomial moment.  On the sets in Remark~\ref{rem:edge-tight-convergence},
for every fixed $0\le j<\infty$ one has
\begin{equation}
 \int |x_a|^j\,d\Pi\le C_j l_a^{j/2},
 \qquad
 \mu^{\rm sp}|x_a|^j\le C_j l_{a,n}^{j/2},
\end{equation}
uniformly in the retained coordinate $a$.

For any sufficiently large fixed $m$, the tail $(x_a)_{a>m}$ under
$\Pi$ has a density relative to $\bigotimes_{a>m}N(0,l_a)$.  Conditional
on this tail, the first $m$ coordinates lie on the sphere of squared radius
\begin{equation}
 D(b)+\sum_{a\le m}l_a-\sum_{a>m}(x_a^2-l_a),
\end{equation}
with the Gaussian angular density on that sphere.  In particular,
$\sum_a(x_a^2-l_a)=D(b)$ holds $\Pi$-almost surely.
statements.section_title: The conditioned edge measure and the Gaussian inputs

statements.title: Cap inputs
statements.label: prop:edge-cap-inputs
statements.text:
Fix a finite field radius $R$ and positive fixed error tolerances.  There
are sufficiently small constants $p_{\rm top},s_0>0$ such that the following
hold with probability tending to one in the range
$np^3\ge c\sqrt{\log n}$ and $p\le p_{\rm top}$.

\emph{Spectral and spherical estimates, at every scale.}
The spectral dimension satisfies $\dim\cH_p\asymp k_p$,
$d_1\ge-o(p^2)$ uniformly in the cap range, and
$\Tr R_{p,0}^2=O(n/p)$.  On $|\alpha|\le s_0p^2$,
$\ell_p(\alpha)\asymp p^2M_p$ and
$\ell_p'(\alpha)\asymp M_p$.  For
$\|h\|\le Rp^2M_p$, the saddle precision has gap comparable to $p^2$.
At $\alpha=\alpha_p(h)$, the density at $n$ of the squared norm of
$\mathsf N(R_{p,\alpha}h,R_{p,\alpha})$ is comparable to $\sqrt{p/n}$.
After multiplication by $e^{v^{\mathsf T}X}$ and renormalization, the
Gaussian mean becomes $R_{p,\alpha}(h+v)$ while its covariance remains
$R_{p,\alpha}$; its squared-norm density at $n$ is at most a fixed
multiple of $\sqrt{p/n}$.  For $m$ replicas, where $m$ is fixed, consider
rowwise linear or quadratic tilts that preserve Gaussianity.  The joint
density of their squared norms is at most $C_m(p/n)^{m/2}$ under the
following hypotheses.  The spectral rows remain independent after the rowwise tilt,
the tilted precision is positive definite, and on at least $ck_p$ rows
the post-tilt row covariance $C_a$ satisfies
$c p^{-2}\Id_m\preceq C_a\preceq C p^{-2}\Id_m$.
All comparison constants here are fixed.

\emph{Curvature estimates, at every scale.}
On the annulus, for any prescribed fixed $\epsilon_0>0$,
\begin{equation}
 K_p\preceq(1+\epsilon_0)p^{-2}\Id_{\cH_p},\qquad
 p^2(K_p)_{ee}\le1-\epsilon_1,
 \quad e=h/\|h\|,\quad \epsilon_1=0.1.
\end{equation}
On the entire field ball one also has $K_p\preceq C_Rp^{-2}\Id_{\cH_p}$,
where $C_R$ may be chosen before $\epsilon_0$.

\emph{Static comparisons and cube projection tails, on geometric lists.}
For any prescribed fixed geometric list of scales, uniformly over the field ball,
\[
 |\phi_p(h)-\phi_p^{\rm sp}(h)|\le\epsilon_v k_p,
 \qquad
 \|P_pm_p(h)-R_{p,\alpha_p(h)}h\|\le\epsilon_gM_p.
\]
Any fixed finite family of such lists is allowed.  For each
$h\in\cH_p$ with $\|h\|\le Rp^2M_p$, the cube posterior $\mu_{p,h}$
satisfies, uniformly for every $v\ge v_0$ with a sufficiently large fixed
threshold $v_0$,
\[
 \mu_{p,h}\{\|P_pX\|>vM_p\}\le C\exp(-ak_pv^6).
\]
For $v>p^{-1/2}$ the event is empty, since $\|X\|=\sqrt n$.
Here $a>0$, and the same bound holds under the uncapped zero-field cube
measure $\mu$ at the same list scales.

The spherical projection-tail estimate holds at every scale in the stated
range, for capped bounded-field and uncapped zero-field measures.  Also, at
every such cap scale, for independent
spherical replicas at a common field in the prescribed ball,
\[
 (\mu_{p,h}^{\rm sp})^{\otimes2}
 \{|n^{-1}X^{\mathsf T}X'|>\rho\}
 \le C\exp(-cn\rho^3),\qquad Cp\le\rho\le\rho_0,
\]
for a sufficiently small fixed $\rho_0>0$.  A fixed finite number of
replicas obeys the corresponding bound for any pair.
