statements.title: Cube edge marginals
statements.label: cor:observations-static
statements.text:
Jointly with the spectral variables, in the sense of
Remark~\ref{rem:edge-tight-convergence}, the quenched cube integrals of
continuous cylinder functions of polynomial growth converge to their
integrals under $\Pi$. In particular, all fixed moments of any fixed finite
set of scaled edge coordinates converge.

statements.title: Mean moments and the initial score
statements.label: cor:observations-means

statements.title: Conditional variance
statements.label: prop:variance-main
statements.text:
There is a fixed $p_*>0$ with the following property. For every
$\varepsilon>0$ there are finite constants $C$, $\xi>0$ and disorder events
$\mathcal V_n$ with $\liminf_n\mathbb P(\mathcal V_n)\ge1-\varepsilon$
such that, on $\mathcal V_n$, simultaneously for every real function $f$
on the cube and every $r\le p\le p_*$,
\begin{equation}
 V_p(f):=Q_\mu[\Var(f\mid h_p)]
 \le Cp^{-2}\cE(f)+Ce^{-n^\xi}\|f\|_\infty^2.
\end{equation}
The constants and the disorder event are independent of $f$. The inequality
also holds componentwise and may be summed for vector-valued functions.
statements.section_title: Conditional variance at the exact cap scale

statements.title: Positive covariance error
statements.label: prop:variance-curvature
statements.text:
There are fixed $a,\xi,C>0$ and a sufficiently small fixed $p_*>0$ such
that, for each deterministic $p\in[r,p_*]$ away from the activation
scales,
\begin{equation}
 p^2K_p\preceq\bigl(1+C(p^a+k_p^{-a})\bigr)\Id
\end{equation}
outside an event $\mathcal N_{n,p}$ satisfying
$\mathbf P(\mathcal N_{n,p}\cap\mathcal G_n)\le Ce^{-n^\xi}$.
The exceptional event may depend on $p$; its probability bound has common
constants for the entire scale range. By Fubini's theorem the same bound
holds after integration in $d\log p$, with a possibly smaller $\xi$.
statements.section_title: Conditional variance at the exact cap scale

statements.title: The conditioned gradient
statements.label: prop:gradient-domain
statements.text:
The Euclidean gradient on smooth compact cylinder functions is closable
from $L^2(\Pi)$ to $L^2(\Pi;\ell^2)$. Its closed graph consists exactly
of the pairs satisfying \eqref{eq:source-23}. In particular, the vector
$G$ in that identity is unique; we denote it by $\nabla F$.

The closed form
\[
 \mathcal E_\Pi(F)=\int|\nabla F|^2\,d\Pi
\]
has kernel equal to the constants. Each coordinate $x_a$ belongs to its
domain and satisfies $\nabla x_a=e_a$, so that
$\mathcal E_\Pi(x_a)=1$.
statements.section_title: The gradient on the conditioned edge measure

statements.title: Limit of the observation slopes
statements.label: prop:gradient-observation
statements.text:
Suppose $f_n$ satisfies the preceding bounds and has weak cylinder
limit $F$. Choose a subsequence on which $T\mathcal E(f_n)$ tends to
its liminf. After further extraction in the quenched convention, there
is a sequence $q_j\downarrow0$ such that the spectral components of
$\overline{J^f}_{q_j}$ have weak cylinder limits $G^{(j)}$ as
$n\to\infty$. Every weak cluster point of $(G^{(j)})$ in
$L^2(\Pi;\ell^2)$ equals $\nabla F$. In particular,
$F$ belongs to the form domain of Proposition~\ref{prop:gradient-domain}
and
\begin{equation}
 \|\nabla F\|_{L^2(\Pi;\ell^2)}
 \le C\left(\liminf_{n\to\infty}T\mathcal E(f_n)\right)^{1/2}.
 
\end{equation}
The constant is the same for all sequences with the stated size bounds.
statements.section_title: The gradient on the conditioned edge measure

statements.title: Microscopic moment measure
statements.label: prop:micro-moment-measure
statements.text:
There is a deterministic finite positive measure $\omega$ on $[0,\infty)$
whose moments are given by \eqref{eq:source-3}. For fixed leading indices
$a,a'$, polynomials $Q,Q'$, and a bounded continuous cylinder $\psi$,
\begin{equation}
 \mu\!\left[\psi(x)\sum_iw_i(A_a^Q)_i(A_{a'}^{Q'})_i\right]
 \longrightarrow
 \1_{\{a=a'\}}\Pi[\psi]\int QQ'\,d\omega.
 
\end{equation}
For every $\varepsilon>0$ one also has
\begin{equation}
 \lim_{q\downarrow0}\limsup_{n\to\infty}
 \mathbb P\!\left(
  \mu\!\left[\left\|P_q(wA_a^Q)-v_a\int Q\,d\omega\right\|^2\right]
      >\varepsilon\right)=0.
 
\end{equation}
Here $wA$ denotes entrywise multiplication. For some $c>0$,
$\int e^{c\sqrt\lambda}\,d\omega(\lambda)<\infty$. The measure is uniquely
determined by its moments, and polynomials are dense in
$L^2((1+\lambda)\omega+\delta_0)$.
statements.section_title: Microscopic relaxation and the effective coefficient

statements.title: Determination by moments and polynomial density
statements.label: cor:micro-moment-density
statements.text:
Let the matrices and normalized linear functions above vary with $n$,
and suppose the moments of the finite measures
\[
 \omega_{n,a}(B)=\langle Y_a,H\mathbf1_B(H)Y_a\rangle_{L^2(\mu)},
 \qquad B\subset[0,\infty)\text{ Borel},
\]
converge at every fixed nonnegative integer order.  They converge weakly
to a finite measure $\omega$ on $[0,\infty)$ with those moments.
This measure is uniquely determined among measures on $[0,\infty)$ by
its moments, and, for some $c>0$,
\[
 \int e^{c\sqrt\lambda}\,d\omega(\lambda)<\infty.
\]
Polynomials are dense in both $L^2(\omega)$ and
$L^2((1+\lambda)\omega+\delta_0)$.
statements.section_title: Microscopic relaxation and the effective coefficient

statements.title: Relaxed energy
statements.label: thm:micro-relaxation
statements.text:
The constant $c_*=\omega(\{0\})$ is deterministic and strictly positive.
On any quenched represented subsequence, suppose that
$\|f_n\|_\infty\le Cn^D$ for fixed $C,D$, that the $L^2$ norms and
$T\cE(f_n)$ are bounded, and that $f_n$ converges weakly against cylinders
to $F$. Then $F$ is in the closed form domain on $L^2(\Pi)$ and
\begin{equation}
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}T\cE(f_n)
        \ge c_*\Pi[\|\nabla F\|_{\ell^2}^2].
 
\end{equation}
Conversely, for each smooth compact cylinder $F$, the functions
$f_{n,Q_j}$ in \eqref{eq:source-39} converge strongly to $F$ for every fixed
$j$, are polynomially bounded at that fixed $j$, and satisfy
\[
 \lim_{j\to\infty}\lim_{n\to\infty}T\cE(f_{n,Q_j})
                       =c_*\Pi[\|\nabla F\|^2].
\]
All assertions for countably many chosen sources and tests hold on a
common represented event. In particular the lower bound and recovery
use the same deterministic coefficient.
statements.section_title: Microscopic relaxation and the effective coefficient

statements.title: Gaussian trace convergence
statements.label: prop:trace-goe
statements.text:
For almost every edge configuration $g$, the series defining $B_g(z)$
is finite for every $z>0$.  For every finite collection $z_1,\ldots,z_k>0$,
\[
 (B_n(z_1),\ldots,B_n(z_k))
 \ \Longrightarrow\ (B_g(z_1),\ldots,B_g(z_k)).
\]
Moreover, for each $z,\epsilon>0$,
\[
 \lim_{\ell\to\infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty}
 \mathbb P\left\{
 \sum_{a>\ell}\langle x_a,(z+TH)^{-1}x_a\rangle_\mu
 >\epsilon\right\}=0.
\]
statements.section_title: Convergence of the Gaussian resolvent trace

statements.title: Vanishing quadratic-feature trace
statements.label: prop:trace-second
statements.section_title: Convergence of the Gaussian resolvent trace

statements.title: Trace universality
statements.label: thm:comparison-universality
statements.text:
For every $z>0$,
\[
 \sup_{0\le t\le1}\mathbb E_t B_n^{[2]}(z)\longrightarrow0.
\]
For each finite collection $z_1,\ldots,z_m>0$, the vector
$(B_n(z_1),\ldots,B_n(z_m))$ under sign disorder converges in law to the
Gaussian limiting vector in \eqref{eq:source-40}.  In particular the
coefficient $c_*$ in that limit is unchanged.

statements.title: Identification of the functional limit
statements.label: prop:functional-identification
statements.text:
The series \eqref{eq:source-2} has a Borel version
$g\mapsto\mathcal A_g$ with values in $C_{\rm loc}((0,\infty))$.
For both Gaussian and symmetric-sign entries,
\[
 \operatorname{Law}(A_{n,J})\Longrightarrow
 Q_{\rm crit}=\operatorname{Law}(\mathcal A_g),
\]
where the same edge law and the same deterministic coefficient $c_*$
are used in \eqref{eq:source-2}.
statements.section_title: The functional limit and its randomness

statements.title: Randomness of the limit
statements.label: prop:functional-randomness
statements.text:
For every fixed $s>0$, the finite random variable $\mathcal A_g(s)$
is essentially unbounded.  In particular $Q_{\rm crit}$ is not a
point mass.
statements.section_title: The functional limit and its randomness

statements.label: prop:support-constant
statements.text:
The constant function $s\mapsto 1$ belongs to the closed topological
support of $Q_{\rm crit}$ in $C_{\rm loc}((0,\infty))$.

title: GOE bulk universality for fixed-degree random regular graphs
abstract: We prove the fixed-degree bulk-universality conjecture for random regular graphs. For every fixed integer d ≥ 3 and every fixed energy in the open Kesten–McKay bulk, the unfolded eigenvalue point process of the adjacency matrix of a uniform simple labelled d-regular graph converges to the GOE bulk process. The convergence holds along all admissible graph sizes, without additional conditioning.

tex.abstract: We prove the fixed-degree bulk-universality conjecture for random regular graphs. For every fixed integer \(d\ge3\) and every fixed energy in the open Kesten--McKay bulk, the unfolded eigenvalue point process of the adjacency matrix of a uniform simple labelled \(d\)-regular graph converges to the GOE bulk process. The convergence holds along all admissible graph sizes, without additional conditioning.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every fixed integer \(d\ge3\), every fixed
\(E\in(-2\sqrt{d-1},2\sqrt{d-1})\), and every nonnegative continuous
compactly supported \(h:\R\to\R\),
\[
 \left|
 \EE\exp\!\left(-\int h\dd\Xi_{n,d,E}\right)
 -
 \EE\exp\!\left(-\int h\dd\Xi_n^{\mathrm{GOE}}\right)
 \right|\longrightarrow0
\]
as \(n\to\infty\) through all admissible sizes.

statements.title: Spectral input
statements.label: prop:spectral-input
statements.text:
There are constants \(c_0,c_1>0\), \(B<\infty\), and a fixed open interval
\(I_E\) containing \(E\), with closure contained in
\((-2\sqrt{d-1},2\sqrt{d-1})\), such that the following hold with probability
tending to one.

\begin{enumerate}
\item After omitting the eigenvalue associated with the constant vector,
the ordered eigenvalues are within \(n^{-c_0}\) of their
Kesten--McKay classical locations. In the normalization above, every
eigenvector entry is bounded by a deterministic \(n^{o(1)}\).
\item Uniformly for \(\Re\zeta\in I_E\) and \(S/n\le\Im\zeta\le1\),
\[
 \left|\frac1n\Tr(A-\zeta)^{-1}-m_d(\zeta)\right|
 \le(\log n)^B\bigl(n^{-c_1}+(n\Im\zeta)^{-c_1}\bigr).
\]
Except at at most \(n^{1-c_1}\) centers, the resolvent entries on a
center and its \(d\) neighbors satisfy the same error bound relative
to the corresponding infinite \(d\)-regular tree entries.
\end{enumerate}
These conclusions hold along all admissible \(n\). In particular,
\[
 \#\{i:|x_i|\le S^2\}=O(S^2)
\]
on an event of probability tending to one.

statements.title: Uniform endpoint moments
statements.label: prop:edge-moments
statements.text:
Fix positive integers \(k,\ell\) and a nonnegative integer \(q\).
There are constants \(c,C>0\) and events of graphs of probability tending
to one with the following property. Choose distinct indices
\(i(1),\ldots,i(\ell)\) satisfying \(|x_{i(j)}|\le S^2\), by any rule
depending only on the graph. Independently sample \(k\) uniform oriented
edges \((v_\alpha,v'_\alpha)\), conditionally on the graph, and set
\[
 b_j=\bigl(u_{i(j)}(v_1),\ldots,u_{i(j)}(v_k),
           u_{i(j)}(v'_1),\ldots,u_{i(j)}(v'_k)\bigr)^\top .
\]
For every coordinate monomial \(P\) of total degree at most \(q\),
\[
 \left|\EE\bigl[P(b_1,\ldots,b_\ell)\mid A\bigr]
       -\EE P(Z_1,\ldots,Z_\ell)\right|\le Cn^{-c},
 \qquad Z_1,\ldots,Z_\ell\ \text{independent }N(0,C_k).
\]
The constants and graph events are uniform over the indicated choices
of eigenindices. They may depend on \(d,E,k,\ell,q\); no assertion is
made for dimensions or moment orders growing with \(n\).

statements.title: Endpoint control
statements.label: prop:endpoint-control
statements.text:
There is a deterministic \(\xi>0\), depending only on \(d,E\), with the
following property. For every fixed \(k\ge1\) and \(D>0\), there are
constants \(C_{k,D}<\infty\) and \(y_{k,D}<\infty\) such that, for every
fixed \(s\in\R\) and every fixed \(y\ge y_{k,D}\),
\begin{equation}
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}
 \PP\left(
 |m_n(s+\mathrm i y)-m_*|
 +\|M_{n,k}(s+\mathrm i y)-K_k(m_*)\|>y^{-\xi}
 \right)
 \le C_{k,D}y^{-D}.
\end{equation}
The limit is through admissible graph sizes. The constants and the height
threshold are independent of \(s\); the argument \(s+\mathrm i y\) is
fixed before taking the limit.

statements.title: Microscopic limits
statements.label: prop:microscopic-limit
statements.text:
From every sequence of admissible sizes tending to infinity one can
extract a subsequence along which
\[
 \bigl(\nu_n,m_n,(M_{n,k})_{k\ge1}\bigr)
 \ \Longrightarrow\
 \bigl(\nu,m,(M_k)_{k\ge1}\bigr)
\]
jointly, in the local vague topology for the point measures and the
compact-open topology on the upper half-plane for the analytic
functions. The limiting point measure \(\nu=\sum_j\delta_{x_j}\) is
locally finite, with multiplicities permitted. There are deterministic
\(\xi,\chi>0\), depending only on \(d,E\), such that the following
properties hold.

For every fixed \(0<\delta<1\), almost surely for all sufficiently
large \(R\),
\begin{equation}
 m(e+\mathrm i u)=m_*+O(u^{-\xi}),
 \qquad |e|\le R,\quad R^\delta\le u\le R^2,
\end{equation}
and, almost surely,
\begin{equation}
 \nu([v,w])=\rho(w-v)+O(R^{1-\chi}),
 \qquad -R\le v\le w\le R,\quad R\longrightarrow\infty.
\end{equation}
The constants and starting values of \(R\) in these almost sure
statements may depend on the sample and on \(\delta\), but the exponents
are deterministic.

On a possible extension of the probability space, for every fixed
\(k\) there are standard Gaussian vectors \(g_j\in\R^{2k}\), independent
over \(j\) conditionally on \(\nu\), such that
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
  m(z)&=m_{\rm r}+\PV\sum_j\frac1{x_j-z},\\
  M_k(z)&=K_k(m_{\rm r})
       +\PV\sum_j
       \frac{C_k^{1/2}g_jg_j^{\mathsf T}C_k^{1/2}}{x_j-z}.
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
These representations are consistent as \(k\) increases by retaining
the first \(k\) edge channels. A separate Gaussian mark is assigned to
each occurrence of a repeated point. The principal values converge
locally uniformly on the upper half-plane, and
\(\Im M_k(z)\) is positive definite there, almost surely simultaneously
for every finite \(k\) and every \(z\) with \(\Im z>0\).

statements.title: Continuous switching symmetry
statements.label: prop:continuous-switching
statements.text:
For every fixed \(k\ge2\) and every \(O\in O(k)\), the joint analytic-function
law of \((m,M_k)\) is invariant under \(\mathcal T_O\).

statements.title: Gaussian insertion
statements.label: prop:gaussian-insertion
statements.text:
The coefficients in \eqref{eq:sw-moments} satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \|\beta\|\le C\theta,\qquad
 cT\le s_2\le CT,\qquad |s_1|\le CT,
\end{equation}
with deterministic positive constants. Moreover, as \(r\to\infty\),
\begin{equation}
 m_{\rm r}+\Tr(H_r-z)^{-1}
 \ \Longrightarrow\ m(z)
\end{equation}
jointly at every finite list of points \(z\in\C_+\), and the unscaled
eigenvalue point measure of \(H_r\) converges locally vaguely in law to
\(\nu\). Both convergences are unconditional.

More precisely, generate the Gaussian marks of \(M_k\) conditionally on
\(\nu\), separately for each \(r\), and write
\[
 \mathcal S_r(z)
 =m(z)-\partial_z\log\det(\Id_{2k}+BM_k(z)).
 \]
For almost every \(\nu\), expectations of every bounded smooth function with
bounded derivatives of finitely many real and imaginary trace values differ
by \(o(1)\) when
\(m_{\rm r}+\Tr(H_r-z)^{-1}\) is replaced by \(\mathcal S_r(z)\).
This is a conditional approximation assertion, not conditional switching
invariance.

statements.title: Fixed-energy DBM input
statements.label: thm:dbm-input
statements.text:
Suppose a sequence of deterministic diagonal matrices \(V\) of dimension
\(m\) satisfies \eqref{eq:dbm-regularity} and
\eqref{eq:dbm-parameter-domain}, with fixed constants. Fix \(\sigma>0\),
and suppose
\begin{equation}
 
 g m^\sigma\le t\le m^{-\sigma}G^2.
\end{equation}
Assume also that \(\rho_{\mathrm{fc},t}(0)=1/\pi\).
For every fixed positive integer \(a\) and
\(O\in C_c^\infty(\R^a)\), the difference
\begin{align}
 
 &\int_{\R^a}O(\boldsymbol\alpha)
   p_{V+\sqrt t\,W_m}^{(a)}
      \left(\frac{\pi\alpha_1}{m},\ldots,
            \frac{\pi\alpha_a}{m}\right)
       \dd\boldsymbol\alpha \notag\\
 &\hspace{12mm}-
 \int_{\R^a}O(\boldsymbol\alpha)
   p_{W_m}^{(a)}
      \left(\frac{\pi\alpha_1}{m},\ldots,
            \frac{\pi\alpha_a}{m}\right)
       \dd\boldsymbol\alpha
 \longrightarrow0.
\end{align}
Consequently, the expected sums of \(O\) over ordered tuples of
distinct points of the two eigenvalue processes, both rescaled by
\(m/\pi\), differ by \(o(1)\).

title: Gaussian free-field limits of weighted integer Lipschitz heights
abstract: We prove a Gaussian free field scaling limit for weighted integer Lipschitz heights on the triangular lattice. With zero boundary values and a factor x for each edge on which the height changes, the field converges after division by a positive constant depending only on x to the zero-Dirichlet Gaussian free field, for every fixed \(x\in[1/\sqrt2,1]\). The convergence holds as a random distribution on every bounded C2 Jordan domain under inside lattice approximations with uniformly convergent boundary parametrizations. This includes the uniform height model and the predicted critical endpoint.
version_note: This version supplies the annulus proof of the circuit estimate used in the discrete argument; see the [previous version](../Gaussian-free-field-limits-of-weighted-integer-Lipschitz-heights-September-25-2026/paper.pdf).

tex.abstract:
We prove a Gaussian free field scaling limit for weighted integer Lipschitz
heights on the triangular lattice. With zero boundary values and a factor $x$
for each edge on which the height changes, the field converges after division
by a positive constant depending only on $x$ to the zero-Dirichlet Gaussian
free field, for every fixed $x\in[1/\sqrt2,1]$. The convergence holds as a
random distribution on every bounded $C^2$ Jordan domain under inside lattice
approximations with uniformly convergent boundary parametrizations. This
includes the uniform height model and the predicted critical endpoint.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every fixed $x\in[1/\sqrt2,1]$ there exists
$\sigma(x)\in(0,\infty)$, independent of $D$ and of the inside approximation
in Definition~\ref{def:approximation}, such that
\[
 \frac{h_\delta}{\sigma(x)}\ \Longrightarrow\ \Phi_D
 \qquad\text{in }\mathcal D'(D).
\]
In particular, the fields are tight as random distributions and, for every
$k\ge1$ and $f_1,\ldots,f_k\in C_c^\infty(D)$, the vector
$(h_\delta(f_i)/\sigma(x))_{i=1}^k$ converges to
$(\Phi_D(f_i))_{i=1}^k$.  All mixed moments of these vectors converge.

statements.title: Annulus circuit estimate
statements.label: thm:circuit-input
statements.text:
For $r\ge0$, let $\Lambda_r$ be the ball of radius $r$ in the triangular
graph metric, with its bounding honeycomb contour; thus
$\Lambda_r=\Lambda_{\lfloor r\rfloor}$. For $a>1$ and an integer
$n\in\N$, consider on
$\Lambda_{an}$ the cell spin law whose
interior cells have weight $(x^2)^{\ind\{B\text{ or }W\text{ nonconstant}\}}$
and whose boundary $Y$ cells are excluded. Fix $B=-$ on the boundary face
layer and leave $W$ free. There is $c=c(x,a)>0$ such
that, for $n\ge 3/(a-1)$, the probability of an occupied open-plus cell
circuit surrounding $\Lambda_n$ and contained in $\Lambda_{an}$ is at
least $c$. The same statement holds with the signs or the two spin colors
interchanged.

statements.title: Association and conditional order
statements.label: prop:history-order
statements.text:
For every feasible history, the unobserved $(B,\tau)$ variables are
positively associated. Two laws with ordered histories and common $E_0$
are stochastically ordered, including the unequal extreme pins just
described. Extra prescribed open-plus cells only in the upper law, or
open-minus cells only in the lower law, can be incorporated by observing
those cells and all their first-spin sites also in the other law. These
claims hold for clipped cells and at $x=1$.

statements.title: Local matching and the free plane law
statements.label: prop:local-mixing
statements.text:
There are $C,\alpha>0$ with the following property. Suppose a finite
ambient graph contains a ball of radius $L$ together with its interaction
cells, and its law has first-spin pins and second-spin equalities, none
in that ball. Then its
pair marginal in the concentric radius-$r$ ball is within
$C(r/L)^\alpha$ in total variation of a common free plane law, for
$L\ge Cr\ge C$. The same is true with the statuses of either fixed
choice of first color. The plane law is the local limit of free ambient
laws along every exhaustion, and its unaugmented pair and increment
laws preserve translations, lattice symmetries, and height symmetries.

Adding extreme first-spin pins in a bounded inner region can be coupled
to the original law so that the configurations agree beyond a common
circuit of the added sign. If there are $k$ separated favorable annular
slots outside all the changes and no adverse pins or equality edges in
their buffers, the failure probability is at most $Ce^{-ck}$.
All matches preserve the individual conditional marginals at every joint
record as in Lemma~\ref{discrete:online}.

statements.title: Plane matching after a stopped cut
statements.label: cor:conditional-plane-matching
statements.text:
Let $\mathcal R$ be an exterior record, and let $G$ be its
successful-search event, determined by that record.  Suppose that on every successful record a good
circuit surrounds $B(z,L)$ together with its interaction cells, and that
conditional on this record the retained law is the open-cut law of
Lemma~\ref{lem:cell-cut}, with no additional inside pins or equality edges.
For $L\ge Cr\ge C$, the pair variables in $B(z,r)$ can be coupled with
variables $P_r$ of the fixed free-plane marginal $\nu_r$ so that
\[
 \Prob(P_r\in A\mid\mathcal R)=\nu_r(A)
 \quad\text{for every event }A,
 \qquad
 \Prob(\text{mismatch}\mid\mathcal R)\le C(r/L)^\alpha
 \quad\text{on }G.
\]
The same plane marginal is assigned on failure.  Consequently $P_r$ is
independent of the entire record and the total mismatch probability is at
most $\Prob(G^c)+C(r/L)^\alpha$.  Agreement of pair variables also matches
increments along paths contained in $B(z,r)$.

statements.title: Separated rare pins
statements.label: prop:rare-pins
statements.text:
Fix $k$ bounded filled simply connected neighborhoods $U_1,\ldots,U_k$
with disjoint closures. In each $U_i$ let $P_i$ prescribe arbitrary first
spins on a finite site set and prescribe second-spin plus on at most
$m_i$ connected lattice subgraphs, singletons allowed. Assume the
supports stay a fixed positive distance from $\partial U_i$, so that
isolating circuit collars fit inside $U_i$, and let $m=\sum_i m_i$ be
fixed. In the free plane law,
\begin{equation}
 c\prod_{i=1}^k\Prob(P_i)
 \le \Prob\Bigl(\bigcap_{i=1}^kP_i\Bigr)
 \le C\prod_{i=1}^k\Prob(P_i).
\end{equation}
The constants depend on $x$, $k$, $m$, and the fixed buffers, but not on
the numbers of pinned sites, the lengths of the connected subgraphs, or
lattice translations preserving the buffers. The comparison also holds
in finite free ambient volumes containing all the required comparison
collars. Previous pins inside the currently considered obstacle are
retained in both comparison laws.

statements.title: Discrete midpoint inequality
statements.label: thm:midpoint
statements.text:
Let $f,g,u,v:\Z^m\longrightarrow[0,\infty)$ have finite support, and
write $m_-(s,t)=\lfloor(s+t)/2\rfloor$ and
$m_+(s,t)=\lceil(s+t)/2\rceil$, with coordinatewise rounding.
If, for every $s,t\in\Z^m$,
\[
 f(s)g(t)\leq u(m_-(s,t))v(m_+(s,t)),
\]
then
\[
 \left(\sum f\right)\left(\sum g\right)
 \leq\left(\sum u\right)\left(\sum v\right).
\]

statements.title: Smearing with bounded boundary values
statements.label: prop:smearing
statements.text:
In a bounded height problem as specified above, suppose its fixed trace
has absolute value at most $K$.  Let $n$ be the distance from the
smearing center to the bounding sites.  For
$1\leq a\leq c_0n$ and every finite $p\geq1$,
\begin{equation}
 \left\|\sum_uw_uH(u)\right\|_p
 \leq C_{p,A}\left(1+K+\sqrt{\log(n/a)}\right).
\end{equation}
The bound is uniform over the shape of the trace and applies in
particular to the interior of a good cut after its complete inner
height layer has been specified.

statements.title: Uniform plane moments for zero-total smearings
statements.label: prop:plane-moments
statements.text:
For the infinite-volume increment law furnished by
Proposition~\ref{prop:local-mixing}, every zero-total
smearing~\eqref{moments:weights} satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \left\|\sum_uw_uH(u)\right\|_p\leq C_{p,A}
 \qquad(1\leq p<\infty).
\end{equation}
The constants are uniform in $a\geq1$ and the center.  The same estimate
holds for the increment law in a finite free simply connected
triangulation containing $B(z_0,C_0a)$, for a sufficiently large fixed
$C_0$.

statements.title: Plane covariance and normalization
statements.label: prop:plane-covariance

statements.title: Positive normal transfer
statements.label: prop:reflection-transfer
statements.text:
Let $\ell$ be any row of lattice sites parallel to one of the three
unoriented nearest-neighbor directions, and choose one of its closed
half-planes.  The plane pair is reflection positive across $\ell$.
The assertion remains valid after adjoining any finite collection of fields
\begin{equation}
 
 Z_s(u)=U_s\exp\{is(H(u)-H(o))\},
\end{equation}
where the $U_s$ are independent unit-circle Haar variables, independent of
the pair, and $o$ is any anchor.

More precisely, let $\theta_\ell$ act on observables by spatial reflection,
and take local functions supported in the chosen half-plane, whose
height differences are evaluated along paths in that half-plane.  Then
\[
 \langle F,G\rangle_\ell
     =\E\big[\overline{\theta_\ell F}\,G\big]
\]
is a positive semidefinite Hermitian form.  In its quotient completion,
translation farther into the half-plane by the pure normal vector of
length $\sqrt3$ is a positive self-adjoint contraction $S$.  Unit
translation along the row is a commuting unitary $U$.  At mesh $\delta$
the normal step is $\sqrt3\delta$.

statements.title: Reflection-null Laplace insertion
statements.label: prop:reflection-null
statements.text:
Fix one of the three row directions.  Let $\ell_\delta$ be site rows
of $\delta\T$ converging to a line $\ell$ in that direction, and
choose the same side of each row.  Suppose that real
$\varphi_\delta\to\varphi$ in $C_c^\infty(\R^2)$, with common
compact support lying on that side at a positive distance from
$\ell_\delta$ for all sufficiently small $\delta$.  Put
$X_\delta=H_\delta(\Delta\varphi_\delta)$, using exact area weights.
Then
\begin{equation}
 
 \|X_\delta\|_{\ell_\delta}^2
   =\E[(\theta_{\ell_\delta}X_\delta)X_\delta]
       \longrightarrow0,
 \qquad \sup_{\delta\text{ small}}\|X_\delta\|_{L^2}<\infty.
\end{equation}
This holds also in every finitely phase-augmented reflection space of
Proposition~\ref{prop:reflection-transfer}.  In particular, if
$Y_\delta$ is supported on the same side and has bounded reflection
norm, then
$\E[(\theta_{\ell_\delta}Y_\delta)X_\delta]\to0$.

statements.title: Checked pin moments
statements.label: prop:pin-moments
statements.text:
Consider any of the fixed separated arrangements above, including
arrangements enlarged by reflected copies.  Let $Y_\delta=H_\delta(f)$,
where $f$ is a real smooth zero-integral test supported in a disk having a
filled cut-search neighborhood disjoint from all $U_i$.  For every
$1\le p<\infty$,
\begin{equation}
 \E\bigl[|Y_\delta|^p\mid P_{\mathrm{loc}}\bigr]\le C_p
\end{equation}
for all sufficiently small $\delta$.  The constants are uniform on
compact families of such arrangements with positive clearances and
bounded smooth test norms.  The same holds for finite collections of
these tests and, by separating real and imaginary parts, for complex
tests.
statements.section_title: Separated pins and transfer to boundary brackets

statements.title: Bracket insertion identity
statements.label: prop:bracket-insertion
statements.text:
Fix a grid, windows, and local factors as in
\eqref{pins:insertion-data}.  Suppose two grid levels strictly bracket
$K_0$, miss every spectator disk, and give the strict middle-strip
geometry \eqref{pins:middle-geometry} for the boundary groups after
arbitrarily small intersection gaps are opened.  Then both filled
brackets satisfy the target identity~\eqref{eq:bracket-insertion}.
In particular, any subsequential distributional bracket limit with
convergent local test statistics satisfies the corresponding identity
against products of bounded continuous functions of those statistics.
statements.section_title: Separated pins and transfer to boundary brackets

statements.title: Boundary arch estimate
statements.label: prop:boundary-arch
statements.text:
There are constants $L>100$, $c,C>0$ and a positive slope tolerance
such that the following holds.  Fix $p\in\partial D$ and a local
radius $R$ satisfying that tolerance.  Suppose the actual prescribed
trace on $S_{0,\delta}$ is at least $-1$ everywhere and at least zero
in $Q_R(p)\setminus Q_r(p)$.  Choose any $N$ positive scales
\[
 16r\le\ell_1,\qquad
 L\ell_j\le\ell_{j+1},\qquad
 \ell_N\le R/10.
\]
At all sufficiently small meshes,
\begin{equation}
 \Prob\!\left(
 \begin{array}{c}
 \text{a site circuit in }\widehat{\mathcal O}_0(H)
 \text{ surrounds }Q_r(p)\\[-2pt]
 \text{and is contained in }Q_R(p)\setminus Q_r(p)
 \end{array}\right)
 \ge 1-Ce^{-cN}.
 
\end{equation}
The constants are independent of $N,p$ and the prescribed trace;
the required mesh threshold may depend on the chosen positive
scales and the boundary approximation.  The same assertion holds
with all inequalities reversed when the original trace is at most
$1$ everywhere and at most zero in the clean annulus.  All usable
sites of the resulting arch have their real height at least zero,
or at most zero in the reversed assertion.

statements.title: Boundary moments with exterior spectators
statements.label: prop:boundary-moments
statements.text:
Fix a nonnegative smooth radial bump $\rho$, supported in the unit
disk, with integral one, and fix a sufficiently small $\theta>0$.
For $z\in D$ write $d(z)=\dist(z,\partial D)$ and
\[
 \rho_z(u)=(\theta d(z))^{-2}
       \rho\!\left(\frac{u-z}{\theta d(z)}\right),\qquad
 Y_z=H(\rho_z),
\]
where $H$ is any subsequential distributional and moment limit of
the true fields.  For every $1\le p<\infty$,
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{z\in D}\|Y_z\|_p\le C_{p,\theta,D,\rho}.
 
\end{equation}
In particular this bound is uniform when $z$ approaches any point
of a fixed compact boundary arc.

Let $p_0\in\partial D$ and let $F$ be a product of a fixed number
of smooth averages supported a positive distance from $p_0$.
The averages may be fixed in the interior, or may be of the same
comparable-depth form with centers approaching fixed boundary
points distinct from $p_0$.  Then, jointly in those allowed
approaches,
\begin{equation}
 \E[Y_zF]\longrightarrow0\qquad(z\longrightarrow p_0).
 
\end{equation}
The same statement holds for finite linear combinations of these
products.

If $p_1,\ldots,p_m$ are distinct fixed boundary points and
$z_i\to p_i$, then the reference average
$Z_m=m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^mY_{z_i}$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \limsup_{z_i\to p_i}\|Z_m\|_2\le C m^{-1/2},
 \qquad \sup_m\sup_{z_1,\ldots,z_m}\|Z_m\|_p\le C_p.
 
\end{equation}
In the first assertion $m$ and its distinct boundary points are
fixed before taking the depth limits.  Subsequently $m\to\infty$
makes these references tend to zero in every finite $L^p$.

statements.title: Tightness and moment convergence
statements.label: prop:tightness
statements.text:
For every \(t>1\), the true fields are tight in
\(H^{-t}_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)\).  The same holds for the upper and lower
brackets, uniformly in their exceptional windows.  Every fixed finite
collection of test pairings has uniformly bounded moments of every
order.  Along a distributional law limit, all its mixed moments
converge.  These assertions hold also for finite joint couplings of
the indicated fields.

statements.title: Harmonic moments
statements.label: prop:harmonic-moments
statements.text:
Let
\[
 \mathcal C_j=\{(z_1,\ldots,z_j)\in D^j:
                         z_i\ne z_k\text{ for }i\ne k\}.
\]
On \(\mathcal C_j\), \(T_j\) is a smooth function and is harmonic in
each variable separately.

statements.title: Moment identification and the full field law
statements.label: thm:wick
statements.text:
For every \(j\ge2\) and distinct \(x,y_2,\ldots,y_j\in D\),
\begin{equation}
 T_j(x,y_2,\ldots,y_j)
   =v\sum_{i=2}^j G_D(x,y_i)\,
          T_{j-2}(y_2,\ldots,\widehat{y_i},\ldots,y_j).
 
\end{equation}
Together with \(T_0=1\) and \(T_1=0\), this identifies every moment
distribution with that of \(\sqrt v\,\Phi_D\).
Every subsequential field limit has that law.  Consequently
\(h_\delta/\sqrt v\) converges to \(\Phi_D\) as a random
distribution, with joint convergence of every finite collection of
smooth compactly supported pairings.

 F_{a,b}(j)=\langle a,S^jb\rangle\quad(j=1,2,\ldots),

Generalized Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetry and Euclidean equality rigidity
abstract: We resolve the generalized Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetric conjecture in every dimension. In a complete simply connected smooth manifold with sectional curvature at most κ ≤ 0, every finite-volume set of finite ambient perimeter has perimeter at least that of the equal-volume ball in curvature κ. For bounded positive-volume sets, equality in the Euclidean comparison holds precisely when the set agrees up to null sets with an open region isometric, with its induced metric, to a round Euclidean ball.

tex.abstract:
We resolve the generalized Cartan--Hadamard isoperimetric conjecture
in every dimension. In a complete simply connected smooth manifold
with sectional curvature at most $\kappa\le0$, every finite-volume set
of finite ambient perimeter has perimeter at least that of the
equal-volume ball in curvature $\kappa$. For bounded positive-volume
sets, equality in the Euclidean comparison holds precisely when the set
agrees up to null sets with an open region isometric, with its induced
metric, to a round Euclidean ball.
sections: From the hypersurface inequality to model comparison

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $n\ge2$, let $\kappa\le0$, and let $(M^n,g)$ be a complete simply
connected smooth Riemannian manifold with $\Sec_g\le\kappa$.
Every measurable set $E\subset M$ with $\vol_g(E)<\infty$ and
$P_g(E)<\infty$ satisfies
\[
 P_g(E)\ge \mathcal I_{\sqrt{-\kappa}}\bigl(\vol_g(E)\bigr).
\]

statements.title: Euclidean equality rigidity
statements.label: thm:equality
statements.text:
Let $(M^n,g)$ be complete, simply connected and smooth, with
$n\ge2$ and $\Sec_g\le0$. Let $E\subset M$ be bounded and measurable,
with $0<\vol_g(E)<\infty$ and $P_g(E)<\infty$. Then
\[
 P_g(E)=n\omega_n^{1/n}\vol_g(E)^{(n-1)/n}
\]
if and only if $E$ agrees up to ambient volume zero with an open region
whose induced Riemannian metric is isometric to a round Euclidean ball.

statements.title: Model-ball Faber--Krahn and Saint--Venant comparisons
statements.label: cor:model-ball-spectral
statements.text:
Let $n\ge2$, $\kappa\le0$ and $1<p<\infty$. Let $(M^n,g)$ be complete,
simply connected, smooth and without boundary, with $\Sec_g\le\kappa$.
For a nonempty smooth domain $D\Subset M$, let $B_\kappa(|D|)$ be a
geodesic ball of volume $|D|=\vol_g(D)$ in the simply connected
$n$-dimensional space form of curvature $\kappa$. Then
\[
 \lambda_{1,p}(D)\ge\lambda_{1,p}\bigl(B_\kappa(|D|)\bigr),
 \qquad T_p(D)\le T_p\bigl(B_\kappa(|D|)\bigr).
\]

statements.title: Distance and metric comparison
statements.label: lem:distance-comparison
statements.text:
Let $(M^n,g)$ be complete and simply connected with $\Sec_g\le0$.
For $p\in M$, write $\log_p=\exp_p^{-1}$, $r_p(x)=d(p,x)$, and
$D_p=r_p^2/2$. Then
\begin{equation}
 \Hess_gD_p\ge g,\qquad (\exp_p)^*g\ge g_p,
 \qquad |d\log_p(X)|_{g_p}\le |X|_g.
\end{equation}
Here $g_p$ on $T_pM$ denotes its constant Euclidean metric.

statements.title: Hypersurface Sobolev inequality
statements.label: thm:extrinsic-sobolev
statements.text:
For every Lipschitz function $v$ with compact support in $\Sigma^\circ$,
\begin{equation}

 Q_\Sigma(v)\ge
 Y_m\left(\int_\Sigma |v|^q\,d\sigma\right)^{2/q}.
\end{equation}
The inequality also holds for the zero extension of every
$v\in H^1_0(U)$, where $U\Subset\Sigma^\circ$ is open.

statements.title: Boundary of an equality set
statements.label: prop:equality-boundary
statements.text:
Let $M^n$ be complete, simply connected and smooth, with $n\ge2$ and
$\Sec_M\le0$. Suppose that a bounded measurable set $E\subset M$ has
positive volume $V$, finite ambient perimeter $A$, and
\[
 A=n\omega_n^{1/n}V^{(n-1)/n}.
\]
Put $m=n-1$, $R=(V/\omega_n)^{1/n}$, and $H_0=m/R$. The support
$\Gamma=\supp|D\chi_E|$ is compact and has a decomposition
$\Gamma=\Sigma\mathbin{\dot\cup}Z$ with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
 \item $\Sigma$ is a relatively open, boundaryless, embedded
 $C^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ hypersurface, and $Z$ is compact, with
 $\dim_{\HH}Z\le n-8$. In particular, $Z=\varnothing$ when $n<8$.
 \item The side occupied by $E$ defines an outward unit normal $N$
 on $\Sigma$, and
 \begin{equation}
 
 |D\chi_E|=d\sigma\lfloor\Sigma,
 \qquad \sigma(\Sigma)=A=s_mR^m,
 \qquad \overline\Sigma=\Gamma.
 \end{equation}
 Here $d\sigma$ denotes induced area on $\Sigma$, extended by zero
 to $M$.
 \item There are $C<\infty$ and $r_0>0$ such that
 \begin{equation}
 
 \sigma\bigl(\Sigma\cap B_r(x)\bigr)\le Cr^m
 \qquad(x\in\Gamma,\ 0<r<r_0).
 \end{equation}
 \item The outward trace mean curvature satisfies
 $H=\divg_{T\Sigma}N=H_0$ almost everywhere on $\Sigma$.
\end{enumerate}
These assertions concern the perimeter support and the measurable
class of $E$, not the topological boundary of an arbitrary
representative.

title: Generalized ionization energies for full Coulomb atoms
abstract: We prove the energy part of the generalized ionization conjecture for full nonrelativistic Coulomb atoms with two electron spin states. The energy needed to remove m electrons is asymptotic to \(a_{\mathrm{TF}}m^{7/3}\) whenever \(m\to\infty\) and \(Z/m\to\infty\), with the Thomas–Fermi constant in atomic units. nonrelativistic Coulomb atoms with two electron spin states. The energy needed
to remove $m$ electrons is asymptotic to $a_{\TF}m^{7/3}$ whenever $m\to\infty$
and $Z/m\to\infty$, with the Thomas--Fermi constant in atomic units.
We also obtain both conjectured iterated limits.

statements.label: thm:main

statements.title: Deficit at a prescribed price
statements.label: thm:priced-deficit
statements.text:
There is a universal number $q>0$ such that, for every sequence satisfying
\[
 \lambda=s^{-4},\qquad s\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad Zs^3\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
and every choice of $n$ minimizing $E_n+\lambda n$, one has
\[
 s^3(Z-n)\longrightarrow q.
\]
The number $q$ is the exterior Coulomb charge of the unique classical solution, tending uniformly to zero at infinity,
of
\[
 \Delta F=4\pi k\bigl((F-1)_+\bigr)^{3/2}
 \quad\text{on }\R^3\setminus\{0\},
 \qquad k=(5T/3)^{-3/2},
\]
that is bounded above and below by positive multiples of $|x|^{-4}$ near
zero. The density $k((F-1)_+)^{3/2}$ has bounded support, and
$F(x)=q/|x|$ outside that support.
Moreover,
\[
 a_{\TF}=\frac37q^{-4/3}.
\]

statements.title: Simultaneous inverse comparison
statements.label: prop:inverse-comparison
statements.text:
There is a universal constant $C_{\mathrm{cap}}$ with the following property.
Fix
\[
 M\geq2,\qquad 0<h_l<h_h<\infty,\qquad 0<\xi<h_l/16.
\]
For all sufficiently far systems along \cref{eq:scaling-regime}, at every
$j<J_*$ there is an event $\mathcal G_j\in\mathcal F_j$ such that, with
$r=r_j$,
\[
 \Prob(\mathcal G_j^c)\leq Cr^{25}.
\]
On $\mathcal G_j$, the following assertions hold simultaneously for
$r\leq d_y\leq4Mr$ and $h_l\leq h\leq h_h$:
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 d_y^4H'_j(y)&\leq C_{\mathrm{cap}},\\
 d_y^6\mu_j(y)>kh^{3/2}
       &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad d_y^4H'_j(y)\geq h-\xi,\\
 d_y^6\mu_j(y)<kh^{3/2}
       &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad d_y^4H'_j(y)\leq h+\xi.
 \end{split}
 
\end{equation}
The probability constant and the threshold for sufficiently far systems
may depend on the displayed fixed parameters and on the fixed packet
conventions; $C_{\mathrm{cap}}$ is independent of the band and accuracy
parameters.
statements.section_title: Conditional density and field comparison at positive price

statements.title: Conditional barrier invariant
statements.label: prop:barrier-invariant
statements.text:
There are fixed positive constants $\eps,B,C_{\mathrm{inv}}$ and $M>2$
with the following property.  For every sufficiently far system in
\cref{eq:scaling-regime}, use the observations and kernels of
\cref{eq:observation-scales,eq:master-kernel} with this $\eps$.
For every $0\le j\le J_*$ there exist $\mathcal F_j$-measurable
functions $u_j,p_j$ such that, with $r=r_j$,
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 \Delta u_j&\ge-4\pi\nu
       +4\pi\ind_{\{d<r\}}\mu_j-4\pi p_j
       +\ind_{\{d\ge r\}}f(u_j),\\
 b_r\le u_j&\le C_{\mathrm{inv}}d^{-4}\quad(d\ge r),\\
 u_j&=b_r\quad(d>Mr).
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The first inequality holds in distributions on $\R^3$.
For each fixed system, $u_j-V$ is continuous and locally Lipschitz,
with deterministic bounds on compact sets; $p_j$ is a nonnegative
bounded density supported in $\{d\le r_j\}$, also with a deterministic
bound.  Its expected total mass satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{0\le j\le J_*}\E\int p_j
 \le C\bigl(r_0^{32}+s^{19/2-3w}\bigr)=o(1).
\end{equation}
The deterministic fixed-system regularity bounds need not be uniform

title: Generalized outer-electron radii of neutral Coulomb atoms
abstract: We prove the radius part of the generalized ionization conjecture for neutral nonrelativistic Coulomb atoms with two spin states. We prove the radius part of the generalized ionization conjecture for
neutral nonrelativistic Coulomb atoms with two spin states. For every
choice of ground states, the upper and lower large-nuclear-charge limits
of the radius defined by an expected exterior electron mass $m$ are both
asymptotic to $(81\pi^2/2)^{1/3}m^{-1/3}$ as $m$ tends to infinity.

statements.text:
For the fixed constants above, there are $B>0$, $C_{\mathrm{inv}}<\infty$,
$s_{\mathrm{bar}}>0$, and a finite integer threshold
$Z_{\mathrm{bar}}(s)$ for every $0<s\le s_{\mathrm{bar}}$, such that
the following holds.  For every $Z\ge Z_{\mathrm{bar}}(s)$ and
every neutral ground state,
\cite[\FoundationIntermediate]{OuterRadius} supplies, at each $0\le j\le J$,
$\mathcal F_j$-measurable functions $u_j,p_j$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
 \Delta u_j\ge-4\pi Z\delta_0+
     4\pi\mathbf1_{\{|y|<r_j\}}\mu_j-4\pi p_j+
     \mathbf1_{\{|y|\ge r_j\}}f(u_j)
       \quad\hbox{in }\mathcal D'(\R^3),\\
 B|y|^{-4}\left(1-\frac{r_j}{8|y|}\right)
       \le u_j(y)\le C_{\mathrm{inv}}|y|^{-4}
       \quad (|y|\ge r_j),\\
 p_j\ge0,\qquad \supp p_j\subset\{|y|\le r_j\},\qquad
 \E\int p_j\le C(s^{32}+s^\gamma),\qquad
 \gamma=\frac{19}{2}-3w>0.
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
For each finite system and index, $p_j$ is bounded and $u_j-V$ is
continuous and locally Lipschitz through zero.  The constants $B$,
$C_{\mathrm{inv}}$, and $C$ and the thresholds are independent of the
ground state and of the number of dyadic scales.
We enlarge $Z_{\mathrm{bar}}(s)$ to include $Z\ge Z_0$ and $2r_0\le s$.

title: Generic C1 Future Inextendibility Near Rotating Subextremal Kerr Spacetimes
abstract: For each fixed Kerr spacetime with mass M > 0 and rotation \(0\lt \mathfrak a\lt M\), we prove that a dense Gδ set of nearby smooth, complete two-ended vacuum data has a maximal globally hyperbolic development with no future C1 extension. The neighborhood and genericity are defined in a weighted smooth topology, and ambient extensions may be nonvacuum.

tex.abstract:
For each fixed Kerr spacetime with mass \(M>0\) and rotation
\(0<\mathfrak a<M\), we prove that a dense \(G_\delta\) set of nearby smooth,
complete two-ended vacuum data has a maximal globally hyperbolic
development with no future \(C^1\) extension. The neighborhood and
genericity are defined in a weighted smooth topology, and ambient
extensions may be nonvacuum.

statements.label: phase:main
statements.text:
For each fixed \(M>0\) and \(0<\mathfrak a<M\), there is
\(\eps_0=\eps_0(M,\mathfrak a)>0\) such that
\(\mathcal U_{\eps_0}\) contains a dense \(G_\delta\) subset
\(\mathcal G\) for which every \(\mathcal M_d\), \(d\in\mathcal G\),
has no future \(C^1\) extension in the sense of
Definition~\ref{phase:extension}.
statements.section_title: The constraint space and the theorem

statements.title: Coverage of future $C^1$ exits
statements.label: test:exit-cover
statements.text:
If $\mathcal M_d$, $d\in\mathcal U$, admits a future $C^1$
extension in the stated sense, then $d\in\mathcal A(O,B)$ for
some $O\in\mathcal O$ and some integer $B\ge1$.
statements.section_title: Closed transport tests and selection of a branch

statements.title: Comparison development and first runout
statements.label: test:comparison
statements.text:
After decreasing the defining $p_{10}$ radius of $\mathcal U$, each
$d\in\mathcal U$ has a smooth globally hyperbolic vacuum comparison
development $\mathcal P_d$ containing the whole bridge $\Sigma$ as
a Cauchy hypersurface and embedded openly and isometrically in
$\mathcal M_d$. It contains a spacelike cylinder $\mathcal S$ and
its full future product wedge, with coordinates
$t=(u+v)/2\ge0$, $x=(v-u)/2\in\mathbb R$,
$\theta\in\mathbb S^2$, in which
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 g&=-2a\,du\,dv+
 \gamma_{AB}(d\theta^A-b^Adu)(d\theta^B-b^Bdu),\\
 a&=q\mathcal A,\qquad
 q=q_0e^{-\kappa(u+v)},\qquad q_0,\kappa>0.
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
The coefficients $\mathcal A^{\pm1}$ and $\gamma^{\pm1}$ are
uniformly bounded, with $\gamma$ uniformly comparable to a fixed
round sphere metric. Every seed with $T_d(w)<\infty$ crosses
$\mathcal S$ before its first runout from $\mathcal P_d$, and
that first runout has exactly one of the following coordinate limits:
\begin{equation}
 \begin{array}{lll}
 \text{first branch:}&u\to u_*<\infty,&v\to+\infty,\\
 \text{second branch:}&v\to v_*<\infty,&u\to+\infty,\\
 \text{corner:}&u\to+\infty,&v\to+\infty.
 \end{array}
\end{equation}
These alternatives describe limiting coordinate regimes; they do not
adjoin boundary points or identify $\mathcal P_d$ with
$\mathcal M_d$.
statements.section_title: Closed transport tests and selection of a branch

statements.title: Corner seeds have measure zero
statements.label: test:corner-null
statements.text:
For a fixed $d\in\mathcal U$, the seeds whose first runout from
$\mathcal P_d$ is a corner are contained in a set of measure zero
for every smooth positive measure on $T\Sigma$.
statements.section_title: Closed transport tests and selection of a branch

statements.title: A branch seed for every passing test
statements.label: test:branch-seed
statements.text:
If $d\in\mathcal A(O,B)$, then there is $w\in O$ whose first
runout from $\mathcal P_d$ is one of the two branches in
Equation~\eqref{test:runout}. After exchanging the optical labels
and preparing the angular coordinates as in
\cite[\CompanionRef{foundation}{in:label-swap}]{Foundation},
the branch can be written
$u\to u_*<\infty$, $v\to\infty$. The seed is still the
same initial seed in $O$.
statements.section_title: Closed transport tests and selection of a branch

statements.title: All-spin geometric interface
statements.label: bg:geometry
statements.text:
There is a choice of $\epsilon>0$, depending only on the fixed Kerr
center and the fixed preparation, such that every
$p_{10}(d-d_*)<\epsilon$ in the stated smooth symbol class has the
following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The cylinder $\mathcal S$ in Proposition~\ref{test:comparison}
has a smooth vacuum development on the full product wedge
$[0,\infty)_t\times\mathbb R_x\times\mathbb S^2$ in
Equation~\eqref{bg:wedge}.  The quantities
$\mathcal A^{\pm1},\gamma^{\pm1}$ are uniformly bounded in angular
$H^6$, and $\xi_i,a^{-1}\partial_vb$ in angular $H^5$.
There are nonnegative functions $g_i(y_i)$ with summable unit-cell
suprema such that, in the indicated low angular norms,
\begin{equation}
 \|\chi_i,\ell_i+\kappa\|_{H^4}\le C(q+g_i(y_i)),
 \qquad \|b\|_{H^5}\le C(q+g_0(u)).
\end{equation}
\item The following quantities are uniformly bounded, and tend to
zero when $t,|u|,|v|\to\infty$:
\begin{equation}
\begin{gathered}
 \|b\|_{H^5}+\sum_i\|\chi_i,\ell_i+\kappa\|_{H^4},\\
 \sum_{k=0}^1\left(\|\partial_{y_k}b\|_{H^2}
       +\sum_i\|\partial_{y_k}\chi_i,
                          \partial_{y_k}\ell_i\|_{H^2}\right),\\
 \sum_{k=0}^1\left(\|\partial_{y_k}\gamma\|_{H^4}
                 +\|\partial_{y_k}\log a+\kappa\|_{H^4}\right).
\end{gathered}
\end{equation}
In particular $D\log a,D\gamma,b,Db$ are uniformly bounded.
\item For each fixed $U\in\mathbb R$, $C>0$, and finite order,
all ordinary derivatives of
\begin{equation}
 \gamma^{\pm1},\quad\log\mathcal A,\quad b,
                  \quad a^{-1}\partial_vb
\end{equation}
are bounded by $e^{o(T)}$ on
\begin{equation}
 t\ge0,\qquad y_d\le U,\qquad y_l\le CT,
 \qquad \{d,l\}=\{0,1\}.
\end{equation}
This includes every restriction and coordinate-path subsegment.
Every fixed derivative of $a$, $\sqrt a$, or $\partial_vb$ retains,
respectively, the factor $a$, $\sqrt a$, or $a$.
\item Either branch can be put in the convention
$v\to\infty$, $u\to u_*<\infty$.  Exchanging the optical labels
and preparing the angular coordinates anew preserves all these
conclusions on the same product spacetime and initial cylinder.
\end{enumerate}
Only $p_{10}$ is required small; no higher seminorm, radiation
coefficient, or curvature measured by a timelike observer is required
small or bounded.
statements.section_title: The all-spin background and the constrained linear packet

statements.title: Entry timing, escape, and flow estimates
statements.label: bg:exterior
statements.text:
On either prepared end use regular exterior time $t_e$, co-moving
coordinates $y$, and lab coordinates $z=y+C_e(t_e)$, with fixed
$\sup|C_e'|\le s_*<1/10$, after decreasing $\epsilon$ if needed.  The relevant slice $t_e=0$ agrees with the
original bridge sufficiently far out.  There is a preparation
parameter $I$ with $0<c_I\le I'\le C_I$ and $I(t_T)=T$.
The launch patch near $v=x=T$ on $\mathcal S$ occurs at
$t_e=t_T+O(1)$, and $t_T\asymp T$.  A fixed enlargement is
contained in $t_e\le t_T+C_2$.  Its selected-end portion
$v<(1-\nu_0)T$ is earlier by at least $c\nu_0T-O(1)$ for each
fixed $\nu_0>0$.

The exterior metric has uniformly regular spacelike temporal
levels.  Its first and second ordinary lab derivatives are bounded
on the computing region and become arbitrarily small at sufficiently
large co-radius, uniformly in time.  Every fixed mixed jet on the
used time and radius ranges $O(1+T)$ is $e^{o(T)}$.  Entry charts
have a noncharacteristic collar with controlled low jets and
subexponential fixed higher jets; the inner exit has a strict margin
deeper than the entry cylinder.

The null covectors $dv$ launched on a sufficiently small fixed patch
at this entry escape towards the past to the same original end.
For each fixed $\beta>0$, after fixing a sufficiently large radius
and taking $T$ large, their bridge arrival points satisfy
\begin{equation}
 (1-\beta)t_T<|z-z_*|<(1+\beta)t_T,
                  \qquad z_*=C_e(t_T).
\end{equation}
The entry crossing is unique and transverse, and separated from
other used ray portions outside a uniform collar.  Every fixed
Hamiltonian flow jet, including launch-center derivatives and the
propagators on all subsegments, is $e^{o(T)}$.  Tensor parallel
transport and its inverse are bounded.  These assertions hold on
short past and future launch enlargements through the deeper exit.

statements.title: Linear packet and exterior beam
statements.label: bg:packet
statements.section_title: The all-spin background and the constrained linear packet

statements.title: Linear construction at any exponentially small amplitude
statements.label: bg:amplitude-independent
statements.text:
Fix any $\alpha>0$ and put $A_T=e^{-\alpha T}$. With this substitution,
all linear conclusions of Proposition~\ref{bg:packet} hold, with the
same order of finite output, frequency and inverse-accuracy choices.
The branch observer needs no bounded-curvature hypothesis.
statements.section_title: The all-spin background and the constrained linear packet

statements.title: Signed preparation and entry
statements.label: prep:signed-entry
statements.text:
Fix a finite data order $m\ge10$, a finite entry order $r$, a loss
$\eta>0$, and $0<\nu_0<1$.  After fixing all the finite derivative
orders needed below, one can choose $\zeta>0$ and then the finite
formal accuracy orders in Proposition~\ref{bg:packet} so that the
following hold for all sufficiently large parameters $T$ in the
packet sequence.

There are smooth positive complete vacuum data $d_T^\pm\in\mathcal D$
on the whole bridge, with
\begin{equation}
 p_m(d_T^\pm-d)\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
In particular $d_T^\pm\in\mathcal U$ for large $T$.
They agree exactly with $d$ on the other end, the connecting region,
and a protected region containing every fixed compact subset for
large $T$.  On the selected asymptotic end the protected ball is
\begin{equation}
 B_T=\{|z-z_*|<\rho_T\},\qquad
 z_*=C_e(t_T),\qquad \rho_T=(1-2\beta)t_T,
\end{equation}
where $\beta>0$ is fixed sufficiently small.  The data have the
weight-one metric and weight-two second-form symbol bounds at every
order.  Their full correction tails are retained; asymptotic
coefficients are allowed to change.

Ordinary exterior vacuum evolutions $g_T^\pm$, in exact wave-map gauge
with the same target $g$, exist on the finite domains needed to reach
$\mathcal S_T$, with fixed overlap margins and strict future-outflow
artificial boundaries.  Set
\[
 H_T^\pm=\widehat{g_T^\pm-g},\qquad
 F_T^\pm=H_T^\pm\mp q_T
 \quad\hbox{on the entry collar}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak J_{r,T}(F_T^\pm)\le A_T^2e^{\eta T},\qquad
 \mathfrak J_{r,T}(F_T^+-F_T^-)\le A_T^3e^{\eta T}.
\end{equation}
The exact changes, packet, and errors vanish on the earlier needed
entry interval $v<(1-\nu_0)T$.  In particular, $r=61$ is permitted,
with an arbitrarily small prescribed loss.  The scaled linear deep
residual can simultaneously be at most $e^{-4\kappa T}$ through
order $60$, or at any other finite orders fixed in advance.
The same statement holds for the separately prepared exchanged branch.
statements.section_title: Exact signed data and exterior entry

statements.title: Signed exterior preparation at a general amplitude
statements.label: prep:amplitude-independent-exterior
statements.text:
Fix any $\alpha>0$. Replace the amplitude in this section by
$A_T=e^{-\alpha T}$ and use Corollary~\ref{bg:amplitude-independent}.
For every fixed data order $m$, entry order $r$, loss $\eta>0$ and
late-support fraction $0<\nu_0<1$, the conclusions of
Proposition~\ref{prep:signed-entry} hold after choosing the frequency
exponent sufficiently small and the inverse accuracy sufficiently
large. This assertion ends at the entry cylinder.

statements.title: Signed interior experiment
statements.label: energy:signed-experiment
statements.section_title: Signed nonlinear propagation through the interior

statements.title: Whole-bridge attachment
statements.label: attach:development
statements.text:
For all sufficiently large finite $T$, there is a smooth time-oriented
vacuum development $\mathcal N_T^\pm$ of the entire datum $d_T^\pm$
with $\Sigma$ as a Cauchy hypersurface. It contains the constructed
finite observation, restricted within its construction margins, and
an optical-coordinate box about $p_T$, of fixed sufficiently small
coordinate radii independent of $T$, in
$I^+_{\mathcal N_T^\pm}(\Sigma)$.
It admits a time-orientation-preserving open isometric embedding into
$\mathcal M_{d_T^\pm}$ that preserves the initial-data embedding.
The full physical constraint-correction tail is part of its initial
data.
statements.section_title: Attachment to the full development and the observing geodesic

statements.title: Adaptive observer and test-frame comparison
statements.label: attach:observer
statements.text:
At $p_T$ put $U_T^\pm=I_T^\pm U$. There are seeds
$w_T^\pm\to w$ on $\Sigma$ whose future unit geodesics in
$\mathcal M_{d_T^\pm}$ reach $p_T$ with tangent $U_T^\pm$, at finite
positive proper times strictly before their full-MGHD future
durations. In particular $w_T^\pm$ belong to the original open
seed set for all sufficiently large $T$.

Choose an angular orthonormal frame $e_A$ near $p_T$, including the
packet polarization direction at the center, and set
\begin{equation}
 E_0^\pm=I_T^\pm L_0,\qquad
 E_1^\pm=a^{-1}I_T^\pm L_1,\qquad
 E_A^\pm=I_T^\pm e_A.
\end{equation}
At $p_T$ the Euclidean norm of components in this frame and the
parallel positive test norm $k_{d_T^\pm,w_T^\pm}$ are uniformly
equivalent, with constants independent of $T$. Their induced
operator norms are uniformly equivalent as well.
statements.section_title: Attachment to the full development and the observing geodesic

statements.title: Signed signal
statements.label: holo:signal
statements.text:
For every sufficiently large $T$, at least one sign satisfies
$|C_T^\pm|>A_T$.

statements.title: Finite small-loop violation
statements.label: holo:violation
statements.text:
Fix a passing test $\mathcal A(O,B)$, a datum
$d\in\mathcal A(O,B)$, and a branch seed $w\in O$ as in

$p_m(d_T^\pm-d)\to0$ such that, for every sufficiently large $T$,
at least one of $d_T^+$ and $d_T^-$ does not belong to
$\mathcal A(O,B)$.

title: Generic Future Inextendibility with Square-Integrable Connection Near a Fixed Kerr Spacetime
abstract: For each fixed rotating subextremal Kerr background with mass M > 0 and rotation \(0\lt |\mathfrak a|\lt M\), we prove that the smooth vacuum data near its complete two-ended bridge whose full maximal globally hyperbolic development admits a future \(C^0\cap W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}\) extension form a meagre set in the weighted smooth topology. The neighborhood requires smallness of only the tenth weighted seminorm, while the topology tests every finite order.

tex.abstract:
For each fixed rotating subextremal Kerr background with mass $M>0$ and
rotation $0<|\mathfrak a|<M$, we prove that the smooth vacuum data near
its complete two-ended bridge whose full maximal globally hyperbolic
development admits a future $C^0\cap W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ extension
form a meagre set in the weighted smooth topology. The extension metric
is continuous and nondegenerate, and its weak connection is locally
square-integrable. The neighborhood requires smallness of only the tenth
weighted seminorm, while the topology tests every finite order.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every fixed $M>0$ and $0<|\mathfrak a|<M$, there is
$\eps=\eps(M,\mathfrak a)>0$ such that the set of $d\in\Ueps$ for which the
full development $(M_d,g_d)$ admits a future extension in the sense
of Definition~\ref{intro:extension} is meagre in $\Ueps$.
Consequently, future $C^0\cap W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$-inextendible
data contain a residual subset of $\Ueps$ in the weighted smooth
topology \eqref{intro:seminorms}.

statements.title: Background estimates
statements.label: prop:bg-package
statements.section_title: Background geometry and finite branch tubes

statements.title: First runout and corner removal
statements.label: prop:bg-runout
statements.text:
Every seed whose future geodesic has finite maximal proper
lifetime in $M_d$ crosses $\mathcal S$. Its first runout from
$\mathcal P_d$ is either a branch, where one optical coordinate
has a finite limit and the other tends to $+\infty$, or a corner,
where both tend to $+\infty$. For each fixed datum, seeds whose
first runout is a corner form a $\mu_d$-null set.
statements.section_title: Background geometry and finite branch tubes

statements.title: A positive family supplied by every weak exit
statements.label: prop:exit-family
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses of \Cref{ex:graph}, there is a measurable
set $S\subset T\Sigma$ of positive smooth section measure such
that every future unit geodesic with seed in $S$ has finite
maximal future proper lifetime in the full $M$ and an ambient
endpoint on $\partial M$.  The endpoints lie in one compact
subset of an ambient chart.  Moreover, there are finitely many
precompact ambient charts $\psi_j:U_j\to V_j\subset\R^4$ and
constants $C<\infty$, $m>0$ with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item on each entire $V_j$, the metric and inverse metric have
      component norms at most $C$, and
      $\|\widetilde\Gamma_j\|_{L^2(V_j)}\le C$;
\item for every seed in $S$ and every proper time from its
      intersection with $\Sigma$ to its full future endpoint,
      excluding only the endpoint itself, at least one $j$
      satisfies
      \begin{equation}
      \operatorname{dist}\bigl(\psi_j(\gamma(\tau)),
                                  \R^4\setminus V_j\bigr)\ge m,
      \qquad
      |(\psi_j)_*\dot\gamma(\tau)|\le C.
      \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
Here the section measure is the pullback of canonical volume
on $T^*\Sigma$ under $w\mapsto h(w,\cdot)$, where $h$ is the
induced metric.  In particular it has the same null sets as
every smooth positive measure on $T\Sigma$.
statements.section_title: From an arbitrary weak exit to countably many tests

statements.title: Countable cover of all future extensions
statements.label: prop:exit-cover
statements.text:
Every datum in $\Ueps$ admitting a future
$C^0\cap W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ extension belongs to some
$E(O,B)$.  Consequently the extendible set is precisely
\[
                  \bigcup_{O\in\mathcal B}\ 
                         \bigcup_{B=1}^{\infty}E(O,B).
\]
This cover includes extensions whose actual exit occurs
after first runout from the comparison development.
statements.section_title: From an arbitrary weak exit to countably many tests

statements.title: Packet preparation
statements.label: prop:packet-preparation
statements.text:
For every finite $m\ge10$, finite jet budget $N$, positive loss
tolerance $\eta_{\rm out}$, and $0<\nu<1$, one can choose $\zeta>0$ and
finite construction orders so that the following objects exist
for arbitrarily large $T$ along the indicated sequence.
\begin{enumerate}
\item There are exact smooth complete vacuum data $d_T\in\Ddata$
on the whole bridge with $p_m(d_T-d)\to0$. They agree with $d$ on
the other end, the connecting region, and an expanding protected
ball on the selected end. The permitted exterior correction tail
is retained.
\item An exact exterior evolution of $d_T$ reaches the required
part of $\mathcal S$, with overlapping collars and strict outflow
margins. In the fixed background wave-map description its entry
spacetime jets differ from $g+h^p$ by $O(\amp^2e^{\eta_{\rm out} T})$.
Here
\begin{equation}
 h^p=\amp\,\operatorname{tr.rev.}_g\operatorname{Re}
       \left(e^{i\lambda v}\sum_{j=0}^{J_*}\lambda^{-j}p_j\right).
\end{equation}
The leading coefficient is real, trace-free, and annihilates
$L_0$. On the entire observation box $\mathcal Q_T$,
\begin{equation}
 |(p_0)_{AB}|_\gamma\ge e^{-o(T)}.
\end{equation}
At every fixed required base order the ordinary mixed coordinate jets
of the normalized amplitude components are $e^{o(T)}$, and the linearized Ricci and gauge errors have
arbitrarily high inverse-frequency accuracy.
\item There is a metric $\bar g$ exactly of double-null form, with
fields $\bar\gamma,\log\bar{\mathcal A},\bar b$ and their exact
geometric derived fields. Through order $N$, its differences from
the background fields, including $q^{-1}\partial_vb$, are
$O(\amp e^{\eta_{\rm out} T})$. Its defects in the null structure and
angular equations \eqref{dn:D2}--\eqref{dn:D3} are
$O(\amp^2e^{\eta_{\rm out} T})$. If the actual exterior induced data are
written in double-null coordinates initialized by the background
values on $\mathcal S$, their full entry jets differ from this
template by the same quadratic bound.
\end{enumerate}
All entry discrepancies and all template changes and defects vanish
for $v<(1-\nu)T$. Any additional finite initial or residual jet
buffers may be included in $N$. Positive frequency powers at these
base orders are independent of the later orders used to improve
linear accuracy. At the finitely many high entry orders ultimately
requested by \Cref{thm:dn-comparison}, the actual fields have
$e^{o(T)}$ bounds.
statements.section_title: Preparing exact data and a double-null template

statements.title: Finite double-null experiment
statements.label: thm:dn-comparison
statements.text:
For every fixed background and branch tube in
\Cref{lem:bg-branch-tube}, every finite $m,s$, and every sufficiently
small fixed $c>0$, the parameters in \Cref{prop:packet-preparation} can
be chosen so that its exact entry data have a smooth vacuum development
on \Cref{dn:domain} in the double-null gauge initialized there.
The relative lapse and the sphere metric remain positive and uniformly
nondegenerate.  For
\[
 \mathcal U=(\gamma,\log\mathcal A,b,\chi_0,\chi_1,
                       \ell_0,\ell_1,\xi_0,\xi_1)
\]
one has, in a fixed sphere atlas and ordinary coordinate derivatives,
\begin{equation}
 \max_{|I|\le s}\|\partial^I(\mathcal U'-\bar{\mathcal U})
                         \|_{L^\infty(\Omega_T)}
       \le e^{-(1+c)\alpha T}
\end{equation}
for all sufficiently large $T$ in the selected experiment sequence.
The same conclusion holds for
$q^{-1}\partial_vb'-q^{-1}\partial_v\bar b$ at any preassigned finite
order, after increasing the finite order budget.  The individual
ordinary jets of the primed relative fields through every order used
in the experiment are $e^{o(T)}$, uniformly for this moving family.
The exact solution and the template equal the background where
$v<(1-\nu)T$.  The exact solution agrees on an entry collar, by local
geometric uniqueness, with the actual exterior solution of
\Cref{prop:packet-preparation}.

statements.title: Quadratic low error
statements.label: prop:dn-low-error

statements.title: Attachment to the full development
statements.label: prop:experiment-attachment
statements.text:
For sufficiently large finite $T$, the exact exterior and deep
experiments, restricted inside their construction margins, lie
in a smooth globally hyperbolic vacuum development of the entire
datum $d_T$. This development embeds isometrically in its full
MGHD $M_{d_T}$. The full initial bridge and the exterior correction
tail are retained. The common earlier branch tubes and the compact
observation region have interior margins in the attached region.
statements.section_title: Attachment, curvature signal, and matched observing states

statements.title: Whole-patch curvature signal
statements.label: prop:curvature-signal
statements.text:
At every point of $\mathcal Q_T$ with
$|\cos(\lambda v)|\ge1/2$, one has, for all large $T$,
\begin{equation}
 |D(g_T)-D(g)|>2\amp.
\end{equation}
The norm is the ordinary angular component norm. No bound on
$D(g)$, or on background parallel-frame curvature, is assumed.
statements.section_title: Attachment, curvature signal, and matched observing states

statements.title: Matched seeds and finite observations
statements.label: prop:matched-seeds
statements.text:
For $v\in T+J_0$, use the same numerical states \eqref{at:terminal-state} in
$g_T$ on its future unit shell. Their backward geodesics give
maps $\Psi_{T,v}:O_0\to O$ with
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{v\in T+J_0}\|\Psi_{T,v}-\operatorname{incl}\|_{C^1}
                                  \longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
Write $\delta_T$ for the left side of \eqref{at:seed-closeness}.
Each map is injective and preserves the corresponding section
measure: $\Psi_{T,v}^*\mu_{d_T}=\mu_d$ on $O_0$. In particular
$\mathcal H_v(O_0)$ has canonical volume $\mu_d(O_0)$ for every such $v$.

Put
\begin{equation}
 r_T=e^{-\kappa T},\qquad
 F=(\partial_u,r_T^{-1}\partial_v,
                    \partial_{\theta^1},\partial_{\theta^2}).
\end{equation}
For $g$ and $g_T$ on the larger observation box, the Gram
matrices in $F$ and their inverses are uniformly bounded and
nondegenerate. Their ordinary coordinate jets through order
thirty are $e^{o(T)}$. The selected unit tangent is bounded
in $F$, all state momenta lie in one bounded box, and
\begin{equation}
 c r_T\,\dd u\,\dd v\,\dd^2\theta
 \le \dd\vol_g,\ \dd\vol_{g_T}
 \le C r_T\,\dd u\,\dd v\,\dd^2\theta.
\end{equation}

For each fixed finite $T$ and each $\eta_{\rm map}>0$, these observations
persist for all data in a sufficiently small relative weighted smooth
neighborhood of $d_T$, with signal lower bound $\amp$ in place of
$2\amp$. The persisted common coordinates need not be optical.
The canonical section volume, injective maps into $O$, and frame
and density bounds persist. Their backward maps satisfy
\[
 \sup_{v\in T+J_0}\|\widehat\Psi_{T,v}-\Psi_{T,v}\|_{C^1}
 <\eta_{\rm map},
 \qquad
 \sup_{v\in T+J_0}\|\widehat\Psi_{T,v}-\operatorname{incl}\|_{C^1}
 \le\delta_T+\eta_{\rm map}.
\]
The neighborhood may depend on $T$ and $\eta_{\rm map}$.
statements.section_title: Attachment, curvature signal, and matched observing states

statements.title: Averaged holonomy obstruction
statements.label: prop:averaged-holonomy
statements.text:
Assume \eqref{ho:gram-assumptions} on the observation box, bounded
$F$ components of the selected unit tangents, and a fixed bounded
momentum box in \eqref{ho:parameter-measure}. Fix one extension and
one collection of at most $B$ charts with the metric, inverse-metric,
and connection bounds in \Cref{def:exit-test}.
Let $\mathcal G_T\subset\mathcal P_T$ be the measurable parameters
whose base point and unit tangent satisfy the margin and velocity
conditions in at least one chart of this same collection.
There is a measurable exceptional set $\mathcal N_T\subset\mathcal G_T$
such that
\begin{equation}
 \nu_T(\mathcal N_T)\le C e^{-\kappa T/16},
\end{equation}
and, for all parameters in $\mathcal G_T\setminus\mathcal N_T$,
\begin{equation}
 |D|\le C e^{-13\kappa T/32}+Q_Te^{-\kappa T}
                 =o(\amp).
\end{equation}
The constants use only $B$ and the uniform observation bounds.
statements.section_title: Averaged holonomy and the category argument

statements.title: Nowhere denseness of the extension tests
statements.label: thm:nowhere-dense
statements.text:
For the single neighborhood $\Ueps$ fixed in
\Cref{prop:bg-package}, every set $E(O,B)$ of \Cref{def:exit-test} is
relatively nowhere dense in $\Ueps$.

title: Geometric Programs for Solenoidal Forcing
abstract: We construct smooth solenoidal mean-zero forces, periodic from time zero, for which a fixed particle on a flat three-torus reaches a fixed open strip exactly when a given machine halts. The initial fluid velocity and the pressure are zero. We also realize positive diagonal maps on coding sheets by incompressible shears, with explicit normal compensation for changes of planar area, and reciprocal maps on whole boxes of positive thickness. Complete local inverses, initialization rules, and intermediate trajectory bounds connect these geometric constructions to finite computations.

tex.abstract:
We construct smooth solenoidal mean-zero forces, periodic from time zero,
for which a fixed particle on a flat three-torus reaches a fixed open strip
exactly when a given machine halts. The initial fluid velocity and the
pressure are zero. We also realize positive diagonal maps on coding sheets
by incompressible shears, with explicit normal compensation for changes
of planar area, and reciprocal maps on whole boxes of positive thickness.
Complete local inverses, initialization rules, and intermediate trajectory
bounds connect these geometric constructions to finite computations.

statements.title: Periodic initialization
statements.label: sv:periodic-theorem
statements.text:
Fix a computable viscosity $\nu>0$.  From a deterministic one-tape
machine, with head moves in $\{-1,0,1\}$, and a finite input, one can
effectively construct a smooth force on $\mathbb T_1^3$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),itemsep=2pt]
\item The force is divergence free, has zero spatial mean, and is
one-periodic from time zero.  Equation~\eqref{sv:NS} has a global
smooth solution with pressure zero, unique in the stated classical class.
\item The velocity is one-periodic, vanishes near every integer time,
has zero instantaneous self-advection, and has uniformly bounded kinetic
energy.  Every mixed derivative of force and velocity is globally bounded.
\item For the fixed label $a_*=(1/4,1/2,1/4)$ and fixed open strip
$O=\{1/2<x_1<7/8\}$, the material trajectory enters $O$ at a finite
real time exactly when the machine halts, including an initially halted
machine.
\end{enumerate}
The construction may use one Cartesian velocity component at a time.
For arbitrary fixed real $\nu>0$ the same formulas hold and are
effective relative to that viscosity.
statements.section_title: The geometry of a finite fluid instruction

statements.title: General diagonal maps on a sheet
statements.label: sv:sheet-theorem
statements.text:
Let $P_i,Q_i\subset[2,3]^2$, $1\le i\le N$, be closed rectangles
with rational vertices and positive side lengths.  Suppose the sources are pairwise
positively separated and the targets are pairwise positively separated.
Let $F_i:P_i\to Q_i$ be the center-to-center affine map with any
positive rational diagonal linear part, with $F_i(P_i)=Q_i$.  For each computable $\nu>0$
there is an effective smooth mean-zero solenoidal force on
$\mathbb T_{10}^3$, one-periodic from time zero, whose unique solution
in the classical class has pressure zero and period map
\[
 (y,2)\longmapsto(F_i(y),2)\qquad(y\in P_i).
\]
Its velocity is zero near integer times and has zero self-advection;
all mixed derivatives of force and velocity are bounded.  No condition
is imposed on source--target intersections.  For $N=0$ use zero.
statements.section_title: The geometry of a finite fluid instruction

statements.title: Cube-root and fourth-root clocks
statements.label: bcs:power-clock
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses on $W$ in Lemma~\ref{bcs:clock}, choose
$g(t)=(1+t)^q-1$, with $q=1/3$ or $1/4$, and put $\beta=1-q$.
The resulting force and velocity have bounded mixed derivatives and
\[
 \|\partial_t^kD_x^\alpha u(t)\|_\infty+
 \|\partial_t^kD_x^\alpha f(t)\|_\infty
 \le C_{k,\alpha}(1+t)^{-\beta}
\]
for every fixed $k,\alpha$.  Each such derivative is square integrable
in time in spatial supremum norm.

title: Gigli’s distributional curvature characterization of Alexandrov spaces
abstract: For every integer n ≥ 2 and κ ∈ ℝ, we prove that a complete separable metric space is an n-dimensional Alexandrov space of curvature at least κ if and only if, with reference measure \(\mathcal H^n\), it is a full-support \(\mathrm{RCD}((n-1)\kappa,n)\) space whose distributional sectional curvature is at least κ in Gigli's original global test classes. This resolves Gigli's characterization conjecture in dimensions at least two.

tex.abstract:
For every integer \(n\ge2\) and \(\kappa\in\mathbb R\), we prove that
a complete separable metric space is an \(n\)-dimensional Alexandrov
space of curvature at least \(\kappa\) if and only if, with reference
measure \(\mathcal H^n\), it is a full-support
\(\RCD((n-1)\kappa,n)\) space whose distributional sectional curvature
is at least \(\kappa\) in Gigli's original global test classes.
This resolves Gigli's characterization conjecture in dimensions at least two.

statements.title: Gigli's characterization
statements.label: main:equivalence
statements.text:
Let \(n\ge2\) be an integer, let \(\kappa\in\R\), and let \((M,d)\)
be a complete separable metric space. The following conditions are
equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\Alph*)}]
\item \((M,d)\) is an \(n\)-dimensional Alexandrov space with curvature
bounded below by \(\kappa\).
\item With \(m=\mathcal H^n_d\), the space \((M,d,m)\) has full support,
is \(\RCD((n-1)\kappa,n)\), and satisfies
\begin{equation}

R(X,Y,Y,X)(f)\ge
\kappa\int_M f\bigl(|X|^2|Y|^2-\langle X,Y\rangle^2\bigr)\dd m
\end{equation}
for every \(X,Y\in\TestV(M)\) and every nonnegative \(f\in\Test(M)\).
\end{enumerate}
The \(\RCD\) condition is unreduced, and the test classes and
curvature sign are exactly those defined above.

statements.label: fwd:curvature
statements.text:
Let \((M,d)\) be a complete \(n\)-dimensional Alexandrov space with
curvature bounded below by \(\kappa\), where \(n\geq2\), and put
\(m=\mathcal H^n_d\). Then \((M,d,m)\) is
\(\RCD((n-1)\kappa,n)\), its measure has full support, and
\begin{equation}

 R(X,Y,Y,X)(f)
 \geq \kappa\int f\bigl(|X|^2|Y|^2-\langle X,Y\rangle^2\bigr)\dd m
\end{equation}
for every nonnegative \(f\in\Test(M)\) and every
\(X,Y\in\TestV(M)\), with the global test classes and curvature
convention of Theorem~\ref{main:equivalence}.

statements.title: A localized error estimate
statements.label: fwd:defect
statements.text:
For the finite centered law above, every semiconcave compactly
supported Lipschitz \(f\geq0\), and every family
\(q_{AB}\in W^{1,2}(M)\),
\begin{equation}

 \frac\kappa6\int f\,\mathbb E|A\wedge B|^2
 \leq\frac16\mathbb ER(A,B,B,A)(f)
 +\frac12\mathbb E\int
 f|\nabla q_{AB}+\nabla_A(B-A)|^2.
\end{equation}

statements.label: fwd:gradient-bound

statements.title: Index inequality along calibrated paths
statements.label: heat:index
statements.text:
Let \(n\ge2\) be an integer and let \((M,d,m)\), with
\(m=\mathcal H^n\), be a full-support \(\RCD((n-1)\kappa,n)\)
space satisfying \eqref{eq:main-curvature} for every global
\(X,Y\in\TestV(M)\) and every nonnegative \(f\in\Test(M)\).
Let \(u\) be bounded globally Lipschitz
and constant outside a compact set, and let \(\Phi_t=Q_tu\).
There is a Borel prescription \(S:x\mapsto S(x)\in\Geo(M)\),
defined outside one \(m\)-null set, with \(S(x)_1=x\) and
\(S(x)\) satisfying \eqref{heat:calibration}. For every
nonnegative compactly supported Lipschitz \(f\), write
\(\pi_f=S_\#(fm)\), with forward velocity \(v\).
The plan has terminal measure \(fm\), uniformly bounded
speed, and bounded compression on every \([\delta,1]\),
\(\delta>0\).

Let \(Z\) be a compactly supported test gradient. For every
\(0<\delta<1\) and every trial \eqref{heat:trial-class}
with the global endpoint identities
\(Y_\delta=0\) and \(Y_1=Z\), one has
\begin{equation}

H_{\Phi_1}(Z,Z)(f)
\le\int_{\Geo(M)}\int_\delta^1
\left(|\partial_tY+\nabla_vY|^2
-\kappa|Y\wedge v|^2\right)(\gamma_t)
\dd t\dd\pi_f(\gamma).
\end{equation}
The left side is the distributional evaluation
\eqref{eq:weak-hessian}; the right side is finite. Neither
the path prescription nor its velocity depends on the
choice of \(Z\), the trial, or the terminal density.
