title: Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture and the 2-converse for elliptic curves
abstract: We prove Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture: for every elliptic curve E over ℚ, the quadratic twists of E with analytic rank zero and one each have density 1/2 among signed squarefree twist parameters ordered by absolute value. We also prove the low-corank 2-converse: if the \(2^\infty\)-Selmer corank of E is zero or one, then it equals the analytic and Mordell–Weil ranks, and the Tate–Shafarevich group is finite.
version_note: This version updates citations to revised manuscripts in this collection; see the [previous version](../Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-September-23-2026/paper.pdf).

tex.abstract:
We prove Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture: for every elliptic curve
$E$ over $\Q$, the quadratic twists of $E$ with analytic rank zero and one
each have density $1/2$ among signed squarefree twist parameters ordered by
absolute value. We also prove the low-corank $2$-converse: if the
$2^\infty$-Selmer corank of $E$ is zero or one, then it equals the analytic
and Mordell--Weil ranks, and the Tate--Shafarevich group is finite.
sections: Arithmetic estimates for finite twist families
Prime graphs and simultaneous unit coefficients
Cyclotomic interpolation at analytic rank zero
The unrestricted converse and Goldfeld's densities

statements.title: The $2$-converse
statements.label: thm:main-converse
statements.text:
For every elliptic curve $E/\Q$ with $c_2(E)\in\{0,1\}$,
\[
 a(E)=r(E)=c_2(E),\qquad \Sha(E/\Q)\text{ is finite}.
\]

statements.title: Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture
statements.label: thm:main-density
statements.text:
For every elliptic curve $E/\Q$ and each $j\in\{0,1\}$,
\[
 \lim_{X\to\infty}
 \frac{\#\{d\in\mathcal D(X):a(E^{(d)})=j\}}{\#\mathcal D(X)}
 =\frac12.
\]
Consequently the twists of analytic rank at least two have density zero.
For a density-one set of signed squarefree parameters $d$, the analytic
and Mordell--Weil ranks of $E^{(d)}$ agree and its whole
Tate--Shafarevich group is finite.

statements.title: A finite Selmer criterion
statements.label: cor:finite-descent
statements.text:
If $d_2(E)\in\{0,1\}$, then
\[
 a(E)=r(E)=c_2(E)=d_2(E),\qquad
 \Sha(E/\Q)\text{ is finite},\qquad \Sha(E/\Q)[2^\infty]=0.
\]

statements.title: Cyclotomic missing vertex
statements.label: thm:cyclotomic-interpolation
statements.section_title: Arithmetic estimates for finite twist families

statements.title: Comparison of the two Heegner constructions
statements.label: prop:heegner-comparison
statements.text:
For either set of data,
\begin{equation}
 \widehat h(P_c(e))
 =C_E\,c\sqrt{|k|}\,
       \left[L(E^{(e)},s)L(E^{(ek)},s)\right]'_{s=1},
\end{equation}
with a fixed nonzero constant determined by the parametrization and height
conventions. In particular, a simple zero of the product gives total
Mordell--Weil rank one and finite Shafarevich--Tate groups.

Suppose $h$ has analytic rank one, and use genus data with a fixed partner
$h_*$ of analytic rank zero and ring data with a possibly varying $k$,
where $L(E^{(hk)},1)\ne0$. Then
\begin{equation}
 2j(P_{|h|}(h))-2j(P_1(h_*))
       =v(\mathcal L(hk))+O_{E,h_*}(1).
\end{equation}
Here the two points are formed in their respective quadratic fields.
If instead $h_*$ has analytic rank one and $L(E^{(h)},1)\ne0$, genus
data give
\begin{equation}
 2j(P_1(h_*))=v(\mathcal L(h))+O_{E,h_*}(1).
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Arithmetic estimates for finite twist families

statements.title: Heegner interpolation
statements.label: thm:heegner-interpolation
statements.text:
Fix $E$ and an initial discriminant $h_0$. Consider families
$h_x$, $x\in\F_2^b$, obtained from $h_0$ by adjoining new prime factors
with linear activation functions on $\F_2^b$. No old factor is removed;
the signed factor belonging to an odd prime $q$ is
$q^*=(-1/q)q$. Suppose the local twisting classes at $2N$ are constant.
For each family let $k$ define an imaginary field satisfying the standing
Heegner conditions, with $(k,h_x)=1$ for every $x$. Each new prime must
either split in $K$ or satisfy $t_q=0$.

Assume that the following bounds are fixed independently of $b$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item a bound for $\omega(k)$;
 \item a bound for the length of the finite quotient of
       $\Sel_{2^\infty}(E^{(h_0)}/K)$ by its divisible subgroup;
 \item a constant $B$.
\end{enumerate}
Assume this base Selmer group has corank one. Suppose, for every $x\ne0$,
the product $L(E^{(h_x)},s)L(E^{(h_xk)},s)$ has a simple zero and
\begin{equation}
 2j(P_{|h_x|}(h_x))-4w(h_x)-s(h_x)-s(h_xk)\le B.
\end{equation}
Then, for sufficiently large $b$, the base product has a simple zero.
The dimension threshold depends only on the fixed base and the displayed
bounds, not on the number or sizes of the new primes. The field $K$ may
vary with the family.
statements.section_title: Arithmetic estimates for finite twist families

statements.title: Cyclotomic lower bound
statements.label: thm:cyclotomic-bound
statements.text:
Suppose that $E[2]$ is an extension of two trivial $\F_2$-modules.
There is a constant $C_E$ such that every odd fundamental discriminant
$h$ prime to $2N$ with
$L(E^{(h)},1)\ne0$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 v(\mathcal L(h))\ge 2w(h)+s(h)-C_E.
\end{equation}
The constant is independent of the number and sizes of the primes
that divide $h$.
statements.section_title: Arithmetic estimates for finite twist families

statements.title: Genus bound
statements.label: thm:heegner-genus-bound
statements.text:
In genus data, suppose the product in
Equation~\eqref{eq:h:height} has a simple zero and $E[2]$ is irreducible.
Then, uniformly in $h$,
\begin{equation}
 2j(P_1(h_*))\ge 2w(h)+s(h)-O_{E,h_*}(1).
\end{equation}
In proving the uniform estimate, one may omit the finitely many $h$ for
which $K$ meets $\Q(E[2])$ nontrivially.
statements.section_title: Arithmetic estimates for finite twist families

statements.title: Ring bound
statements.label: thm:heegner-ring-bound
statements.text:
In ring data, suppose the product in
Equation~\eqref{eq:h:height} has a simple zero, every $q\mid h$ splits in
$K$, and $\omega(k)\le a$, where $\omega$ counts distinct prime factors.
Then
\begin{equation}
 2j(P_{|h|}(h))\ge
       4w(h)+s(h)+s(hk)-O_{E,a}(1).
\end{equation}
There is no irreducibility assumption on $E[2]$.
statements.section_title: Arithmetic estimates for finite twist families

statements.title: Auxiliary nonvanishing
statements.label: prop:rough-nonvanishing
statements.text:
Let $E/\Q$ have conductor $N$, and let $S$ be a finite set of primes
containing the prime divisors of $2N$. Prescribe a real sign
$\sigma\in\{1,-1\}$ and a unit squareclass
$c_p\in\Z_p^\times/\Z_p^{\times2}$ for each $p\in S$.
Suppose that these data are realized by an odd fundamental discriminant,
and that twists in this filter have root number $\varepsilon$.
For every finite set $B$ of primes there are odd fundamental
discriminants $D$ of arbitrarily large absolute value such that
\[
 \operatorname{sign}(D)=\sigma,\qquad [D]_p=c_p\quad(p\in S),\qquad
 p\nmid D\quad(p\in B),
\]
Moreover:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If $\varepsilon=1$, they can be chosen with
$L(E^{(D)},1)\ne0$ and $\omega(|D|)\le5$.
\item If $\varepsilon=-1$, they can be chosen with
$L'(E^{(D)},1)\ne0$, so the central zero is simple.
\end{enumerate}
The bound five in \textup{(i)} is independent of $E,S,B$ and the
prescribed classes. In either case, every prime factor of $D$ can be
required to exceed any previously fixed bound.
statements.section_title: Arithmetic estimates for finite twist families

statements.title: Even coefficients
statements.label: prop:even-coefficients
statements.text:
Fix a nonempty filter with even functional sign.  There are a holomorphic
weight-$3/2$ cusp form
\[
                         g=\sum_{n\geq1}a(n)q^n
\]
of level supported on $S$, after enlarging exponents at those primes,
and finite-order characters $\psi,\eta$ of $2$-power order, with
$\psi/\eta$ quadratic, having the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item The coefficients vanish off the filter and, for $p\notin S$,
\begin{equation}
 a(p^2n)=\bigl(\eta(p)a_p(E)-\psi(p)(-n/p)\bigr)a(n)
                   -p\eta(p)^2a(n/p^2).

\end{equation}
As usual a coefficient with a nonintegral index is zero.
\item After normalizing at one nonzero squarefree index, every squarefree
coefficient in the filter is a rational number times a root of unity of
$2$-power order.  For a fixed nonzero squarefree index $D_0$,
\begin{equation}
 2v\left(\frac{a(D)}{a(D_0)}\right)
 =v\left(\frac{\mathcal L(\sigma D)}{\mathcal L(\sigma D_0)}\right)
 \quad\text{whenever }a(D)\ne0.

\end{equation}
Equivalently, there is a constant $c_g$, independent of $D$, such that
\begin{equation}
       2v(a(D))=v\bigl({\cal L}(h)\bigr)+c_g.

\end{equation}
In particular $a(D)\ne0$ if and only if $L(E^{(h)},1)\ne0$.
\item After the fixed auxiliary exclusions described below, there is a
constant $C_g$ such that, at every nonzero squarefree coefficient,
\begin{equation}
           v(a(D))\geq w(D)+\tfrac12s(h)-C_g.

\end{equation}
The constants depend on the fixed curve, filter and auxiliary choices,
and not on $D$ or its number of prime factors.
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Odd coefficients under a genus-index bound
statements.label: prop:odd-coefficients
statements.text:
Assume that a constant $C_*$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
              j(P_D)\geq w(D)+\tfrac12s(h)-C_*

\end{equation}
for every $h$ in the filter with a simple zero.  There are arbitrarily
large precisions $M$, good odd primes $\ell$ outside the fixed support,
and holomorphic weight-$3/2$ forms $g_M=\sum a_M(n)q^n$, of level
supported on $S\cup\{\ell\}$, with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item The additional filter at $\ell$ is
\begin{equation}
  (h_*/\ell)=-\sigma,\qquad (h/\ell)=\sigma,
               \qquad \rho_T(\Fr_\ell)\equiv C\pmod{2^M},

\end{equation}
where $C$ is the action of a complex conjugation.  In particular
$\ell\equiv-1\pmod{2^M}$.
\item After a fixed harmless decrease in the working precision, the
forms satisfy Equation~\eqref{cs:hecke-recurrence} modulo that precision,
with characters $\eta_M,\psi_M$ of $2$-power order and quadratic ratio.
Their squarefree coefficients have the form of a $2$-power phase times
an integer modulo $2^M$.
\item If a coefficient is visible, meaning $v(a_M(D))<M$, then
$E^{(h)}$ has a simple zero and
\begin{equation}
                    j(P_D)\leq v(a_M(D))+C_1.

\end{equation}
For every admissible $D$ the coefficient lower bound is
\begin{equation}
 v(a_M(D))\geq
       \min\{M,\,w(D)+\tfrac12s(h)-C_2\}

\end{equation}
when the product derivative is nonzero; if it is zero, the coefficient
is zero modulo $2^M$.  Here $C_1,C_2$ are independent of $\ell,M,D$.
\item A fixed squarefree witness $D_w$ in the original filter is
admissible at every chosen $\ell$ and has $v(a_M(D_w))$ bounded as
$M\to\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
For irreducible $E[2]$, the hypothesis is
Theorem~\ref{thm:heegner-genus-bound}.  For rational two-torsion, the positive filters used in the pointwise
argument have this bound by Proposition~\ref{prop:rational-odd-bound},
using only the even source. An arbitrary twist is first absorbed into
the fixed curve, so only these positive filters are needed there.

statements.title: Detection by a unit symbol
statements.label: prop:unit-symbol-detection
statements.text:
For either coefficient source, $A(D)=1$ implies the prescribed analytic
order: zero in the even case and one in the odd case.  At every such
index,
\begin{align}
 v({\cal L}(h))&\leq2w(D)+C &&\text{in the even case},
 \\
 j(P_D)&\leq w(D)+C &&\text{in the odd case},
 \\
 s(h)&\leq C,\qquad \dim_{\mathbf F_2}\Sel_2(E^{(h)}/\Q)\leq C.
 
\end{align}
The constants are fixed after choosing the original curve, filter,
coefficient normalization and genus partner.  For the odd source they
are independent of the detecting prime and the working precision, and
of the number and size of active primes.  Statements about its symbols
are used through finite realizations as in
Lemma~\ref{cs:fixed-weight-uniformity}.

statements.title: Rational trace and contraction rules
statements.label: tc:rational-rules
statements.text:
Suppose $E(\Q)[2]\ne0$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item For matching $U$, on the subtracted vector $H_U$,
\[
                         t(g)t(u)=0\quad(u\text{ split}).
\]
The trace on split elements factors through the elementary extension
of $F$ supported on $S\cup U$.  For opposite $U$, on $B_U$, every
product of two traces is zero, and traces factor through the rational
elementary extension supported there.
\item If $U\cup\{q\}$ has the parity of the filter, its symbol is
read at coefficient $1$ by $t(\Fr_q)$ on $H_U$ for split $q$, and on
$B_U$ for simple $q$.
\item Fix $p\in U$ and put $g=\Fr_q$.  Replacing $g$ by $g\tau_p$
changes the symbol, additively in $\mathbf F_2$, by
\begin{equation}
                  A\bigl((U/p)\cup\{q'\}\bigr),
       \qquad \Fr_{q'}\sim g\phi_p,
 
\end{equation}
if $p$ and $q$ are not both simple.  The label of $q'$ is required
only away from the omitted primes and carries their product labels.
The replacement uses the original source with level support
$S\cup(U/p)$: the \emph{whole rational prime} $p$ is omitted,
including both places over it if $p$ splits in $F$. If both endpoints
are simple, the change is zero.
\item A split vertex with trivial label relative to the level with
that vertex omitted has symbol zero.
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Insertion of a pair of simple primes
statements.label: tc:simple-twins
statements.text:
Suppose $E(\Q)[2]\ne0$ and $U$ has matching parity.  Let a rational
elementary label, relative to $S$ and all existing split vertices,
be realized by a simple prime $q$ with
\[
                         \#E(\mathbf F_q)\equiv2\pmod4.
\]
Inserting two fresh simple primes with this same label leaves $A(U)$
unchanged.  Their mutual simple-edge label, and their labels against
other simple vertices, do not affect this assertion.

statements.title: Irreducible substitution rules
statements.label: tc:irreducible-rules
statements.text:
Suppose $E[2]$ is irreducible.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item On matching $B_U$, coefficient $1$ of a product of root
traces reads $A$ on the union of $U$ and those roots.  It depends
on the roots only through their total rational elementary label
relative to $S\cup U$.  Any finite collection of roots, including
the empty collection, may be replaced in this test by one virtual
root with that label.
\item Changing the Legendre bit of that root against a split
vertex $p$ has additive derivative equal to deletion of $p$,
with its rational labels away from $p$ transferred to the total
root label.  Changing the root bit against a simple vertex has
derivative zero.
\item To vary a simple vertex $q$, omit it and use opposite
$B_V$, retaining the other root probes.  At another simple
vertex $p$, choose Frobenius lifts $g$ and $\phi_p$ for $q$ and
$p$.  If their transposition images are different, the derivative
under $g\mapsto g\tau_p$ deletes both $p$ and $q$ and transfers
their rational labels to the root total.  If their transposition
images are equal, the derivative is zero.
\item In the test in (iii), variation at a split $p$ is given by
the first-shell factors $c_p$ times symbols of merged
configurations whose weight is one less.  It consequently
vanishes whenever all symbols of that lower weight vanish.
\end{enumerate}
All these assertions preserve every specified label at the other
vertices, and use the chosen place for inertia and Frobenius.

statements.title: Symbol rules
statements.label: thm:symbol-rules
statements.text:
For either coefficient source of
Propositions~\ref{prop:even-coefficients} and
\ref{prop:odd-coefficients}, assume its stated coefficient
lower bound and use its normalized symbol and filter.
Then the following rules hold for finite configurations of
primes outside the level support.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item With rational two-torsion, the elementary-label
factorizations, contraction except in the simple--simple
case, and isolation by a trivial split label are those of
Proposition~\ref{tc:rational-rules}.  A pair of identical
simple labels realized with $\#E(\mathbf F_q)/2$ odd can be
inserted without changing the symbol, as in
Proposition~\ref{tc:simple-twins}.
\item With irreducible $E[2]$, all root probes combine into
one total rational elementary label.  A root-bit derivative
at a split vertex deletes that vertex, while at a simple
vertex it is zero.  The derivative between two simple
vertices deletes both when their transposition images are
different, and is zero when they are equal.  The remaining
simple--split shell has weight one less.  These are the
rules of Proposition~\ref{tc:irreducible-rules}.
\item At the least weight supporting a nonzero symbol in
the irreducible case, each nonroot may be moved with only
its fixed-support elementary Frobenius label prescribed;
internal edges impose no further condition on the value,
subject to matching the total root label.  This is
Lemma~\ref{tc:minimum-transfer}.
\end{enumerate}
The analytic and finite-Selmer consequences of a nonzero
symbol remain those of
Proposition~\ref{prop:unit-symbol-detection}.  In the odd
source the rules mean finite tests at arbitrarily high stages
chosen in the ultrafilter-large sets of the prescribed stabilization.

statements.title: Address lemma
statements.label: gr:address
statements.text:
Assume the contraction, isolation, and whole-prime omission rules of
Proposition~\ref{tc:rational-rules}, or the same rules for another
symbol, together with the realization freedoms of
Lemma~\ref{gr:realization}.  Let $b\ge1$ and
consider either of the following terminal arrangements:
\begin{enumerate}
\item One symbol on a nonempty set of always active terminals, whose
polynomial in the independent pair bits is nonzero.
\item One or two symbols on terminals with nonzero linear activations,
including a terminal for every nonzero linear form.  At each $x\ne0$,
each symbol separately is a nonzero polynomial in the active bits.
The symbols may have stationary external data and may read compatible
projections of a common graph.
\end{enumerate}
At every $x\ne0$, assume that the active terminal data and the stationary
external data obey each required filter.  Then finitely many primary
auxiliaries with nonzero linear activations, and one realizable assignment
of graph bits, make all the symbols $1$ at every $x\ne0$.  No auxiliary
is present at $0$.  All may satisfy fixed splitting and neutral-incidence
conditions included in their primary type.

A nonzero evaluation or a nonzero iterated edge difference suffices for
the polynomial hypothesis.  In particular, a partition as in
Definition~\ref{gr:partitionable} suffices in the stationary case.
statements.section_title: Prime graphs and simultaneous unit coefficients

statements.title: Partitionable even estimate
statements.label: pw:partitionable-even

statements.title: Uniform lower bound for the odd detector
statements.label: pw:odd-lower

statements.title: Families with a fixed companion
statements.label: pw:fixed-companion-families
statements.text:
With the fixed odd coefficient system and companion $k$ chosen in
Section~\ref{pw:fixed-companion-section}, suppose the odd symbol at $1$
is zero. There is a constant $C$ with the following property. For every $b\ge1$ there are distinct primes outside
$2Nk$ and the fixed supports of both coefficient tests, with nonzero
linear activations, such that their signed products $h_x$,
$x\in\F_2^b$, satisfy $h_0=1$. Every $h_x$ is positive and has the fixed
local classes of $1$, and every new prime splits in $K=\Q(\sqrt{k})$.
The primes also avoid the detecting prime of the actual odd coefficient
stage. In particular $(h_x,k)=1$ for every $x$. For every $x\ne0$,
\[
 a(E^{(h_x)})=1,\qquad L(E^{(h_xk)},1)\ne0,
\]
and
\[
 j(P_{h_x})\le w(h_x)+C,\qquad
 v(\mathcal L(h_xk))\le 2w(h_x)+C.
\]
The constant $C$ and the discriminant $k$ are independent of $b$.

statements.title: The rational-two-torsion converse
statements.label: thm:rational-converse
statements.text:
Let $E/\Q$ satisfy $E(\Q)[2]\ne0$ and
$c_2(E)=\operatorname{corank}_{\Z_2}\Sel_{2^\infty}(E/\Q)\in\{0,1\}$,
with the local Kummer conditions at every place.  Then
\[
                 \operatorname{ord}_{s=1}L(E,s)=c_2(E).
\]
There is no restriction on the rational isogeny configuration, complex
multiplication, or reduction at $2$ or at the bad primes.

statements.title: Nullity forces Selmer dimension
statements.label: prop:selmer-matrix-bound
statements.text:
Fix the curve, support types, a bound for the number of additional
constrained places, and a bound for the dimension of a stationary
environment. Partition a finite configuration into blocks with zero
cross-$M$ entries, and denote their matrices by $M_i$. There is a
constant depending only on these fixed data such that
\begin{equation}
 \dim_{\F_2}\Sel_2(E^{(h)}/\Q)
 \geq\sum_i\dim_{\F_2}\ker M_i-C.
\end{equation}
At a unit coefficient symbol the sum of nullities, and hence the
number of singular blocks, is therefore uniformly bounded. The bound
works for both coefficient sources and is independent of the moving
prime $\ell$.

statements.title: The irreducible converse
statements.label: thm:irreducible-converse
statements.text:
Let $E/\Q$ be an elliptic curve for which $E[2]$ is irreducible as a
$G_{\Q}$-module.  If
\[
 c_2(E)=\corank_{\Ztwo}\Sel_{2^\infty}(E/\Q)\in\{0,1\},
\]
then $\ord_{s=1}L(E,s)=c_2(E)$.

statements.title: An odd cube with a bounded even companion
statements.label: prop:sa:bounded-companion
statements.text:
For the fixed symbols $A,A_0$ just chosen, suppose $A(1)=0$.
There is a constant $C$ such that, for every sufficiently large $b$,
one can find an odd negative fundamental discriminant $k$ and a finite
family
\[
 h_x=\prod_p(p^*)^{f_p(x)},\qquad x\in\F_2^b,
 \qquad f_p:\F_2^b\longrightarrow\F_2\ \text{linear},
\]
with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item The primes are distinct good odd primes outside the fixed
exclusions; $h_0=1$, and every $h_x$ has the local squareclasses of
$1$ at the fixed support and at infinity. Each $h_x$ is coprime to $k$.
The field $K=\Q(\sqrt{k})$ satisfies the standing Heegner conditions.
\item The prime support of $k$ has cardinality at most $C$. At every
nonroot prime $p\mid\prod_xh_x$, the parameter $k$ is a local square.
At every nonroot prime $q\mid k$, every $h_x$ is a local square.
\item The simultaneous symbol values are
\[
 A_0(|k|)=1,\qquad
 A(|h_x|)=A_0(|kh_x|)=1\quad(x\ne0).
\]
Consequently $E^{(k)}$ has analytic rank zero and $s(k)\le C$.
\end{enumerate}
For the odd source, these assertions mean simultaneous actual tests at
arbitrarily high admissible precisions after $b$ and its finite set of
tests have been fixed. The constant $C$ is independent of $b$, that
precision, and all moving primes. The parameter $k$ may vary with the
finite realization.

statements.title: Central determinant formula
statements.label: prop:cy:specialization
statements.text:
There is a constant $C_{\mathrm{loc}}$, depending only on the fixed curve
and local classes, with the following property. Suppose
$c_2(E^{(h_x)})=0$. If $L(E^{(h_x)},1)=0$, then $u_x(0)=0$; if
$L(E^{(h_x)},1)\ne0$, then
\begin{equation}
 \bigl|v_2(u_x(0))-D(h_x)\bigr|\leq C_{\mathrm{loc}}.
\end{equation}
The rational positive complex at $t=0$ has cohomology only in degree one,
of dimension two, so these are specializations of the same determinant.

statements.title: Ring-class characters with prescribed local values
statements.label: rl:characters
statements.text:
Fix finitely many split primes of $K$ above odd rational primes, outside
$2N$, and orient one prime in each conjugate pair.  There are distinct
split rational primes $r_i$ avoiding all the fixed data and characters
\[
 \xi_i:\operatorname{Gal}(H_{r_i}/K)\longrightarrow
                 \mathbf Z/2^{n_i}\mathbf Z,
 \qquad n_i\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
such that $\xi_i$ is surjective on the inertia quotient at $r_i$, is zero
at the primes above $2N$, and has odd value at each prescribed oriented
prime.  We can require $r_i\to1$ in $\mathbf Z_2$ and
\begin{equation}
 v_2(2+a_{r_i}(E)),\quad v_2(2-a_{r_i}(E)),\quad
 v_2\det(1\pm\operatorname{Fr}_{r_i}\mid T)\ \leq c_E.
\end{equation}
The constant $c_E$ is independent of the list and of $K$.

statements.title: Integral evaluation through the outer limit
statements.label: rl:outer-evaluation
statements.text:
Let $C_j$ be any family of the preceding limiting complexes, completed
over $\mathcal O_j=\widehat{\Lambda_{(2)}}$, possibly for different
quadratic fields $K_j$.  Suppose their minimal ranks are bounded.
Assume a common bounded cohomological degree interval. Keep the
actual evaluation matrices and transport them to the minimal models
through integral contractions.  For a nonprincipal
ultrafilter $\mathcal U$, put
\[
 \mathcal O_\infty=
 \left(\prod_{\mathcal U}\mathcal O_j\right)/\mathfrak a,
 \qquad
 \mathfrak a=\{(x_j):
    \{j:v_2(x_j)\geq n\}\in\mathcal U\text{ for every }n\}.
\]
Then $\mathcal O_\infty$ is a DVR with uniformizer $2$ and a
characteristic-zero fraction field $L_\infty$. The outer $H^1$ over
$L_\infty$ injects into crossed classes on the inner quadratic sequence
group product, or its extension by one simultaneous complex conjugation
for the induced representation.  Its restriction to the product
of their exact common kernels is injective.  All arbitrary-sequence
degree-two evaluation identities survive.  These conclusions also
hold after retaining any fixed finite collection of additional
integral diagrams.

statements.title: Compatibility of the limit constructions
statements.label: rl:limit-evaluation-package
statements.text:
The finite free models, ring-class characters, local conditions and
pairings constructed above can be retained simultaneously. Their
inner limits have the stated height-one acyclicity and all-sequence
cohomology detection. For all-split ring data with bounded
$\omega(\operatorname{disc}K)$, the residual model sizes are bounded
independently of the active conductor support. Their outer limits
retain arbitrary evaluations, exact-kernel injectivity and finite
Chebotarev realization after any fixed number of additional
integral arithmetic operations.

Graph Decompositions at the Integral Expectation Threshold
abstract: We prove the graph-decomposition conjecture of Ascoli, He, Park, and Talagrand. Every graph admits a partition into a universally bounded number of fixed edge pieces, each having ordinary containment threshold at most a universal constant times the original graph's integral expectation threshold. The partition is chosen before sampling the random host, and the separate embeddings of the pieces need not agree on shared vertices.

tex.abstract:
We prove the graph-decomposition conjecture of Ascoli, He, Park,
and Talagrand. Every graph admits a partition into a universally
bounded number of fixed edge pieces, each having ordinary containment
threshold at most a universal constant times the original graph's
integral expectation threshold. The partition is chosen before
sampling the random host, and the separate embeddings of the pieces
need not agree on shared vertices.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There exist an absolute integer $k\geq2$ and an absolute constant
$L\geq1$ such that, for every $n\geq2$ and every graph $H$ on
at most $n$ vertices, the edges of $H$ admit a partition
\[
 E(H)=E(H_1)\,\dot\cup\,\cdots\,\dot\cup\,E(H_k)
 \quad\text{with}\quad
 p_c(H_i;n)\leq Lq(H;n)\qquad(1\leq i\leq k).
\]
The pieces may be empty and may share vertices. The partition
depends only on $H,n$ and is fixed before the random host is sampled.

statements.title: Discrete convexity, {\cite[Theorem~1.1]{OpenAI26DC}}
statements.label: thm:discrete
statements.text:
Set $K_0=2^{75}$. For every nonempty finite set $X$, every
$r\in(0,1)$, and every family $\calD\subseteq2^X$ with
$\mu_r(\calD)\geq1-1/K_0$, the family
\[
 \mathcal E_{K_0}(\calD)=
 \{S\subseteq X:S\not\subseteq D_1\cup\cdots\cup D_{K_0}
                   \text{ for every }D_1,\ldots,D_{K_0}\in\calD\}
\]
has a cover of cost at most $1/2$ at the same parameter $r$.
The family $\calD$ need not be monotone, and members of a tuple
may repeat.

statements.label: cor:typical-cover
statements.text:
Let $n\geq2$, let $H$ have an edge and at most $n$ vertices,
and suppose $q(H;n)<r<1$. If a family of graphs on $[n]$
satisfies $\mu_r(\calD)\geq1-1/K_0$, then some copy of $H$
has its edges contained in the union of $K_0$ members of $\calD$.

statements.label: prop:transfer
prop:degree-embedding
statements.text:
There is an absolute integer $N_2$ such that, for $n\geq N_2$
and $r,s$ satisfying \eqref{eq:parameters}, every graph $J$
with
\[
 |V_+(J)|\leq n/4,\qquad \degen(J)\leq s,
 \qquad\Delta(J)\leq n^{2/3}
\]
and at most $n$ vertices satisfies $p_c(J;n)\leq r$.

statements.label: prop:stars
statements.text:
Put $A=400e^4$. There is an absolute integer $N_3$ such that,
for every $n\geq N_3$ and every star forest $J$ on at most $n$
vertices with $|V_+(J)|\leq n/100$,
\begin{equation}
 p_c(J;n)\leq2Aq(J;n).
\end{equation}
If $q(J;n)<1/(2A)$, the stronger bound
$p_c(J;n)\leq Aq(J;n)$ holds.

title: Ground-state condensation in the dilute hard-sphere gas
abstract: We prove Bose–Einstein condensation in every ground state of a dilute three-dimensional hard-sphere Bose gas. At every sufficiently small fixed gas parameter, the constant orbital contains a positive fraction of the particles in the thermodynamic limit. The fraction can be chosen independently of the gas parameter, and the conclusion holds for arbitrary complex ground states.

tex.abstract:
We prove Bose--Einstein condensation in every ground state of a dilute
three-dimensional hard-sphere Bose gas. At every sufficiently small fixed gas
parameter, the constant orbital contains a positive fraction of the particles
in the thermodynamic limit. The fraction can be chosen independently of the
gas parameter, and the conclusion holds for arbitrary complex ground states.

statements.title: Condensation in every ground state
statements.label: main:theorem
statements.text:
There are absolute constants $\varepsilon_0,c_0>0$ with the following
property. Fix $a,\rho>0$ satisfying $\rho a^3<\varepsilon_0$.
For every sequence of particle numbers $N_k$ and lengths $L_k$ such that
\[
 N_k\longrightarrow\infty,\qquad L_k\longrightarrow\infty,
 \qquad \frac{N_k}{L_k^3}\longrightarrow\rho,
\]
and every choice of normalized, possibly complex, bosonic ground
eigenvectors $\Psi_k$ of the hard-sphere Hamiltonians,
\begin{equation}
 \liminf_{k\to\infty} B(\Psi_k)\ge c_0.
\end{equation}

statements.title: Ground-space states
statements.label: main:mixed
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{main:theorem}, the same lower
bound holds for every sequence of density operators supported on the
bosonic ground eigenspaces. In particular, it holds for the normalized
ground-space projections $\Pi_k/\Tr\Pi_k$, and for every sequence of
normalized nonnegative ground functions.

statements.title: Averaged collision bound
statements.label: bridge:averaged-hit
statements.text:
Fix $m\ge\ell D/2$ pairs $(y_i,z_i)$ with $y_i\in B_v$ and
$|z_i-v|\le3$.  Assume that each of the two endpoint lists is
$s_0$-separated.  Let $c$ be a deterministic regular torus path whose
outer endpoints are at distance greater than $s_0$ from the corresponding
endpoints of every label under consideration.  Then, for every target
cell $B$,
\begin{equation}
 \frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m
 Q_{y_i,z_i}^{B}(\mathcal C_v\cap\mathcal H(c))
 \le Ctr+C\frac{rD^{3\gamma}}{D\sqrt{h_0}}.
\end{equation}
The same conclusion holds if $c$ is the original path of one of these
labels: omit that label's summand and retain the divisor $m$, assuming
endpoint separation for all the remaining labels.  The constant $C$ may
depend on $b,\ell,C_{\rm reg}$, but is independent of small $t$.

statements.title: Supply of successful labels
statements.label: bridge:success-supply
statements.text:
Consider a collection of deterministic torus paths with endpoints
$(y_j,z_j)$, and fix a cell $v$.  Suppose that at most $H_1D$ of these
paths visit the ball of radius $12$ about $v$, and that every visiting
path is regular.  Suppose a list of $m\ge\ell D/2$ labels satisfies
$y_i\in B_v$, $|z_i-v|\le3$, and that both endpoints of every listed
label are at distance greater than $s_0$ from every other endpoint in
the corresponding full configuration.

Call a trial for label $i$ successful if it satisfies $\mathcal C_v$
and avoids every obstacle path except the original path of $i$.
For sufficiently small fixed $t>0$ and then sufficiently large $D$,
at least $9m/10$ listed labels have the following property: for each
of the seven target cells $B$, the set
\begin{equation}
 T_{i,B}=\{u\in B:
     Q_{y_i,z_i}^u(\text{successful trial})\ge9/10\}
\end{equation}
has volume at least $99/100$.
All choices are uniform in the deterministic collection, $v$, and
$\alpha\in[\alpha_0/2,2\alpha_0]$.

statements.title: Exact conditional law
statements.label: group:conditional-law
statements.text:
For almost every exposed datum the normalizers in
Equation~\eqref{group:reference} are positive, and the conditional law
of the unexposed trajectories is
\begin{equation}
 \lambda_{\mathcal I}(\dd\omega_{\mathcal I})
 =\frac{1}{Z_{\mathcal I}}
   \ind_{\{\text{all pairs in $\mathcal I$ avoid each other}\}}
   \prod_{i\in\mathcal I}P_i(\dd\omega_i),
 \qquad Z_{\mathcal I}>0.
\end{equation}
All reference trajectories obey their own regularity and confinement
cutoffs.  Each label has at most $C M$ other labels in this group with
which a collision can be possible, where $C$ is a fixed geometric
constant.

statements.title: Density and deterministic compatibility
statements.label: group:comparison
statements.text:
There is a constant $G\ge2$, fixed after $t$ and independent of $D,K,M$,
such that
\begin{equation}
 \Pi_i^U\ll P_i,\qquad
 0\le\frac{\dd\Pi_i^U}{\dd P_i}\le G,
 \qquad \int\frac{\dd\Pi_i^U}{\dd P_i}\dd P_i=1.
\end{equation}
There is also $\eta_D\to0$, uniform in the exposed datum, with the
following property.  Fix any regular, confined trajectory of a distinct
label in $\mathcal I$, keeping its recorded endpoints.  Under either
$P_i$ or $\Pi_i^U$, the probability of colliding with that deterministic
trajectory is at most $\eta_D$.  Its label need not be accessible.
One may take
\begin{equation}
 \eta_D=C_t\bigl(tr+rD^{3\gamma}h_0^{-1/2}\bigr)
 \le C_t' D^{-1/4}.
\end{equation}

statements.title: Good paths with bounded encounters
statements.label: lat:paths
statements.text:
Fix an integer $R\ge1$.  There are constants
$p_0,\kappa>0$, $C_{\rm path}<\infty$, and an integer $K_0$, depending
only on $R$, with the following property.  Suppose $K\ge K_0$ and
\eqref{lat:bad-law} holds with $p\le p_0$.  For every admissible ordered
pair $(v,w)$ there is a $\mathcal D$-measurable event $\mathcal E_{v,w}$
of probability at least $1/2$.  On this event there is a measurable
probability kernel on simple good nearest-neighbor paths from $v$ to $w$.
Two independent draws from this kernel, conditional on $\mathcal D$,
satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \E\left[
   \ind_{\mathcal E_{v,w}}
   \E\left[e^{\kappa J_R(\pi,\pi')}\mid\mathcal D\right]
       \right]\le C_{\rm path}.
\end{equation}
The constants are uniform in the datum, its law, and the endpoint pair.
For every sufficiently large $K$, at least $\upsilon_0K^6$ ordered pairs
are admissible.
statements.section_title: Paths through a sparse set of obstacles

statements.title: Uniform modulus occupation
statements.label: cmp:modulus
statements.text:
After the fixed choices above, there are constants $D_0<\infty$ and
\begin{equation}
 c_*:=\frac{\upsilon_0\ell}{32M G C_{\mathrm{path}}}>0,
 \qquad \upsilon_0=\frac1{2000}
\end{equation}
such that, whenever $D\ge D_0$, $\alpha=Dr\in[\alpha_0/2,2\alpha_0]$,
and $K$ is sufficiently large, every normalized nonnegative bosonic ground
function satisfies $B(\Phi)\ge c_*$. The constant $c_*$ is unchanged if
the lower threshold on $D$ is subsequently increased. The volume thresholds
can be taken locally uniform for $D$ in compact subintervals of
$[D_0,\infty)$.
statements.section_title: A common measure and a uniform modulus bound

statements.title: Small omitted volume
statements.label: geom:omitted-volume
statements.text:
Fix the constants as above and take $D$ sufficiently large. There are
absolute constants $C,C_{\rm an}$ such that, for $K\ge100$ and
$C_{\rm an}p_D\le1/2$,
\begin{equation}
 \delta_{\rm geom}:=\int\frac{|\cA(Y)|}{V}\,\nu(\dd Y)
 \le C r^2D+C p_D
       +K^3(C_{\rm an}p_D)^{\lfloor K/10\rfloor}.
\end{equation}
The retained points belong to one component of the open slice
$S_Y$ whenever the retained set is nonempty. The estimate is uniform
over the normalized ground vector and $\alpha\in[\alpha_0/2,2\alpha_0]$.
statements.section_title: A common component in each one-particle slice

statements.label: main:scaled
statements.text:
There are absolute constants $\alpha_0,D_*,c_*>0$ such that, for
$D=N/K^3\ge D_*$ and $r=\alpha/D$ with
$\alpha\in[\alpha_0/2,2\alpha_0]$, every normalized complex bosonic
ground vector satisfies
\[
 B(\Psi)\ge c_*/2
\]
for all sufficiently large integer $K$. The volume threshold can be
chosen uniformly when $D$ ranges over a fixed compact subinterval of
$[D_*,\infty)$, and is independent of the chosen ground vector.

title: Hamiltonian Fixed Points Below the Stable Morse Number
abstract: We disprove the stable Morse lower bound for nondegenerate Hamiltonian fixed points by constructing a simply connected closed Kähler manifold with sixteen fewer fixed points than its stable Morse number. All the corresponding periodic orbits are contractible. The construction combines a Hamiltonian involution with integral homology torsion at two different primes; its proof uses finite-dimensional Morse theory and complex blowups.

tex.abstract: We disprove the stable Morse lower bound for nondegenerate Hamiltonian fixed points by constructing a simply connected closed Kähler manifold with sixteen fewer fixed points than its stable Morse number. All the corresponding periodic orbits are contractible. The construction combines a Hamiltonian involution with integral homology torsion at two different primes; its proof uses finite-dimensional Morse theory and complex blowups.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There exist a simply connected closed Kähler manifold $(M,\omega)$ and a smooth one-periodic Hamiltonian $H$ such that every fixed point of $\phi_H^1$ is nondegenerate and
\[
 \#\Fix_0(\phi_H^1;H)=\#\Fix(\phi_H^1)=\SM(M)-16.
\]
One may take $\dim_{\R}M=1412$, with $\SM(M)=318968$ and $\#\Fix(\phi_H^1)=318952$.

statements.text:
Let $W$ be a simply connected closed smooth manifold of dimension $D\geq9$.
There is an ordinary Morse function on $W$ with
\[
 r_i(W)+t_i(W)+t_{i-1}(W)
\]
critical points of index $i$ for every $i$.  In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \SM(W)=\Morse(W)=\lambda(W).
\end{equation}

statements.label: prop:blowup
statements.text:
Let $A$ be a compact connected K\"ahler manifold, and let $Z\subset A$
be a closed connected complex submanifold of complex codimension
$c\geq2$. Its complex blow-up $\pi:\widehat A\to A$ is compact,
connected, and K\"ahler. If $A$ is simply connected, then so is
$\widehat A$. For every integer $i$ there is an isomorphism of abelian
groups
\begin{equation}

 H_i(\widehat A;\Z)
 \cong H_i(A;\Z)\oplus
 \bigoplus_{j=1}^{c-1}H_{i-2j}(Z;\Z).
\end{equation}

statements.label: prop:involution
statements.text:
Let $(P,\omega)$ be a closed symplectic manifold, and let $g:P\to P$ be a
Hamiltonian diffeomorphism satisfying $g^2=\mathrm{id}_P$.  Write
\[
  \Fix(g)=F_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup F_r
\]
for its connected fixed components.  For each $j$, choose a smooth Morse
function $h_j:F_j\to\R$.  There exists a $g$-invariant smooth function
$f:P\to\R$ with $f|_{F_j}=h_j$ such that, for all sufficiently small
$\epsilon>0$, the map
\[
  \Phi_\epsilon=\psi^\epsilon\circ g,
\]
where $\psi^s$ is the Hamiltonian flow of $f$, satisfies
\begin{equation}
  \Fix(\Phi_\epsilon)
    =\bigsqcup_{j=1}^r\operatorname{Crit}(h_j).
\end{equation}
Every fixed point of $\Phi_\epsilon$ is nondegenerate.  Moreover,
$\Phi_\epsilon$ is the time-one map of a smooth one-periodic Hamiltonian.
If $P$ is simply connected, all its fixed-point loops for this Hamiltonian
are contractible.

statements.label: prop:surface
statements.text:
Let $Y$ be the complex blow-up of $\CP^1\times\CP^1$ at the four points
\[
  \{0,\infty\}\times\{0,\infty\}.
\]
There is a circle-invariant K\"ahler form $\omega_Y$ for which the lifted
diagonal circle action is Hamiltonian.  Its half-turn $g_Y$ has precisely
four fixed components, the exceptional curves $E_1,\ldots,E_4$, each
isomorphic to $\CP^1$.  Along each $E_j$, the derivative of $g_Y$ is the
identity on the tangent bundle and minus the identity on the symplectic
normal bundle.  The surface $Y$ is simply connected, and
\begin{equation}
  H_i(Y;\Z)\cong
  \begin{cases}
    \Z,&i=0,4,\\
    \Z^6,&i=2,\\
    0,&\text{otherwise}.
  \end{cases}
\end{equation}

statements.label: cor:product-realization
statements.text:
Let $(X,\omega_X)$ be a connected closed simply connected K\"ahler manifold,
let $(Y,\omega_Y)$ be the surface in Proposition~\ref{prop:surface}, and give
$M=X\times Y$ the product symplectic form
$\omega_X\oplus\omega_Y$.  Put $C=X\times\CP^1$.
For every smooth Morse function $h:C\to\R$, there is a smooth one-periodic
Hamiltonian $H$ on $M$ such that every fixed point of its time-one map is
nondegenerate and contractible for its Hamiltonian path, and
\[
  \#\Fix(\phi_H^1)=\#\Fix_0(\phi_H^1;H)
       =4\,\#\operatorname{Crit}(h).
\]

title: Hamiltonian Fixed Points Below the Stable Morse Number in Dimension Twenty-Two
abstract: We disprove the stable Morse lower bound for nondegenerate Hamiltonian fixed points with examples in fixed real dimension twenty-two. For every integer m ≥ 1, we construct a simply connected closed Kähler manifold with stable Morse number \(80+1968m\) and a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism with exactly \(80+1952m\) fixed points, all nondegenerate and with contractible orbit loops. The deficit is therefore unbounded, and the fixed-point count is at most 127/128 of the stable Morse number.

tex.abstract:
We disprove the stable Morse lower bound for nondegenerate Hamiltonian
fixed points with examples in fixed real dimension twenty-two. For every
integer $m\geq1$, we construct a simply connected closed Kähler manifold
with stable Morse number $80+1968m$ and a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism with
exactly $80+1952m$ fixed points, all nondegenerate and with contractible
orbit loops. The deficit is therefore unbounded, and the fixed-point count
is at most $127/128$ of the stable Morse number.
sections: Torsion in a fixed complex dimension
From Morse functions to Hamiltonian fixed points
The integral counts and the relative deficit
Attaining the integral bound by handle cancellation

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every integer $m\geq1$, there exist a simply connected closed Kähler
manifold $(M_m,\omega_m)$ of real dimension $22$ and a smooth one-periodic
Hamiltonian $H_m$ such that all fixed points of $\phi_{H_m}^1$ are
nondegenerate and
\begin{align*}
 \SM(M_m)&=80+1968m,\\
 \#\Fix(\phi_{H_m}^1)
 &=\#\Fix_0(\phi_{H_m}^1;H_m)=80+1952m.
\end{align*}
Consequently, with $\delta=1/128$, for every $R>0$ some member of this
family satisfies
\[
 \SM(M_m)\geq R,\qquad
 \#\Fix(\phi_{H_m}^1)\leq(1-\delta)\SM(M_m).
\]

statements.label: morse:equality
statements.text:
Let $W$ be a simply connected closed smooth manifold of dimension
$D\geq9$.  There is an ordinary Morse function on $W$ with exactly
\[
 r_i(W)+t_i(W)+t_{i-1}(W)
\]
critical points of index $i$ for every $i$.  Consequently
\begin{equation}
 \SM(W)=\Morse(W)=\lambda(W).
\end{equation}

statements.label: geo:blowup
statements.text:
Let $A$ be a compact connected K\"ahler manifold and
$Z\subset A$ a nonempty closed connected complex submanifold of complex
codimension $c\geq2$. The complex blow-up
$\pi:\widehat A\to A$ is compact, connected, and K\"ahler.
If $A$ is simply connected, then $\widehat A$ is simply connected.
For every integer $i$,
\begin{equation}

 H_i(\widehat A;\Z)\cong
 H_i(A;\Z)\oplus\bigoplus_{j=1}^{c-1}H_{i-2j}(Z;\Z),
\end{equation}
where homology in negative degrees is zero.

statements.title: Perturbing a Hamiltonian involution
statements.label: dyn:involution
statements.text:
Let $(P,\omega)$ be a closed symplectic manifold and let $g:P\to P$
be a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism with $g^2=\mathrm{id}_P$.  Write
$\Fix(g)=F_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup F_r$ for its connected fixed
components.  For each $j$, let $h_j:F_j\to\R$ be a smooth Morse
function.  There is a smooth $g$-invariant function $f:P\to\R$
restricting to $h_j$ on $F_j$ such that, for all sufficiently small
$\epsilon>0$, its Hamiltonian flow $\psi^s$ satisfies
\begin{equation}

  \Fix(\psi^\epsilon\circ g)
    =\bigsqcup_{j=1}^r\Crit(h_j).
\end{equation}
Every fixed point in this equality is nondegenerate.  Moreover,
$\psi^\epsilon\circ g$ is the time-one map of a smooth one-periodic
Hamiltonian.  If $P$ is simply connected, all fixed-point loops along
the resulting Hamiltonian path are contractible.

statements.title: The surface with four fixed curves
statements.label: dyn:surface
statements.text:
Let $Y$ be the complex blow-up of $\CP^1\times\CP^1$ at
\[
  \{0,\infty\}\times\{0,\infty\}.
\]
There is a circle-invariant K\"ahler form $\omega_Y$ for which the
lifted diagonal circle action is Hamiltonian.  Its half-turn $g_Y$
has fixed locus precisely the four exceptional curves
$E_1,\ldots,E_4$, each isomorphic to $\CP^1$.  Along these curves,
$d g_Y$ is the identity on the tangent bundle and minus the identity
on the symplectic normal bundle.  Moreover, $Y$ is simply connected
and its integral homology is
\begin{equation}

  H_i(Y;\Z)\cong
  \begin{cases}
    \Z,&i=0,4,\\
    \Z^6,&i=2,\\
    0,&\text{otherwise}.
  \end{cases}
\end{equation}

statements.title: Product realization
statements.label: dyn:product
statements.text:
Let $X$ be a connected closed simply connected K\"ahler manifold,
let $\omega_X$ be any K\"ahler form on $X$, and let $(Y,\omega_Y)$ be as in
Proposition~\ref{dyn:surface}.  Give $M=X\times Y$ the product form
$\omega_X\oplus\omega_Y$ and put $C=X\times\CP^1$.
For every smooth Morse function $h:C\to\R$, there is a smooth
one-periodic Hamiltonian $H$ on $M$ whose time-one map has only
nondegenerate fixed points and satisfies
\begin{equation}

  \#\Fix(\phi_H^1)
   =\#\Fix_0(\phi_H^1;H)
   =4\,\#\Crit(h).
\end{equation}

title: Hard-sphere fluctuations on the regular Boltzmann lifespan
abstract: We prove a finite-dimensional central limit theorem away from equilibrium for a deterministic grand-canonical hard-sphere gas in three dimensions. The initial probability density is smooth, with spatially summable Gaussian velocity bounds on the density and its spatial gradient. The limit holds on every finite interval on which the classical Boltzmann solution has uniform Gaussian velocity decay. The empirical measure is centered by its exact microscopic expectation. Its fluctuations converge to the Gaussian solution of the linear fluctuating Boltzmann equation.

tex.abstract:
We prove a finite-dimensional central limit theorem away from equilibrium
for a deterministic grand-canonical hard-sphere gas in three dimensions.
The initial probability density is smooth, with spatially summable
Gaussian velocity bounds on the density and its spatial gradient.
The limit holds on every finite interval on which the classical Boltzmann
solution has uniform Gaussian velocity decay.
The empirical measure is centered by its exact microscopic expectation.
Its fluctuations converge to the Gaussian solution of the linear
fluctuating Boltzmann equation.

The initial ensemble and the Gaussian target
Layered histories and the analytic inputs
A componentwise expansion with particle records
Sharp bounds and the limiting tree measures
Identification of the covariance and the Gaussian limit
The probability of a dynamical cutoff
Exact centering and the hard-sphere fluctuation limit

statements.title: Finite-dimensional fluctuation limit
statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Under \Cref{ass:kinetic}, the centered Gaussian generalized field
\(\zeta\) with weak equation
\begin{equation}
 \dd\zeta_t(\phi)=\zeta_t(A_t\phi)\,\dd t+\dd W_t(\phi)
\end{equation}
is well defined by its backward mild form on a scale of tests with small
Gaussian growth. Its initial field is independent of \(W\), and
\begin{align}
 \E[\zeta_0(\phi)\zeta_0(\psi)]
   &=\int_{\R^6}f_0\phi\psi\,\dd z,\\
 \E[W_t(\phi)W_s(\psi)]
   &=\int_0^{t\wedge s}C_r(\phi,\psi)\,\dd r.
\end{align}
The Gaussian noise \(W\) has independent increments. For every integer
\(m\ge1\), fixed times \(t_1,\ldots,t_m\in[0,T]\), and real tests
\(\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_m\in C_c^\infty(\R^6)\),
\begin{equation}
 \bigl(\zeta_{t_1}^\eps(\phi_1),\ldots,
       \zeta_{t_m}^\eps(\phi_m)\bigr)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \bigl(\zeta_{t_1}(\phi_1),\ldots,
       \zeta_{t_m}(\phi_m)\bigr)
 \qquad(\eps\downarrow0).
\end{equation}

statements.title: DHM analytic package
statements.label: thm:dhm-package
statements.text:
Assume \Cref{ass:kinetic}, the parameter hierarchy
\eqref{eq:dhm-cutoffs}--\eqref{eq:dhm-exponents}, and a common bound on
the Gaussian Bol norms of all birth inputs. For sufficiently large
fixed \(L\) and sufficiently small \(\eps\), the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
 \item For admissible dependent histories with prescribed labeled roots,
 fixed \(b\), and complexity \(\rho\), the sum of their normalized
 positive integrals is at most
 \begin{equation}
 C^b\tau^{b/10}\eps^{c_*\rho}
       |\log\eps|^{C_*\rho}.
 \end{equation}
 The sum includes the graph enumeration and the admissible indicator
 restrictions; a bounded observable multiplier costs its supremum.
 The birth inputs need not equal the approximate density constructed
 in the source, but must satisfy its common Gaussian Bol envelope.

 \item Suppose the independent input \(g\) in slab \(i\) satisfies
 \begin{equation}
 \|g-f_{(i-1)\tau}\|_{\Bol,\beta_{i-1}}
       \le\eps^{\theta_{i-1}}.
 \end{equation}
 Let \(\mathsf T_i^\eps[g]\) be the leading signed sum just defined.
 Then
 \begin{equation}
 \|\mathsf T_i^\eps[g]-f_{i\tau}\|_{\Bol,\beta_i}
       \le\tfrac12\eps^{\theta_i}.
 \end{equation}
 In the fixed-top-endpoint norm \(\Bol,\widetilde\beta_i\), the summed
 absolute contributions of cyclic members of \(\mathcal T_i\), members
 of \(\mathcal T_i^{\mathrm{err}}\), and tree members of
 \(\mathcal T_i\) with at least \(\Lambda_i/3\) lines are
 \(o(\eps^{\theta_i})\). Fixed powers of the cutoffs, arising from a
 bounded number of selected edge positions, can be included. A fixed
 exponential factor per atom can also be included by choosing \(L\)
 sufficiently large.
\end{enumerate}
Part (b) also holds uniformly when the final slab stops at any
\(0\le\sigma\le\tau\). With the same cutoffs and exponent budgets,
write \(\mathsf T_{i,\sigma}^\eps\) for its signed tree sum. Then
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{0\le\sigma\le\tau}
 \|\mathsf T_{i,\sigma}^\eps[g]
          -f_{(i-1)\tau+\sigma}\|_{\Bol,\beta_i}
       \le\tfrac12\eps^{\theta_i},
\end{equation}
and the positive error classes obey the same full-\(\tau\) upper
majorants uniformly in \(\sigma\). At \(\sigma=0\) the map is the
identity and its contact error classes vanish.
The assertion in (b) is about the specified complete signed tree sum
and positive error classes. Identifying a different one-root operator
with that sum up to those errors requires a separate combinatorial
argument.
statements.section_title: Layered histories and the analytic inputs

statements.title: Independent factors
statements.label: prop:one-root
statements.text:
The measures $g_i$ have Gaussian Bol-bounded density representatives.
With the exponents $\beta_i,\theta_i$ of
\Cref{thm:dhm-package}, for sufficiently small $\eps$,
\begin{equation}
 \|g_i-f_{i\tau}\|_{\Bol,\beta_i}\le\eps^{\theta_i},\qquad
 \sup_{0\le i\le L}\|g_i\|_{\Bol,\beta_i}\le C.
\end{equation}
The same estimates hold for the one-root map run through any portion
$\sigma\in[0,\tau]$ of slab $i$, with target
$f_{(i-1)\tau+\sigma}$ and exponent $\beta_i$.
statements.section_title: A componentwise expansion with particle records

statements.title: Marked component expansion
statements.label: thm:marked-expansion
statements.text:
Choose $\Gamma$ and then $L$ as above.  These choices are independent of
the moment order and the fixed observation list.  On this single pasted
dynamics the following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
 \item The factorial hierarchy with any fixed finite list of records
 has the finite componentwise expansion
 \eqref{eq:retained-hierarchy}, with the variation error
 \eqref{eq:retained-variation-error}.  Its independent inputs are the
 $g_i$ in \Cref{prop:one-root}; its label weights, continuations, and
 record projections are those of
 \Cref{lem:marked-regrouping,lem:diagram-labels}.
 \item At each fixed final order $h$, the actual normalized marked
 factorial cumulant $c_h^\eps$ is the sum of retained globally connected
 diagrams, plus an error of total variation at most
 $C_h e^{-c\Lambda_L}$.  A nontrivial initial cumulant block is part of
 this connectivity.  Dummy links are not.
 \item For any fixed accuracy power $P$, one can choose a constant
 $K$ after the observation list and $h$ such that all remaining
 retained diagrams with $\rho>K$ have summed absolute variation at
 most $\eps^P$.  At $\rho\le K$ the original fresh-label factorials
 satisfy \eqref{eq:bounded-crossing-factorials}.  Neither increasing
 $K$ nor increasing a fixed moment order changes the exponential base
 per ordinary atom in the preceding estimates.
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: A componentwise expansion with particle records

statements.title: Terminal-witness expansion
statements.label: cor:terminal-witness
statements.text:
In slab $i$, let a terminal witness be a connected true C history on
$n\le3\Lambda_i$ incoming labels, of excess at most $2\Gamma$, stopped
at a contact time in that slab.  It may carry arbitrary further
nonnegative realizability restrictions.  Sum its indicator with the
full activity normalization
\begin{equation}
 \sum_n\frac{\mu^n}{n!}
       \int F_{i-1,n}(\dd Z_n)\,
                       \ind_{\text{terminal witness}}(Z_n).
\end{equation}
For the terminal classes in \Cref{lem:dhm-dummies}(ii), this
expression has the preceding retained
layer expansion, with independent $g$ inputs and initial blocks.
All lower C/O components attach through particle lines to the
terminal witness.  The preceding variation error is smaller than every
fixed power of $\eps$.  After the artificial-top-root normalization
cost $\mu$, the coarse part with $\rho>K$ can also be made smaller than
any assigned power by choosing $K$ sufficiently large.  The remaining
low-complexity witness integrals retain their realizability restrictions.
statements.section_title: A componentwise expansion with particle records

statements.title: Sharp connected bounds
statements.label: thm:sharp-cumulants
statements.text:
Choose the parameters \(\Gamma,L\) as in
\Cref{thm:marked-expansion}, increasing \(L\), if necessary,
by an amount depending only on the uniform bounds for the Boltzmann
solution and on \(T\).  This one choice works for every fixed factorial
order and every fixed bounded observation list.  For each fixed \(h\),
\begin{equation}
 \|c_h^\eps\|_{\TV}\le C_h\mu^{1-h}.
\end{equation}
For \(h=1,2\), the measures \(\mu^{h-1}c_h^\eps\) converge against
bounded continuous record tests to the signed sums of the retained
global trees with trivial initial cumulants.  At a contact their weight
is the incoming flux
\([(v-v_*)\cdot\omega]_+\,\dd t\,\dd\omega\); a scattering contact
has sign \(+1\), and a non-scattering contact has sign \(-1\).
The independent birth factors are \(f_{i\tau}\).

The sums of the absolute retained diagram measures, after multiplication
by \(\mu^{h-1}\), are bounded uniformly with a sufficiently small
Gaussian weight in their designated endpoint velocities.  The same
bound holds for the limiting tree measures, and for the Gaussian weights
in finitely many retained record velocities after decreasing the exponent.
Among the retained connected diagrams, the sum of the absolute measures
having a nontrivial initial cumulant or a global cycle is
\(o(\mu^{1-h})\).  The assertions about Gaussian weights concern retained
diagrams and their limits; no weighted estimate for a microscopic
expansion remainder is asserted.
statements.section_title: Sharp bounds and the limiting tree measures

statements.title: Evolution of the marked tree laws
statements.label: prop:tree-evolution
statements.text:
Between observation updates the limiting measures satisfy
\begin{align}
 \partial_tF_t(\Phi)
  &=F_t(D\Phi)+\frac12\int BF_tF_{t,*}\Delta\Phi,
       \\
 \partial_tJ_t(\Phi\otimes\Psi)
  &=J_t\bigl((D+H_t)\Phi\otimes\Psi
                     +\Phi\otimes(D+H_t)\Psi\bigr)\notag\\
  &\quad+\int BF_tF_{t,*}
          \bigl(\Phi(\xi')\Psi(\xi_*')
                         -\Phi(\xi)\Psi(\xi_*)\bigr).
       
\end{align}
The identities hold in transport mild form, and hence in weak
differential form for smooth tests for which the displayed integrals
exist.  At an update \(t_j\),
\begin{equation}
       F_{t_j+}=(\Theta_j)_\#F_{t_j-},
       \qquad
       J_{t_j+}=(\Theta_j\otimes\Theta_j)_\#J_{t_j-}.
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Identification of the covariance and the Gaussian limit

statements.title: Gaussian limit on the pasted dynamics
statements.label: prop:cumulant-clt
statements.text:
For the single pasted dynamics fixed above and every fixed observation
list,
\[
 \frac{\sum_i y_i(T)-\E\sum_i y_i(T)}{\sqrt\mu}
       \ \Longrightarrow\
           \sum_j\zeta_{t_j}(\phi_j).
\]
All centered moments of the scalar random variable on the left
converge to the corresponding Gaussian moments.
statements.section_title: Identification of the covariance and the Gaussian limit

statements.title: Accuracy of the pasted dynamics
statements.label: prop:cutoff
statements.text:
There is a sufficiently large dimensional integer \(\Gamma_0\) with the
following property.  Fix \(\Gamma\geq\Gamma_0\).  There is
\(L_0=L_0(\Gamma,f_0,f,T,\beta)\) such that, for any fixed \(L\geq L_0\),
the true dynamics and the pasted dynamics of
\Cref{thm:marked-expansion}, coupled using the same initial configuration,
satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \P\{\text{the two trajectories differ at some time in }[0,T]\}
 \leq C\eps^{1+\eta}
\end{equation}
for all sufficiently small \(\eps\), where one may take
\(\eta=1/20\).  Here the size cutoffs are the \(A_i,\Lambda_i\) of
\Cref{thm:dhm-package}, and \(C\) and the upper bound on \(\eps\) may
depend on the displayed fixed parameters.
statements.section_title: The probability of a dynamical cutoff

statements.title: Pure-collision cutting alternatives, imported
statements.label: prop:cutoff-import
statements.text:
Let \(M\) be a connected, full, realizable graph containing only
scattering contacts.  Full means that all its end variables are
integrated.  Define a transversal set \(A\subset M\) to be a set for
which \(M\setminus A=A^-\sqcup A^+\), with no directed bond from
\(A^+\) to \(A\cup A^-\), or from \(A\) to \(A^-\).
Let \(X_0(A)\) consist of vertices outside \(A\) with two bonds to
\(A\), and let \(X(A)\) be the closure obtained by repeatedly adding
vertices with two bonds to the set already grown.  The following
statements hold; in parts \textup{(ii)--(iv)}, \(A\) is assumed to be
connected.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item
There is a chain of connected transversal sets
\(A_1,\ldots,A_m=M\), with \(A_1\) a tree, such that
\(X_0(A_j)\neq\varnothing\) for \(j<m\),
\[
 A_j\cup X(A_j)\subset A_{j+1},\qquad
 r(A_{j+1})=r(A_j\cup X(A_j)),\qquad
 r(A_{j+1})-r(A_j)\leq10|X(A_j)|.
\]
The intermediate growth from \(A_j\cup X(A_j)\) to \(A_{j+1}\)
adds one bond at each new vertex.
For any \(D\) transitions in this chain there is a cutting sequence
of all of \(M\) with one type \(\{4\}\), no type \(\{44\}\) or
type-B pair, and at least \(D\) type-A pairs.
\item
One can choose \(A^\pm\) such that each component of \(A^+\) is
attached to \(A\).  The two parts
\(X^\pm(A)=X(A)\cap A^\pm\) are equivalently obtained by adding
vertices with two predecessors, or two successors, in the grown set.
They are convex along particle lines.  If \(m_\pm\) is the number
of bonds from \(A\) to \(X^\pm(A)\), then
\[
 |X^\pm(A)|\leq G(m_\pm),
 \qquad
 G(q)=(2q+1)\binom q2(32q^{3/2})^{q^2}\quad(q\geq2).
\]
The harmless values \(G(0),G(1)\) may be replaced by one.
\item
Put \(z=|X_0^\pm(A)|\) and \(a=r(A)\).  There is a cutting
sequence of \(M\) having one type \(\{4\}\), no type \(\{44\}\)
or type-B pair, and at least \(z/2-a-1\) type-A pairs.
\item
For this same choice of side there is a finite Borel partition
of the contact-parameter domain, with a subcase-dependent integer
\(y\geq0\), and the following two available sequences in each
subcase:
\begin{itemize}
\item a sequence with one type \(\{4\}\), no type \(\{44\}\)
or type-B pair, and at least \(y/10-3(a+1)\) uniformly good
singletons;
\item a sequence with no type \(\{44\}\), at most
\(S=a+z+y\) type \(\{4\}\) singletons, all type-B pairs
uniformly good, and at least
\[
 \frac{m_\pm-10^5S}{10}
\]
type-A or type-B pairs in total.
\end{itemize}
\end{enumerate}
The singleton and pair types not counted for a gain have the neutral
kernels described above.  On graphs of polylogarithmic size and
bounded excess the indicated partitions and operation sequences
have at most \(C^b|\log\eps|^{C_*}\) subcases.  The exponential
base \(C\) depends on dimensional choices, not on \(L\).
The required local restrictions at each uniformly good piece involve
its own variables and data exposed earlier in the cutting order.

title: Hardness of finding large independent sets in three-colorable graphs
abstract: We prove that, for every fixed \(0\lt \delta\lt 1/3\), it is NP-hard to distinguish three-colorable graphs from graphs in which every independent set has fewer than δ times the number of vertices. Consequently, for every fixed integer c ≥ 3, finding a proper c-coloring of a three-colorable graph is NP-hard.

tex.abstract:
We prove that, for every fixed $0<\delta<1/3$, it is NP-hard to distinguish
three-colorable graphs from graphs in which every independent set has fewer
than $\delta$ times the number of vertices. Consequently, for every fixed
integer $c\ge3$, finding a proper $c$-coloring of a three-colorable graph is
NP-hard.
sections: Two standard inputs and an analytic consequence
From an independent set to bounded subchain lists
Aligning the lists on a sampled set of layers
Choosing the constants and completing the reduction

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every fixed real $0<\delta<1/3$, there is a deterministic
polynomial-time algorithm $R_\delta$ that maps each explicitly encoded
Boolean $3$-CNF formula $\phi$ to a nonempty finite simple undirected
unweighted graph $G_\phi$ such that
\[
 \begin{array}{ll}
 \phi\text{ is satisfiable}
   &\Longrightarrow G_\phi\text{ is three-colorable},\\[2pt]
 \phi\text{ is unsatisfiable}
   &\Longrightarrow \alpha(G_\phi)<\delta\,|V(G_\phi)|.
 \end{array}
\]
The running time and explicit output size are polynomial in the ordinary
binary encoding length of $\phi$. Their constants and polynomial degree
may depend on the fixed $\delta$, but not on $\phi$.
The coloring in the first implication covers every vertex and is not
supplied with the graph.

statements.label: cor:coloring
statements.text:
For every fixed pair of integers $3\le k\le c$, it is NP-hard to
distinguish $k$-colorable graphs from graphs that are not $c$-colorable.

statements.title: Perfect-completeness Label Cover
statements.label: thm:label-cover
statements.text:
For every fixed rational $\sigma\in(0,1)$ there are nonempty constant
alphabets and a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from $3$SAT to
explicit Label Cover instances with nonempty occurrence lists such that
satisfiable formulas have value $1$ and unsatisfiable formulas have value
at most $\sigma$.
statements.section_title: Two standard inputs and an analytic consequence

statements.title: Dimension-independent junta approximation
statements.label: thm:junta
statements.text:
For every $0\le L<\infty$ and $\tau>0$ there is an integer $J(L,\tau)\ge1$
such that every $L$-Lipschitz function
$f:[0,1]^N\to[-1,1]$, for every positive integer $N$, admits a junta
on at most $J(L,\tau)$ coordinates with $L^2$ error less than $\tau$.
The junta may be taken to be a coordinate conditional expectation of $f$.
statements.section_title: Two standard inputs and an analytic consequence

statements.title: Explicit deterministic encoding
statements.label: prop:encoding
statements.text:
For fixed choices of the parameters and Label Cover alphabets, this rule
constructs a nonempty finite simple
unweighted graph in deterministic polynomial time and output size,
measured in the size of the explicit Label Cover instance. Composing
with Theorem~\ref{thm:label-cover} for any fixed $\sigma$ gives polynomial
time and output size in the binary encoding length of the original
$3$-CNF formula.

statements.label: prop:aligned-bound
statements.text:
Assume \eqref{eq:parameter-bounds}. Suppose that the construction does not
take the clique branch, and let
$\mathcal A$ be a nonempty independent set of its output graph.  Form the
functions and lists associated with $\mathcal A$ as above.  For every
chain and $s$-element set $B$ admitting a map
\[
 a:M_r\longrightarrow B,
 \qquad a(A_I)\subseteq I
 \quad\text{for every nonempty }I\subseteq B,
\]
the conditional probability that the sampled output vertex belongs to
$\mathcal A$ is at most $6\eps$.

title: Harmonic heights and the Artin K(pi,1) conjecture
abstract: We prove that the standard Salvetti complex of every Artin group with finitely many standard generators is aspherical. This resolves the Artin \(K(\pi,1)\) conjecture in finite rank.

tex.abstract:
We prove that the standard Salvetti complex of every Artin group with
finitely many standard generators is aspherical. This resolves the Artin
\(K(\pi,1)\) conjecture in finite rank.
sections: The Salvetti complex and spherical parabolic cosets
A framed category and its Artin action
Weighted height data and convex subobjects
A two-point estimate on spherical cosets

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every Coxeter matrix on a finite set \(S\), the universal cover
of \(X(W,S)\) is contractible.  Equivalently,
\[
  \pi_n\bigl(X(W,S)\bigr)=0\qquad(n\ge2).
\]
The conclusion allows arbitrary finite labels, infinite labels,
and connected or disconnected diagrams.

statements.title: Standard parabolic embedding
statements.label: thm:topology-parabolic-embedding
statements.text:
For every $T\subseteq S$, the homomorphism from the Artin group defined
by the submatrix on $T$ to $A$, sending its standard generators to the
corresponding $\sigma_t$, is injective.  Its image is $A_T$.
statements.section_title: The Salvetti complex and spherical parabolic cosets

statements.title: Finite-type positive monoids
statements.label: thm:topology-finite-monoid
statements.text:
Suppose that $T$ is spherical, and let $A_T^+$ be its positive Artin
monoid.  Then the following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
  \item The natural map $A_T^+\to A_T$ is injective.  In particular,
    $A_T^+$ is cancellative on both sides.
  \item Every element of $A_T$ can be written both as $ab^{-1}$ and
    as $c^{-1}d$, with $a,b,c,d\in A_T^+$.
  \item Any two elements of $A_T^+$ have a greatest common right
    divisor, and also a greatest common left divisor.
  \item If $w_T$ is the longest element of $W_T$, then
    $\Delta_T=\iota(w_T)$ is the finite-type fundamental element.
    Its left divisors and its right divisors coincide and are exactly
    the elements $\iota(w)$, $w\in W_T$.
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: The Salvetti complex and spherical parabolic cosets

statements.title: Spherical asphericity
statements.label: thm:topology-spherical-asphericity
statements.text:
If $T$ is spherical, the universal cover of the CW complex
$X(W_T,T)$ with the preceding permutahedral attaching maps is
contractible.
statements.section_title: The Salvetti complex and spherical parabolic cosets

statements.label: prop:fusion-construction
statements.text:
There is a finite semisimple spherical $\C$-linear tensor category
$\mathscr C$ with strictly positive real dimensions, and, for every
ordered edge $(s,t)$ of $\widehat S$, an object $D^1_{st}$ of dimension
$b_{st}$, with $D^1_{ts}$ its dual, having the following properties.
For every finite edge and simple objects $L,L'$,
\[
 \dim_\C\Hom_{\mathscr C}(L,D^1_{st}\otimes L')\leq1.
\]
On a label-$3$ edge or a frame edge one may take $D^1_{st}=\mathbf1$;
on an infinite edge one may take $D^1_{st}=\mathbf1\oplus\mathbf1$.
statements.section_title: A framed category and its Artin action

statements.label: prop:twist-action
statements.text:
For each original color $i$, let
\[
 B_i=\prod_{\alpha\in\widetilde{\{i\}}}B_\alpha,
 \qquad
 D_i=\prod_{\alpha\in\widetilde{\{i\}}}D_\alpha.
\]
These products are independent of their order up to bimodule homotopy.
The assignments $\sigma_i\mapsto B_i$ and $\sigma_i^{-1}\mapsto D_i$
define an action of the original Artin group by invertible bimodule
homotopy classes. For $x\in A$ write $B_x$ for a representing complex,
and write $F_i=B_i\otimes_Z-$ on left complexes.

For every $H\in\mathscr C$, right tensoring of labels,
\[
 T_H(P_{s,X})=P_{s,X\otimes H},
\]
is an additive functor on projectives that preserves path lengths and
extends to their bounded homotopy category. It commutes naturally up
to homotopy with the positive and inverse color twists, and hence
with each $B_x\otimes_Z-$. All the action identities above are
bimodule chain homotopy equivalences, so they remain valid upon
tensoring with finite complexes of modules that are not projective.
statements.section_title: A framed category and its Artin action

statements.title: Reduced-word amplitude
statements.label: cor:reduced-amplitude
statements.text:
For spherical $J$, a positive lift of any reduced expression in
$W_J$ has layer amplitude $[0,1]$.  A negative lift of a reduced
expression has amplitude $[-1,0]$.

statements.title: Convex subobjects
statements.label: prop:convex-subobjects
statements.text:
Let $J\subseteq S$ be spherical, and suppose that at
$x$ the data are capped at $q$ on $J\cup\partial J$.
Let $p$ agree with $m^q(x)$ outside $J$ and be harmonic
on $J$, and put $e=m^q(x)-p$, which is supported on $J$.
Assume that for \emph{every} representative $z\in A_Jx$
whose data are capped at $q$ on $J\cup\partial J$,
\begin{equation}
 m_j^q(z)\geq p_j\qquad(j\in J).
 
\end{equation}
Then $e_J$ belongs to the convex hull in $\R^J$ of
vectors $s_J$ with the following property: $s$ is zero
outside $J$, and there are graded subrepresentations
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal S_L\subseteq Y_L^q(x),\qquad
 \supp\mathcal S_L\subseteq\widetilde J,
 \qquad
 \sum_Lw_L\dim\mathcal S_L=\phi s.
 
\end{equation}
One may use a finite collection of such vectors,
together with the zero vector.

If all inequalities in
\eqref{eq:height-data-universal-cap-inequality} are
strict, $e_J$ is in the ordinary interior in $\R^J$
of such a convex hull.  For $J=\varnothing$ the
interior convention is that $\{0\}$ is open in
$\R^0$.

statements.label: prop:candidate-uniqueness
statements.text: There is at most one candidate in \(A_Tx_0\).
statements.section_title: A two-point estimate on spherical cosets

statements.title: Isolated harmonic layer
statements.label: prop:isolated-layer
statements.text:
Let $I\subseteq S$ be nonempty and connected.  Let $c_I$ be a strictly
positive vector with $C_Ic_I=0$, and extend $c$ by zero on
$\widehat S\setminus I$.  Let $J\subseteq I$ be spherical, possibly
empty, let $q>0$ be an integer, and fix a coset $A_Jx$.  Suppose that the
fixed data on $(I\setminus J)\cup\partial I$ are capped at $q$ and
satisfy
\begin{equation}
 m^q|_{(I\setminus J)\cup\partial I}
   =c|_{(I\setminus J)\cup\partial I}.
 
\end{equation}
It is impossible that every representative $z\in A_Jx$ capped at $q$ on
$I$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 m_j^q(z)>c_j\qquad\text{for every }j\in J.
 
\end{equation}
Equivalently, if $J\ne\varnothing$ and
\eqref{eq:rigidity-exterior-data} holds, there is a representative capped
on $I$ and a color $j\in J$ with $m_j^q\le c_j$.  If $J=\varnothing$,
the exterior situation \eqref{eq:rigidity-exterior-data} itself is
impossible.

statements.title: Spherical-residue sublevels
statements.label: prop:residue-sublevels
statements.text:
For every nonempty spherical $T$ and the data just specified:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
 \item $\mathcal R_{<}(T,A_Tx;q)$ is empty or contractible;
 \item whenever the additional exterior hypotheses hold,
 $\mathcal R_{\le}(T,A_Tx;q,I,c)$ is nonempty and contractible.
\end{enumerate}
For $T=\varnothing$, the strict sublevel is empty, and the exterior
hypotheses for the special closed sublevel cannot hold.

statements.label: prop:global-upper-link
statements.text: The earlier strict upper part of $P$ is empty or contractible.

statements.label: prop:global-lower-link
statements.text:
The earlier strict lower part of every $P\in\mathcal D$ is empty or
contractible.

statements.label: thm:deligne-contractible
statements.text:
For every Coxeter matrix on a finite set $S$, the order complex of the
spherical-coset poset $\mathcal D$ is contractible.

statements.title: Torsion, center, and monoid consequences
statements.label: cor:artin-structural
statements.text:
Let \(A=A(W,S)\) be an Artin group with \(S\) finite, let \(A^+\) be its
positive Artin monoid, and let \(k\) be the number of irreducible
spherical components of the Coxeter diagram of \((W,S)\).  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
  \item \(A\) is torsion-free.
  \item The center satisfies \(Z(A)\cong\Zbb^k\).
  \item The natural homomorphism \(\eta\colon A^+\to A\) induces a
    homotopy equivalence
    \[
      B\eta\colon BA^+\longrightarrow BA.
    \]
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Boyd stability for fixed-core braid-tail families
statements.label: cor:boyd-stability
statements.text:
Let \(A_1\) be the Artin group of a Coxeter matrix \(m_1\) on a finite
set \(\Sigma_1\), and choose a vertex \(\sigma_1\in\Sigma_1\).  For each
\(n\ge2\), adjoin new vertices \(\sigma_2,\ldots,\sigma_n\) and let
\(A_n\) be the Artin group of the Coxeter matrix \(m_n\) on
\(\Sigma_n=\Sigma_1\sqcup\{\sigma_2,\ldots,\sigma_n\}\).  Retain \(m_1\)
on \(\Sigma_1\), put diagonal entries equal to \(1\), and set the
remaining off-diagonal entries, symmetrically, by
\[
\begin{aligned}
 m_n(\sigma_j,\sigma_{j+1})&=3
     &&(1\le j<n),\\
 m_n(\sigma_j,\sigma_\ell)&=2
     &&(1\le j<\ell\le n,\ \ell-j\ge2),\\
 m_n(u,\sigma_j)&=2
     &&(u\in\Sigma_1\setminus\{\sigma_1\},\ 2\le j\le n).
\end{aligned}
\]
Let \(s_n\colon A_{n-1}\hookrightarrow A_n\) be the natural inclusion
for \(n\ge2\).  For every \(n\ge2\), every abelian group \(C\), used as
a constant coefficient group, and every integer \(i\ge0\), the induced map
\[
 (Bs_n)_*\colon H_i(BA_{n-1};C)\longrightarrow H_i(BA_n;C)
\]
is an isomorphism when \(i<n/2\) and a surjection when \(i=n/2\).

title: Hellinger contraction with arbitrary Boolean output bias
abstract: We prove the Hellinger conjecture for Boolean functions on the uniform discrete cube, with arbitrary output bias. For a Boolean function of mean m and every \(\rho\in[-1,1]\), the loss \(\sqrt{1-m^2}-\mathbb E\sqrt{1-(T_\rho f)^2}\) is at most \(1-\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\), with equality for signed coordinates. The proof combines asymmetric dimension induction, a calibrated noise-semigroup energy estimate, and finite exact arithmetic certificates. The Hellinger inequality also yields the Courtade–Kumar information bound.

tex.abstract:
We prove the Hellinger conjecture for Boolean functions on the uniform discrete cube, with arbitrary output bias. For a Boolean function of mean $m$ and every $\rho\in[-1,1]$, the loss
$\sqrt{1-m^2}-\E\sqrt{1-(T_\rho f)^2}$ is at most
$1-\sqrt{1-\rho^2}$, with equality for signed coordinates.
The proof combines asymmetric dimension induction, a calibrated noise-semigroup energy estimate, and finite exact arithmetic certificates.
The Hellinger inequality also yields the Courtade--Kumar information bound.

 I(f(X);Y)\le1-h_2(\varepsilon).
