title: Logarithmic Kodaira dimension and whole-fiber variation
abstract: We prove the logarithmic Iitaka–Viehweg inequality for projective surjective morphisms with connected fibers between smooth complex quasi-projective varieties whose base has nonnegative logarithmic Kodaira dimension. The variation measures the birational field of definition of the whole geometric generic fiber. This resolves Popa's logarithmic variation conjecture positively.

tex.abstract:
We prove the logarithmic Iitaka--Viehweg inequality for projective
surjective morphisms with connected fibers between smooth complex
quasi-projective varieties whose base has nonnegative logarithmic
Kodaira dimension. The variation measures the birational field of
definition of the whole geometric generic fiber. This resolves
Popa's logarithmic variation conjecture positively.
sections: The parameter field detected by logarithmic forms
The root cover and its Hodge line
General-type models over a logarithmic base
Markings and a constant finite normalization

statements.title: Logarithmic variation
statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $f:U\to V$ be a projective surjective morphism with connected fibers
between smooth connected quasi-projective complex varieties.
Assume $\kbar(V)\geq0$, and let $F$ be its geometric generic fiber.
Then
\begin{equation}
 \kbar(U)\geq\kappa(F)+\max\{\kbar(V),\Var(f)\}.
\end{equation}

statements.title: Projective Iitaka--Viehweg inequality
statements.label: thm:projective-variation
statements.text:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a surjective morphism with connected fibers between
smooth connected projective complex varieties, with $\kappa(Y)\geq0$.
For its geometric generic fiber $F$,
\[
 \kappa(X)\geq\kappa(F)+\max\{\kappa(Y),\Var(f)\}.
\]

statements.title: Variation and birational isotriviality
statements.label: cor:nonuniruled-rigidity
statements.text:
Let $f:U\to V$ be a smooth projective surjection with connected fibers
between smooth connected complex quasi-projective varieties. Assume
that every closed fiber is non-uniruled. Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \kbar(V)=-\infty&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \Var(f)<\dim V,\\
 \kbar(V)\geq0&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \Var(f)\leq\kbar(V).
\end{aligned}
\]
If $V$ is Campana-special, then $\Var(f)=0$. In particular, if
$\kbar(V)=0$, the family is birationally isotrivial.

statements.title: Reduced-SNC logarithmic subadditivity
statements.label: spec:logarithmic
statements.text:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a surjective morphism with connected fibers between
smooth connected projective complex varieties. Let $D_X,D_Y$ be
reduced simple normal crossing divisors, with the zero divisor allowed,
such that
\[
 \operatorname{Supp}(f^*D_Y)\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}(D_X).
\]
For a very general fiber $F$, put $D_F=D_X|_F$. Then
\[
 \kappa(X,K_X+D_X)
 \geq\kappa(F,K_F+D_F)+\kappa(Y,K_Y+D_Y).
\]
The same assertion holds for compact manifolds in Fujiki class
$\mathcal C$ and holomorphic fibrations between them.
statements.section_title: The parameter field detected by logarithmic forms

statements.label: it:diagram
statements.text:
There are smooth connected projective varieties $X_*,X',W,Z$, a birational
morphism $X'\to X_*$, and morphisms
\[
 X'\xrightarrow{x}W\xrightarrow{g}Y,
 \qquad h:W\to Z,\qquad q=h\circ x,
\]
with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item The variety $X_*$ is a smooth model of $X$ carrying a resolved
 absolute Iitaka map for $K_X+D_X$.  Its boundary $D_*$, and the boundary
 $D'$ on $X'$, follow the strict-transform-plus-reduced-exceptional
 convention.  The map $q$ is the pullback of this Iitaka map, and
 \begin{equation}
  \dim Z=\kbar(U).
 \end{equation}
 \item The morphisms $x,g,h$ are surjective and have connected fibers and
 geometrically integral generic fibers.  The induced map from $W$ to
 its image in $Y\times Z$ is generically finite.  In particular,
 $W_z\to g(W_z)$ is generically finite for very general $z$.
 \item The divisor
 $D_W^0=(g^*D_Y)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is SNC.  On very general fibers over $Z$,
 all the relevant varieties and boundary strata are smooth, and
 \begin{equation}
  \kappa\bigl(X_{*,z},K_{X_{*,z}}+D_*|_{X_{*,z}}\bigr)
  =\kappa\bigl(X'_z,K_{X'_z}+D'|_{X'_z}\bigr)=0.
 \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
One may make further compatible smooth birational modifications, retaining
these assertions.  After the finite preparations in this section, $X_*$
can be fixed as an earlier model, and every subsequent source model is
taken to dominate it.
statements.section_title: The parameter field detected by logarithmic forms

statements.label: it:dimensions
statements.section_title: The parameter field detected by logarithmic forms

statements.title: Divisorial normalization
statements.label: ro:divisors
statements.text:
For a prime divisor $P$ on $W$, and for a prime divisor $Q$ on the actual
source $X'$ dominating $P$, set
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 m_Q&=\ord_Q(x^*P),\qquad
 r_Q=\frac1p\ord_Q(\omega_J),\qquad
 d_Q=\operatorname{coeff}_Q(D'),\\
 t_P&=\min_{\substack{Q\mapsto P\\Q\text{ on }X'}}
                   \frac{r_Q+d_Q}{m_Q},\\
 \lambda_P&=\inf_{Q\mapsto P}\frac{1+r_Q}{m_Q},\qquad
 B_P=1-\lambda_P+t_P.
 \end{aligned}
 
\end{equation}
In the definition of $\lambda_P$, $Q$ runs over divisorial valuations on all higher
smooth source models.  In both formulas $r_Q$ is measured in the actual
relative canonical bundle with respect to the smooth base $W$.

The two rational divisors
\[
 T=\sum_Pt_PP,
 \qquad B=\sum_PB_PP
\]
have finite support.  The divisor $B$ is an effective boundary and
\begin{equation}
 0\le B_P\le1,
 \qquad B\ge D_W^0=(g^*D_Y)_{\mathrm{red}}.
 
\end{equation}
The formulas at unchanged codimension-one base points are invariant
under further source resolutions with the prescribed boundary
convention.  They are also preserved, allowing splitting of components,
by an \'etale extension of the base DVR and the corresponding source
base change.  After a further birational preparation of $W$, $B$ can be
assumed to have SNC support.
statements.section_title: The root cover and its Hodge line

statements.title: A zero boundary coefficient
statements.label: ro:zero-boundary
statements.section_title: The root cover and its Hodge line

statements.title: The Hodge order
statements.label: ro:metric
statements.text:
At every prime $P$ of $W$, the parabolic order of the root form $\eta$ is
$\lambda_P-1$.  Consequently
\begin{equation}
 M\sim_{\Q}\sum_P(\lambda_P-1)P,
 \qquad
 T\sim_{\Q}B+M.
 
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: The root cover and its Hodge line

statements.title: The Iitaka-fiber section bound
statements.label: ro:transfer
statements.text:
The models in Proposition~\ref{it:diagram} can be chosen, with the
divisors of Proposition~\ref{ro:divisors} recomputed on them, so that
\begin{equation}
 \kappa\bigl(W_z,K_{W_z}+B|_{W_z}+M|_{W_z}\bigr)\le0
 
\end{equation}
for very general $z\in Z$.  The comparison is a comparison with the
section system on the fixed fiber $X_{*,z}$ in
\eqref{ro:initial-zero}.
statements.section_title: The root cover and its Hodge line

statements.title: Full-period adjoint comparison
statements.label: period:adjoint
statements.text:
Let $B$ be a smooth compact connected manifold in Fujiki class
$\mathcal C$, and let $B^\circ\subset B$ be a dense Zariski open
whose complement is an SNC divisor. Let $\mathbb V$ be a
real-polarizable pure variation of Hodge structures on $B^\circ$
with an integral lattice. Suppose a complex direct summand of
$\mathbb V_{\C}$ has a highest nonzero Hodge filtration step of rank
one, with rational parabolic extension $L$. There exist a modification
$\tau:B'\to B$, a connected-fiber surjective morphism $p:B'\to R$ to
a smooth projective variety, and a nef rational line bundle $A$ on
$R$ such that
\[
 \tau^*L=p^*A\quad\text{in }\operatorname{Pic}(B')\otimes\Q,
 \qquad K_R+cA\text{ is big for some }c\in\Q_{>0}.
\]
Positive rational rescaling of $L$ is allowed, and the line identity
persists under further modifications. A point is allowed for $R$;
then $\tau^*L$ is rationally trivial.
statements.section_title: The root cover and its Hodge line

statements.title: Projective adjoint comparison
statements.label: hd:adjoint
statements.text:
Let $P$ be smooth connected projective, let $D$ be reduced SNC,
and let $L$ be the rational parabolic extension of the entire
highest Hodge line of a polarizable integral pure variation on
$P\setminus D$. There are a birational morphism
$\mu:P'\to P$ with $P'$ smooth projective, a surjective morphism
$a:P'\to R$ with connected fibers to a smooth projective variety,
and a nef rational line bundle $A$ on $R$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \mu^*L\sim_{\mathbf Q}a^*A,
 \qquad K_R+bA\text{ is big for all sufficiently large rational }b.
\end{equation}
The point quotient is allowed, in which case $\mu^*L$ is
rationally trivial.
statements.section_title: The root cover and its Hodge line

statements.title: Triviality on the Iitaka fiber
statements.label: ro:trivial
statements.text:
For very general $z\in Z$,
\begin{equation}
 M|_{W_z}\sim_{\Q}0,
 \qquad
 \kappa(W_z,K_{W_z}+B|_{W_z})=0.
 
\end{equation}
These assertions also hold on the geometric generic $h$-fiber.
statements.section_title: The root cover and its Hodge line

statements.title: Degree zero on a curve
statements.label: hodge:degree-zero
statements.text:
In Lemma~\ref{hodge:extensions}, suppose that $P$ is a smooth
projective curve. If $\deg L=0$, the projective highest-line map is
constant on the connected universal cover of $P\setminus D$.
Equivalently, $L^\circ$ is a flat line subbundle.
statements.section_title: The root cover and its Hodge line

statements.title: Finite character of a line
statements.label: lem:finite-character
statements.text:
Let $\mathbb V$ be a polarized integral variation of Hodge structures
on a connected smooth complex algebraic variety. Every rank-one
complex local subsystem of $\mathbb V_{\C}$ has finite monodromy.
statements.section_title: The root cover and its Hodge line

statements.title: Restriction and finite character
statements.label: hodge:restricted-character
statements.text:
Let $T$ be a connected smooth complex algebraic variety mapping into
the domain of a polarized integral pure variation whose entire highest
Hodge step is a line. If the pulled-back projective highest-line map is
constant, its highest line has finite monodromy character.
statements.section_title: The root cover and its Hodge line

statements.title: Flatness and finite character on the Iitaka fiber
statements.label: ro:flat-character
statements.text:
For very general $z\in Z$, the projective entire top line of the
restricted root-cover variation is constant on the connected good
locus of $W_z$, and its top-line character has finite image.
statements.section_title: The root cover and its Hodge line

statements.title: Birational constancy over a curve
statements.label: cc:criterion
statements.text:
Let $\pi^\circ:P^\circ\to C^\circ$ be a smooth projective morphism with
connected fibers, where $C^\circ$ is a smooth connected complex algebraic
curve.  Suppose that its very general fiber $D$ satisfies
\[
                 \kappa(D)=0,\qquad h^0(D,K_D)=1.
\]
Put $n=\dim D$ and assume that the entire top Hodge bundle
$F^n(R^n\pi^\circ_*\C\otimes\cO_{C^\circ})$ is a flat line with
finite monodromy character.  Then there are a finite
extension $L/\C(C^\circ)$ and a smooth connected projective variety
$D_0/\C$ such that the generic fiber after extension to $L$ is birational
to $(D_0)_L$.

If a finite group $\Gamma$ acts on $P^\circ$ over $C^\circ$, one can choose
$D_0$ with a $\Gamma$-action and choose this birational identification
$\Gamma$-equivariantly.  The same conclusion holds for a finite
fiberwise birational action, after replacing the family by an
equivariant smooth projective model.

statements.title: Constant-line loci
statements.label: cc:loci
statements.text:
Let $\pi:\mathcal P\to B$ be a smooth projective morphism with
connected fibers over a smooth connected complex algebraic variety.
Let $T\subseteq B$ be a connected smooth algebraic locus on which the
very general fiber $D$ satisfies $\kappa(D)=0$ and $h^0(D,K_D)=1$.
If the entire ordinary top Hodge line of the restricted family has
constant projective period in a flat reference, its geometric generic
fiber is birational to a smooth projective variety over $\C$.
The conclusion is equivariant for any prescribed finite fiberwise
birational group action.

More generally, let $B\to Z$ be a morphism of smooth connected complex
algebraic varieties with geometrically integral generic fiber.  If the
same fiber and constant-line hypotheses hold on a nonempty smooth
open of every very general fiber over $Z$, then the family over the
geometric generic fiber of $B\to Z$ is birationally constant over
$\overline{\C(Z)}$, with the prescribed finite action.  These
birational identifications remain valid after algebraically closed
extension of their fields of definition.

statements.title: Constancy in the $h$-fiber directions
statements.label: ro:constancy
statements.text:
For very general $z\in Z$, the geometric generic fiber of the
$J$-family over $W_z$ is birational to the base change of a smooth
projective variety over $\C$.  More intrinsically, after extending the
function field of $Z$ to its algebraic closure, the geometric generic
fiber of $x$ over the resulting $h$-fiber is birationally constant over
that algebraically closed field.

statements.title: Model-pair variation over a logarithmic base
statements.label: num:model-pair
statements.text:
Let $B$ be an effective rational SNC boundary on $H$, and let $D_I$
be a reduced SNC divisor on $I$, such that
\[
 B\geq(p^*D_I)_{\red},\qquad \kappa(I,K_I+D_I)\geq0.
\]
Suppose the log canonical divisor of a geometric generic fiber
component is big. Then $\kappa(H,K_H+B)\geq r$. If that generic pair
is klt, then
\begin{equation}
 \kappa(H,K_H+B)\geq r+\operatorname{Var}(p,C),
 \qquad C=B_{\mathrm{hor}},
\end{equation}
Here $\operatorname{Var}(p,C)$ is the minimum transcendence degree
over $k$ of an algebraically closed field over which the geometric
generic log canonical \emph{model pair}, including its boundary, is
isomorphic to a base extension. Thus it measures descent of that
marked model; the invariant $\Var(f)$ in
Equation~\eqref{eq:variation-definition} measures birational descent
of the whole geometric generic fiber.
In the klt case, if the left side is at most $r$, this model pair
becomes constant after a finite extension of the base function field. For disconnected
geometric generic fibers, the model and its variation refer to a chosen
component after adjoining the Stein field.
statements.section_title: General-type models over a logarithmic base

statements.label: mk:product
statements.text:
After a finite extension of $b(I)$ there is a normal projective variety
$V'$ over $b$, finite over $P_0$, such that the generic $I$-fiber of
$H_0$ is birational over $P_0$ to the base extension of $V'$.  Equivalently,
after replacing $I$ by a smooth projective model of that finite extension,
there is a birational product description over $I\times_bP_0$,
\begin{equation}
 H_0\dashrightarrow I\times_b V'.
\end{equation}
Here $H_0$ denotes the main component after the parameter extension.
Every component of the old $B_0$ which has a divisorial image on $V'$
over the generic point of $I$ has an image defined over $b$.

Put
\begin{equation}
 k=b(V'),\qquad K=k(I).
\end{equation}
The original generic $x$-fiber, viewed by \eqref{mk:product-field} as a
variety $J/K$, is geometrically birational to a smooth projective
geometrically integral variety $J_0/k$.  One has
$\kappa(J_{0,\bar k})=0$, and, for the minimal positive pluricanonical
index $p$ of $J$, there is a nonzero ordinary $p$-pluricanonical form on
$J_0$ and
\begin{equation}
 \dim_k H^0(J_0,pK_{J_0})
 =\dim_{\bar k}H^0(J_{0,\bar k},pK_{J_{0,\bar k}})=1.
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Markings and a constant finite normalization

statements.title: Unramifiedness at moving divisors
statements.label: ds:unramified
statements.text:
The extension $\widetilde K/K$ in
Lemma~\ref{ds:cocycle} is unramified at every moving divisor.
After a finite extension $E/L_0$, each field component of
\[
 \widetilde K\otimes_K E(V')
\]
is likewise unramified at every moving divisor of $V'_E$.

statements.title: Descent of the whole fiber
statements.label: ds:whole

statements.title: The dimension retained by interpolation
statements.label: num:main
statements.text:
Let $g:W\to Y$ and $h:W\to Z$ be surjective morphisms with connected
fibers between smooth projective complex varieties.  Let $B$ be an
effective rational SNC boundary, and let $D_Y$ be a reduced SNC
divisor, with the zero divisor allowed. Assume
\[
 B\geq(g^*D_Y)_{\red},\qquad
 \kappa(Y,K_Y+D_Y)\geq0.
\]
Let $A$ be a nef rational divisor on $Z$ such that $K_Z+aA$ is big
for all sufficiently large rational $a$.  Put
\[
 M=h^*A,\qquad L(c)=K_W+B+cM,\qquad d=\dim(W/Y),
\]
and suppose $L(1)$ is big over $Y$.
On smooth birational models, with the boundary rule of
Lemma~\ref{setup:log-modification}, there are morphisms
\[
 W\xrightarrow{q}U\xrightarrow{j}Z,
 \qquad U\xrightarrow{s}T_0,\qquad S\xrightarrow{p}T_0,
 \qquad \rho:S\to Y
\]
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $h=jq$, and $q$ is the relative Iitaka fibration of $K_W+B$
over $Z$.  Its geometric general fiber $G$ is integral and satisfies
$\kappa(G,K_G+B_G)=0$.
\item The map $g$ factors through $S$; $\rho$ is birational, and
$W\to(S\times_{T_0}U)_{\mathrm{main}}$ is dominant and generically
finite.  The generic fibers of $S\to T_0$ and $U\to T_0$ are
geometrically integral. With $D_S=(\rho^*D_Y)_{\red}$ made SNC,
one has $\kappa(S_t,K_{S_t}+D_S|_{S_t})=0$ for very general $t$.
\item One has
\begin{equation}
 \kappa(W,L(1))=\dim U=d+\dim T_0,
 \qquad \kappa(Y,K_Y+D_Y)\leq\dim T_0.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
Rational linear equivalence in the definition of $M$ is sufficient.
All section comparisons are with the fixed initial source model.

statements.title: Complete systems in an isotrivial family
statements.label: num:full-systems
statements.text:
Let $p:H\to I$ be a surjective morphism of smooth integral
projective varieties over an algebraically closed field of
characteristic zero. Let $B$ be an effective rational SNC boundary on
$H$, let $D_I$ be a reduced SNC divisor on $I$, and assume
$B\geq(p^*D_I)_{\red}$ and $\kappa(I,K_I+D_I)\geq0$.
Put $r=\dim H-\dim I$. Choose a geometric generic fiber
component after adjoining the Stein field. Suppose it is klt of log
general type and its log canonical model pair is isotrivial; denote
its fixed model by $(F_c,\Delta_c)$. There are a finite Galois base
extension, the normalization $\tau:H^a\to H$ in the corresponding
compositum component, and an integer $m_0>0$ such that
\begin{equation}
 H^0(F_c,m(K_{F_c}+\Delta_c))
 \lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow H^0(H^a,m\tau^*(K_H+B))
 \qquad(m\in m_0\N).
\end{equation}
On one fixed dense open of a smooth altered base, restriction to a
general fiber gives the pulled-back complete system of this model,
times a common nonzero factor. Both the open and $m_0$ work for all
these degrees. The isotriviality hypothesis holds in particular if
$\kappa(H,K_H+B)\leq r$.

statements.title: Ordinary relative reduction
statements.label: input:reduction
statements.text:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a surjective morphism with connected fibers between
smooth connected projective complex varieties. Assume $\kappa(Y)\geq0$,
and put $d=\kappa(F)\geq0$ for the geometric generic fiber $F$. On smooth projective models there is a
factorization
\[
 X'\xrightarrow{x}W\xrightarrow{g}Y
\]
with connected geometric generic fibers and $\dim(W/Y)=d$.
There are an effective SNC rational boundary $B$ on $W$, a nef
rational divisor $M$, and a morphism $h_0:W\to Z$ with connected
fibers, with $Z$ smooth projective, such that
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $K_W+B+M$ is big over $Y$;
\item $M\sim_{\Q}h_0^*A$ for a nef rational divisor $A$ on $Z$,
      and $K_Z+aA$ is big for every sufficiently large rational $a$;
\item the divisible section systems of $K_W+B+M$ identify with
      those of $K_X$, preserving their rational-map dimensions;
\item the generic pair $(J,D_J)$ of $x$, with the reduced exceptional
      boundary inherited from $X'\to X$, has logarithmic Kodaira
      dimension zero. Its minimal-index cyclic root cover is
      geometrically connected and has entire logarithmic top-form
      space of dimension one, with every positive logarithmic
      plurigenus at most one;
\item $M$ is the rational parabolic extension of this entire top
      line, identified with the top line of the unique rational
      polarized pure weight grade carrying it.
\end{enumerate}
On an initial reduction model $B$ is the normalized boundary of
\cite[\PoneNormalization]{SubadditivityCompanion}. Subsequent source models of
$W$ carry its strict transform plus reduced exceptional boundary,
and the pullback of $M$; their section systems remain those of the
original $X$.

statements.title: The ordinary second Iitaka construction
statements.label: input:second-iitaka
statements.text:
For the data of Proposition~\ref{input:reduction}, there are
a morphism $q:W\to U$ with connected fibers to a smooth projective
variety $U$ and a morphism
$j:U\to Z$ with $h_0=j\circ q$. The general $q$-fiber $G$ satisfies
\[
 \kappa(G,K_G+B|_G)=0,
 \qquad G\longrightarrow g(G)\text{ is generically finite}.
\]
There are smooth projective varieties $T_0,S$ and a diagram
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large]
 W\arrow[r,"{(g_S,q)}"]\arrow[d,"q"'] &
 (S\times_{T_0}U)_{\mathrm{main}}\arrow[r]\arrow[d] &
 S\arrow[r,"\rho"]\arrow[d] &Y\\
 U\arrow[r,equal]&U\arrow[r]&T_0&
\end{tikzcd}
\]
with $g=\rho\circ g_S$, where $\rho$ is birational and the map
to the main product component is dominant and generically finite.
The geometric generic fibers of $S\to T_0$ and $U\to T_0$ are
integral, and
\begin{equation}
 \kappa(S_t)=0,
 \qquad \kappa(X)=\kappa(W,K_W+B+M)=\dim U=d+\dim T_0.
\end{equation}
Here $t$ is a very general point of $T_0$.
All models use the section-preserving boundary convention of
Proposition~\ref{input:reduction}.

statements.title: Ordinary cyclic covers along the second Iitaka fibers
statements.label: prop:ordinary-period
statements.text:
In the notation of Proposition~\ref{input:reduction} and
Corollary~\ref{input:second-iitaka}, let $J$ be the generic fiber of
$x:X'\to W$ over $K=\C(W)$. The minimal logarithmic generator
$\omega\in H^0(J,p(K_J+D_J))$ is an ordinary regular pluriform.
Its resolved connected cyclic root cover $\widetilde J$ satisfies
\[
 H^0(\widetilde J,aK_{\widetilde J})=K\eta^a
 \qquad(a\geq1),
\]
where $\eta$ is its root top form. In particular,
$\kappa(\widetilde J)=0$ and $h^0(\widetilde J,K_{\widetilde J})=1$.

On a dense smooth open of every very general fiber of $q:W\to U$,
the family of these covers is geometrically birationally constant
with its deck action, and the same holds for the $J$-family after
taking the quotient. More precisely, over the geometric generic
$q$-fiber these families become birational to varieties over
$b_U=\overline{\C(U)}$ after a finite extension of that fiber's
function field, equivariantly for the deck group in the cover case.
These identifications persist under algebraically closed field extension.

statements.title: The absolute Iitaka base and descent of the whole fiber
statements.label: ordinary:absolute-bases
statements.text:
The variety $U$ in Corollary~\ref{input:second-iitaka} is a
birational model of the absolute Iitaka base of $X$. Inside
$\C(X)$, the field $\C(W)$ is the relative algebraic closure of
$\C(Y)\C(U)$. Consequently the field $\C(T_0)\subset\C(Y)$
in that Corollary agrees with the field obtained from
Propositions~\ref{it:diagram} and~\ref{it:dimensions} applied to
the projective morphism $f$ with empty original boundaries.

In particular, inside the prescribed algebraic closure $\Omega$
of $\C(Y)$, put $b=\overline{\C(T_0)}$. There is a finitely
generated field $E_b/b$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Frac}(\Omega\otimes_bE_b)
 \simeq
 \operatorname{Frac}(\Omega\otimes_{\C(Y)}\C(X)).
\end{equation}
Thus the whole geometric generic fiber of $f$ is birationally
defined over this specific field $b$, and
$\operatorname{Var}(f)\leq\dim T_0$.

title: Logarithmic Relative Fluctuations in the Weakly Disordered Planar Ising Model
abstract: Assuming the stated deterministic critical-reference estimates, we prove that the relative second moment of the quenched critical spin correlation in the square-lattice Ising model with independent fair bonds \(1\pm\varepsilon\) grows as \((\log r)^{1/4+o(1)}\) for each sufficiently small fixed ε > 0. The correlation is evaluated at the physical critical temperature, with the thermodynamic limit taken before the disorder moments and the large-distance limit.

tex.abstract:
Assuming the stated deterministic critical-reference estimates, we prove
that the relative second moment of the quenched critical spin correlation
in the square-lattice Ising model with independent fair bonds $1\pm\eps$
grows as $(\log r)^{1/4+o(1)}$ for each sufficiently small fixed $\eps>0$.
The correlation is evaluated at the physical critical temperature, with
the thermodynamic limit taken before the disorder moments and the
large-distance limit.

statements.title: Averaging and charge cancellation
statements.label: ref:operator
statements.text:
Fix $\nu>0$ smaller than $p-b$ in the applicable row of
\eqref{ref:exponents}.  For all sufficiently large $w$ and $R\ge Cw$, a
function $F$ of that parity, supported in $B_w(z)$, satisfies
\begin{align}
 \norm{P_{R,z}F^\circ}_\infty
   &\le C(w/R)^b\norm{F}_\infty,\\
 \norm{P_{R,z}F^\circ-\ell_b(F)P_{R,z}\mathcal O_b(z)}_\infty
   &\le C(w/R)^{p-\nu}\norm{F}_\infty.
   
\end{align}
In particular, the second bound is the improved decay bound for a function
of charge zero.  We shall use $\nu=1/4$.  The exponent $3-\nu$ requires
the individual even function to be invariant under right-angle rotations;
invariance of its probability law alone does not suffice.
For a site at fixed positive relative distance from the cutting contour,
\begin{equation}
 \norm{P_{R,z}e(y)}_\infty\le CR^{-1},\qquad
 \norm{P_{R,z}\sigma_y}_\infty\le CR^{-d}.
\end{equation}
The first bound also holds for a single plane-centered bond product.

statements.label: block:exact

statements.title: Large generating footprints
statements.label: block:diameter
statements.text:
Retain the animal footprint of a connected coefficient before projecting
onto constants.  For background coefficients from the small-entry
expansion whose footprint has physical diameter at least $D$, the total
absolute sum at a fixed output anchor is at most
\[
 C_L\delta e^{-cD/R}.
\]
The same gain can be retained together with any fixed number of
specified input norm factors, including marked factors.  On a torus of
side $N$, writing $m=N/R$, the total absolute sum of small-expansion
scalar terms whose footprints wrap or fail to fit in a chart of fixed
relative size is at most $C_L\delta m^2e^{-cm}$.  Here $m$ is sufficiently
large relative to the fixed halos.  Pure bad scalar terms have chart
footprints and do not contribute to this last sum.
statements.section_title: An exact local change of scale

statements.title: Uniform smallness of the tails
statements.label: block:tails
statements.text:
For sufficiently large $L$ and then sufficiently small $\delta$, the
transformed nonprincipal background satisfies
$\|h'_{A,c}\|_\infty\le\delta e^{-w|A|}$ for every disorder realization.
More precisely, with the same output weight $w$,
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{(A,c)}e^{w|A|}\|h'_{A,c}\|_\infty
       \le C_L\delta^2+C_Le^{-cL}\delta.
 
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: An exact local change of scale

statements.title: Finite-volume implementation
statements.label: block:finite
statements.text:
The preceding transformation and partition identity apply to finite
boxes with fixed or free boundary data, and to tori whose side is
an integer multiple of the working scales, while the scale is
sufficiently below the side length.  The input finite-volume lists
have finitely many possible anchors and admissible source jets.
On a torus, wrapping interactions remain in torus animal slots.  At
every fixed number of steps the principal norms have deterministic
bounds uniform in volume, disorder and decision seeds whenever the
microscopic principal norms have such a bound.  The total list sums
are finite, with bounds that may grow with the volume.  Bulk slots whose
full ancestral footprints avoid the boundary agree exactly with the
plane construction.  Infinite-plane lists require only the indexed
and rooted sums proved above; no infinite-volume partition integral
is used in their definition.
statements.section_title: An exact local change of scale

statements.title: Taylor transport of background moments
statements.label: norm:taylor
statements.text:
Under \eqref{norm:input}, the mean and the raw moment and cumulant arrays
with at most four arguments are given by the ordinary zero-background
Taylor rule, retaining total background degree at most four, with error
$O(s^5)$ in the prescribed weighted indexed projective norms.  The
coefficient maps are bounded uniformly in the scale.  An output cumulant
vanishes if its dependence carriers split into two nonempty mutually
separated families.
statements.section_title: Moment estimates for local random lists

statements.title: High moments and recovery of $L^2$
statements.label: norm:reproduction
statements.text:
Choose $L$ sufficiently large and then $\delta$ sufficiently small.
Under \eqref{norm:input},
\begin{align}
 \norm{h'}_{v,p}&\le Bs/8+C_L^*B_2s+o(s),\\
 \norm{h'}_{v,2}&\le C_{\eta,L}F_*s+\eps_* Bs+o(s).
                                                    
\end{align}
Here $C_L^*$ grows at most polynomially in $L$.  For the second inequality,
assume that each output principal slot has diagonal second-moment
bound
\begin{equation}
 \sup_\sigma\E|h'_a(\sigma)|^2\le e^{-2v}F_*^2s^2,
 \qquad F_*\ge1.
\end{equation}
A bound on its raw second tensor implies this hypothesis.  One can
choose $\eps_*<[100(1+C_L^*)]^{-1}$: first use the long-slot suppression,
then choose the dictionary accuracy $\eta$ and the mesh threshold $r_0$.
These choices do not depend on $B,B_2,F_*$.

statements.title: Background linear splitting
statements.label: lin:background
statements.text:
Fix the finite set of weights needed in Section~\ref{sec:norms}.  By taking
$L$ sufficiently large, all the following contraction constants can be made
smaller than any prescribed $\kappa>0$:
\[
 \|T_jm\|\le\kappa\|m\|\quad(x_{r_j}(m)=0),\qquad
 \|T_j^{(2)}K\|\le\kappa\|K\|\quad(g_{r_j}(K)=0),
\]
and $\|T_j^{(k)}A\|\le\kappa\|A\|$ for homogeneous connected arrays of
orders $k=3,4$.  Norms here and below have the fixed input and output weights
allocated to the corresponding estimate.  The bounds are uniform in $j$.
The two projections above intertwine transport with multipliers $L$ and $1$.
statements.section_title: Linear transport and its distinguished coordinates

statements.title: Marked linear splitting
statements.label: lin:marked
statements.text:
For each fixed finite set of positive integers $q$, the operators
$\mathcal T_j^{(q)}$ are bounded uniformly in $j,y,L$.  On
$\ker Q_{j,q,y}$ their norms tend to zero as $L\to\infty$.
A connected array comprising this marked tensor as one grouped argument and
at least one even background argument contracts without removal of a line.
The one-source kernel estimate also holds pathwise, and hence in each of the
weighted random-list $L^p$ norms used in Section~\ref{sec:norms}.
statements.section_title: Linear transport and its distinguished coordinates

statements.title: Averages of the marginal coefficients
statements.label: coef:averages
statements.text:
The coefficients in~\eqref{coef:b}--\eqref{coef:c} satisfy
\begin{align}
 \sum_{j<J}b_j&=-4\pi a^2\log r_J+o(\log r_J),\\
 \sum_{j<J}c_{j,q}(y)&=\binom q2\frac{\pi a^2}{2}\log r_J
                         +o(\log r_J),
\end{align}
where the second error is uniform in $y$ for each fixed $q$.  Equivalently,
their Ces\`aro means are $-4\pi a^2\log L$ and
$\binom q2(\pi a^2/2)\log L$.

statements.title: Bounded first-charge sums
statements.label: coef:bounded-first
statements.text:
There is a constant independent of $J$ and $y$ such that
\[
 \left|\sum_{j<J}c_{j,1}(y)\right|\le C.
\]

statements.title: Finite-prefix estimates
statements.label: flow:prefix
statements.text:
There are fixed constants $X,C$ and $\rho<1$ such that, for sufficiently
small $D>0$, every trajectory kept through scale $N$ satisfies the
background tail and moment bounds of Section~\ref{sec:norms} with $s=s_j$,
and
\begin{equation}
 \norm{m_j}+\norm{K_j}\le CG_j,\qquad
 \norm{W_j}+\norm{Y_j}\le CG_j^2,\qquad
 \tfrac12G_j<g_j<2G_j .
\end{equation}
The tensor and moment bounds also hold for the tested next step, with a
larger fixed constant for its mean.  Moreover, for $1\le j\le N$,
\begin{align}
 K_j-g_jV_j&=O\bigl(G_j(G_j+\rho^j)\bigr),\\
 m_j-g_jm_j^*&=O\bigl(G_j(G_j+\rho^j+\rho^{N-j})\bigr),
 \\
 W_j-g_j^2W_j^*,\quad Y_j-g_j^2Y_j^*
 &=O\bigl(G_j^2(s_j+\rho^j+\rho^{N-j})\bigr).
 
\end{align}
Here $V_j,m_j^*,W_j^*,Y_j^*$ are the bounded formal profiles of
Section~\ref{sec:coefficients}.  For $0\le j\le N$, including the tested
next covariance,
\begin{equation}
 g_{j+1}=g_j+b_jg_j^2+
 O\bigl(G_j^2(s_j+\rho^j+\rho^{N-j})\bigr).
\end{equation}
The constants are independent of $N$ and of the kept trajectory.

statements.title: Existence of a tuned trajectory
statements.label: flow:tuned
statements.text:
For every sufficiently small $D>0$ there is $t_*(D)=O(D^2)$ whose
background trajectory satisfies $|x_j|\le XG_j$ at every scale.
All the bounds of Proposition~\ref{flow:prefix} hold along this
trajectory.  In the profile estimates its terminal geometric term may
be omitted.

statements.title: Decay of the disorder coordinate
statements.label: flow:variance
statements.text:
Along every tuned trajectory obtained above,
\begin{equation}
 g_j\sim\frac1{B_0j}\quad(j\to\infty),\qquad
 \sum_{j\ge0}|g_{j+1}-g_j|\le C\bar g.
\end{equation}
The uniform comparison~\eqref{flow:uniform-ratio} also holds over all
$j\ge0$ as $D\downarrow0$.

statements.title: Disorder moments at tuning
statements.label: read:moments
statements.text:
Let $C_{*,\omega}(y_1,y_2)$ be the free infinite-volume spin correlation
at $t_*(D)$, and let $J$ be determined by \eqref{read:stop}.  For every
fixed sufficiently small $D>0$, uniformly in the two marks as their
separation tends to infinity,
\begin{equation}
 r_J^{2d}\E C_{*,\omega}(y_1,y_2)\asymp1,
 \qquad
 r_J^{4d}\E C_{*,\omega}(y_1,y_2)^2
       =J^{1/4+o(1)}.
 
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Quenched partition readout and boundary arms

statements.title: Wired arm at tuning
statements.label: read:arm
statements.text:
For any square box of radius $n$ centered at a lattice site $y$, let
$\phi^w_{n,*,\omega}$ be the FK--Ising law at $t_*(D)$ with wired
boundary.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \E\left[\phi^w_{n,*,\omega}
    (y\longleftrightarrow\partial\Lambda_n(y))^{400}\right]
       \le n^{-400/8+o(1)}.
 
\end{equation}
The estimate is uniform in $y$.  It also holds if the fixed wall is
one lattice layer inside or outside the indicated square, including
the convention with bonds crossing to an exterior wired layer.
statements.section_title: Quenched partition readout and boundary arms

statements.label: crit:tuning-zero
statements.text:
For every sufficiently small fixed $D>0$, the tuned parameter is
$t_*(D)=0$.

statements.title: Transition in the $(t,D)$ coordinates
statements.label: crit:identification
statements.text:
For every sufficiently small fixed $D>0$, the disorder-averaged plus
magnetization vanishes at $t\le0$ and is positive at every $t>0$.

title: Marked polygon correlations and one-arc bounds
abstract: At the critical honeycomb vertex activity, the squared-length mass of simple polygons of diameter at most H, counted modulo translations, is at most \(H^{2/3+o(1)}\). We also prove a quantitative two-mark cylinder estimate and a polynomial one-arc bound uniform even for arbitrarily unequal marked intervals.

tex.abstract: At the critical honeycomb vertex activity, the squared-length mass of simple polygons of diameter at most $H$, counted modulo translations, is at most $H^{2/3+o(1)}$. We also prove a quantitative two-mark cylinder estimate and a polynomial one-arc bound uniform even for arbitrarily unequal marked intervals.

statements.title: Squared-length polygon mass
statements.label: thm:polygon-moment
statements.text:
For every $\eta>0$ there is $C_\eta<\infty$ such that, for $H\ge1$,
\[
 \sum_{\substack{[P]\ \operatorname{diam}P\le H}}
       \rho_{\rm v}^{|P|}|P|^2\le C_\eta H^{2/3+\eta}.
\]
The sum is over the simple unoriented polygon translation classes just
defined.

statements.title: Uniform real-energy coercivity
statements.label: thm:06-real-positivity
statements.text:
For the magnetic contours there are constants \(0<c_2<C_2<\infty\)
such that
\begin{equation}
 c_2\left(\|D\|_2^2+\sum_I\|\xi_I\|_{-1/2}^2\right)
 \le B(\xi)\le
 C_2\left(\|D\|_2^2+\sum_I\|\xi_I\|_{-1/2}^2\right).
 
\end{equation}
They are uniform in \(t\in[1/2,1]\) and in all sufficiently small
positive far-contour parameters \(\varepsilon\).
The form extends to the completion in this norm.

statements.title: Reference sources
statements.label: prop:reference-source
statements.text:
For fixed $C_1$, integer dimensions $0\le N_g\le C_1e^{\gamma L}$,
and a real smooth reflected test $\ell(Q)$,
\begin{equation}
 \log\mathbb E_0 e^{\ell(Q)}\le C_2L+\tfrac12\|\ell\|_*^2.
\end{equation}
If $\ell(Q)=(f,q)$ and
$f_g(t)=f_{g,0}+2\sum_{k\ge1}f_{g,k}\cos kt$, then
$\|\ell\|_*^2=\sum_{g,k\ge1}k|f_{g,k}|^2$.
Constants in $f$ do not affect the test.
statements.section_title: Magnetic fluctuations and the rare central scale

statements.title: Compensated quadratic integration
statements.label: prop:quadratic-integration
statements.text:
Let $F$ be real symmetric and bounded on $\mathcal X$, with
$F\ge gI$, $g>0$, and $F-I$ trace class. Suppose its perturbation
and a real linear functional $h_0(l,\cdot)$ are represented by smooth
reflected physical kernels and tests. Let $c\in\mathbb R$. For
\[
 V(Q)=c+h_0(l,Q)+\tfrac12h_0(Q,(F-I)Q),\qquad
 m_F=c-\tfrac12h_0(l,F^{-1}l),
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
 \log\mathbb E_0e^{-V(Q)}\le -m_F+C_2L
        +\tfrac12\sum_{\lambda<1,\ \lambda\in\operatorname{spec}F}
                   -\log\lambda.
\end{equation}
The sum counts multiplicity. If the sharper source bound
\eqref{eq:G-14} holds, the gap is inverse-polynomial, and the data
and required fixed-order derivatives have polynomial bounds, the
same estimate on $\mathcal G$ has $o(L)$ in place of $C_2L$.
statements.section_title: Magnetic fluctuations and the rare central scale

statements.title: Implementation of magnetic trial actions
statements.label: prop:07_magnetic_analysis-transport
statements.text:
Let \(Z_0\) be the primitive of the coarse or sharp tilt, and set
\[
 C_z(Y)=\mathcal D(m'p_L+(Y+iZ_0)',\zeta),\qquad
 m_z=\inf_{Y\in\mathcal X\text{ real}}\operatorname{Re}C_z(Y).
\]
Derivatives here denote densities pushed from \(\tau\) to the physical
coordinate. After the reference transport, the logarithm of the modulus
of the unnormalized sector integral is at most
\[
 -m_z+\tfrac{7\gamma}{8}L_X+\tfrac{5\gamma}{16}(L_Y-L_X)
       -\tfrac{\gamma}{4}(L_X+L_Y)+o_{\rm proj}(L)+o(L).
\]
The discarded part can be made smaller than
\(\exp(-L^{E_2})\) for any required fixed \(E_2\). The coefficient of
\(o_{\rm proj}(L)\) is arbitrarily small after the core projection is
improved. Without a tilt one also has the bound \(-m_0+O(L)\),
which permits polynomial truncation of \(n_e,|M|,\ell_e\).
statements.section_title: Magnetic fluctuations and the rare central scale

statements.title: The sharp marked-pair bound
statements.label: thm:07_magnetic_analysis-moment
statements.text:
Fix $c_1\in(0,1]$ and a sufficiently small $c_4>0$. Consider the
physical cyclic row $[p,X,p',Y]$ with $s=|X|$, $b=|Y|$, and
$N=s+b+2$ even. All real site offsets vanish. Ordinary $Y$ sites
have height zero; ordinary $X$ sites and both marks have heights in
$\{0,\beta\}$. Let $t$ be the upper-height fraction in $X$ and set
$L_X=\gamma^{-1}\log s$, $L_Y=\gamma^{-1}\log b$.
Uniformly as $L_Y\to\infty$ under
\[
 c_1L_Y\le L_X\le L_Y,\qquad \tfrac12\le t\le1,
 \qquad t<1\ \Longrightarrow\ s(1-t)\ge e^{c_4L_Y},
\]
one has
\[
 \log\mathcal C(p,p')
 \le-\frac43\log s+\frac{617}{1200}\log(b/s)+o(\log b).
\]
statements.section_title: Magnetic fluctuations and the rare central scale

statements.title: Uniform one-arc bound
statements.label: 09_fast_paths:one-arc-bound
statements.text:
There are constants $\delta_1>0$, $L_*>0$, and $C<\infty$ such
that
\[
                         A(p,p')\le b^C
\]
whenever $L_Y\ge L_X\ge L_*$, $s\le b$, and at least
$1/2-\delta_1$ of the ordinary $X$ sites have height $\beta$.
The marks may each have either height in $\{0,\beta\}$.
There is no positive lower bound on $L_X/L_Y$.

tex.abstract: For uniform self-avoiding walks of every sufficiently large integer length on the honeycomb lattice, we prove diameter exponent $3/4$ and simultaneous local-mass and covering exponent $4/3$, with arbitrary positive exponent slack and arbitrary polynomial failure probability.

statements.title: Fixed-length mass and covering exponents
statements.label: thm:main

statements.title: Span in every lattice normal
statements.label: cor:directional-span
statements.text:
For every \(\delta,k>0\), outside an event of \(\Prob_n\)-probability
\(O_{\delta,k}(n^{-k})\), the projection of \(V(\gamma)\) onto each
unit normal to a direction of triangular-lattice edges has span at least
\(n^{3/4-\delta}\). This holds for every sufficiently large integer \(n\).

statements.title: Covering dimension at polynomially separated scales
statements.label: cor:dimension
statements.text:
For each fixed $\epsilon\in(0,3/4)$,
\[
\sup_{1\le s\le n^{3/4-\epsilon}}
\left|\frac{\log\mathcal N_\gamma(s)}{\log(D(\gamma)/s)}-\frac43\right|
\longrightarrow0
\quad\hbox{in }\Prob_n\hbox{-probability}.
\]
The statistic can be defined arbitrarily when $D(\gamma)\le n^{3/4-\epsilon}$.

statements.title: Radius of gyration and moments
statements.label: cor:gyration
statements.text:
Let
\[
\bar\gamma=\frac1{n+1}\sum_{j=0}^n\gamma_j,
\qquad R_g(\gamma)^2=\frac1{n+1}\sum_{j=0}^n|\gamma_j-\bar\gamma|^2.
\]
Then $R_g=n^{3/4+o(1)}$ with the same arbitrary polynomial probability convention as in Theorem~\ref{thm:main}. For every fixed $p>0$,
\[
\E_n[D^p]=n^{3p/4+o(1)},\qquad
\E_n[R_g^p]=n^{3p/4+o(1)}.
\]

statements.title: Boundary flux and strip mass
statements.label: thm:01-strip
statements.text:
For every finite simply connected union \(D\) of triangular tiles with
simple polygonal boundary and each boundary source port \(a\),
\[
 \sum_{b\in\partial D}\sum_{\gamma:a\to b}
       \rho^{|\gamma|}e^{3iW(\gamma)/8}=1,
\]
where \(W\) is total signed turning from the initial inward direction to
the final outward direction. If \(D\) is convex, its unsigned exit mass
is at most \(1/c\). For each \(h\ge1\), all strip sums defined above
are finite and
\[
 cA_h+B_h=1,\qquad B_{h+1}\le B_h,\qquad
 B_h\asymp(1+h)^{-1/4},\qquad
 m_h\asymp h^{3/4},\qquad m_{h+1}-m_h\asymp B_h.
\]
The constants are independent of \(h\), and \(b_h(x)=b_h(-x)\).
statements.section_title: Critical masses and the analytic inputs

statements.title: Length and nesting
statements.label: lem:02-length-nests
statements.text:
For the two face centers \(f_1,f_2\) adjacent to \(p\),
\[
 \frac1{\sqrt2}\bigl(Z_{f_1}(D)+Z_{f_2}(D)\bigr)
 \le L_p(D)\le Z_{f_1}(D)+Z_{f_2}(D).
\]
The same comparison holds with finite quantities in every infinite strip
of fixed positive height. Moreover,
\(P_2(r)=r^{1/12+o(1)}\) and \(S_k=k^{1/12+o(1)}\).
statements.section_title: Critical masses and the analytic inputs

statements.title: Raw strip first-length mass
statements.label: prop:02-length-reduction
statements.text:
From one fixed bottom port of the \(h\)-band strip,
\[
 \sum_{\gamma\text{ arch or bridge}}\rho^{|\gamma|}|\gamma|
       \le h^{13/12+o(1)}.
\]
statements.section_title: Critical masses and the analytic inputs

statements.title: Polygon length-square mass
statements.label: thm:07_magnetic_analysis-moment
statements.text:
For unrooted, unoriented simple honeycomb polygons modulo triangular-lattice
translations,
\[
 \sum_{[\ell]:\,\operatorname{diam}\ell\le H}
             \rho^{|\ell|}|\ell|^2\le H^{2/3+o(1)}.
\]
statements.section_title: Critical masses and the analytic inputs

statements.title: Uniform one-arc bound
statements.label: 09_fast_paths:one-arc-bound
statements.text:
There are constants \(\delta_1>0\), \(L_*>0\), and \(C<\infty\)
such that \(A(p,p')\le b^C\) whenever
\[
 L_Y\ge L_X\ge L_*,\qquad s\le b,\qquad
 L_X=\tfrac34\log s,\quad L_Y=\tfrac34\log b,
\]
and at least fraction \(1/2-\delta_1\) of the ordinary \(X\)-sites
are upper. There is no positive lower bound on \(L_X/L_Y\).
statements.section_title: Critical masses and the analytic inputs

statements.title: Full-box susceptibility
statements.label: 09_fast_paths:full-box
statements.text:
Let \(S(H)\) be the maximum, over starting vertices in a box of side
\(H\), of the critical mass of walks confined to that box, with
arbitrary endpoint and length. There are constants \(C_0,C_1\) such
that \(S(H)\le C_0(1+H)^{C_1}\).
statements.section_title: The critical mass of paths in a box

statements.title: Localized strip second moment
statements.label: prop:08-strip-second
statements.section_title: Localized bridges, recoverable cuts, and length moments

statements.title: A localized bridge length lower bound
statements.label: prop:08-localized-length
statements.text:
For a sufficiently large fixed \(C\), the height \(M\) bridges from a
fixed source and of diameter at most \(CM\) have first-length mass
\(M^{13/12-o(1)}\) in the lower-exponent sense. Consequently, for every
fixed \(\xi>0\), the normalized critical bridge law satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \Prob_M^{\mathrm{br}}\{|\gamma|\ge M^{4/3-\xi}\}\ge M^{-o(1)}.
 
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Localized bridges, recoverable cuts, and length moments

statements.title: A long arch in a shallow strip
statements.label: lem:08-long-arch
statements.text:
For every fixed $\sigma>0$ and all sufficiently large fixed $D'$, there
are $c,C>0$ and $h_0$ with the following property for $h\ge h_0$. From any horizontal boundary port $a=(x_A,u)$,
there is arch mass between $ch^{-1/4}$ and $Ch^{-1/4}$ which stays in
\[
 u<y<u+\sigma h,\qquad x>x_A-\sigma h,
\]
except at its two boundary endpoints, and has free terminal port on
$y=u$ with abscissa exceeding $x_A+D'h$. The arches can be confined
to a box of diameter $Ch$.
statements.section_title: Localized bridges, recoverable cuts, and length moments

statements.title: Typical finite-bridge length
statements.label: thm:08-bridge-length
statements.text:
For every \(\varepsilon>0\) there is \(c_\varepsilon>0\) such that a
critical height-\(H\) bridge satisfies
\[
 \Prob_H^{\mathrm{br}}\{H^{4/3-\varepsilon}\le|\gamma|
                         \le H^{4/3+\varepsilon}\}
       \ge1-O_\varepsilon(H^{-c_\varepsilon}).
\]
Its diameter is at least \(d_0H\) and at most \(CH^{1+\varepsilon}\)
with polynomially small exceptional probability.
statements.section_title: From localized moments to a typical bridge

statements.title: Ordered probes, with one or two giant ends
statements.label: thm:10-ordered-probes
statements.text:
The constants \(L,L_2,K_1,K_2,K_3\) can be chosen so that, for all integer
\(1\le h,h_1,h_2\le r\), with \(r\) dyadic and \(d\ge0\),
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf P(E(h))\le K_1h^{-\alpha},\qquad
 F(h,r,d)\le K_2r^{-\alpha}\Phi(d),\qquad
 F_{12}(h_1,h_2,r)\le K_3r^{-\alpha}.
\end{equation}
Either adjacent-port choice and each reflected orientation obey the same
bounds.

statements.title: First-hit avoidance with logarithmic loss
statements.label: cor:10-log-first-hit

statements.title: Adjacent-arm avoidance
statements.label: 09_fast_paths:adjacent-arms
statements.text:
For every \(\epsilon>0\), the probability \(S_2(H)\) of disjoint
first-hit paths from neighboring ports satisfies
\(S_2(H)\le C_\epsilon H^{-3/4+\epsilon}\).

statements.title: Fast bridges
statements.label: 09_fast_paths:fast-bridges

statements.title: Uniform local length bound
statements.label: thm:11-local-length
statements.text:
For every $\tau>0$ and $A>0$ there is $C_{\tau,A}<\infty$ such that,
for every $H\ge2$, outside a set of $\mu_H$-mass at most
$C_{\tau,A}H^{-A}$, every vertex subwalk $\sigma$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 |\sigma|\le H^\tau(1+s(\sigma))^{4/3},
 \qquad s(\sigma)=\text{its vertical span in band units}.
 
\end{equation}
The same conclusion holds for each of the finitely many lattice
normal directions simultaneously.
statements.section_title: Length in small regions and repeated crossings

statements.title: Uniform local mass bound
statements.label: prop:11-local-mass
statements.text:
For every $\tau>0$ and $A>0$, there is $C_{\tau,A}<\infty$ such that
for all $H\ge2$, outside a set of $\mu_H$-mass at most
$C_{\tau,A}H^{-A}$, simultaneously for every visited vertex $v$ and
every real radius $1\le s\le H$,
\begin{equation}
 \#\bigl(V(\gamma)\cap\overline B(v,s)\bigr)\le H^\tau s^{4/3}.
 
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Length in small regions and repeated crossings

statements.title: Uniform temporal modulus
statements.label: prop:11-modulus
statements.text:
For every $\tau>0$ and $A>0$ there is $C_{\tau,A}<\infty$ such that,
for every $H\ge2$, outside a set of $\mu_H$-mass at most
$C_{\tau,A}H^{-A}$, every subwalk $\sigma$ of $l$ steps satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{diam}(\sigma)\le H^\tau(1+l)^{3/4}.
\]

title: An Upper Bound of 9/4 for the Matrix Multiplication Exponent
abstract: We prove that the exponent of matrix multiplication over the complex numbers is at most 9/4.

tex.abstract:
We prove that the exponent of matrix multiplication over the complex
numbers is at most $9/4$.
sections: Discrete growth and the arithmetic exponent

statements.label: thm:main

statements.title: Finite separation
statements.label: prop:separation
statements.text:
Let $M\geq1$ and
\[
 A=\sum_{h=1}^M A_h,\qquad A_h\in X\otimes Y_h\otimes Z_h,
\]
where the $Y_h$ are disjoint coordinate spaces and so are the $Z_h$.
There are no terms between unmatched second- and third-leg sectors.
Then
\begin{equation}
 A^{\oplus5M}\degen
 \bigoplus_{h=1}^M\bigl(A_h\otimes B_X(M)\bigr).
\end{equation}
Each $A_h$ on the right has its own copy of $X$.

statements.title: Shared-leg entropy inequality
statements.label: cor:entropy
statements.text:
Let $T=\sum_{i=1}^s T_i$ be a sum of nonzero tensors with a common first
space and matched, pairwise disjoint sectors on the other two legs, as
in Proposition~\ref{prop:separation}. For every tensor character
$\lambda$ and every probability vector $q=(q_1,\ldots,q_s)$,
\begin{equation}
 \lambda(T)\geq
 e^{p_X H(q)}\prod_{i=1}^s\lambda(T_i)^{q_i},
 \qquad H(q)=-\sum_{i=1}^s q_i\log q_i.
\end{equation}
Here logarithms are natural and $0\log0=0$.

title: Maximal Multipoint Seshadri Constants in Higher Dimensions
abstract: Let L be an ample line bundle on a smooth integral complex projective variety X of dimension n ≥ 3. We prove that there is a threshold \(r_0=r_0(X,L)\) such that for every integer \(r\ge r_0\), the ordinary multipoint Seshadri constant at r very general points equals the volume bound \((L^n/r)^{1/n}\). This establishes the qualitative Nagata–Biran–Szemberg assertion in these dimensions.

tex.abstract:
Let $L$ be an ample line bundle on a smooth integral complex projective variety
$X$ of dimension $n\ge3$. We prove that there is a threshold
$r_0=r_0(X,L)$ such that for every integer $r\ge r_0$, the ordinary multipoint
Seshadri constant at $r$ very general points equals the volume bound
$(L^n/r)^{1/n}$. This establishes the qualitative Nagata--Biran--Szemberg
assertion in these dimensions.
sections: A simplex from a complete-intersection flag

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $X$ be a smooth integral complex projective variety of dimension
$n\ge3$, and let $L$ be an ample line bundle on $X$. There is an integer
$r_0=r_0(X,L)\ge1$ such that for every integer $r\ge r_0$ there is a
countable union $Z_r$ of proper Zariski-closed subsets of $U_r(X)$, with
nonempty complement, for which
\[
 \eps(X,L;\mathbf p)=\left(\frac{L^n}{r}\right)^{1/n}
 \qquad\text{for every }\mathbf p\in U_r(X)\setminus Z_r.
\]

statements.title: The initial simplex
statements.label: prop:flag-simplex
statements.text:
Let $X$ be a smooth integral complex projective variety of dimension
$n\geq3$, let $L$ be ample, and put $V=L^n$. Choose a positive integer $D$
such that $DL$ is very ample. There is a graded support family
$S_k\subset\Z_{\geq0}^n$ such that
\begin{align}
 S_k&\subset kP_0,
 &P_0&=\Delta(1/D,\ldots,1/D,D^{n-1}V),
 \\
 \#S_k&=h^0(X,kL)
       =\frac{V}{n!}k^n+O(k^{n-1}),
 &\vol(P_0)&=\frac{V}{n!}.
 
\end{align}
For all integers $k\geq1$, $m\geq0$, and $r\geq1$, if
$\M(S_k)$ separates jets through degree $m$ at some distinct $r$-tuple
in $\Torus^n$, then $H^0(X,kL)$ does so at some distinct $r$-tuple in $X$.
statements.section_title: A simplex from a complete-intersection flag

statements.title: Two-intercept reshaping
statements.label: prop:reshape
statements.text:
Let $n\ge2$, let $A,B,a_3,\ldots,a_n$ be positive real numbers, and let
$(S_k)_{k\ge1}$ be finite exponent sets satisfying
\[
 S_k\subset k\Delta(A,B,a_3,\ldots,a_n)\cap\Z^n,
 \qquad S_k+S_l\subset S_{k+l}\quad(k,l\ge1).
\]
Set $H=AB$ and $d=\max(3/A,2/B)$.  For every real number $w>0$ with
$dw<1/16$, there are finite sets $(S'_k)_{k\ge1}$ such that
\begin{align}
 S'_k&\subset k\Delta(w,H/w,a_3,\ldots,a_n)\cap\Z^n,
                                                        \\
 \#S'_k&=\#S_k,
 \qquad S'_k+S'_l\subset S'_{k+l}.                       
\end{align}
Moreover, for every $k\ge1$, $m\ge0$, and $r\ge1$, if $\M(S'_k)$ surjects
onto jets through degree $m$ at some $r$ distinct points of $\Torus^n$,
then $\M(S_k)$ does so at some $r$ distinct points of $\Torus^n$.

statements.title: Jets from full-volume supports
statements.label: prop:asymptotic-jets
statements.text:
Let $n\ge2$ and $r\ge1$ be integers, let $w>0$, and set
\[
 P=\Delta(w,\ldots,w,rw).
\]
Suppose that finite sets $F_k\subset kP\cap\Z^n$, indexed by all integers
$k\ge1$, satisfy
\[
 F_k+F_l\subset F_{k+l},
 \qquad
 \#F_k=\vol(P)k^n+o(k^n).
\]
For every $0<\theta<w$ and every choice of distinct
$c_1,\ldots,c_r\in\C^*$, the space $\M(F_k)$ surjects onto jets through
degree $\lfloor k\theta\rfloor$ at $(1,\ldots,1,c_i)$ for all sufficiently
large $k$.

abstract: We prove that, for every smooth integral complex projective surface S and every ample line bundle L, the multipoint Seshadri constant at r very general points equals \(\sqrt{L^2/r}\) for every sufficiently large integer r. This resolves positively the qualitative Nagata–Biran conjecture for surfaces.

tex.abstract:
We prove that, for every smooth integral complex projective surface $S$
and every ample line bundle $L$, the multipoint Seshadri constant at $r$
very general points equals $\sqrt{L^2/r}$ for every sufficiently large
integer $r$. This resolves positively the qualitative Nagata--Biran
conjecture for surfaces.
sections: Finite jet tests and initial monomials
A nodal divisor and its exponent diagram

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every smooth integral complex projective surface $S$ and every ample
line bundle $L$ on $S$, there is an integer $r_0=r_0(S,L)$ with the following
property. For each integer $r\ge r_0$, there is a countable union
$Z_r$ of proper Zariski-closed subsets of $U_r$, with nonempty complement,
such that for every $\mathbf p\in U_r\setminus Z_r$ the class
\[
 \pi^*L-\sqrt{\frac{L^2}{r}}\sum_{i=1}^r E_i
\]
is nef on the blow-up at $\mathbf p$. Consequently,
\[
 \varepsilon(S,L;\mathbf p)=\sqrt{\frac{L^2}{r}}.
\]

statements.title: Transfer from initial monomials
statements.label: prop:initial-transfer
statements.text:
Let $F\subset\C\{x,z\}$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector space
of convergent holomorphic germs, and let $t>0$.  The set $E_t(F)$ has
exactly $\dim F$ elements, and $F$ admits a basis whose initial exponents
are these distinct elements.

Let $r,m$ be positive integers.  If the monomial space
\[
 \Span_{\C}\{X^\alpha Z^\beta:(\alpha,\beta)\in E_t(F)\}
\]
has an injective order-$m$ jet test at some distinct points
$q_1,\ldots,q_r\in\T$, then representatives of $F$ on a common
neighborhood of the origin have an injective order-$m$ jet test at
distinct points arbitrarily close to the origin.
statements.section_title: Finite jet tests and initial monomials

statements.title: The quadrilateral bound
statements.label: prop:quadrilateral
statements.text:
For the surface, line bundle, nodal divisor, coordinates and frame fixed
above, every integer $k\ge1$, every $t>T$, and every nonzero
$s\in H^0(S,kL)$ satisfy
\[
 \nu_t(s)\in kQ_t.
\]
Moreover, $H^0(S,kL)$ has a basis with pairwise distinct initial exponents
in $kQ_t$; the basis is empty if this section space is zero.
statements.section_title: A nodal divisor and its exponent diagram

statements.title: Diagonal compression
statements.label: prop:compression
statements.text:
Let $k,m,r$ be positive integers.  If $\mathcal M(kP_t)$ has injective
order-$m$ jets at some $r$ distinct points of $\T$, then
$\mathcal M(kQ_t)$ has injective order-$m$ jets at some $r$ distinct
points of $\T$.
statements.section_title: A nodal divisor and its exponent diagram

statements.title: From the triangle to the surface
statements.label: cor:surface-transfer
statements.text:
Let $k,m,r$ be positive integers.  If $\mathcal M(kP_t)$ has injective
order-$m$ jets at some $r$ distinct torus points, then $H^0(S,kL)$ has
injective order-$m$ jets at some $r$ distinct points of $S$.
statements.section_title: A nodal divisor and its exponent diagram

statements.label: prop:subgroup-test
statements.text:
Let $H>0$, let $r$ be a positive integer, and let $P\subset\R^2$ be a
triangle of area $H/2$.  Suppose there is a primitive vector $u\in\Z^2$
such that
\[
 \max_{\xi\in P}\det(u,\xi)
 -\min_{\xi\in P}\det(u,\xi)=\sqrt{rH}.
\]
Then there is a subgroup $G\subset\T$ of exactly $r$ distinct points
such that, for all positive integers $k,m$ with
$m>k\sqrt{H/r}$, the order-$m$ jet test on $\mathcal M(kP)$ at $G$ is
injective.

statements.label: cor:torus-test
statements.text:
For the fixed parameters $d,H,T$ of Section~\ref{sec:node}, there is an
integer $r_0$ such that for every integer $r\geq r_0$ one can choose a
single $t>T$ and a subgroup $G\subset\T$ of $r$ distinct points for
which the following holds: for all positive integers $k,m$ satisfying
\[
 m>k\sqrt{H/r},
\]
the order-$m$ jet test on $\mathcal M(kP_t)$ at $G$ is injective.

statements.title: Homogeneous tests imply nefness
statements.label: prop:homogeneous-nef
statements.text:
Let $S$ be a smooth integral complex projective surface, let $L$ be
ample, and let $p_1,\ldots,p_r$ be distinct points. Put
$H=L^2$ and $w=\sqrt{H/r}$. Suppose that, for all positive integers
$k,m$ with $m>kw$, no nonzero section of $L^{\otimes k}$ vanishes to
order at least $m$ at every $p_i$. On the blow-up
$\pi:Y\to S$ of these points, with exceptional curves $E_i$, the real
divisor class
\[
 D_0=\pi^*L-w\sum_{i=1}^rE_i
\]
is nef.

statements.label: cor:fields
statements.text:
Let $K$ be an uncountable algebraically closed field of characteristic
zero, let $S$ be a smooth integral projective surface over $K$, and let
$L$ be an ample line bundle on $S$. There is an integer $r_0=r_0(S,L)$
such that, for every $r\ge r_0$, outside a countable union of proper
Zariski-closed subsets of $U_r$, with nonempty complement, one has
\[
 \varepsilon(S,L;p_1,\ldots,p_r)=\sqrt{L^2/r}.
\]

title: Maximal multipoint Seshadri constants in positive characteristic
abstract: Let L be an ample line bundle on a smooth integral projective variety X over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic, with \(\dim X=n\ge3\). We prove that there is a threshold \(r_0=r_0(X,L)\) such that for every integer \(r\ge r_0\), the ordinary multipoint Seshadri constant at the geometric generic tuple of r points equals the volume bound \((L^n/r)^{1/n}\). The same conclusion holds in dimension two. This establishes the positive-characteristic form of the qualitative Nagata–Biran–Szemberg assertion at geometric generic tuples.

tex.abstract:
Let $L$ be an ample line bundle on a smooth integral projective variety $X$
over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic, with
$\dim X=n\ge3$. We prove that there is a threshold $r_0=r_0(X,L)$ such that
for every integer $r\ge r_0$, the ordinary multipoint Seshadri constant at
the geometric generic tuple of $r$ points equals the volume bound
$(L^n/r)^{1/n}$. The same conclusion holds in dimension two. This establishes
the positive-characteristic form of the qualitative Nagata--Biran--Szemberg
assertion at geometric generic tuples.
sections: Leading terms and transfer of jets
An initial simplex from a flag
From jets to the Seshadri constant

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $X/k$ be a smooth integral projective variety over an algebraically
closed field of characteristic $p>0$, with $\dim X=n\ge3$, and let $L$
be ample. There is an integer $r_0=r_0(X,L)$ such that
\[
 \varepsilon_r(X,L)=\left(\frac{L^n}{r}\right)^{1/n}
 \qquad\text{for every integer }r\ge r_0.
\]

statements.label: prop:initial-simplex
statements.text:
Let $X$ be a smooth integral projective $n$-dimensional variety over an
algebraically closed field, with $n\geq2$, and let $L$ be ample.  Put
$V=L^n$, and choose an integer $D\geq1$ such that $DL$ is very ample.
There is a graded family of finite sets $S_N\subset\Z_{\geq0}^n$ such
that
\begin{align}
 S_N&\subset NP_0,
 &P_0&=\Delta(1/D,\ldots,1/D,D^{n-1}V),
 \\
 \#S_N&=h^0(X,NL)
       =\frac{V}{n!}N^n+o(N^n).
 
\end{align}
For every $N,r\geq1$ and $m\geq0$, if $M(S_N)$ separates jets through
order $m$ at some $r$ distinct torus points, then $H^0(X,NL)$ separates
the same jets at some $r$ distinct points of $X$.
statements.section_title: An initial simplex from a flag

statements.title: Two-intercept reshaping
statements.label: prop:reshape
statements.text:
Let $n\ge2$, let $A,B,a_3,\ldots,a_n>0$, and let $(S_N)_{N\ge1}$ be a
graded family of finite subsets of $\Z^n$ satisfying
\[
 S_N\subset N\Delta(A,B,a_3,\ldots,a_n).
\]
Put $H=AB$ and $d=\max\{3/A,2/B\}$.  For every $w>0$ with $dw<1/16$,
there is a graded family $(S'_N)_{N\ge1}$ such that
\[
 S'_N\subset N\Delta(w,H/w,a_3,\ldots,a_n),
 \qquad \#S'_N=\#S_N \quad(N\ge1).
\]
The transformation from $S_N$ to $S'_N$ has backward jet transfer in every
degree.  For $n=2$, the lists $a_3,\ldots,a_n$ are empty.

statements.title: Jets at the geometric generic tuple
statements.label: prop:generic-jets
statements.text:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic, let $X/k$
be a smooth integral projective variety of dimension $n\ge2$, and let $L$ be
ample.  Put $V=L^n$.  There is an integer $r_0=r_0(X,L)$ such that, for every
integer $r\ge r_0$ and every real number
\[
 0<\theta<\left(\frac Vr\right)^{1/n},
\]
there is an integer $N_0=N_0(r,\theta)$ such that, for every $N\ge N_0$,
the sections of $NL$ separate jets through order $\lfloor N\theta\rfloor$
at some ordered $r$-tuple of distinct $k$-points, which may depend on $N$.
For each such $N$, the same jet separation holds after base change to $K_r$
at the geometric generic tuple $p_1,\ldots,p_r$.

title: Mean-payoff parity games in quasipolynomial time
abstract: We give a uniform deterministic quasipolynomial-time algorithm for mean-payoff parity games. It computes all vertices from which a player can enforce both nonnegative liminf mean payoff and the parity condition, with arbitrary signed binary rewards and unrestricted binary priorities. The running time is \(2^{O((\log(L+2))^2)}\) bit operations, where L is the complete input length.

tex.abstract:
We give a uniform deterministic quasipolynomial-time algorithm for
mean-payoff parity games. It computes all vertices from which a player
can enforce both nonnegative liminf mean payoff and the parity condition,
with arbitrary signed binary rewards and unrestricted binary priorities.
The running time is $2^{O((\log(L+2))^2)}$ bit operations, where $L$ is
the complete input length.
sections: Complexity in the full binary input length

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
A uniform deterministic algorithm returns exactly all vertices from
which Max can force~\eqref{eq:objective} against every Min strategy.
For an absolute constant $C>0$, it uses at most
\[
                     2^{C(\log_2(L+2))^2}
\]
bit operations. The number of distinct priorities and the magnitudes
of the rewards are unrestricted.

statements.title: Mean-payoff input
statements.label: prop:mp-interface
statements.text:
For a finite nonempty total arena $H$ with signed binary integer
weights, its ordinary mean-payoff winning set
\[
 U_{\mathrm{mp}}(H)=
 \{v:\text{Max can force liminf mean payoff at least }0\}
\]
is computable deterministically in
$2^{O((\log_2(L_H+2))^2)}$ bit operations, where $L_H$ is its full
binary encoding length. There is a single positional Max strategy
winning from every vertex of $U_{\mathrm{mp}}(H)$, and a single
positional Min strategy forcing strictly negative liminf mean payoff
from every vertex outside it. Both guarantees hold against every
history-dependent opposing strategy.

statements.label: thm:determinacy
statements.text:
In every finite arena, each vertex is winning for exactly one of \Max\
and \Min.  From each vertex winning for \Max, there is a
conjunction-winning strategy satisfying \eqref{eq:uniform-prefix}.

statements.title: Bounded-dominion guarantee
statements.label: thm:labels
statements.text:
For every subarena $H$ of the original game and every
$\mathbf b\in\{0,\ldots,n\}^2$, the procedure
$\Solve(H,\mathbf b)$ terminates and returns a partition satisfying
\eqref{eq:label-guarantee} for both players.

statements.title: Cost of the reduction
statements.label: prop:reduction-cost
statements.text:
For an arena with $n\ge1$ vertices and complete binary input length $L$,
the call $\Solve(G,(n,n))$ makes
\[
 2^{O((\log_2(n+2))^2)}
\]
calls to the ordinary mean-payoff winning-set subroutine.  Each such
call has an explicit input of length $(L+2)^{O(1)}$.  Apart from those
subroutine calls, the computation takes
\[
 2^{O((\log_2(n+2))^2)}(L+2)^{O(1)}
\]
bit operations.  All constants are absolute.

title: Memory and precision in noiseless Gaussian regression
abstract: For every fixed A > 0, a learner that retains at most \(Ad^2\) bits between fresh exact Gaussian linear measurements needs \(\Omega_A(d\log(1/\epsilon))\) measurements to estimate a uniformly random unit vector to angular error at most ϵ, for any \(0\lt \epsilon\le 1/10\), with probability at least 2/3. The constant is absolute for \(o(d^2)\) memory.

tex.abstract:
For every fixed \(A>0\), a learner that retains at most \(Ad^2\) bits
between fresh exact Gaussian linear measurements needs
\(\Omega_A(d\log(1/\epsilon))\) measurements to estimate a uniformly
random unit vector to angular error at most \(\epsilon\), for any
\(0<\epsilon\le 1/10\), with probability at least \(2/3\). The constant
is absolute for \(o(d^2)\) memory.
sections: From one block to a finite stream
Constant accuracy and the main lower bound
Selection on a common data domain

statements.title: Memory and precision
statements.label: h:main
statements.text:
For every fixed finite \(A>0\), there are constants \(c_A>0\) and
\(d_A\) such that the following holds. Let \(d\ge d_A\), let
\(0\le M\le Ad^2\) be an integer, and let \(0<\epsilon\le1/10\).
For any learner in Definition~\ref{h:model}, draw
\(S\sim\sigma_d\) independently of the rows and the learner's
data-independent randomness. If
\[
 \Prob\{\arccos\ip{\widehat s}{S}\le\epsilon\}\ge\frac23,
\]
then its prescribed horizon satisfies
\[
 T\ge c_A\,d\log(1/\epsilon).
\]

statements.title: Subquadratic memory
statements.label: h:subquadratic
statements.text:
Let \(M(d)\ge0\) be integer-valued with \(M(d)=o(d^2)\), and let
\(0<\epsilon(d)\le1/10\) be any accuracy sequence. A family of learners
in Definition~\ref{h:model} with uniform-sphere average success at
least \(2/3\) satisfies
\[
 T(d)\ge c\,d\log(1/\epsilon(d))
\]
for all sufficiently large \(d\), where \(c>0\) is absolute. The
dimension threshold may depend on the memory sequence.

statements.title: A guarantee for every signal
statements.label: h:worst-signal
statements.text:
The conclusions of Theorem~\ref{h:main} and
Corollary~\ref{h:subquadratic} also hold when their average-success
assumption is replaced by
\[
 \Prob\{\arccos\ip{\widehat s}{s}\le\epsilon\}\ge\frac23
 \qquad\text{for every }s\in S^{d-1},
\]
where this probability is over the rows and the learner's randomness.

statements.title: Exact projection density from an ambient ball bound
statements.label: h:dv:finite-density

statements.title: Affine-distance and Gram bounds
statements.label: h:dv:ambient-gram

statements.title: Normalized exact projection
statements.label: h:proj:normalized
statements.text:
Use the parameters in \eqref{h:local:parameters}, and let
\(1\le m\le q\). Let \(\nu\) be a finite nonnegative Borel measure
of mass at most one, supported on the unit ball in \(\mathbb R^d\),
such that
\begin{equation}
 \nu(B(t,\rho))\le\rho^a
 \qquad(t\in\supp\nu,\ \rho>0).
\end{equation}
The image of \(\gamma_m(dA)\nu(dt)\) under
\((A,t)\mapsto(A,At)\) has a nonnegative jointly Borel density
\(f_\nu\) relative to \(\lambda_m\), and
\begin{equation}
 \|f_\nu\|_{L^q(\lambda_m)}\le\exp(Cd).
\end{equation}
The constant is independent of \(\nu\) and \(m\).

statements.title: Success after a bounded number of samples
statements.label: h:stream:success
statements.text:
There are absolute constants $C,d_0>0$ with the following property.
For $d\ge d_0$, every learner in the stated finite-state model with
$M\ge0$ bits and an integer deterministic horizon $T\ge0$ has, for
$S\sim\sigma$ independent of its fresh Gaussian rows,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P\{\arccos\langle\widehat s,S\rangle\le\epsilon\}
 \le
 \min\left\{1,
 \left[2\epsilon\exp\!\left(
 C\left(1+\frac{M}{d^2}\right)
 \left\lceil\frac{T}{q}\right\rceil\right)\right]^a
 \right\},
\end{equation}
where $0<\epsilon\le1/10$ and
$a=(d-1)/2$, $q=\lfloor(d-1)/8\rfloor$ as in
\eqref{h:local:parameters}. The probability includes data-independent
initialization, the shared seed, and fresh random choices.
statements.section_title: From one block to a finite stream

statements.title: A block on the paired-coordinate prior
statements.label: h:cube:block
statements.text:
Let \(k,N\) be integers with \(1\le k\le p\) and \(N\ge1\), and let Borel
\(f_1,\ldots,f_N:Q\to[0,1]\) satisfy \eqref{h:cube:local} with the
same \(L\ge0\).  Suppose Borel functions
\(g_v:\mathbb R^{k\times d}\times\mathbb R^k\to[0,\infty)\) obey
\(\sum_{v=1}^N g_v(A,y)\le1\).  Then
\[
 F(u)=\mathbb E_{A\sim\gamma_k}
       \sum_{v=1}^N g_v(A,A\iota(u))f_v(u)
\]
satisfies \eqref{h:cube:local} with \(C_3^nN^{1/p}L\) in place of
\(L\), for a universal \(C_3\ge1\).

statements.title: Precision bound for the cube prior
statements.label: h:cube:success
statements.text:
There are universal constants \(D\ge e\), \(d_0\ge16\), and \(c>0\)
with the following property.  Let \(d\ge d_0\), \(M\ge0\), and \(T\ge0\)
be integers, with \(M\le d^2\) and \(0<\epsilon\le1/10\).
Every learner in Definition~\ref{h:model} with these memory and sample
bounds has angular success probability under \(s=\iota(u)\), \(u\sim du\),
at most
\begin{equation}
 \min\left\{1,\,
       D^{n(m+1)}\epsilon^{n/4}\right\},
 \qquad
 m=\left\lceil\frac{T}{k_0}\right\rceil,\qquad
 k_0=\left\lfloor\frac n4\right\rfloor.
\end{equation}
The probability averages over \(u\), the fresh Gaussian samples, and
the learner's randomness.  If that same learner has angular success
probability at least \(2/3\) for every \(s\in S^{d-1}\), then
\begin{equation}
 T\ge c\,d\log(1/\epsilon).
\end{equation}

statements.title: A direct inequality for measurable tests
statements.label: h:dv:measurable-test

statements.title: Joint \(L^1\) convergence
statements.label: h:dv:joint-l1
statements.text:
In addition to the assumptions of
Proposition~\ref{h:dv:ambient-gram}, suppose that \(d\ge2\),
\(1\le m<d\), and \(\mu\ll\sigma_d\).  Let \(F\) be the joint density
from Lemma~\ref{h:dv:joint-density}, and let \(F_\delta\) be the
Gaussian regularization in Lemma~\ref{h:dv:gaussian-moment}.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \|F_\delta-F\|_{L^1(\lambda_m)}\longrightarrow0
 \quad\hbox{as }\delta\downarrow0,
 \qquad
 \|F\|_{L^p(\lambda_m)}\le\mathcal B.
 
\end{equation}

statements.title: A pointwise joint density version
statements.label: h:dv:pointwise-density

statements.title: The dimension-scale parameter regime
statements.label: h:dv:parameters
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{h:dv:ambient-gram}, suppose that
\begin{equation}
 d\ge16,\qquad p=\lfloor d/8\rfloor,\qquad
 1\le m\le p,\qquad \frac{d-1}{2}\le\beta\le\frac d2,
 
\end{equation}
Then, for every \(0\le j\le p-2\),
\begin{equation}
 \beta-j-m\ge\frac{d-1}{2}-2p+2
 \ge\frac d4+\frac32,
 \qquad J_j\le C^d,
 
\end{equation}
where \(C\ge1\) is an absolute constant.  Thus the right side of
\eqref{h:dv:gram-product} is at most
\(C^{d(p-1)}H^pR^{\beta p-m(p-1)}\), uniformly also for short blocks
\(m<p\).

statements.title: Backward coefficient step
statements.label: h:ev:coefficient-step
statements.text:
Assume \eqref{h:dv:parameters}.  Let \(H>0\) and let \(N\ge1\) be an
integer.  Let
\(h_1,\ldots,h_N:S^{d-1}\to[0,1]\) be Borel functions satisfying
\[
 \int_{B(x,r)}h_w\,d\sigma\le H r^\beta
 \qquad(x\in\mathbb R^d,\ r>0,\ 1\le w\le N).
\]
Let \(g_w(A,y)\ge0\) be Borel functions with \(\sum_wg_w\le1\), and
define
\[
 h(s)=\mathbb E_A\sum_{w=1}^N g_w(A,As)h_w(s).
\]
There is an absolute \(C_{\mathrm{step}}\ge1\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \int_{B(z,R)}h\,d\sigma
 \le C_{\mathrm{step}}^dN^{1/p}H R^\beta
 \qquad(z\in\mathbb R^d,\ R>0).
\end{equation}

statements.title: A common finite success bound
statements.label: h:ev:coefficient-success
statements.text:
Assume \(d\ge16\), set \(n=d-1\), \(p=\lfloor d/8\rfloor\), and let
\(n/2\le\beta\le d/2\). Let \(M,T\ge0\) be integers,
\(0<\epsilon\le1/10\), and consider a learner in
Definition~\ref{h:model}. Under the uniform-sphere signal prior, write
\(P_{\mathrm{succ}}\) for its success probability with either angular
or chordal error at most \(\epsilon\), and put \(b=\lceil T/p\rceil\).
Then
\begin{equation}
 P_{\mathrm{succ}}\le
 \min\left\{1,\,
 4^n\epsilon^{n-\beta}
 \left[C_{\mathrm{step}}^d
       \bigl((p+2)2^M\bigr)^{1/p}\right]^b\right\}.
\end{equation}
The same assertion holds with the initial factor \(4^n\) replaced
by the polar-cap constant \(C_0^d\).

statements.title: Finite success bounds for the two coefficients
statements.label: h:ev:success
statements.text:
Assume \(d\ge16\) and \(p=\lfloor d/8\rfloor\).
Let \(M,T\ge0\) be integers, let \(0<\epsilon\le1/10\), and consider
a learner in Definition~\ref{h:model} with these parameters.
Draw \(S\sim\sigma\) independently of its Gaussian rows
\(x_1,\ldots,x_T\) and its data-independent randomness, and set the
exact labels \(y_t=\langle x_t,S\rangle\).  Write \(\Pr_\sigma\) for
the resulting joint law and
put \(b=\lceil T/p\rceil\).  With an absolute
\(C_{\mathrm{step}}\ge1\), the uniform-prior angular success
probability satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{angle}(\widehat S,S)\le\epsilon\}
 \le
 \min\!\left\{1,\,
 4^d\epsilon^{(d-1)/2}
 \left[C_{\mathrm{step}}^d
       \bigl((p+2)2^M\bigr)^{1/p}\right]^b
 \right\}.
\end{equation}
The uniform-prior chordal success probability satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\|\widehat S-S\|\le\epsilon\}
 \le
 \min\!\left\{1,\,
 C_0^d\epsilon^{d/2-1}
 \left[C_{\mathrm{step}}^d
       \bigl((2p+4)2^M\bigr)^{1/p}\right]^b
 \right\}.
\end{equation}
The second event contains the angular success event.

title: Metric Markov Cotype Two of ℓ1
abstract: We prove that the real Banach space ℓ1 has metric Markov cotype two, answering a question of Mendel and Naor. As a consequence, every Lipschitz map from an arbitrary subset of a real Hilbert space into ℓ1 extends to the whole Hilbert space with a universal multiplicative loss in its Lipschitz constant, resolving Ball's extension problem for this target.

tex.abstract:
We prove that the real Banach space $\ell_1$ has metric Markov cotype two,
answering a question of Mendel and Naor. As a consequence, every Lipschitz
map from an arbitrary subset of a real Hilbert space into $\ell_1$ extends
to the whole Hilbert space with a universal multiplicative loss in its
Lipschitz constant, resolving Ball's extension problem for this target.
sections: A flat map and a quartic potential
The stopped walk and the main theorem

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
The real space $\ell_1$ satisfies
\[
 N_2(\ell_1)\leq12\sqrt{21}.
\]

statements.label: cor:martingale
statements.text:
Let $(M_m)_{m\geq0}$ be an $H$-valued martingale with respect to
a filtration $(\calF_m)$, taking values in $Q$ and converging
almost surely to $M_\infty$. If $e$ is an
$\calF_0$-measurable binary vector, then
\begin{align}
 \E\sum_{m=0}^\infty
 \|\Phi(M_{m+1})-\Phi(M_m)\|_{1,w}^2
 &\leq108\bigl(\E\|M_\infty-e\|_H^4
                    -\E\|M_0-e\|_H^4\bigr)\notag\\
 &\leq108\E\|M_\infty-e\|_H^4.
 
\end{align}
statements.section_title: A flat map and a quartic potential

statements.label: cor:complex
statements.text:
For complex scalars,
$N_2(\ell_1(\mathbb C))\leq12\sqrt{42}$.

statements.label: cor:extension
statements.text:
There is a universal constant $K<\infty$ such that, for every
real Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, every subset $S\subseteq\mathcal H$,
and every Lipschitz map $f:S\to\ell_1$, there is an extension
$F:\mathcal H\to\ell_1$ with
$\Lip(F)\leq K\Lip(f)$.
