title: Microscopic jamming in the negative spherical perceptron
abstract: We prove a sharp feasibility threshold and limiting gap and force laws for the spherical perceptron with margin −1 and quadratic penalty. The limits are taken successively in system size, inverse temperature, and density approaching the threshold from above. They agree for Gaussian coordinates and for the equal mixture of centered Gaussian coordinates with variances \(1-\varepsilon\) and \(1+\varepsilon\), for every sufficiently small fixed ε. The contact-removed gap cumulative law and the mean-one force cumulative law satisfy \(\displaystyle G_J(u)=u^{1-\gamma+o(1)},\qquad F_J(s)=s^{1+\theta+o(1)},\) as \(u\downarrow0\) and \(s\downarrow0\), with \(\gamma=(2+\theta)^{-1}\), \(0.4126930\lt \gamma\lt 0.4126934\), and \(0.4231063\lt \theta\lt 0.4231088\). A finite numerical certificate for these exponent intervals, together with its mathematical error bounds, is included.

tex.abstract:
We prove a sharp feasibility threshold and limiting gap and force laws for
the spherical perceptron with margin $-1$ and quadratic penalty. The limits
are taken successively in system size, inverse temperature, and density
approaching the threshold from above. They agree for Gaussian coordinates
and for the equal mixture of centered Gaussian coordinates with variances
$1-\eps$ and $1+\eps$, for every sufficiently small fixed $\eps$.
The contact-removed gap cumulative law and the mean-one force cumulative
law satisfy
\[
 G_J(u)=u^{1-\gamma+o(1)},\qquad F_J(s)=s^{1+\theta+o(1)},
\]
as $u\downarrow0$ and $s\downarrow0$, with $\gamma=(2+\theta)^{-1}$,
$0.4126930<\gamma<0.4126934$, and
$0.4231063<\theta<0.4231088$.
A finite numerical certificate for these exponent intervals, together with
its mathematical error bounds, is included.
sections: The problem and the proof architecture
Hierarchical Gaussian functionals and spherical entropy
Concavity and stability of the row functional
Ground energy and the sharp satisfiability threshold
A convex critical problem and the limiting microscopic laws
Uniform control of the critical layer
Selection of the critical similarity profile

statements.title: Microscopic criticality and mixture universality
statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There exist $\alpha_c\in(0,\infty)$ and $\eps_0\in(0,1)$ with the following properties for every fixed $\eps\in[0,\eps_0)$ and coordinate law $\nu_\eps$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item The SAT probability tends to one at every fixed $\alpha<\alpha_c$ and to zero at every fixed $\alpha>\alpha_c$.
\item All the ordered limits in \eqref{eq:intro-GJ}--\eqref{eq:intro-FJ} exist for their indicated positive arguments. They are independent of $\eps$.
\item $F_J$ is the cumulative distribution function on $(0,\infty)$ of a probability law of mean one. It has no atom at zero. There are exponents $\gamma,\theta$ such that
\[
 G_J(u)=u^{1-\gamma+o(1)},\qquad
 F_J(s)=s^{1+\theta+o(1)},
\]
as the corresponding argument decreases to zero, and
\[
 \gamma=\frac1{2+\theta},\qquad
 0.4126930<\gamma<0.4126934,\qquad
 0.4231063<\theta<0.4231088.
\]
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: The problem and the proof architecture

statements.title: Explicit spherical entropy
statements.label: prop:hier-spherical-limit
statements.section_title: Hierarchical Gaussian functionals and spherical entropy

statements.title: Concavity and supergradients
statements.label: prop:hier-spin-concavity
statements.text:
The functional $\mathcal S$ is concave on bounded nonnegative nondecreasing
profiles.  At a finite-step profile its differential is
\begin{equation}
 \dd\mathcal S(p)=-\frac12\sum_{j=0}^k w_jr_j\,\dd p_j,
 \quad
 r_j=\frac{p_0}{\lambda_0^2}
       +\sum_{i=1}^j\frac{p_i-p_{i-1}}{\lambda_i\lambda_{i-1}},
 \quad r_k=1-\frac1b.
 
\end{equation}
For every general bounded profile $p$ there exists a nonnegative
nondecreasing profile $r$, with $r_*<1$, such that
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal S(\widetilde p)
 \le\mathcal S(p)-\frac12\int_0^1r(s)(\widetilde p-p)(s)\,\dd s
 
\end{equation}
for every bounded nonnegative nondecreasing $\widetilde p$.
The profile $r$ can be chosen so that $p=\mathcal I(r)$ almost everywhere.
If $p\le B$, $r$ may be chosen with
$r_*\le1-[2(B+1)]^{-1}$.
statements.section_title: Hierarchical Gaussian functionals and spherical entropy

statements.title: Entropy conjugacy
statements.label: prop:hier-entropy-conjugacy
statements.section_title: Hierarchical Gaussian functionals and spherical entropy

statements.title: Concavity
statements.label: prop:conc-concavity
statements.text:
For every concave terminal in the class
\eqref{eq:conc-terminal-class}, $q\mapsto\Phi_u(q;Q)$ is concave on
smooth strictly increasing profiles.  For every concave globally Lipschitz
terminal, which need not be smooth or bounded above, and for
the quadratic hinge $u=-\beta V$, it is concave on the full convex set
of nonnegative nondecreasing profiles bounded by $Q$.
statements.section_title: Concavity and stability of the row functional

statements.title: Uniform strictness and stability
statements.label: prop:conc-stability
statements.section_title: Concavity and stability of the row functional

statements.title: The uncapped row functional
statements.label: cor:conc-hinge-stability
statements.text:
Fix $\beta>0$ and $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\R)$.  There are constants
$c_\beta>0$ and $d_0=d_0(\beta,\psi)>0$ such that, for
$u_d=-\beta V+d\psi$, $|d|\le d_0$, $Q\in[1/2,2]$, and all
$q,r\in\mathcal Q_Q$,
\begin{equation}
 \Phi_{u_d}((1-t)q+tr;Q)
 \ge(1-t)\Phi_{u_d}(q;Q)+t\Phi_{u_d}(r;Q)
       +\frac{c_\beta}{4}t(1-t)\|r-q\|_2^2,
 \qquad 0\le t\le1.
 
\end{equation}
When $d=0$, the last coefficient can be replaced by $c_\beta/2$.
The derivative formula \eqref{eq:src1}, including its one-sided endpoint
interpretation, holds with the terminal $u_d$ and fixed diagonal $Q$.
Its nonnegative nondecreasing derivative profile satisfies
$\sup_{q,Q,d}\|D^{u_d}_q\|_\infty\le C_{\beta,\psi}$ in these ranges
and depends continuously on $q$ in $L^1$ at fixed $Q,d$.
The functional values and derivative profiles are limits of those for
$u_{L,\delta}+d\psi$, uniformly over $q,Q,d$, with derivative convergence
in $L^1(\dd s)$.  Here $\delta\downarrow0$ at each fixed cap before
$L\to\infty$.
statements.section_title: Concavity and stability of the row functional

statements.title: Convex perturbations of the loss
statements.label: cor:conc-convex-loss
statements.text:
Let
\[
 W(z)=cV(z)+\chi(z),\qquad c>0,\qquad
 \chi\in C_c^\infty((-\infty,-1)),
\]
and suppose that $W\geq0$, $W'\leq0$, and $W''\geq0$ distributionally.
For every fixed $\beta>0$, the terminal $u=-\beta W$ has a concave row
functional on all profiles with fixed diagonal $Q\in[1/2,2]$.
The derivative formula \eqref{eq:src1}, continuity of $D_q$ in $L^1$, and
the uniform tangent-cap limits hold for this terminal.  In particular,
the Gaussian interpolation upper bound derived for smooth concave caps
applies to $-\beta W$ after removal of the cap.
statements.section_title: Concavity and stability of the row functional

statements.title: Entropy form of the pressure
statements.label: prop:press-formula
statements.text:
For Gaussian rows, $u=-\beta V$, and $\alpha>0$,
\begin{equation}
 P(u)=\min_{q:\,q_*<1}\{\alpha\Phi_u(q)+E(q)\},
 \qquad q_*:=\esssup q.
\end{equation}
Every minimizer of $\mathcal P_u$ has $q_*<1$ and satisfies the spin inverse
relations of Section~\ref{sec:hierarchy} with $p=p_q$.

statements.title: Upper bound for convex loss perturbations
statements.label: cor:press-convex-loss-upper
statements.text:
Let $\psi\in C_c^\infty(( -\infty,0))$. There is $w_0>0$, independent
of $\beta$, such that for both signs of $w$ with $|w|<w_0$ the loss
$L_w(z)=V(z)+w\psi(1+z)$ is nonnegative, convex, and nonincreasing. For every
fixed $\beta>0$ and every fixed profile $q$ with $q_*<1$,
\begin{equation}
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}P_N(-\beta L_w)
 \le\alpha\Phi_{-\beta L_w}(q)+E(q).
\end{equation}
More generally this upper bound holds for any nonpositive, concave,
nondecreasing terminal of at most quadratic growth which agrees with a
negative quadratic hinge outside a compact set.

statements.title: Pressure and upper supports
statements.label: thm:univ-pressure
statements.text:
There is $\eps_0(B_0)>0$, independent of $\beta>0$, with the following
property.  If $0<\alpha\le B_0$ and $0\le\eps<\eps_0(B_0)$, then
\[
 \lim_{N\to\infty}P_{N,\eps}(u)=P(u).
\]
If $q$ is any Gaussian minimizer in \eqref{eq:src9} and
$\psi\in C_c^\infty(\R)$, then, for all sufficiently small $|d|$,
\[
 \limsup_{N\to\infty}P_{N,\eps}(u+d\psi)
 \le \alpha\Phi_{u+d\psi}(q;1)+E(q).
\]
The allowed size of $d$ can depend on $\beta,\psi$ and $B_0$.

statements.title: Empirical row law and force normalization
statements.label: prop:univ-observables
statements.text:
For either the Gaussian law or any mixture in
Theorem~\ref{thm:univ-pressure}, at fixed $\beta>0$ and
$0<\alpha\le B_0$, $L_N$ converges weakly in probability to
$\mu_{\beta,\alpha}$.  This measure is atomless, assigns positive mass
to $(-\infty,-1)$, and has finite moments of its negative part.
The gap and normalized-force observables in the problem have inner
$N\to\infty$ limits at every fixed argument, and those limits agree
for all these entry laws.

statements.title: Subextensive parent energy implies satisfiability
statements.label: thresh:deletion
statements.text:
Let $0<\alpha<\alpha'\leq B_0$, and let the entries have any one of the
laws $\nu_\eps$, $0\leq\eps\leq1/2$.  If
\[
 \frac1N\E\min H_{\lfloor\alpha'N\rfloor\times N}\longrightarrow0,
\]
then a matrix with $\lfloor\alpha N\rfloor$ rows is satisfiable with
probability tending to one.
statements.section_title: Ground energy and the sharp satisfiability threshold

statements.title: Sharp common satisfiability threshold
statements.label: thresh:sharp
statements.text:
For Gaussian entries and, with the choice of $B_0$ above, for every
fixed $0\leq\eps<\eps_0(B_0)$, the number $\alpha_J$ in
\eqref{thresh:eq:threshold-definition} satisfies
$1\leq\alpha_J<\infty$ and
\[
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\Prob(\mathrm{SAT})=
 \begin{cases}
 1,&0<\alpha<\alpha_J,\\
 0,&\alpha>\alpha_J.
 \end{cases}
\]
In particular the threshold itself agrees for all these laws.
No assertion at $\alpha=\alpha_J$ is needed here.
statements.section_title: Ground energy and the sharp satisfiability threshold

statements.title: Transfer of the remaining ordered limits
statements.label: thresh:ordered-limits
statements.text:
Fix $0\leq\eps<\eps_0(B_0)$.  On a full interval above the common
threshold, the thermodynamic gap and normalized-force observables at
every fixed positive temperature and fixed argument agree with their
Gaussian counterparts.  Consequently each further ordered limit in
the problem exists for the mixture law if and only if it exists for
the Gaussian law, and their values agree whenever it exists.
statements.section_title: Ground energy and the sharp satisfiability threshold

statements.title: Zero-temperature variational principle
statements.label: zero:variational
statements.text:
For every subsequential limit in Lemma~\ref{zero:compactness}, let \(g\)
be the solution of
\[
 g_t=-\tfrac12\bigl(g_{zz}+\gamma(t)g_z^2\bigr),
 \qquad g(1,z)=-\frac{V(z)}{1+\Delta}.
\]
It satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal E_\alpha(\gamma,\Delta)
 :=\alpha g(0,0)+\frac12\int_0^1\frac{\dd t}{\bar\chi(t)}
 =-e,
 
\end{equation}
and minimizes this functional over nonnegative nondecreasing
integrable \(\gamma\) and \(\Delta>0\).
Here solutions have quadratic growth, nonnegative first derivative,
and second derivative in \([-1,0]\); an integrable time coefficient
is interpreted by approximation in \(L^1\).

statements.title: Subsequential endpoint law
statements.label: zero:endpoint
statements.text:
Let \(Z_0=0\) and
\(\dd Z_t=\gamma(t)g_z(t,Z_t)\,\dd t+\dd B_t\), and put \(H=1+Z_1\).
Along the subsequence defining \((\gamma,\Delta)\), the tilted row gap
converges in distribution to
\begin{equation}
 h^*=\begin{cases}
 H,&H\ge0,\\[2pt]
 H/(1+\Delta),&H<0.
 \end{cases}
 
\end{equation}
Every fixed moment of the negative part converges.  Both \(H\) and
\(h^*\) are atomless and assign positive probability to every nonempty
open interval.  This statement is subsequential; uniqueness is addressed
separately below and in Section~\ref{sec:critical}.

statements.title: Identification of negative gaps
statements.label: zero:negative-law
statements.text:
For every subsequential endpoint law in Proposition~\ref{zero:endpoint},
the restriction of the law of $h^*$ to $(-\infty,0)$ is the same.  For
$\psi\in C_c^\infty((-\infty,0))$, uniformly over Gaussian ground
minimizers $y_N$,
\[
 \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^M\psi(1+A_i y_N)
       \longrightarrow\alpha\E\psi(h^*)
 \quad\text{in probability}.
\]
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \alpha\E(h^*)_-^2=2e.
\end{equation}

statements.title: Cutoffs after susceptibility normalization
statements.label: zero:normalized-force-cutoff
statements.text:
For every subsequential endpoint law, put
\(R=L(h^*)_-\) and \(p=\Prob(h^*<0)\).
There are constants \(c,C,u_0>0\), independent of the density, such
that throughout the fixed UNSAT interval and for \(0<u<u_0\),
\[
 c\le \E R\le C,\qquad
 \Prob(0<R\le u)\le\frac C{|\log u|}
 \qquad \alpha p\longrightarrow1
 \quad(\alpha\downarrow\alpha_J).
\]

statements.title: Positive-gap cutoffs
statements.label: zero:positive-cutoffs
statements.text:
Constants \(c,C,u_0>0\), independent of the density, exist such
that, for \(0<\delta<u<1\),
\(G_{N,\beta,\alpha}(\delta,u)\ge c(u-\delta)\).
For every fixed UNSAT density in the interval under consideration
and every \(0<u<u_0\),
\begin{equation}
 \limsup_{\beta\to\infty}\limsup_{N\to\infty}
 \E\left\langle\frac1M\sum_{i=1}^M
       \ind_{\{0<h_i\le u\}}\right\rangle
 \le\frac C{|\log u|}
\end{equation}
with the same constants \(C,u_0\) at every such density.
In particular every subsequential endpoint law in
\eqref{eq:src16} satisfies the direct bound
\(\Prob(0<h^*\le u)\le C/|\log u|\).
The same estimate bounds the ordered zero-temperature and density
limsups of \(G_{N,\beta,\alpha}(\delta,u)\), uniformly in
\(0<\delta<u\).
The upper bound requires no identification of positive gap tests at
exact ground minimizers.

statements.label: zero:threshold-characterization

statements.title: Joint martingale formulation
statements.label: crit:duality
statements.section_title: A convex critical problem and the limiting microscopic laws

statements.title: Uniqueness in the UNSAT phase
statements.label: crit:unsat-unique
statements.text:
At each fixed $\alpha>\alpha_c$ the minimizing physical susceptibility in
\eqref{eq:src15} is unique.  Thus the entire zero-temperature endpoint law
in \eqref{eq:src16}, including its restriction to positive gaps, is unique.
statements.section_title: A convex critical problem and the limiting microscopic laws

statements.title: Existence of a normalized critical pair
statements.label: crit:compactness
statements.text:
The functional $J_{\alpha_c,0}$ is nonnegative on the whole admissible
class, without a normalization constraint. Every sequence of normalized physical
pairs with $\alpha_n\downarrow\alpha_c$ has a subsequence such that
\[
 \chi_n\to\chi\text{ uniformly on every }[0,T],\ T<1,
 \qquad R_n\rightharpoonup R\text{ in }L^2(\mathcal F_1).
\]
Its limit is normalized, satisfies $s\in L^2(0,1)$ and $c\ge c_0$, and
attains $J_{\alpha_c,0}(R,s)=0$.
statements.section_title: A convex critical problem and the limiting microscopic laws

statements.title: Uniqueness of the normalized critical limit
statements.label: crit:unique-critical
statements.text:
Any two subsequential limits supplied by
Proposition~\ref{crit:compactness} coincide on the common Wiener space.
In particular the normalized susceptibility and the law of $(H_1,R)$
are independent of the density sequence.
statements.section_title: A convex critical problem and the limiting microscopic laws

statements.title: No critical endpoint susceptibility
statements.label: crit:no-endpoint
statements.text:
The critical susceptibility satisfies $\Delta=0$.  Its increase measure
$\nu$ accumulates at $1$, and with $k=-\chi f_{hh}$ one has, at every
interior support point,
\begin{equation}
 \alpha_c\E k(t,H_t)=1+\alpha_c c\chi(t),
 \qquad \alpha_c\E k(t,H_t)^2\le1.
\end{equation}
The second inequality is an equality at non-isolated interior support
points.
statements.section_title: A convex critical problem and the limiting microscopic laws

statements.title: Strong critical convergence
statements.label: crit:strong
statements.text:
As $\alpha_n\downarrow\alpha_c$, the normalized physical variables
satisfy
\[
 R_n\to R\text{ in }L^2,\qquad
 \gamma_n\to\gamma\text{ in }L^1(0,1),\qquad
 H_{n,1}\to H_1\text{ in }L^2.
\]
The physical endpoint gap is
$h_n^*=H_{n,1}+\chi_n(1)R_n$, its residual is
$(h_n^*)_-=\lambda_nR_n$, and $h_n^*\to H_1\ge0$ in $L^2$.
statements.section_title: A convex critical problem and the limiting microscopic laws

statements.title: The ordered limiting observables
statements.label: crit:ordered-laws
statements.text:
The Gaussian observables in the problem have all their stated ordered
limits, at every $u>0$ and $s>0$, and are given by
\begin{equation}
 G_J(u)=\Prob(0<H_1\le u),\qquad
 F_J(s)=\Prob\left(\frac{R}{\alpha_c c}\le s\,\middle|\,R>0\right).
\end{equation}
The force law has mean one and no atom at zero.  These limiting laws
are also the laws for all Gaussian scale mixtures in the
fixed-temperature comparison range.
More explicitly, for every $0<\delta<u$ and $s>0$, the individual
limits at each level of
\begin{gather*}
 \lim_{\alpha\downarrow\alpha_c}\lim_{\beta\to\infty}
       \lim_{N\to\infty}G_{N,\beta,\alpha}(\delta,u)
                  =\Prob(\delta<H_1\le u),\\
 \lim_{\alpha\downarrow\alpha_c}\lim_{\beta\to\infty}
       \lim_{N\to\infty}F_{N,\beta,\alpha}(s)
                  =F_J(s)
\end{gather*}
exist; the additional limit $\delta\downarrow0$ in the first line
gives $G_J(u)$.
statements.section_title: A convex critical problem and the limiting microscopic laws

statements.title: Bounded scale ratio
statements.label: prop:scale-bounded-D
statements.text:
There is a constant $C$ such that $1\le D\le C$ near the endpoint.
Consequently $w\asymp\tau/\chi^2$ and
$\int_t^1s\asymp\tau/\chi$.

statements.title: Rigidity of the logarithmic-time limit
statements.label: prop:contr-rigidity
statements.text:
Let $(M_i,P_i,A)$ be a density input as defined in
Subsection~\ref{subsec:contr-comparisons}, and suppose that the two
identities \eqref{eq:contr-homogeneous} hold at every entire time.
Then $A\equiv a_*$.  In particular every entire limit of the critical
rescaled profiles has this coefficient, and
\[
 \lim_{\tau\downarrow0}\frac{\tau\gamma(\tau)}{\chi(\tau)}=a_*,
 \qquad
 \lim_{\tau\downarrow0}\frac{\log\chi(\tau)}{\log\tau}=a_*.
\]
The root of $\lambda(a)=a$ in the certified interval is unique.

title: Midpoint convexity from bounded tree potentials and path costs
abstract: Four real Banach spaces defined by bounded tree potentials satisfy the averaged asymptotic midpoint bound \(\widehat\delta(t)\ge\sqrt{1+t^2/4}-1\) for \(0\lt t\lt 1\), while none admits an asymptotically uniformly convex (AUC) renorming. On finite-height trees, the globally constrained norm equals the least additive cost of a Hilbert vector and root paths. The quadratic path and segment-start outer Hilbert sums are reflexive and asymptotically midpoint uniformly convex, and admit no equivalent AUC norm.

tex.abstract:
Four real Banach spaces defined by bounded tree potentials satisfy the
averaged asymptotic midpoint bound $\widehat\delta(t)\ge\sqrt{1+t^2/4}-1$
for $0<t<1$, while none admits an asymptotically uniformly convex
(AUC) renorming. On finite-height trees, the globally constrained norm
equals the least additive cost of a Hilbert vector and root paths.
The quadratic path and segment-start outer Hilbert sums are reflexive
and asymptotically midpoint uniformly convex, and admit no equivalent
AUC norm.
sections: Four potential norms, one pair of inward tests
A free root and a planar perturbation
Charging segments at their starting nodes

statements.label: thm:four
statements.text:
Each of the four completed spaces $X_K$ is a separable infinite-dimensional
real Banach space. For $K\in\{K_{\rm s},K_{\rm p},K_{\rm a},K_{\rm g}\}$
and $0<t<1$,
\begin{equation}
 \widehat\delta_{X_K}(t)\ge\sqrt{1+t^2/4}-1.
\end{equation}
None of these spaces admits an equivalent AUC norm.
statements.section_title: Four potential norms, one pair of inward tests

statements.label: thm:free-root-modulus
statements.text:
The real Banach space $X_{\mathrm e}$ defined by \eqref{fr:tests} and
\eqref{fr:norm} satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \widehat\delta_{\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm e}}(t)
 \ge\frac{\sqrt{1+t^2/576}-1}{4}\qquad(0<t<1).
 
\end{equation}
It admits no equivalent AUC norm.  More precisely, if
$\alpha\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm e}\le N\le\beta\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm e}$,
where $0<\alpha\le\beta<\infty$, then
$\overline\delta_N(\alpha/(4\beta))=0$.
statements.section_title: A free root and a planar perturbation

statements.title: Exact duality for the linear cost
statements.label: prop:linear-duality
statements.text:
The space $X_n=(H_n,L_n)$ is complete and
\[
 \frac{\|x\|_2}{\sqrt{n+1}}\le L_n(x)\le\|x\|_2,
 \qquad
 L_n(x)=\sup_{p_n(f)\le1}\langle f,x\rangle.
\]
Every coordinate satisfies $|x_s|\le L_n(x)$.
Its continuous dual is $H_n$, under the Hilbert pairing, with norm
$p_n$.  In particular $L_n$ is exactly the global test norm on $T_n$.

statements.title: Duality and branching in the outer sum
statements.label: prop:linear-geometry
statements.text:
The space $X$ is reflexive, has separable dual, and its dual is the
Hilbert sum of the spaces $(H_n,p_n)$, with pairing
\[
 f(x)=\sum_n\langle f_n,x_n\rangle,
 \qquad \|f\|_*^2=\sum_np_n(f_n)^2.
\]
Every coordinate vector $e_{n,s}$ and every root path $b_{n,s}$ has norm
one.  For fixed $n$ and $|s|<n$, the children
$(e_{n,s^\frown j})_{j\ge1}$ are weakly null.
If $\alpha\|\cdot\|\le N\le\beta\|\cdot\|$, with
$0<\alpha\le\beta$, then $\overline\delta_N(t)=0$ for every
$0<t\le\alpha/\beta$.  In particular no equivalent norm on $X$
is asymptotically uniformly convex.

statements.title: Clipping estimate on a head and its complement
statements.label: thm:linear-head-tail-clipping

statements.title: Clipping along a weakly null sequence
statements.label: thm:linear-weak-sequence
statements.text:
Let $x\in X$ and let $(y_j)$ be a bounded weakly null sequence in $X$.
If $L=\liminf_j\|y_j\|$, then
\[
 \liminf_j\max\{\|x+y_j\|,\|x-y_j\|\}
 \ge\sqrt{\|x\|^2+L^2/16}.
\]

statements.title: A tail estimate from positive mass
statements.label: thm:linear-positive-tail

statements.title: The bottom-up tail estimate
statements.label: thm:linear-bottom-up-tail
statements.text:
Suppose \(0\le\varepsilon\le1\), \(P_Ax=x\), \(P_Ay=0\),
\(L_n(x\pm y)\le1\), and \(L_n(x)\ge1-\varepsilon\). Then
\begin{equation}
 L_n(y)\le3\sqrt{2\varepsilon}+8\varepsilon.
\end{equation}
Moreover the following uniform implication holds on \(X\): for any
sequence of finite head projections \(P_j\) and vectors satisfying
\[
 P_jx_j=x_j,\quad P_jy_j=0,\quad
 \|x_j\pm y_j\|\le1,\quad\|x_j\|\longrightarrow1,
\]
one has \(\|y_j\|\longrightarrow0\).

statements.title: A squared estimate by quota removal
statements.label: thm:linear-trimming-242
statements.text:
For a finite head projection \(P\) on \(X\),
\begin{equation}
 \|y\|^2\le242\bigl(\|x+y\|^2+\|x-y\|^2-2\|x\|^2\bigr)
 \qquad(Px=x,\ Py=0).
\end{equation}
The same assertion, with \(L_n\) in place of \(\|\cdot\|\), holds in
each component.

statements.title: A fresh-layer squared estimate
statements.label: thm:linear-fresh-layer-400
statements.text:
Let \(A\subseteq A'\) be finite ancestor-closed subsets of the disjoint
union of the \(T_n\), and put \(E=A'\setminus A\). If
\(P_Ax=x\) and \(P_{A'}y=y\), then
\begin{equation}
 \|P_Ey\|^2\le400\left(
       \frac{\|x+y\|^2+\|x-y\|^2}{2}-\|x\|^2\right).
\end{equation}
There is no condition on \(P_Ay\).

statements.title: Predictable-layer energy
statements.label: thm:linear-predictable-energy
statements.text:
Let \(x_0,\ldots,x_m\) be an \(X\)-valued dyadic martingale.  Let \(P_0\)
be a fixed finite initial set, and, for \(1\le i\le m\), let \(P_i\)
be a finite initial set measurable with respect to \(\mathcal F_{i-1}\).
Suppose, on every history, that
\[
 P_{i-1}\subseteq P_i\quad(1\le i\le m),\qquad
 \operatorname{supp}x_i\subseteq P_i\quad(0\le i\le m),\qquad \|x_m\|\le C.
\]
Then, for \(\Delta_i=P_i\setminus P_{i-1}\),
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{i=1}^m\mathbb E\|R_{\Delta_i}x_i\|^2\le495C^2.
\end{equation}

statements.title: Variation energy
statements.label: thm:linear-variation-energy

statements.title: Adaptive-window energy
statements.label: thm:linear-sign-energy
statements.text:
There is an absolute constant \(K\) with the following property.
Let \(x_t=\mathbb E_t x_m\), \(0\le t\le m\), be an \(X\)-valued dyadic
martingale.  For \(0\le t<m\), let \(A_t\subseteq D_t\) be finite
initial sets measurable with respect to \(\mathcal F_t\), and suppose
\(D_t\subseteq A_{t+1}\) whenever \(t+1<m\).  Put
\(U_t=D_t\setminus A_t\).  Then
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{t=0}^{m-1}\mathbb E\|R_{U_t}x_{t+1}\|^2
 \le K\left(\mathbb E\|x_m\|^2+
                  \sum_{t=0}^{m-1}\mathbb E\|R_{U_t}x_t\|^2\right).
\end{equation}
No support condition on \(x_t\) is imposed.

statements.title: Energy with leakage
statements.label: thm:linear-leakage-energy
statements.text:
Let \(W_i=\mathbb E_iW_m\), \(0\le i\le m\), be an \(X\)-valued dyadic
martingale.  Let \(A_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq A_m\) be fixed finite
initial sets and put \(\Delta_i=A_i\setminus A_{i-1}\).  Then
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{i=1}^m\mathbb E\|R_{\Delta_i}W_i\|^2
 \le1024\left(\mathbb E\|W_m\|^2+
              \sum_{i=1}^m\mathbb E\|R_{\Delta_i}W_{i-1}\|^2\right).
\end{equation}

statements.label: qp:construction
qp:no-auc
statements.text:
No equivalent norm on $X_{\mathrm q}$ is asymptotically uniformly
convex.  More precisely, if
$a\|z\|_{\mathrm q}\le N(z)\le b\|z\|_{\mathrm q}$, with
$0<a\le b<\infty$, then
$\overline\delta_N(t_0)=0$ at $t_0=a/(\sqrt2 b)$.

statements.label: thm:quadratic-tail
statements.text:
Let $A$ be a finite ancestral head in $X_{\mathrm q}$ and let
$P_Ax=x$.  For every $y\in X_{\mathrm q}$ and $R\ge0$,
\begin{equation}
 \|x+y\|_{\mathrm q},\ \|x-y\|_{\mathrm q}\le R
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \|Q_Ay\|_{\mathrm q}\le8\sqrt{R^2-\|x\|_{\mathrm q}^2}.
\end{equation}
The displacement $y$ need not vanish on the head.

statements.label: qp:lens-eight
statements.text:
If $x\in X_{\mathrm q}$ and an infinite sequence $(y_j)$ satisfies
$\|x\pm y_j\|_{\mathrm q}\le R$ and
$\|y_i-y_j\|_{\mathrm q}\ge\varepsilon>0$ for $i\ne j$, then
\[
 \|x\|_{\mathrm q}^2+\frac{\varepsilon^2}{256}\le R^2.
\]

statements.label: qp:symmetric-twelve
qp:lens-twelve
statements.text:
If $\|x\pm y_j\|_{\mathrm q}\le r$ and
$\|y_i-y_j\|_{\mathrm q}\ge2d>0$ for $i\ne j$ in an infinite
sequence, then
\[
 \|x\|_{\mathrm q}^2+d^2/144\le r^2.
\]

statements.label: qp:tail-seven
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:quadratic-tail},
\[
 \|Q_Ay\|_{\mathrm q}\le7\sqrt{R^2-\|x\|_{\mathrm q}^2}.
\]

statements.label: qp:lens-seven
statements.text:
For $0<c\le1$ put $\delta=c^2/2000$.  If
$\|x\pm y_j\|_{\mathrm q}\le1$ and
$\|y_i-y_j\|_{\mathrm q}\ge2c$ for all distinct indices of an
infinite sequence, then $\|x\|_{\mathrm q}\le1-\delta$.

statements.label: qp:tail-nine
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:quadratic-tail},
\[
 \|Q_Ay\|_{\mathrm q}\le9\sqrt{R^2-\|x\|_{\mathrm q}^2}.
\]

statements.label: qp:lens-nine
statements.text:
For every $\rho>0$, choose $0<\gamma<1/2$ such that
\[
 9\sqrt{(1+\gamma)^2-(1-2\gamma)^2}<\rho/3.
\]
If $\|x\|_{\mathrm q}\ge1-\gamma$, its symmetric lens
$\{y:\|x\pm y\|_{\mathrm q}\le1\}$ has no infinite
$\rho$-separated subset.

statements.label: qp:relative-seventytwo
statements.text:
For every nonzero $x\in X_{\mathrm q}$ and $0<\delta\le1$ there
is a finite ancestral head $A$, depending only on $x,\delta$, such
that for every $u\in X_{\mathrm q}$,
\[
 \|x+u\|_{\mathrm q},\ \|x-u\|_{\mathrm q}
       \le(1+\delta)\|x\|_{\mathrm q}
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \|Q_Au\|_{\mathrm q}\le72\sqrt\delta\,\|x\|_{\mathrm q}.
\]

statements.title: Finite centers in the Hilbert sum
statements.label: qp:rec:finite-center
statements.text:
Let \(x\in X_{\mathrm q}\) be a unit vector with finite coordinate
support.  For each \(n\) with \(x_n\ne0\), choose a finite nonempty
ancestor-closed \(A_n\subset T_n\) containing its support, and set
\[
 Y_x=\{y\in X_{\mathrm q}:P_{A_n}y_n=0
                           \text{ whenever }x_n\ne0\}.
\]
Then \(Y_x\) is a closed finite-codimensional subspace.  If
\(0<e\le1/8\), \(y\in Y_x\), and
\(\|x+y\|_{\mathrm q},\|x-y\|_{\mathrm q}\le1+e\), then
\begin{equation}
 \|y\|_{\mathrm q}^2\le\frac{519}{2}e^{1/3},
 \qquad \|y\|_{\mathrm q}\le17e^{1/6}.
\end{equation}

statements.title: Completed centers
statements.label: qp:rec:all-centers
statements.text:
For every \(x\in X_{\mathrm q}\) with \(\|x\|_{\mathrm q}=1\) and
\(0<e\le1/16\), there is a closed finite-codimensional subspace
\(Y\subset X_{\mathrm q}\) such that
\begin{equation}
 y\in Y,\quad
 \|x+y\|_{\mathrm q},\|x-y\|_{\mathrm q}\le1+e
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \|y\|_{\mathrm q}\le17(2e)^{1/6}.
\end{equation}
In particular, for every \(t>0\) there is an \(e_t>0\), independent
of the unit center \(x\), for which some closed finite-codimensional
\(Y\) satisfies
\[
 \inf_{u\in S_Y}
 \max\{\|x+tu\|_{\mathrm q},\|x-tu\|_{\mathrm q}\}\ge1+e_t.
\]
Here \(S_Y=\{u\in Y:\|u\|_{\mathrm q}=1\}\).  Thus the maximum
asymptotic midpoint modulus is positive at every positive radius.

statements.label: sm:s:space
statements.text:
On $\ell_2(\mathcal T_n)$ the formula
\[
 \|x\|_{S,n}=\inf\{M_n(m(a)):Pa=x\}
\]
defines a complete reflexive norm, with
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\|x\|_2}{n+1}\le\|x\|_{S,n}
 \le\sqrt{n+1}\,\|x\|_2.
\end{equation}
Consequently
\[
 X_S=\Bigl(\bigoplus_{n\ge1}(\ell_2(\mathcal T_n),\|\cdot\|_{S,n})
       \Bigr)_{\ell_2}
\]
is a reflexive Banach space. Write $\|\cdot\|_S$ for its norm. Equivalently,
$\|x\|_S$ is the infimum of $M(m(a))$ over all forest representations of
$x$. Finite-support vectors are dense.
statements.section_title: Charging segments at their starting nodes

statements.label: thm:segment-start-tail
statements.text:
Let $C$ be a finite ancestral subset of $\mathcal T$. If $p\in X_S$ is
supported in $C$ and $y\in X_S$ satisfies $y|_C=0$, then
\begin{equation}
 \max\{\|p+y\|_S,\|p-y\|_S\}^2
 \ge\|p\|_S^2+\frac{\|y\|_S^2}{64}.
\end{equation}
The conclusion includes $C=\varnothing$, $p=0$ and $y=0$.
statements.section_title: Charging segments at their starting nodes

statements.label: sm:s:midpoint-consequence
statements.text:
For every $x\in X_S$ with $\|x\|_S=1$, every $t>0$ and every $\varepsilon>0$
there is a closed finite-codimensional subspace $F\subset X_S$ such that
\[
 \inf_{\substack{y\in F\\\|y\|_S=1}}
 \max\{\|x+ty\|_S,\|x-ty\|_S\}
 \ge\sqrt{1+t^2/64}-\varepsilon.
\]
In particular, define the maximum form of the asymptotic midpoint modulus
by
\[
 \delta^{\max}_{X_S}(t)=
 \inf_{\|x\|_S=1}\sup_{\substack{F\subset X_S\text{ closed}\\\dim(X_S/F)<\infty}}
 \inf_{\substack{y\in F\\\|y\|_S\ge1}}
 \bigl(\max_{\pm}\|x\pm ty\|_S-1\bigr).
\]
Then $\delta^{\max}_{X_S}(t)\ge\sqrt{1+t^2/64}-1$.
statements.section_title: Charging segments at their starting nodes

statements.label: sm:i:reflexivity
sm:i:auc-obstruction
statements.text:
The real reflexive space $X_{\mathrm I}$ admits no equivalent
asymptotically uniformly convex norm.

statements.label: sm:i:tail-estimate
statements.text:
Let $E\subset\mathcal T$ be finite and prefix closed.  If
$x,y\in X_{\mathrm I}$ satisfy
\[
 P_E x=x,\qquad \|x+y\|_{\mathrm I}\leq1,
 \qquad \|x-y\|_{\mathrm I}\leq1,
\]
then
\begin{equation}
 \|Q_Ey\|_{\mathrm I}
 \leq (\sqrt2+\sqrt6)\sqrt{1-\|x\|_{\mathrm I}}.
 
\end{equation}
In particular, if $Q_Ey=y$, the same bound holds for $\|y\|_{\mathrm I}$.

statements.label: sm:i:separated-midpoints
statements.text:
Let $0<c\leq1$ and let $x,u_j\in X_{\mathrm I}$, $j\in\mathbb N$,
satisfy
\[
 \|x+u_j\|_{\mathrm I},\ \|x-u_j\|_{\mathrm I}\leq1,
 \qquad \|u_j-u_k\|_{\mathrm I}\geq2c\quad(j\ne k).
\]
Then, with $K=\sqrt2+\sqrt6$,
\begin{equation}
 \|x\|_{\mathrm I}\leq1-(c/K)^2<1.
 
\end{equation}

title: Midpoint convexity from two recursive potentials
abstract: We study tree norms computed by two least nonnegative fields whose difference is the vector. For Euclidean child aggregation, two root-sum spaces have an averaged asymptotic midpoint modulus of at least \(t^3/128\) for \(0\lt t\lt 1\), including a reflexive joining-root space. A reflexive construction with a fixed zero root also satisfies a homogeneous cubic estimate. These spaces admit no equivalent asymptotically uniformly convex norm. We also obtain sixth-power and cubic estimates when the aggregation exponent depends on the height of a finite component.

tex.abstract:
We study tree norms computed by two least nonnegative fields whose difference
is the vector. For Euclidean child aggregation, two root-sum spaces have an
averaged asymptotic midpoint modulus of at least $t^3/128$ for $0<t<1$,
including a reflexive joining-root space. A reflexive construction with a
fixed zero root also satisfies a homogeneous cubic estimate. These spaces
admit no equivalent asymptotically uniformly convex norm. We also obtain
sixth-power and cubic estimates when the aggregation exponent depends on
the height of a finite component.
sections: The fields, the roots, and the completed spaces
From root defect to boundary energy
Stopping the propagation of normalized defects
Logarithmic propagation on the joined tree
Changing the child exponent with the height

statements.label: rec:main
statements.section_title: The fields, the roots, and the completed spaces

statements.label: rec:completion
statements.text:
These formulas define infinite-dimensional Banach spaces after completion.
Coordinate evaluations and the fields extend continuously. If $H$ is a
finite set containing the root and all predecessors of its nodes, then
coordinate restriction $\Pi_H$ is a contractive projection. Its kernel
$F_H$ has finite codimension, and finitely supported elements of $F_H$
are dense in $F_H$. Both $X_0$ and $X_J$ are reflexive.
statements.section_title: The fields, the roots, and the completed spaces

statements.label: stop:all-radii
statements.text: For every $t>0$, the averaged asymptotic modulus of $N_\Sigma$ is positive.
statements.section_title: Stopping the propagation of normalized defects

statements.title: Separated midpoint families
statements.label: log:lens-gap
statements.text:
For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $\eta(\varepsilon)\in(0,1)$ such
that, for $x,z_1,z_2,\ldots\in X_J$,
\[
 \left.
 \begin{gathered}
 N_J(x+z_j),N_J(x-z_j)\le1\quad(j\ge1),\\
 N_J(z_i-z_j)\ge\varepsilon\quad(i\ne j)
 \end{gathered}
 \right\}
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad N_J(x)\le1-\eta(\varepsilon).
\]
For $0<\varepsilon\le2$, one can take
$\eta(\varepsilon)=\min\{1/2,\gamma(2,\varepsilon/16)\}$.
statements.section_title: Logarithmic propagation on the joined tree

statements.label: var:space
statements.text:
The recursion \eqref{var:recursion} defines a norm equivalent to the
usual $\ell_{p_h}(T_h)$ norm.  In particular, $E_h$ is complete and
reflexive, with separable dual.  The space $X_{\mathrm v}$ is complete
and reflexive, its dual is separable, and vectors with finite total
coordinate support are dense in it.  Every finite coordinate
projection is bounded and has finite rank.
statements.section_title: Changing the child exponent with the height

statements.label: var:no-auc
statements.text:
The space $X_{\mathrm v}$ admits no equivalent asymptotically uniformly
convex norm.  More precisely, if
$a\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm v}\le N\le b\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm v}$ with
$0<a\le b$, then $\overline\delta_N(a/b)=0$.
statements.section_title: Changing the child exponent with the height

statements.label: var:sixth-stability
statements.text:
Let $x\in X_{\mathrm v}$ have finite total support.  In each component
where $x^{(h)}\ne0$, choose a finite ancestral set $A_h$ containing
that support.  Suppose $y\in X_{\mathrm v}$ vanishes on every such
$A_h$.  With
$S=\|x+y\|_{\mathrm v}^2+\|x-y\|_{\mathrm v}^2$, one has
\begin{equation}
 S-2\|x\|_{\mathrm v}^2
 \ge c_6 S^{-2}\|y\|_{\mathrm v}^6,
 \qquad c_6=2\exp(-(\mathrm e-1))4^{-6}.
\end{equation}
The right side is zero when $S=0$.
statements.section_title: Changing the child exponent with the height

statements.label: var:cubic-stability
statements.text:
Let $x\in X_{\mathrm v}$ have finite total support.  In every
component with $x^{(h)}\ne0$, choose a finite ancestral set $A_h$
containing its support, and let $y\in X_{\mathrm v}$ vanish on these
sets.  If $R>0$ and $\|x+y\|_{\mathrm v},\|x-y\|_{\mathrm v}\le R$,
then
\begin{equation}
 R^2\ge\|x\|_{\mathrm v}^2+
       \frac{c_3}{2\sqrt2\,R}\|y\|_{\mathrm v}^3,
 \qquad c_3=(6\mathrm e)^{-3}.
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Changing the child exponent with the height

statements.label: var:cubic-weak-null
statements.text:
Let $x\in X_{\mathrm v}$ and $0<\varepsilon\le1$.  Suppose
$(y_j)$ is weakly null,
$\|y_j\|_{\mathrm v}\ge\varepsilon$, and
$\|x+y_j\|_{\mathrm v},\|x-y_j\|_{\mathrm v}\le1$ for every $j$.
Then
\begin{equation}
 \|x\|_{\mathrm v}\le\theta(\varepsilon)
 :=\left(1-\frac{c_3}{2\sqrt2}\varepsilon^3\right)^{1/2}<1.
\end{equation}

title: Midpoint lenses in segment spaces
abstract: For a real segment-forest dual with unbounded finite component heights and the real infinite-height coordinate predual, we bound the tail of an arbitrary displacement in a symmetric lens by \(2\sqrt{R^2-\|x\|^2}\), where R is the lens radius and x is its finitely supported center. Both given norms are asymptotically midpoint uniformly convex, although neither space admits an equivalent asymptotically uniformly convex norm. The finite-height forest dual is reflexive.

tex.abstract:
For a real segment-forest dual with unbounded finite component heights
and the real infinite-height coordinate predual, we bound the tail of
an arbitrary displacement in a symmetric lens by
$2\sqrt{R^2-\|x\|^2}$, where $R$ is the lens radius and $x$ is
its finitely supported center. Both given norms are asymptotically
midpoint uniformly convex, although neither space admits an equivalent
asymptotically uniformly convex norm. The finite-height forest dual is
reflexive.
sections: The coordinate structure of the forest
Keeping the coefficient and slack budgets together
A radial deficit and separate endpoint laws
Further consequences of the joint budget
Stability from a nearly norming head test
Signs determined by the target tail
Qualitative midpoint arguments in infinite height

statements.label: thm:main-tail
statements.text:
Let $Y$ be either the finite-height forest dual $X=J^*$ or the
infinite-height coordinate predual $B_\infty$. For every finite
ancestral $H$, every $x,y\in Y$ with $x=P_Hx$, and every $R\ge0$
with $\|x+y\|,\|x-y\|\le R$,
\begin{equation}
 \|Q_Hy\|\le2\sqrt{R^2-\|x\|^2}.
\end{equation}

statements.title: The completed atomic ball
statements.label: cor:closed-atomic-ball
statements.text:
Let $\mathcal A$ be the set of all represented atoms in $X$. Then
\[
 B_X=\overline{\operatorname{conv}\mathcal A}^{\,\|\cdot\|}.
\]
Every segment functional $d_S$ has norm one.

statements.label: mol:cor:all-radius-averaged
foundation:height-variants
statements.text:
Let $I$ be countable and let $(h_i)_{i\in I}$ be nonnegative integers.
On the disjoint forest
\[
 \mathcal F_{\boldsymbol h}
   =\coprod_{i\in I}(\{i\}\times\mathbb N^{\le h_i})
\]
define $J_{\boldsymbol h}$ by the same disjoint-segment norm and set
$X_{\boldsymbol h}=J_{\boldsymbol h}^*$. If $J(h)$ denotes the
single-tree completion on $\mathbb N^{\le h}$, then
\[
 J_{\boldsymbol h}
   =\Big(\bigoplus_{i\in I}J(h_i)\Big)_{\ell_2},
 \qquad
 X_{\boldsymbol h}
   =\Big(\bigoplus_{i\in I}J(h_i)^*\Big)_{\ell_2}
\]
isometrically under coordinate restriction. Both spaces are reflexive,
and finite coordinate vectors are dense in each. The projection and
complementary-subtree formulas remain valid for this forest.

The convention of one tree with $n$ levels, including the root, for
every $n\ge1$ gives exactly
\[
 J_{\mathrm{levels}}=\mathbb R\oplus_2 J,
 \qquad X_{\mathrm{levels}}=\mathbb R\oplus_2 X.
\]
Its component estimate is
$\|u\|_2\le\rho(u)\le\sqrt n\,\|u\|_2$, and a root-to-leaf path
has $n-1$ extension steps.

statements.label: foundation:bounded-tree
statements.text:
Suppose an infinite-dimensional real Banach space $(Z,\|\cdot\|)$
contains, for every positive
integer $k$, vectors $(u_s)_{s\in\mathbb N^{\le k}}$ such that
\[
 0<m\le\|u_s\|\le M,
 \qquad \|u_{s^\frown j}-u_s\|\ge c>0,
\]
where $m,M,c$ are independent of $k$, and for each nonterminal $s$ the
sequence $(u_{s^\frown j}-u_s)_j$ is weakly null against the whole
continuous dual of $Z$. If
$0<a\le b<\infty$ and $a\|z\|\le N(z)\le b\|z\|$, then
\[
 \overline\delta_N\!\left(\frac{ac}{bM}\right)=0.
\]
In particular the same conclusion holds at $ac/(2bM)$, and $Z$ admits
no equivalent asymptotically uniformly convex norm.

statements.label: foundation:forest-obstruction
statements.text:
If the finite component heights $h_i$ in
Proposition~\ref{foundation:height-variants} are unbounded, then every
equivalent norm $N$ on $X_{\boldsymbol h}$ with
$a\|x\|\le N(x)\le b\|x\|$ satisfies
\[
 \overline\delta_N(a/b)=\overline\delta_N(a/(2b))=0.
\]

statements.title: The bounded-path obstruction
statements.label: binf:obstruction
statements.text:
The unit root-path vectors in $B_\infty$ have unit child increments
which are weakly null among the children of each fixed vertex. Every
sequence of distinct coordinate vectors is in fact weakly null.
If $a\|\cdot\|\le N\le b\|\cdot\|$, with $0<a\le b<\infty$,
then the one-sided asymptotic modulus of $N$ vanishes at $a/(2b)$
and at $a/b$. In particular, $B_\infty$ has no equivalent AUC norm.
The same obstruction holds for the finite-height forest, using trees
of arbitrarily large finite height.

statements.label: stab:sign:obstruction
statements.text:
In $B_\infty$, the root paths $h_v=d_{[o,v]}$ and the coordinates
$e_v^*$ have norm one, and the children $(e_{v^\frown j}^*)_j$ of
each fixed vertex are weakly null. If
$a\|z\|\le N(z)\le b\|z\|$, with $0<a\le b<\infty$, then
$\overline\delta_N(a/(2b))=0$.

More precisely, put $t_0=a/(2b)$, with $d,\varepsilon>0$ below.
Each of the following assumptions
would permit a finite-codimensional subspace and a child whose
approximation error and growth factor satisfy the corresponding row:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
 \text{assumed positive lower bound}&
 \text{error less than}&\text{growth factor}\\\hline
 0<d<\overline\delta_N(t_0)&\min(a/2,ad/2)&1+d/2\rule{0pt}{13pt}\\
 2\varepsilon<\overline\delta_N(t_0)&
       \min(a/2,a\varepsilon/2)&1+\varepsilon/2\\
 d=\overline\delta_N(t_0)>0&\min(a/2,ad/4)&1+d/4
\end{array}
\]
Here the error is $N(e_v^*-f)$ for the chosen child and its
approximant $f$ in the finite-codimensional subspace. Growth is
measured relative to the $N$-norm of the parent root-path vector.

statements.title: The averaged clipping estimate
statements.label: clip:paired-modulus
statements.text:
For the infinite-height coordinate predual $B_\infty$ and the
finite-height forest space $X$,
\[
 \widehat\delta_Z(t)\ge\sqrt{1+t^2/12}-1\qquad(t>0).
\]

statements.label: dir:primal:add:head-tail-lens
statements.text:
If \(x=P_Hx\) and \(y=Q_Hy\), then
\begin{equation}
 \max_{\pm}\|x\pm y\|\ge\sqrt{\|x\|^2+\|y\|^2/12}.
\end{equation}
If \(0<\sigma\le1\) and \(w,Z_1,Z_2,\ldots\in X\) satisfy
\(\|w\pm Z_j\|\le1\) and \(\|Z_j-Z_l\|\ge2\sigma\) for \(j\ne l\),
then \(\|w\|\le1-\sigma^2/24\).

statements.title: Selection before testing
statements.label: clip:selection-prop
statements.text:
Suppose $x=P_Hx$, $\|x\|=1$, $y\in\ker P_H$, and
$v=Q_Hv$, $\rho(v)\le1$, and $y(v)>\|y\|/2$.
For every $s>0$, each of
the following constructions produces an exterior test $w$ with
\[
 |y(w)|>\|y\|/8,\qquad \rho(w)\le1,
 \qquad \rho(f+sw)^2\le1+3s^2,
\]
where $f=P_Hf$ norms $x$ and the inward signs are chosen with full
cone budgets $q_g$.

\begin{enumerate}
\item Take the positive and negative cumulative parts globally, choose
one by its total pairing, then retain one of the two groups of cones
having the same prescribed inward sign.
\item Form all four combinations of a cumulative positive/negative
part and a prescribed inward-sign group, and select one by its pairing.
\item Choose a cumulative part separately in each cone, orient it
inward, then retain the cones on which the resulting pairings have
one common sign.
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Frontier shift and selected endpoint
statements.label: clip:frontier-prop
dir:primal:add:separated
statements.text:
For each \(D\ge1\), there exists \(c_D>0\) such that, if
\(x,z_i\in X\), \(1\le\|x\|\le D\), \(\|z_i\|\le2D\), and
\(\|z_i-z_j\|\ge1\) for distinct indices in an infinite sequence, then
some \(i\) satisfies \(\max_{\pm}\|x\pm z_i\|>\|x\|+c_D\).

statements.title: A radial-deficit estimate
statements.label: thm:tail
statements.section_title: A radial deficit and separate endpoint laws

statements.label: cor:max-modulus
statements.text:
For the specified dual norm on $X$,
\[
 \overline\theta_X(t)\ge\frac{\sqrt{1+t^2/4}-1}{2}\qquad(t>0).
\]
statements.section_title: A radial deficit and separate endpoint laws

statements.label: prop:endpoint
statements.text:
Let $0\le d<1$, let $H$ be finite and ancestral, and suppose
$x=P_Hx$, $\|x\|\ge1-d$, and $\|x\pm y\|\le1$. Fix a head
norming test $p$ with $\rho(p)=1$ and $x(p)=\|x\|$, and a finite
ancestral set $K\supset H$. For each $\tau\in\{-1,1\}$ choose
any finite represented atom law with mean $P_K(x+\tau y)$, and denote
its expectation by $\mathbb E_\tau$. For an atom $A=\sum_i a_i d_{S_i}$,
put $b_i=p(S_i)$, $A^\circ=\sum_i b_i d_{S_i}$, and
$L=1-\sum_i b_i^2$. Then
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E_\tau\!\left[L+\sum_i(a_i-b_i)^2\right]\le4d,
 \qquad \mathbb E_\tau\|A-A^\circ\|\le2\sqrt d.
\end{equation}
If $b(g)$ is the replaced crossing sum at gate $g$, put
$m_\tau(g)=\mathbb E_\tau|b(g)|$ and
$m=(m_1+m_{-1})/2$. These nonnegative vectors satisfy
\begin{equation}
 m_\tau\le2m\text{ coordinatewise},\qquad\|m\|_2\le\sqrt{6d}.
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: A radial deficit and separate endpoint laws

statements.label: mol:prop:conditional-joint
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{mol:prop:joint-budget}, assume
in addition that $P_Hy=0$ and $r=\|x\|>0$, and put $\Delta=R^2-r^2$.
Fix a head norming test $p=P_Hp$ with $\rho(p)=1$ and $x(p)=r$.
For every finite ancestral $K\supset H$ and each sign
$\tau\in\{-1,1\}$, choose any finite law of represented vectors
\[
 A=\sum_i a_i d_{S_i},\qquad \sum_i a_i^2\le R^2,
 \qquad \mathbb E_\tau A=P_K(x+\tau y),
\]
where each represented family consists of disjoint segments. Put
\[
 b_i=r p(S_i),\qquad A^\circ=\sum_i b_i d_{S_i},\qquad
 V=\sum_i(a_i-b_i)^2,\qquad L=r^2-\sum_i b_i^2.
\]
These laws exist by the finite atomic-ball formula. For every such
choice, the replacement satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E_\tau(V+L)\le\Delta,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_\tau\|Q_H(A-A^\circ)\|\le\sqrt\Delta.
\end{equation}
At each gate $g$, let $b(g)$ be the replaced crossing coefficient,
or zero when there is no crossing segment. The mixed absolute crossing
vector
$m(g)=\bigl(\mathbb E_1|b(g)|+\mathbb E_{-1}|b(g)|\bigr)/2$
satisfies $\|m\|_2\le\sqrt{2\Delta}$. Consequently a separate
endpoint argument, followed by ancestral exhaustion, yields
\begin{equation}
 \|y\|\le(1+2\sqrt2)\sqrt\Delta.
\end{equation}
If the same two nonnegative errors are bounded separately, without
retaining their sum, the corresponding calculation gives
\begin{equation}
 \|y\|\le(1+2\sqrt3)\sqrt\Delta.
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Further consequences of the joint budget

statements.label: presentation:identity
statements.text:
The coordinate identity satisfies $a(x)=q(x)=\|x\|$ on
$c_{00}(\mathcal F)$ and extends to surjective linear isometries
\[
 X_a=X_q=X=J^*.
\]
The finite unit balls and completed atomic ball are therefore exactly
those of Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-hull} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:closed-atomic-ball}.

statements.label: presentation:subtrees
statements.text:
Let $(r_j)$ be a finite or countable family of incomparable vertices,
and put $U_j=\{v:r_j\preceq v\}$. For $x\in X_a$ supported in
$\bigcup_jU_j$,
\[
 a(x)^2=\sum_j a(P_{U_j}x)^2.
\]

statements.label: stab:weighted
statements.text:
Let $z_1,\ldots,z_m\in B_Z$ and let
$\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m>0$ with $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$.  Put
\[
 z=\sum_i\lambda_i z_i,\qquad
 \delta_i=1-z_i(p),\qquad
 \delta=1-z(p)=\sum_i\lambda_i\delta_i,
 \qquad \eta=\|Q_Hz\|.
\]
Then, for each $i$,
\begin{equation}
 \|Q_Hz_i\|
 \le\lambda_i^{-1}
       \sqrt{(\eta+\sqrt{2\delta})^2+4\delta}
       +\sqrt{2\delta_i}.
\end{equation}
All deficits are nonnegative, and $\delta_i\le\delta/\lambda_i$.
For two equally weighted endpoints this gives
\begin{equation}
 \|Q_Hz_\pm\|
 \le2\sqrt{(\eta+\sqrt{2\delta})^2+4\delta}+2\sqrt\delta.
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Stability from a nearly norming head test

statements.title: Bounded multipliers
statements.label: stab:bounded-multiplier
statements.section_title: Stability from a nearly norming head test

statements.label: stab:supported-pair
statements.section_title: Stability from a nearly norming head test

statements.label: stab:original-crossing
statements.section_title: Stability from a nearly norming head test

statements.label: stab:small-center-tail
statements.text:
Let $0<e<1/4$, let $x\in Z$ satisfy $\|x\|=1$, and let $H$ be
finite ancestral with $\|Q_Hx\|\le e$.  Suppose $p=P_Hp$,
$\rho(p)=1$, and $x(p)\ge1-e$.  For every $u\in\ker P_H$,
\begin{equation}
 \max\{\|x+u\|,\|x-u\|\}\le1+e
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \|u\|\le25\sqrt e.
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Stability from a nearly norming head test

statements.label: stab:averaged-gain
statements.text:
For either coordinate model,
\[
 \widehat\delta_Z(t)\ge t^2/1024\qquad(0<t<1).
\]
For every $t>0$ and every $0<e<1/4$ with $25\sqrt e<t$, one also
has $\widehat\delta_Z(t)\ge e/2$.
statements.section_title: Stability from a nearly norming head test

statements.label: molw:average
statements.text:
Let $A\subset T_\infty$ be finite and ancestral, let
$x\in B_\infty$ be supported in $A$, and let $z\in\ker P_A$. Write
\[
 r=\|x\|,\qquad L_+=\|x+z\|,\qquad L_-=\|x-z\|,
 \qquad L=\frac{L_++L_-}{2}.
\]
Then $L_+,L_-\ge r$ and
\begin{equation}
 \|z\|\le C\sqrt{L(L-r)},\qquad C=\sqrt2+\sqrt6.
\end{equation}

statements.label: molw:modulus
statements.text:
For every $t>0$, put
\begin{equation}
 \omega(t)=\frac{\sqrt{1+4(t/C)^2}-1}{2},\qquad C=\sqrt2+\sqrt6.
\end{equation}
Then the averaged asymptotic modulus of $B_\infty$ satisfies
$\widehat\delta_{B_\infty}(t)\ge\omega(t)/2>0$. The bound holds when
the cofinite infimum allows every perturbation direction of norm at
least one.

statements.label: mola:conditional
statements.text:
Let $H$ be finite and ancestor-closed, $x=P_Hx$, and
$x+h,x-h\in B_X$, with arbitrary $h\in X$.
Suppose $0<d<1$ and $\|x\|\ge1-d$. For every $\eta>0$, choose
finite represented-atom laws with means $z_\pm$ such that
$\|z_\pm-(x\pm h)\|\le\eta$. Such laws exist, and every such pair gives
\begin{equation}
 \|Q_Hh\|\le\eta+2\sqrt{d+\eta}
       +2\sqrt{(\eta+\sqrt{2(d+\eta)})^2+4(d+\eta)}.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\[
 \|Q_Hh\|\le(2+2\sqrt6)\sqrt d.
\]

statements.label: mol:closed-hull-signed
statements.text:
In the forest space $X=J^*$, let $H$ be finite and ancestral,
$x=P_Hx$, $y=Q_Hy$, and $x\pm y\in B_X$. Put $d=1-\|x\|$.
For every $\varepsilon>0$, the finite atomic approximation argument gives
\begin{equation}
 \|y\|\le e_\varepsilon+
 \sqrt{e_\varepsilon^2+4(d+\varepsilon)},\qquad
 e_\varepsilon=\varepsilon+\sqrt{2(d+\varepsilon)}.
\end{equation}
Consequently $\|y\|\le(\sqrt2+\sqrt6)\sqrt d$.

statements.label: molb:unscaled-tail
stab:coef:exact-tail
statements.text:
Let $H$ be finite and ancestral, $x=P_Hx$, $P_Hz=0$, and
$\|x\pm z\|\le1$. Put $d=1-\|x\|\in[0,1]$ and
\[
 \omega_{\mathrm{coef}}(d)=2\bigl(\sqrt{2d}+\sqrt{6d+4\sqrt{2d}}\bigr)
 \qquad(d\ge0).
\]
The original coefficients give both
\begin{align}
 \|z\|&\le(\sqrt{12}+2\sqrt2)\sqrt d,
        \\
 \|z\|&\le\omega_{\mathrm{coef}}(d).
        
\end{align}
More generally, if $0\le d_0<1$ and $\|x\|\ge1-d_0$, the
right side of \eqref{stab:coef:fourth-root} may be replaced by
$\omega_{\mathrm{coef}}(d_0)$.

statements.label: mola:actual
statements.text:
In the forest space $X$, suppose $H$ is finite and ancestor-closed,
$x=P_Hx$, $y=Q_Hy$, and
$\|x+y\|,\|x-y\|\le1$.  Then
\[
 \|y\|\le g(1-\|x\|),\qquad
 g(s)=\sqrt{2s}+\sqrt{6s+4\sqrt{2s}}\quad(s\ge0).
\]

statements.label: stab:coef:unit-head-lens
stab:coef:approximate-tail
molb:prop:original-lens
statements.text:
For \(0<\delta<1\) and every unit \(x\in X\), one can choose a finite
ancestor-closed \(H\) such that \(\|x\pm y\|\le1+\delta\) implies
\[
 \|Qy\|\le\eta(\delta):=(1+\delta)
 \left\{2\sqrt{(2\delta+\sqrt{6\delta})^2
                    +4(3\delta+\sqrt{6\delta})}
             +2\sqrt{6\delta}+\delta\right\}.
\]
In particular \(\eta(\delta)\to0\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\).

statements.label: molx:actual-center-fourth
stab:coef:modulus-conversions
statements.text:
For $0<t<1$, each of the following conclusions holds.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $e>0$ satisfies
\[
 (\sqrt{12}+2\sqrt2)\sqrt{(1+e)e}<t/2,
\]
then $\widehat\delta_Z(t)\ge e/4$.
\item If $0<c<1$, $R=1+4c$, and $R\omega_{\mathrm{coef}}(5c/R)<t$, then
$\widehat\delta_Z(t)\ge c$.
\item If $d>0$, $3d<1$, and $(1+2d)\omega_{\mathrm{coef}}(3d)<t$, then
$\widehat\delta_Z(t)\ge d/2$.
\item The completed atomic-ball route gives
$\widehat\delta_Z(t)\ge t^2/16384$.
\end{enumerate}

statements.label: stab:coef:conditional-modulus
molb:prop:matching-lens
statements.text:
For \(0<h<1/4\) and every unit \(x\in X\), there is a finite
ancestor-closed \(H\), depending only on \(x,h\), such that
\(\|x\pm y\|\le1+h\) implies
\begin{equation}
 \|Qy\|\le h+(1+h)
  \bigl[h+2\sqrt{6h}+2(2h+3\sqrt{6h})\bigr].
\end{equation}

statements.label: molx:minimum-tail
statements.text:
Let $X=J^*$ be the finite-height forest space defined by
\eqref{eq:segment-norm}, with the atomic and polar norm identifications
of Proposition~\ref{presentation:identity}. For a finite ancestor-closed
set $A\subset\mathcal F$, let $P_A$ be coordinate restriction on $X$
and let $Q_A=I-P_A$.
If
\[
 P_Ax=x,\qquad Q_Ay=y,\qquad \|x+y\|,\|x-y\|\le1,
\]
then, with $d=1-\|x\|$,
\begin{equation}
 \|y\|\le(\sqrt6+2\sqrt2)\sqrt d\le6\sqrt d.
\end{equation}

statements.label: molc:oriented-lens
statements.text:
Let $A$ be a nonempty finite ancestral set and let $x,y\in B_\infty$
with $x=P_Ax$ and $P_Ay=0$.
For every $\varepsilon\ge0$,
\[
 \max\{\|x+y\|,\|x-y\|\}\le1,
 \qquad \|x\|\ge1-\varepsilon
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \|y\|\le (\sqrt2+\sqrt{10})\sqrt\varepsilon.
\]

statements.label: molb:prop:target-signs
statements.section_title: Signs determined by the target tail

statements.label: stab:sign:parent-lens
stab:sign:parent-modulus
statements.text:
Let $b_L=\sqrt{L^2-1}+2\sqrt{(1-L^{-2})/2}$ for $L>1$.
If $0<t<1$ and $L$ is chosen so that $3b_L<t$, then
\[
 \widehat\delta_Z(t)\ge (L-1)/8>0.
\]

statements.title: A forest lens from preferred parent signs
statements.label: stab:sign:forest-parent-lens
stab:sign:exit-lens
statements.text:
Let $x=P_Hx$, $\|x\|=1$, and $y\in\ker P_H$. Put
$C_{\mathrm{ex}}=2+3\sqrt2$. For every $\delta>0$, with
$\eta=\delta/(1+\delta)$,
\begin{equation}
 \max\{\|x+y\|,\|x-y\|\}\le1+\delta
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \frac{\|y\|}{1+\delta}\le3C_{\mathrm{ex}}\sqrt\eta.
\end{equation}

statements.label: stab:sign:exit-modulus
statements.text:
For $0<t<1$ and $C_{\mathrm{ex}}=2+3\sqrt2$,
\[
 \widehat\delta_{B_\infty}(t)\ge\frac{t^2}{576C_{\mathrm{ex}}^2}.
\]

statements.label: stab:trim:vanishing-lens
statements.text:
There are no sequences of finite ancestral sets $H_n$, finite-head
unit vectors $x_n=P_{H_n}x_n$, and finitely supported
$z_n\in\ker P_{H_n}$ such that
\[
 \max\{\|x_n+z_n\|,\|x_n-z_n\|\}\longrightarrow1,
 \qquad \liminf_n\|z_n\|>0.
\]
The same assertion holds with $z_n$ in the completed tail spaces.

statements.label: stab:trim:modulus
statements.text:
For the coordinate segment space, $\widehat\delta_{B_\infty}(t)>0$ for
every $0<t<1$.

statements.label: mola:uniform-sequential
statements.text:
For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $\delta>0$ such that, for every
finite ancestor-closed $H$ and all $x=P_Hx$, $y=Q_Hy$ with
$\|x\pm y\|\le1$ and $\|x\|>1-\delta$, one has $\|y\|<\varepsilon$.
The given norm is asymptotically midpoint uniformly convex, with the
maximum of the two endpoint norms in the definition.

statements.label: mola:separated-sequential
statements.text:
For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $\delta>0$ such that any infinite
$\varepsilon$-separated family $(v_j)$ satisfying $x\pm v_j\in B_X$
has $\|x\|\le1-\delta$.

statements.label: molx:coordinate-null
statements.text:
Let $x\in X$ and let $(z_j)\subset X$ satisfy
$x\pm z_j\in B_X$ and $z_j(e_v)\to0$ for every forest vertex $v$.
Then, with $C=\sqrt2+2\sqrt6<7$,
\begin{equation}
 \limsup_{j\to\infty}\|z_j\|
 \le C\sqrt{1-\|x\|}\le7\sqrt{1-\|x\|}.
\end{equation}

statements.label: molc:sequential-positive
statements.text:
For each fixed $0<t<1$, the space $B_\infty$ satisfies
$\widehat\delta_{B_\infty}(t)>0$.

title: Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties
abstract: We prove Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties, including residue characteristic 2. After good reduction, the pairing of a rational Hodge class with any complementary product of divisor classes on the reduction is the same rational number in every prime-to-p realization and in crystalline cohomology. Using the Hodge theorem for CM abelian varieties, we also show that every such specialized Hodge class is represented by a single rational algebraic cycle in all these realizations.
version_note: This version updates a citation to a revised manuscript in this collection; see the [previous version](../Milnes-rationality-conjecture-for-abelian-varieties-September-23-2026/paper.pdf).

tex.abstract:
We prove Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties, including
residue characteristic \(2\). After good reduction, the pairing of a
rational Hodge class with any complementary product of divisor classes
on the reduction is the same rational number in every prime-to-\(p\)
realization and in crystalline cohomology. Using the Hodge theorem for CM
abelian varieties, we also show that every such specialized Hodge class
is represented by a single rational algebraic cycle in all these realizations.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let \(A/\Qbar\) be an abelian variety of dimension \(d\) with good
reduction \(A_0/\F\) at \(w\). Let \(0\leq r\leq d\), and let
\[
 \gamma\in H^{2r}(A(\C),\Q(r))
\]
be a rational Hodge class. For every list of Cartier divisors
\(D_1,\ldots,D_{d-r}\) on \(A_0\), there is a number \(q\in\Q\)
such that
\begin{align*}
 \Tr_\ell\bigl(\gamma_{0,\ell}
       c_{1,\ell}(D_1)\cdots c_{1,\ell}(D_{d-r})\bigr)&=q
       &&\text{in }\Q_\ell\quad(\ell\ne p),\\
 \Tr_p\bigl(\gamma_{0,p}
       c_{1,\mathrm{cris}}(D_1)\cdots
       c_{1,\mathrm{cris}}(D_{d-r})\bigr)&=q
       &&\text{in }\Cw.
\end{align*}
Here \(\gamma_{0,\ell}\) is the smooth proper specialization of the
\(\ell\)-adic realization, and \(\gamma_{0,p}\) is the
de Rham--crystalline specialization in
\[
 H^{2r}_{\mathrm{cris}}(A_0/W(\F))[1/p](r)
       \otimes_{\Kzero}\Cw.
\]
The traces use the top Tate twist and send the class of a zero-cycle to
its degree. If \(r=d\), the divisor product is \(1\).

statements.title: Transport
statements.label: prop:transport
statements.text:
Let $A/\Qbar$ be an abelian variety of positive dimension with good
reduction at $w$, and put $V=H_1(A(\C),\Q)$. Suppose
\[
 G\subset\GSp(V,\psi)
\]
is connected reductive, its Hodge homomorphism $h$ gives the
Hodge structure of $A$, and its conjugacy class $X$ makes this
inclusion a Hodge embedding. Let $\gamma$ be a rational Hodge
class of codimension $r$, represented on $V$ by an alternating
form satisfying \eqref{eq:transport-multiplier}.

Then there exist a positive integer $n$, an auxiliary
good-reduction abelian variety $B$, a quasi-isogeny
$a:A_0^n\to B_0$, and a rational Hodge class $\kappa$ of
codimension $r$ on $B$ such that, for the first-factor inclusion
$j:A_0\to A_0^n$,
\begin{equation}
 (aj)^*\kappa_0=\gamma_0.
 
\end{equation}
The equality holds simultaneously in every $\ell$-adic
realization with $\ell\ne p$ and in the crystalline realization
after extension to $\Cw$. Either of the following two further
specifications can be imposed.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The variety $B$ is of CM type and is defined over $\Qbar$,
with its indicated good reduction at $w$.
\item Put $D_A=H^1_{\mathrm{cris}}(A_0/W(\F))[1/p]$. Suppose
$\mathcal F_A$ is a filtration in degrees $0,1$ on $D_A$, over a
finite extension of $\Kzero$, which is weakly admissible and has
finite local-field descent together with the specialized tensors
specifying the $G$-structure. Suppose
also that, after a geometric tensor-preserving identification, it
lies in the $G$-orbit of the original Hodge filtration. Then $B$
can be defined over a finite extension $K/\Kzero$ inside $\Cw$,
and $a$ can be chosen so that
\begin{equation}
 a^*\Fil^1H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}(B/K)
       =(\mathcal F_A^1)^{\oplus n}.
 
\end{equation}
Here the equality is made after a common finite extension and
crystalline--de Rham identification. To discuss Hodge classes on
this $B$, choose a complex embedding of an algebraic closure of
$K$ extending the fixed embedding of $\Qbar$.
\end{enumerate}
In the second case the realizations of $\kappa$ are supplied by
the canonical tensor sections of the Hodge-type model and the
polarization. In the first case these agree with the usual
realizations and specialization of its absolute Hodge class.

statements.title: CM transport of a Hodge class
statements.label: cor:cm-transport
statements.text:
Let \(A/\Qbar\) be an abelian variety of positive dimension with
good reduction at \(w\), and let
\(\gamma\in H^{2r}(A(\C),\Q(r))\) be a rational Hodge class,
where \(0\leq r\leq\dim A\). There are a positive integer \(n\),
a CM abelian variety \(B/\Qbar\) with good reduction at \(w\),
a rational Hodge class \(\kappa\) of codimension \(r\) on \(B\),
and a quasi-isogeny \(a:A_0^n\to B_0\) such that
\[
 \gamma_0=(aj)^*\kappa_0,
\]
where \(j:A_0\to A_0^n\) is the first-factor inclusion. This is an
equality of the usual absolute-Hodge specializations in every
prime-to-\(p\) realization and in crystalline cohomology extended
to \(\Cw\).

statements.title: The filtration construction
statements.label: thm:filtration
statements.text:
Let $A_0/\overline{\F}_p$ be an abelian variety equipped with a rational
action of a CM field $E$ and a polarization whose Rosati involution
restricts to conjugation on $E$.  Suppose that
\[
 D=H^1_{\mathrm{cris}}(A_0/W(\overline{\F}_p))[1/p]
\]
has rank $2s$ over $E\otimes_\Q\Kzero$, where $s\geq 1$.  Suppose also
that there is an invertible $u\in\End^0(A_0)$ such that
\[
 u^\dagger=u,\qquad ue=\bar e u\quad(e\in E).
\]
Let $\beta$ be the dual polarization pairing on $D$, with values in
the isocrystal line of slope $1$.

Then there are a finite extension $K/\Kzero$ and a subspace $L\subset
D_K$ with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The one-step filtration with $\Fil^1D_K=L$ is weakly admissible.
\item $L$ is stable under the cohomological actions of $E$ and $u$,
and is Lagrangian for $\beta$.
\item After extending to an algebraically closed field $\Omega/K$,
one has $\dim_\Omega L_\tau=s$ for every embedding
$\tau:E\hookrightarrow\Omega$.
\item The isocrystal, its indicated tensors, and this filtration have
finite local field descent.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, geometrically $L$ belongs to the balanced polarized
cocharacter orbit.  More explicitly, define
\[
 G_D=\left\{g\in\GSp(D,\beta)\cap
 \GL_{E\otimes_\Q\Kzero}(D):
 \det_{E\otimes_\Q\Kzero}(g)=c(g)^s\right\},
\]
where the scalar on the right is viewed in
$(E\otimes_\Q\Kzero)^\times$.  The balanced $E$-stable
$\beta$-Lagrangians form a single $G_D(\Omega)$-orbit.  Each is the
weight-$1$ space of a cocharacter of $G_{D,\Omega}$ with weights $0,1$.
In particular $L$ belongs to the orbit of any original filtration of
this type under a tensor-preserving comparison.

statements.label: cor:filtration-admissible
statements.text:
The filtration of Theorem~\ref{thm:filtration}, with its finite local
field descent, is admissible: the descended filtered isocrystal is
the filtered crystalline module of a crystalline representation.

statements.title: The divisor filtration condition
statements.label: cor:filtration-divisor
statements.text:
Let \(D,L\) be as in Theorem~\ref{thm:filtration}, and let \(\psi\)
and \(U\) denote the homological polarization and the homological
action of \(u\) on \(D_K^\vee\). The untwisted divisor form
\(\psi(\cdot,U\cdot)\) belongs to
\[
 \Fil^1\bigl(\bigwedge^2D_K\bigr)=L\wedge D_K,
\]
and hence to filtration degree zero after its codimension-one Tate
twist. If a marked power is realized by an abelian lift, the
corresponding pulled-back divisor satisfies the filtration condition
for its symmetric homomorphism in Lemma~\ref{lem:lift-hom}.

statements.label: prop:weil
statements.text:
Every $\gamma\in W_E^s(A)$ satisfies the Lefschetz pairing property
at $w$.  More precisely, if $\mathcal U$ in \eqref{eq:weil-U} has no
invertible element, all complementary pairings are zero.  If it has
an invertible element, $\gamma_0$ is a simultaneous rational
Lefschetz class.

statements.label: cor:cm-pairing
statements.text:
The Lefschetz pairing property holds for the specialization of every
rational Hodge class on a CM abelian variety over $\Qbar$ with good
reduction at $w$.

statements.title: Specialization of all rational Hodge classes
statements.label: cor:all-hodge-specialization
statements.text:
For every abelian variety \(A/\Qbar\) of dimension \(d\) with good
reduction \(A_0/\F\) at \(w\), every \(0\leq r\leq d\), and every
rational Hodge class
\[
 \gamma\in H^{2r}(A(\C),\Q(r)),
\]
there is a unique class \(\rho_\gamma\in\mathcal R^r(A_0)\) such that
\[
 (\rho_\gamma)_\ell=\gamma_{0,\ell}\quad(\ell\ne p),\qquad
 (\rho_\gamma)_p\otimes 1=\gamma_{0,p}.
\]
The prime-to-\(p\) equalities are in
\(H^{2r}_{\acute{e}t}(A_0,\Q_\ell(r))\); the crystalline equality is in
\[
 H^{2r}_{\mathrm{cris}}(A_0/W(\F))[1/p](r)
       \otimes_{\Kzero}\Cw.
\]
The specialization components are those of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.
The assertion holds for every prime \(p\),
including \(p=2\), with the prime, place, and theory fixed before
\(A\) and \(\gamma\) vary.

statements.title: Algebraic specialization of rational Hodge classes
statements.label: cor:algebraic-specialization
statements.text:
Fix the prime and place as in Theorem~\ref{thm:main}. Let
\(A/\Qbar\) be an abelian variety of dimension \(d\) with good
reduction \(A_0/\F\) at \(w\), and let
\(\gamma\in H^{2r}(A(\C),\Q(r))\) be a rational Hodge class,
where \(0\leq r\leq d\). There is one rational algebraic cycle
\(z_\gamma\in\operatorname{CH}^r(A_0)_{\Q}\) such that
\[
 \operatorname{cl}_\ell(z_\gamma)=\gamma_{0,\ell}
       \quad(\ell\ne p),\qquad
 \operatorname{cl}_{\mathrm{cris}}(z_\gamma)\otimes1=\gamma_{0,p}.
\]
The crystalline equality is in
\[
 H^{2r}_{\mathrm{cris}}(A_0/W(\F))[1/p](r)
       \otimes_{\Kzero}\Cw.
\]
This holds for every prime \(p\), including \(p=2\).
Consequently, for every
\(y\in\operatorname{CH}^{d-r}(A_0)_{\Q}\), the traces of
\(\gamma_{0,\ell}\operatorname{cl}_\ell(y)\) for \(\ell\ne p\)
and of \(\gamma_{0,p}\operatorname{cl}_{\mathrm{cris}}(y)\)
are all the same rational number \(\deg(z_\gamma\cdot y)\).

title: Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties
Minimal metrics and interior injectivity for nef adjoints
abstract: Let \((H,\Theta)\) be a projective complex klt pair with effective rational boundary and nef ℚ-Cartier adjoint. On any projective log resolution, minimal semipositive metrics on the pulled-back adjoint exist and have zero Lelong numbers everywhere. On smooth projective complex varieties, we also prove an H1-injectivity theorem for rational interior boundaries with simple-normal-crossing support when both endpoint bundles carry zero-Lelong semipositive metrics.

tex.abstract:
Let \((H,\Theta)\) be a projective complex klt pair with effective rational
boundary and nef \(\Q\)-Cartier adjoint. On any projective log resolution,
minimal semipositive metrics on the pulled-back adjoint exist and have zero
Lelong numbers everywhere. On smooth projective complex varieties, we also
prove an \(H^1\)-injectivity
theorem for rational interior boundaries with simple-normal-crossing support
when both endpoint bundles carry zero-Lelong semipositive metrics.
sections: Zero Lelong numbers for nef klt adjoints
Abundance for fourfolds with nonzero Euler characteristic

statements.label: thm:adjoint-metric
statements.text:
Let $(H,\Theta)$ be a normal connected projective complex klt pair, with
$\Theta$ an effective rational divisor.  Suppose that
$D_H=K_H+\Theta$ is a nef $\Q$-Cartier divisor.  For every projective log
resolution $\pi:V\to H$, the rational line bundle $N=\pi^*D_H$ has the following property: every semipositive singular Hermitian
metric with minimal singularities on $N$ has Lelong number zero
at every point of $V$. Such a metric exists. Neither $K_H$ nor $\Theta$ is required to be separately $\Q$-Cartier.

statements.label: thm:interior-injectivity
statements.text:
Let $V$ be a smooth projective complex variety, let $L$ be an integral
divisor, and let $0\le C_0\le C_2$ be effective rational divisors whose
combined support is simple normal crossing.  Suppose that both
rational line bundles $L-C_0$ and $L-C_2$ admit singular Hermitian
metrics of semipositive curvature with zero Lelong numbers at every
point.  For a rational number $0<\lambda<1$, set
\[
 C_1=(1-\lambda)C_0+\lambda C_2,\qquad
 L_i=L-\floor{C_i}\quad(i=0,1).
\]
Then the natural inclusion of line bundles induces an injection
\[
 H^1\bigl(V,\cO_V(K_V+L_1)\bigr)
 \longrightarrow H^1\bigl(V,\cO_V(K_V+L_0)\bigr).
\]

\label[corollary]{cor:minimal-multiplier}
Under the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:adjoint-metric}, let $\phi$ be a
minimal weight on the actual rational line bundle $N$. Then
\[
 \mathcal I(t\phi)=\cO_V\qquad\text{for every real }t>0,
\]
where the ideal is defined by local integrability of $|f|^2e^{-t\phi}$.
The conclusion is independent of the choice of minimal metric and of
the Cartier multiple used to normalize its weights.
statements.section_title: Zero Lelong numbers for nef klt adjoints

statements.text:
\label[proposition]{prop:uniform-primitives}
Let $F$ be a fixed holomorphic line bundle on $V$, and let $h_k$ be
smooth metric weights on $F|_U$.  Suppose that, for a fixed constant
$A_0\ge0$,
\[
 i\partial\bar\partial h_k\ge-A_0\omega_c,
\]
and that in local frames on $V$ the weights are uniformly bounded
above and the functions $e^{-h_k}$ have uniformly bounded local
integrals on punctured coordinate neighborhoods.  Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item There is a continuous linear map
\[
 \kappa_k:Z^1_{h_k}\longrightarrow H^1(V,K_V\otimes F)
\]
agreeing with the ordinary Dolbeault class on smooth closed forms on
$V$.  It annihilates the closure in $L^2_{h_k}(n,1)$ of the image of
$\dbar:L^2_{h_k}(n,0)\to L^2_{h_k}(n,1)$.
\item There is a constant $C$ independent of $k$ such that every
$f\in Z^1_{h_k}$ with $\kappa_k(f)=0$ has a global primitive on $U$
satisfying
\[
 \dbar v=f,\qquad \|v\|_{h_k}\le C\|f\|_{h_k}.
\]
No continuous linear choice of these global primitives is asserted.
\end{enumerate}

\label[corollary]{cor:euler-abundance}
Let $(X,\Delta)$ be a projective complex klt fourfold with effective
rational boundary and nef adjoint $D=K_X+\Delta$.
If $\chi(X,\cO_X)\ne0$, then $D$ is semiample.

statements.title: Lazi\'c--Peternell, fourfold nonvanishing
statements.label: mm:thm:lp-fourfold
statements.text:
Let $(X,\Delta)$ be a normal projective complex klt pair of dimension
four, with effective rational boundary, and put $D=K_X+\Delta$.
Suppose $D$ is pseudoeffective and $N$ is a nef $\mathbb Q$-Cartier
divisor. If both $D$ and $D+N$ satisfy the metric condition
\eqref{mm:eq:generalized-algebraic} and $\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)\ne0$,
then some rational $t_0>0$ satisfies
\[
 \kappa(X,D+tN)\geq0\qquad
 \text{for every rational }t\in[0,t_0].
\]

statements.title: Gongyo--Matsumura, fourfold semiampleness
statements.label: mm:thm:gm-fourfold
statements.text:
Let $(X,\Delta)$ be a normal projective complex klt pair of dimension
four, with effective rational boundary, and set $D=K_X+\Delta$.
Suppose that for a projective birational morphism $f:Z\to X$ with
$Z$ smooth and some positive integer $r$ with $rD$ Cartier, the bundle
$f^*\mathcal O_X(rD)$ carries a semipositive singular Hermitian metric
with zero Lelong numbers at every point of $Z$.
If $\kappa(X,D)\geq0$, then $D$ is semiample.

title: Minimal models and Mori fibre spaces for generalized log canonical Q-pairs
abstract: We resolve the existence form of the minimal-model conjecture for projective generalized log canonical ℚ-pairs over algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero. Such a pair admits a minimal model when its adjoint divisor is pseudo-effective, and a Mori fibre space otherwise, while keeping the nef ℚ-Cartier b-divisor fixed. Taking the nef part to be zero gives the corresponding result for ordinary log canonical ℚ-pairs.

tex.abstract:
We resolve the existence form of the minimal-model conjecture for projective
generalized log canonical $\Q$-pairs over algebraically closed fields of
characteristic zero. Such a pair admits a minimal model when its adjoint
divisor is pseudo-effective, and a Mori fibre space otherwise, while keeping
the nef $\Q$-Cartier b-divisor fixed. Taking the nef part to be zero gives
the corresponding result for ordinary log canonical $\Q$-pairs.
sections: From local phases to minimal models
Equivariant cones and an lc projective slice
The product of independent degree scales
Cartier selection on the leading field
Completing tuples and rounding their phases
Bounded presentations and relative logarithmic frames
Trait comparison, base forms and integral lifting
Lc incidence and completion of the bounded-fibre argument

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let
$(X,B+M)$ be a projective generalized log canonical $\Q$-pair. Thus $X$ is
normal and integral, $B$ is an effective rational boundary, and $M$ is the
trace of a nef rational Cartier divisor on a higher projective birational
model, with $K_X+B+M$ $\Q$-Cartier.

There are a normal integral projective variety $Y$ and a birational map
$\phi\colon X\dashrightarrow Y$ whose inverse contracts no divisors such
that, writing $B_Y=\phi_*B$ and taking $M_Y$ to be the trace of the same
nef b-divisor, the generalized pair $(Y,B_Y+M_Y)$ is log canonical and
\[
 A_{X,B+M}(E)\le A_{Y,B_Y+M_Y}(E)
\]
for every prime divisor $E$ over their common function field. The
inequality is strict for every divisor on $X$ contracted by $\phi$.
More precisely, the following alternatives are determined by $D=K_X+B+M$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item if $D$ is pseudo-effective, then $K_Y+B_Y+M_Y$ is nef;
\item if $D$ is not pseudo-effective, there is a projective contraction $h\colon Y\to T$ to a normal
projective variety with connected fibres such that
\[
 \dim T<\dim Y,\qquad \rho(Y/T)=1,
 \qquad -(K_Y+B_Y+M_Y)\text{ is ample over }T.
\]
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Ordinary log canonical pairs
statements.label: cor:ordinary
statements.text:
Let $(X,B)$ be a projective log canonical $\Q$-pair over an algebraically
closed field of characteristic zero. There is a birational map
$\phi:X\dashrightarrow Y$ extracting no divisors, with $B_Y=\phi_*B$,
such that $(Y,B_Y)$ is log canonical and
\[
 A_{X,B}(E)\leq A_{Y,B_Y}(E)
\]
for every prime divisor over the common function field, strictly for
prime divisors on $X$ contracted by $\phi$. If $K_X+B$ is
pseudo-effective, $K_Y+B_Y$ is nef; otherwise $Y$ admits a Mori fibre
contraction with relative Picard number one and relatively ample
$-(K_Y+B_Y)$.

statements.title: Local phase assertion
statements.label: thm:phase
statements.text:
Let $(V_i,o_i)$ be a sequence of pointed algebraic Gorenstein klt germs of a
fixed dimension $n\geq2$, with $o_i$ closed.  Suppose that a finite cyclic
group $G_i$ acts on an affine representative of each germ, fixes $o_i$, and
admits a semi-invariant canonical generator $\theta_i$, a volume form with
zero divisor near $o_i$.  Choose
an arbitrary element $\gamma_i\in G_i$ for each $i$.

After passage to a subsequence, there are divisorial valuations $w'_i$
centred at $o_i$, a constant $C>0$, and a positive integer $\ell$, independent
of $i$ on that subsequence, such that
\[
 A_{\theta_i}(w'_i)\leq C
\]
and, for every nonzero rational semi-invariant function $h$ on $V_i$ of
character $\chi$,
\begin{equation}
 w'_i(h)\equiv\ell\,\phaseangle\bigl(\chi(\gamma_i)\bigr)
 \pmod{\Z}.
\end{equation}
In particular, $w'_i$ restricts to an integral-valued valuation of
$\C(V_i)^{G_i}$.
statements.section_title: From local phases to minimal models

statements.label: prop:smooth-termination
statements.text:
Assume Theorem~\ref{thm:phase}.  Let $X$ be a smooth projective complex
variety with pseudo-effective canonical divisor.  A $K_X$-MMP with scaling
of an effective ample rational divisor $H$, chosen so that $(X,H)$ is klt
and $K_X+H$ is ample, terminates with nef canonical divisor.
Consequently, on a smooth projective birational model $p:U\to X$ one has
\[
 p^*K_X=P+N,
 \qquad P\text{ nef and rational Cartier},\quad N\geq0
 \text{ rational Cartier}.
\]
statements.section_title: From local phases to minimal models

statements.label: prop:relative-wzd
statements.text:
Assume Theorem~\ref{thm:phase}.  Let $X$ be a smooth complex
quasi-projective variety, projective over a normal quasi-projective
variety $Z$.  If $K_X$ is pseudo-effective over $Z$, it admits an NQC weak
Zariski decomposition over $Z$ with rational Cartier parts.
statements.section_title: From local phases to minimal models

statements.label: prop:field-descent
statements.text:
The conclusion of Theorem~\ref{thm:main} over $\C$ implies its conclusion
over every algebraically closed field of characteristic zero.
