title: Nonhomeomorphic closed aspherical four-manifolds with the same homotopy type
abstract: We construct closed connected aspherical topological four-manifolds that are homotopy equivalent but not homeomorphic, disproving the homeomorphism-existence formulation of the Borel conjecture in dimension four. Their common fundamental group is word-hyperbolic. One of the manifolds also has a self-homotopy equivalence not homotopic to a homeomorphism.

tex.abstract:
We construct closed connected aspherical topological four-manifolds
that are homotopy equivalent but not homeomorphic, disproving the
homeomorphism-existence formulation of the Borel conjecture in dimension
four.  Their common
fundamental group is word-hyperbolic.  One of the manifolds also has a
self-homotopy equivalence not homotopic to a homeomorphism.
sections: Two manifold models of the same double cover
The reflection extension and its outer actions
The normalizer of the label subgroup
Marked chambers and the even cover
A tensor obstruction on a graph
The obstruction in odd cyclic covers

statements.label: thm:pair
statements.text:
There exist closed connected aspherical topological four-manifolds
$M$ and $N$ that are homotopy equivalent but not homeomorphic.
Their common fundamental group is word-hyperbolic.

statements.label: thm:self-map
statements.text:
There exist a closed connected aspherical topological four-manifold
$M$ and a homotopy equivalence $f\colon M\to M$ such that no
homeomorphism $M\to M$ is homotopic to $f$.

statements.title: Cyclic-cover criterion
statements.label: cyc:criterion
statements.text:
Let $Q$ be a connected finite aspherical CW complex, put
$G=\pi_1(Q)$, and let $w\colon G\twoheadrightarrow\mathbb Z$ be an
epimorphism.  For every positive integer $d$, write
\[
 G_d=w^{-1}(d\mathbb Z)
 \qquad\text{and}\qquad
 Q_d\longrightarrow Q
\]
for the associated connected cyclic cover.  Fix an integer $n\geq1$.
Suppose that $Q_2$ has a closed topological $n$-manifold model $M$, but
that $Q_d$ has no such model for every sufficiently large odd integer
$d$.

Choose $\gamma\in G$ with $w(\gamma)=1$, and use the model equivalence
to identify $\pi_1(M)$ with $G_2$.  The outer automorphism of $G_2$
represented by
\[
 \alpha(g)=\gamma g\gamma^{-1}
\]
is induced by a self-homotopy equivalence of $M$.  No homeomorphism of
$M$ induces this outer automorphism.  In particular, that
self-homotopy equivalence is not homotopic to a homeomorphism.

statements.title: A Sylow criterion for manifold models
statements.label: sym:criterion
statements.text:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be connected topological manifolds whose fundamental
groups are marked by a group $\Pi$, and suppose that $\Out(\Pi)$ is
finite.  Let $\mathsf A,\mathsf B\leq\Out(\Pi)$ be $2$-subgroups of
the same order.  Suppose that there is an involution $\delta$ for which
\[
 N_{\Out(\Pi)}(\mathsf A)=\mathsf A\times\langle\delta\rangle
\]
is an internal direct product, and that
\[
 \mathsf A\leq R_X,\qquad \mathsf B\leq R_Y,
 \qquad \delta\notin R_X.
\]
If $\mathsf A$ and $\mathsf B$ are not conjugate in $\Out(\Pi)$, then
$X$ and $Y$ are not homeomorphic.

statements.title: Reflection and marked fillings, \cite{PD}
statements.label: refl:input
statements.text:
Let $D$ be a compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold with
connected boundary $S$ and free fundamental group $H$.  Suppose that
$D$ has the homotopy type of a finite graph with $2k$ two-spheres,
and that its whole middle module $H_2(\widetilde D;\mathbb Z)$ over
$\mathbb ZH$ has a specified
framed immersed hyperbolic basis of $k$ planes, with vanishing
quadratic self-intersections.  Attach three-cells along the basis
spheres to obtain a map of collared pairs
\[
 (D,S)\longrightarrow(P,S)
\]
that is the identity on $S$ and induces the given identification of
fundamental groups.  Assume that $(P,S)$ is an oriented Poincar\'e
pair of dimension four, that $P\simeq BH$, and that
$\pi_1(S)\to H$ is surjective.

For a finite flag triangulation of $S$, let
$Q=\mathcal R_A(P)$ be \eqref{refl:finite-reflection}.  Then $Q$ is a
finite aspherical oriented Poincar\'e complex of dimension four.
If $Q$ has a closed topological four-manifold model, then $S$ admits
a marked graph-type filling: there is a compact oriented topological
four-manifold $V$ with an orientation-preserving boundary identification
$\partial V=S$ and a homotopy
equivalence $V\to P$ whose boundary restriction is homotopic to the
given inclusion $S\to P$.

statements.title: Parity chamber data
statements.label: refl:chamber-data
statements.text:
There are chamber data $(D,P,S,H)$ satisfying the chamber hypotheses of
Theorem~\ref{refl:input}, with $H$ a finitely generated nonabelian free
group, and a distinguished epimorphism $w\colon H\to\mathbb Z$ with the following
properties.  For $d\geq1$, put $H_d=w^{-1}(d\mathbb Z)$, let
$D_d,P_d$ be the associated connected cyclic covers, and let $S_d$ be
the preimage of $S$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $d$, the boundary $S_d$ is connected, and
$(D_d,P_d,S_d,H_d)$ satisfies all the chamber hypotheses of
Theorem~\ref{refl:input}, with the full framed immersed hyperbolic
basis and its vanishing quadratic self-intersections lifted from $D$.
\item There is a compact oriented topological four-manifold $V$ with
an orientation-preserving boundary identification $\partial V=S_2$
and a homotopy equivalence
\[
 j:(V,S_2)\longrightarrow(P_2,S_2)
\]
equal to the identity on the boundary.
\item For every odd $d\geq3$, there is no compact oriented topological
four-manifold $V_d$ with an orientation-preserving boundary
identification $\partial V_d=S_d$ and a homotopy equivalence
$V_d\to P_d$ whose boundary restriction is homotopic to the inclusion
$S_d\to P_d$.
\end{enumerate}

statements.label: refl:odd-models
statements.text:
For every odd integer $d\geq3$, the space $Q^0_d$ has no closed
topological four-manifold model.

statements.label: mod:odd-models
statements.text:
For every odd integer \(d\geq3\), the space \(Q_d\) has no closed
topological four-manifold model.
statements.section_title: Two manifold models of the same double cover

statements.title: Manifold models from doubled chambers
statements.label: mod:models
statements.text:
Let \(K\) be a finite PL triangulation of \(S\).  Let \(\mathsf F\)
be a finite-dimensional \(\Ftwo\)-vector space with labels
\((\lambda_u)_{u\in\mathcal U}\) spanning \(\mathsf F\) and linearly
independent on every simplex of \(K\).  Using the fixed relative
filling \(j:(V,S_2)\to(P_2,S_2)\), for every linear map
\(\epsilon:\mathsf F\to\Ftwo\) the space \(\mathcal M_\epsilon\)
defined by \eqref{mod:boundary-relation} is a closed connected
topological four-manifold, and
\(\varphi_\epsilon:\mathcal M_\epsilon\to R_2\) in
\eqref{mod:comparison-map} is a homotopy equivalence.  If \(R_2\) is
aspherical, then \(\mathcal M_\epsilon\) is aspherical.
statements.section_title: Two manifold models of the same double cover

statements.title: The double cover of a full reflection
statements.label: refl:even-model
statements.text:
For every finite flag triangulation \(K\) of \(S\), let \(Q^0(K)\)
be its full reflection, using one independent basis label for each
vertex.  The connected double cyclic cover of \(Q^0(K)\) defined by
the folding character has a closed connected aspherical topological
four-manifold model.
statements.section_title: Two manifold models of the same double cover

statements.title: Actions on the manifold models
statements.label: mod:actions
statements.text:
The action \eqref{mod:ambient-action} is faithful.  For each linear
\(\epsilon:\mathsf A\to\Ftwo\), its restriction to
\(\mathsf B_\epsilon\) is realized by a faithful action by
homeomorphisms on \(M_\epsilon\), and \(f_\epsilon\) is equivariant
for these actions.  Under the marking by \(\Pi\), the outer
automorphism induced by each of these homeomorphisms is the one
induced by the corresponding action on \(Q_2\).
statements.section_title: Two manifold models of the same double cover

statements.label: ext:development
statements.text:
The space $\widetilde Q$ is contractible.  If $\overline x$ and
$x_2$ are the images of $x$ in $P$ and $P_2$, respectively, the
maps
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 [c,x]&\longmapsto[\chi_0(c),\overline x]\in Q^0,\\
 [c,x]&\longmapsto[\chi(c),\overline x]\in Q,\\
 [c,x]&\longmapsto[\chi(c),x_2]\in Q_2
 \end{aligned}
\]
are universal coverings.  With the chosen deck-group convention,
\begin{equation}
 \pi_1(Q^0)=\ker\chi_0,\qquad
 G:=\pi_1(Q)=\ker\chi,\qquad
 \Pi:=\pi_1(Q_2)=\ker\eta .
\end{equation}
The homomorphism $w\colon G\to\mathbb Z$ induced by the folding map
is $w$ composed with the projection $\mathcal E\to H$.
statements.section_title: The reflection extension and its outer actions

statements.label: ext:embedding
statements.text:
Conjugation gives an injection
$\mathcal E\hookrightarrow\Aut(\Pi)$.  It identifies $\Pi$ with
$\Inn(\Pi)$ and induces an inclusion
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal E/\Pi
   =\mathsf A\times\langle\delta\rangle
   \ \leq\ \Out(\Pi),
 \qquad \delta=(0,1).
\end{equation}
Here $\langle\delta\rangle\cong\Ftwo$.  Inside $\Aut(\Pi)$,
$\mathcal E$ is the full preimage of the product in
\eqref{ext:outer}; $\mathcal E_2$ and $G$ are the full preimages of
its factors $\mathsf A$ and $\langle\delta\rangle$, respectively.
statements.section_title: The reflection extension and its outer actions

statements.label: ext:outer-actions
statements.text:
Under \eqref{ext:outer}, the action of $\mathcal E/\Pi$ on $Q_2$
is the label-translation and cyclic-deck action
\[
 (a,t)[b,y]=[a+b,\theta^t y],
 \qquad (a,t)\in\mathsf A\times\Ftwo.
\]
With the markings supplied by Proposition~\ref{mod:models}, the
graph action on $M_\epsilon$ from Proposition~\ref{mod:actions}
induces exactly the subgroup
\[
 \mathsf B_\epsilon
   =\{(a,\epsilon(a)):a\in\mathsf A\}
   \leq\Out(\Pi).
\]
In particular, every element of $\mathsf A=\mathsf B_0$ is
induced by a homeomorphism of $M$, and every element of
$\mathsf B_\ell$ is induced by a homeomorphism of $N$.
statements.section_title: The reflection extension and its outer actions

statements.label: ext:delta
statements.text:
With the marking $\pi_1(M)\cong\Pi$, no homeomorphism of $M$
induces the outer automorphism $\delta$.
statements.section_title: The reflection extension and its outer actions

statements.label: ext:nonconjugate
statements.text:
The subgroups $\mathsf A$ and $\mathsf B_\ell$ of $\Out(\Pi)$
are not conjugate.
statements.section_title: The reflection extension and its outer actions

statements.label: hyp:word-hyperbolic
statements.text: The groups \(\mathcal E\) and \(\Pi\) are word-hyperbolic.

statements.label: hyp:finite-out
statements.text: The outer automorphism group \(\Out(\Pi)\) is finite.

statements.label: nor:rigidity
statements.text:
Every automorphism of $W$ is a composite of an inner
automorphism and an automorphism induced by a simplicial
automorphism of $\widehat{\mathcal L}$.
statements.section_title: The normalizer of the label subgroup

statements.label: nor:normalizer
statements.section_title: The normalizer of the label subgroup

statements.title: The chamber homotopy type
statements.label: ch:homotopy-type
statements.text:
With the markings induced by the preceding construction,
\begin{equation}

 H:=\pi_1D=\pi_1X*F(z_1,\ldots,z_k),\qquad
 D\simeq BH\vee\bigvee^{2k}S^2,
\end{equation}
where $BH$ is a finite graph and $z_j$ is the normal-circle generator
of the $j$th replacement.  On the common surgery-link exterior in
the boundary, killing the $z_j$ recovers the original marking into
$\pi_1X$.
statements.section_title: Marked chambers and the even cover

statements.title: The Poincar\'e chamber
statements.label: ch:poincare-chamber
statements.text:
The manifold $D$ has a specified framed immersed hyperbolic basis
for its full module $\pi_2D$, with vanishing quadratic
self-intersections.  Attach one three-cell on each of these
$2k$ basis spheres, and call the resulting space $P$.  Then
$(P,S)$ is an oriented finite four-dimensional Poincar\'e pair,
the inclusion $(D,S)\to(P,S)$ preserves the fundamental group
and the boundary, and $P\simeq BH$.
statements.section_title: Marked chambers and the even cover

statements.title: Connected lifted boundary
statements.label: ch:boundary-surjectivity
statements.text: The boundary marking $\pi_1S\to H$ is surjective.
statements.section_title: Marked chambers and the even cover

statements.title: The double-cover filling
statements.label: ch:even-filling
statements.text:
The boundary $S_2$ has a marked filling $D'_2$.  It can be
obtained from $D_2$ by replacing disjoint punctured
$S^2\times S^2$ neighbourhoods by four-balls.  In particular,
there is a homotopy equivalence $(D'_2,S_2)\to(P_2,S_2)$
equal to the identity on the boundary.
statements.section_title: Marked chambers and the even cover

statements.title: Endpoint assignment
statements.label: ten:assignment
statements.text:
Let \(K\) have characteristic zero, and let \(\Gamma\) be a finite
loopless multigraph with distinguished endpoints as above.  For each edge
\(e\), choose a coordinate block \(h_e\) of dimension \(N_e\geq0\) and
functions \(F_e,b_e\in K\langle h_e\rangle\).  For each vertex \(v\),
choose a family \(\mathcal L_v\) of nonempty subsets of \(E(v)\), and set
\begin{align}
 T_v&=K[t_e:e\in E_+(v)]/(t_e^2:e\in E_+(v)),\\
 \mathcal S_v(h,t)
 &=\sum_{e\in E_+(v)}(F_e(h_e)+t_e b_e(h_e))
       -\sum_{e\in E_-(v)}F_e(h_e).
\end{align}
Suppose there are formal parametrizations
\[
 M_v(y_v,t)\in (y_v,t)T_v[[y_v]]^{\sum_{e\in E(v)}N_e},
 \qquad y_v=(y_{v,1},\ldots,y_{v,a_v}),
\]
satisfying the following conditions.
\begin{enumerate}
 \item The central tangent maps \(A_v=\partial_{y_v}M_v(0,0)\) are
 injective, and the difference map
 \begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 \Lambda:\bigoplus_{v\in V}K^{a_v}&\longrightarrow
                         \bigoplus_{e\in E}K^{N_e},\\
 (\xi_v)_v&\longmapsto
 \bigl((A_{v_+(e)}\xi_{v_+(e)})_e
             -(A_{v_-(e)}\xi_{v_-(e)})_e\bigr)_e
 \end{split}
 \end{equation}
 is an isomorphism.
 \item One has \(\mathcal S_v(M_v(y_v,t),t)=0\) identically for every
 vertex \(v\).
 \item For every \(L\in\mathcal L_v\), put
 \(I=L\cap E_+(v)\) and \(J=L\cap E_-(v)\).  Then
 \begin{equation}
 \left(\prod_{i\in I}t_i\right)
 \left(\prod_{j\in J}b_j\right)(M_v)
 \in
 \bigl((\partial_h\mathcal S_v)(M_v)\bigr)
                         \subset T_v[[y_v]].
 \end{equation}
 The ideal on the right is generated by all restricted internal
 partial derivatives of \(\mathcal S_v\).
\end{enumerate}
There is an endpoint assignment \(a:E\to V\) such that, for every
\(v\in V\) and \(L\in\mathcal L_v\), at least one edge of \(L\) is
assigned to its endpoint other than \(v\).

title: Nonsingular systems of equations over arbitrary groups
abstract: Every finite nonsingular system of equations over an arbitrary group has a simultaneous solution in an overgroup. This proves Howie's conjecture on nonsingular systems.

tex.abstract:
Every finite nonsingular system of equations over an arbitrary group has
a simultaneous solution in an overgroup. This proves Howie's conjecture
on nonsingular systems.
sections: From a kernel relation to a solution

statements.title: Nonsingular systems
statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $G$ be any group, let $1\le m\le n$ be integers, and let
$w_1,\ldots,w_m\in G*F_n$. If their exponent-sum matrix has row rank
$m$ over $\mathbb Q$, then the canonical homomorphism
\[
 G\longrightarrow
 (G*F_n)/\langle\!\langle w_1,\ldots,w_m\rangle\!\rangle
\]
is injective. Equivalently, the system has a simultaneous solution in
an overgroup of $G$.

statements.title: Simultaneous fixed spaces
statements.label: thm:fixed-space
statements.text:
Let $r\geq 0$ and $n\geq 1$, and let $k_1,\ldots,k_r$ be positive integers.
For each $j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $\mathcal B_j$ be a finite ordered list
of pairs $(i,s)$ with $1\leq i\leq r$ and $s\in\{1,-1\}$; repetitions
are allowed.  Set
\[
 d_j=\sum_{(i,s)\in\mathcal B_j}k_i,
 \qquad
 b_{ij}=\sum_{\substack{(i',s)\in\mathcal B_j\\i'=i}}s,
 \qquad B=(b_{ij}).
\]
Suppose that $B$ has row rank $r$ over $\mathbb Q$.  For arbitrary
$P_j\in\mathrm U(d_j)$, define
\[
 D=\prod_{i=1}^r\mathrm U(k_i),
 \qquad
 F_j(X)=\operatorname{diag}_{(i,s)\in\mathcal B_j}(X_i^s)P_j
 \quad (X\in D).
\]
Then there is $X\in D$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{j=1}^n\dim_{\mathbb C}\ker(F_j(X)-I_{d_j})
 \ \geq\ \sum_{i=1}^r k_i.
\end{equation}
Here $\mathrm U(0)$ and an empty product of groups are points, and the
fixed-space dimension in dimension zero is zero.

statements.title: Planar boundary obstruction
statements.label: prop:planar
statements.text:
Let $w_1,\ldots,w_m\in G*F_n$ have exponent-sum matrix of row rank $m$
over $\mathbb Q$.  Let $\Sigma$ be a connected oriented surface of genus
zero obtained from a nonempty finite collection of signed word disks for
these words by attaching bands that pair every slot exactly once, always
with the same variable index and opposite traversal signs.  If the words
on all boundary components except possibly one are trivial in $G$, then
every boundary word is trivial in $G$.

title: Nontrivial Markov Type Forces Superreflexivity
abstract: We prove that every real Banach space with Markov type p > 1 is superreflexive. Together with the known converse, this characterizes superreflexivity by nontrivial Markov type. This answers Naor's question: every real Banach space with nontrivial Markov type admits an equivalent uniformly smooth norm.

tex.abstract:
We prove that every real Banach space with Markov type $p>1$ is
superreflexive. Together with the known converse, this characterizes
superreflexivity by nontrivial Markov type. This answers Naor's question:
every real Banach space with nontrivial Markov type admits an equivalent
uniformly smooth norm.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Every real Banach space with Markov type $p$ for at least one $p>1$
is superreflexive.

statements.title: A finite walk with linear displacement
statements.label: prop:walks
statements.text:
Let $N$ be a spreading invariant norm on $c_{00}$ for which merging
adjacent entries is contractive. For every integer $n\geq1$, there are
a finite stationary reversible marked chain and an odd labeling $g$
in a finite coordinate span such that
\[
 N(g(e))=1\qquad\text{for every edge }e,
\]
and, for the first $n$ edges $E_1,\ldots,E_n$ of the stationary chain,
\begin{equation}
 \Prob\left\{N\left(\sum_{i=1}^n g(E_i)\right)
                 \geq\frac n{24}\right\}\geq\frac3{20}.
\end{equation}

statements.title: Reversible chart transport
statements.label: prop:chart-transport
statements.text:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite ordered set, and let
$T_s:D_s\to R_s$ be order-preserving bijections between its subsets,
indexed by a nonempty finite set $\cS$ with a fixed-point-free involution
$s\mapsto s^{-1}$ and $T_{s^{-1}}=T_s^{-1}$.
For every $\epsilon>0$, there are an integer $B$ and a finite stationary
reversible marked chain on charts $C:\Lambda\to\{1,\ldots,B\}$ whose
successive edge letters are independent and uniform in $\cS$.
At every stationary step $(C,s,C')$,
\[
 C'(a)=C(T_s(a))\quad(a\in D_s)
\]
holds simultaneously with probability at least $1-\epsilon$.

title: Nonuniqueness for bounded measurable scalar conductivities in three dimensions
abstract: We construct two distinct uniformly positive bounded measurable scalar conductivities on a ball in ℝ<sup>3</sup> with the same full Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator. Both conductivities equal one near the boundary. This gives nonuniqueness in the scalar Calderón problem at bounded measurable regularity.

tex.abstract:
We construct two distinct uniformly positive bounded measurable scalar
conductivities on a ball in $\R^3$ with the same full
Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator. Both conductivities equal one near the
boundary. This gives nonuniqueness in the scalar Calder\'on problem at
bounded measurable regularity.
sections: Weak equations and changes of variables
Exact scalarization of two Cauchy pairs
From a branching block to identical boundary measurements

statements.label: thm:main

statements.title: Localized nonuniqueness
statements.label: cor:localized
statements.text:
Let $c,C$ be the constants in Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.
For every bounded connected Lipschitz domain $\Omega\subset\R^3$
and every finite family of pairwise disjoint balls
$B_1,\ldots,B_m\Subset\Omega$, $m\geq1$, there are $2^m$
pairwise distinct real scalar conductivities
$\gamma_\varepsilon\in L^\infty(\Omega)$, indexed by
$\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}^m$, such that
\[
 c\leq\gamma_\varepsilon\leq C\quad\text{almost everywhere},
 \qquad
 \gamma_\varepsilon=1\quad\text{on }
 \Omega\setminus\bigcup_{i=1}^m B_i,
\]
and all their full weak Dirichlet-to-Neumann operators from
$H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ to $H^{-1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ agree.
Distinct conductivities differ on a set of positive measure.

statements.title: Exact finite-field scalarization
statements.label: thm:scalarization
statements.text:
Let $U\subset\R^3$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain. Let $A$ be a
measurable symmetric matrix field satisfying
\[
 c_0\Id\leq A\leq C_0\Id\qquad\text{almost everywhere in }U,
 \qquad 0<c_0\leq C_0<\infty.
\]
Suppose the real-valued potentials $u_1,u_2\in H^1(U)$ satisfy
$\Div(A\nabla u_j)=0$. Assume that there is an open cover of a
full-measure subset of $U$ on whose members $A,u_1,u_2$ are smooth
and have the following local rank property. On each member, a fixed
subset of the potentials has everywhere independent gradients, and
every remaining potential is a constant affine combination of that
subset. The subset may have zero, one, or two elements; a zero-element
subset means that both potentials are constant there.

There exist constants $0<a<b<\infty$, a measurable scalar
$a\leq\gamma\leq b$, and $v_1,v_2\in H^1(U)$ such that
\begin{align}
 \Div(\gamma\nabla v_j)&=0,
 &v_j-u_j&\in H^1_0(U), \\
 \int_U\gamma\nabla v_j\cdot\nabla\psi\,\dd x
 &=\int_U A\nabla u_j\cdot\nabla\psi\,\dd x
 &&\text{for every }\psi\in H^1(U). 
\end{align}
The bounds $a,b$ may be chosen using only $c_0,C_0$.

statements.title: Weak approximation by scalar-near matrices
statements.label: sc:weak-approximation
statements.text:
Given a subsolution, a weak $L^2$ neighborhood of its pair $(E,F)$,
and $\eps>0$, there is a subsolution in that neighborhood whose
matrix has distance less than $\eps$ from the scalar matrices
outside a set of volume less than $\eps$.
statements.section_title: Exact scalarization of two Cauchy pairs

statements.title: Branching block
statements.label: prop:branching-block
statements.text:
Let $B\subset\R^3$ be a bounded connected Lipschitz domain whose boundary
has three components $\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2$.  Suppose these components
have disjoint product collars parametrized by
$\T^2\times[0,\eta_i]$, where $\T^2=(\R/2\pi\mathbb Z)^2$.
Assume the parametrizations are bi-Lipschitz, smooth with nonsingular
derivative on open pieces covering up to a null set, and that removing
sufficiently thin collars leaves a connected Lipschitz central region.
Let $\mu_i$ be the probability measure obtained by pushing forward
$(2\pi)^{-2}\dd\theta$ to $\Gamma_i$ by its collar parametrization.

There is a scalar conductivity $\gamma_B$, bounded above and bounded away
from zero, with the following property.  For every $c=(c_0,c_1,c_2)\in\R^3$,
the weak $\gamma_B$-harmonic function $U_c$ with boundary value $c_i$ on
$\Gamma_i$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \int_B\gamma_B\nabla U_c\cdot\nabla\psi\,\dd x
   =\sum_{i=0}^2 I_i(c)\int_{\Gamma_i}\psi\,\dd\mu_i,
 \qquad \psi\in H^1(B),
\end{equation}
where $\sum_i I_i(c)=0$.  The linear map $c\mapsto I(c)$ has kernel
$\R(1,1,1)$ and image $\{I\in\R^3:\sum_i I_i=0\}$.

statements.label: nu:identical-dn
statements.text:
The full weak Dirichlet-to-Neumann operators of \(\gamma\) and
\(\widetilde\gamma\) on \(\Omega\) are equal.

title: Nonuniqueness for the periodic hard-sphere Boltzmann equation
abstract: We prove nonuniqueness for the periodic hard-sphere Boltzmann equation by constructing two distinct global renormalized solutions with the same nonnegative initial density on \(\mathbb T^3\times\mathbb R^3\). This density has bounded velocity support and finite mass, energy, and absolute entropy. Both solutions conserve local mass and total momentum and satisfy the global energy and entropy-dissipation inequalities. On a common initial interval, they are strongly continuous in L1, and their collision gains and losses are integrable.

tex.abstract:
We prove nonuniqueness for the periodic hard-sphere Boltzmann equation by
constructing two distinct global renormalized solutions with the same
nonnegative initial density on \(\T^3\times\R^3\). This density has bounded
velocity support and finite mass, energy, and absolute entropy. Both
solutions conserve local mass and total momentum and satisfy the global
energy and entropy-dissipation inequalities. On a common initial interval,
they are strongly continuous in \(L^1\), and their collision gains and
losses are integrable.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is a nonnegative density \(F_0\) on \(\T^3\times\R^3\), with bounded
velocity support and
\[
\int_{\T^3\times\R^3}
 F_0(1+|v|^2+|\log F_0|)\dd x\dd v<\infty,
\]
for which the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation has two distinct global
admissible solutions, in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:admissible},
with initial datum \(F_0\).
On some common initial interval both solutions are strongly continuous
in \(L^1\), and their collision gains and losses are integrable in
space-time-velocity.

statements.title: Uniform cold control
statements.label: prop:cold-control
statements.text:
There is a constant \(L\), depending on the fixed parameters, such
that after imposing the additional condition
\begin{equation}
 Ld_0\overline s^9\le1,
 
\end{equation}
the following statements hold at every time of existence of the
finite approximation in \(0\le t\le\overline T\).
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item For every retained label \(i=(j,\sigma,n)\),
 \begin{equation}
  0\le c_i\le f_i+\varepsilon_j m_i,\qquad
  \varepsilon_j=Ld_{s_j}/s_j .
  
 \end{equation}
 \item At each spatial point call the unique label with
 \(x\in\mathcal O_i(t)\), if one exists and is retained, the main
 label.  Let \(c_{\mathrm{main}}\) be that color, or zero, and set
 \(e=c-c_{\mathrm{main}}\).  For every \(A\ge0\),
 \begin{equation}
  0\le e(t,x,v)\le C_A t^A e^{-4|v|^2}.
  
 \end{equation}
 The upper bound remains valid after restricting the escaped sum
 to any subset of its labels.
 \item If the main label has scale \(s\), its velocity measure is
 bounded by a fixed multiple of \((t+s)^{-1}\) times a sum of
 admissible probability sheets from Lemma~\ref{lem:sheet-bound}.
 Its free-core contribution has the exact parameterization
 \eqref{eq:core-jacobian} below.  The remainder has the smaller
 velocity-mass coefficient \(Cd_s/s^2\).
 In particular, for every fixed \(k\ge0\),
 \begin{equation}
  \int_{\R^3}\langle v\rangle^k c_{\mathrm{main}}\,\dd v
       \le\frac{C_k}{t+s},\qquad
  \int_{|v|>R}\langle v\rangle^k c_{\mathrm{main}}\,\dd v
       \le\frac{C_k e^{-c_kR^2}}{t+s}\quad(R\ge3).
  
 \end{equation}
 \item For the mixed-cold source in the hot equation,
 \begin{equation}
  \sum_{\substack{i,j\in\mathcal I_N\\i\ne j}}
       P^b(c_i,c_j)(t,x,v)
       \le C_A t^{A-1}H(v)\qquad (t>0)
  
 \end{equation}
 for every \(A\ge0\), with constants uniform in \(N\) and \(b\).
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: Cold jets and uniform color estimates

statements.title: Survival of a cold core under the cap
statements.label: jet:survival
statements.text:
Suppose a finite approximation satisfies
\[
 0\le h(t,x,v)\le(t+s_N)H(v)
\]
on an initial interval \([0,T]\subset[0,\overline T]\).
All conclusions below concern times \(t\in[0,T]\).
For every \(M\ge0\) there are constants \(C,C_M\), independent of
\(T,N\), the cutoff, and the seed, such that
\begin{equation}
\begin{gathered}
 e^{-E_{s,N}(t)}f_i(t,x,v)
       \le c_i(t,x,v)
       \le f_i(t,x,v)+L(d_s/s)m_i(t,x,v),\\
 E_{s,N}(t)=C(d_st/s+t^2+s_Nt)+C_Mt^{M+1}
\end{gathered}
 
\end{equation}
for every label of scale \(s\).
Consequently, if \(r\to0\), \(s_N\le r\), \(s/r\in[\epsilon,R]\)
for fixed \(0<\epsilon<R<\infty\), and \(0\le t\le\min(T,Ar)\), then
\[
 E_{s,N}(t)\le
 C_{\epsilon,R,A}(d_s+r^2)+C_{M,A}r^{M+1}\longrightarrow0
\]
uniformly in the label and in points of its free core.
The transverse free displacement divided by the stripe period
satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \frac{td_s}{s^2}\le
       C_{\epsilon,R,A}r^9\longrightarrow0.
 
\end{equation}
On these scales the difference between cold and free-core
velocity measures also satisfies, uniformly in position and time,
\begin{equation}
 r\int_{\R^3}|c_i-f_i|(t,x,v)\,\dd v\longrightarrow0.
 
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Cold jets and uniform color estimates

statements.label: prop:finite-cap
statements.text:
There is a fixed \(T_0>0\) such that the following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item With \(\lambda=0\), the finite approximations exist on \([0,T_0]\)
and satisfy \(0\le h\le t^2H\).
\item There is a fixed finite \(L_0\) such that, for every
\(0<T\le T_0\) and every \(N\), some \(\lambda\in[0,L_0]\) gives an
approximation on \([0,T]\) with
\begin{equation}
0\le h(t,x,v)\le(t+s_N)H(v),\qquad
\max_{0\le t\le T}\frac{\|h(t)\|_H}{t+s_N}=1.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
In both cases all cold components obey Proposition~\ref{prop:cold-control}.

statements.label: prop:admissible-limits
statements.text:
Fix \(T\in(0,T_0]\). Either the zero-seed approximations of
Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-cap}, or any sequence of its cap shots on
\([0,T]\), has a subsequence whose total densities \(F_N=c_N+h_N\)
converge weakly in \(L^1([0,T]\times\Omega)\) to a nonnegative density
\(F\). The subsequence can be chosen so that
\(F_N(t)\rightharpoonup F(t)\) in \(L^1(\Omega)\) at every
\(t\in[0,T]\), with uniformly small polynomially weighted velocity
tails. The limit has the common initial datum \eqref{eq:datum}, and
\[
Q^\pm(F,F)\in L^1([0,T]\times\Omega),\qquad
F\in C([0,T];L^1(\Omega)).
\]
It satisfies every condition of Definition~\ref{def:admissible} on this
interval, including the inequalities at every time. Each such limit has
an admissible global continuation. The dormant upper bound, consisting
of the cold majorants of Proposition~\ref{prop:cold-control} and
\(t^2H\), passes to a zero-seed limit.

statements.label: prop:blowup-limit
statements.text:
Every sequence \eqref{eq:rescaling} has a subsequence for which
\(h_{r_N}\rightharpoonup g\) in local spacetime \(L^1\) on
\((0,U)\times\R^3_x\times\R^3_v\), where
\begin{equation}
0\leq g(t,x,v)\leq(t+l)H(v),\qquad
\D g=2P(B,g)-g\nu_B.
\end{equation}
Here \(B\) is \eqref{eq:background}; its gain and loss are defined by
integration against the velocity measure. Both terms on the right are
locally integrable, with a velocity majorant uniform in position on
each compact positive-time interval. Compactly supported velocity
averages of \(h_{r_N}\) converge strongly in local \(L^1_{t,x}\).
The limit has a locally strongly continuous \(L^1\) representative
at positive times and obeys the integrating-factor formula
\eqref{dil:mild} below.

If \(l>0\), pass also to a limit \(\lambda_N\to\lambda_0\) of the
shot parameters. The conclusion and its local continuity extend to
time zero, with
\begin{equation}
g(0,x,v)=\lambda_0 l\,\chi(x/l,v).
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: The cap dilation and its linear limit

statements.title: Nonvanishing of every cap limit
statements.label: prop:nonzero-limit
statements.text:
Consider any sequence of cap shots with horizons \(T_n\to0\),
approximation indices \(N_n\to\infty\), and
\(s_{N_n}/T_n\to0\).  Make the rescaling
\eqref{eq:rescaling}, and pass to any subsequence supplied by
Proposition~\ref{prop:blowup-limit}.  Its limit satisfies
\[
 g\not\equiv0\qquad\text{on }(0,U)\times\R^3_x\times\R^3_v.
\]
This conclusion includes \(l=1\), \(U=1\), and \(U=\infty\).
statements.section_title: A cap event produces a nonzero limit

statements.label: prop:finite-dilated-horizon
statements.text:
There are fixed positive choices of \(\eta,\alpha,\gamma,K\), with
\(\eta,\alpha,\gamma\) small and \(K\) large, for which every limit in
Propositions~\ref{prop:blowup-limit} and~\ref{prop:nonzero-limit} has
\(U<\infty\). These parameters can be fixed before the final choices of
\(s_0,d_0,T_0\). The same choices work for every limiting mesh and every
\(l\in[0,1]\).

title: Nonuniqueness of percolation on nonamenable quasi-transitive graphs
abstract: We prove the bond-percolation nonuniqueness conjecture of Benjamini and Schramm: every infinite connected, locally finite, nonamenable quasi-transitive graph has a nonempty interval of parameters for which Bernoulli bond percolation almost surely has infinitely many infinite clusters. We also prove Hutchcroft's stronger operator-threshold conjecture, establishing \(p_c\lt p_{2\to2}\le p_u\).

tex.abstract:
We prove the bond-percolation nonuniqueness conjecture of Benjamini and
Schramm: every infinite connected, locally finite, nonamenable quasi-transitive
graph has a nonempty interval of parameters for which Bernoulli bond
percolation almost surely has infinitely many infinite clusters. We also prove
Hutchcroft's stronger operator-threshold conjecture, establishing
$p_c<p_{2\to2}\le p_u$.
sections: Critical clusters remain controlled after deletions
A subpower bound for the triangle trace
Paths with an escape at each endpoint
Critical boundedness and the nonuniqueness interval

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $G$ be an infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph
with $h_V(G)>0$. For Bernoulli bond percolation on $G$,
\[
 \sup_{0\le p<\pc}\norm{T_p}_{2\to2}
       =\norm{T_{\pc}}_{2\to2}<\infty,
 \qquad \pc(G)<\ptwo(G)\le\pu(G).
\]
There exist $\pc<p_1<p_2<1$ such that, in the coupling obtained from
independent uniform edge labels, almost surely there are infinitely
many infinite open clusters simultaneously for every $p\in[p_1,p_2]$.

statements.title: Arbitrary Cayley graphs
statements.label: cor:cayley
statements.text:
Let $\Lambda$ be a nonamenable finitely generated group, and let $S$
be any finite symmetric generating set with the identity removed.
For Bernoulli bond percolation on the simple undirected Cayley graph
with edges $\{x,xs\}$, $x\in\Lambda$, $s\in S$, the critical connection
operator is bounded on counting-measure $\ell^2(\Lambda)$ and
\[
 \pc<\ptwo\le\pu.
\]
The simultaneous nonuniqueness interval in \cref{thm:main} exists for
every such fixed generating set. At every fixed $p\in(\pc,\pu)$,
there are almost surely infinitely many infinite open clusters.

statements.title: Critical laws and exponential connectivity
statements.label: cor:critical-laws

statements.title: Reduction to a unimodular action
statements.label: pre:unimodular-reduction
statements.text:
If $\Aut(G)$ is nonunimodular, then $\pc<\ptwo\le\pu$ and
$T_\pc$ is bounded.
For the proof of the operator gap it therefore remains to treat the
case in which $\Gamma=\Aut(G)$ is unimodular.

statements.title: Critical boundedness for a unimodular action
statements.label: thm:critical-operator
statements.text:
Let $G$ be an infinite connected locally finite simple quasi-transitive
graph with $h_V(G)>0$. If $\Aut(G)$ is unimodular, then
$\norm{T_{\pc}}_{2\to2}<\infty$.

statements.title: Good critical clusters
statements.label: good:good-clusters
statements.text:
For each $\epsilon\in(0,1/2)$, uniformly in $x$ and for all sufficiently
large $M$,
\begin{equation}
 \Prob_\pc(s_x\le M,\ C_x\text{ is not good for cap }M)
 \le e^{-M^\epsilon}.
\end{equation}
The event that a cluster has size at most $M$ and is good for cap $M$
is determined by the percolation bits in a deterministic finite-radius
ball about its root.
statements.section_title: Critical clusters remain controlled after deletions

statements.title: Efficient endpoint maps
statements.label: amp:efficient-maps
statements.text:
Under \eqref{eq:s09}, for every $\eta>0$ there is a local endpoint map on
the orbit $O$ of \cref{amp:scales}, with $M\ge2$ and $H>1$, such that
\[
 \frac{U+m}{H}<\eta.
\]
Moreover the maps can be chosen so that $H$ tends to infinity.  Their
radii are finite, but need not be bounded uniformly over the construction.

statements.label: mom:critical-moments

statements.label: mom:susceptibility

statements.label: trace:subpower

statements.title: Small change of operator norm
statements.label: def:norm

statements.title: Decrease of the averaged susceptibility
statements.label: def:decrease
statements.text:
For all $t\ge0$,
\begin{equation}
 -\chi_t'\ge e^{-tc_k}
 \left(
 \E_{\rm path}\left[
       \one_{\{\ell_w\ge3\}}s_t^{D_w}(u)s_t^{D_w}(v)\right]
       -C'(\chi_0^+)^2\rho^ka_3
 \right),
\end{equation}
where $C'>0$ depends only on $G$.
The product term is defined to be zero for discarded raw paths.

statements.title: One coupling for an interval
statements.label: con:coupled-interval
statements.text:
Let $G$ be infinite, connected, locally finite, and quasi-transitive.
Suppose $\pc<p_1<p_2<1$ and $T_{p_2}$ is bounded on $\ell^2(V)$.
In the coupling obtained by assigning independent uniform labels to
edges and opening an edge at parameter $p$ when its label is at most
$p$, almost surely there are infinitely many infinite clusters
simultaneously at every $p\in[p_1,p_2]$.

title: Nonuniqueness with local conservation for the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation
abstract: We prove nonuniqueness for the three-dimensional periodic hard-sphere Boltzmann equation among global entropy solutions satisfying exact local conservation of mass, momentum, and kinetic energy. We construct one nonnegative initial density with bounded velocity support and finite mass, energy, and absolute entropy that gives rise to two distinct such solutions. Both are strongly continuous in L1, and their collision gain and loss terms are integrable with every polynomial velocity weight on every bounded time interval.

tex.abstract:
We prove nonuniqueness for the three-dimensional periodic hard-sphere
Boltzmann equation among global entropy solutions satisfying exact local
conservation of mass, momentum, and kinetic energy. We construct one
nonnegative initial density with bounded velocity support and finite mass,
energy, and absolute entropy that gives rise to two distinct such solutions.
Both are strongly continuous in \(L^1\), and their collision gain and loss
terms are integrable with every polynomial velocity weight on every bounded
time interval.

The datum and the finite colored evolutions

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There exist \(R<\infty\) and a nonnegative datum \(F_0\) with
\[
 \supp_vF_0\subset B_R(0),\qquad
 \int_\Omega F_0(1+|v|^2+|\log F_0|)\dd x\dd v<\infty,
\]
for which \eqref{eq:collision} has two global entropy solutions with local
conservation in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:admissible}, differing on
a set of positive \((t,x,v)\)-measure. Both solutions belong to
\(C([0,\infty);L^1(\Omega))\). Moreover, for every finite \(T\) and
every \(k\ge0\), they satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \int_0^T\!\!\int_\Omega
 \langle v\rangle^k\bigl[Q^+(F,F)+Q^-(F,F)\bigr]
                       \dd x\dd v\dd t<\infty,
 \qquad \langle v\rangle=(1+|v|^2)^{1/2}.
\end{equation}

statements.title: Finite evolution and its identities
statements.label: con:finite-evolution
statements.text:
For fixed \(N,b,T,\lambda\), the colored equations have a unique
nonnegative local mild solution with bounded total \(H\)-norm.  It
continues while that norm remains bounded, with the prescribed
transfers at retirement times, and depends continuously in this norm
on its initial data on every common bounded interval of existence.
The norm of each component is continuous between transfers.

On every such interval, total mass, momentum, and energy are conserved.
The exact local collision-invariant balances hold, with all polynomial
velocity fluxes integrable.  For \(\rho=M\) or \(\rho=\mu\), one has
at every time of existence
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal H_\rho(F(t))+
       \int_0^t\mathcal D^b(F(s))\dd s
       \le\mathcal H_\rho(F(0)),
 
\end{equation}
where \(\mathcal D^b\) is the entropy dissipation with the same cutoff.
statements.section_title: The datum and the finite colored evolutions

statements.title: Control of every active color
statements.label: cold:control
statements.text:
There is a fixed constant \(C_*\) such that, with
\[
 \epsilon_s=C_*L_sd_s/s,\qquad
 \mathcal U_i=f_i+\epsilon_s m_i,
\]
and sufficiently small \(s_0\), every finite colored evolution obeys
\begin{equation}
 0\le c_i(t,x,v)\le\mathcal U_i(t,x,v)\qquad (0\le t\le L_{s_i})
 
\end{equation}
as long as that color is active and the solution exists.
If, on an interval beginning at \(t_1\), one also has
\(\nu_F^b\ge\kappa>0\), then
\begin{equation}
 c_i(t,x,v)\le e^{-\kappa(t-t_1)}\mathcal U_i(t,x,v)\qquad
                   (t_1\le t\le L_{s_i})
 
\end{equation}
throughout that interval.  None of the constants in
\eqref{cold:upper} uses a bound on the bath or hot density.
statements.section_title: Cold estimates up to the retirement times

statements.title: Cap selection
statements.label: early:cap-selection
statements.text:
For fixed $\delta>0$, there are $\bar s_0,T_0>0$, uniform in $N$ and
the collision cutoff, with the following property.
For each $0<s_0\le\bar s_0$, each $0<T\le T_0$, and each finite
approximation, a seed parameter
$\lambda\in(0,L_0)$ gives a solution on $[0,T]$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
 Z(t)\le m_T(t+s_N)\quad(0\le t\le T),
 \qquad
 \max_{0\le t\le T}\frac{Z(t)}{m_T(t+s_N)}=1.
\end{equation}
The dormant solution exists on a fixed initial interval and satisfies
\begin{equation}
 Z(t)\le C'_{A,\delta}t^A.
\end{equation}
The interval and constant in \eqref{early:dormant-bound} are independent
of $N$, the collision cutoff, and sufficiently small $s_0$.
statements.section_title: Selection and continuation on the initial time interval

statements.title: Uniform early continuation
statements.label: early:continuation
statements.text:
Fix $\delta>0$ and $\zeta\in(0,1)$.
There are $\bar s_0>0$ and $T_0\in(0,t_1)$, depending on $\delta$ and
$\zeta$ and on the fixed jet parameters, such that for every
$0<s_0\le\bar s_0$, every finite approximation, and every
$0<T\le T_0$, the dormant solution and every solution selected in
Proposition~\ref{early:cap-selection} continue to $t_1$ and satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{0\le t\le t_1}\|h(t)\|_H\le\zeta.
\end{equation}
The choices are uniform in $N$, the collision cutoff, $R_\mu$, and $T$.
For dormant solutions, \eqref{early:dormant-bound} also holds on an
initial interval independent of these indices, with the fixed exponent
$A>p+1$ chosen in \eqref{early:exponents}.
statements.section_title: Selection and continuation on the initial time interval

statements.title: Uniform global continuation
statements.label: prop:global-control
statements.text:
The construction parameters can be fixed so that every dormant finite
evolution and every cap solution with $0<T\le T_0$ continues globally.
There are constants $B<\infty$ and $\kappa>0$, independent of $N$,
$b_N\ge1$, and $T$, such that
\begin{equation}
 \|w(t)\|_H\le B,\qquad \nu_F^{b_N}(t,x,v)\ge\kappa,
 \qquad t\ge t_1.
\end{equation}
Every active jet satisfies \eqref{global:cold-decay} through its
retirement, the total retirement increment is bounded by
\eqref{global:retirement}, and the hot component satisfies the small
bound of \cref{early:continuation} on $[0,t_1]$.
statements.section_title: A uniform global bound for the finite evolutions

statements.label: prop:global-limits
statements.text:
Fix the construction parameters supplied by
Proposition~\ref{prop:global-control}, and let $b_N\to\infty$.
Either the dormant family, or a family of cap solutions at one fixed horizon
$T\in(0,T_0]$, has a subsequence of total densities $F_N$ converging
weakly in $L^1([0,\tau]\times\Omega)$ for every $\tau<\infty$ to a
nonnegative density $F$. This subsequence can be chosen so that
$F_N(t)\rightharpoonup F(t)$ in $L^1(\Omega)$ at every $t\ge0$,
with uniformly small polynomially weighted velocity tails on each
bounded time interval.

The limit has initial datum $F_0$ and is a global entropy solution
obeying local conservation in the sense of
Definition~\ref{def:admissible}. More precisely,
\begin{equation}
 F\in C([0,\infty);L^1(\Omega)),\qquad
 \int_0^\tau\!\int_\Omega
 \langle v\rangle^k\bigl(F+Q^+(F,F)+Q^-(F,F)\bigr)
 \dd x\dd v\dd t<\infty
 \quad(k\ge0,\ \tau<\infty).
\end{equation}
Total mass, momentum, and energy are conserved at every time.
The common early-time pointwise majorant of the dormant approximations
also bounds any dormant limit.

statements.label: prop:blowup-limit
statements.text:
Every sequence \eqref{eq:rescaling} has a subsequence for which
\(h_{r_N}\rightharpoonup g\) in local spacetime \(L^1\) on
\((0,U)\times\R^3_x\times\R^3_v\), where
\begin{equation}
0\leq g(t,x,v)\leq(t+l)H(v),\qquad
\D g=2P(B,g)-g\nu_B.
\end{equation}
Here \(B\) is \eqref{eq:background}; its gain and loss are defined by
integration against the velocity measure. Both terms on the right are
locally integrable, with a velocity majorant uniform in position on
each compact positive-time interval. Compactly supported velocity
averages of \(h_{r_N}\) converge strongly in local \(L^1_{t,x}\).
The limit has a locally strongly continuous \(L^1\) representative
at positive times and obeys the integrating-factor formula
\eqref{dil:mild} below.

If \(l>0\), pass also to a limit \(\lambda_N\to\lambda_0\) of the
seed parameters. The conclusion and its local continuity extend to
time zero, with
\begin{equation}
g(0,x,v)=\lambda_0 l\,\chi(x/l,v).
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: The cap dilation and its linear limit

statements.title: Nonvanishing of every cap limit
statements.label: prop:nonzero-limit
statements.text:
Consider any sequence of cap solutions with horizons \(T_n\to0\),
approximation indices \(N_n\to\infty\), and
\(s_{N_n}/T_n\to0\).  Make the rescaling
\eqref{eq:rescaling}, and pass to any subsequence supplied by
Proposition~\ref{prop:blowup-limit}.  Its limit satisfies
\[
 g\not\equiv0\qquad\text{on }(0,U)\times\R^3_x\times\R^3_v.
\]
This conclusion includes \(l=1\), \(U=1\), and \(U=\infty\).
statements.section_title: A cap event produces a nonzero limit

statements.label: prop:finite-dilated-horizon
statements.text:
There are fixed choices
\[
K\ge1,\qquad 0<\eta\le\log2,\qquad
0<\alpha\le\tfrac14,\qquad 0<\gamma\le1
\]
with the following property. For every allowed geometric mesh with
lower endpoint \(l\in[0,1]\), the only nonnegative density solving
\eqref{eq:limit-equation} on \(0<t<\infty\), with locally integrable
gain and loss, the positive-time mild formula \eqref{dil:mild}, and the
bound \(g(t,x,v)\le(t+l)H(v)\), is zero.
Consequently every nonzero limit in
Propositions~\ref{prop:blowup-limit} and~\ref{prop:nonzero-limit} has
\(U<\infty\). The four parameters can be fixed before the thermal,
seed, bath, and final horizon parameters of the construction. Their
choice is independent of the mesh phase and of \(l\).

title: Nuclear dimension and Jiang–Su stability without elementary subquotients
abstract: For separable nuclear C∗-algebras with no nonzero elementary ideal subquotients, finite nuclear dimension is equivalent to Jiang–Su stability. More generally, \(\dim_{\mathrm{nuc}}(A_0\otimes\mathcal Z)\le1\) for every separable nuclear A0. This proves Robert and Tikuisis's Conjecture (C1) and the nuclear-dimension equivalence in the nonsimple Toms–Winter regularity question.

tex.abstract:
For separable nuclear $C^*$-algebras with no nonzero elementary ideal
subquotients, finite nuclear dimension is equivalent to Jiang--Su
stability. More generally, $\dim_{\mathrm{nuc}}(A_0\otimes\mathcal Z)\le1$
for every separable nuclear $A_0$. This proves Robert and Tikuisis's
Conjecture (C1) and the nuclear-dimension equivalence in the nonsimple
Toms--Winter regularity question.

statements.label: thm:main

statements.title: Regularity and Cuntz-semigroup criteria
statements.label: cor:regularity-cu
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, let
$\iota_A:A\to A\otimes\Z$ be $\iota_A(a)=a\otimes1_\Z$.
The conditions of that theorem are also equivalent to each of the following:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item the canonical map $\Cu(\iota_A):\Cu(A)\to\Cu(A\otimes\Z)$ is
an isomorphism in $\mathbf{Cu}$;
\item there is an abstract isomorphism $\Cu(A)\cong\Cu(A\otimes\Z)$
in $\mathbf{Cu}$.
\end{enumerate}
The abstract isomorphism need not be induced by a $*$-homomorphism.

statements.title: Sharp bound after Jiang--Su absorption
statements.label: intro:main
statements.text:
For every separable nuclear complex $C^*$-algebra $A_0$,
\[
 \nucdim(A_0\otimes\Z)\le1.
\]

statements.title: Full signs in a finite maximal tensor power
statements.label: thm:tensor-intro
statements.text:
For every nonzero unital complex $C^*$-algebra $D$ with no characters,
there is a finite integer $n\ge1$ such that
$D^{\otimes_{\max}n}$ contains two full orthogonal positive elements.

statements.title: Brown--Carri\'on--White
statements.label: prelim:bcw
statements.text:
For every separable nuclear $D$ there are finite-dimensional algebras
$F_n$ and c.p.c. maps
\[
 D\xrightarrow{\alpha_n}F_n\xrightarrow{\beta_n}D
\]
such that $\beta_n\alpha_n\to\id_D$ in point-norm,
$\|\alpha_n(a)\alpha_n(b)\|\to0$ for orthogonal $a,b\in D_+$, and
each $\beta_n$ is a finite convex combination of c.p.c. order-zero maps
$F_n\to D$.

statements.title: R\o rdam's comparison criterion
statements.label: prelim:comparison
statements.text:
If $D\cong D\otimes\Z$, then $W(D)$ is almost unperforated.
More generally, if $W(D)$ is almost unperforated, $u,v\in D_+$,
$u\in\Ideal_D(v)$, and
\[
 d([u])<d([v])\quad\text{for every dimension function $d$ with }d([v])=1,
\]
then $u\precsim v$.

statements.title: Gabe's approximate domination theorem
statements.label: prelim:domination
statements.text:
Let $D$ be exact and let $\Phi,\Psi:D\to E$ be nuclear completely
positive maps, with $\Psi$ of order zero.  Suppose
\[
 \Phi(a)\in\Ideal_E(\Psi(a))\qquad(a\in D_+).
\]
For every finite $\mathcal F\subset D$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there are
$y_1,\ldots,y_N\in E$ such that
\[
 \left\|\Phi(a)-\sum_{l=1}^Ny_l^*\Psi(a)y_l\right\|<\varepsilon
 \qquad(a\in\mathcal F).
\]

statements.title: Localized comparison
statements.label: trace:comparison
statements.text:
There is a sequence $m(n)\geq2$ with $m(n)\to_\omega\infty$ such
that, on putting
\[
 P_n=D_{m(n)}\in\Z_2,\qquad P=(P_n)_\omega\in B,
 \qquad
 \Psi(a)=P(q-1/2)_+\pi(a),
\]
the map $\Psi\colon A\to B$ is c.p.c. order zero and, for every
$j\geq1$,
\begin{equation}
 e\pi(x_j),\ e\theta(x_j)
 \precsim (\Psi(a_j)-c_j)_+
 \quad\text{in }B,
 \qquad c_j=\gamma_j/64.
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: The common part and localized trace comparison

statements.title: A supporting map preserving ideals
statements.label: support:map
statements.text:
There is a c.p.c. order-zero map $\widehat\theta\colon A\to B$
whose range commutes with the constant copy of $\Z_3$ and such that
\begin{align}
 h\widehat\theta(a)=\widehat\theta(a)h&=\theta(a),
       \qquad a\in A,\\
 [e,\widehat\theta(a)]&=0,
 \qquad q\widehat\theta(a)=q\pi(a),\qquad a\in A,
       \\
 e\widehat\theta(a'),\ e\pi(a')&\in\Ideal_B(\Psi(a')),
       \qquad a'\in A_+.
       
\end{align}

statements.title: Packing the error part
statements.label: comm:packing
statements.text:
For $i\in\{0,1\}$ and every positive contraction $c\in C_i$,
\begin{align}
 m[(c^{1/2}ec^{1/2})^{(i)}]&\leq[Q_0],
       &&m\in\N,\\
 [c^{(i)}]&\leq2[Q_0]
       &&\text{in }W(C).
\end{align}
statements.section_title: The supporting map and its relative commutant

statements.label: comm:fullness
statements.text:
The elements $Q_0,Q_1$ and $H$ are full in $C$, and $C$ is full
in $M_2(B)$.
statements.section_title: The supporting map and its relative commutant

statements.label: comm:unperforated
statements.text: The ordered semigroup $W(C)$ is almost unperforated.
statements.section_title: The supporting map and its relative commutant

statements.label: conjugacy:hereditary
statements.text:
Let $D\subset C$ be a full hereditary subalgebra.  Suppose that
$y\in D$ and that totally full positive elements $e_l,e_r\in D$
satisfy
\[
 e_l y=ye_r=0.
\]
Then there is a full element $s\in D$ with $sy=ys=0$.
statements.section_title: The supporting map and its relative commutant

statements.label: conjugacy:functions
statements.text:
The elements $h_0,h_1$ are totally full in $C$.  For every
$g\in C_0((0,1])_+$, the elements $g(h_0)$ and $g(h_1)$ are
Cuntz equivalent in $C$.
statements.section_title: The supporting map and its relative commutant

statements.title: Weighted unitary equivalence
statements.label: conjugacy:weighted
statements.text:
Put $k^{[0]}=k$ and $k^{[1]}=1-k$, in the constant third leg.
There are unitaries $U_0,U_1\in M_2(B)$ such that
\begin{equation}
 U_i\bigl(k^{[i]}\theta(a)\bigr)^{(1)}U_i^*
   =\bigl(k^{[i]}\pi(a)\bigr)^{(0)},
 \qquad a\in A,\quad i=0,1.
\end{equation}
They can be chosen to commute with $\rho(A)$.
statements.section_title: The supporting map and its relative commutant

statements.title: Two-colour corner approximation
statements.label: end:corner
statements.text:
Let $A$ be a nonzero separable unital nuclear $C^*$-algebra and put
$R=A\otimes\Z^{\otimes3}$. For every finite $\mathcal F\subset A$
and $\varepsilon>0$, the map
\[
 \kappa_A:A\longrightarrow M_2(R),\qquad
 \kappa_A(a)=\begin{pmatrix}a\otimes1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}
\]
admits a finite-dimensional approximation with two colours:
there are a finite-dimensional algebra $F$, a c.p.c. map
$\alpha:A\to F$, and c.p.c. order-zero maps
$\varphi_0,\varphi_1:F\to M_2(R)$ such that
\[
 \|\varphi_0\alpha(a)+\varphi_1\alpha(a)-\kappa_A(a)\|
 <\varepsilon\qquad(a\in\mathcal F).
\]

statements.title: Winter--Zacharias and Robert--Tikuisis
statements.label: thm:imports
statements.text:
Let \(A\ne0\) be separable with \(\nucdim A\leq d<\infty\).
\begin{enumerate}
\item If no hereditary subalgebra of \(A\) has a finite-dimensional
irreducible representation, then there are finitely many finite-dimensional
algebras $E_j$, completely positive order-zero maps
$\varphi_j:E_j\to F(A)$, and elements $c_j\in F(A)$ such that every
matrix summand of every $E_j$ has size at least two and
\[
 1_{F(A)}=\sum_jc_j^*\varphi_j(1_{E_j})c_j.
\]
This is the matrix-threshold-two consequence of the covering-number
bound $\operatorname{cov}(F(A))\le(d+1)^2$
\cite[Definition~4.1 and Proposition~4.3]{WZNuclear}.
\item If \(F(A)\) contains two full orthogonal positive elements, then \(A\cong A\otimes_{\min}\Z\) \cite[Theorem 1.2]{RT}.
\end{enumerate}
Both assertions apply to nonunital \(A\), with the annihilator quotient just defined.

title: Numerical Semiampleness of Nef Adjoint Divisors
abstract: We prove the Generalised Abundance Conjecture: if \((X,B)\) is a projective klt ℚ-pair over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, \(K_X+B\) is pseudo-effective, M is a nef ℚ-Cartier divisor on X, and \(K_X+B+M\) is nef, then \(K_X+B+M\) is numerically equivalent to a semiample ℚ-Cartier divisor on X.

tex.abstract:
We prove the Generalised Abundance Conjecture: if $(X,B)$ is a projective
klt $\Q$-pair over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero,
$K_X+B$ is pseudo-effective, $M$ is a nef $\Q$-Cartier divisor on $X$,
and $K_X+B+M$ is nef, then $K_X+B+M$ is numerically equivalent to a
semiample $\Q$-Cartier divisor on $X$.

statements.text:
Let $(X,B)$ be a projective klt $\Q$-pair over an algebraically closed

statements.label: input:models
statements.text:
Let $(X,B+\mathbf M)$ be a projective generalized klt $\Q$-pair over $\C$,
with $X$ $\Q$-factorial and with fixed nef rational Cartier b-divisor
data. If $K_X+B+M_X$ is pseudo-effective, there is a terminating choice
of its minimal-model program, with $\Q$-factorial generalized klt
models and a nef endpoint. The program extracts no divisors and
generalized log discrepancies do not decrease. On a common resolution
of its initial and final models, the pullback of the initial adjoint
is the pullback of the final adjoint plus an effective divisor
exceptional over the final model.

statements.label: prop:full-positive
statements.text:
Assume $(P_j)$ for $j<n$.  Let $(X,B)$ be a projective klt
$\Q$-pair of dimension $n$, let $T=K_X+B$ be pseudo-effective, and
let $M$ be a nef $\Q$-Cartier divisor on $X$.  If
\eqref{eq:full-condition} holds and $\kappa(X,T)>0$, then $T+cM$ is
big for every $c\in\Q_{>0}$.
statements.section_title: Reduction of full nef dimension to Calabi--Yau pairs

statements.label: prop:reduction-cy
statements.text:
Assume $(P_j)$ for $j<n$.  Suppose that on every projective klt
$\Q$-pair $(V,\Delta)$ of dimension $n$ with
$K_V+\Delta\equiv0$, every nef $\Q$-Cartier divisor of full nef
dimension is big.  Then $(P_n)$ holds.
statements.section_title: Reduction of full nef dimension to Calabi--Yau pairs

statements.label: thm:terminal-big
statements.text:
Let $n\ge2$, and assume $(P_j)$ for $j<n$. Let $X$ be a projective
$\Q$-factorial terminal complex variety of dimension $n$ with
$K_X\sim0$. If $L$ is a nef Cartier divisor on $X$ with full nef
dimension, then $L$ is big.
statements.section_title: Jets on a terminal variety with trivial canonical class

statements.label: prop:large-seshadri
statements.text:
For a suitable fixed positive integer $q$, and all sufficiently
small $t$ in \eqref{eq:scaling}, there is a smooth point $z\in Z$
in the torus open, lying over smooth points of both factors, such
that
\begin{equation}
                         \varepsilon(R;z)>2n+2.
\end{equation}
More generally, for any prescribed dense open subsets $U_1,U_2$
of the smooth locus of $X$, the point may be chosen over
$U_1\times U_2$. In particular, these opens may be the
isomorphism loci of fixed resolutions of $X$.
statements.section_title: Jets on a terminal variety with trivial canonical class

statements.title: Finite-data Frobenius incompatibility
statements.label: thm:finite-data
statements.text:
Let $W$ be a smooth connected projective complex variety of
dimension $n\ge2$. Let $D,H$ be rational Cartier divisors, with
$H$ ample, let $S$ be an integral Cartier divisor, and fix an
integer $q>0$ and real numbers $r>1$, $\epsilon>0$. Suppose
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
 H^n\le(2\epsilon)^n,\qquad
 K_WH^{n-1}\le2H^n/r,\qquad
 (2D+qS)H^{n-1}\le4H^n,\\
 (14\epsilon)^n<\tfrac14,\qquad 80\epsilon<\tfrac34.
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
Assume that the following fixed data exist.
\begin{enumerate}
\renewcommand{\labelenumi}{\textup{(\roman{enumi})}}
\item A smooth integral complete-intersection flag from $W$ to
a curve $C$, whose successive divisor classes are $h_i=l_iH$
for fixed positive integers $l_i$ for which $l_iH$ is Cartier, with
$\mu_{\min}(\Omega_W^1|_C)\ge0$.
\item On the projective bundle
\[
 Z=\PP\bigl(\mathcal O_W(S)_1\oplus
                         \mathcal O_W(S)_2\bigr)\longrightarrow W\times W,
 \qquad \xi=c_1(\mathcal O_Z(1)),\qquad M=D_1+D_2+q\xi,
\]
use the convention that the direct image of $\mathcal O_Z(a\xi)$
is the $a$-th symmetric power of the displayed sum for $a\ge0$;
subscripts indicate pullback from the corresponding factor of
$W\times W$. The two axes are the sections defined by the two
summands. A smooth point $z_*$ in their complement and finitely many
sections of $k_0M$, for some integer $k_0>0$ with $k_0D$ Cartier,
generate jets through order $(2n+2)k_0$ at $z_*$.
\item A point $x\in W$, its blowup
$\pi_x:\widehat W\to W$ with exceptional divisor $J$, and a
curve class
\[
 \gamma=f_*(A_1\cdots A_{n-1}),
\]
where $f:V\to\widehat W$ is one fixed birational morphism,
$V$ is smooth integral projective, and the $A_i$ are ample
integral Cartier divisors, such that $J\cdot\gamma>0$ and
\begin{equation}
 \pi_x^*(D+K_W/2+\lambda S)\cdot\gamma
 \le40\epsilon J\cdot\gamma\qquad(0\le\lambda\le q).
\end{equation}
It suffices to check the two endpoints in this affine inequality.
\end{enumerate}
These data cannot coexist.

statements.label: prop:full-all
statements.text:
Let $n\geq 2$, and assume $(P_j)$ for every $j<n$, together with
Theorems~\ref{input:abundance}
and~\ref{input:models}.  Let $(X,B)$ be a projective klt $\Q$-pair over
$\C$ of dimension $n$, and let $M$ be a nef $\Q$-Cartier divisor on $X$.
Suppose that $T=K_X+B$ is pseudo-effective and that, for some rational
$a>0$,
\[
  (T+aM)\cdot C>0
\]
for every integral curve $C$ through a very general point of $X$.
Then $T+cM$ is big for every rational $c>0$.

statements.label: prop:positive-part
statements.text:
For every projective klt $\Q$-pair $(X,B)$ over $\C$ with
$K_X+B$ pseudo-effective and every nef $\Q$-Cartier divisor $M$ on
$X$, there is a smooth projective birational model $w\colon W\to X$
such that
\[
                     P_\sigma\bigl(w^*(K_X+B+M)\bigr)
\]
is rational and numerically equivalent to a semiample $\Q$-divisor.

title: Numerical semiampleness of nef adjoint classes on compact Kähler manifolds
Numerical semiampleness of nef adjoint classes on compact Kähler manifolds
abstract: Let X be a smooth connected compact Kähler manifold, let B be an effective rational simple normal crossing divisor with coefficients less than one, and let M be a nef rational holomorphic line bundle on X. If \(K_X+B\) is pseudo-effective and \(K_X+B+M\) is nef, we prove that its first Chern class in real Bott–Chern cohomology is represented by a semiample rational line bundle. This numerical statement allows a flat change of line bundle; it does not assert semiampleness of the original adjoint.
version_note: This version states the Iitaka, model, and contraction inputs used in the divisorial-decomposition argument explicitly; see the [previous version](../Numerical-semiampleness-of-nef-adjoint-classes-on-compact-Kahler-manifolds-October-4-2026/numerical-generalized-abundance.pdf).

tex.abstract:
Let \(X\) be a smooth connected compact K\"ahler manifold, let \(B\) be an
effective rational simple normal crossing divisor with coefficients less
than one, and let \(M\) be a nef rational holomorphic line bundle on \(X\).
If \(K_X+B\) is pseudo-effective and \(K_X+B+M\) is nef, we prove that its
first Chern class in real Bott--Chern cohomology is represented by a semiample
rational line bundle. This numerical statement allows a flat change of line
bundle; it does not assert semiampleness of the original adjoint.
sections: Descent of nef and flat lines
An ordinary adjoint on the projective base
Nef classes in algebraic dimension zero
The nef summand on the algebraic-reduction fibers

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let \(X\) be a smooth connected compact K\"ahler manifold, let
\(B\geq0\) be a rational simple normal crossing divisor whose
coefficients are strictly less than one, and let
\(M\in\Pic(X)\otimes_{\Z}\Q\).
Assume that \(K_X+B\) is pseudo-effective, \(M\) is nef, and
\(D=K_X+B+M\) is nef. Then there is a semiample rational line bundle
\(L\) on \(X\) such that
\[
 c_1(L)=c_1(D)\quad\text{in }H^{1,1}_{\mathrm{BC}}(X,\R).
\]

statements.label: thm:decomposition
statements.text:
Let \(T\) be a smooth connected compact K\"ahler manifold, \(B\geq0\)
a rational simple normal crossing divisor with coefficients less than
one, and \(M\) a nef rational line bundle. Suppose
\(J=K_T+B\) is pseudo-effective. There are a smooth compact K\"ahler
modification \(\mu:U\to T\), a semiample rational line \(P\) on \(U\),
and an effective rational divisor \(R\) on \(U\), such that
\[
 \mu^*(J+M)\num P+R,\qquad
 R=N\bigl(c_1(\mu^*(J+M))\bigr).
\]
Here \(\num\) denotes equality of real Chern classes.
Moreover, if \(a(T)=0\), then \(c_1(M)=0\).

statements.title: Ordinary divisorial decomposition
statements.label: pre:ordinary
statements.text:
Let \(X\) be a smooth compact K\"ahler manifold, and let \(B\) be a
rational simple normal crossing divisor with coefficients in \([0,1]\).
If \(J=K_X+B\) is pseudo-effective, there is a smooth compact K\"ahler
modification \(\mu:U\to X\) and an identity
\[
 \mu^*J\qsim P+R,\qquad P\text{ semiample},\qquad
 R=N(\mu^*J)\geq0,
\]
where \(P\) is a rational line and \(R\) is a rational divisor.

statements.title: Contraction of a known negative part
statements.label: pre:contract
statements.text:
Let \((X,B)\) be a smooth compact K\"ahler klt pair with rational
simple normal crossing boundary. Suppose
\[
 K_X+B\qsim P+R,\qquad P\text{ semiample},\qquad
 R=N(K_X+B)\geq0
\]
with \(P,R\) rational. A finite ordinary \((K_X+B)\)-negative program
reaches a normal compact K\"ahler klt model on which the log canonical
line is semiample. Its steps contract or flip detected analytic extremal
rays, are \(P\)-trivial, and preserve a fixed generated Cartier multiple
of \(P\) as an actual line. The final adjoint is rationally linearly
equivalent to the descended semiample line. The steps extract no
divisors; on a common resolution the initial adjoint equals the
pullback of the final adjoint plus an effective divisor exceptional
over the final model.

statements.title: Projective positive parts
statements.label: pre:projective
statements.text:
Let \((S,\Delta)\) be a normal projective klt pair with rational boundary,
and let \(M\) be a nef rational Cartier divisor. Suppose
\(K_S+\Delta\) is pseudo-effective.
There is a smooth projective modification \(u:S'\to S\), a birational
morphism \(v:S'\to S_m\) to a normal projective variety, a nef rational
Cartier divisor \(H_m\) on \(S_m\), and an effective rational
\(v\)-exceptional divisor \(E\), such that
\begin{equation}
 u^*(K_S+\Delta+M)\qsim v^*H_m+E.
\end{equation}
On a sufficiently high such model, \(v^*H_m\) is numerically equivalent
to a semiample rational divisor and
\[
 N\bigl(u^*(K_S+\Delta+M)\bigr)=E.
\]

statements.title: Numerical descent of a nef line
statements.label: desc:nef
statements.text:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a fibration of smooth connected compact K\"ahler
manifolds, and let $M\in\Pic(X)\otimes\Q$ be analytically nef.
Suppose that $c_1(M|_{X_y})=0$ on a general smooth fiber.
There are smooth compact K\"ahler modifications $p:X'\to X$ and
$q:Y'\to Y$, a fibration $g:X'\to Y'$ satisfying $fp=qg$, and a
rational line $N$ on $Y'$ such that
\begin{equation}
                 p^*M\num g^*N.
\end{equation}
If $Y$ is projective, $Y'$ can be chosen projective and $N$ is nef.
statements.section_title: Descent of nef and flat lines

statements.title: Choosing a descended representative
statements.label: desc:representative
statements.text:
In the notation and under the hypotheses of
Proposition~\ref{desc:nef}, there is a rational line $M^*$ on $X$
with $M^*\num M$ such that
\[
                          p^*M^*\qsim g^*N.
\]
statements.section_title: Descent of nef and flat lines

statements.title: An adjoint on the base
statements.label: adj:base
statements.text:
Let $(Y,D)$ be an effective klt pair with rational boundary on a normal
compact K\"ahler space.  Let $f:Y\to Z$ be a surjective morphism with connected
fibers to a normal projective variety, and suppose that
$\dim Y>\dim Z$.  If $H$ is a rational Cartier line bundle on $Z$ and
\begin{equation}

                         K_Y+D\qsim f^*H,
\end{equation}
then there is an effective rational divisor $D_Z$ such that $(Z,D_Z)$ is klt
and
\[
                         H\qsim K_Z+D_Z.
\]
statements.section_title: An ordinary adjoint on the projective base

statements.label: zero:vanishing
statements.text:
Let \(n\ge1\).  Assume that the algebraic-dimension-zero assertion of
Theorem~\ref{thm:decomposition} holds in every dimension less than \(n\).
Let \(T\) be a smooth connected compact Kähler \(n\)-fold with
\(a(T)=0\), and let \(B\) be an effective rational simple normal crossing
boundary with coefficients less than one.  If \(K_T+B\) is
pseudo-effective, then every nef rational holomorphic line bundle \(M\)
on \(T\) satisfies \(c_1(M)=0\).
statements.section_title: Nef classes in algebraic dimension zero

statements.label: zero:line-nonvanishing
statements.text:
Let \(X\) be a smooth simple compact Kähler manifold of dimension
\(n\ge2\), with \(a(X)=0\) and irregularity zero.  Assume that the only
positive-dimensional proper compact irreducible analytic subvarieties
through a very general point of \(X^2\) are its factor slices.
Let \(\mathscr L\) be a holomorphic line bundle with pseudo-effective
class \(L\).  Assume the following line-subsheaf bounds:
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every line bundle \(\mathscr H\), every integer \(k\ge0\),
and every nonzero map \(\mathscr H\to\Omega_X^{\otimes k}\), one has
\(c_1(\mathscr H)\le kL\).
\item Outside a countable union of proper analytic subsets of \(X\),
every point \(x\) has this property: if
\(a:Y=\operatorname{Bl}_xX\to X\), then for every line bundle
\(\mathscr H_Y\), every \(k\ge0\), and every nonzero map
\(\mathscr H_Y\to(a^*\Omega_X)^{\otimes k}\), one has
\(c_1(\mathscr H_Y)\le ka^*L\).
\end{enumerate}
Then some positive power of \(\mathscr L\) has a nonzero meromorphic
section.
statements.section_title: Nef classes in algebraic dimension zero

statements.label: zero:slope-descent
statements.text:
Let \(Y\) be a smooth compact Kähler manifold and \(\mathscr E\) a
holomorphic vector bundle of rank at least two.  Write
\(\pi_{\mathscr E}:\mathbb{P}_Y(\mathscr E)\to Y\) and
\(\zeta_{\mathscr E}=c_1(\cO_{\mathbb{P}(\mathscr E)}(1))\).
Suppose that a real class \(D\) on \(Y\) satisfies
\[
 c_1(\mathscr H)\le kD
 \quad\text{whenever}\quad
 0\ne\bigl(\mathscr H\longrightarrow\mathscr E^{\otimes k}\bigr)
\]
for a line bundle \(\mathscr H\) and integer \(k\ge0\).
For a real class \(A\) on \(Y\) and a real number \(b\ge0\),
\begin{equation}
 \pi_{\mathscr E}^*A+b\zeta_{\mathscr E}\ge0
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad A+bD\ge0 .
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Nef classes in algebraic dimension zero

statements.label: zero:simple-vanishing
statements.text:
Let \(X\) be a smooth simple compact Kähler manifold of algebraic
dimension zero carrying a generically nondegenerate holomorphic
two-form.  Every nef rational holomorphic line bundle on \(X\) has zero
first Chern class.
statements.section_title: Nef classes in algebraic dimension zero

statements.label: cycle:nef-summand
statements.text:
Assume Theorem~\ref{thm:decomposition} in dimensions less than $n$.
Let $T$ be a smooth connected compact K\"ahler $n$-fold with
$0<a(T)<n$, and let $h:T\to W$ be a holomorphic algebraic reduction
with smooth projective base and connected fibers.  Let $B$ be an
effective rational SNC divisor with coefficients less than one,
assume that $J=K_T+B$ is pseudo-effective, and let $M$ be a nef
rational line bundle.  Then
\[
                              c_1(M|_F)=0
\]
for a general smooth fiber $F$ of $h$.
statements.section_title: The nef summand on the algebraic-reduction fibers

statements.label: cycle:base-descent
statements.text:
Under the assumptions of Proposition~\ref{cycle:nef-summand},
there are modifications $p:T'\to T$ and $b:W'\to W$, with
$T'$ smooth compact K\"ahler and $W'$ smooth projective, a
fibration $h':T'\to W'$ lifting $h$, and a nef rational line
bundle $N$ on $W'$ such that
\[
                              p^*M\num(h')^*N.
\]
statements.section_title: The nef summand on the algebraic-reduction fibers

statements.label: finish:over-base
statements.text:
Let \(T\) be a smooth compact K\"ahler manifold of dimension \(n\), let
\((T,B)\) be a rational simple normal crossing klt pair with
\(J=K_T+B\) pseudo-effective, and let
\(h:T\to W\) be a surjective morphism to a smooth projective variety.
There are a smooth compact K\"ahler modification \(T_1\to T\), an
effective klt adjoint \(J_1\) on \(T_1\) as in
\eqref{pre:resolution-error}, and a finite ordinary \(J_1\)-negative
program over \(W\), ending at a normal compact K\"ahler klt pair
\((Y,\Delta)\), such that for some positive integer \(b\) and an ample
Cartier divisor \(A_W\) on \(W\),
\[
 K_Y+\Delta+b h_Y^*A_W
\]
is semiample. Here \(h_Y:Y\to W\) is the descended morphism.

title: One Rational Matrix Hitting Point for Noncommutative Formulas
abstract: We construct, in deterministic polynomial bit time, one tuple of rational matrices that detects every nonzero polynomial computed by a noncommutative division-free formula of a prescribed size. The matrices have dimension \(O(ns^2)\) for n variables and formula size s, and the same tuple works over every field of characteristic zero.

tex.abstract:
We construct, in deterministic polynomial bit time, one tuple of rational
matrices that detects every nonzero polynomial computed by a noncommutative
division-free formula of a prescribed size. The matrices have dimension $O(ns^2)$ for
$n$ variables and formula size $s$, and the same tuple works over every
field of characteristic zero.
sections: A faithful encoding by iterated integrals
A bound on the order of vanishing

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is a deterministic algorithm which, given integers $n,s\ge1$,
constructs a tuple
\[
 \mathbf T_{n,s}\in\Mat_d(\Q)^n,
 \qquad d\le 2ns^2,
\]
in time polynomial in $n,s$, measured in bit operations. The numerators and
denominators of its entries have bit length
$O(\log(ns+1)+ns^2\log(n+1))$.
For every field $F$ of characteristic zero and every
$0\ne f\in\mathsf{Form}_{n,s}(F)$,
\[
 f(\mathbf T_{n,s})\ne0,
\]
where the tuple is viewed over $F$ through the canonical embedding
$\Q\hookrightarrow F$. The construction uses $d=2ns^2$ when $ns\ge2$
and $d=1$ when $n=s=1$.

statements.title: Multiplicity estimate of Moura
statements.label: thm:multiplicity
statements.text:
Let $F$ be a field of characteristic zero, and let $n,m\ge1$.
Suppose that $q\in F[z]$ has degree $n$ and $q(0)\ne0$, that
$P\in\operatorname{Mat}_m(F[z])$ has entries of degree at most $n-1$,
and that
\[
 G\in\operatorname{GL}_m(F[[z]]),\qquad G'=(P/q)G.
\]
For a constant row $u\in F^{1\times m}$ and a constant column
$v\in F^{m\times1}$, if $y=uGv$ is nonzero, then
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{ord}_0 y\le(n-1)\binom{m}{2}+m-1.
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: A bound on the order of vanishing

statements.label: prop:path-programs
statements.text:
For every pair of integers $n,m\ge1$,
the matrices in
\eqref{eq:explicit-matrices}, with
\[
 d=(n-1)\binom m2+m,
\]
form a rational hitting point for the following class over every
characteristic-zero field $F$: nonzero polynomials
$f=\sum_w f_wx_w\in F\langle x_1,\ldots,x_n\rangle$ whose coefficients admit
a representation $f_w=uB_wv$, where $u\in F^{1\times m}$,
$v\in F^{m\times1}$, and $B_1,\ldots,B_n\in\Mat_m(F)$ are strictly upper
triangular. The tuple depends only on $n,m$ and can be constructed in time
polynomial in $n,m$, measured in bit operations.

title: One Sample Suffices for Matroid Prophet Inequalities against an Almighty Adversary
abstract: We prove that one independent sample per element suffices for a constant-competitive prophet inequality on every finite matroid. The guarantee holds even when the arrival-order adversary observes all samples, all online values, and the algorithm's entire random seed. The rule needs no description of the value distributions and achieves the absolute competitive ratio \(2^{-310}\).

tex.abstract: We prove that one independent sample per element suffices for a constant-competitive prophet inequality on every finite matroid. The guarantee holds even when the arrival-order adversary observes all samples, all online values, and the algorithm's entire random seed. The rule needs no description of the value distributions and achieves the absolute competitive ratio $2^{-310}$.
sections: From safe samples to unobserved rank
Rank and payoff for every arrival order

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is a measurable online selection rule, independent of the value
distributions, with the following property. Let $M=(E,\mathcal I)$ be any
finite known labeled matroid, and let $(S_e,V_e:e\in E)$ be mutually
independent nonnegative real random variables, with $S_e$ and $V_e$ having
the same arbitrary law $D_e$. Assume
$\Ex[\OPT_M(V)]<\infty$. The rule receives exactly the sample vector $S$
before arrivals and uses a seed $R$ independent of $S,V$.

For every measurable permutation rule $\pi$ depending on $M$, the laws
$(D_e)$, $S$, $V$, and $R$, the rule accepts an independent set $A$,
irrevocably deciding at each arrival using only the available history, and
\begin{equation}
 \Ex\left[\sum_{e\in A}V_e\right]
       \ge 2^{-310}\Ex[\OPT_M(V)].
\end{equation}

statements.label: prop:hidden
statements.text:
There is a measurable rule in the fixed-vector formulation that is feasible for every
realization and every permutation, and for every $w\in[0,\infty)^E$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \Ex_R\left[\min_{\pi}\sum_{e\in A(w,R,\pi)}w_e\right]
 \ge 2^{-293}\OPT_M(w).
\end{equation}
Its revealed mask is selected before any weights are seen.

statements.title: Order-oblivious selection with full-seed visibility
statements.label: cor:secretary
statements.text:
For each known finite labeled matroid $M=(E,\mathcal I)$, there is one
measurable randomized online rule $\mathcal S_M$ with the following
property. Fix any vector $w\in[0,\infty)^E$ of finite nonnegative weights
before all rule and arrival randomness. Without knowing $w$, the rule
draws its complete initial seed $Q$, independently of a uniformly random
permutation $\sigma$ of $E$, and fixes a possibly random prefix length
$K$ before any arrival. It observes the first $K$ label--weight pairs of
$\sigma$ in order and rejects those labels.

After this ordered prefix is observed and before any suffix arrival, an
adversary may know $M$, the entire fixed vector $w$, the ordered prefix,
and the complete seed $Q$, including $K$, the branch choice, and unused
coins. It may choose any
measurable permutation $\tau$ of the remaining labels as a function of
this information. The rule is not told the future suffix order and decides
irrevocably at each suffix arrival while maintaining an independent set.
Writing $A_{\mathcal S}$ for its accepted set, for every such adversary,
\begin{equation}
 \Ex\left[\sum_{e\in A_{\mathcal S}}w_e\right]
 \ge 2^{-293}\OPT_M(w).
\end{equation}
The expectation is over the rule seed and random prefix, and over any
adversary randomization. The adversary cannot alter the random-prefix law
or choose the weights after observing the seed or prefix.
