title: Petty’s projection-volume conjecture in dimensions at least four
abstract: We prove that ellipsoids uniquely minimize the volume of the projection body among convex bodies of fixed volume in every dimension at least four. This proves Petty's projection-volume conjecture in these dimensions.

tex.abstract:
We prove that ellipsoids uniquely minimize the volume of the projection body
among convex bodies of fixed volume in every dimension at least four.
This proves Petty's projection-volume conjecture in these dimensions.

statements.title: First variation of volume
statements.label: cor:volume-first-variation
statements.text:
Let $K,M\subset\R^n$ be convex bodies, with the origin interior to
$K$.  Then
\begin{align}
 \left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{0+}|K+tM|
 &=n\kappa_n\E\!\left[g_K(u)^{-n}
                 h_M\bigl(\nabla g_K(u)\bigr)\right]
                 \\
 &\ge n|K|^{(n-1)/n}|M|^{1/n}.\nonumber
\end{align}
Equality in the inequality holds if and only if $K$ and $M$ are
homothetic up to translation.  The derivative identity remains valid
when $M$ is an arbitrary nonempty compact convex set.

thm:norm-estimate
statements.text:
Let $g$ be a norm on $\R^n$, where $n\ge4$, normalized by
$\E g^{-n}=1$ on $\Sph$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 c_{n,k}\|Q(g^k)\|_2^2
 \le (\E g^k)^2-(\E g^{k-1})^2.
\end{equation}
The inequality is strict unless $g=1$ on $\Sph$.

statements.label: thm:bilinear
statements.text:
Let $\eta,\zeta$ be finite positive measures on $\R^n$ with bounded,
spanning support. Suppose that both satisfy
\eqref{eq:functional-condition}. Then
\begin{equation}
 \iint |x\cdot y|\,d\eta(x)d\zeta(y)\ge b_n.
\end{equation}
If equality holds, there is an origin-centered ellipsoid $E_0$ such that
\[
 \int h_{E_0}\,d\eta=(|E_0|/\kappa_n)^{1/n}.
\]

statements.title: Holmes--Thompson isoperimetry
statements.label: cor:holmes-thompson
statements.text:
Let $n\ge3$, let $B=-B\subset\R^n$ be the unit ball of a real normed
space, and let $C\subset\R^n$ be a convex body. Write $B^\circ$ for the
polar unit ball and put $I_B=\Pi(B^\circ)/\kappa_{n-1}$. Normalize the
Holmes--Thompson volume and boundary area by
\[
 \mathcal V_B(C)=\frac{|B^\circ|}{\kappa_n}|C|,
 \qquad
 \mathcal A_B(\partial C)=nV(C[n-1],I_B),
\]
where $V(C[n-1],I_B)$ is mixed volume with $n-1$ copies of $C$,
normalized by $V(C[n])=|C|$. Then
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal A_B(\partial C)^n
 \ge n^n\kappa_n\,\mathcal V_B(C)^{n-1}.
\end{equation}
Equality holds if and only if $B$ is an ellipsoid and $C=x+tB$ for some
$x\in\R^n$ and $t>0$.

title: Planar Graph Metrics Embed into L1 with Constant Distortion
abstract: We prove that every finite connected planar graph with arbitrary positive real edge lengths embeds into real L1 with a universal distortion bound. This resolves the planar embedding conjecture positively.

tex.abstract:
We prove that every finite connected planar graph with arbitrary positive
real edge lengths embeds into real $L_1$ with a universal distortion bound.
This resolves the planar embedding conjecture positively.
sections: The main update and a packing bound for secondary seeds
Ordered fields and separation on the two arcs
Preserving charts and assembling the embedding

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is a finite universal constant $C\ge1$ with the following property.
For every finite connected planar graph $G=(V,E)$ with strictly positive real
edge lengths, there exist a measure space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mu)$ and a map
$f:V\to L_1(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mu;\R)$ such that
\[
 d_G(x,y)\le\|f(x)-f(y)\|_1\le C d_G(x,y)
 \qquad(x,y\in V).
\]

statements.title: Planar graphs admit column models
statements.label: geo:realization
statements.text:
Every finite connected planar graph with positive edge lengths has an
isometric realization of its geometric edge metric in a noncrossing column
model satisfying the terminal-switch condition.  The added parts of the
model consist of separate infinite tails and do not shorten distances in
the original graph.

statements.title: Thin-band interpolation
statements.label: int:interpolation
statements.text:
Let $0<\zeta<1$, let $E>0$, and set
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
 \delta=E/8,\qquad a_0=10^{-6}\zeta\delta,\qquad
 q=\zeta\delta/20,\\
 \rho_0=\zeta\delta/1000,\qquad
 M=\lceil15/\zeta\rceil+3,\qquad N=6(M+1).
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
Suppose $0<a\le a_0$, and let $p:Y\to\R$ be
$(1-\zeta)$-Lipschitz for $d_J$.  There is a random function
$Q:Y\to\R$, obtained using finitely many independent scalar noises
uniform on $[q,2q]$, with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every realization, $Q$ respects all switches, is
$1$-Lipschitz for $d_J$, and satisfies $|Q(v)-p(v)|\le6\delta<E$.
\item Its pieces use finitely many named atoms of the form
\begin{equation}
 A(v)=C+\varepsilon d_J(k,v),\qquad \varepsilon\in\{-1,1\},\quad k\in Y.
\end{equation}
Each name specifies a source $k$ and sign $\varepsilon$ fixed before the
noises are sampled; the intercept $C$ is random. Whenever the construction
reuses an atom, it retains its name.
\item For a fixed $x\in Y$ and $0<\rho\le\rho_0$, there is a list
$\mathcal A(x,\rho)$ of at most $N$ atom names and sources, determined
without the noises, that contains the name of every atom selected by $Q$ on
$B_{d_J}(x,\rho)$.  Except on an event of probability at most
\begin{equation}
 \frac{N^2}{q}(8\rho+\eta),
\end{equation}
one named atom is selected throughout this ball.
\end{enumerate}
Here $\eta=0$ for continuous uniform noises.  Alternatively, each noise
may be uniform on an equally spaced grid including both endpoints of
$[q,2q]$, and $\eta$ in \eqref{int:probability} may be the largest grid
spacing.  The same conclusions hold for any set of points reached
from $x$ by band paths of length at most $\rho$, including the points
and representatives encountered on those paths.

statements.title: Comparison with other branches
statements.label: int:comparisons
statements.text:
Condition on arbitrary prior data. Let $W$ be the union of a nonempty
family of band paths issuing from a fixed point $x$, each of length at
most $\rho$. The set $W$ and these paths are fixed by the prior data.
Suppose that $Q_1,\ldots,Q_s$ are interpolation constructions, each
on a band component containing all these paths. Their geometries,
inputs, and portals are fixed by the prior data, and their fresh noise
families are mutually independent. The bands and their intrinsic metrics
may differ; each of the specified paths must be permitted in every band.
Denote the constants of $Q_i$ in \eqref{int:constants} by
$q_i,N_i,\rho_{0,i}$.

Allow inputs $c_i+\varepsilon_iQ_i$, with
$\varepsilon_i\in\{-1,1\}$ and $c_i$ fixed by the prior data.
Also allow one fixed branch $f$ and $t$ branches $g_j+\beta_j$,
where $f$ and the $g_j$ are fixed functions whose restrictions to each
specified path, parametrized by arclength, are $L$-Lipschitz. The
$\beta_j$ are fresh independent uniform noises on intervals of length
$w_j>0$, independent also of the interpolation noises. All functions respect the switches used by the paths.
Set
\[
 L_* =\max(1,L),\qquad
 S=1+t+\sum_{i=1}^sN_i,\qquad
 q_* =\min\bigl(\{q_i:1\le i\le s\}\cup
                         \{w_j:1\le j\le t\}\bigr).
\]
Assume that there is at least one randomized input and that
$\rho\le\min_i\rho_{0,i}$ when $s>0$. Any fixed expression formed
from these inputs by finitely many minima and maxima selects one
branch and, for a selected interpolation, one atom throughout $W$,
except with conditional probability at most
\begin{equation}
 \frac{S^2}{q_*}(8L_*\rho+\eta).
\end{equation}
Continuous noises have $\eta=0$; for equally spaced endpoint grids
$\eta$ can be the largest spacing of any noise used here. The
expression uses each interpolation with a single chosen sign and
shift; repeated appearances of that same input are given the same
name.

statements.title: Separation supplied by the main test
statements.label: main:pair-separation
statements.text:
Let $(x,y)$ be an eligible pair satisfying the interior requirements,
$1\le d(x,y)\le2$, and $|s(x)-s(y)|\le E_A$.  If either endpoint
has no descending path, then, conditional on main-update mode,
the independent cell coins give probability at least $1/4$ of
system-A symmetric-difference separation at least $\kappa_A E_A$
at this step.
statements.section_title: The main update and a packing bound for secondary seeds

statements.title: Restricted packing bound
statements.label: pack:bound
statements.text:
Fix a narrow band $J_2$.  In any component of $X_{J_2}$, every
closed $d_{J_2}$-ball of radius $4R$ meets seeds from at most
\begin{equation}
 M_{\mathrm{pack}}=2+\left\lceil1600R/g\right\rceil
 
\end{equation}
groups.  This bound is independent of the graph, the number of
columns, and the history of the construction.
statements.section_title: The main update and a packing bound for secondary seeds

statements.title: Movement and success
statements.label: pad:success
statements.text:
There are constants $M<\infty$ and $b,p>0$ such that the following hold
at every step of scale $r$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item At every point of $X$, in either system, the symmetric-difference
movement of the unrefined set is at most $Mr$.
\item Given any past for which a vertex pair at distance in $[r,2r)$ is
eligible, the step has probability at least $p$ of producing one of these
certificates:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item unrefined symmetric-difference separation at least $br$ in one
system;
\item a non-neighbor tip $e$ and a set of labels of measure at least $br$
in system $A$ on which both pair vertices are active and $e$ is inactive,
with the vertices strictly on opposite sides of that link.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: Preserving charts and assembling the embedding

statements.title: Chart persistence
statements.label: pad:persistence
statements.text:
There exist constants $C_0<\infty$ and $\rho_0>0$ such that the following
holds. Condition on the past at a step of scale $r$. Suppose a fixed
closed ball $B_d(v,\rho r)$ lies in a single old region in each system.
For $0<\rho\le\rho_0$, the probability that this ball is split between
different new regions in either system is at most
\begin{equation}
 C_0(\rho+\eta_0).
\end{equation}
Here $\eta_0$ is the relative mesh allowance from
Section~\ref{sets:setup}.
statements.section_title: Preserving charts and assembling the embedding

statements.title: Fixed almost-embeddable families
statements.label: cor:almost-embeddable
statements.text:
Fix nonnegative integers $g,k,w,a$, and interpret
$\mathrm{AE}(g,(k,w),a)$ exactly as the almost-embeddable family of
Lee and Sidiropoulos~\cite[Theorem~1.7]{LS09}. Let
$h_0=h_0(g,k,w,a)\in\N_0$ be the target treewidth bound and let
$D=D(g,k,w,a)\ge1$ be a finite stochastic distortion bound supplied there.
Put
\[
 \widehat h=\max\{h_0,1\},\qquad
 K(g,k,w,a)=D\max\{C_{\mathrm{pl}},C_{\widehat h+1}\},
\]
where $C_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the constant of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, and
$C_t$ is the companion's constant for bags of cardinality at most
$t\ge2$. Every finite connected simple graph $G$ in this named family,
with strictly positive real edge lengths, admits a map $f$ into a real
$L_1$ space satisfying
\[
 d_G(u,v)\le\|f(u)-f(v)\|_1
 \le K(g,k,w,a)d_G(u,v)\qquad(u,v\in V(G)).
\]
For the same underlying graph, $K(g,k,w,a)$ also bounds the undirected
fractional concurrent flow--cut gap $\phi_*/\lambda_*$ for the finite
nonnegative capacities and demands defined in Section~\ref{intro:flow},
whenever $\lambda_*>0$.

title: Pointwise Multiple Ergodic Averages for Mixing Transformations
abstract: Let T be an invertible mixing probability-preserving transformation. For every integer n ≥ 2 and every fixed tuple of bounded measurable functions, we prove that the consecutive multiple ergodic averages of length n converge almost everywhere to the product of the integrals, as the averaging length tends to infinity through all positive integers. The probability space need not be standard, and no rate of mixing is required.

tex.abstract:
Let $T$ be an invertible mixing probability-preserving transformation.
For every integer $n\ge2$ and every fixed tuple of bounded measurable
functions, we prove that the consecutive multiple ergodic averages of
length $n$ converge almost everywhere to the product of the integrals,
as the averaging length tends to infinity through all positive integers.
The probability space need not be standard, and no rate of mixing is
required.
sections: Selected lengths and their joining laws
Channels and closure under selected laws

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Suppose that $T$ satisfies \eqref{eq:mixing}. For every integer
$n\ge2$ and every fixed $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in L^\infty(\mu)$,
\[
 A_N(f_1,\ldots,f_n)(x)
 \longrightarrow\prod_{j=1}^n\int_X f_j\dd\mu
 \qquad\text{for $\mu$-almost every }x,
\]
as $N$ tends to infinity through all positive integers. The probability
space need not be standard, and no rate of mixing is required.

statements.title: Higher-order mixing, companion input
statements.label: thm:multiple-mixing
statements.text:
Let $T$ be an invertible mixing probability-preserving transformation.
For any fixed $s\ge2$, $g_1,\ldots,g_s\in L^\infty(\mu)$,
and integer times $t_1,\ldots,t_s$,
\[
 \int_X\prod_{j=1}^s g_j(T^{t_j}x)\dd\mu(x)
 \longrightarrow\prod_{j=1}^s\int_Xg_j\dd\mu
 \quad\text{as}\quad
 \min_{i\ne j}|t_i-t_j|\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
For $s=1$ the equality holds for every time.

statements.title: Smooth triple averages, companion input
statements.label: prop:smooth-input
statements.text:
Let $R$ be any invertible probability-preserving transformation, and
let $b_1,b_2,b_3$ be distinct nonzero integers with greatest common
divisor one. For bounded $g_1,g_2,g_3$ and every averaging profile,
\[
 V_k^\varphi(y)=\sum_{l\in\Z}2^{-k}\varphi(l/2^k)
              \prod_{j=1}^3g_j(R^{b_jl}y)
\]
converges almost everywhere as $k\to\infty$. Moreover, for each
$c\in[1,2]$ and $\epsilon>0$ there is such a profile with
\[
 \norm{\varphi-c^{-1}\mathbf1_{(0,c]}}_{L^1(\R)}<\epsilon.
\]

statements.title: Relative structure
statements.label: prop:structure
statements.text:
The following statements hold for standard probability-preserving
systems, without an ergodicity assumption.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Every system $Y$ has a maximal measure-distal factor $W_Y$,
and $Y\to W_Y$ is relatively weakly mixing. Every distal factor
pulls into the maximal distal factor of an extension. Automorphisms
commuting with the transformation preserve $W_Y$.
\item Factors and joinings of distal systems are distal. A distal
system is relatively distal over each of its factors. Distality is
equivalent for a transformation and any of its nonzero integer powers.
\item Relative weak mixing passes to nonzero integer powers. The
conditional product of relatively weakly mixing fibre laws over an
invariant joining of their base laws is relatively weakly mixing
over that joining.
\item A relatively weakly mixing extension and a relatively distal
extension of the same base are relatively disjoint: every invariant
joining identifying their bases is the conditional product over
that base.
\item For a distal transformation $R$, every $d\ge1$, and bounded
$g_1,\ldots,g_d$, the averages
\[
 \frac1N\sum_{l=1}^N\prod_{i=1}^d g_i\circ R^{il}
\]
converge almost everywhere.
\end{enumerate}
For a flow, the maximal distal factor of time one is preserved by
the flow, and its action at every nonzero rational time is distal.

statements.title: Selected joining laws
statements.label: prop:selected-law
statements.text:
Every flow $Y$ over $C$ has a unique probability law $\lambda_Y$ on
$Y^I$ satisfying, for all bounded measurable functions $G_i$ on $Y$,
\begin{equation}
 \int_{Y^I}\prod_{i\in I}G_i(y_i)\,\dd\lambda_Y
 =\lim_{a\to\mathcal U}\int_Y\frac1{N_a(\pi_Yy)}
   \int_0^{N_a(\pi_Yy)}\prod_{i\in I}G_i(S_Y^{it}y)
   \,\dd t\,\dd m_Y(y).
\end{equation}
Its marginals are $m_Y$, and it is invariant under
$(y_i)_i\mapsto(S_Y^{it}y_i)_i$, $t\in\R$.
If $\rho:Y'\to Y$ is an extension over $C$, then
$(\rho^I)_*\lambda_{Y'}=\lambda_Y$.

Countable inverse limits of extensions over $C$ exist in this
category.  The selected law at such a limit projects to the selected
law at every stage.  Pullbacks of the stage selected-law spaces have
dense union in $L^2$ of the limit selected law.

statements.title: Channel closure
statements.label: prop:channel-closure
statements.text:
Let $Y$ be a channel and $b\in I$.  On $\mathsf M_b(Y)$ take
$\pi_Y(y_b)$ as original factor and take every $D_\gamma(y_i)$,
$i\in I$, as an output, in the old group of $\gamma$.
These data make $\mathsf M_b(Y)$ a channel.

statements.label: cor:channel-copied-law
statements.text:
For every channel $Y$, the copied spatial list
$(d_Y(y_i))_{i\in I}$ under $\lambda_Y$ has its full product law
conditional on $P=(\omega_Y(y_i))_{i\in I}$.

statements.title: Tensor packing
statements.label: thm:packing
statements.text:
There is a universal constant $C$ with the following property.  Let
$0<\varepsilon\le1$, and let $d\ge1$ and $L\ge0$ be integers.
Let $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ and $y_1,\ldots,y_m$ lie in the unit balls of
real Hilbert spaces $H_1,H_2$.  For each family suppose that a graph
on $\{1,\ldots,m\}$ of maximum degree at most $L$ contains every
off-diagonal pair whose absolute inner product exceeds $\eta$, where
\[
 0\le\eta\le\varepsilon^2/10^4.
\]
The two exceptional graphs may differ.  For every orthogonal projection
$P$ on $H_1\otimes H_2$ of rank at most $d$,
\begin{equation}
 \#\{j:\norm{P(x_j\otimes y_j)}\ge\varepsilon\}
 \le C(1+L)\varepsilon^{-2}
       \exp\!\left(C\varepsilon^{-2}\sqrt d\log(2+d)\right).
\end{equation}
For $d=d_m$ as defined in \eqref{eq:channel-dimension}, this is
$o_{\varepsilon,L}(m)$, uniformly over the Hilbert spaces, vectors,
projections, and allowed values of $\eta$.

title: Pointwise convergence of fourfold ergodic averages for mixing transformations
abstract: We prove that fourfold ergodic averages along the times \(n,2n,3n,4n\) converge almost everywhere to the product of the integrals for every invertible, bimeasurable, mixing probability-preserving transformation and every fixed choice of bounded measurable inputs. Convergence holds along all positive integer averaging lengths. No quantitative mixing rate is assumed, and the probability space need not be standard.

tex.abstract:
We prove that fourfold ergodic averages along the times $n,2n,3n,4n$
converge almost everywhere to the product of the integrals for every
invertible, bimeasurable, mixing probability-preserving transformation
and every fixed choice of bounded measurable inputs. Convergence holds
along all positive integer averaging lengths. No quantitative mixing
rate is assumed, and the probability space need not be standard.

Packing tensors into a subspace of small dimension
Pointwise convergence for the proper subsets of four times

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $(X,\mathcal F,\mu)$ be a probability space and let $T:X\to X$
be invertible, bimeasurable, measure preserving, and mixing in the sense
of \eqref{eq:mixing}. For every $f_1,f_2,f_3,f_4\in L^\infty(\mu)$,
\[
 \frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N
 f_1(T^nx)f_2(T^{2n}x)f_3(T^{3n}x)f_4(T^{4n}x)
 \longrightarrow \prod_{j=1}^4\int_X f_j\dd\mu
\]
for $\mu$-almost every $x$, along all positive integers $N$.
The original probability space need not be standard.

statements.title: Relative structure
statements.label: prop:structure
statements.text:
The following statements hold for standard probability-preserving
systems.
\begin{enumerate}
\item There is a maximal measure-distal factor $W_Y$.  It contains the
invariant factor, and $Y\to W_Y$ is relatively weakly mixing.  A distal
factor pulls back into the maximal distal factor of any extension.
Every measure-preserving automorphism commuting with $R$ preserves
$W_Y$.
\item Factors and joinings of distal systems are distal.  A distal
system is relatively distal over each of its factors.  For every
nonzero integer $q$, $R$ is distal if and only if $R^q$ is distal.
\item Relative weak mixing passes to nonzero integer powers and to
conditionally independent base change.  More generally, the product
of relatively weakly mixing fibre laws over any invariant joining of
their base laws is relatively weakly mixing over that joining.
\item A relatively weakly mixing extension and a relatively distal
extension of the same base are relatively disjoint: the only invariant
joining which identifies their base coordinates is the relatively
independent joining.
\item If $R$ is distal, then, for every $d\ge1$ and bounded
$g_1,\ldots,g_d$, the averages
\[
 \frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N\prod_{i=1}^d g_i(R^{in}y)
\]
converge almost surely.
\end{enumerate}
If $(S_Y^t)_{t\in\R}$ is a probability-preserving flow, the maximal
distal factor $W_Y$ of $S_Y^1$ is a flow factor.  Its action at every
nonzero rational time is distal.

statements.title: Selectors witnessing failure
statements.label: prop:selectors
statements.text:
If Theorem~\ref{thm:main} fails, there are real functions
$f_i\in L^\infty(\mu)$ with $\|f_i\|_\infty\le1$ and
$\int f_i\,\dd\mu=0$, a finite set $F\subset[1,2]$, measurable
functions
\[
 N_a:C\longrightarrow\{c2^k:c\in F,\ k\ge a\},\qquad a\ge1,
\]
a continuous real function $\Psi$ on $(\R/\Z)^I$, and
$\epsilon_0>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $a$,
\begin{equation}
 \int_C\frac1{N_a(z)}\int_0^{N_a(z)}
 \Psi\bigl((\upsilon(S_C^{it}z))_{i\in I}\bigr)
 \prod_{i\in I}f_i\bigl(\xi(S_C^{it}z)\bigr)
 \,\dd t\,\dd m_C(z)\ge\epsilon_0.
\end{equation}
The selectors may be chosen independent of the initial phase.
statements.section_title: Selected laws and their distal parameters

statements.title: Selected laws
statements.label: prop:selected
statements.text:
Formula~\eqref{eq:selected-law} defines a probability measure
$\lambda_Y$ on $Y^I$ with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Every marginal is $m_Y$, and $\lambda_Y$ is invariant under
$(y_i)_i\mapsto(S_Y^{it}y_i)_i$ for every $t\in\R$.
If $\theta:Y'\to Y$ is an extension over $C$, then
$(\theta^I)_*\lambda_{Y'}=\lambda_Y$.  These projections also hold
for countable inverse limits of extensions.
\item The law $\Lambda_Y$ of $P$ is its deterministic-length law:
for bounded $H_i$ on $W_Y$,
\begin{equation}
 \int\prod_iH_i(w_i)\,\dd\Lambda_Y
 =\lim_{L\to\infty}\int_Y\frac1L\int_0^L
       \prod_i H_i(\omega_Y(S_Y^{it}y))\,\dd t\,\dd m_Y(y).
\end{equation}
\item For every proper subset $J\subsetneq I$, the conditional law
of $(y_i)_{i\in J}$ given the \emph{entire} parameter array $P$ is
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Law}_{\lambda_Y}\bigl((y_i)_{i\in J}\mid P\bigr)
 =\bigotimes_{i\in J}m_{Y,P_i}.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
In a countable inverse limit, functions pulled back from the selected
laws at finite stages are dense in the $L^2$ space of the limiting
selected law.
statements.section_title: Selected laws and their distal parameters

statements.title: Tensor packing
statements.label: thm:packing
statements.text:
There is a universal constant $C$ with the following property.  Let
$0<\varepsilon\le1$, $d\ge1$, and $L\ge0$ be given, with $d,L$ integers.
Let $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ and $y_1,\ldots,y_m$ lie in the unit balls of real
Hilbert spaces $H_1,H_2$.  For each family suppose that a graph on
$\{1,\ldots,m\}$ of maximum degree at most $L$ contains every off-diagonal
pair whose absolute inner product exceeds $\eta$, where
\[
                         0\le\eta\le\varepsilon^2/10^4.
\]
The two exceptional graphs may differ.  For every orthogonal projection
$P$ on $H_1\otimes H_2$ of rank at most $d$,
\begin{equation}
 \#\{n:\norm{P(x_n\otimes y_n)}\ge\varepsilon\}
 \le \frac{C(1+L)}{\varepsilon^2}
       \exp\!\left(C\varepsilon^{-2}\sqrt d\log(2+d)\right).
\end{equation}
In particular, for
\begin{equation}
                  d_m=\left\lceil(1+\log m)^{3/2}\right\rceil,
\end{equation}
the left side is $o_{\varepsilon,L}(m)$, uniformly over the Hilbert
spaces, the vectors, the projections, and the allowed values of $\eta$.
statements.section_title: Packing tensors into a subspace of small dimension

statements.title: Closure under selected laws
statements.label: prop:channel-closure
statements.text:
Let $Y$ be a channel and $b\in I$.  On $\mathsf M_b(Y)$ use
$\pi_Y(y_b)$ as original factor.  For each $j\in\{1,2,3\}$, let
the new group $j$ contain the outputs $D_\alpha(y_i)$ with
$\alpha\in\mathcal D_j$ and $i\in I$.  With these factors,
$\mathsf M_b(Y)$ is a channel.

statements.label: cor:channel-array-distal
statements.text:
In Proposition~\ref{prop:channel-closure}, let
$P=(\omega_Y(y_i))_{i\in I}$ be the array of old distal parameters.
The spatial coordinates of all copied outputs are independent with
their product law conditionally on $P$.  The corresponding assertion
holds after any finite iteration of that proposition, conditionally
on the complete array of old $W_Y$-parameters.

statements.label: prop:role-bound
statements.text:
Every nonzero correlation \eqref{eq:role-correlation} has at most two
output roles. In particular, the maximal number $r$ just defined
satisfies $r\le2$.

statements.label: prop:saturation
statements.text:
Every standard flow over $C$ has a standard extension $Y$ with the
following property. For every further standard extension
$\rho:Y'\to Y$ over $C$, every $f\in L^2(\lambda_Y)$, and every
$l\in\{0\}\cup I$,
\begin{equation}
 \E_{\lambda_{Y'}}[f\circ\rho^I\mid\mathcal D_l(Y')]
 =\E_{\lambda_Y}[f\mid\mathcal D_l(Y)]\circ\rho^I.
\end{equation}
If the initial flow is a channel, the extension is a channel with the
same outputs pulled back to it.

statements.label: prop:activation
statements.text:
For the saturated channel $Y$ and maximal nonzero correlation chosen
above, the regrouped channel $Z$ has a nonzero correlation
\eqref{eq:role-correlation} with output roles $A\cup\{b\}$.

statements.title: The local analytic input with changed coefficients
statements.label: prop:ll-depth
statements.text:
Let $S=\{0\}\cup J$, where $J$ is a three-element subset of
$\{1,2,3,4\}$.  Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite rooted dyadic tree with
root $K_*$ and largest depth $d$, and let $\mathcal K\subset\mathcal T$
have kernels satisfying \eqref{eq:ll-kernels}.  For each $j\in S$, let
$(z_{j,s})_{0\le s\le d}$ be measurable scalar functions on $K_*$.
Extend these functions by zero outside $K_*$.
Suppose that $\{0,\ldots,d\}$ has a deterministic partition into
$W_j\ge1$ nonempty consecutive blocks, on each of which
\[
 \mathcal V_B(z_j)(y)\le W_j^{-1/2}
 \quad\text{for almost every }y\in K_*.
\]
The partitions may differ between the four roles.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{K\in\mathcal K}|K|
   \bigl|\mathcal H_{K,S}((z_{j,s(K)})_{j\in S})\bigr|
 \le C(c_0,C_0)|K_*|.
 
\end{equation}
The constant is independent of the tree, kernels, depth range, and
block partitions.  It can be chosen uniformly over the four sets $S$.
statements.section_title: Pointwise convergence for the proper subsets of four times

statements.title: Oscillation for the four triples
statements.label: prop:ll-oscillation
statements.text:
Let $(Y,\nu,R)$ be an invertible probability preserving system,
let $J\subset\{1,2,3,4\}$ have three elements, and let the functions
$g_j:Y\to\C$, $j\in J$, be measurable with $|g_j|\le1$.
For an averaging profile set
\[
 V_k^\varphi(y)=\sum_{n\in\Z}\varphi_{2^k}(n)
                   \prod_{j\in J}g_j(R^{jn}y),\qquad k\ge0.
\]
There is $C_\varphi<\infty$ such that, for all deterministic integers
$0\le k_1<\cdots<k_{W+1}$,
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{b=1}^W\int_Y
   \max_{k_b\le\ell\le k_{b+1}}
      |V_\ell^\varphi-V_{k_b}^\varphi|\,\dd\nu
 \le C_\varphi\sqrt W.
 
\end{equation}
The constant is independent of the system, inputs, endpoints, and $W$.

title: Pointwise convergence of triple ergodic averages for mixing transformations
abstract: We prove pointwise convergence of triple ergodic averages for every invertible mixing probability preserving transformation T of an arbitrary probability space \((X,\mathcal F,\mu)\), with measurable inverse. For every triple of bounded measurable functions \(f_1,f_2,f_3:X\to\mathbb C\), \(\displaystyle \frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N f_1(T^nx)f_2(T^{2n}x)f_3(T^{3n}x) \longrightarrow \prod_{j=1}^3\int_X f_j\,d\mu\) for μ-almost every x as \(N\to\infty\) through all positive integers.

tex.abstract:
We prove pointwise convergence of triple ergodic averages for every
invertible mixing probability preserving transformation \(T\) of an
arbitrary probability space \((X,\mathcal F,\mu)\), with measurable inverse.
For every triple of bounded measurable functions
\(f_1,f_2,f_3:X\to\mathbb C\),
\[
 \frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N f_1(T^nx)f_2(T^{2n}x)f_3(T^{3n}x)
 \longrightarrow \prod_{j=1}^3\int_X f_j\,d\mu
\]
for \(\mu\)-almost every \(x\) as \(N\to\infty\) through all positive
integers.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $(X,\mathcal F,\mu)$ be an arbitrary probability space and let
$T:X\to X$ be an invertible mixing probability preserving transformation
with measurable inverse.  For every triple of bounded measurable functions
$f_1,f_2,f_3:X\to\C$,
\[
 A_N(f_1,f_2,f_3)(x)
 \longrightarrow \prod_{j=1}^3\int_X f_j\,d\mu
 \quad\text{for $\mu$-almost every }x
\]
as $N\to\infty$ through all positive integers.  The exceptional null set
may depend on the triple of functions.

statements.title: Finite oscillation of smooth orbit averages
statements.label: prop:orbit-oscillation
statements.text:
For every averaging profile \(\varphi\), there is a constant
\(C_\varphi<\infty\) with the following property.  On every invertible
probability preserving system, let \(f_1,f_2,f_3:X\to\mathbb C\) be
measurable with \(|f_j(x)|\leq1\) for all \(x\), and define
\[
 V_k^\varphi(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}\varphi_{2^k}(n)
                 \prod_{j=1}^3f_j(T^{jn}x),
       \qquad k=0,1,2,\ldots .
\]
For every integer \(w\geq1\) and every deterministic list of integers
\(0\leq k_1<\cdots<k_{w+1}\),
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{i=1}^w\int_X
   \max_{k_i\leq\ell\leq k_{i+1}}
      |V_\ell^\varphi-V_{k_i}^\varphi|\,d\mu
       \leq C_\varphi\sqrt w.
 
\end{equation}
The constant is independent of the system, the inputs, \(w\), and the
endpoints.
statements.section_title: Smooth orbit averages and the pointwise theorem

statements.title: Local estimate with variation in depth
statements.label: thm:depth-local
statements.text:
Fix the admissibility parameters \(c_0,C_0\).  Let \(J\) be an interval
in any dyadic lattice, let \(\mathcal T\) be a finite rooted tree below
\(J\), and let \(d\) be its largest depth in \(J\).  Let
\(\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal T\), with an admissible kernel on each of
its intervals.  For each \(j\in\{0,1,2,3\}\), let
\(f_{j,s}:J\to\C\), \(0\le s\le d\), be measurable, and write
\(f_j=(f_{j,s})_{s=0}^d\).  Suppose that
\(\{0,\ldots,d\}\) is partitioned into \(W_j\ge1\) deterministic nonempty
consecutive blocks and that, on every block \(B\),
\[
 \mathcal V_B(f_j)(y)\le W_j^{-1/2}
 \quad\text{for almost every }y\in J.
\]
The four partitions may differ.  Extend the inputs by zero outside \(J\).
Then
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{I\in\mathcal I}|I|
  \bigl|H_I(f_{0,s(I)},f_{1,s(I)},f_{2,s(I)},f_{3,s(I)})\bigr|
 \le C_{\mathrm{loc}}(c_0,C_0)|J|.
 
\end{equation}
The constant is independent of the lattice, root, tree, kernels, depth
range, blocks, and their numbers.

statements.title: Increments of inherited projections
statements.label: cor:row-projections
statements.text:
Use the catalog of Lemma~\ref{lem:row-catalog}.  On a finite
interval of integers $h\ge s_R$, let $\mathcal P_h$ be the full
partition of $R$ into cells of depth $h$.  On each
$Q\in\mathcal P_h$, let $P_{h,Q}$ be the orthogonal projection in
$L^2(Q;\mathcal H)$ onto constant-coefficient combinations of
a subset $\mathcal M_h(Q)\subset\mathcal V(Q)$.  Assume inheritance:
if $Q'\in\mathcal P_{h+1}$ is contained in $Q$, then
$\mathcal M_h(Q)\subset\mathcal M_{h+1}(Q')$.  Let $P_h$ be the
direct sum of the $P_{h,Q}$ on $L^2(R;\mathcal H)$.

Suppose $(F_s)_{s\in\mathsf S}$ satisfies
Equation~\eqref{eq:row-input-normalization}.  For any integer $J\ge1$ and
\[
 r_1\le t_1\le r_2\le t_2\le\cdots\le r_J\le t_J
\]
in the projection depth range and nondecreasing
$s_1,\ldots,s_J\in\mathsf S$, one has
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{j=1}^J\|(P_{t_j}-P_{r_j})F_{s_j}\|_2^2
 \le \mathfrak C_D^2|R|.
 
\end{equation}
If the intervals can be divided into $\mathfrak m$ such ordered
families whose reads are nondecreasing, the right side is multiplied
by $\mathfrak m$.

For each $s\in\mathsf S$ with $s\ge s_R$, let $\mathcal U_s$ be any
subcollection of the depth-$s$ cells of $R$.  In particular fix an integer
$\ell$ and retain only those $s$ for which $s+\ell$ and $s+\ell+1$ are in
the projection range.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \sum_s\sum_{I\in\mathcal U_s}|I|\,
       \|(P_{s+\ell+1}-P_{s+\ell})F_s\|_{2,I}^2
 \le \mathfrak C_D^2|R|.
 
\end{equation}
For every integer $L\ge0$, retaining only $s\in\mathsf S$ with $s\ge s_R$
for which $s$ and $s+L$ are in the projection range,
\begin{equation}
 \left(\sum_s\sum_{I\in\mathcal U_s}|I|\,
       \|(P_{s+L}-P_s)F_s\|_{2,I}^2\right)^{1/2}
 \le L\mathfrak C_D|R|^{1/2}
 \le (1+L)\mathfrak C_D|R|^{1/2}.
 
\end{equation}

statements.title: A finite predictor list for scheduled opponents
statements.label: cor:hbase-predictor-list
statements.text:
Fix the two bounded scalar atoms \(\varphi_i,\varphi_j\) on \(J'\),
of complexity at most \(H_{\rm low}\), and let \(B\ge1\).
There is a finite index set \(\mathfrak A\), a bound \(D_{\rm pred}\),
scalar coefficients \(c_{r,\alpha}\), and fixed triples
\((\psi_{a,\alpha},\psi_{b,\alpha},\lambda_\alpha)\) on \(J'\)
with \(\|\psi_{e,\alpha}\|_\infty\le1\), such that
\[
 \#\mathfrak A,\quad
 \operatorname{complexity}(\psi_{e,\alpha}),\quad
 |c_{r,\alpha}|\le D_{\rm pred},\qquad
 \log D_{\rm pred}\le
 \operatorname{poly}\bigl(1+B+\log(2H_{\rm low})\bigr).
\]
Here \(c_{r,\alpha}\) is a scalar depending only on the fixed pair,
its scalar construction, \(B\), and the dyadic scale \(r\); it is
zero unless \(|\lambda_\alpha|r^2\le D_{\rm pred}\).  The list and
these coefficients are chosen before any opposing sequences or
completed high catalogs.

Define its forms explicitly by
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 T_I^\alpha(z_a,z_b)
 :=|I|^{-2}\int_{\mathbb R^2}&w_I(x,t)e(\lambda_\alpha t^2)
       \psi_{a,\alpha}(y_a)z_a(y_a)\\
       &\qquad\cdot\psi_{b,\alpha}(y_b)z_b(y_b)\,dx\,dt .
 \end{split}                                                   
\end{equation}
For every dyadic \(K\subseteq J'\), selected finite use collection
\(\mathcal U\) below \(K\), and pair of admissible opposing sequences
on \(K\), define the actual error \(e_I\) by the per-cell identity
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal L_I^{\varphi_i,\varphi_j}(z_{a,I},z_{b,I})
 =\sum_{\alpha\in\mathfrak A}c_{|I|,\alpha}
       T_I^\alpha(z_{a,I},z_{b,I})+e_I.                        
\end{equation}
Then, uniformly over those opposing sequences and their completed
catalogs,
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{I\in\mathcal U}|I||e_I|
 \le e^{-B}\operatorname{poly}
       \bigl(\log(2D_{\rm h}),1+L\bigr)|K|.                    
\end{equation}
The error \(e_I\) may depend on the opposing sequence; the assertion
is its aggregate bound.

statements.title: Base data and active reduction
statements.label: prop:hbase-data
statements.text:
Fix the constructed tuple with later accuracy \(t\), put \(k=k_t\),
and use its final segments \(R\in\mathcal R_{\rm base}\) and original owner
sets \(\mathcal I_R\) from Equation~\eqref{eq:hbase-high-replacement}.
On an owned cell of depth \(s\), define
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
 Y_l=B_l+U_l,\qquad B_i=X_i,\quad B_j=X_j,\quad U_i=U_j=0,\\
 B_e=P^{\rm new}_{e,s}F_{e,s}-g_{e,\mathrm{prev},I},\qquad
 U_e=(P^{\rm new}_{e,s+K_0}-P^{\rm new}_{e,s})F_{e,s}
       \quad(e=a,b),\\
 \|B_{l,I}\|_{2,I},\ \|U_{l,I}\|_{2,I},\ \|Y_{l,I}\|_{2,I}\le C,\\
 \Lambda_k=C(1+K_0)\log(2D_{\rm base})\le k^C,\qquad
 \sum_{I\in\mathcal I_R}|I|\|U_{e,I}\|_{2,I}^2
       \le\Lambda_k^2|R|\quad(e=a,b).
 \end{gathered}                                               
\end{equation}
Each \(B_l\) is a signed sum of at most two current nested-catalog
projections applied to \(F_{l,s}\).  Their basic catalogs have
distinct private directions and inherited masks.  Their path counts,
column sizes, inverse private weights, bounded scalar atom
complexities, and current coefficient sums are bounded by
\(D_{\rm base}\), with
\[
 e^k\le D_{\rm base}\le\exp(k^C).
\]
For \(t\ge12\), the associated full \(Y\) tuple has the pair bound
and pointwise form bound \(\eta\) of Equation~\eqref{eq:hbase-quality}.

For three available basic scalar columns \(\boldsymbol\varphi\) in
distinct slots, let \(\operatorname{act}_I(\boldsymbol\varphi)\)
be their form norm against a normalized \(L^2(I)\) input in the
fourth slot.  For a sufficiently large fixed \(C_{\rm act}\), put
\[
 \mathcal A_R=
 \left\{I\in\mathcal I_R:
   \operatorname{act}_I(\boldsymbol\varphi)>D_{\rm base}^{-C_{\rm act}}
   \text{ for some available triple }\boldsymbol\varphi\right\}.
\]
This common active set has path multiplicity
\[
 \sum_{I\in\mathcal A_R}\mathbf1_I(y)\le M\le D_{\rm base}^C.
\]
Define three patterns in their original slots by
\[
 \begin{array}{lll}
 z^\varnothing_l=B_l&\text{for every }l,\\
 z^a_a=U_a,&z^a_l=B_l& (l\ne a),\\
 z^b_b=U_b,&z^b_l=B_l& (l\ne b),
 \end{array}
 \qquad \mathcal P=\{z^\varnothing,z^a,z^b\}.
\]
For \(z\in\mathcal P\), let
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak M_R(z)
 :=\sum_{I\in\mathcal A_R}|I|
       \min\{\eta,|H_I(z_I)|\}.                               
\end{equation}
Then for \(t\ge12\),
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{I\in\mathcal I_R}|I|\,|H_I(Y_I)|
 \le C\eta\Lambda_k^2|R|+e^{-k}|R|
       +\sum_{z\in\mathcal P}\mathfrak M_R(z).                 
\end{equation}
The \(e^{-k}|R|\) term is the total inactive error for the three
patterns.  The finitely many leading accuracy levels have a bound
independent of the number of spatial depths.  These base data and
their estimates hold anew on normalized subroots with the inherited
basic lists and their local continuations.

statements.title: The endpoint histories used by filter transfer
statements.label: cor:h-transfer-endpoint-variation
statements.text:
Fix one source search leaf, one step in the
\emph{Outgoing filters and near-band defects} Lemma of
\cite[Section~6]{H}, and one choice in that step's expansion of
the complementary factors.  In its outgoing complementary slot
write \(x_{c,s}=\mathcal C_{c,s}B_{c,s}\) for exactly the
input-side source history left after deleting the outgoing positive
filter.  This inner history is shared across groups.  It retains
the source order, its normalized averages or
identities, its \(O(\log\mathcal L)\) length, and the specified
input-side basic \(Q_s^\tau\) in each nonzero constituent.  Write
\(x_{d,s}\) for the whole remaining source history in the other
complementary slot.  All endpoint evaluations use the complete
inherited families, with coupled pads at compared depths, and may
occur when the group is not current.

Let \(Q_{c,p,s}\), \(1\le p\le P\), be exactly that step's
individual outgoing projections, and put
\(Q_{c,0,s}=0\), \(Q_{c,P+1,s}=1\).
For a ball transfer, each \(Q_{c,p,s}x_{c,s}\) with
\(1\le p\le P\) is an eligible group-indexed ball endpoint, while
\(x_{c,s}\) is shared.  For a cumulative transfer the outer ball
has already been removed and all these endpoints are shared.
The other endpoint \(x_{d,s}\) either has its one source positive
ball average outermost, with shared inner history, or is shared
after that ball has been removed.

Each specified eligible ball output, using its source positive
average or one individual allowed pad as a singleton average,
satisfies \eqref{eq:h-certified-variation}.  Each specified shared
output satisfies the shared conclusion of
Lemma~\ref{lem:h-certified-variation}, with one union of required
right-endpoint cells across its uses.

title: Polynomial Hitting Lists for Noncommutative Rational Formulas
abstract: We construct, in deterministic polynomial bit time, a polynomial-size list of rational matrix tuples for noncommutative rational formulas over ℚ of bounded tree size. Every nonzero admissible formula has a defined, invertible value at one tuple, with no separate bounds on inverse nesting or rational constant heights. Matrix dimensions, entry bit lengths, and total output length are polynomially bounded.

tex.abstract: We construct, in deterministic polynomial bit time, a polynomial-size list of rational matrix tuples for noncommutative rational formulas over $\Q$ of bounded tree size. Every nonzero admissible formula has a defined, invertible value at one tuple, with no separate bounds on inverse nesting or rational constant heights. Matrix dimensions, entry bit lengths, and total output length are polynomially bounded.
sections: Encoding a formula and its evaluation domain
A rational hitting list and its bit complexity

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There are a deterministic Turing machine $G$ and fixed positive integers $C,k$ with the following property. Given $1^n,1^s$, where $n,s\geq1$, the machine outputs a finite list $\mathcal H_{n,s}$ of $n$-tuples of rational square matrices, in at most $C(n+s+1)^k$ bit operations. The entire output, with signed binary numerators and positive binary denominators, has at most $C(n+s+1)^k$ bits. For every nonzero admissible rational formula $\Phi$ in $n$ variables of size at most $s$, some tuple in $\mathcal H_{n,s}$ is a defined evaluation of $\Phi$ with invertible value.

The same list works for all such formulas, regardless of the bit lengths of their rational constants or their inverse depth. The generator receives no formula, oracle, randomness, or advice.

statements.title: Rectangular rank bound
statements.label: prop:rectangular
statements.text:
Let $1\leq q\leq B$ and $A_0,\ldots,A_n\in\Mat_q(\Q)$.  Suppose that,
for some extension field $E/\Q$, some integer $e\geq1$, and some
$X_1,\ldots,X_n\in\Mat_e(E)$, the matrix
\[
  A_0\otimes I_e+\sum_{i=1}^n A_i\otimes X_i
\]
is invertible.  Then $\sum_{i=0}^n A_i\otimes T_i$ is injective over $F$,
and
\begin{equation}
  \rank_{\Q(t)}\left(\sum_{i=0}^n A_i\otimes R_i(t)\right)
  \geq qN>(q-1)M.
  
\end{equation}

statements.title: Full-rank deformed pencils
statements.label: prop:pencil-deformation
statements.text:
Fix a primitive $M$th root of unity $\omega\in\C$, and lift the
padded matrices $R_0(t),\ldots,R_n(t)$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:division-lift} with $d=M$ and
$K=\Q(\omega)(t)$.  Let
\[
  L(x)=A_0+\sum_{i=1}^n A_i x_i,
  \qquad A_i\in\Mat_q(\Q),\qquad 1\leq q\leq B,
\]
be an affine pencil admitting an invertible matrix evaluation over
some extension field of $\Q$.  Then
\begin{equation}
  P_{L,\omega}(t,p,r)
   :=\det\!\left(\sum_{i=0}^n A_i\otimes R_i^*(t,p,r)\right)
   \ne0.
\end{equation}
This is a polynomial in $\Q(\omega)[t,p,r]$ of total degree at most
$3BM^2$.  In particular $\det R_0^*$ is a nonzero polynomial.

statements.title: Pencil certificates for the original formula tree
statements.label: prop:formula-certificates
statements.text:
Let $\Phi$ be a formula of size at most $s$, and put $B=2s+1$.  Form the
indexed collection $\mathcal C_\Phi$ consisting of $L_h$ for every
inverse-node occurrence $h$ of $\Phi$, together with $J_\Phi$.
Then:
\begin{enumerate}
 \item The collection contains at most $s+1$ affine pencils over $\Q$,
       each of positive order at most $B$.
 \item At every tuple of matrices of a common positive order over a
       field extension of $\Q$, all pencils in $\mathcal C_\Phi$ are
       invertible if and only if the original formula tree $\Phi$ is
       defined there and its value is invertible.
 \item If $\Phi$ is admissible and nonzero, there is a single tuple over
       some field extension of $\Q$ at which every pencil in
       $\mathcal C_\Phi$ is invertible.
\end{enumerate}
Adding the order-one constant pencil $1$ for normalization gives at
most $s+2$ pencils, still of order at most $B$, with the same simultaneous
feasibility property in the third assertion.

statements.label: prop:generator-hitting
statements.text:
Every nonzero admissible formula of size at most~$s$ has a defined,
invertible evaluation at a tuple in~$\mathcal H_{n,s}$.

statements.label: cor:pencil-hitting
statements.text:
Let $L=A_0+\sum_{i=1}^n A_i x_i$ be a rational affine linear pencil
of order $q\le B$ that admits an invertible matrix evaluation over
an extension field of~$\Q$. There is a tuple
$X\in\mathcal H_{n,s}$ for which $L(X)$ is invertible.
statements.section_title: A rational hitting list and its bit complexity

statements.label: prop:generator-complexity
statements.text:
The list $\mathcal H_{n,s}$ can be constructed and written by one
deterministic Turing machine in a number of bit operations bounded
by a fixed polynomial in $n+s+1$. Its entire binary encoding has
length bounded by a fixed polynomial in the same quantity.
statements.section_title: A rational hitting list and its bit complexity

statements.label: cor:rank-detecting-list
statements.text:
Let $a,b\geq1$ and $k\geq0$, and put $P=a+b+k+1$. From these
parameters in unary, a deterministic generator constructs a nonempty
finite list $\mathcal R_{a,b,k}$ of pairs
\[
 (e,X),\qquad e\geq1,\quad
 X=(X_1,\ldots,X_k)\in\Mat_e(\Q)^k,
\]
in a fixed polynomial in $P$ bit operations. Its number of entries,
total binary encoding length, and every matrix dimension $e$ are
bounded by fixed polynomials in $P$. The list depends only on $a,b,k$.

For every rectangular rational affine pencil
\[
 A(x)=A_0+\sum_{i=1}^k A_i x_i,\qquad A_i\in\Q^{a\times b},
\]
write $\operatorname{ncrk}A$ for its rank over the free skew field on
$x_1,\ldots,x_k$ over $\Q$, with ordinary rational rank when $k=0$.
Then the exact identity
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{ncrk}A
 =\max_{(e,X)\in\mathcal R_{a,b,k}}
   \frac{\rank_{\Q}\!\left(A_0\otimes I_e+
             \sum_{i=1}^k A_i\otimes X_i\right)}{e}
 
\end{equation}
holds for all choices and bit lengths of the coefficients.

Suppose that, at each requested pair $(e,X)$, an oracle returns
either the complete exact rational $ae$ by $be$ matrix in
\eqref{eq:rank-detecting-list}, in binary rational encoding, or its
exact ordinary rank. Querying the whole list nonadaptively and taking
the maximum of the exact quotients returns $\operatorname{ncrk}A$.
If $L$ is the total binary length of the responses, list generation,
query writing, and response processing use $\operatorname{poly}(P+L)$
bit operations, in addition to the sum of the oracle's costs.
The response lengths and oracle costs may depend on the coefficient
heights. If $a=0$ or $b=0$, the rank is zero and no queries are needed.

title: Polynomial mixing of the switch chain for every graphical degree sequence
abstract: We prove the simple-undirected form of the Kannan–Tetali–Vempala conjecture: the switch chain on simple undirected graphs mixes in polynomial time for every graphical degree sequence. For a lazy chain that proposes switches uniformly on four vertices, the total-variation mixing time at distance 1/4 is at most \(2n^8\). We also give an exactly uniform sampler for every graphical labeled degree vector. It uses unbiased random bits, terminates almost surely, and has expected polynomial bit running time.

tex.abstract:
We prove the simple-undirected form of the Kannan--Tetali--Vempala
conjecture: the switch chain on simple undirected graphs mixes in polynomial
time for every graphical degree sequence. For a lazy chain that proposes
switches uniformly on four vertices, the total-variation mixing time at
distance $1/4$ is at most $2n^8$.
We also give an exactly uniform sampler for every graphical labeled degree
vector. It uses unbiased random bits, terminates almost surely, and has
expected polynomial bit running time.
sections: A variance inequality for three rows
From pair resampling to the switch chain

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every $n\ge4$ and every graphical degree vector $d$,
\[
 t_{\mathrm{mix}}(d)\le 2n^8.
\]
If $|\Omega_d|>1$, the spectral gap of $P_d$ is at least
$[24n^2\binom n4]^{-1}$.

statements.title: Exact uniform sampling
statements.label: cor:exact-sampling
statements.text:
There is a uniform randomized algorithm that, given any finite graphical
labeled degree vector $d=(d_1,\ldots,d_n)$, uses unbiased random bits,
terminates almost surely, and outputs a graph chosen exactly uniformly
from the simple undirected graphs on $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with labeled
degree vector $d$. Its expected bit running time is bounded by a fixed
polynomial in the binary encoding length of $d$.

title: Polynomial PEPS approximation of gapped square-grid ground states
abstract: We prove that the unique ground state of a uniformly gapped nearest-neighbor Hamiltonian on an \(L\times L\) square lattice admits a projected entangled-pair state approximation with bond dimension polynomial in L and global vector error at most L−1 after normalization. Only the gap of the full Hamiltonian is assumed. The result is an existence theorem, with constants uniform over Hamiltonians of fixed local dimension, interaction strength, and gap.

tex.abstract:
We prove that the unique ground state of a uniformly gapped nearest-neighbor
Hamiltonian on an $L\times L$ square lattice admits a projected entangled-pair
state approximation with bond dimension polynomial in $L$ and global vector
error at most $L^{-1}$ after normalization. Only the gap of the full Hamiltonian is assumed.
The result is an existence theorem, with constants uniform over
Hamiltonians of fixed local dimension, interaction strength, and gap.

statements.title: Entropy area law, {\cite[Theorem~1.1 and Corollary~1.2]{RepoAreaLaw}}
statements.label: prop:area-law
statements.text:
Under \eqref{eq:model}--\eqref{eq:global-gap}, there is
$C_A=C_A(q,J,\Delta)$ such that every $A\subseteq\Lambda$ satisfies
\[
 S_\Omega(A)\le C_A|\partial_\Lambda A|,
 \qquad
 \partial_\Lambda A=\{\{x,y\}\in E(\Lambda):x\in A,
                                      \ y\notin A\}.
\]
The same constant works for every $L$ and every Hamiltonian in the class.

statements.title: Coarse information outside a sublinear collar
statements.label: prop:coarse
statements.text:
Fix an integer $N_0\ge1$ and a constant $A_0\ge1$.  There are
$\beta<1$, $C<\infty$, and $u_0<\infty$ such that the following holds.
Let $u\ge u_0$ and let $T$ be the full ambient lattice sample of a union
of at most $N_0$ axis-parallel rectangles, with
$\diam_\infty T\le A_0u$.  For every physical set $E\subseteq\Lambda$
satisfying
\[
 \dist_\infty(E,T)>u^\beta,
\]
one has
\[
 I_\Omega(\Lambda\cap T:E)\le C.
\]
The same statement holds for any subset of $\Lambda\cap T$ in its first
argument, for rectangles with consistently assigned open or closed
sides, and after a common translation of the lattice coordinates.

statements.title: Information under angular separation
statements.label: prop:angular
statements.text:
Fix $a>0$, $A_0\ge1$, an integer $m_0\ge0$, and $p>0$.
There is $D<\infty$ such that the following holds for all sufficiently
large $L$.  Let $\mathcal V$ be a set of at most $m_0$ marked points
in the plane, let $X,E\subseteq\Lambda$ be disjoint, and let
\[
 D\log L\le n\le A_0L,
 \qquad \diam_\infty X\le A_0n.
\]
Put $s_{\min}=D\log L$ and
$d_{\mathcal V}(x)=\min_{v\in\mathcal V}|x-v|_\infty$, with
$d_{\varnothing}=+\infty$.  Suppose that for every $x\in X$,
\begin{equation}
 \dist_\infty(x,E)
   \ge a\max\{s_{\min},\min(n,d_{\mathcal V}(x))\}.
 
\end{equation}
Then
\[
 I_\Omega(X:E)\le L^{-p}.
\]
The constant $D$ and the scale threshold are uniform in the marked
points, physical sets, and Hamiltonian.

statements.title: Adaptive patch constraint
statements.label: prop:patch
statements.text:
Fix \(B_0>0\) and \(p>0\).  There are constants \(C,c>0\), depending
only on \(q,J,\Delta,B_0,p\), with the following property.  For every
\(L\geq2\), center \(z\in\mathbb R^2\), and
\(0<u\leq B_0\log L\), there is an orthogonal projection \(P\),
supported on \(X(2u)\), such that
\[
 \norm{(\id-P)\Omega}\leq L^{-p}.
\]
There are radii \(u\leq r_1\leq\cdots\leq r_m\leq2u\), sets
\(X_j=X(r_j)\), and unit vectors
\(v_{j\ell}\in\mathcal H_{X_j}\), \(1\leq\ell\leq d_j\), for which
\begin{equation}
 P=\sum_{j=1}^m\sum_{\ell=1}^{d_j}
       \lvert v_{j\ell}\rangle\langle v_{j\ell}\rvert_{X_j}
          \otimes\id_{\Lambda\setminus X_j},
 \qquad
 \sum_{j=1}^m d_j\leq C L^c.
 
\end{equation}
All the summands in \eqref{eq:patch-cylinder-projection} have pairwise
orthogonal ranges as operators on \(\mathcal H_\Lambda\).
No bound on the internal tensor complexity of the individual
\(v_{j\ell}\) is asserted.

statements.title: Distributed density compression
statements.label: thm:compression
statements.text:
Consider a family of distributed constructions indexed by $L\ge2$ with
the following uniform properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The number of parties and gates is uniformly polynomial.  The
initial vector is a tensor product of normalized private vectors, one
at each party, and every gate is a contraction.
\item There is a constant $b$ such that each nonprivate gate involves at
most $b$ parties, and each party participates in at most $b$ nonprivate
gates over the entire construction.
\item Each nonprivate gate is a sum of uniformly polynomially many
allowed monomials with uniformly polynomially bounded scalar
coefficients.  There is a constant $r$ bounding the number of pair
sources, pair effects, and polynomial-dimensional messages in each
monomial.  All constituent local maps are contractions.
\item At the end, the intended physical output space of each party has
uniformly polynomial dimension.  All other registers are traced out
party by party.
\end{enumerate}
Write $\rho$ for the resulting physical output density operator; it is
positive and may have trace less than one.  For every fixed $p>0$, there
is an operator tensor network $\sigma$ satisfying
\[
 \norm{\sigma-\rho}_1\le L^{-p}.
\]
It has one node per party, a bounded number of incident virtual links at
each node, and uniformly polynomial link dimensions.  Every link joins
two parties which participate in a common nonprivate gate of the
original construction.  The physical legs at a node are the ket and bra
legs of that party's intended output.
The constants in these bounds depend only on $p$ and the fixed uniform
data in the assumptions, including $b,r$ and the polynomial bounds,
and not on private dimensions or source Schmidt ranks.

The same conclusion holds if the gate expansions in the third
assumption are available to every fixed inverse-polynomial
operator-norm accuracy, with uniform polynomial bounds at each fixed
accuracy.

statements.title: Distribution through a dyadic hierarchy
statements.label: prop:protocol
statements.text:
For all sufficiently large $L$, there is a protocol with the following
properties.  All constants in this statement are uniform in the
Hamiltonian and $L$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item
There are $O(L^2)$ parties, one for each square in a padded dyadic
hierarchy and at most a fixed number of additional parties for each
repainting of a square.  Initialization is a pure product across
parties.  One party initially holds the main copy of $\Omega$; all
auxiliary copies are initialized privately at their designated parties.
\item
The schedule has at most $C L^3$ changes.  Each change is implemented by
a fixed number of contraction gates involving at most a fixed number of
parties and having the bipartite-resource expansions established in
Lemmas~\ref{lem:small-rewrite}, \ref{lem:birth}, and
\ref{lem:exchange}.  The expansions can be made accurate to any fixed
inverse power of $L$ in operator norm where an approximation is needed.
Each party participates in at most a fixed number of gates involving
other parties over its entire lifetime.
\item
Every linked gate involves parties at the same or adjacent dyadic
scales.  Parties at a gate have addresses at distance $O(n)$ from one
another, where $n$ is either endpoint scale; additional parties have the
scale and address of the square to whose repainting they belong.
\item
There is a designated reference vector at every stage, formed from the
main encoded frame and the auxiliary encoded frames.  All its factors
have norm at most one.  Each change takes its preceding reference vector
within $C L^{-20}$ in vector norm of its following reference vector.
At the end, the reference is
\[
 \Omega\otimes\Xi,
 \qquad 1-C L^{3-60}\le \norm{\Xi}\le1,
\]
where $\Xi$ contains only registers to be discarded.  Every original
physical site is a raw register at its own unit-square party.  No other
party has a physical output, so every party's physical output dimension
is at most $q$.
\end{enumerate}

title: Polynomial-Time Unitary Synthesis from a Boolean Oracle
abstract: We give a positive answer to the constant-error formulation of the Aaronson–Kuperberg unitary synthesis problem. For every n, a quantum oracle circuit generated in polynomial time from n alone can approximate the channel of every n-qubit unitary to full diamond-norm error at most 1/2, after a suitable Boolean oracle is chosen. Using the fixed gates \(H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}\), the circuit has polynomially many qubits, elementary gates, and oracle calls, and its oracle queries have polynomial length. The oracle may depend on the target unitary; the theorem does not give an efficient classical procedure for constructing it.

tex.abstract:
We give a positive answer to the constant-error formulation of the
Aaronson--Kuperberg unitary synthesis problem. For every $n$, a quantum oracle
circuit generated in polynomial time from $n$ alone can approximate the channel
of every $n$-qubit unitary to full diamond-norm error at most $1/2$, after a
suitable Boolean oracle is chosen. Using the fixed gates
$H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$, the circuit has polynomially many qubits,
elementary gates, and oracle calls, and its oracle queries have polynomial
length. The oracle may depend on the target unitary; the theorem does not give
an efficient classical procedure for constructing it.
sections: Fourier fields for a smaller unitary

statements.title: Polynomial-time unitary synthesis
statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There are a polynomial $p$ and a deterministic classical algorithm which, on
input $1^n$ for any integer $n\ge1$, outputs in time at most $p(n)$ a quantum
oracle circuit $A_n$ with the following properties.  The circuit uses the gates
$H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$ and a single Boolean oracle of input length
$m(n)\le p(n)$.  Its total number of qubits, elementary gates, and oracle calls
are each at most $p(n)$.  For every unitary $U\in U(2^n)$ there is a function
$f:\{0,1\}^{m(n)}\to\{0,1\}$ for which the output channel $\Phi_{n,f}$ of
$A_n^{O_f}$ satisfies
\[
 \norm{\Phi_{n,f}-\mathcal U}_\diamond\le\frac12.
\]

statements.title: A block of uniformly small norm
statements.label: contract:block
statements.text:
For every unitary $U$ on $\C^d$, there are unitaries $P_{\mathrm L}$ and
$P_{\mathrm R}$ on $\C^d$ such that
\begin{equation}
 V=P_{\mathrm L}UP_{\mathrm R}
 =\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad \norm D\leq r,
\end{equation}
where the block sizes are $k,s$ from~\eqref{contract:orders}.
The transformations $P_{\mathrm L},P_{\mathrm R}$ and their inverses have
implementations using $O(n)$ programmable slots and $O(n)$ clean working
qubits, with a structure determined by $n,d$.  The same structure works
simultaneously for any family $U_\lambda$, using the label $\lambda$ as an
additional control.

statements.text:

statements.label: encode:implementation
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses and definitions of Section~\ref{sec:fields}, there
are exact-slot unitaries $\mathsf U_E,\mathsf U_R$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \norm{\mathsf U_E\iota-\jmath\mathcal E_L}\le5r^{2L},
 \qquad
 \norm{\mathsf U_R\iota-\jmath\mathcal R_L}\le5r^{2L}.
\end{equation}
Each uses $O\bigl(L(K+n+h)+K\bigr)$ slots and $K+n+h+2$ fresh qubits,
with slot structure independent of $V$. The construction works coherently
with any additional label register.

statements.title: Uniform programmable synthesis
statements.label: rec:skeleton
statements.text:
Let $n\geq1$, $1\leq d\leq2^n$, and $t\geq0$.  There is a programmable-slot
circuit structure, determined by $n,d,t$, with the following property.
For every family $(U_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\{0,1\}^t}$ of unitaries on
$\C^d$, its slot tables can be chosen so that the circuit implements the
controlled unitary $U_\lambda$, preserves the labels, and has clean-workspace
operator norm error less than $1/100$ in the sense of~\eqref{slot:clean-error}.
The circuit uses
\begin{equation}
 t+O((n+1)^{10})\quad\text{qubits},
 \qquad O((n+1)^{13})\quad\text{slots}.
\end{equation}
Its structure, including each slot's ordered control list, is generated
deterministically in time polynomial in $n+t$ from $n,d,t$.

statements.title: Compilation of slots
statements.label: compile:slots
statements.text:
Let a skeleton have $S$ slots on $Q$ qubits, and put $\eta=1/h$ for an integer
$h\ge2$.
There is a deterministic procedure, polynomial in $Q,S,1/\eta$, that produces
a circuit over $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$ and one Boolean oracle, with
polynomially many qubits, gates, calls, and address bits. For every assignment
of the slot tables, some contents of that oracle make the circuit differ
from the prescribed skeleton by at most $S\eta$ on inputs with its added
scratch qubits zero, with the comparison circuit keeping those scratch
qubits zero.

title: Polynomial removal fails for ordered binary matrices
abstract: We construct a fixed \(66\times66\) binary matrix for which ordered matrix removal has no polynomial bound. This disproves the polynomial ordered binary matrix-removal conjecture. Ordered copies preserve the separate row and column orders and match both zeros and ones; removal permits changing entries in either direction.

tex.abstract:
We construct a fixed $66\times66$ binary matrix for which ordered matrix
removal has no polynomial bound. This disproves the polynomial ordered
binary matrix-removal conjecture. Ordered copies preserve the separate
row and column orders and match both zeros and ones; removal permits
changing entries in either direction.
sections: A fixed pattern and its tree matrices
Copies are confined to the leaf diagonal

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is a fixed binary $66\times66$ matrix $H$ with the following
property. For every integer $h\ge1$, put
\[
 n_h=(386h+2)2^h,\qquad \epsilon_h=(386h+2)^{-2}.
\]
There is a binary $n_h\times n_h$ matrix $A_h$ such that
\[
 \operatorname{dist}_H(A_h)\ge\epsilon_h,
 \qquad
 \frac{N_H(A_h)}{n_h^{132}}\le\epsilon_h2^{-h}.
\]
Consequently, no positive constants $c,C$ give a polynomial removal
bound for this fixed $H$.

statements.label: prop:distance
statements.text:
Let $h\geq 1$, let $m=2^h$, and let $A=A_h$ be the matrix constructed
above, of order $n=d_hm$, where $d_h=386h+2$.  Every $H$-free binary
$n\times n$ matrix differs from $A$ in at least $m^2$ entries.
Consequently $A$ is $d_h^{-2}$-far from being $H$-free.

statements.title: The two body roles
statements.label: cor:body-roles
statements.text:
In every ordered copy of $H$ in $A_h$, the first $64$ rows and
columns are anchor representatives of one mode $t$. Its two body
rows belong respectively to $\mathsf R_1(t),\mathsf R_2(t)$, and its
two body columns belong respectively to
$\mathsf C_1(t),\mathsf C_2(t)$.
statements.section_title: Copies are confined to the leaf diagonal

statements.label: prop:copy-count
statements.text:
For every integer $h\geq 1$, every ordered copy of $H$ in $A_h$ maps the
pattern entry $(s+1,s+1)$ into
\[
 \mathcal L_h
 =\bigcup_{p=0}^{m-1} R_h^+(p)\times C_h^+(p).
\]
In particular, $|\mathcal L_h|=m$ and
\begin{equation}
 N_H(A_h)\leq m n^{2k-2},
 \qquad
 \frac{N_H(A_h)}{n^{2k}}
 \leq \frac{2^{-h}}{d_h^2}.
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Copies are confined to the leaf diagonal

statements.title: Canonical row--column sampling
statements.label: cor:canonical-testing
statements.text:
Fix $h\ge1$ and an integer $0\le q\le n_h$. Consider a tester that
chooses a uniformly random $q$-element row set $R\subseteq[n_h]$ and,
independently, a uniformly random $q$-element column set
$C\subseteq[n_h]$. It rejects only if the induced submatrix $A_h[R,C]$,
with the inherited orders, contains an ordered copy of $H$. Then
\[
 \Pr(\text{reject on }A_h)\le\epsilon_h2^{-h}q^2,
\]
and the rejection probability is zero when $q<66$. For every fixed
$\rho\in(0,1]$, rejection probability at least $\rho$ requires
\[
 q\ge\sqrt{\rho}\,\epsilon_h^{-1/2}2^{h/2},
\]
hence $q\ge\exp(\Omega(\epsilon_h^{-1/2}))$ along the sequence
$\epsilon_h$ as $h\to\infty$. Here $q$ is the sample size on each axis;
the induced submatrix has $q^2$ entries.

title: Polynomial vacuum representations and bridge mass for honeycomb walks
abstract: We prove that, under the all-length critical measure, a honeycomb bridge crossing a strip of h layers, with its initial port fixed and its terminal port free, has mean length \(h^{4/3+o(1)}\). We also obtain central visit probability \(R^{-2/3+o(1)}\) and mean length \(R^{4/3+o(1)}\) for macroscopic free-boundary chords in a regular hexagon.

tex.abstract: We prove that, under the all-length critical measure, a honeycomb bridge crossing a strip of $h$ layers, with its initial port fixed and its terminal port free, has mean length $h^{4/3+o(1)}$. We also obtain central visit probability $R^{-2/3+o(1)}$ and mean length $R^{4/3+o(1)}$ for macroscopic free-boundary chords in a regular hexagon.

statements.title: Strip mass and bridge length
statements.label: thm:pv:bridge
statements.text:
As the integer layer height $h$ tends to infinity,
\[
 b_h=h^{-1/4+o(1)},\qquad
 \ell_h=h^{13/12+o(1)},\qquad
 \mathbb E_h|\gamma|=h^{4/3+o(1)}.
\]
All three sums are finite. These exponents are unchanged if the paths
are also confined to horizontal distance $h\log^2h$ from their initial
port.
statements.section_title: Critical bridge length and a polynomial polygon observable

statements.title: Hexagon visits
statements.label: thm:pv:hexagon
statements.text:
The mass normalizing $\mathbb P_R$ is $R^{3/4+o(1)}$. Uniformly at
vertices in the concentric hexagon of side $R/3$,
\[
 \mathbb P_R(v\in\gamma)=R^{-2/3+o(1)}.
\]
The corresponding upper bound holds at every vertex, and
$\mathbb E_R|\gamma|=R^{4/3+o(1)}$.
statements.section_title: Critical bridge length and a polynomial polygon observable

statements.title: Mixed exits
statements.label: prop:pv:mixed
statements.text:
The conditioned event has unnormalized mass $h^{-1/4+o(1)}$ and
first-length mass $h^{13/12+o(1)}$. Hence its normalized mean length is
$h^{4/3+o(1)}$. Restricting horizontal distance to $h\log^2h$ preserves
these exponents. The total first-length mass of all exits, without the
height condition, is at most $h^{13/12+o(1)}$.
statements.section_title: Critical bridge length and a polynomial polygon observable

statements.title: Normalized separator pairing
statements.label: thm:pv:puncture
statements.text:
For every compact set $K\subset\{s\in\mathbb C:|\Im s|<\pi\}$ there
is $C_K<\infty$ such that, for all $n\ge1$ and $s\in K$,
\[
 |F_n(2\cosh s)|\le
 C_K n^{1/6+2\Re(s^2)/(3\pi^2)}.
\]
There is a disk about $\eta=0$, independent of $n$, in which $F_n$ has
no zeros. For each fixed $k$, the order-$k$ Taylor coefficient of
$\log F_n$ at zero is $O_k(1+\log n)$. At the positive fugacity two,
\[
 F_n(2)=n^{1/6+o(1)}.
\]
statements.section_title: Critical bridge length and a polynomial polygon observable

statements.title: Strip flux and crude bridge bounds
statements.label: cor:pv:strip-flux
statements.text:
The strip masses \(A_h,b_h\) are finite and satisfy
\begin{equation}
 b_h+\cos(\sigma\pi)A_h=1.
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\[
 A_{h+1}-A_h\le x_*^{-1} b_{h+1}^2,
 \qquad \frac{c}{h+1}\le b_h\le1.
\]

statements.title: Polynomial vacuum
statements.label: prop:pv:vacuum
statements.text:
Use twist \(\zeta=t^2=i\). Let \(\rho X=(x_N,x_1,\ldots,x_{N-1})\), and \(\Pi_\kappa\) the corresponding rotation of spin slots with factor \(\kappa^{h_N}\) from the last (now first) spin. We construct a charge-zero vector polynomial \(\Psi_N(X)\) with
\[
 F_{i,i+1}(x_i/x_{i+1})\Psi(X)=\Psi(s_i X),\qquad
 \Pi_\zeta\Psi(X)=\Psi(\rho X)
\]
(\(s_i\) adjacent transposition), homogeneous of degree \(\binom N2\),
with degree at most \(N-1\) in each variable. For a spin component
\(\Psi_{N,\boldsymbol h}\), the refined bounds are
\[
 h_j=+1\ \Longrightarrow\ \deg_{x_j}\Psi_{N,\boldsymbol h}\le N-2,
 \qquad
 h_j=-1\ \Longrightarrow\ x_j\mid\Psi_{N,\boldsymbol h}.
\]
It has the adjacent-pair reduction
\[
 \Psi_N(\ldots,a,Ta,\ldots)=s_C(a;Y)\ \iota_C \Psi_{N-2}(Y),
 \qquad
 s_C(a;Y)=(1+T)a\prod_{x\in Y}(x-t^5a)(x-t^6a),
\]
where \(Y\) is the remaining list and \(\iota_C\) inserts a \(C\) tensor in the indicated positions; and at last parameter zero its projection onto last spin zero is \((\prod_{j<N}x_j)\Psi_{N-1}\).

statements.title: Empty component
statements.label: prop:pv:empty-component
statements.text:
Put \(D(a,b)=a^2+\sqrt2 ab+b^2\) and
\(K(a,b)=(a^2-b^2)/D(a,b)\). The symmetric empty component is
\[
 S_N(X)=\prod_{i<j}\frac{D(x_i,x_j)}{x_i-x_j}\ {\rm Pf}[K(x_i,x_j)]
\]
where for odd size an extra last Pfaffian index has
\(K_{i,N+1}=1\), \(i\le N\), corresponding to parameter zero.
It satisfies
\[
 S_N(X^{-1})=\frac{S_N(X)}{\prod_i x_i^{N-1}}
\]
and the second fusion identity
\[
 S_N(a,t^2a,Y)=\sqrt2\,t a\prod_{y\in Y}(y-t^5 a)\ S_{N-1}(ta,Y).
\]

statements.title: Normalized reductions
statements.label: cor:pv:normalized-reductions
statements.text:
At generic parameters, the normalized states reduce by insertion of
\(C\) at adjacent sites \((a,Ta)\), and by insertion of \(I\) at
\((a,t^2a)\), replacing those sites by the single site \(ta\).
When one parameter tends to zero or infinity, the spin-zero component
at that slot tends to the reduced \(\Omega\), with scalar factor one.

statements.title: Physical separator pairing
statements.label: prop:pv:physical-pairing
statements.text:
For two homogeneous blocks of equal size $n$,
\[
 X_{n,n}(1,\ldots,1;\kappa)=F_n(\kappa+\kappa^{-1}).
\]
Here the left side is the bilinear vacuum contraction just defined and the right side is the positive polygon polynomial from Section~\ref{sec:pv:introduction}.

statements.title: Interpolation of the pairing
statements.label: prop:pv:pairing-interpolation
statements.text:
Fix \(\kappa\ne0\) and put \(\eta=\kappa+\kappa^{-1}\).
The family \(X_{n,m}\) is uniquely determined among rational functions
by the following properties. It is symmetric separately in its two
blocks, and \(S_N^2X_{n,m}\) is polynomial of degree at most
\(2(N-1)\) in each site, where \(N=n+m\). Within block A its
reductions are
\[
\begin{aligned}
 X_{n,m}(a,Ta,A';B)&=X_{n-2,m}(A';B),\\
 X_{n,m}(a,t^2a,A';B)&=X_{n-1,m}(ta,A';B),\\
 \lim_{a\to0\text{ or }\infty}X_{n,m}(a,A';B)
 &=X_{n-1,m}(A';B),
\end{aligned}
\]
The pair reductions require \(n\ge2\), and the extreme reduction
requires \(n\ge1\); the analogous rules hold in block B with \(m\)
in place of \(n\). The initial value is
\(X_{0,0}=1\), and at every balanced size \(n=m>0\),
\[
 X_{n,n}(a_1,\ldots,a_n;Ta_n,\ldots,Ta_1)=(1+\eta)^n.
\]

statements.title: Boundary exponent
statements.label: prop:pv:boundary
statements.text: For critical bridges across $h$ layers from a fixed bottom port to all top ports, $b_h=h^{-1/4+o(1)}$. The half-plane arch mass to the right is $1/(2\cos(3\pi/8))$; its height and diameter tails both have exponent $-1/4$.

statements.title: Pfaffian denominator
statements.label: prop:pv:denominator
statements.text:
The homogeneous empty component satisfies (\(D_0=2+\sqrt2,\ \delta=3/8\))
\[
 S_{2n}(1,\ldots,1)\ge c\,D_0^{-n}(4D_0^2/9)^{n^2} n^{5/48}.
\]

statements.label: prop:pv:planar-localization
statements.text:
The disk partition function satisfies
\[
 Z(R)=R^{1/12+o(1)}.
\]

statements.label: cor:pv:oversized-polygons
statements.text:
Fix \(\delta>0\). Suppose \(\mathcal U\) is a family of planar honeycomb
polygons enclosing 0 whose interiors are disjoint from their nontrivial
translates by a common pure lattice period of length \(p\). For all
sufficiently large \(p\),
\[
 \sum_{\substack{P\in\mathcal U\\
             \max_{z\in P}|z|>p^{1+\delta}}}x_*^{|P|}=O(1).
\]
The constant is independent of the family and the period direction.

statements.title: Finite visit recursion
statements.label: prop:pv:visits
statements.text:
For every finite filled vertex set $D$ and $v\in D$,
\begin{align}
 T_D(v)=3
 &+\sum_{\substack{P\subset D\\v\in P}}
 2x_*^{|P|-1}\big[-\cos\big(\sigma(2\pi-\tau_v(P))\big)\big]
 \\
 &+\sum_{\substack{P\subset D\\v\in P^\circ}}
 2x_*^{|P|}T_{P^\circ}(v).\notag
\end{align}
Here $P^\circ$ is the strict interior vertex set and
$\tau_v(P)\in\{\pi/3,-\pi/3\}$ is the counterclockwise turn at $v$.
Every coefficient on the right is positive. Thus $T_D(v)\ge3$,
it is monotone under inclusion of filled sets containing $v$, and
there are absolute constants $c,C>0$ such that
\[
 c\sum_{f\sim v}Z_D(f)\le T_D(v)\le C\sum_{f\sim v}Z_D(f).
\]
If $D$ is cut out by admissible tiling lines in a convex polygon and
$A_D(v)$ is the positive ordered excursion weight through $v$, then
\[
 \cos(3\pi/8)A_D(v)\le T_D(v)\le A_D(v).
\]

title: Positive Metric Entropy for the Standard Map at Large Parameters
abstract: We prove that the standard sine map of the two-dimensional torus has positive metric entropy with respect to normalized area for every sufficiently large positive parameter. This gives a full parameter tail, and hence answers Sinai's positive-parameter-measure conjecture affirmatively.

tex.abstract:
We prove that the standard sine map of the two-dimensional torus has
positive metric entropy with respect to normalized area for every
sufficiently large positive parameter. This gives a full parameter tail,
and hence answers Sinai's positive-parameter-measure conjecture
affirmatively.
sections: A product estimate across a fast bridge
Product distances and measures across scales
Support restrictions and the geometry of limiting distances
A capped deficit and the final balance

statements.label: main:entropy
statements.text:
There exists $k_0>0$ such that
\[
 h_m(f_k)>0\qquad\text{for every }k\ge k_0.
\]
Equivalently, for every such $k$ the largest Lyapunov exponent of $f_k$
is positive on a set of positive $m$-measure.

statements.title: Nonuniformly hyperbolic ergodic component
statements.label: main:components
statements.text:
For each $k\ge k_0$ there is a measurable $f_k$-invariant set $E=E(k)$
with $m(E)>0$ such that $(E,m(E)^{-1}m|_E,f_k)$ is ergodic and $f_k$ has
one positive and one negative Lyapunov exponent almost everywhere on $E$.
For some integer $N=N(k,E)\ge1$, there is a measurable partition
$E=E_0\sqcup\cdots\sqcup E_{N-1}$ such that
$f_k(E_j)=E_{j+1\bmod N}$ and
$(E_j,m(E_j)^{-1}m|_{E_j},f_k^N)$ is Bernoulli for every $j$.
All invariance and partition statements are modulo $m$-null sets;
each $E_j$ has area $m(E)/N>0$.

statements.title: Product estimate across a fast bridge
statements.label: bridge:theorem
statements.text:
There are absolute constants $c_b\in(0,1)$, $\kappa>0$, and $\sigma>0$
with the following property. Fix observation bounds $(R,L,B)$ and a
threshold $h>0$. For sufficiently large $M$ and sufficiently large
$n=b-a$, let $W,H$ be observations with these bounds, with $W\geq0$.
All indices occurring in one observation are within $\kappa n$ of $a$,
and all indices occurring in the other are within $\kappa n$ of $b$.
Either assignment of $W,H$ to the two ends is allowed. Then
\begin{equation}
 \E\!\left[
   \one_{\{\log_M\norm{T_{a,b}}\geq c_b n\}}
   W\one_{\{H>h\}}
 \right]
 \leq
 C\bigl(\E W+M^{-\sigma n}\bigr)\PP(H>h/2).
 
\end{equation}
The constants $c_b,\kappa,\sigma$ are independent of the observation
bounds and threshold. The constant $C$ and the lower size requirements
for $M,n$ may depend on $(R,L,B)$ and $h$, but not on the indices,
the defining functions, or the bridge location.

statements.title: Limits away from affinity
statements.label: scale:limits
statements.text:
After passing to a subsequence, the restrictions of $\mu_K$ and
$\nu_K$ to $\mathcal U$ converge vaguely to locally finite
nonnegative Borel measures $\mu$ and $\nu$, respectively. Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \xi_K\longrightarrow0\quad\hbox{vaguely on }\mathcal U.
\end{equation}
The measures $\mu$ and $\nu$ are supported on the closed class
$X_0\subset X$ consisting of arrays satisfying $d(s,t)\le|s-t|$
and the inequalities
\begin{equation}
 B_v(s,t)\ge\min\{B_v(s,p),B_v(p,t)\},\qquad
 B_v(s,t)=d(v,s)+d(v,t)-d(s,t)
\end{equation}
for every $v,s,t,p\in\mathcal D$. Every member of $X_0$ extends
uniquely to a continuous semimetric on $\R$, obeying the same
inequalities at all real arguments. Both limiting measures are
invariant under
\[
 (\tau_r d)(s,t)=d(s+r,t+r)\qquad(r\in\mathcal D).
\]
For every interval $I$ as in \cref{scale:local-mass},
\begin{equation}
 \int(J(I)+V(I))\,\dd\mu<\infty,
 \qquad
 \int(h(I)+J(I)+V(I))\,\dd\nu<\infty.
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \int h([0,1])\,\dd\nu\le1.
\end{equation}

title: Positive eigenvalues of the relative SU(2) BFSS Hamiltonian
abstract: We prove that the relative \(\mathop{\mathrm{SU}}\nolimits (2)\) BFSS Hamiltonian has infinitely many positive eigenvalues tending to infinity, with square-integrable eigenvectors. The operator is defined by closing the gauge-invariant supercharge form. This refutes, at N = 2, the exclusion of normalizable positive-energy states stated in the original BFSS paper.

tex.abstract:
We prove that the relative $\SU(2)$ BFSS Hamiltonian has infinitely many
positive eigenvalues tending to infinity, with square-integrable
eigenvectors. The operator is defined by closing the gauge-invariant
supercharge form. This refutes, at $N=2$, the exclusion of normalizable
positive-energy states stated in the original BFSS paper.

title: Positive lower density of large prime gaps
abstract: For every fixed C > 0, we prove that a positive proportion of consecutive prime gaps exceed \(C\log p\), where p is the smaller prime. The proportion is bounded below for every sufficiently large initial segment of the prime sequence, with a constant depending on C. It follows that the indices at which \(p_n/n\) increases have positive lower asymptotic density, answering a question of Erdős and Prachar.

tex.abstract:
For every fixed $C>0$, we prove that a positive proportion of consecutive
prime gaps exceed $C\log p$, where $p$ is the smaller prime. The proportion
is bounded below for every sufficiently large initial segment of the
prime sequence, with a constant depending on $C$. It follows that the
indices at which $p_n/n$ increases have positive lower asymptotic density,
answering a question of Erd\H{o}s and Prachar.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every fixed real $C>0$, there are constants $c(C)>0$ and $N_0(C)$
such that, for every integer $N\ge N_0(C)$,
\[
 \#\{1\le n\le N:p_{n+1}-p_n>C\log p_n\}\ge c(C)N.
\]

statements.title: Weights for adjacent intervals
statements.label: prop:weights
statements.text:
For each fixed $\lambda>0$ there is a finite constant $K_\lambda>0$
with the following property. For every $\varepsilon>0$, there are
weights $W_X(m)\ge0$, defined for integers $X<m\le2X$, such that
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E_X W_X&\longrightarrow1,
 &\mathbb E_X(W_XV_J)&\longrightarrow\lambda,\\
 \limsup_{X\to\infty}\mathbb E_X(W_XV_I)&\le\varepsilon,
 &\limsup_{X\to\infty}\mathbb E_X(W_XV_J^2)&\le K_\lambda,\\
 \mathbb E_X W_X^2&=O_{\lambda,\varepsilon}(1).
\end{align}
The constant $K_\lambda$ is independent of $\varepsilon$.
