statements.title: Moment identities and a detector bound
statements.label: prop:weight-moments
statements.text:
Hold $\lambda$, $k$, and the family $(f_j)_{0\le j\le k}$ fixed.
Then, as $X\to\infty$,
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E_XZ^2&\longrightarrow
       w:=\sum_{j=0}^k\alpha_j\|f_j\|_2^2,
       &\mathbb E_XZ^4&=O_{\lambda,k,\mathbf f}(1),
       \\
 \mathbb E_X(Z^2V_J)&\longrightarrow\lambda w,
       &\mathbb E_X(Z^2V_I)&\longrightarrow
       v:=\lambda\sum_{j=0}^k\alpha_j
                         \|f_j+Tf_{j+1}\|_2^2.
       
\end{align}
Choose once and for all a real $G\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$ with
$G(0)=1$ and $G(u)=0$ for $u\ge\tau$, and put
\[
 c_G=\int_0^\infty |G'(u)|^2\,du,
 \qquad C_*=\lambda+\lambda^2c_G^2.
\]
For every fixed family as above,
\begin{equation}
 \limsup_{X\to\infty}\mathbb E_X(Z^2V_J^2)\le C_*w.
 
\end{equation}
In particular, $C_*$ is independent of $k$ and of the family $(f_j)$.

statements.title: Cancellation between high dimensions
statements.label: prop:dimension-cancellation
statements.text:
For every fixed $\lambda>0$, there are families of the type used in
Proposition~\ref{prop:weight-moments}, with increasing finite maximum
dimension $k$, for which $w\to1$ and $v\to0$.

statements.title: Uniform mixed moments
statements.label: prop:mixed-moments
statements.text:
Put $L=\log X$, where $X$ tends to infinity through integers, and let
$\mathbb E_X$ denote the average over $X<m\le2X$. Fix nonnegative integers
$j_1,\ldots,j_R$. For each $r$, let $F_r$ be a real function on
$[0,\infty)^{j_r}$ admitting a smooth compactly supported extension to
$\mathbb R^{j_r}$, and suppose that on the orthant it vanishes outside
\[
 v_1+\cdots+v_{j_r}\le\rho_r.
\]
Here the support budgets $\rho_r\ge0$ are fixed. Dimension zero means a scalar,
with support budget zero. For positive divisors
define
\[
 D_{F_r}(m;\mathbf b^{(r)})=
 \sum_{d_{r,\ell}\mid m+b_{r,\ell}\ (1\le\ell\le j_r)}
 \prod_{\ell=1}^{j_r}\mu(d_{r,\ell})
 F_r\left(\left(\frac{\log d_{r,\ell}}L\right)_{\ell=1}^{j_r}\right).
\]
For $j_r=0$, this means $D_{F_r}=F_r$.

Let $\Gamma=\{(r,\ell):1\le r\le R,\ 1\le\ell\le j_r\}$, and fix a
surjection $\kappa:\Gamma\to\{1,\ldots,t\}$. Write
$\mathcal M_i=\kappa^{-1}(\{i\})$. Take distinct integer shifts
$a_1,\ldots,a_t$ with $|a_i|\le DL^B$, where $D>0$ and $B\ge1$ are fixed,
and set $b_{r,\ell}=a_{\kappa(r,\ell)}$. Choose $\delta\in\{0,1\}$.
In the marked case take one more
shift $a_0$, distinct from these and satisfying the same bound. Put
\[
 (\chi_\delta(m),\mathcal H)=
 \begin{cases}
 (1,\{a_1,\ldots,a_t\}),&\delta=0,\\
 (\vartheta(m+a_0),\{a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_t\}),&\delta=1,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad \vartheta(n)=(\log n)1_{\{n\text{ prime}\}}.
\]
Assume $\sum_r\rho_r<1$ if $\delta=0$, and $\sum_r\rho_r<1/2$ if
$\delta=1$. Then there is a real constant $\mathcal C$, depending only on
the functions and $\kappa$, such that
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E_X\left[\chi_\delta(m)\prod_rD_{F_r}(m;\mathbf b^{(r)})\right]
 =L^{-t}\left\{\mathfrak S(\mathcal H)\mathcal C
 +O\!\left(L^{-1/2}(\log L)^A\right)\right\}.
\end{equation}
Here $A$ is a fixed finite number depending only on $\sum_rj_r$; the implied
constant may depend on all the fixed data, but is uniform in the actual
shifts. In particular the error is additive when $\mathfrak S(\mathcal H)=0$.

If each $|\mathcal M_i|$ is at most two, the constant is
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal C=
 \int\prod_r\left((-1)^{j_r}\partial_1\cdots\partial_{j_r}F_r\right)
       \big((y_{\kappa(r,\ell)})_{\ell=1}^{j_r}\big)
       \prod_{i:\,|\mathcal M_i|=2}dy_i,
\end{equation}
where $y_i=0$ for $|\mathcal M_i|=1$, and each integrated variable ranges over
$[0,\infty)$. The zero-dimensional derivative is the original scalar.
When $\Gamma$ is empty, take $t=0$ and $\mathcal C=\prod_rF_r$.

title: Positive scalar curvature and uniform codimension-two width
abstract: We prove the quantitative continuous form of Gromov's scalar-curvature conjecture in every dimension n ≥ 4. Every complete connected smooth boundaryless n-manifold with scalar curvature at least one admits a continuous map to a simplicial complex of dimension at most \(n-2\) whose entire fibers have diameter bounded only in terms of n. We also obtain the continuous macroscopic-dimension conclusion for universal covers of closed manifolds with positive scalar curvature in every dimension n ≥ 2.

tex.abstract:
We prove the quantitative continuous form of Gromov's scalar-curvature
conjecture in every dimension $n\ge4$. Every complete connected smooth
boundaryless $n$-manifold with scalar curvature at least one admits a
continuous map to a simplicial complex of dimension at most $n-2$ whose
entire fibers have diameter bounded only in terms of $n$. We also obtain
the continuous macroscopic-dimension conclusion for
universal covers of closed manifolds with positive scalar curvature in
every dimension $n\ge2$.

Wide separations at a fixed original scale
Reconstruction and the map to a complex
Universal covers and the uniform simplex metric
Packets, finite horizons, and the induction invariant
Weighted minimizing cuts and the forms on retained sides
Global shielding and extension to cofaces
Regularization and restoration of the curvature invariant

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every integer \(n\ge4\), there is a finite constant \(C_n\) such
that every connected complete smooth Riemannian \(n\)-manifold
\((M,g)\), without boundary and with \(\Scal_g\ge1\), admits a
continuous map \(f:M\to K\) to a simplicial complex of dimension at
most \(n-2\) satisfying
\[
 \diam_g f^{-1}(y)\le C_n\qquad(y\in K).
\]
In particular, \(\UW_{n-2}(M,g)\le C_n\).

statements.title: Closed-manifold filling-radius bound
statements.label: cor:filling-radius
statements.text:
Let \((M,g)\) be a closed connected smooth Riemannian \(n\)-manifold
with \(n\ge4\) and \(\Scal_g\ge\sigma^2\) for some \(\sigma>0\). Then
\[
 \operatorname{FillRad}(M,g)\le \frac{C_n}{2\sigma},
\]
where \(C_n\) is the constant in Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.

statements.title: Continuous macroscopic dimension of universal covers
statements.label: cover:main
statements.text:
Let $(M,h)$ be a closed connected smooth Riemannian manifold of
dimension $n\ge2$ with positive scalar curvature.  Its universal cover,
with the lifted original metric $\widetilde h$, satisfies
\[
 \dim_{\mathrm{mc}}(\widetilde M,\widetilde h)\le n-2.
\]

statements.title: Aspherical obstruction
statements.label: cor:aspherical
statements.text:
No closed smooth aspherical manifold of dimension \(n\ge4\) admits
a Riemannian metric of strictly positive scalar curvature.

statements.title: Pressure law
statements.label: pressure:law
statements.text:
For every $A_0,P_0,\eps,b_0>0$ there exist $0<S_0\le1$, $T\ge1$, and a
smooth function
\[
 F:(-S_0,S_0)\times[T,\infty)\longrightarrow\R
\]
which is odd in $x$, has $F_x>0$, and satisfies
\begin{equation}
\begin{gathered}
 F_x\ge A_0t,\qquad |F_t|\le\eps|F|,\qquad FF_t\le\eps F_x,\\
 F_x\le b_0t^2\quad\text{or}\quad -FF_t\ge P_0F_x,\\
 F_x\le b_0t^2+\eps F^2.
\end{gathered}
\end{equation}
For each fixed $t\ge T$,
\[
 \lim_{x\to-S_0}F(x,t)=-\infty,
 \qquad \lim_{x\to S_0}F(x,t)=+\infty.
\]
These limits are uniform when $t$ ranges over a compact subinterval of
$[T,\infty)$.  The choices depend only on $A_0,P_0,\eps,b_0$ and fixed
numerical constants.  In particular, they are independent of any manifold,
metric, local cutoff, or subsequent deformation parameter.  The lower bound
$T$ may be increased after the construction.
statements.section_title: A pressure law with a quadratic budget

statements.title: Local stretching
statements.label: step:main
statements.text:
Fix $n\ge2$ and $0<\delta<1/10$, and put $L_*=1.004$.  There are
constants $W,T\ge1$, depending only on $n,\delta$, with the following
property.  Let $h_0$ be a complete smooth metric on a manifold $M^n$
without boundary, let $h\ge h_0$ be smooth, and let $t\ge T$ be smooth.
Let $A$ be a nonempty compact set and $B$ a nonempty closed set such that
\[
 \dist_{h_0}(A,B)\ge W.
\]
For every $0<d<\delta$ there are smooth $h'\ge h$ and $t'\ge t$ such that
the changes have compact support in $\{\dist_{h_0}(A,\cdot)<W\}$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal D(h',t')\ge \mathcal D(h,t)+(t'^2-t^2)
 -\delta\bigl(\tr_h h_0-\tr_{h'}h_0\bigr)t'^2-dt'^2,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 \dist_{h'}(A,B)\ge L_*W.
\end{equation}
In particular, $h'$ is complete.  Neither $W$ nor $T$ depends on $d$,
the geometry of $M$, or the sets $A,B$.

statements.title: Prescribed widths for a locally finite family
statements.label: rounds:wide
statements.text:
Let \((M,g)\) be complete, connected and smooth, with
\(\Scal_g\ge1\). There is a countable set of centers \((x_i)\) such that
\[
 A_i=\overline B_g(x_i,D),\qquad
 B_i=M\setminus B_g(x_i,2D)
\]
have the following properties: the \(A_i\) cover \(M\), and the closed
balls \(\overline B_g(x_i,2D)\) are locally finite. Suppose that every
\(B_i\) is nonempty. Given arbitrary finite numbers \(L_i>0\), there
exist a complete smooth metric \(h\ge g\) and a countable family of
smooth functions \((p_\alpha)\), whose supports form a locally finite
family of compact sets, for which
\begin{align}
 \dist_h(A_i,B_i)&>L_i \quad(i\ge1),\\
 \Scal_h-2\Delta_h\sum_\alpha p_\alpha
       -\left|\dd\sum_\alpha p_\alpha\right|_h^2
       -\sum_\alpha|\dd p_\alpha|_h^2&\ge\frac25.
\end{align}
Every sum in \eqref{rounds:stabilized} is locally finite. If some
\(B_i\) is empty, then \(\diam_g M\le4D\).
statements.section_title: Wide separations at a fixed original scale

statements.title: Finite compatible cutting
statements.label: finite:cut
statements.text:
Fix a finite number $N_*$ of labels and the stage constants in
\eqref{packet:constants}. Suppose a stage-$r$ packet diagram is obtained by
the regular splitting construction of \cref{packet:split}, with compatible
smooth base metrics and a finite common list of positive circle warps,
and satisfies \cref{packet:invariant}. After the radial stage, require the
complete compact-part/product-end geometry of \cref{packet:category,packet:geometry}.
Let $j_0$ be the next label, and suppose every nonempty parent packet has
base dimension at least two. Then $j_0$ can be processed as follows.

On every parent there is a compatible smooth regular defining function
with the prescribed signs on the current forced core closures. Keep its
zero wall as the new hit space. To each closed sign side attach the full
product cylinder over its boundary. These pieces form a compatible smooth
stage-$(r+1)$ packet diagram with the continuous projections described
above. The wall on a parent $E$ lies in $\operatorname{int}G_{j_0}$.
The remaining profiles may first be modified, their cores enlarged,
and their potentials increased in the parents; these data are then carried to the new pieces by restriction and cylinder projection.
There are compatible smooth metrics and potentials, and exactly $399$
new positive circle factors on each new packet, for which the entire
stage-$(r+1)$ invariant holds. Earlier forced signs are preserved.
The new packets have complete compact-part/product-end geometry. This
assertion includes a possible one-dimensional output, on which its scalar
lower bound holds everywhere.

The operation fixes every old warp identically equal to $1$. For a
remaining label that is passive on the finite downward source diagrams
and the face copies used in their comparisons---constant pole profile, full corresponding core, and spatially
constant potential $c_j$ agreeing on compared faces---the construction
can preserve the pole and core and choose its new potential to be exactly
$(1+3\eta_r/2)c_j$, where $\eta_r=1/(200N_*)$.

At stage zero the single parent may instead be an arbitrary complete
smooth manifold with no product-end or bounded-geometry assumption. Subject to the same scalar and separation assumptions, if its
data are the radial initialization of \cref{packet:initialization}, the
same conclusion holds for the first split. Every resulting wall component and every closed-side component is compact before the cylinders are attached, and these components form locally finite
families.

statements.title: Preservation of the invariant
statements.label: countable:step
statements.text:
Suppose that all nonempty parents at stage $r$ have base dimension at
least two and satisfy \eqref{countable:profile-invariant}--\eqref{countable:scalar-invariant}.
At $r=0$ use the compact radial blocks of \Cref{countable:initial}; at
$r\ge1$ suppose also that the packet geometry and
\Cref{countable:finite-data} hold. Processing label $r$ produces the
compatible smooth split, preserves the forced signs, and gives the
same assertions at stage $r+1$. Exactly $399$ new warp factors, with
common indices, are appended at this stage. Each whole resulting
packet has a finite relevant old warp list.

statements.title: The countable compatible construction
statements.label: countable:construction
statements.text:
All labels can be processed successively. At every finite stage the
packet diagram has the invariant above and no nonempty packet of
dimension at most one. After the radial stage it has finite exceptional
data on whole packets; at stage zero this assertion holds on buffered
compact radial blocks.
Its finite reconstruction $X_r$ has a proper collapse $q_r:X_r\to M$
and closed signed sides $P_i^{(r)},N_i^{(r)}$ for each processed center
label, with
\[
 P_i^{(r)}\cup N_i^{(r)}=X_r,\qquad
 P_i^{(r)}\cap N_i^{(r)}=W_i^{(r)},
\]
where $W_i^{(r)}$ is its wall. The forced preimages satisfy
\[
 q_r^{-1}(A_i)\subset P_i^{(r)}\setminus W_i^{(r)},\qquad
 q_r^{-1}(B_i)\subset N_i^{(r)}\setminus W_i^{(r)}.
\]
These inclusions hold in open phases and persist at every subsequent
finite stage. No $n-1$ distinct walls, even including the radial wall,
have a common point. Each center wall lies over its original open
outer ball, and its components are compact and locally finite.

Old horizons can be enlarged by identifications preserving collapse,
all walls, and all signed statuses. For any prescribed sequence
$\eps_r>0$ with $\sum_r\eps_r<1$, the next finite collar compression
can be chosen with collapse displacement less than $\eps_r$, preserving
the previously decided wall strata and signed sides. These are
finite-stage conclusions; the limiting fixed-copy construction is
made in the next section.

statements.title: Reconstructed partitions
statements.label: topology:partitions
statements.text:
The compatible cuts of \cref{countable:construction} give a continuous
proper map $q:M\to M$, and for every color $i$ closed sets $P_i,N_i,W_i$
such that
\begin{align}
 &d_0(q(x),x)<1,\\
 &P_i\cup N_i=M,\qquad P_i\cap N_i=W_i,
   \qquad W_i\subset q^{-1}\bigl(B_0(x_i,2D)\bigr),
   \\
 &q^{-1}(A_i)\subset P_i\setminus W_i,
   \qquad q^{-1}(B_i)\subset N_i\setminus W_i.
   
\end{align}
The wall family $(W_i)$ is locally finite, and no $n-1$ distinct walls
have a common point.
statements.section_title: Reconstruction and the map to a complex

statements.title: Finite-horizon reconstruction
statements.label: packet:reconstruction
statements.text:
Starting with $X$, perform finitely many compatible regular splits as
in \cref{packet:split}.  For the first split require locally finite
compact radial wall and side components.  At the later split for
color $i$, require the defining functions to be positive on the inverse
image of $A_i$ and negative on the inverse image of $B_i$, with those
inverse images contained in open regions of the stipulated signs.
After any $r\ge1$ of these splits, the diagram has a reconstruction
$X_r$, obtained by finite collar truncations and gluing at hit faces,
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=*]
\item $X_r$ is a smooth manifold homeomorphic to $X$.  Its $r$ labelled
walls are closed smooth hypersurfaces with simultaneous transverse
intersection charts.  Each wall component is compact, the component
families are locally finite, and the closed sign/hit pieces are exactly
the compact cornered truncations of the analytic packets, by components.
\item The packet maps glue to a proper continuous map $q_r:X_r\to X$.
There is a homeomorphism $H_r:X_r\to X$ such that
\begin{equation}
 d_0\bigl(H_r(z),q_r(z)\bigr)\le r\qquad(z\in X_r).
\end{equation}
\item Horizons can be enlarged to exceed any already specified
compatible product thresholds on the full analytic packets.  A horizon
is constant for all occurrences of a normal coordinate belonging to
one connected global wall component.  Such enlargement has an
identification with the previous reconstruction which preserves
$q_r$, every old wall, and every old side status.
\item Once color $i$ has been processed, $q_r^{-1}(A_i)$ remains in its
open positive phase and $q_r^{-1}(B_i)$ remains in its open negative
phase at every subsequent stage.  In particular its wall misses
$q_r^{-1}(A_i\cup B_i)$.
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: Packets, finite horizons, and the induction invariant

statements.title: Generic uniqueness on all required products
statements.label: cut:generic-uniqueness
statements.text:
After the radial split one common shift $c$, with $|c|<c_*$, can be chosen
such that there is exactly one local absolute minimizer, modulo null
sets, on every packet $E$ and every product $E\times\R^d$, $d\ge0$, for
the pulled-back weight and pressure $p_0+c$.  The unique product phase
is exactly $A_E\times\R^d$ modulo null sets, where $A_E$ is the unique
phase on $E$.
statements.section_title: Weighted minimizing cuts and the forms on retained sides

statements.title: Local GMT properties used here
statements.label: cut:gmt
statements.text:
Let $A$ satisfy \eqref{cut:local-minimality} on a smooth $m$-manifold,
$m\ge2$, with smooth positive $\omega$ and smooth $p$.  Put
$S=\supp|D\chi_A|$.  Then $S=S_{\rm reg}\cup\Sigma$, where $S_{\rm reg}$
is a smooth embedded hypersurface, $\Sigma$ is relatively closed, and
\begin{equation}
                         \dim_{\mathcal H}\Sigma\le m-8.
\end{equation}
A negative dimension bound means that $\Sigma$ is empty.  The outward
measure-theoretic normal extends smoothly on $S_{\rm reg}$.  With
$B(u,v)=\langle\nabla_u\nu,v\rangle$, its base mean curvature satisfies
\begin{equation}
                    H_g=p-\partial_\nu\log\omega.
\end{equation}
The unweighted multiplicity-one perimeter varifold has locally bounded
generalized mean curvature.  Its density exists at every support point;
monotonicity gives local uniform area upper bounds and positive area
lower bounds at support points.  Under the convergences of
\cref{cut:bv-compactness}, densities are upper semicontinuous at
converging points, provided the local generalized-mean-curvature bounds
are uniform.  The supports converge locally, and on every compact
subset of the regular limiting hypersurface convergence is smooth and
single-sheeted when the data converge smoothly.  On compact subsets of
the interiors of the limiting phases there is eventually no boundary.

Every tangent at a point of $S$ is a multiplicity-one locally
perimeter-minimizing boundary cone in the Euclidean tangent space.
A flat tangent implies regularity.  A tangent at a singular point is
therefore nonflat, and its translation-invariance spine has dimension
at most $m-8$.
statements.section_title: Weighted minimizing cuts and the forms on retained sides

statements.title: True cuts converge at packet ends
statements.label: cut:end-convergence
statements.text:
For the common generic shift, let $A_E$ be the true phase on each packet
and let $A_B$ be that on a face.  On translated windows escaping in a
product collar over a compact part of $B$, the phases $A_E$ converge to
$A_B\times\R^d$ in $L^1_{\rm loc}$, their perimeter measures and
varifolds converge, and their regular boundaries converge smoothly on
compact sets off the limiting singular set.  Their boundary supports
converge locally as well.  The same conclusions hold after passage to
any deeper product furnished by \cref{packet:escape}.
statements.section_title: Weighted minimizing cuts and the forms on retained sides

statements.title: Raw scalar domination
statements.label: cut:raw-domination
statements.text:
Let $V=R-1.02\Pi_{j_0}$, restricted to the wall and pulled back to the
cylinder when necessary.  Then
\begin{align}
 Q_S(v)&\ge\int_S Vv^2\,\dd\mu_S
                    +1.99\int_S|\grad v|^2\,\dd\mu_S,\\
 Q_\Omega(v)&\ge\int_\Omega Vv_b^2\,\dd\mu
       +\int_0^\infty\!\int_S Vv_c^2\,\dd\mu_S\,\dd t\notag\\
 &\quad+.94\int_\Omega|\grad v_b|^2\,\dd\mu
       +1.99\int_0^\infty\!\int_S|\grad v_c|^2
                                      \,\dd\mu_S\,\dd t.
                                      
\end{align}
Here $|\grad v_c|^2=|\grad_Sv_c|^2+|\partial_tv_c|^2$.
statements.section_title: Weighted minimizing cuts and the forms on retained sides

statements.title: The local shielding estimate
statements.label: local:sharp
statements.text:
There is a sufficiently small flatness number $\eta>0$, depending
only on $m$ and the fixed numerical coefficients, with the following
property.  Let $F$ be any piece from \cref{local:flat-pieces} for this
flatness number, in a sufficiently accurate chart.  For the potential
of \cref{local:shell}, there are $\varepsilon_F>0$ and $C_F<\infty$
such that, for every $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_F$,
\begin{equation}
 1.16\int D_\varepsilon v^2
           \le .78\mathcal N(v)+C_F\|v\|_2^2.
\end{equation}
This holds on the true wall and either joined side, and hence on
translated compact tests in a pure wall cylinder.  The constants
$\varepsilon_F,C_F$ may depend on the local smooth data and $F$,
but are independent of $\varepsilon$.  No vanishing trace condition
is imposed at a joined seam.

statements.title: The global shielding output
statements.label: shield:global
statements.text:
At a fixed stage $r$, let $j_0$ be the current label and keep its true
minimizers fixed.  There are updates of every remaining profile and
core, and compatible smooth additions $D_j\ge0$, with the following
properties on every parent packet $E$ of dimension $m$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item The updated profiles have locally Lipschitz finite truncations
and satisfy, almost everywhere on their finite bands,
\begin{equation}
 2\abs{\nabla\mu'_j}\le a_r(\mu'_j)^2+\Pi_j+D_j.
\end{equation}
All these data are exact compatible products.  Each core only enlarges,
and its closure remains in the interior of its designated updated pole
set.  The original forced sets and the anchor sign restrictions are
preserved.
\item With $G'_j=E\setminus(U_j^{\prime+}\cup U_j^{\prime-})$, the set
\begin{equation}
 H_E^*=\left\{x:\#\{j\ne j_0:x\in G'_j\}\ge m-2\right\}
\end{equation}
is closed and misses $\Sigma_E$.  In an exact collar over a face $B$,
its projection is contained in $H_B^*$.  This holds for every further
face and every simultaneous product limit.
\item For one common $\theta_*<.9$, all walls and joined sides satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \int 1.16\sum_{j\ne j_0}D_jv^2
 \le\theta_*\bigl(\mathcal N(v)+e_0\norm v_2^2\bigr)
 \le .9\bigl(\mathcal N(v)+e_0\norm v_2^2\bigr).
\end{equation}
The additions are bounded with their derivatives on each post-radial
packet.  There are only finitely many local additions on each such
packet and only finitely many extensions into it.
\end{enumerate}
For the initial radial parent the same conclusions hold with locally
finite additions over its compact transition shells; boundedness is
asserted on the corresponding compact blocks and
\cref{shield:form-output} holds on every compact test.  No convergence
assertion at an end of the original manifold is needed.
statements.section_title: Global shielding and extension to cofaces

statements.title: The full invariant step
statements.label: regular:step
statements.text:
Assume the stage $r$ invariant and the conclusion of
\Cref{shield:global}.  For every nonempty parent packet of base
dimension at least two, processing $j_0$ produces the compatible
smooth split packets of
\Cref{packet:split}, with the required forced signs and continuous
projection maps.  There are smooth compatible old metrics and $399$
new torus factors on every packet such that the profiles, cores,
potentials, and scalar curvature satisfy the stage $r+1$ invariant.
This includes a possible one-dimensional output, on which the scalar
lower bound is global.  After the radial split the packets have the
complete compact-part/product-end geometry of
\Cref{packet:geometry}.

title: Positive scalar curvature forces rational inessentiality
abstract: We prove that every closed connected oriented smooth manifold admitting strictly positive scalar curvature is rationally inessential: its rational fundamental class maps to zero under the classifying map. No spin or fundamental-group hypothesis is needed, and there is no upper dimension bound. This proves the Gromov–Lawson aspherical conjecture; moreover, every nonnegative-scalar-curvature metric on a closed aspherical manifold is flat. We also show that every closed oriented smooth manifold of positive dimension with nonnegative scalar curvature has zero real simplicial volume, proving the qualitative vanishing consequence of Gromov's conjectural comparison.

tex.abstract:
We prove that every closed connected oriented smooth manifold admitting
strictly positive scalar curvature is rationally inessential: its rational
fundamental class maps to zero under the classifying map. No spin or
fundamental-group hypothesis is needed, and there is no upper dimension bound.
This proves the Gromov--Lawson aspherical conjecture; moreover, every
nonnegative-scalar-curvature metric on a closed aspherical manifold is flat.
We also show that every closed oriented smooth manifold of positive dimension
with nonnegative scalar curvature has zero real simplicial volume, proving the
qualitative vanishing consequence of Gromov's conjectural comparison.

statements.title: Rational inessentiality
statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $M^n$ be a closed connected oriented smooth manifold of dimension
$n\ge2$. If $M$ admits a Riemannian metric of strictly positive scalar
curvature, then
\[
 (c_M)_*[M]=0\qquad\text{in }H_n(B\pi_1(M);\Q).
\]

statements.title: The Gromov--Lawson aspherical conjecture
statements.label: cor:aspherical
statements.text:
No closed smooth aspherical manifold, whether orientable or not, admits a
Riemannian metric of strictly positive scalar curvature.

statements.title: Aspherical nonnegative-scalar-curvature rigidity
statements.label: cor:aspherical-flat
statements.text:
Let $g$ be a Riemannian metric of nonnegative scalar curvature on a closed
smooth aspherical manifold $M$, not necessarily oriented. Then $g$ is flat.

statements.title: Oriented target-map obstruction
statements.label: cor:degree-aspherical
statements.text:
Let $M^n$ and $N^n$ be closed connected oriented smooth manifolds of
dimension $n\ge2$, with $N$ aspherical. If a continuous map $f:M\to N$
has nonzero ordinary oriented degree $d\in\Z\setminus\{0\}$, then $M$
admits no Riemannian metric whose scalar curvature is strictly positive
everywhere.

In particular, if $P^n$ is any closed connected oriented smooth manifold,
the oriented connected sum $N\#P$ admits no such metric.

statements.title: Simplicial-volume vanishing
statements.label: cor:simplicial
statements.text:
Every closed oriented smooth manifold of positive dimension
admitting a Riemannian metric of nonnegative scalar curvature has zero
real simplicial volume.

statements.title: Comparison data from rational essentiality
statements.label: thm:comparison-data
statements.text:
Let $(M^n,g_M)$ be a closed connected oriented Riemannian manifold,
$n\ge2$, let $\Gamma=\pi_1(M)$, and suppose that its classifying map
$c_M:M\to B\Gamma$ satisfies
\[
 (c_M)_*[M]\ne0\quad\text{in }H_n(B\Gamma;\Q).
\]
There are constants $J>0$ and $R_0\ge1$ such that, for every real
$R\ge R_0$, there exist a closed oriented smooth manifold $A$, a
principal left $\Gamma$-cover $\widehat A\to A$, and an integer
$q=n+\dim A>n$ with the following properties.  The diagonal cover
\[
 Z=(\widetilde M\times\widehat A)/\Gamma\longrightarrow M\times A
\]
is oriented and has dimension $q$.  There are a smooth compactly
supported map $G:Z\to\R^q$ and a relatively compact open set
$\Omega\subset Z$ such that
\begin{equation}

 \deg(G,\Omega,0)\ne0,
 \qquad \norm{G}_\infty>3\quad\text{on }\partial\Omega,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}

 \max_{1\le i\le q}\sup_Z\abs{d_{\widetilde M}G_i}_{g_M}
 \le\frac JR,
 \qquad \log q\le JR.
\end{equation}
Write $\pi_Z:Z\to M\times A$ for the covering projection. Its
differential gives a global splitting
\[
 TZ=E_M\oplus E_A,\qquad
 E_M=(d\pi_Z)^{-1}(TM\oplus0),\qquad
 E_A=(d\pi_Z)^{-1}(0\oplus TA).
\]
The bundle $E_M$ is tangent to the $\widetilde M$ fibres of $Z\to A$,
and $E_A$ is the flat lift of the parameter directions. We write
$d_{\widetilde M}G_i=dG_i|_{E_M}$. For each fixed $R$, after choosing any
smooth metric on $A$, all derivatives of $G$ in the lifted product
geometry are bounded.  No bound uniform in $R$ is asserted for
parameter derivatives or for derivatives of order greater than one.
The covers and the parameter manifolds need not be connected.

statements.title: Compact diagonal pairing
statements.label: prop:compact-pairing

statements.title: Exact scalar-curvature identity
statements.label: prop:scalar-update
statements.text:
At a point where $t>0$, choose a $g$-orthonormal frame
$e_1=\nabla f/t,e_2,\ldots,e_{\dim B}$, and put
\[
 \mathfrak p=\frac{tN'(t)}{N(t)},\qquad
 A=d\log t,\qquad
 C_{jk}=t^{-1}\Hess_g f(e_j,e_k)\quad(j,k>1).
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 \Scal_{g^+}-\Scal_g
 ={}&D^2-2U(D)+r^2\abs{C}^2+(e_1r)^2\\
 &+2r^2(1+\mathfrak p)(v^2-\mathfrak p r^2)
       \sum_{j>1}A(e_j)^2.
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
In particular, the final term is nonnegative whenever
$\mathfrak p\ge0$ and $\mathfrak p N(t)^2t^2\le1$.
For $N\equiv1$, one also has, everywhere,
\begin{equation}
 \Scal_{g^+}-\Scal_g=\abs{II}^2+D^2-2U(D),
\end{equation}
where $II$ is the second fundamental form of the ordinary product graph.
The inverse graph metric on base covectors and the volume form of $g^+$ are
\begin{equation}
 P=g^{-1}-U\otimes U,
 \qquad dV_{g^+}=dV_g\,d\theta.
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: A scalar-curvature identity for graph stabilization

statements.title: Uniform graph solvability
statements.label: thm:uniform-graph
statements.text:
Let $(B,g)$ be uniformly controlled as above, and let $\ell\in C_b^\infty(B)$. Fix $\eps,w,B_0,s>0$ and $0\le\beta<1$. Suppose $N$ is smooth, positive, nondecreasing, constant near zero, and equal to $1$ for $t\ge1/2$. Define the quantities in \eqref{eq:graph-quantities} and
\[
 \lambda(r)=B_0(r^2+s^2)^{\beta/2}.
\]
There is a unique solution in the uniform $C^{2,\alpha}$ class with a uniform band margin to
\begin{equation}
 -\diver_g U
   =\lambda(r)\tan\left(\frac{\ell-\eps f}{w}\right),
 \qquad \abs{\ell-\eps f}<\frac{\pi w}{2}.
\end{equation}
This solution lies in $C_b^\infty(B)$, and the band has a positive uniform margin.
The metric \eqref{eq:graph-metric-update} is uniformly controlled and complete.

The solution is invariant under every isometry preserving the equation's
data. The following parameter statement will be used below. Fix the
reference cover, its metric and nested charts, and the equation parameters
$\eps,w,B_0,s,\beta,N$. Let $(g_a,\ell_a)$ be a jointly smooth family over
a finite-dimensional parameter manifold $A$. For every relatively compact
subset $V'\Subset V$ of a parameter chart, assume common constants
$c_{V'},C_{V'}>0$ such that
\[
 c_{V'}g_{\rm ref}\le g_a\le C_{V'}g_{\rm ref}\qquad(a\in V'),
\]
and common bounds in the fixed reference charts for every mixed derivative
of the coefficients of $g_a$ and of $\ell_a$, including order zero. Then
$a\mapsto f_a$ is smooth in every $C_b^{j,\alpha}$ norm, for $j\ge0$ and
$0<\alpha<1$. If $A$ is compact,
all mixed derivatives of $f_a$ are uniformly bounded and the tangent band
has a common positive margin. For a bundle of such covers, the local
solutions glue whenever fixed reference deck transformations carry one
local data set to another.
statements.section_title: Solving the graph equation on a cover

statements.title: Logarithmic shortening
statements.label: thm:shortening
statements.text:
Suppose $\Scal_M\ge\kappa>0$. On the above bundle $Z$, let
$G:Z\to\R^q$ be smooth and bounded with all mixed derivatives bounded, and suppose $L_0>0$ and
\[
 \sup_{1\le i\le q}\abs{d_{\widetilde M}G_i}\le L_0,
 \qquad q\ge2.
\]
There is a constant $C_n$ depending only on $n$ such that, if
\begin{equation}
 C_n(2+\log q)L_0^2\le\kappa/4,
\end{equation}
then for every finite integer $k\ge1$ there are a complete stabilized metric
\[
 \mathfrak g_k=h_k+\sum_{\nu=1}^{kq}m_{k,\nu}^2d\theta_\nu^2
 \quad\text{on }Z\times\T^{kq}
\]
and a smooth bounded map $G^{(k)}:Z\to\R^q$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \Scal_{\mathfrak g_k}\ge\kappa/2,\qquad
 \norm{G^{(k)}-G}_{\infty}<\pi/10,\qquad
 \abs{dG^{(k)}}_{\rm op}\le\sqrt{q+1}\,4^{-k}L_0.
\end{equation}
The infinity norm in the middle inequality is the target coordinate maximum, followed by the supremum over $Z$. All metric coefficients, warps, and maps have uniform bounds of every order at each fixed finite stage; their equivalence and derivative constants may depend on that stage.

statements.title: Stabilized contraction at a fixed scale
statements.label: cor:stabilized-contraction
statements.text:
Assume $\Scal_M\ge\kappa>0$ and take the comparison data of
\cref{thm:comparison-data} at scale $R$, so that
\[
 L_0=J/R,\qquad \log q\le JR.
\]
For all sufficiently large $R$, fix these data once and for all. Then for every finite $k\ge1$ there is a stabilized metric $\mathfrak g_k$ on $Z\times\T^{kq}$ with scalar curvature at least $\kappa/2$, and a smooth map
\[
 F_k:Z\longrightarrow S^q
\]
equal to a single value outside a compact set, with nonzero degree, such that
\begin{equation}
 \abs{dF_k}_{\rm op}\le C(q)4^{-k}J/R.
\end{equation}
The sphere has its standard unit metric. The constant $C(q)$ is independent of $k$. If desired, the circle lengths may be increased so that the projection to the standard $\T^{kq}$ also has operator norm at most $4^{-k}J/R$; this does not change scalar curvature or the bound on $dF_k$.

statements.title: Stabilized torical obstruction
statements.label: thm:torical-obstruction
statements.text:
For every integer $d\geq2$ and every $\chi>0$ there is a number
$\delta(d,\chi)>0$ for which the following data do not exist:
\begin{enumerate}
 \item a smooth oriented $d$-manifold $Y$ without boundary, possibly
 disconnected, with a torus-stabilized metric $\mathcal G$ satisfying
 $\Scal_{\mathcal G}\geq\chi$;
 \item a smooth map $F:Y\to S^d$, equal to one value outside a compact
 set, such that $\deg F\ne0$ and
 $\norm{dF}_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\delta(d,\chi)$ everywhere.
\end{enumerate}
The constant is independent of the finite circle count in
\cref{eq:stabilized-metric}. Neither the base metric nor the stabilized
metric is assumed complete.
statements.section_title: The stabilized obstruction from the torical theorem

title: Positively curved Einstein four-manifolds
abstract: We prove the classification conjecture for connected smooth closed Einstein four-manifolds with strictly positive sectional curvature. Up to positive scaling and isometry, every such manifold is the round four-sphere, the complex projective plane with its Fubini–Study metric, or real projective four-space with its round metric. No orientability assumption is needed.

tex.abstract: We prove the classification conjecture for connected smooth closed Einstein four-manifolds with strictly positive sectional curvature. Up to positive scaling and isometry, every such manifold is the round four-sphere, the complex projective plane with its Fubini--Study metric, or real projective four-space with its round metric. No orientability assumption is needed.

statements.label: thm:classification
statements.text:
Let $(M,g)$ be a connected smooth closed Einstein four-manifold with
strictly positive sectional curvature, without an orientability
assumption. There is a constant $a>0$ such that $(M,ag)$ is isometric to
the standard round $S^4$, to $\mathbb{CP}^2$ with its Fubini--Study
metric, or to $\mathbb{RP}^4$ with its standard round metric.

statements.title: Differential equations for the Weyl blocks
statements.label: prop:weyl-derivative-equations
statements.text:
The tensor $Z=\nabla T$ belongs to the parallel subbundle
$G$ of type $(5/2,1/2)$. On this bundle, put
$B_{\mathrm{op}}=Q_{5/2}(T)$. Then
\[
 \Delta T=6(T-N),\qquad
 N=(T^2)_0=T^2-2v^2\operatorname{Id},
\]
and
\begin{equation}
 \Delta Z=(13-20B_{\mathrm{op}})Z.
 \tag{1}
\end{equation}
Every statement has an exchanged counterpart for $U$.

statements.title: Characteristic identities
statements.label: prop:characteristic-identities
statements.text:
Let $n_+$ and $n_-$ be the finite nonnegative integer dimensions of
the spaces of harmonic self-dual and anti-self-dual two-forms. The Euler
characteristic and signature of $M$ are, respectively,
\[
 \chi=2+n_++n_-,\qquad \tau=n_+-n_-.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 8\pi^2\chi
   &=6\operatorname{Vol}(M)
        \bigl(1+\mathbf E(v^2+b^2)\bigr),\\
 12\pi^2\tau
   &=6\operatorname{Vol}(M)\,\mathbf E(v^2-b^2).
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{6}
\end{equation}
If $U=0$, then $n_-=0$; likewise $T=0$ implies $n_+=0$.

statements.title: Upper volume deficit
statements.label: prop:upper-volume-deficit
statements.text:

\[
 \frac{V_M}{8\pi^2/3}\le 1-\frac{3}{40}s_0.
 \tag{7}
\]

statements.title: Weighted Hessian inequality
statements.label: prop:weighted-hessian
statements.text:
For every global Lipschitz scalar weight \mbox{$m\ge m_0>0$},
\begin{equation}
 0\le\mathbf E\left[
 mG_v(p,k,l)
 -\frac56\sum_i m_i\,
    \frac{\operatorname{tr}\bigl(Z_i\sum_jZ_j^2\bigr)}6
 +\frac{\langle\mathcal P(L_m)_Y,(L_m)_Y\rangle}{24m}
 \right],
 \tag{10}
\end{equation}
where \(i,j\) in the middle term are derivative indices and
\[
 G_v=\left(-42-3b^2-\frac{10}{3}v^2\right)e
       +75B+\frac{25}{3}C_N-\frac{100}{3}E_B
       +5v^2|p|^2.
\]

statements.title: Three bounds for the combined integrand
statements.label: prop:coupling-estimates
statements.text:
For this decomposition, define
\[
 r=R_v|p|^2+R_b|q|^2,\qquad
 j=(|p|^2+|q|^2)
       \left(\frac{|p|^2}{v}+\frac{|q|^2}{b}\right).
\]
Then, almost everywhere,
\[
 \mathcal I_4\le-cj,\qquad
 \mathcal I_2\le2\Theta r,\qquad
 \mathcal I_0\le-\frac{\Theta^2}{c}.
\]
The corresponding derivative summands are assigned value zero on a
zero set, as in \eqref{eq:3}. The total integrand and the bounds are
integrable, and $\mathbf E\mathcal I\ge0$.

statements.label: prop:parallel-models

statements.title: The oriented classification
statements.label: cor:oriented-classification
statements.text:
Every connected oriented smooth closed Einstein four-manifold with
strictly positive sectional curvature is, after positive scaling,
isometric to the round $S^4$ or to $\mathbb{CP}^2$ with its
Fubini--Study metric.

title: Positivity of Serre's Intersection Multiplicity
abstract: We prove Serre's positivity conjecture, including ramified mixed characteristic. If two nonzero finitely generated modules over a regular local ring have tensor product of finite length and complementary dimensions, then their intersection multiplicity is strictly positive.

tex.abstract:
We prove Serre's positivity conjecture, including ramified mixed
characteristic. If two nonzero finitely generated modules over a regular local
ring have tensor product of finite length and complementary dimensions, then
their intersection multiplicity is strictly positive.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $(R,\m)$ be a commutative Noetherian regular local ring of dimension
$d$, and let $M,N$ be nonzero finitely generated $R$-modules. If
$\length_R(M\otimes_R N)<\infty$ and
$\dim_R M+\dim_R N=d$, then
\[
  \chi^R(M,N)>0.
\]

statements.title: Finite strict-transform intersection
statements.label: cor:tangent-cone
statements.text:
Let $(A,\m)$ be a commutative Noetherian regular local ring with residue
field $k$, and let $P,Q$ be prime ideals such that $A/(P+Q)$ has finite
length and $\dim(A/P)+\dim(A/Q)=\dim A$. Write $e_\m$ for Hilbert--Samuel
multiplicity and put
\[
 T=\operatorname{gr}(A/P)\otimes_{\operatorname{gr}A}\operatorname{gr}(A/Q),
\]
where all associated graded rings use the maximal-ideal filtrations.
If $\dim T\leq1$, then
\[
 \chi^A(A/P,A/Q)\geq e_\m(A/P)e_\m(A/Q),
\]
with equality if and only if $\dim T=0$.

statements.title: Normalized-length input
statements.label: len:input
statements.text:
Let $(D,\mathfrak d,k)$ and a chosen finite generically separable base
$A\subseteq D$ be as in Lemma~\ref{len:normalization}, and let
$\Lambda$ be the tower \eqref{len:tower-definition}.  There is a
$D$-algebra $C_D$, carrying a compatible $\Lambda$-action, such that
restriction of scalars defines an additive nonnegative length
$\lambda_D=\lambda_\infty$ on its modules annihilated by a power of
$\mathfrak d$.  For every parameter system $z_1,\ldots,z_h$ of $D$
and every integer $v\geq1$,
\begin{align}
 \lambda_D H_i(z_1^v,\ldots,z_h^v;C_D)&=0\qquad(i>0),
                                      \\
 \lambda_D\bigl(C_D/(z_1^v,\ldots,z_h^v)C_D\bigr)
                    &=v^h e((z_1,\ldots,z_h),D).
                                      
\end{align}
The right side is positive and finite.  The algebra and length are
independent of the parameter system $z$.
For the regular parameters of $A$, in particular,
\begin{equation}
 \lambda_D\bigl(C_D/(t_1^v,\ldots,t_h^v)C_D\bigr)
                         =v^h\rank_A D.
\end{equation}
The finite-stage, infimum, and supremum properties of
Lemma~\ref{len:tower} remain available on underlying tower modules;
they do not require that the relevant submodules or covers be
$C_D$-modules.

statements.title: Finite-length base change
statements.label: len:finite-length-base-change
statements.text:
In Theorem~\ref{len:input}, put $r=\rank_A D$.
For every finite-length $A$-module $V$,
\[
 \lambda_D\Tor_i^A(V,C_D)=0\quad(i>0),\qquad
 \lambda_D(V\otimes_A C_D)=r\length_A(V).
\]
Moreover $\lambda_D(C_D/\mathfrak d C_D)>0$.

statements.title: Supported rational descent
statements.label: ds:descent
statements.text:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian $\Z_{(p)}$-algebra of finite Krull
dimension, let $J\subset A$ be an ideal containing $p$, and let $H$ be a connective
associative $A$-algebra with central $A$-action.
Let $T$ be a finite commutative $A$-algebra with an action of a finite
group $G$ over $A$. Suppose that $\Spec T\to\Spec A$ is surjective and
that $G$ acts transitively on the points of every geometric fiber.
Then pullback induces an equivalence
\begin{equation}
 \K^J(H)_\Q
 \simeq
 \bigl(\K^J(H\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}T)_\Q\bigr)^{hG}.
 
\end{equation}
In particular, the map
\begin{equation}
 K_0^J(H)\otimes\Q
 \longrightarrow
 \bigl(K_0^J(H\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}T)\otimes\Q\bigr)^G
 
\end{equation}
is surjective.

statements.label: as:evaluations
statements.text:
There are homological functors
\[
 \mathsf H_i^{\mathrm{ord}}:\mathcal P_T^J
       \longrightarrow\overline{\mathcal A}_T,
 \qquad
 \mathsf H_i^C:\mathcal P_T^J
       \longrightarrow\overline{\mathcal A}_C
\]
whose values on a uniformly supported lift are its ordinary homology
sequence and its homology sequence after tensoring with $C$,
respectively. For each object $X$, their lengths
\[
 b_i^{\mathrm{ord}}(X)=\overline\length_T
       \mathsf H_i^{\mathrm{ord}}(X),
 \qquad
 b_i^C(X)=\overline\lambda\mathsf H_i^C(X)
\]
are finite nonnegative real numbers, zero outside a finite range.
Their Euler sums define homomorphisms
\[
 \chi_{\mathrm{ord}},\chi_C:K_0(\mathcal P_T^J)\longrightarrow\mathbb R.
\]
If $F=(F_n)$ is a bounded free sequence whose image is supported,
and $v$ makes all $z_j^v$ act as zero on that image, then for either
choice of evaluation, writing $b_i(F)=b_i(q_TF)$,
\begin{equation}
 (1+t)^e\sum_i b_i(F)t^i
  =\sum_i t^i\lim_{n\to\mathcal U}
     \frac{\operatorname{len}
       H_i(K_v\otimes_A F_n)}{s_n}.
 
\end{equation}
Here $\operatorname{len}=\length_T$ in the ordinary case; in the
$C$ case the complex on the right is further tensored over $T$
with $C$, and $\operatorname{len}=\lambda$. The identity is one
of finite Laurent polynomials.

statements.label: as:base-equality
statements.text:
For every $X\in\mathcal P_A^J$,
\[
 \chi_{\mathrm{ord}}(X\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}T)
   =r\chi_A(X)
   =\chi_C(X\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}T).
\]
These equalities hold for summands defined by idempotents in the
Verdier quotient, without assuming that the idempotents lift to
chain maps before localization.

statements.title: Asymptotic norm comparison
statements.label: as:norm
statements.text:
Let $A,J,T,C,\lambda$ satisfy the setup of this section and
\eqref{as:length-hypotheses}. Suppose a finite group $G$ acts on $T$
over $A$, the map $\Spec T\to\Spec A$ is surjective, and $G$ is
transitive on every geometric fiber. Then, for every
$X\in\mathcal P_T^J$,
\[
 \sum_{g\in G}\chi_{\mathrm{ord}}(gX)
   =\sum_{g\in G}\chi_C(gX).
\]
Neither invariance of $\lambda$ under $G$ nor equality of the two
evaluations on individual classes is assumed.

title: Posterior replicas and conditional information in Gaussian regression
abstract: For a signal with density bounded by L relative to uniform probability on \(S^{d-1}\), we bound the information in a finite message W formed from exact Gaussian measurements, conditional on an independent projection revealed only to the analyst. For explicit row counts proportional to d, the bound is \(O(H(W)/d+d+\log(2+\log L))\). Consequently, a finite-state learner with \(o(d^2)\) persistent bits and a deterministic sample horizon needs \(\Omega(d\log(1/\epsilon))\) fresh noiseless Gaussian measurements for constant-probability angular accuracy \(0\lt \epsilon\le1/10\) under the uniform spherical prior.

tex.abstract:
For a signal with density bounded by $L$ relative to uniform probability
on $S^{d-1}$, we bound the information in a finite message $W$ formed
from exact Gaussian measurements, conditional on an independent projection
revealed only to the analyst. For explicit row counts proportional to $d$,
the bound is $O(H(W)/d+d+\log(2+\log L))$.
Consequently, a finite-state learner with $o(d^2)$ persistent bits and a
deterministic sample horizon needs $\Omega(d\log(1/\epsilon))$ fresh
noiseless Gaussian measurements for constant-probability angular accuracy
$0<\epsilon\le1/10$ under the uniform spherical prior.
sections: Finite states and the information required at the endpoint
Posterior replicas and exact equal-label measures
A Gaussian test that cancels the affine volume
Current-state recurrences and the streaming bound
Haar projections and posterior replica information
Stiefel incidence and conditional block information

statements.title: Gaussian replica block bound
statements.label: thm:gaussian-block
statements.text:
For all sufficiently large $d$, set
\[
 k=2\lfloor d/16\rfloor,\qquad m=k,\qquad t=m+1,\qquad \ell=4k.
\]
Suppose $p=f\sigma_d$ is a probability with $0\le f\le L<\infty$.
In the block experiment above, let $A$ have $k$ rows and let $B$ have
$\ell$ rows. There is an absolute constant $C$ such that
\begin{equation}
 I(S;W\mid B,BS)
 \le \frac{H(W)}{t}+Cd+C\log(2+\log L).
\end{equation}
The bound is uniform over the prior, the density bound $L$, and the message
kernel. The labels used to produce $W$ are the exact values $AS$.

statements.title: Uniform-prior sample lower bound
statements.label: thm:streaming
statements.text:
Let $M(d)=o(d^2)$ be nonnegative integer-valued, and let
$0<\epsilon(d)\le1/10$. Suppose a family of learners in
Definition~\ref{def:streaming-model} satisfies
\[
 \Prob\{\arccos\langle\widehat S,S\rangle\le\epsilon(d)\}\ge\frac23
 \qquad\text{when }S\sim\sigma_d,
\]
where the probability includes the signal, samples, and learner randomness.
Then there is an absolute $c>0$ such that
\[
 T(d)\ge c\,d\log\frac1{\epsilon(d)}
\]
for all sufficiently large $d$. The eventual threshold may depend on the
memory sequence.

statements.title: Three endpoint substitutions
statements.label: cor:replica-endpoints
statements.text:
Assume $0<\epsilon\le1/10$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:residual-information}.
For sufficiently large $d$ the following bounds hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item If $G$ is Gaussian, $p\ge3/5$, and $0\le b\le d/2$, the beta-variance bound (with
the separate deterministic case at $b=0$) and the angular cap just described
give
\begin{equation}
 I(S;V\mid G,GS)\ge
 \tfrac12(d-b-1)\log\frac1{5\epsilon}-\log2.
\end{equation}
\item If $G$ is a Haar frame, $p\ge2/3$, and $b=\lfloor d/4\rfloor$, Markov's bound
$\Prob\{R<1/2\}\le4b/(3d)\le1/3$ gives
\begin{equation}
 I(S;V\mid G,GS)\ge
 \tfrac13(d-b-1)\log\frac1{4\epsilon}-\log2.
\end{equation}
\item If $G$ is Gaussian, $p\ge3/5$, and $b=\lfloor d/2\rfloor$, the direct Gaussian bound
$\Prob\{R<1/2\}\le90/d$ gives
\begin{equation}
 I(S;V\mid G,GS)\ge
 \tfrac12(d-b-1)\log\frac1{4\epsilon}-\log2.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
Each right side is at least $c\,d\log(1/\epsilon)$ for an absolute $c>0$
and all sufficiently large $d$.
statements.section_title: Finite states and the information required at the endpoint

statements.title: Finite measure for equal Gaussian labels
statements.label: thm:equal-label-measure
statements.text:
Let $k,m\ge1$, $t=m+1$, and $k+m\le d-2$. Let $P^0$ be either uniform
probability on $S^{d-1}$ or standard Gaussian probability on $\R^d$,
and let $\nu=fP^0$ for a bounded nonnegative Borel function $f$.
With the notation in \eqref{eq:equal-label-geometry} and
\eqref{eq:finite-tilt}, for every nonnegative Borel function
$H(A,y,\mathbf u)$,
\begin{align}
 &\int\gamma_{k,d}(dA)\int_{\R^k}p_A(y)^t
       \int H(A,y,\mathbf u)\,\nu_{A,y}^{\otimes t}(d\mathbf u)\,dy
 \notag\\
 &\quad=(2\pi)^{-km/2}\int J(\mathbf u)^{-k}\,\nu^{\otimes t}(d\mathbf u)
       \int H(A,Au_1,\mathbf u)\,\gamma_{k,d}^{F_{\mathbf u}}(dA).
 
\end{align}
Both sides are finite measures before the test $H$ is inserted. They are
supported on $Au_i=y$ for every $i$, full-column-rank $D_{\mathbf u}$,
and full-row-rank $A$. In the spherical case the common fiber has positive
radius. Thus \eqref{eq:equal-label-measure} is an identity of finite measures
on $(A,y,\mathbf u)$; the right side places $y$ at $Au_1$.

For a full-rank $A$, alternatively define $p_A(y)$ by the lower limit of
its radius-$1/n$ Lebesgue ball averages or by the lower limit of its Gaussian
convolutions with covariance $n^{-2}I_k$. Each choice is jointly measurable
and agrees with \eqref{eq:finite-tilt} for Lebesgue-almost every $y$.
All three versions agree at $y=Au_1$, with a finite positive value, almost
everywhere for the finite reference measure
\begin{equation}
 R(d\mathbf u,dA)=\nu^{\otimes t}(d\mathbf u)
                 \gamma_{k,d}^{F_{\mathbf u}}(dA).
\end{equation}
When $\nu=0$ the last assertion is vacuous. The equality is obtained using
either ball or Gaussian approximate identities in both integration orders
for the base law $P^0$, then multiplying the resulting measure identity by
the bounded density factors.
statements.section_title: Posterior replicas and exact equal-label measures

statements.title: Posterior replica likelihood
statements.label: cor:replica-likelihood
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:equal-label-measure}, suppose
$p=fP^0$ is a probability. Draw $A\sim\gamma_{k,d}$ independently of
$S\sim p$, put $Y=AS$, and conditionally on $(A,Y)$ draw $t$ independent
replicas from $p_{A,Y}$. Let $Q$ be the law of their tuple together with
$A$, and let $R=p^{\otimes t}(d\mathbf u)\gamma_{k,d}^{F_{\mathbf u}}(dA)$.
Then $R$ is a probability and
\begin{equation}
 \frac{dQ}{dR}(\mathbf u,A)
 =(2\pi)^{-km/2}J(\mathbf u)^{-k}p_A(Au_1)^{-m}.
\end{equation}
In particular, the tuple marginal of $Q$ is absolutely continuous relative
to $p^{\otimes t}$.
statements.section_title: Posterior replicas and exact equal-label measures

statements.title: Information from shared exact data
statements.label: thm:distance-block
statements.text:
Let $P=f\sigma_d$ be a probability with a nonnegative Borel density
$f\le e^b$, where $b\ge0$. Let $S\sim P$, let $A$ be an independent
$k\times d$ standard Gaussian matrix, and put $Y=AS$. Let a finite message
$W$ be drawn from a kernel of $(A,Y)$, conditionally independently of $S$.
Let $B$ be a $p\times d$ standard Gaussian matrix independent of the
entire joint experiment producing $(S,A,Y,W)$. Then
\begin{equation}
 I(S;W\mid B,BS)\le\frac{H(W)}q+C\left(d+\frac bd\right)
\end{equation}
for an absolute $C$, uniformly over the prior and message kernel.

statements.title: Current-state iteration of Gaussian replicas
statements.label: prop:gaussian-streaming
statements.text:
Let $M(d)=o(d^2)$ be nonnegative and integer-valued, and let
$0<\epsilon(d)\le1/10$. A learner in
Definition~\ref{def:streaming-model} whose uniform-prior angular success is
at least $3/5$ satisfies
\[
 T(d)\ge c\,d\log(1/\epsilon(d))
\]
for an absolute $c>0$ and all sufficiently large $d$. The threshold may
depend on the memory sequence.
statements.section_title: Current-state recurrences and the streaming bound

statements.title: Current-state iteration of distance bins
statements.label: prop:distance-streaming
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:streaming}, the distance-bin
block estimate \eqref{eq:distance-block} also gives
$T(d)\ge c\,d\log(1/\epsilon(d))$ for an absolute $c>0$ and all
sufficiently large $d$.
statements.section_title: Current-state recurrences and the streaming bound

statements.title: Haar block information bound
statements.label: haar:block
statements.text:
Let $S\sim\sigma$, let $V$ be a finite-valued state, and let a block
consist of $k=\lfloor d/16\rfloor$ fresh independent standard Gaussian
designs, independent of $(S,V)$ and the past, with their exact labels.
Suppose a finite-valued state $W$ is
generated by a measurable randomized kernel from $V$ and the full block,
with no other retained information from the past.  Let $B$ be a Haar
$\ell=\lfloor d/4\rfloor$ frame drawn independently of the entire joint
experiment producing $S,V$, the block, and $W$.  Then
\begin{align}
 I(S;W\mid V,B,BS)\le{}&\frac{H(W\mid V)}{m}+Cd
       +\log(1+Cd+H(V))\notag\\
 &+C\frac{H(V)+\log d}{d^2},
 \qquad m=\lfloor d/16\rfloor+1.
 
\end{align}
The constant $C$ is absolute.  If every state has logarithmic width at
most $H_*=o(d^2)$, the left side is at most $Cd$ for all sufficiently
large $d$.
statements.section_title: Haar projections and posterior replica information

statements.title: Streaming consequence
statements.label: haar:streaming
statements.text:
For each dimension $d$, let $S\sim\sigma$ and consider a learner in
Definition~\ref{def:streaming-model}, with deterministic horizon $T=T(d)$
and nonnegative integer memory $M=M(d)$.  If $M(d)=o(d^2)$,
$0<\epsilon(d)\le1/10$, and its angular success probability averaged over
the signal, samples, and learner randomness is at least $2/3$, then
\[
 T(d)=\Omega\bigl(d\log(1/\epsilon(d))\bigr).
\]
The implicit constant is absolute; the dimension threshold may depend on
the memory sequence.
statements.section_title: Haar projections and posterior replica information

statements.title: Information beyond an independent Gaussian projection
statements.label: syn:block
statements.text:
Let \(P=f\sigma_d\) be a probability, where \(f\) is a nonnegative Borel
function satisfying \(f\le\Lambda<\infty\), with \(\Lambda\ge1\).
Draw \(X\sim P\) and \(A\sim\gamma_{k,d}\) independently.  Let
\(z=z(A,AX)\) be a measurable function taking at most \(K\ge1\) values.
Independently of this entire experiment draw \(B\sim\gamma_{m,d}\), and put
\(Y=BX\).  With the parameters in \eqref{syn:parameters},
\begin{equation}
 I(X;z\mid B,Y)
 \le \frac{\log K}{\ell}
       +C\bigl[d+\log(1+\log\Lambda)\bigr],
\end{equation}
where \(C\) is absolute and independent of \(P,\Lambda,K\), and the message
rule.

statements.title: The synthetic route to the sample bound
statements.label: syn:streaming
statements.text:
For every nonnegative integer-valued \(M(d)=o(d^2)\) and every sequence
\(0<\epsilon(d)\le1/10\), consider learners in
Definition~\ref{def:streaming-model} with deterministic horizon \(T(d)\)
and signal \(X\sim\sigma_d\).  If their angular
success probability, averaged over the uniform signal, rows, and learner
randomness, is at least \(2/3\), then
\[
 T(d)\ge c\,d\log(1/\epsilon(d))
\]
for all sufficiently large \(d\), with an absolute \(c>0\).  The threshold
may depend on the memory sequence.

statements.title: Information in one block
statements.label: inc:block
statements.text:
Let \(\mu=f\sigma\) be a probability measure with a Borel density
\(0\le f\le F<\infty\), where \(F\ge1\).  Draw \(S\sim\mu\) and standard
Gaussian matrices \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}\) and
\(B\in\mathbb R^{p\times d}\), all independently.  For an integer
\(w\ge1\), a message \(J\) takes values in a fixed \(w\)-point alphabet
(unused symbols are allowed) and is drawn by an arbitrary measurable
probability kernel from
\((A,AS)\); conditional on \((A,AS)\), its randomness is independent of
\((S,B)\).  There is an absolute constant \(C\) such that
\begin{equation}
 I_\mu(S;J\mid B,BS)
 \le \frac{\log w}{k}+Cd+C\log(1+\log F).
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Stiefel incidence and conditional block information

statements.title: Average-prior precision bound
statements.label: inc:precision
statements.text:
There is a universal \(c>0\) with the following property.  Let
\(M=M(d)\) be a nonnegative integer with \(M(d)=o(d^2)\).
For all sufficiently large \(d\), with the
threshold allowed to depend on the rate \(M(d)/d^2\to0\), suppose
\(S\sim\sigma\) and a learner in Definition~\ref{def:streaming-model} stops by a
deterministic integer horizon \(T\ge0\).  If
\[
 \Pr\{\angle(\widehat S,S)\le\epsilon\}\ge2/3,
 \qquad 0<\epsilon\le1/10,
\]
then
\begin{equation}
 T\ge c\,d\log(1/\epsilon).
\end{equation}
The bound permits arbitrary computation within a transition.

title: Power-law violations of Yau's nodal upper bound
abstract: We construct a smooth Riemannian metric on \(S^4\times S^1\) and a sequence of real Laplace eigenfunctions whose nodal four-volume grows faster than \(\lambda^{1/2+\epsilon_0}\) for one fixed \(\epsilon_0\gt 0\). This disproves the smooth upper-bound assertion in Yau's nodal-set conjecture and the proposed bound with an arbitrarily small positive power loss.

tex.abstract:
We construct a smooth Riemannian metric on $S^4\times S^1$ and a sequence
of real Laplace eigenfunctions whose nodal four-volume grows faster than
$\lambda^{1/2+\epsilon_0}$ for one fixed $\epsilon_0>0$.
This disproves the smooth upper-bound assertion in Yau's nodal-set
conjecture and the proposed bound with an arbitrarily small positive
power loss.
sections: Envelopes with a fixed power gain
Exact eigenfunctions and a fixed metric

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There exist a smooth Riemannian metric $g$ on $S^4\times S^1$, a number
$\epsilon_0>0$, and nonzero real smooth functions $u_j$ with positive
eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ such that
\[
 -\Delta_g u_j=\lambda_j u_j,\qquad
 \lambda_j\longrightarrow\infty,\qquad
 \frac{\Hh_g^4(\Z(u_j))}
      {\lambda_j^{1/2+\epsilon_0}}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
The metric and $\epsilon_0$ are fixed throughout the sequence.

statements.label: prop:step
statements.text:
There exist a $C^1$ neighborhood $\mathcal U$ of the round pair
$(g_0^{-1},1)$ among smooth positive pairs, a chart $\Omega$ as above,
and a number $\gamma>0$ with the following property.
Fix a smooth pair $(A,\rho)\in\mathcal U$, numbers
\[
 \frac14\le l_-<l_+\le\frac12,
\]
and suppose that $(A,\rho)=(g_0^{-1},1)$ on $\{t<l_+\}$.
For every integer $r\ge0$ and every $\eta>0$, there exist $c>0$ and
$N_0$ such that for every integer $N\ge N_0$, with $k$ as in
\eqref{eq:round-beam}, there are a smooth positive pair
$(\widehat A,\widehat\rho)\in\mathcal U$ and a nonzero real smooth
function $u$ satisfying:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item $\|(\widehat A-A,\widehat\rho-\rho)\|_{C^r}<\eta$, and
 $(\widehat A,\widehat\rho)=(g_0^{-1},1)$ on $\{t<l_-\}$;
 \item for $\widehat L$ defined by \eqref{eq:weighted-operator},
 $-\widehat Lu=k^2u$, and $k^2$ is a simple eigenvalue of
 $-\widehat L$ on the base $B$;
 \item $u$ has a sign certificate in $\Omega$ of size at least
 $c k^{1+\gamma}$.
\end{enumerate}
The neighborhood $\mathcal U$, chart $\Omega$, and exponent $\gamma$
are common to all stages. The constant $c$ and threshold $N_0$ may
depend on the fixed input pair, $l_-,l_+,r,\eta$.

statements.label: prop:envelope
statements.text:
After fixing the data of Lemma~\ref{lem:seed} and possibly shrinking
$\mathcal G$, there are common constants $\gamma>0$ and $c>0$
with the following property.  For every smooth $G\in\mathcal G$
and all sufficiently large $k$, there is a smooth real envelope
$h=h_k$ on $B$ such that $h=-a_*t+c_k$ on $\{t\le1/2\}$ and
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
  \|h\|_{C^j}\le C_j k^{\delta(j+1)}
  \quad\text{for every fixed integer }j\ge0,\\
  \max_{\substack{|e|_G=1\\\dd h(e)=0}}J_h(e)
       \ge c k^{-\delta}\quad\text{on }\{t\ge1/4\},
  \qquad
  \int_V\sqrt{1+|\nabla_Gh|_G^2}\,\dd x\ge c k^\gamma.
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
Here $\delta=10^{-6}$, and the chart $\Omega$ and region
$V\Subset\Omega$ are fixed.  All corrugations are supported in
one fixed initial cube compactly contained in $V$.
The constants $c_k$ may be any bounded prescribed real numbers.
The exponent $\gamma$ and all construction parameters are
independent of derivative orders, subsequent accuracy requirements,
and round gluing collars.  Constants $C_j$ may depend on the order,
the fixed smooth metric and coordinate systems, and the bound for
$|c_k|$; no uniform bound as $j\to\infty$ is asserted.
statements.section_title: Envelopes with a fixed power gain

statements.title: Packets with arbitrary finite accuracy
statements.label: prop:packets
statements.text:
Fix a nonnegative integer \(J\) and a real number \(M>0\). Finite
construction orders can be chosen, before taking \(k\) large, so that
every center \(z\) with \(t(z)\ge1/4\) has a family \(\mathcal W_z\) of
four smooth complex packets with the following properties.

Each packet is supported in an ordinary coordinate ball about \(z\)
of radius at most \(Ck^{-1/3-100\delta}\). For every fixed
nonnegative integer \(j\),
\begin{equation}
 |D_x^j w(x)|\le C_j k^{2j}e^{kh(x)}.
\end{equation}
For the prescribed orders,
\begin{equation}
 |D_x^j(L+k^2)w(x)|\le C e^{kh(x)}k^{-M},
 \qquad 0\le j\le J.
\end{equation}
The center jets and the nearby jets satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \sigma_{\min}(\mathcal J_z(z))\ge c k^{-3/4},\qquad
 \sigma_{\min}(\mathcal J_z(x))\ge k^{-1}
 \quad\text{if }\operatorname{dist}(x,z)\le k^{-10},
\end{equation}
for sufficiently large \(k\). Any fixed smooth reference distance
may be used here. The same conclusion holds if the latter radius
is multiplied by a fixed constant.

The exponents in the support, derivative, and jet bounds are
independent of \(J,M\). Constants and lower frequency thresholds may
depend on the chosen finite orders.

For every integer $n>5$ there is a smooth closed connected
$n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold and a fixed $\epsilon_0>0$
with the same divergence of nodal measure divided by
$\lambda^{1/2+\epsilon_0}$.

title: Prefix Instructions and Incompressible Flows
abstract: Finite prefix instructions may change area and erase information. We give explicit history processors and smooth incompressible motions that retain that information and realize every instruction on its full domain. A first application assigns each machine and finite input a smooth mean-zero force on the flat unit three-torus, at any fixed positive computable viscosity. The solution starts from rest; a fixed particle enters a fixed open strip exactly when the machine halts. The force repeats with period one after an initial loading interval. We then prove alternative realizations using full boxes, normal compensation, invariant planes, and a spatial clock. The constructions specify their initialization, comparison class, derivative bounds, and continuous-time observation. Exact formulas and effective cutoffs provide finite descriptions of the fields and all their derivatives.

tex.abstract:
Finite prefix instructions may change area and erase information. We give
explicit history processors and smooth incompressible motions that retain
that information and realize every instruction on its full domain. A first
application assigns each machine and finite input a smooth mean-zero force
on the flat unit three-torus, at any fixed positive computable viscosity.
The solution starts from rest; a fixed particle enters a fixed open strip
exactly when the machine halts. The force repeats with period one after an
initial loading interval. We then prove alternative realizations using
full boxes, normal compensation, invariant planes, and a spatial clock.
The constructions specify their initialization, comparison class, derivative
bounds, and continuous-time observation. Exact formulas and effective
cutoffs provide finite descriptions of the fields and all their derivatives.

statements.title: Interspersed history on moving sheets
statements.label: thm:sa-interleaved
statements.text:
At fixed positive computable viscosity, every machine and finite input
effectively determine a smooth mean-zero general force on the unit
$\mathbb T^3$, with all mixed derivatives bounded and period one for
$t\ge1$.  Its zero-data solution is globally smooth and unique in the
classical periodic comparison class, with uniformly bounded kinetic
energy.  Its material trajectory from $(1/8,1/4,1/4)$ enters
$\{x:1/2<x_1<1\}$ at some finite time exactly when the machine halts.
The repeated template depends only on the table, and the input enters
only the loading pulse.

statements.title: Projection on a flat torus
statements.label: prop:projection-l2
statements.text:
An effective smooth mean-zero force $g$ on $\T_L^3$ has an effective
mean-zero potential $\phi$ satisfying $\Delta\phi=\operatorname{div}g$.
Replacing $(g,p)$ by $(g-\nabla\phi,p-\phi)$ preserves velocity and makes
the force solenoidal. Uniform mixed-derivative bounds, temporal $L^2$
bounds of their spatial suprema, and separately imposed time periodicity,
eventual stationarity, or orderwise decay bounds are preserved.
statements.section_title: Analytic classes and changes of physical coordinates

statements.title: Input shifts and periodic full-box motion
statements.label: thm:sa-cell-records
statements.text:
This recorder gives an effective smooth general force on $\mathbb R^3$
with fixed compact spatial support, period one from $t=0$, and all mixed
derivatives bounded.  Its zero-data solution is globally smooth with
uniformly bounded energy.  The particle starting at the origin has first
coordinate greater than $2$ at some time exactly when the machine halts.
Uniqueness holds for smooth velocities in $C_tH^2\cap C_t^1L^2$ with
velocity and gradient bounded on finite intervals, and pressure in $H^1$
modulo constants at each time.  Pressure is determined modulo a function
of time.

statements.title: Delimiter processors on invariant planes
statements.label: thm:sa-delimiter
statements.text:
For every machine and finite input, each row below gives an effective
smooth mean-zero general force on the unit torus, periodic of period one
for $t\ge1$, with all mixed derivatives bounded.  Its zero-data solution
is unique in the classical periodic class and has uniformly bounded
energy.  The stated fixed particle enters the stated fixed open set
exactly when the machine halts.
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{lll}
Processor & Initial label & Open set\\\hline
Delimiter & $(1/2,1/2,0)$ & $(2/3,5/6)^2\times\mathbb T$\\
Delimiter, origin coordinates & $(0,0,0)$ & $\{x:2/3<x_1<11/12\}$\\
Separate marker push & $(1/4,1/4,0)$ & $\{x:3/4<x_1<1\}$
\end{tabular}\end{center}
The repeated pulse uses only the machine; a separate loader uses the
input.  All formulas allow arbitrary fixed positive real viscosity as
a parameter; absolute computability uses computable viscosity.

statements.title: Input insertion in a periodic compact force
statements.label: thm:sa-prefix-insertion
statements.text:
This processor gives an effective smooth general force on $\mathbb R^3$
with period one from zero, a fixed compact spatial support, and all mixed
derivatives bounded.  Its zero-data solution is globally smooth, has
uniformly bounded energy, and is unique among smooth classical solutions
with $u\in C_tH^2\cap C_t^1L^2$, $p\in C_tH^1$, and bounded velocity
and gradient on each finite time interval.  The particle from the origin has
first coordinate greater than $2$ at some time exactly when the machine
halts.  The formula is effective relative to any fixed real $\nu>0$.

statements.title: Finite windows and a fixed slab
statements.label: thm:sa-delimiter-history
statements.text:
This processor gives an effective smooth mean-zero force on the unit
torus, periodic of period one for $t\ge1$, with every mixed derivative
bounded.  Its zero-data solution is globally smooth, unique in the
classical periodic class, and has uniformly bounded energy.  The particle
from $(1/4,1/4,1/4)$ enters $\{x:1/2<x_1<3/4\}$ exactly when the
machine halts.  A general residual force with pressure zero or a
solenoidal projected force with its accompanying pressure may be chosen;
both give the same velocity.  The repeated pulse depends only on the
table and the loader on the input.

statements.title: A periodic processor with quadratic sample times
statements.label: thm:sa-repeated-loader
statements.text:
Every machine and finite input give an effective smooth mean-zero general
force on the unit torus, periodic of period one from time zero.  Force
and velocity have all mixed derivatives bounded and vanish near integer
times.  Their spatial supports lie in one compact subset of the cube
chart.  The unique classical periodic zero-data solution is globally
smooth with uniformly bounded energy.  From the fixed label
$(1/2,1/2,1/4)$, the event $3/4<X_1(t)<7/8$ occurs exactly when the
machine halts.  Whenever reached, the configuration after $k$ ordinary
steps is encoded at time $(k+1)^2$.

statements.title: A delayed head move on an invariant plane
statements.label: thm:sa-marked-head-plane
statements.text:
The marked-head compiler gives an effective smooth mean-zero general
force on the unit torus, with all mixed derivatives bounded and period
one for $t\ge1$.  Its unique classical periodic zero-data solution is
globally smooth with bounded energy.  The particle from
$(1/4,1/4,1/2)$ enters $(5/8,7/8)^2\times\mathbb T$ exactly when the
original machine halts.  Only its loader depends on the input.

statements.title: Two invariant-plane realizations
statements.label: thm:sa-neighbor-realizations
statements.text:
The neighboring-cell recorder has the following effective zero-data
forced Navier--Stokes realizations at fixed positive computable viscosity.
Both have all mixed derivatives bounded, period one for $t\ge1$, and
uniformly bounded kinetic energy.
\begin{enumerate}
\item On the unit torus, any tape differing from blank on a specified
finite set of cells is allowed.  The force is mean zero and general,
and the solution is unique in the classical periodic class.  The particle
from $(1/16,1/16,0)$ enters $\{x:1/2<x_1<7/8\}$ exactly when the
machine halts.
\item On $\mathbb R^3$, for a finite word starting at cell zero, the
force is general with one compact spatial support uniform in time.
The particle from the origin has negative first coordinate at some time
exactly when the machine halts.  Uniqueness holds for smooth solutions
with bounded velocity on finite intervals and
$u\in C_tH^2\cap C_t^1L^2$, $p\in C_tH^1$; no bound on the competing
velocity gradient is required.
\end{enumerate}
The repeated field depends only on the table; only the loader uses the
input.  Neither force is required to decay or be solenoidal.  The same
formulas are effective relative to arbitrary fixed real positive viscosity.

statements.title: Marked words and a fixed middle arc
statements.label: thm:sa-marked-five-stage
statements.text:
This recorder gives an effective smooth mean-zero general force on the
unit torus, with all mixed derivatives bounded and period one for $t\ge1$.
Its unique classical periodic zero-data solution is global with bounded
energy.  The particle from $(1/4,1/4,0)$ enters
$(1/2,3/4)\times\mathbb T^2$ exactly when the machine halts.
The repeated protocol uses only the table and initialization uses the
input.  Separately, one may choose either a solenoidal force with the
same eventual periodicity, or a mean-zero force satisfying
$\|f(t)\|_{C^m}=O((1+t)^{-1})$ for every spatial order $m$, with all
mixed derivatives bounded and hence temporal $L^2$ in every $C^m$ norm.
These two alternatives are separate prescriptions.
statements.section_title: Marked tape words and a separate history stack

statements.title: Box, sheet, and invariant-plane realizations
statements.label: thm:sb-realizations
statements.text:
For every deterministic machine and finite input, and every fixed positive computable viscosity $\nu$, each row of the following table has a finite effective prescribed force $f=\mathcal F_\nu[U]$.  The initial velocity is zero.  The force and velocity are smooth with all mixed derivatives bounded; the velocity has bounded kinetic energy.  On $\mathbb R^3$ their spatial supports lie in one compact set independent of time, allowed to depend on the finite instance.  On the unit torus both fields have spatial mean zero.  Their global solution is $(u,p)=(U,0)$. On the torus it is unique in the classical periodic class. For the Euclidean rows it is unique among smooth classical solutions with $u\in C_tH^2\cap C_t^1L^2$, $p\in C_tH^1$, and bounded $u,\nabla u$ on every finite time interval; pressure representatives differing by spatial constants have the same velocity conclusion. These are the specified cases of Lemma~\ref{lem:b-comparison}.

The material trajectory from the listed fixed label $a$ enters the listed fixed open set $O$ if and only if the machine halts.  In a torus row, the displayed interval is an arc of $\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ and $O$ is that interval times $\mathbb T^2$.
\begin{center}\footnotesize
\begin{tabular}{llll}
Construction&Domain and fixed label $a$&Observation $O$&Period one from\\\hline
\multicolumn{4}{l}{\emph{Euclidean full boxes}}\\
Left-word boxes&$\mathbb R^3$, $(0,0,0)$&$x_1<-1$&$t=1$\\
Right-word boxes&$\mathbb R^3$, $(0,0,0)$&$x_1<-1/2$&$t=1$\\
Tagged storage&$\mathbb R^3$, $(-4,0,0)$&$(-1,2)^2\times(-1,1)$&$t=1$\\
Boot-window prisms&$\mathbb R^3$, $(-3,0,0)$&$x_1>0$&$t=0$\\
\multicolumn{4}{l}{\emph{Reserved-loader sheets}}\\
Left reserved sheets&$\mathbb T^3$, $(1/2,1/2,1/4)$&$(1/8,1/4)$&$t=0$\\
Right reserved sheets&$\mathbb T^3$, $(1/2,1/8,1/4)$&$(3/4,15/16)$&$t=0$\\
\multicolumn{4}{l}{\emph{Invariant planes}}\\
Frontier sine plane&$\mathbb T^3$, $(1/2,1/4,0)$&$(5/8,15/16)$&$t=1$\\
Previous-tag plane&$\mathbb T^3$, $(1/8,1/4,0)$&$(2/3,5/6)$&$t=0$\\
Shifted-start plane&$\mathbb T^3$, $(3/4,3/4,1/2)$&$(0,1/3)$&$t=0$\\
Separator sine plane&$\mathbb T^3$, $(1/4,1/2,0)$&$(1/2,1)$&$t=1$\\
Two-cell-frontier plane&$\mathbb T^3$, $(1/8,1/8,0)$&$(2/3,7/8)$&$t=1$\\
Zero-blank plane&$\mathbb T^3$, $(1/4,1/2,1/2)$&$(3/4,7/8)$&$t=1$
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
For the rows beginning at $t=1$, the repeated program depends only on the machine table, while the input appears in the loading pulse.  The rows beginning at zero incorporate loading into the repeated prefix table, reserve a disjoint loader image, or place the initial code at the fixed label as specified in the proof.  No force in this theorem is required to be solenoidal.  The separator sine-plane row additionally permits an effective mean-zero solenoidal force with the same velocity and event. For arbitrary fixed real $\nu>0$, the same algebraic formulas and conclusions hold, with numerical evaluation relative to that parameter.

statements.title: Logarithmic alternatives
statements.label: prop:sb-log
statements.text:
For each of the left-word-box, right-word-box, and tagged-storage constructions, retain its fixed initial label and observation set.  There is also an effective smooth force of fixed compact spatial support in
$L^2([0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^3)$ with exactly the same halting event and zero initial velocity.  It and all its derivatives are bounded.  The velocity's spatial derivatives are $O((1+t)^{-1})$, and their first time derivatives are $O((1+t)^{-2})$, uniformly in space.  The force itself is $O((1+t)^{-1})$ uniformly in space. The viscosity
in this statement is the same fixed physical $\nu$ as before the time
change.

statements.title: Two compact periodic processors
statements.label: prop:p2:rapid-periodic
statements.text:
For every deterministic machine and finite input, and every fixed
computable viscosity $\nu>0$, there are effective smooth velocities
$U$ and forces $f$ on $\mathbb R^3$ with the following properties.
Both have all mixed derivatives bounded, support in a compact spatial
set independent of time, and period one for $t\ge1$; $U(0)=0$.
The solution with pressure zero is unique in the class
\[
 u\in C([0,T];H^2)\cap C^1([0,T];L^2),\qquad
 p\in C([0,T];H^1),\qquad
 \sup_{[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3}(|u|+|\nabla u|)<\infty
\]
for every finite $T$, and its kinetic energy is uniformly bounded.
The following are two separate constructions with their stated fixed
particle events:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Four successive stationary localized fields, with initial label
$(-1,0,0)$ and detector $\{x_1>0\}$.
\item Three successive phases of moving full-box fields, with initial
label $(0,0,0)$ and detector \mbox{$\{x_1<-1\}$}.
\end{enumerate}
In each case the particle enters the detector at some real time if and
only if the machine halts. The repeated part of the prescription depends
only on the machine; the input appears only in a one-time loading pulse.
statements.section_title: Two compact realizations of the reciprocal recorder

statements.label: thm:sa-autonomous
statements.text:
At fixed positive computable viscosity, a deterministic one-tape machine
and finite input effectively determine a smooth mean-zero general force
on the unit torus such that, for every $k\ge0$ and spatial multi-index
$\beta$,
\begin{equation}
 \|\partial_t^k\partial_x^\beta f(t)\|_\infty
       \le C_{k,\beta}(1+t)^{-1}.
\end{equation}
Its zero-data Navier--Stokes solution is globally smooth and unique in
the classical periodic comparison class, with uniformly bounded kinetic
energy and mean-zero pressure.  For the fixed label and open set
\begin{equation}
 y_*=(1/2,1/2,1/4),\qquad
 \mathcal O=\{(x_1,x_2,z):1/2<x_1<1,\ 0<z<1/8\},
\end{equation}
its material trajectory enters $\mathcal O$ exactly when the machine
halts.  Samples encode the full machine computation through the first
halt, or indefinitely if there is none.  The prescription uses only the
finite table and input; arbitrary fixed real positive viscosity is allowed
as a relative coefficient.
