statements.title: Degree and coset inputs
statements.label: shear:prop:fourier-inputs
statements.text:
For every fixed \(u>0\), \(C_u<\infty\) and \(Z_u(s)\to0\) as \(s\to\infty\).

Let \(H_1,\ldots,H_r\) be subgroups of a finite group \(G\), and let
\(\mu\) be a probability measure. Write \(\mu_H\) for its image on
\(G/H\). If
\[
 \delta=\sum_{i=1}^r
 \|\mu_{H_i}-U_{G/H_i}\|_{\TV},
\]
there is a measure \(0\le f\le\mu\), of mass \(z\ge1-\delta\), with
\[
 f(gH_i)\le [G:H_i]^{-1}\qquad(g\in G,\ 1\le i\le r).
\]
It can be obtained by successive trimming of excess coset mass or by
taking the pointwise minimum of the separately trimmed measures.
When \(z>0\), its normalization is within \(1-z\) of \(\mu\) in TV and
has coset cap \(z^{-1}\) times uniform.

Alternatively, delete the union of all cosets whose original \(\mu\)-mass
exceeds twice uniform. The deleted mass is \(\eta\le2\delta\).
If \(\delta<1/2\), the normalized retained law is exactly \(\eta\) away
from \(\mu\) in TV and has coset cap \(2/(1-\eta)\) times uniform.
statements.section_title: Fourier amplification of partial permutation laws

statements.title: Fourier bounds from disjoint coset systems
statements.label: shear:prop:disjoint-transfer
statements.text:
Let \(X\) have \(N\) elements and \(G=\Sym(X)\). Let
\(M_1,\ldots,M_r\) be disjoint nonempty subsets of \(X\), where \(r\ge1\),
and put \(H_i=\Sym(M_i)\), fixing the complement pointwise.
Their union need not be \(X\). Suppose \(f\ge0\) has mass \(z\le1\) and
\[
 f(gH_i)\le K[G:H_i]^{-1}\qquad(g\in G,\ 1\le i\le r)
\]
for some \(K\ge0\). For an irreducible unitary representation \(\rho\)
of degree \(D\), set
\[
 S_i(D)=
 \sum_{\substack{\tau\in\widehat H_i\\ \dim\tau\le D^{1/r}}}
       (\dim\tau)^2.
\]
For every \(u>0\), the separate orbit and isotypic estimates are
\begin{align}
 \|\widehat f(\rho)\|_{\op}
 &\le \left(\frac{zK}{D}\sum_iS_i(D)\right)^{1/2}
 \le \sqrt{zKrC_u}\,D^{-1/2+(u+2)/(2r)},
 \\
 \|\widehat f(\rho)\|_{\HS}^2
 &\le \frac{zK}{D}\sum_iS_i(D)
 \le zKrC_uD^{-1+(u+2)/r}.
 
\end{align}
In particular, when \(r>4\), the inverse-square orbit estimate gives
\begin{equation}
 \|\widehat f(\rho)\|_{\op}
 \le\sqrt{rKC_2}\,D^{-(1-4/r)/2}.
 
\end{equation}
A separate coefficient-projection argument gives
\begin{equation}
 \|\widehat f(\rho)\|_{\HS}^2
 \le\frac{K^2}{D}\sum_{i=1}^r
       \sum_{\substack{\tau\in\widehat H_i\\
                            \dim\tau\le D^{1/r}}}(\dim\tau)^2
 \le K^2rC_{10}D^{-1+12/r}.
 
\end{equation}
Finally, for \(\rho=\rho_\lambda\) with \(\lambda\vdash N\), put
\[
 k_\lambda=N-\max(\lambda_1,\lambda'_1),
 \qquad M(k)=\sum_{j=0}^k p(j),
\]
where \(p(j)\) is the partition number and \(p(0)=1\). The branching
refinement is
\begin{equation}
 \|\widehat f(\rho_\lambda)\|_{\HS}^2
 \le zKrM(k_\lambda)D^{-1+2/r}.
 
\end{equation}
All these statements allow unequal support sizes and unrestricted
restriction multiplicities. In particular they include the
probability-law cases \(z=1\).

statements.title: Two time blocks from the isotypic transfer
statements.label: shear:cor:512
statements.text:

 \qquad(d\longrightarrow\infty).
\]

statements.title: Eight time blocks from the orbit estimate
statements.label: shear:thm:2048
statements.text:
For the physical shuffle on \(N=2^d\) labeled cards,
\begin{equation}
 \|q_d^{*(2048d)}-U_G\|_{\TV}=o(1).
 
\end{equation}
The fixed-list estimate at \(257d\) also gives a proof using eight time blocks
at \(2056d\) with a retained subprobability. The random omitted set
estimate gives another proof at \(2056d\) using normalized deletion.
All three conclusions hold for every deterministic starting deck.

statements.title: Sixteen time blocks from averaged input lists
statements.label: frames:average-marginals
statements.text:
Let \(d\ge6\), \(b=64\), \(q=N(1-1/b)\), \(T=2048d\), and
\(\mu_T=q_d^{*T}\). The average over uniform ordered lists of \(q\)
distinct input labels of the total-variation distance of their outputs
from a uniform injection is \(o(1)\). There is a subprobability
\(f\le\mu_T\) of mass \(1-o(1)\) and a partition into 64 equal parts
for which every complementary marginal of \(f\) is bounded above by
the corresponding uniform marginal. Consequently,
\[

statements.label: frames:char:main
statements.text:
Let $n=2^d$, and count one physical Thorp shuffle as one time step, using
$n/2$ independent fair switches. For all sufficiently large integers $d$,
the worst-initial-deck total-variation mixing time at threshold $1/4$
satisfies
\[
 d\le t_{\mathrm{mix}}(d)\le 6060000d.
\]
In fact, the worst-initial-deck distance at time
$60000(101d-1)$ tends to zero as $d\to\infty$.

statements.label: frames:char:block-norm
statements.text:
There is an absolute $C_0$ such that, for every sufficiently large
$n=2^d$, every modified block above, and every irreducible $\rho$ of
$S_n$ of degree $D$ other than trivial or sign,
\[
 \|\mathbb E\rho(\sigma\pi)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le C_0D^{-1/20000}.
\]

uniform in its starting phase.

statements.label: char:main
statements.text:
There are absolute positive integers $C,K$ such that the Thorp shuffle
on $n=2^d$ cards has worst-start total-variation distance tending to zero
from uniform after
\[
 K\bigl((d-1)+Cd\bigr)
\]
physical shuffles. For every fixed ordered list of $n/2$ distinct input
positions, its image after $Cd$ consecutive coordinate layers is within
$o(1)$ of the uniform injection, uniformly in the input list and the
starting phase of the coordinate cycle.

title: Randomized quasipolynomial-time mean-payoff games
abstract: We give a randomized algorithm that computes the complete zero-threshold winning set of a finite mean-payoff game with arbitrary signed integer edge weights encoded in binary. For total explicit input length L, it uses \(2^{O((\log(L+2))^2)}\) bit operations on every random tape and is correct with probability at least 7/8. A polynomial-time check certifies the winning regions and positional strategies for both players or reports failure. Independent repetition therefore gives an always-correct algorithm with the same expected quasipolynomial bit bound.

tex.abstract:
We give a randomized algorithm that computes the complete zero-threshold
winning set of a finite mean-payoff game with arbitrary signed integer edge
weights encoded in binary. For total explicit input length $L$, it uses
$2^{O((\log(L+2))^2)}$ bit operations on every random tape and is correct
with probability at least $7/8$. A polynomial-time check certifies the winning
regions and positional strategies for both players or reports failure.
Independent repetition therefore gives an always-correct algorithm with the
same expected quasipolynomial bit bound.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is a uniform randomized algorithm that, for every such game,
returns the entire set
\[
 U=\{v\in V:\text{there is a Max strategy }\sigma
       \text{ such that for every Min strategy }\tau,\ 
       \operatorname{MP}_w(\pi_{v,\sigma,\tau})\ge0\}
\]
correctly with probability at least $7/8$.
For an absolute constant $C>0$, on every random tape its total cost is at
most
\[
 2^{C(\log_2(L+2))^2}
\]
bit operations in a standard model polynomially equivalent to a uniform
probabilistic Turing machine. The bound includes preprocessing, recursive
calls, intermediate arithmetic, and random-bit generation.

statements.title: Reduction to a box solution
statements.label: prop:game-reduction
statements.text:
Let $x$ solve the constant box $[0,B_*]$, with $B_*=8nW$ as in
Equation~\eqref{eq:transformed}. Then the original game's exact
zero-threshold winning set is
\[
 U=\{i\in V:x_i>B_*/2\}.
\]
A positional Max strategy guarantees original mean payoff at least zero
from every vertex of $U$. Outside $U$, a positional Min strategy ensures
that every consistent play has original upper limiting average at most
$-1/n$, including against arbitrary history-dependent Max strategies.
statements.section_title: Integer boxes and the winning-set reduction

statements.title: Orientation
statements.label: prop:orientation
statements.text:
Assume the lower-rank comparison guarantees stated at the beginning of
this section. On a fixed permitted input
\((a,b;B,\alpha,\beta,k,m)\) of rank \(r\), let
\((\chi,\mathcal H)\) be the output of \(\Orient\).
For every fixed admissible subsolution \(y\) of \([a,b]\) whose core
in Equation~\eqref{eq:orientation-cores} satisfies
\(\alpha(I_y)>\eta k\),
\begin{equation}

  \Pr\left(
     \chi=Y
     \ \text{or}\
     \exists H\in\mathcal H:
          \alpha(S_y\cap H)>\eta k
  \right)\geq 1-\frac1{16}.
\end{equation}
Separately, for every fixed admissible supersolution \(z\) of
\([a,b]\) with \(\beta(I_z)>\eta m\),
\begin{equation}

  \Pr\left(
     \chi=Z
     \ \text{or}\
     \exists H\in\mathcal H:
          \beta(S_z\cap H)>\eta m
  \right)\geq 1-\frac1{16}.
\end{equation}
On every tape, every set in \(\mathcal H\) has \(\mu\)-measure at
most \(1/2\). Each probability statement remains valid conditional
on a pre-call history that fixes its input and qualifying comparison,
when the call uses fresh random bits.

statements.title: Pointwise comparisons for the solver
statements.label: thm:solve-comparisons
statements.text:
Let \([a,b]\) be an allowed integer box with positive integer
reference width \(B\le B_*\), and let the support weights and
budgets be positive rationals. For the output \(p\) of \(\Solve\),
each fixed admissible subsolution \(y\) and, separately, each fixed
admissible supersolution \(z\) satisfy
\[
 \Pr(p\ge y)\ge 1-\frac1{16},
 \qquad
 \Pr(p\le z)\ge 1-\frac1{16}.
\]
These are whole-vector inequalities, as in
Equation~\eqref{eq:comparison-guarantees}: a fixed comparison is
chosen before the invocation, and its inequality holds at every
coordinate on its success event.

statements.title: Exact recovery of the top box solution
statements.label: cor:top-success
statements.text:
Let \(x\) be the box solution for \([0,B_*]\). Let \(p\) be the
output of \(\Solve\) on that box with unit support weights,
budgets \(k=m=n\), and reference width \(B_*\). Then
\[
 \Pr(p=x)\ge\frac78.
\]
Hence \(\{i:p_i>B_*/2\}\) is the complete winning set with
probability at least \(7/8\).

statements.label: thm:bit-complexity
statements.text:
The algorithm has a uniform implementation in a standard bit-operation
model such that, for every input of bit length \(L\) and every random
tape, the running time is at most
\[
              2^{C(\log_2(L+2))^2}
\]
for an absolute constant \(C>0\). The bound includes preprocessing,
every recursive execution, intermediate arithmetic, and random-bit
generation.

statements.title: Certified winning regions and strategies
statements.label: cor:certified-output
statements.text:
There is a randomized algorithm which, on every tape, uses
$2^{O((\log_2(L+2))^2)}$ bit operations and returns either a failure
symbol or the exact winning set together with an integer potential and
positional strategies for both players. Whenever it returns these
objects, the Max strategy wins from every vertex of the winning set and
the Min strategy ensures upper limiting average at most $-1/n$ from
every other vertex, against arbitrary opposing strategies. It returns
these objects with probability at least $7/8$.

Repeating independent trials until a certificate is accepted terminates
almost surely, never returns an incorrect answer, and has expected bit
cost $2^{O((\log_2(L+2))^2)}$.

title: Rational homology and Quillen's conjecture
abstract: We prove Quillen's conjecture for all finite groups and all primes. More precisely, if a finite group G has trivial largest normal p-subgroup \(O_p(G)\), then the poset of nontrivial elementary abelian p-subgroups of G has nonzero augmented reduced rational homology. This establishes the stronger rational-homology form of the conjecture.

More precisely, if a finite group $G$ has trivial largest normal
$p$-subgroup $O_p(G)$, then the poset of nontrivial elementary abelian
$p$-subgroups of $G$ has nonzero augmented reduced rational homology.
This establishes the stronger rational-homology form of the conjecture.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every finite group $G$ and every prime $p$, if $\Op(G)=1$, then
\[
\widetilde H_*(\Ap(G);\Q)\ne0.
\]
Here reduced homology is augmented, so that the empty poset has
$\widetilde H_{-1}(\varnothing;\Q)=\Q$.

statements.title: Reduction at two
statements.label: thm:reduction-two
statements.text:
Let $G$ be a minimal-order counterexample to \eqref{eq:HQC} for $p=2$.
Then $G$ has a simple component $L$ in the following list, where the
field parameter $q$ has characteristic at least five:
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\PSL_n(q),\ \PSU_n(q)& n\geq4,\\
\PSp_{2n}(q)& n\geq3,\\
\Omega_{2n+1}(q)& n\geq2,\\
\mathrm P\Omega_{2n}^{\pm}(q)& n\geq4.
\end{array}
\]

statements.title: Odd-prime reduction
statements.label: thm:reduction-odd
statements.text:
Suppose that, for every odd prime $p$, every odd prime power $q$ with
$p\mid q+1$, and every simple $L=\PSU_n(q)$ with $n\geq5$, each
elementary $p$-extension of $L$ inside $\Aut(L)$ has the Quillen
dimension property. Then \eqref{eq:HQC} holds for every finite group
and every odd prime.

statements.label: cor:maximal-family
statements.text:
Assume the inductive hypothesis on proper subgroups of $G$ in
Lemma~\ref{lem:propagation}, and let $L$ be a nonabelian simple
component with $p\mid|L|$.  Let $\mathcal F$ be a nonempty family
of faithful configurations for $L$ in $G$ such that
\[
 A\in\mathcal F,\quad D\in\Ap(G),\quad D>A,
 \quad D\text{ a faithful configuration}
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad D\in\mathcal F.
\]
Let $r$ be the largest rank of a member of $\mathcal F$.
If some $A\in\mathcal F$ of rank $r$ is the final subgroup of a
saturated flag having nonzero coefficient in a cycle of degree $r-1$
in $\Delta\Ap(LA)$, then
$\widetilde H_*(\Delta\Ap(G);\Q)\ne0$.
statements.section_title: Propagation from a faithful component extension

statements.title: Frame coefficient bound
statements.label: thm:frame-bound
statements.text:
Let $W$ have dimension $h\geq2$ and one of the four structures above,
and suppose that $W$ admits an allowed frame.  The space
$\mathcal Z(W)\subseteq\bigoplus_{\mathcal D\in\mathfrak F(W)}V_{\mathcal D}$
consists of cycles of degree $h-2$, each supported on full flags ending
at sign groups of rank $h-1$.  Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 \dim\mathcal Z(W)\ \geq\
 F_h\,|\mathfrak F(W)|(h-1)!.
\end{equation}
The following choices of $F_h$ are valid for each individual isometry
type of $W$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item In the no-form case over $\F_u$, and in the hermitian case over
$\F_{u^2}$, set
\[
 \rho=\frac1{u(u+1)}\quad\hbox{and}\quad
 \rho=\frac1{u(u-1)},
 \quad\hbox{respectively},\qquad
 y=\frac{1+\sqrt{1-4\rho}}2.
\]
For $u\geq5$ one may take $F_h=y^h+(1-y)^h\geq(17/25)^h$.
\item For a symmetric space over $\F_u$, with both line types allowed
and $u\geq5$ odd, put
\[
 x=\frac{1+\sqrt{1-4u/(u^2-1)}}2.
\]
One may take
\begin{equation}
 F_h=x^h+(1-x)^h-\mathbf1_{2\mid h}\,2(u^2-1)^{-h/2}
 \ \geq\ (17/25)^h.
\end{equation}
In particular $F_3\geq3/8$.
\item For a symmetric space over $\F_u$ with one fixed line type,
where $u\geq7$ is odd, write $\chi$ for the quadratic character of
$\F_u^\times$ and set
\[
 \rho=\frac2{u-\chi(-1)},\qquad
 y=\frac{1+\sqrt{1-4\rho}}2.
\]
One may take $F_h=y^h+(1-y)^h>0$.
\end{enumerate}
The same statements hold for any realization by projective sign
subgroups in which coarsened decompositions give the indicated subgroup
flags and the complete flags ending at the full frames remain distinct.
statements.section_title: Cycles from frames and a dimension estimate

statements.label: prop:linear-two
statements.text:
Let $G$ have least order among finite groups with $O_2(G)=1$ and
$\widetilde H_*(\mathcal A_2(G);\Q)=0$.
Then $G$ has no simple component isomorphic to $\PSL_n(q)$ or
$\PSU_n(q)$ with $n\ge5$ and $q$ of characteristic at least five.

statements.label: prop:unitary-odd
statements.text:
Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $q$ be odd with $p\mid q+1$, and let
$L=\PSU_n(q)$ with $n\ge5$.  If $L\le H\le\Aut(L)$ and $H/L$ is
elementary abelian of $p$-power order, then
\[
 \widetilde H_{m_p(H)-1}(\Ap(H);\Q)\ne0.
\]
Here $m_p(H)$ denotes the maximum rank of an elementary abelian
$p$-subgroup of $H$.

statements.label: prop:symplectic
statements.text:
A minimal-order counterexample to \eqref{eq:HQC} at $p=2$ cannot have a
simple component isomorphic to $\PSp_{2n}(q)$, where $n\geq3$ and $q$
has characteristic at least five.

statements.label: prop:orthogonal
statements.text:
Let $G$ be a minimal-order counterexample to rational augmented reduced
homology nonvanishing at the prime two.  Thus $O_2(G)=1$ and
$\widetilde H_*(\mathcal A_2(G);\Q)=0$, whereas the asserted nonvanishing
holds for smaller groups with trivial $2$-core.  Then $G$ has no simple
component $L=\mathrm P\Omega(V)$, where $V$ is a nondegenerate symmetric
space over $\F_q$, the characteristic of $\F_q$ is at least five, and
its dimension $N$ is odd with $N\ge5$, even with $N\ge8$, or equal to six,
except possibly when $N=6$, $q=5$, and the determinant of the form is a
square.  In odd dimension $\mathrm P\Omega(V)=\Omega(V)$.

statements.title: Equivalent poset for a centerless component
statements.label: thm:psl45-equivalent-poset
statements.text:
Let $G$ be a finite group, let $p$ be a prime, and let $L$ be a
centerless component of $G$ with $p\mid |L|$. Put $K=C_G(L)$ and
\[
 \mathcal Q=
 \bigl((\mathcal A_p(L)\cup\{1\})\times
             (\mathcal A_p(K)\cup\{1\})\bigr)\setminus\{(1,1)\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal F=\{F\in\mathcal A_p(G):F\cap LK=1\}.
\]
Give $\mathcal Q$ the coordinatewise order and $\mathcal F$ the
inclusion order. Define
\[
 \mathcal F_0=
 \{F\in\mathcal F:F\leq N_G(L),\
                         O_p(C_G(LF))\ne1\}.
\]
The disjoint union $\mathcal X=\mathcal Q\sqcup\mathcal F$ is
ordered by these orders and by the following crossed comparisons:
\begin{equation}
 F<(U,V)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \begin{cases}
 C_{UV}(F)\ne1,\\
 C_{UV}(F)\not\leq L&\text{if }F\in\mathcal F_0.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
There are no comparisons directed from $\mathcal Q$ to
$\mathcal F$. These rules define a poset, and
$\mathcal X\simeq\mathcal A_p(G)$.

statements.label: prop:psl45
statements.text:
A minimal-order counterexample to the rational homological
implication at $p=2$ has no simple component isomorphic to
$\PSL_4(5)$.

title: Rationality of the Canonical Unramified Arthur Filtration
abstract: Under the characteristic hypotheses of restricted geometric Langlands theory, we prove that the canonical Arthur filtration on finitely supported unramified automorphic functions is defined over ℚ for split connected semisimple groups. The result includes the noncuspidal part and every closed invariant nilpotent support, establishing the rationality conjecture of Gaitsgory–Lafforgue–Raskin in this setting.

tex.abstract:
Under the characteristic hypotheses of restricted geometric Langlands theory,
we prove that the canonical Arthur filtration on finitely supported
unramified automorphic functions is defined over $\Q$ for split connected
semisimple groups. The result includes the noncuspidal part and every closed
invariant nilpotent support, establishing the rationality conjecture of
Gaitsgory--Lafforgue--Raskin in this setting.

statements.label: intro:characteristic
statements.text:
The following four conditions hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item The Lie algebra $\mathfrak h$ has an $H$-invariant nondegenerate
symmetric bilinear form whose restriction to the center of $\Lie(M)$ is
nondegenerate for every Levi subgroup $M$ of $H$.
\item For each Levi subgroup $M$ of $H$, including $H$ itself, and each
maximal torus $T_M\subset M$, restriction induces an isomorphism
\[
k_0[\mathfrak m]^M\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
k_0[\mathfrak t_M]^{W_M},\qquad
\mathfrak m=\Lie(M),\quad \mathfrak t_M=\Lie(T_M),\quad
W_M=N_M(T_M)/T_M.
\]
\item The scheme-theoretic centralizer in $H$ of every semisimple element
of $\mathfrak h$ is a Levi subgroup.
\item For every extension $K/k_0$ and every nilpotent
$n\in\mathfrak h\otimes_{k_0}K$, there is a parabolic subgroup
$P\subset H_K$, defined over $K$, such that
$n\in\Lie(R_u(P))$.
\end{enumerate}
Here a Levi subgroup is a Levi factor of a parabolic subgroup. Semisimple
means geometrically conjugate into the Lie algebra of a maximal torus;
nilpotent means that the geometric adjoint orbit closure contains zero.

statements.label: intro:main
statements.text:
Under Assumption~\ref{intro:characteristic}, for every prime
$\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(\mathbb F_q)$ and every closed invariant
$Y\subset\Nhat$, the natural map
\begin{equation}
E\otimes_\Q\bigl(\cA_\Q\cap\cF_Y\cA_E\bigr)
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\cF_Y\cA_E
\end{equation}
is an isomorphism. The intersection is taken inside $\cA_E$.

statements.title: Restricted geometric Langlands
statements.label: inp:langlands
statements.text:
There is a Frobenius-invariant union $Z$ of connected components of
$\LocSys^{\mathrm{restr}}_{\Ghat}(\overline X)$ and an equivalence
\[
 \mathbb L_G^{\mathrm{restr}}:\cC
       \xrightarrow{\sim}\IndCoh_{\Nhat}(Z).
\]
It identifies $\cC_Y$ with $\IndCoh_Y(Z)$ for every closed
$\Ghat$-invariant $Y\subset\Nhat$ and intertwines Hecke functors with
tensoring by the corresponding evaluation bundles.  If
$f:Z\to Z$ sends a local system to its pullback along geometric
Frobenius of $\overline X$, the functor corresponding to
$\Phi=(\operatorname{Frob}_{\Bun})_*$ is $f^!$.
The embedding $\cC\hookrightarrow\Shv(\Bun_G(\overline X),\E)$
preserves compact objects.

statements.title: Trace and ordinary local terms
statements.label: inp:trace
statements.text:
There is a canonical isomorphism of complexes
\[
 \operatorname{LT}:\Tr(\Phi,\cC)\xrightarrow{\sim}\cA_{\E},
\]
with the right-hand side in degree zero.  For a compact object $M$ and
a morphism $b:M\to\Phi M$, it sends the categorical class $[M,b]$ to
the ordinary alternating trace function of the adjoint morphism
$(\operatorname{Frob}_{\Bun})^*M\to M$.  The function has finite support.
This comparison is compatible with Hecke operations and with the
sheaf--function operations of pullback, star tensor product, and
compactly supported pushforward.

statements.title: Nonstandard duality
statements.label: inp:duality
statements.text:
The pairing
\begin{equation}
 \cC\otimes\cC\longrightarrow\operatorname{Vect}_{\E},\qquad
 (M,N)\longmapsto
 R\Gamma_c\bigl(\Bun_G(\overline X),M\overset{*}{\otimes}N\bigr)
\end{equation}
defines a self-duality of $\cC$.  It is invariant under simultaneous
Frobenius.  If $M,N$ are compact, its value is a perfect complex, also
after any finite Hecke representation is inserted in either variable.

statements.title: Components and deformation theory
statements.label: inp:components
statements.text:
Every connected component $Z_\sigma$ of the restricted local-system
stack has a unique semisimple isomorphism class $\sigma$.  Its
automorphism group $J=\Aut(\sigma)$ is reductive, possibly disconnected.
There is a formal affine coarse space $S_\sigma$ with reduced space a
point, and $Z_\sigma\to S_\sigma$ is relatively algebraic.
After choosing a frame at a geometric point, the component is formal
affine.  For an affine infinitesimal stage $S_n\to S_\sigma$, its
base change is affine; almost finite type stages and bounded Postnikov
truncations may be used.  These affine stages have coherent cohomology
in each bounded range.  The tangent complex at a local system $\tau$ is
\begin{equation}
 T_\tau\LocSys^{\mathrm{restr}}_{\Ghat}(\overline X)
       \simeq R\Gamma(\overline X,\ghat_\tau)[1].
\end{equation}
In particular the stack is quasi-smooth.

statements.title: Pure Weil lift
statements.label: inp:pure-lift
statements.text:
Fix an abstract field isomorphism $\iota:\E\xrightarrow{\sim}\C$.
If $Z_\sigma$ is Frobenius invariant, its semisimple point $\sigma$
admits a Weil structure that is $\iota$-pure of weight zero.  In
particular, writing $\ghat_\sigma$ for its adjoint local system, every
Frobenius eigenvalue on
$H^i(\overline X,\ghat_\sigma)$ has $\iota$-absolute value $q^{i/2}$,
for $0\leq i\leq2$.

statements.title: The framed quadratic model
statements.label: mod:model
statements.text:
The retained component $Z_\sigma$, with its Frobenius action,
evaluation bundles at the chosen cyclic tuple, and singular-support
map, admits the model
\begin{equation}

 Z_\sigma\simeq
 \bigl[(\mu^{-1}(0))^{\wedge}_{\mathrm{unst}}/J\bigr].
\end{equation}
Here $\mathrm{unst}$ is the inverse image of the origin under
$V\to V/\!/J$, and completion is along this invariant null fiber.
In this model:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item the singularity scheme has points $(x,z)$ satisfying
      $\mu(x)=0$ and $zx=0$, with $z\in\mathfrak j$;
\item the support condition defined by $Y$ is the condition that the
      image of $z$ under $\mathfrak j\hookrightarrow\ghat$ belongs
      to $Y$;
\item every evaluation representation of $K=\Ghat^d$ is the bundle
      associated to its restriction along $J\hookrightarrow K$;
      Frobenius has constant cyclic transport on these bundles;
\item after removing the scalars $q^{1/2}$ on deformation points and
      $q^{-1}$ on singular points, Frobenius is a linear
      automorphism of the moment-map data, normalizing $J$ and the
      framed representation labels. Its eigenvalues on these
      normalized linear data have modulus one.
\end{enumerate}
The meaning of Frobenius on Hom complexes in \textup{(iv)} is fixed
explicitly in Lemma~\ref{mod:hom-action} below.
statements.section_title: A quadratic model with its Frobenius action

statements.title: Orbit generation
statements.label: orb:generation
statements.text:
The objects $M_P$, for simple $P\in\mathsf E_e$, generate the compact
category supported on $J.e$ in an open where it is closed.  Here
``generate'' allows finite cones, shifts and summands.
The category $\mathsf E_e$ is semisimple.
statements.section_title: The category on a nilpotent orbit

statements.title: Compact orbit-closure lifts
statements.label: orb:weil-lifts
statements.text:
Every $M_P$ is the restriction of a compact object with $z$-support in
$\overline{J.e}$.  If $P$ has a compatible locally finite cyclic
structure, the extension can be given that structure.  For a simple
label fixed by Frobenius, a structure may be chosen whose
triple-translated coefficient eigenvalues have modulus one.
The same assertions hold for a power of Frobenius, for a finite cyclic
list of labels, and after tensoring $P$ by any finite-dimensional
$L_e$-representation with compatible cyclic structure, placed in
lifted degree zero.  Inverse structures are available for opposite
category classes.
statements.section_title: The category on a nilpotent orbit

statements.title: The orbit Hom calculation
statements.label: orb:hom-calculation
statements.text:
For $P,P'\in\mathsf E_e$, the Hom complex between the orbit generators
has a finite equivariant calculation with Euler terms
\begin{equation}
 \left[
 \C[\ker(e:V\to V)]\otimes
 \Hom_{D_e}(P,P')\otimes
 \Lambda^\bullet(N_e[-1])\otimes
 \Lambda^\bullet(\Lie(U_e)^*[-1])
 \right]^{L_e}.
\end{equation}
Here the coefficient factor has lifted degree zero; the shifts in the
normal and Lie factors add one to the degrees in
\eqref{orb:weight-table}.  The formula is an equality of alternating
equivariant characters, and a finite-filtration calculation bounding
weights, rather than an assertion that the Hom complex splits as the
displayed tensor product.

For pure coefficient normalizations, all nonconstant terms have
strictly negative absolute $S_e$-weight.  The weight-zero cohomology is
\begin{equation}
 H^\bullet\Hom(M_P,M_{P'})_{\mathrm{wt}=0}
       =\Hom_{D_e,L_e}(P,P')[0],
\end{equation}
with ordinary composition.  Before the finite invariant calculation,
weight pieces are finite-dimensional and their dimensions grow at most
polynomially over bounded-length weight intervals.  In particular,
the character sums in \eqref{orb:hom-euler} are absolutely convergent
on every normalized compact $L_e$-coset, uniformly on that coset.
statements.section_title: The category on a nilpotent orbit

statements.title: Trace of an orbit
statements.label: tr:orbit-trace
statements.text:
The trace on the supported category of a Frobenius-stable nilpotent
orbit is concentrated in degree zero.  A basis is given by the classes
of $M_P$ for Frobenius-fixed simple $P\in\mathsf E_e$, with chosen
pure normalized structures.  Every basis class lifts to an actual
compact Weil object supported on the orbit closure, and also to one
with invariant null-fiber support up to a nonzero scalar.
The same conclusions hold for the compact opposite category with
simultaneous Frobenius.
statements.section_title: Frobenius traces and compact Weil classes

statements.title: Concentration, injection, and Weil spanning
statements.label: tr:spanning
statements.text:
On a fixed retained spectral component, the trace of every closed
invariant nilpotent support category is concentrated in degree zero.
If $\Omega'\subset\Omega$ are such support bounds, then
\begin{equation}
 H^0\Tr(\Phi,\operatorname{Ind}\mathscr B_{\Omega',0})
   \longrightarrow
 H^0\Tr(\Phi,\operatorname{Ind}\mathscr B_{\Omega,0})
\end{equation}
is injective.  A finite filtration by invariant unions of orbits has
the orbit traces as its actual successive quotients.  Every trace
class is a finite linear combination of classes of compact objects
with Weil structures; those objects can be chosen with support in the
prescribed bound.  All assertions hold on the compact opposite side.

After assembling retained components, these statements apply to
$\cC_Y$ and $\cC$.  In particular, the image defining $\cF_Y\cA_{\E}$
is the injective image of the supported trace, and every function in
$\cA_{\E}$ and every vector in $\cF_Y\cA_{\E}$ is a finite linear
combination of the corresponding actual compact Weil trace functions.
The analogous statement supplies all tests through the
nonstandard self-duality of Theorem~\ref{inp:duality}.
statements.section_title: Frobenius traces and compact Weil classes

statements.title: Bilinear support detector
statements.label: meas:detector
statements.section_title: Hecke matrix coefficients and support detection

statements.label: meas:common-support
statements.text:
Suppose $M,N$ belong to one retained component and have closed
$z$-support bounds $Z_M,Z_N\subset\mathfrak j$.  Their measure satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{supp}(\nu_{f_N,g_M})
 \subset
 \bigcup_{e\in Z_M\cap Z_N}B_{\Ghat.e}.
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Hecke matrix coefficients and support detection

statements.label: desc:unique-measure
statements.text:
A finite complex Borel measure on $B$ is determined by its integrals
against all representation characters.
statements.section_title: Compact spectral sets and rational descent

statements.label: desc:coefficient-independence
statements.text:
For a fixed closed invariant support $Y$, the subspace
$\iota_*(\cF_Y\cA_E)\subset\cA_\C$ is independent of the abstract
isomorphism $\iota:E\xrightarrow{\sim}\C$, after matching nilpotent
orbits by the split root datum. Consequently $\cF_Y\cA_E$ is invariant
under every automorphism of $E$ fixing $\Q$.
statements.section_title: Compact spectral sets and rational descent

statements.title: Cuspidal comparison across coefficient primes
statements.label: desc:cuspidal-comparison
statements.text:
Keep the curve $X/\mathbb F_q$, the split connected semisimple group
$G/\mathbb F_q$, and all four conditions of
Assumption~\ref{intro:characteristic}. Put
$p=\operatorname{char}(\mathbb F_q)$ and
$E_\ell=\overline{\Q}_\ell$ for $\ell\ne p$. At unramified level $D=0$,
let $C_{0,\Q}\subset\cA_\Q$ be the cuspidal function space and
$C_{0,\mathcal O,\Q}$ its rational orbit summands from
\cite[Theorem~1.1]{CuspidalArthur}, and set
$C_{0,\ell}=E_\ell\otimes_\Q C_{0,\Q}$.
For each $\ell\ne p$, let $Y_\ell\subset\Nhat_{E_\ell}$ be closed and
invariant, with the same nilpotent-orbit subset $\mathscr Y$ under the
fixed pinned split rational dual group. Write $Y=(Y_\ell)_{\ell\ne p}$ and
define
\[
 F^{\Q}_{Y,\ell}:=\cA_\Q\cap\cF_{Y_\ell}\cA_{E_\ell},
 \qquad
 V_{Y,\Q}:=\bigoplus_{\mathcal O\in\mathscr Y}C_{0,\mathcal O,\Q}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 C_{0,\Q}\cap F^{\Q}_{Y,\ell}&=V_{Y,\Q},\\
 C_{0,\ell}\cap\cF_{Y_\ell}\cA_{E_\ell}
   &=E_\ell\otimes_\Q V_{Y,\Q}.
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
The intersections are taken in the corresponding finitely supported
function spaces. The equalities include the zero cusp space and empty or
full $Y_\ell$.

title: Reconstruction from Milnor K-theory modulo the characteristic
abstract: Let K and L be finitely generated extensions of transcendence degree at least two over algebraically closed fields of characteristic p. We prove that every isomorphism of their first Milnor K-groups modulo p preserving the degree-two Steinberg relations is a nonzero scalar multiple of the map induced by a unique field isomorphism. The proof recovers projective lines over the subfields of pth powers by an elementary calculation with derivations.

tex.abstract:
Let $K$ and $L$ be finitely generated extensions of transcendence degree
at least two over algebraically closed fields of characteristic $p$.
We prove that every isomorphism of their first Milnor $K$-groups modulo
$p$ preserving the degree-two Steinberg relations is a nonzero scalar
multiple of the map induced by a unique field isomorphism. The proof
recovers projective lines over the subfields of $p$th powers by an
elementary calculation with derivations.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $K/k$ and $L/l$ be finitely generated extensions of algebraically
closed fields of characteristic $p$, with
\[
              \trdeg(K/k)\ge2,\qquad \trdeg(L/l)\ge2.
\]
The canonical map
\[
 \Isom(K,k;L,l)\longrightarrow
 \Isom_{\mathrm M}(V_K,V_L)/\Lambda^\times,
 \qquad \alpha\longmapsto[\alpha_*],
\]
is bijective.

statements.title: Intersection and exponent
statements.label: prop:intersection
statements.text:
Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $p$ with $[F:F^p]<\infty$, and put
$C=F^p$.  Let $X,Y\in F^\times$ be $p$-independent.  Suppose
\[
 U\in C(X)^\times,\qquad V\in C(Y)^\times,
 \qquad [U]\notin\Fp[X],\qquad [V]\notin\Fp[Y].
\]
If
\begin{equation}

 X\,C(Y/X)^\times\ \cap\ U\,C(V/U)^\times\ne\varnothing,
\end{equation}
then there is a unique integer $n$, $1\le n<p$, such that
\begin{equation}

 U^n\in C+CX^n,\qquad V^n\in C+CY^n.
\end{equation}
In fact, either inclusion in \eqref{eq:intersection-conclusion} determines
$n$ uniquely.  In each inclusion, both coefficients are nonzero.
statements.section_title: An intersection that determines an exponent

statements.label: prop:lines
statements.text:
Let $K/k$ and $L/l$ be finitely generated extensions of algebraically
closed fields of characteristic $p$, both of transcendence degree at
least two.  For every compatible isomorphism $\Theta:V_K\to V_L$, there
is a unique $n\in\Fp^\times$ such that $\Psi=n\Theta$ sends every
projective line over $K^p$ onto a projective line over $L^p$.
statements.section_title: One scalar recovers all projective lines

statements.title: Projective lifting
statements.label: prop:projective-lift
statements.text:
Let $E$ and $E'$ be finite-dimensional vector spaces over fields $H$
and $C$, respectively, with dimensions at least three. Every bijection
$\psi:\PP_H(E)\to\PP_C(E')$ that maps lines onto lines is induced by
an additive bijection $S:E\to E'$ satisfying
\[
 S(av)=\sigma(a)S(v)\qquad(a\in H,\ v\in E)
\]
for a field isomorphism $\sigma:H\to C$. The map $\sigma$ is unique,
and $S$ is unique up to multiplication by an element of $C^\times$.

title: Reconstruction of Function Fields from Mod-ℓ Milnor K-Theory
abstract: We prove a mod-ℓ Bogomolov–Pop reconstruction theorem for function fields of transcendence degree at least two over arbitrary algebraically closed fields of characteristic different from ℓ. The groups \(K^{\mathrm M}_1/\ell\) and \(K^{\mathrm M}_2/\ell\), together with their full bilinear product, determine the perfect closure and its constant field. Every compatible isomorphism of these data is induced by a field isomorphism up to a single scalar in \(\mathbb F_\ell^\times\), with only Frobenius ambiguity in the field isomorphism in positive characteristic.

tex.abstract:
We prove a mod-$\ell$ Bogomolov--Pop reconstruction theorem for function
fields of transcendence degree at least two over arbitrary algebraically
closed fields of characteristic different from $\ell$. The groups
$K^{\mathrm M}_1/\ell$ and $K^{\mathrm M}_2/\ell$, together with their full
bilinear product, determine the perfect closure and its constant field.
Every compatible isomorphism of these data is induced by a field isomorphism
up to a single scalar in $\F_\ell^\times$, with only Frobenius ambiguity in
the field isomorphism in positive characteristic.
sections: A uniform bound for the support of a pencil
Recovering the field from simultaneous values

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $\ell$ be any prime. Let $K/k$ and $L/l$ be finitely generated
extensions of arbitrary algebraically closed fields, with
$\charac k,\charac l\ne\ell$ and
$\trdeg(K/k),\trdeg(L/l)\ge2$. Then \eqref{eq:main-map} is bijective.
In particular, a compatible isomorphism $V_K\to V_L$ forces equality
of the characteristics and of the relative transcendence degrees.

statements.title: Alternating-pair valuation theory
statements.label: thm:local-input
statements.text:
Let~\(F\) be a field and set
\(A_F^{\pm}=\{f\in A_F:f(-1)=0\}\).
\begin{enumerate}
\item Every valuative subset~\(\Sigma\subset A_F\) has a unique coarsest
valuation~\(v_\Sigma\) with~\(\Sigma\subset I_{v_\Sigma}\).  In particular,
\(v_\Sigma\) coarsens every valuation whose inertia contains~\(\Sigma\).
For such a valuation~\(w\), this coarsening is obtained by quotienting
\(wF\) by its largest convex subgroup contained in
\(w(\bigcap_{f\in\Sigma}\ker f)\).
\item If~\(S\subset A_F^{\pm}\) is an alternating linear subspace, its
valuative elements form a valuative subspace~\(S_0\) of codimension at
most one.  Moreover~\(S\subset D_{v_{S_0}}\).
\item If~\(\Sigma\subset A_F^{\pm}\) is valuative and~\(g\in A_F^{\pm}\)
is alternating with every element of~\(\Sigma\), then
\(g\in D_{v_\Sigma}\).
\end{enumerate}

statements.label: prop:local-dimension
statements.text:
The maximum dimension of an alternating subspace of~\(A_F\) is~\(s\).
If~\(S\subset A_F\) is alternating of dimension~\(s\), and~\(v\) is
the valuation associated to its valuative part~\(S_0\), then
\(S_0=I_v\) and equality holds in~\eqref{eq:local-abhyankar} for~\(v\).

statements.label: prop:quasi-recovery
cor:flag-matching
statements.text:
For the fields~\(K/k,L/l\) of Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, a compatible
isomorphism~\(\Theta\) forces
\(\trdeg(K/k)=\trdeg(L/l)=d\), say.  Its dual~\(\Phi\) matches the
inertia--decomposition pairs of quasi-prime divisors, and, successively,
the pairs of quasi-prime~\(r\)-divisors for~\(1\leq r\leq d-1\).
For a matched pair of valuations~\(v\) on~\(K\) and~\(w\) on~\(L\),
it induces a topological linear isomorphism
\[
 A_{Lw}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }A_{Kv}
\]
preserving alternating pairs in both directions.

statements.title: Pop's residual density input
statements.label: thm:density-input
statements.text:
Let \(F/\kappa\) be a function field over an algebraically closed field
of characteristic different from \(\ell\). Suppose that a valuation
\(v\) of \(F\), with \(Fv/\kappa v\) a function field, has the following
properties:
\begin{enumerate}
 \item \(vF\) has no nonzero \(\ell\)-divisible convex subgroup;
 \item there is a subfield \(\kappa\subset\kappa_1\subset F\) such that
 \[
   \kappa_1v=\kappa v,\qquad
   \trdeg(F/\kappa_1)=\trdeg(Fv/\kappa_1v)=1.
 \]
\end{enumerate}
Then \(\widehat J_v\) contains the full minimized inertia group
\(\widehat I_u\) of every c.r.\ quasi-prime divisor \(u\) of
\(Fv/\kappa v\).

statements.label: prop:point-recognition
statements.text:
For a quasi-prime \((d-1)\)-divisor \(v\) of \(F/\kappa\), the family
\(\mathcal L_v\) satisfies the preceding two conditions if and only if
\(\kappa v\) is algebraic over a finite field.
When this holds, \(\mathcal L_v\) consists exactly of the point inertia
lines of the smooth projective curve of \(Fv/\kappa v\).
Consequently the matching in Corollary~\ref{cor:flag-matching}
recognizes these terminal valuations and matches their full point
families.

statements.title: Correspondence of curve subfields
statements.label: thm:curve-matching
statements.text:
For every curve subfield $E\subset K$ there is a unique curve subfield
$P\subset L$ such that $\Theta(V_E)=V_P$.  This assignment is a bijection
between the curve subfields of $K/k$ and those of $L/l$.

statements.title: Recognition of true divisors
statements.label: prop:true-divisors
statements.text:
Let $F/\kappa$ be one of $K/k$ or $L/l$.  A quasi-divisorial valuation
$v$ of $F/\kappa$ is a true prime divisor if and only if there is a curve
subfield $E\subset F$ for which
\begin{equation}

                         \dim_\Lambda(V_E\cap D_v^\perp)<\infty.
\end{equation}
Consequently $\Phi$ matches the inertia and decomposition groups of true
prime divisors of $L/l$ with those of $K/k$.

statements.title: Recognition of good subfields
statements.label: prop:good-matching
statements.text:
The curve-subfield correspondence of Theorem~\ref{thm:curve-matching}
restricts to a bijection on good subfields.  For matched good subfields
$E\subset K$ and $P\subset L$, the induced character isomorphism gives
a bijection between the points of their smooth projective rational curves.

statements.title: Alignment of the constants
statements.label: prop:constant-alignment
statements.text:
The fields \(k\) and \(l\) have the same characteristic.  There is a field
isomorphism \(\sigma:k\longrightarrow l\) such that, for every good function
\(t\), there is \(H_t\in\mathcal H_l\) with
\begin{equation}
 B_t=H_t\circ\sigma
 \qquad\text{outside a finite subset of }\Pj^1(k),
\end{equation}
where \(\sigma(\infty)=\infty\).
statements.section_title: Recovering the field from simultaneous values

statements.label: thm:field-isomorphism
statements.text:
There is a field isomorphism
\[
 \alpha:K^i\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }L^i,\qquad \alpha|_k=\sigma,
\]
such that \(\alpha(t)=u_t\) for every good function \(t\).
In particular, if \(k(t)\) and \(l(t')\) are matched good rational
subfields, then \(\alpha(k(t)^i)=l(t')^i\).
statements.section_title: Recovering the field from simultaneous values

statements.label: prop:global-scalar
statements.text:
Let $\Psi:V_K\to V_K$ be a compatible $\Lambda$-linear automorphism.
If $\Psi(V_E)=V_E$ for every good rational subfield $E\subset K$,
then $\Psi=a\,\mathrm{id}$ for one $a\in\Lambda^\times$.

statements.label: prop:uniqueness
statements.text:
Suppose $\beta:K^i\to K^i$ is a field automorphism preserving $k$
whose action on $V_K$ is a scalar. Then $\beta$ is the identity in
characteristic zero and an integral power of Frobenius in positive
characteristic.

title: Regular trajectories, pruning and quantum parity
abstract: We prove that constant-depth quantum circuits with arbitrary one-qubit gates and unbounded-arity Toffoli gates cannot compute parity with any fixed positive worst-case advantage using polynomially many total qubits. Ancillary qubits are initialized to \(|0\rangle\), one output qubit is measured, and all other final registers may be discarded without restriction. This resolves Moore's parity conjecture in the measured-output model.

tex.abstract:
We prove that constant-depth quantum circuits with arbitrary one-qubit
gates and unbounded-arity Toffoli gates cannot compute parity with
any fixed positive worst-case advantage using polynomially many total
qubits. Ancillary qubits are initialized to $|0\rangle$, one output qubit
is measured, and all other final registers may be discarded without
restriction. This resolves Moore's parity conjecture in the
measured-output model.

statements.label: thm:parity
statements.text:
Fix positive integers $d,k,C$ and a real $0<\varepsilon\le1/2$.
There is an integer $n_0=n_0(d,k,C,\varepsilon)$ such that,
for every $n\ge n_0$, every allowed circuit of depth at most $d$
on at most $C(n+1)^k$ total qubits has an input $x\in\{0,1\}^{n}$ on which its answer equals
$\Parity_n(x)$ with probability strictly less than $1/2+\varepsilon$.

statements.title: Low-degree propagation
statements.label: prop:propagation
statements.text:
Let $V$ be a circuit with a bounded number of analytic layers, and suppose
the trajectory from $\zeta$, with $\norm{\zeta}\le 1$, is regular for $V$.
Here $k,K$ denote degree exponents: fix $0<k<K<1$.  For every operator $E$
with
\[
 \deg E\le m^k,
 \qquad \norm{E}\le \exp(m^k),
\]
there is, eventually, an operator $E'$ such that
\begin{equation}
 
 \begin{gathered}
  \norm{VE\zeta-E'V\zeta}\le \exp(-m^k),\\
  \deg E'\le m^K,
  \qquad \norm{E'}\le \exp(m^K).
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
The starting vector need not be a product vector.

statements.title: Projection insertion
statements.label: prop:projection-insertion
statements.text:
Let $W=U_t\cdots U_1$ have a bounded number of layers, and suppose the
trajectory
\[
 \psi_j=U_j\cdots U_1\psi_0,\qquad 0\le j\le t,
\]
is regular, with $\norm{\psi_0}\le1$.  For any product test $B$ at the
output, set
\[
 \chi_t=P_B\psi_t,\qquad
 \chi_j=U_{j+1}^{\dagger}\cdots U_t^{\dagger}\chi_t
 \quad(0\le j<t).
\]
Then the trajectory $(\chi_j)_{j=0}^t$ is regular for $W$.

statements.title: Pruning from a product state
statements.label: prop:pruning
statements.text:
For any sequence of circuits $U=U_t\cdots U_1$ on $m$ qubits, with a
bounded number $t$ of analytic layers, and any normalized product
starting states $\psi_0$, the following construction produces a
circuit $W$ with a regular trajectory from $\psi_0$.  Leave all
one-qubit layers unchanged.  At a reflection layer, use the exact
state reached by the pruned prefix and retain exactly the gates in
\eqref{eq:retention-rule}.  The output vectors satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \norm{U\psi_0-W\psi_0}\le 2t m^{-2}.
\end{equation}

title: Relative denominators and effective systems for log Calabi-Yau fibrations
abstract: We prove uniform denominator and effective-system bounds for log Calabi-Yau fibrations from projective log canonical complex pairs of dimension at most four onto positive-dimensional bases, with boundary coefficients in a fixed finite rational set. The bounds give a uniform trivializing degree and a uniform b-Cartier multiple of the moduli b-divisor. When the base divisor is big, a uniform complete rounded adjoint system has section ratios generating the full base function field.

tex.abstract:
We prove uniform denominator and effective-system bounds for log Calabi-Yau
fibrations from projective log canonical complex pairs of dimension at most
four onto positive-dimensional bases, with boundary coefficients in a fixed
finite rational set. The bounds give a uniform trivializing degree and a
uniform b-Cartier multiple of the moduli b-divisor. When the base divisor is
big, a uniform complete rounded adjoint system has section ratios generating
the full base function field.

statements.title: Uniform relative denominators
statements.label: thm:relative-denominators
statements.text:
Fix a finite set $\Phi\subset[0,1]\cap\Q$ and an integer $1\leq d\leq4$.
There are positive integers $p_0\mid p$, with $p_0$ clearing $\Phi$, and a
rational DCC set $\mathcal B\subset[0,1]$, depending only on $d$ and
$\Phi$, with the following property. Suppose $(X,B)$ is a projective lc
pair of dimension $d$ with coefficients in $\Phi$, and
\[
 f:X\longrightarrow Z,\qquad \dim Z>0,\qquad K_X+B\sim_\Q f^*D,
\]
where $f$ is a contraction and $D$ is a rational Cartier divisor. There
exist $\psi\in\C(X)^*$ and $D_Z\sim_\Q D$ such that
\begin{equation}
 K_X+B+\frac{1}{p_0}\Div(\psi)=f^*D_Z,
 \qquad D_Z=K_Z+B_Z+M_Z.
\end{equation}
Here $B_Z$ is effective with coefficients in $\mathcal B$, the pair
$(Z,B_Z+M_Z)$ is generalized lc, and $\mathbf M$ is b-nef with
$p\mathbf M$ b-Cartier. If $(X,B)$ is klt, the generalized pair is
generalized klt.

statements.label: prop:effective-base
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:relative-denominators}, suppose in
addition that $D$ is big.  There is a positive integer $m=m(d,\Phi)$ such
that, for every positive multiple $l$ of $m$, the complete divisorial
system
\[
 \left|\left\lfloor l(K_X+B)\right\rfloor\right|
\]
is nonempty and generates precisely the subfield $\C(Z)\subset\C(X)$.
Its rational map is therefore birationally equivalent to $f$ and to the
Iitaka fibration of $K_X+B$.
statements.section_title: Effective systems recovering the entire base field

statements.label: prop:rc-torsion
statements.text:
Fix an integer $1\leq d\leq 4$, a DCC set
$I\subset [0,1]\cap\Q$, and a positive integer $p$.
There exists a positive integer $\ell=\ell(d,I,p)$ with the following
property.  Let $Z$ be a normal projective complex variety of dimension $d$
with a rationally connected smooth projective resolution.  Suppose that
$(Z,B+M_Z)$ is generalized klt, that $B\geq 0$ has coefficients in $I$,
and that the b-nef rational b-divisor $\mathbf M$ has $p\mathbf M$
b-Cartier.  If
\[
 D=K_Z+B+M_Z\sim_{\Q}0,
\]
then $\ell D$ is an integral principal divisor.  Consequently, for every
integer $a\geq1$, the divisor $a\ell D$ is principal and
\[
 h^0\bigl(Z,\OO_Z(a\ell D)\bigr)=1.
\]
The same integer can be chosen for all dimensions in any fixed subset of
$\{1,2,3,4\}$.
statements.section_title: Integral principal multiples over rationally connected bases

statements.label: cor:relative-rc-torsion
statements.text:
Fix a finite rational coefficient set $\Phi\subset[0,1]\cap\Q$.
There is a positive integer $r=r(\Phi)$ such that the following holds.
Let $(X,B)$ be a projective klt fourfold pair with effective boundary
having coefficients in $\Phi$, and suppose that
$K_X+B\sim_{\Q}0$.  If there is a contraction $f:X\to Z$ with
$\dim Z>0$ and with a rationally connected smooth projective resolution
of $Z$, then $r(K_X+B)$ is an integral principal divisor. This includes
$B=0$, and every positive multiple is also principal.
statements.section_title: Integral principal multiples over rationally connected bases

title: Relative generation and the generator problem for finite factors
abstract: We prove that every type II<sub>1</sub> factor with separable predual is generated by one operator, equivalently by two self-adjoint operators. Combined with the established direct-integral reduction to this case, this gives an affirmative solution of the generator problem for von Neumann algebras with separable predual.

tex.abstract:
We prove that every type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor with separable predual is
generated by one operator, equivalently by two self-adjoint operators.
Combined with the established direct-integral reduction to this case,
this gives an affirmative solution of the generator problem for von
Neumann algebras with separable predual.
sections: Free Haar unitaries in an ultrapower
Consequences for generation and free entropy

statements.label: thm:relative-generation
statements.text:
Let $P\subset M$ be an irreducible inclusion of type $\mathrm{II}_1$
factors, with $M$ of separable predual. The set
\[
 \{u\in\mathcal U(M):W^*(P,u)=M\}
\]
is a dense $G_\delta$ subset of the unitary group $\mathcal U(M)$
for the trace $2$-norm topology.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Every type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $M$ with separable predual is
generated by two self-adjoint elements. Equivalently, there is an
$x\in M$ such that $M=W^*(x)$.

statements.title: Popa's independence theorem
statements.label: thm:popa-independence
statements.text:
Let $P\subset M$ be an irreducible inclusion of $\mathrm{II}_1$
factors, and put $\mathbf Q=P^\omega\subset M^\omega=\mathbf M$.
For every linear subspace $X\subset\mathbf M$ that is separable in
$2$-norm and satisfies $\tau(x)=0$ for all $x\in X$, there is a
diffuse abelian von Neumann algebra $A\subset\mathbf Q$ such that
\begin{equation}

  \tau(x_0a_1x_1\cdots a_mx_m)=0
\end{equation}
whenever $m\geq1$, $x_0\in X\cup\{1\}$,
$x_1,\ldots,x_m\in X$, and $a_1,\ldots,a_m\in A$ have trace zero.
statements.section_title: Free Haar unitaries in an ultrapower

statements.label: prop:perturbation
statements.text:
Let $P\subset M$ be an irreducible inclusion of $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors.
Given $u,z\in\mathcal U(M)$, $\xi\in M$, and $0<\alpha<1/2$,
for every integer $\ell\ge1$ there are
$\widetilde u\in\mathcal U(M)$ and
$\widetilde t_0,\ldots,\widetilde t_\ell\in\mathcal U(P)$ such that,
with
\[
  \widetilde W=\widetilde t_0
     \prod_{k=1}^{\ell}(\widetilde u\,\widetilde t_k),
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
  \norm{\widetilde u-u}_2
    &\le \frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{2\ell}}+\frac1\ell,\\
  \left|\tau(\xi^*\widetilde W)
           -\frac\alpha2\tau(\xi^*z)\right|
    &\le \norm{\xi}_2\frac{4\alpha^2}{1-2\alpha}+\frac1\ell.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
All products indexed by $k$ are taken in increasing order from left
to right.  The unitaries may depend on $\ell$.

statements.title: Popa
statements.label: thm:irreducible-hyperfinite
statements.text:
Let $N\subset M$ be an irreducible inclusion of $\mathrm{II}_1$
factors with separable preduals. There is a hyperfinite
$\mathrm{II}_1$ subfactor $R\subset N$ such that
$R'\cap M=\mathbb C1$.

statements.label: prop:four-generators
statements.text:
Every $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor with separable predual is generated
by four self-adjoint elements.

statements.label: cor:entropy-generators
statements.text:
For every integer $n\geq3$, the factor $L(\mathbb F_n)$ with its
canonical trace has two finite self-adjoint generating tuples on
which both $\delta$ and $\delta_0$ take different values. In
particular, neither dimension is determined by the generated
tracial von Neumann algebra.

title: Relative independence of the separable quotient problem
abstract: The separable quotient problem asks whether every infinite-dimensional Banach space has a separable infinite-dimensional quotient. We prove that this statement is independent of ZFC, relative to the consistency of ZFC with a measurable cardinal. This holds over both the real and complex fields. For spaces of norm density ℵ<sub>1</sub>, we obtain independence relative to the consistency of ZFC alone.

tex.abstract:
The separable quotient problem asks whether every infinite-dimensional Banach
space has a separable infinite-dimensional quotient. We prove that this
statement is independent of ZFC, relative to the consistency of ZFC with a
measurable cardinal. This holds over both the real and complex fields. For
spaces of norm density $\aleph_1$, we obtain independence relative to the
consistency of ZFC alone.
sections: A measure on the continuum gives separable quotients
Passing between real and complex spaces
A dual space with coded norming functionals
Infinite paths and weak-Cauchy block sequences
Vectors detected at a prescribed weight

statements.label: intro:main
statements.text:
For each $\mathbb F\in\{\R,\C\}$, ZFC proves the following implications.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item If $\mathfrak c$ is real-valued measurable, then $\SQ_{\mathbb F}$
 holds.
 \item If the continuum hypothesis holds, then $\SQ_{\mathbb F}$ fails.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, if ZFC with a measurable cardinal is consistent, then
$\SQ_{\mathbb F}$ is independent of ZFC. Consistency of its failure
requires only consistency of ZFC.

statements.label: intro:small-density
statements.text:
If ZFC is consistent, then $\SQ^{\aleph_1}_{\mathbb F}$ is independent
of ZFC for each $\mathbb F\in\{\R,\C\}$.

statements.title: Evaluation criterion
statements.label: ev:criterion
statements.text:
For an infinite-dimensional real or complex Banach space $X$, the following
are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ admits a bounded linear surjection onto a separable
      infinite-dimensional Banach space.
\item There is a closed infinite-dimensional subspace $F\subset X^*$
      for which $R_F(X)$ is norm separable.
\end{enumerate}
In the second assertion, $F$ may be required to be separable.

statements.label: pos:theorem
statements.text:
Suppose that $\mathfrak c$ carries a $\mathfrak c$-additive probability
measure on its full power set that vanishes on singletons, with additivity
understood for disjoint families of cardinality strictly less than
$\mathfrak c$.  Then every infinite-dimensional real Banach space has a
separable infinite-dimensional quotient.
statements.section_title: A measure on the continuum gives separable quotients

statements.label: ev:positive-transfer
statements.text:
Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space, and let $X_{\R}$
be its underlying real space.  If $X_{\R}$ has a separable
infinite-dimensional real quotient, then $X$ has a separable
infinite-dimensional complex quotient.
statements.section_title: Passing between real and complex spaces

statements.label: ev:fields
statements.text:
The universal separable quotient assertions over $\R$ and over $\C$
are equivalent.  More specifically, if a real Banach space $X$ has no
separable infinite-dimensional quotient, its complexification has no
separable infinite-dimensional complex quotient.
statements.section_title: Passing between real and complex spaces

statements.label: ch:predual
statements.text:
Let
\[
 X_0=\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{e_\alpha^*:\alpha<\omega_1\}
 \subset E^*.
\]
The canonical evaluation map $E\longrightarrow X_0^*$ is an isometric
isomorphism.
statements.section_title: A dual space with coded norming functionals

statements.title: Weak-Cauchy blocks
statements.label: path:weak-cauchy
statements.text:
Every bounded block sequence in a fixed family has a weak-Cauchy
subsequence.
statements.section_title: Infinite paths and weak-Cauchy block sequences

statements.label: pair:exact
statements.text:
Let $(z_n)$ be an infinite admissible block sequence in $E$.  Given a tail
of this sequence and an integer $J\ge1$, there are a finite block $y$ in
that tail and a Type~I functional $\phi$ of weight $J$ in the same family
such that
\[
 \|y\|\le500,\qquad \phi(y)\ge\tfrac12.
\]
The support of $\phi$ lies in the ordinal range of $y$, and also in its
color range in the mixed case.
statements.section_title: Vectors detected at a prescribed weight

statements.label: branch:separation
statements.text:
For every infinite-dimensional closed subspace $F\subset E$, there are
a single operation family, a number $\delta_F>0$, and actual path
functionals $P_b\in B_{E^*}$ of that family, indexed by
$b\in\{0,1\}^{\N}$, such that
\[
          \|P_b|_F-P_c|_F\|\geq\delta_F
          \qquad(b\ne c).
\]

statements.label: twist:counterexample
statements.text:
Under CH there is an infinite-dimensional real Banach space with no
separable infinite-dimensional quotient.

statements.label: twist:density
statements.text:
Under CH, the real counterexample $X$ constructed above satisfies
$\dens X=\dens X^*=\aleph_1$. Its complexification is a counterexample
over $\C$ of norm density $\aleph_1$.

statements.title: Solovay
statements.label: model:solovay
statements.text:
If $\kappa$ is real-valued measurable, then forcing with a measure algebra
preserves its real-valued measurability.  In particular, in the extension
there is a $\kappa$-additive probability measure on the full power set of
$\kappa$ in that extension, vanishing on singletons.

statements.label: model:positive
statements.text:
If ZFC with a measurable cardinal is consistent, then ZFC with a
real-valued measurable continuum is consistent.

title: Removable Boundaries and Rigidity of Circle Domains
abstract: We prove that a circle domain with conformally removable boundary is conformally rigid, with no restriction on the number of complementary components. This establishes the removability-to-rigidity direction of the He–Schramm Conjecture.

tex.abstract:
We prove that a circle domain with conformally removable boundary is
conformally rigid, with no restriction on the number of complementary
components. This establishes the removability-to-rigidity direction of
the He--Schramm Conjecture.
sections: Models retaining finitely many scalar tests
Almost straight coordinates and null trace pairs
Null projections of the common point traces

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Every circle domain with conformally removable boundary is conformally
rigid.  More explicitly, if $\Omega,\Omega'\subset\Chat$ are circle
domains, $\partial\Omega$ is conformally removable, and
$f\colon\Omega\to\Omega'$ is a conformal equivalence, then there is a
M\"obius transformation $M$ such that $f=M|_\Omega$.

statements.label: prop:models
statements.text:
Every finite list in Definition~\ref{def:model} satisfying
\eqref{eq:pair-null} has a model.  A model can, in fact, be chosen with
circle-domain image.
statements.section_title: Models retaining finitely many scalar tests

statements.label: prop:height
statements.text:
Suppose $d>0$ and $h\in\mathcal M$ satisfies $\Re b(h)>\beta-d$.
Set $F=\C\setminus h(G)$. There is a continuous
$v\in W^{1,2}_{\loc}(\C)$, constant on every component of $F$, such that
$\nabla v=0$ almost everywhere on $F$ and
\begin{equation}
 \int_{\C}|\nabla(v-Y)|^2\,\dd A\le 2\pi d.
\end{equation}
The function $v$ is a locally uniform limit of imaginary coordinates of
normalized plane homeomorphisms conformal outside a fixed disk.
Moreover, for each compact $K\subset\C$, the quantities
$\|v-Y\|_{C(K)}$ tend to zero as $d\downarrow0$, uniformly over these
choices of nearly maximizing models. The exterior bounds used here
depend only on $B$.
statements.section_title: Almost straight coordinates and null trace pairs

statements.title: Continuous Sobolev extension
statements.label: thm:dust-sobolev
statements.text:
If $B\subset\C$ is compact, totally disconnected, and conformally
removable, then every continuous real function $u$ on $\Chat$ whose
restriction to $G=\Chat\setminus B$ belongs to $W^{1,2}(G)$ belongs
to $W^{1,2}(\Chat)$.

statements.title: Common point traces
statements.label: prop:trace-null
statements.text:
Let $\Omega,\Omega'$ be circle domains containing infinity, and let
$f:\Omega\to\Omega'$ be a conformal equivalence with $f(\infty)=\infty$.
Suppose $\partial\Omega$ is conformally removable.  Let $C$ be the set
of point components of $\Chat\setminus\Omega$ whose corresponding
components in $\Chat\setminus\Omega'$ are also points, and denote their
positions by $f_*(x)$, $x\in C$.  For each $e\in\{1,i\}$ and almost
every line $\ell$ parallel to $e$,
\[
 \bigl|\{\pi_e(f_*(x)):x\in C\cap\ell\}\bigr|=0.
\]
Here and below $|\cdot|$ for a subset of a line denotes Lebesgue length.

title: Renewal and changes of law for critical honeycomb walks
abstract: For critical honeycomb self-avoiding walk, we prove spatial exponent 3/4 for the infinite irreducible-bridge law and for bridges of every sufficiently large compatible even length. We establish the corresponding thermal laws at every large discount scale, including all positive length and spatial moments. For unrestricted uniform walks, the endpoint lower law holds on a common set of lengths of natural density one. We also determine the near-critical exponential correlation scale and small-force free-energy exponent, and prove spatial local lower bounds that permit conditioning on a prescribed terminal vertex.

tex.abstract: For critical honeycomb self-avoiding walk, we prove spatial exponent $3/4$ for the infinite irreducible-bridge law and for bridges of every sufficiently large compatible even length. We establish the corresponding thermal laws at every large discount scale, including all positive length and spatial moments. For unrestricted uniform walks, the endpoint lower law holds on a common set of lengths of natural density one. We also determine the near-critical exponential correlation scale and small-force free-energy exponent, and prove spatial local lower bounds that permit conditioning on a prescribed terminal vertex.
