statements.title: Finite bridge estimates
statements.label: R:renew:finite-input
statements.text:
There are constants $c,C>0$ such that, for every sufficiently large integer $h$,
\[
 c h^{-1/4}\le B_h\le C h^{-1/4},\qquad M_h\le C h^{13/12},\qquad
 B_h\{L\ge c h^{4/3}\}\ge c h^{-1/4}.
\]
For all $h\ge1$ and $x\ge1$, one also has
\[
 B_h\{D>x\}\le C x^{-1/4}.
\]
The same estimates hold in the symmetry-related pure directions.
statements.section_title: One probability space for the different laws

statements.title: Renewal factorization
statements.label: R:renew:factorization
statements.text:
The masses $p(\gamma)$ sum to one. If $H,L,X,D$ denote respectively the height, visited-vertex length, signed transverse displacement and Euclidean diameter of an irreducible, then, for $s>0$ and $u\ge0$,
\[
 b(s,u):=\sum_{h\ge0}\sum_{\gamma\in\mathcal B_h}
       \rho^{L(\gamma)}e^{-sh-uL(\gamma)}
 =\frac1{1-\E_p e^{-sH-uL}}.
\]
In particular $b(s,0)\asymp s^{-3/4}$ as $s\downarrow0$. Under independent successive samples from $p$, $B_h$ is the probability that some renewal occurs at height $h$.
statements.section_title: One probability space for the different laws

statements.label: R:renew:increments
statements.text:
Put $\beta=3/4$ and $\alpha=9/16$. Under $p$,
\begin{align*}
 1-\E_p e^{-sH}&\asymp s^\beta,&
 p(H>x)+p(D>x)&\le Cx^{-\beta},\\
 \E_p[L;H\le x]&\le Cx^{7/12},&
 p(L>n)&\le Cn^{-\alpha},&
 1-\E_p e^{-uL}&\asymp u^\alpha.
\end{align*}
The constants are uniform for sufficiently small positive $s,u$ and sufficiently large $x,n$.
statements.section_title: One probability space for the different laws

statements.title: Infinite spatial law
statements.label: R:renew:infinite
statements.text:
Concatenate independent irreducibles of law $p$, and enumerate the resulting vertices as $\gamma_1,\gamma_2,\ldots$. Almost surely,
\[
 |\gamma_n-\gamma_1|=n^{3/4+o(1)},\qquad
 \#\{n:|\gamma_n-\gamma_1|\le R\}=R^{4/3+o(1)}.
\]
statements.section_title: One probability space for the different laws

statements.label: R:renew:uniform
statements.text: One has $a_{n+2}/a_n\to\rho^{-2}$. The uniform half-plane laws converge on each fixed initial path to the infinite law of Theorem~\ref{R:renew:infinite}.
statements.section_title: One probability space for the different laws

statements.title: Local renewal mass
statements.label: R:exact:local
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{R:exact:concentration}, for every sufficiently large integer $m$,
\[
 V_m:=\sum_{k\ge1}\Prob(S_k=m)\ge c_2m^{a-1}.
\]
The constants depend only on the law and the constants in the hypotheses. No regular-variation limit of its tail is required.

statements.label: R:exact:bridge
statements.text:
Choose a strict bridge uniformly from all bridges with $n$ visited vertices, rooted at a fixed bottom port, with terminal height and port free. For every $\xi>0$, along every sufficiently large even integer $n$,
\[
 \Prob_n\{n^{3/4-\xi}\le A\le D\le n^{3/4+\xi}\}\longrightarrow1.
\]
Here $A$ is the Euclidean distance between the ports and $D$ the diameter of the visited trace together with its ports. Replacing either by its vertex-endpoint convention changes it by a bounded amount.

statements.label: R:exact:height
statements.text:
Under critical weights normalized on strict bridges of exact height $h$ with free terminal port,
\[
 L=h^{4/3+o(1)},\qquad D=h^{1+o(1)}
\]
in probability as every integer $h\to\infty$. The same holds after restricting to any event whose critical mass is at least a fixed positive fraction of $B_h$.

statements.title: Finite calibrated input
statements.label: R:cal:inputs
statements.text:
Let $B_h$ be the critical mass of strict bridges of height $h$ from one
fixed port, and let $B_0=1$. Then $B_h\asymp(1+h)^{-1/4}$. For sufficiently
large fixed $T$, bridges confined to transverse width $Th$ have mass at
least $c_T h^{-1/4}$ and first-length mass at most $C_T h^{13/12}$.
The arch-plus-bridge mass in a height-$h$ strip with diameter larger than
$r\ge Ch$ is at most $C h^{-1/4}e^{-cr/h}$. Since a self-avoiding path of
diameter $r$ has at most $Cr^2$ centers, this estimate also controls every
fixed length moment in the tail. In particular the mass at
$D>h\log^2 h$, including any fixed length power, is smaller than every
inverse power of $h$.

The half-plane arch mass at prescribed horizontal gap $g$ satisfies
$A_g\asymp g^{-5/4}$; its lower bound remains valid with diameter at most
$Cg$ for a sufficiently large fixed $C$.
The normalized irreducible law satisfies
\[
 1-\mathbb E_p e^{-tH}\asymp t^{3/4}\quad(0<t\le1),\qquad
 p(D>r)\le C r^{-3/4}\quad(r\ge1).
\]
For $h$ large, put $R_0=h(\log h)^{1/64}$ and
\[
 l_-=h^{4/3}(\log h)^{-1/8},\qquad
 l_+=h^{4/3}(\log h)^{1/2}.
\]
For a fixed finite $C$,
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{j\le2R_0}B_j\{l_-\le L\le2l_+\}
       \ge h^{3/4}(\log h)^{-C}.
 
\end{equation}
The estimate sums over heights and terminal ports; it does not prescribe
either one of them.
statements.section_title: Conditioning on length from logarithmic finite estimates

statements.title: Exact compatible lengths from a logarithmic window
statements.label: R:cal:exact
statements.text:
Let $u_n=p(\exists k:S_L(k)=n)$. For every sufficiently large even $n$,
\[
 u_n\ge n^{-7/16-o(1)},\qquad \frac{u_{n+2}}{u_n}\longrightarrow1.
\]
Conditioning the independent sequence on hitting $n$ gives the uniform
strict bridge of length $n$, with height and terminal port free. Under this
law the height, endpoint distance, and maximum radius are
$n^{3/4+o(1)}$ in probability. The finite bridge laws converge locally to
the independent-irreducible law.
statements.section_title: Conditioning on length from logarithmic finite estimates

statements.label: R:geo:marked-pair
statements.text:
For every nonnegative function $f$ of an irreducible, with $p(f)<\infty$,
and every $\epsilon>0$,
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{R\le h\le2R}D_h\left[\sum_{i\text{ in the first path}}f(I_i)\right]
       \le C_\epsilon R^{-5/4+\epsilon}p(f).
\end{equation}
Either path can carry the mark.  If the two bottom ports instead have
any prescribed separation, while the top ports remain adjacent, the
right side becomes $C_\epsilon R^{-1/2+\epsilon}p(f)$.  In that second
estimate, requiring the marked path to contain at most
$R^{3/4-\delta}$ increments improves the bound by
$R^{-\delta+\epsilon}$, with the exponent slacks combined in the
constant.
statements.section_title: Geometric estimates before a change of law

statements.label: R:geo:deficit
statements.text: The length deficit satisfies $q(t)=t^{-9/16+o(1)}$.
statements.section_title: Geometric estimates before a change of law

statements.label: R:geo:fixed-height
statements.text:
Under the critical law on strict bridges of height $h$, with terminal
port unrestricted, $L=h^{4/3+o(1)}$ and $D=h^{1+o(1)}$ in probability.
The same holds after any restriction retaining a fixed positive
fraction of $B_h$.
statements.section_title: Geometric estimates before a change of law

statements.label: R:geo:arch-law
statements.text:
For the critical upper-half-plane law between two prescribed boundary
ports at separation $r$, one has $L=r^{4/3+o(1)}$ and
$D=r^{1+o(1)}$ in probability.  Any restriction retaining a fixed
positive fraction of the arch mass has the same exponents.
statements.section_title: Geometric estimates before a change of law

statements.title: Independent coordinates at a turn
statements.label: R:geo:chain
statements.section_title: Geometric estimates before a change of law

statements.title: Two ends with a reserved height variable
statements.label: R:geo:two-ends
statements.text:
Suppose two bridges start at adjacent prescribed ports and stay disjoint
through a fixed positive fraction of the smaller height.  Their heights
and counts lie in the independent bins above, all bounded by $CN^2$.
For every $\epsilon>0$ their critical mass is at most
\begin{equation}
 C_\epsilon N^\epsilon F,\qquad
 F=\frac{\kappa_1^2\kappa_2^2}
              {K_1K_2\min(\kappa_1,\kappa_2)}.
\end{equation}
An interval of $C(1+r)$ allowed heights on node $i$, measurable outside
its reserved group, adds $\min(1,(1+r)\kappa_i^{-4/3})$.
In particular this applies to the difference of the final endpoint
heights after any two terminal pieces have been fixed up to translation.
For one nonempty bridge the factor is $\kappa_i^2/K_i$, with the same
optional concentration test.
statements.section_title: Geometric estimates before a change of law

statements.label: R:geo:absolute-count
statements.text:
Let $a_n$ be the total critical mass of plane walks with $n$ visited
vertices, rooted at one specified vertex, or counted up to translations
with both possible initial vertex types.  For every $\delta>0$,
\[
                         a_n\le C_\delta e^{n^\delta}.
\]
The same bound holds for the mass with length at most $n$.  In the
extremum decomposition below, a bounded number of specified pieces may
be omitted and counted separately; all other pieces still cost at most
$C_\delta e^{n^\delta}$, including their count, position, and local
records.
statements.section_title: Geometric estimates before a change of law

statements.title: Absolute fast-path estimate
statements.label: R:geo:fast
statements.section_title: Geometric estimates before a change of law

statements.title: Unrestricted thermal law
statements.label: thm:thermal
statements.text:
Choose an ordinary plane honeycomb walk from a fixed vertex with probability proportional to $(\rho e^{-1/N})^n$, where $n$ is its edge length. For every $\xi>0$, its vertex length $L$, endpoint distance $A$ and diameter $D$ satisfy
\[
 \Pp_N\{N^{1-\xi}\le L\le N^{1+\xi},\quad
 N^{3/4-\xi}\le A\le D\le N^{3/4+\xi}\}\longrightarrow1.
\]
For every fixed $p>0$,
\[
 \E_N L^p=N^{p+o(1)},\qquad
 \E_N A^p=N^{3p/4+o(1)},\qquad
 \E_N D^p=N^{3p/4+o(1)}.
\]
statements.section_title: From renewal pieces to the unrestricted thermal law

statements.title: Absolute suppression of rapid travel
statements.label: R:cal:fast
statements.section_title: Censored arms and absolute spatial estimates

statements.title: Critical mass in a bounded region
statements.label: R:cal:volume
statements.section_title: Censored arms and absolute spatial estimates

statements.title: Moment and half-plane consequences
statements.label: R:cal:halfplane-laws
statements.text:
For the independent-irreducible infinite walk, and for uniform strict
bridges at every sufficiently large even center length $n$, both endpoint
distance and maximum radius have positive-moment powers $3p/4$: for either
variable $R_n$,
\[
 \mathbb E R_n^p=n^{3p/4+o(1)}\qquad(p>0\text{ fixed}).
\]
The same holds for the vertex-bridge conventions of
Section~\ref{R:cal:section}.

For endpoint-free uniform walks in the plane or half-plane, the probability
of maximum radius exceeding $n^{3/4+\epsilon}$ is smaller than every fixed
inverse power of $n$, for each fixed $\epsilon>0$. In the half-plane there
is one natural-density-one set of lengths along which endpoint distance and
maximum radius have exponent $3/4$ in probability and all the preceding
positive-moment exponents.

Under the half-plane law of free center length $n\ge1$ with weights
$\rho^n e^{-tn}$, length is $t^{-1+o(1)}$ and endpoint distance and maximum
radius are $t^{-3/4+o(1)}$ in probability as $t\downarrow0$; their positive
moments have the corresponding powers. At fixed bridge height $h$, the
critical bridge length is $h^{4/3+o(1)}$ both in probability and in first
mean.

statements.title: Unrestricted spatial laws by refolding
statements.label: R:cal:plane-laws
statements.text:
For full-plane uniform walks rooted at a fixed center, there is a set
$\mathcal N\subset\mathbb N$ of natural density one such that, as
$n\to\infty$ through $\mathcal N$, endpoint distance and maximum radius
are $n^{3/4+o(1)}$ in probability. For every fixed $p>0$ their $p$th
moments are $n^{3p/4+o(1)}$ on the same set.
Under the normalized full-plane law with edge weights $(\rho e^{-t})^n$,
as $t\downarrow0$ the length is $t^{-1+o(1)}$ and both spatial variables
are $t^{-3/4+o(1)}$ in probability, with corresponding positive-moment
powers. The thermal assertion holds without exceptions in $t$.

statements.title: Power-cardinality of favorable lengths
statements.label: R:cal:good-cardinality
statements.text:
Fix $0<\epsilon<1$. For unrestricted uniform honeycomb walks rooted at a
fixed center, the number of integers $m\in[R^{1-\epsilon},R]$ for which
\[
 \Pr_m\{m^{3/4-\epsilon}\le |\omega_m-\omega_0|
       \le\operatorname{diam}(\omega)\le m^{3/4+\epsilon}\}
       \ge1-\epsilon
\]
is $R^{1+o(1)}$ as $R\to\infty$. In particular, the limsup of each positive
moment exponent of endpoint distance or diameter is $3/4$ times its moment
order. If the corresponding spatial exponent in probability exists at all
exact lengths, it equals $3/4$.

statements.title: Exponential thresholds and force
statements.label: R:resp:force
statements.text:
Uniformly over unit vectors $e$, as $t\downarrow0$,
\[
 m_e(t)=t^{3/4+o(1)},\qquad m_{\mathrm{rad}}(t)=t^{3/4+o(1)}.
\]
More precisely, for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently small $t$,
\[
 t^{3/4+\varepsilon}\le m_{\mathrm{rad}}(t)\le m_e(t)\le C t^{3/4},
\]
where $C$ is independent of $e$. For each unit vector $e$ and $s\ge0$, the limit
\[
 f_e(s)=\lim_{j\to\infty}\frac1j\log
 \sum_{\ell(\gamma)=j}\rho^j e^{s e\cdot(\gamma_j-o)}
\]
exists. It satisfies $f_e(0)=0$ and
\[
 f_e(s)=s^{4/3+o(1)}\qquad(s\downarrow0),
\]
uniformly in $e$.
statements.section_title: Correlation lengths, pulling, and prescribed spatial endpoints

statements.title: One-sided force response
statements.label: R:resp:force-derivatives
statements.text:
For $s>0$ the convex function $f_e$ has one-sided derivatives, and
\[
 f'_{e,-}(s)=s^{1/3+o(1)},\qquad f'_{e,+}(s)=s^{1/3+o(1)}
 \qquad(s\downarrow0).
\]
At a point where $f_e$ is differentiable, the mean displacement in direction $e$, divided by length, under the force-weighted $j$-edge law tends to $f'_e(s)$ as $j\to\infty$.
statements.section_title: Correlation lengths, pulling, and prescribed spatial endpoints

statements.title: Prescribed displacement with controlled length and diameter
statements.label: R:resp:point-local
statements.section_title: Correlation lengths, pulling, and prescribed spatial endpoints

statements.title: Prescribed spatial offsets
statements.label: R:resp:prescribed
statements.text:
At each fixed $N>0$ put $t=1/N$. Define
\[
 \underline m(N)=\liminf_{|b-o|\to\infty}
        \frac{-\log G_{1/N}(b)}{|b-o|},\qquad
 \overline m(N)=\limsup_{|b-o|\to\infty}
        \frac{-\log G_{1/N}(b)}{|b-o|},
\]
where both limits range over all lattice vertices and directions. Then
\[
 \underline m(N)=N^{-3/4+o(1)},\qquad
 \overline m(N)=N^{-3/4+o(1)}\qquad(N\to\infty).
\]
If a sequence of terminal vertices satisfies $|b_N-o|=N^{3/4+o(1)}$, the probability law
\[
 \mathbb P_{N,b_N}(\gamma)=
       \frac{(\rho e^{-1/N})^{\ell(\gamma)}}{G_{1/N}(b_N)},
       \qquad \gamma:o\to b_N,
\]
satisfies $\ell=N^{1+o(1)}$ and $D=N^{3/4+o(1)}$ in probability. For each fixed $r>0$ it also satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E_{N,b_N}\ell^r=N^{r+o(1)},\qquad
 \mathbb E_{N,b_N}D^r=N^{3r/4+o(1)}.
\]
statements.section_title: Correlation lengths, pulling, and prescribed spatial endpoints

statements.title: Length responses at a prescribed endpoint
statements.label: R:resp:thermal-derivatives
statements.text:
For each fixed vertex $b$ and $t>0$, $G_t(b)$ can be differentiated term by term any fixed number of times. If $|b_N-o|=N^{3/4+o(1)}$, then for each positive integer $j$,
\[
 \left.\frac{(-1)^j\partial_t^jG_t(b_N)}{G_t(b_N)}\right|_{t=1/N}
       =N^{j+o(1)},\qquad
 -\left.\partial_t\log G_t(b_N)\right|_{t=1/N}=N^{1+o(1)}.
\]
The terminal vertex is held fixed while taking each derivative.
statements.section_title: Correlation lengths, pulling, and prescribed spatial endpoints

statements.title: Truncated and discounted irreducible rewards
statements.label: R:alt:pv:reward
statements.text:
For this irreducible law,
\begin{align}
 p(H>r)&=r^{-\beta+o(1)},&
 \mathbb E_p[L;H\le r]&=r^{d-\beta+o(1)},
 \\
 \mathbb E_p[Le^{-H/r}]&=r^{d-\beta+o(1)}.
 
\end{align}
The lower bound in \eqref{R:alt:pv:discounted} is retained after imposing
$H\le r\log^2r$ and $S\le r\log^4r$.  Furthermore,
\begin{equation}
 p(L>n)\le n^{-9/16+o(1)},\qquad
 p(D>r)\le r^{-3/4+o(1)},\qquad
 1-\mathbb E_p e^{-L/n}\ge n^{-17/24-o(1)}.
\end{equation}

statements.title: Consequences under the weaker finite inputs
statements.label: R:alt:pv:laws
statements.text:
Let $\gamma_0$ be the source port, $\gamma_n$ the $n$th visited vertex
of the infinite concatenation, and $Y_n$ its forward height from the source.
Almost surely,
\[
 Y_n\ge n^{3/4-o(1)},\qquad
 |\gamma_n-\gamma_0|\le n^{17/18+o(1)}.
\]
For the normalized finite bridge law summed over heights with weight
$\rho^Le^{-L/n}$, its height is at least $n^{3/4-\varepsilon}$ with
probability tending to one, for every $\varepsilon>0$.
The unnormalized mass of half-plane arches of length greater than $n$
is at most $n^{-3/16+o(1)}$.
The completed-vertex rewards just defined satisfy, for some fixed $C>0$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E V_h=h^{4/3+o(1)},\qquad
 \mathbb E V_h^{(C h\log^2h)}=h^{4/3+o(1)}.
\end{equation}
Consequently the expected number of vertices before first exit from a disk
of radius $R$ is at least $R^{4/3-o(1)}$.

statements.title: A fixed-ball completed-prefix expectation
statements.label: R:alt:pd:prefix
statements.text:
Under the irreducible law from \eqref{R:alt:pd:input}, let
$\mathcal V_R$ be the vertices through the last block ending at cumulative
layer height at most $R$, excluding the overshooting block, and let
$\mathcal V_\infty$ be the full infinite trace.  With the starting port as
origin,
\[
 \mathbb E|\mathcal V_R|=R^{4/3+o(1)},\qquad
 \mathbb E|\mathcal V_R\cap B(0,R)|=R^{4/3+o(1)},
\]
and almost surely
\[
 |\mathcal V_\infty\cap B(0,R)|\le R^{4/3+o(1)}.
\]
Changing the ball radius by any fixed positive factor preserves the
expectation exponent.

statements.title: Length tail from boundary folding
statements.label: R:alt:j:theorem
statements.text:
Under the irreducible critical bridge law $p$, the finite estimates above
imply
\[
 p(L\ge n)=n^{-9/16+o(1)}.
\]
They also give $p(H>r)=r^{-3/4+o(1)}$ and
$p(D>r)\le r^{-3/4+o(1)}$.  Consequently the iid infinite bridge satisfies
$|\gamma_n-\gamma_0|=n^{3/4+o(1)}$ and has
$R^{4/3+o(1)}$ vertices in a radius-$R$ disk, almost surely.
At every integer strip height $h$, the critical fixed-source,
free-terminal bridge law has length $h^{4/3+o(1)}$ in probability and
mean length $h^{4/3+o(1)}$.  Under the bridge law summed over heights with
weight $\rho^Le^{-L/t}$, length is $t^{1+o(1)}$ and diameter is
$t^{3/4+o(1)}$ in probability.

statements.title: Stopped renewal paths
statements.label: R:alt:g:infinite
statements.text:
For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $c_\varepsilon>0$ such that
\[
 \mathbb P\{h^{4/3-\varepsilon}\le L(\Gamma_h)
            \le h^{4/3+\varepsilon},\quad
             \operatorname{diam}(\Gamma_h)\le Ch^{1+\varepsilon}\}
       \ge1-O_\varepsilon(h^{-c_\varepsilon}).
\]
Consequently, if $\omega_n$ is the $n$-th vertex of the infinite
concatenation and its initial port is $o$, then almost surely
\[
 |\omega_n-o|=n^{3/4+o(1)},\qquad
 \#\{n:|\omega_n-o|\le R\}=R^{4/3+o(1)}.
\]

title: Replacing Gaussian observations in memory-constrained inference
abstract: Replacing the Gaussian rows used to select a finite message by independent rows increases the remaining conditional information by at most \(Cd\), for a uniform spherical signal, message entropy at most d2, and the specified row dimensions proportional to d. As an application, we prove that learners with \(M=o(d^2)\) persistent bits need \(T=\Omega(d\log(1/\epsilon))\) exact observations to attain uniform-sphere angular success at least 3/5, for \(0\lt \epsilon\le1/10\) and a deterministic finite horizon.

tex.abstract:
Replacing the Gaussian rows used to select a finite message by
independent rows increases the remaining conditional information
by at most \(Cd\), for a uniform spherical signal, message entropy
at most \(d^2\), and the specified row dimensions proportional to \(d\).
As an application, we prove that learners with \(M=o(d^2)\) persistent
bits need \(T=\Omega(d\log(1/\epsilon))\) exact observations to attain
uniform-sphere angular success at least \(3/5\), for
\(0<\epsilon\le1/10\) and a deterministic finite horizon.

statements.title: The information identity and its density bound
statements.label: prop:r-information-comparison
statements.text:
In the two experiments just defined, all quantities below are finite,
and
\begin{align}
 J_0(W)-J_1(W)
 &=h_0(Y\mid G,W)-h_1(Y\mid G,W)-I_1(S;G\mid W)
 \\
 &\le h_0(Y\mid G,W)+\E_1\log p_{\nu_W}(G,Y).
 
\end{align}
If \(E=E(S,W)\) is countable and \(H(E\mid W)<\infty\), and the
same deterministic refinement \(W'=(W,E)\) is used in both laws,
then
\begin{equation}
 J_0(W)-J_1(W)
 \le J_0(W')-J_1(W')+H(E\mid W).
\end{equation}

statements.title: Mixed projection moment and exact density version
statements.label: thm:r-mixed-moment
statements.text:
Let \(n=d-1\), let \(m,r,q\ge1\) be integers, and put
\(\ell=m+r\).  Suppose
\begin{equation}
 \ell<n,\qquad \ell-m-(q-1)\ge1.
\end{equation}
Let \(\rho\) be a finite nonnegative Borel measure on \(S^{d-1}\).
Suppose that \(B,D>0\) and, for every \(z\in\R^d\) and \(t>0\),
\begin{equation}
 \rho(B(z,t))\le Bt^\ell,\qquad
 \rho(B(z,t))\le Dt^n.
\end{equation}
Let \(X\sim\gamma_m\) and \(Z\sim\gamma_r\) be independent, and set
\(G=(X;Z)\).  For \(\delta>0\), define the cube average
\[
 p_{\rho,\delta}(g,y)
   =(2\delta)^{-\ell}\int
       \ind_{\{\norm{gu-y}_\infty\le\delta\}}\,d\rho(u).
\]
There is an absolute \(C\) such that, for every fixed
\(s\in S^{d-1}\) and every \(\delta>0\),
\begin{equation}
 \left[\E_X
       \left(\E_Z p_{\rho,\delta}((X;Z),(X;Z)s)\right)^q
 \right]^{1/q}
 \le e^{Cd}B\bigl(1+\log^+(D/B)\bigr).
\end{equation}

If in addition \(\rho\ll\sigma\), use the jointly Borel density
\(p_\rho\) in \eqref{eq:r-density-version}.  There is a measurable
set \(E_\rho\subset S^{d-1}\), with \(\rho(E_\rho)=0\), such that
for every \(s\notin E_\rho\) the cube averages converge to
\(p_\rho(G,Gs)\) for \(\gamma_\ell\)-almost every \(G\), and
\begin{equation}
 \left[\E_X
       \left(\E_Zp_\rho((X;Z),(X;Z)s)\right)^q
 \right]^{1/q}
 \le e^{Cd}B\bigl(1+\log^+(D/B)\bigr).
\end{equation}
When \(\rho\ne0\), \(E_\rho\) may also be chosen so that
\(0<p_\rho(G,Gs)<\infty\) for \(\gamma_\ell\)-almost every \(G\)
and every \(s\notin E_\rho\).

statements.title: Actual-row tilt and exact-label limit
statements.label: prop:r-actual-row-limit
statements.text:
Keep the dimensions of Theorem~\ref{thm:r-mixed-moment}.  Let
\(\nu\le H\sigma\), \(H<\infty\), be a probability measure.
Let \(S\sim\nu\) and \(X\sim\gamma_m\) be independent, let \(W\)
be countable with \(H(W)<\infty\) and any joint law with
\((S,X)\), and let \(Z\sim\gamma_r\) be independent of
\((S,X,W)\).  Put \(G=(X;Z)\) and \(Y=GS\).
For every positive-probability \(w\), let \(\rho_w\ll\sigma\)
be a finite nonnegative measure satisfying
\eqref{eq:r-mixed-growth} with constants \(B_w,D_w>0\), and set
\[
 C_w=e^{Cd}B_w\bigl(1+\log^+(D_w/B_w)\bigr),
\]
where \(C\) is the constant in the theorem.  Assume
\(\E\log(1+C_W)<\infty\).

The actual conditional law of \(Y\) given \((G,W)\) has a
Lebesgue density.  With the versions
\eqref{eq:r-density-version},
\[
 p_{\rho_W,1/j}(G,Y)\longrightarrow p_{\rho_W}(G,Y)
 \quad\text{almost surely under the actual law}.
\]
For every \(\delta>0\), and also for the exact density,
\begin{align}
 \E\log\bigl(1+p_{\rho_W,\delta}(G,Y)\bigr)
 &\le \frac{I(X;W\mid S)}q+\E\log(1+C_W),
 \\
 \E\log\bigl(1+p_{\rho_W}(G,Y)\bigr)
 &\le \frac{I(X;W\mid S)}q+\E\log(1+C_W)
 \le \frac{H(W)}q+\E\log(1+C_W).
 
\end{align}
In particular \(\log^+p_{\rho_W}(G,Y)\) is integrable, and the
extended expectation of \(\log p_{\rho_W}(G,Y)\), with
\(\log0=-\infty\), is defined and bounded above by the same
right-hand side.  For a deterministic countable refinement
\(W'=(W,E(S,W))\) of finite entropy, the row charge is unchanged:
\[
 I(X;W'\mid S)=I(X;W\mid S).
\]

statements.title: Critical-radius comparison
statements.label: thm:r-critical-comparison
statements.text:
In the two experiments of Subsection~\ref{subsec:r-two-experiments},
use the dimensions \eqref{eq:r-critical-parameters}.  Thus
\(S\sim\sigma\), \(A\sim\gamma_m\) is independent of \(S\), and
\(W\) is countable with an arbitrary joint dependence on \((S,A)\).
The aligned law retains \((S,A,W)\) and appends independent
\(r\)-row \(C\), whereas the independent law retains \((S,W)\)
and draws an independent \(\ell\)-row matrix \(G\).
If \(H(W)\le d^2\), then, for an absolute constant \(K\),
\begin{equation}
 I_0(S;W\mid G,GS)\le I_1(S;W\mid G,GS)+Kd.
\end{equation}

\begin{equation}
 \mathcal D(U)\le\widetilde{\mathcal D}(U)
 +C\left(d+\log(1+d+H(U))+\frac{H(U)}d\right).
\end{equation}
The proposition applies to every finite \(U\) with the specified
joint law.

statements.label: rhyb:block

For the block above, with \(1\le m\le h_0\) and \(H(V)\le B\),
\begin{equation}
 \overline J(V)-\overline J(U)
 \le Cm+\frac{m}{N_k}\left(C+\frac{B}{h_0}\right)+\frac{B}{q}.

statements.title: Information through a Gaussian block
statements.label: rfib:block
statements.text:
Let \(S\sim\sigma\), let \(V\) be finite-valued, and let \(A\) have
\(n\) independent standard Gaussian rows, independently of \((S,V)\).
Suppose \(W\) takes at most \(N\) values, where \(N\ge1\) is an integer, and is obtained from
\((V,A,AS)\) by a Borel transition kernel.  If \(\log N\le d^2\), then
for the dimensions in \eqref{rfib:parameters} and all sufficiently
large \(d\),
\begin{equation}
 \Phi(W)\le\Phi(V)+Kd .
\end{equation}
The auxiliary matrix in each occurrence of \(\Phi\) is independent of
the pair consisting of the signal and the state in that occurrence.

statements.title: Streaming consequence of the critical radius
statements.label: thm:r-critical-streaming
statements.text:
Let \(M(d)\) be a nonnegative integer sequence with \(M(d)=o(d^2)\),
and let \(0<\epsilon(d)\le1/10\).  For each \(d\), consider a learner
in Definition~\ref{def:r-streaming-model} with deterministic finite
horizon \(T(d)\).  If its uniform-sphere angular success probability,
including all learner randomness, is at least \(3/5\), then
\[
 T(d)\ge c\,d\log\frac1{\epsilon(d)}
\]
for an absolute \(c>0\) and all sufficiently large \(d\).  The
eventual dimension threshold may depend on the memory sequence.

title: Riesz transforms and uniform rectifiability in higher codimension
abstract: We prove that an n-Ahlfors–David regular Radon measure on ℝd is uniformly n-rectifiable if its n-dimensional Riesz transform is uniformly bounded from scalar \(L^2(\mu)\) to vector-valued \(L^2(\mu)\) over all positive hard truncations, for integers d ≥ 4 and \(2\le n\le d-2\). This gives a positive answer to the David–Semmes Riesz-transform question in its remaining higher-codimension range. The conclusion gives uniform big pieces of Lipschitz images of Euclidean balls.

tex.abstract:
We prove that an $n$-Ahlfors--David regular Radon measure on $\R^d$
is uniformly $n$-rectifiable if its $n$-dimensional Riesz transform is
uniformly bounded from scalar $L^2(\mu)$ to vector-valued $L^2(\mu)$
over all positive hard truncations, for integers $d\ge4$ and
$2\le n\le d-2$.
This gives a positive answer to the David--Semmes Riesz-transform question
in its remaining higher-codimension range. The conclusion gives uniform
big pieces of Lipschitz images of Euclidean balls.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $d\ge4$ and $2\le n\le d-2$ be integers. Let $\mu$ be an
$n$-Ahlfors--David regular Radon measure on $\R^d$ satisfying
\eqref{eq:riesz-bound}. Then $\mu$ is uniformly $n$-rectifiable in the
sense of Definition~\ref{def:ur}. Its constants $\theta$ and $M$ can
be chosen in terms of $d,n,C_{\rm AD}$ and $C_{\rm R}$ alone.
statements.section_title: The quantitative theorem and normalized pairings

statements.title: Regular dyadic cells
statements.label: prop:dyadic-lattice
statements.text:
If $D_E>0$, there are a common $\mu$-null set $N\subset E$ and
families $\mathcal D_k$ of Borel cells in $E\setminus N$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item each $\mathcal D_k$ partitions $E\setminus N$, and cells of
different generations are disjoint or nested;
\item writing $\ell(Q)=2^{-k}$ for $Q\in\mathcal D_k$, there are
centers $z_Q\in Q$ and constants $0<c_0\le1/2$, $C_0\ge2$ for which
\[
 (E\setminus N)\cap B(z_Q,c_0\ell(Q))\subset Q
 \subset E\cap B(z_Q,C_0\ell(Q)),\qquad
 c_1\ell(Q)^n\le\mu(Q)\le C_1\ell(Q)^n;
\]
\item every non-top cell has one parent, and every cell has finitely
many children. When
$D_E=\infty$, all integer generations are available. When
$D_E<\infty$, there is a largest scale $\ell_0$ with
$D_E\le\ell_0<2D_E$, and finitely many cells at that scale.
\end{enumerate}
All constants depend only on $d,n,C_{\rm AD}$.
statements.section_title: The quantitative theorem and normalized pairings

statements.title: Oscillation packing
statements.label: prop:oscillation-packing
statements.text:
For every $J>1$ and $v>0$, the family
\[
 \mathcal O(J,v)=\{Q\in\mathcal D:W_J(Q)>v\ell(Q)^n\}
\]
is Carleson. Its constant depends only on the fixed data, $J$, and $v$.

statements.title: Flat seeds outside a Carleson family
statements.label: prop:flat-seeds
statements.text:
For every $A_{\rm F}\ge1$ and $\eta>0$ there are an integer $N_{\rm F}\ge1$
and a Carleson family $\mathcal F$ such that every
$Q\in\mathcal D\setminus\mathcal F$ has a proper descendant $P\subset Q$
with
\begin{equation}
 1\le\operatorname{depth}_Q(P)\le N_{\rm F},
 \qquad b_\mu(z_P,A_{\rm F}\ell(P))<\eta.
\end{equation}
One may also require
$B(z_P,A_{\rm F}\ell(P))\subset B(z_Q,c_0\ell(Q)/4)$.
The constants are uniform in $Q$ and the top cube used in the Carleson
estimate; they depend only on the fixed data, $A_{\rm F}$ and $\eta$.

statements.title: The flat limit
statements.label: prop:flat-limit
statements.text:
Fix $1\le n<d$, $c>0$, $0<G<\infty$, $0\le D_0<\infty$, and
$0<\gamma<1/2$.  Let $\mu_j$ be Radon measures on $\R^d$ with
$0\in E_j=\supp\mu_j$, global upper $n$-growth $G$, and
\[
 \mu_j(B(x,r))\ge cr^n
 \quad(x\in E_j,\ 0<r\le\diam E_j).
\]
Assume every hard-truncated Riesz transform on $L^2(\mu_j)$ has norm at
most $D_0$.  Let $\delta_j>0$, integers $K_j\ge0$, and $A_j,v_j>0$
satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
 \delta_j\longrightarrow0,\quad K_j\longrightarrow\infty,\quad
 \delta_j2^{\gamma K_j}\longrightarrow0,\\
 2^{K_j}\le\diam E_j,\quad A_j\longrightarrow\infty,\quad v_j\longrightarrow0.
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
Suppose
\begin{equation}
 e_{\mu_j}(0,2^k)\le\delta_j2^{\gamma k}
 \qquad(0\le k\le K_j)
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 |\mathcal R_{\mu_j}(\varphi)|\le v_j
 \quad\text{if }\ \Lip\varphi\le1,\quad
 \supp\varphi\Subset B(0,A_j),\quad\int\varphi\,d\mu_j=0.
\end{equation}
There is a subsequence, relabeled by $j$, with the following properties.
All the input sequences are restricted along this same subsequence when
we relabel them.
For each index there are an affine plane
$S_j=a_j+L_j(\R^n)$, tangent and normal linear isometries
\[
 L_j:\R^n\longrightarrow\R^d,
 \qquad N_j:\R^{d-n}\longrightarrow\R^d,
 \qquad L_jL_j^*+N_jN_j^*=I,
\]
such that $a_j$ is the point of $S_j$ nearest $0$,
$a_j\to0$, and $L_j\to L_\infty$ in operator norm, where $L_\infty$ is
an isometry.  Along this same subsequence,
\begin{equation}
 \mu_j\rightharpoonup q(L_\infty)_\#\mathcal L^n,
 \qquad \frac{c}{4^n\omega_n}\le q\le\frac{2^nG}{\omega_n},
 \qquad \omega_n=\mathcal L^n(B(0,1)).
\end{equation}
Here convergence is against continuous compactly supported tests, and
$\mathcal L^n$ in \eqref{eq:flat-limit-measure} denotes Lebesgue measure.
The planes obey \eqref{eq:fixed-plane-moments} with a single constant
$M=M(n,d,c,G,\gamma)$.  In particular, writing $e_i$ for the standard
basis of $\R^{d-n}$ and
\begin{equation}
 u_{j,i}(x)=\langle N_je_i,x-a_j\rangle,
\end{equation}
we have
\begin{equation}
 \int_{B(0,2^k)}|u_{j,i}|^2\,d\mu_j
 \le M\delta_j^2 2^{k(n+2+2\gamma)}
 \qquad(0\le k\le K_j, 1\le i\le d-n).
\end{equation}
Moreover, on every bounded ball, the supports converge bilaterally to
$L_\infty(\R^n)$: each source support point approaches that plane uniformly,
and each point of the plane approaches $E_j$ uniformly.
statements.section_title: Reflectionless limits and compatible normal coordinates

statements.title: The limiting height equation
statements.label: prop:height-equation
statements.text:
Assume the hypotheses and conclusions of
Lemmas~\ref{lem:height-energy} and~\ref{lem:moving-compactness} for a scalar
height. We retain their notation and record the conditions used below.
Let $\mu_j$ converge on compact tests to
$\nu=q\H^n|_L$, where $q>0$ and $L$ is an $n$-plane through $0$.
Here $\H^n|_L$ has Euclidean normalization, equal to Lebesgue measure
in orthonormal coordinates on $L$.
Let $u_j$ satisfy \eqref{eq:affine-source-height} with $|e_j|\le1$, let
$w_j=u_j/\delta_j$, and let $v$ be the common limit given by
Lemma~\ref{lem:moving-compactness}.  Suppose $\delta_j>0$, $\delta_j\to0$,
$K_j\to\infty$,
and, for some fixed $0<\gamma<1$ and $M<\infty$,
\begin{equation}
 \int_{B(0,2^k)}|u_j|^2\,d\mu_j
       \le M\delta_j^2\,2^{k(n+2+2\gamma)}
       \quad(0\le k\le K_j),\qquad
 \delta_j^{-1}2^{-K_j}\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
Assume that there are radii $A_j\to\infty$ such that, for every $j$ and
every compact Lipschitz test $\xi$ supported in $B(0,A_j)$ with
$\int\xi\,d\mu_j=0$,
\begin{equation}
 |\mathcal R_{\mu_j}(\xi)|
      \le C(\Lip\xi+1)\delta_j^3.
\end{equation}
The constant here is independent of $j$ and of the test.

Then $v$ has finite local fractional energy and satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \int_L |v(x)|(1+|x|)^{-n-2}\,d\H^n(x)<\infty.
\end{equation}
After identifying $L$ isometrically with $\R^n$, for every compactly
supported smooth complex function $g$ with $\int_{\R^n}g=0$,
\begin{equation}
 \int_{\R^n}v(x)\mathcal Lg(x)\,dx=0,
 \qquad
 \mathcal Lg(x)=\frac12\int_{\R^n}
       \frac{2g(x)-g(x+h)-g(x-h)}{|h|^{n+1}}\,dh.
\end{equation}
The integral on the left is absolutely convergent.  The same conclusions
hold simultaneously for the finite family of normal heights in
Lemma~\ref{lem:moving-compactness}, without further extraction.

statements.label: prop:normalized-excess-limit

statements.title: Uniform excess propagation
statements.label: thm:excess-propagation
statements.text:
Fix $1\le n<d$, $c,G>0$, $D_0\ge0$, $0<\gamma<1/2$, and
$\varepsilon>0$. For every integer $J_0\ge0$, there is an integer
$J\ge J_0$, depending only on these fixed data, with the following
property. Set
\begin{equation}
 \delta=2^{-J},\qquad K=2J+3,\qquad A=8\,2^K.
\end{equation}
Let $\mu$ satisfy \eqref{eq:prop-upper}--\eqref{eq:prop-riesz},
let $a\in\supp\mu$, and let $r>0$. Assume
\begin{align}
 2^Kr&\le\diam(\supp\mu),\\
 e_\mu(a,2^\ell r)&\le\delta2^{\gamma\ell}
       &&(0\le\ell\le K),
\end{align}
and assume
\begin{equation}
 |\mathcal R_\mu(\varphi)|\le\delta^3r^n
\end{equation}
for every compactly supported scalar function $\varphi$ satisfying
\[
 \Lip(\varphi)\le r^{-1},\qquad
 \supp\varphi\subset B(a,Ar),\qquad
 \int\varphi\,d\mu=0.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 e_\mu(a,r/2)\le\delta,\qquad
 b_\mu(a,r/2)<\varepsilon.
\end{equation}
Equivalently, the oscillation hypothesis can be stated with
$\Lip(\varphi)\le1$ and threshold $\delta^3r^{n+1}$.
The constants $J,\delta,K,A$ are chosen before the measure, center,
and radius. The test radius $Ar$ need not be admissible.

statements.title: Bilateral flatness has Carleson failures
statements.label: prop:beta-packing
statements.text:
For each $H\geq4(C_0+1)$ and $\varepsilon>0$, there is a constant
$C_{H,\varepsilon}<\infty$, depending only on
$d,n,C_{\rm AD},C_{\rm R},H,\varepsilon$, such that
\[
 \sum_{\substack{Q\subset R\\\beta_H(Q)\geq\varepsilon}}\mu(Q)
 \leq C_{H,\varepsilon}\mu(R)
 \qquad(R\in\mathcal D).
\]
statements.section_title: Packing failures and the Lipschitz-image conclusion

statements.title: David--Semmes bilateral criterion
statements.label: thm:bwgl
statements.text:
Let $E\subset\R^d$ be closed, of positive diameter, and $n$-AD regular
with respect to $\H^n$.  Suppose that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is
$C_\varepsilon<\infty$ such that
\[
 \int_{E\cap B(a,R)}\int_0^R
   \mathbf1_{\{b_E(x,t)>\varepsilon\}}\,\frac{dt}{t}\,d\H^n(x)
 \leq C_\varepsilon R^n
 \quad(a\in E,\ 0<R<\diam E).
\]
Then $E$ has big pieces of uniformly Lipschitz images: there are
$\theta_0>0$ and $L<\infty$ such that for every $a\in E$ and
$0<r<\diam E$ there is an $L$-Lipschitz map
$f:B^n(0,r)\to\R^d$ for which
\[
 \H^n\bigl(E\cap B(a,r)\cap f(B^n(0,r))\bigr)\geq\theta_0r^n.
\]
The constants depend only on the dimensions, AD constants, and the
constants in the bilateral weak geometric lemma.
statements.section_title: Packing failures and the Lipschitz-image conclusion

statements.title: Consequences of Mas--Tolsa
statements.label: cor:variation
statements.text:
Let $d\ge4$ and $2\le n\le d-2$ be integers, and let $\mu$ be an
$n$-Ahlfors--David regular Radon measure satisfying
\eqref{eq:riesz-bound}. Fix $\rho>2$ and a real odd $C^2$ convolution
kernel $K$ satisfying \eqref{eq:variation-kernel}. For every real
$f\in L^2(\mu)$,
\begin{equation}
 \bigl\|V_\rho((T^{K,\mu}_\varepsilon f)_{\varepsilon>0})\bigr\|_{L^2(\mu)}
 \le C_2\|f\|_{L^2(\mu)}.
\end{equation}
The principal value
\[
 T^{K,\mu}f(x)=\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}T^{K,\mu}_\varepsilon f(x)
\]
exists finitely for $\mu$-almost every $x$, belongs to $L^2(\mu)$, and
\[
 \|T^{K,\mu}_\varepsilon f-T^{K,\mu}f\|_{L^2(\mu)}
 \longrightarrow0\qquad(\varepsilon\downarrow0).
\]
The vector Riesz family $R_{\mu,\varepsilon}f$ satisfies the analogous
hard-variation bound and has an almost-everywhere principal-value limit,
with strong convergence in $L^2(\mu;\R^d)$. The exceptional null set
may depend on $K$ and $f$. These are strong-convergence assertions on
each input; no operator-norm convergence is asserted.

For the fixed profile \eqref{eq:variation-cutoff}, every real
$f\in L^p(\mu)$ with $1<p<\infty$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \bigl\|V_\rho((T^{K,\mu}_{\varphi,\varepsilon}f)_{\varepsilon>0})
 \bigr\|_{L^p(\mu)}
 \le C_p\|f\|_{L^p(\mu)}.
\end{equation}
For every real $f\in L^1(\mu)$ and $\lambda>0$,
\[
 \mu\left\{x:
 V_\rho((T^{K,\mu}_{\varphi,\varepsilon}f)_{\varepsilon>0})(x)
 >\lambda\right\}
 \le \frac{C_1}{\lambda}\|f\|_{L^1(\mu)}.
\]
The constants may depend on the dimensions, the fixed $\rho$, the kernel
bounds, the uniform-rectifiability data, and, for the smooth estimates,
the chosen profile and $p$ when relevant.

title: Rigidity of Smooth Billiards with a Continuous Caustic Collar
abstract: We prove that a smooth strictly convex planar billiard with positive curvature is an ellipse whenever a full neighborhood of its boundary is continuously foliated by smooth closed convex caustics. No differentiability across the leaves is assumed. This resolves the near-boundary Birkhoff conjecture in the stated smooth class.

tex.abstract:
We prove that a smooth strictly convex planar billiard with positive
curvature is an ellipse whenever a full neighborhood of its boundary is
continuously foliated by smooth closed convex caustics. No differentiability
across the leaves is assumed. This resolves the near-boundary Birkhoff
conjecture in the stated smooth class.
sections: A jointly analytic parametrization of the glancing collar
The shape strip and its intrinsic coordinate
Normalized chord equations and passage through cones
Exponential profiles and exclusion of infinite growth
Critical estimates at a finite shape boundary
The critical moment law and its first-field model
An odd periodic slice and its stopped geometry
Sign tests and the last moving site

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
If \(\Omega\) has a continuous caustic collar, then \(\Omega\) is an ellipse.
Equivalently, there are \(c\in\R^2\) and a real symmetric positive-definite
matrix \(Q\) such that
\[
\Omega=\{x\in\R^2:(x-c)^TQ(x-c)<1\}.
\]
Circles are included.

statements.title: Analytic regularity
statements.label: thm:analytic
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:main}, the support function of the table
and its boundary are real analytic.

statements.label: prop:high-frequency-estimate
ana:analytic-action-interface
statements.text:
For the actual table, the normalized action in
\Cref{ana:normalized-action} is holomorphic in a neighborhood of the
real diagonal, diagonally \(2\pi\)-periodic, and antisymmetric.
It satisfies
\[
D(X,X+T)=-T^3/24+O(T^5),\qquad
D_1(X,X+T)=T^2/8+O(T^4),
\]
locally uniformly with all fixed derivatives.  The unique rational
graphs and their identities in \Cref{lem:rational-periodicity}
are available for every sufficiently small positive reduced \(l/q\).

statements.title: Joint glancing parametrization
statements.label: thm:joint-parametrization
statements.text:
There are \(s,r_1>0\), with \(r_1<s\), and a real-symmetric holomorphic
function \(U(y,t)\) on
\[
 \{(y,t):|\Im y|<2s,\ |t|<r_1\}
\]
such that \(U-y\) is \(2\pi\)-periodic in \(y\), \(U\) is even in \(t\),
\(U(y,0)=y\), and
\begin{equation}
 D_1\bigl(U(y,t),U(y+t,t)\bigr)
 +D_2\bigl(U(y-t,t),U(y,t)\bigr)=0
 
\end{equation}
for \(|\Im y|<s\), \(|t|<r_1\). Here real symmetry means
\(U(\bar y,\bar t)=\overline{U(y,t)}\).

Set
\begin{equation}
 \Theta(y,t)=\phi(U(y,t)),\qquad
 p(y,t)=-\mathcal S_1\bigl(\Theta(y,t),\Theta(y+t,t)\bigr).
 
\end{equation}
On a possibly smaller product neighborhood, both functions are
holomorphic, real-symmetric, and even in \(t\). For positive small real
\(t\), the billiard map sends the line \((\Theta(y,t),p(y,t))\) to the
line \((\Theta(y+t,t),p(y+t,t))\). The variables \((y,t^2)\) give analytic
coordinates on a full one-sided phase collar. Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 dp\wedge d\Theta=A(t)\,dy\wedge dt,
 \qquad A(t)=\frac{c}{4}t+O(t^3),
 
\end{equation}
where \(A\) is holomorphic and real on the real axis. In particular
\(t^2\) is a nondegenerate analytic first integral on that collar.
statements.section_title: A jointly analytic parametrization of the glancing collar

statements.title: A Newton step across all retained resonances
statements.label: prop:joint-newton
statements.text:
There are constants \(C,B_0\), depending only on the fixed action domain
and the fixed smallness bounds above, with the following property.
Suppose \(U\) is real-symmetric, even in \(t\), and \(U-y\) is periodic,
and
\[
 \|E(U)\|_{\mathcal D^1_0}\le\eps<1.
\]
Let \(N\ge1\) satisfy \(e^{-N\delta}\le\eps\), and put
\(Q=1+N+\delta^{-1}\). If \(CQ^{B_0}\eps\) is sufficiently small, there
is a real-symmetric, even correction \(\Delta U\), periodic in \(y\),
such that
\begin{align}
 \max_{0\le j\le3}\|\partial_y^j\Delta U\|_{\mathcal D^0_{20}}
     &\le CQ^{B_0}\eps,\\
 \|E(U+\Delta U)\|_{\mathcal D^1_{20}}
     &\le CQ^{B_0}\eps^2.
 
\end{align}
The exponent \(B_0\) is fixed; it is independent of \(N\), the retained
rationals, and the order of any formal approximation used to initialize
the iteration.
statements.section_title: A jointly analytic parametrization of the glancing collar

statements.title: Line-endpoint determination
statements.label: thm:lens-lines
statements.text:
Fix an integer \(k\ge2\), and put \(L_i=L(y+it,t)\).
Every intermediate line \(L_i\), \(0<i<k\), is algebraic over
the differential field generated by \(L_0,L_k\).
For each fixed \(k\), finitely many endpoint derivatives suffice.
The same assertion holds for translated index intervals.
All derivatives of the intermediate fields are algebraic over
the corresponding endpoint differential field.

statements.title: Point-endpoint determination
statements.label: thm:lens-points
statements.text:
Let \(k\ge2\), and put \(P_i=X(y+it,t)\), \(0\le i\le k\).
Every intermediate point and every edge of this chain is
algebraic over the differential field generated by \(P_0,P_k\)
and the analytic coefficient \(A(t)\) in
\[
 \dd p\wedge\dd\Theta=A(t)\,\dd y\wedge\dd t.
\]
For each fixed \(k\), finitely many jets suffice.  The assertion
persists under translation and analytic continuation.

statements.title: Continuation along a family of disks
statements.label: cont:disc-sweep
statements.text:
Suppose a continuous path in one complex center variable has a neighborhood
on which a family of analytic disks is holomorphic in the center
and disk variables.  Assume that the pulled-back primary data are
jointly meromorphic on a common boundary collar of these disks,
that these collar germs agree on overlaps, and that a nonempty
open set of starting centers has a full-disk extension.  The
extensions then propagate along the center path.  The same
statement holds holomorphically.  In that case a uniform
boundary modulus bound, or a uniform bound on the real or
imaginary part of a scalar holomorphic component, is preserved
inside each disk.

statements.label: prop:width-superharmonic
statements.text:
Both \(h_L\) and \(h_X\) satisfy superharmonic comparison on \(B\).
They are positive lower semicontinuous superharmonic functions,
with the identically infinite case admitted.

statements.title: No-patch property
statements.label: thm:no-patch
statements.text:
Let \(F=L\) or \(F=X\), and let \(t_0\in B\cap\R\).
If \(h_F(t_0)=H_1<\infty\), no joint meromorphic patch of the
primary branch passes through any point of \(\Im y=H_1\).
The corresponding assertion at the lower wall follows by
real symmetry.

statements.title: Natural boundary of the shape
statements.label: cor:shape-natural-boundary
statements.text:
Put \(H=h_X(0)=h_L(0)\).  The parametrization
\(\Gamma(y)=X(y,0)\) is meromorphic on
\[
 D_H=\{y\in\C:|\Im y|<H\}.
\]
If \(H<\infty\), it has no meromorphic continuation patch
through any point of either boundary line of \(D_H\).
Moreover, on its meromorphic domain,
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\det(\Gamma',\Gamma'')^4}
      {(\Gamma'\cdot\Gamma')^3}=c^2,
 
\end{equation}
where \(c\ne0\) is the normalized curvature constant from
the glancing construction.

statements.title: Classification in the presence of isotropic centers
statements.label: thm:isotropic-classification
statements.text: If \(a\) has a zero or a pole in \(D_H\), the boundary is an ellipse.
statements.section_title: The shape strip and its intrinsic coordinate

statements.title: The global shape lift
statements.label: thm:shape-lift
statements.section_title: The shape strip and its intrinsic coordinate

statements.title: The first impact displacement
statements.label: shape:first-displacement
statements.text:
For the normalization \eqref{shape:mean-normalization},
\[
 \mathfrak s(y,t)=y+t^2V(y)+O(t^4),
\]
where \(V\) is holomorphic and periodic on \(D_H\), has zero mean,
and satisfies
\begin{equation}
 V'=\frac{f^2+8q-\langle f^2+8q\rangle}{120}.
 
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: The shape strip and its intrinsic coordinate

statements.title: Cone passage
statements.label: thm:cone
statements.text:
Fix \(1/2<\alpha<1\), a finite target aperture \(m_0\), and a fixed
\(\delta_b\in(0,H/2)\). There is an input aperture \(L\), depending on
\(\alpha\) and \(m_0\), with the following property. Fix \(K<\infty\),
let \(d\to0\), choose real centers \(x_0\), and let \(0<r\le Kd\).
Suppose
\begin{equation}
 rM(s)\le\eps(d/\delta_s)^\alpha
 \quad\text{if}\quad
 d/10\le\delta_s\le\delta_b,
 \quad |\Re s-x_0|\le L\delta_s.
\end{equation}
For sufficiently small \(\eps>0\) and then sufficiently small \(d\),
the lift continues jointly holomorphically along vertical paths from a
fixed lower row throughout
\begin{equation}
 d<\delta<\delta_*,\qquad
 |\Re y-x_0|<m_0\delta,\qquad
 |t|<r(\delta/d)^\alpha,
\end{equation}
where \(\delta_*>0\) is fixed. With
\(B=1+(\eps/r)d^\alpha\), it satisfies
\begin{equation}
 |\mathfrak s(y,t)-y|
 \le C B^2|t|^2\delta^{1-2\alpha}.
\end{equation}
The relative depth error is small, so these continuations remain in the
shape strip, and they agree with the original lift wherever the latter
is defined below them.

The input aperture can be chosen independently of \(K\). Once it
contains the fixed geometric enlargements described in the proof, the
constant \(C\) and the smallness requirement on \(\eps\) can be chosen
independently of the target aperture. They may depend on \(K\),
\(\alpha\), and the fixed lower-strip data.
statements.section_title: Normalized chord equations and passage through cones

statements.title: Coarse bounds and quiet profiles
statements.label: cor:quiet-cone
statements.text:
Let \(d_n\to0\), \(b_n\ge1\), and \(x_n\in\R\). Suppose, on a
sufficiently large fixed cone starting at depth \(d_n\), that
\begin{equation}
 \frac{d_n}{b_n}M(s)\le C(d_n/\delta_s)^\alpha,
 \qquad \frac12<\alpha<1.
\end{equation}
The following statements hold; whenever an arbitrary fixed aperture is
used, the hypothesis is required on its corresponding fixed
enlargement.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item On a strictly coarser cone, starting at a fixed sufficiently large
multiple of \(d_n\), there is a passage with parameter radius
\(c(d_n/b_n)(\delta/d_n)^\alpha\), and
\begin{equation}
 |\mathfrak s-y|
 =O\left(b_n^2|t|^2d_n^{2\alpha-2}\delta^{1-2\alpha}\right).
\end{equation}
Equivalently, for
\(Y=(y-x_n-\ii H)/d_n\),
\(S=(\mathfrak s-x_n-\ii H)/d_n\), and \(T=tb_n/d_n\),
\[
 |S-Y|\le C|T|^2(-\Im Y)^{1-2\alpha}
\]
far enough down at each bounded \(T\).
\item Suppose in addition that
\begin{equation}
 \frac{d_n}{b_n}M(x_n+\ii H+d_n S)\longrightarrow0
\end{equation}
uniformly on every compact subset of \(\Im S<0\).
For every \(c_1,T_1>0\), lift passages reach depth \(c_1d_n\) for all
\(|t|\le T_1d_n/b_n\), for large \(n\). At real parameters, with
\(\Delta(t)=H-h_X(t)\),
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{|T|\le T_1}\frac{\Delta(Td_n/b_n)}{d_n}\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
\item The hypotheses in \textup{(ii)} are impossible if \(b_n\) stays
bounded. In fact a vanishing weighted cone bound down to a sufficiently
small fixed positive depth ratio already gives this contradiction.
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: Normalized chord equations and passage through cones

statements.title: Subcritical growth is impossible
statements.label: prop:subcritical-exclusion
statements.text:
At a finite shape edge, a uniform bound
\(\max_{\Im s=H-\delta}M(s)=O(\delta^{-p_0})\) with \(p_0<1\) is
impossible in the nonisotropic alternative.
statements.section_title: Normalized chord equations and passage through cones

statements.title: A witness near every center
statements.label: cone:no-quiet-witness
statements.text:
Suppose, for all sufficiently small \(\delta_s\), that
\[
 \delta_s\max_{\Im s=H-\delta_s}M(s)
 \le C\bigl(1+\log(1/\delta_s)\bigr)^A
\]
for some fixed \(C,A\). Then there are constants
\(L,C_1,C_2,c_*>0\) such that for every sufficiently large
\(k=\log(1/d)\) and every real center \(x_0\), there is a point \(s\)
with
\begin{equation}
 |\Re s-x_0|\le L\delta_s,\qquad
 k-C_1\log k\le\log(1/\delta_s)\le k+C_2,
 \qquad \delta_sM(s)\ge c_*.
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Normalized chord equations and passage through cones

statements.title: Exclusion of finite superlinear growth
statements.label: thm:finite-superlinear-exclusion
statements.text:
Suppose \(H<\infty\), and define
\[
 g(k)=\log\max_{\Im s=H-e^{-k}}M(s).
\]
In the nonisotropic alternative it is impossible that
\begin{equation}
 1<\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{g(k)}{k}<\infty.
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Normalized chord equations and passage through cones

statements.title: Exponential-profile obstruction
statements.label: thm:exponential-obstruction
statements.text:
There is no sequence of centers \(s_n=x_n+\ii h_n\in D_H\), length scales
\(\ell_n>0\), and field scales \(m_n>0\) with the following properties.
Put \(b_n=\ell_nm_n\) and
\begin{equation}
 
 F_n(S)=\frac{f(s_n+\ell_n S)}{m_n},\qquad
 Q_n(S)=\frac{q(s_n+\ell_n S)}{m_n^2},\qquad
 Y=\frac{y-s_n}{\ell_n},\quad T=m_nt.
\end{equation}
Assume that \(b_n\to\infty\), that \((D_H-s_n)/\ell_n\) exhausts
\(\C\), and that, locally uniformly on \(\C\), either
\begin{equation}
 
 (F_n,Q_n)\longrightarrow(c_0e^{-\ii S},0)
 \quad\hbox{or}\quad
 (F_n,Q_n)\longrightarrow(0,c_0^2e^{-2\ii S}),
 \qquad c_0\ne0.
\end{equation}
The following additional assumptions are imposed according to the value
of \(H\).
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
 \item If \(H<\infty\), then \(h_n\to H\), \(\ell_n\to0\), and
 there are \(\alpha_0\in(1/2,1)\) and
 \(\delta_b\in(0,H/2)\) such that, for every fixed \(L<\infty\),
 there is a constant \(C_L\) for which eventually
 \begin{equation}
  
  M(s)\le C_Lm_n\left(\frac{\ell_n}{\delta}\right)^{\alpha_0},
  \qquad
  \ell_n\le\delta=h_n-\Im s\le\delta_b,
  \quad |\Re s-x_n|\le L\delta.
 \end{equation}
 The exponent is independent of \(L\); the constant and the eventual
 sequence threshold may depend on \(L\).
 \item If \(H=\infty\), then \(h_n\to\infty\),
 \(0<\ell_n\le C\), and \eqref{profile:coarser-cone} holds with a
 single constant for all horizontal positions and for
 \(\ell_n\le\delta\le h_n\). Moreover,
 \begin{equation}
  
  \log(1+h_n/\ell_n)=o(\log m_n).
 \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Exclusion of entire and infinite-order growth
statements.label: thm:infinite-growth-exclusion
statements.text:
In the nonisotropic case, \(H=\infty\) implies that the table is a
circle. If \(H<\infty\), then
\[
 \limsup_{k\to\infty}
 \frac{\log\max_x M(x+\ii(H-e^{-k}))}{k}<\infty.
\]

statements.title: Exclusion of vanishing profiles at individual centers
statements.label: thm:no-trivial-profile
statements.text:
Consider sequences of levels \(k_n\to\infty\), scales
\(d_n=e^{-k_n}\), and amplitudes \(B_n=\mu(k_n)\to\infty\).
Suppose there are envelopes \(N_n\) satisfying the hypotheses of
\Cref{thm:critical-bootstrap} with constants independent of \(n\),
and \(N_n(k_n)\le C B_n\).

For a fixed \(\alpha\in(1/2,1)\) and a sufficiently large fixed
aperture \(L\), there cannot be centers \(x_n\) such that, for every
fixed \(c>0\),
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{\substack{c d_n\le\delta\le\delta_b\\
                  |\Re s-x_n|\le L\delta\\
                  \delta=H-\Im s}}
 \frac{d_nM(s)}{B_n}\left(\frac{\delta}{d_n}\right)^\alpha
 \longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
In particular, suppose the profiles
\begin{equation}
 F_n(S)=\frac{d_n}{B_n}f(x_n+\ii H+d_nS),\qquad
 Q_n(S)=\left(\frac{d_n}{B_n}\right)^2q(x_n+\ii H+d_nS)
\end{equation}
converge to \((0,0)\) on compact subsets of the lower half-plane.
They cannot also satisfy, for some fixed \(\alpha_0>1/2\) and an
aperture \(L\) sufficiently large for a chosen exponent
\(1/2<\alpha<\min(1,\alpha_0)\),
\begin{equation}
 \frac{d_n}{B_n}M(s)\le C\left(\frac{d_n}{\delta}\right)^{\alpha_0}
 \quad(d_n\le\delta\le\delta_b,
             \ |\Re s-x_n|\le L\delta).
\end{equation}
Every compact holomorphic limit of the pair in
\eqref{critical:eq:profiles} is pure: its product \(FQ\) vanishes
identically.

 \mu(k)\le C(1+k),\qquad

All fixed tile enlargements have the corresponding bounds.

statements.title: The pure first-field model
statements.label: prop:pure-model
statements.text:
There is a limiting impact coordinate \(S(T,Y)\) with the following
properties.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item For every fixed aperture and every bounded complex parameter
range, it is jointly holomorphic sufficiently deep in the corresponding
cone and is the locally uniform limit of \eqref{model:phase-scaling}.
There,
\begin{equation}

 S(T,Y)-Y=O\bigl(|T|^2D^{1-2\alpha}\bigr),
\qquad D=-\Im Y\longrightarrow\infty.
\end{equation}

\item Put
\begin{equation}

 J=S_Y,\qquad z=\frac{TF(S)J}{2},\qquad
 g(z)=\frac{3(\sin z-z\cos z)}{z^3},\quad g(0)=1.
\end{equation}
The limiting equation is
\begin{equation}

 J^3g(z)=1.
\end{equation}

\item For every fixed \(\eps>0\), set \(r=1/(\lambda+\eps)\).
There are constants \(C_\eps,t_0>0\) such that, for every real
\(|T|<t_0\), the model is holomorphic in \(Y\) and maps
\begin{equation}

 \{Y:\Im Y<-C_\eps|T|^r\}\ \longrightarrow\ \mathbb H_-.
\end{equation}
It satisfies \(S(0,Y)=Y\), obeys
\eqref{model:energy-equation} throughout this domain, and depends
continuously on real \(T\), locally uniformly on strict common
interiors.

\item At every strict interior point of \eqref{model:real-domains}
with \(T\) real, these functions have a joint holomorphic germ in
\((T,Y)\).  The germs agree when continued along vertical \(Y\)-paths
from the deep model.
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Witnesses near every horizontal center
statements.label: prop:model-witnesses
statements.text:
There is a fixed sufficiently large aperture \(L_0\) with
the following property.  For every compact interval
\(I\subset\R\), there is an error function
\(\eta_I(u)\to0\), for \(u\in E\), such that every
sufficiently large \(u\in E\) and every \(x\in I\) admit
a point \(w=p-\ii\delta\in\mathbb H_-\) satisfying
\begin{equation}

 |p-x|\le L_0\delta,\qquad
 |-\log\delta-u|\le\eta_I(u)u,\qquad
 \log|F(w)|\ge\lambda u-\eta_I(u)u.
\end{equation}
The epochs are common to all centers; a center-dependent
subsequence is not needed.

statements.title: High-modulus mesh contradiction
statements.label: thm:mesh-contradiction
statements.text:
Let \(F\not\equiv0\) be holomorphic in
\(\mathbb H_-:=\{z\in\C:\Im z<0\}\), and suppose that \(F''/F\)
extends holomorphically to \(\mathbb H_-\).  There cannot exist a number
\(\lambda\ge1\) and an unbounded set of epochs
\(E\subset(0,\infty)\) with all of the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item For every compact interval \(I\subset\R\),
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{x\in I}\log|F(x-\ii e^{-v})|
 \le \lambda v+o(v),\qquad v\longrightarrow\infty.
 
\end{equation}
The error is uniform in \(x\in I\).
\item The epochs are relatively dense in the sense that
\begin{equation}
 \dist(v,E)=o(v),\qquad v\longrightarrow\infty.
 
\end{equation}
\item For every compact interval \(I\), there are a fixed aperture
\(A_I<\infty\) and a function \(r_I(u)\to0\) such that, for every
sufficiently large \(u\in E\) and every \(x\in I\), there is a point
\(w=p-\ii\delta\) satisfying
\begin{equation}
 |p-x|\le A_I\delta,\qquad
 |{-\log\delta}-u|\le r_I(u)u,\qquad
 \log|F(w)|\ge\lambda u-r_I(u)u.
 
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
In particular, the epochs in \textup{(iii)} are common to all the centers
in \(I\); no choice of an epoch depending on the center is allowed.

\]

For the deterministic level in \Cref{thm:row-sign}, put
\begin{equation}
 h_1=\tfrac12K^{\alpha/2},\qquad
 r_{\mathrm{rob}}=e^{-k-h_1/4}.

Outside a set of relative horizontal measure tending to zero on

with constant sign on that disk.  In the odd-slice Brownian
experiment, for each fixed site the probability that its first hit
of the tested shape depth occurs at a point without this property
tends to zero.

title: Rigidity of the Turing degrees
abstract: We prove that every order automorphism of the full partial order of Turing degrees is the identity, resolving the rigidity conjecture for the Turing degrees positively.

tex.abstract:
We prove that every order automorphism of the full partial order of
Turing degrees is the identity, resolving the rigidity conjecture for
the Turing degrees positively.

statements.label: thm:rigidity
statements.text:
Every order automorphism of the full Turing-degree structure is
the identity:
\[
\forall\pi\in\Aut(\DT,\leT)\ \forall\mathbf a\in\DT
\qquad \pi(\mathbf a)=\mathbf a.
\]

statements.title: Slaman--Woodin
statements.label: thm:representation
statements.text:
For every $\pi\in\Aut(\DT,\leT)$ there is an arithmetic function
$\widehat F:2^\N\to2^\N$ such that
\[
\degT{\widehat F(A)}=\pi(\degT A)
\qquad\text{for every }A\subseteq\N.
\]

statements.title: Recovery from four values
statements.label: prop:recovery
statements.text:
Let $F:\R\to2^\N$ be Borel with countable fibers, and suppose
\[
F(x+y)\leT F(x)\oplus F(y)\qquad(x,y\in\R).
\]
For every irrational $t\in(0,1)$ there is a comeager set
$G_t\subseteq\R^2$ such that for each $(u,v)\in G_t$ there
is a rational $\delta\in(0,1)$ for which
\begin{equation}
C(t)\leT
F(u)\oplus F(u-v)\oplus
F(v-u+\delta t)\oplus F(v-u+\delta(t-1)).
\end{equation}

statements.label: cor:biinterpretability
statements.text:
The Turing-degree ordering is biinterpretable without parameters
with full second-order arithmetic, in the sense of
\cite[Definition~7.5.1]{SlamanWoodin2005}.

title: Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem for one transformation
abstract: Every invertible mixing probability-preserving transformation is mixing of every finite order. Thus Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem for a single transformation has an affirmative answer.

tex.abstract: Every invertible mixing probability-preserving transformation is mixing of every finite order. Thus Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem for a single transformation has an affirmative answer.
sections: A finite-alphabet witness of zero entropy

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Every invertible mixing probability-preserving transformation is mixing
of every finite order. More explicitly, under the assumptions above, for
every $k\ge3$ and every $A_1,\ldots,A_k\in\mathcal F$,
\[
 \mu\bigl(A_1\cap T^{-n_1}A_2\cap\cdots\cap
             T^{-(n_1+\cdots+n_{k-1})}A_k\bigr)
 \longrightarrow\prod_{i=1}^k\mu(A_i)
\]
as $\min(n_1,\ldots,n_{k-1})\to\infty$ through positive integers.
No standardness or countable-generation assumption is imposed on the
original probability space.

statements.title: Zero-entropy witness
statements.label: prop:zero-entropy-witness
statements.text:
Suppose an invertible mixing transformation fails to be mixing of every
order.  There then exist an integer $k\geq3$, a finite alphabet $\mathcal A$,
a shift-invariant probability measure $\mu_X$ on
$X=\mathcal A^{\Z}$, and real one-site functions $f_1,\ldots,f_k$ such that
the shift $T_X$ is mixing of every order less than $k$,
\[
 \int f_i\dd\mu_X=0,\qquad \norm{f_i}_{\infty}\leq1,
 \qquad
 \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac1nH_{\mu_X}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=0.
\]
Moreover, there are $\delta>0$ and integer layouts
\[
 0=d_1(b)<d_2(b)<\cdots<d_k(b),\qquad
 \min_{i<k}\bigl(d_{i+1}(b)-d_i(b)\bigr)\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
for which
\begin{equation}
 \int_X\prod_{i=1}^k f_i(T_X^{d_i(b)}x)\dd\mu_X(x)\geq\delta
 \quad\text{for every }b.
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: A finite-alphabet witness of zero entropy

statements.title: Saturation
statements.label: prop:saturation
statements.text:
Every array object has an extension with the following property.  For
every $n\geq1$, every $F\in L^2(m_n)$, and each
\[
 \mathcal D\in\{\mathcal P_n\}\cup
 \{\mathcal G_{n,j},\mathcal O_{n,j}:j\in I\},
\]
no extension increases the norm of $\E[F\mid\mathcal D]$ after
pullback.  More precisely, if $\theta_n$ is the coordinatewise factor
map from any extension and $\mathcal D'$ is the corresponding data in
that extension, then
\begin{equation}
 \E[F\circ\theta_n\mid\mathcal D']
 =\E[F\mid\mathcal D]\circ\theta_n.
\end{equation}

statements.title: Square locality
statements.label: prop:square-locality
statements.text:
The following properties hold in $m_2$, and can be imposed
simultaneously on one conull set of full parameter arrays $E$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Conditional on $E$, every proper family of columns is independent,
with column $j$ having law $\lambda_{q_j}$.  Every proper family of rows
is independent, with row $a$ having law $\lambda_{p_a}$.
\item Let $R\subset I$, $|R|\leq k-2$.  Given $E$ and the full parent
rows $Y_{R,I}$, every proper family of columns is independent, and each
column has law $\lambda_{q_j}$ conditioned on its own parent entries
$Y_{R,j}$.
\item If $a\notin R$ and $j_0\in I$, then
\begin{equation}
 \Law(y_{a,j_0}\mid E,Y_{R,I},Y_{I,I\setminus\{j_0\}})
 =\lambda_{p_a}(\dd y_{a,j_0}\mid Y_{a,I\setminus\{j_0\}}).
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
There is also the following grouped form.  Partition the rows into
three nonempty groups $P,A,B$ and the columns into three nonempty groups
$r,s,t$.  At a fixed typical $E$, each grouped row
\[
 (Y_{D,r},Y_{D,s},Y_{D,t}),\quad D\in\{P,A,B\},
\]
has a three-coordinate law with pairwise independent coordinates, and
the same holds for each grouped column.  Given $Y_{P,I}$, any two
grouped columns are independent with their own column laws conditioned
on their entries in $P$.  Finally, putting
$\Lambda_A=\bigotimes_{a\in A}\lambda_{p_a}$, we have
\begin{equation}
 \Law(Y_{A,t}\mid E,Y_{P,I},Y_{I,r\cup s})
 =\Lambda_A(\dd Y_{A,t}\mid Y_{A,r},Y_{A,s}).
\end{equation}
All these grouped assertions hold for every ordering of the three row
groups and the three column groups.

statements.title: Common exact lines
statements.label: prop:common-exact-lines
statements.text:
For almost every parameter square $E$, the following assertions hold
simultaneously at all individual cells.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The orthogonal projections onto $V_{a,j}$ and $W_{a,j}$ commute.
Their common range $V_{a,j}\cap W_{a,j}$ is spanned by the lines exact
for both the full $k$-coordinate row law $\lambda_{p_a}$ and the full
$k$-coordinate column law $\lambda_{q_j}$.
\item For distinct columns $s,t$, let $L^a_{s\leftarrow t}(v)$ be the
row Markov operator from cell $(a,t)$ to $(a,s)$, conditioned on the
remaining $k-2$ row entries $v$.  Then, for almost every $v$,
\[
 P^W_{a,s}L^a_{s\leftarrow t}(v)
 =L^a_{s\leftarrow t}(v)P^W_{a,t}.
\]
Column operators likewise intertwine the corresponding row-active
projections.
\item If $(\chi_j)_{j\in I}$ is an exact tuple for row $a$, with
$\prod_j\chi_j(Y_{a,j})=c$, then
\begin{equation}
 L^a_{s\leftarrow t}(v)\chi_t
 =c\!\prod_{j\ne s,t}\overline{\chi_j(v_j)}\,
   \overline{\chi_s}.
\end{equation}
In particular, membership of one partner line in the column-active
space is equivalent to membership of any other partner line in its
column-active space.  The analogous assertion holds with rows and
columns exchanged.
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Measurable local labels
statements.label: prop:measurable-labels
statements.text:
There is a measurable countable family of abelian groups
$u\mapsto\mathcal L(u)$, defined on a $\nu$-conull set, with the
following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Each $\ell\in\mathcal L(u)$ labels a line in $H_u$ with a
measurable modulus-one representative $\chi_{u,\ell}$. The identity
label $0$ has representative $1$. Distinct labels are orthogonal,
every nonidentity representative has mean zero, and
\[
 \chi_{u,\ell}\chi_{u,\ell'}
 \in\T\chi_{u,\ell+\ell'}.
\]
\item For $\pi$-almost every $p$, the exact lines at slot $i$ of
$\lambda_p$ are precisely $\mathcal L(p_i)$, for every $i$, and they
span its active space. Unique exact matching gives measurable group
isomorphisms
\[
 \Phi_{st}(p):\mathcal L(p_s)\longrightarrow\mathcal L(p_t)
 \qquad(s,t\in I),
\]
where $\Phi_{ss}(p)=\id$.
\item Local time gives measurable group isomorphisms
\[
 \tau_u:\mathcal L(u)\longrightarrow\mathcal L(T_Uu),
 \qquad [\chi]\longmapsto[\chi\circ T_Y^{-1}].
\]
They respect exact matching. All local time assertions may be imposed
on an invariant conull set.
\item For $\vartheta$-almost every parameter square, prescribing a
label at any one cell gives a unique array of labels matched along
every row and every column.
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: A block carrying the witness
statements.label: prop:block-witness
statements.text:
Let the saturated array object lie over the zero-entropy finite-alphabet
mixing process $(X,\mu_X,T_X)$ supplied by
Proposition~\ref{prop:zero-entropy-witness}, with its centered
finite-valued one-site functions $f_1,\ldots,f_k$ and nonzero
level-$1$ product integral. There exist a function
$f\in\{f_1,\ldots,f_k\}$, a countable abelian group $\mathcal L$,
an automorphism $G$ of $\mathcal L$, a finite nonempty set
$B\subset\mathcal L$, and a number $c>0$ with the following properties.

For $\nu$-almost every $u$, the probability space $(Y,\eta_u)$
has factor map $x:Y\to X$ with $x_*\eta_u=\mu_X$, and admits
representatives $(\chi_\ell^u)_{\ell\in\mathcal L}$ such that
\begin{gather}
 \chi_0^u=1,\qquad |\chi_\ell^u|=1,\qquad
 \chi_\ell^u\chi_{\ell'}^u\in\T\chi_{\ell+\ell'}^u,
 \\
 \int\chi_\ell^u\dd\eta_u=0\quad(\ell\ne0),\qquad
 \ip{\chi_\ell^u}{\chi_{\ell'}^u}_{L^2(\eta_u)}
       =\mathbf1_{\{\ell=\ell'\}}.
 \nonumber
\end{gather}
For every $r\ge0$ the function
\begin{equation}
 s_r(u)=\sum_{\ell\in B}
 \left|\int f(T_X^r x(y))\,
               \overline{\chi_{G^r\ell}^u(y)}\dd\eta_u(y)\right|
\end{equation}
has a measurable version and satisfies
\begin{equation}
 0\le s_r(u)\le |B|\norm f_\infty,
 \qquad \int_U s_r(u)\dd\nu(u)=c>0.
\end{equation}
The group identifications used to choose the representatives in
\eqref{eq:block-character-laws} need not be measurable in $u$.
Their finite sums in \eqref{eq:block-witness-sum} are intrinsic sums
over the measurable moving blocks. In particular, no time invariance
of an individual $\eta_u$ is asserted or required.

statements.title: Endomorphisms and continuous flows
statements.label: cor:endomorphisms-flows
statements.text:
Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mu)$ be an arbitrary probability space.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Suppose $T:\Omega\to\Omega$ is measurable, preserves $\mu$, and
$\mu(A\cap T^{-n}B)\to\mu(A)\mu(B)$ as $n\to+\infty$ for every
$A,B\in\mathcal F$. Then, for every fixed $k\ge2$ and measurable
$A_1,\ldots,A_k$,
\[
 \mu\left(\bigcap_{i=1}^kT^{-t_i}A_i\right)
 \longrightarrow\prod_{i=1}^k\mu(A_i)
\]
along nonnegative integer times $t_1<\cdots<t_k$ whose least successive
gap tends to infinity. Only preimages under forward iterates are used.
\item Let $(S_t)_{t\in\R}$ be a probability-preserving group of invertible
measurable transformations. Assume
$\mu(A\cap S_t^{-1}B)\to\mu(A)\mu(B)$ as $t\to+\infty$ for every
$A,B\in\mathcal F$, and that its Koopman operators $U_t f=f\circ S_t$
are strongly continuous on $L^1(\mu)$; equivalently,
\[
 \norm{U_s1_A-1_A}_1\longrightarrow0\qquad(s\to0)
 \quad\text{for every }A\in\mathcal F.
\]
The same product limit holds with $T^{-t_i}A_i$ replaced by
$S_{t_i}^{-1}A_i$ and with arbitrary real times
$t_1<\cdots<t_k$ whose least successive gap tends to infinity.
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Routing density and representation contraction
statements.label: fac:main
statements.text:
There are absolute constants $\eta,c,C>0$ such that, with $a=1/1000$,
\[
 \log\E_{y\sim u_{N,k}}R_x(y)^{1+a}
 \le Ck(k/N)^\eta
 \qquad(1\le k\le N),
\]
uniformly over every starting injection $x$. For every sufficiently
large dyadic $N$ and every nontrivial irreducible representation,
\[
 T_N(\lambda)=0\quad\hbox{or}\quad
 \|T_N(\lambda)\|_{\op}\le D_\lambda^{-c}.
\]
Consequently an absolute number of forward sweeps has worst-start
total-variation distance from uniform tending to zero as $d\to\infty$.

statements.title: High-height cycle tail
statements.label: net:hightail
statements.text:
There are absolute $b,\delta>0$ and an integer $J_0\ge1$ such that, uniformly in the tracked input injection of size $r$ and for every integer $J\ge J_0$,
\begin{align}
 \log_2\E 2^{b\sum_{j\ge J}C_j}&\le O(r2^{-bJ}),\\
 \log_2\E 2^{b\sum_jC_j}&\le O(r(r/n)^\delta).
\end{align}
The first bound also holds with expectation conditional on all input-side
switches and all output switches of heights at most $s$, for every integer
$0\le s\le d$ with $2s<J$, uniformly in the fixed switch values and with
the same absolute implied constant.
statements.section_title: Certificate tails and numerical dense bounds

statements.title: Dense truncation
statements.label: net:densetruncation
statements.text:
For every $\rho_0\in(0,1]$ and $\epsilon>0$, there are
$c>0$ and $n_0$ such that, for every dyadic $n\ge n_0$ and
every integer $r$ with $\rho=r/n\in[\rho_0,1]$, the density
exponent \eqref{net:exponent} exceeds
\[
 r\left[H(\rho)+\frac{-\rho-(1-\rho)\ln(1-\rho)}{\rho\ln2}+\epsilon\right]
\]
with probability at most $\exp(-cr)$, uniformly in the input injection.
The constants depend only on $\rho_0,\epsilon$, and the expression
is interpreted continuously at $\rho=1$.

statements.label: net:main
statements.text:

\[
 \|T_n(\lambda)\|_{\op}\le D^{-c}.
\]
Consequently a fixed absolute number of sweeps has total-variation distance tending to zero.

$\lambda=(N-k,\beta)\vdash N$, with
$\beta=(\lambda_2,\lambda_3,\ldots)\vdash k$,

statements.title: Uniform sparse contact estimate
statements.label: n:coherent-contact
statements.text:
There is an absolute constant $C_*>0$ such that for every dyadic
$n=2^d\ge2$, every $1\le k<n$, and every partition
$\lambda=(n-k,\beta)\vdash n$,
\begin{equation}
 \|T_n(\lambda)\|_{\op}^2
 \le \min\left\{1,\left(\frac{C_*dk}{n}\right)^{k/2}\right\}.
\end{equation}
For $k=1$ this operator is zero.  In particular, with an absolute
constant $C$ independent of $n,k,\lambda$,
\begin{equation}
 \|T_n(\lambda)\|_{\op}^2
 \le C^k(1+d)^{Ck}(k/n)^{k/2}.
\end{equation}
The same statements hold with the coordinate order reversed.

statements.title: Exponential sparse-level saving
statements.label: n:coherent-contact-sparse-saving
statements.text:
There are absolute constants $C,d_0>0$ such that for every dyadic
$n=2^d$ and $\lambda=(n-k,\beta)\vdash n$ satisfying
$1\le k<n$ and $\log(n/k)\ge d^{3/4}$,
\[
 \|T_n(\lambda)\|_{\op}^2
 \le e^{Ck}(k/n)^{k/4}.
\]
For $d\ge d_0$, the factor $e^{Ck}$ can be omitted.

statements.label: n:coherent-sparse-consequence
statements.text:
There are absolute $c>0$ and $d_0$ such that, for every
$N=2^d$ with $d\ge d_0$ and every partition
$\lambda=(N-k,\beta)\vdash N$ satisfying
$1\le k<N$ and $\log(N/k)\ge d^{3/4}$,
\[
 \|T_N(\lambda)\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\le D_\lambda^{-c}.

statements.title: Cycle density and Casimir contraction
statements.label: cas:main
statements.text:
There are absolute constants $a,C>0$ such that for every dyadic $n$,
every $1\le k\le n$, and every $x\in X_{n,k}$,
\[
 \|R_x\|_{L^{65/64}(u_{n,k})}\le e^{C h_n(k)}.
\]
For every nontrivial partition $\lambda\vdash n$, put $k=n-\lambda_1$.
Then
\[
 \|K_n(\lambda)\|_{\op}\le e^{-a h_n(k)},\qquad
 D_\lambda\Tr K_n(\lambda)^{65}\le e^{C h_n(k)}.
\]
Consequently there is an absolute integer $l$ for which
$\|\mu_n^{*l}-U_{S_n}\|_{\TV}\to0$ as $n\to\infty$ through powers of two.
Here $U_{S_n}$ is the uniform permutation law and total variation includes
the factor $1/2$.  The same bound holds from every deterministic initial
permutation.  When $n=2^d$, these $l$ sweeps take $ld$ physical shuffles.

statements.title: Weighted sweep moments
statements.label: thm:weighted
statements.text:
There are positive weights $W_\lambda$, an absolute finite $p_*$, and real
exponents $2\le p_d\le p_*$ such that, for every $d\ge1$ and every
$\lambda\vdash2^d$,
\begin{equation}
 D_\lambda^{3/4}\le W_\lambda\le D_\lambda,
 \qquad W_\lambda\|K_d(\lambda)\|_{p_d}^{p_d}\le1.
\end{equation}
Consequently $\|K_d(\lambda)\|_{\rm op}\le D_\lambda^{-3/(4p_*)}$.

statements.title: Optimal order of mixing
statements.label: cor:optimal-mixing
statements.text:
There is an absolute constant $C$ such that, for every $d\ge1$,
\[
 \left\lceil\frac2N\log_2\frac{3N!}{4}\right\rceil
 \le t_{\rm mix}(d)\le Cd,
 \qquad N=2^d.
\]
In particular $t_{\rm mix}(d)=\Theta(d)$, and its lower bound is
$2d-O(1)$.

statements.title: Overlap on an arbitrary occupied board
statements.label: thm:occupied
statements.text:
Take a grid with \(m\) rows and \(n\) columns, \(mn=N\), and consider any subset of \(s=N-t\) cells, with the group \(G_s\) on those cells. Let \(a\vdash s\) lie in the \(h,h\)-hook, \(1\le h\le N\). Decompose \(V_a\) under the within-row permutation subgroup of \(G_s\), and also (separately) the within-column subgroup. For types \(\sigma,\theta\) of these two groups, let \(I_{\sigma,u}: V_\sigma\to V_a\), \(I_{\theta,v}: V_\theta\to V_a\) be isometric embeddings giving orthogonal copies and spanning the respective isotypic spaces. Then
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{u,v}\|I_{\sigma,u}^* I_{\theta,v}\|_\infty^2
 \ \le\
 \exp\{C[(m+n+1)h^2\log(N+2)+t]\}\ \min\left\{1,\frac{D_\sigma D_\theta}{D_a}\right\}.       
\end{equation}
Here \(\sigma\) and \(\theta\) can each consist of a tuple of partitions, and the infinity norm is the operator norm. For \(s=0\) the empty representation has dimension one.

statements.title: Support obstruction
statements.label: ten:support
statements.text:
Let $q_d$ be the law of one physical Thorp shuffle. For every integer $t\ge0$, its $t$-fold convolution satisfies
\[
 \|q_d^{*t}-U_{S_N}\|_{\rm TV}\ge1-\frac{2^{tN/2}}{N!}.
\]
Thus mixing to distance $1/4$ requires at least
$\lceil(2/N)\log_2(3N!/4)\rceil=2d-O(1)$ physical shuffles.

statements.title: Coherent overlap on surviving cells
statements.label: prop:coherent-hook
statements.text:
Let $M,R,Q\ge1$ be integers.  Consider an $M$ by $R$ grid,
$n=MR$, with $l$ holes and $m=n-l$ surviving cells.  Let $K,J$ be the row and column permutation groups
on surviving cells.  Suppose $\mu\vdash m$ lies in a $(Q,Q)$ hook.
For Fourier projections $E=\bigotimes_i E_{\sigma_i,e_i}$ and $F=\bigotimes_j E_{\tau_j,f_j}$ selecting one unit carrier vector on each row or column, write $\sigma=(\sigma_i)$ and $\tau=(\tau_j)$. Then
\begin{equation}
 D_\mu\Tr_{V_\mu}(EF)
 \le D_\sigma D_\tau
       \exp\{l+C(1+M+R)Q^2\log(2n)\}.
\end{equation}
Here $D_\sigma,D_\tau$ denote products over lines, and $C$ is
absolute.  For $m=0$ the
surviving representation is the one-dimensional trivial representation.

statements.title: Restoration with ordered holes
statements.label: prop:coherent-restoration
statements.text:
Let $E,F$ select product unit carrier vectors of types $\sigma,\tau$
in $K,J$, respectively.  For $\lambda\vdash n$ and integer $Q\ge1$,
let $l$ be the number of boxes outside the union of its first $Q$
rows and first $Q$ columns.  Then
\begin{equation}
 D_\lambda\Tr_{V_\lambda}(EF)
 \le D_\sigma D_\tau
 e^{3l+\log\binom nl+C(1+M+R)Q^2\log(2n)}.
\end{equation}

title: SLE3 universality for weak finite-range Ising interactions
abstract: We prove that every sufficiently small, square-symmetric finite-range perturbation of the planar Ising contour energy has a domain-independent inverse temperature at which its spin interface converges to chordal SLE<sub>3</sub>. The result allows interactions of either sign, arbitrary admissible exterior contours, and uniformly approximated Jordan domains. Convergence holds for the full oriented curve law in uniform distance modulo increasing reparametrization.

tex.abstract:
We prove that every sufficiently small, square-symmetric finite-range
perturbation of the planar Ising contour energy has a domain-independent
inverse temperature at which its spin interface converges to chordal
\(\mathrm{SLE}_3\). The result allows interactions of either sign, arbitrary
admissible exterior contours, and uniformly approximated Jordan domains.
Convergence holds for the full oriented curve law in uniform distance
modulo increasing reparametrization.
