statements.title: Continuum form and inverse
statements.label: prop:continuum-form
statements.text:
Almost surely, the closure in $L^2(\mu_h)$ of the smooth form
$\frac12\mathcal E^0$ has domain
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal D_h=R_{\mu_h}(H^1(\Sph,\mathrm{vol}_0)),\qquad
 \mathcal E_h(R_{\mu_h}f,R_{\mu_h}g)=\frac12\mathcal E^0(f,g).
\end{equation}
It is a densely defined closed regular Dirichlet form.  Let $A_h$ be its
nonnegative self-adjoint operator, and set $B_h=2A_h$, the operator of the
raw form $\mathcal E^0$.  Put $\mu=\mu_h$ and define
\begin{align}
 G_\mu(x,y)={}&G(x,y)-\int G(x,z)\dd\mu(z)-\int G(z,y)\dd\mu(z)
       +\iint G(z,w)\dd\mu(z)\dd\mu(w),\\
 K_hg(x)={}&\int G_\mu(x,y)g(y)\dd\mu(y).
       
\end{align}
The kernel $G_\mu$ is in $L^2(\mu\otimes\mu)$ and has zero $\mu$-mean
in each variable.  The operator $K_h$ is zero on constants and is the
positive, injective inverse of $B_h$ on $L^2_0(\mu)$, the subspace of
$\mu$-mean-zero functions.

Both $B_h$ and $A_h$ have compact resolvent.  On the infinite-dimensional
space $L^2(\mu)$ their eigenvalues, counted with multiplicity, can be
written
\[
 0=\nu_0<\nu_1\le\nu_2\le\cdots\longrightarrow\infty,
 \qquad \Lambda_j=\frac{\nu_j}{2}\quad(j\ge0),
\]
respectively.  The constant eigenfunction is the only zero mode, and
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{j\ge1}\nu_j^{-2}=\|K_h\|_{\HS}^2<\infty,
 \qquad
 \Tr e^{-tA_h}=1+\sum_{j\ge1}e^{-t\nu_j/2}<\infty\quad(t>0).
\end{equation}
The heat series converges locally uniformly on $(0,\infty)$.  The ordered
eigenvalues and this $C_{\mathrm{loc}}((0,\infty))$ heat trace have Borel
versions as functions of the area measure in the fixed sphere coordinate.
The form and these readouts are invariant under conformal or
anticonformal changes of that coordinate.

title: Spectral scalar curvature and Urysohn width in dimension three
abstract: Every connected complete smooth Riemannian three-manifold without boundary satisfying \(-4\Delta+\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}\nolimits \ge\lambda\gt 0\) as a quadratic-form inequality admits a continuous map to a graph whose entire fibers have diameter at most \(500/\sqrt\lambda\) in the original metric. No orientability, spin, compactness, or bounded-geometry assumption is required.

tex.abstract:
Every connected complete smooth Riemannian three-manifold without
boundary satisfying $-4\Delta+\Scal\ge\lambda>0$ as a quadratic-form
inequality admits a continuous map to a graph whose entire fibers have
diameter at most $500/\sqrt\lambda$ in the original metric.
No orientability, spin, compactness, or bounded-geometry assumption
is required.
sections: Graph maps and gluing across the cuts

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $(M^3,g)$ be a connected complete smooth Riemannian three-manifold
without boundary. Suppose that $\lambda>0$ and
\begin{equation}
 \int_M\bigl(4|\nabla_g\phi|_g^2+\Scal_g\phi^2\bigr)\,d\vol_g
 \ge \lambda\int_M\phi^2\,d\vol_g
 \qquad\bigl(\phi\in C_c^\infty(M;\R)\bigr).
\end{equation}
Then there exist a simplicial complex $K$ of dimension at most one and a
continuous map $f:M\to K$ such that
\[
 \diam_g f^{-1}(y)\le \frac{500}{\sqrt\lambda}
 \qquad(y\in K).
\]
The complex has its usual polyhedral topology. No orientability, spin,
compactness, or bounded-geometry assumption is imposed on $M$.

statements.title: Closed stable surfaces
statements.label: prop:stable-surface
statements.text:
Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth closed connected two-sided surface in a
Riemannian three-manifold $(X,h)$.  Let $T,\mu$ be smooth ambient
functions.  Suppose that $\Sigma$ satisfies $H-\nu T=\mu$, is stable
for weighted area with pressure $\mu$, and satisfies
\eqref{eq:pressure-curvature-condition} for a constant $c>0$.
Then, in the induced metric $k=h|_\Sigma$,
\[
 \diam_k\Sigma\le\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt c}.
\]
Moreover, $\Sigma$ is diffeomorphic to $S^2$ or $\R P^2$.

statements.label: prop:separating-cut
statements.text:
There is a locally finite family $\mathcal S$ of pairwise disjoint closed
connected embedded two-sided stable weighted minimal surfaces in $M$
such that the following statements hold. Let $N$ be the manifold obtained
by cutting $M$ along $\mathcal S$, and let $q:N\to M$ be the natural
gluing map.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The map $q$ is proper and is a quotient map. Each connected component
$P$ of $N$, with the intrinsic length metric of the pulled-back metric
$g$, is proper.
\item Each boundary component of $P$ is a sphere or a real projective
plane, is stable weighted minimal, and has intrinsic $g$-diameter at most
$2\pi$. Each surface of $\mathcal S$ gives two boundary copies in $N$.
\item Every compact connected neatly embedded two-sided hypersurface
in $P$ separates $P$.
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Separating interfaces
statements.label: prop:separating-interfaces
statements.text:
Let $\ell\ge100$, and suppose that $\{r>\ell\}$ is nonempty.  There are finitely
many disjoint smooth compact connected two-sided neat hypersurfaces
$F_1,\ldots,F_m$ in $P$ such that
\begin{equation}
 F_i\subset\{\ell-91<r<\ell-18\},\qquad \diam_d F_i\le4\pi.
\end{equation}
Each $F_i$ separates $P$.  Moreover,
$P\setminus\bigcup_iF_i$ is the disjoint union of two open sets
$U_+,U_-$, with $o\in U_+$ and $\{r>\ell\}\subset U_-$.

statements.title: Slab diameter bound
statements.label: prop:slab-diameter
statements.text:
For $\ell<u\le\ell+2$, every connected component $C$ of
\[
 \{x\in P:\ell<r(x)<u\}
\]
has $d$-diameter at most $220$.

title: Spectral scalar curvature and uniform Urysohn width
abstract: For every n ≥ 4, a complete connected smooth Riemannian n-manifold without boundary satisfying \(-4\Delta+\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}\nolimits \ge1\) as a quadratic-form inequality admits a continuous map to a simplicial complex of dimension at most \(n-2\) whose entire fibers have diameter bounded only in terms of n. The bound is measured in the original metric. This extends the uniform Urysohn width theorem from a pointwise scalar-curvature lower bound to a spectral lower bound.

tex.abstract:
For every $n\ge4$, a complete connected smooth Riemannian $n$-manifold
without boundary satisfying $-4\Delta+\Scal\ge1$ as a quadratic-form
inequality admits a continuous map to a simplicial complex of dimension
at most $n-2$ whose entire fibers have diameter bounded only in terms
of $n$. The bound is measured in the original metric. This extends the
uniform Urysohn width theorem from a pointwise scalar-curvature lower
bound to a spectral lower bound.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every integer $n\ge4$ there is a finite constant $C_n$ with the
following property. Every connected complete smooth Riemannian
$n$-manifold $(M,g)$ without boundary satisfying
\eqref{eq:spectral-bound} admits a continuous map $f:M\to K$ to a
simplicial complex of dimension at most $n-2$ such that
\[
 \diam_g f^{-1}(y)\le C_n\qquad(y\in K).
\]
In particular, $\UW_{n-2}(M,g)\le C_n$.

statements.title: Partition theorem for stretched data {\cite{OpenAIWidth}}
statements.label: interface:width
statements.text:
For each integer $n\ge4$, there is a finite number $D_{\mathrm{nat}}(n)>0$
with the following property.  Let $(M^n,g)$ be a connected complete smooth
Riemannian manifold without boundary, and let $D\ge D_{\mathrm{nat}}(n)$.
Choose a maximal $D$-separated set of centers $(x_i)_{i\in I}$, where
$I=\{1,\ldots,N\}$ or $I=\mathbb N$, and put
\[
 A_i=\overline B_g(x_i,D),\qquad
 B_i=M\setminus B_g(x_i,2D).
\]
Suppose every $B_i$ is nonempty.  Choose positive numbers $p_i^*$ for
$i\in\{0\}\cup I$ such that
\[
 \sum_{i\in\{0\}\cup I}p_i^*=\frac1{20}.
\]
Assume there are a complete smooth metric $h\ge g$ and a finite or
countable family of smooth real functions $(p_\alpha)$ with locally
finite compact supports such that
\begin{equation}
 \dist_h(A_i,B_i)>10+2\pi\sqrt{2/p_i^*}\quad(i\in I),
 \qquad R(h,(p_\alpha))\ge\frac25\quad\hbox{on }M.
\end{equation}
Then there is a continuous map $f:M\to K$ to a simplicial complex of
dimension at most $n-2$, with its usual polyhedral topology, such that
\[
 \sup_{y\in K}\diam_g f^{-1}(y)\le4D+2.
\]
The diameter bounds the entire fiber, including all its components.

statements.title: Quadratic reserve
statements.label: pre:reserve
statements.text:
For every integer $n\ge4$ there is a constant $C(n)<\infty$ with the
following property. If $h$ is a complete smooth metric on a connected
boundaryless $n$-manifold $M$ and $w\in C^\infty(M)$, there are a smooth
complete metric $h^+\ge h$ and a smooth real-valued function $t^+$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \Dcal(h^+,t^+)\ge \Dcal(h,w)+(t^+)^2-C(n)
 \quad\hbox{on }M.
\end{equation}
One may take $C(n)=100n+203$.
statements.section_title: From spectral positivity to a quadratic reserve

statements.title: Signed pressure law
statements.label: pressure:law
statements.text:
For every \(A_0,P_0,\epsilon,b_0>0\), there are constants
\(S_0\in(0,1]\), \(T\ge10\), and a smooth function
\[
 F:(-S_0,S_0)\times\R\longrightarrow\R
\]
that is odd in its first variable and has the following properties.  Set
\begin{equation}
 N(t)=\sqrt{t^2+T^2},\qquad V(t)=N(t)^2=t^2+T^2.
\end{equation}
At every \((x,t)\in(-S_0,S_0)\times\R\),
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
 F_x\ge A_0N(t),\qquad |F_t|\le\epsilon|F|,
       \qquad FF_t\le\epsilon F_x,\\
 F_x\le b_0N(t)^2\quad\text{or}\quad -FF_t\ge P_0F_x,\\
 F_x\le b_0N(t)^2+\epsilon F^2.
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
Moreover, \(F(x,t)\to+\infty\) as \(x\uparrow S_0\) and
\(F(x,t)\to-\infty\) as \(x\downarrow-S_0\), uniformly for \(t\)
in each compact subset of \(\R\).

title: Spontaneous magnetization in the quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet
abstract: For every dimension d ≥ 3 and every spin \(S\in\{\frac12,1,\frac32,\ldots\}\), we prove that the nearest-neighbor isotropic quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet has a translation-invariant, spontaneously magnetized equilibrium state at every sufficiently low positive temperature. The same state satisfies the KMS condition for the zero-field dynamics and has magnetization at least \(S/4\). This resolves the low-temperature ordering problem in the spontaneous-magnetization formulation.

tex.abstract:
For every dimension $d\geq3$ and every spin $S\in\{\frac12,1,\frac32,\ldots\}$,
we prove that the nearest-neighbor isotropic quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet
has a translation-invariant, spontaneously magnetized equilibrium state
at every sufficiently low positive temperature.
The same state satisfies the KMS condition for the zero-field dynamics
and has magnetization at least $S/4$.
This resolves the low-temperature ordering problem in the
spontaneous-magnetization formulation.

finite or a finite set together with $D_0$, and every nonempty finite
single-time set $T$ disjoint from $E$, the return fraction in
\eqref{eq:pin-return-fraction} satisfies

       \mathbb P_E(T\subseteq\mathcal B_E)\le (2r)^{|T|}.

statements.title: Conditional next-pin first moment
statements.label: prop:first-moment
statements.text:
Let \(V=J\sqcup Q\) be a finite set with \(J\ne\varnothing\).
Let \(\Pi\) be a random permutation matrix satisfying
\eqref{eq:exterior-moments}, and put \(K=\mathbb E\Pi\).
Let \(G_J\) be the event that every cycle of \(\Pi\) meets \(J\).
On \(G_J\), let \(\Sigma\) be the column-forward permutation matrix
of the next visit to \(J\) at positive time along the cycles.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P(G_J)=\det(I-K_{QQ}).
 
\end{equation}
If this probability is positive, \(K_{QQ}\) is transient and
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E[\Sigma\mid G_J]
   =H:=K_{JJ}+K_{JQ}(I-K_{QQ})^{-1}K_{QJ}.
 
\end{equation}
The matrix \(H\) is the first positive \(J\)-hitting kernel for the
Markov chain with transition matrix \(K\), using independent transitions
on successive steps.  More strongly, for every complex \(J\times J\)
matrix \(W\),
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E[\det(I-W\Sigma)\mid G_J]=\det(I-WH).
 
\end{equation}
An empty \(Q\) is allowed, with determinant of the empty matrix equal
to one and the Schur correction in \eqref{eq:conditional-first-moment}
equal to zero.
statements.section_title: Exposed paths and a one-particle return identity

statements.title: Probability of irregularity
statements.label: prop:regularity
statements.text:
Fix \(M_*\).  Under \(\mathsf I_p(P)\), for all \(0<p\le p_0\),
all deterministic times \(t\), and all spatial anchors \(x\),
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P_P(t\text{ is not regular for }x)
 \le \delta:=C R^d p^{2d}+C\exp(-cR^\xi),
 \qquad \xi=\nu\gamma>0.
\end{equation}
Here \(R\ge1\), and the constants may depend on \(M_*\) but are
uniform in \(p\le p_0\), volume, period, grid, pin set and anchor.

statements.title: Local Nash inequality
statements.label: prop:local-nash
statements.text:
Fix \(d\ge3\), \(\ell\), and \(M_*\) as in
\eqref{eq:local-radius-choice}.  Let \(\mathcal H_t\) be an available-slot
graph with at least one and at most \(\ell\) slots at every unblocked
site, and suppose \(t\) is regular for \(x\) at scale
\(R\ge M_*+K_{\mathrm{conn}}+3\).
Every nonnegative function \(v\) supported on slots above \(B_R(x)\)
satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \|v\|_2^{2+4/d}\le C\mathcal D_t(v)\|v\|_1^{4/d},
\end{equation}
where \(C\) depends only on \(d,\ell\) and the fixed local radii.

statements.title: Decay of a routed unit flow
statements.label: prop:flow-decay
statements.text:
Let $d\ge3$, $\nu=1/(100d)$, and suppose the anchor $x$ is regular in the
sense of Definition~\ref{def:regular-anchor}.  Fix the local constant
$M_*$ as in~\eqref{eq:local-radius-choice} and take $R$ sufficiently
large in terms of those fixed constants.  For every available slot $a$
at any site $y\in B_R(x)$ there is a flow $J_a$ on the available-slot
graph such that
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{div}J_a=\1_{\{a\}},\qquad
 |J_a(e)|\le C(1+\dist(e,y))^{-k},
 \qquad k=d-1-d\nu.
\end{equation}
In particular, $\sum_e J_a(e)^2<\infty$.

statements.title: Energy for arbitrary injections
statements.label: prop:flow-energy
statements.text:
Let $d\ge3$, $\alpha=1/100$, and $\nu=1/(100d)$.  Fix $M_*$ as in
\eqref{eq:local-radius-choice} and take $R$ sufficiently large as in
Proposition~\ref{prop:flow-decay}.  Let $T$ be a finite
set of $m$ anchor slots with sites $x_i$, satisfying
\[
 \#\{i\in T:x_i\in B_h(z)\}\le L(1+h)^\alpha
 \quad\text{for all }z\in\Z^d,\ h\ge0.
\]
Fix an available-slot graph and a subset $I\subset T$ of anchors regular
for this graph.  For each $i\in I$, let $\mu_i$ be any nonnegative mass
on its slots, supported over $B_R(x_i)$ and satisfying
$\sum_a\mu_i(a)\le1$.  There is a flow $J$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{div}J=\sum_{i\in I}\mu_i,
 \qquad \sum_e J(e)^2\le C|I|R^\alpha\le CmR^\alpha.
\end{equation}
Consequently every finitely supported real function $g$ on the graph
satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \left|\left\langle\sum_{i\in I}\mu_i,g\right\rangle\right|
 \le \bigl(CmR^\alpha\mathcal D(g)\bigr)^{1/2},
 \qquad \mathcal D(g)=\frac12\sum_e(g(e^-)-g(e^+))^2.
\end{equation}
All constants are uniform over the choices of $I$ and of the masses.

statements.title: Expected leakage
statements.label: prop:leakage
statements.text:
Fix the constants in the preceding geometric estimates and choose
$C_*$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem:localization}.  For all sufficiently small
$p>0$, every finite cube, every circular grid of mesh at most $p^{4d}$,
every $E$ consisting of $D_0$ and grid pins, and every disjoint
single-time grid test $T$ satisfying \eqref{eq:leakage-growth}, assume
$\mathsf I_p(P)$ for $P=E\cup T$.  If $\beta\ge5s$, then, for
each of the forward and reverse propagations,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E_P\bigl[\|f\|_2^2-\|C_{2s}f\|_2^2\bigr]
             \ge m[1-\varepsilon(p)],
\end{equation}
where one may take
\begin{equation}
 \varepsilon(p)=C\left[e^{-cs}
       +R^\alpha\left(s^{-d/2}+\delta+s^{-1}\right)\right],
 \qquad \delta=C R^d p^{2d}+C e^{-cR^\xi}.
\end{equation}
All constants are independent of the volume, period, grid, pin sets,
and final $p$.
statements.section_title: Heat-flow leakage and the pin bootstrap

statements.title: Uniform pin estimate
statements.label: thm:pin-bootstrap
statements.text:
For every integer $d\ge3$ and integer slot multiplicity $\ell\ge1$, there
exist $L\ge\max\{2d,\ell,4\}$ and $p_*\in(0,1/4)$ with the
following property.  Let $0<p\le p_*$ and
$\beta\ge5p^{-11/10}$.  In any finite cube $\Lambda$, choose a
finite circular time grid containing zero and of mesh at most
$p^{4d}$.  Let $E$ consist of $D_0$ and any subset of the slot
points on this grid.  Then every nonempty test $T$ at a single grid
time, disjoint from $E$ and satisfying
\eqref{eq:leakage-growth}, obeys
\begin{equation}
                  \mathbb P_E(T\subseteq\mathcal B_E)\le p^{|T|}.
\end{equation}
In particular, with $p=p_*$ and
$\beta_0=5p_*^{-11/10}<\infty$, for every finite
$\beta\ge\beta_0$, every cube, and every slot $j$ at time zero,
\begin{equation}
                  \mathbb P_{D_0}(j\in\mathcal B_{D_0})\le p_*.
\end{equation}
The constants depend only on $d$ and $\ell$.
statements.section_title: Heat-flow leakage and the pin bootstrap

statements.title: An explicit vanishing-field limit
statements.label: prop:magnetized-limit
statements.text:
For \(N\geq1\), set
\[
 h_N=N^{-1/2},\qquad K_N=H_N-h_NM_N,
 \qquad
 \rho_N^{\mathrm{in}}(C)=
   \frac{\Tr(e^{-\beta K_N}C)}{\Tr(e^{-\beta K_N})}
 \quad(C\in\mathcal A_{\Lambda_N}).
\]
Extend \(\rho_N^{\mathrm{in}}\) to a state \(\rho_N\) on
\(\mathcal A\) by the product normalized trace outside \(\Lambda_N\),
and define
\begin{equation}
 \omega_N(A)=\frac1{V_N}\sum_{x\in\Lambda_N}\rho_N(T_x(A)).
\end{equation}
There is a subsequence \(N_j\to\infty\) on which \(\omega_{N_j}\)
converges pointwise on \(\mathcal A\) to a translation-invariant state
\(\omega\), and every such subsequential limit satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \omega(S_0^z)\geq S/4.
\end{equation}

title: Square-lattice FK interfaces and nested loops for 1 <= q < 4
abstract: For every fixed \(1\le q\lt 4\), critical square-lattice random-cluster Dobrushin interfaces converge as ordered curves to chordal \(\mathop{\mathrm{SLE}}\nolimits _{\kappa(q)}\), where \(\kappa(q)=4\pi/\arccos(-\sqrt q/2)\), confirming the Rohde–Schramm prediction in this parameter range. This holds in every bounded Jordan domain under uniform marked boundary approximation. The complete nested plane loop collections converge to whole-plane \(\mathop{\mathrm{CLE}}\nolimits _{\kappa(q)}\) in a spherical matching topology retaining multiplicities and traversals. At q = 1 we obtain Cardy's formula for square-lattice bond percolation with free boundary edges.

tex.abstract:
For every fixed $1\le q<4$, critical square-lattice random-cluster
Dobrushin interfaces converge as ordered curves to chordal
$\SLE_{\kappa(q)}$, where $\kappa(q)=4\pi/\arccos(-\sqrt q/2)$,
confirming the Rohde--Schramm prediction in this parameter range.
This holds in every bounded Jordan domain under uniform marked boundary
approximation. The complete nested plane loop collections converge
to whole-plane $\CLE_{\kappa(q)}$ in a spherical matching topology
retaining multiplicities and traversals. At $q=1$ we obtain Cardy's
formula for square-lattice bond percolation with free boundary edges.

statements.title: Interfaces and all nested loops
statements.label: intro:main
statements.text:
For every fixed real $1\le q<4$, the following assertions hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item For every bounded Jordan domain $D$ with distinct boundary marks
$a,b$, and every approximation satisfying
\eqref{intro:marked-jordan}, the Dobrushin strand $\eta_n$ converges in
law, in \eqref{intro:curve-metric}, to chordal $\SLE_{\kappa(q)}$ from
$a$ to $b$ in $D$.
\item Under the specified free infinite-volume law,
$\Gamma_\delta$ converges in law as $\delta\downarrow0$ to the nested
whole-plane $\CLE_{\kappa(q)}$, in the spherical collection topology
just defined.  The limit is M\"obius invariant.
\end{enumerate}
Both conclusions hold along every mesh sequence.  No uniformity in $q$
is asserted.

statements.title: Cardy's formula for square-lattice bond percolation
statements.label: intro:cardy

statements.title: Square-bond arm and thermodynamic exponents
statements.label: intro:bond-exponents

statements.title: Three logarithmic comparisons
statements.label: exp:comparisons

statements.title: Balanced corner parities
statements.label: exp:polygon-budget
statements.text:
Let a fixed simple rectilinear polygon have $m$ concave and $m+4$
convex true corners, with wire changes in side interiors. It has tile
approximants differing by $O(1)$ mesh units such that at least
$\lfloor m/2\rfloor$ corners of each relative wire type occur in each
of the convex and concave sets, also after global wire reversal.
For these approximants,
\begin{equation}
 3P+D_*+\sum_{v\,\mathrm{convex}}C_{i(v)}
       +\sum_{v\,\mathrm{concave}}L_{i(v)}
 \le\frac12P-\frac32D_*+o(\log n).
\end{equation}
Each fixed family of negative endpoint charges with magnitudes summing
to one has total wrong-to-correct local logarithmic cost at most
$-P+o(\log n)$.

statements.title: Angular transfer estimate
statements.label: bulk:angular-estimate
statements.text:
Fix a compact interval $I\subset(-v,v)$. Let $B_{\rm in}$ be a
product of $P_\zeta$ rows and $B_{\rm out}$ a product of $P_\xi$ rows,
at real angles in $[-v,v]$. Suppose each product contains at least
$n\ge1$ angles in $I$. Uniformly for $x,y\in[-v,v]$,
\begin{align}
 \|B_{\rm out}N(x)B_{\rm in}\|&\le Cn^{-1+\rho},
 \\
 \|B_{\rm out}\{N(x)-e^{i\tau(x-y)}N(y)\}B_{\rm in}\|
 &\le Cn^{-1-\rho}.
\end{align}
The constant depends on $q$ and $I$. Boundedly many additional pairs
of before-twist rows may be inserted immediately to the right of
$N$, and additional pairs of after-twist rows immediately to its
left. The two terms in \eqref{bulk:high-estimate} may use different
such insertions; on each side their counts must be even. The
constant may depend on a bound for these counts. Multiplication of
$D$ by a common scalar multiplies the bounds by its absolute value.

The same estimates hold in the physical square array sliced in a
diagonal time direction: its time angles are $\pm\gamma_0$, where
$\gamma_0=\pi/4$, and its space angles alternate between
$\pi-\gamma_0$ and $\gamma_0$. The exterior states may contain any
finite number of physical row and spin insertions outside the
sandwich. A scalar contraction is bounded by the displayed rate
times the two reflection norms, with the squares centered on a cut
included in its reflection kernel.
statements.section_title: Angular transfer and its two leading modes

statements.title: Extraction in a clear slab
statements.label: cur:slab-estimate
statements.text:
Suppose a diagonal-time slab of macroscopic thickness about a
low or high stencil contains no other non-diagonal tensors or
endpoints. Diagonal chains may cross the slab. The stencil has an
intact neighborhood disjoint from all other chains except its
own prefix, and the slab has spare margins for routing and cuts.
Bounded lattice errors are permitted inside these margins.
Then the stencil contraction can be written as the corresponding
low or high expression in Theorem \ref{bulk:angular-estimate},
between exterior states independent of the choice of stencil
term. Only boundedly many compensating pairs of rows and a
common bounded scalar are introduced.

In particular, if the two clear parts of the slab contain at
least $n$ physical steps, its scalar contraction is bounded by
$Cn^{-1+\rho}$ for a low stencil, and by $Cn^{-1-\rho}$ for a
high stencil, times the two exterior reflection norms. Reflected
stencils satisfy the same statement.
statements.section_title: Local path calculus for the current

statements.title: Identification of a holomorphic subsequential limit
statements.label: four:conditional-map
statements.text:
Suppose an interior subsequential limit $h$ of $h_n$ is holomorphic in
the ordinary complex coordinate, and pass simultaneously to a limit
$r$ of $P_{\mathfrak A}$.  Then $0<r<1$.  Put
\begin{equation}
 U_0=r+d(1-r),\qquad V_0=dr+1-r,\qquad T_0=r+y(1-r).
 
\end{equation}
The function $h$ maps $\Omega$ conformally onto the interior of the
simple polygon with successive vertices $0,U_0,T_0,yV_0$, taking
$p,b,c,d_0$ to those vertices.  If a conformal half-plane coordinate
takes the marks to $0,\chi,1,\infty$, respectively, then
\begin{equation}
 r=\frac{\displaystyle\int_1^\infty
        u^{\rho-1}|u-\chi|^{\rho-1}|u-1|^{1-3\rho}\,du}
       {\displaystyle\int_\chi^\infty
        u^{\rho-1}|u-\chi|^{\rho-1}|u-1|^{1-3\rho}\,du}.
 
\end{equation}
Under deterministic separate $\mathfrak A$ caps the corresponding
crossing probability is $r/(r+d(1-r))$.
statements.section_title: The four-change observable and its boundary values

statements.title: Complete-wall factorization
statements.label: wall:factorization
statements.text:
For the complete wall, there are probe-independent complex numbers
$a_n(R_0,L)$, bounded above and away from zero in modulus for the fixed
large $L$, such that
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal H_{\rm full}(z,u)
       =a_n(R_0,L)h_n(z)J_n(u)+o(1)
 
\end{equation}
uniformly on interior compact probe sets.  The error tends to zero
with mesh first and then $R_0\to\infty$.  No limit of $a_n$ is asserted
or needed.

statements.title: Gap closure
statements.label: gap:closure
statements.text:
Keep the distant charges and their locations fixed.  Let $g$ denote
the gapped wall and $f$ the wall obtained by closing the specified
$h$-gaps, retaining any other gaps and tip factors.  There are positive
probe-independent numbers $b_n$, bounded above and below, such that
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal H_g(z,u)=b_n\mathcal H_f(z,u)+o(1)
 
\end{equation}
uniformly on interior compact probe sets.  The error vanishes in the
mesh limit followed by $h\to0$.  Constants may depend on the fixed
remaining features.  In particular, a second, smaller collection of
gaps may be closed before the first collection.

statements.title: Mixed derivative saving
statements.label: hol:mixed-bound
statements.text:
For fixed primary gaps and sufficiently small fixed secondary gaps
chosen as in Lemma~\ref{hol:templates}, there is $c>0$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \left| (\delta_{1,z}^{(2)}+i\delta_{2,z}^{(2)})
               \delta_{j,u}^{(2)}\mathcal H_g(z,u)\right|
       =O(n^{-2-c})
 
\end{equation}
uniformly on the eligible compact probe sets.  The constants and
reflection-tree size may depend on these fixed gaps.

statements.title: Holomorphic disk limit
statements.label: hol:disk
statements.text:
For every rational orthogonal polygon with the four flat marks and
balanced approximations specified above, every locally continuous
subsequential limit of $h_n$ is holomorphic.  Consequently the boundary
identification and crossing formula of
Proposition~\ref{four:conditional-map} hold without its holomorphicity
premise for these polygons.

statements.title: Jordan-quad transfer
statements.label: jordan:transfer
statements.text:
Consider the marked, uniformly convergent square lattice polygon
approximations $(D_n;a_n,b_n,c_n,d_n)$ to a bounded Jordan quadrilateral
$(D;a,b,c,d)$ in the four-mark sense of Subsection~\ref{intro:crossings}.
Keep every edge of the polygon graph random, and separately wire the two closed arcs $a_nb_n$ and
$c_nd_n$, with no other primal identifications.  If
$\psi:D\to\mathbb H$ sends $(a,c,d)$ to $(0,1,\infty)$ and
$\chi=\psi(b)$, the probability of an actual open path between these
arcs tends to $g(\chi)$.

statements.title: The prescribed bond-percolation crossing
statements.label: jordan:cardy
statements.text:
At $q=1$, with every edge, including every boundary edge, sampled
independently with probability $1/2$ and with no wiring, the probability
of the event $C_n$ defined in Subsection~\ref{intro:crossings} tends to
\[
 \frac{\displaystyle\int_0^\chi [t(1-t)]^{-2/3}\,dt}
      {\displaystyle\int_0^1 [t(1-t)]^{-2/3}\,dt}.
\]

statements.title: Moving four-change test
statements.label: moving:slit
statements.text:
Let a four-change strand in $V_n$ be stopped before completing its
strand, revealing only the switches it has encountered.  Let $U_n$
be its remaining simple slit disk, with the tip as the new starting
mark.  Consider histories for which a fixed basepoint has a fixed
positive disk in $U_n$, and the four prime-end marks in a disk chart
normalized at that basepoint remain mutually separated by a fixed
positive amount.  Then, on these histories,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P_{\mathrm{open}}(E_{\mathrm P}\mid\mathcal F_n)
       -f(\chi_{U_n})\ \longrightarrow\ 0
 \quad\hbox{in probability}.
\end{equation}
Here $E_{\mathrm P}$ is the primal pairing event, equivalently the
actual bridge event after separate primal closure, and $\chi_{U_n}$
is its current ordered cross-ratio.  The assertion holds for arbitrary
mesh-dependent stopping rules satisfying this localization.

statements.title: Driving convergence
statements.label: chordal:driver

statements.title: No return from a small target cap
statements.label: chordal:target
statements.text:
After the strand first enters a shrinking initial conformal cap
around its target, the probability of a subsequent displacement of
fixed positive physical size tends to zero.

statements.title: Dobrushin convergence for $1\le q<4$
statements.label: chordal:trace
statements.text:
For every bounded marked Jordan domain and every marked uniform
polygon approximation satisfying Equation~\eqref{intro:marked-jordan}
with the boundary conventions of Subsection~\ref{intro:model}, the Dobrushin
strand converges in law, in the uniform Euclidean oriented-curve
topology modulo increasing reparametrization, to chordal
$\mathrm{SLE}_{\kappa(q)}$.

statements.title: Tests away from coincidence
statements.label: peel:martingales
statements.text:
For $x>0$ beyond these localization bounds, the quantities
\begin{equation}
 M_t(x)=\left(\frac{xg_t'(x)}{g_t(x)-W_t^{\mathbb H}}\right)^h
\end{equation}
satisfy the approximate martingale identities between arbitrary causal
stops on the segment.  Tests may include the entire earlier exploration
history of finitely many targets.  The errors tend to zero after the
mesh limit.  The assertion concerns the averaged identities for this
history law, not a uniform assertion over all deterministic mazes.

statements.title: The endpoint convention is determined
statements.label: tree:reflection
statements.section_title: Identification of the joint angular tree

statements.title: Joint target tree
statements.label: tree:joint-law
statements.text:
For every finite family of deterministic interior targets, the peeling
converges in its joint radial driving data to the target-invariant
branching radial $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa(\kappa-6)$ tree.  Branches agree
until their target kernels separate and then have independent
continuation noises.  At successive full turns the force side is
reversed, equivalently the angular gap remains instantaneously
reflected on $[0,2\pi]$.
statements.section_title: Identification of the joint angular tree

statements.title: Identification away from the square wall
statements.label: loop:identification
statements.text:
Every positive lattice-limit loop with an interior point has a
canonical label.  Matched elements have the same winding indicators
on $\mathcal Z$.  If either matched element stays away from the square
wall, the two elements are equal as curves modulo reparametrization
and orientation.  Without that restriction, every canonical element
is still contained in order in its lattice-limit partner.
statements.section_title: Recovery of the nested loop collection

statements.title: Nested full-plane convergence for $q<4$
statements.label: loop:plane
statements.text:
For every fixed $1\le q<4$, the loop collection of the free
infinite-volume critical square-lattice FK law converges, through the
full mesh sequence, to the nested whole-plane
$\mathrm{CLE}_{\kappa(q)}$ in the spherical loop-matching topology
of Subsection~\ref{intro:collections}.  The limit is M\"obius invariant and includes every
nested generation.

title: Squared-logarithmic randomized k-server on arbitrary metrics
abstract: We prove that randomized k-server has competitive ratio \(O((\log(k+1))^2)\) on every metric space against oblivious request sequences, matching the known worst-case lower bound. For each metric and initial configuration, one policy works for all finite request sequences, including on infinite and unbounded spaces. When the initial server positions are distinct, no additive term is needed.

tex.abstract:
We prove that randomized \(k\)-server has competitive ratio
\(O((\log(k+1))^2)\) on every metric space against oblivious request
sequences, matching the known worst-case lower bound. For each metric
and initial configuration, one policy works for all finite request
sequences, including on infinite and unbounded spaces. When the initial
server positions are distinct, no additive term is needed.
sections: Finite laws, posterior motion, and the proof architecture
Allocation on a separated tree: rank data
Feasible outputs and completion of the allocation bound
A compact potential for partition edits
Online partitions and the embedded comparator
Balanced rounding and realization in the metric
One policy on an arbitrary metric space

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is an absolute constant \(C<\infty\) such that, for every
integer \(k\ge2\), every metric space \((X,d)\) with at least \(k+1\)
points, and every \(s\in X^k\), there exist a randomized online policy
\(A\) and a finite \(B\ge0\) satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \E\,\cost_{A,s}(\sigma)
 \le C\bigl(\log(k+1)\bigr)^2\OPT_{X,d,k,s}(\sigma)+B
\end{equation}
for every finite request sequence \(\sigma\).
The constant \(C\) is independent of every property of the metric.
The number \(B\) may depend on \((X,d),k,s\), but not on the sequence
or its length. The same policy serves all finite sequences and
horizons. If the initial positions are distinct, one may take \(B=0\).

statements.title: Budget for summably weighted templates
statements.label: cor:pilot-edits
statements.text:
Let templates be indexed by a finite or countable set $I$, with fixed
weights $\omega_\alpha\ge0$.  Each template has fixed admissible
parameters and the drift constant $C_{\mathrm{dr},\alpha}$ of
Lemma~\ref{lem:pilot-drift}.  Assume
\[
 A:=\sum_{\alpha\in I}\omega_\alpha<\infty,
 \qquad
 B:=\sum_{\alpha\in I}\omega_\alpha C_{\mathrm{dr},\alpha}<\infty.
\]
At each step, filter and drift the counting measure while keeping the
previous functions $g_{\alpha,j}$ fixed.  Then edit these functions using
the new history, retaining their template bounds.  Suppose the weighted
total potential drop in the edit stage is at least a nonnegative charge
$c_t$, taking $c_t=0$ on steps without edits.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \E\sum_t c_t
 \le B\ell Q+2kA\sum_{j=1}^Jr_j
 \le B\ell Q+\frac{2kr_0A}{\tau-1}.
 
\end{equation}
In particular, if $A,B$ are absolute constants, the multiplicative
budget is $O(\ell Q)$ and the additive bound is independent of the input
law and horizon.
statements.section_title: A compact potential for partition edits

statements.title: Embedded comparator cost
statements.label: prop:embedded-cost
statements.text:
There are finite alphabets \(\mathcal A_1,\ldots,\mathcal A_J\), depending
only on \(Y,k\) and the fixed constants, and online random maps
\[
 \xi_t:Y\longrightarrow\mathcal A_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal A_J
\]
with the following properties.  Each coordinate cell at level \(j\) has
diameter at most \(40r_j\) and an anchor within \(20r_j\) of all its points.
Thus \(\xi_t\) is injective.  Give the full alphabet tree the leaf distance
\(r_{j-1}\) when the first differing coordinate is \(j\).  For the selected
hidden members \(X_t^1,\ldots,X_t^k\),
\begin{equation}
 P:=\E\sum_t\sum_{a=1}^k
 d_{\mathcal T}\bigl(\xi_{t-1}(X_{t-1}^a),\xi_t(X_t^a)\bigr)
 \le C\ell Q+D_{\rm part}.
\end{equation}
Here \(C\) is absolute and \(D_{\rm part}<\infty\) is independent of the
input law and its horizon.  A coordinate label common to successive maps
has a fixed anchor, except for the explicit heavy-ball reuse below, when
its anchor moves by at most \(40r_j\).
statements.section_title: Online partitions and the embedded comparator

statements.title: Retained-anchor travel
statements.label: prop:anchor-travel
statements.text:
There is an absolute constant $C$ and a finite constant $D_{\rm anchor}$,
independent of the input law and horizon, such that
\begin{equation}
 T_{\rm anchor}\le C\bigl(V+\ell P+\ell Q\bigr)+D_{\rm anchor}.
\end{equation}
Consequently the expected cost of moving the new parked masses with
their retained anchors is at most $40T_{\rm anchor}$.  No multiplicative
constant in this statement depends on the number of levels or on $k$.

statements.title: Rounding and metric realization
statements.label: prop:rounding
statements.text:
Assume the fractional allocations and anchors constructed in the preceding
sections, with $\tau\ge22$.  They admit a causal rounding satisfying
\eqref{eq:rounding-invariants} for which
\begin{equation}
 N_{\rm rnd}:=\E\sum_{t=1}^H\sum_{v\ne{\rm root}}
                 r_{|v|-1}|n_v(t)-n_v(t-1)|\le132V.
\end{equation}
Placing the integer parks at their current anchors gives simulated
configurations $S_t$ of exactly $k$ members containing each current request.
There is a matching of consecutive configurations with expected total cost
at most
\begin{equation}
                         120N_{\rm rnd}+40T_{\rm anchor}.
\end{equation}
Consequently their expected movement is at most
$C(V+\ell P+\ell Q)+D$ for an absolute $C$ and a finite additive term $D$
depending only on the fixed finite structure.
statements.section_title: Balanced rounding and realization in the metric

title: Squarefree values of quartics and power-free values of polynomials
abstract: We prove that every irreducible integer quartic with no fixed prime-square divisor takes squarefree values with the predicted positive Euler-product density. More generally, we obtain the corresponding \((d-2)\)-power-free density in degrees \(4\le d\le8\). The proof combines number-field factorization, determinant estimates with adaptive auxiliary primes, and explicit low-degree geometry. Together with Browning's theorem for higher degrees, this gives the \((d-2)\)-power-free density for every d ≥ 4.

tex.abstract:
We prove that every irreducible integer quartic with no fixed prime-square
divisor takes squarefree values with the predicted positive Euler-product
density. More generally, we obtain the corresponding $(d-2)$-power-free
density in degrees $4\le d\le8$. The proof combines number-field factorization,
determinant estimates with adaptive auxiliary primes, and explicit
low-degree geometry. Together with Browning's theorem for higher degrees,
this gives the $(d-2)$-power-free density for every $d\ge4$.
sections: From a large-prime tail to the exact density
Affine counting with adaptive auxiliary primes
Weighted Hilbert bounds from selected pairs
Parameters and an exact finite certificate
The cyclotomic quartic as a worked example

statements.label: thm:density
statements.text:
Let $f\in\Z[x]$ be irreducible over $\Q$, of degree $d$ with
$4\le d\le8$, and put $k=d-2$. If \eqref{eq:local-admissibility} holds,
then
\[
 S_{f,k}(X)=c_{f,k}X+o_f(X),\qquad
 c_{f,k}=\prod_p\left(1-\frac{\rho_f(p^k)}{p^k}\right)>0.
\]
No primitivity or sign condition on the leading coefficient is required.

statements.label: cor:all-degrees
statements.text:
Let $f\in\Z[x]$ be irreducible over $\Q$ of degree $d\ge4$, and
put $k=d-2$. If $f$ has no fixed prime $k$th-power divisor, then
\[
 S_{f,k}(X)=c_{f,k}X+o_f(X),\qquad
 c_{f,k}=\prod_p\left(1-\frac{\rho_f(p^k)}{p^k}\right)>0.
\]

statements.title: Separable products and simultaneous values
statements.label: cor:separable-products
statements.text:
Fix an integer $k\ge2$. Let $F\in\Z[x]\setminus\{0\}$ be separable over
$\Q$, with every nonconstant irreducible factor of degree at most $k+2$.
If $\rho_F(p^k)<p^k$ for every prime $p$, then
\[
 S_{F,k}(N)=c_{F,k}N+o_{F,k}(N),\qquad
 c_{F,k}=\prod_p\left(1-\frac{\rho_F(p^k)}{p^k}\right)>0.
\]
More generally, let $\mathbf F=(F_1,\ldots,F_r)$, with $r\ge1$, be a fixed
family of nonzero integer polynomials, each separable over $\Q$ with all
nonconstant irreducible factors of degree at most $k+2$. Factors may be
shared by different $F_i$. Put
\[
 \Omega_p=\{a\in\Z/p^k\Z:p^k\mid F_i(a)\text{ for at least one }i\}.
\]
Let $S_{\mathbf F,k}(N)$ count the integers $1\le n\le N$ for which every
$F_i(n)$ is $k$-power-free. If $\#\Omega_p<p^k$ for every prime $p$, then
\[
 S_{\mathbf F,k}(N)=c_{\mathbf F,k}N+o_{\mathbf F,k}(N),\qquad
 c_{\mathbf F,k}=\prod_p\left(1-\frac{\#\Omega_p}{p^k}\right)>0.
\]

statements.label: prop:large-prime-tail
statements.text:
Let $f\in\Z[x]$ be primitive and irreducible, with positive leading
coefficient and degree $4\le d\le8$. Put $k=d-2$. There exists
$\delta=\delta_f>0$ such that
\[
 \#\{n\in\Z:X<n\le2X,\ p^k\mid f(n)
          \text{ for some prime }p>X\}
 \ll_f X^{1-\delta}.
\]

statements.title: Sieve transfer
statements.label: prop:sieve-transfer
statements.text:
Let $f\in\Z[x]$ be irreducible over $\Q$, of degree $d\ge2$, and let
$k\ge2$. Suppose that $\rho_f(p^k)<p^k$ for every prime $p$.
Write
\[
 f=s c g,\qquad s\in\{-1,1\},\quad c\in\N,
\]
where $c$ is the positive content of $f$ and $g\in\Z[x]$ is primitive
with positive leading coefficient. Assume that
\begin{equation}
 T_g(X):=\#\{n\in\Z:X<n\le2X,\ p^k\mid g(n)
                 \text{ for some prime }p>X\}=o_{g,k}(X).
 
\end{equation}
Then
\[
 S_{f,k}(N)=c_{f,k}N+o_{f,k}(N),\qquad
 c_{f,k}=\prod_p\left(1-\frac{\rho_f(p^k)}{p^k}\right)>0.
\]
statements.section_title: From a large-prime tail to the exact density

statements.label: thm:affine-counting
statements.text:
Fix integers $1\le r\le N$, a degree bound $e_0$, a constant $C$, positive coordinate
weights $\omega_l$, and positive numbers $\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_r$.
For $X\ge2$, let $S\subseteq\Z^N$ satisfy
\[
 |z_l|\le C X^{\omega_l}\quad(z\in S),
\]
and suppose $S$ lies on an algebraic set $Z$ of degree at most $e_0$
and dimension at most $r$.  Assume the following uniform alternative.
For every fixed degree bound $e$, each irreducible subvariety
$A\subseteq Z$ defined over $\Q$, of degree at most $e$ and dimension
$h>0$, meeting $S$, satisfies either
\begin{equation}
 |S\cap A|\ll_{e,\alpha} X^\alpha
 \quad\text{for every fixed }\alpha>0,
\end{equation}
or
\begin{equation}
 H_A(T)\ge \frac{T^h}{h!\delta_h^h}-C_eT^{h-1}
 \quad(T\ge1).
\end{equation}
The constants in these alternatives are uniform in $X,Z,S,A$.
Put $E_h=\max_{h\le s\le r}\delta_s$.  Then, for every $\eps>0$,
\begin{equation}
 |S|\ll_\eps X^{E_1+\cdots+E_r+\eps}.
\end{equation}
The implied constant depends only on the fixed data and the uniform
constants in the hypotheses.  In particular, no bound on the
coefficients initially defining $Z$ is required.
statements.section_title: Affine counting with adaptive auxiliary primes

statements.label: prop:archimedean-cuts
statements.text:
Fix positive upper exponents $\eta_+,b_+$.  Consider a paired box
as in Lemma~\ref{lem:paired-boxes}, with
integer coordinates satisfying
\[
 |x_i|\ll X^{\eta_+/d},\qquad |y_i|\ll X^{b_+/d}.
\]
Assume that its normalized chart variables have width \(O(X^{-w})\),
that \(z=1/n=O(X^{-1})\), and that the forward and reverse analytic
chart functions have the uniform derivative bounds of that lemma.
Let \(t_*,w>0\) be fixed rational numbers satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 w^{d-1}H(t_*)&>
 \left(\frac{(d+1)(\eta_++b_+t_*)}{d^2}\right)^d,\\
 w^{d-2}\min\{H_a(t_*),H_b(t_*)\}&>
 \left(\frac{\eta_++b_+t_*}{d-1}\right)^{d-1}.
 \end{split}
 
\end{equation}
For sufficiently large \(X\), the points in this box lie on a bounded
number of bounded-degree algebraic sets of the following two types:
\begin{enumerate}
\item a mixed hypersurface section of \(\mathcal V\), whose bicone is
a prime complete intersection with one additional equation of
bidegree \((\lambda,s_0)\), where \(\lambda,s_0\geq1\);
\item a set of biprojective dimension at most \(d-2\).
\end{enumerate}
On returning to the affine equations \(a_i^kb_i=n-\theta_i\), the
corresponding dimensions are \(d\) and at most \(d-1\).
All number and degree bounds are uniform over the boxes and \(X\).

statements.label: prop:lattice-boxes
statements.text:
For the paired boxes of Lemma~\ref{lem:paired-boxes}, assume the
coordinate bounds above and fix parameters satisfying
\eqref{eq:lattice-parameters}. The paired boxes can be grouped into
finitely many ranges indexed by $j=\ell\tau$, $\ell\in\Z_{\ge0}$,
with $j\le m/d$. The number of paired boxes in range $j$ is
\begin{equation}
 O\bigl(X^{m-dj}\bigr).
\end{equation}
For each paired box there are integral unimodular changes
$x\leftrightarrow x'$ and $y\leftrightarrow y'$ such that all
its selected points satisfy
\begin{equation}
 |x'_i|\ll X^U,\qquad |y'_i|\ll X^V,
 \qquad U=u+j+\tau,\quad V=v+j+\tau.
\end{equation}
The matrices of these changes and their inverses have entries
bounded by a fixed power of $X$.

statements.label: prop:weighted-hilbert
statements.text:
For each nonzero coefficient polynomial \(f_I\), define
\[
 \nu_{i,I}=\operatorname{ord}_{n-\theta_i}f_I,\qquad
 e_i=\min_I(I_i+k\nu_{i,I}),
\]
and put
\begin{equation}
 D=\max_I\{U|I|+(kU+V)\deg f_I\}-U\sum_i e_i.
 
\end{equation}
Then \(D>0\), and the weighted filtered Hilbert function of the
pair image satisfies
\begin{equation}
 H_{Y_{\mathrm{pair}}}(T)=
 \frac{(kU+V)^{h-1}D}{U^hV^h}\frac{T^h}{h!}
 +O(T^{h-1}+1).
 
\end{equation}
This is a lower bound for \(H_Y(T)\).
If the function field degree of \(Y\) over its pair image is at least
two, the leading coefficient in this lower bound can be doubled.
For fixed weights and bounded degree of \(Y\), all error constants
are uniform, independently of the coefficients of its equations.
statements.section_title: Weighted Hilbert bounds from selected pairs

statements.label: prop:quartic-surface
statements.text:
Let $Y$ be a geometrically irreducible surface defined over $\Q$ in the
rational coordinates of the arithmetic boxes.  Suppose that it meets the open
$a_1a_2a_3a_4\ne0$, satisfies
\[
 a_i^2b_i=n-\theta_i\qquad(1\le i\le4),
\]
and that $n$ is nonconstant and algebraic over the field generated by
$a_1,\ldots,a_4$.
Give the two coordinate blocks positive rational weights $U,V$,
respectively, and put
\[
 D_0=\min(3U,2V,U+V).
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 H_Y(T)\ge \frac{T^2}{2}
    \min\left\{\frac{(2U+V)D_0}{U^2V^2},\frac3{U^2}\right\}-O(T).
\end{equation}
For fixed weights and a bound on $\deg Y$, the error is uniform in the
moving coordinate changes and defining equations.

statements.label: prop:quintic-discard
statements.text:
There are finitely many polynomials $\Phi\in L[t]$ of degree five with
distinct critical points $z_1=0,z_2=1,z_3,z_4$ satisfying
\[
 \Phi(z_i)=\theta_i\qquad(1\le i\le4).
\]
Let $\mathcal F_f$ be this finite family and put
\[
 \mathcal E_f=
  \{n\in\Z:n=\Phi(z)\text{ for some }
                    \Phi\in\mathcal F_f, z\in L\}.
\]
Then, for $X\ge1$,
\begin{equation}
 \#\bigl(\mathcal E_f\cap[-2X,2X]\bigr)\ll_f X^{1/5}.
\end{equation}
Moreover, if $N(s)\in L[s]$ has degree five and distinct critical
points $\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_4\in L$ with
$N(\tau_i)=\theta_i$, every integer value $N(s)$ at $s\in L$ belongs
to $\mathcal E_f$.

statements.title: Curve alternatives
statements.label: prop:curve-alternatives
statements.text:
Put
\[
 g=(d-1)(k-1)+\mathbf 1_{d=4},\qquad
 \delta_1(U,V)=\max\{U/2,\min(U,V/g)\}.
\]
Fix a degree bound $E$, and let $C$ be a geometrically irreducible
curve of degree at most $E$, defined over $\Q$, in the arithmetic
variety $a_i^k b_i=n-\theta_i$ in the coordinates just described.
For every $\eps>0$, either
\[
 |S\cap C|\ll_{f,E,\eps}X^\eps,
\]
or its filtered Hilbert dimension, with weight $U$ on $x'$ and weight
$V$ on $y'$, satisfies
\begin{equation}
 H_C(T)\ge \frac{T}{\delta_1(U,V)}-O_{f,E}(1).
\end{equation}
The implied constants may also depend on a fixed compact subset of
$(0,\infty)$ containing $U,V$.  They are otherwise uniform in the
weights and in the integral coordinate changes.  In particular they
are uniform for the weights arising from
Proposition~\ref{prop:lattice-boxes}.

statements.title: Parameter choice
statements.label: prop:parameter-certificate
statements.text:
For each $d\in\{4,5,6,7,8\}$, the stopping index in
\eqref{eq:parameter-stop} is the one listed in
Table~\ref{tab:parameter-certificate}.  For every integer
$K_0\le z<z_d$, there are positive rational numbers $t_*,w$ such that,
with $m=(d-1)w$,
\begin{equation}
\begin{gathered}
 0<m<1,\qquad \min(\eta_-,b_-)>m,\\
 w^{d-1}H(t_*)>
 \left(\frac{(d+1)(\eta_++b_+t_*)}{d^2}\right)^d,\\
 w^{d-2}\min\{H_a(t_*),H_b(t_*)\}>
 \left(\frac{\eta_++b_+t_*}{d-1}\right)^{d-1}.
\end{gathered}

\end{equation}
In particular, the cut conditions \eqref{eq:cut-conditions} hold.
For
\[
 u=\frac{\eta_+-m}{d},\qquad
 v=\frac{b_+-m}{d},
\]
these choices also satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \frac3{20}\le\frac vu\le5,\qquad
 m+\sum_{h=1}^dE_h(u,v)<\frac{999}{1000},
 \qquad
 m+2u<\frac{999}{1000}\quad(\text{mode }\mathsf Q).
 
\end{equation}
Moreover, for either fixed mode, every $U,V>0$ with
$3/20\le V/U\le5$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \delta_h(U+s,V+s)\le\delta_h(U,V)+s
 \quad(s\ge0,\ 1\le h\le d).
 
\end{equation}

statements.label: cor:cyclotomic-density
statements.text:
Put
\[
 c_8=\prod_{p\equiv1\pmod8}\left(1-\frac4{p^2}\right).
\]
Then $c_8>3/4$, and
\[
 \#\{1\le n\le X:n^4+1\text{ is squarefree}\}=c_8X+o(X).
\]
Consequently, for every sufficiently large real $N$,
\[
 \#\{n\in\Z:N\le n\le2N,\ n^4+1\text{ is squarefree}\}
 \ge N/2.
\]

title: Stabilizer orbits and thick tensor ideals of dualizable K(n)-local spectra
abstract: We classify the prime and radical ideals of the Lubin–Tate deformation ring invariant under an open Morava stabilizer subgroup, at every prime and positive height. This proves Chai's invariant-ideal conjecture in the standard finite-residue-field formulation. It also proves the Hovey–Strickland conjecture: the dualizable \(K(n)\)-local category has exactly \(n+2\) thick tensor ideals, and its Balmer spectrum is a chain of \(n+1\) points.

tex.abstract:
We classify the prime and radical ideals of the Lubin--Tate deformation
ring invariant under an open Morava stabilizer subgroup, at every prime
and positive height.  This proves Chai's invariant-ideal conjecture in
the standard finite-residue-field formulation.  It also proves the
Hovey--Strickland conjecture: the dualizable \(K(n)\)-local category has
exactly \(n+2\) thick tensor ideals, and its Balmer spectrum is a chain
of \(n+1\) points.
sections: A nondegeneracy lemma from the Fargues--Fontaine curve
Invariant ideals and the spectral classification

statements.title: Stabilizer-invariant ideals
statements.label: thm:invariant-radicals
statements.text:
Let \(U\subseteq A_n^\times\) be any open subgroup.
The proper prime ideals of \(E_0\) stabilized by \(U\) are precisely
\[
 0,\ I_1,\ldots,I_n.
\]
The \(U\)-invariant radical ideals are precisely
\[
 0,\ I_1,\ldots,I_n,\ E_0.
\]
The latter list also gives the radical ideals invariant under the full
canonical \(G_n\)-action.

statements.title: Hovey--Strickland conjecture
statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every prime \(p\) and every \(n\geq 1\), the thick tensor ideals of
\(\mathcal D_{(n,p)}\) are exactly
\[
 \mathcal D_{(n,p)}=\mathcal D_0
 \supsetneq\mathcal D_1\supsetneq\cdots
 \supsetneq\mathcal D_n\supsetneq\mathcal D_{n+1}=0.
\]
In particular, there are \(n+2\) such ideals, and each \(\mathcal D_k\)
is independent of the chosen finite type-\(k\) spectrum.

statements.title: Formal closure
statements.label: formal:closure
statements.text:
Let $h,r\geq1$, and let $S$ be a subgroup of
$\Gamma_h^r(\mm_C)$. If a nonzero power series in
$k[[T_1,\ldots,T_r]]$ vanishes on $S$, then there are
$a_1,\ldots,a_r\in A_h$, not all zero, such that
\[
  a_1(s_1)+_{\Gamma_h}\cdots+_{\Gamma_h}a_r(s_r)=0
  \qquad\text{for every }s\in S.
\]

statements.title: Fargues--Fontaine
statements.label: bundles:geometry
statements.text:
The curve $X_C$ is integral, regular and Noetherian of dimension one,
and $H^0(X_C,\OO_{X_C})=\Qp$.  Degrees of vector bundles are integers,
and every nonzero effective divisor has positive degree.  For each
$s\geq1$ there is a stable bundle
\[
  \mathcal E_s=\OO_{X_C}(1/s)
\]
of rank $s$ and degree one.
statements.section_title: A nondegeneracy lemma from the Fargues--Fontaine curve

statements.title: Fargues--Fontaine and Le Bras
statements.label: bundles:input
statements.text:
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(i)}]
For every $s\geq1$, after choosing an identification of a height-$s$
Lubin--Tate special fiber with $\Gamma_s$, there is a natural isomorphism of
$\Qp$-vector space sheaves
\[
  \mathcal H_s\ \cong\ \mathcal B(\mathcal E_s).
\]
In particular, its value at $\operatorname{Spa}(C,\OO_C)$ identifies
$\Gamma_s(\mm_C)$ with $H^0(X_C,\mathcal E_s)$.

\item[\textup{(ii)}]
For vector bundles $\mathcal V,\mathcal W$ on $X_C$ with nonnegative
Harder--Narasimhan slopes, the natural map
\[
  \Hom_{X_C}(\mathcal V,\mathcal W)
  \longrightarrow
  \Hom_{\operatorname{Sh}_{\mathrm{Ab}}(\Perf_C)}
       \bigl(\mathcal B(\mathcal V),\mathcal B(\mathcal W)\bigr)
\]
is an isomorphism.  Thus every additive sheaf morphism between these
section sheaves is induced by a unique bundle morphism.
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: A nondegeneracy lemma from the Fargues--Fontaine curve

statements.title: Nondegeneracy
statements.label: bundles:nondegeneracy
statements.text:
Let $0<h<n$ and $1\leq r<n$.  Suppose that
$z_1,\ldots,z_r\in\mathcal H_n(C)$ are $\Qp$-linearly independent
and that
\[
  \nu:\mathcal H_n\longrightarrow\mathcal H_h
\]
is a nonzero morphism of $\Qp$-vector space sheaves on $\Perf_C$.
Then the subgroup
\[
  S_\nu=\bigl\{\bigl(\nu(dz_1),\ldots,\nu(dz_r)\bigr):
                    d\in A_n\bigr\}
       \subseteq\Gamma_h^r(\mm_C)
\]
satisfies no nonzero formal power series equation over $k$.
statements.section_title: A nondegeneracy lemma from the Fargues--Fontaine curve

statements.title: Specialization
statements.label: def:transport
def:ks
statements.text:
The first-order parameter deformation of $\mathcal G$ induces an
isomorphism of free $R_0$-modules
\[
 \mathsf K:R_0^{n-1}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
       \Hom_{R_0}(\omega_{\mathcal G^\vee},\Lie\mathcal G).
\]
For every small $C$-valued parameter point $x$, its specialization is the
linear isomorphism from parameter directions to marked first-order
deformations of $\mathcal G_x$, with the constant deformation as origin.

statements.title: Tate coordinates
statements.label: def:coordinates
def:natural-comparison
statements.text:
Choose a formal group isomorphism
$\alpha_x:H_x\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma_h$ over $C$.
Its forward coefficients are integral, and composition gives a nonzero
natural $\Qp$-linear morphism of sheaves on perfectoid spaces over $C$,
\begin{equation}
 \nu_x:\mathcal H_n\longrightarrow\mathcal H_h,
       \qquad \nu_x(z)=\alpha_x(\Theta_x(z)).
 
\end{equation}

statements.title: Local orbit density
statements.label: orb:density
statements.text:
Fix $1\leq h<n$ and a $C$-valued point $x$ of the parameter polydisc
$I_h=0$ with $u_h(x)\neq0$.
For $g\in A_n^\times$, write $y_g$ for its orbit point, with the
transport convention of Lemma~\ref{def:stabilizer}.
Let $G$ be any open subgroup of $A_n^\times$.  If an analytic germ $P$
at $x$ on the parameter polydisc defined by $I_h=0$ vanishes at all
points of the orbit $\{y_g:g\in G\}$ sufficiently close to $x$, then
$P=0$.

It suffices to assume that, for every $d\in A_n$,
$P(y_{1-p^Nd})=0$ for all sufficiently large $N$.

statements.title: Characteristic-zero orbit germs
statements.label: fin:charzero
statements.text:
Let \(U\subseteq A_n^\times\) be an open subgroup and
\(x\in\mathfrak X_{\Cp}(\Cp)\).
If an analytic germ at \(x\) vanishes at \(g x\) for every
\(g\in U\) sufficiently close to the identity, that germ is zero.
statements.section_title: Invariant ideals and the spectral classification

statements.label: fin:primes
statements.text:
Every proper prime ideal of \(E_0\) stable under an open subgroup of
\(A_n^\times\) is one of
\[
  0,\ I_1,\ldots,I_n.
\]
statements.section_title: Invariant ideals and the spectral classification

statements.label: fin:radicals
statements.text:
For every open subgroup \(U\subseteq A_n^\times\), the
\(U\)-invariant radical ideals of \(E_0\) are precisely
\[
  0,\ I_1,\ldots,I_n,\ E_0.
\]
The same list gives the radical ideals invariant under the full
canonical extended stabilizer group \(G_n\).
statements.section_title: Invariant ideals and the spectral classification

statements.title: Established support comparison
statements.label: fin:support
statements.text:
For every prime \(p\) and height \(n\ge1\), the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The functor
\(\mathcal F:\mathcal D\to\Perf(E)\) is exact and symmetric monoidal,
where the source uses the \(K(n)\)-localized product.
It detects tensor-nilpotence of morphisms.
\item The set \(S(X)\) is a closed \(G_n\)-invariant subset
of \(\Spec(E_0)\), and
\[
 S(X\otimes Y)=S(X)\cap S(Y).
\]
For \(X,Y\in\mathcal D\),
\[
  X\in\langle Y\rangle_\otimes
       \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  S(X)\subseteq S(Y).
\]
\item For any finite \(p\)-local spectrum \(F(k)\) of type \(k\),
\(0\le k\le n\),
\[
  S\bigl(L_{K(n)}F(k)\bigr)=V(I_k).
\]
Also \(S(0)=\varnothing\) and
\(S(L_{K(n)}S)=\Spec(E_0)\).
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: Invariant ideals and the spectral classification

statements.label: fin:balmer
statements.text:
For every prime $p$ and every $n\geq1$,
\[
 \Spc(\mathcal D_{(n,p)})
      =\{\mathcal D_1,\ldots,\mathcal D_{n+1}\},\qquad
 \overline{\{\mathcal D_j\}}
      =\{\mathcal D_l:j\leq l\leq n+1\}.
\]
Thus $\mathcal D_1$ is the generic point and
$\mathcal D_{n+1}=0$ is the unique closed point.  For $0\leq k\leq n$,
\[
 \operatorname{supp}(L_{K(n)}F(k))
      =\{\mathcal D_j:k<j\leq n+1\}.
\]

title: Stable self-similar blowup for a supercritical defocusing Schrödinger equation on the torus
abstract: We prove stable self-similar finite-time blowup for a supercritical defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the twelve-dimensional torus. For a sufficiently large odd power, the blowup initial data contain a nonempty open set in a high Sobolev space. As a consequence, Gaussian Fourier initial data of arbitrarily high Sobolev regularity can have positive probability of finite-time blowup.

tex.abstract:
We prove stable self-similar finite-time blowup for a supercritical
defocusing nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on the twelve-dimensional
torus. For a sufficiently large odd power, the blowup initial data contain
a nonempty open set in a high Sobolev space. As a consequence, Gaussian
Fourier initial data of arbitrarily high Sobolev regularity can have
positive probability of finite-time blowup.
sections: Smooth profiles with a pressurized core
Linear decay and transfer to expanding tori
Nonlinear stability, open sets, and Gaussian data

statements.title: An open set of blowup data
statements.label: thm:blowup
statements.text:
There exist an odd integer $p\geq3$, a finite integer $k>8$, and a
nonempty open set $\mathcal U\subset H^k(\mathbb T^{12};\mathbb C)$
with the following property. For every $u_0\in\mathcal U$, the unique
local solution of \eqref{eq:nls} extends to
\[
 u\in C([0,T);H^k)\cap C^1([0,T);H^{k-2})
\]
for some finite $T>0$, but has no continuous $H^k$ extension through $T$.
More precisely, there are $x_*\in\mathbb T^{12}$ and $c_0>0$ such that
\[
 \lim_{t\uparrow T}(T-t)^{1/(p-1)}|u(t,x_*)|=c_0.
\]
The power can be chosen sufficiently large, and $k$ is then fixed after
that choice.

statements.title: Failure of universal Gaussian global existence
statements.label: cor:gaussian
statements.text:
For the fixed power $p$ and index $k$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:blowup}, and
for every $\alpha>k+6$, the initial datum
\begin{equation}
 u_0^\omega(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z^{12}}
       g_n(\omega)\langle n\rangle^{-\alpha}e^{in\cdot x}
\end{equation}
belongs to $H^k$ almost surely and has positive probability of finite-time
blowup. In particular, the following assertion is false: for every
energy-supercritical pair $(d,p)$ there is a finite $\alpha_0(d,p)$
such that, for every $\alpha>\alpha_0(d,p)$ and every
\[
 d/2+2<m<\alpha-d/2,
\]
the local $H^m$ solution with the Gaussian datum extends almost surely
to $C(\mathbb R;H^m(\mathbb T^d))$.

statements.title: Free matching
statements.label: free:main
statements.text:
For every $(b,Z)\in\mathcal D$, the following conclusions hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The quotient
\[
 j(b,Z)=-\frac{H'(-ib,6,-iZ)}{H(-ib,6,-iZ)}
\]
is well defined and satisfies $|j(b,Z)|<3\cdot10^{-9}$.  It is nonzero on
$\partial\mathcal D$, and, identifying $\mathbb C$ with $\mathbb R^2$ in the
order real part, imaginary part,
\[
 \deg(j,\mathcal D,0)=-1.
\]
\item For every real $z\ge Z$, $H(-ib,6,-iz)\ne0$ and
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Re}j(b,z)<.043.
\end{equation}
For $z\ge3$ one also has $\operatorname{Im}j(b,z)>0$.
\item For $\ell\in\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ and $h\in\{1,-1\}$ define
\begin{equation}
 q_h=\lambda+\ell/2-hi b,\qquad
 J_h(\lambda)=
 \begin{pmatrix}H(q_h,6+\ell,-hiZ)\\-H'(q_h,6+\ell,-hiZ)\end{pmatrix}.
\end{equation}
The columns $J_h$ are holomorphic and nonzero on a neighborhood of
$\operatorname{Re}\lambda\ge-1/32$.  The determinant
$\Delta_\ell(\lambda;b,Z)=\det(J_+(\lambda),J_-(\lambda))$ has no zero on
$\operatorname{Re}\lambda=-1/32$.  In the closed half-plane
$\operatorname{Re}\lambda\ge-1/32$ its numbers of zeros, counted with
holomorphic multiplicity, are
\[
 \begin{array}{c|ccc}
 \ell&0&1&\ell\ge2\\ \hline
 \#\{\Delta_\ell=0\}&2&1&0.
 \end{array}
\]
\end{enumerate}
The locations of the symmetry zeros are identified later at parameters
where $j(b,Z)=0$; the count in this proposition holds on the entire disk.

statements.title: Profiles and uniform estimates
statements.label: profile:existence
statements.section_title: Smooth profiles with a pressurized core

statements.title: Classification of regular modes
statements.label: spectrum:classification
statements.text:
For all sufficiently small admissible $a>0$, the only regular outgoing
modes with $\operatorname{Re}\lambda\ge-1/32$ are the phase, translation,
and time modes. Their first circular components and eigenvalues are
\[
 iQ\quad(\lambda=0),\qquad
 \partial_jQ\quad(\lambda=1/2, 1\le j\le12),\qquad
 (a-ib+D/2)Q\quad(\lambda=1).
\]
The second component of each listed real symmetry generator is the
conjugate of the displayed component. Their complex spans are the
corresponding complexified eigenspaces. In
each fixed spherical harmonic, each eigenvalue that occurs is
algebraically simple; degrees $\ell\ge2$ have no such eigenvalue.

Here ``outgoing'' means that, in each component, for every fixed integer
$j\ge0$,
\begin{equation}
 D^jv_h=O(r^{-2(a+\operatorname{Re}\lambda)})\qquad(r\longrightarrow\infty).
\end{equation}
The same classification holds for regular solutions for which
$\partial_r^kv_h\in L^2(r^{11}\,dr)$ for some integer $k\ge7$.
There is no regular generalized mode above any of these eigenvectors
with this top-derivative integrability. Algebraic simplicity for
outgoing modes means simplicity of the analytic regular/outgoing
boundary problem, including its differentiated outgoing condition.

statements.title: Energy observation inequality
statements.label: lin:observation
statements.text:
There are $c>0$, $C<\infty$, and $R_0<\infty$ such that every whole-space
linear solution, and every torus linear solution with sufficiently large
starting scale, satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \frac{d}{ds}\|v(s)\|^2
 \le-c\|v(s)\|^2+C\|v(s)\|_{L^2(B_{R_0})}^2.
\end{equation}
The derivative can equivalently be understood through the integrated
inequality.  The constants are independent of the torus scale and of
the slab length.  In particular, for $t\ge0$,
\begin{equation}
 \|v(t)\|^2\le e^{-ct}\|v(0)\|^2
   +C\int_0^t e^{-c(t-s)}\|v(s)\|_{L^2(B_{R_0})}^2\,ds.
\end{equation}

statements.title: Stable whole-space evolution
statements.label: linear:decay
statements.section_title: Linear decay and transfer to expanding tori

statements.title: Uniform expanding-torus transfer
statements.label: linear:torus
statements.text:
For each fixed $M>0$ the step maps $\mathcal F_L^{(M)}$ are uniformly
bounded for all sufficiently large $L$.  Writing $L'=Le^{M/2}$,
\begin{equation}
 \lim_{L\to\infty}
 \|\pi_{L'}\mathcal F_L^{(M)}-e^{M\Lambda}\pi_L\|
 _{\mathcal L(Y_L,\mathbb R^{14})}=0.
\end{equation}
There exists $M_0<\infty$ such that for every fixed $M\ge M_0$
there is $L_0(M)<\infty$ for which
\begin{equation}
 \|(I-P_{L'})\mathcal F_L^{(M)}|_{\ker\pi_L}\|
       _{\mathcal L(Y_L,Y_{L'})}\le\frac18,
 \qquad L\ge L_0(M).
\end{equation}
Moreover $\|(I-P_{L'})\mathcal F_L^{(M)}E_L\|\le C_M$.
Any prescribed positive bound on the coordinate defect can be imposed
by enlarging $L_0(M)$ after $M$ has been fixed.  These bounds persist
after restarting a step at any larger scale.

After identifying torus spaces by dilation, the maps above and the
step propagator are continuous when the scale and the input vary
continuously.  This last assertion is strong continuity for varying
inputs, and does not assert operator-norm continuity of Schr\"odinger
time evolution.

title: Stretched-exponential barriers for typical SK initial states
abstract: At every fixed inverse temperature β > 1, we prove a stretched-exponential obstruction to mixing for the zero-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model from typical equilibrium configurations held fixed as initial states. The Gibbs mass of states whose total-variation distance from equilibrium at time \(\exp(n^{1/10000})\) exceeds 1/4 tends to one in probability over the disorder. This holds for rate-one-per-site heat-bath dynamics and after the same stated number of discrete update attempts.

tex.abstract:
At every fixed inverse temperature $\beta>1$, we prove a stretched-exponential
obstruction to mixing for the zero-field Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model from
typical equilibrium configurations held fixed as initial states. The Gibbs
mass of states whose total-variation distance from equilibrium at time
$\exp(n^{1/10000})$ exceeds $1/4$ tends to one in probability over the
disorder. This holds for rate-one-per-site heat-bath dynamics and after the
same stated number of discrete update attempts.

title: Strict convexity and differentiability of the planar exponential first-passage limit shape
abstract: We prove that the limit shape of undirected nearest-neighbor first-passage percolation on ℤ2 with independent exponential edge weights is strictly convex and has a C1 boundary. This resolves the strict convexity and differentiability conjectures for the planar exponential model. More generally, we prove differentiability of the time-constant norm for every Gamma edge-weight law with positive shape and rate.

tex.abstract:
We prove that the limit shape of undirected nearest-neighbor
first-passage percolation on $\Z^2$ with independent exponential edge
weights is strictly convex and has a $C^1$ boundary. This resolves the
strict convexity and differentiability conjectures for the planar
exponential model. More generally, we prove differentiability of the
time-constant norm for every Gamma edge-weight law with positive shape
and rate.

statements.title: Uniform finite-volume collection bound
statements.label: access:collection
statements.text:
For the iid tunnel field associated with any fixed local type and phase
template there are constants $C,C_0<\infty$, independent of $n$ and the
input-road rule, such that the following holds.  Let $G_n(L)$ be the
maximum of $\sum_{p\in\Gamma}Y_p$ over finite distinct chains in an
arbitrary deterministic translated coordinate square of side at most
$L$, whose consecutive differences have both coordinates at least $2S$.
The empty chain and singletons are allowed.  Then
\begin{equation}
                       \E G_n(L)\le CL+C_0.
\end{equation}
The same bound therefore holds if consecutive differences are additionally
required to lie in any fixed inner cone of the positive quadrant.

statements.title: Uniform extraction from a long geodesic
statements.label: links:extraction
statements.text:
For every sufficiently small fixed \(\delta,\eta>0\), the final
geometric choices above can be made so that there are deterministic
\(\epsilon_n,\pi_n\to0\) and fixed constants \(H,C,C_K,c>0\) and
integers \(q_K,m_0\) with the following property. For each
\(\mathfrak r\in\mathfrak R_n\) there is an event \(\Omega_{n,\mathfrak r}\)
such that
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{\mathfrak r\in\mathfrak R_n}
 \mathbb P_{\mathfrak r}(\Omega_{n,\mathfrak r}^{\,c})\le\pi_n.
 
\end{equation}
Let \(x_n^\star\) be a deterministic nearest vertex of \(\mathcal G_n\)
to \(Na\), and put
\[
 j_n=\left\lfloor u(x_n^\star)/d+\tfrac12\right\rfloor,\qquad
 \mathcal J_n=\{0,1,\ldots,j_n-1\}.
\]
For large \(n\), \(cN\le j_n\le CN\). On \(\Omega_{n,\mathfrak r}\),
a geodesic from \(0\) to \(x_n^\star\) has consecutive selected pieces
\(\gamma_i:x_i\to x_{i+1}\), \(0\le i<m_N\), after two bounded terminal
fragments are removed, and the following objects and bounds.
\begin{enumerate}
\item There are at most \(CN/K+C\) pieces, each of diameter \(O(K)\),
with consecutive cut displacement between \(K/2\) and \(2K\) in the
\((A,B)\) maximum norm. The shared data in
\eqref{links:piece-cost} have
\(|\widetilde g_i-g_{\rm ref}|\le\lambda n\). A removed set \(R\)
contains every bad piece of Lemma~\ref{links:halos} and satisfies
\begin{equation}
 |R|\le\epsilon_nN,\qquad
 \sum_{i\in R}c_i^{\rm cost}\ge0,\qquad
 \sum_{i\notin R}c_i^{\rm cost}\le\epsilon_nN.
 
\end{equation}

\item The retained pieces have types \(t_i\) from the fixed access
family and centers \(z_i\) on its fixed finite family of full-rank
center lattices, after bounded rounding. Let \(E=[e_1\ e_2]\), where
the \(e_j\) are the boundary generators of \(\mathcal C_2\), normalized
by \(h(e_j)=1\) and ordered so that \(e_1\to a\) and \(e_2\to b\)
as \(\mathcal C_2\) shrinks to \(\mathcal C\). In
chronological order the centers satisfy
\begin{equation}
 E^{-1}(z_j-z_i)\ge-H(1,1)\quad(i<j),\qquad
 z_i\in E([-H,CN+H]\times[-H,\delta N+H]).
 
\end{equation}
The inequality is coordinatewise. Each rounded site occurs at most
\(m_0\) times, and the initial distance from the origin plus total
successive center distance is at most \(C(N+1)\). These bounds persist
on every type and sparse-residue subsequence. The matrices \(E\) range
in a fixed compact family, and \(H,C,m_0\) remain bounded when the
final cone is narrowed.

\item An irregular retained set \(\mathcal I\) has
\(|\mathcal I|\le(C_K\eta+\epsilon_n)N\). Each
\(i\notin R\cup\mathcal I\) supplies at most \(q_K\) admissible links
\(\mathcal L_i\), with
\begin{equation}
 c_i^{\rm cost}\ge\sum_{(j,k)\in\mathcal L_i}X_{j,k}/\beta.
 
\end{equation}
In the chronological list
\(\mathcal L=\bigcup_{i\notin R\cup\mathcal I}\mathcal L_i\), columns
are distinct, increasing, and belong to \(\mathcal J_n\). For
sufficiently small fixed \(\eta\), \(|\mathcal L|\ge cN\) for all
large \(n\), after decreasing \(c\) once. If \(k_1,\ldots,k_\ell\)
are the selected rows, then
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
 |\mathcal J_n\setminus\{j:(j,k)\in\mathcal L\}|
       \le(C_K\eta+\epsilon_n)N,\qquad |k_1|\le j_n^2,\\
 \sum_{\nu<\ell}|k_{\nu+1}-k_\nu|
       \le(C_K\eta+\epsilon_n)N.
 \end{gathered}
 
\end{equation}
Rows can be held across omitted columns without increasing their variation.

\item Every retained piece obeys the charged-tunnel bound
\begin{equation}
 (c_i^{\rm cost})^-\le Y_{z_i,t_i}+E_{z_i}.
 
\end{equation}
Here \(Y\) is the local saving of Section~\ref{access:tunnels}, and
\(E\) is a fixed local sum at the piece center that dominates both
selected endpoint errors for every allowed piece. The finite
phase-template fields for \(Y\) satisfy
Proposition~\ref{access:collection}; those for \(E\) have fixed range
and tail \(C_K\min(1,t^{-m_*})\).
\end{enumerate}
Set every selected list and count, including \(m_N,R,\mathcal I,\mathcal L\),
to the empty or zero value off \(\Omega_{n,\mathfrak r}\).
For finitely many link templates, apply the proposition separately,
intersect their events, and take the maximum of their error sequences
and the sum of their failure sequences.

statements.title: Matched caps in a finite dyadic range
statements.label: links:matched
statements.text:
Let \(X^{(1)},\ldots,X^{(r)}\) be finitely many required row-link
templates, and let \(U_1,\ldots,U_p\) be additional nonnegative local
variables with a uniform bound on the sum of their first moments.
For every \(\zeta>0\) and every prescribed lower bound
\(M_{\rm prescribed}\), there is a fixed finite dyadic set
\(\mathcal M=\{M_0,2M_0,\ldots,2^{H-1}M_0\}\), with
\(M_0\ge M_{\rm prescribed}\), and fixed geometric tolerances, such
that for every sufficiently large \(n\) some deterministic law-dependent
\(M\in\mathcal M\) satisfies, simultaneously,
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E f_{M,M}(X^{(a)}/\beta)&\le\zeta
       &&(1\le a\le r),\\
 M\left[\sum_{a=1}^r\mathbb P((X^{(a)}/\beta)^->M)
       +\sum_{b=1}^p\mathbb P(U_b>M)\right]&\le\zeta.
 
\end{align}
In particular \(U_1\) may be the positive part of the normalized
primary increment used in the road improvement.

statements.label: improvement:contraction-proposition
statements.text:
For suitable fixed rational $v,w$ near the flat endpoints and $s>0$,
there are an integer $D\ge1$ and $\rho<1$ such that
\[
 b(Dn)\le\rho b(n)
\]
for every sufficiently large admissible $n$. The infimum on both sides
uses the road class of Definition~\ref{def:fb-road}, with costs in their
original units.

statements.label: cor:fixed-direction
statements.text:
Fix a deterministic unit vector $u$. There is an event $\Omega_u$ of
probability one on which all the following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $x\in\Z^2$ there is exactly one infinite geodesic
      $\Gamma_x^u$ from $x$ with direction $u$. For every sequence $(z_n)$
      directed toward $u$, including a sequence chosen from the edge
      configuration,
      $\Gamma(x,z_n)\to\Gamma_x^u$ locally.
\item For every $x,y\in\Z^2$, the paths $\Gamma_x^u$ and
      $\Gamma_y^u$ have a common tail.
\item No bigeodesic has an end with direction $u$.
\item For every $x,y\in\Z^2$, the limit
\[
 B_u(x,y)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\bigl(T(x,z_n)-T(y,z_n)\bigr)
\]
      exists and is independent of the choice of sequence directed toward
      $u$. Moreover,
\[
 \E B_u(0,x)=\nabla\mu(u)\cdot x,
\]
      and, for every $\varepsilon>0$, only finitely many $x\in\Z^2$
      satisfy
\[
 |B_u(0,x)-\nabla\mu(u)\cdot x|>\varepsilon\lVert x\rVert_1.
\]
\end{enumerate}

statements.label: cor:midpoint
statements.text:
For every nonzero $v\in\Z^2$,
\[
 \lim_{n\to\infty}
 \PP\bigl(\lfloor n/2\rfloor v\in\Gamma(0,nv)\bigr)=0.
\]
More generally, let $a_n,b_n,z_n$ be deterministic lattice vertices with
\[
 \lVert a_n-z_n\rVert_2\to\infty,
 \quad\lVert b_n-z_n\rVert_2\to\infty,
 \quad
 \frac{b_n-z_n}{\lVert b_n-z_n\rVert_2}\longrightarrow u
\]
for a deterministic unit vector $u$. Then
$\PP(z_n\in\Gamma(a_n,b_n))\to0$.

statements.title: Quantitative midpoint bound for the Gamma family
statements.label: cor:gamma-quantitative-midpoint
statements.text:
For every $\kappa>0$ there is $C_\kappa<\infty$ such that, for every
$\lambda>0$ and all $a,b,z\in\Z^2$ with
$D=\min\{\lVert a-z\rVert_1,\lVert b-z\rVert_1\}\geq1$,
\[
 \PP\bigl(z\in\Gamma_{\kappa,\lambda}(a,b)\bigr)
 \leq C_\kappa\frac{\log^2(D+2)}{D^{1/16}},
\]
where $\Gamma_{\kappa,\lambda}$ denotes the unique geodesic for
iid $\operatorname{Gamma}(\kappa,\lambda)$ edge weights.

statements.title: Gamma and Richardson cone-tip survival
statements.label: cor:gamma-cone-tip
statements.text:
Fix $\kappa,\lambda>0$, a deterministic unit vector $\theta\in S^1$,
and a geometric half-angle $0\le\alpha\le\pi$. Define the closed cone
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 C^\theta_\alpha&=\{0\}\cup
 \{x\in\R^2\setminus\{0\}:\angle(x,-\theta)\le\alpha\},\\
 I_1&=(C^\theta_\alpha\cap\Z^2)\setminus\{0\},
 \qquad I_2=\{0\},
 \end{aligned}
\]
where $\angle(x,-\theta)$ is the Euclidean angle between the two vectors.
Use one iid $\operatorname{Gamma}(\kappa,\lambda)$ field on unoriented
nearest-neighbor edges of $\Z^2$, with passage metric $T$. At time zero,
start type 1 from every site of $I_1$ and type 2 from $I_2$.
Both types use this same realization of $T$, and each site is permanently
claimed by the type that reaches it first. With
$T(I,z)=\inf_{x\in I}T(x,z)$, interpreting the infimum of the empty set
as $\infty$, the sites eventually claimed by type 2 are almost surely
\[
 \mathcal E_2=\{z\in\Z^2:T(0,z)<T(I_1,z)\}.
\]
Then
\[
 \PP\bigl(|\mathcal E_2|=\infty\bigr)>0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \alpha<\pi/2.
\]
In particular, at $\alpha=\pi/2$, when the cone is the closed half-plane
$\{x:x\cdot\theta\le0\}$, type 2 claims only finitely many sites almost
surely. At $\kappa=1$, this gives Benjamini's cone-tip prediction for
equal-rate Richardson competition with any common rate $\lambda>0$ in
the same initial configuration.

title: Strong Ulam Stability Characterizes Amenability
abstract: A countable discrete group is amenable if and only if it is strongly Ulam stable: every sufficiently accurate unitary almost representation, on any complex Hilbert space, is uniformly close in operator norm to a genuine representation on the same space. We prove the converse to Kazhdan's amenable stability theorem, answering the question of Burger, Ozawa, and Thom. The inclusion of infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces is essential.

tex.abstract:
A countable discrete group is amenable if and only if it is strongly Ulam
stable: every sufficiently accurate unitary almost representation, on any
complex Hilbert space, is uniformly close in operator norm to a genuine
representation on the same space. We prove the converse to Kazhdan's
amenable stability theorem, answering the question of Burger, Ozawa, and
Thom. The inclusion of infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces is essential.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
A countable discrete group is strongly Ulam stable if and only if it is
amenable.

statements.title: Compatible sparse flags
statements.label: prop:flags
statements.text:
Let $G$ be a nonamenable discrete group.  For every integer $N\geq1$
and every $0<\beta<1$, there are finite nonempty sets
$\mathcal X_1,\ldots,\mathcal X_N$ and
$\mathcal Y_0,\ldots,\mathcal Y_{N-1}$, maps
\[
 s_k:\mathcal X_k\times\mathcal Y_{k-1}\longrightarrow G,
 \qquad
 b_k:G\times\mathcal X_k\times\mathcal Y_{k-1}
       \longrightarrow\{\E,\F\},
\]
with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\textup{(F1)}] If $k<N$ and $b_k(w;x,y)=\E$, then, with
$v=w s_k(x,y)$,
\[
 b_{k+1}(v;x',y')=\E
 \quad\text{for every }(x',y')\in
            \mathcal X_{k+1}\times\mathcal Y_k.
\]
\item[\textup{(F2)}] For every $k,w,x$,
\[
 \frac{\#\{y\in\mathcal Y_{k-1}:b_k(w;x,y)=\F\}}
      {|\mathcal Y_{k-1}|}\leq\beta.
\]
\item[\textup{(F3)}] For every $k,v,y$,
\[
 \frac{\#\{x\in\mathcal X_k:
          b_k(v s_k(x,y)^{-1};x,y)=\E\}}
      {|\mathcal X_k|}\leq\beta.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Each alphabet may subsequently be replaced by any positive integer
number of copies, independently of the others, while preserving these
properties.  In particular, its cardinality can be made arbitrarily
large and divisible by any prescribed positive integer.
