title: The abelian Zilber–Pink conjecture
abstract: We prove the abelian Zilber–Pink conjecture over \(\overline{\mathbb Q}\). Every irreducible subvariety of an abelian variety has only finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties, where atypicality is measured inside its smallest containing torsion coset.

tex.abstract:
We prove the abelian Zilber--Pink conjecture over
$\overline{\mathbb Q}$. Every irreducible subvariety of an abelian variety
has only finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties, where atypicality
is measured inside its smallest containing torsion coset.
sections: Height scales and an auxiliary sequence theorem
Auxiliary subvarieties over fields of bounded degree
Arithmetic positivity at the bounded scale
The product cut and bounded-degree descent
From non-density to maximal atypical finiteness

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every number field $K$, every abelian variety $A/K$, and every
irreducible subvariety $X\subseteq A_{\bar K}$, there are only finitely
many maximal atypical subvarieties of $X$ in
$S=\langle X\rangle_{\mathrm{sp}}$. Equivalently, there are finitely many
proper atypical subvarieties $Y_1,\ldots,Y_m\subsetneq X$ such that every
atypical subvariety is contained in one of the $Y_j$.

statements.label: thm:nondensity
statements.text:
Let $A$ be an abelian variety over $\Qbar$, and let $X\subseteq A$ be an
irreducible subvariety contained in no proper torsion coset. Then
$X\cap A^{[\dim X+1]}$ is not Zariski dense in $X$.

statements.title: Finite-rank translated intersections
statements.label: cor:finite-rank-translates
statements.text:
Let $A$ be an abelian variety over $\Qbar$, let
$\Gamma\subseteq A(\Qbar)$ be a subgroup satisfying
\[
 \dim_{\mathbb Q}\bigl(\Gamma\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q\bigr)<\infty,
\]
and let $X\subseteq A$ be an irreducible closed subvariety of dimension
$d$ contained in no translate of a proper algebraic subgroup of $A$.
Then
\[
 X(\Qbar)\cap\bigl(A^{[d+1]}(\Qbar)+\Gamma\bigr)
\]
is not Zariski dense in $X$. If $d=1$, this intersection is finite.

statements.title: Auxiliary sequence theorem
statements.label: thm:sequence
statements.text:
For sequence data as in Definition~\ref{def:sequence-data}, let
$V\subseteq\Lie(W)$ be the image of an idempotent in
$\End(\cA)_{\mathbb R}$. Let $\Phi$ be the orthogonal projector with
kernel $V$, and put
\[
 q_i=(y_{i\ell}/\sqrt{H_{i\ell}})_{\ell\in I}
 \in\mathcal H(\cA).
\]
The following two conditions cannot both hold:
\begin{equation}
 
 \codim_{\Lie(W)}V>\sum_{\ell\in I}m_\ell,
 \qquad \|\Phi(q_i)\|\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Height scales and an auxiliary sequence theorem

statements.label: prop:sequence-implies-nondensity
statements.text:
The auxiliary sequence theorem implies Theorem~\ref{thm:nondensity}
for every abelian variety over $\Qbar$.
statements.section_title: Height scales and an auxiliary sequence theorem

statements.title: Uniform tangent positivity
statements.label: prop:tangent
statements.text:
Consider fixed sequence data as in Definition~\ref{def:sequence-data},
and let $V$ and $\Phi$ be as in Theorem~\ref{thm:sequence}.
Suppose that the conclusion of Lemma~\ref{lemma:projection} excludes
every fixed nonzero product $C=\prod_\ell C_\ell$ for which
\begin{equation}
 \sum_\ell\dim_{y_{i\ell}}
 \bigl(Y_\ell\cap(y_{i\ell}+C_\ell)\bigr)
 \geq\rank\bigl(\Phi|_{\Lie(C)}\bigr)
\end{equation}
holds for infinitely many $i$.
Put $r=\dim\cA+1$, and, for a linear map $g$ on $\Lie(\cA)$, define
\[
 \Delta g(v_1,\ldots,v_r)
   =\bigl(g(v_2)-g(v_1),\ldots,g(v_r)-g(v_{r-1})\bigr).
\]
Then the following assertions hold.
\begin{enumerate}
 \item There are a neighborhood $\mathcal U$ of $\Phi$ in
 $\End(\cA)_{\mathbb R}$ and an index $i_0$ such that
 $P_Z(g)>0$ for every $i\geq i_0$, every $g\in\mathcal U$, and every
 subproduct $Z=\prod_\ell Z_\ell$ with
 $y_{i\ell}\in Z_\ell\subseteq Y_\ell$.
 \item For every sufficiently large $i$ and every such subproduct $Z$,
 $P_{Z^r}(\Delta\Phi)>0$.
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Dill
statements.label: thm:dill-form
statements.text:
Let $X_1,\ldots,X_s$ be fixed irreducible positive-dimensional
projective varieties over $\Qbar$, with $s\ge2$, and fix embeddings
$X_\ell\subseteq\mathbb P^{N_\ell}$ given by very ample bundles
$L_\ell$.  For positive integral weights $a_\ell$, put
$N_a=\boxtimes_\ell L_\ell^{a_\ell}$.
Let $\mathcal M$ be a nef bundle on $\prod_\ell X_\ell$ and
$\mathcal P=N_a^{t_1}$, with its full monomial coordinate system $\Xi$.
Suppose $\mathcal P\otimes\mathcal M^{-1}$ is generated by $J$ sections
$\mathcal Z$, whose images under an injection
\[
 \mathcal P\otimes\mathcal M^{-1}\hookrightarrow N_a^{t_2}
\]
are polynomials of multidegree $t_2a$ with joint coefficient height at
most $\sum_\ell a_\ell\delta_\ell$.  Assume the injection is an
isomorphism on a nonempty open set $U^0$.  Here $t_1,t_2,J$ are positive
integers and $\delta_\ell\ge1$.

Let $x=(x_\ell)\in U^0(\Qbar)$.  Suppose that, for every irreducible
subproduct $Z=\prod_\ell Z_\ell$ with $x_\ell\in Z_\ell\subseteq X_\ell$,
\begin{equation}
 (\mathcal M^{\dim Z}\cdot Z)
 \ge \theta^{-1}\prod_\ell
       (\deg Z_\ell)^{-\omega}a_\ell^{\dim Z_\ell},
\end{equation}
where $\theta\ge1$ and $\omega\ge-1$ are integers.  Put
\[
 \begin{split}
 u_0&=\sum_\ell\dim X_\ell,\\
 \Lambda&=\theta(2t_1u_0)^{u_0}
          \max_\ell(N_\ell+1)\prod_\ell\deg X_\ell,\\
 \psi(u)&=\prod_{j=u+1}^{u_0}((3+\omega)j+1),
 \qquad c_1=c_2=\Lambda^{\psi(0)},\\
 c_3^{(\ell)}&=\Lambda^{2\psi(0)}(Jt_2)^{u_0}
                      (h(X_\ell)+\delta_\ell).
 \end{split}
\]
If $a_\ell\ge c_2a_{\ell+1}$ for $\ell<s$ and
$h(x_\ell)\ge c_3^{(\ell)}$ for every $\ell$, then
\begin{equation}
 \sum_\ell a_\ell h(x_\ell)
 \le c_1\bigl(h(\Xi(x))-h(\mathcal Z(x))\bigr).
\end{equation}

statements.label: thm:all-high
statements.text: Theorem~\ref{thm:sequence} holds for all-high sequence data.

statements.label: prop:minimal-products
statements.text:
For a minimal admissible choice, the following assertions hold after
discarding finitely many indices and passing to a subsequence.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every pair of positive integers $D,B$, there is an index
$i_0(D,B)$ such that, for every $i\ge i_0(D,B)$ and every factor
$\ell$, any hypersurface of degree at most $D$ defined over an
extension $F_i/k_i$ with $[F_i:k_i]\le B$ which contains
$y_{i\ell}$ also contains $Z_{i\ell}$.
\item For each fixed degree, the equations of $Z_{i\ell}$ in that
degree have a $k_i$-basis of coefficient heights $O(H_{i\ell})$.
The points $y_{i\ell}$ are smooth on $Z_{i\ell}$, and equations of
bounded degree and height $O(H_{i\ell})$ span their conormal spaces.
\item The low factor belongs to a finite set of varieties.  We may
therefore suppose $Z_{i0}=Z_0$ independent of $i$.
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: Auxiliary subvarieties over fields of bounded degree

statements.label: prop:arithmetic-positive
statements.text:
Let \(Z_i=\prod_{\ell=0}^s Z_{i\ell}\) be the bounded-degree,
bounded-field-degree subproducts above, with fixed positive-dimensional
low factor \(Z_0\), dense factorwise height bounds
\(h_{L_\ell}=O(H_{i\ell})\), and fixed high cycle classes.  Suppose the
two tangent integrals for \(\Phi\) in
Proposition~\ref{prop:tangent} are positive.  For the homomorphisms and
scalings in \eqref{eq:scaled-homomorphisms}, one has
\begin{equation}
 \liminf_{i\to\infty}
 \frac{(\bar E_i^{d+1}\cdot Z_i)}{M_i^2B_i}>0.
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Arithmetic positivity at the bounded scale

statements.label: prop:index
statements.text:
Fix projective embeddings of abelian varieties $A_\ell$ by symmetric
very ample bundles $L_\ell$, a symmetric very ample canonically metrized
bundle $\bar L$ on $\cA=\prod_\ell A_\ell$, and integral bases of the
homomorphism groups between the fixed varieties.  Let
$F_i:\cA\to\cA$ be homomorphisms.  Suppose that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $y_{i\ell}$ is a smooth point of an irreducible
$Z_{i\ell}\subset A_\ell$, its projective height is $O(H_{i\ell})$,
and its conormal space is spanned by equations of bounded degree and
coefficient height $O(H_{i\ell})$, with $H_{i\ell}\ge1$;
\item $M_i\longrightarrow\infty$, the positive integers $b_{i\ell}$
satisfy $b_{i\ell}\ll M_i$ and
$b_{i\ell}^2H_{i\ell}\asymp M_i^2$, and the coefficients of
$F_i|_{A_\ell}$ in the fixed bases are $O(b_{i\ell})$;
\item for $\bar E_i=F_i^*\bar L$ one has
$h_{\bar E_i}(y_i)=o(M_i^2)$, and a nonzero section $s_i$ of
$E_i^{n_i}$ on a resolution of $Z_i=\prod_\ell Z_{i\ell}$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \|s_i\|_{v,\sup}\le
 \begin{cases}
 e^{-c n_iM_i^2},&v\mid\infty,\\
 1,&v\nmid\infty,
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
for a fixed $c>0$, over a number field containing its data.
\end{enumerate}
Assume that the resolution is an isomorphism over the smooth locus.
Then, for some $\eta>0$ independent of $i$,
$\operatorname{ind}_{n_i,b_i}(s_i;y_i)\ge\eta$ for all sufficiently
large $i$.  No bound on the degree of the field of $y_i$ is required.

statements.label: prop:product-cut
statements.text:
For the minimal products of Proposition~\ref{prop:minimal-products}
with $d_0>0$, the small sections of
Lemma~\ref{lemma:small-sections} cannot satisfy the positive index
conclusion of Proposition~\ref{prop:index} along an infinite
subsequence.

statements.label: prop:optimal-finite
statements.text:
Every irreducible subvariety of every abelian variety over $\Qbar$
contains only finitely many optimal subvarieties.

title: The approximation threshold for metric k-median
abstract: For every fixed ε > 0, we give a deterministic polynomial-time \((1+2/e+\varepsilon)\)-approximation for finite rational metric k-median with specified candidate facilities, opening at most k facilities. Under \(P\ne NP\), the infimum approximation factor in this model is therefore \(1+2/e\).

tex.abstract:
For every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), we give a deterministic polynomial-time
\((1+2/e+\varepsilon)\)-approximation for finite rational metric
\(k\)-median with specified candidate facilities, opening at most \(k\)
facilities. Under \(P\ne NP\), the infimum approximation factor in this
model is therefore \(1+2/e\).
sections: A finite inequality for the drift
Exact certificates for the scalar bounds

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), there is a deterministic algorithm which,
given a finite rational metric \(k\)-median instance with \(1\le k\le |F|\),
returns \(S\subseteq F\), \(|S|\le k\), such that
\[
 \sum_{j\in J}d(j,S)\le
 \left(1+\frac2e+\varepsilon\right)\OPT_k.
\]
Its running time is polynomial in the binary encoding length of the instance.
The polynomial may depend on \(\varepsilon\).

statements.label: cor:threshold
statements.text:
If \(P\ne NP\), the infimum of deterministic polynomial-time approximation
factors for metric \(k\)-median with specified candidate facilities is \(1+2/e\).

statements.title: Li--Svensson~\cite{LiSvensson2016}, Theorem~4 of the 2014 manuscript
statements.label: thm:li-svensson
statements.text:
Let \(\alpha>1\), and suppose \(\mathcal A\) is a \(c\)-additive
\(\alpha\)-approximation algorithm for metric \(k\)-median.
For every \(\eta>0\), there is an ordinary
\((\alpha+\eta)\)-approximation algorithm with running time
\(n^{O(c/\eta)}\) times the running time of \(\mathcal A\).
For fixed \(\alpha,c,\eta\), this is polynomial overhead.

statements.label: thm:preparation
statements.text:
For every $\eta>0$, there is a constant $\Delta_0$ with the following
property.  Given a finite rational metric instance and feasible rational
openings $0\le y_i\le1$ with a nearest-unit assignment of cost $V_j$
for each client $j$, fix any constant even integer $\Delta\ge\Delta_0$ and let
$g=1/\Delta$.  There is a randomized procedure, running in expected
polynomial time on rational inputs, that produces openings
$\widetilde y_i\in[0,1]\cap g\mathbb Z$, allowing polynomially many
co-located labeled facility pieces, such that
\[
 1\le\sum_i\widetilde y_i\le\sum_i y_i+3g
\]
for every output, and the expected nearest-unit assignment cost of every
client $j$ is at most $(1+\eta)V_j$.
In particular the grid can be required to satisfy any additional
positive instance-independent upper bound on $g$.

statements.title: Finite comparison inequality
statements.label: thm:finite-inequality
statements.section_title: A finite inequality for the drift

statements.title: Rounding a grid solution
statements.label: thm:grid-rounding
statements.text:
For every fixed $\tau>0$ and all sufficiently large constant integers
$\Delta$, put $g=1/\Delta$.  Suppose a finite rational metric instance has openings
$\widetilde y_i\in[0,1]\cap g\mathbb Z$ of total mass $M\ge1$.
For a client $j$, let $V_{j,0}$ be the cost of its nearest unit of this mass.
There is a constant $C=C(\tau,\Delta)$ and a randomized algorithm of
expected polynomial running time that outputs a set $O$ of facilities with
\[
 |O|\le M+C,
 \qquad
 \E d(j,O)\le(1+2/e+\tau)V_{j,0}\quad\text{for every client }j.
\]
All parameters and the additive constant are independent of the instance.
In particular, an initial mass at most $k+c_0$, for a fixed constant
$c_0$, gives at most $k+c_0+C$ facilities.
The deterministic implementation of the resulting total-cost guarantee
is given in Section~\ref{sec:derandomization}.

statements.title: Deterministic additive approximation
statements.label: thm:pseudo
statements.text:
For every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), there is an
instance-independent integer \(c\ge0\) and a deterministic
polynomial-time algorithm for metric \(k\)-median that opens at
most \(k+c\) facilities and has total connection cost at most
\[
 \left(1+\frac2e+\varepsilon\right)\operatorname{LP},
\]
where \(\operatorname{LP}\) is the optimum value of the assignment
relaxation. In particular, its cost is at most the same factor times
\(\OPT_k\).

title: The Artinian Lex-Plus-Powers Betti Theorem
abstract: We prove the Eisenbud–Green–Harris and lex-plus-powers conjectures over every characteristic-zero field for homogeneous regular sequences of any positive length, with degrees at least two. For every homogeneous ideal containing such a sequence, the corresponding lex-plus-powers ideal has the same Hilbert function and at least as large a graded Betti number in every homological and internal degree.

tex.abstract:
We prove the Eisenbud--Green--Harris and lex-plus-powers conjectures over every
characteristic-zero field for homogeneous regular sequences of any positive
length, with degrees at least two. For every homogeneous ideal containing such
a sequence, the corresponding lex-plus-powers ideal has the same Hilbert
function and at least as large a graded Betti number in every homological and
internal degree.
sections: Graded resolutions and leading coefficient spaces
A monomial bound containing the prescribed powers
Shadows and end slices in an exponent box
Arbitrary regular-sequence length and characteristic-zero fields

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every \(n\ge1\), every ordered degree sequence
\(2\le a_1\le\cdots\le a_n\), and every homogeneous ideal
\(I\subseteq\C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) containing a regular sequence of these
degrees, the spaces in \eqref{eq:prescription} exist and
\(J=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}J_d\) is a homogeneous ideal. For this single ideal,
\[
 \beta^S_{p,j}(S/I)\le\beta^S_{p,j}(S/J)
 \qquad\text{for every \(p\ge0\) and \(j\in\Z\)}.
\]
There is no restriction on the degrees or number of the additional
generators of \(I\).

statements.title: Eisenbud--Green--Harris and lex-plus-powers in characteristic zero
statements.label: cor:characteristic-zero
statements.text:
Let \(F\) be a field of characteristic zero, let
\[
 S_F=F[x_1,\ldots,x_n],\qquad
 1\le c\le n,\qquad 2\le a_1\le\cdots\le a_c,
 \qquad P_F=(x_1^{a_1},\ldots,x_c^{a_c}),
\]
with the standard grading and lexicographic order \(x_1>\cdots>x_n\).
Suppose that a homogeneous ideal \(I\subseteq S_F\) contains a homogeneous
regular sequence \(f_1,\ldots,f_c\) with \(\deg f_i=a_i\).
For \(d\ge0\), put
\[
 q_d=\dim_F I_d-\dim_F(P_F)_d.
\]
This integer lies between zero and the number of degree-\(d\) monomials
outside \(P_F\). Let \(J_d\) be the sum of \((P_F)_d\) and the span of the
\(q_d\) lexicographically greatest such monomials. Then
\(J=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}J_d\) is a homogeneous ideal, and for this single ideal
\[
 \dim_F(S_F/I)_d=\dim_F(S_F/J)_d\quad(d\ge0),\qquad
 \beta^{S_F}_{p,j}(S_F/I)\le\beta^{S_F}_{p,j}(S_F/J)
 \quad(p\ge0,\ j\in\Z).
\]
There is no restriction on the degrees or number of the additional
generators of \(I\).

statements.title: Commuting-form construction, {\cite[Theorem~1.1]{ArtinianEGH}}
statements.label: thm:forms
statements.text:
Let \(f_1,\ldots,f_n\) be a homogeneous regular sequence in
\(\C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), of degrees \(2\le a_1\le\cdots\le a_n\).
There are a field extension \(k/\C\), a central division \(k\)-algebra
\(\Delta\), and a commutative graded \(k\)-subalgebra
\[
 k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\subseteq A\subseteq N=\Delta[x_1,\ldots,x_n]
\]
generated by finitely many elements of degree one, containing
\(t_1,\ldots,t_n\in A_1\), such that
\begin{equation}
 t_h^{a_h}=c_h f_h+\sum_{\ell<h}B_{h\ell}f_\ell
                  +\sum_{\ell>h}C_{h\ell}t_\ell
 \qquad(1\le h\le n).
\end{equation}
Here \(c_h\in k^\times\), \(B_{h\ell},C_{h\ell}\in A\), and every summand
has degree \(a_h\). Moreover,
\[
 \{t^\alpha=t_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots t_n^{\alpha_n}:
       \alpha\in\N^n\}
\]
is a graded left-\(\Delta\) basis of the \emph{full} algebra \(N\).

statements.title: Leading-submodule comparison
statements.label: filt:comparison
statements.text:
With $A,V,E,W$ and $\prec$ as above, for every $d\in\Z$, every
$p\geq0$, and every $j\in\Z$ one has
\begin{align}
 \dim_F(E/W)_d
    &=\dim_F(E/\operatorname{in}_{\prec}W)_d,
       \\
 \beta^A_{p,j}(E/W)
    &\leq\beta^A_{p,j}(E/\operatorname{in}_{\prec}W).
       
\end{align}
statements.section_title: Graded resolutions and leading coefficient spaces

statements.title: Monomial reduction
statements.label: mono:bound
statements.text:
Let $S=\C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, let
$2\leq a_1\leq\cdots\leq a_n$, and let $I\subseteq S$ be a
homogeneous ideal containing a homogeneous regular sequence
$f_1,\ldots,f_n$ with $\deg f_h=a_h$.  Put
$P=(x_1^{a_1},\ldots,x_n^{a_n})$.
There is a monomial ideal $M\subseteq S$ containing $P$ such that
\begin{align}
 \dim_\C(S/M)_d&=\dim_\C(S/I)_d
                   &&(d\in\Z),\\
 \beta^S_{p,j}(S/I)&\leq\beta^S_{p,j}(S/M)
                   &&(p\geq0,\ j\in\Z).
                   
\end{align}
statements.section_title: A monomial bound containing the prescribed powers

statements.label: stab:main
statements.text:
Let $S=\C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, let $2\le a_1\le\cdots\le a_n$,
and put $P=(x_1^{a_1},\ldots,x_n^{a_n})$.
For every monomial ideal $K\supseteq P$, there is a monomial ideal
$H\supseteq P$ stable in the box such that
\[
 \dim_\C(S/H)_d=\dim_\C(S/K)_d\quad(d\in\Z)
\]
and
\[
 \beta^S_{p,j}(S/K)\le\beta^S_{p,j}(S/H)
 \qquad(p\ge0,\ j\in\Z).
\]

statements.title: Lex replacement is an ideal
statements.label: box:ideal
statements.text:
Let \(b_1,\ldots,b_r\) be positive integers, and let
\(H\subseteq\C[x_1,\ldots,x_r]\) be a monomial ideal containing
\(P_r=(x_1^{b_1+1},\ldots,x_r^{b_r+1})\) and stable in the box
sense.  Then the subspace \(\Lambda H\) defined in
\eqref{box:lex-replacement} is a monomial ideal containing \(P_r\).
It is stable in the box sense and has the same Hilbert function as
\(H\).
statements.section_title: Shadows and end slices in an exponent box

statements.label: tor:stable
statements.text:
Let $r\ge1$, let $2\le a_1\le\cdots\le a_r$, and let
$A=\C[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$.  Suppose that $H\subseteq A$ is a
monomial ideal containing $(x_1^{a_1},\ldots,x_r^{a_r})$ and is
stable in the box.  Let $G=\Lambda H$ be its degreewise lex
replacement inside the box, together with the prescribed pure powers.
Then, for every $p\ge0$ and $j\in\Z$,
\[
 \beta^A_{p,j}(H)\le\beta^A_{p,j}(G),
 \qquad
 \beta^A_{p,j}(A/H)\le\beta^A_{p,j}(A/G).
\]

title: The Bass trace conjecture and the characteristic-zero Kaplansky idempotent conjecture
abstract: We prove the complex group-ring Bass trace conjecture for every discrete group: the Hattori–Stallings trace of a finitely generated projective module over its complex group ring is supported on conjugacy classes of finite-order elements. As a consequence, for every torsion-free group G and every commutative unital domain R of characteristic zero, the only idempotents in \(RG\) are 0 and 1. This proves Kaplansky's idempotent conjecture in characteristic zero.

tex.abstract:
We prove the complex group-ring Bass trace conjecture for every discrete
group: the Hattori--Stallings trace of a finitely generated projective module
over its complex group ring is supported on conjugacy classes of finite-order
elements. As a consequence, for every torsion-free group $G$ and every
commutative unital domain $R$ of characteristic zero, the only idempotents
in $RG$ are $0$ and $1$. This proves Kaplansky's idempotent conjecture in
characteristic zero.
sections: A vanishing theorem for sparse simplicial cycles
A metric and volume bound for connected supports

From separating filtrations to finite chains

Torsion-free groups: trace rank and idempotents

statements.label: thm:bass
statements.text:
Let $G$ be any discrete group. For every $x\in K_0(\C G)$ and every
infinite-order element $g\in G$,
\[
 \HS_G(x)([g]_G)=0.
\]
Equivalently, if $\con_{\mathrm{fin}}(G)$ denotes the conjugacy classes of
finite-order elements, then
\[
 \HS_G\bigl(K_0(\C G)\bigr)
 \subseteq\bigoplus_{C\in\con_{\mathrm{fin}}(G)}\C C.
\]

statements.label: cor:torsion-free
statements.text:
Let $G$ be any torsion-free discrete group.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item For every $q\geq1$ and every idempotent $e\in M_q(\C G)$,
 \[
  \tau_{G,q}(e)=\operatorname{rank}_{\C}\bigl(\epsilon_{G,q}(e)\bigr).
 \]
 Consequently $\tau_{G,*}=\operatorname{rk}_{\epsilon}$, with
 $\Z$ viewed as a subgroup of $\C$, and
 \[
  \tau_{G,*}\bigl(K_0(\C G)\bigr)=\Z.
 \]
 \item For every commutative unital domain $R$ of characteristic zero,
 every $e\in RG$ satisfying $e^2=e$ is either $0$ or $1$.
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Sparse-chain vanishing
statements.label: thm:sparse
statements.text:
For each integer $D\geq2$ there is an integer $n_0(D)$ with the following
property. Let $Y$ be the vertex set of a countable connected simple graph
of degree at most $D$, and let a countable group $H$ act by graph
automorphisms, freely on vertices. Suppose $n\geq n_0(D)$ and $K$ is an
$H$-invariant subcomplex of the full simplex on $Y$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item $K$ is generated by its $n$-simplices and has finitely many
 $H$-orbits of simplices;
 \item the vertices of each $n$-simplex span a connected subgraph of $Y$.
\end{enumerate}
Then every $H$-invariant cocycle $\psi:E_n\to\C$ evaluates to zero on
the image in $(E_n)_H$ of every cycle in $C_n(K)_H$.
statements.section_title: A vanishing theorem for sparse simplicial cycles

statements.label: prop:zero-strata
statements.text:
For every $\epsilon>0$ there is an admissible equivariant locally constant
filtration $(Z_j,T_j)_{j=0}^n$ such that, for every original top simplex
$\sigma$ of $K$,
\begin{equation}
 \int_X\#\bigl(Z_0(x)\cap\sigma\bigr)\,d\mu(x)
 \le C_\sigma\epsilon.
\end{equation}
Here $C_\sigma$ depends on the fixed geometric data but is independent of
$\epsilon$ and of the complexity of the chosen triangulations.
statements.section_title: Local replacement and the number of zero strata

statements.label: prop:path-cycle
statements.text:
For every positive even integer $n$, the chain $z_n$ is a cycle.
Moreover, either its defining sum has no nonzero distinct-vertex terms,
so $z_n=0$, or it is the image of a cycle in $C_n(K)_H$ for an
$H$-invariant simplicial complex $K$ generated by $n$-simplices, with
finitely many simplex orbits, whose top vertex sets span connected
subgraphs of $Y$.  The graph and its degree bound $D$ are independent
of $n$.

statements.label: prop:detector
statements.text:
For every integer $m\ge1$, the formula
\begin{equation}
 \psi_m(y_0,\ldots,y_{2m})
   =\sum_{i=0}^{2m}(-1)^i
       p_m(h_0,\ldots,\widehat{h_i},\ldots,h_{2m}),
\end{equation}
where $h_i\in G$ is any lift of $y_i\in Y$, defines an $H$-invariant
linear functional $\psi_m:E_{2m}\to\C$ satisfying
\[
 \psi_m\partial=0,\qquad
 \psi_m(z_{2m})=2^{-m}\lambda.
\]
Here evaluation on the coinvariant chain $z_{2m}$ is defined by
$H$-invariance.
statements.section_title: A Pfaffian cocycle detecting the trace coefficient

statements.label: cor:integral
statements.text:
For every discrete group $G$, the Hattori--Stallings trace of every
class in $K_0(\Z G)$ is supported on $[1]_G$.

statements.title: Berrick--Chatterji--Mislin consequences
statements.label: cor:homotopy-idempotents
statements.text:
Let $M$ be a connected closed smooth oriented manifold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
 \item If $\dim M>2$ and $f:M\to M$ satisfies $f\circ f\simeq f$
 by free homotopy, then some self-map freely homotopic to $f$ has
 exactly one fixed point.
 \item Choose $x_0\in M$ and put $G=\pi_1(M,x_0)$. If
 $f:(M,x_0)\to(M,x_0)$ satisfies $f\circ f\simeq_* f$ by based
 homotopy and $f_\#=\id_G$, then
 \[
  L(f)=L^{(2)}(\widetilde f).
 \]
 Here $\widetilde f$ is the lift to the universal cover fixing a chosen
 point above $x_0$; it is $G$-equivariant. The left side is the ordinary
 Lefschetz number, and the right side is the alternating sum of von
 Neumann traces on the induced $L^2$-homology maps, as in
 \cite[Definition 7.1]{BCM2006}.
\end{enumerate}

title: The Blockwise Alperin Weight Conjecture
abstract: We prove the numerical blockwise Alperin weight conjecture for every finite group and every prime p. For each p-block B, the number of irreducible Brauer characters in B equals the number of conjugacy classes of B-weights.

tex.abstract:
We prove the numerical blockwise Alperin weight conjecture for every
finite group and every prime $p$. For each $p$-block $B$, the number of
irreducible Brauer characters in $B$ equals the number of conjugacy
classes of $B$-weights.
sections: From block counts to generating tuples
A genus-one curve with large index and independent labels
Absolute differentials and the inseparable genus estimate
A valued lift and descent of marked covers
Specialization, connectedness, and the tuple count

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every prime $p$, every finite group $G$, and every $p$-block $B$ of $G$,
\[
                  l(B)=|W_p(B)|.
\]

statements.title: Local--global and principal-block bounds
statements.label: cor:block-consequences
statements.text:
Let $p$ be a prime, $G$ a finite group, $B$ a $p$-block with defect group
$D$, and $b$ its Brauer correspondent in $N_G(D)$. Then
\[
 l(B)\geq l(b),\qquad
 D\text{ abelian}\Longrightarrow l(B)=l(b).
\]
For $P\in\operatorname{Syl}_p(G)$, one also has
\[
 |\IBr_p(G)|\geq|\IBr_p(N_G(P))|.
\]
Let $B_0$ be the principal $p$-block of $G$, and let $k_p(G)$ count the
conjugacy classes of $p$-power-order elements, including the identity.
Then
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 k_p(G)=3&\Longrightarrow l(B_0)\geq (p-1)/2,\\
 p\mid |G|&\Longrightarrow l(B_0)\geq 2\sqrt{p-1}+1-k_p(G).
 \end{aligned}
\]

statements.title: Uniform divisibility for generating tuples
statements.label: thm:tuple-divisibility
statements.text:
Let $J$ be a finite group with $O_p(J)=1$. For $s\geq0$, $n=p^s$,
and a multiset
$\mathcal M$ of $n$ conjugacy classes of $p$-singular elements of $J$,
let $N_{J,s}(\mathcal M)$ be the number, modulo simultaneous
$J$-conjugation, of ordered tuples
\[
 (x,y,u_1,\ldots,u_n)\in J^{n+2}
\]
satisfying
\begin{equation}
 [x,y]u_1\cdots u_n=1,\qquad
 \langle x,y,u_1,\ldots,u_n\rangle=J,
 \qquad \{[u_1],\ldots,[u_n]\}=\mathcal M.
\end{equation}
For every integer $h\geq1$, there is an integer $s_0=s_0(p,J,h)$
such that
\[
 p^h\mid N_{J,s}(\mathcal M)
 \qquad(s\geq s_0)
\]
for every such multiset $\mathcal M$.
statements.section_title: From block counts to generating tuples

statements.title: Reduction to uniform tuple divisibility
statements.label: prop:group-reduction
statements.text:
If \Cref{thm:tuple-divisibility} holds for every finite group with
trivial $p$-core, then for every finite group $X$ and central
idempotent $E\in kX$ one has $l(X,E)=((1+T)z)(X,E)$.
In particular the block equality in \Cref{thm:main} follows, with
the stated block assignment and with $Q=1$ included.
statements.section_title: From block counts to generating tuples

statements.label: prop:twist-index
statements.text:
Fix $s\geq1$, put $n=p^s$, and choose $A_0/\kappa$ and
$P\in A_0(\kappa)$ of exact order $n$ as in
\Cref{lem:ordinary-elliptic}.  There are finitely generated fields
$F_0\subset F'$ over $\kappa$, each of transcendence degree $n$,
and a smooth projective geometrically integral genus-one curve
$E/F_0$ with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $F'=\kappa(A_0^n)$, and $F'/F_0$ is cyclic Galois of degree
$n$.  With $t_i\in A_0(F')$ the generic projection points, a
generator satisfies
\begin{equation}
                 \sigma(t_i)=t_{i+1}-P
                 \qquad(i\text{ modulo }n).
\end{equation}
\item Under an identification $E_{F'}\simeq A_{0,F'}$, the descent
action on points is $x\mapsto\sigma(x)+P$.  The two disjoint divisors
\begin{equation}
       \mathcal B_{F'}=\sum_{i=1}^n[t_i],\qquad
       D_{F'}=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}[jP]
\end{equation}
descend to finite \'{e}tale effective divisors $\mathcal B,D$ of
degree $n$ on $E$, and $D$ is ample.
\item The index of $E/F_0$ is exactly $n$.
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: A genus-one curve with large index and independent labels

statements.label: cor:index-base-change
statements.text:
Let $h\geq1$ and $s\geq h$, and let $F/F_0$ be a finite extension
with $[F:F_0]_p\leq p^h$.  Every divisor on $E_F$ has degree over
$F$ divisible by $p^{s-h}$.  More generally, if $C/F$ is a regular
projective integral curve with a finite dominant morphism
$C\to E_F$, then every divisor and every invertible sheaf on $C$
has degree over $F$ divisible by $p^{s-h}$.
statements.section_title: A genus-one curve with large index and independent labels

statements.title: Exact purely inseparable genus estimate
statements.label: thm:inseparable-genus
statements.text:
Fix $h\ge1$ and take $s\ge h$ such that
\begin{equation}
 p^{s-h}>m\bigl(h+\log_p m\bigr).
 
\end{equation}
Let $F/F_0$ be finite with $[F:F_0]_p\le p^h$, and let $Z$ be the
normalization of $E_F$ in a finite purely inseparable extension of its
function field of degree $d\le m$.  Choose a compositum $S=FF'$.
The curve $Z_S$ is integral and regular.  Let $r_i$ be the ramification
index of $Z_S\to E_S$ at the unique point over $t_i$.
With $\nu(Z)$ computed over $F$, one has
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\nu(Z)}d\ge\sum_{i=1}^n\left(1-\frac1{r_i}\right).
 
\end{equation}
The bound is uniform in $F$, $Z$, and the tuple-class multiset used
later in the counting argument.
statements.section_title: Absolute differentials and the inseparable genus estimate

statements.title: The absolute determinant computes arithmetic genus
statements.label: prop:absolute-genus
statements.section_title: Absolute differentials and the inseparable genus estimate

statements.label: prop:mixed-lift
statements.text:
There are complete discretely valued fields $K_b\subset K_b'$ of
characteristic zero, with valuation rings $R_b\subset R_b'$, and a smooth
projective genus-one curve $\mathcal X/R_b$ with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item The extension $K_b'/K_b$ is cyclic Galois of degree $n$;
the extension $R_b'/R_b$ is finite \emph{\'{e}tale} Galois, its residue
extension is $F'/F_0$, and the two fields have the same value group.
Moreover, $K_b$ contains $\mathbb Q_p$ and all $m$th roots of unity,
where $m=|J|$.
\item The special fiber of $\mathcal X$ is $E/F_0$.
There is a relatively ample effective divisor $D$ on $\mathcal X$ of
fiber degree $n$.
\item Over $R_b'$ there are pairwise disjoint sections
$\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n$ reducing respectively to $t_1,\ldots,t_n$.
They avoid $D$, and their union descends to a finite \emph{\'{e}tale}
effective divisor on $\mathcal X$.
Under the cyclic descent action the sections are permuted by
$\xi_i\mapsto\xi_{i+1}$.
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: A valued lift and descent of marked covers

statements.label: prop:spherical-base
statements.text:
There is an extension $K_s/K_b$ with value group $\mathbb Q$ and residue
field $F_0$ which is spherically complete.  Every finite extension
$L/K_s$, equipped with an extension of its valuation, has value group
$\mathbb Q$, is spherically complete, and satisfies
\begin{equation}
                   [\operatorname{res}(L):F_0]=[L:K_s].
\end{equation}
The valuation on $K_s$, and on each such $L$, has a unique extension to
every algebraic extension.  Moreover
$\overline{K_s}\simeq\mathbb C$ as abstract fields.
statements.section_title: A valued lift and descent of marked covers

statements.title: Descent from a small Sylow orbit
statements.label: prop:small-orbit-descent
statements.text:
Assume $O_p(J)=1$ and fix a multiset $\mathcal C$ as in
\Cref{lem:marked-cover-classification}.  There is a finite Galois
extension $M/K_s$ through which the action on $\mathcal T_{\mathcal C}$
factors.  Let $P_\Gamma$ be a Sylow $p$-subgroup of
$\Gamma=\operatorname{Gal}(M/K_s)$.
If a $P_\Gamma$-orbit has size less than $p^h$, one of its marked covers
descends to a finite extension $L/K_s$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
                [L:K_s]_p<p^h,
                \qquad [F:F_0]_p=[L:K_s]_p,
                \qquad F=\operatorname{res}(L).
\end{equation}
The descended map $Y\to X=\mathcal X_L$ has geometrically connected
smooth projective source, degree $m$, the specified $J$-action, and all
branch indices at the $\xi_i$ divisible by $p$.
statements.section_title: A valued lift and descent of marked covers

statements.label: prop:no-small-cover
statements.text:
Suppose $O_p(J)=1$ and \eqref{eq:specialization-threshold} holds. There is no
finite extension $L/K_s$ with $[L:K_s]_p<p^h$ over which the marked curve
$X=\mathcal X_L$ admits a geometrically connected smooth projective
$J$-Galois cover $f:Y\to X$, with its $J$-action defined over $L$, branched
only at the marked points and with ramification index divisible by $p$ at
every marked point.
statements.section_title: Specialization, connectedness, and the tuple count

statements.label: prop:specialization-model
statements.text:
The degree equality \eqref{eq:residue-degree-equality} and the
Euler-characteristic equality in \eqref{eq:sharp-specialization}
produce a flat projective scheme $\mathcal Y$ of finite presentation
over $R$, with
\[
 \mathcal Y_L\simeq Y,\qquad
 \mathcal Y_F\simeq\coprod_{w\in\mathcal V}C_w.
\]
statements.section_title: Specialization, connectedness, and the tuple count

statements.title: Character-count and defect data
statements.label: cor:character-data
statements.text:
Let $B$ be a $p$-block of a finite group with defect group $D$ of order
$p^d$, and write $k(B)=|\Irr(B)|$. If $k(B)-l(B)=1$, then the possible
numerical data $(p^d,l(B))$ are exactly the following:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item There are positive integers $n,m$ such that $d=nm$, every prime divisor of $n$
      divides $p^m-1$, and $4\mid n$ implies $4\mid p^m-1$, with
      \[
       l(B)=\sum_{e\mid n}\frac{p^{em}-1}{ne}J_2(n/e),\qquad
       J_2(t)=t^2\prod_{\substack{q\mid t\\q\text{ prime}}}(1-q^{-2}).
      \]
\item The exceptional pairs are
      \[
       \begin{aligned}
       (p^d,l(B))\in\{&(5^2,7),(7^2,8),(11^2,9),(11^2,35),\\
                       &(23^2,88),(29^2,63),(59^2,261)\}.
       \end{aligned}
      \]
\end{enumerate}
All listed data occur, and in every case $k(B)=l(B)+1$.

statements.title: Functorial Alperin weight identity
statements.label: cor:functorial-awc
statements.text:
Let $b$ be a block idempotent of $kG$, where $G$ is finite. Let
$\mathcal S_p(G)$ consist of all strict chains
$\sigma=(1=P_0<P_1<\cdots<P_n)$ of $p$-subgroups, including $(1)$.
Put
\[
 |\sigma|=n,\qquad
 G_\sigma=\bigcap_{i=0}^nN_G(P_i),\qquad
 b_\sigma=\operatorname{Br}_{P_n}(b).
\]
Since $C_G(P_n)\leq G_\sigma$ and the Brauer image is invariant
under $G_\sigma$, the element $b_\sigma$ is a central idempotent
of $kG_\sigma$, possibly zero or a sum of blocks. Thus the pair
$(G_\sigma,b_\sigma)$ is an object of the category just described.
Then, summing over representatives of the $G$-conjugacy classes of chains,
\[
 \sum_{\sigma\in[G\backslash\mathcal S_p(G)]}
 (-1)^{|\sigma|}[[G_\sigma,b_\sigma]]_F
 =\begin{cases}
 [S_{1,1,F}],&\text{if $b$ has defect zero},\\
 0,&\text{if $b$ has positive defect}
 \end{cases}
 \quad\text{in }K_0(\mathcal F\mathcal B\ell_{F,k}).
\]

title: The Bogomolov-Pop reconstruction theorem
abstract: We prove the Bogomolov–Pop reconstruction conjecture for function fields of transcendence degree at least two over arbitrary algebraically closed fields of characteristic different from ℓ. The pro-ℓ abelian-by-central datum determines the perfect closure and its constant field, with precisely the Frobenius and ℓ-adic unit ambiguities.

tex.abstract:
We prove the Bogomolov--Pop reconstruction conjecture for function fields of
transcendence degree at least two over arbitrary algebraically closed fields
of characteristic different from $\ell$.
The pro-$\ell$ abelian-by-central datum determines the perfect closure and its
constant field, with precisely the Frobenius and $\ell$-adic unit ambiguities.

statements.title: Bogomolov--Pop reconstruction
statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $k$ and $l$ be arbitrary algebraically closed fields of characteristics
different from $\ell$, and let $K/k$ and $L/l$ be function fields with
$\trdeg(K/k),\trdeg(L/l)\ge2$.  Then
\[
 \Phi_{K,L}:\Isom_F^i(K,L)\longrightarrow
 \Isom^c(\Pi_L^a,\Pi_K^a)/\Zell^\times,
 \qquad [\alpha]\longmapsto[\alpha^*],
\]
is a bijection.

statements.label: local:transport
statements.text:
Let $K/k$ and $L/l$ be function fields over algebraically closed
fields of characteristic different from~$\ell$, each of
transcendence degree at least two.  Let
$\varphi:W_L\to W_K$ be a continuous bracket-compatible
$\Zell$-module isomorphism.  Then their transcendence degrees agree,
say they are~$d$.  For every $1\leq r<d$, the map $\varphi$ carries
exactly the pairs $I_w\subset D_w$ of quasi-prime $r$-divisors of
$L/l$ onto the corresponding pairs of $K/k$.
For matched pairs it induces a continuous isomorphism
\[
 D_w/I_w\cong W_{Lw}\ \longrightarrow\
 D_v/I_v\cong W_{Kv}
\]
that preserves alternating pairs.

statements.label: local:curves
statements.text:
In the setting of Proposition~\ref{local:transport}, let
$w$ and $v$ be matched quasi-prime $(d-1)$-divisors.
Then $lw$ is algebraic over a finite field if and only if $kv$ is.
When this holds, the induced isomorphism $W_{Lw}\to W_{Kv}$ carries
the full family of point inertia subgroups of the respective smooth
projective curves onto each other.  Corresponding normalized order
characters differ by units of~$\Zell$.

statements.title: Uniform pencil support
statements.label: pencil:uniform
statements.text:
For every $t\in K\setminus k$, there is a finite constant $B_t$ such that
\[
 \sum_{D\in\operatorname{Supp}_X(\Theta[t-a])}\deg D\le B_t
 \qquad\text{for every }a\in k.
\]
In particular, all these supports are finite, with a bound independent
of the member of the pencil.

statements.label: pencil:finite
statements.text:
For every $z\in K^\times$, the class $\Theta[z]$ has finite support on
$X$.

statements.label: recovery:curves
statements.text:
The map $\Theta$ gives a bijection between the completed curve
subfields of $K/k$ and those of $L/l$. More precisely, for every curve
subfield $E\subset K$ there is a unique curve subfield $P\subset L$
such that
\[
 \Theta(\widehat E)=\widehat P.
\]

statements.label: recovery:divisorial
statements.text:
A quasi-prime divisor $v$ of $K/k$ is divisorial if and only if
\begin{equation}
 D_v^\perp\cap\widehat E=0
\end{equation}
for some curve subfield $E$ of $K/k$. Consequently $\varphi$
preserves divisorial inertia and decomposition groups in both
directions.

statements.label: recovery:rational
statements.text:
The point inertia lines of every curve subfield $E$ are precisely
the saturations of the nonzero images $\rho_E(I_v)$ for divisorial
valuations $v$ of $K/k$. The correspondence of
Theorem~\ref{recovery:curves} preserves these lines and the genus.
In particular, it matches exactly the relatively algebraically closed
rational subfields.

If $\Theta(\widehat E)=\widehat P$, the induced continuous
isomorphism $\varphi_E:W_P\to W_E$ makes the diagram
\begin{equation}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large]
 W_L \arrow[r,"\varphi"] \arrow[d,two heads,"\rho_P"']
   & W_K \arrow[d,two heads,"\rho_E"] \\
 W_P \arrow[r,"\varphi_E"'] & W_E
\end{tikzcd}
\end{equation}
commute and matches the point inertia lines on its targets.
For rational $E$ and $P$, these are the geometric rational quotient
diagrams, with their point decomposition data.

statements.title: Pop's reconstruction theorems
statements.label: reconstruction:pop
statements.text:
Let $F/\kappa$ and $F'/\kappa'$ be function fields of transcendence
degree greater than one over algebraically closed fields of
characteristic different from $\ell$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item From $\Pi_F^c\to\Pi_F^a$ and the union of its true divisorial
inertia groups, one recovers the total decomposition graph, functorially
under class-two isomorphisms whose abelianizations preserve this union.
\item Suppose an isomorphism between the total decomposition graphs of
$F$ and $F'$ is compatible with all their geometric rational quotient
diagrams.  Then its map on the top abelian groups is induced, up to one
unit in $\Zell$, by an isomorphism of perfect closures in the opposite
direction carrying the constant fields onto each other.  That field
isomorphism is unique modulo Frobenius twists in positive characteristic,
and unique in characteristic zero.
\end{enumerate}
In (2), a geometric rational quotient is restriction to
$\kappa(u)\subset F$ with $F/\kappa(u)$ regular, together with the
point inertia and decomposition data on its target.  Compatibility
means that restriction commutes with the graph isomorphisms and the
induced isomorphisms of these targets.

title: The Boltzmann–Grad limit for stable radial potentials on regular kinetic intervals
abstract: We derive the nonlinear Boltzmann equation from a grand-canonical Newtonian gas with initial pair exclusion. We treat stable, finite-range radial potentials that are C2 except for an allowed repulsive singularity at the origin, and C1 initial probability densities with spatially summable Gaussian bounds on the density and its spatial gradient. All fixed-order rescaled factorial marginals converge in L1, uniformly throughout every finite interval on which the classical kinetic solution has a uniform Gaussian bound. The result allows attractive wells and dynamically formed clusters, without restrictions on the differential scattering cross-section.

tex.abstract:
We derive the nonlinear Boltzmann equation from a grand-canonical
Newtonian gas with initial pair exclusion. We treat stable, finite-range
radial potentials that are $C^2$ except for an allowed repulsive singularity
at the origin, and $C^1$ initial probability
densities with spatially summable Gaussian bounds on the density and
its spatial gradient.
All fixed-order rescaled factorial marginals converge in $L^1$,
uniformly throughout every finite interval on which the classical
kinetic solution has a uniform Gaussian bound.
The result allows attractive wells and dynamically formed clusters,
without restrictions on the differential scattering cross-section.

statements.title: Potential class
statements.label: pre:potential
statements.text:
Write $\Phi(q)=\phi(|q|)$, with $\Phi(q)=0$ for $|q|\geq1$.
Assume either $\Phi\in C^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$, or
$\Phi\in C^2(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})$ with
$\Phi(q)\to+\infty$ as $q\to0$.
In the latter case set $\Phi(0)=+\infty$.
Assume thermodynamic stability: for some $B\geq0$,
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{\substack{i,j\in R\\i<j}}\Phi(q_i-q_j)\geq-B|R|
\end{equation}
for every finite configuration of distinct points.
The potential is fixed independently of $\varepsilon$.

statements.title: Global finite-particle flow
statements.label: pre:flow
statements.text:
For each fixed $\varepsilon>0$ and finite label set $R$,
\eqref{pre:dynamics} has a unique global flow from every finite-energy
initial state in its domain. The flow preserves phase volume and
$\mathscr H_R$. In the singular case, every pair distance along a given
trajectory is bounded away from zero. In the nonsingular case coincident
positions are permitted.

statements.title: Scattering nondegeneracy
statements.label: pre:scattering
statements.text:
Outside a set of zero incoming flux, an encounter either is a straight
force-free passage or satisfies
\begin{equation}
 v'\ne v,\qquad v_*'\ne v .
\end{equation}
For $M<\infty$ and $\eta>0$, the non-free relative incoming data $(n,g)$
with $|g|\leq M$
can be restricted to a rotation-invariant compact set, losing at most
$\eta$ relative incoming flux, on which the duration is bounded and
$|g|$, $|v'-v|$, and $|v_*'-v|$ have positive lower bounds.
For fixed radial scattering parameters, each of these nonzero
increments has a uniform spherical directional marginal under common
rotation. The two increments need not be independent.

statements.title: Diagramwise factorization
statements.label: cell:factorization
statements.text:
Split the labels into $S=S_1\sqcup S_2$ and the roots into
$R=R_1\sqcup R_2$, where $R_i\subset S_i$.  Let $\gamma_i$ be a
diagram on $(R_i,S_i)$.  Define $\eta_I(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)$ to be the
indicator that every displayed particle trajectory of $\gamma_1$
has distance greater than $\varepsilon$ throughout $I$ from every
displayed trajectory of $\gamma_2$.  This includes detached groups
and includes the initial and terminal times.
For a single global diagram $\gamma$, define
$\eta_I(\gamma;S_1,S_2)$ by the same condition between its labelled
paths in $S_1$ and $S_2$, using their prescribed force-group flows.

On this indicator, merge the two root groups, and take the union of
the two batches at each generation, padding a finished list by empty
batches.  This gives a diagram on $(R,S)$.  Conversely, every nonzero
diagram term satisfying $\eta_I(\gamma;S_1,S_2)=1$ splits uniquely in
this manner.  Its detached groups necessarily belong to one $S_i$,
and its root flow splits over its two intersections with $S_i$.
Under this bijection the signed transport measures, with this
indicator imposed, agree with the tensor product of the two
diagram transport measures:
\begin{equation}
 \sigma(\gamma)w_I(\gamma)\mathsf H^I_{R,A}\,\eta_I
  =\eta_I\bigl[
       \sigma(\gamma_1)w_I(\gamma_1)\mathsf H^I_{R_1,A_1}
       \otimes
       \sigma(\gamma_2)w_I(\gamma_2)\mathsf H^I_{R_2,A_2}
             \bigr].
 
\end{equation}
Summation over the bijection preserves this equality.  Factorial
weights split as
\begin{equation}
 \binom{m_1+m_2}{m_1}
       \frac{\mu^{m_1+m_2}}{(m_1+m_2)!}
   =\frac{\mu^{m_1}}{m_1!}\frac{\mu^{m_2}}{m_2!}.
 
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: An exact finite expansion on one cell

statements.title: Stopped cell expansion and positive domination
statements.label: cell:stopping
statements.text:
For $k>|R|$, the finite-cloud expansion equals its complete diagrams
with fewer than $k$ selected labels plus a finite signed remainder.
Each remainder term is of one of the following types.
\begin{enumerate}
 \item Its root group $A$ already has $|A|\geq k$.  Its transport is
 $c_I^R(A)\mathsf H^I_{R,A}$ times the factor
 $\Xi_I(\{A\};S\setminus A)\in[0,1]$.
 \item Its completed generations and its final partial generation
 select a union $U$ with $|U|\geq k$.  Immediately before the last
 selected component $B_*$, the number of selected labels is less
 than $k$.  All displayed groups satisfy the connectivity,
 initial-polymer, same-generation avoidance, and preceding-generation
 touch conditions of Definition~\ref{def:cell-diagram}.  Its weight
 is the corresponding sign and indicators times a factor
 $\vartheta_I$ of the form \eqref{eq:cell-stop-theta}, lying in $[0,1]$.
\end{enumerate}
In the second case the overshoot is by at most one additional
component.  In particular, if every component of every trial
subsystem formed from initial polymers has size at most $D$, then
$|A|\leq |R|D$, and a stopped union has size at most
$\max\{|R|D,k-1+D\}$.

Replacing the sign by $+1$ and dropping the last factor gives a
pointwise positive domination of the total variation of the
remainder.  Its expected version is a sum of these positive
contact expressions integrated against the initial isolated
factorial measures of the selected unions, with the factors
$\mu^m/m!$ of \eqref{eq:cell-factorial}.  This is an identity and
a domination statement, not a claim that this sum tends to zero.

statements.title: Centering and inversion
statements.label: cent:identity
statements.text:
For every $\pi$ and almost every $Z_R$,
\begin{equation}
 \chi_\pi^\eps\widetilde F_R^\eps(t)
 =\chi_\pi^\eps
 \sum_{A\subset S(\pi)}f_{S(\pi)\setminus A}(t)
 E_{\pi_A}^\eps(t).
\end{equation}
Both formulas hold for arbitrary factorial densities, without a
smallness or factorization assumption.

statements.title: Collapsing the pattern sum
statements.label: cent:pattern-collapse
statements.text:
For $D\subset R$ let
\begin{equation}
 \iota_D^R(Z_R)
 =\prod_{i\in D}\prod_{j\in R\setminus\{i\}}
       \1_{\{|x_i-x_j|>\eps\}},\qquad
 \mathcal E_R=\sum_{\pi\in\mathcal P(R)}E_\pi,
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal P(R)$ is the set of partitions of $R$. Then
\begin{align}
 \mathcal E_R
 &=\sum_{D\subset R}(-1)^{|D|}\iota_D^R f_D
                       \widetilde F_{R\setminus D},
       \\
 \widetilde F_R
 &=\sum_{D\subset R}\iota_D^R f_D
                       \mathcal E_{R\setminus D}.
       
\end{align}
Thus a cut carries subset choices, but no additional factor equal to
the number of partitions. For arbitrary signed families $G$ and $e$
with each $e_\pi$ supported on its pattern, write
\[
 \|G\|_{1,\leq U}=\max_{0\leq r\leq U}\|G_{[r]}\|_1,
 \qquad
 \|e\|_{\pi,1,\leq U}
   =\max_{0\leq r\leq U}\sum_{\pi\in\mathcal P([r])}\|e_\pi\|_1.
\]
Let $\mathsf M_t$ be the transform \eqref{cent:definition-eq} and
$\mathsf I_t$ its inverse \eqref{cent:inverse}, summed over full
patterns. They satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \|\mathsf M_tG\|_{\pi,1,\leq U}\leq2^U\|G\|_{1,\leq U},
 \qquad
 \|\mathsf I_te\|_{1,\leq U}\leq2^U\|e\|_{\pi,1,\leq U}.
\end{equation}

statements.title: Short-layer residual
statements.label: cent:residual
statements.text:
Set $\beta_0=\beta/2$. There is $b_*>0$, depending only on the fixed
bounds in Proposition~\ref{pre:envelopes}, for which the following
holds. Suppose $b\leq b_*$, $K(\eps)\to\infty$, and
$J(\eps)\to\infty$ is a fixed power of $1+|\log\eps|$.
Then
\begin{equation}
 r_{u,t}^{\eps}=f(t)-\mathscr G_{u,t}^{\eps,J,K},\qquad
 \sup_{\substack{0\leq u\leq t\leq T\\t-u\leq b}}
 \|r_{u,t}^{\eps}\|_{\mathrm{Bol},\beta_0}
 =:\eta_\eps\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation}
All the reference sums and residuals have uniformly bounded norms at
this one fixed exponent. The proof uses only short-layer tree
summability and two-body scattering.

statements.title: Exact simple-family cancellation
statements.label: cent:cancellation
statements.text:
In the retained operator $\mathsf A_j$ of
\eqref{cent:reference-mismatch}, a singleton root
whose displayed family satisfies the reference-history conditions
$\mathscr S_n^{\eps,J}$ above, ends entirely on independent
$f(t_{j-1})$, and avoids every displayed trajectory of every other
family throughout the layer cancels with its tensor-subtraction
term. The avoidance requirement includes all detached generation
groups and all reference trees coming from tensor subtraction.
It also includes the full-array pattern restrictions at cuts.
A residual factor is treated as a stopped slot, not as an unexamined
trajectory. The pairing is exact coefficientwise for total formal
size $p<K_j$. The finite complementary operator $B_j$ stays in
\eqref{cent:layer-identity}; no cancellation or positive physical
remainder bound is asserted for it.

statements.title: Cross-layer charge count
statements.label: cent:charges
statements.text:
Consider a term remaining after Proposition~\ref{cent:cancellation},
with no unresolved cutoff interruption. Let $H$ count the root slots
entering each expanded layer at its upper cut, including the starting
roots and residual slots, summed over those layers.
Retained inputs at time zero are terminal charges,
not additional root occurrences in $H$. Let $h_0$ count uncentered
restarting top roots, let $d$ be the number of distinct marked lives,
let $r$ be the number of residual factors, and let $i$ be the number
of retained singleton factors at time zero. With at most $L$ expanded
layers,
\begin{equation}
 H\leq Lh_0+L^2d+Lr+Li.
\end{equation}
In particular, if $H\geq\delta p$ and $h_0\leq\delta p/(2L)$, then
\begin{equation}
 d+r+i\geq\frac{\delta}{2L^2}p.
\end{equation}
The statement is purely combinatorial and imposes no smallness on an
uncentered restarting top.

statements.title: Finite-term bound with its time factors
statements.label: hist:basic

statements.title: Finite parameter discards
statements.label: hist:irregular
statements.text:
Fix $L$, $A$, $\delta>0$, and $M_0<\infty$.  The source-energy cutoff
$R$ and fixed numbers
\[
 U,W<\infty,\qquad \gamma,\kappa>0
\]
can be chosen so that, for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon$,
the total finite history integral with at least $\delta p$ marked
additions is at most $\eta_\Gamma e^{-M_0p}$.  An addition is marked
if it is in a multiple-addition cell, is an endpoint pin, or is an
ordinary pin satisfying any of the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item its original parent speed exceeds $U$, its added absolute
velocity exceeds $W$, or its relative speed is below $\gamma$;
\item for a genuine non-force-free isolated continuation, either
output increment relative to the incoming parent has magnitude below
$\kappa$;
\item its isolated two-body duration in physical time exceeds
$\varepsilon^{.96}$;
\item its contact time is within $\varepsilon^{.95}$ of a cell
boundary, or it belongs to a pair of birth times separated by less
than $2\varepsilon^{.9}$.
\end{enumerate}
The contribution of $S>Rp$ has the same bound.  The constants in this
proposition may depend on $L$; they do not enter the $C$ in
\eqref{eq:hist-finite-bound}.

statements.title: Extensive simultaneous crowding
statements.label: hist:crowding
statements.text:
Fix $A,Q,L,R$ and $\delta>0$.  Among independently enveloped finite
histories with $p\leq P^A$ and $S\leq Rp$, the activity-normalized integral
for which at some time at least $\delta p$ displayed labels have a
companion within $\rho=\varepsilon^{.85}$ is bounded by
\begin{equation}
 \eta_\Gamma P^{C_{A,Q,L,R}p}
       \varepsilon^{.275\delta p-1}.
 
\end{equation}
For $\delta p\geq8$ this is at most
$\eta_\Gamma\varepsilon^{.1\delta p}$ for sufficiently small
$\varepsilon$, uniformly in the stated range of $p$.

statements.title: Separated original parents
statements.label: hist:separated
statements.text:
Given $L,A,\delta>0$ and $M_0<\infty$, one can discard finite terms
of total integral at most $\eta_\Gamma e^{-M_0p}$ so that, except at
fewer than $\delta p$ ordinary pins, the original parent is at
distance greater than $\varepsilon^{.85}$ from every other already
displayed path immediately before the insertion.  This assertion is
used for large histories; fixed bounded orders are treated by their
direct geometric estimates.

statements.title: Causal exposure for mixed prescriptions
statements.label: exp:exposure
statements.text:
Fix an admissible mixed whole-cell prescription with $p\le P^a$ labels and
a total energy budget $\mathcal K\le Rp$.  Fix a collection of $k$ disjoint
regular terminal trees as in Lemma~\ref{exp:terminal}.  Sum the absolute
activity-normalized chart integrals over the event that every selected tree has a
first defect.  The result is bounded by
\begin{equation}

 \mathcal A_p\,(pJ)^{C p}\bigl(p^C\varepsilon^c\bigr)^{k/2},
\end{equation}
The factor $(pJ)^{Cp}$ includes cell-segment choices.  Constants may
depend on the fixed layer count, compact cutoffs, $M$, and $R$.
statements.section_title: Terminal trees and exposure of first defects

statements.title: An extensive-defect gain
statements.label: exp:defects
statements.text:
Fix $0<\alpha\le1$, $A>0$, the layer count, and the polynomial size
exponent $a>0$.  There exist fixed constants $\theta=\theta(\alpha,A)>0$,
$p_0<\infty$, and sufficiently small $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that, after
the compact cutoffs are chosen, the following bound holds uniformly for
\[
 0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0,\qquad
 p_0\le p\le P^a,\qquad h_0\le\theta p.
\]
For histories with at least $\alpha p$ affected lives, their absolute
integral, divided by
the source factor $\mathcal A_p$ of \eqref{exp:source-factor}, is bounded
by the sum of the exceptional-parameter contributions bounded by $e^{-Ap}$
and a contribution bounded by
\begin{equation}

 P^{C_Lp}\varepsilon^{c_Lp}.
\end{equation}
The constants $c_L>0$ and $C_L$ are fixed before $\varepsilon\downarrow0$.
The assertion includes recollisions, interference with a long-lived cluster,
and contacts with detached or subtracted trajectories.
statements.section_title: Terminal trees and exposure of first defects

statements.title: Finite marked histories
statements.label: exp:finite
statements.text:
Fix the layer count and an integer $p_*$.  Sum the absolute integrals of the
original prescribed histories with at most $p_*$ labels, integrating all
top phase points, and suppose their independent source norms in
\eqref{exp:source-factor} are uniformly bounded.  The contribution with at
least one unprescribed contact, an incomplete isolated scattering at a
required cut, an interfering birth, or an endpoint-polymer defect tends to
zero as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$.  This statement includes $p=h_0$ and
contacts between distinct top roots.  The bounds are uniform over the
observation times and shortened endpoint cells in the fixed interval.
If instead a source has norm tending to zero, its finite-history integral
tends to zero by the same uniform finite-size majorant.
statements.section_title: Terminal trees and exposure of first defects

statements.title: Summability of completed finite terms
statements.label: close:summability
statements.text:
Fix any desired number $a>0$. One can choose a finite $L$, then
the rarity cutoffs, with the following property. For every fixed
polynomial label cap $p\leq P^A$, choose $J$ to be a sufficiently
large fixed power of $P$. There exist $\eta_L>0$ and $p_L<\infty$
such that, for sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, the sum of the
integrated absolute weights of completed histories with exactly
$p$ labels is at most
\begin{equation}
 e^{-ap},\qquad p\geq p_L,\qquad h_0\leq\eta_Lp.
\end{equation}
The same bound holds for an admissible mixed uncentered upper
block followed by centered lower layers, after the lower
simple-family cancellations. It is uniform over shortened endpoint
cells and layers and over tests of absolute value at most one.
For the original centered expansion, in which the upper
simple-family cancellations are also made, every fixed-size term
with a retained centered upper root tends to zero after integration.

statements.title: Actual witnesses and layer remainders
statements.label: close:tails
statements.text:
With the preceding schedule, for sufficiently small
$\varepsilon$ and every $1\leq j\leq L$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P\bigl(\mathcal B_j(D_j)\bigr)\leq e^{-8D_j},
 \qquad R_j\leq e^{-8K_j}.
\end{equation}
The estimates use the original Newtonian process, without
conditioning it to stay in a good set.

title: The Campana–Peternell conjecture in dimension six
abstract: We prove that every smooth connected complex projective Fano sixfold with nef tangent bundle is rational homogeneous, resolving the Campana–Peternell conjecture in complex dimension six. As a consequence, a connected compact Kähler manifold X with nef holomorphic tangent bundle and \(\dim_{\mathbb C}X-\widetilde q(X)\leq6\) has ordinary universal cover \(F\times\mathbb C^{\widetilde q(X)}\), where F is a rational homogeneous manifold and \(\widetilde q(X)\) is the maximal irregularity of a connected finite étale cover.

tex.abstract:
We prove that every smooth connected complex projective Fano sixfold with nef
tangent bundle is rational homogeneous, resolving the Campana--Peternell
conjecture in complex dimension six.
As a consequence, a connected compact K\"ahler manifold $X$ with nef
holomorphic tangent bundle and
$\dim_{\mathbb C}X-\widetilde q(X)\leq6$ has ordinary universal cover
$F\times\mathbb C^{\widetilde q(X)}$, where $F$ is a rational homogeneous
manifold and $\widetilde q(X)$ is the maximal irregularity of a connected
finite \'{e}tale cover.
sections: The sixfold theorem and its consequences

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Every smooth connected complex projective Fano variety of dimension six
with nef tangent bundle is rational homogeneous.

statements.title: Albanese fibres and uniformization
statements.label: cor:nef-tangent-uniformization
statements.text:
Let $X$ be a connected compact K\"ahler manifold whose holomorphic
tangent bundle is nef in the analytic sense. Suppose
\[
 0\leq d=\dim_{\mathbb C}X-\widetilde q(X)\leq6.
\]
Then there is a connected finite \'{e}tale cover $X'\to X$ with the
following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The Albanese map
      $\alpha:X'\to A=\operatorname{Alb}(X')$ is a smooth proper
      surjection with connected fibres, where $A$ is a complex torus of
      dimension $\widetilde q(X)$. Every fibre is rational homogeneous
      of dimension $d$, with a point allowed when $d=0$.
\item There is one such fibre $F$ for which $\alpha$ is a holomorphically
      locally trivial $F$-bundle. The ordinary universal cover of $X$
      is biholomorphic to
      \[
       \widetilde X\simeq F\times\mathbb C^{\widetilde q(X)}.
      \]
      It is therefore biholomorphic to a quasi-projective variety and
      is holomorphically convex. Its Remmert reduction is the projection
      \[
       F\times\mathbb C^{\widetilde q(X)}
       \longrightarrow\mathbb C^{\widetilde q(X)}.
      \]
\end{enumerate}
In particular, these conclusions hold whenever $\dim_{\mathbb C}X\leq6$.

statements.label: prop:minimal-family
statements.text:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex Fano manifold of dimension $n$ with nef tangent
bundle, and let $V$ be a component of rational curves of minimal
anticanonical degree $d$.  Then $U$ and $V$ are smooth projective varieties,
$\dim V=n+d-3$, the map $\pi:U\to V$ is a smooth $\mathbb P^1$-fibration,
and $e:U\to X$ is smooth and surjective with connected fibres of dimension
$d-2$.  For every fibre $C$ of $\pi$,
\begin{equation}
 T_e|_C\simeq\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(-1)^{\oplus(d-2)}.
\end{equation}

statements.label: prop:pseudoindex-reduction
statements.text:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex Fano sixfold with $\rho(X)=1$ and nef tangent
bundle.  Then either $X\simeq\mathbb P^6$, $X\simeq Q^6$, or its
pseudoindex is $4$ or $5$.

statements.label: prop:pseudoindex-four
statements.text:
A smooth complex Fano sixfold with nef tangent bundle, Picard number one
and pseudoindex four is rational homogeneous.

statements.label: prop:pseudoindex-five-recognition
statements.text:
Every smooth complex Fano sixfold with nef tangent bundle, Picard number
one and pseudoindex five is isomorphic to $\operatorname{Gr}(2,5)$.

statements.label: cor:positive-ke
statements.text:
Let $X$ be a smooth connected complex projective Fano variety with nef
tangent bundle and $1\leq\dim_{\mathbb C}X\leq6$.
Then $X$ admits a positive K\"ahler--Einstein metric. More precisely,
with the Ricci-form convention
\[
 \rho(\omega)=-i\partial\bar\partial\log\det(g_{a\bar b}),
\]
there is a K\"ahler form $\omega$ such that
\[
 \rho(\omega)=\omega,\qquad [\omega]=2\pi c_1(-K_X).
\]

title: The Critical Spin Field of the Planar XY Model
abstract: Using the companion critical Bessel-height and pin-limit theorems, we prove that at the mass-defined critical inverse temperature of the nearest-neighbor XY model on the square lattice, the spin field on a square with boundary angles fixed to zero converges along the full sequence to the full-variance imaginary exponential of a zero-Dirichlet Gaussian free field with stiffness \(2/\pi\). The normalization uses the exact center magnetization and the lattice Green-function factor. Convergence holds in law in \(H^{-3}_{\mathrm{loc}}((-1,1)^2)\); all mixed moments and joint laws of fields smeared against smooth compactly supported test functions in \((-1,1)^2\) converge as well.

tex.abstract:
Using the companion critical Bessel-height and pin-limit theorems, we
prove that at the mass-defined critical inverse temperature of the
nearest-neighbor XY model on the square lattice, the spin field on a
square with boundary angles fixed to zero converges along the full
sequence to the full-variance imaginary exponential of a zero-Dirichlet
Gaussian free field with stiffness \(2/\pi\). The normalization uses
the exact center magnetization and the lattice Green-function factor.
Convergence holds in law in \(H^{-3}_{\mathrm{loc}}((-1,1)^2)\);
all mixed moments and joint laws of fields smeared against smooth
compactly supported test functions in \((-1,1)^2\) converge as well.
sections: Magnetic sectors with holes of positive radius
Flat pins across a long annulus
Gluing kernels and stability from a fixed core
Laws and moments of the critical field

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For the fixed-boundary critical XY law \eqref{eq:pinned-spin-law},
the distributions \(S_n\) in \eqref{eq:spin-field} converge in law
along the full sequence \(n\to\infty\) to \(V_*\) in
\(H^{-3}_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)\).
Moreover, for every \(k\ge1\), every
\(f_1,\ldots,f_k\in C_c^\infty(D;\C)\), and every collection of
nonnegative integers \(p_1,q_1,\ldots,p_k,q_k\),
\begin{equation}
 \E_n^0\prod_{j=1}^k
       S_n(f_j)^{p_j}\overline{S_n(f_j)}^{\,q_j}
 \longrightarrow
 \E\prod_{j=1}^k
       V_*(f_j)^{p_j}\overline{V_*(f_j)}^{\,q_j}.
\end{equation}
The joint laws of these complex smeared fields converge as well.

statements.title: Critical height coefficient {\cite[Section~6]{C}}
statements.label: heights:critical-input
statements.text:
For the free-box spin mass threshold \(b_c\) of Section~\ref{sec:intro},
the Bessel height coefficient satisfies \(a(b_c)=8\pi\).

statements.title: Free rectangle limits {\cite[Theorem~2.4]{C}}
statements.label: heights:free-input
statements.text:
Let \(U_n\) be free axis-parallel rectangles at mesh \(n^{-1}\), with
endpoints converging to those of a nondegenerate rectangle \(U\).
For any finite collection of smooth functions defined near
\(\overline U\), the observations
\(\langle h,A_{U_n}g\rangle\) converge jointly, in Laplace transforms
and all moments, to centered Gaussians with covariance
\[
                  a\int_U\nabla g\cdot\nabla g'.
\]
For bounded piecewise continuous mean-zero densities and the exactly
centered profiles just specified, height smears converge jointly in
Laplace transforms and all moments, with covariance
\(a(-\Delta_{U,N})^{-1}\), where the inverse is on mean-zero functions.

statements.title: Mixed height limits {\cite[Theorem~3.1]{C}}
statements.label: heights:mixed-input
statements.text:
In any fixed mixed geometry, the centered massless Bessel height law
with primary hard pins has Gaussian Laplace and moment limits for each
finite collection of bounded piecewise continuous density smears.
On a component \(U\) meeting a pin \(p\), the covariance is the inverse
of the form
\[
  a^{-1}\int_U|\nabla u|^2
  \quad\hbox{on}\quad
  \{u\in H^1(U):u=0\text{ almost everywhere on }p\}.
\]
Free walls have the variational Neumann condition. On an unpinned
component, the assertion concerns mean-free smears; the fractional mean
modulo \(2\pi\) tends to an independent uniform variable.

A fixed finite-rank nonnegative quadratic penalty in box averages gives
the corresponding Gaussian limit. When the penalty controls every
unpinned component constant, lattice translation copies are summed and
the limiting constants are integrated. The assertions hold along
every admissible sequence of rounded discretizations.

statements.title: Separated primary pins {\cite[Theorem~3.2]{C}}
statements.label: heights:pin-input
statements.text:
In a fixed mixed geometry, start with no hard pins and add the centered
penalty \(\|Bh\|^2/2\), where \(B\) is a fixed finite list of
component-local box averages controlling every component constant.
For positively separated pin regions \(H,p\), put
\[
 D_n(H,p)=
 \log\frac{\Pbb(h_H=0\mid h_p=0)}{\Pbb(h_H=0)}.
\]
Then \(D_n(H,p)\ge0\) and it converges to the Gaussian pin interaction
for the Hilbert-space inner product associated with
\[
         \mathcal T(u)=a^{-1}\sum_U\int_U|\nabla u|^2+\|Bu\|^2,
         \qquad u\in\bigoplus_U H^1(U).
\]
More precisely, with orthogonality and projections taken for
\(\mathcal T\),
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
 V_Q=\{u:u=0\text{ almost everywhere on }Q\}^{\perp_{\mathcal T}},
 \qquad \Pi_Q=\operatorname{proj}_{V_Q},\qquad
 C=\Pi_H|_{V_p},\\
             D_n(H,p)\longrightarrow
                  -\frac12\log\det(1-C^*C).
 \end{gathered}
 \tag{1}
\end{equation}
The operator \(C\) is Hilbert--Schmidt and has norm strictly below one.

statements.title: Restoration at prescribed data
statements.label: heights:restoration
statements.text:
For an edge restoration with prescribed absolute or relative data
on \(p\), define
\[
       T^s(u)=\frac{Z_{\rm restored}^s(u)}{Z_{\rm cut}^s(u)},
       \qquad d=T^0(0_p).
\]
Use quotient constants on free components and sum all relative
integer translations when components are joined. Then
\[
                            0<T^s(u)\le d.
\]

statements.title: Average loss
statements.label: kernels:average-loss
statements.text:
For a regular interface,
\begin{equation}
 \int(T_i^s/d_i)\prod_\ell dm_\ell^s
 =
 \left(\int(T_i^0/d_i)\prod_\ell dm_\ell^0\right)
       \frac{F_{\mathrm{restored}}^s}{F_{\mathrm{cut}}^s}.
 \tag{10}
\end{equation}
Given any \(\xi>0\), first choose \(\varepsilon\) sufficiently small
and fix a polygon \(P\) satisfying its disk inclusions. Then choose
\(\lambda\) sufficiently large. There is a fixed aligned
threshold \(R_0\) such that every regular interface with smaller
inner scale at least \(R_0\) satisfies
\begin{equation}
             \int(1-T_i^s/d_i)\prod_\ell dm_\ell^s\le\xi
 \tag{11}
\end{equation}
in each of the two unit-period sectors and in the centered sector.
The individual flat-pin interactions in
Equation~\eqref{eq:source-9} can also be made arbitrarily small
with these choices.

statements.title: The last guard law
statements.label: kernels:last-guard
statements.text:
For these fixed choices, the last-guard law in a nest of \(N\)
annuli has density at most \(2\) relative to \(m_N^s\) for all
sufficiently large \(N\), in the centered sector and in either
unit-period sector. The conclusion holds for identical lattice
translates of the nest with the same threshold in \(N\).

statements.title: Convergence of every mixed moment
statements.label: fields:moments
statements.text:
For every $m\geq1$, signs $\sigma_i\in\{-1,1\}$, and
$f_i\in C_c^\infty(D;\C)$,
\begin{equation}
 \lim_{n\to\infty}\E_n^0\prod_{i=1}^m S_n^{\sigma_i}(f_i)
       =\E\prod_{i=1}^m V_*^{\sigma_i}(f_i).
\end{equation}
The right side is the integral in
Equation~\eqref{fields:continuum-moments} with $K=K_*$.
statements.section_title: Laws and moments of the critical field

statements.title: Joint convergence of test-function laws
statements.label: fields:law
statements.text:
For every $k\geq1$ and $f_1,\ldots,f_k\in C_c^\infty(D;\C)$,
\[
 (S_n(f_1),\ldots,S_n(f_k))
    \ \Longrightarrow\
 (V_*(f_1),\ldots,V_*(f_k)).
\]
Every mixed moment of this vector and its complex conjugate
converges.

statements.title: Tightness in the local Sobolev topology
statements.label: fields:tightness
statements.text:
The laws of $S_n$ are tight in $H^{-3}_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$.
They converge there, along the full sequence, to the law of $V_*$.

title: The Deligne-Drinfeld conjecture
abstract: We prove the Deligne–Drinfeld conjecture: the rational Grothendieck–Teichmüller Lie algebra is freely generated by one element in every odd weight at least three, with the corresponding isomorphism after weight completion.

tex.abstract: We prove the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture: the rational Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller Lie algebra is freely generated by one element in every odd weight at least three, with the corresponding isomorphism after weight completion.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There are homogeneous elements
\(\sigma_{2k+1}\in W_{2k+1}\), one for each \(k\ge1\), for which
\[
 \Lie_{\Q}\langle e_3,e_5,e_7,\ldots\rangle
 \longrightarrow (W,\{\, ,\,\}),\qquad
 e_{2k+1}\longmapsto\sigma_{2k+1},
\]
is an isomorphism of graded Lie algebras.
In particular, \(W\) is closed under the bracket
\eqref{eq:ihara}.  The induced map on completions by weight is a
continuous graded isomorphism.

statements.title: Saturated reduction
statements.label: prop:saturated-reduction
statements.text:
Let
\[
 K_n=\Lie_R\langle x,y\rangle_n,
 \qquad L_n=W_n\cap K_n.
\]
Then \(L_n\) is a saturated finite free \(R\)-submodule of \(K_n\),
and its reduction embeds in \(K_n/2K_n\).  Writing its image as
\(\overline L_n\), one has
\begin{equation}
 \dim_{\F}\overline L_n=\dim_{\Q}W_n.
\end{equation}
More generally, for any rational subspace \(V_n\subset W_n\), the
lattice \(M_n=V_n\cap K_n\) has an embedded reduction
\(\overline M_n\subset\overline L_n\) of dimension
\(\dim_{\Q}V_n\).

Every element of \(\overline L_n\) satisfies the reductions of the
three defining identities.  If \(n>2\), it also satisfies
\eqref{eq:special} and \eqref{eq:special-linearization} after
reduction, together with all formal coefficient consequences of
these identities.  In particular, putting \(z=x+y\),
\begin{equation}
 [x,\overline\psi(x,y)+\overline\psi(z,y)]
       +[y,\overline\psi(z,y)]=0
 \qquad(\overline\psi\in\overline L_n).
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Integral Lie algebras and the special identity

statements.label: prop:leading-pentagon
statements.text:
Let $\bar\psi\in\overline L_n$, $n>2$, and suppose its expression
$\Psi(A,C,B)$ lies in $F^r$.  Let $\chi$ be its component of count $r$,
and write $n=2m+r$, with $m>0$.  In $U(\mathfrak h)$ let
$\mathcal U_{\ell,<r}$ be the span of all products of exactly $\ell$
symbols from $\{a_i,v_{ij},u_{ij}\}$ that contain fewer than $r$
symbols $u$.  Then
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
 0\equiv{}&\chi(a_1,v_{12}+v_{13},u_{12}+u_{13})
       +\chi(a_2+v_{12},v_{23},u_{23})\\
 &+\chi(a_1+a_2+v_{12},v_{13}+v_{23},u_{13}+u_{23})\\
 &+\chi(a_1,v_{12},u_{12})\pmod{\mathcal U_{m+r,<r}}.
\end{split}
\end{equation}
For $r=0$ the indicated lower-count subspace is zero.
statements.section_title: A filtered degeneration of the pentagon

statements.label: prop:deletion-representation
statements.text:
The assignment $t_H\mapsto T_H$ defines a representation of
$\mathfrak h_{\Z}$ on $E_N$.  Equivalently, for every codimension-two
flat $X$ and every hyperplane $H_0\supset X$,
\begin{equation}
 \left[T_{H_0},\sum_{H\supset X}T_H\right]=0.
\end{equation}
It therefore extends to the ordinary enveloping algebra, over $\Z$ and
after reduction over $\F$.
statements.section_title: Deletion operators and injectivity of the leading projection

statements.label: prop:projection-injective
statements.text:
For $n>2$ and every $r\geq0$, the leading projection
\[
 \operatorname{gr}^{r}\overline L_n\longrightarrow
 \Lie_{\F}\langle C,B\rangle,\qquad
 \chi\longmapsto\chi(0,C,B)
\]
is injective.  Its source is zero unless $n=2m+r$ for an integer
$m\geq0$; in that case its image has $C$-count $m$ and $B$-count $r$.
statements.section_title: Deletion operators and injectivity of the leading projection

statements.title: The image bound
statements.label: prop:image-bound
statements.text:
Set $g_k=\ad_C^kB$ for $k\geq1$.
These elements freely generate an ordinary free Lie algebra inside
$\Lie_{\F}\langle C,B\rangle$.
For $n>2$, the image of the leading projection of
$\operatorname{gr}^r_F\overline L_n$ belongs to its weight-$n$,
length-$r$ component, where $\wt(g_k)=2k+1$ and each $g_k$ has
length one.
The associated graded piece with $r=0$ is zero.
statements.section_title: The image of the leading projection

statements.title: The all-weight upper bound
statements.label: cor:dimension-bound
statements.text:
For every $n$ and $r\geq0$ there is an injection
\[
 \operatorname{gr}^r_F\overline L_n
 \lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow
 \mathfrak f_{\mathrm{odd},n,r},
\]
obtained by the leading projection and the identification
$g_k\leftrightarrow z_k$.  In particular,
\begin{equation}
 
 \dim_{\Q}W_n
 =\dim_{\F}\overline L_n
 \leq\sum_{r\geq0}d_{n,r}=d_n.
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: The image of the leading projection

statements.title: The leading Ihara bracket
statements.label: prop:leading-ihara
statements.text:
Let $\psi\in F^r\overline L_n$ and
$\phi\in F^s\overline L_{n'}$, where $n,n'>2$ and $r,s\geq1$.
Write $f,g$ for their leading projections at counts $r,s$.
Their Ihara bracket, computed in the ambient Lie algebra in
$x,y$, belongs to $F^{r+s}$ in the $A,C,B$ presentation, and
the projection of its component of count $r+s$ is
\begin{equation}
 
 [f,g].
\end{equation}
This assertion does not require prior closure of the full solution
space under the Ihara bracket.
statements.section_title: The image of the leading projection

statements.label: prop:categorical-values
statements.text:
For $n\geq2$, evaluation $\delta\mapsto\delta(\alpha)$ takes
$\mathcal D_n(\Q)$ into $W_n$.  Its images
\[
 V_n=\{\delta(\alpha):\delta\in\mathcal D_n(\Q)\},\qquad
 V=\bigoplus_{n\geq2}V_n,
\]
form a rational Lie subalgebra under the Ihara bracket \eqref{eq:ihara}.
statements.section_title: A rational Lie algebra of categorical values

statements.title: Regularized transport
statements.label: prop:regularized-holonomy
statements.text:
For the tree endpoints and frames just defined,
\eqref{eq:holonomy-regularized} has a limit in every weight.
The limit is independent of the admissible scale exponents under
real interpolation of the endpoint collars.  The insertion recipes
define coherent operations on the continued path classes, and the
limit respects relabeling, outer block insertion, and inner insertion.
The same assertions hold for $H_-$.  The two transport rules agree
on all arity-two paths, including paths reversing the two real points.

statements.label: prop:odd-depth-one
statements.text:
For every odd $n\geq3$ there exists $\psi_n\in V_n$ for which the
coefficient of $x^{n-1}y$ is nonzero.  Equivalently, its ordinary
$y$-depth-one part is a nonzero multiple of $\ad_x^{n-1}y$.
