title: The Dimension of the Two-Adic Hecke Algebra at Odd Level
abstract: For every odd positive integer N, every irreducible component of the full two-adic Hecke algebra of level \(\Gamma_1(N)\) has Krull dimension four. This proves the p = 2 case of Emerton's dimension conjecture, including all residual components.

tex.abstract:
For every odd positive integer $N$, every irreducible component of the
full two-adic Hecke algebra of level $\Gamma_1(N)$ has Krull dimension
four. This proves the $p=2$ case of Emerton's dimension conjecture,
including all residual components.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every odd positive integer $N$, every irreducible component of
$\Spec T_2(N)$ has dimension exactly $4$.

statements.label: prop:noetherian
statements.text:
The ring $A$ is a finite product of complete Noetherian local rings
with finite residue fields. Its given topology on each factor is
the maximal-ideal-adic topology.

statements.text:
The closure of the classical points of bounded weight has dimension

statements.label: cor:classical-point
statements.text:
For every minimal prime $P$ of $A$, there is a classical cuspidal
map $\lambda:A\to\OO_E$ of weight at least $3$ such that
$P\subseteq\frakx:=\ker\lambda$ and $\frakx$ belongs to no other
irreducible component of $\Spec A$.
statements.section_title: Finding cuspidal points on every component

statements.label: prop:tangent
statements.text:
Let $R$ be a compact Hausdorff Noetherian topological
$\Z_p$-algebra, with continuous structure map $\Z_p\to R$.
Suppose a profinite
group $H$ has a continuous two-dimensional determinant over $R$,
with trace $t$ and determinant $d$, and that their values
topologically generate $R$ over $\Z_p$. Let
$\lambda:R\to\OO_E$ be a continuous $\Z_p$-algebra map, where
$E/\Q_p$ is finite, and suppose its specialized determinant is
that of an absolutely irreducible continuous representation
$r:H\to\GL_2(E)$. For $\frakx=\ker\lambda$,
\begin{equation}
 \dim R_{\frakx}\leq\edim R_{\frakx}
 \leq\dim_E H^1(H,\ad r).
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: A tangent bound in characteristic zero

statements.label: prop:cohomology
statements.text:
For the representation $r$ of a cuspidal newform of weight at
least $3$ and odd level dividing $N$,
\[
 \dim_E H^1(G_{\Q,S},\ad r)\leq3.
\]

title: The E×CM component of Zilber–Pink for curves in A2
abstract: We prove the \(E\times\mathrm{CM}\) component of Zilber–Pink for Hodge-generic algebraic curves in \(\mathcal A_2\) over \(\overline{\mathbb Q}\). Each such curve contains only finitely many points whose abelian surface is isogenous to a product of elliptic curves with at least one factor having complex multiplication.

tex.abstract:
We prove the \(E\times\CM\) component of Zilber--Pink for Hodge-generic
algebraic curves in \(\A_2\) over \(\Qbar\). Each such curve contains only
finitely many points whose abelian surface is isogenous to a product of
elliptic curves with at least one factor having complex multiplication.
sections: Heights, periods, and CM elliptic curves
A uniform height estimate on a curve
An essential period on a threefold

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let \(C\subset\A_2\) be a reduced, irreducible, closed algebraic curve
defined over \(\Qbar\). Suppose that \(C\) is Hodge generic, meaning that
it is contained in no proper special subvariety of \(\A_2\).
Then the set
\[
 \bigl\{s\in C(\Qbar):
 A_s\text{ is isogenous to }E_1\times E_2
 \text{ with at least one }E_i\text{ having CM}\bigr\}
\]
is finite.

statements.label: thm:orbits
statements.text:
Let \(C\) be as in Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, and let \(K\) be a number
field over which it is defined. There is a constant \(c>0\), depending
on \(C\) and \(K\), such that every mixed point \(s\in C(\Qbar)\)
satisfies
\[
 \#\bigl(\Gal(\Qbar/K)\cdot s\bigr)
 \ge c\,\cplx(s)^{1/42}.
\]

statements.label: prop:height
statements.text:
There are constants \(c,n_0>0\), depending only on this fixed family,
such that at every mixed point \(t\in S(\Qbar)\), with the notation
of Lemma~\ref{lem:gluing} and \(D=|\disc\End(F)|\),
\[
 n\ge n_0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad h(j_E)\le c\,n(1+\sqrt D).
\]

title: The Euclidean Steinitz–Bergström theorem
abstract: Every prescribed-order finite sequence of vectors in the Euclidean unit ball of ℝd has one signing for which every signed prefix has norm at most \(C\sqrt d\), with C absolute and independent of the sequence length. Consequently, every indexed zero-sum family of unit-ball vectors admits an ordering with the same bound for its unsigned partial sums. This determines the Euclidean Steinitz constant up to absolute factors, \(S_2(d)=\Theta(\sqrt d)\), and resolves the Euclidean Steinitz–Bergström conjecture.

tex.abstract:
Every prescribed-order finite sequence of vectors in the Euclidean unit
ball of $\R^d$ has one signing for which every signed prefix has norm at
most $C\sqrt d$, with $C$ absolute and independent of the sequence length.
Consequently, every indexed zero-sum family of unit-ball vectors admits an
ordering with the same bound for its unsigned partial sums. This determines
the Euclidean Steinitz constant up to absolute factors,
$S_2(d)=\Theta(\sqrt d)$, and resolves the Euclidean
Steinitz--Bergstr\"om conjecture.
sections: From low energy to shifted signs

statements.title: Prescribed-order signed prefixes
statements.label: thm:signing
statements.text:
There is an absolute constant $C$ such that, for all integers $d,N\ge1$ and
every sequence $v_1,\ldots,v_N\in\R^d$ with $\lVert v_i\rVert_2\le1$,
there are signs $\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_N\in\{-1,1\}$ for which
\[
 \max_{0\le k\le N}
 \left\lVert\sum_{i=1}^k\varepsilon_i v_i\right\rVert_2\le C\sqrt d.
\]
The same signs control all prefixes, and $C$ is independent of $d$, $N$
and the sequence.

statements.title: Euclidean Steinitz--Bergstr\"om bound
statements.label: thm:steinitz
statements.text:
There is an absolute constant $C$ such that, for all integers $d,N\ge1$ and
every indexed family $v_1,\ldots,v_N\in\R^d$ satisfying
$\lVert v_i\rVert_2\le1$ and $\sum_{i=1}^N v_i=0$, some permutation
$\pi\in\mathfrak S_N$ satisfies
\[
 \max_{0\le k\le N}\left\lVert\sum_{i=1}^k v_{\pi(i)}\right\rVert_2
 \le C\sqrt d.
\]
The constant in Theorem~\ref{thm:signing} also suffices here.

statements.title: Signs with adaptive shifts
statements.label: prop:adaptive
statements.text:
Let $K\subset\R^m$ be nonempty, bounded, open, convex and centrally
symmetric.  Suppose that
\begin{equation}
 \lambda_Q(K)\le\kappa^2\tr Q
 \quad\text{for every positive definite diagonal }Q.
\end{equation}
Let $j_1,\ldots,j_s$ be distinct elements of $\{1,\ldots,m\}$, and let
$q_i:\R^{i-1}\to[-\delta,\delta]$ be arbitrary functions, for
$1\le i\le s$.  There exist signs $\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_s$
such that the recursion
\[
 x^{(0)}=0,\qquad
 x^{(i)}=x^{(i-1)}+
 \bigl(q_i(x^{(i-1)}_{j_1},\ldots,x^{(i-1)}_{j_{i-1}})
       +\varepsilon_i\bigr)e_{j_i}
\]
has $x^{(s)}\in K$.  For $i=1$, the function $q_1$ has a one-point domain.

statements.title: Energy of a filtered path body
statements.label: prop:filtered
statements.text:
There are positive absolute constants $A_0,B_0,H_0$ with the following
property.  Let $d\ge1$ and $n\ge0$ be integers and put $m=d+n$.  For
$1\le t\le n$, let $C_t$ be an invertible real $d\times d$ matrix and let
$b_t\in\R^d$ satisfy
\[
 C_tC_t^T+b_tb_t^T=I_d.
\]
Define linear maps $R_t:\R^m\to\R^d$ by
\begin{equation}
 R_0x=(x_1,\ldots,x_d),\qquad
 R_tx=C_tR_{t-1}x+b_tx_{d+t}\quad(1\le t\le n).
\end{equation}
Then the bounded open convex centrally symmetric set
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal D=
 \left\{x\in\R^m:
 \begin{array}{ll}
 |x_j|<B_0 & (1\le j\le m),\\
 \lVert R_tx\rVert_2<A_0\sqrt d & (0\le t\le n)
 \end{array}\right\}
\end{equation}
satisfies
\[
 \lambda_Q(\mathcal D)\le H_0\tr Q
 \quad\text{for every positive definite diagonal }Q.
\]

statements.title: Finite-dimensional $\ell_p$ bounds
statements.label: cor:lp-steinitz
statements.text:
Let $1\le p\le\infty$, with $1/\infty=0$, and let $d,N\ge1$ be integers.
Every sequence $v_1,\ldots,v_N\in\R^d$ with $\lVert v_i\rVert_p\le1$
admits signs $\varepsilon_i\in\{-1,1\}$ such that
\[
 \max_{0\le k\le N}
 \left\lVert\sum_{i=1}^k\varepsilon_i v_i\right\rVert_p
 \le C d^{\max\{1/p,\,1-1/p\}}.
\]
If additionally $\sum_{i=1}^N v_i=0$, there is a permutation
$\pi\in\mathfrak S_N$ such that
\[
 \max_{0\le k\le N}
 \left\lVert\sum_{i=1}^k v_{\pi(i)}\right\rVert_p
 \le C d^{\max\{1/p,\,1-1/p\}}.
\]
Here $C$ is the same absolute constant as in
Theorems~\ref{thm:signing} and~\ref{thm:steinitz}, independent of $p,d,N$.
For $1\le p\le2$, both bounds have sharp dimension order $d^{1/p}$:
for every $d$ there is a unit-ball sequence for which every signing has
a prefix of norm at least $d^{1/p}$, and a finite indexed zero-sum
unit-ball family for which every permutation has a prefix of norm at
least $\tfrac13d^{1/p}$.

statements.title: Euclidean colorful Steinitz bound
statements.label: cor:colorful-steinitz
statements.text:
Let $d,k,n\ge1$ be integers and let $a_i^j\in\R^d$, for
$1\le j\le k$ and $1\le i\le n$, satisfy
\[
 \lVert a_i^j\rVert_2\le1,
 \qquad
 \sum_{j=1}^k\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^j=0.
\]
There is one tuple of permutations
$(\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_k)\in\mathfrak S_n^k$ such that
\[
 \max_{0\le m\le n}
 \left\lVert\sum_{j=1}^k\sum_{i=1}^m a_{\pi_j(i)}^j\right\rVert_2
 \le 2C\sqrt d,
\]
where $C$ is the absolute constant in Theorem~\ref{thm:signing}.
The same tuple works for every $m$ and may be chosen jointly from the
whole array. Only the global total sum is assumed to vanish; the bound
controls the displayed aggregate synchronous prefixes, not each row
separately.

title: The Euclidean plane is not five-colorable
abstract: We prove that every coloring of the Euclidean plane with five colors has a monochromatic unit-distance pair, with no regularity assumption on the color classes. Consequently, the chromatic number of the plane is either six or seven.

tex.abstract:
We prove that every coloring of the Euclidean plane with five colors has a
monochromatic unit-distance pair, with no regularity assumption on the color
classes. Consequently, the chromatic number of the plane is either six or seven.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
The Euclidean plane has no proper five-coloring, even when arbitrary
color classes are allowed. Consequently,
\[
  6\le \chi(\R^2)\le 7.
\]

statements.title: Transfer of colorability
statements.label: thm:transfer
thm:weak-five
statements.text: There is no weak measurable five-coloring of the Euclidean plane.

statements.title: Positive five-color badness
statements.label: cor:positive-badness
statements.text:
There is a constant $\delta>0$ with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] For every coloring $c:\R^2\to\{1,\ldots,5\}$ and every
normalized finitely additive left-invariant measure $\mu$ on all subsets
of the plane-isometry group $E(2)$, the invariant-mean badness satisfies
\[
 p_5^\mu(c):=\mu\bigl(\{T\in E(2):c(T^{-1}0)=c(T^{-1}1)\}\bigr)
 \ge\delta,
\]
where $\R^2$ is identified with $\C$.
\item[(ii)] If $c$ is a Lebesgue-measurable five-coloring with two
linearly independent periods, then
$\mathbb P(c(A)=c(A+U))\ge\delta$, where $A$ is uniform in a
fundamental parallelogram and $U$ is an independent uniform unit
direction. For any Lebesgue-measurable five-coloring, if the conditional
square-table frequencies
\[
 \mathbb P\bigl(c(A_R)=c(A_R+U)\mid A_R+U\in[-R,R]^2\bigr)
 \qquad(R>1)
\]
converge as $R\to\infty$, their limit is at least $\delta$; here
$A_R$ is uniform in $[-R,R]^2$ and independent of $U$.
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: A cycle of common exclusion continua
statements.label: prop:interface-cycle
statements.text:
For the weak measurable five-coloring under consideration, there
exist an integer $\ell\in\{3,4,5\}$, distinct labels
$i_0,\ldots,i_{\ell-1}\in\mathcal I$, a point $x\in\R^2$, and a
radius $\rho>0$ with the following properties.  For each edge
$i_ji_{j+1}$ of the simple label cycle, with indices modulo $\ell$,
there are a compact connected set
$K_j\subset\overline{B(x,\rho)}$, a direction $v_j\in S$, and a
sequence $q_{j,k}\in K_j\setminus\{x\}$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $x\in K_j$ and $K_j\cap\partial B(x,\rho)\ne\varnothing$;
\item $q_{j,k}\to x$ and
$(q_{j,k}-x)/|q_{j,k}-x|\to v_j$;
\item both endpoint supports are excluded from the same open set:
\[
 H_{i_j}\cap\Delta(K_j)=
 H_{i_{j+1}}\cap\Delta(K_j)=\varnothing.
\]
\end{enumerate}
The extracted cycle need not consist of edges of $\Gamma_x$.

title: The Factor-Two Hardness Threshold for Vertex Cover
abstract: We prove that minimum Vertex Cover is NP-hard to approximate within every fixed factor below two, even on simple unweighted graphs.

tex.abstract:
We prove that minimum Vertex Cover is NP-hard to approximate within
every fixed factor below two, even on simple unweighted graphs.
sections: The source problem and construction parameters
A fixed function from an independent set

statements.title: Explicit cover gap
statements.label: thm:gap
statements.text:
For every fixed integer \(m\geq4\), there is a deterministic
polynomial-time reduction from \(\mathrm{3SAT}\) to finite simple
undirected unweighted graphs with the following guarantees:
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{the formula is satisfiable}
 &\Longrightarrow\quad
 \tau(G)<\left(\dfrac12+\dfrac1m\right)|V(G)|,\\[6pt]
\text{the formula is unsatisfiable}
 &\Longrightarrow\quad
 \tau(G)>\left(1-\dfrac1m\right)|V(G)|.
\end{array}
\]
The output lists all vertices and edges explicitly.

statements.label: thm:hardness
statements.text:
For every fixed real \(\alpha\) with \(1\leq\alpha<2\),
approximating Vertex Cover within factor \(\alpha\) is NP-hard.
Thus, unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\), no deterministic
polynomial-time algorithm achieves factor \(2-\varepsilon\)
for any fixed \(\varepsilon\in(0,1]\).

statements.title: Perfect-completeness Label Cover hardness
statements.label: src:hardness
statements.text:
For every fixed rational \(\sigma\in(0,1)\), there are nonempty
constant alphabets and a deterministic polynomial-time reduction
from \(\mathrm{3SAT}\) to instances of the form above such that
satisfiable formulas give \(\val(\Phi)=1\), and unsatisfiable
formulas give \(\val(\Phi)\leq\sigma\).
statements.section_title: The source problem and construction parameters

statements.title: Deterministic polynomial construction
statements.label: graph:polynomial
statements.text:
For a fixed integer $m\geq4$, a fixed even square $d$ satisfying
\Cref{src:dimension-bounds}, and fixed source alphabets,
the graph $G$ can be output explicitly in deterministic time
polynomial in the source bit length.  Every edge test is exact.

statements.title: Completeness
statements.label: graph:completeness
statements.text:
If $\val(\Phi)=1$, then $G$ has an independent set of size greater
than $(1/2-1/m)n$.  Consequently,
\[
 \tau(G)<\left(\frac12+\frac1m\right)n.
\]

statements.title: Local lists and compatible hits
statements.label: ana:lists
statements.text:
The functions \(\mathcal L_j\) are deterministic total measurable maps
returning at most \(\ell\) valid labels. Once
\(\Phi,F,J,\boldsymbol a\) and the conditional kernels above are
fixed, each list uses only its own questions \(u_j\) and weights
\(s_j\). In particular it has no additional access to the actual
hidden seed occurrences or to any other actual batch input.
Under the fixed restricted product law,
\begin{equation}
 \E Z\geq\frac{\beta h}{2}=2.
 
\end{equation}

statements.title: Soundness
statements.label: dec:soundness
statements.text:
For the graph constructed in \Cref{graph:section}, assume
\eqref{src:restriction-budget}.
If \(\val(\Phi)\leq\sigma\), every independent set has size
strictly less than \(n/m\).
Consequently \(\tau(G)>(1-1/m)n\).

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let \(d\ge2\) be an integer and let \(E\subset\R^d\) be compact. If
\(\dim_H E>d/2\), then
\[
 \cL^1(\Delta(E))>0.
\]

statements.title: Linear projection gain
statements.label: ang:linear-gain
statements.text:
Fix $k\ge2$ and
\[
 k-1\le q\le k-\tfrac12<t<k.
\]
Fix a tube-width constant $C$. In the case $q=k-1$, also fix
$\zeta>0$. There exist $\epsilon,c>0$ such that, for all sufficiently
small $\delta$, the following holds. Let $\mu$ be a bounded point
subprobability in $\R^{k+1}$ and $\nu$ a direction subprobability on $S^k$
with respective $t$- and $q$-ball bounds of loss $\delta^{-\epsilon}$
down to $\delta$. At $q=k-1$ assume in addition
\begin{equation}
 \nu\{w:\dist(w,H)\le r\}\le\delta^{-\epsilon}r^\zeta
       \qquad(\delta\le r\le1)
\end{equation}
for every linear hyperplane $H$. Let $E\subset\R^{k+1}\times S^k$ be a
measurable incidence relation, and write $E_w=\{x:(x,w)\in E\}$.
If each direction fiber $E_w$ is covered by at most
$\delta^{-q-\epsilon}$ tubes parallel to $w$ of width $C\delta$, then
\[
 (\mu\otimes\nu)(E)\le\delta^c.
\]
All constants are uniform over the measures and the incidence relations
with these fixed parameters.

statements.title: Planar discretized Furstenberg estimate
statements.label: ang:furstenberg
statements.text:
Let $0<b<1$ and $b<f<2$. There is $\epsilon_0>0$ such that the
following holds for sufficiently small $\delta$. Suppose that $P$ is
a nonempty bounded $(\delta,f,\delta^{-\epsilon_0})$-set and that
each $x\in P$ has a nonempty family $\mathcal T_x$ of incident
$\delta$-tubes whose line parameters form a
$(\delta,b,\delta^{-\epsilon_0})$-set. Then
\[
 \left|\bigcup_{x\in P}\mathcal T_x\right|_\delta
       \ge\delta^{-2b-\epsilon_0}.
\]
The exponent may be decreased to absorb fixed bounded charts and fixed
width multiples.

statements.title: Small mass of bad directions
statements.label: ang:bad-directions
statements.text:
Fix the parameters of Theorem~\ref{ang:linear-gain}. There are
$c_1,\epsilon_1>0$ such that the following holds at sufficiently small
$\delta$. Let $\mu$ be a bounded point probability satisfying the
$t$-ball bound with loss $\delta^{-\epsilon_1}$. Let $B_\delta$
be the set of directions for which at most
$\delta^{-q-c_1}$ width-$C\delta$ tubes capture $\mu$-mass at
least $\delta^{c_1}$. There is a Borel set
$B_\delta^+\supset B_\delta$, depending only on the point law and this
geometric test, such that every direction subprobability $\nu$
satisfying the $q$-ball bound with loss $\delta^{-\epsilon_1}$,
and, when $q=k-1$, Equation~\eqref{ang:endpoint-plate} with
$\epsilon_1$ in place of $\epsilon$, satisfies
\[
 \nu(B_\delta^+)\le\delta^{c_1}.
\]
In particular this bounds the outer $\nu$-measure of the original
geometric bad set. The direction law need not be normalized on either
set or on any individual incidence fiber. All predetermined fixed
widths are allowed.

statements.title: Thin-tube upgrade
statements.label: prep:thin-upgrade
statements.text:
Let $k\ge2$ and $k-\tfrac12<s<k$. Let $\rho,\nu$ be bounded,
separated $s$-Frostman probabilities in $\R^{k+1}$. Suppose that the
two directional measures of $G_N$ have plate bounds $Cu^\zeta$,
uniformly for $2^{-N}\le u\le1$, with fixed $\zeta>0$.
If $k-1$ is available, then $k-\tfrac12$ is available.

statements.title: Starting pair measures
statements.label: prep:starting-pairs
statements.text:
Let $E\subset\R^d$ be compact, $d\ge2$, and
$\dim_HE>S=d/2$. Either Lemma~\ref{prep:classical-plane} already
proves that its distance set has positive Lebesgue measure, or the
following construction is possible.

After a similarity there are compact separated sets $E_1,E_2\subset E$
and probabilities $\mu_i$ supported on them, each satisfying
\[
 \mu_i(B(x,u))\le C u^{S+\chi}
\]
for a fixed $\chi>0$. Their cross directions lie in a fixed
arbitrarily small spherical patch. For every sufficiently small fixed
$\omega>0$, there are decreasing Borel pair sets
$\Gamma_N\subset E_1\times E_2$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $(\mu_1\otimes\mu_2)(\bigcap_N\Gamma_N)>0$;
\item $\Gamma_N$ is a disjoint union of at most $C2^{2d\omega N}$
products of spatial Borel sets;
\item for every $e>0$, there are $c(e)>0$, $C_e<\infty$ and
Borel $B_N\subset\Gamma_N$ with
$(\mu_1\otimes\mu_2)(B_N)\le C_e2^{-c(e)N}$, such that for
$G_N=\Gamma_N\setminus B_N$, all $2^{-N}\le u\le1$, and
all spherical caps $B(w,u)$,
\begin{align*}
 \mu_2\{y:(x,y)\in G_N,\ \pi_x(y)\in B(w,u)\}
     &\le2^{eN}u^S,\\
 \mu_1\{x:(x,y)\in G_N,\ \pi_y(x)\in B(w,u)\}
     &\le2^{eN}u^S.
\end{align*}
\end{enumerate}
The last bounds integrate the original opposite marginal, without
normalizing its individual fibers. The $B_N$ need not have a product
partition or be nested. All constants are independent of $N$, but
may depend on the fixed measures, $\omega$, and $e$.

statements.title: Weighted shell conversion
statements.label: osc:shell-conversion
statements.text:
Let $0\le a\le v\le N$ be integer depths, and let $X,Y$ be separated
cells at depth $a$ of one or two classes.  Let
$m_x(w)$ and $n_y(w)$ be products of the undifferentiated masks at one
index $i<J_0$ for two specified indexed descriptor lists.  Assume both
lists have at most $N^{C_{\mathcal A}}$ occurrences, where one exponent
$C_{\mathcal A}$ is fixed independently of $N$ for the whole family under
consideration, as in Definition~\ref{osc:symbols}.  Let $L$ be the largest
nominal length in either list, with $L=0$ when both lists are empty.
For measurable $|f|,|g|\le1$
define a possibly complex measure $\nu$ on the distance line by
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 \int F(s)\,d\nu(s)
 &=\frac1{M_1(a)M_2(a)}
   \int_{X\times Y} F(D(x,y))\,
       (D(x,y)2^a)^{-n_*/2}\\
 &\qquad\qquad\cdot f(x)\overline{g(y)}\,
       m_x(e(x,y))n_y(e(x,y))\,
       d\rho_1(x)d\rho_2(y).
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
If
\begin{equation}
 v-a\ge20\sigma N,\qquad L\le(v-a)/2+\sigma N,
\end{equation}
then for every fixed $T>0$,
\begin{equation}
 2^{-a}\int_{2^{v-1}}^{2^{v+1}}|\widehat\nu(r)|^2\,dr
 \le R^{o(1)}\sup\mathsf H_F(a,v)+O(R^{-T}).
\end{equation}
The supremum has the same cells, class normalizations, lists and
smoothing index as in Equation~\eqref{osc:weighted-measure}.  Its symbols
are admissible with a derivative budget and common bounds for smooth angular factors
depending only on $T,d,C_{\mathcal A}$ and the fixed parameters.  All
these bounds are independent of $N$.
When $f=g=1$, the measure $\nu$ is positive.  The assertion also holds on
the fixed outer supports with $a=0$.
statements.section_title: Spherical oscillatory integrals and distance shells

statements.title: Graph estimate for the independent angular energy
statements.label: graph:estimate
statements.text:
Let $\rho_1,\rho_2$ be two regularized class laws, possibly equal, and
write $M_j$, $A_{j,n}$, $I_j$ and $k_j$ for their profiles and associated
quantities from Section~\ref{test:section}.  Let $X,Y$ be occupied
cells of depth $a$.  Put $X_1=X$, $X_2=Y$, and let
$b^{(j)}_z(w)$ be an admissible endpoint symbol on $X_j$ in the sense
of Definition~\ref{osc:symbols}.  Let $L$ be the largest nominal
length of a descriptor in either symbol, with $L=0$ if both lists are
empty.  Suppose that the integer depths satisfy $0\le a<p\le v\le N$
and
\begin{equation}
 p-a\le v-p+2\sigma N,\qquad
 L\le v-p+2\sigma N,\qquad v-p\ge10\sigma N.
\end{equation}
At endpoint $j$, suppose that the symbol imposes the parallel test
$[g_j,p]$ at a level $\ell_j\in\{0,\ldots,J_0\}$: for
$\rho_j$-almost every $z\in X_j$ and every $w\in S^{d-1}$,
\begin{equation}
 b^{(j)}_z(w)\ne0
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 w\in G^{(j)}_{\ell_j,[g_j,p]}(z).
\end{equation}
The superscript $j$ indicates the class used in the test.  Assume
\begin{equation}
 a\le g_j<p,\qquad g_j\le a+2\sigma N.
\end{equation}

Form the general independent energy $\mathsf H^{X,Y}(a,v)$ of
Definition~\ref{osc:states} using these specified symbols.  For every
fixed $T>0$,
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 \mathsf H^{X,Y}(a,v)
 &\le
 R^{-\sum_{j=1}^2(A_{j,p}-A_{j,a})
       +\min_{j=1,2}k_j(a,p)+O_d(\sigma)+o(1)}\\
 &\qquad\cdot
 \max_{\substack{P\subset X,\ Q\subset Y\\
                   P,Q\text{ occupied depth-}p\text{ cells}}}
       \mathsf H^{P,Q}(p,v)
 +O(R^{-T}).
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
No separation of $X$ and $Y$ is required.  Every child in
\eqref{graph:bound} is formed by restricting the same endpoint symbols
to $P$ and $Q$.  It retains every original mask factor, including any
whose anchor is $p$.  Constants are uniform over cells and allowed
symbols with fixed list-size exponents and derivative budgets, and with
fixed common numerical bounds for their smooth angular factors at the
derivative orders used.  The $o(1)$ tends to zero as $N\to\infty$ with
these bounds, the parameters, and $T$ fixed.

statements.title: The separated angular form
statements.label: graph:separated-form
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{graph:estimate}, suppose also
that $X,Y$ and their supported laws have the separated geometry used
to define $\mathsf H_F^{X,Y}(a,v)$ in Section~\ref{osc:section}.  Then
\eqref{graph:bound} holds with its left-hand side replaced by
$\mathsf H_F^{X,Y}(a,v)$ and with the same child energies.  This includes
the outer root $a=0$ with separated actual supports inside possibly
equal depth-zero cells $X,Y$.

statements.title: State reductions
statements.label: rec:reductions
statements.text:
Suppose the current state is nonterminal, its smoothing index satisfies
$i<J_0$, and $N$ is sufficiently large with all parameters fixed.  For
every prescribed $T>0$, it is bounded, apart from an error $O(R^{-T})$
from oscillatory operations, by a sum of child bounds whose number is
polynomial in $N$, and possibly a low-frequency stopping term.  For every
non-low child,
if the old start is $a$ and the new start is $a'$, its multiplier is
\begin{equation}
 R^{-2(A_{a'}-A_a)+\mathrm{cost}+C_d\sigma+o(1)}.
\end{equation}
A low child has cost zero and the entire multiplier $R^{o(1)}$, with no
fixed $C_d\sigma$ loss.  A low-frequency stopping term is
$R^{C_d\sigma+o(1)}$.  The legal children are
\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.2}
\begin{tabular}{lll}
Reduction & Parent and child & Cost \\ \hline
Suffix & $\mathsf D_i(a,t)\to\mathsf D_{i+1}(a,p)$
 & $A_p-\min_{[p,t]}A$ \\
Low & $\mathsf D_i(a,t)\to\mathsf D_{i+1}(a,v)$
 & $0$; full factor $R^{o(1)}$ \\
High & $\mathsf D_i(a,t)\to\mathsf H_i^{[a,t]}(p,v)$
 & $k(a,p)$ \\
Direct & $\mathsf H_i^{\mathcal B}(a,v)\to\mathsf H_i^{\mathcal B}(p,v)$
 & $k(a,p)$ \\
Near & $\mathsf H_i^{\mathcal B}(a,v)\to\mathsf H_i^{\mathcal B}(h,v)$
 & $0$ \\
Far & $\mathsf H_i^{\mathcal B}(a,v)\to\mathsf D_{i+1}(b,v)$
 & $0$
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

For a positive parent, $p$ is its current interval's fixed policy choice.
The suffix row is used when $2p>a+t$.  When $2p\le a+t$, the shell index
is an integer $a<v\le t$: the low row has $t-v\ge\sigma N$, and the high
row has $0\le t-v<\sigma N$.  A high child has base $[a,t]$ and carries
the fixed enlarged derivative budget and common angular bounds produced
by the inverse conversion; these depend on $T$ and the fixed parameters,
not on $N$.

For an angular parent, use $L_0,h$ from
Equation~\eqref{rec:angular-split-depth}.  If $h\le a$, the direct row
chooses a remaining descriptor of maximal length $L$, its anchor $p$,
and an origin $[b_0,u_0]\subseteq\mathcal B$ for that membership.  This
choice has $L=L_0$, $a<p<v$,
\[
 b_0\le p-L,\qquad p+L\le u_0,\qquad v-a\le2L,
\]
and it supplies the parallel descriptor $[\max(a,p-L),p]$ used by the
graph estimate.  If $h>a$, the near row uses the displayed depth $h$.
The far rows range over integer depths $b$ arising from the comparable
far displacements, with $a<b\le h+O_d(1)<v$, and use separated depth-$b$
cell pairs.  Direct and near children keep the same base, index,
derivative budget and common angular bounds.  A far child has the fresh
positive list $\mathcal M(b,v)$.

Finite maxima over child cells use the stated geometry.  Whenever admissible
symbols vary, take a supremum over the symbol family just specified.  An
empty collection of child terms contributes zero.  Constants outside powers
of $R$ may depend on
the fixed parameters, derivative budgets and angular bounds.  The
constants $C_d$ in exponent losses depend only on $d$.  A terminal state
is bounded by
\begin{equation}
 R^{C_d(\kappa+\sigma)+o(1)}.
\end{equation}

statements.title: Single-profile angular bound
statements.label: ledger:bound
statements.text:
Let \(\mathsf H_0^{[c,N]}(c,N)\) be a recursive angular state of
nonterminal width, as in Definition~\ref{rec:angular-state}.
Fix its initial derivative budget \(B\) and its common numerical angular
bounds \(Q_j\), independently of \(N\), as in
Definition~\ref{osc:symbols}.
Then
\begin{equation}
 \mathsf H_0^{[c,N]}(c,N)
 \le R^{2A_c-\mathcal V([c,N])
                   +C_d(\kappa+\sigma/\kappa)+o(1)}.
\end{equation}
This bound holds uniformly over its two occupied cells, including
two copies of the same cell, and over its admissible bounded
spatial multipliers and symbols with these fixed bounds.  The \(o(1)\)
term may depend on \(B\) and the \(Q_j\).

title: The Gaussian propeller bound in every dimension
abstract: We prove the Gaussian propeller conjecture: for every finite measurable partition of a Euclidean space, the sum of the squared lengths of its Gaussian first moments is at most \(9/(8\pi)\). For dimension at least two and at least three cells, three planar sectors of angle \(2\pi/3\), extended by an orthogonal Euclidean factor, attain the bound.

tex.abstract:
We prove the Gaussian propeller conjecture: for every finite measurable
partition of a Euclidean space, the sum of the squared lengths of its
Gaussian first moments is at most $9/(8\pi)$.
For dimension at least two and at least three cells, three planar
sectors of angle $2\pi/3$, extended by an orthogonal Euclidean factor,
attain the bound.
sections: Excluding five or more active cells
Elementary certificates for the numerical inequalities

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For all positive integers $d$ and $k$, every measurable partition
$(A_1,\ldots,A_k)$ of $\mathbb R^d$ satisfies
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^k\left\|\int_{A_i}x\,d\gamma_d(x)\right\|^2
 \le\frac9{8\pi}.
\]
Empty cells are allowed. The constant is sharp whenever $d\ge2$ and
$k\ge3$: three planar sectors of angle $2\pi/3$, multiplied by the
orthogonal complement of their plane, attain equality, with any further
cells empty.

statements.title: Constraints on the three largest radii
statements.label: geo:constraints
statements.text:
The quantities $L,c,t$ satisfy
\begin{align}
 (c-t^2)(L-c-2t^2)
 &\le8\left(\frac3\pi\right)^2t^2,
 \\
 \frac32(c-t^2)^2
 &\le10\left(\frac3\pi\right)^2t^2.
 
\end{align}

statements.title: Gaussian maxima
statements.label: cor:gaussian-maxima
statements.text:
Let $d,k$ be positive integers, let $g$ be standard Gaussian in
$\mathbb R^d$, and let $v_1,\ldots,v_k\in\mathbb R^d$, with
$\bar v=k^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^k v_i$. Then
\[
 \mathbb E\max_{1\le i\le k}\langle v_i,g\rangle
 \le\frac{3}{2\sqrt{2\pi}}
       \left(\sum_{i=1}^k\|v_i-\bar v\|^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
The constant is sharp already for three vectors in the plane.

statements.title: Kernel-clustering hardness
statements.label: kc:main
statements.text:
For each fixed \(k\ge3\) and every fixed
\(1\le\alpha<\alpha_k\), it is NP-hard, given a rational symmetric
matrix \(A\succeq0\) with \(A\one=0\) and the identity-target
objective \eqref{kc:value}, to find
\(\sigma:[N]\to[k]\) such that
\[
 \val_A(\sigma)\ge\Clust(A\mid I_k)/\alpha.
\]
In particular, such a deterministic polynomial-time approximation
would imply \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).

statements.title: Khot--Naor low-influence bound
statements.label: kc:kn-input
statements.text:
For fixed \(k\) and every \(\eta>0\), there exists \(0<\tau_0<1/2\),
independent of \(r\), such that every \(r\in\N\) and every
\(f:\Omega^r\to\Delta_k\) satisfying
\[
 \Inf_j^{\le\log(1/\tau_0)}(f_i)\le\tau_0
 \quad(i\in[k],\ j\in[r])
\]
obey \(\OBJ(f)\le C_k+\eta\).

statements.title: Unique Games input
statements.label: kc:ug-input
statements.text:
For every fixed \(\varepsilon,\delta\in(0,1/2)\), there are an
integer \(s\ge1\) and a deterministic polynomial-time reduction
from \(\mathrm{3SAT}\) to explicit unweighted simple bipartite
Unique Games instances over \(\mathbb F_2^s\). If the formula is
satisfiable the game has a labeling satisfying at least
\(1-\varepsilon\) of its edges; if it is unsatisfiable every
labeling satisfies at most \(\delta\) of its edges. The edge set
is nonempty and each constraint is a translation of the alphabet.
The alphabet size and the polynomial's degree and constants depend
only on \(\varepsilon,\delta\).

title: The Gaussian free field limit of integer Lipschitz heights with two-arc boundary data
abstract: We prove that the centered uniform odd integer height function on triangular-lattice approximations of a smooth simply connected domain, with neighboring differences zero or two and boundary values +1 and −1 on two arcs, converges to a universal multiple of the Dirichlet Gaussian free field. This resolves the field part of Schramm's Problem 2.2. We give an absolutely convergent finite-volume formula for the normalization. The proof combines reflection positivity, a spectral sum rule, and boundary comparison with Gaussian moment identities.
version_note: This version derives the conditional cut and loop estimates from the companion weighted annulus circuit theorem at $x=1$; see the [previous version](../The-Gaussian-free-field-limit-of-integer-Lipschitz-heights-with-two-arc-boundary-data-September-25-2026/paper.pdf).

tex.abstract: We prove that the centered uniform odd integer height function on triangular-lattice approximations of a smooth simply connected domain, with neighboring differences zero or two and boundary values $+1$ and $-1$ on two arcs, converges to a universal multiple of the Dirichlet Gaussian free field. This resolves the field part of Schramm's Problem~2.2. We give an absolutely convergent finite-volume formula for the normalization. The proof combines reflection positivity, a spectral sum rule, and boundary comparison with Gaussian moment identities.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $D$ be a bounded smooth simply connected planar domain with two
distinct marked boundary points.  Let $D_\delta$ be simply connected
triangular-lattice polygonal approximations with uniformly converging
marked boundary parametrizations and edge-midpoint marks, and let
$h_\delta$ have the uniform odd-height law \eqref{eq:odd-model}.
There is a constant $\sigma>0$, depending only on the unit triangular-lattice
model, such that
\[
 h_\delta\ \Longrightarrow\ \bar g+\sigma\Phi_D
 \qquad\text{in }\mathcal D'(D).
\]
For every $f\in C_c^\infty(D)$, $\EE h_\delta(f)\to\int_D\bar g f$.
Consequently
\begin{equation}
 \frac{h_\delta-\EE h_\delta}{\sigma}
 \ \Longrightarrow\ \Phi_D
 \qquad\text{in }\mathcal D'(D).
\end{equation}
All finite vectors of test-function integrals converge jointly to the
corresponding Gaussian vectors, and all their mixed moments converge.
The constant is specified by the absolutely convergent finite-volume series
in \cref{prop:normalization-series}; in the spectral convention below,
$\sigma=4\pi\sqrt{c_*}$.

statements.title: Loop estimates
statements.label: prop:loop-estimates
statements.text:
There are constants $c_0>0$ and $0<\rho<1$ such that, for all sufficiently
large integer $n$, the following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item If the interior of a simple contour $L$ contains $\Lambda_{2n}(z)$,
then $\PP_L$ gives probability at least $c_0$ to a loop contained in
$\Lambda_{2n}(z)$ and surrounding $\Lambda_n(z)$.
\item If $L$ has graph inradius $n$ about $z$, then
\begin{equation}
 \PP_L\bigl(\text{at least two loops surround }\Lambda_{\rho n}(z)\bigr)
 \le 1-c_0.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
There is no aspect-ratio or boundary-regularity assumption on $L$.
statements.section_title: Buffered circuits, mixing, and rare pins

statements.title: Plane law and quantitative local comparison
statements.label: prop:plane-mixing
statements.text:
Free coherent pairs in expanding regular hexagons converge on cylinder
events to a law $\mu_\infty$.  This law is invariant under lattice
translations, lattice symmetries, global sign changes, and interchange
of the colors.  If the domain of a finite pair law $\mu^{E_0,\eta}$
contains a ball of radius $L$ and has no constraints in that ball, then
its restriction to a concentric
ball of radius $r$ differs from that of $\mu_\infty$ in total variation
by at most $C(r/L)^\alpha$, for $L\gg r\geq1$.

The associated plane height increments exist and have the same spatial
symmetries.  Every finite feasible prescription of $B$ pins together with
$W=+1$ on finitely many connected paths has positive plane probability.
statements.section_title: Buffered circuits, mixing, and rare pins

statements.title: Products of separated pin probabilities
statements.label: prop:pin-product
statements.text:
For a separated family as above, there are constants $0<c\leq C<\infty$
such that
\begin{equation}
 c\prod_i p_i\ \leq\ \mu_\infty\Bigl(\bigcap_iP_i\Bigr)
 \ \leq\ C\prod_i p_i.
\end{equation}
The constants depend on the collars, their buffers, the number of
obstacles, and $\sum_i m_i$.  They do not depend on the mesh, the number
or the values of the microscopic $B$ pins, or the probabilities $p_i$.
The same estimates hold in all sufficiently large finite free volumes.
statements.section_title: Buffered circuits, mixing, and rare pins

statements.title: Interior smearing moments
statements.label: prop:smearing-moments
statements.text:
Consider a uniform height problem with boundary values bounded in absolute
value by $K$.  Let the center of a radius-$a$ smearing have distance $n$
from the boundary, with $1\leq a\leq c_0n$ for a sufficiently small fixed
$c_0>0$.  Then, for every finite $p$,
\begin{equation}
 \norm{\textstyle\sum_xw_xH(x)}_{L^p}
 \leq C_p\bigl(1+\sqrt{\log(n/a)}\bigr).
\end{equation}
Here $C_p$ depends on $p,A,K$, but not on boundary regularity.  The same
statement holds for bounded data on the inner face chain of a dual cut,
and in the bounded skeleton faces considered above.

statements.title: Plane zero-total moments
statements.label: prop:plane-moments
statements.text:
For every zero-total smearing satisfying \eqref{eq:normalized-weights},
\begin{equation}
 \norm{\textstyle\sum_x w_xH(x)}_{L^p(\mu_\infty)}\leq C_p,
 \qquad p<\infty,
\end{equation}
uniformly in its radius, location, and lattice rotation.  The same bound
holds in sufficiently larger finite free volumes, for a height anchored
outside the construction.

statements.title: Conditional obstacle moments
statements.label: prop:obstacle-moments
statements.text:
Fix finitely many separated interval-compatible obstacles with filled
isolating neighborhoods $U_i$ as in \cref{prop:pin-product}.  Let a test
disk lie in a pin-free simply connected neighborhood $U_0$, with room
for a surrounding buffered cut whose filled interior lies in $U_0$.
Require $\overline U_0$ to be disjoint from every $\overline U_i$.
Let $Y$ be a zero-total smearing in the test disk, satisfying
\eqref{eq:normalized-weights} at its scale.  Conditional on all the pins,
\begin{equation}
 \norm Y_{L^p}\leq C_p\qquad(p<\infty).
\end{equation}
The constants depend on the macroscopic arrangement, the weight bound,
the number of obstacles, and the bound on W-subpath counts, but not on
the mesh or the microscopic pin probabilities.  No uniformity as obstacle
separations vanish is asserted here.

statements.title: Equal-offset moments with varying separations
statements.label: cor:equal-offset-moments
statements.text:
For a nonempty obstacle family in the preceding setup, impose the additional event
$\mathcal E=\{t_i=t_1\hbox{ for every }i\}$.  The obstacles may now vary
or approach one another, while staying away from a fixed test disk.
Fix an annular buffer around that disk, with positive clearance from
the disk and with fixed inner and outer radii.  Suppose the buffer and
its filled interior contain no pins.
Suppose that, under conditioning on the pins and $\mathcal E$, an exterior
search finds a surrounding double-$B$ cut in this buffer, with probability
at least $c>0$ uniformly in the varying arrangements.  Suppose that
$\mathcal E$ can be checked in the exterior of the selected cut, so its
strict interior remains free given the trace.  Then the zero-total test
in that disk has moments bounded uniformly in those arrangements.

A sufficient condition is that the cut probability conditional on the
pins alone is at least $c_0>0$, that
$\PP(\mathcal E\mid\hbox{pins})\to1$ uniformly along the varying family,
and that the same exterior measurability holds.

statements.title: Reflection positivity with auxiliary phases
statements.label: prop:reflection-positivity
statements.text:
Let \(\ell\) be a line of lattice sites parallel to a nearest-neighbor direction.
The plane law is reflection positive across \(\ell\). This remains true after
adjoining any finite collection of phase fields
\begin{equation}
 
 Z_\theta(u)=U_\theta\exp\{i\theta(H(u)-H(o))\},\qquad \theta\in\R,
\end{equation}
where the \(U_\theta\)'s are independent uniform points of the unit circle,
independent of the pair, and \(o\) is any anchor.

More precisely, let \(\Theta_\ell\) denote spatial reflection, and let
\(\mathcal A_\ell\) consist of cylinder functions supported in one closed
half-plane, with increments evaluated along paths in that half-plane. Then
\[
 \langle F,G\rangle_\ell
   =\EE\big[\overline{\Theta_\ell F}\,G\big]
\]
is positive semidefinite. In its quotient completion, normal translation farther
into the half-plane by \(\sqrt3\) is a positive self-adjoint contraction \(S\).
Tangential translation by one lattice unit is a commuting unitary operator.
On mesh \(\delta\), the normal step is \(\sqrt3\delta\).

statements.text:

\(c_*\ge0\) such that every limit in \cref{lem:spectral-subsequences} has
coefficient \(c_*\), and
\begin{equation}
 
 \sum_{j\ge0}I_j=-\frac\pi2 c_*.

The value is independent of the choice of \(q\) satisfying
\cref{eq:cutoff-properties}.

statements.title: Reflection null vector
statements.label: cor:reflection-null
statements.text:
Let \(\phi\in C_c^\infty(\R^2)\) be supported strictly on one side of a line
parallel to a lattice reflection direction. Choose site rows \(\ell_\delta\)
converging to that line, still separated from the support by a positive
margin. For
\begin{equation}
 
 X_\delta=H_\delta(\Delta\phi),
\end{equation}
its reflection norm at \(\ell_\delta\) tends to zero. This holds in every
finite phase augmentation of \cref{prop:reflection-positivity}, and also for
lattice translations and reflected placements converging to the stated
configuration.

statements.title: Identity with separated gaps
statements.label: prop:gapped-identity

statements.title: Bracket identity
statements.label: prop:bracket-identity
statements.text:
Fix a window system $\mathcal W$ for a finite grid
$\mathcal L$, and either bracket from
\cref{lem:boundary-brackets}.  Let $K_0,\ldots,K_q\Subset D$
be disks, with $K_0$ at positive distance from every $K_j$,
$j\ge1$, and let $X_\delta,F_\delta$ be as in
\eqref{eq:pins-insertion}.  Suppose there are two levels
$\ell_-<\ell_+$ in $\mathcal L$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
\item $K_0$ is strictly between the two levels, and both levels
      avoid every spectator disk $K_j$ with positive margin;
\item after opening sufficiently small gaps inside their
      corresponding windows, every pin arc and spectator disk
      in the middle band belongs to one of the two strictly
      separated $u$-projection families in
      \eqref{eq:middle-projections}.
\end{enumerate}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \lim_{\delta\downarrow0}
   \EE_{\mu^{\pm,\mathcal W}_\delta}
       [H_\delta(\Delta\phi)F_\delta]=0.
\end{equation}
In particular it applies to products of bounded continuous
functions of finitely many smooth zero-total tests in each
$K_j$.  There is no disjointness requirement between spectator
disks.  For this latter class the identity passes to any
subsequential distributional limit of the bracket laws.

For any fixed bound $q$ on the number of spectator disks these
geometric hypotheses can be arranged locally as follows.  Fix
$x\in D$ and $\rho>0$ with $\overline{B(x,\rho)}\subset D$.
Take $K_0$ sufficiently small about $x$, and take at most $q$
spectator disks of sufficiently small radii, all outside
$B(x,\rho)$.  From a sufficiently dense grid of regular levels
one can choose the two levels within a fixed small fraction of
$\rho$ above and below $x$.  The choices and smallness bounds
depend on $q$ and $\rho$, not on the number of terms in a later
linear combination of such products.

statements.title: Constant-arc arch estimate
statements.label: thm:boundary-arches
statements.text:
There are constants $M>1$, $c,C>0$, and a positive geometric tolerance with
the following property.  Fix a positive integer $N$ and scales
\begin{equation}
  16r<\ell_1<\cdots<\ell_N<R/10,
  \qquad \ell_{i+1}\ge M\ell_i.
\end{equation}
Suppose that, in $Q_R$, the limiting boundary is the single graph
$y=f(x)$, with $f(0)=f'(0)=0$ and $\|f'\|_\infty$ smaller than the
geometric tolerance, and that its inward side is above this graph.  The
original polygon boundary is a sufficiently fine uniform parametric
approximation of this arc and has the same inside and outside away from
its shrinking boundary neighborhood.  Its approximation error, divided by
$\ell_1$, tends to zero.  A smooth boundary has these properties after
decreasing the fixed outer scale.
Allow, in addition, a fixed finite number of boundary-attached patch
replacements as above, whose diameters are sufficiently small relative to
the selected scales.  Suppose that the actual usable boundary data satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \eta\ge k-2\quad\hbox{everywhere},
 \qquad
 \eta\ge k\quad\hbox{on the usable boundary in }Q_R\setminus Q_r,
\end{equation}
where $k\in\Z$.  For sufficiently small mesh and sufficiently fine boundary
and replacement approximations,
\begin{equation}
 \PP_\eta\bigl(\text{an arch at threshold }k\text{ surrounds }Q_r
       \text{ in }Q_R\bigr)\ge 1-Ce^{-cN}.
\end{equation}
The constants do not depend on the boundary heights or on the number of
vertices in a boundary or separator.  They also do not depend on the fixed
number of tiny replacements; the required approximation accuracy may do so.
There is a reversed statement with $\eta\le k+2$, clean data $\eta\le k$,
and a separator at height at most $k$.

statements.title: Random traces and tiny boundary replacements
statements.label: cor:boundary-robustness
statements.text:
The arch estimate remains valid conditional on an exterior sigma-field
whenever, conditional on that field, the remaining free heights have a
uniform Gibbs law and their actual usable boundary data obey
\eqref{eq:arch-boundary-data}.  It also remains valid after a fixed finite
number of boundary-attached patches have been removed by exposed simple
circuits, provided the same data bounds hold on the new usable boundary.

For a prescribed error, first fix a finite collection of arch scales and
their boxes.  The replacement diameters, boundary approximation errors, and
mesh may then be made sufficiently small for all comparisons.  The success
constants of the resulting blocks have no factor depending on the number
of microscopic pins or on the fixed number of replacements.

statements.label: prop:boundary-trace
statements.text:
Both limiting bracket means are the harmonic extension $m$ of $g$.
Consequently $H^-=H=H^+$ almost surely in the ordered coupling, and
$\EE H=m$.

Let $p$ be on an open boundary arc on which $g=k$, where $k$ is
$0$ or $-1$, and let $x\to p$ from within $D$. For the true limiting
field put $Y_x=H(\rho_{x,\kappa d(x)})$. If $F$ is a product of a fixed
finite number of height averages supported away from a neighborhood
of $p$, then
\begin{equation}
                      \EE[(Y_x-k)F]\longrightarrow0.
 
\end{equation}
The same assertion holds when those averages approach finitely many
other, distinct, nonmarked boundary points, with their radii a fixed
small fraction of their depths. In that assertion the points and their
finite number are fixed before the depths tend to zero.

statements.title: Gaussian moment recursion
statements.label: thm:gaussian-moments
statements.text:
For distinct points $(x,y_1,\ldots,y_{j-1})$,
\begin{equation}
 T_j(x,\mathbf y)
   =m(x)T_{j-1}(\mathbf y)
      +v\sum_{i=1}^{j-1}G_D(x,y_i)
                    T_{j-2}(\mathbf y\setminus y_i).
 
\end{equation}
For $j=1$ the assertion is $T_1=m$. These functions, as locally
integrable distributions, are the moment distributions of
$m+\sqrt v\,\Phi_D$, where $\Phi_D$ is the zero-boundary GFF with
covariance $G_D$. The limiting field $H$ has this law.

statements.title: Full convergence and the odd-height normalization
statements.label: cor:field-limit
statements.text:
For every $t>1$,
\begin{equation}
 H_\delta\ \Longrightarrow\ m+\sqrt v\,\Phi_D,
 \qquad
 H_\delta-\EE H_\delta\ \Longrightarrow\ \sqrt v\,\Phi_D
 \quad\text{in }H^{-t}_{\mathrm{loc}}(D).
 
\end{equation}
All finite joint test moments converge. In particular
\begin{equation}
 \frac{h_\delta-\EE h_\delta}{\sigma}
       \ \Longrightarrow\ \Phi_D,
 \qquad
            \sigma=2\sqrt v=4\pi\sqrt{c_*}>0.
 
\end{equation}
The constant has the absolutely convergent finite-volume expression
of \cref{prop:normalization-series}; it is independent of $D,a,b$.
The uncentered odd-height limit has mean $2m+1$, the harmonic
extension of its prescribed values $+1,-1$.

title: The Gaussian free field limit of integer Lipschitz heights with two-arc boundary data
The Gaussian free field limit of the balanced six-vertex model with variance multiplier 1/arcsin(c/2)
abstract: We prove that the height function of the square-lattice six-vertex model with weights \(a=b=1\) and \(0\lt c\le2\), in the plane state obtained from balanced tori, converges to a multiple of the Gaussian free field. For unit height jumps and Green kernel \(-(2\pi)^{-1}\log|x-y|\), the squared multiplier is \(1/\arcsin(c/2)\).

tex.abstract:
We prove that the height function of the square-lattice six-vertex model
with weights \(a=b=1\) and \(0<c\le2\), in the plane state obtained from
balanced tori, converges to a multiple of the Gaussian free field.
For unit height jumps and Green kernel \(-(2\pi)^{-1}\log|x-y|\), the
squared multiplier is \(1/\arcsin(c/2)\).

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every fixed \(c\in(0,2]\), the prescribed iterated balanced-torus limit
\(\P_c\) exists. Define
\begin{equation}
 \Delta=1-\frac{c^2}{2},\qquad
 \sigma(c)^2=\frac2{\arccos\Delta}=\frac1{\arcsin(c/2)}.
\end{equation}
As \(\delta\downarrow0\) through arbitrary positive real values,
the fields \(h_\delta\) converge to
\(\sigma(c)\Gamma\) in each of the following senses.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every finite family \(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_m\) of compactly supported
finite signed measures of total mass zero and finite energy,
\[
 \bigl(\langle h_\delta,\mu_j\rangle\bigr)_{j=1}^m
 \ \Longrightarrow\
 \mathcal N\!\left(0,
       \bigl(\sigma(c)^2\mathcal E(\mu_i,\mu_j)\bigr)_{i,j=1}^m\right).
\]
\item For every bounded open \(U\subset\R^2\) and \(-1<\alpha<0\),
there is convergence in law, with tightness, in the ordinary restriction
spaces
\[
 \mathcal C^\alpha_{\mathrm{res}}(U):=B^\alpha_{\infty,\infty}(U),
 \qquad B^\alpha_{p,q}(U),\qquad W^{\alpha,p}(U),
 \quad 1\le p<\infty,\quad 1\le q\le\infty,
\]
modulo constants. Convergence also holds in the outward completion
\eqref{eq:source-holder} defined below. No regularity of
\(\partial U\) is required. One may fix a smooth compactly supported
\(\rho\) of integral one and replace each field \(X\) by
\(X-\langle X,\rho\rangle\), using the same pinning for the limit.
\item For every \(k\ge1\) and every tuple
\((u_i,u_i')_{i=1}^k\) with
\(\{u_i,u_i'\}\cap\{u_j,u_j'\}=\varnothing\) for \(i\ne j\),
\begin{equation}
 \E_c\prod_{i=1}^k
    \bigl(h_\delta(u_i')-h_\delta(u_i)\bigr)
 \longrightarrow
 \sigma(c)^k\sum_{\pi}\prod_{\{i,j\}\in\pi}C_{ij},
\end{equation}
where the sum is over pairings of \(\{1,\ldots,k\}\), is zero for odd \(k\),
and
\[
 C_{ij}=G(u_i',u_j')-G(u_i',u_j)-G(u_i,u_j')+G(u_i,u_j).
\]
The convergence is uniform on compact sets of such tuples.
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Limits of fixed row words
statements.label: prop:word-kernel
statements.text:
For each fixed integer $m\ge0$ and fixed $2\times2$ matrices
$D_1,\ldots,D_m$, the homogeneous plane coefficients
\begin{equation}
 \left\langle\Omega_L,
     A_L^{D_m}(x_m)\cdots A_L^{D_1}(x_1)\Omega_L\right\rangle
\end{equation}
converge locally uniformly on $\mathcal S_\lambda^m$ to a
holomorphic function
$\mathcal K_{D_m,\ldots,D_1}(x_m,\ldots,x_1)$.
It is invariant under every common complex translation for which
the translated arguments remain in the strip.
For $\lambda>2\pi/3$, the same functions are the array limits in
\eqref{eq:array-limit-convention}.

If $v_L$ is any fixed finite linear combination of row words applied to
$\Omega_L$, then
\[
 \lim\|A_L^D(x)v_L\|^2
       \le4\|D\|^2\lim\|v_L\|^2.
\]
The two limits are determined by the word coefficients and the adjoint
rule. This is the bound used to construct bounded row actions in
Section~\ref{sec:angular}.
For $\lambda>2\pi/3$, in the regular-filling procedure the expectations of every fixed
equal-time local matrix product converge to those of the
homogeneous plane construction.

statements.title: Separated diagonal words
statements.label: prop:word-clustering
statements.text:
Partition a fixed finite list of diagonal marked rows into groups.
Within each group fix its internal arguments in the strict angle
strip.  Translate the arguments of group $g$ by a common imaginary
amount $it_g$, and let every $|t_g-t_{g'}|$ tend to infinity.
Then the plane word kernel factors into the product of the
individual group kernels.  Convergence is locally uniform in
the internal strict arguments.  The order within each group is
retained.

statements.title: The angular representation
statements.label: prop:angular-space
statements.text:
On $\mathcal H$ the rows act as bounded holomorphic operator families, with
\[
 \|A^D(z)\|\le 2\|D\|,\qquad
 A^D(z)^*=A^{X\overline D X}(-\overline z).
\]
They satisfy the finite RTT exchange identities wherever their auxiliary
intertwiner is invertible.  There is a strongly continuous unitary group
$U_b$, $b\in\R$, fixing $\Omega$, such that
\begin{equation}
 U_bA^D(z)U_b^*=A^D(z+ib).
\end{equation}
Words with real arguments in any nonempty open subinterval of $(-v,v)$
span a dense subspace.  The family $P=A^I$ consists of commuting normal
operators and has a simultaneous representation by almost surely
holomorphic scalar functions $f$ on the strip, with
\begin{equation}
 f(-\overline z)=\overline{f(z)},\qquad |f(z)|\le2.
\end{equation}
In the half-plane coordinate this reality condition reads
$f(\overline w)=\overline{f(w)}$.

statements.title: Physical law, both axes, and reflection
statements.label: prop:physical-plane
statements.text:
The row representation gives the local probabilities of the plane law
$\P_c$ in Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.  In particular its prescribed iterated
balanced-torus limit exists when $c<1$.  Quantization with time pointing
east and quantization with time pointing north describe this same law.
For an ordinary observable supported on one side of either coordinate
cut, the squared norm of its prepared state is its expectation paired
with its complex-conjugate reflected observable, with the corresponding
spin reflection.  Products of neutral height observables may be prepared
using paths confined to that side.

statements.title: Neutral blocks
statements.label: cor:neutral-blocks
statements.text:
Let \(b\in\R^2\), \(r>0\), and let \(f\) be a measurable real density
supported in a square of side \(Ar\) centered within distance \(Ar\)
of \(b\), with
\[
 \int f=0,\qquad |f|\le A r^{-2}.
\]
For every finite \(q\),
\begin{equation}
 \|\langle h_\delta,f\rangle\|_{L^q}\le C_{A,q}
\end{equation}
uniformly in \(b,r,\delta\). Products of finitely many such blocks have
uniform absolute moment bounds, even when their supports overlap.
statements.section_title: Moment bounds and convergence of the height field

statements.label: prop:smooth-tests
statements.text:
For every finite family of smooth compactly supported densities
\(\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_m\) of integral zero, the vector
\(\bigl(\langle h_\delta,\phi_i\rangle\bigr)_i\) converges jointly in law
and in every joint moment to the corresponding pairings of
\(\mathcal H_\kappa\). The moment convergence is uniform when the tests
vary in a compact smooth family with a common compact support.

statements.label: prop:offdiagonal
statements.text:
For every \(k\ge1\), all \(k\)-point height-increment moments converge
to the Wick increment moments of \(\mathcal H_\kappa\), uniformly on
compact sets of tuples whose endpoint sets belonging to different
increments are disjoint.

statements.label: prop:finite-energy
statements.text:
For every finite family of compactly supported, neutral, finite signed
measures of the ordinary finite-energy class in
Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, the associated height pairings converge jointly
in law to the centered Gaussian vector with covariance obtained by
integrating \(K_\kappa\) against the pairs of measures.

statements.label: prop:negative-regularity
statements.text:
For every bounded open \(U\subset\R^2\) and every \(-1<\alpha<0\),
the pinned fields converge in law, with tightness, in the ordinary
restriction spaces
\[
 \mathcal C^\alpha_{\mathrm{res}}(U):=B^\alpha_{\infty,\infty}(U),\qquad
 B^\alpha_{p,q}(U),\qquad W^{\alpha,p}(U),
 \quad 1\le p<\infty,\quad1\le q\le\infty,
\]
to the corresponding pinning of \(\mathcal H_\kappa\).
Here the Hölder laws are supported on the separable closure of smooth
functions in the displayed norm. Convergence also holds in the literal
outward-scaling completion defined by (16) of
\cite[Definition~2.6(iii)]{DKLM2026}. No boundary regularity of \(U\) is
assumed. An intrinsic dual interpretation of the negative Sobolev norms
is treated at the end of this section.

statements.title: Intrinsic dual convergence
statements.label: prop:intrinsic-dual
statements.text:
Let \(U\subset\R^2\) be bounded and open, let \(0<s<1\), and let
\(1\le p<\infty\), with conjugate exponent \(q=p'\).
The pinned fields converge in law, with norm tightness, in
\((W^{s,q}(U))^*\) to the canonically pinned Gaussian field with kernel
\(K_\kappa\). The laws are supported on a separable closed subspace of
this dual. No extension property or regularity of \(\partial U\) is
required.
statements.section_title: Moment bounds and convergence of the height field

statements.title: Endpoint topology implication
statements.label: prop:endpoint-topologies
statements.text:
At \(c=2\), suppose that the height pairings with every finite family
of ordinary finite-energy neutral measures converge jointly to those
of \(\sigma\Gamma\). Then the commonly pinned fields also converge,
with tightness, in all the negative-regularity spaces stated in
Propositions~\ref{prop:negative-regularity} and~\ref{prop:intrinsic-dual}.
This includes the ordinary restriction H\"older, Besov and Sobolev
spaces on every bounded open set, the outward-scaling completion,
and the explicitly defined intrinsic Sobolev duals.

title: The generalized Mukai conjecture
abstract: We prove the generalized Mukai conjecture: every positive-dimensional smooth complex Fano manifold of dimension n, Picard number ρ, and pseudoindex ι satisfies \(\rho(\iota-1)\le n\). Equality holds precisely for the product of ρ copies of \(\mathbb P^{\iota-1}\).

tex.abstract:
We prove the generalized Mukai conjecture: every positive-dimensional
smooth complex Fano manifold of dimension $n$, Picard number $\rho$, and
pseudoindex $\iota$ satisfies $\rho(\iota-1)\le n$. Equality holds
precisely for the product of $\rho$ copies of $\mathbb P^{\iota-1}$.
sections: A lower bound for point descendants
From divisor eigenvalues to independent curve degrees

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $X$ be a smooth connected complex projective Fano manifold of
positive dimension $n$, Picard number $\rho_X$ and pseudoindex $\iota_X$.
Then
\[
 \rho_X(\iota_X-1)\le n.
\]
Equality holds if and only if
\[
 X\cong(\mathbb P^{\iota_X-1})^{\rho_X}.
\]

statements.title: Point-descendant lower bound
statements.label: prop:descendant-bound
statements.text:
Suppose that \(\beta\) is represented by a nonconstant free map
\(\mathbb P^1\to X\).  Put \(d=d_\beta\) and \(b=ad\).  Then
\[
  \left\langle\tau_{d-2}(\mathrm{pt})\right\rangle_\beta
  \ge \frac{1}{b^{d-1}}.
\]
statements.section_title: A lower bound for point descendants

statements.label: prop:spectral
statements.text:
At least one joint diagonal tuple $(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r)$ of the
quantum divisor matrices has coordinates algebraically independent over
$\mathbb C$.

statements.title: Independent curve correspondences
statements.label: prop:independent-correspondences
statements.text:
Suppose that the quantum divisor operators $A_1(q),\ldots,A_r(q)$
have an algebraically independent joint eigenvalue tuple over
$\mathbb C$.  There are linearly independent numerical degree vectors
$\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_r$ of positive genus-zero stable maps such that
\begin{equation}

 S_{\gamma_1}\cdots S_{\gamma_r}\ne0,
 \qquad
 \sum_{j=1}^r(d_{\gamma_j}-1)\le n.
\end{equation}
Consequently $r(\iota-1)\le n$.
statements.section_title: From divisor eigenvalues to independent curve degrees

statements.title: The ordered-chain bound
statements.label: thm:ordered-chain-bound
statements.text:
Let $Y$ be a smooth complex projective variety.  Let
$V^1,\ldots,V^k$ be proper irreducible components of
$\operatorname{RatCurves}^{\mathrm n}(Y)$ whose numerical classes are
linearly independent.  For every $y\in Y$, the ordered endpoint locus
is either empty or satisfies
\[
 \dim\operatorname{Locus}(V^1,\ldots,V^k)_y
 \ge\sum_{j=1}^k(-K_Y\cdot V^j-1).
\]

statements.title: Occhetta's product characterization
statements.label: thm:occhetta-product
statements.text:
Let $Y$ be a smooth complex projective variety of dimension $n$.
Suppose $Y$ has numerically independent unsplit covering families
$V^1,\ldots,V^k$ with anticanonical degrees $n_1+1,\ldots,n_k+1$,
where each $n_j$ is positive and $\sum_jn_j=n$.  Then
$Y\cong\mathbb P^{n_1}\times\cdots\times\mathbb P^{n_k}$.

statements.title: Rigidity at equality
statements.label: prop:equality-rigidity
statements.text:
Suppose $\iota\ge2$, $r(\iota-1)=n$, and the independent nonzero
product in \eqref{eq:nonzero-independent-product} exists.  Then
\[
 X\cong(\mathbb P^{\iota-1})^r.
\]

title: The Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis via elementary expansions
abstract: We prove the Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis for every Grothendieck coherator in the Ara–Henry convention: its weak globular infinity-groupoids recover the homotopy theory of spaces. We also resolve Henry's pushout conjecture, showing that elementary expansions preserve components and all homotopy groups of cellular infinity-groupoids.

tex.abstract:
We prove the Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis for every Grothendieck
coherator in the Ara--Henry convention: its weak globular infinity-groupoids
recover the homotopy theory of spaces.
We also resolve Henry's pushout conjecture, showing that elementary expansions
preserve components and all homotopy groups of cellular infinity-groupoids.
sections: Globular models and the weak-equivalence test
Semi-model structure and the homotopy hypothesis

statements.label: thm:main

statements.title: Weak-equivalence test
statements.label: prop:weak-test
statements.text:
For a model map $f:X\to Y$, the following are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f\in\mathcal W$.
\item It induces a bijection on $\pi_0$ and a bijection
\[
 \pi_r(X;u,v)\longrightarrow\pi_r(Y;fu,fv)
\]
for every $r\ge1$ and every parallel pair $u,v$ in $X$.
\item For every $r\ge0$, every specified boundary
$b:\partial D_r\to X$, and every $r$-cell $y$ of $Y$ with
boundary $fb$, there are an $r$-cell $x$ with boundary
\emph{exactly} $b$ and an $(r+1)$-cell $fx\to y$ in $Y$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, a weak equivalence reflects homotopy between
parallel cells, including equality of components for vertices.
statements.section_title: Globular models and the weak-equivalence test

statements.title: Contractibility of free shapes
statements.label: prop:shape-contractible
statements.text:
For every nonempty finite globular-sum shape $S$, the models $F(S)$
and $F_q(S)$ are contractible, for every $q\geq0$.

statements.title: Contractibility of tree diagrams
statements.label: prop:tree-contractible
statements.text:
Under the fixed-cutoff induction hypotheses above, $F_q(K)$ is
contractible for every tree diagram $K$ at depth $n$.

statements.title: Contractibility after adjoining whiskers
statements.label: prop:whiskered-shape
statements.text:
Under the fixed-cutoff induction hypotheses above,
$H_\epsilon(S)$ is contractible for both choices of $\epsilon$.
The same conclusion holds if the orientation of the join is
chosen independently for each $n$-cell of $S$.

statements.label: prop:cylinder-contractibility
statements.text:
Every \(P_j\) is contractible.  For \(n<j\le q\), both
one-sided domains \(A_j^\epsilon\) are contractible, and
\(A_j^\epsilon\to P_j\) is an upper cellular weak equivalence.
For every pasting scheme \(S\) of height at most \(q\), the model
\(P(S)\) is cellular and contractible.

statements.label: prop:partial-path
statements.text:
The construction in Equation~\eqref{eq:partial-path-cells} admits
interpretations of every operation of \(\mathcal C\), making
\(\mathcal P:\mathcal A_q\to\mathcal A_q\) a functor and
both \(p_\epsilon\) natural model morphisms.  They lift all
boundary inclusions \(I_j\).  Their joint map
\[
              (p_0,p_1):\mathcal P Y\longrightarrow Y\times Y
\]
lifts \(J_n\).

statements.label: cor:semimodel
statements.text:
For every Grothendieck coherator \(\mathcal C\), the category
\(\mathcal A\) admits a cofibrantly generated left semi-model structure
with
\[
 \begin{aligned}
  \text{weak equivalences}&=\mathcal W,\\
  \text{cofibrations}&=I\text{-}\mathrm{cof},\\
  \text{fibrations}&=J\text{-}\mathrm{inj},\\
  \text{trivial fibrations}&=I\text{-}\mathrm{inj}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here \(\mathcal W\) is the class defined by components and based
homotopy groups.  Cofibrant objects are exactly retracts of cellular
objects, and every object is fibrant.
statements.section_title: Semi-model structure and the homotopy hypothesis

statements.label: cor:homotopy-hypothesis
statements.text:
For every Grothendieck coherator \(\mathcal C\), the canonical
semi-model category \(\Mod(\mathcal C)\) is Quillen equivalent to
spaces.  More precisely, there is a geometric-realization/fundamental-
infinity-groupoid adjunction
\[
 |-|:\Mod(\mathcal C)\ \rightleftarrows\ \Spaces:\Pi_\infty
\]
which is a Quillen equivalence.  In particular,
\[
 \Mod(\mathcal C)[\mathcal W^{-1}]
       \simeq \operatorname{Ho}(\Spaces).
\]
Thus the Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis holds for these groupoids.
statements.section_title: Semi-model structure and the homotopy hypothesis

title: The Hilbert–Smith conjecture in every finite dimension
abstract: We prove the Hilbert–Smith conjecture in every finite dimension: every locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group acting faithfully and jointly continuously on a connected Hausdorff second-countable finite-dimensional topological manifold without boundary is a Lie group.

tex.abstract:
We prove the Hilbert--Smith conjecture in every finite dimension: every
locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group acting faithfully and
jointly continuously on a connected Hausdorff second-countable
finite-dimensional topological manifold without boundary is a Lie group.
sections: Compact-source sheaf categories and homotopy invariance
A bounded lattice on the test sphere
Duality shifts and the cylinder signs

statements.title: The Hilbert--Smith conjecture
statements.label: cor:lie
statements.text:
Let \(n\geq1\). A locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group
acting faithfully and jointly continuously on a connected Hausdorff
second-countable topological \(n\)-manifold without boundary is a Lie
group.

statements.title: $p$-adic exclusion
statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let \(n\geq1\) be an integer and \(p\) a prime. Every jointly continuous
action of \(\Zp\) on a connected Hausdorff second-countable topological
\(n\)-manifold without boundary has nonzero kernel. Consequently the
action factors through a finite quotient of \(\Zp\).

statements.title: Duality and compact support
statements.label: prop:test-duality
statements.text:
The Verdier operation restricts to a triangulated duality on each of
$\Tzero(X)$, $\T(X)$, $\Pzero(X)$, and $\Pcat(X)$.  In particular, for
every object $A$ in one of these categories, $\D_X A$ belongs to the same
category and the canonical map
\[
 \eta_A:A\xrightarrow{\sim}\D_X^2A
\]
is an isomorphism.  There is a compact $K\subset X$ outside which both
$A$ and $\D_X A$ vanish.
statements.section_title: Compact-source sheaf categories and homotopy invariance

statements.title: Direct images and open extension
statements.label: prop:test-pushforward
statements.text:
For an allowed map $g:X\to Y$, direct image induces exact functors
\[
 g_*:\Tzero(X)\longrightarrow\Tzero(Y),
 \qquad g_*:\T(X)\longrightarrow\T(Y),
\]
and the analogous functors for $\Pzero,\Pcat$.  They are given by
$Rg_!\simeq Rg_*$ on these categories, commute coherently with Verdier
duality and its shifts, and are compatible with composition.
For an open inclusion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, this functor is $j_!$ and
is fully faithful.
statements.section_title: Compact-source sheaf categories and homotopy invariance

statements.title: Homotopy invariance
statements.label: thm:homotopy
statements.text:
If $h:I\times X\to Y$ is a continuous homotopy of maps of test
spaces, its endpoint maps induce equal homomorphisms
\[
 h_{0*}=h_{1*}:E_r(X)\longrightarrow E_r(Y)
 \qquad(r\in\Z).
\]
The same assertion holds for $W_r(\Pcat(-))$ under the allowed
semialgebraic homotopies.  In particular, homotopy equivalences induce
isomorphisms, and a nonempty contractible test space has the Witt groups
of a point.  The semialgebraic assertion uses a contraction in the
allowed semialgebraic category.
statements.section_title: Compact-source sheaf categories and homotopy invariance

statements.title: Objects supported in an open set
statements.label: prop:compact-support
statements.text:
For an open inclusion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, the essential image of
$j_!: \Bcat(U)\to\Bcat(X)$ consists exactly of those objects whose
cohomology vanishes outside some compact subset of $U$.  This image is
a thick, duality-stable subcategory.

statements.title: Germ description
statements.label: thm:germs
statements.text:
Restriction induces natural isomorphisms
\[
 \Hom_{\Bcat(X)/\Bcat(U)}(A,B)
 \simeq
 \operatorname*{colim}_{N\supset X\setminus U}
 \Hom_{\mathsf D(N)}(A|_N,B|_N)
\]
for every $A,B\in\Bcat(X)$.  These isomorphisms respect composition,
open restriction of duality, and restriction of distinguished triangles.
The quotient here is the Verdier quotient itself.

statements.title: Witt localization
statements.label: thm:witt-localization
statements.text:
For every open $U\subset X$ and every $r\in\Z$, there is a natural
long exact sequence
\begin{equation}

 \cdots\longrightarrow W_r(\Bcat(U))
 \longrightarrow W_r(\Bcat(X))
 \longrightarrow W_r(\Bcat(X)/\Bcat(U))
 \xrightarrow{\partial}W_{r-1}(\Bcat(U))
 \longrightarrow\cdots.
\end{equation}
The sequence is natural for $\Pcat\to\T$ and for the pushforwards
of \Cref{prop:test-pushforward}: a map $g:X\to X'$ with
$g(U)\subset U'$ induces a morphism from the sequence for $(X,U)$
to the sequence for $(X',U')$.

statements.title: An open cover gives a dense inclusion
statements.label: prop:open-cover
statements.text:
If $X=U\cup V$ with $U,V$ open, extension by zero induces a fully
faithful exact functor preserving duality
\begin{equation}

 \Bcat(V)/\Bcat(U\cap V)
 \longrightarrow\Bcat(X)/\Bcat(U).
\end{equation}
Its replete image is dense: every object of the target is an actual
summand of an object in the image.  These functors commute with
$\Pcat\to\T$.

statements.title: Dense doubling
statements.label: thm:dense-doubling
statements.text:
Let $\mathcal A\subset\mathcal C$ be a full replete triangulated
subcategory stable under duality, and suppose it is dense: each object
of $\mathcal C$ is a summand of an object of $\mathcal A$.
Assume these categories admit triangular Witt groups.  In every degree,
the inclusion homomorphism
\[
 \iota:W_r(\mathcal A)\longrightarrow W_r(\mathcal C)
\]
has kernel and cokernel annihilated by $2$.  More precisely, there is
a homomorphism
$d:W_r(\mathcal C)\to W_r(\mathcal A)$ satisfying
\[
 \iota d=2\id,
 \qquad d\iota=2\id.
\]
No closure of $\mathcal A$ under arbitrary summands is required.

statements.label: loc:cor-open-cover-bound
statements.text:
The map on Witt groups induced by \eqref{loc:eq-open-cover} has kernel
and cokernel annihilated by $2$, in every degree and for either test
category.

statements.title: Bounded comparison
statements.label: thm:bounded-comparison
statements.text:
For every $j\ge0$ there is a nonnegative integer $e_j$, independent
of $r$, such that the kernel and cokernel of
\[
 F_r(S^j)\longrightarrow E_r(S^j)
\]
are annihilated by $2^{e_j}$ for every integer $r$.
statements.section_title: A bounded lattice on the test sphere

statements.title: Rational sphere calculation
statements.label: prop:sphere-rank
statements.text:
For either $G_r=F_r$ or $G_r=E_r$, and for $j\ge0$,
\[
 G_r(S^j)\otimes\Q\simeq
 \bigl(G_r(\pt)\otimes\Q\bigr)
 \oplus\bigl(G_{r-j}(\pt)\otimes\Q\bigr).
\]
In particular, for the fixed odd integer $d$, both
$F_d(S^d)\otimes\Q$ and $E_d(S^d)\otimes\Q$ are
one-dimensional rational vector spaces.
statements.section_title: A bounded lattice on the test sphere

statements.title: Signature on a finite semialgebraic relation
statements.label: prop:generic-signature
statements.text:
Every finite collection of objects of $\Pcat(S^d)$ has finite
dimensional locally constant cohomology on a common dense open
subset of $S^d$.  On a sufficiently small oriented ball there, a
degree-$d$ form has an integral signature on its degree-zero
cohomology.  For any finite
Witt relation one can choose such a ball simultaneously for all
objects and lagrangian diagrams in the relation; the signatures
then respect that relation.

Consequently $u_{F,d}$ is nontorsion and
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 F_d(S^d)\otimes\Q=\Q\overline{u}_{F,d},\\
 \im\bigl(F_d(S^d)\to F_d(S^d)\otimes\Q\bigr)=\Z\overline{u}_{F,d}.
 \end{gathered}
\]
statements.section_title: A bounded lattice on the test sphere

statements.title: The fixed sphere lattice
statements.label: thm:sphere-lattice
statements.section_title: A bounded lattice on the test sphere

statements.title: Action of degree
statements.label: prop:degree-action
statements.text:
Let $d\geq3$ be odd. If $f:S^d\to S^d$ is continuous and has
degree $s\in\Z$, then
\[
 f_*\overline{u}_d=s\overline{u}_d\quad\text{in }E_d(S^d)\otimes\Q.
\]
Consequently $f_*$ acts on this entire rational group by
multiplication by $s$.  More generally, if $N$ is a connected
closed oriented triangulable $d$-manifold and $f:N\to S^d$
has degree $s$, its pushed orientation form has rational class
$s\overline{u}_d$.
statements.section_title: A bounded lattice on the test sphere

statements.title: A contractible open set can be localized away
statements.label: prop:contractible-quotient
statements.text:
Let $d\geq3$ be odd. Let $X$ be any test space for $\T$, and let
$U\subset X$ be a
nonempty contractible open subset.  Then the quotient functor
induces an integral isomorphism
\begin{equation}
 
 E_d(X)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
 \Witt_d\bigl(\T(X)/\T(U)\bigr).
\end{equation}
In particular this applies to compact test polyhedra and to
their manifold-with-boundary models.  It is natural for
continuous maps $g:X\to X'$ with $g(U)\subset U'$, whenever
$U'$ is also a nonempty contractible open subset.
statements.section_title: A bounded lattice on the test sphere

statements.title: An invariant chart subset
statements.label: prop:chart-reduction
statements.text:
There are an open subgroup $G\cong\Zp$ and a nonempty connected
$G$-invariant open subset $O$ of a coordinate chart of $M$ such that
$G$ acts faithfully and preserves orientation on $O$.  In particular,
we may regard $O$ as the actual open subset of $\R^n$ supplied by that
chart.

statements.title: Moving a test into a prescribed open set
statements.label: prop:move-test
statements.text:
For every nonempty open $V\subset Y\setminus\{y_\infty\}$, set
$F=Y\setminus V$.  There are a positive integer $s$, a degree
$s$ map $D_s:S^d\to S^d$, and a map $h:Y\to S^d$ such that
\[
 h\simeq D_sa,
 \qquad h|_F\equiv b
\]
for some $b\in S^d$.  In particular $h(y_\infty)=b$ and
$q^{-1}h^{-1}(S^d\setminus\{b\})\subset q^{-1}(V)\subset W$.

statements.title: Sum of the character classes
statements.label: prop:sum-classes
statements.text:
Let $t:Y\to X$ be a compact test map as in \eqref{char:test-form},
with a contractible open neighborhood basis at $b_t$. For every finite
partition $\Lambda=D_0\sqcup\cdots\sqcup D_{m-1}$, its character
classes satisfy the integral identity
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{i=0}^{m-1}z_i(t)=2[A_t,\alpha_t]\quad\text{in }E_d(X).
\end{equation}

statements.title: Covariance on compact tests
statements.label: prop:class-covariance
statements.text:
Let $t:Y\to X$ be a compact test map as in \eqref{char:test-form},
and let $g:X\to X'$ be a continuous map of compact tests. Suppose $X$
has a contractible neighborhood basis at $b_t$ and $X'$ has one at
$b_{gt}=g(b_t)$.  For every fixed finite partition of $\Lambda$,
\begin{equation}
 g_*z_i(t)=z_i(gt)\quad\text{in }E_d(X').
\end{equation}

statements.title: Homotopy of character classes
statements.label: prop:class-homotopy
statements.text:
For a fixed partition of $\Lambda$, homotopic maps
$t_0,t_1:Y\to S^d$ satisfy $z_i(t_0)=z_i(t_1)$ in $E_d(S^d)$.

statements.title: Equality for a concentrated test
statements.label: prop:equal-parts
statements.text:
Let $k\geq1$, and let $V$ and its character multiplier $\beta$ be as
in \Cref{lem:finite-sheets}. If $h:Y\to S^d$ is constant on
$Y\setminus V$, then the classes for
\eqref{char:cyclic-partition} satisfy
\[
 z_0(h)=z_1(h)=\cdots=z_{m-1}(h)\quad\text{in }E_d(S^d).
\]

statements.title: Contradiction on the invariant chart
statements.label: thm:contradiction
statements.text:
For every $n\geq1$ and every prime $p$, an orientation-preserving
continuous $\Zp$-action on a connected open subset of $\R^n$ has
nonzero kernel.
