title: The complete Crouzeix theorem: optimal similarity and a common positive boundary representation
abstract: We resolve the complete Crouzeix conjecture by proving the sharp constant-two numerical-range inequality for every bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space and every matrix-valued polynomial. No separability assumption is needed. The closure of the numerical range is a complete 2-spectral set, and the bound extends to finite matrix-valued functions holomorphic near that closure. For a finite matrix and a bounded convex domain containing its numerical range with regular real-analytic Jordan boundary, the optimal similarity making its conformal disk image contractive is attained with condition number at most two. For the similar matrix, one continuous positive boundary density of mass the identity represents the evaluation of every matrix-valued function holomorphic near the closed domain.

tex.abstract:
We resolve the complete Crouzeix conjecture by proving the sharp
constant-two numerical-range inequality for every bounded operator on a
complex Hilbert space and every matrix-valued polynomial. No separability
assumption is needed. The closure of the numerical range is a complete
$2$-spectral set, and the bound extends to finite matrix-valued functions
holomorphic near that closure. For a finite matrix and a bounded convex
domain containing its numerical range with regular real-analytic Jordan
boundary, the optimal similarity making its conformal disk image contractive
is attained with condition number at most two. For the similar matrix, one
continuous positive boundary density of mass the identity represents the
evaluation of every matrix-valued function holomorphic near the closed domain.

statements.title: The optimal metric
statements.label: thm:structural
statements.text:
For every admissible $\Omega$, every finite $n\ge1$, every
$A\in M_n(\C)$ with $W(A)\subset\Omega$, and the interior conformal
coordinate $f$ above, the problem \eqref{eq:minimum} is strictly feasible
and has an attained minimum $1\le\kappa^2\le4$. If $H$ is a minimizing
metric, then
\[
 S=H^{1/2},\qquad A'=SAS^{-1},\qquad D=Sf(A)S^{-1}=f(A')
\]
satisfy
\[
 D^*D\preceq I,\qquad \rho(D)<1,
 \qquad \|S\|\|S^{-1}\|=\kappa\le2.
\]

statements.title: A common positive representation
statements.label: thm:representation
statements.text:
With the same $\Omega,A,f,G$ and any chosen minimizing metric in
Theorem~\ref{thm:structural}, there is one continuous function
$\Lambda:\T\to M_n(\C)$ satisfying
\[
 \Lambda(t)\succeq0,\qquad \int_\T\Lambda(t)\,d\sigma(t)=I_n,
\]
such that, for every positive integer $m$ and every $M_m(\C)$-valued
function $v$ holomorphic on a neighborhood of $\overline\Omega$,
\begin{equation}
 v[A']=\int_\T\Lambda(t)\otimes v(G(t))\,d\sigma(t),
 \qquad
 \|v[A]\|\le\kappa\max_{\overline\Omega}\|v\|.
\end{equation}
The same $S$, $\Lambda$, and $\kappa$ work for all $m$ and $v$.

statements.title: One density for every coefficient size
statements.label: prop:density
statements.text:
For the fixed minimizing metric, the representation
\eqref{eq:representation-target} holds, before any bound on $\kappa$ is
proved, with
\begin{align}
 \Phi_D(\zeta)&=(I-D/\zeta)^{-1}+[(I-D/\zeta)^{-1}]^*-I,
                                                        \\
 j(t)&=\frac{tG'(t)f'(G(t))}{\psi(t)}>0,
 &\Lambda(t)&=j(t)\Phi_D(\psi(t)).                      
\end{align}
statements.section_title: The metric, its representation, and its extremal data

statements.title: Endpoint extremal
statements.label: prop:extremal
statements.text:
If $\kappa>1$, there are $X,Y\in M_n(\C)$ with
\[
 \tr(XX^*)=\tr(YY^*)=1,\qquad SX=\kappa X,\qquad SY=Y,
 \qquad X^*Y=0,
\]
and an $M_n$-valued rational function $F_\D$, holomorphic on a neighborhood
of $\overline\D$ and contractive on $\overline\D$, such that, for
$x=\vecop(X)$ and $y=\vecop(Y)$,
\[
 F_\D[D]x=y.
\]
In particular $F_\Omega=F_\D\circ f$ is holomorphic near
$\overline\Omega$ and satisfies $F_\Omega[A']x=y$. Its boundary trace
$F=F_\Omega\circ G$ is contractive.
statements.section_title: The metric, its representation, and its extremal data

statements.title: Exterior coefficients and the original-matrix resolvent
statements.label: input:analytic
statements.text:
Assume the admissible $\Omega$ and the exterior map $G$ supplied above.
Write $G(t)=at+b+O(t^{-1})$ at infinity, where $a\ne0$, and
$q_G(t)=tG'(t)$. There are scalar polynomials
$b_k$, with $b_0=1$, $\deg b_k=k$, and leading coefficient $a^{-k}$,
defined by
\begin{equation}
 \frac{q_G(t)}{G(t)-z}=\sum_{k\ge0}b_k(z)t^{-k}
 \quad\text{at infinity}.
\end{equation}
There is also the mixed expansion
\begin{equation}
 B(w,t)=\frac{q_G(t)}{G(t)-G(w)}-\frac{t}{t-w}
       =\sum_{i,j\ge1}\beta_{ij}w^{-i}t^{-j},
 \qquad
 b_j(G(w))=w^j+\sum_{i\ge1}\beta_{ij}w^{-i}\quad(j\ge1).
\end{equation}
Here $B$ is holomorphic through the diagonal and both infinities of the
exterior product collar. For each $r<\rho<1$ there is a constant
$C_\rho$ such that $|\beta_{ij}|\le C_\rho\rho^{i+j}$; the series
converges normally on the product collar and absolutely uniformly on
$\T^2$. The kernel
\[
 m(w,t)=1+B(w,t)+\overline{B(w,t)}
\]
is continuous and nonnegative, with each normalized-circle marginal one.

For every finite $n$ and every original matrix $A\in M_n(\C)$ with
$W(A)\subset\Omega$,
\begin{equation}
 K_A(t)=q_G(t)(G(t)I-A)^{-1}
       =\sum_{k\ge0}b_k(A)t^{-k},\qquad
 E_A(t)=K_A(t)+K_A(t)^*\succeq0\quad(t\in\T).
\end{equation}
Its coefficients decay geometrically and its series converges absolutely
uniformly on $\T$.
The scalar case applies to every fixed $z\in\Omega$.

statements.title: The local projection theorem
statements.label: prop:projection
statements.text:
For finite Laurent data $u$, the polynomial $c_u$ has boundary trace
$\cC u=c_u\circ G$. This map extends to a bounded projection on every
$\cH_k$. With $\widetilde\cC u=(\cC(u^*))^*$, one has
\[
 \cC=P_0+P_++\M P_+,\qquad
 \widetilde\cC u=(\cC(u^*))^*.
\]
Its actual Hilbert-space adjoints satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \cC^\dagger u=u_0+u_++\M^\dagger u_-,\qquad
 \widetilde\cC^\dagger u=u_0+u_-+\M^\dagger u_+
                         =(\cC^\dagger(u^*))^*.
\end{equation}
All four operators preserve the mean, and
\begin{equation}
 \|\cC^\dagger u\|_2^2+\|(\cC^\dagger u)_0\|_2^2
 \le2\|u\|_2^2\qquad(u\in\cH_k).
\end{equation}
If $F=F_\Omega\circ G$ with $F_\Omega$ holomorphic near
$\overline\Omega$ and $M_k$-valued, then for every $u\in\cH_k$,
\begin{equation}
 \cC(F\cC u)=F\cC u,\qquad
 \cC((\cC u)F)=(\cC u)F.
\end{equation}

For every finite coefficient size and every matrix Laurent polynomial $u$,
\begin{equation}
 \int_\T E_A\otimes u\,d\sigma
 =c_u[A]+c_{u^*}[A]^*.
\end{equation}
In particular, $\int E_A\,d\sigma=2I_n$.

statements.title: The sharp complete polynomial inequality for matrices
statements.label: cor:polynomial
statements.text:
For every pair of positive integers $n,m$, every $A\in M_n(\C)$,
every nonnegative integer $d$, and every choice of matrices
$B_0,\ldots,B_d\in M_m(\C)$, the polynomial
$P(z)=\sum_{j=0}^dB_jz^j$ satisfies
\[
 \|P[A]\|=\left\|\sum_{j=0}^dA^j\otimes B_j\right\|
 \le2\max_{z\in W(A)}\|P(z)\|.
\]
The constant is independent of both matrix sizes and the degree.
No smaller constant holds uniformly over these choices.
statements.section_title: From admissible domains to bounded Hilbert-space operators

statements.title: The sharp complete inequality for bounded operators
statements.label: cor:hilbert
statements.text:
Let $\mathcal H$ be a complex Hilbert space, with no separability assumption,
and let $A\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)$. Suppose first that
$\mathcal H\ne\{0\}$, and put
\[
 W(A)=\{\langle x,Ax\rangle:x\in\mathcal H,\ \|x\|=1\},
 \qquad K=\overline{W(A)}.
\]
Then $K$ is compact and convex and contains $\spec(A)$. For every positive
integer $m$, every nonnegative integer $d$, and every matrix polynomial
$P(z)=\sum_{k=0}^d B_kz^k$ with $B_k\in M_m(\C)$, the operator
$P[A]=\sum_{k=0}^d A^k\otimes B_k$ on $\mathcal H\otimes\C^m$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \|P[A]\|\le 2\sup_{z\in W(A)}\|P(z)\|
             =2\max_{z\in K}\|P(z)\|.
\end{equation}
More generally, if $U$ is an open neighborhood of $K$ and
$F=(f_{ij}):U\to M_m(\C)$ is holomorphic, its entrywise holomorphic
evaluation, in the same base-first tensor convention, satisfies
\begin{equation}
 F[A]:=\sum_{i,j=1}^m f_{ij}(A)\otimes E_{ij},
 \qquad \|F[A]\|\le2\max_{z\in K}\|F(z)\|.
\end{equation}
Here $E_{ij}$ are the standard matrix units and $f_{ij}(A)$ is given by the
holomorphic functional calculus. In particular, $K$ is a complete
$2$-spectral set for $A$: the same estimate holds at every finite coefficient
size for every matrix-valued rational function whose poles lie outside $K$,
with evaluation by the rational functional calculus. The constant two is
optimal uniformly over all these choices.

If $\mathcal H=\{0\}$, every evaluation is the zero operator. With the
supremum over the empty numerical range defined to be zero, the corresponding
supremum-norm inequalities are $0\le0$; the compact spectral-set assertion
above is stated for nonzero $\mathcal H$.

title: The complexity of identifying a graph by Weisfeiler–Leman refinement
abstract: We prove that deciding whether Weisfeiler–Leman refinement of an input dimension identifies a given graph is EXPTIME-complete. The input is a nonempty finite simple uncolored graph in adjacency-matrix form and a positive binary-encoded dimension. Identification quantifies over every comparison graph.

tex.abstract:
We prove that deciding whether Weisfeiler--Leman refinement of an input
dimension identifies a given graph is EXPTIME-complete. The input is a
nonempty finite simple uncolored graph in adjacency-matrix form and a
positive binary-encoded dimension. Identification quantifies over every
comparison graph.
sections: Weisfeiler--Leman refinement and the bijective game
Encoding comparisons by locally reconstructible graphs
Exact projection and a local game strategy
A computation described by product schemas

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
The following problem is EXPTIME-complete under deterministic
polynomial-time many-one reductions: given a nonempty finite simple
undirected uncolored graph $G$ by its adjacency matrix and a positive
integer $k$ in binary, decide whether $\WLdim(G)\le k$.
Here dimension one uses ordinary neighbor color refinement, and
dimensions at least two use the joint-update rule described above.

statements.label: prop:upper
statements.text:
For a nonempty graph given by its binary adjacency matrix and a
positive integer $k$ in binary, deciding whether its
Weisfeiler--Leman dimension is at most $k$ belongs to EXPTIME.
statements.section_title: Weisfeiler--Leman refinement and the bijective game

statements.title: Reconstruction of an arbitrary mate
statements.label: prop:mate
statements.text:
For any comparison data just described, with $r\ge 32$, every graph
$H$ satisfying $H\equiv_r G(0)$ is isomorphic to $G(\beta)$ for
some choice of one bit $\beta_B$ per square block.
statements.section_title: Encoding comparisons by locally reconstructible graphs

statements.title: Isomorphisms and global offsets
statements.label: prop:isomorphism
statements.text:
For every choice of square bits $\beta$, the graphs $G(0)$ and
$G(\beta)$ are isomorphic if and only if there is a global offset
assignment solving all shifted square constraints.
statements.section_title: Encoding comparisons by locally reconstructible graphs

statements.title: Image consistency
statements.label: prop:image-consistency
statements.text:
For the construction of Section~\ref{sec:encoding}, suppose
$G(0)\equiv_r G(\beta)$. There are nonempty sets
$Q_{P,a}\subseteq\F^{d_P}$ for every real type $P$ and every
$a\in\{0,1\}^r$ such that, for every comparison $e:P\to R$,
\begin{equation}
 \lambda_{e,0}(Q_{P,a})
   =\Delta_e(a)+\lambda_{e,1}(Q_{R,\sigma_e(a)})
 \qquad(a\in D_e).
 
\end{equation}
Here the equality concerns scalar image sets for one comparison at
a time, not a simultaneous choice of vectors for all comparisons.

statements.title: Global offsets
statements.label: prop:global-offsets
statements.text:
For any right-hand sides $\beta$ in the construction of
Section~\ref{sec:encoding}, all square equations admit a simultaneous
assignment to the readout names if and only if there are row-sum
functions
$h_P:\{0,1\}^r\to\F^{d_P}$, one for each real type, satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \lambda_{e,0}(h_P(a))+\lambda_{e,1}(h_R(\sigma_e(a)))
       =\Delta_e(a)
 \qquad(e:P\to R,\ a\in D_e).
 
\end{equation}
Equivalently, these functions exist exactly when
$G(0)\cong G(\beta)$.

statements.title: Special-twist sufficiency
statements.label: thm:special-twist
statements.text:
Consider the graph construction with $r\geq32$ and $K=r+1$.
Let $\beta$ be given by Equation~\eqref{eq:special-twist}. Suppose that,
for every real type $P$ and every $a\in\{0,1\}^r$, there is a nonempty
set $Q_{P,a}\subseteq\F^{d_P}$, and that these sets satisfy
\begin{equation}
  \lambda_{e,0}(Q_{P,a})
  =b_e+\lambda_{e,1}(Q_{R,\sigma_e(a)})
  \qquad(e:P\longrightarrow R,\ a\in D_e).
  
\end{equation}
Then $G(0)\equiv_r G(\beta)$.
statements.section_title: Exact projection and a local game strategy

statements.title: Exact projection
statements.label: prop:exact-projection
statements.text:
For $V\subseteq U$ with $|U|\leq r+1$, restriction to the readout names
occurring in $V$ maps $\mathcal H_U$ onto $\mathcal H_V$.
statements.section_title: Exact projection and a local game strategy

statements.label: prop:computation
statements.text:
For the fixed machine \(M\) and each input \(w\), with parameters
\eqref{eq:computation-parameters}, one can construct in time polynomial in
\(r+m\) an acyclic monotone circuit description with \(O_M(1)\) gate types and
\(O_M((r+1)^2+m)\) connection schemas, seed requests, and test requests.
Every schema has a nonempty product domain and coordinate injections;
the whole description contains \(O_M(r((r+1)^2+m))\) constant-size
coordinate entries. All tests are scalar terminal gates.
The machine \(M\) accepts \(w\) if and only if at least one designated test
gate is true.
statements.section_title: A computation described by product schemas

statements.label: prop:acceptance
statements.text:
If \(M\) accepts \(w\), then every finite simple uncolored graph
\(H\equiv_r G(0)\) is isomorphic to \(G(0)\).

statements.label: prop:rejection
statements.text:
If \(M\) does not accept \(w\), then there is a choice of square bits
\(\beta\) such that \(G(\beta)\equiv_r G(0)\) but
\(G(\beta)\not\cong G(0)\).

statements.label: cor:unary
statements.text:
The identification problem of Theorem~\ref{thm:main} remains
EXPTIME-complete when the positive dimension is encoded in unary.

title: The cotype–cotype conjecture under the approximation property
abstract: We prove the cotype–cotype conjecture under the ordinary approximation property. A nonzero real Banach space with this property is K-convex if and only if both the space and its dual have finite Rademacher cotype, possibly with different exponents.

tex.abstract:
We prove the cotype--cotype conjecture under the ordinary approximation
property. A nonzero real Banach space with this property is \(K\)-convex
if and only if both the space and its dual have finite Rademacher cotype,
possibly with different exponents.
sections: Uniform Walsh decay for finite-rank operators
Compact factorization and the approximation property

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let \(X\) be a nonzero real Banach space with the ordinary approximation
property. Then \(X\) is \(K\)-convex if and only if
\[
C_q(X)<\infty
\quad\hbox{and}\quad
C_r(X^*)<\infty
\qquad\text{for some }q,r\in[2,\infty).
\]
The exponents \(q\) and \(r\) may differ. The forward implication holds
for every real Banach space, without an approximation hypothesis.

statements.title: Uniform cotype bounds and entropy duality
statements.label: cor:uniform-cotype-entropy
statements.text:
Fix \(q,r\in[2,\infty)\) and \(C,D\in[1,\infty)\). There is a
finite constant \(\kappa=\kappa(q,r,C,D)\) such that every nonzero
real Banach space \(X\) with AP and
\[
C_q(X)\le C,\qquad C_r(X^*)\le D
\]
satisfies \(K(X)\le\kappa\).
Consequently there are \(a,b\ge1\), depending only on \(q,r,C,D\),
such that for every \(n\ge1\), all origin-symmetric convex bodies
\(K,L\subset\R^n\), and every \(t>0\),
\begin{equation}
\frac1b\log N(L^\circ,atK^\circ)
\le \log N(K,tL)
\le b\log N(L^\circ,a^{-1}tK^\circ),
\end{equation}
provided either \(X_K\) or \(X_L\) satisfies the displayed primal
and dual cotype bounds.

statements.title: Uniform finite-rank decay
statements.label: thm:uniform-decay
statements.text:
Fix \(m,D_g,D_f\) satisfying the assumptions of Lemma~\ref{lem:growth}.
There is an integer \(n_0\), depending only on these parameters,
such that every finite-rank \(T:G\to F\) with
\(c_m(G^*)\le D_g\) and \(c_m(F)\le D_f\) satisfies
\begin{equation}
w_n(T)\le\tfrac12 w_{n-2m}(T)\qquad(n\ge n_0).
\end{equation}
In particular there are numbers \(\rho_N\to0\), independent of
\(G,F,T\), such that
\begin{equation}
w_N(T)\le\rho_N\|T\|.
\end{equation}
Both bounds also hold for every \(T:G\to F\) that is an
operator-norm limit of finite-rank maps, under the same moment
hypotheses on \(G^*\) and \(F\).
statements.section_title: Uniform Walsh decay for finite-rank operators

statements.label: cor:grothendieck
statements.text:
If \((\mathcal E,F)\) is a Grothendieck pair and \(F\) is
infinite-dimensional with the approximation property, then
\((\mathcal E,\ell_2)\) is a Grothendieck pair.
In particular, Pisier's conjecture
\cite[Conjecture 1.4]{GMR25} holds, with the approximation property
in place of the bounded approximation property.

title: The critical Liouville quantum sphere and geometric limits of FK maps at q=4
abstract: We construct the field and area law of the unit-area critical Liouville quantum sphere as a limit of ordinary subcritical quantum spheres, and equip it with its critical intrinsic metric. We then prove that spherical Fortuin–Kasteleyn planar maps at q = 4, embedded by their equilateral flag uniformizations, converge jointly to this sphere decorated by an independent nested conformal loop ensemble CLE4. With deterministic distance normalization, the convergence includes the area measure, the full embedded distance function, and every macroscopic interface through all positive integer edge counts.

tex.abstract:
We construct the field and area law of the unit-area critical Liouville
quantum sphere as a limit of ordinary subcritical quantum spheres, and
equip it with its critical intrinsic metric. We then prove that spherical
Fortuin--Kasteleyn planar maps at $q=4$, embedded by their equilateral flag
uniformizations, converge jointly to this sphere decorated by an independent
nested conformal loop ensemble $\CLE_4$. With deterministic distance
normalization, the convergence includes the area measure, the full embedded
distance function, and every macroscopic interface through all positive
integer edge counts.
sections: Construction of the critical quantum sphere
Exact disk encoding and the loop-counting law
Marked disk laws and uniform boundary control
Critical cutting, Palm comparison, and peeling
Whole-plane walls, canonical fans, and finite local orders
Peeling mosaics and conditional observation kernels
The flag conformal structure and field-local passage laws
Open-port comparisons and the deterministic distance scale
Balanced segments and continuity at all endpoints
Address counting and completion of the joint limit

statements.title: The critical area-marked sphere
statements.label: thm:continuum
statements.text:
As $\gamma\uparrow2$, the laws of $(H_\gamma,\nu_\gamma)$ converge to a unique nondegenerate probability law $\mathsf P_{\rm crit}$ in
\[
 H^{-1}(S^2,g_{\rm round})\times\mathcal P(S^2),
\]
with the norm topology in the first factor and the weak topology in the second. Let $(H,\nu)$ have this law and set $h=H+\log g_{\rm round}$ in local conformal coordinates. Then $\nu=\mu_h^{\rm crit}$, where on compact sets avoiding $0,1,\infty$,
\begin{equation}
 \mu_h^{\rm crit}(\dd z)
 =\lim_{\eps\downarrow0}
  \bigl(2\log(1/\eps)-h_\eps(z)\bigr)
        \eps^2e^{2h_\eps(z)}\,\dd^2z
\end{equation}
locally weakly in probability. This positive measure extends across the three marks without atoms, has full support, and has total mass one.

After forgetting the three marks, sampling three new conditionally independent area points and normalizing them to $0,1,\infty$ recovers $\mathsf P_{\rm crit}$. If $f$ maps the new coordinate to the old one, the field transforms as
\[
 h_{\rm new}=h_{\rm old}\circ f+2\log|f'|.
\]

With any one fixed deterministic normalization of the Ding--Gwynne critical local metric, the compatible chart metrics define an intrinsic length metric on the sphere punctured at the three marks. Its completion adds exactly those marks and is a finite continuous metric $D_h$ on $S^2$, inducing the usual topology. The area and completed metric are measurable functions of the same field and obey the corresponding charge-$2$ coordinate rules.

statements.title: Joint critical universality
statements.label: thm:main

statements.title: The compact metric-measure limit
statements.label: intro:ghp
statements.text:
Define a probability measure on the primal vertices by
\[
 \eta_n=\sum_{v\in V(M_n)}\frac{\deg_{M_n}(v)}{2n}\,\delta_v.
\]
With the deterministic normalization of Theorem~\ref{thm:main},
\[
 (V(M_n),a_nd_n,\eta_n)
 \ \xrightarrow{\ d\ }\
 (S^2,D_h,\mu_h^{\rm crit})
\]
in the Gromov--Hausdorff--Prokhorov topology, jointly with the embedded
area and loop convergence in that theorem.

statements.title: The prescribed limiting probability law
statements.label: cont:limit-law
statements.text:
The field-measure laws in the continuum approximation of
Theorem~\ref{thm:continuum} converge, independently of the sequence
$\gamma\uparrow2$, in round-background $H^{-1}$ norm and weak measure
topology.  In cylinder coordinates their limit is obtained from
\begin{equation}
 h_{\mathcal C}=G^\perp-R_0-\tfrac12\log L,
 \qquad \nu_{\mathcal C}=M_0/L,
\end{equation}
by sending the two ends to $0,\infty$ and an additional independent area
sample to $1$, using charge $2$.  Denote this law by $\mathsf P_{\rm crit}$.
It is invariant under resampling three conditionally independent area marks
and normalizing them to $0,1,\infty$.
statements.section_title: Construction of the critical quantum sphere

statements.title: Derivative normalization and area marking
statements.label: cont:area-identification
statements.text:
For $(H,\nu)\sim \mathsf P_{\rm crit}$, put $h=H+\log g_{\rm round}$ in local
conformal coordinates.  On $\widehatC\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$, its law is
locally absolutely continuous modulo constants and
\[
 \nu(dz)=\mu_h^{\rm crit}(dz)
   =\lim_{\eps\downarrow0}
      (2\log\eps^{-1}-h_\eps(z))\eps^2e^{2h_\eps(z)}\,d^2z
\]
locally weakly in probability.  The measure extends with zero atoms at the
three marks, is diffuse with full support, has total mass one, and is
measurable from $h$.  Its fixed-coordinate covariance and its covariance
under re-marking are the charge-two rule.  The law $\mathsf P_{\rm crit}$ is
nondegenerate.
statements.section_title: Construction of the critical quantum sphere

statements.title: Fixed conformal covariance
statements.label: cont:metric-covariance
statements.text:
For every fixed conformal coordinate map, the local critical metrics of
Lemma~\ref{cont:local-metric} obey the charge-two coordinate-change rule.
Equivalently, the metrics $d$ and $\widetilde d$ above have the same local
lengths and hence the same intrinsic distances on common domains.
statements.section_title: Construction of the critical quantum sphere

statements.title: Short surrounding detours and random charts
statements.label: cont:detours
statements.text:
Almost surely, every regular point has arbitrarily small surrounding
rectifiable loops whose metric lengths tend to zero.  The conformal
covariance of Proposition~\ref{cont:metric-covariance} also holds on common
nonsingular regions for the random maps obtained from finitely many area
samples in the preceding construction.
statements.section_title: Construction of the critical quantum sphere

statements.title: The metric sphere
statements.label: cont:sphere-completion
statements.text:
The intrinsic critical metric on
$\widehatC\setminus\{0,1,\infty\}$ for $\mathsf P_{\rm crit}$ completes to a finite
continuous metric $D_h$ on the sphere.  Its completion adds exactly the three
marked points and induces the usual sphere topology.  The extended metric
is measurable from the original field alone and obeys the charge-two
coordinate rule, including the re-marking operation.
statements.section_title: Construction of the critical quantum sphere

statements.title: Partition function and loop-counting intensity
statements.label: disk:palm
statements.text:
For a loop let \(k,l\) be the numbers of its visited Tutte triangles with blue, respectively red base.
Call the side adjacent to the blue bases (i.e. toward the blue endpoints of crossed links) its blue side, and let \(u\) be the \(m_n\)-area of that side of the loop on the sphere, including everything nested there.
Write \(d_s(v)=s^2 v^{-2}\exp(-s^2/v)\) for \(s,v>0\), extended by zero at \(v=0\).
Then
\begin{equation}
\begin{gathered}
X^{2n}Z_n(4)\sim \frac{8\pi^2}{n^2\log^2 n},\\
\lim_n \mathbb E\sum_{\rm loops}\psi(k/B_n,u)
 =\frac1{2\pi^2}\int_0^\infty\int_0^1
 \psi(s,v)\frac{ds\,dv}{s^5}\,d_s(v)d_s(1-v).
\end{gathered}
 
\end{equation}
Here \(\psi\) is continuous with compact support in \((0,\infty)\times[0,1]\), extended by zero at length zero.
This does not assert that loop lengths can be read from a geometric limit or that every macroscopic loop has \(k\) in a range of order \(B_n\).
statements.section_title: Exact disk encoding and the loop-counting law

statements.title: Marked disk factorization
statements.label: proxy:marked-factorization
statements.text: For almost every prescribed positive initial perimeter pair, run the independent symmetric $\SLE^0_\kappa(\kappa-6)$ branch on the corresponding boundary-marked disk.  At a fixed surviving trunk time $t$, conditional on the signed boundary-length path up to $t$, the offspring discovered by $t$ are independent once-boundary-marked disks with perimeters equal to their absolute jump sizes.  Their mark is the actual attachment or disconnection point.  Independently, the remaining surface with its tip and target is a twice-marked disk conditioned on its two arc lengths.  The assertion concerns abstract marked surfaces and retains the component laws of the unobserved CLEs.
statements.section_title: Marked disk laws and uniform boundary control

statements.title: All-point boundary-chain estimate
statements.label: proxy:boundary-chain
statements.text:
For a disk \(g\) in standard twice-typical strip coordinates with perimeter \(s\), paths in its interior approaching any flat boundary point \(z\) and \(+\infty\) can be joined, along the direction to the right, at cost bounded (including the above deterministic upper weight) by

\begin{equation}
K\,s^{2\xi_0/\gamma}\left(\frac{m([z,+\infty))}{s}\right)^{\theta 2\xi_0/\gamma},
 
\end{equation}
where $m$ denotes boundary length on that side.  The moment quantifier is as follows: for each $M\in(0,\infty)$, choose $\theta<1$ sufficiently close to $1$ and then $\gamma_M<2$ so that
\[
 \sup_{\gamma\in(\gamma_M,2]}\E[K^M]<\infty.
\]
The value $\gamma=2$ denotes the limiting disk law.  The choice of $\theta$ is allowed to depend on $M$.
More precisely we assert existence of connected chains/paths \emph{between arbitrarily small neighborhoods} of the two points, simultaneously at every \(z\).
The reverse statement toward \(-\infty\) also holds, and the chains may approach an end on either side using central Whitney slab paths.
No exact internal metric extension to boundary is needed.
statements.section_title: Marked disk laws and uniform boundary control

statements.title: Critical cutting and the exact contact rule
statements.label: cut:critical-cutting
statements.text:
Consider a critical field disk with a boundary-typical source and a target
at any prescribed strictly interior relative boundary length.  Its independent
symmetric \(\mathrm{bSLE}^{0,0}_4\) exploration admits a trunk-time
parametrization in which the left and right boundary lengths have the law of
Lemma~\ref{cut:lifetime}.  Conditional on the full length path, the jump
interiors are independent critical disks with the corresponding perimeters
and pinch marks.  At the compact-surviving deterministic times and selected
jump stops used below, the remaining disk has the marked disk law conditional
on the observed past length data.

The trunk is a simple continuous arc, all jump domains are Jordan domains,
and two contour occurrences have the same physical image exactly when
they satisfy the contact relation of Definition~\ref{cut:contact-relation}.  In particular no side class links two distinct real trunk times,
no class identifies distinct points of one outer or jump circle, and no
inserted positive circle visits the original boundary.  The full exploration,
including its ordered loop tours, is obtained as the limit of the subcritical
cuttings on compact surviving pieces, with the terminal remainder shrinking
spatially to the target.
statements.section_title: Critical cutting, Palm comparison, and peeling

statements.title: One auxiliary field for compatible branches
statements.label: cut:branching-fields
statements.text:
The critical branches can be realized as full signed-CLE explorations of
one constant-boundary Dirichlet GFF \(J\), independent of the Liouville input.
Branches with the same source and compatible transmitted targets agree until
the targets separate, and continue in the resulting components with the
signed exploration Markov law.  Negative complementary components have the
unchanged constant boundary value; positive loop interiors have the signed
increment \(\pm2\lambda\) and retain their independent Dirichlet fillings.
These statements concern the full exploration, including encountered loops.
They allow countably many compatible continuations and preserve the abstract
marked-disk factorization stated in Proposition~\ref{cut:critical-cutting}.
statements.section_title: Critical cutting, Palm comparison, and peeling

statements.title: Critical sphere cuts
statements.label: cut:palm
statements.text:
For the unit-area critical sphere of Section~\ref{sec:continuum} with an
independent nested \(\CLE_4\), the counting intensity of a loop, a fair choice
of side, its intrinsic perimeter \(s\), and that side's area
\(v\) has density
\[
 \frac1{2\pi^2}s^{-5}d_s(v)d_s(1-v)\,ds\,dv,
 \qquad s>0,\quad 0<v<1.
\]
The corresponding actual cut surfaces are the critical disk pair with these
areas and perimeter, with independent uniform relative boundary phase and
independent nested CLEs in the two interiors.  Matching is by the intrinsic
boundary-length labels.  The identity also holds, after integrating scale,
as a measure-class identity for arbitrary total area.  No uniqueness theorem
for critical conformal welding is required.
statements.section_title: Critical cutting, Palm comparison, and peeling

statements.title: Compatible target routes
statements.label: cut:marked-targets
statements.text:
For any finite compatible family of transmitted or independently sampled
interior target labels from a common source, the localized path and offspring
comparisons hold jointly, for arbitrary converging positive initial
perimeters and splits.  The same holds recursively in fresh matched jump
disks, with the prescribed pinch source or a single fresh common source;
transmitted targets are chosen without inspecting the fresh filling.
Countably many such observations are obtained by increasing finite tests.
Only compatible routes use common prefixes; independence is asserted for
fresh components under the marked conditional laws.
statements.section_title: Critical cutting, Palm comparison, and peeling

statements.title: Finitely many labels on a fixed frontier
statements.label: cut:finite-frontier-labels
statements.text:
Fix a pre- or post-state $v$ of a critical branch.  For every physical point
$z$, the set
\[
 \{(\alpha,h):\alpha\in\{L,R\},\ 0\leq h\leq Z^\alpha(v),
                   \ B^\alpha_v(h)=z\}
\]
is finite.  This assertion concerns one fixed frontier.  It does not bound
the number of historical contour occurrences in a contact class.
statements.section_title: Critical cutting, Palm comparison, and peeling

statements.title: Spatial comparison under coupled cutting data
statements.label: cut:disk-spatial
statements.text:
Consider a pair joined by a central ring of two positive asymptotically equal rescaled degrees, matching equal relative slots uniformly.
Take an actual matched continuum pair, a sphere topologically, with the two closed disks glued by the indicated cyclic length alignment.
Use any compatible sphere coordinates, possibly sampled from a continuum conditional law.
In each disk take a recursive routing as above with continuous trunks, Jordan jump disks shrinking at accumulating jump times (including at terminal), exact quotient contacts, and mesh tending to zero down the nested tiling.
This holds in particular for the fresh-target primary experiment.
Suppose the pathwise localized couplings and vertex estimates of the preceding paragraphs hold on this countable recursion including the indicated ring alignment.
At a matched child the path(s) there are treated within the child's own chart; a continuation toward transmitted targets can use the pinch slot specified by the split.
Then one can align the entire flag spheres by orientation-preserving homeomorphisms to the continuum sphere with vanishing flag mesh so that all sites in matched disks project in the limit within their assigned closures, and the contour, tip/frontier and ring observations above compare uniformly as specified.
Full macroscopic loop tours converge with multiplicities and no macroscopic extras if these cutting trees carry the stated CLE, including all remaining loops inside children.
This assertion does not control either graph distance or actual conformal distance in the lattice maps.
statements.section_title: Critical cutting, Palm comparison, and peeling

statements.title: Joint path, volume, and area comparison
statements.label: cut:joint-volumes
statements.text:
At perimeter scale \(P=B_n\), normalize triangle counts by \(2n\).
In the unconditioned pair construction, all matched cell volumes converge
jointly with the compatible path data to the areas of the corresponding
critical field disks.  Under the homeomorphisms of
Proposition~\ref{cut:disk-spatial}, the normalized flag-area measures converge
weakly to the quantum area measure.
statements.section_title: Critical cutting, Palm comparison, and peeling

statements.title: Transfer to exact total volume
statements.label: cut:fixed-volume
statements.text:
Fix a compact positive window for the rescaled perimeter of a centrally
marked loop.  The exact fixed-size counting intensity converges to the
unit-area critical sphere Palm law of Proposition~\ref{cut:palm}, jointly
with every finite compatible surviving path test and every finite collection
of cell-volume labels.  The spatial, area, and full loop-tour comparisons of
Propositions~\ref{cut:disk-spatial} and~\ref{cut:joint-volumes} hold in this
conditioned coupling.
statements.section_title: Critical cutting, Palm comparison, and peeling

statements.title: The unbiased topological comparison
statements.label: cut:unbiased
statements.text:
The ordinary finite FK sphere admits a joint coupling to the prescribed
unit-area critical sphere in which orientation-preserving topological
placements give weak area convergence, full nested-loop matching with
multiplicities, intrinsic loop-length label convergence, and vanishing flag
mesh.  Three independent flag-area samples converge jointly to three
independent quantum-area samples.  The conformal identification of these
placements with the prescribed uniformizations and the comparison of graph
distances are established separately in the following sections.
statements.section_title: Critical cutting, Palm comparison, and peeling

statements.title: Whole-plane walls and local determination
statements.label: wall:local-determination
statements.text:
There are two signed nested wall systems $O,E$, coupled with $J$, with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item Each has the marginal law of a whole-plane nested $\CLE_4$.  Domain means for $O$ are even multiples of $\lambda$ and its wall levels are odd multiples; $E$ has the shifted parity.
\item Under counting Palm measure at a loop, its two side disks carry independent Dirichlet fields with constant side data differing by $2\lambda$, modulo the common period.  The nesting on either side is the deterministic level-CLE construction of that side field.
\item Both systems are determined by $J$.  Under conditionally independent resampling outside an open patch with its field fixed, their arc portions within the patch, together with directions and local data, agree almost surely.  This statement does not fix the outside grouping of separated arcs.
\item The two systems do not cross.  If a wall has a proper open arc in one side of another wall and touches that wall, its level equals the actual mean on that side in a common real lift.  For two conditionally independent copies of the same system given $J$, unequal loops cannot meet.
\end{enumerate}
All assertions about conditional resampling hold simultaneously for countably many sampled conditional extensions and countably many buffered observations.
statements.section_title: Whole-plane walls, canonical fans, and finite local orders

statements.title: Returns and finite capture
statements.label: wall:returns
statements.section_title: Whole-plane walls, canonical fans, and finite local orders

statements.title: Finitely many local callers
statements.label: wall:finite-local-patterns
statements.text: After further buffering, the following data have only finitely many joint possibilities over the compared conditional extensions: canonical callers that have boundary, trunk, or hit-wall operations near $K$ and interact with the exterior buffer; their local open domains and Jordan boundary arcs; their first two half-layer pieces and relevant child groupings; and their half-layer depths relative to the corresponding local shield.  A separate common shift is suppressed for each local depth array.  Whole internal subtrees have common determined geometry.  The finiteness is pathwise, with a random finite cover and random finite lists; it is not a deterministic bound and does not bound the number of preceding remote-only steps.
statements.section_title: Whole-plane walls, canonical fans, and finite local orders

statements.title: Local path uniqueness
statements.label: wall:fan-local-uniqueness
statements.text:
Compare ordinary fan paths in locally identical caller geometry, with the same real field $J-c$.  Consider portions from a common directed interior marker to a common later marker $B$, lying entirely, with room, in the agreement region.  Either endpoint may instead be the shared actual source or shared actual local target.  In the initial-marker case retain one binary tag: the true-boundary direction toward the target at the first boundary contact in the portion, if there is one.  With matching tags the portions coincide.  For a common terminal target $y$ this tag is already determined by the boundary grouping and linear order away from the source $x$: at a contact proceed toward $y$ without passing back across $x$.

The assertion holds simultaneously for the countably many marginal samples and ordinary endpoint tests used above.  It requires no new tag at each later boundary contact.
statements.section_title: Whole-plane walls, canonical fans, and finite local orders

statements.title: Simultaneous target order
statements.label: wall:simultaneous-targets
statements.text: Use the finite caller patterns and coupled pools above.  On a buffered compact observation region, the full family of local target-path portions has only finitely many joint possibilities, including their path order and shared-prefix tree, simultaneously for a dense family of ordinary targets and for length-almost every target.  Matching portions coincide exactly.  No separate finite choice is introduced for each target.  The conclusion holds jointly in a finite cover of comparison charts and is unchanged by increasing or reordering the dense target lists used to represent the fan.
statements.section_title: Whole-plane walls, canonical fans, and finite local orders

statements.title: Births and length readouts in matched blocks
statements.label: wall:birth-length
statements.text: The finite local comparison may include positive-loop discoveries, negative cut domains, the positions at which internal children attach to the traversal tree, and inherited target intervals.  For a block retained wholly in the agreement region, it also includes its macroscopic length path, elapsed Cauchy clock, and uncharted future tree with the shared internal sources.  It does not determine the absolute offset from a possibly exterior path origin.  Under a constant local Weyl length scaling, both these lengths and elapsed Cauchy time scale by the same constant.
statements.section_title: Whole-plane walls, canonical fans, and finite local orders

statements.title: Exact local gluing projections
statements.label: kern:local-projections
statements.text:
Fix a finite mosaic history on a supported valid chart. Along a convergent lattice realization,
all sufficiently large approximations have their buffered local readouts determined by the retained
raw pieces and finitely many affine integer gluing tests. The tests retain every viable
closed macroscopic prefix, including singleton cases. Every binding translation is accounted for
by arcs inside the private buffer.
statements.section_title: Peeling mosaics and conditional observation kernels

statements.title: Product kernels given the whole tree
statements.label: kern:product-kernels
statements.text:
Consider any compatible joint extraction of countably many local readouts from separated retained
blocks. There are reference disintegrations \(k_b\), fixed for the countable local types, such that
the conditional law of the retained payloads given \((\mathcal T,\text{chart})\) is
\begin{equation}
 \prod_b k_b(dU_b^*\mid S_b,I_b,G_b).
\end{equation}
The only conditioning within block $b$ is on $S_b,I_b$, and its actual
projection $G_b$; unused hypothetical continuations are not conditioned on.
statements.section_title: Peeling mosaics and conditional observation kernels

statements.title: Fixed sphere volume
statements.label: kern:fixed-volume
statements.text:
The product rule \eqref{eq:original-15}, with the same reference versions at matched local
inputs, holds given the full unit-area sphere input and chart, including after removing Palm
weights. A different fresh nuisance reservoir may be used for each finite-cylinder comparison.
statements.section_title: Peeling mosaics and conditional observation kernels

statements.title: Common finite local chart data
statements.label: kern:matching-charts
statements.text:
Fix a compact inner test with a strict field buffer. In the conditional exterior comparison with
private source pools, successful mosaics can be chosen so that the retained raw-piece instructions,
local open geometry and order, interface parametrizations, actual entry projections, and effective
macroscopic gluing shifts range over one finite collection. The collection includes all closed
viable matching cases and does not depend on the cost units or the readout extraction. This
collection is finite almost surely for the common local data and pools; no deterministic bound
on its size is asserted.
statements.section_title: Peeling mosaics and conditional observation kernels

statements.title: One finite alternative for a countable kernel vector
statements.label: kern:finite-vector
statements.text:
Let \(\mathcal A\) be any countable family of common cost extractions and fixed unit conversions.
Conditional on the local real fields (including their heights), the local auxiliary field, and
the private source pools, the vector of full-input conditional profile laws
\((K_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathcal A}\) has finite support. Equivalently, one tag \(T\) with finite conditional support almost surely suffices to write every coordinate as \(K_\alpha=F_\alpha(L,T)\), where
\(L\) denotes these common local data. The tag is common to all coordinates; its number of
possible values may depend on \(L\).
statements.section_title: Peeling mosaics and conditional observation kernels

statements.title: Uniform fixed-label candidate tests
statements.label: kern:candidate-draws
statements.text:
In a fixed prototype law, the number of candidate kernel vectors and the reciprocal of their
smallest positive conditional mass can be truncated once in probability. Arbitrarily high
marginal success at a fixed label therefore gives arbitrarily high success for draws from all
candidates, with a loss bound uniform in the label. The conclusion concerns each fixed label;
it does not require simultaneous success over infinitely many labels. Across separated patches,
independent arrays of candidate draws can include the actual selected draws.
statements.section_title: Peeling mosaics and conditional observation kernels

statements.title: Aligned all-point shells
statements.label: conf:aligned-shells
statements.text:
Fix \(\alpha>0\), the buffered annular geometry above, and a
countable common extraction of field and regularized-profile observations
with its fixed label conversions. Let \(E_i\) be a local success test at
label \(i\), with strict band margins, evaluated in the fixed prototype
probability law. For sufficiently small \(q>0\), chosen after these
fixed comparisons, the following implication holds. Suppose that for
each \(N\) in an unbounded set of integers there is
\(G_N\subset[N,2N]\cap\Z\) satisfying
\[
 |G_N|\ge\alpha N,
 \qquad \Prob(E_i)\ge1-q\quad(i\in G_N).
\]
Then, as \(N\to\infty\) through this set, with probability tending to
one every point of any fixed planar compact away from the ends lies,
with central-hole clearance, in at least \(\beta N\) successful shell
holes along its fine-grid ancestry. Here \(\beta>0\) and all the radii
are at most \(e^{-aN}\) for a fixed \(a>0\). For each label, disks of
any fixed large multiple \(P_0\) of these radii can be required to have
bounded overlap.

For each fixed \(N\) only finitely many shells are tested, although the
number of spatial size levels may be exponential in \(N\). The discrete
index is sent to infinity for this finite family before \(N\) is
increased. The same conclusion applies along jointly extracted
subsequences; the required prototype probability is chosen after the
geometry, fraction, density comparisons, and simultaneous-candidate
requirements have been fixed.
statements.section_title: The flag conformal structure and field-local passage laws

statements.label: conf:el-nondegeneracy
statements.section_title: The flag conformal structure and field-local passage laws

statements.title: Raw extremal-length budgets
statements.label: conf:raw-el-budgets
statements.text:
In every diverging perimeter extraction, the following conclusions hold along the good
spatial-comparison subsequences.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The family of all curves making a fixed positive spherical advance has extremal length
bounded below by a strictly positive constant, eventually along the extraction.
\item For circular rings in an ordinary planar chart, with a fixed
comparable-radius ratio and fixed comparable buffer margins, there is a
strictly positive lower bound on through extremal length that is uniform
in radius and location. For each fixed ring test the bound holds
eventually along the extraction; the eventual discrete index may depend
on the ring.
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: The flag conformal structure and field-local passage laws

statements.label: conf:flag-uniformization
statements.text:
Include three fresh independent samples from normalized area in the spatial comparison. The actual
orientation-preserving uniformizations of the flag surfaces, normalized at these samples, converge
along every good extracted subsequence to the prescribed conformal normalization of the continuum
sphere. The area, full nested-loop, and maximal flag-mesh comparisons therefore hold in these actual
uniformization coordinates, in their common joint law.
statements.section_title: The flag conformal structure and field-local passage laws

statements.title: Removal of the auxiliary sampling choices
statements.label: conf:source-elimination
statements.text:
Given \(h,J\), the conditional laws of the regularized true profile arrays are unchanged by
revealing the central loop, associated end choices and phase, and the entire canonical source
family. Conditional profile kernels for disjoint strictly buffered observations multiply given
\(h,J\).
statements.section_title: The flag conformal structure and field-local passage laws

statements.label: conf:cm-comparison
statements.text:
Compactly supported deterministic Cameron--Martin changes in an ordinary observation patch preserve
the full-field arbitrary-area measure class. Quantitative comparisons for any finite list of smooth
recipes in similar shells away from the ends can be made with bounded likelihood on events of
arbitrarily high marginal probability, using ordinary local Gaussian pairings and energies. The
exterior can be retained in these comparisons.
statements.section_title: The flag conformal structure and field-local passage laws

statements.title: Equality of local comparison factors
statements.label: metric:rigidity
statements.text:
In an extraction with diverging denominator units for which upper chaining
gives a finite positive upper optimum $C$, the lower optimum equals $C$.
The common factor is deterministic. This conclusion holds simultaneously
in the fixed-offset experiments with their converted units.
statements.section_title: Open-port comparisons and the deterministic distance scale

statements.title: Deterministic scale and local comparison
statements.label: metric:scale-bootstrap
statements.text:
Define
\[
 \mathcal B(P)=A_{\lfloor\log_2P\rfloor}
\]
for large $P$, extending it positively for small $P$. For every
$\sigma\in(0,\xi)$ there is a finite deterministic $K_\sigma$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\mathcal B(P')}{\mathcal B(P)}
 \le K_\sigma\left(\frac{P'}P\right)^\sigma,
 \qquad 1\le P'\le P.
\end{equation}
Along every sequence of diverging perimeter units there is a further
joint extraction on which the lower and upper open-port comparison
factors in denominator units $\mathcal B(P)$ agree. Their common value
is deterministic and lies in a universal compact positive range.
These local almost-sure comparisons also hold on ordinary patches of
the unit-area sphere.
statements.section_title: Open-port comparisons and the deterministic distance scale

statements.title: Simultaneous segment counts
statements.label: end:band-counts
statements.text:
Start a balanced recursion at $p_{\rm init}\asymp B_n$ and stop a branch when it
first exceeds $p_*=C_*B_n$. The probability of any such crossing tends to zero
as $C_*\to\infty$. For every $\delta_1>0$, sufficiently small, the expected
number of nodes with $k=\lfloor\log(p_*/p)\rfloor$ is at most
$C e^{(2+\delta_1)k}$. With arbitrarily high probability, simultaneously for all
ancestry lines and all $k\ge0$, the number of such nodes on any one line is at
most $C e^{\delta_1k}$, with a suitable deterministic $C$.
statements.section_title: Balanced segments and continuity at all endpoints

statements.title: Bad grid times
statements.label: end:bad-grid
statements.text:
For each prescribed \(B,C\), with failure probability \(O(e^{-B N})\) under \(T_p\),
\textbf{every} such base interval (intersect the executed path) has at most
\(\exp(\tau(b-1)N)\) bad grid times, outside the stated strips. It suffices to use a mesh
of base intervals and allow a constant multiple of this bound on arbitrary intervals. In
this reduction and the estimate one can spend strict exponent slack in all the displayed
inequalities.
statements.section_title: Balanced segments and continuity at all endpoints

statements.title: Uniform endpoint continuity
statements.label: end:endpoint-reduction
statements.text:
Assume Proposition~\ref{end:bad-grid}. For every $\varepsilon>0$,
\[
 \lim_{r\downarrow0}\limsup_{n\to\infty}
 \Prob\left[
 \sup_{\substack{u,v\in V(M_n)\\\rho(\phi_n(u),\phi_n(v))\le r}}
 \frac{d_n(u,v)}{\mathcal B(B_n)}>\varepsilon
 \right]=0.
\]
Normalized diameters are tight. Every subsequential limit of the entire embedded
distance graph equals the same deterministic multiple of $D_h$ already
identified by the local open-port comparisons, including at the excluded points.
statements.section_title: Balanced segments and continuity at all endpoints

statements.title: Exclusion of uncharged passage configurations
statements.label: end:passage-exclusion
statements.section_title: Balanced segments and continuity at all endpoints

statements.title: Equality gain
statements.label: addr:equality-smoothing
statements.text:
After extracting equality constraints, the remaining bin weights
can be bounded by $\prod_\ell B_\ell^{-\beta}$, with a
factor $\exp(O(n_0))$.  The equality profit is at least
\begin{equation}
                           g\sum_j(v_j-c_j-l_j),
\end{equation}
with a nonnegative rank contribution used at levels where a summand
is negative.
statements.section_title: Address counting and completion of the joint limit

statements.title: Completion of the bad-grid estimate
statements.label: addr:bad-grid-proof
statements.text:
The bad-grid bound in Proposition~\ref{end:bad-grid} holds, with
every prescribed failure exponent and in all the parameter ranges
specified there.
statements.section_title: Address counting and completion of the joint limit

statements.title: Joint subsequential comparison
statements.label: addr:subsequential-joint
statements.text:
Put $b_n=\mathcal B(B_n)$.  From every sequence of positive
integers tending to infinity one can extract a further sequence
on which, in the prescribed flag uniformization,
\[
 \bigl((\phi_n)_*m_n,K_n(b_n^{-1}),\Gamma_n\bigr)
\]
converges jointly to
\[
 \left(
   \mu_h^{\rm crit},
   \{(z,w,cD_h(z,w)):z,w\in\widehatC\},
   \Gamma
 \right),
\]
where $0<c<\infty$ is deterministic.  The law of the marked
surface is the law constructed in Theorem~\ref{thm:continuum},
and $\Gamma$ is the independent nested $\CLE_4$ of
Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.  The maximal spherical flag mesh tends
to zero jointly on these extractions.
statements.section_title: Address counting and completion of the joint limit

title: The critical correlation exponent of the planar XY model
abstract: For the ordinary nearest-neighbor XY model on the square lattice, we prove the Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless prediction that the critical spin-correlation exponent is 1/4. More precisely, at the mass-defined critical inverse temperature, the infinite-volume correlation is \(n^{-1/4+o(1)}\). The infinite-volume limit through free square boxes is taken before the separation limit.

tex.abstract:
For the ordinary nearest-neighbor XY model on the square lattice,
we prove the Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless prediction that the
critical spin-correlation exponent is \(1/4\). More precisely, at
the mass-defined critical inverse temperature, the infinite-volume
correlation is \(n^{-1/4+o(1)}\). The infinite-volume limit through
free square boxes is taken before the separation limit.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For the model \eqref{eq:xy-law} and the threshold
\eqref{eq:critical-definition},
\[
 \lim_{\substack{n\to\infty\\n\in\N,\ n\ge2}}
       \frac{\log C_{b_c}(n)}{\log n}=-\frac14.
\]
Equivalently, for every \(\eps>0\) there is \(n_0<\infty\) such that
\[
 n^{-1/4-\eps}\le C_{b_c}(n)\le n^{-1/4+\eps}
 \qquad(n\ge n_0).
\]

statements.title: Uniform phase and forbidden range
statements.label: thm:coefficient-gap
statements.text:
For every \(b>0\),
\[
 a(b)=0\quad\hbox{or}\quad a(b)\ge8\pi.
\]
If \(a(b)>0\), the fractional mean
\(\ip{h}{u_m}\bmod2\pi\) converges to uniform measure on the circle,
independently of any fixed finite collection of the Gaussian
observations of Theorem~\ref{thm:free-limits}.
More generally, for a fixed nonzero integer \(l\) and any zero-total
profiles \(t_m\) of bounded reference cost,
\begin{equation}
 w_m(lu_m+t_m)\longrightarrow0.
 
\end{equation}

statements.title: Mixed height limits
statements.label: thm:mixed-limits
statements.text:
For every fixed geometry above and every \(a(b)>0\), the massless
height law with primary hard pins has Gaussian Laplace and moment
limits for fixed bounded, piecewise continuous density smears.
On a component meeting a pin, the covariance is the inverse of
\[
                   a^{-1}\mathcal E_U
                   \quad\hbox{on }\mathcal H_{U,p}.
\]
On an unpinned component this assertion concerns mean-free smears.
Its fractional mean modulo \(2\pi\) is asymptotically uniform and
independent of the mean-free Gaussian field.

Adding a fixed finite-rank nonnegative quadratic penalty in box
averages gives the corresponding Gaussian law. If the penalty
controls every unpinned component constant, lattice translations
are summed and the limiting constants are integrated; the result
is an ordinary, unprojected Gaussian law. The assertions include
energy-approximable shifts and hold along every admissible primary
mesh sequence.

statements.title: Separated pin interaction and conditional laws
statements.label: thm:pin-interaction
statements.text:
Under the centered high law, \(D_n(H,p)\ge0\) converges to the
Gaussian pin interaction for precision
\[
                 a^{-1}\mathcal E_U(v)+\norm{Bv}^2.
\]
For every fixed finite list of density or box smears \(X\), the
conditional Laplace transforms and conditional weak laws given
\(h_p\) have the Gaussian finite-observation approximations just
defined. Moreover,
\[
 0<r_{H,n}\le1,\qquad
 \E_{\mu_n}r_{H,n}=e^{-D_n(H,p)},
\]
and \(r_{H,n}\) has the corresponding Gaussian approximation,
whose limit is strictly positive almost surely.
The convergence assertions persist when data are sampled under
a fixed finite linear exponential tilt, with \(D_n\) and
\(r_{H,n}\) retaining their centered definitions and the limiting
law sampled under the corresponding Gaussian tilt.
The displayed expectation identity concerns \(\mu_n\), not its
tilts. Conditional transforms for a tilted baseline also
converge, by taking ratios of the centered conditional transforms.

statements.title: Vanishing reach
statements.label: prop:pins-reach
statements.text:
Under the band law, the probability that an exploration
starting in a fixed positive-area region on one side of a separating
positive-width band reaches a fixed closed region on the
other side tends to zero in \eqref{eq:pins-limit-order}.
The assertion includes exploration from a filled exterior
or from a primary hard-pin region before imposing its pin.

statements.label: prop:spin-lower
statements.text:
For the prescribed free-box correlation,
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log C_b(n)}{\log n}
       \ge -\frac{2\pi}{a}.
\]
In particular, \(m(b)=0\).

statements.title: Many-scale sector comparison
statements.label: prop:sector-comparison
statements.text:
For the preceding geometry there are numbers \(\eta_R\to0\) such that,
for each sufficiently large fixed \(R\), one can choose a fixed
\(m_*\) for which
\begin{equation}
 \left|\log\frac{Z^s}{Z^0}
       -\log\frac{Z_{\mathrm g}^s}{Z_{\mathrm g}^0}\right|
       \le C_M(1+\log n)\eta_R.
\end{equation}
For these fixed choices, heights on the two inner rims, in the
bounded cut coordinates just specified, are uniformly tight in
\(n\) and in the outer volume. This is absolute tightness, without
subtracting an additive constant.

statements.label: prop:openness
statements.text:
If \(a(b)>8\pi\), there is an open interval \(I\) containing \(b\),
contained in \((0,\infty)\), such that \(a(\widetilde b)>0\) for
every \(\widetilde b\in I\).

title: The critical dimension for one-phase Bernoulli minimizers
abstract: We prove that seven is the critical dimension for the one-phase Bernoulli problem: every nonzero one-homogeneous global minimizer in dimensions at most six is flat, while a nonflat one-homogeneous global minimizer exists in dimension seven. It follows that the interior free boundary of a local minimizer is smooth in dimensions at most six. In dimension n ≥ 7, its singular set has Hausdorff dimension at most \(n-7\), and this bound is sharp. In dimension seven, the singular set is locally finite.

tex.abstract:
We prove that seven is the critical dimension for the one-phase Bernoulli
problem: every nonzero one-homogeneous global minimizer in dimensions at most
six is flat, while a nonflat one-homogeneous global minimizer exists in
dimension seven. It follows that the interior free boundary of a local
minimizer is smooth in dimensions at most six. In dimension $n\ge7$, its
singular set has Hausdorff dimension at most $n-7$, and this bound is sharp.
In dimension seven, the singular set is locally finite.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Every nonzero one-homogeneous global minimizer of \eqref{eq:energy}
in \(\R^d\), \(1\leq d\leq6\), is flat. There is a nonflat
one-homogeneous global minimizer in \(\R^7\). Consequently,
\[
  d_*=7.
\]

statements.title: Sharp singular-set bound
statements.label: cor:singular-set
statements.text:
Let $n\ge2$, let $D\subset\R^n$ be open, and let $u\in H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$ be a nonnegative local
minimizer of the one-phase Bernoulli energy in $D$.
Its interior free boundary is smooth outside $\operatorname{Sing}(u)$.
This set is empty when $n\le6$, is locally finite when $n=7$, and satisfies
\[
 \dim_{\mathrm H}\operatorname{Sing}(u)\le n-7\qquad(n\ge7).
\]
For every $n\ge7$, a global minimizer attains this dimension bound.

statements.title: Regularity and blowups of minimizers
statements.label: red:regularity
statements.text:
Let $d\geq2$ and let $u\geq0$ be a local minimizer of the one-phase energy
with volume coefficient $1$ in an open set $D\subset\R^d$.
\begin{enumerate}
\renewcommand{\labelenumi}{\textup{(\roman{enumi})}}
\item There is a locally Lipschitz representative of $u$, and it is harmonic
in $\{u>0\}$.
\item If $x_0\in D\cap\partial\{u>0\}$, every sequence $r_j\downarrow0$
has a subsequence for which
\begin{equation}
 u_{x_0,r_j}(y):=\frac{u(x_0+r_jy)}{r_j}\longrightarrow U(y)
\end{equation}
locally uniformly in $\R^d$.  The limit is a nonzero, nonnegative,
one-homogeneous global minimizer.  Along a further subsequence the convergence
is strong in $H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$, and the positivity indicators converge in
$L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$.
\item If one such limit equals $(y\cdot e)_+$ with $|e|=1$, then near
$x_0$ the free boundary is a smooth hypersurface and $\{u>0\}$ is exactly
one of its sides.  The function $u$ is smooth up to that hypersurface from
the positive side, and
\begin{equation}
 u=0,\qquad \nabla u=N_E
 \quad\hbox{on the free boundary},
\end{equation}
where $N_E$ is the Euclidean unit normal pointing into $\{u>0\}$.
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: Reduction to a smooth link and its suspension

statements.title: Smooth original link
statements.label: red:original-link
statements.text:
Every point of $\partial\{u>0\}\setminus\{0\}$ is regular.  Put
$m_o=d-1$ and $g_o=u|_{S^{m_o}}$.  The set $\{g_o>0\}$ is nonempty and
proper, has finitely many connected components, and their closures are
pairwise disjoint compact smooth manifolds with boundary.  On each such
component $\Omega_o$, the restriction of $g_o$ is smooth up to the boundary
from within $\Omega_o$ and satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \Delta_{S^{m_o}}g_o=-m_o g_o\quad\hbox{in }\Omega_o,
 \qquad g_o=0,\quad \nabla_{S^{m_o}}g_o=N_o
       \quad\hbox{on }\partial\Omega_o,
\end{equation}
where $N_o$ is the inward spherical unit normal.  In particular,
$\partial\Omega_o\ne\varnothing$.
statements.section_title: Reduction to a smooth link and its suspension

statements.title: Suspension preserves global minimality
statements.label: red:suspension
statements.text:
If $u\geq0$ is a global minimizer in $\R^k$, then
$\widetilde u(x,s)=u(x)$ is a global minimizer in $\R^{k+1}$.
If $u$ is the cone in \eqref{red:first-dimension} with $d=5$, the singular
free-boundary set of $\widetilde u$ is exactly $\{0\}\times\R$.
For the component chosen in Lemma~\ref{red:nonflat-component}, the
corresponding positive component on $S^5$ is
\begin{equation}
 \widetilde\Omega
 =\bigl\{\Phi(t,y):=(\sin t\,y,\cos t):
              0<t<\pi,\ y\in\Omega_o\bigr\},
 \qquad
 \widetilde g(\Phi(t,y))=\sin t\,g_o(y).
\end{equation}
Its boundary consists of the smooth side
$\Phi((0,\pi)\times\partial\Omega_o)$ and the two singular tips
$p_+=(0,1)$ and $p_-=(0,-1)$.

statements.title: Interior identities
statements.label: geo:interior-identities
statements.text:
The tensor $T$ is symmetric and trace-free, and $B$ is fully symmetric
and trace-free in every pair of slots. In particular $\diver T=0$.
The following identities hold:
\begin{align}
 \nabla_lB_{ijk}-\nabla_iB_{ljk}
 &=\delta_{lj}T_{ik}+\delta_{lk}T_{ij}
   -\delta_{ij}T_{lk}-\delta_{ik}T_{lj},
 \\
 \Delta T&=mT,
 &\Delta w^2&=2m w^2+2|B|^2,
 \\
 \nabla_l p_i&=T_{li}-g\delta_{li},
 &\nabla_l g&=p_l,
 \\
 \nabla s^2&=2Tp,
 &\Delta s^2&=2w^2.
 
\end{align}
On the open set $\{w>0\}$ one also has
\begin{equation}
 \nabla_l w=w^{-1}T_{jk}B_{ljk},\qquad |\nabla w|\le |B|.
\end{equation}
The inequality
$|\nabla(w^2)|^2\le4w^2|B|^2$ holds everywhere, including at $w=0$.
statements.section_title: Spherical geometry and the stability inequality

statements.title: Boundary jets
statements.label: geo:boundary-jets
statements.text:
Suppose $g=0$, $p=N$, and $T(N,N)=-H<0$ on a smooth boundary portion,
where $N$ is inward. Let Greek indices be tangent to this boundary and
put
\[
 \mathfrak h_{\alpha\beta}
 =\langle\nabla_{\alpha}N,e_\beta\rangle.
\]
Then $T_{N\alpha}=0$, $T_{\alpha\beta}=\mathfrak h_{\alpha\beta}$,
and $H=\tr\mathfrak h$; in particular $H$ is a sum of principal
curvatures with the specified convention, without division by $m-1$.
If $\nabla^{\partial}$ is the boundary connection, all components of
$B$ are described, up to permutation of slots, by
\begin{align}
 B_{\alpha\beta\gamma}
   &=(\nabla^{\partial}_{\alpha}\mathfrak h)_{\beta\gamma},
 &B_{NN\alpha}&=-\partial_\alpha H,
 \\
 B_{N\alpha\beta}
   &=T_{NN}T_{\alpha\beta}-(T^2)_{\alpha\beta},
 &B_{NNN}&=w^2.
 
\end{align}
The components with an odd number of normal slots are thus determined
by the pointwise tensor $T$; the other components involve tangential
derivatives of curvature. The tensor $V$ below encodes this odd-normal
part after normalization.
Here $w>0$. Define the normalized tensors and eigenvalue
\[
 A=T/w,\qquad \lambda=T_{NN}/w=-H/w,
 \qquad S_0=\lambda A-A^2,
\]
and the symmetric tensor
\begin{equation}
 V_{ijk}=p_i(S_0)_{jk}+p_j(S_0)_{ki}+p_k(S_0)_{ij}
           +p_ip_jp_k.
\end{equation}
Then $|p|=1$, $Ap=\lambda p$, $\lambda<0$, $S_0p=0$,
$\tr S_0=-1$, and $V$ is trace-free. The tensors $B/w^2$ and $V$
agree in every component with an odd number of normal slots. Moreover,
\begin{equation}
 V_{Njk}=(S_0+p\otimes p)_{jk},\qquad
 \partial_N w=w^2\bigl(2\lambda-\tr A^3\bigr).
\end{equation}

statements.title: Euclidean stability on a component
statements.label: geo:euclidean-stability
statements.text:
Let $D$ be the selected positivity component of a global minimizing
cone in $\R^{m+1}$. Let $\phi$ be any real smooth function up to the
regular boundary of $D$, with compact support in that regular closure
away from the vertex and from any other singular points. Then
\begin{equation}
 \int_D |\nabla\phi|^2\,dx
 \ge \int_{\partial D}H_E\phi^2\,d\sigma_E,
 \qquad H_E=-D^2u(N_E,N_E),
\end{equation}
where $N_E$ is the inward Euclidean unit normal. No restriction is
imposed on the boundary trace or normal derivative of $\phi$.
statements.section_title: Spherical geometry and the stability inequality

statements.title: Spherical stability
statements.label: geo:spherical-stability
statements.text:
For every real function $v$ smooth up to the regular boundary of the
working component $\Omega\subset S^5$, with compact support in its
closure away from the tips if present,
\begin{equation}
 \int_{\partial\Omega}H v^2\,d\sigma
 \le \int_\Omega\bigl(|\nabla v|^2+4v^2\bigr)\,dV.
\end{equation}
The trace of $v$ on the regular boundary is arbitrary.

statements.title: Universal inequalities
statements.label: cert:universal
statements.text:
There are rational tensor polynomials $f,U_{jk},K_{lijk},M_l,P_l$ in
$A,p,g,\delta$, with the following properties. They are equivariant under
orthogonal changes of coordinates, with $f$ invariant. Their coefficients
are specified by Table~I in Appendix~\ref{app:tables}, using the decoding in
Section~\ref{cert:decode}. Put
\[
 C_{lijk}=K_{lijk}-K_{iljk},\qquad
 G_{lijk}=\delta_{li}U_{jk}+C_{lijk}.
\]
For every choice of the data above with $\chi\ge0$,
\begin{align}
 \mathcal I:={}&z^2\left[5U_{jk}A_{jk}
       +C_{lijk}(\delta_{lj}A_{ik}+\delta_{lk}A_{ij})-4f\right]\notag\\
 &+\left[D_lG_{lijk}+(2a-1)q_lG_{lijk}\right]X_{ijk}\notag\\
 &+w\left[D_lM_l+(2a+1)q_lM_l\right]
       +z\left[D_lP_l+2aq_lP_l\right]\notag\\
 &+f|\ell|^2-(D_lf+2aq_lf)\ell_l
 \ \ge\ \epsilon_*(z^2+|\ell|^2).
\end{align}
In particular, $f\ge\epsilon_*$ whenever $g^2+|p|^2\le1$.

For every symmetric trace-free unit matrix $A$ and vector $p$ satisfying
\[
 g=0,\qquad |p|=1,\qquad Ap=\lambda p,\qquad\lambda<0,
\]
define
\[
 S_0=\lambda A-A^2,\qquad
 V_{ijk}=p_i(S_0)_{jk}+p_j(S_0)_{ki}+p_k(S_0)_{ij}+p_ip_jp_k.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal S:=-\lambda f+U_{jk}(S_0+p\otimes p)_{jk}
                 +C_{lijk}p_lV_{ijk}+p_lM_l
 \ \ge\ \delta_*.
\end{equation}
Moreover, $U$ and $K$ are even in $p$, and $P=0$ when $g=0$.

statements.text:
On the regular side boundary,
\begin{equation}
 N\cdot Z+Hh^2=w^{2a+1}\mathcal S
   \geq\delta_*w^{2a+1}>0,
 \qquad
 \delta_* =\frac{6984137359}{31250000000},
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal S$ is the boundary polynomial in
\eqref{cert:boundary}.  In particular $N\cdot Z+Hh^2\geq0$.
