title: The higher-dimensional Erdős distinct-distances conjecture
abstract: For every fixed integer d ≥ 3, we prove that every set of n ≥ 2 distinct points in ℝd determines at least \(c_d n^{2/d}\) distinct distances, where \(c_d\gt 0\) depends only on d. This resolves the higher-dimensional Erdős distinct-distances conjecture positively.

tex.abstract:
For every fixed integer $d\ge3$, we prove that every set of $n\ge2$ distinct
points in $\mathbb R^d$ determines at least $c_d n^{2/d}$ distinct
distances, where $c_d>0$ depends only on $d$. This resolves the
higher-dimensional Erd\H{o}s distinct-distances conjecture positively.
sections: The reduction to sparse cones and concentration
Very rich rigid motions in three dimensions

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every integer \(d\ge3\), there is a constant \(c_d>0\) such that
every finite set \(P\subset\mathbb R^d\) of \(n\ge2\) distinct points
satisfies
\[
 |\Delta(P)|\ge c_d n^{2/d}.
\]

statements.label: red:directions
statements.section_title: The reduction to sparse cones and concentration

statements.title: Independent evaluations in every star
statements.label: red:independent-stars
statements.text:
A further symmetric selection retains at least \(c'N^2\) pairs and
has the following property: the direction-evaluation vectors of the
partners in each star are linearly independent for homogeneous
polynomials of degree \(D=\lfloor A\rfloor\).
In particular each selected star admits homogeneous separators of
degree \(D\).
statements.section_title: The reduction to sparse cones and concentration

statements.label: red:main-contradiction
statements.text:
The graph \(\mathcal H\) cannot satisfy both bounds in
Lemmas~\ref{red:global-concentration} and
\ref{red:local-concentration}.
statements.section_title: The reduction to sparse cones and concentration

statements.title: Mixed-dimensional envelopes
statements.label: poly:envelope
statements.text:
Let $Z$ be a locus of equations of degree at most $L\ge1$, and let
$a_k$ be the total degree of any chosen subfamily of its
$k$-dimensional irreducible components.  For their union $V$,
\[
 H_V(L)\ge c_n\sum_{k=0}^n a_kL^k.
\]
For an arbitrary reduced union with dimension-by-dimension degrees
$a_k$, without a hypothesis on its equations,
\[
 H_V(D)\le\sum_{k=0}^n a_k\binom{D+k}{k}.
\]
In particular these statements apply to the components of
$\Env_L(T)$.

statements.title: A bounded-degree test for high multiplicity
statements.label: poly:high-multiplicity
statements.text:
Let $X\subsetneq\C^n$ be irreducible of degree $a$, and let
$S\subset X$ be finite with $\mult_pX>a/2$ for every $p\in S$.
For any specified $x_*\notin X$, there is a polynomial of degree
at most $2(n+1)$ which vanishes on $S$ and is nonzero at $x_*$.
In particular the specified high-multiplicity centers lie in a
proper hypersurface of degree bounded in terms of the ambient
dimension alone.

statements.title: A tangent hyperplane controls the projection loss
statements.label: poly:tangent-projection
statements.text:
Let an irreducible affine curve $C$ lie in a variety $X$ smooth at
$p\in C$.  Suppose $C$ has a point $z$ for which the direction
$z-p$ is not in $T_pX$.  Then
\[
 \mult_pC\le\tfrac12\deg C.
\]
Consequently, if projection of $C$ from $p$ is nonconstant, its
image degree times its generic map degree is at least
$\tfrac12\deg C$.

statements.title: Terminal-curve deletion
statements.label: geo:terminal
statements.text:
Assign sample points to finitely many irreducible physical curves
$Y_i$, each containing its assigned points. Pool repetitions of a
curve, and require every line member to be real. Then the number of
ordered pairs $(p,q)$, $p\ne q$, for which $q$ is assigned to $Y_i$
and
\[
 \overline{\pi_pY_i}\subseteq C_p
\]
is $o(N^2)$. The estimate is uniform in the assignment and the curves.

statements.title: Multiscale partition
statements.label: prof:partition
statements.text:
There are $s_*\to\infty$ and partitions of all but $o(N)$ sample points
into a core and non-core pieces with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The core is simultaneously isolated by equations of a degree $L$
such that $EL^2=o(N)$.
\item Each non-core piece has a dyadic width
$s=2^{-a}\log B\ge s_*$ and size $n=N\exp(-o(s))$.  Its path has $d$
proper hypersurface cuts.  Along any sequence of pieces, after passing
to a subsequence, their normalized cut times converge to
\[
 -1\le b_1\le\cdots\le b_d\le1,\qquad
 \max_i|b_i|\ge\tfrac12.
\]
The degree of cut $i$ is at most
$D_i\exp(o(s))$, where $D_i=B\exp(b_i s)$.
\item Let $b$ lie strictly between consecutive distinct limiting cut
times, and let $j=\#\{i:b_i<b\}$ and $l=d-j$.  At each point of the
piece the current system is pure of local dimension $l$.  Uniformly
over polynomials of degree $O(T_s(b))$, the number of points where such
a polynomial vanishes but contains none of the local carriers is
$o(n)$.  The same assertion holds before the first cut whenever
$T_s(b)\ge1$ and $b<b_1$, and it is automatic after the last cut.
\end{enumerate}
The assertions about error terms and negligible proportions hold along
every sequence of pieces.  In particular, a violating choice of one
piece at each index is not permitted.

statements.title: Budgets and balanced profiles
statements.label: prof:budget

statements.title: Regularity and individual cuts
statements.label: prof:regularity
statements.text:
Inside an open plateau, individual proper cuts of degree $O(T_s(b))$
on the different carriers collectively capture only $o(n)$ points.
At a slightly later interior testing time there are common equations
for the entire carrier family whose Jacobian has full codimension
rank at all but $o(n)$ points.  At those surviving points the carrier
is unique and smooth, and its tangent space is testable by equations
and minors of the same interior degree scale.

The assertions also hold for the union of two such families, and
for unions from $\exp(o(s))$ pieces with the same limiting profile
and width, provided each piece retains its own assigned masses.
Common equations vanish on the whole union.  In particular, two
different members of that union cannot meet at a surviving point
where the common Jacobian has full rank.
Flat carriers which are not defined over $\R$ may be discarded
with negligible mass.

statements.title: Selection of profile pairs
statements.label: prof:pair-selection
statements.text:
For every $p\in P$, let $C_p$ be a finite family of irreducible
projective curves in $\PP^{d-1}$, each spanning a projective subspace
of dimension at most two, with total degree at most $E=\delta N/A$.
Suppose that $1-o(1)$ of
the unordered pairs $\{p,q\}$ satisfy $\pi_p(q)\in C_p$ or
$\pi_q(p)\in C_q$.  After the global terminal deletion described
below, one of the following configurations occurs.
\begin{enumerate}
\item A core of positive relative size is covered.
\item Two sequences of non-core pieces have a common dyadic width
$s$, the same limiting profile, and an ordered product covered in
one orientation with positive relative density.
\item Two sequences of non-core pieces have widths with ratio
tending to infinity, both $o(\log B)$, the same limiting profile,
and such a positively covered ordered product.
\end{enumerate}
In the common outermost window $s=\log B$, the two factors may
instead be the same pool of pieces in a shrinking profile bin.
That pool has size $n\ge N\sqrt\delta$, is the union of
$\exp(o(s))$ pieces, and retains all the preceding degree, mass,
regularity, and product-testing conclusions to exponential
accuracy.  All selected incidences may be required to lie on
physical lines containing at most $B^{o(1)}$ sample points.

The global terminal deletion means the following.  Whenever a
target point was assigned to its carrier curve after the
$(d-1)$st cut, its projection from the center is not a curve
contained in the center's directional family.

statements.title: Sparse cones
statements.label: sc:theorem
statements.text:
Along a sequence with $M=o(A)$, there cannot be families $C_p$,
one for each $p\in P$, of irreducible projective curves, each
spanning projective dimension at most two, such that
\[
 \deg C_p\le E=\delta N/A,\qquad \delta\to0,
\]
and $1-o(1)$ of the unordered pairs $\{p,q\}$ satisfy
$\pi_p(q)\in C_p$ or $\pi_q(p)\in C_q$.

statements.title: Very rich motions
statements.label: mot:rich
statements.text:
There are absolute constants \(C_{\mathrm{rich}},K_{\mathrm{rich}}>0\)
with the following property.  Let \(P\subset\mathbb R^3\) consist of
\(N\ge2\) distinct points, and set
\[
 A=N^{2/3},\qquad M=1+|\Delta(P)|.
\]
If \(M\le A\), then the motions satisfying
\(k_g\ge C_{\mathrm{rich}}A\) form a finite set and
\begin{equation}

 \sum_{g:\,k_g\ge C_{\mathrm{rich}}A} k_g^2
 \le K_{\mathrm{rich}}\frac{N^4}{A}.
\end{equation}
The same estimate holds with \(k_g=|gP\cap Q|\) for any rigidly
congruent copy \(Q\) of \(P\).
statements.section_title: Very rich rigid motions in three dimensions

statements.title: Uniform concentration
statements.label: conc:theorem
conc:degree
statements.text:
Let \(V\subsetneq S\) be irreducible of dimension \(k=s_0+h\), where
\(1\le h<r\), and let \(\Gamma\) be a ruling incidence provided by
Lemma~\ref{conc:rulings}.  Write \(j\in\{0,1\}\) for the dimension
of its fibers over the working open subset \(\Omega\subset V\).
Let \(\Lambda\) be the projective closure of its parameter image
\[
 (z,v)\longmapsto[v:zv]
 \quad\hbox{in}\quad
 \mathcal Q=\{[v:y]\in\mathbf{P}(E\oplus E^*):y(v)=0\}.
\]
Then
\[
 \dim\Lambda=h+j,
 \qquad \deg\Lambda\le C_e\deg V.
\]
If \(j=1\), then \(h=r-1\) and \(\Lambda\) is a linear
\(\mathbf{P}^r\subset\mathcal Q\), hence a maximal isotropic
projective subspace.

statements.title: Szemer\'edi--Trotter
statements.label: ci:st
statements.text:
For finite sets $Q$ of $n$ points and $\mathcal L$ of $L$ distinct real
lines in the plane,
\[
 I(Q,\mathcal L)\le C\bigl(n^{2/3}L^{2/3}+n+L\bigr).
\]
Consequently the number of points incident to at least $k\ge2$ lines is
at most $C(L^2/k^3+L/k)$, and the number of lines containing at least
$k\ge2$ points of an $n$-point set is at most
$C(n^2/k^3+n/k)$.
The same assertions apply to finite point--line configurations in
$\mathbb R^s$ and in real projective space.

statements.title: Guth--Katz, higher richness
statements.label: ci:rich-lines
statements.text:
Let $\mathcal L$ be $L$ distinct lines in $\mathbb R^3$, with at most
$B_0$ in any affine plane.  For every integer $k\ge3$, the number
$R_k$ of points lying on at least $k$ lines satisfies
\[
 R_k\le C\left(\frac{L^{3/2}}{k^2}
             +\frac{LB_0}{k^3}+\frac Lk\right).
\]
There is no assumption about lines on quadrics in this theorem.

statements.title: Planar motions with many matches
statements.label: ci:planar-motions
statements.text:
Let $U,V\subset\mathbb R^2$ have respective cardinalities $u,v$.
For $3\le k\le\min(u,v)$, at most $C(uv)^{3/2}/k^2$ Euclidean
isometries $g$ have $|g(U)\cap V|\ge k$.

statements.title: Two-rich points
statements.label: ci:two-rich
statements.text:
For $m$ distinct real affine lines, with at most $s\ge1$ in any
plane or regulus, the number $P_2$ of points lying on at least two
lines satisfies
\[
 P_2\le K\bigl(m^{3/2}+ms\bigr)
\]
for an absolute constant $K$.

statements.title: Planar distinct distances
statements.label: ci:planar-distances
statements.text:
Every finite set $Q\subset\mathbb R^2$ of $n\ge2$ points determines
at least $c n/\log(2n)$ distinct positive distances.

statements.title: Planar occupancy
statements.label: ci:planar-occupancy
statements.text:
If a finite set in Euclidean space determines at most $M\ge1$ positive
distances, then any affine two-plane contains at most
$CM\log(2M)$ of its points.  In particular, along a sequence with
$B\longrightarrow\infty$ and $M=o(B^2)$, every two-plane has at
most $B^{2+o(1)}$ points, uniformly in the plane.

title: The irrationality exponent of pi is 2
abstract: We prove the conjecture that the irrationality exponent of π is 2. As a consequence, the classical Flint–Hills series \(\sum_{n\ge1}1/(n^3\sin^2 n)\) converges, with angles in radians.

tex.abstract:
We prove the conjecture that the irrationality exponent of \(\pi\) is \(2\).
As a consequence, the classical Flint--Hills series
\(\sum_{n\ge1}1/(n^3\sin^2 n)\) converges, with angles in radians.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
The irrationality exponent of \(\pi\) is \(2\). More precisely, for every
real \(\nu>2\), there is an integer \(Q(\nu)\) such that
\[
\left|\pi-\frac pq\right|\ge q^{-\nu}
\qquad(p\in\ZZ,\ q\in\ZZ,\ q\ge Q(\nu)).
\]

statements.title: Separated-weight interpolation
statements.label: geom:interpolation
statements.text:
Fix integers $m,K\ge1$ and positive rational numbers $w_0,v_0,\theta$ such
that $0<\theta<1$ and
\begin{equation}

 K\theta^m<1,
 \qquad K\frac{w_0}{v_0}\theta^m<1.
\end{equation}
There are successive lower thresholds for positive rational numbers
$w_1,\ldots,w_m$, depending only on these fixed data and the previously
chosen weights, with the following property. Put
\[
 W=(w_0,w_1,\ldots,w_m),\qquad
 V=(v_0,w_1/\theta,\ldots,w_m/\theta).
\]
For any points
\[
 a_j=(1,c_{j1},\ldots,c_{jm})\in\CC^{m+1},\qquad 0\le j<K,
\]
whose coordinates $c_{0i},\ldots,c_{K-1,i}$ are pairwise distinct for each
$i$, the map
\begin{equation}

 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal P_W(H)&\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{j=0}^{K-1}\mathcal J_V(H),\\
 P&\longmapsto
 \left(P\bigl(1+t,(c_{ji}+u_i+\log(1+t))_{i=1}^m\bigr)\right)_{j=0}^{K-1}.
 \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
is surjective for all sufficiently large, sufficiently divisible integers $H$.
The divisibility requirement can be chosen using only the weights. The
remaining lower threshold for $H$ may depend on the points.

\begin{equation}
 g=\nu\bigl(A(1-\eta)-\theta\bigr)-(1-\theta),
 \qquad
 L=\frac{\eta^2K\theta^m}{(m+1)v_0A^m}.
 
\end{equation}
The approximations \eqref{det:approximations} and the interpolation
hypotheses cannot hold simultaneously if
\begin{equation}
 g>0,\qquad
 E_{\rm ar}+E_{\rm an}<g,
 \qquad
 cL>1+E_{\rm ar}+E_{\rm an}.
 
\end{equation}

title: The joint Dickman law for consecutive integers
abstract: Let \(P^+(n)\) denote the largest prime factor of n. We prove that \(\log P^+(n)/\log n\) and \(\log P^+(n+1)/\log n\) are asymptotically independent in ordinary natural density, with Dickman marginals. This resolves the Erdős–Pomerance joint Dickman conjecture positively and implies that the ordering \(P^+(n)\lt P^+(n+1)\) has natural density 1/2.

tex.abstract:
Let $P^+(n)$ denote the largest prime factor of $n$. We prove that
$\log P^+(n)/\log n$ and $\log P^+(n+1)/\log n$ are asymptotically
independent in ordinary natural density, with Dickman marginals. This resolves the Erd\H{o}s--Pomerance
joint Dickman conjecture positively and implies that the ordering
$P^+(n)<P^+(n+1)$ has natural density $1/2$.

statements.title: Joint Dickman law
statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every fixed $a,b\in(0,1)$,
\[
 \lim_{X\to\infty}\frac1X
 \#\{2\leq n\leq X:\Pplus(n)\leq n^a,
                         \ \Pplus(n+1)\leq n^b\}
 =\rho(1/a)\rho(1/b).
\]
Here the limit is taken over all real $X$, with ordinary, unweighted
counting.

statements.label: cor:comparison
statements.text:
One has
\[
 \lim_{X\to\infty}\frac1X
 \#\{2\leq n\leq X:\Pplus(n)<\Pplus(n+1)\}=\frac12.
\]
The reverse ordering has the same natural density.

statements.title: Integrated row moments
statements.label: prop:moments:rows
statements.text:
For a sufficiently fine fixed regularity grid and then a sufficiently
small fixed tolerance, the independent-site latent kernel satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{k\ne i}\E\,\mathcal L_{ik}^{2}\ll B^{-.21}
 \qquad (1\le i\le M).
 
\end{equation}
Moreover, its normalized total mass has bounded second moment:
\[
 \E\left(\frac1M\sum_{i,k}\mathcal L_{ik}\right)^2\ll1.
\]
For every set $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,M\}$, the same estimates hold after
replacing $\mathcal L_{ik}$ by
$\ind_{\{i,k\in I\}}\mathcal L_{ik}$; the normalization remains $M$.

statements.title: Coarse site features
statements.label: cor:channels-features
statements.text:
For the chosen coarse partition, define
\[
 V_l(S)=\frac1{|I_l|}
          \Prob_{\rm split}(x_b\in I_l\mid S).
\]
Then \(0\le V_l\le |I_l|^{-1}\), and for every \(g\in L^2(\Omega_B)\)
the coarse value of \(P_{m_1}u_g\) on \(I_l\) is exactly
\[
 \E[g(S)V_l(S)].
\]
In particular the bounds \eqref{eq:31}--\eqref{eq:32} and this identity
hold uniformly when \(g\) varies with a position, with \(B\), or with
an external parameter.

statements.title: Integral comparison
statements.label: prop:kernel-comparison
statements.text:
For the matrix \(\mathcal M\) in \eqref{eq:43}, put
\(\mathcal E_{ik}=\mathcal L_{ik}-\mathcal M_{ik}\), with all three
matrices zero on nonpairs.  Given \(\epsilon_1>0\), choose the coarse
partition as in \eqref{eq:32}.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{\substack{g_i,h_k:\Omega_B\to[-1,1]\\
                  g_i,h_k\ \text{real measurable}}}
 \frac1M\left|
  \sum_{i,k}\E_{S_i,S_k}
      [\mathcal E_{ik}(S_i,S_k;s)g_i(S_i)h_k(S_k)]\right|
 \le C e^{-c_3C_*}+C_\eta\epsilon_1+o(1).
\end{equation}
The \(o(1)\) is uniform in \(s\) and in all the indicated tests.
The coefficient of \(e^{-c_3C_*}\) is independent of \(\eta\),
\(C_6\), and \(C_*\).  In addition, for every realization of the
site types,
\begin{equation}
 \sup_i\sum_k|\mathcal M_{ik}|\ll_{\eta,m_1}1,
 \qquad
 \sup_i\sum_k|\mathcal M_{ik}|^2\ll_{\eta,m_1}T^{-1}.
\end{equation}

title: The joint scaling limit of critical Ashkin-Teller currents
abstract: For each fixed point on the critical Ashkin–Teller line, including the four-state Potts endpoint, we prove the conjectured joint scaling limit of the height and both current-cluster collections in every bounded Jordan domain, for every admissible polygonal approximation. The height converges to a Gaussian free field with the predicted coupling constant, and the clusters converge to canonical recursive two-valued local sets of that same field. The joint limit includes all nesting depths and the distinguished wired boundary cluster.
version_note: This version corrects the transmission and boundary-collar arguments, replaces excursion convergence with a signed-loop-soup/GMC argument tied to the same limiting field, and updates the companion-paper citation; see the [previous version](../The-joint-scaling-limit-of-critical-Ashkin-Teller-currents-September-25-2026/main.pdf).

tex.abstract:
For each fixed point on the critical Ashkin--Teller line, including the
four-state Potts endpoint, we prove the conjectured joint scaling limit
of the height and both current-cluster collections in every bounded
Jordan domain, for every admissible polygonal approximation. The height
converges to a Gaussian free field with the predicted coupling constant,
and the clusters converge to canonical recursive two-valued local sets
of that same field. The joint limit includes all nesting depths and the
distinguished wired boundary cluster.
sections: The model and the limiting objects
Reflection positivity and the plane covariance
Stopped local sets and canonical clusters
Local cable tests and the no-crossing principle
Identification of the complete cluster collections
Conventions and elementary corrections in the inputs

statements.title: Joint critical-line limit
statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every fixed pair $J>0$, $U\le J$ with $\sinh(2J)=e^{-2U}$,
every bounded Jordan domain $D$, and every admissible polygonal
approximation as defined in \cref{sec:lattice-domains},
\[
 \bigl(H_\delta,\cC_\delta^{\rm w},\cC_\delta^{\rm f},
                         C_{\partial,\delta}\bigr)
 \ \xrightarrow[\delta\downarrow0]{\mathrm{law}}\
 \left(\frac{h}{\pi\sqrt g},\cC^{\rm w},\cC^{\rm f},
                         \TVS{a}{a}(h)\right).
\]
The height converges in \(H^s_{\rm loc}(D)\) for every \(s<-1\).
Each cluster collection converges in the matching topology just
defined, and the distinguished component converges in Hausdorff
topology. The continuum collections are locally finite above every
positive diameter. All convergences are joint, and the same GFF
determines both continuum collections.
statements.section_title: The model and the limiting objects

statements.title: Comparison with pins and wires
statements.label: prop:comparison
statements.text:
The finite $(s,W)$ law is positively associated in
\eqref{eq:spatial-order}, as is every conditional law obtained by fixing
vertex spins and compatible edge states with both endpoints fixed.
Increasing additional vertex and compatible edge prescriptions, or
changing retained connections according to the ordered boundary rule,
increases the residual law. The analogous statement holds with the two
colors reversed.

These comparisons permit monotone circuit couplings: search from the
changed data toward the region of interest, and stop at an open plus
circuit in the lower configuration, or an open minus circuit in the
upper configuration. Beyond such a common cut, the two configurations,
including complementary cluster colors, can be sampled identically.

statements.title: Buffered circuits and attached-wall bounds
statements.label: prop:circuits
statements.text:
Fix positive aspect and buffer ratios. There are $p>0$ and a fixed
lattice cutoff $c_*>0$ with the following properties, uniformly for
every physical test radius $r\ge c_*\delta$ and every mesh. Test
neighborhoods must lie in the ambient domain, apart from matching
cell regions to which one of the preceding completion rules applies.
\begin{enumerate}
\item In a buffer containing no pins, a circuit of either prescribed
$W$ color in a fixed-aspect annulus has probability at least $p$,
conditional on arbitrary admissible $(s,W)$ data outside the buffer.
Compatible pins of the requested color inside the buffer only improve
the bound. Finite chains of overlapping circuit tests give a positive
lower bound for a fixed-aspect tube connection.
\item After any admissible $(s,W)$ stopping exploration, failure of
matching circuits on $m$ separated available scales has probability
at most $(1-p)^m$, when each scale is chosen from the current history
before its interior is examined. In particular, suppose a prescribed
connected
matching wall reaches from $B(z,r)$ to outside $B(z,R)$, with a fixed
buffer around $B(z,R)$. A path avoiding that wall and all attached
matching circuits, and joining $B(z,r)$ to outside $B(z,R)$, has
probability at most
\begin{equation}
       C\left(\frac{r+\delta}{R}\right)^\alpha
\end{equation}
for some $C,\alpha>0$.
\item When a test buffer meets $F$, the circuit and tube events mean
circuits and connections in the augmented matching graph just defined.
They have the same lower bounds under the exact completion of one
component or the exact completion with a common fill. A circuit
attached to $F$ blocks an accessible dual path by its actual part
together with the forbidden region $F$.
If only the $k$-label comparison is available, the probability bounds
lose at most $2^{O(k)}$ in total. The number of local entrances of one
label does not enter this cost.
\end{enumerate}
The bulk assertion in item~1 also holds before removing the model's
single wired $N$ component. Conditioning in a search concerns $(s,W)$;
an exact cut history with exterior colors is allowed because its
accessible marginal is already a fresh flat kernel.

statements.title: Cluster and transmission counts
statements.label: prop:cluster-counts
statements.text:
The following bounds hold in fixed buffered boxes, uniformly in the
mesh and in allowed conditional histories. A joint count of actual
clusters across chambers in items~1 and~3 requires the product class
with a common fill. Item~2 has the interior scope stated there.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For fixed $b>0$, the number of unsearched free $N$ clusters
having a connected passage of diameter at least $b$ in a fixed box
has an exponential tail. Its constants depend on $b$ and the fixed
box geometry, not on the roughness of the surrounding walls or on
the number of chambers in the realization with a common fill.
\item For one chamber, let a lattice-aligned rectangle and its joining buffer lie
wholly in the unprescribed accessible interior. Use the relative dual
restriction with separate side ports defined in the proof. The number of distinct
components of the restricted $N$ graph crossing between two specified
opposite sides has a geometric tail. Consequently, if
$Q_0\Subset Q_1$, the number of restricted components in $Q_1$
which meet $Q_0$ and a vertex incident to an edge outside the
restriction has a geometric tail, provided the fixed covering
rectangles in $Q_1\setminus Q_0$ and every joining buffer have the
same unprescribed interior clearance. Arbitrary admissible $(s,W)$
prescriptions outside a larger buffer are allowed. The same interior
assertion holds in the original wired law before removal of its
boundary cluster.
\item Counts of distinct free $N$ clusters of the residual kernels
enclosing or passing through a fixed
aspect-ratio annular shell have moments of every fixed order, uniformly
after rescaling the shell down to lattice order. Under a stopping
history these are the unsearched clusters. A distinguished wired
cluster adds at most one. For arbitrary
independent chambers with pairwise disjoint interiors this last
statement is available separately in each chamber; it asserts no
bound for their total count without a common fill. The precise
no-shadowing consequence at indexed discoveries is stated in
\cref{cor:indexed-no-shadowing} below.
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Counts in an enclosing box
statements.label: cor:global-cluster-counts
statements.text:
Fix a bounded box $L$ and $b>0$. Suppose the finite lattice domain
and the supports under consideration lie in $L$, and place $L$ in
a fixed larger regular ambient box. For one free flat $N$ law, or
the residual product law with a common fill conditional on its initial
exact cut data, let
\[
 \mathcal N_\delta(b)
   =\#\{\,\text{free }N\text{ clusters }C:\diam C\ge b\,\}.
\]
There are constants $C,c>0$, depending on $L,b,t$ but not on the
initial walls or the mesh, such that
\begin{equation}
       \P[\mathcal N_\delta(b)\ge n\mid\text{initial cut data}]
                       \le C e^{-cn}.
\end{equation}
The unconditioned free dual current is included. For the original
wired current, expose its boundary cluster first; its free
descendants satisfy this estimate conditionally, and adding the
distinguished boundary cluster increases the count by at most one.
The boxes and all cover buffers are fixed before the mesh limit.

There is also a pathwise consequence for a seed exploration. Suppose
a compact set $Q$ is at distance at least $r>0$ from the seed and
initial removed support. List the discovered free clusters whose
support meets $Q$, or whose union of odd holes meets $Q$. If
$\mathcal L_\delta(\tau;Q,r)$ is the number listed up to any stop,
then, for all sufficiently small $\delta$,
\begin{equation}
       \mathcal L_\delta(\tau;Q,r)
                       \le \mathcal N_{\delta,\mathrm{initial}}(r/3).
\end{equation}
Add one on the right if the distinguished wired cluster is listed.
This is domination by the initial count, not a tail conditional on
the completed stop.

statements.title: No shadowing at recorded stops
statements.label: cor:indexed-no-shadowing
statements.text:
Fix a buffered box $Q$ and $b>0$. At a stop $\tau$ of an
exterior-attached seed exploration, let $F_\tau$ be its frozen
connected cell region, including the initial walls, all visited seed
vertices, and all clusters already revealed. Let
\[
 \Xi_\delta(\tau;b,\eta)
  =\left\{\begin{array}{c}
   \text{some unsearched }N\text{ cluster has a connected}\\[-2pt]
   \text{passage }\gamma\subset Q,\quad \diam\gamma\ge b,\quad
              \gamma\subset F_\tau^\eta
          \end{array}\right\}.
\]
For allowed exact cut or $(s,W)$ stopping histories $\mathcal H_\tau$
with the supported residual product class,
\begin{equation}
 \P[\Xi_\delta(\tau;b,\eta)\mid\mathcal H_\tau]
       \le\omega_{Q,b}(\eta,\delta),\qquad
 \lim_{\eta\downarrow0}\limsup_{\delta\downarrow0}
       \omega_{Q,b}(\eta,\delta)=0,
\end{equation}
uniformly over positive probability histories. Exterior colors
rendered irrelevant by a completed cut are allowed. Arbitrary
interior $d$ pins, or conditioning on a later visibility event,
are not part of this statement.

For an exploration in the enclosing box of
\cref{cor:global-cluster-counts}, index stops by their rank among
discoveries of clusters of diameter at least $b$, and let
$\tau_0$ be the initial stop. All intervening smaller discoveries
are included in each frozen $F_{\tau_i}$. If $D_\delta(b)$ is the
number of these records, then, for every integer $K$,
\begin{equation}
 \P[\exists\,0\le i\le D_\delta(b):
             \Xi_\delta(\tau_i;b,\eta)
       \mid\text{initial cut data}]
 \le C e^{-cK}+(K+1)\omega_{Q,b}(\eta,\delta).
\end{equation}
The indices here are recorded macroscopic ranks, not raw discovery
numbers.

If a random width $\eta_\delta$ tends to zero only on a limiting
event $E$, the usable deterministic inclusion is, for fixed $\eta$,
\begin{equation}
 E\cap\Xi_\delta(\tau;b,\eta_\delta)
 \subseteq
 \Xi_\delta(\tau;b,\eta)\ \cup\
       \bigl(E\cap\{\eta_\delta>\eta\}\bigr).
\end{equation}
Thus one first fixes $\eta$, takes the mesh limit (and Fatou's
inequality when passing to a limit event), and then sends $\eta$ to
zero. No estimate is asserted after conditioning on $E$.

statements.title: Pattern comparison
statements.label: prop:pattern-comparison
statements.text:
Fix regular compact sets $Q_i$ and filled buffered neighborhoods
$B_i$, $1\le i\le m$, with the $B_i$ pairwise disjoint and a fixed
positive separation between $Q_i$ and $\partial B_i$. Assume each
$B_i$ is contained in the domain, with no prescribed data there
other than the pattern being tested in $Q_i$. Exterior data may be
arbitrary admissible $(s,W)$ data and their retained connections.
There is a constant $C$ such that, for complete patterns $p_i$,
\begin{equation}
 C^{-m}\prod_{i=1}^m\pi_i(p_i)
 \le \mu[p_i\text{ on every }Q_i]
 \le C^m\prod_{i=1}^m\pi_i(p_i).
\end{equation}
Here $\mu$ is any such conditional flat law, and $\pi_i$ is the
plane pattern law in $Q_i$. The constant depends on the fixed
buffer geometry and $t$, not on the patterns or on their number
of microscopic prescriptions. Copies under parity-preserving lattice
translations and reflections satisfy the same assertion.

In particular, the single-box pattern laws have uniformly bounded
Radon--Nikodym density ratios, and the same remains true locally
after conditioning on any collection of separated patterns in the
other boxes.

statements.title: Full-spin contiguity
statements.label: prop:full-contiguity
statements.text:
Fix compactly nested regular boxes $Q\Subset B$ in the interior
of a $W$-flat domain, with fixed positive buffer ratios. Thus the
complementary $N$ components are free. Let $\mu_\delta$
be its law and $\pi_\delta$ the plane law, restricted to the full
spin pair in $Q$. The domains and any allowed exterior $(s,W)$
data may depend on $\delta$, but their walls and prescriptions stay
outside $B$. There is a uniform contiguity modulus: for every
$\eps>0$ there is $\zeta>0$ such that, for every sufficiently small
mesh and every event $E$ determined by the full spin pair in $Q$,
\begin{equation}
             \pi_\delta(E)<\zeta
           \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
             \mu_\delta(E)<\eps.
\end{equation}
The conclusion also holds if the tested data include $W$ in $Q$.
In particular it applies to mesh-dependent tests. Either flat
parity can be used by assigning $W$ to the parity carrying that
flat wall. This statement does not include a fixed-color wired
$N$ component before its removal.

statements.title: Summable dispersion defect
statements.label: prop:dispersion-defect
statements.text:
In each of the four reflection frames,
\begin{equation}
 \int_{0<|k|<\kappa}D(k,s)\,\nu(\dd k,\dd s)<\infty,
 \qquad
 \nu\{r\le|k|\le2r\}\le C_1.
 
\end{equation}
The second bound holds for every $r>0$.
statements.section_title: Reflection positivity and the plane covariance

statements.title: Subsequential plane Green covariance
statements.label: prop:plane-green
statements.text:
Every mesh sequence has a subsequence and a finite positive number $\beta$
such that, for all neutral smooth compactly supported tests,
\begin{equation}
 \E[K_\delta(f)K_\delta(g)]\longrightarrow\beta\mathcal L(f,g).
 
\end{equation}
The possible values of $\beta$ are bounded above and bounded away from zero.
The convergence also holds for smoothly converging tests in a common compact
set. At this stage $\beta$ is allowed to depend on the subsequence.
statements.section_title: Reflection positivity and the plane covariance

statements.title: Reflection-null Laplace insertion
statements.label: cor:reflection-null
statements.text:
Let $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\R^2)$ be supported a positive distance to one side
of a line in any of the four reflection frames. For site rows converging to
that line, the reflection norm of $X_\delta=K_\delta(\Delta\phi)$ tends to
zero. The assertion includes converging placements and the local
augmentations in \cref{lem:positive-transfer}.
statements.section_title: Reflection positivity and the plane covariance

statements.title: Exterior orthogonality
statements.label: prop:screened-orthogonality
statements.text:
Let $Q$ be a square and let $B$ be a concentric disk whose radius is less
than one thousandth of the side length of $Q$. For
$\phi\in C_c^\infty(B)$, let $\mathscr E_\delta(Q)$ be the sigma-field
generated by the full pair of spins outside $Q$, the $W$ states on
mutually dual edge pairs whose incident corner-grid plaquette is disjoint
from $Q$ (and hence the corresponding $N$ states), and all height
increments computable there. Then
\begin{equation}
 \left\|\E_{\P_\delta}
       [X_\delta\mid\mathscr E_\delta(Q)]\right\|_1
       \longrightarrow0.
 
\end{equation}
The same assertion holds under any sequence of flat-domain laws having a
fixed larger square $Q^+$ compactly in their interiors, with
$\overline Q\subset Q^+$. It is uniform over those domains, including
the component laws supplied by an earlier exact flat cut. In the latter
case it is applied to the conditional law at that cut, before any later
data are revealed. Additive height constants do not affect the assertion.

statements.title: Flat-domain limit
statements.label: thm:flat-gff
statements.text:
Let \(U_\delta\) be a single deterministic flat chamber, or a finite
mesh-dependent union of independent chambers with pairwise disjoint
interiors, as above. Suppose \(F_\delta\) converges in Hausdorff distance to
\(F\), and set \(U=B_0\setminus F\). Then
\[
                K_\delta\ \Longrightarrow\ h_U/a
             \quad\text{in }H^s_{\mathrm{loc}}(U),\qquad s<-1,
\]
where the restrictions of \(h_U\) to the components of \(U\) are independent
zero-Dirichlet GFFs with logarithmic singularity \(-\log|x-y|\). All finite
joint smooth-test moments with supports in \(U\) converge. Different limiting
components are independent even if their discrete precursors were the same
chamber. Either wall parity and either atomic or interpolated smearing gives
the same limit. The fields extended by zero off \(U_\delta\) are uniformly
tight in \(H^s_{\mathrm{loc}}(B_0)\) for every \(s<-1\).

statements.title: Logarithmic moments
statements.label: prop:log-moments

statements.title: Boundary decay
statements.label: prop:boundary-decay
statements.text:
Consider deterministic flat chambers in a fixed bounded region, with
connected accessible walls, and a Hausdorff limit of their complements.
For any limiting open component, moment kernels obtained from
\cref{eq:flat-log-moments} have zero boundary trace in a distinguished
variable when the other variables remain at distinct interior points.
The bounds and the trace conclusion are uniform for the discrete chambers.
More precisely, a shared cluster joining the height contribution at a site
within distance $r$ of a matching connected wall to one at distance at least
$R$ from that site has probability at most $C(r/R)^\eta$, with fixed
positive outer clearance and $\delta\le r\ll R$.

statements.title: Collision coefficient
statements.label: prop:collision-coefficient

statements.title: Gaussian moment recursion
statements.label: prop:gaussian-moments
statements.text:
For every $j\geq2$ and distinct points in $U$,
\begin{equation}
 T_j(x_1,\ldots,x_j)
 =\kappa\sum_{i=2}^j G_U(x_1,x_i)
          T_{j-2}(x_2,\ldots,\widehat{x_i},\ldots,x_j).
 
\end{equation}
Consequently the limiting centered field in $U$ is a Gaussian
field with covariance $\kappa G_U$. In particular its restrictions
to different components are independent.

statements.title: Plane Gaussian correlations
statements.label: prop:plane-gaussian-moments
statements.text:
Along the chosen subsequence, all plane increment correlation functions
satisfy Wick's rule with covariance \(C_\kappa\). More precisely,
\(\Phi_{m,\delta}\to Q_m\) uniformly on compact subsets of \(\mathcal D_m\)
at every order, and \(Q_m\) is zero for odd \(m\), while for even \(m\)
it is the sum over pairings of products of \(C_\kappa(d_i,d_j)\).

statements.title: Plane normalization
statements.label: prop:plane-normalization

statements.title: Conditional flat remainders
statements.label: prop:conditional-flat-gff
statements.text:
Suppose a stopping exploration uses the cuts in \cref{lem:finite-cuts}, so
that, conditional on its revealed data $\mathcal E_\delta$, the unexplored
chambers have independent flat laws with pairwise disjoint interiors. Let
$R_\delta$ be their centered unit-height remainders, patched by zero, and
let $U_\delta,F_\delta$ be their open union and closed complement in
$\overline B_0$. Fix real tests $f_1,\ldots,f_\ell\in C_c^\infty(B_0)$,
$u_1,\ldots,u_\ell\in\R$, and $d_0>0$. Put
\[
 A_{\delta,d_0}
 =\left\{\dist\left(\bigcup_i\supp f_i,F_\delta\right)\ge d_0\right\}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
 \E\Bigg[\ind_{A_{\delta,d_0}}
 \Bigg|&
 \E\left[\exp\left(i\sum_i u_iR_\delta(f_i)\right)
                  \,\middle|\,\mathcal E_\delta\right]\\
 &-\exp\left(-\frac1{2a^2}
                  \sum_{i,j}u_i u_jG_{U_\delta}(f_i,f_j)\right)
 \Bigg|\Bigg]\longrightarrow0.
\end{split}

\end{equation}
Here \(G_{U_\delta}\) is the continuum Dirichlet kernel of the resolved
open chamber union, with zero covariance between its components.

Multiplying the displayed difference by any uniformly bounded
\(\mathcal E_\delta\)-measurable variable preserves the same estimate with
its clearance indicator. To state the limiting consequence, let
\(\mathsf E\) be a Polish space and let \(e_\delta\) be an
\(\mathcal E_\delta\)-measurable \(\mathsf E\)-valued variable. Suppose,
for one fixed \(s<-1\), that along a subsequence
\[
 (e_\delta,F_\delta,R_\delta)\Longrightarrow(e,F,R)
 \quad\text{in }\mathsf E\times\mathcal K(\overline B_0)
                   \times H^s_{\mathrm{loc}}(B_0),
\]
where \(\mathcal K(\overline B_0)\) is the space of nonempty compact sets
with the Hausdorff metric. The limit \(F\) is almost surely connected and
contains \(\partial B_0\). Put \(U=B_0\setminus F\) and
\[
 A_F=\left\{\dist\left(\bigcup_i\supp f_i,F\right)>0\right\}.
\]
Then, almost surely,
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
 &\ind_{A_F}\,
 \E\left[\exp\left(i\sum_i u_iR(f_i)\right)
             \,\middle|\,\sigma(e,F)\right]\\
 &\qquad=\ind_{A_F}\,
 \exp\left(-\frac1{2a^2}
                \sum_{i,j}u_i u_jG_U(f_i,f_j)\right).
\end{split}

\end{equation}
Thus, conditional on \(\sigma(e,F)\), the restrictions of \(R\) to the
component interiors of \(U\) are independent zero-boundary GFFs divided by
\(a\), including components born from a pinched single precursor. This is
first tested on deterministic compact buffers with positive limiting
clearance and then extended by a countable exhaustion. The retained variable
\(e_\delta\) may encode any exact-cut coordinates and flat constants for
which this joint convergence holds; the constants are added after the
centered assertion. Its \(\mathcal E_\delta\)-measurability excludes data
from any later revelation.

statements.title: Convergence of stopped carpets
statements.label: prop:stopped-tvs
statements.text:
The wired boundary cluster converges jointly with \(h_\delta\), with its
labels, to \(\TVS{a}{a}(h)\). In a free flat parent, after subtracting
its label and writing \(f\) for the zero-boundary limiting remainder,
the first odd carpet converges to \(\TVS{2a}{2a}(f)\). At depth \(r\),
define the global closed carpet as the closed complement of the holes
still unsearched after every branch has met \(r\) odd rims; it includes
all earlier layers and, in the wired case, the first wired layer. For each fixed
finite \(r\), this global carpet converges in ordinary Hausdorff distance
to the corresponding canonical nested carpet. Its labels and restarted
zero-boundary fields converge on every finite family of pointed compact
buffers in the limiting holes. These pointed conclusions include distinct
limiting components with the same discrete precursor; they do not assign
one whole precursor carpet to several separate Hausdorff limits.
statements.section_title: Stopped local sets and canonical clusters

statements.title: Conditional fields at a cluster stop
statements.label: prop:exploration-thin
statements.text:
Consider a seed stop in an initial free parent of label \(b_0\), or
the composite wired stop defined above. Let \(A,S,W_0,\mathscr E\)
be its limiting explored set, seed trace, initial wall, and retained
stopped sigma-field. The set \(A\) is connected to the original
boundary, and every component \(O\) of \(D\setminus A\) is simply
connected. Conditionally on \(\mathscr E\),
\begin{equation}
 h|_O=m_O+h^O,\qquad m_O-b_0(O)\in2a\Z,
 
\end{equation}
where the \(h^O\) are independent zero-boundary GFFs. Here \(b_0(O)\)
is the label of its initial parent chamber; it is \(0\) in the
initial free domain and \(\pm a\) in a wired hole. The labels are
tight on every finite family of pointed components.

On every compact subset of \(D\) away from \(W_0\cup S\), \(A\) has
zero area and the full conditional mean \(M\) is the locally
integrable piecewise constant function \(m_O\). On the same region,
\cref{eq:stopped-full-characteristic} gives the full zero-extended
conditional GFF law of \(h-M\), also for tests whose supports meet
\(A\). Locally \(M\) is the limit of the finite signed odd-hole
contributions of the discovered clusters, with the initial parent
label added. These statements hold for every member of a specified
countable family of sweeps and observable indexed stops, each
conditional only on its own retained state.

For a composite wired stop, every \(O\) is contained in one pointed
limiting wired hole. The conclusions use the global exploration of
the original \(h\); they do not require a separate lattice sweep
selected from that limiting hole.
statements.section_title: Stopped local sets and canonical clusters

statements.title: No crossing
statements.label: prop:no-crossing
statements.text:
Let \(O\) be a component of a stopped exploration from
\cref{prop:exploration-thin}, with retained sigma-field \(\mathscr E\).
Suppose \(O\) lies in an initial free parent \(P_0\) of label \(b_0\in a\Z\), or in
one pointed wired parent \(P_0\) of label \(b_0=\pm a\). As provided there,
\(O\) is simply connected and, conditionally on \(\mathscr E\),
\[
              h|_O=m+g^O,\qquad m-b_0\in2a\Z.
\]
No canonical free cluster descended from that parent meets both \(O\)
and \(\partial O\). The conclusion holds simultaneously for all
pointed components and all recursive generations, and after a restart
in a captured odd layer with its new incoming label.

In the wired case \(O\) may be a residual component of the global
composite exploration of the original \(h\). The proof uses
\(O\subset P_0\), simple connectedness, and the
displayed conditional law. It requires no connectedness of the
explored set relative to that parent and no separately selected
lattice sweep inside a limiting wired hole.

statements.title: The visible partition
statements.label: prop:partition
statements.text:
Almost surely, \(i\sim_*j\) if and only if \(i\sim j\), simultaneously
for every pair of marked addresses in either current family. Their
relative signs also agree. Each retained canonical cluster \(C\) has
a marked address \(i\) such that every Hausdorff limit of
\(C_\delta(i)\) contains \(C\). For every finite family of distinct
canonical clusters, their chosen supplying lattice clusters are
eventually distinct.
statements.section_title: Identification of the complete cluster collections

statements.title: All-generation local finiteness
statements.label: cor:canonical-local-finiteness
statements.text:
Almost surely, the entire canonical free cluster family has only
finitely many members of diameter greater than any given
$\eps>0$. The same holds for the wired family, including all
descendants. These bounds are compatible with the uniform tight
macroscopic lattice counts.
statements.section_title: Identification of the complete cluster collections

statements.title: The discovered mean
statements.label: prop:discovered-mean
statements.text:
Let \(\tau\) be one of the fixed stopped sweeps above, with limiting
explored set \(A_\tau\), and write
\(M_\tau=\E[h\mid\mathscr E_\tau]\) as a distribution on tests.
On each connected compact localization \(Q\subset\operatorname{int}Q^+\)
above at positive distance from \(W_0\) and the moving seed,
\(M_\tau\) is the finite signed sum
\begin{equation}
 M_\tau=b_0+2a\sum_{\substack{j\text{ visible}\\
                       \text{in the localized list}}}
       \epsilon_j\ind_{\mathcal O(C_j^{\rm can})}.
 
\end{equation}
Here \(b_0=0\) for the original free family. For the wired composite
exploration, \(b_0\in\{-a,a\}\) is the label of the initial pointed
wired hole containing the region. The sum is finite on each such
localization because its contributor list is finite. An invisible
entry has zero contribution. Consequently \(M_\tau\) is a constant
distribution on every ball missing \(W_0\), the moving seed, and the
canonical supports associated with its local contributors.
statements.section_title: Identification of the complete cluster collections

statements.title: Matching of all positive-diameter clusters
statements.label: prop:complete-matching
statements.text:
Every positive-diameter Hausdorff limit of lattice free-current clusters
is one retained canonical cluster, and every retained canonical cluster
is the limit of its visible precursor. No distinct invisible precursor
has a positive-diameter limit. The same assertions hold for the free
primal descendants after the wired layer, jointly with that layer and
the height. Consequently
\[
 F_*^{\mathrm f}=F(\cC^{\rm f}),\qquad
 F_*^{\mathrm w}=F(\cC^{\rm w}),
\]
and both collections converge in the matching topology of
\cref{thm:main}.

We prove the $\ell^1$-Bass conjecture for every discrete group. The
Hattori--Stallings trace of every idempotent matrix over the complex

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $G$ be a discrete group, let $q\ge1$, and let
$e\in M_q(\ell^1(G))$ be idempotent.
There is a finite set $F\subset\mathcal C_{\rm fin}(G)$ such that
$\tau_C(e)=0$ for every $C\notin F$. Equivalently,
\[
 \operatorname{HS}^1\bigl(K_0(\ell^1(G))\bigr)
 \subseteq \bigoplus_{C\in\mathcal C_{\rm fin}(G)}\C[C].
\]

statements.title: Exponentially decaying representative
statements.label: red:reduction
statements.text:
Let $e\in M_q(\ell^1(G))$ satisfy $e^2=e$. There are a finitely generated
subgroup $\Gamma\le G$, a word length $|\cdot|$ on $\Gamma$, a number
$c>0$, and an idempotent $p\in M_q(\ell^1(\Gamma))$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{h\in\Gamma}|p(h)|_1e^{c|h|}<\infty,
\end{equation}
and $p$ is similar to $e$ in $M_q(\ell^1(G))$.
If the trace of every such $p$ has finite support on finite-order
conjugacy classes of $\Gamma$, the same conclusion holds for every $e$
over every discrete group.

statements.title: Trace as a curvature average
statements.label: cy:trace-identity
statements.text:
Let $n=2m>0$ and let $\alpha$ be a compatible connection family through
dimension $n$. Write $A_h$ for the matrix of $d\alpha_h$ on the section
$t_0=0$. If $\mathbb E_{\Delta_n}$ denotes uniform probability on
$\Delta_n$, then
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{h\in\mathcal T_n(g)}v_{n+1}(h)\,
       \mathbb E_{\Delta_n}\Pf(A_h)
   =(-1)^m\tau_{[g]}(p).
\end{equation}
The series converges absolutely.

statements.title: Spatial summary channels
statements.label: ch:summary
statements.text:
Fix $r\ge1$ and $0<\epsilon\le10^{-3}$.  There are channels $A,L$ and a
cross kernel $\kappa$ with either of the following two choices of radius:
the early version has $r'=6r$, and the later version has $r'=r$.
In both versions $A$ is labelled by $G$, and for every
$P\in\mathcal P_f(G)$ and $y\in G$,
\begin{align}
 \sum_{z\in G}A(P)_z\bigl(E_r(P,z)-a_*\bigr)
       &\ge\phi_r(P)-10\epsilon,
       \\
 \operatorname{pred}(P,y)
       &\le E_{r'}(P,y)+10\epsilon,
       \\
 \operatorname{pred}(P,y)
       &\ge E_r(P,y)-10\epsilon
       \qquad\text{if }A(P)_y>0.
       
\end{align}
For $Y=A$ or $Y=L$, derivatives in every transfer direction vanish at zero
coordinates and satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal F_Y(P;h,h')\le C(1+d(h,h'))
 \begin{cases}
   \epsilon^{-10},&\text{early version},\\
   r^{10}\epsilon^{-10},&\text{later version}.
 \end{cases}
 
\end{equation}
Here $C$ depends only on the fixed word metric.  The numerical error constant
$10$ in \eqref{ch:selection-bound}--\eqref{ch:prediction-lower} is independent
of the group and of the parameters.

statements.title: Averaged curvature bound
statements.label: pf:bound
statements.text:
Fix a sufficiently large $R$, and set $S=b_*+2$.  Let $n$ be an even
integer with $n>10\beta_{b_*}$.  Suppose either that $g$ has infinite
order, or that $g$ has finite order and
\[
 \min_{h\in G}d(h,gh)>4r.
\]
For every tuple $(h_0,\ldots,h_n)$, the connection $\alpha=B/C_{\rm nor}$
of Proposition~\ref{co:connection} satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E_{\Delta_n}|\Pf(d\alpha)|
 \le C_R\bigl(CS^{3/2}R^{-1/10}\bigr)^n
          \prod_{i=1}^n l_i,
 \qquad l_i=1+d(h_{i-1},h_i).
 
\end{equation}
The constants are independent of $n,g$, and the tuple.  Moreover,
$S=O(1+\log R)$ as $R\to\infty$.

title: The logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski conjecture
abstract: We prove the logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski conjecture for arbitrary origin-symmetric convex bodies in every dimension. The theorem also gives the symmetric Lp Brunn–Minkowski inequality for every \(0\lt p\lt 1\). Combined with Saroglou's transfer theorem and a support-subspace reduction, it yields the logarithmic inequality for every even log-concave Radon measure and the scalar-dilation \((B)\)-conjecture.

tex.abstract:
We prove the logarithmic Brunn--Minkowski conjecture for arbitrary
origin-symmetric convex bodies in every dimension. The theorem also gives
the symmetric $L_p$ Brunn--Minkowski inequality for every $0<p<1$.
Combined with Saroglou's transfer theorem and a support-subspace reduction,
it yields the logarithmic inequality for every even log-concave Radon
measure and the scalar-dilation $(B)$-conjecture.

title: The low-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick fluctuation scale
abstract: For the zero-field Gaussian Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model at every fixed inverse temperature β > 1, we prove that the standard deviation of the log partition function is \(n^{1/6+o(1)}\). The same exponent describes its typical centered absolute fluctuations, establishing the predicted one-sixth exponent in this regime.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every fixed $1<\beta<\infty$,
\[
 \sd(F_n)=n^{1/6+o(1)},\qquad \Var(F_n)=n^{1/3+o(1)}.
\]
More explicitly, for every $\eta>0$ there is $n_0(\beta,\eta)$ such that
\[
 n^{1/6-\eta}\le\sd(F_n)\le n^{1/6+\eta}
 \qquad(n\ge n_0(\beta,\eta)).
\]
Moreover, for every $\eta>0$,
\[
 \mathbb P\!\left(n^{1/6-\eta}\le|F_n-\mathbb EF_n|
                         \le n^{1/6+\eta}\right)\longrightarrow1.
\]

statements.title: Covariance differentiation
statements.label: prop:found-replica
statements.text:
Let $K_\theta(u;\sigma,\tau)$ be an affine family of cumulative Gaussian
covariance kernels of a finite hierarchy. Assume that the independent
increment covariances are positive semidefinite throughout the parameter
interval. Let $V=\partial_\theta K_\theta$ and let $P$ be a fixed bounded
spin test on a fixed observed split tree. Then
\begin{equation}
 \frac{d}{d\theta}\nu_\theta[P]
      =\frac12\sum_{c,d}\nu_\theta[P V_{cd}].
 \tag{2}
\end{equation}
The signed sum includes coincidences with old labels and between $c,d$.
For distinct labels, $V_{cd}$ is evaluated at their common revelation;
on the diagonal it is evaluated at the terminal covariance. The exact
weights are the real-power weights described in the proof. A constant
diagonal contribution, independent of the summation label, sums to zero.
Conditional means in $P$ can be represented by independent additional
replicas at their specified prefixes before this formula is applied.

statements.title: Source derivative bounds
statements.label: cor:found-source-bounds
statements.text:
For fixed $n$, every derivative order of a continuation in bounded
feature directions has a bound independent of the mass partition,
uniform over the external source and the admissible bounded covariance
clocks. The bound depends only on the order and the suprema of the
feature directions.

statements.title: Path limits
statements.label: prop:found-limits
statements.text:
The preceding construction and estimates extend to bounded nonnegative
nondecreasing paths $b,h$ by step approximation. The limit is independent
of the approximations, provided the terminal clocks converge and the
before/after clocks at every specified cut converge to the specified
values. Planted expectations of bounded spin tests on a fixed finite
split tree with cuts before or after jumps, fixed-order source derivatives,
the signed calculus, and the mass-integrated pressure and moment formulas
have these limits. The susceptibility inequality holds on the continuous
parts, with nonnegative total increments of $S$ at jumps. For intermediate
cuts and the separate clock contributions inside a filled jump, use
approximations retaining the prescribed joint filling; no independence
from the choice of that filling is asserted. All constants in
the finite-tree variation and Taylor bounds are unchanged.

statements.title: Raw moments
statements.label: comp:raw-moments

statements.title: Local second moments
statements.label: comp:direct-moments
statements.text:
On every regular outer dyad of mass $u\asymp v$ beyond a sufficiently
large fixed multiple of $x$, for every sufficiently small fixed
$\epsilon>0$,
\begin{equation}
 \left(\operatorname{avg}_{u\asymp v}D_u^2\right)^{1/2}
 \lesssim_\epsilon n^\epsilon\left[
 (ne(v)v)^{-1/3}+(ne(v)v^2)^{-1/2}
 +(n^{-\delta}E/d^3)^{1/2}+n^{\delta/2}u_*\right].
 \tag{18}
\end{equation}
Fixed enlargements of a dyad are permitted in this assertion.

For a small direct test impose additionally $e(x)\gtrsim x^2$, and set
$W=\max(x,\sqrt{e(x)})$.  Then $W\lesssim d$ and
$e(v)\gtrsim W^2$ for $v=O(W)$.  On regular dyads of scale at least
a fixed multiple of $W$, including comparable dyads at $W$ that lie in
the regular region, the right side of \eqref{eq:18} is polynomially
smaller than $x^2/W$.  Between $Cx$ and $O(W)$ it is polynomially
smaller than $x^2/(W^2v)^{1/3}$.  Moreover
\begin{equation}
 \int_0^{CW}D_u\,du=o(x^2),\qquad D=o(x).
 \tag{19}
\end{equation}
The integral is truncated at mass $1$, and $C$ may be any fixed
constant.  The second assertion means normalized mean-square
convergence on every compact band
$r\le Cx$, $cx\le u\le Cx$, both in mass and in radius:
\[
 x^{-3}\int_{\{r\le Cx,\,cx\le u\le Cx\}}D^2\,du\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 x^{-3}\int_{\{r\le Cx,\,cx\le\alpha(r)\le Cx\}}D^2\,dr
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
If $W=o(1)$, there is a split $*$ in a regular band of scale $W$ with
$S_*\asymp W$, satisfying \eqref{eq:17}, and with $D_*$ polynomially
smaller than $x^2/W$.  It can be chosen above any fixed multiple of $x$.

statements.title: Conditional comparison error
statements.label: comp:conditional-error
statements.text:
Let $\lambda\ge n^{-10}$ and
$A=A_\lambda=n^\delta\sqrt n E/\sqrt\lambda$.  If $A=o(1)$,
assume that a minimizer has a regular outer region above $A$.
Then its integral \eqref{eq:7} is at most $n^{10\delta}E$ for all
sufficiently large $n$.  If $A$ stays bounded below by a positive
constant, the same conclusion holds without a regularity hypothesis.

Consequently, if these hypotheses hold along an admissible sweep from
zero to any strength at most $d^2$, then
$0\le\mathcal M_\lambda-f_n(b_0,h_0)\le n^{20\delta}E$.
The fixed-strength assertions apply also to the wall variant, whereas
this last conclusion requires an admissible sweep.

statements.title: Uniform one-site closure
statements.label: prop:cavity-closure
statements.text:
Fix \(0<c<C<\infty\). At a target cut \(i\) satisfying
\(r_i\le Cx\) and \(cx\le u_i\le Cx\), along every sequence with
\(D_i=o(x)\),
\begin{equation}\tag{22}
                         S_i=\Gamma(K_i)+o(x^3).
\end{equation}
The bound is \(O(x^3)\), uniformly over these targets, if \(D_i=O(x)\).
More precisely, for a fixed direct-test sequence there are
\(\eta_n\to0\), \(C_0<\infty\), and \(\vartheta>0\), independent of
the target in this band, such that
\[
 \frac{|S_i-\Gamma(K_i)|}{x^3}
       \le C_0\{\eta_n+(D_i/x)^\vartheta\}.
\]
When \(W=O(x)\), the \(O(x^3)\) assertion also holds at every omitted
lower cut, without a lower bound on its mass and without
\eqref{eq:4} at that cut. On the bands in \eqref{eq:19},
the error in \eqref{eq:22}, divided by \(x^3\), tends to zero in
normalized \(L^1\), in both mass and radius coordinates.
statements.section_title: The one-site comparison and susceptibility calibration

statements.title: Rigidity at a small test scale
statements.label: prof:direct-profile

statements.title: Rigidity at macroscopic scales
statements.label: prof:macro-profile
statements.text:
Consider minimizers in \eqref{eq:6} satisfying the endpoint and
constraint hypotheses \eqref{eq:3}--\eqref{eq:5}. Suppose
$x\ge c>0$, $e(x)/x^2\ge c>0$, and $d^2\le T-c$ along the
sequence. Then
\[
 r_n\longrightarrow q_T\quad\text{in }L^1(0,1)
 \quad\text{and locally uniformly on }(0,1).
\]
An omitted mass $u_0=o(a)$ and its specified admissible changed
paths are allowed, provided the changed paths of the minimizing
sequence and the smooth competitors used in the proof are admissible.
In particular all macroscopic quantile limits
are bounded above and below by fixed positive multiples of mass.

statements.title: Finite propagation
statements.label: reg:finite-propagation
statements.text:
For every sequence of comparison families in Definition~\ref{reg:families}
with data \eqref{eq:3}--\eqref{eq:5}, there are fixed positive
constants $c<C$ such that every minimizing quantile at a positive
strength $0<\lambda\le d^2$ satisfies
\[
 cu\le r(u)\le Cu\qquad
 \left(n^\delta\frac{\sqrt n E}{\sqrt\lambda}\le u\le1\right)
\]
for all sufficiently large $n$ along that sequence.  For ordinary admissible bare
endpoints, the entire comparison satisfies
\[
 0\le\mathcal V(\lambda)-f_n(b_0,h_0)
                  \le n^{20\delta}E,
       \qquad 0\le\lambda\le d^2.
\]
For a fixed strength family only the profile assertion is made;
its proof uses error estimates exclusively for admissible child
endpoints.
statements.section_title: Propagation of regularity and the comparison error

statements.title: Uniformity for the field wall
statements.label: reg:wall-uniformity
statements.text:
Let the parent have data \eqref{eq:3}--\eqref{eq:5} and work on
$[s,1]$, with $s=o(a)$, at final strength
$e(q)=d^2f(q/d)$ and lower wall
$0<r_{\min}\le u_*/M(s)$.  Suppose $d=o(1)$ and $d^2=o(\varepsilon)$.
For $0<\varepsilon\le T$ and $0\le\theta\le1$, put
\[
 c_L=\frac12\min(\varepsilon,T-\varepsilon),\qquad
 r_0=\frac{d^2r_{\min}}{2\varepsilon},
\]
and take increasing $0\le\varphi\le1$ on $[0,s]$.  The bare
algebraic coefficients are
\[
 b_0=T-(\varepsilon+\theta c_L)\mathbf1_{u<s},\qquad
 h_0=\theta c_Lr_0\varphi(u)\mathbf1_{u<s}.
\]
The profile conclusion of Proposition~\ref{reg:finite-propagation}
holds uniformly along arbitrary sequences of these wall parameters,
including $\theta\to0$ and $T-\varepsilon\to0$.
statements.section_title: Propagation of regularity and the comparison error

statements.title: A positive Laplace window
statements.label: fl:laplace-window
statements.text:
For every fixed $T>1$ and $0<m<1/300$, there exist $c_{T,m}>0$,
$C_{T,m}<\infty$, and $n_0(T,m)$ such that
\[
 c_{T,m}n^{20m}\le
 \log\mathbb E\exp\{s(F_n^c-\mathbb EF_n^c)\}
 \le C_{T,m}n^{100m},\qquad s=n^{-1/6+5m},
\]
for all $n\ge n_0(T,m)$.

title: The low-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick free-energy limiting law
abstract: For every fixed inverse temperature β > 1, we prove that the zero-field Gaussian Ising Sherrington–Kirkpatrick free energy, centered by its expectation and divided by its standard deviation, converges in distribution to a nondegenerate law as the system size tends to infinity through all integers. We also prove that its variance divided by n1/3 converges to a finite positive constant.

tex.abstract: For every fixed inverse temperature $\beta>1$, we prove that the zero-field Gaussian Ising Sherrington--Kirkpatrick free energy, centered by its expectation and divided by its standard deviation, converges in distribution to a nondegenerate law as the system size tends to infinity through all integers. We also prove that its variance divided by $n^{1/3}$ converges to a finite positive constant.

statements.title: Limiting law
statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every fixed real $\beta>1$, there is a nondegenerate Borel probability measure $\nu_\beta$ such that
\[
 X_n(\beta)\ \Longrightarrow\ \nu_\beta
 \qquad\text{as }n\to\infty\text{ through all integers}.
\]
The measure $\nu_\beta$ has mean zero, variance one, and a finite exponential moment in a neighborhood of the origin. It is the unique probability measure with the moments specified in Proposition~\ref{def:law} below.

statements.title: Moment convergence at the fluctuation scale
statements.label: thm:moments

statements.title: Moment specification
statements.label: def:law
statements.text:
Fix $\beta>1$ and let $C=\sum_{l=2}^{\infty}l^{-2}$. For an integer $k\ge1$, draw an integer $J\ge2$ with
\[
 \mathbb P(J=l)=\frac{l^{-2}}C.
\]
Conditional on $J$, draw $k+1$ independent copies $F_J^{c,0},\ldots,F_J^{c,k}$ of the completed free energy in \eqref{eq:completed-free-energy}. Set
\[
 t=\log J,
 \qquad P_k=\prod_{i=1}^k J^{-1/6}(F_J^{c,0}-F_J^{c,i}).
\]
Conditional averaging over the independent comparison copies gives
$\mathbb E[P_k\mid J=l]=\mathbb E Y_l^k$.
The constants in Theorem~\ref{thm:moments} satisfy
\begin{equation}
 a_k=C\sum_{h=0}^{\infty}
 \mathbb E\!\left[P_k\left(\frac{t^h}{h!}
       -\mathbf1_{\{h\ge1\}}\frac{t^{h-1}}{(h-1)!}\right)\right],
\end{equation}
where the second term is absent for $h=0$. Each expectation is taken before the series is summed. The series of these scalar expectations is absolutely convergent. We have $a_2>0$, and the law in Theorem~\ref{thm:main} is uniquely determined by
\[
 \int z^k\,\nu_\beta(dz)=\frac{a_k}{a_2^{k/2}},\qquad k\ge1.
\]

statements.title: SK--Curie--Weiss fluctuations below unit coupling
statements.label: cor:skcw
statements.text:
Fix $\beta>1$ and $0\le\gamma<1$. Using the same independent standard
Gaussian couplings as in \eqref{eq:model}, define the exponent and log
partition function
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \mathcal H_n^{\mathrm{CW}}(\sigma;\beta,\gamma)
 =
 \frac{\beta}{\sqrt n}\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}g_{ij}\sigma_i\sigma_j
 +\frac{\gamma}{2n}\left(\sum_{i=1}^n\sigma_i\right)^2,\\
 F_n^{\mathrm{CW}}(\beta,\gamma)
 =\log\sum_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^n}
 e^{\mathcal H_n^{\mathrm{CW}}(\sigma;\beta,\gamma)}.
 \end{gathered}
\]
Here $\gamma$ is the ferromagnetic coupling already in the exponent.
As $n\to\infty$ through all integers,
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \Var F_n^{\mathrm{CW}}(\beta,\gamma)
 \sim a_2(\beta)n^{1/3},\\
 \frac{F_n^{\mathrm{CW}}(\beta,\gamma)
       -\mathbb E F_n^{\mathrm{CW}}(\beta,\gamma)}
      {\sqrt{\Var F_n^{\mathrm{CW}}(\beta,\gamma)}}
 \Longrightarrow\nu_\beta.
 \end{gathered}
\]
Here $a_2(\beta)>0$ is the constant $a_2$ above at the same $\beta$.
The centering and standard deviation are the perturbed model's own
exact finite-size quantities.

statements.title: Upper disorder-chaos scales in zero-field SK
statements.label: cor:disorder-chaos
statements.text:
Fix $\beta>1$ and $n\ge2$. Put $E_n=\{(i,j):1\le i<j\le n\}$ and
$M=|E_n|=n(n-1)/2$, and let $g'$ be an independent copy of
$g=(g_{ij})_{(i,j)\in E_n}$ in \eqref{eq:model}. Write
$\langle\cdot\rangle_{g,h}$ for expectation under the product of that
model's Gibbs laws with disorders $g,h$, and
$R=n^{-1}\sum_i\sigma_i\tau_i$ for the overlap. Thus the replicas are
independent conditional on their disorders; $\mathbb E$ below also
averages the disorder and any replacement set.

For $t>0$, set $g^t=e^{-t}g+\sqrt{1-e^{-2t}}\,g'$. For an integer
$0\le k\le M$, let $A$ be independent of $g,g'$ and uniform over the
$k$-element subsets of $E_n$. Set $g^A_{ij}=g'_{ij}$ on $A$ and
$g^A_{ij}=g_{ij}$ otherwise. Then
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E\langle R^2\rangle_{g,g^t}
 &\le \frac1n+\frac{2\Var F_n(\beta)}
                 {\beta^2n(1-e^{-t})},\\
 \mathbb E\langle R^2\rangle_{g,g^A}
 &\le \frac1n+\frac{2(M+1)\Var F_n(\beta)}
                 {\beta^2n(k+1)}+C_\beta n^{-1/2},
\end{align}
for a finite constant $C_\beta$ depending only on $\beta$. As $n\to\infty$, for
$t_n\ge0$ and integers $0\le k_n\le M$, these bounds imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 t_n n^{2/3}\to\infty
 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \mathbb E\langle R^2\rangle_{g,g^{t_n}}\to0,\\
 (k_n/M)n^{2/3}\to\infty
 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \mathbb E\langle R^2\rangle_{g,g^{A_n}}\to0,
 \end{aligned}
\]
where $A_n$ has size $k_n$ as above.

statements.title: Comparison of the two regularizations
statements.label: paths:switch
statements.text:
At final strength \(\lambda=x^{p_*}\), with
\((\chi_{\rm lin},\chi_e)=(1,0)\), the direct and smoothed systems
satisfy \eqref{eq:P11}, uniformly with the same parameters
\(\gamma,\ell\). Their scalar trial gaps
\[
 f_{\rm spin}(K)+\frac14\int b^{-1}(K-h)^2\,dv-f_m^0,
\]
where \(f_{\rm spin}\) is the self-corrected one-site pressure at
the corresponding terminal mass, also differ by \(O(x^{5+c})\).
The same fixed \(c>0\) works for these three comparisons, independently
of the site count.
statements.section_title: Scalar reference paths and admissible perturbations

statements.title: Stopped pressure increments
statements.label: prop:increment
statements.text:
There is a choice of the exponents in \eqref{eq:P1} and a constant
\(c>0\) with the following property. For every sufficiently small fixed
\(\varepsilon>0\), every fixed \(q>0\), and
\(s=q x^{1+\varepsilon}\), the following bounds hold for every
sufficiently large fixed stencil order:
\begin{enumerate}
\item On each direct segment,
\[
 \int \mathbf E_\gamma\!\left[
  {\bf1}_{\{\mathcal K_m(s)\le3x^\varepsilon\}}
       |\dot\psi_m(s)|\right]\,|d\vartheta|
 \lesssim x^{5+c},
\]
uniformly for \(N/2\le m\le3N\), where \(\vartheta\) is that
segment's parameter.
\item On the size segment the corresponding bound holds for
\begin{equation}
 \left|\dot\psi_m(s)+\sum_{j=0}^r
                   c_j(m+j)\psi_{m+j}(s)\right|.\tag{I}
\end{equation}
It also holds when \(m\) is a measurable function of \(\theta\) with
values in this integer range, or when the observables are averaged
with nonnegative probability weights on these integers depending
measurably on \(\theta\).
\end{enumerate}
All integrations use absolute path-parameter length. The saving \(c\)
can be chosen independently of sufficiently small \(\varepsilon\).
Constants may depend on the fixed test coefficient \(q\), stencil order,
and the fixed temperature.

statements.title: Dyadic transform comparison
statements.label: red:prop-dyadic
statements.text:
Assume Proposition~\ref{prop:increment}. There is \(c'>0\), independent
of sufficiently small fixed \(\varepsilon\), such that for every fixed
positive test coefficient \(q\), every integer \(N'\in[N,2N]\), and
\(s=q x^{1+\varepsilon}\),
\[
 \left|\log\mathbb E e^{(s/x)Y_{N'}}
       -\log\mathbb E e^{(s/x)Y_N}\right|
 \lesssim x^{\varepsilon+c'},\qquad
 Y_m=m^{-1/6}(F_m^c-\mathbb EF_m^c).
\]
The constants are uniform in the integer \(N'\).

statements.title: Consequences of the increment bound
statements.label: red:prop-moments
statements.text:
Assume Proposition~\ref{prop:increment}. For every fixed integer
\(k\ge1\), the moments \(\mathbb EY_n^k\) converge at a positive
power rate. Their limiting second moment is finite and strictly
positive, and the centered variables \(Y_n\) have uniformly bounded
exponential moments on some constant neighborhood of the origin.
They converge weakly to a moment-determinate law. Removing the
completion and standardizing by the exact finite-size variance gives
the convergence asserted in Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.

statements.title: Validity of the law specification
statements.label: red:prop-identification
statements.text:
Under Proposition~\ref{prop:increment}, the constants in
Proposition~\ref{def:law} are well defined by an absolutely convergent
series after the indicated expectations. They are precisely the
limiting centered moments of \(Y_n\), with \(a_2>0\).
The standardized moments \(a_k/a_2^{k/2}\) determine one Borel
probability measure uniquely. Each \(a_k\) is also the expectation of
a single integrable random variable constructed from fixed priors and
finitely many Gaussian systems almost surely.

statements.title: Pair inverse with absolute attachment domination
statements.label: inv:pair-inverse
statements.text:
The kernel \eqref{eq:A8} is considered on extensions of any \emph{fixed} finite list of old labels. A pair function \(u_{ab}\) may depend on the topology with those labels but ignores any unused extra labels (is pulled back by restriction). Indices in this section used as pair arguments are distinct leaves. Normalize terminal mass to 1; other bounded terminal masses reduce to this by mass rescaling, scaling cumulative covariances by the square of the mass. Take a monotone step scalar path \(K\), nonnegative bounded-variation step multiplier \(b\), and retain pair levels in a terminal interval of the hierarchy (the whole interval is allowed). Suppose at these levels
\[
 1-b_r\mathbf E\chi_r^2\ge e>0,\qquad \chi_r=V_{zz}(K_r,Z_{K_r}).
\]
Bounds called polynomial in this section are in \(1+K_{\rm top}+\|b\|_\infty+\operatorname{var}b+e^{-1}\), independent of the number of steps. On the retained levels
\[
 u_{ab}\ \longmapsto\ u_{ab}-\sum_{cd\ {\rm retained}}{\bf M}_{ab,cd} b_{cd}u_{cd}
                                                                     \tag{H1}
\]
has an inverse on each finite step resolution. Each output is an integral of inputs over allocations of up to two more labels (some arguments can also be reused), with weights dominated by a polynomial times the ordinary \emph{absolute} unrestricted attachment rules to the old tree including \(ab\). Restrictions and bounded weights can depend on the topology. This formulation in particular controls new split densities, allowing coincidences and ties to existing forks. It applies with \(ab\) using old labels too. We only need symmetric arrays (on antisymmetric ones the subtracted sum is zero).

statements.title: Accuracy before field seeding
statements.label: global:trial-gap
statements.text:
For the direct paths, use the matrix \(b\) of \eqref{eq:P3} and the
\emph{unmasked, unseeded} field \(h_*=t-bq\) in the untilted system.
Fix \(T>1\) and the exponent choices of Section~\ref{sec:paths}.
For \(m\) in the stated dyad, the following bound is uniform over the
allowed \(\lambda,\ell,\gamma\). There is a saving \(c_G>0\)
independent of the allowed \(p_*\) and of \(s_*\) sufficiently close
to \(1/2\), such that for all sufficiently large \(N\),
\[
 0\le F_*-f_m^0\le x^{4+c_G},\qquad
 F_*= f_{\rm spin}(t)+\tfrac14\int bq^2\,dv .                           \tag{G1}
\]

Here \(f_m^0=f_m(b,h_*)\), and \(f_{\rm spin}(t)\) is the
one-site scalar pressure with the same terminal mass \(\ell\).
The size threshold may depend on the fixed exponent choices.

statements.title: Uniform weighted comparison budgets
statements.label: bud:targets
statements.text:
The averaging bounds needed are, on all segments of Proposition~\ref{prop:increment}, uniformly,
\[
 \mathbf E_\gamma\left[\max_{U\lesssim u\lesssim1}
       u\int_{v\asymp u} A_v\,dv\right]\lesssim_\circ U^4,              \tag{C1}
\]
where one can use ordinary dyads with fixed comparable enlargements, and on size paths in addition
\[
 \int (v^2+U^2)\mathbf E_\gamma A_v\,dv \le x^{4+c},\qquad
 f_{\rm spin}(K)+\int (K-h)^2/(4b)- f_m^0 \le x^{4+c}.                  \tag{C2}
\]
The second assertion of \eqref{eq:C2} is pointwise, with some \(c>0\) independent of sufficiently small \(p_*\).

statements.title: Comparability and the calibrated initial slope
statements.label: bud:coarse-profile
statements.text:
For every optimizer in \eqref{eq:C5}, uniformly,
\[
 r(v)\asymp v\ (w_c\le v\le1),\qquad
 \sup_{c u\le v\le C u}|r(v)-q(v)|=o(u)                                 \tag{C7}
\]
for each fixed \(0<c<C\) (fixed numeric multiples, not the removal profile).

statements.title: Closure for the modified constraints
statements.label: bud:modified-closure
statements.text:
Along any fixed sequence of optimizers with the strong-removal hypotheses
above and fixed outer-comparability constants, the following estimate holds
for targets \(i\) with
\(cw\le v_i\le Cw\) and \(r_i\le Cw\),
\begin{equation}
 \frac{|S_i-\Gamma_{\widehat K}(\widehat K_i)|}{w^3}
 \le C'\{\varepsilon_m+(D_i/w)^\vartheta\},
 \qquad \varepsilon_m\longrightarrow0,\quad\vartheta>0.
\end{equation}
The constants and modulus are common to the fixed target band. Thus
this difference is \(O(w^3)\) throughout the band, and is
\(o(w^3)\) along any moving target with \(D_i=o(w)\).
Since the target-band integrals of \(D^2\) are \(o(w^3)\), the same
modulus gives, separately in the two coordinates,
\begin{equation}
 \frac1w\int
 \frac{|S_i-\Gamma_{\widehat K}(\widehat K_i)|}{w^3}\,dv_i=o(1),
 \qquad
 \frac1w\int
 \frac{|S_{\alpha(r)}-\Gamma_{\widehat K}(\widehat K_{\alpha(r)})|}
      {w^3}\,dr=o(1).
\end{equation}
Each integral is restricted to the target band just described.

statements.title: Buffered one-row closure
statements.label: bud:closure
statements.text:
In any of the boxes of \eqref{eq:C15} we claim
\[
 \operatorname{avg}|S_i-\Gamma_s(K_s(i))|=o(u^3 P_1).                     \tag{C19}
\]

statements.title: Pointwise moments
statements.label: prop:statistics-pointwise

statements.title: Projection to a common low cut
statements.label: cor:statistics-low-projection
statements.text: One more consequence of \eqref{eq:A3}, \eqref{eq:D2} is the following: for \(Y\lesssim c'\) up to a sufficiently small fixed scale, a pair split well before \(c'\) (say mass \(\le c'/8\)) changes in overlap by at most \(O_{p,\circ}(z_{c'}^0 c')\) in every fixed moment upon projecting down from later cuts to mass \(c'\).

statements.title: Uniform all-moment accuracy
statements.label: prop:statistics-size-accuracy

statements.title: A deterministic cap on the low scale
statements.label: cor:statistics-cap
statements.text:
For \eqref{eq:D1} and the low statistics on size paths we may cap
$Y$ at $x^{\delta_*/3}$, decreasing $p_*$ if necessary, and still write
$Y=UZ$.  Indeed \eqref{eq:D11} gives
$|S_v-q(v)|^2\lesssim x^{2\delta_*}$, whereas on every bounded band
\[
 x^{2\delta_*}\lesssim x^{4\delta_*/3}/r^2.
\]
Thus the capped scale still satisfies \eqref{eq:D1}.  Its new majorant
$Z=\min(Z_{\rm old},x^{\delta_*/3}/U)$ is at least one and no larger
than the old majorant, so its fourth parameter moment is preserved.

statements.title: High-mass means and variances
statements.label: prop:statistics-high

statements.title: Coefficients after compression
statements.label: exp:prop-low-coefficients
statements.text:
Fix the dyadic restrictions on the base factors and a cut \(c\gg w\)
within the region where the small inverse is regular. A sufficiently
large fixed separation factor is enough; on size paths require also
\(c\lesssim\lambda\). Group base slots into blocks that share their
path through \(c\). Their split tree below \(c\) is the \emph{skeleton},
and every designated pair joins distinct blocks.

Apply the operator \({\cal O}\) defined above to the pressure
polynomial \eqref{eq:E3}: it is \(1+\partial_\theta\), with the
formal action \(\partial_\theta\Delta=-\Delta/6\), on a size path,
and \(\partial_{\log\lambda}\), holding \(\Delta\) fixed, on a
direct path. Group the resulting signed allocation coefficients by
this skeleton and sum their internal placements within each block.
The bound below concerns these differentiated, grouped coefficients.
This is a rearrangement of a signed measure. The probabilistic
expectations used to evaluate
the coefficients remain positive scalar laws on each fixed topology.
The spin-model pair tests have been projected to \(c\), or to a
neighboring smaller cut, so they depend only on the skeleton and can
be kept outside the internal sums. For \(j=2,3,4\), the resulting
coefficient, including the skeleton allocation weight, is bounded by
\[
 O_\diamond(\lambda c^{5-j})\prod_{s\ {\rm skeleton\ fork}} dv_s/c .       \tag{E4}
\]
If \(j=2\), the designated vertices are distinct, and \(c\asymp w\),
the bound includes the further factor
\(O_\diamond(\min_s r_s/c)\). A factor \(d\) or \(\dot d\) may first
contribute \(\lambda c^2\) to the coefficient, leaving a deterministic
factor bounded by the ordinary envelope because \(r\lesssim c\).
Like \(b\) and \(\dot b\), these weights are constant during each
internal block sum.

Combine contributions only when they multiply the same product of
pair tests on the same skeleton. In particular, this combines a
repeated pair with the square counterterm. Give such terms the same
dyadic restrictions and projection cuts. The cut, shape, and mass
coordinates are fixed during coefficient differentiation. Internal
summation may then be done before or after that differentiation.
The spin tests receive only the formal action on \(\Delta\) already
specified: project the differentiated polynomial, without
differentiating a random test or a projection law.

title: The maximal triangular Hilbert transform at the symmetric point
abstract: For arbitrary complex inputs in \(L^3(\mathbb R^2)\), we prove the pointwise maximal \(L^3\times L^3\to L^{3/2}\) estimate for the triangular Hilbert transform, with the supremum over both hard truncation endpoints. The estimate yields joint almost-everywhere and L3/2 convergence as the lower endpoint tends to zero and the upper endpoint tends to infinity. This also proves the conjectured scalar estimate at the symmetric point.

tex.abstract:
For arbitrary complex inputs in $L^3(\R^2)$, we prove the pointwise
maximal $L^3\times L^3\to L^{3/2}$ estimate for the triangular Hilbert
transform, with the supremum over both hard truncation endpoints.
The estimate yields joint almost-everywhere and $L^{3/2}$ convergence
as the lower endpoint tends to zero and the upper endpoint tends to infinity.
This also proves the conjectured scalar estimate at the symmetric point.
