title: The maximum number of mutually unbiased bases in dimension six
abstract: We prove that the maximum number of mutually unbiased orthonormal bases in ℂ<sup>6</sup> is three, resolving Zauner's dimension-six MUB conjecture. The upper bound is computer-assisted: under the stated binary64 arithmetic and compiler conditions, a complete execution of the documented verification pipeline excludes four arbitrary complex bases.

tex.abstract:
We prove that the maximum number of mutually unbiased orthonormal bases
in $\C^6$ is three, resolving Zauner's dimension-six MUB conjecture.
The upper bound is computer-assisted: under the stated binary64 arithmetic
and compiler conditions, a complete execution of the documented verification
pipeline excludes four arbitrary complex bases.

statements.text:
Under the arithmetic and compiler conditions in
Appendix~\ref{sec:rounding}, the fresh complete execution documented in
Section~\ref{execute:observed} certifies that there are no four pairwise mutually unbiased orthonormal bases in
$\C^6$. Consequently, $N(6)=3$.

statements.label: cor:adjoint-cartan
statements.text:
Under the arithmetic and compiler conditions of
Appendix~\ref{sec:rounding}, using the complete execution documented in
Section~\ref{execute:observed} as in Theorem~\ref{thm:main},
the maximum number of pairwise Killing-orthogonal Cartan subalgebras of
$\mathfrak{sl}_6(\C)$ that are all closed under the same standard adjoint
$X\mapsto X^*=\overline X^{\,T}$ is three.

under the arithmetic conditions of Section~\ref{sec:rounding}, the written
rational midpoint centers, each with its recorded selected position, cover
the seed coordinates of every exact complex Hadamard matrix up to the
equivalences of Lemma~\ref{seed:equivalences}, by closed Euclidean balls
of radius $0.032$.  After the indicated column ordering and conversion of
the centers to binary phase values, radius $0.0320001$ is sufficient.

Suppose that every final unitary cell is either excluded by a certified
necessary-condition test or covered by a certified phase ball as in

Definition~\ref{phase:root-data}.  Suppose the basic bounds
\eqref{phase:root-basic} hold and an auxiliary stored real
\(36\)-by-\(30\) matrix \(M\) satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \|M\|\leq\mathtt{mnorm},\qquad
 \mathtt{mnorm}\,\mathtt{froot}\leq\mathtt{n0},\qquad
 \|\Pi-TT^*-ML_P\Pi\|\leq\mathtt{id},
 
\end{equation}
and \(\mathtt C\) is an upper bound for a remainder constant
\(\pi b\) in Lemma~\ref{phase:remainder}.  Then these data form a

\eqref{phase:root-basic}, \eqref{phase:projector-certificate}, and a valid

statements.label: phase:bootstrap
statements.text:
Suppose \(s_0\geq\|\delta\|\) and
\(t_0\geq\|T^*\delta\|\) for every feasible solution in a completion
cell, using the particular alignment \eqref{phase:delta}.  Starting
with any such upper \(s\), a further upper is
\begin{equation}
 \left(n_P(s)^2+(1+\mathtt{ort})t_0^2\right)^{1/2}.
 
\end{equation}
Replacing \(s\) by this number only when it decreases \(s\), and
stopping after any finite number of steps, preserves coverage of
every feasible solution in the cell.

processes all its seeds with no failed or unresolved seed.  Then

equivalence, every exact second-basis Hadamard matrix required

statements.label: refine:relation-estimates
statements.text:
Suppose $t\geq\|\xi\|$.  Choose upper bounds
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 D&\geq R+\|d_q\|,\qquad
 v_0\geq n_P(R)+n_q,\\
 \lambda&\geq\alpha_P+\gamma_PD,\qquad
 e_0\geq\mu_P\varepsilon_Q.
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
Let $S_h=\Pi S$ and choose
\begin{equation}
 \sigma\geq\|S_h^*A\|,
 \qquad
 \beta=(1+o_P)\sqrt{(1+o_P)(1+o_Q)}.
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{align}
 d&\leq D,
 & d^2&\leq(1+o_P)t^2+\|\nu\|^2,
 \\
 \|\nu\|&\leq
 \min\{v_0,(1+o_P)d,\lambda d+e_0\},
 \\
 \|S^*h'\|&\leq\beta t+\sigma\|\nu\|,
 \\
 d^2&\leq(1+o_Q)\|S^*h'\|^2+n_Q(d)^2.
 
\end{align}

statements.label: refine:cover-preservation
statements.text:
Suppose Stage B is run on a finite list of records with valid Root
certificates, under the arithmetic assumptions and error bounds of
Section~\ref{sec:rounding}.  On a completed run, let $\mathcal A$ be its final atlas
of children and let $\mathcal B$ be the list of input parents whose
refinement failed.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 \bigcup_{(P,R)\,\mathrm{input}}\mathcal S(P,R)
 &\subseteq
 \bigcup_{(Q,r)\in\mathcal A}\mathcal S(Q,r)\\
 &\qquad\cup
 \bigcup_{(P,R)\in\mathcal B}\mathcal S(P,R).
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
In particular, a completed run with no bad parents replaces the input
cover by a child cover.  A nonempty bad list remains an obligation.

statements.label: refine:batch-cover
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{refine:cover-preservation},
suppose a batching invocation completes with no bad parents and every
emitted batch is included.  Then the input solution sets are covered,
up to the permitted equivalences, by the emitted records with their
stored target radius $\tau$.

statements.title: Local exclusion certificate
statements.label: exclude:local-certificate
statements.text:
Assume the root certificate
\eqref{exclude:root-data}--\eqref{exclude:root-decomposition} and the
arithmetic guarantees of Section~\ref{sec:rounding}.
If Stage C returns a negative result for the Record, then no exact
Hadamard $e(P+\delta)$ in its closed horizontal radius-$r$ ball can
be extended, together with the coordinate basis, by two further
mutually unbiased orthonormal bases.

statements.text:
Use the seven specified source files and the arithmetic conditions of
Appendix~\ref{sec:rounding}. Suppose the invocations in
Section~\ref{execute:control} meet all of its terminal conditions, with
the record provenance and batch checks stated there. Then four mutually
unbiased orthonormal bases in $\C^6$ do not exist.

statements.title: Comparison with the independent model
statements.label: analytic:comparison
statements.text:
Let $\ell=\log X$, where $X$ is sufficiently large, and let
\[
 c_1\ell^{-1/10}\leq\Delta\leq\frac12
\]
for a fixed $c_1>0$. There are fixed constants $\eta,c_2>0$ for which
the following holds. Let
\[
 S_V(x)=\sum_{n\geq1}\frac{\lambda_F(n)V(n)}{\sqrt n}\,
                         w_x(\ell^{-1}\log n),\qquad
 H_V=\sum_{r'\leq R_0}h(r')V(r'),
\]
where $V=z_m$ or $Z$. Suppose that $S_V$ has length at most
$X^{1-\Delta}$, that
\begin{equation}
 1\leq R_0\leq X^{\eta\Delta},\qquad
 \sum_{r'\leq R_0}|h(r')|\leq C_H R_0^2,
\end{equation}
and that $w_x$ and a function $A(x)$ have bounds by a fixed power of
$\ell$ for all derivatives up to a sufficiently large fixed order.
For $w_x$ these bounds are required after smooth dyadic localization
in $n$, on the scaled variables $n/N$ and $x$ in a fixed neighborhood
of $\operatorname{supp}\Psi$. They may in particular follow from
bounds in $u=\ell^{-1}\log n\geq0$ and $x$, with a smooth extension
at $n=1$. Then
\begin{align}
 &\frac1X\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}\Psi(m/X)
       |H_{z_m}S_{z_m}(m/X)-A(m/X)|^2
 \nonumber\\
 &\hspace{8mm}=
 \int_{\mathbb R}\Psi(x)\,
       \mathbb E|H_ZS_Z(x)-A(x)|^2\,dx
       +O\big(\exp(-c_2\Delta\ell)\big).
 
\end{align}
The constants and the sufficiently large $X$ threshold are uniform
when the stated support, coefficient, and derivative bounds are
uniform. They do not depend on $\Delta$ or on an index parametrizing
such weights. One may take
\begin{equation}
 C'=C_{\rm ar}+1=257,\qquad
 \eta=\frac1{4(4+2C')},\qquad c_2=\frac12.
\end{equation}

statements.label: weights:comparison-interface
statements.text:

the smoothness assumptions of Proposition~\ref{analytic:comparison}
with derivative bounds \(\ell^{C_r}\), uniformly in \(j,k,X\).
They have length \(X^{1-\Delta_j}\), with
\[
 \Delta_j=\delta_j/4,\qquad
 \tfrac14\ell^{-1/10}\le\Delta_j\le\tfrac14 .
\]
The deterministic term
\begin{equation}
 s=k/\ell,\qquad A_x=(C_F|x|)^s\Gamma(1+s)
 
\end{equation}
has uniformly bounded derivatives of each fixed order on
\(\mathcal K\), and is bounded above and below by positive constants.
The endpoint enlargement at \(n=1\) can be made inside the fixed
range \(n\ge1/2\).

   &\ge2^{-jk/8} &&(1\le j\le J),

 P_0^{\mathrm{eu}}(z_m)&\ge2^{-Jk/8}.
 
\end{align}
The implied constant and the lower threshold $k_0$ do not depend on
$k,j,X$.

statements.title: The metric Blaschke theorem
statements.label: thm:blaschke
statements.text:
Let $(M,g)$ be a connected closed smooth Riemannian manifold of
positive dimension. If $\inj(M,g)=\diam(M,g)$, then $(M,g)$ is
isometric, up to multiplication of the metric by a positive constant,
to a round sphere, a standard real, complex or quaternionic projective
space, or the Cayley plane.

statements.title: Sharp volume comparison
statements.label: thm:comparison
statements.text:
Every Blaschke manifold and its model at the same diameter satisfy
\[
 \Vol(M,g)\ge\Vol(M_0,g_0).
\]
Equality holds if and only if $(M,g)$ is isometric to $(M_0,g_0)$.

statements.title: Reduction to an upper volume bound
statements.label: thm:volume-reduction
statements.text:
If a Blaschke manifold has volume at most that of its model at the
same diameter, then it is isometric to that model.

statements.title: Classical Blaschke structure
statements.label: geom:structure
statements.text:
Every unit-speed geodesic is simply closed with period $2D$.
For each $p\in M$, the map $v\mapsto\exp_p(Dv)$ from $S_pM$
onto the cut locus is a smooth sphere fibration whose fibers are
great spheres of one dimension $k$, independent of $p$. Its
differential has nullity $k$. The model is determined as follows:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If $k=n-1$, the model is a sphere; if $k=0$, it is a real
projective space. In these two cases the metric classification is
known: the manifold is isometric to its equally scaled model.
\item If $0<k<n-1$, the manifold is simply connected and its
integral cohomology ring has one generator of degree $k+1$.
The possibilities are complex-projective type, quaternionic-projective
type, and Cayley-plane type, with the dimensions listed below.
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Jacobi determinant normalization
statements.label: lag:determinant
statements.text:
Choose $G_x$- and $G_y$-orthonormal frames
$Z_x=(Z_{x,1},\ldots,Z_{x,d})$ and
$Z_y=(Z_{y,1},\ldots,Z_{y,d})$ of $L_x$ and $L_y$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 f(x,y)=\left|\det\bigl(\omega(Z_{x,a},Z_{y,b})\bigr)_{a,b=1}^d\right|
 
\end{equation}
is independent of these choices.  It is continuous, symmetric in its
arguments, and separately $T$-periodic.  It is the absolute normal
Jacobi determinant at $y$ of fields vanishing at $x$ with orthonormal
initial derivatives there.  In particular, for $0<y-x<D$ it is the
polar volume density with respect to $dt$ and ordinary sphere area at
$\gamma(x)$.

Use the same orthonormal basis of $\dot\gamma(0)^\perp$ for the
coordinates
\[
 (q,p)=(J(0),J'(0))\in\R^d\oplus\R^d,
\]
choosing its first $k$ vectors to be the initial derivatives of a basis
of $L_0\cap L_D$.  On
\[
 \mathcal I=(0,D)\cup(D,T)
\]
there is a smooth symmetric matrix $A(t)$ such that
$L_t=\{(q,A(t)q):q\in\R^d\}$, and $A'(t)>0$.  For $x,y\in\mathcal I$,
\begin{equation}
 f(x,y)=
 \frac{|\det(A(y)-A(x))|}
 {\sqrt{\det A'(x)\det A'(y)}}.
 
\end{equation}

statements.title: Comparison on each geodesic
statements.label: weighted:geodesic
statements.text:
In the normalized intermediate case of Proposition~\ref{geom:structure},
let $f(x,y)$ be the Jacobi determinant of any fixed unit-speed geodesic,
as in Proposition~\ref{lag:determinant}.  Put
\[
 \mathcal R=(0,T)^2,\qquad
 w(z)=(\sin z)^m\left|\frac{\sin(2z)}2\right|^k
 \quad(0\leq z\leq T).
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \int_{\mathcal R}f(x,y)\,dx\,dy
 \ \geq\ \int_{\mathcal R}w(|y-x|)\,dx\,dy.
 
\end{equation}
Equality holds if and only if
$f(x,y)=w(|y-x|)$ for every $(x,y)\in[0,T]^2$.

statements.label: inc:normal
statements.text:
The cut incidence
\[
 F=\{(p,q)\in M\times M:q\in C_p\}
\]
is a smooth embedded submanifold. Both projections are smooth
fiber bundles with fiber a cut locus. If $u_1,u_2$ are the two
pullbacks of $u$, its rank-four normal bundle $\mathcal V$ can be oriented
so that
\begin{equation}
 e(\mathcal V)=u_1-u_2,\qquad p_1(\mathcal V)=2s(u_1+u_2),\qquad s\in2\Z+1.
\end{equation}
Projection of $\mathcal V_{(p,q)}$ into $T_pM$ identifies it with
$N_pC_q$. The unit sphere of this four-plane is exactly the
great sphere of initial directions of minimizing geodesics
from $p$ to $q$.

actual tautological four-plane bundle of every tangent great-sphere
fibration at a point of $M$ satisfies $p_1=\pm2e$.

statements.title: The first attachment and its coefficient
statements.label: geo:attachment
statements.text:
There is an oriented rank-three vector bundle $E\to B$ and an
attaching map
\[
 f:S(E)\longrightarrow M.
\]
Let $p:S(E)\to B$ and put $x=f^*u\in H^4(S(E);\Z)$.
The following properties hold:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item The pullback $\rho^*E$ is the first negative bundle for the
      free-loop energy.  It is isomorphic as a real vector bundle
      to the rank-three bundle $K\to U$ with fiber
      \[
       K_w=\{a\in w^\perp:
          J_a(D)=0\},
       \quad J_a(0)=0,\quad J_a'(0)=a,
      \]
      where $J_a$ is the normal Jacobi field along $\gamma_w$.
\item Let $\widetilde p:S(\rho^*E)\to U$ and
      $\widehat\rho:S(\rho^*E)\to S(E)$ be the pullback square.
      Then
      \begin{equation}
       \widehat\rho^*x=\widetilde p^*z.
      \end{equation}
\item After choosing the orientation of $E$, one has
      \begin{equation}
       p_!x=e.
      \end{equation}
      With either orientation its coefficient is $\pm1$.
\item The actual negative bundle satisfies
      \begin{equation}
       \rho^*p_1(E)=4z.
      \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Arithmetic parameters
statements.label: geo:parameters
statements.text:
Let $p:S(E)\to B$ and $x$ be as in
Proposition~\ref{geo:attachment}, and let
\[
 \xi=\frac12e(T_{\mathrm{vert}}S(E))\in H^2(S(E);\mathbb Q),
 \qquad X=e^2\in H^4(B;\Z).
\]
There is a class $Y\in H^4(B;\mathbb Q)$ such that, with
pullbacks by $p$ suppressed,
\begin{equation}
 x=Y+e\xi,\qquad
 \xi^2=p_1(E)/4,\qquad p_!\xi=1,\qquad
 \rho^*Y=z,\qquad 2Y\in H^4(B;\Z).
\end{equation}
For an integer $b$,
\begin{equation}
 Y=v+\frac b2e^2.
\end{equation}
There are rational numbers $\alpha,\beta$ with
\begin{equation}
 L:=e^2p_1(E)/4=\alpha X^2+\beta XY,\qquad
 4\alpha\in\Z,\qquad |\beta|=1.
\end{equation}
Here $\beta=1$ for \eqref{geo:incidence-input}; retaining $\beta$
also allows the opposite generator convention, for which
$\beta=-1$.
Moreover
\begin{equation}
 (Y+e\xi)^{r+1}=(Y-e\xi)^{r+1}=0
 \quad\text{in }H^*(S(E);\mathbb Q).
\end{equation}

Count $X,Y$ as polynomial degree one, corresponding to
cohomological degree four.  For homogeneous polynomials of
degree $2r-1$, set
\[
 \ell(P)=\int_B eP(X,Y).
\]
Then the middle moment matrix satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \left|\det\left[
 \ell\big(X^{2r-1-i-j}Y^{i+j}\big)
 \right]_{0\le i,j<r}\right|=r+1,
 \qquad \ell(X^{2r-1})=N.
\end{equation}
Pullback $p^*:H^*(B;\mathbb Q)\to H^*(S(E);\mathbb Q)$
is injective, and multiplication by $e$ on $H^n(B;\mathbb Q)$
is injective.

title: The nonmaximal anti-de Sitter Penrose Inequality and original-data rigidity
abstract: We prove the spacetime Penrose Inequality for smooth three-dimensional initial-data exteriors with one spherical asymptotically anti-de Sitter end, satisfying the stated decay and integrability assumptions, the dominant energy condition, and a compact weakly future outer trapped boundary. We assume that the hyperbolic metric four-flux is future timelike; its Lorentz norm is the mass, and the area is the infimum over full enclosing cuts. On the connected outermost, outer area-minimizing horizon subclass, equality characterizes the original data as a spacelike hypersurface in Schwarzschild–anti-de Sitter spacetime with matching metric mass. No maximality, evolution, or auxiliary solvability assumption is used.

tex.abstract: We prove the spacetime Penrose Inequality for smooth three-dimensional initial-data exteriors with one spherical asymptotically anti-de Sitter end, satisfying the stated decay and integrability assumptions, the dominant energy condition, and a compact weakly future outer trapped boundary. We assume that the hyperbolic metric four-flux is future timelike; its Lorentz norm is the mass, and the area is the infimum over full enclosing cuts. On the connected outermost, outer area-minimizing horizon subclass, equality characterizes the original data as a spacelike hypersurface in Schwarzschild--anti-de Sitter spacetime with matching metric mass. No maximality, evolution, or auxiliary solvability assumption is used.

statements.title: Nonmaximal anti-de Sitter Penrose Inequality
statements.label: thm:main-numerical
statements.text:
Let $(\Omega,g,K)$ satisfy Definition~\ref{def:setup-data}, the same
future boundary condition $H+\tr_{TS}K\le0$ on every component, and
the future-timelike metric mass condition in Definition~\ref{def:setup-mass}.
Then
\begin{equation}
 m_{\AH}(g)\ge
 \sqrt{\frac{A_{\min}(S)}{16\pi}}
 \left(1+\frac{A_{\min}(S)}{4\pi}\right)
 =\frac{r_A+r_A^3}{2}.
\end{equation}
The coefficient is sharp. No maximality assumption, restriction on the
compact topology or boundary genera, or outermostness hypothesis is required.

statements.title: Original-data equality
statements.label: thm:main-rigidity
statements.text:
Assume in addition the connected horizon hypotheses of
Definition~\ref{def:setup-horizon}. Equality in Equation~\ref{eq:main-penrose}
holds if and only if the original pair $(g,K)$ is realized by a smooth
proper spacelike embedding of $\Omega$, with boundary, into the smooth
maximally extended Schwarzschild--anti-de Sitter spacetime of parameter
exactly $M=m_{\AH}(g)$. Its interior lies in one black-hole exterior;
its boundary maps diffeomorphically onto a full smooth spacelike
cross-section of that exterior's future event horizon, with the
bifurcation sphere also allowed; and its unique end reaches that
exterior's conformal infinity. The embedding induces both $g$ and $K$
with the future-normal convention of Equation~\ref{eq:setup-expansion}.

statements.title: The one-sign component inequality
statements.label: thm:str-one-sign
statements.text:
Let $(\Omega,g,K)$ satisfy Definition~\ref{def:setup-data}, and assume
$H+\tr_{TS}K\le0$ on every component of $S$, with the convention of
Equation~\eqref{eq:setup-expansion}. Suppose that $K$
is compactly supported and that one of the two tensors
\[
 K-(\tr_gK)g,\qquad -K+(\tr_gK)g
\]
is positive semidefinite throughout $\Omega$. In each fixed admissible
hyperbolic chart for which the metric fluxes exist,
\begin{equation}
 p_0(g)\geq \sqrt{\frac{A_g(S)}{16\pi}}
       +\frac12\left(\frac{A_g(S)}{4\pi}\right)^{3/2}.
 
\end{equation}
This assertion does not require the flux covector to be timelike.
If that covector is future timelike, its Lorentz norm satisfies the
same lower bound.

statements.title: Fixed-height stress potential
statements.label: thm:str-stress-dirichlet
statements.section_title: A saturating conserved stress and reduction to a flat end

statements.title: Bending with arbitrarily small mass cost
statements.label: str-bc-bending
statements.text:
Suppose $(\Omega,g,B)$ is smooth, has one end, has strictly negative future
boundary expansion, and satisfies
$\mathcal H_g-2|\mathcal D_g|_g>0$ everywhere. Suppose its end is
$g=e^{4v}b$, where
\begin{equation}
 v=r^{-3}v_3(\omega)-d_0r^{-3-\delta}+O_3(r^{-4}),
 \qquad 0<\delta<1,\quad d_0>0,
 
\end{equation}
with smooth angular coefficients. Suppose also that on this end there are a
positive smooth $C(\omega)$ and a unit covector $e$ such that
\begin{equation}
 B=-g+\frac{C^3}{r^3}
       \left(\frac12g-\frac32e\otimes e\right)+O_1(r^{-4}),
 \qquad e\otimes e=n_r^\flat\otimes n_r^\flat+O_1(r^{-1}),
 
\end{equation}
where $n_r$ is the outward unit normal to the coordinate spheres.
The scalar remainder has three symbol derivatives so that the change to the
area coordinate has two controlled metric derivatives. The initial
interpolation needs two derivatives of the metric error and one of the
tensor error; the preparation in Lemma~\ref{lem:str-preparation} supplies
the stronger scalar expansion with all symbol derivatives.

For every $\varepsilon>0$ and every fixed compact subset there exist smooth
data $(q_\varepsilon,B_\varepsilon)$ agreeing with $(g,B)$ on that subset
and near the original boundary, such that
\begin{align}
 &q_\varepsilon\geq(1-\varepsilon)g,
 \\
 &R_{q_\varepsilon}+(\tr B_\varepsilon)^2-|B_\varepsilon|^2
 -2|\divg(B_\varepsilon-(\tr B_\varepsilon)q_\varepsilon)|
 \geq c_\varepsilon(1+s)^{-3-\delta}>0,
 \\
 &q_\varepsilon-\delta_{\mathrm{Eucl}}=O_\infty(s^{-1}),\qquad
 R_{q_\varepsilon}=O_\infty(s^{-3-\delta}),\nonumber\\
 &B_\varepsilon=O_\infty(s^{-2}),\qquad
 \tr_{q_\varepsilon}B_\varepsilon=0
 \quad\hbox{on the final end}.
 
\end{align}
Its metric ADM energy satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \fint_{\mathbb S^2}(8v_3-C^3/2)
 \leq E(q_\varepsilon)
 \leq\fint_{\mathbb S^2}(8v_3-C^3/2)+\varepsilon.
 
\end{equation}
Consequently its full-cut area infimum is at least
$(1-\varepsilon)A_g(S)$.

statements.title: Flat deformation estimate
statements.label: thm:fl-deformation
statements.text:
Let \((\Omega_{\mathrm{orig}},q,B)\) be smooth three-dimensional initial
data on a connected orientable manifold with nonempty compact smooth
boundary \(S_0\).  Assume that the metric space including \(S_0\) is
complete and has exactly one asymptotically Euclidean end.  On that end,
in Euclidean coordinates of radius \(r\), suppose that, for some
\(0<\delta<1\),
\begin{equation}

 q-\delta_{\mathrm{Eucl}}=O_\infty(r^{-1}),\qquad
 R_q=O_\infty(r^{-3-\delta}),\qquad
 B=O_\infty(r^{-2}),\qquad \tr_qB=0.
\end{equation}
Here \(O_\infty(r^{-a})\) includes all differentiated symbol estimates:
each Euclidean derivative lowers the indicated order by one.  Extend
\(r\) to a positive smooth function on the whole manifold.  Suppose that
there is \(c_*>0\) such that
\begin{equation}

 R_q+(\tr_q B)^2-\lvert B\rvert_q^2
 -2\bigl\lvert\operatorname{div}_q
          \bigl(B-(\tr_qB)q\bigr)\bigr\rvert_q
 \ge c_*(1+r)^{-3-\delta},
\end{equation}
and that \(H_q+\tr_{S_0}B<0\) on every component of \(S_0\), with the
normal pointing into the exterior.

For every connected smooth codimension-zero submanifold-with-boundary
\(D\subset\Omega_{\mathrm{orig}}\), closed as a subset and with
\(\operatorname{int}D\subset\operatorname{int}\Omega_{\mathrm{orig}}\),
that contains the entire sufficiently distant end and whose
\emph{full compact intrinsic boundary} is smoothly embedded and
two-sided, use that entire boundary as an enclosing cut.
Allow coincidence with components of \(S_0\), and allow
\(D=\Omega_{\mathrm{orig}}\), whose cut is \(S_0\).  Set
\[
 A_*=\inf_D\Area_q(\partial D).
\]
Then the metric ADM energy satisfies
\[
 E_q\ge \sqrt{\frac{A_*}{16\pi}}.
\]
The boundary, the intermediate cuts, and the compact interior topology
are otherwise unrestricted.
statements.section_title: Flat deformation: equations and floor separation

statements.title: The continuation family
statements.label: prop:fl-homotopies
statements.text:
There is a continuous piecewise smooth family, with parameter
\(\xi\in[0,4]\), starting at Equations~\eqref{eq:fl-trace},
\eqref{eq:fl-scalar}, and \eqref{eq:fl-boundary}, and ending at the
zero trace solution and scalar equation with zero source and inner
flux.  In the first three stages the source is the \(\Xi\) just
defined, always evaluated using the current trace \(F\).
Every trace right side has derivative at least one in \(h\), at fixed
point, \(Z\), and \(\dd f\).  The outer values remain \(f=Z=0\).
statements.section_title: Flat deformation: equations and floor separation

statements.title: Floor separation along the full homotopy
statements.label: prop:fl-floor
statements.text:
Fix \(0<\delta_0<\min\{c_0/2,1/4\}\), where \(c_0\) is from
Lemma~\ref{lem:fl-floor-ledger}.  There is a polynomial choice of
\(\Pi_N\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(N\), followed by
all \(R\ge R_{\mathrm{floor}}(N,\epsilon)\), no smooth solution
of Proposition~\ref{prop:fl-homotopies} satisfies \(t\ge-\epsilon\)
and attains \(t=-\epsilon\).  Every such solution has \(t>-\epsilon\)
on the closed truncation.
statements.section_title: Flat deformation: equations and floor separation

statements.title: Rank-one gradient and Hessian estimates
statements.label: reg-rank-one
statements.text:
Let $U$ be an interior coordinate ball or a smooth boundary half-ball,
with a uniformly controlled $C^2$ metric $g$. In the boundary case use
Gaussian coordinates, so $g_{33}=1$ and $g_{a3}=0$ for $a=1,2$.
Suppose that $z$ is smooth on $U$, up to the face on its original side
in the boundary case, and satisfies
\begin{equation}
 A^{ij}\nabla_i\nabla_j z=G,\qquad
 A^{ij}=g^{ij}-(1-b)e^i e^j,\qquad
 e=\frac{\nabla z}{|\nabla z|},\qquad c_0\le b\le1,
 
\end{equation}
where $c_0>0$. In the boundary case assume that $z$ is constant on
the face. At a zero of $\nabla z$, an arbitrary measurable unit
direction is allowed, provided Equation~\eqref{reg-trace-equation}
holds with that choice. Assume $|\nabla z|\le L$ and $|G|\le Q$.
There are $\alpha\in(0,1)$, a uniform positive radius $r_0$, and $C$,
depending only on $c_0$, the indicated geometry, and separation from
the other faces of the patch, such that on a smaller patch
\begin{equation}
 \|Dz\|_{C^{0,\alpha}}\le C(L+Q),\qquad
 \int_{B_r(x)\cap U}|\Hess z|^2\,dV_g
       \le C(L+Q)^2r^{1+2\alpha}\quad(0<r\le r_0).
 
\end{equation}
The constants $\alpha,r_0,C$ do not depend on a modulus of continuity
of $b$ or $G$.
The same assertion holds for uniformly controlled families of patches.
statements.section_title: Local regularity for the rank-one trace equation

statements.title: The regularity interface for the coupled system
statements.label: reg-coupled-bootstrap
statements.text:
Consider a family of smooth solutions $(f,Z)$ on smooth finite
domains with uniformly controlled interior and boundary patches.
Assume $|f|+|Df|+|Z|\le M$ and the following structural bounds,
uniformly in the family:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item The $f$-equation has the form of
Equation~\eqref{reg-trace-equation}, with $b\ge c_0>0$ and
bounded $G$. Its actual matrix and source are smooth functions of
$(x,Z,f,Df)$ on the bounded variable range, including at $Df=0$.
The value of $f$ on each boundary face is constant.
\item After multiplication by the coordinate volume density, the
$Z$-equation is
\begin{equation}
 \partial_i\bigl(a^{ij}(x,Z,f,Df)\partial_jZ
                           +B^i(x,Z,f,Df)\bigr)=Q,
 \qquad
 |Q|\le C(1+|DZ|^2+|D^2f|^2),
 
\end{equation}
where $a$ is symmetric and uniformly elliptic and $B$ is bounded.
The functions $a,B$ and $Q$, as a function also of $(DZ,D^2f)$,
are smooth on the ranges on which they are used.
\item Each boundary component for $Z$ has either constant
Dirichlet data, or bounded total conormal flux. In the latter case
its equation can also be solved as
\begin{equation}
 \partial_\nu Z=H(x,Z,f,Df),
 
\end{equation}
where $H$ is smooth on the bounded variable range. These faces
are disjoint and have no edges where the type of data changes.
\end{enumerate}
Assume that the derivatives of the displayed smooth functions and
the geometry are bounded to the order needed for each stated
estimate. Then $f$ and $Z$ have uniform local classical estimates
of every such finite order, including at the boundary. The constants
are independent of the size of a finite exhaustion domain if the
patch geometry and all the displayed data bounds are independent
of that size.
statements.section_title: Local regularity for the rank-one trace equation

statements.title: Bounded variables in every stage
statements.label: prop:fc-bounded-range
statements.text:
There are $N_0$ and $R_{\min}(N)\to\infty$ such that, for
$N\ge N_0$ and $R\ge R_{\min}(N)$, every smooth solution of the
four-stage family with $t\ge-\epsilon$ satisfies
\[
 |h|\le C_0,\qquad |f|\le C_0/\tau,
 \qquad-\epsilon\le t\le Z\le C_N,
 \qquad |df|\le C_N.
\]
The constants are uniform in the homotopy and truncation.
statements.section_title: Existence of the flat deformation and its mass comparison

statements.title: Classical bounds
statements.label: prop:fc-classical-bounds
statements.text:
At fixed $\epsilon,N$, the solutions in
Proposition~\ref{prop:fc-bounded-range} have local bounds of every
finite classical order, up to the inner and outer faces, uniform
in $\xi$ and in all sufficiently large $R$.  On the end one can
use patches with a fixed positive radius and uniform constants.
statements.section_title: Existence of the flat deformation and its mass comparison

statements.title: A scalar trace equation with bounded input
statements.label: prop:fc-trace-solve
statements.text:
Let $M$ be a compact smooth Riemannian three-manifold with smooth,
disjoint boundary components carrying constant Dirichlet values.
For prescribed $Z\in C^{1,b'}(M)$, $0<b'<1$, consider
\begin{equation}
 A_b(x,Z,Df):\Hess_g f=Q(x,Z,f,Df),
 \qquad A_b=I+(b-1)e\otimes e,
 \quad e=\nabla f/|df|.
\end{equation}
Suppose the actual coefficients extend smoothly at $df=0$, are
smooth on bounded ranges of their displayed variables, and the
principal coefficient is independent of the height $f$.
Suppose, uniformly on bounded input sets and any auxiliary compact
parameter family, the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
 \item constant upper and lower height barriers bound $|f|\le M_1$
 for every solution and for the normalized interpolation to
 $\Delta_g f=c_*f$, with fixed $c_*>0$;
 \item on that height range, $0<b\le1$,
 $b\ge c/(1+|df|)$, and $|Q|\le C(1+|df|)$;
 \item $Q_f>0$, uniformly away from zero on bounded variable
 ranges.
\end{enumerate}
Then the Dirichlet equation has a unique solution in $C^{3,b'}$.
It depends continuously on the input and parameters and is bounded
in $C^{3,b'}$ on bounded input sets.  No prospective floor
condition on an implicit auxiliary variable is required.
statements.section_title: Existence of the flat deformation and its mass comparison

statements.title: The flat trace solution operator
statements.label: cor:fc-flat-trace-solve
statements.text:
For fixed $N\ge4$, $\tau>0$, a finite $\Omega_R$, and any
$\xi\in[0,4]$, the trace equation of
Proposition~\ref{prop:fl-homotopies} has a unique solution
$f=S_\xi(Z)\in C^{3,b'}$ for every $Z\in C^{1,b'}$ with zero outer
value.  It has the continuity and bounded-input estimates of
Proposition~\ref{prop:fc-trace-solve}, without a floor assumption.
statements.section_title: Existence of the flat deformation and its mass comparison

statements.title: Finite-domain existence
statements.label: prop:fc-degree
statements.text:
For each fixed sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$, all sufficiently
large $N$, and every $R\ge R_{\min}(N)$, the physical flat system
has a smooth solution on $\Omega_R$ with $t> -\epsilon$ on its
closure.  Its classical local bounds are uniform as $R\to\infty$
at fixed $N$.
statements.section_title: Existence of the flat deformation and its mass comparison

statements.title: Existence and end estimates
statements.label: prop:fc-existence
statements.text:
For every fixed sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$ and sufficiently large $N$, the
physical system has a smooth solution on $\Omega$, including its
inner boundary, with $t\ge-\epsilon$.  For some $c_N>0$ and
every fixed derivative order $j$,
\begin{equation}
 |\nabla^j f|\le C_{N,j}e^{-c_Nr},\qquad
 Z,t=O_2(r^{-1}).
\end{equation}
The differences $Z-t$ and $l^2df^2$, with their derivatives, decay
exponentially.  Moreover
\begin{equation}
 V=4\nabla_g t+O(r^{-3}),\qquad
 \mathcal F_N:=\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S_r}V_{\nu_g}\,dA_g
 \quad\hbox{exists and is finite}.
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Existence of the flat deformation and its mass comparison

statements.title: Completion of the flat deformation estimate
statements.label: thm:fc-mass-completion
statements.text:
The flat exterior of Theorem~\ref{thm:fl-deformation} satisfies
\[
 E_g\ge\sqrt{\frac{A_*}{16\pi}}.
\]
statements.section_title: Existence of the flat deformation and its mass comparison

statements.title: The time component inequality
statements.label: thm:ah-component
statements.text:
Let \((\Omega,g,K)\) satisfy the regularity, completeness, one-end,
dominant energy, weighted integrability, and future boundary hypotheses
of the initial-data class, with
\[
 g-b\in C^{2,\alpha}_{\tau_{\rm data}},\qquad
 K\in C^{1,\alpha}_{\tau_{\rm data}},\qquad
 \frac32<\tau_{\rm data}<3 .
\]
Suppose the four metric fluxes in the designated chart are finite.
There is no causal or sign assumption on their vector in this theorem.
Then
\begin{equation}
 p_0(g)\ge
 \sqrt{\frac{A_{\min}(S;g)}{16\pi}}
 \left(1+\frac{A_{\min}(S;g)}{4\pi}\right).
 
\end{equation}
The tensor \(K\) may have arbitrary trace, and the boundary may have
arbitrarily many components.
statements.section_title: Removal of the second fundamental form on an asymptotically hyperbolic end

statements.title: Existence at fixed profiles
statements.label: prop:ah-existence
statements.text:
Choose \(\delta_0,P_0\) as in Lemma~\ref{lem:ah-floor}.
There is a fixed sufficiently large \(B_0\), followed by a fixed
exponent \(a\) satisfying Equation~\eqref{eq:ah-R-conditions}, such
that for every sufficiently large \(N\) the physical system has a
smooth solution on the infinite exterior with \(t\ge-\epsilon\).
It is a smooth compact limit of solutions on sufficiently distant
spherical truncations. At fixed profiles, \(Z,t,D\), and all their
derivatives on hyperbolic unit patches are bounded; derivatives
of \(f\) are bounded after multiplication by the local value of
\(\lambda\). These bounds are uniform in outer truncation.
Moreover \(R_{\widehat g}\ge-6\), and its inner boundary has strictly
negative mean curvature.
statements.section_title: Removal of the second fundamental form on an asymptotically hyperbolic end

statements.title: Vanishing loss in the time flux
statements.label: prop:ah-mass-loss
statements.text:
The profiles can be chosen in the stated order so that the physical
solutions satisfy
\[
 \lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S_r}g(V_*,\nu_g)\,dA_g\ge-o_N(1).
\]
Consequently \(p_0(\widehat g)\le p_0(g)+o_N(1)\).
The error depends on the fixed prepared data and tends to zero as
\(N\to\infty\).
statements.section_title: Removal of the second fundamental form on an asymptotically hyperbolic end

statements.title: The AH mass inequality
statements.label: thm:ah-invariant
statements.text:
If the metric flux covector of the data in
Theorem~\ref{thm:ah-component} is future timelike, then
\[
 m_{\rm AH}:=\sqrt{p_0^2-p_1^2-p_2^2-p_3^2}
 \ge
 \sqrt{\frac{A_{\min}(S;g)}{16\pi}}
 \left(1+\frac{A_{\min}(S;g)}{4\pi}\right).
\]
statements.section_title: Removal of the second fundamental form on an asymptotically hyperbolic end

statements.title: Causal Killing data produced by equality
statements.label: eq-causal-killing
statements.section_title: First variations of equality and the original-data adjoint

statements.title: Regular static quotient
statements.label: geo-static-quotient
statements.text:
Under these hypotheses, $N>0$ throughout $M$, and $M$ is simply connected.
The fields
\begin{equation}
 h=g+N^{-1}X^\flat\otimes X^\flat,
 \qquad \lambda=\sqrt N,\qquad \mathcal A=N^{-1}X^\flat
 
\end{equation}
satisfy $h\geq g$ and $\dd\mathcal A=0$, and there is a global smooth
function $H$ on $M$
with $\dd H=-\mathcal A$.  They obey
\begin{equation}
 \Delta_h\lambda=3\lambda,
 \qquad \Hess_h\lambda=\lambda(\Ric_h+3h),
 \qquad R_h=-6.
 
\end{equation}
Attaching $S$ in the regular boundary coordinates of
Lemma~\ref{geo-boundary-collars} gives a smooth complete Riemannian manifold
with compact connected nondegenerate boundary.  Its underlying completion is homeomorphic to
$\Omega$, and its boundary is identified diffeomorphically with $S$.  On that
boundary,
\begin{equation}
 h|_{TS}=g|_{TS},\qquad \Area_h(S)=\Area_g(S),\qquad \lambda=0,
 \qquad \partial_{\nu_h}\lambda=\kappa_h,
 \qquad \mathrm{II}_h=0.
 
\end{equation}
Moreover, in the original end chart,
\begin{equation}
 h-g=O_2(r^{-2\tau'}),\qquad
 \lambda-V_0=O_2(r^{1-\tau'}),\qquad \frac{\lambda}{V_0}\longrightarrow1.
 
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: The timelike region and the regular static quotient

statements.title: Simple connectivity of the timelike region
statements.label: geo-simple-connectivity
statements.text: The connected manifold $P$ is simply connected.
statements.section_title: The timelike region and the regular static quotient

statements.title: No interior null set
statements.label: geo-no-null-set
statements.text: One has $Z=\varnothing$, and hence $P=M$.
statements.section_title: The timelike region and the regular static quotient

statements.title: The complete equality base
statements.label: st-base-equality
statements.text:
The metric $h$ has a smooth completion by the original boundary $S$,
with its possibly changed transverse smooth coordinate.  Its boundary
data are
\begin{equation}
 h|_{TS}=g|_{TS},\qquad
 \lambda|_S=0,\qquad
 \partial_{\nu_h}\lambda=\kappa,\qquad
 \mathrm{II}_h|_S=0.
 
\end{equation}
The completed metric is complete, and $S$ is outer area-minimizing for
$h$.  Its four metric fluxes agree with those of $g$ in the original
balanced chart.  In particular,
\begin{equation}
 A_{\min,h}(S)=A_0,
 \qquad p(h)=(m,0,0,0),
 \qquad p_0(h)=\frac{r_h+r_h^3}{2}.
 
\end{equation}
For some $\tau_1>3/2$, the end satisfies
\begin{equation}
 h-b=O_{2,\alpha_1}(r^{-\tau_1}),\qquad
 \lambda-V_0=O_{2,\alpha_1}(r^{1-\tau_1}),\qquad
 h-g=O_{2,\alpha_1}(r^{-2\tau_1}).
 
\end{equation}
The last estimate is in physical tensor norm.
statements.section_title: The static base and its conformal compactification

statements.title: The normalized smooth expansion
statements.label: st-end-regularity
statements.text:
There is a geodesic defining function $z$ for the conformal
representative $d\theta^2+\sigma$ and a boundary-identity spatial
collar identification in which
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 h&=z^{-2}(dz^2+H(z)),\\
 H(z)&=\sigma-\frac12z^2\sigma+z^3H_3+O(z^4),\\
 z\lambda&=1+\frac14z^2+z^3\lambda_3+O(z^4).
 \end{split}
 
\end{equation}
All functions and tensor coefficients are smooth up to $z=0$.
The full third coefficient of the compactified four-metric is
\begin{equation}
 G_3=H_3+2\lambda_3d\theta^2,
 \qquad \operatorname{tr}_{d\theta^2+\sigma}G_3=0,
 \qquad \operatorname{div}_{d\theta^2+\sigma}G_3=0.
 
\end{equation}
The geodesic gauge preserves the circle factor and time reflection.
The original and new defining radii are comparable, their collar
maps extend to the same conformal boundary, and the resulting
spatial mass comparison is covered by
\cref{lem:setup-mass-covariance}.
statements.section_title: The static base and its conformal compactification

statements.title: A static Heintze--Karcher deficit
statements.label: hw-public-rigidity
statements.text:
Let $(M^3,q,V)$ be a smooth static system satisfying
\[
 \Hess_qV=V(\Ric_q+3q),\qquad \Delta_qV=3V,
\]
with $V>0$ in the interior and connected compact nondegenerate
horizon boundary $S=\{V=0\}$.  Suppose a bounded smooth domain
$\Omega$ has boundary $S\sqcup\Sigma$, where $\Sigma$ has strictly
positive mean curvature $H$ toward the exterior of $\Omega$.
Set $A=\Area_q(S)$ and $\kappa=|\nabla V|_S$.  Then
\[
 D=3A+2\pi\chi(S)>0,\qquad c=\frac{2A}{3D}>0.
\]
The unique smooth solution of
\begin{equation}
 (\Delta_q-3)v=-1\quad\hbox{in }\Omega,\qquad
 v=c\quad\hbox{on }S,\qquad v=0\quad\hbox{on }\Sigma
\end{equation}
satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \frac23\int_\Sigma\frac{V}{H}
       -\int_\Omega V-c\kappa A
 \geq\frac32\int_\Omega
       V\left|\Hess_qv-v(\Ric_q+3q)+\frac13q\right|^2\geq0.
\end{equation}
The measures in the surface and volume integrals are those of $q$.
statements.section_title: Rigidity of the normalized static base

statements.title: Global identification of the equality base
statements.label: hw-static-rigidity
statements.section_title: Rigidity of the normalized static base

statements.title: Properness, the future second form, and infinity
statements.label: emb-global
statements.text:
The extended map $I$ is a smooth proper spacelike embedding of the
original $(\Omega,g,K)$ into the smooth maximal Schwarzschild--AdS
extension of parameter $M=m_{\AH}$.  Its interior lies in one
exterior, its boundary is the full future horizon section described
in \cref{emb-horizon}, and its end reaches that exterior's conformal
infinity.

statements.title: Converse on the stated horizon subclass
statements.label: emb-converse
statements.text:
Suppose the original data satisfy the connected horizon hypotheses
of \cref{def:setup-horizon} and have the embedding required in
\cref{thm:main-rigidity}, with its stipulated actual metric mass
$M=m_{\AH}$.  Then equality holds in the Penrose Inequality.

statements.title: Mass-matched static and nonstatic examples
statements.label: emb-examples
statements.text:
For every $M>0$, the static exterior with its bifurcation boundary
attains equality.  It also admits smooth compactly supported time
graph perturbations with $K\not\equiv0$ which satisfy all the
initial-data and connected horizon hypotheses and still attain
equality with actual mass $m_{\AH}=M$.

title: The normalized-volume gap in dimension four
abstract: We prove that every singular complex algebraic klt fourfold germ with zero boundary has normalized volume at most 162, with equality precisely for an analytic ordinary double point. This resolves the ordinary-double-point volume-gap conjecture in dimension four.

tex.abstract: We prove that every singular complex algebraic klt fourfold germ with zero boundary has normalized volume at most \(162\), with equality precisely for an analytic ordinary double point. This resolves the ordinary-double-point volume-gap conjecture in dimension four.
sections: Volume conventions and the cone reduction
A terminal threefold section and the main theorem

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let \(x\in X\) be a singular closed point of a normal complex algebraic variety of dimension four. Suppose that \(K_X\) is \(\Q\)-Cartier and that \(X\) is klt near \(x\), with boundary zero. Then
\[
\nvol(x,X)\le 162.
\]
Equality holds if and only if the analytic germ \((X,x)\) is isomorphic to
\[
\left(\left\{z_0^2+z_1^2+z_2^2+z_3^2+z_4^2=0\right\}\subset\C^5,0\right).
\]

statements.label: prop:cone
statements.text:
Suppose that \(x\in X\) satisfies the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:main} and that
\[
V:=\nvol(x,X)\ge162.
\]
There is a positively graded affine fourfold \(C=\Spec S\), with vertex \(o\), such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item \(C\) is Gorenstein and klt, and \(C\setminus\{o\}\) is smooth;
\item \(\nvol(o,C)=V\), and \(\edim(x,X)\le\edim(o,C)\);
\item an effective torus acts on \(C\), with a minimizing Reeb vector \(\xi_*\). Primitive positive integral gradings along rational rays approaching \(\xi_*\) have degree valuations of discrepancies \(r\in\Z_{>0}\) and volumes \(h>0\), with
\[
r^4h\ge V,\qquad r^4h\longrightarrow V.
\]
For each such grading, the canonical module has a homogeneous generator of degree \(r\).
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, \(o\) is singular.
statements.section_title: Volume conventions and the cone reduction

statements.label: prop:stabilizer

statements.title: Short-interval nonvanishing
statements.label: prop:short
statements.text:
Let \(D=5/3\).
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item The ring \(S\), with the rescaled grading \eqref{eq:rescale}, has a nonzero homogeneous element of weight in \((0,D)\).
\item Let \(T\) satisfy the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:hilbert}, with \(n=2\) or \(3\), and admit an injection \eqref{eq:injection} lowering weights by a positive amount. Then \(T\) has a nonzero homogeneous element of weight in \((0,D)\).
\end{enumerate}

statements.label: prop:threshold
statements.text:
At the vertex,
\[
\lct_o(C;\m_o)>\frac32.
\]

statements.label: prop:section
statements.text:
For the cone \(C\) of Proposition~\ref{prop:cone}, a general affine hyperplane section through \(o\) is a terminal Gorenstein threefold near \(o\). In particular,
\[
\edim(o,C)\le5.
\]

title: The ordinary-double-point gap in every dimension
abstract: We prove the ordinary-double-point gap conjecture for boundary-zero complex algebraic klt germs in every dimension: a singular n-dimensional germ has normalized volume at most \(2(n-1)^n\), with equality precisely at an analytic ordinary double point.

tex.abstract:
We prove the ordinary-double-point gap conjecture for boundary-zero
complex algebraic klt germs in every dimension: a singular \(n\)-dimensional germ
has normalized volume at most \(2(n-1)^n\), with equality precisely
at an analytic ordinary double point.
sections: Normalized volume and the cone reduction
Jet cones and the canonical interior point
Adjoint jets and the saturated semigroup
Two filtrations and a second stabilizer
The slice estimate and the supremum bootstrap
Equality at the original germ and global consequences

statements.title: The ordinary double point gap
statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let \(n\ge2\), and let \(x\) be a
singular closed point of a normal complex algebraic \(n\)-fold \(X\).
Suppose that \(K_X\) is \(\QQ\)-Cartier and that \(X\) is klt near \(x\),
with zero boundary. Then
\[
                    \nvol(x,X)\le2(n-1)^n.
\]
Equality holds if and only if
\[
 (X,x)_{\mathrm{an}}\cong
 \left(\{z_0^2+\cdots+z_n^2=0\}\subset\CC^{n+1},0\right).
\]

statements.title: Global volume bounds
statements.label: cor:global
statements.text:
Let \(V\) be an \(n\)-dimensional
K-semistable \(\QQ\)-Fano variety, where \(n\ge2\).
If \(V\) is singular, then
\[
       (-K_V)^n\le
       2\left(\frac{n^2-1}{n}\right)^n<2n^n.
\]
If \(V\not\cong\PP^n\), then \((-K_V)^n\le2n^n\), with equality
precisely when \(V\) is a smooth quadric \(Q^n\subset\PP^{n+1}\) or
\(\PP^1\times\PP^{n-1}\). These two descriptions coincide for \(n=2\).

statements.title: The fourfold gap
statements.label: inp:fourfold
statements.text:
Let \(x\) be a singular closed point of a normal complex algebraic
fourfold \(X\). Suppose that \(K_X\) is \(\QQ\)-Cartier and \(X\) is klt
near \(x\), with zero boundary. Then
\[
                  \nvol(x,X)\le162.
\]
Equality holds if and only if the complex analytic germ is
\[
       \left(\{z_0^2+z_1^2+z_2^2+z_3^2+z_4^2=0\},0\right).
\]
No isolatedness, complete-intersection, quotient, or smoothability
assumption is made.
statements.section_title: Normalized volume and the cone reduction

statements.title: Cone reduction
statements.label: cone:reduction
statements.text:
Under \eqref{cone:eq-induction}, there is a singular
K-polystable Fano cone \(C=\Spec S\), with vertex \(o\), such that
\[
 d(o,C)=d(x,X),\qquad
 \edim(X,x)\le\edim(C,o).
\]
The puncture \(C\setminus\{o\}\) is smooth, \(S\) is a normal
Gorenstein ring, and its canonical module has a homogeneous
generator. The cone has zero boundary.
statements.section_title: Normalized volume and the cone reduction

statements.title: Small-stabilizer classification
statements.label: small:classification
statements.text:
Let \(\zeta_i\) be primitive positive integral gradings satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \zeta_i=\frac{r_i}{n}\xi+\epsilon_i,
 \qquad r_i=A(\zeta_i),\qquad \|\epsilon_i\|\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad m_{\max}(\zeta_i)\leq\frac{r_i}{N}.
 
\end{equation}
For all sufficiently large \(i\), every stabilizer is trivial and
\(r_i\in\{N,N+1\}\).  More precisely, the polarized quotient is
\[
 (B_i,L_i)\cong
 \begin{cases}
  (\PP^N,\cO_{\PP^N}(1)),&r_i=N+1,\\
  (Q^N,\cO_{Q^N}(1)),&r_i=N,
 \end{cases}
\]
where \(Q^N\subset\PP^{N+1}\) is a smooth quadric.  Consequently the cone
\(C\) is respectively smooth or an ordinary double point.  The assertion
includes the constant exact primitive grading when the ray of \(\xi\)
is rational.

statements.title: Jet setup
statements.label: jet:setup
statements.section_title: Jet cones and the canonical interior point

statements.title: The exponential bound
statements.label: prob:bound
statements.section_title: Jet cones and the canonical interior point

statements.title: Canonical interior point
statements.label: jet:interior
statements.text:
For every sufficiently large grading in the subsequence under
consideration,
\begin{equation}
 c_0=(r,\mathbf1)\in\Int K
                 \qquad\text{in the original degree coordinates}.
\end{equation}
Equivalently, $f(\mathbf1)<N$. For an exact minimizing rational grading
with $m\ge r/N$, the conclusion holds without passage to a limit.
statements.section_title: Jet cones and the canonical interior point

statements.title: The saturated jet semigroup
statements.label: adj:saturation
statements.text:
Suppose $c_0\in\Int K$.  Then the following statements hold:
\begin{enumerate}
 \item $K$ is a rational polyhedral cone.
 \item Every facet has a primitive nonnegative support form
       $\eta\in\Lambda^*$ satisfying $\eta(c_0)=1$.
 \item The semigroup and its interior lattice points satisfy
 \begin{equation}
   \Gamma=K\cap\Lambda,
   \qquad \Int K\cap\Lambda=c_0+\Gamma.
 \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
In particular, $\Gamma$ is a finitely generated saturated affine
semigroup with group $\Lambda$.  These conclusions apply to every
sufficiently far grading and chosen point covered by
Theorem~\ref{jet:interior}, including its exact rational case.
statements.section_title: Adjoint jets and the saturated semigroup

statements.title: The two-filtration structure
statements.label: filt:structure
statements.text:
The filtration $W$ is multiplicative, with
\begin{equation}
 G=\gr_WS\simeq D[\mathtt v],\qquad
 \deg_W\mathtt v=1,\qquad \deg_W|_D=T.
\end{equation}
Here $\mathtt v$ is a regular polynomial variable of original degree
$m$.  Moreover
\begin{equation}
 \Hilb_WG(z)=(1-z)^{-n},\qquad
 \deg\omega_G=(r,n).
\end{equation}
The $W$-Rees space is a finite-type normal Gorenstein variety.  Its
canonical generator has bidegree $(r,n-1)$ and, on $\lambda\ne0$, is
$c\lambda^{-n}\Omega_C\wedge d\lambda$.
statements.section_title: Two filtrations and a second stabilizer

statements.title: A nontrivial second stabilizer
statements.label: filt:stabilizer
statements.text:
There is a nonvertex closed point of $\Spec D$ whose $T$-grading
stabilizer has order $h\geq2$.
statements.section_title: Two filtrations and a second stabilizer

statements.title: The refined slice estimate
statements.label: boot:refined-estimate
statements.section_title: The slice estimate and the supremum bootstrap

statements.title: The upper bound
statements.label: boot:upper
statements.text:
Assume the local ODP volume theorem in all dimensions smaller
than $n$.  Then $M_n\leq p_n$.  Equivalently, every singular
boundary-zero klt $n$-dimensional germ satisfies
\[
 \nvol(x,X)\leq 2(n-1)^n.
\]
statements.section_title: The slice estimate and the supremum bootstrap

statements.title: The equality cone
statements.label: boot:equality-cone
statements.text:
If a singular cone obtained in
Proposition~\ref{cone:reduction} satisfies $d(o,C)=p_n$,
then it is the standard ordinary double point cone.
statements.section_title: The slice estimate and the supremum bootstrap

statements.title: Hypersurface equality
statements.label: end:hypersurface
statements.text:
If \(x\in X\) is a singular klt hypersurface germ of
dimension \(n\ge2\), then
\[
                        \nvol(x,X)\le2(n-1)^n.
\]
If equality holds, the quadratic part of a local equation
is nondegenerate, and \((X,x)\) is analytically an ordinary
double point.

title: The p-adic section conjecture
abstract: We prove the local p-adic section conjecture for smooth proper geometrically connected curves of genus at least two, over every finite extension of ℚp. Combined with established finite-descent theorems, this also yields the global section conjecture for smooth proper geometrically connected curves of genus at least two over number fields when their finite-cover descent locus equals their rational points; this includes \(X_0(N)\) and \(X_1(N)\) of genus at least two over ℚ.
version_note: This version updates citations to revised manuscripts in this collection; see the [previous version](../The-p-adic-section-conjecture-September-24-2026/main.pdf).

tex.abstract:
We prove the local $p$-adic section conjecture for smooth proper
geometrically connected curves of genus at least two, over every finite
extension of $\mathbb Q_p$.
Combined with established finite-descent theorems, this also yields the
global section conjecture for smooth proper geometrically connected
curves of genus at least two over number fields when their finite-cover
descent locus equals their rational points; this includes $X_0(N)$ and
$X_1(N)$ of genus at least two over $\mathbb Q$.
sections: Fields, analytic points, and horizontal ramification
Replacing branch disks by trivial covers
From collar roots to the completed universal tower

statements.label: thm:section
statements.text:
For every prime $p$, every finite extension $k/\mathbb Q_p$, and every
smooth proper geometrically connected curve $X/k$ of genus at least two,
the map
\[
 X(k)\longrightarrow
 \left\{\begin{gathered}
 s:G_k\to\pi_1(X)\text{ a continuous group homomorphism}\\
 \text{such that }(\pi_1(X)\to G_k)\circ s=\mathrm{id}_{G_k}
 \end{gathered}\right\}\big/\pi_1(X_{\bar k})
\]
is bijective. The quotient is by conjugation by the full geometric
\'etale fundamental group.

statements.label: thm:completion
statements.text:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $k/\mathbb Q_p$ be finite, and let $X/k$ be a
smooth proper geometrically connected curve of genus at least two.
Put $K=k(X)$, choose a separable closure $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$, and let
$\widetilde K\subset K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ be the compositum of the function
fields of all connected finite \'etale covers of $X$, with all their
$K$-embeddings.
For every real-valued rank-one norm on $K$ extending the normalized
$p$-adic norm on $k$, and every prolongation to $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$, set
\[
 E=\widehat{K^{\mathrm{sep}}},\qquad
 H=\widehat{\widetilde K}\subset E,
\]
where the completions use that fixed prolongation.
Then the specified subfield $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ of $E$ is contained in $H$.

statements.label: prop:patching
statements.text:
Let $f:C\to X_{\bar k}$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:local-normal-form},
of degree $d$, with branch set $B$.  Choose pairwise disjoint disks $B_b$
as in that lemma.
For each $b\in B$, let $m_b$ be a positive multiple of all ramification
indices above $b$.  Suppose that $g:Y\to X_\Omega$ is a finite
surjective morphism from a smooth proper connected curve and that there
are radii $0<r_b<R_b$ in $|\Omega^\times|$, strictly inside $B_b$, such
that $g^*t_b$ has an analytic $m_b$-th root on the whole inverse image of
\[
                       A_b=\{r_b<|t_b|<R_b\}.
\]
Set
\[
 U=X_\Omega^{\mathrm{an}}\setminus
       \bigcup_{b\in B}\{|t_b|\le r_b\},
\]
where each indicated closed disk is taken inside $B_b$.
Then there is a smooth proper connected curve $V_\Omega$ and a finite
étale surjective map $V_\Omega\to Y$, together with an analytic map
\[
 (V_\Omega^{\mathrm{an}})|_U\longrightarrow C_\Omega^{\mathrm{an}}
 \quad\text{over }X_\Omega^{\mathrm{an}}.
\]
The notation on the left denotes the inverse image of $U$ under the
composite map to $X_\Omega^{\mathrm{an}}$.
statements.section_title: Replacing branch disks by trivial covers

statements.title: The first stage
statements.label: prop:first-stage
statements.text: The field $L_\ell$ is contained in $H$.

statements.title: An auxiliary branched cover
statements.label: prop:arbitrary-roots
statements.text:
Let $m\ge1$ be an integer, choose an integer
\[
 D>v_p(m)+\frac1{p-1},
\]
and let $\alpha\in\overline{k}^{\times}$ satisfy $a=v(\alpha)>2D$.
There is a smooth, proper, connected curve $Q/\overline{k}$ and a finite
map $Q\to\mathbb P^1_{\overline{k}}$ whose ramification indices divide
$\ell$, such that the pullback of the coordinate $T$ has an analytic
$m$-th root on the entire inverse image, over $\Omega$, of
\[
 A^\circ=\{D<v(T)<a-D\}.
\]

statements.label: cor:decomposition
statements.text:
Let $k/\mathbb Q_p$ be finite and let $X/k$ be a smooth proper
geometrically connected curve of genus at least two.  Put $K=k(X)$ and
let $\widetilde K\subset K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ be the extension corresponding
to the full arithmetic \'etale fundamental group of $X$.  Let $w$ be a
real-valued rank-one valuation of $K$ extending the $p$-adic valuation,
normalized by $w(p)=1$, and fix a prolongation $w^{\mathrm{sep}}$ to
$K^{\mathrm{sep}}$.  Restriction induces an isomorphism of profinite
groups
\[
 D_{w^{\mathrm{sep}}}(K^{\mathrm{sep}}/K)
 \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
 D_{\widetilde w}(\widetilde K/K),
 \qquad \widetilde w=w^{\mathrm{sep}}|_{\widetilde K}.
\]

statements.title: The localization image
statements.label: prop:localization-image

statements.title: Finite-cover descent criterion
statements.label: thm:global-descent

statements.title: Abelian targets
statements.label: cor:global-abelian-target
statements.text:
Let $C/K$ be a smooth proper geometrically connected curve of genus at
least two over a number field. The map $\kappa_C$ is bijective if either
of the following conditions holds:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
\item there is a nonconstant $K$-morphism $C\to A$ to an abelian
variety with $A(K)$ finite and $\operatorname{Sha}(A/K)_{\mathrm{div}}=0$;
\item the Jacobian $J$ of $C$ has $J(K)$ finite and
$\operatorname{Sha}(J/K)_{\mathrm{div}}=0$.
\end{enumerate}

statements.text:

genus at least two. Suppose that there is a nonconstant
$\mathbb Q$-morphism $C\to E$ to an elliptic curve and that $s_p(E)=0$
for at least one prime $p$. Then $\kappa_C$ is bijective.

statements.title: Modular curves
statements.label: cor:global-modular-curves
statements.text:
For every positive integer $N$ such that the smooth projective
geometrically connected curve $X_0(N)/\mathbb Q$ has genus at least two,
the map $\kappa_{X_0(N)}$ is bijective. The same assertion holds for the
smooth projective geometrically connected curve $X_1(N)/\mathbb Q$
whenever its genus is at least two.

title: The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties
abstract: We prove the rational Hodge conjecture for complex abelian varieties with complex multiplication: every rational Hodge class on such a variety is a rational linear combination of algebraic cycle classes. As consequences, we obtain the generalized Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, the Tate conjecture for abelian varieties over finite fields, and the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in arbitrary characteristic.
version_note: This version updates citations to revised manuscripts in this collection; see the [previous version](../The-rational-Hodge-conjecture-for-CM-abelian-varieties-September-30-2026/paper.pdf).

tex.abstract:
We prove the rational Hodge conjecture for complex abelian varieties
with complex multiplication: every rational Hodge class on such a
variety is a rational linear combination of algebraic cycle classes.
As consequences, we obtain the generalized Hodge conjecture for CM
abelian varieties, the Tate conjecture for abelian varieties over finite
fields, and the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in
arbitrary characteristic.

statements.label: thm:cm
statements.text:
Let \(A\) be a complex CM abelian variety.  For every integer
\(p\geq0\), the Betti cycle-class map
\[
 \operatorname{cl}_B:\CH^p(A)_{\Q}
 \longrightarrow H^{2p}(A,\Q)\cap H^{p,p}(A)
\]
is surjective, where \(\CH^p(A)_{\Q}=\CH^p(A)\otimes_{\Z}\Q\) and
the intersection is taken in \(H^{2p}(A,\C)\).  In particular, the
rational Hodge conjecture holds in every codimension on every finite
product of complex CM abelian varieties and on every power of such a
product.

statements.title: Four-factor switch
statements.label: thm:switch
statements.text:
Let \(E\) be a Galois CM field and let
\(v_1,v_2,v_3,v_4:G_E\to\{1,-1\}\) be odd sign functions satisfying
\(v_1+v_2=v_3+v_4\).  Under the Künneth inclusion, the following line is algebraic:
\begin{equation}
 U(v_1)_1\otimes U(v_2)_1\otimes U(v_3)_c\otimes U(v_4)_c
 \ \subset\
 H^4\!\left(\prod_{i=1}^4B(v_i),\Qbar\right)
\end{equation}

statements.label: prop:switch-reduction
statements.text:
If Theorem~\ref{thm:switch} holds for every Galois CM field and every
quadruple of odd sign functions satisfying its relation, then
Theorem~\ref{thm:cm} holds.

statements.title: Surface criterion
statements.label: prop:surface-switch
statements.text:
Let \(E\) be a Galois CM field with conjugation \(c\), and let
\(v_1,v_2,v_3,v_4:G_E\to\{1,-1\}\) be odd sign functions satisfying
\(v_1+v_2=v_3+v_4\).  Put \(\lambda=(1,1,c,c)\).
Suppose that \(S\) is a smooth connected projective complex surface
and that there are rational Hodge maps
\[
 h_i:U(v_i)\longrightarrow H^1(S,\Q),\qquad 1\leq i\leq4,
\]
and nonzero vectors
\(\alpha_i\in U(v_i)_{\lambda_i}\subset U(v_i)_{\Qbar}\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \int_S h_1(\alpha_1)\smile h_2(\alpha_2)
             \smile h_3(\alpha_3)\smile h_4(\alpha_4)\ne0.
\end{equation}
Here each \(h_i\) is extended to \(\Qbar\)-coefficients.  Then the
line in Equation~\eqref{eq:switch-line} is algebraic.
statements.section_title: A surface criterion for the switch

statements.title: Surface criterion for complex spans
statements.label: cor:surface-span
statements.text:
Let \(E\), \(v_1,\ldots,v_4\), and \(\lambda=(1,1,c,c)\) be as in
Proposition~\ref{prop:surface-switch}, and let \(S\) be a smooth
connected projective complex surface.  Suppose that, for each
\(1\leq i\leq4\), a class \(\eta_i\in H^1(S,\C)\) belongs to
\[
 \operatorname{span}_{\C}
 \{h(U(v_i)_{\lambda_i}):
       h\in\Hom_{\mathrm{Hdg}}(U(v_i),H^1(S,\Q))\}
\]
and that
\[
 \int_S\eta_1\smile\eta_2\smile\eta_3\smile\eta_4\ne0.
\]
Then the line in Equation~\eqref{eq:switch-line} is algebraic.
statements.section_title: A surface criterion for the switch

statements.label: prop:theta-one
statements.text:
For every finite input \(\phi\), the form \(\Theta_i(\phi)\) is
holomorphic on \(D\) and descends to every sufficiently deep
principal congruence quotient.  At any fixed point of \(D\), the
values \(\Theta_i(\phi)\), as \(\phi\) varies over finite
Schwartz inputs, span the cotangent fiber.  Finitely many actual
inputs already span that fiber and descend at a common sufficiently
deep principal level.
statements.section_title: Theta differentials and a nonzero mixed period

statements.label: prop:theta-top
statements.text:
The rank-two construction has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item At period data induced by a rational orthogonal
  decomposition \(W=W_1\perp W_2\), the form \(\Xi_W(\phi)\)
  is holomorphic.  On a sufficiently deep common principal
  quotient it is a finite sum, with constant coefficients, of
  forms \(\Theta_1(\phi_{1,r})\wedge\Theta_2(\phi_{2,r})\).
\item There is an input which is a product in adapted rational
  coordinates and for which \(\Xi_W(\phi)\) is nonzero.
\item Fix \(W\), the total finite input \(\phi\), and a
  torsion-free principal quotient \(X\) whose finite level fixes
  \(\phi\) under \(\omega_{W,f}\).  With locally smooth
  constant-line trivializations, the map
  \[
    t\longmapsto\Xi_W(\phi;t)
  \]
  is continuous in the \(C^\infty\) topology of differential
  forms on this fixed compact quotient.  The same finite level
  works throughout the parameter neighborhood.
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: Theta differentials and a nonzero mixed period

statements.label: cor:theta-switch-continuity
statements.text:
Suppose \(d_1+d_2=d_3+d_4\), with \(d_i(\mu)=1\) for
all \(i\).  Start with \(W=W_1\perp W_2\) as above, let
\(t_0\) be its compact-place data, and choose a total input
\(\phi\) for which
\(\xi=\Xi_W(\phi;t_0)\) is a nonzero holomorphic top form
on a sufficiently deep compact principal quotient \(X\).
There are rational orthogonal decompositions
\(W=W_3\perp W_4\) with line signs \(d_3,d_4\) whose
total compact-place positive Lagrangians are arbitrarily close
to those at \(t_0\).  The total active positive Lagrangian is
exactly unchanged.

For a sufficiently close rational choice \(t'\), the form
\(\xi'=\Xi_W(\phi;t')\) is holomorphic on the same quotient
\(X\), with the same total finite input, and
\begin{equation}
 \int_X\xi\wedge\overline{\xi'}\ne0.
\end{equation}
Both endpoints admit the wedge expansions of
Proposition~\ref{prop:theta-top} on a further common principal
cover, and their pairing remains nonzero there.
statements.section_title: Theta differentials and a nonzero mixed period

statements.title: Degree-one CM extraction
statements.label: thm:cm-extraction
statements.text:
Let \(v:G_E\to\{1,-1\}\) be odd with \(v(1)=1\), and use the
multiplicity-line theta construction prescribed by
\(d(\tau)=v(\tau^{-1})\). Given a finite collection of its finite
adelic Schwartz inputs, there is a common sufficiently deep principal
ball quotient \(S_0=\Gamma\backslash D\) on which every associated
theta one-form class belongs to
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{span}_{\C}\left\{
f\bigl(U(v)_1\bigr):
f\in\Hom_{\mathrm{Hdg}}\bigl(U(v),H^1(S_0,\Q)\bigr)
\right\}.
\end{equation}
The maps in this formula are rational Hodge maps, and their images
are viewed after extension to \(\C\). The conclusion persists after
passage to a deeper principal level.
statements.section_title: Projective ball quotients and a Frobenius identity

statements.label: prop:albanese-congruence
statements.section_title: Projective ball quotients and a Frobenius identity

statements.label: prop:theta-satake
statements.text:
Every active spherical character occurring in a theta class of
the multiplicity line \(P\) has half-modulus projective parameter
\begin{equation}
\{q^{1/2},q^{-1/2},e\},
\end{equation}
where \(e=e_0^{-1}\) for a root \(e_0^M=\omega\) from
Lemma~\ref{lem:scalar-radial-relation}.  It is algebraic and all
its complex conjugates have modulus one.  For every
\(\sigma\in\Gal(\Qbar/\Q)\),
\begin{equation}
\nu_\iota(\sigma e)
 =-\frac32d\bigl((\sigma|_E)^{-1}\bigr)
 =-\frac32v(\sigma|_E).
\end{equation}
A scalar-conjugate active character has a representative of the
form \eqref{eq:active-satake-triple} with third entry
\(e'=\pm\sigma e\).
statements.section_title: CM sources of the theta one-forms

statements.label: prop:active-hodge-types
statements.text:
Let \(\eta\) be an active numerical character with projective parameter
\(\{q^{1/2},q^{-1/2},e'\}\) supplied by
Proposition~\ref{prop:theta-satake} or by scalar conjugation, and put
\[
t_\eta=\frac12-\frac13\nu_\iota(e')\in\{0,1\}.
\]
For every full numerical character \(\chi\) extending \(\eta\), the
space \(H_\chi\otimes_{\Qbar}\C\) is contained in \(H^{1,0}(A_S)\)
if \(t_\eta=1\), and in \(H^{0,1}(A_S)\) if \(t_\eta=0\).
Consequently \(H^{\mathrm{act}}_\eta\otimes_{\Qbar}\C\) has the same
pure Hodge type.
statements.section_title: CM sources of the theta one-forms

statements.title: Finite-family CM extraction
statements.label: cor:finite-family-extraction
statements.text:
Fix \(E,V,D,\Lambda\) and the principal lattice levels of
Section~\ref{sec:arithmetic}.
Let \(v_1,\ldots,v_m:G_E\to\{1,-1\}\) be odd with \(v_j(1)=1\).
For each \(j\), choose a finite family of finite adelic Schwartz inputs
in the multiplicity-line construction
\(d_j(\tau)=v_j(\tau^{-1})\).  Let \(X_{\mathrm{base}}\) be a
principal quotient at a torsion-free level in this framework.
There is a common deeper principal cover \(Y\to X_{\mathrm{base}}\),
with \(Y\) a smooth connected projective surface, on which every
associated theta one-form class from the \(j\)-th family belongs to
\[
\operatorname{span}_{\C}\left\{
f\bigl(U(v_j)_1\bigr):
f\in\Hom_{\mathrm{Hdg}}\bigl(U(v_j),H^1(Y,\Q)\bigr)
\right\}.
\]
The maps are rational Hodge maps, with their images viewed after
extension to \(\C\).  The conclusion persists after pullback to every
deeper principal level.  The auxiliary primes used for different
\(v_j\) may differ.
statements.section_title: CM sources of the theta one-forms

statements.title: Generalized Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties
statements.label: cc:ghc
statements.text:
Let \(A\) be a complex CM abelian variety. For integers \(k,r\ge0\)
and a rational Hodge substructure \(W\subset H^k(A,\Q)\) such that
\(W(r)\) is effective, there is a closed algebraic subset \(Z\subset A\)
of codimension at least \(r\) such that
\[
 W\subset\ker\bigl(H^k(A,\Q)\longrightarrow
                         H^k(A\setminus Z,\Q)\bigr).
\]
This includes every finite product of CM abelian varieties and every
power of such a product.

statements.title: Tate conjecture for abelian varieties over finite fields
statements.label: cc:tate
statements.text:
For every abelian variety \(A/\Fq\), every integer \(r\ge0\), and every
prime \(\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(\Fq)\), the cycle-class map
\[
 \CH^r(A)\otimes_\Z\Q_\ell\longrightarrow
 H^{2r}_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(\bar A,\Q_\ell(r))^{G_q}
\]
is surjective. Numerical equivalence and \(\ell\)-adic homological
equivalence coincide on rational algebraic cycles on \(\bar A\).

statements.title: Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties
statements.label: cc:standard
statements.text:
Let \(K\) be an algebraically closed field and \(A/K\) an abelian
variety of dimension \(g\). For every prime
\(\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(K)\), numerical
and \(\ell\)-adic homological equivalence coincide on rational
algebraic cycles on \(A\). For every rational ample divisor class
\(h\) and every integer \(0\le r\le g/2\), the rational symmetric form
\[
 P_h^r(A)\times P_h^r(A)\longrightarrow\Q,\qquad
 (x,y)\longmapsto(-1)^r\deg(xy\,h^{g-2r})
\]
is positive definite after extension of scalars to \(\R\). Thus the
Hodge standard conjecture for \(\ell\)-adic étale cohomology holds
for abelian varieties in arbitrary characteristic.

withdrawal_note:
The proof relies on an adaptation of the flawed stabilization-trace construction in [Algebraicity of Weil classes on split abelian eightfolds](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/preprints/Algebraicity-of-Weil-classes-on-split-abelian-eightfolds-September-18-2026/paper.pdf). The sign error in that construction prevents the required signed-double-point cancellation. The resulting gap leaves this paper's claimed rational Hodge theorem for products of projective K3 surfaces unproved.

This withdrawal concerns the proof; it does not assert that the mathematical statement is false.

title: The reverse logarithmic Kodaira inequality and additivity

tex.abstract:
We prove the reverse logarithmic Kodaira inequality for a surjective
connected-fiber morphism $f:(X,E)\to(Y,D)$ of smooth projective
reduced simple-normal-crossing pairs, with
$\Supp(f^*D)\subseteq\Supp E$, such that $X$ and every boundary
stratum are smooth over $Y\setminus\Supp D$. Together with logarithmic
subadditivity, the inequality gives additivity, including both
negative-infinity cases. This resolves Popa's logarithmic additivity
conjecture positively in the projective reduced-SNC, stratum-smooth setting.

prop:section-construction
statements.text:
Let $f,E,D$ satisfy the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:upper-bound}, and
let $0\ne s\in H^0(X,mL_X)$ for some $m>0$. Then
$\kappa(Y,L_Y)\geq0$. If $\kappa(Y,L_Y)=0$ and $s$ vanishes identically
on $X_y$ for some $y\in V$, there are an integer $a>0$ and a nonzero
$\tau\in H^0(Y,aL_Y)$ with $\tau(y)=0$.

statements.title: Logarithmic Hodge input
statements.label: prop:logarithmic-vector
statements.text:
There are a dense smooth open $Y^\circ\subset V$, a polarizable pure
rational variation $\mathbb V$ on $Y^\circ$ with an invariant lattice
and quasi-unipotent boundary monodromy, and a nonzero algebraic map
\begin{equation}
 u:\OO_{Y^\circ}(-L_Y)\longrightarrow
 \mathcal E^d,
 \qquad
 \mathcal E^p=\Gr_F^p(\mathbb V\otimes\OO_{Y^\circ}),
 \qquad F^{d+1}\mathbb V=0.
\end{equation}
On every model $(Y',D')$ just described, the rationally identified map
and all its Higgs iterates
\begin{equation}
 \theta^j(u):\OO_{Y'}(-L_{Y'})\dashrightarrow
 \mathcal E^{d-j}\otimes(B')^{\otimes j}
\end{equation}
have regular coefficients at every prime of $Y'$ in the preceding
sense.  Here the variation and its Hodge bundles are understood over
the common dense open, and a grade outside their range is zero.

The same statement holds for the homogeneous tensor replacement used
in \Cref{prop:marked-period}.  More precisely, if $u_*$ is obtained
from $u$ by homogeneous tensor operations of positive degree $a$ and
flat Hodge-compatible projections, then
\begin{equation}
 u_*:\OO(-aL_{Y'})\dashrightarrow E_0,
 \qquad
 \theta^j(u_*):\OO(-aL_{Y'})\dashrightarrow
 E_j\otimes(B')^{\otimes j}
\end{equation}
have the same coefficient property. Here $\mathbb A$ is the resulting
pure variation, $p_*$ is its highest nonzero Hodge index, and
$E_j=\Gr_F^{p_*-j}\mathbb A$. Finite levels and a common
further unipotent ramification may be used in these assertions.

statements.title: Marked-period construction
statements.label: prop:marked-period
statements.text:
Let $B^\circ$ be a smooth irreducible complex quasi-projective variety,
and let $\mathbb V$ be a polarizable rational pure variation with an
invariant integral lattice.  Suppose that a line bundle $\mathcal L$ has
a generically nonzero algebraic morphism
\[
 u:\mathcal L\longrightarrow F^p\mathbb V_{\C},
 \qquad F^{p+1}\mathbb V_{\C}=0.
\]
There are a positive integer $a$, a homogeneous tensor construction
followed by flat Hodge-compatible projections, and a generically nonzero
morphism
\begin{equation}
 u_*:\mathcal L^{\otimes a}\longrightarrow E_0,
 \qquad E_0=F^{p_*}\mathbb A,
 \qquad F^{p_*+1}\mathbb A=0,
\end{equation}
where $\mathbb A$ is a polarized complex pure variation.  The operations
may first be performed equivariantly at finite monodromy level.  They
descend to $B^\circ$ after shrinking it.  On smooth projective
birational models there is a dominant morphism
$b:B\to S$ with connected fibers and the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Descent.} On dense smooth opens, $\mathbb A$ is the pullback of an actual
variation on $S^\circ$.  Its connected representation is irreducible
and factors through a rational semisimple adjoint group $G$.  The full
monodromy acts through its projected action on
$\mathfrak g=\Lie G$.  In particular, finite scalar monodromy in the
kernel of that action has been eliminated.
\item \emph{The marks.} There is an algebraic compact-flag section $j_{\mathrm u}$,
possibly empty, determined pointwise and equivariantly by $[u_*]$.
In flat coordinates the joint marks
\[
 j=(E_0,j_{\mathrm u})
\]
take values in a closed product flag orbit $J$ of $G_{\C}$.  The two
kinds of marks use disjoint complex simple factors.  Every rational
simple factor of $G$ has a complex factor acting nontrivially on $J$.
The full Lie-period map together with $j_{\mathrm u}$ is generically
immersive on $S^\circ$.
\item \emph{The nef lines and adjoint positivity.} If $S$ is a point, $\mathbb A$ is constant and we set
$\mathcal H=\mathcal H_{\mathrm u}=0$.  Otherwise $S$ has
nef rational line bundles $\mathcal H$ and $\mathcal H_{\mathrm u}$,
with $\mathcal H-\mathcal H_{\mathrm u}$ nef.  On a smooth unipotent
connected-monodromy cover their pullbacks are respectively
\[
 \det E_0+\mathcal H_{\mathrm u}
 \quad\hbox{and the positive compact-flag line.}
\]
The generic curvature rank of $\mathcal H$ is the generic rank of
$dj$, and equals $\nu(\mathcal H)$.  If $D_0$ denotes the reduced
union of boundary components with nonidentity local monodromy on
$\mathfrak g$, then
\begin{equation}
 K_S+D_0+c\mathcal H_{\mathrm u}\quad\text{is big for }c\gg0.
\end{equation}
Furthermore,
\begin{equation}
 K_S+b_0\mathcal H\quad\text{is big for }b_0\gg0.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
All assertions about extensions are compatible with further smooth
projective modifications and pullback at unipotent level.  In
particular, the iterated Higgs fields of $u_*$ are polynomial tensor
expressions in those of $u$; the construction introduces no division
by a local function.
