statements.label: thm:main

statements.title: Even functional Mahler inequality
statements.label: cor:functional-mahler
statements.text:
For every integer $n\ge1$ and every even proper lower-semicontinuous
convex function $\varphi:\R^n\to\R\cup\{+\infty\}$ such that
$0<\int_{\R^n}e^{-\varphi(x)}\,dx<\infty$,
\[
 \left(\int_{\R^n}e^{-\varphi(x)}\,dx\right)
 \left(\int_{\R^n}e^{-\varphi^*(y)}\,dy\right)\ge4^n.
\]
The second integral is allowed to be infinite, in which case the
inequality is immediate.

statements.title: Symmetric entropy--transport inequality
statements.label: cor:entropy-transport
statements.text:
For every integer $n\ge1$, let $\eta_i(dx)=e^{-V_i(x)}\,dx$, $i=1,2$,
be full-dimensional log-concave probability measures, both symmetric
about the origin, with proper lower-semicontinuous convex potentials
$V_i$. Suppose their densities are essentially continuous, meaning that
$e^{-V_i}=0$ at $\mathcal H^{n-1}$-almost every point of
$\partial\operatorname{supp}\eta_i$. Their moment measures
$\nu_i=(\nabla V_i)_\#\eta_i$ have finite first moments,
$H(\eta_i)=-\int V_i\,d\eta_i$ is finite, and
\[
 H(\eta_1)+H(\eta_2)\le -n\log(4e^2)+\mathcal T(\nu_1,\nu_2).
\]

statements.title: Feasible-simplex identity
statements.label: prop:simplex-integral
statements.text:
Let $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ be nonzero, pairwise nonproportional real rows
spanning $(\R^d)^*$, and let $F,D,\lambda$ be as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:planar-lens}. With $A$, $S$, and $\Sigma_X$ defined in
\eqref{eq:strip-body}, \eqref{eq:feasible-probabilities}, and
\eqref{eq:feasible-simplex-union}, respectively,
\begin{equation}
 1\leq S
   =\frac{d!}{4^d}\int_A|\Sigma_X|\,dX
   \leq\frac{d!}{4^d}|A|\,|A^\circ|.
\end{equation}
In particular, $|A|\,|A^\circ|\geq4^d/d!$, and
\begin{equation}
 0\leq\int_A\bigl(|A^\circ|-|\Sigma_X|\bigr)\,dX
       \leq |A|\,|A^\circ|-\frac{4^d}{d!}.
\end{equation}

statements.title: The symmetric volume-product inequality
statements.label: cor:symmetric-inequality
statements.text:
For every origin-symmetric convex body $K\subset\R^d$, $d\geq1$,
\[
 |K|\,|K^\circ|\geq\frac{4^d}{d!}.
\]

statements.title: A representation minimizing the lens cost
statements.label: prop:optimal-representation
statements.text:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge1$, be an origin-symmetric convex body
with $P(K)=4^n/n!$. Put $Q=K^\circ$, $d=n+1$, and define the lifted
bodies $B,C$ by \eqref{eq:segment-lift}.
For every $X\in\operatorname{int}B$ and every nonzero
$\xi=(q,a)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R$, put
\[
 T=p_C(\xi)=\max\{p_Q(q),|a|\}.
\]
There are $1\le r\le d$ vectors $c_i=(b_i,\sigma_i)$ with
$b_i\in Q$ and $\sigma_i\in\{-1,1\}$, nonnegative numbers
$\alpha_i$, and a vector $Y\in\mathbb R^d$, such that
\begin{equation}
 \xi=\sum_{i=1}^r\alpha_i c_i,
 \qquad \sum_{i=1}^r\alpha_i=T,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 |h\cdot Y|\le\lambda(h\cdot X)\quad(h\in C),
 \qquad
 c_i\cdot Y=\lambda(c_i\cdot X)\quad(1\le i\le r).
\end{equation}
In particular, for every finite representation
$\xi=\sum_{j=1}^s\beta_jh_j$ with $\beta_j\ge0$ and $h_j\in C$,
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{i=1}^r\alpha_i\lambda(c_i\cdot X)
 \le \sum_{j=1}^s\beta_j\lambda(h_j\cdot X).
\end{equation}
The choices may depend on $X$ and $\xi$; the same choice satisfies
\eqref{eq:optimal-cost} for all the competing representations.

statements.title: Medians of an equality body
statements.label: prop:metric-median
statements.text:
Let $K\subset\R^n$, $n\ge1$, be an origin-symmetric convex body with
$P(K)=4^n/n!$, and put $Q=K^\circ$. Every triple of points in
$(\R^n,p_Q)$ has a metric median.

statements.text:

title: The trace cone classifies Razak–Jacelon stabilizations
abstract: We prove that the canonical topological cone of all extended lower-semicontinuous tracial weights determines a separable nuclear C∗-algebra after tensoring with the Razak–Jacelon algebra and the compact operators, answering Robert's trace-cone classification question positively. The isomorphism realizes the prescribed cone map, with arbitrary ideal structure and without a density assumption on the finite domains of the weights.

tex.abstract:
We prove that the canonical topological cone of all extended
lower-semicontinuous tracial weights determines a separable nuclear
\(C^*\)-algebra after tensoring with the Razak--Jacelon algebra and the
compact operators, answering Robert's trace-cone classification question
positively. The isomorphism realizes the prescribed cone map, with
arbitrary ideal structure and without a density assumption on the finite
domains of the weights.
sections: The invariant, its ideals, and matrix conventions
Sequence models and local error ideals

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let \(A\) and \(B\) be separable nuclear complex \(C^*\)-algebras.
If \(T(A)\) and \(T(B)\) are isomorphic as topological cones, then
\[
 A\otimes\W\otimes\K\ \cong\ B\otimes\W\otimes\K,
\]
where \(\K=\K(\ell^2(\N))\) and all tensor products are spatial.

statements.title: Trace realification
statements.label: st:realification
statements.text:
For every \(C^*\)-algebra \(C\), the trace cone with topology
\eqref{intro:trace-topology} is compact Hausdorff, and it is second
countable when \(C\) is separable. If \(C\) is exact, the assignment
\(\tau\mapsto d_\tau\) identifies this cone with the topological
cone of functionals on \(\Cu(C)\).

For every \(C^*\)-algebra \(C\),
\[
 \Cu(C\otimes\W)\cong\Cu(C)_{\R}.
\]
Realification is determined functorially by the topological functional
cone. Its realization as functions on that cone has pointwise order,
pointwise addition, and multiplication by positive real scalars.
It has the same functional cone as \(\Cu(C)\).

Consequently the given trace-cone isomorphism induces isomorphisms
\begin{equation}
 F:T(Q)\longrightarrow T(P),\qquad
 G:\Cu(P)\longrightarrow\Cu(Q),\qquad
 d_\tau(Gx)=d_{F\tau}(x).
\end{equation}
In particular, for \(x,y\in\Cu(Q)\),
\begin{equation}
 x\leq y
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 d_\tau(x)\leq d_\tau(y)\quad\hbox{for every }\tau\in T(Q).
\end{equation}
Multiplication by every positive real scalar is an order automorphism
preserving increasing suprema and compact containment.
statements.section_title: The invariant, its ideals, and matrix conventions

statements.title: Transport of ideals
statements.label: st:ideals
statements.text:
The maps \(F,G\) identify the complete ideal lattices of \(P\) and
\(Q\), and these identifications agree. They identify the finite
and zero ideals of corresponding weights. The resulting
homeomorphism of primitive ideal spaces will be used to regard
\(\Prim(P)=\Prim(Q)=X\). For an open \(U\subseteq X\), write
\(P(U)\) and \(Q(U)\) for the corresponding ideals. Then
\[
 G(\Cu(P(U)))=\Cu(Q(U)),
\]
and
\[
 \Fin(\tau)=Q(U)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \Fin(F\tau)=P(U),
 \qquad
 \Ker(\tau)=Q(U)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \Ker(F\tau)=P(U).
\]
statements.section_title: The invariant, its ideals, and matrix conventions

statements.title: Regularized limits
statements.label: seq:regularized
statements.text:
Let \(\omega\) be a free ultrafilter on \(\N\), and let
\(\tau_n\in T(Q)\) be arbitrary. For a bounded positive sequence
\((x_n)\), the formula
\begin{equation}
 \rho([(x_n)])=
 \sup_{\eps>0}\lim_{n\to\omega}\tau_n((x_n-\eps)_+)
\end{equation}
defines a lower-semicontinuous tracial weight on \(D\).
Its rank functional is
\begin{equation}
 d_\rho([(x_n)])=
 \sup_{\eps>0}\lim_{n\to\omega}d_{\tau_n}((x_n-\eps)_+).
\end{equation}
If \(\sigma=\lim_{n\to\omega}\tau_n\) in the canonical topology
on \(T(Q)\), then \(\rho|_Q=\sigma\).
statements.section_title: Sequence models and local error ideals

statements.title: Sandwich comparisons
statements.label: seq:sandwich
statements.text:
Let \(p:S_Y\to D\) be a model, let \(s=f\otimes a\geq0\), and
suppose that \(0<m_0:=m(f>0)<\infty\). For \(r>0\), choose
\(c_r\in Q_+\) representing \(rG[a]\). Then
\begin{equation}
 c_r\precsim p(s)\quad(0<r<m_0),
 \qquad
 p(s)\precsim c_r\quad(r>m_0).
\end{equation}
The following versions have fixed target cuts.

If \(\eta,\delta>0\), \(0<r<m(f>\eta)\), and \(c\) represents
\(rG[(a-\delta)_+]\), then, for every \(0<\kappa<\eta\delta\),
\begin{equation}
 c\precsim(p(f\otimes a)-\kappa)_+.
\end{equation}
If \(r'>m_0\) and \(\eps>0\), then a representative \(b\) of
\(r'G[a]\) has a positive cut \((b-\kappa)_+\) such that
\begin{equation}
 (p(f\otimes a)-\eps)_+\precsim(b-\kappa)_+.
\end{equation}
The choices in these two displays can be made independently of
the model \(p\). The complete collection of such comparisons on
the countable compact tests characterizes the model equation.
statements.section_title: Sequence models and local error ideals

statements.title: Constant ideals and all traces
statements.label: seq:all-traces
statements.section_title: Sequence models and local error ideals

statements.title: Properties of the local error ideals
statements.label: seq:smallideal-properties
statements.section_title: Sequence models and local error ideals

statements.title: Small stabilizers
statements.label: sm:stabilizers
statements.text:
Let \(S=C_0(Y)\otimes P\), and prescribe countably many pairs
\[
 x_l\in S_+,
 \qquad e_l\in J(U_{x_l}),
 \qquad l\in\N.
\]
There is a homomorphism \(\theta:S\to D\) satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \theta(S(U))\subseteq J(U),
 \qquad
 e_l\in\Ideal_D(\theta(x_l))
 \quad(U\subseteq X\text{ open},\ l\in\N),
\end{equation}
in either of the following situations.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item An existing model \(\chi:S\to D\) is given.
In this case \(\theta\) can be a slowly vanishing rational UHF
fraction of \(\chi\), and it also satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \theta(S(U_x))\subseteq\Ideal_D(\theta(x))
 \qquad(x\in S_+).
\end{equation}
For every fixed \(N\), \(N\) copies of its defining fraction
fit in the defining copy of \(\chi\) at all sufficiently late
coordinates.
\item \(Y=(0,1]\).  No model is needed in this case, and
\eqref{sm:coarse-fullness} is not asserted.
\end{enumerate}
In both cases, for every \(l\) and \(\eps>0\) there is
\(\delta_{l,\eps}>0\) such that
\begin{equation}
 [ (|e_l|-\eps)_+]
 \leq[(\theta(x_l)-\delta_{l,\eps})_+]
 \quad\text{in }\Cu(D).
\end{equation}
The construction permits the prescribed errors and the stabilizer
to occupy separate matrix corners.

statements.title: Simultaneous coefficient domination
statements.label: sm:coefficient-domination
statements.text:
Suppose that one of the hypotheses of
\Cref{sm:stabilizers} holds.  Let \(E_j\) be countably
many bounded multilinear maps
\[
 E_j:S\times Z_{j,1}\times\cdots\times Z_{j,r_j}\longrightarrow D,
\]
where the parameter spaces are separable normed spaces.
Assume that
\[
 E_j(S(U),Z_{j,1},\ldots,Z_{j,r_j})\subseteq J(U)
 \quad\text{for every open }U.
\]
Then the stabilizer may also be chosen so that, for every
\(x\in S_+\),
\begin{equation}
 E_j(S(U_x),Z_{j,1},\ldots,Z_{j,r_j})
 \subseteq\Ideal_D(\theta(x)).
\end{equation}
The same conclusion holds for norm-continuous separably
parametrized families of such maps, with local norm bounds,
and for any choice of the localized multilinear input.

statements.title: Norm uniqueness
statements.label: un:uniqueness
statements.text:
Let $p,q:S_Y\to Q_\infty$ be models for the same data.  For any
c.p.c. lifts $p_n,q_n:S_Y\to Q$, there are
$u_n\in\mathcal U(\mathcal M(Q))$ such that
\[
 \lim_{n\to\infty}\|u_np_n(a)u_n^*-q_n(a)\|=0,
 \qquad a\in S_Y.
\]

statements.title: Ideal-related absorption
statements.label: un:absorption
statements.text:
Let $S$ be separable, exact, and lower semicontinuous over $X$, and
let $H$ be sigma-unital.  Suppose
$\theta:S\to H\otimes\K$ is a nuclear $X$-full homomorphism, meaning
\[
 \Ideal_{H\otimes\K}(\theta(a))=H(U_a)\otimes\K
 \qquad(a\in S_+).
\]
Then its infinite repeat is weakly $X$-nuclear and absorbs every
weakly $X$-nuclear representation on the standard module, by unitary
equivalences with compact errors tending to zero on each input.

statements.title: Multiplier stable uniqueness
statements.label: un:stable-uniqueness
statements.text:
Suppose $S$ is separable, nuclear, and lower semicontinuous over $X$,
$H$ is sigma-unital, and $\theta:S\to H\otimes\K$ is an $X$-full
homomorphism.
Let $\phi,\psi:S\to\mathcal L(E_H)$ be weakly equivariant
representations with compact difference and $[\phi,\psi]_X=0$.
Writing $\theta^\infty$ for an infinite repeat, for every finite
$\mathcal F\subset S$ and $\eps>0$ there is a unitary
$v\in1+\mathcal K(E_H\oplus E_H)$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \|v(\phi\oplus\theta^\infty)(a)v^*
       -(\psi\oplus\theta^\infty)(a)\|<\eps,
 \qquad a\in\mathcal F.
\end{equation}

statements.title: Uniqueness with a spare model
statements.label: un:spare
statements.text:
Let $p,q:S\to D$ be equal-data models satisfying
$(p-q)(S(U))\subseteq J(U)$ for every open $U$.  Let $\chi$ be a
model for a strictly positive multiple of the same data.  Then
$p\oplus\chi$ and $q\oplus\chi$ are coordinate approximately
unitarily equivalent, with the matrix and trace conventions of
\Cref{st:folding}.

statements.label: tc:rough-model

statements.title: Simultaneous finite approximation
statements.label: tc:finite-convexity

statements.title: Cone correction
statements.label: cc:correction
statements.text:
Suppose $h:S\to D$ is \cpc and satisfies
\eqref{cc:mixed-defects}.  After trace-preserving coordinate
corner padding, there is a homomorphism $\lambda:S\to D$ such
that
\begin{equation}
 (\lambda-h^{\mathrm{pad}})(S(U))\subset J(U)
 \qquad(U\subset X\text{ open}).
\end{equation}
The padding can be chosen to fix the constant copy of $Q$ in
the sequence quotient.  Consequently it preserves the constant
ideal comparisons and the regularized trace formulas prescribed
for $h$.

statements.title: Existence of cone models
statements.label: cc:cone-existence
statements.text:
Let $m$ be a finite full-support Radon measure on $(0,1]$.
There is a homomorphism $p:S\to D$ such that, for every
regularized limit trace $\rho$ with $\sigma=\rho|_Q$,
\begin{equation}
 \rho\circ p=m\otimes F(\sigma).
\end{equation}
This includes weights whose densely finite ideal is proper
or zero.

statements.title: A covariant line model
statements.label: pt:suspension
statements.text:
There is a model
\[
 \lambda:C_0(\R)\otimes P\longrightarrow D
\]
for Lebesgue measure and \(F\).
Let \(\alpha(f)(t)=f(t-1)\), acting trivially on \(P\).
For c.p.c. coordinate lifts \(\lambda_n\), there are
unitaries \(u_n\in M(Q)\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \|\Ad(u_n)(\lambda_n(s))-\lambda_n(\alpha(s))\|
 \longrightarrow0\qquad(s\in C_0(\R)\otimes P).
\end{equation}

statements.title: Existence of point models
statements.label: pt:point-model
statements.text:
There is a homomorphism \(\varphi:P\to Q_\infty\) such that
\[
 \rho\circ\varphi=F(\rho|_Q)
\]
for every regularized limit \(\rho\).

statements.title: An actual homomorphism
statements.label: pt:actual-map
statements.text:
There is a homomorphism \(\phi:P\to Q\) satisfying
\[
 \tau\circ\phi=F(\tau)\qquad(\tau\in T(Q)),
 \qquad \Cu(\phi)=G.
\]
It is injective, and its constant sequence is a point model.

statements.title: Trace-cone classification
statements.label: pt:intertwining
statements.text:
There is an isomorphism \(\Phi:P\to Q\) such that
\[
 \tau\circ\Phi=F(\tau)\quad(\tau\in T(Q)),
 \qquad \Cu(\Phi)=G.
\]
Consequently \Cref{thm:main} holds.

title: The two-primary Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer formula in Selmer corank at most one
abstract: We prove the two-primary Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer leading-term formula for every elliptic curve over the rationals whose two-power Selmer group has corank at most one. In this range, the algebraic rank, analytic rank, and Selmer corank are equal, and the Tate–Shafarevich group is finite. Combined with the quadratic-twist Selmer distribution, this gives the exact two-primary formula for a density-one set of signed squarefree twists of each fixed curve, ordered by absolute value; the common rank is zero or one, with each value having density one half.
version_note: This version updates citations to revised manuscripts in this collection; see the [previous version](../The-two-primary-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-formula-in-Selmer-corank-at-most-one-September-24-2026/paper.pdf).

tex.abstract: We prove the two-primary Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer leading-term formula for every elliptic curve over the rationals whose two-power Selmer group has corank at most one. In this range, the algebraic rank, analytic rank, and Selmer corank are equal, and the Tate--Shafarevich group is finite. Combined with the quadratic-twist Selmer distribution, this gives the exact two-primary formula for a density-one set of signed squarefree twists of each fixed curve, ordered by absolute value; the common rank is zero or one, with each value having density one half.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let \(E/\mathbb Q\) be any elliptic curve with \(s_2(E)\leq1\).
Then
\[
 r:=\operatorname{rank}E(\mathbb Q)
   =\operatorname{ord}_{s=1}L(E,s)=s_2(E),
 \qquad \#\Sha(E/\mathbb Q)<\infty.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 Q_E=\frac{L^{(r)}(E,1)\,(\#T_E)^2}
 {r!\,\Omega_E\Reg_E\prod_{\ell\ \mathrm{finite}}c_\ell(E)}
 \in\mathbb Q_{>0},
 \qquad
 v_2(Q_E)=v_2\bigl(\#\Sha(E/\mathbb Q)\bigr).
\]
There is no restriction on \(E[2]\) or on the reduction of \(E\) at two.

statements.title: An any-prime input criterion
statements.label: cor:any-prime-bsd
statements.text:
Let \(E/\mathbb Q\) be an elliptic curve. Suppose that, for some prime
\(p\), its full \(p\)-power Selmer group with the usual local Kummer
conditions at every place satisfies
\[
 s_p(E):=\corank_{\mathbb Z_p}\Sel_{p^\infty}(E/\mathbb Q)\le1.
\]
Then all conclusions of Theorem~\ref{thm:main} hold, with common rank
\(r=s_p(E)\).

statements.title: Positive comparison
statements.label: prop:positive
statements.text:
Let \(A/\mathbb Q\) be non-CM.  If \(\an(A)\leq1\), then
\(X(A)\geq0\).  Suppose a positive fundamental discriminant \(a\)
prime to \(2N_A\), or \(a=1\), satisfies
\(\an(A^a)\leq1\) and \(X(A^a)=0\).  Then \(s_2(A)\leq1\)
implies \(\an(A)=s_2(A)\) and \(X(A)=0\).

statements.title: Split-pair anchor
statements.label: prop:anchor
statements.text:
Let \(A/\mathbb Q\) be non-CM.  There exist a fundamental
discriminant \(h\) prime to \(2N_A\), allowing \(h=1\), and an
imaginary quadratic field of discriminant \(k\) prime to \(2hN_A\),
in which all primes dividing \(2hN_A\) split, such that
\[
 \an(A^h)+\an(A^{hk})=1,
 \qquad X(A^h)+X(A^{hk})=0.
\]

statements.title: CM comparison
statements.label: prop:cm
statements.text:
If \(A/\mathbb Q\) has complex multiplication and \(s_2(A)\leq1\),
then \(\an(A)=s_2(A)\) and \(X(A)=0\).

statements.title: Split Gross--Zagier formula
statements.label: thm:classical-gz
statements.text:
With the preceding hypotheses and units modulo signs one,
\[
 \frac{\sqrt D}{8\pi^2(f,f)_N}\,L'(f/K,1)=2H_{\rm abs,f}(P_X).
 \tag{GZ}
\]

statements.title: The full-index discrepancy
statements.label: cor:classical-G
statements.text:
Under these assumptions, the single Hilbert-class trace satisfies
\[
  X(E)+X(E^k)
  =v_2\!\left(\frac{[E(K):\mathbb ZP]^2}
      {c_E^2\,\prod_\ell c_\ell(E)^2\ \#\Sha(E/K)}\right).       \tag{G}
\]
Here \([E(K):\mathbb ZP]\) is the full group index, including torsion.

statements.title: Integral classes and dyadic compatibility
statements.label: prop:siegel-integral
statements.text:
The classes obtained from \eqref{eq:K1} are integral for support containing
the primes of \(2n_2\) and infinity.  They are compatible with the dyadic
division traces and, after the mark and determinant projection, with
corestriction as the dyadic part of \(M\) increases with \(c,d,A,\xi\)
fixed.  The projected smoothed classes on \(\mathbb Q\), with group or
character coefficients, admit integral lifts to ordinary positive
cohomology.
statements.section_title: A Siegel-unit period and lattice calculation

statements.title: The full-level differential
statements.label: prop:siegel-reciprocity
statements.text:
In square order, the dual exponential of the inverse-root-twisted trace
\eqref{eq:K1}, before cuspidal projection, is on each determinant component
a scalar multiple of
\[
  (c^2 E_P-c E_{cP})(d^2 E_Q-d E_{dQ})\,\frac{dq}{q}.     \tag{K2}
\]
The scalar is
\[
                              \pm M^{-2},               \tag{K3}
\]
with one common sign determined by the cup, pairing, and orientation
conventions.  The statement holds for all \(c,d\) prime to \(6M\).
statements.section_title: A Siegel-unit period and lattice calculation

statements.title: Good-prime norms and rectangular filling
statements.label: prop:siegel-norms
statements.text:
For either order pattern, adjoining a fresh prime
\(\ell\nmid cdn_2L\) to both orders and to \(M\) gives, after the
elliptic projection, the rational norm multiplier
\[
                   1-\frac{a_\ell(f)[\ell]}{\ell}
                               +\frac{[\ell]^2}{\ell}.
\]
The trace defining this norm is integral.  At complete splitting in a
lower abelian field the scalar is
\(\det(1-\rho_T(\mathrm{Fr}_\ell))/\ell\).

In rectangular order, let \(q_0^a\parallel b\), \(q_0\nmid b_1\).
At a finite even field character \(\nu\) of conductor dividing \(M\),
filling \(q_0^a\) into the first row gives the rational identity
\[
 z_{\mathrm{filled}}
       =\bigl(1-a_{q_0}(f)\nu(q_0)/q_0\bigr)
                                      z_{\mathrm{before}}.
\]
statements.section_title: A Siegel-unit period and lattice calculation

statements.title: The period formula
statements.label: prop:siegel-period
statements.text:
Use square order or first-row-unfilled rectangular order \(b_1=1\).
Suppose \(c,d\equiv1\pmod L\), and let \(\nu\) be an even finite
character of \(\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb Q(\mu_M)/\mathbb Q)\).
For the projected, weighted class \(z_\nu\), the coefficient of its
dual exponential relative to \(\omega\) is
\[
 \pm\Delta_\nu\,
       \frac{L^{(M)}(f,\nu,1)}{\Omega_0}\,\delta_\xi(a),
 \qquad
 \Delta_\nu=(c^2-c\nu(c)^{-1})(d^2-d\nu(d)^{-1}).
                                                        \tag{K4}
\]
Here \(L^{(M)}(f,\nu,s)\) twists the Fourier coefficients by \(\nu\)
and omits every prime dividing \(M\).  Scalars are compared in the
algebraic differential realizations and the fixed embeddings.  The
sign is common across the symbols.  No character-orbit average occurs.
statements.section_title: A Siegel-unit period and lattice calculation

statements.title: Primitive evaluation and positive twisting
statements.label: cor:siegel-positive-twist
statements.text:
For the square construction with \(A=1\), one may use an integral
combination of symbols with \(\delta(a)=1\) and common smoothing
integers.  If a fixed positive fundamental quadratic character
\(\chi_h\), prime to \(2N\), is included in the field weight, the
integral coefficient identification with the twist \(E'^{\,h}\)
transports \eqref{eq:K4} to the corresponding twist-period formula,
with its actual smoothing factors and omissions.
statements.section_title: A Siegel-unit period and lattice calculation

statements.title: Integral positive determinant
statements.label: prop:positive-determinant:integral
statements.text:
The auxiliary tuples \(R_i\) can be chosen with the following properties.
The construction permits one prescribed sequence among their entries, provided
that it satisfies the varying-support and cyclic-quotient conditions above,
splits on \(W\) and in the fixed twisting field, and has a limiting Tate
Frobenius matrix of determinant one and trace different from two.

The complex \(C^+\otimes_B B_{(2)}\) is a free module of rank two in degree
one, up to homotopy. Generically over \(B\), the tensor \(a\wedge z\) is
nonzero and gives a coordinate \(U_{\rm raw}\in\operatorname{Frac}B\) relative
to a generator of \(\mathcal D(C^+)\). In a simultaneous twist comparison the
generator is inherited from the common diagram before the two character
evaluations. The tensor is independent of the positive lift of \(z\) after
passing to the fraction field.

Define the normalized coordinate by
\[
 U=\frac{U_{\rm raw}}{\Delta}
                    \prod_{\substack{q\in S_f\\q\ne2}}\frac{D_q}{P_q},
 \qquad
 D_q=\det(1-\chi({\rm Fr}_q)\rho_T({\rm Fr}_q)/q\mid V_{I_q}).   \tag{L1}
\]
Here \(I_q\) indicates inertia and the subscript in \(V_{I_q}\) takes coinvariants. \(P_q\) is the \emph{actual} local inverse \(L\)-polynomial at 1 of the curve being tested with the unramified scalar twist in the period-law orientation. \(\Delta\) is the smoothing factor of \eqref{eq:K4} with the actual field weight including the fixed character if present. All exponents in this formula are the limiting exponents. There is no
\(D/P\) correction for a moving place. The assertion is that \(U\in B\setminus\{0\}\).
If the construction is made simultaneously for \(E'\) and a positive
fundamental twist \(E'^{(h)}\), the two reductions of \(U\) differ by a unit
of \(B/2B\). In particular, they are simultaneously units at the closed point.

statements.title: Generic nonvanishing and the first divisibilities
statements.label: cor:positive-determinant:generic
statements.text:
The positive complex has only degree-one generic cohomology, of dimension
two, and \(a\wedge z\ne0\). The coordinate \(U\) has nonnegative order at
every height-one prime outside the fixed factors
\(2\Delta\prod_{q\in S_f,\,q\ne2}D_qP_q\).

statements.title: Tame logarithmic comparison
statements.label: tame:logarithm
statements.text:
Suppose \(\an(E)=1\), and let \(P\in E(\Q)\) be nontorsion. Then
\[
 \frac{\log_\omega z}{(\log_\omega P)^2}
   =\pm d_0\,\frac{L'(f,1)}{\Omega_0H(P)}.
 \tag{T1}
\]
The complex-side quotient is rational, and is viewed in a fixed dyadic
embedding. Here \(H\) is the height fixed in the introduction.

statements.title: Spectral-height comparison
statements.label: tame:spectral

statements.title: Intersection realization
statements.label: tame:intersection
statements.text:
The negative of the local sum in Lemma~\ref{tame:local-divisor},
summed over \(C_0,y_0,b\), is the intersection of the oriented
Hilbert-class sum based at \(\infty\) with \(T_m\) of the same
sum based at \(0\), at the places of \(K\) over \(q\), weighted
by their residue degrees over \(q\).

statements.title: Positivity and transfer of a central unit
statements.label: cor:positive-completion:unit
statements.text:
The following assertions hold for a non-CM curve \(A\).
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item If \(\mathrm{an}(A)\le1\), then \(X(A)\ge0\).
\item Suppose the positive twist hypothesis of Proposition~\ref{prop:positive}
holds, without assuming the analytic rank of \(A\). Then the positive
determinant of \(E'\) is a unit for every completed auxiliary-prime
construction permitted by Proposition~\ref{prop:positive-determinant:integral},
including those with one prescribed admissible sequence. If \(s_2(E')=0\),
then \(\mathrm{an}(E')=0\) and \(X(E')=0\).
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Reducible split-product comparison
statements.label: split-measures:reducible-input
statements.text:
Let \(E/\mathbb Q\) be a non-CM elliptic curve with
\(E(\mathbb Q)[2]\ne0\), and put \(N=\mathrm{cond}(E)\).
Let \(d\equiv7\pmod {16}\) be prime and suppose that every prime dividing
\(2N\) splits in \(K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-d})\).  If \(s_2(E/K)=1\), then
\(L(E/K,s)=L(E,s)L(E^{-d},s)\) has a simple zero at \(1\), and
\[
                              X(E)+X(E^{-d})=0 .
\]
If the product is already known to have a simple zero at \(1\), the same
valuation identity holds without separately assuming the Selmer corank
condition.
statements.section_title: Split Heegner determinants and\\paired logarithmic measures

statements.title: Character and central interpolation
statements.label: split-measures:interpolation
statements.text:
Let \(\theta\) be a sufficiently high finite character of \(\Gamma\), and
let \(\theta_l=\theta\circ\eta\) have primitive conductor \(2^m\).
Let \(X\) be the point with \(z=\zeta_{2^m}\) in the base disk, at the
original primitive level, and put \(\chi=\theta\psi_s\).  Then
\[
 \left(\sum_{j\ {\rm odd}\bmod 2^m}\theta_l(j)\zeta_{2^m}^{j}\right) b_s(\theta,u)
     =
 \left(\sum_{\rho\in\operatorname{Pic}(\mathcal O_{2^m s})}
                        \chi(\rho)\,G(X^\rho)\right)
                         \prod_{\ell\in S^\circ}P_\ell(\chi(\sigma_\ell)).
                                                                    \tag{M2}
\]
Here \(\sigma_\ell\) is the inverse class translation for the oriented
\(V_\ell\), namely one of the two Frobenius classes.  At the trivial
character in \(t\), the corresponding identity is the sum over
\(\operatorname{Pic}(\mathcal O_s)\) of the disk-center logarithms, with
its odd Euler factors and the additional factor
\(P_2(\psi_s(\sigma_2))\).  For the elliptic curve \(E\), when
\(S^\circ\) is precisely the set of odd primes dividing \(N\), this gives
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 B(0)=\pm c_E^{-2}\log_{\omega_E}(P)^2
       \prod_{\ell\mid2N}P_\ell(1)^2,\\
 P=\sum_{\rho\in\operatorname{Pic}(\mathcal O_K)}
       \phi(X_1^\rho)\in E(K).
 \end{gathered}
 \tag{M3}
\]
where \(X_1\) is a split Heegner point of conductor one.
statements.section_title: Split Heegner determinants and\\paired logarithmic measures

statements.title: Inert derivative identity
statements.label: split-local:derivative
statements.text:
Fix a finite collection of auxiliary inert prime sequences satisfying
the full-Tate approximation conditions above
Lemma~\ref{split-local:inert-planes}.  Over the lower conductor fields
\(H_{b_i}\), form the compatible CM points and derivative operators
\(D_I\) of Lemma~\ref{split-local:descent}, using its common nonzero
multiplier \(L\) for this collection.  Let \(Z_I\) be their descended,
\(\chi\)-weighted corestrictions to \(K\), transferred to the limiting
coefficient model.  In the finite and singular coordinates
\(f_{\rm loc},s_{\rm loc}\) of
Lemma~\ref{split-local:inert-planes}, at a newly switched prime
\(\ell\notin I\) one has
\[
 s_{\rm loc}(Z_{I\cup\{\ell\}})=J f_{\rm loc}(Z_I),
                 \qquad f_{\rm loc}(Z_{I\cup\{\ell\}})=0,             \tag{K}
\]
and the transverse condition in the second identity holds at every switched prime. The identities persist after any fixed equivariant projection onto a Hecke plane, with its denominators absorbed in the common \(L\).
statements.section_title: Local comparisons on horizontal tests\\of the split determinant

statements.title: Selmer membership and the logarithmic comparison
statements.label: split-local:point-measure
statements.text:
For the horizontal test currently considered the \(Z_I\) over \(A\) lie in the Selmer problems with \(U_v\) at \(2N\), full at \(r\), and the switched planes as indicated (finite at additional unswitched derivative places). For \(Z=Z_\varnothing\), their logarithmic comparison with the paired measure is
\[
 B_r(\theta,u)=\epsilon\,
 \lambda_w(\operatorname{loc}_wZ)^2\prod_{q\in S^\circ}D_q,
 \qquad \epsilon\in(A')^\times.\tag{B1}
\]
statements.section_title: Local comparisons on horizontal tests\\of the split determinant

statements.title: The horizontal determinant inequality
statements.label: split-local:horizontal
statements.text:
For a sufficiently high finite character \(\theta\), suppose \(B_r(\theta,u)\ne0\). Impose the unramified conditions \(U_v\) at the fixed odd places and the Kummer conditions at both dyadic places, and call the resulting Selmer complex \(C_F\). Let \(Z=Z_\varnothing\) and write \(\operatorname{loc}_wZ=p_0e\) for a basis \(e\) of the Kummer line over \(A\). Put
\[
 L_{\rm prim}=\frac{L_{\rm alg,r}(\theta,u)}{\prod_{q\in S^\circ}D_q}.
\]
At every height-one valuation \(v\) of \(A\), the complex has generic cohomology of rank one in each of degrees one and two, and
\[
 d(C_F,(Z,Z^\vee))=2v(p_0)-v(L_{\rm prim})\ge0.
 \tag{D2}
\]
The same conclusion holds for the Hecke-plane variant provided its strict determinant is nonzero, its point-measure and local comparisons satisfy the same hypotheses, its restriction to \(G_K\) is absolutely irreducible, and the stated high-character condition holds.
statements.section_title: Local comparisons on horizontal tests\\of the split determinant

statements.title: Integral unit comparison
statements.label: split-local:unit
statements.text:
For the reducible split-product construction,
\[
 B_r=L_{\rm alg,r}\,U_r,
 \qquad U_r\in\mathcal V^*[[t,u]]^\times.
\]
Likewise \(B/L_{\rm alg}(C(t))\) is a unit in \(\mathcal V^*[[t]]\).
statements.section_title: Local comparisons on horizontal tests\\of the split determinant

statements.title: Rank detection from Selmer corank one
statements.label: split-local:center-rank
statements.text: Under the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{split-measures:reducible-input}, assume \(s_2(E/K)=1\). The conductor-one Hilbert trace \(P\) in \eqref{eq:M3} is nontorsion. Consequently \(L(E/K,s)\) has a simple zero at \(s=1\).
statements.section_title: Local comparisons on horizontal tests\\of the split determinant

statements.title: The exact factor at the center
statements.label: split-local:exact-factor
statements.text:
In the reducible split-product setting, assume that \(L(E/K,s)\) has a simple zero at \(1\), either as a hypothesis or by Proposition~\ref{split-local:center-rank}. Then
\[
 X(E)+X(E^{-d})=0.
\]
In the notation of \eqref{eq:Kum}, the exact arithmetic identity producing this equality is
\[
 2(n_P+\tau_g)=2v_2(c_E)+2\sum_\ell v_2(c_\ell)+s_K.
 \tag{E}
\]
statements.section_title: Local comparisons on horizontal tests\\of the split determinant

statements.title: Characteristic-zero Heegner rank test
statements.label: split-local:heegner-rank
statements.section_title: Local comparisons on horizontal tests\\of the split determinant

statements.title: Finite Selmer seed
statements.label: prop:reducible-seed
statements.text:
There are a permitted twisting factor \(h\) and an elliptic curve \(E_0\),
isogenous over \(\mathbb Q\) to \(E^h\), with rational two-torsion and
\[
                    \dim{\rm Sel}_2(E_0)=\dim E_0(\mathbb Q)[2].
                    \tag{seed}
\]
statements.section_title: Selmer seed for the reducible split-pair anchor

statements.title: Split imaginary Selmer partner
statements.label: prop:reducible-partner
statements.text:
For \(h,E_0\) in Proposition~\ref{prop:reducible-seed}, there is a fresh
prime \(d\equiv7\pmod{16}\) such that
\(K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-d})\) splits all primes of \(2hN_E\), and
\[
 d_2(E_0^{-d})=s_2(E_0^{-d})=1,\qquad
 s_2(E_0)=0,\qquad s_2(E_0/K)=1.
\]
statements.section_title: Selmer seed for the reducible split-pair anchor

statements.title: The reducible split-pair anchor
statements.label: cor:reducible-anchor
statements.text:
Proposition~\ref{prop:anchor} holds for every non-CM elliptic curve over
\(\mathbb Q\) with rational two-torsion.
statements.section_title: Selmer seed for the reducible split-pair anchor

statements.title: Individual-character elliptic-unit comparison
statements.label: cm:external-units
statements.text:
Let \(\Gamma\simeq\mathbb Z_2^2\) be the free pro-\(2\) factor of the ray-tower group,
let \(\Lambda_{\mathcal O}=\mathcal O[[\Gamma]]\), and let
\(\Lambda(\chi)(1)\) have the finite-character and regular variable
actions of \cite[Section~4.1]{BF23}. If
\(\mathfrak f_\chi\mid\mathfrak f\), then, inside generic
rank-one cohomology,
\[
 \Lambda_{\mathcal O}z_{2^\infty\mathfrak f}
 =
 \det_{\Lambda_{\mathcal O}}^{-1}
 R\Gamma\bigl(\mathcal O_L[1/2\mathfrak f],\Lambda(\chi)(1)\bigr).
\]
For the character motive of type \((1,0)\) in the ideal-character
convention of Lemma~\ref{cm:realization}, a modulus divisible by its
conductor, and a compatible Betti vector \(\gamma\), elliptic-unit
reciprocity gives the period equation
\[
 \operatorname{per}\bigl(\exp^*z(\gamma)\bigr)
       =L_{2\mathfrak f}(\bar\varphi,1)\gamma
\]
on the holomorphic component, with the corresponding labeling of
\(\varphi\). The equation includes the case of a zero \(L\)-value.

statements.title: Horizontal CM logarithm
statements.label: cm:tame-log
statements.text:
Suppose that \(L(f_B,s)\) has a simple zero at \(1\).
Then the rational compact Selmer group at the chosen coefficient
embedding is one-dimensional, generated by any nontorsion rational
point \(P\) after extension of scalars. Write
\(z_B=\alpha\lambda_{B,*}(P)\) in projected Kummer notation.
With the absolute \(F\)-valued Poincar\'e height pairing,
\[
 \alpha=\pm e_S\log_\omega P\,
       \frac{L'(f_B,1)}{p_\gamma H_{\lambda_B,F}(P,P)}.
 \tag{C4}
\]
The height-normalized complex expression is interpreted dyadically
through the algebraic comparison in the proof.

statements.title: The torsion-trace implication
statements.label: cm:torsion-trace
statements.text:
In the CM elliptic setting, suppose only that the functional sign is
odd. Choose a split Heegner companion \(K'\) with nonzero central
value and form the same horizontal exponential coordinate \(Z\).
The prime choices need satisfy the spectral conditions above, but
need not satisfy the additional prescription involving a rational
point \(P\). If the projected Hilbert trace \(P_0\) is torsion,
then \(Z'=0\).

statements.title: The CM leading coefficient in known low rank
statements.label: cm:known-low-rank
statements.text: If \(E/\mathbb Q\) is CM and \(\an(E)\le1\), then \(X(E)=0\).

statements.title: CM corank zero
statements.label: cm:corank-zero
statements.text:
If \(E/\mathbb Q\) is CM and \(s_2(E)=0\), then
\(\an(E)=0\) and \(X(E)=0\).

statements.title: Paired CM comparison
statements.label: cm:paired
statements.text:
Let \(A=e_fJ_0(N)\) have the normalization \eqref{eq:C1}. Suppose \(K\) has odd fundamental
discriminant \(-D<-4\), splitting \(2N\), and \(L(f/K,s)\) has a simple zero at 1. Use \(S\)
above finite rational primes splitting in \(K\), including \(2N\) in the prime-support sense,
archimedean places understood, and \(e_S\) for the omission multiplier of \(f\) over \(\mathbb
Q\). Put \(P=e_f P_X\) on \(A(K)_{\mathbb Q}\) for the Hilbert trace of \eqref{eq:GZ}. Over
\(K\) consider the complex \(C_*\) on \(M^*\). Fix one of the two primes \(w\mid2\),
impose the strict condition there, and impose full conditions at every other finite
prime of the support, including \(\bar w\). Then \(C_*\) is rationally acyclic and its characteristic determinant
has valuation
\[
                 -d(C_*,1)=2v_2(e_S\log_{\omega,w} P).               \tag{C-pair}
\]
The differential in this identity is the normalized newform
differential, as in \eqref{eq:M3}.

statements.title: CM corank one
statements.label: cm:corank-one
statements.text:
If \(E/\mathbb Q\) is CM and \(s_2(E)=1\), then
\(\an(E)=1\) and \(X(E)=0\).

statements.title: Parity of special and generic ranks
statements.label: alternation-imaginary:parity
statements.text: For a perfect two-term DVR complex in degrees \(1,2\) with perfect self-duality of shift \(-3\), arising from the preceding local conditions and satisfying \eqref{eq:H1}, the generic and special first-cohomology dimensions have the same parity.

statements.title: Imaginary \(S_3\) anchor
statements.label: alternation-imaginary:anchor
statements.text: Proposition~\ref{prop:anchor} holds for every non-CM elliptic curve \(E/\mathbb Q\) whose residual image is \(S_3\) and whose quadratic residual subfield is imaginary.

statements.title: Compatible primes and residual concentration
statements.label: alternation-imaginary:concentration
statements.text:
A finite collection of auxiliary prime sequences can be chosen to satisfy all prescriptions of Lemmas~\ref{alternation-imaginary:local-factors} and~\ref{alternation-imaginary:central-switch}, to have nonzero fixed-place Frobenius exponents in one tame variable, and to satisfy
\[
 D\big|_{t=\pi=0}\ne0
\]
for both the CM comparator and the elliptic curve. The non-CM limiting traces \(a_{j,*}\) can all be required to be nonzero.

statements.title: Integral quotient and its unit value
statements.label: alternation-imaginary:unit
statements.text: Embed the arithmetic coefficient ring into the common integral measure coefficient ring. For each of the two coefficient planes, \(D\mid B\) in the resulting integral series ring, and both quotients in that ring are units.

statements.title: The real \(S_3\) anchor
statements.label: real:anchor
statements.text:
There are a fundamental discriminant \(h\) prime to \(2N_E\), allowing
\(h=1\), and an imaginary quadratic field \(K\) of discriminant \(-d\)
prime to \(2hN_E\), in which every prime dividing \(2hN_E\) splits, such
that
\[
 \an(E^h)+\an(E^{h(-d)})=1,
 \qquad X(E^h)+X(E^{h(-d)})=0.
\]
statements.section_title: The real \texorpdfstring{$S_3$}{S3} anchor and the detector at infinity

statements.title: The detector at infinity
statements.label: real:detector
statements.text:
There is an \(\mathbb F_2\)-linear functional
\[
 \Theta:H^1(\langle\sigma\rangle,T_2J)\to\mathbb F_2,\quad
 \Theta T_p=\operatorname{tr}W(\mathrm{Fr}_p)\Theta\ (p\nmid2n),
 \qquad \Theta([Y'])\ne0 .                                             \tag{R0}
\]
where \([Y']\) denotes the twisted real Kummer class.
statements.section_title: The real \texorpdfstring{$S_3$}{S3} anchor and the detector at infinity

statements.title: Residual transversality
statements.label: real:transversality
statements.text:
The moving inert primes can be chosen so that
\[
                   (\det\delta_C)|_{t=\mathfrak m_A=0}\ne0             \tag{R1}
\]
and likewise for the full strict determinants on \(P\) and \(T_2E_0\).
statements.section_title: The real \texorpdfstring{$S_3$}{S3} anchor and the detector at infinity

statements.title: Integral cofactor divisibility
statements.label: real:cofactor-divisibility
statements.text:
Further specialize \(u_j=0\) for every \(j>0\), so that the
coefficient ring is \(R_1=A[[u_0]]\). For an integral input \(\eta\),
the global coordinates of the cycle in Lemma~\ref{real:cofactor-lift}
are divisible by
\[
 Q_{\rm aux}=\prod_{j>0}\alpha_j.\tag{R2}
\]
For an input cleared by \(c\), the same assertion holds for \(cz\).
The assertion also holds with multiplicity coefficients \(D\).
statements.section_title: The real \texorpdfstring{$S_3$}{S3} anchor and the detector at infinity

statements.title: Paired and Pfaffian division
statements.label: real:division
statements.text:
The quotients
\[
 V_A=b^+ b^- /s_F,\qquad V_*=b_*^+ b_*^-/s_*,\qquad R_b=b^+/\mathcal P
                                                                        \tag{R3}
\]
are integral in the power-series rings just described. If \(V_*\)
is a nonunit, then \(R_b\) is a nonunit.
statements.section_title: The real \texorpdfstring{$S_3$}{S3} anchor and the detector at infinity

statements.title: Identification with the Heegner class
statements.label: real:heegner-identity
statements.text:
Over the generic fields,
\[
                             Y(\mathbf u)=R_b z .                     \tag{R5}
\]
statements.section_title: The real \texorpdfstring{$S_3$}{S3} anchor and the detector at infinity

statements.title: Primitivity detected at infinity
statements.label: real:primitivity
statements.text:
The paired elliptic quotient \(V_*\) of \eqref{eq:R3} is an integral
unit.
statements.section_title: The real \texorpdfstring{$S_3$}{S3} anchor and the detector at infinity

statements.title: Primitive ray determinant
statements.label: cyclic:ray-basis
statements.text:
The class
\[
 z_S=e_Sz_{\rm ray}
\]
is a basis of the inverse determinant of the unrestricted global
complex on \(\mathcal O(\tau)(1)\tau\), with support \(S'\), over the
dyadic character integers.  Rationally this determinant is its single
\(H^1\)-line.

statements.title: Comparator determinant
statements.label: cyclic:determinant
statements.text:
At every stage and high-order character selected above,
\[
           v_2(D)=2v_2(\ell_w z_{\rm ray})+
                  \sum_{q\in S,\,v_0\mid q}
                             v_2(P_q(\chi(\mathrm{Fr}_{v_0}))).
                  \tag{Y2}
\]
The two terms above the rational prime two sum to \(2a_w-2\).

statements.label: cyclic:anchor
statements.text:
For the original curve \(E_0\), the discriminants \(h\) and \(-d\)
of Lemma~\ref{cyclic:seed} satisfy
\[
 \an(E_0^h)+\an(E_0^{-dh})=1,\qquad
 X(E_0^h)+X(E_0^{-dh})=0.
\]
Thus Proposition~\ref{prop:anchor} holds for cyclic-cubic residual
image.

statements.title: Exact two-primary BSD for almost all quadratic twists
statements.label: cor:quadratic-twist-density
statements.text:
Fix an elliptic curve \(E/\mathbb Q\). For each nonzero squarefree integer
\(d\), write \(E^d\) for the quadratic twist of \(E\) by \(d\), and put
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal D(X)&=\{d\in\mathbb Z:0<|d|\le X,\ d\text{ squarefree}\},\\
 \mathcal D_j(E;X)&=\{d\in\mathcal D(X):s_2(E^d)=j\}
 \qquad(j=0,1).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Then
\[
 \lim_{X\to\infty}\frac{\#\mathcal D_j(E;X)}{\#\mathcal D(X)}
 =\frac12\qquad(j=0,1).
\]
For every nonzero squarefree \(d\) with \(s_2(E^d)=j\in\{0,1\}\), put
\(F=E^d\). Then
\[
 \operatorname{rank}F(\mathbb Q)
 =\operatorname{ord}_{s=1}L(F,s)=s_2(F)=j,
 \qquad \#\Sha(F/\mathbb Q)<\infty,
\]
and
\[
 Q_F=\frac{L^{(j)}(F,1)\,(\#T_F)^2}
 {j!\,\Omega_F\Reg_F\prod_{\ell\ \mathrm{finite}}c_\ell(F)}
 \in\mathbb Q_{>0},
 \qquad v_2(Q_F)=v_2\bigl(\#\Sha(F/\mathbb Q)\bigr).
\]
Here the period, regulator, torsion, and Tamagawa factors have the
normalizations fixed before Theorem~\ref{thm:main}. In particular, the
exact two-primary formula holds on the density-one union of these
subfamilies, whose common ranks are respectively zero and one. The
density is in the full signed squarefree family for fixed \(E\); the
formula asserts equality only at the prime two.

tex.abstract:
For every finite \(N\ge2\), we prove that undeformed \(\SU(N)\) BFSS matrix
quantum mechanics has exactly one normalizable zero-energy state after
removing the center of mass. This establishes the threshold-bound-state
conjecture.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every integer \(N\ge2\),
\[
\dim\Ker H_N=1.
\]
The kernel consists of \(\Spin(9)\)-invariant states and is even in the
fermion grading just specified.

statements.title: Square of a charge
statements.label: prop:square
statements.section_title: The charge algebra, domains, and rotational invariance

statements.title: Singlet property and parity
statements.label: prop:singlet-parity
statements.text:
Every gauge-invariant \(L^2\) vector in the undeformed kernel is
\(\Spin(9)\)-invariant and even. In particular it is \(G\)-invariant.
This assertion does not require finite-dimensionality of the kernel
or any moment of its vectors.
statements.section_title: The charge algebra, domains, and rotational invariance

statements.title: Massive index
statements.label: prop:massive-index
statements.text:
For every \(h>0\), the graph domain of \(D_h\) embeds compactly into
\(\mathscr H_G\), and its even-to-odd part is Fredholm. Its index is
\begin{equation}

 \operatorname{ind}_G D_u(h,1)
 :=\dim\Ker(D_h|_{\mathscr H_G^+})
   -\dim\Ker(D_h|_{\mathscr H_G^-})=p(N),
\end{equation}
where \(p(N)\) is the number of unordered integer partitions of
\(N\). For all sufficiently small \(h>0\), the massive kernel itself
has dimension \(p(N)\), consists of even vectors, and is separated
from the rest of the spectrum of \(D_h\) by a positive gap uniform
in \(h\).

statements.title: Corrected test lifts
statements.label: prop:test-lifts
statements.text:
Fix $m\geq0$, a unit spinor $v$, and a partition $C$ with $k\geq2$.
For every $f\in\mathcal T_C$ there are gauge-singlet graph-domain
states $I_{h,v,m}f$, defined for all sufficiently large $h$, such that
\begin{align}
 \|I_{h,v,m}f-\mathcal J_hf\|&\longrightarrow0,\notag\\
 \|D_v(h,m)I_{h,v,m}f-
                  \mathcal J_h(D_v^C(m)f)\|&\longrightarrow0.
 
\end{align}
The construction is linear on any fixed finite-dimensional space
of tests, and both conclusions hold simultaneously for every fixed
finite test family. In particular, all inner products of their
leading states and indicated charge outputs converge to the
corresponding profile inner products. For distinct partitions the
families, including their outputs, are asymptotically orthogonal.
The leading identifications intertwine block permutations and
$\Spin(3)\times\Spin(6)$; each fixed symmetry may be passed through
these norm limits. The lifts may depend on $v$ and $m$.
statements.section_title: Profile spaces and corrected test states

statements.title: Exterior estimate
statements.label: prop:exterior-estimate
statements.text:
For each \(n\ge2\) there are constants \(c_n>0\) and \(R_n<\infty\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \norm{rD_u(h,0)F}\ge c_n\norm{F},
 \qquad
 \supp F\subset\{h^{1/3}r>R_n\},
 \qquad r=|x|,
\end{equation}
for every \(h>0\) and every compactly supported gauge-invariant graph-domain
vector for the \(\SU(n)\) operator. No rotation invariance is required.
statements.section_title: Exterior estimates and exhaustion by profiles

statements.title: Profiles on proper strata
statements.label: prop:profile-compactness
statements.text:
Assume the induction hypotheses at all sizes less than \(N\). Fix \(m\ge0\),
let \(h_j\to\infty\), and suppose that \(\psi_j\) is a bounded sequence of
gauge-invariant vectors with locally bounded \(D_u(h_j,m)\) graph norms.
Here local boundedness means that
\(\norm{D_u(h_j,m)(a\psi_j)}\) is bounded for every smooth compactly
supported gauge-invariant multiplier \(a\).
After a subsequence there is a profile \(F_C\in\mathcal P_C\) on each proper
stratum such that the limiting norm measure restricted to that stratum is
exactly its squared norm density. Moreover, for every test
\(f\in\mathcal T_C\) of Proposition~\ref{prop:test-lifts},
\begin{equation}
 \ip{\psi_j}{I_{h_j,u,m}f}\longrightarrow\ip{F_C}{f}.
\end{equation}
The extraction can be made simultaneously for any finite list of
sequences, and then the analogous restrictions of all their polarized
norm measures and test overlaps hold. Parity and rotation symmetries of
the original sequences pass to the profiles under the identifications of
Lemma~\ref{lem:chart-compatibility}.
statements.section_title: Exterior estimates and exhaustion by profiles

statements.title: Liminf for the center charges
statements.label: prop:profile-liminf
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:profile-compactness}, suppose
in addition that \(\norm{D_u(h_j,m)\psi_j}\) is globally bounded. On a
subsequence realizing its lower limit, the profiles satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{C\text{ proper}}\norm{D_u^C(m)F_C}^2
       \le\liminf_{j\to\infty}\norm{D_u(h_j,m)\psi_j}^2.
\end{equation}
The derivatives on the left are the full-space graph derivatives.
statements.section_title: Exterior estimates and exhaustion by profiles

statements.title: Exhaustion for tight sequences
statements.label: prof:full-exhaustion
statements.section_title: Exterior estimates and exhaustion by profiles

statements.title: Massive tightness
statements.label: prop:massive-tightness
statements.text:
There are \(a>0\), \(h_0>0\), and \(R_0<\infty\), depending on \(N\),
such that
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak q_{h,1}(\psi)\ge aR^2\norm{\psi}^2
 \quad\text{if}\quad
 h\ge h_0,\quad R\ge R_0,\quad
 \supp\psi\subset\{R<|x|<4R\}.
\end{equation}
This inequality is on gauge invariants, with no rotation restriction.
Consequently, for \(R\ge R_0\), after enlarging the constants if needed,
\begin{equation}
 \int_{|x|>4R}|\psi|^2
 \le\frac{C}{R^2}\mathfrak q_{h,1}(\psi)
             +\frac{C}{R^4}\norm{\psi}^2,
 \qquad h\ge h_0.
\end{equation}
In particular, every bounded sequence of gauge- and \(G\)-invariant
vectors with \(h\to\infty\) and bounded \(D_u(h,1)\) graph norms has tight
squared norm measures.

title: The Weak Inhomogeneous Duffin–Schaeffer Conjecture
abstract: We prove the weak inhomogeneous Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture. For every fixed γ ∈ ℝ and finite-valued \(\psi:\mathbb N\to[0,\infty)\), divergence of \(\sum_{q\ge1}\phi(q)\psi(q)/q\) implies \(\|qx-\gamma\|\lt \psi(q)\) for infinitely many q, for almost every x. Here ϕ is Euler's totient and \(\|\cdot\|\) is distance to the nearest integer. Numerators need not be reduced, and the shift satisfies no Diophantine restriction.

tex.abstract:
We prove the weak inhomogeneous Duffin--Schaeffer conjecture. For every
fixed $\gamma\in\mathbb R$ and finite-valued
$\psi:\mathbb N\to[0,\infty)$, divergence of
$\sum_{q\ge1}\phi(q)\psi(q)/q$ implies
$\|qx-\gamma\|<\psi(q)$ for infinitely many $q$, for almost every $x$.
Here $\phi$ is Euler's totient and $\|\cdot\|$ is distance to the nearest integer.
Numerators need not be reduced, and the shift satisfies no Diophantine
restriction.
sections: Projected tables and the second-moment reduction
First joins of previously constructed tables

statements.title: Weak inhomogeneous Duffin--Schaeffer
statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $\gamma\in\mathbb R$ be fixed, and let
$\psi:\mathbb N\to[0,\infty)$ be finite-valued. If
\begin{equation}
  \sum_{q=1}^{\infty}\frac{\phi(q)}q\,\psi(q)=\infty,
\end{equation}
then, for Lebesgue-almost every $x\in\mathbb R$, the inequality
\[
  \|qx-\gamma\|<\psi(q)
\]
holds for infinitely many positive integers $q$.

statements.title: Hausdorff-measure divergence
statements.label: cor:hausdorff
statements.text:
Fix $\gamma\in\mathbb R$ and a finite-valued
$\psi:\mathbb N\to[0,\infty)$. Let
$f:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be continuous and nondecreasing, with
$f(r)\to0$ as $r\downarrow0$, and suppose that $f(r)/r$ is monotone.
Set $f(0)=0$ and
\[
  W_\gamma(\psi)=\{x\in\mathbb R:
    \|qx-\gamma\|<\psi(q)\text{ for infinitely many }q\}.
\]
If
\[
  \sum_{q=1}^{\infty}\phi(q)f\!\left(\frac{\psi(q)}q\right)=\infty,
\]
then, for every bounded interval $I$,
\[
  \mathcal H^f(I\cap W_\gamma(\psi))=\mathcal H^f(I),
\]
where $\mathcal H^f$ denotes Hausdorff $f$-measure.

statements.title: First-sharing comparison input
statements.label: tab:first-join-input
statements.text:
For the selected finite blocks, there is a static additional birth
test, depending only on the row data and squarefree low numerator
moduli and not on the running tables, with arbitrarily small relative
first-mass loss against the hard birth means, such that the following
statements hold.

For any fixed required absolute $C$, the sum, over first-sharing
times and centre pairs, of the broad currencies
\eqref{tab:product-law} for point pairs at distance at most
$Cr_{xy}^+$ is $O(1)$.

For exact same-width, same-remaining-mask point pairs in one new
cell, sum the currencies \eqref{tab:one-law}, excluding pairs from
the same old child and including all newborn self and diagonal
contributions.  This sum is
\begin{equation}
 \ll W+O_{k_0}(W^{1+c})
 
\end{equation}
for a fixed $c>0$.  Both bounds are uniform in the finite block and
in prior table histories obeying the stated operations and core
symmetries.  The constants in \eqref{tab:narrow-input} may depend on
the preceding fixed cutoffs but not on $N_0$.
statements.section_title: Projected tables and the second-moment reduction

statements.title: Sparse-alignment input
statements.label: tab:sparse-input
statements.text:
For each sparse-prime step in bin $Y$, there is an equivariant
selection of exceptional same-width successful plus pairs at
distance at most
\[
 r_i\exp\left(-\tfrac12\exp(\sigma_gY)\right).
\]
Coarsen accounting classes by every nonexceptional pair in this
range whose two arriving masses are retained.  Uniformly under the
allowed prior histories, the following three sums over components,
steps, applicable centre pairs, masks, and locations are bounded.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Actual simultaneous plus successes at distances between
$r_{xy}^+\exp(-\exp(\sigma_gY))$ and $Cr_{xy}^+$, weighted by
$r_{xy}^-$ times the product of their raw arrival weights and their
two after-prime mask probabilities.
\item Before-prime plus pairs at distance at most $Cr_{xy}^+$,
weighted by $r_{xy}^-/p^2$ times the product of their before-prime
raw weights and their two after-prime mask probabilities.
\item The selected exceptional actual successful pairs in the
relaxed same-width range above, with the same product-law currency
as in the first item.
\end{enumerate}
The constants are uniform in the block, in $N_0$, and in the
allowed preceding histories.  In the first and third items one may
use raw arrival weights immediately after the update and before
coarsening.  The successful linked and unpaired portions of a plus
entry have total mass at most that raw arrival weight.  The first
two items impose no equality of widths, and $C$ may be any required
fixed absolute constant.
statements.section_title: Projected tables and the second-moment reduction

statements.title: Chronological partition input
statements.label: tab:partition-input
statements.text:
The cells and accounting classes described above can be constructed
chronologically for every finite block.  The construction preserves
current-core equivariance, the cell spans and padding stated in
\eqref{tab:cell-span} and the paragraph following it, all inherited
accounting classes without splitting, and the property that one
new cell meets at most one surviving old cell of each old child.
After clipping, the raw cap per cell and remaining mask is $N_0$.
It supports the coarsening rule of
Proposition~\ref{tab:sparse-input} at each subsequent sparse step.

Aside from the cap clipping separately bounded by
\eqref{tab:narrow-input}, its total first-mass loss can be made
arbitrarily small relative to the selected block mass by the fixed
parameter cutoffs.  An expected loss bound over the specified
finite partition jitters suffices; the structural assertions and
core equivariance hold for every realized construction.  The
comparison bounds apply to the actual running tables or to the
nonnegative majorants indicated in their proofs.
statements.section_title: Projected tables and the second-moment reduction

statements.title: Broad-energy bound
statements.label: tab:energy-bound
statements.text:
Assuming Propositions~\ref{tab:first-join-input}--\ref{tab:partition-input},
the final broad energy is bounded uniformly down the finite-block
tail.  The bound may depend on the fixed cap $N_0$ and preceding
hierarchy parameters, but not on the block.
statements.section_title: Projected tables and the second-moment reduction

statements.title: Virtual product marginals
statements.label: tab:virtual-marginals
statements.text:
For each retained good row, there is a nonnegative virtual weight
on its true numerator grid with the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item It dominates the actual final weight, and its first mass
lies between $c_{\rm hard}\phi(v)r(v)$ and $\phi(v)r(v)$.
\item Its total excess over the actual final first mass is exactly
accounted for by the first-moment discard losses in the projected
tables, when the virtual weight omits the soft and additional
static tests, cap clipping, and partition discards.
\item At fixed static anchor choices, every subset of the
actual hard and adaptive fields has mean equal to the product
of its local means.  An actual hard field has mean $1-b_p/p$
when it forbids $b_p\le2$ distinct residues, or mean $R_p$
when it is a prescribed scalar; adaptive full fields have mean
$R_p$.  For upper counts one may retain just one hard birth
exclusion at each applicable prime, or the scalar $R_p$ when
there is no exclusion.  Any subset of the resulting hard and
adaptive fields has the product of its ordinary local means.
\item Fields through a prime $p$, restricted to a later projection
of denominator $v'$, have a joint period dividing $v'$ of size
at most $\exp(O(p))$.
\end{enumerate}
Domination in the first item is after the static anchor average;
it is not required separately for each auxiliary anchor choice.
statements.section_title: Projected tables and the second-moment reduction

statements.title: Upper fields on an intermediate projection
statements.label: tab:intermediate-fields
statements.text:
Fix an admissible realized table history and a row whose current
projected grid is $(z+a\gamma)/(L_i/d)$, where $I$ is the remaining
prime-power part and $a\mid I$. On this grid the actual raw weight
is bounded, after averaging static anchors, by a product of fields
at the processed primes. Each nonconstant field lies in $[0,1]$.
At a full adaptive prime use the multiplier computed from the actual
matching, extended by $R_p$ where its prefix is unavailable; at a
birth prime retain one active hard exclusion, or its prescribed scalar
if none is active. An adaptive omission contributes only its residual
scalar when a positive power remains.

For every fixed choice of the static anchors, every subset of these
fields has mean equal to the product of its ordinary local means.
In particular the full upper product has mean
\[
 R_{\mathrm{done}}(L_i/d)
 :=R\bigl((L_i/I)/d\bigr).
\]
The joint numerator period of any retained fields through a prime $p$
divides the current projected denominator and is at most $\exp(O(p))$,
with the same fixed-parameter uniformity as in
Proposition~\ref{tab:virtual-marginals}.
statements.section_title: Projected tables and the second-moment reduction

statements.title: Finite-block reduction
statements.label: tab:conditional-reduction
statements.text:
Assume the selections and birth prescriptions of
Sections~\ref{sec:centres} and~\ref{sec:prescriptions}, and
Propositions~\ref{tab:first-join-input}--\ref{tab:partition-input}.
Then no measurable set of positive measure can avoid the
original approximation intervals in a whole tail.  Consequently
these inputs imply Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.
statements.section_title: Projected tables and the second-moment reduction

statements.title: Lcm bound
statements.label: ar:lcm
statements.text:
Suppose $f(v)\le\phi(v)$, $g(w)\le\phi(w)$, and
\[
 e(v,w)\le f(v)g(w)
 h\bigl(v/(v,w)\bigr)h\bigl(w/(v,w)\bigr).
\]
If every positive edge satisfies $[v,w]\le Z$, then, for each fixed
$1/2<u<1$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal E\ll Z^{2(1-u)}(FG)^u.
\end{equation}
More generally, in a cell fixing the exponents $i_p,j_p$ at a specified
set of primes, its edge total satisfies the same bound with its own
vertex totals and the additional factor
\[
 h(K)K^{-(1-u)},\qquad K=\prod_p p^{|i_p-j_p|}.
\]

statements.title: Small-scale extraction
statements.label: ar:extraction
statements.text:
Fix positive constants $c_-,c_+$. Suppose $F,G\le1$ and every positive
edge satisfies
\[
 c_-\eta/r_+'\le[v,w]\le c_+\eta/r_+',\qquad 0<\eta<1.
\]
Given any sufficiently small fixed $\vartheta>0$, there are
$u\in(1/2,1)$, $\chi>0$, and $\eta_0>0$ such that for $\eta<\eta_0$
either
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal E\le\eta^{1+\chi}\mathcal R^{-1/10}(FG)^u,
\end{equation}
or $\mathcal R\le\eta^{-\vartheta}$ and a subfamily of edges has the
form
\[
 v=NU_0a/b,\qquad w=NT_0c/d_1,\qquad
 [v,w]=NU_0T_0ac.
\]
Here $N,U_0,T_0$ are fixed positive integers,
\[
 (U_0,T_0)=1,\qquad U_0T_0\le\eta^{-\vartheta},
\]
$b,d_1\mid N$, and $a,b,c,d_1$ are pairwise coprime squarefree integers
coprime to $U_0T_0$. Moreover, $a\in[A,2A)$ and $c\in[C,2C)$ for fixed
dyadic $A,C$. The capacities
\[
 D_1=r_1'NU_0A^2,\qquad D_2=r_2'NT_0C^2
\]
satisfy $\eta^{2+\vartheta}\le D_i\le\eta^{-\vartheta}$, and the
captured normalized edge weight is at least $\eta^\vartheta D_1D_2$.
Every prime in the parameters occurs in the original lists.

statements.title: Negligible subsets of a saturated box
statements.label: ar:box-sampling
statements.text:
Use a box given by Proposition~\ref{ar:extraction}. Suppose that each
vertex weight is obtained by integrating a nonnegative density bounded
by its normalized totient weight against a probability law of auxiliary
variables; restrictions may reduce this density. Suppose also that the
edge majorant holds before integration against the independent product
of the two auxiliary laws.

Sample $a,c$ uniformly from their dyadic integer intervals, sample
$b,d_1$ independently with law $\pi_N$, and then sample the auxiliary
variables with their unrestricted laws. Invalid or nonintegral parameter
choices may be assigned zero weight. An event of sampling probability
$O(\eta^{10\vartheta})$ carries
$o(\eta^\vartheta D_1D_2)$ of the normalized edge weight. The same is
true of edges whose first vertex belongs to a set of total normalized
vertex weight $O(\eta^{10\vartheta}D_1)$.
The auxiliary law on a side may be conditional on that side's vertex
parameters. This statement is only an event-mass bound: an application
that varies an integer factor while holding an auxiliary phase fixed
must separately verify the required independence or a uniform
conditional sampling law.

statements.title: Direct birth bounds
statements.label: dir:birth-comparisons
statements.text:
Use the retained centres of one type and colour, the good masks, and the
birth prescriptions of Sections~\ref{sec:centres}
and~\ref{sec:prescriptions}, with the hierarchy fixed in
Section~\ref{cen:hierarchy}. Let the finite block have mass $W\le1$.
For every fixed $C>0$, the sum over all
direct pairs of
\[
 r_{\min}\iint_{|x-y|\le C r_{\max}}
       d\lambda_i(x)\,d\lambda_j(y)
\]
is $O(1)$. The same-width, one-law sum
\[
 \sum_{\substack{(i,j)\text{ direct}\\r_i=r_j=r}}
 r\sum_{a\mid P_I}\pi_{P_I}(a)
 \iint_{|x-y|\le C r e^{-E_gX_0}}
       d\nu_{i,a}(x)\,d\nu_{j,a}(y)
\]
is $O(W)+O_{k_0}(W^{1+c})$ for some fixed $c>0$. Each ordered centre pair
is counted once, at its common birth. Constants may depend on the fixed
hierarchy, cutoffs, and distance constant, but not on the finite block or
the slot cap $N_0$.

The additional discard used here is a static rule on medium groups,
determined by their good assigned-row lists before any running-table
deletions. Given any fixed $\delta>0$, its total first-mass loss is at most
$\delta W$ after choosing the fixed threshold $\lambda_0$ sufficiently
large. It uses only squarefree low numerator moduli. The comparison bounds
remain valid after any further nonincreasing thinning of birth weights.

statements.title: Sparse-step estimates
statements.label: sp:sparse-estimates
statements.text:
Consider any finite table history up to a sparse-prime update that satisfies
the centre and good-mask prescriptions and the preceding chronological
core-equivariance rules.  Suppose its operational cells have the span and
padding required in Section~\ref{sec:tables}.  Uniformly in that history
and in the slot cap, the following costs, for a fixed centre pair and bin,
are at most
\[
 C\Theta_{ij}e^{-cY}\tau(UT)^C,
\]
where $c>0$ and $C$ are fixed independently of the block:
\begin{enumerate}
 \item the width-weighted product-mask counts of actual successful plus
 pairs at distances between
 $r_{\max}\exp(-\exp(\sigma_gY))$ and $C_0r_{\max}$;
 \item the corresponding counts of before-$q$ plus pairs at distance at
 most $C_0r_{\max}$, multiplied by $1/q^2$, with after-$q$ mask coefficients;
 \item for equal widths $r$, the actual successful plus pairs at distance
 at most $r\exp(-\tfrac12\exp(\sigma_gY))$ that fail the deterministic
 train test of Construction~\ref{sp:danger-trains} at either endpoint.
\end{enumerate}
Here each count is summed over the primes of the bin and uses the factor
$r_{\min}$, or $r$ in the third case.  The first and third counts may use
the actual raw arrival weights immediately after the update; the second
uses the before-update raw plus weights.  The constant $C_0$ can be any
fixed positive constant.

Join accounting classes by all actual surviving equal-width successful
plus pairs at the relaxed scale in the third case that pass both train
tests.  Each connecting segment is covered by the deterministic train
history, which is invariant under the post-generation core translations.
Summing the displayed errors over centre pairs, bins, and components is
bounded.  Consequently this construction proves
Proposition~\ref{tab:sparse-input}.

statements.title: Remaining first-join comparisons
statements.label: join:remaining-first-joins
statements.text:
Consider a finite block and the retained centres, masks, and table
operations of Sections~\ref{sec:centres}--\ref{sec:partitions}, with the
stated parameter hierarchy. At each first sharing of a component, omit
the simultaneous-birth comparisons already treated in
Section~\ref{sec:direct}. For the remaining comparisons, the following
estimates hold uniformly over the permitted prior table history.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The sum of broad pair counts in $\lambda\otimes\lambda$, at
distance at most $C r_{\max}$ and with width weight $r_{\min}$, is $O(1)$.
Here $C$ is any fixed positive constant.
\item The same-width, same-remaining-mask counts in common new cells,
weighted by the single factor $r_i\pi_I(a)$ and the product of the two
raw weights, have total
\[
 O(W)+O_{k_0}(W^{1+c})
\]
for some fixed $c>0$.
\end{enumerate}
The constants are independent of the slot cap $N_0$ and of the finite
block. Thus, together with the direct comparisons, these estimates
establish Proposition~\ref{tab:first-join-input}.

title: Thermal FK–Ising interfaces and massive SLE
abstract: We prove convergence of thermal FK–Ising interfaces, for every fixed nonzero mass of either sign, on uniformly angle-bounded isoradial lattices in bounded simply connected domains. The limit is independent of the lattice and the admissible domain approximation. For positive mass it is the unique massive SLE\(_{16/3}\) law with locally finite-energy drift prescribed by a massive boundary value problem; negative mass follows by duality and reversal. The theorem also allows Carathéodory approximations whose diameters diverge.

tex.abstract:
We prove convergence of thermal FK--Ising interfaces, for every fixed nonzero
mass of either sign, on uniformly angle-bounded isoradial lattices in bounded
simply connected domains. The limit is independent of the lattice and the
admissible domain approximation. For positive mass it is the unique massive
SLE$_{16/3}$ law with locally finite-energy drift prescribed by a massive
boundary value problem; negative mass follows by duality and reversal.
The theorem also allows Carath\'eodory approximations whose diameters diverge.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every $(\Omega,a,b,m)$ as above, there is a curve law
$\mu_{\Omega,a,b,m}$ such that, for every sequence with mesh tending
to zero and satisfying all the preceding domain, marked
Carath\'eodory, angle and nome assumptions,
\[
 \mathcal L(\chi_\delta\circ\gamma_\delta)
       \ \Longrightarrow\ \chi_*\mu_{\Omega,a,b,m}
\]
in the metric~\eqref{mod:curve-metric}, along the full sequence.
The physical prime-end curve law $\mu_{\Omega,a,b,m}$ is independent
of the lattices, admissible domain approximations and nome sequence.

For $m>0$, $\mu_{\Omega,a,b,m}$ is the unique law in
Definition~\ref{def:law}. For $m<0$, it is the reversal of the
positive-mass law in $(\Omega,b,a)$ with mass $|m|$, with primal and
dual boundary labels interchanged. In either case we call it
thermal massive $\mathrm{SLE}_{16/3}$.

statements.label: mod:bvp-unique
statements.text:
Equation~\eqref{mod:bvp} has exactly one solution in this class.
It satisfies $0\le h\le1$. On interior compact sets, $h$ and its
first derivatives depend continuously on the marked domain in the
Carath\'eodory topology, when the domains lie in a fixed bounded
physical region.

statements.title: Observable convergence and rectangle crossings
statements.label: prop:inputs
statements.text:
Consider the weights of Section~\ref{mod:section}, with
\(r_\delta/\delta\to m/2\), on isoradial meshes whose rhombus half-angles
belong to \([\eta,\pi/2-\eta]\).
\begin{enumerate}
\item
For marked Carath\'eodory convergence to a bounded simply connected
two-point domain, the reconstructed two-point FK fermion converges
locally uniformly, up to its common sign, to a smooth massive-holomorphic
function \(f\):
\[
 \bar\partial f+\ii m\overline f=0.
\]
Its square integral \(h\), normalized by its two boundary values, is the
unique bounded solution
\[
 \lap h=-4m|\grad h|,\qquad
 h=1\ \hbox{on the wired bank},\qquad
 h=0\ \hbox{on the dual-wired bank}.
\]
The boundary values are prime-end limits away from the two marked ends,
and \(0\le h\le1\). The convergence includes uniform interior bounds
on protected compact subsets.
\item
For every fixed rectangle aspect ratio and every finite physical scale
bound, the crossing probabilities of both colors are bounded away from
zero, uniformly over all boundary conditions and all nondegenerate
lattice rectangles below that scale whose side lengths exceed a fixed
multiple of the mesh. The scale constants are independent of the mesh.
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Conditional unforced crossings
statements.label: geo:g2
statements.text:
The regularly drawn medial interfaces in domains of diameter at most
\(L\) satisfy condition G2 of \cite{KS}, uniformly over the allowed
meshes, domains, and thermal parameters.

statements.title: Joint compactness
statements.label: geo:compactness
statements.text:
Under the common diameter bound, the laws of the interfaces transferred
by their normalized maps to the closed disc are tight in the oriented
curve metric. Every subsequential limit is a chordal Loewner trace with
a continuous driving function and strict capacity growth. It reaches
the target only at the end and is continuously completed in disc
coordinates. Along a further coupling, the curves and their
half-plane drivers converge jointly, with uniform convergence of the
drivers and capacity-parametrized curves on every finite capacity
interval.
statements.section_title: Geometry, compactness, and the martingale observable

statements.title: Conditional geometric estimates in the limit
statements.label: geo:restart
statements.text:
Every limit of Proposition~\ref{geo:compactness} inherits the conditional
crossing estimates needed below in its natural driving filtration.
They hold after a live stopping time and after localization on a
finite interval on which the relevant Loewner coordinates remain
nondegenerate. In the following two estimates, reset capacity time
to zero at the chosen live stopping time.
\begin{enumerate}
\item In the current half-plane chart, put the tip at \(0\), rescale a
given live point to modulus \(1\), and write \(x\) for its real part.
If its imaginary part is small, so \(x\) is near \(1\) or \(-1\), then
\[
 \Prob\{\text{the future trace visits }B(x,d)\mid\text{past}\}
 \le Kd^\alpha
\]
for all sufficiently small \(d\).
\item For a live physical point \(w\),
\[
 \Prob\left\{
   \inf_{s\text{ before swallowing}}
   \crad_{O_s}(w)
      <\varepsilon\,\crad_{O_0}(w)
   \,\middle|\,\text{past at the restart}\right\}
 \le K\varepsilon^\alpha .
\]
\end{enumerate}
The assertions apply in particular at inverse elapsed-clock times
and at first angular-level crossings used in Section~\ref{eng:section}.
No semimartingale property of the driver is assumed here.
statements.section_title: Geometry, compactness, and the martingale observable

statements.title: Continuum fermion martingales
statements.label: geo:martingale
statements.text:
Every subsequential curve law of Proposition~\ref{geo:compactness}
has a joint realization with a complex field \(M_t(w)\), \(w\in O_t\),
such that
\[
 M_t(w)^2=D h_t(w),\qquad
 \bar\partial M_t+\ii m\overline{M_t}=0.
\]
The field is continuous locally in space and time before swallowing,
and is smooth in its spatial variable. On every protected compact
subset of the live domain, after localization, \(M_t(w)\) is a
continuous martingale in the joint natural filtration of the curve
and field. In particular it is a continuous local martingale at
each fixed point before its swallowing time.

statements.title: Identification of the driver
statements.label: cal:driver
statements.text:
The subsequential driving process is a continuous semimartingale and,
in the above joint filtration, satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \dd W_t=\sqrt{\frac{16}{3}}\,\dd B_t+
                \frac{2\pi}{3}C_t\,\dd t,
 \qquad
 \int_0^T C_t^2\,\dd t<\infty\quad\text{almost surely for every }T<\infty,
 
\end{equation}
where $B$ is a Brownian motion and
\begin{equation}
 C_t=\frac4\pi\int_{\Hh}P(v)\mu_t(v)
              |\nabla(h_t\circ\psi_t)(v)|\,\dd A(v).
 
\end{equation}
In particular, neither absolute continuity of the quadratic variation
nor absolute continuity of the finite-variation part of $W$ is an
assumption of the argument.

statements.label: uni:bounded
statements.text:
Definition~\ref{def:law} determines exactly one law. Every
admissible approximation whose physical domains have a common
diameter bound converges to this law in the disc curve topology.

statements.title: Reduction to bounded Dobrushin problems
statements.label: loc:reduction
statements.text:
From every admissible approximation sequence one can extract
a further subsequence and perform finite edge revelations
with success probability tending to one, so that on success:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the unqueried connecting domain \(\widehat\Omega_n\)
is a Dobrushin polygon on the original mesh with the
same thermal parameters and diameter at most \(2S+20\);
\item conditional on the complete revelation record, its
interface has the ordinary Dobrushin FK law;
\item every deterministic sequence of possible successful
outputs \((\widehat\Omega_n,\widehat a_n,\widehat b_n)\)
converges in the marked Carath\'eodory sense to
\((\Omega,a,b)\);
\item the normalized coordinates on the retained domain
are uniformly \(o(1)\) from its original normalized
coordinates, including prime-end occurrences, and
the removed endpoint heads have vanishing disc
diameter.
\end{enumerate}
All error bounds are uniform over successful outcomes.

statements.title: Universality without a diameter assumption
statements.label: loc:universality
statements.text:
For \(m>0\), every approximation sequence in
Theorem~\ref{thm:main} converges to the law of
Definition~\ref{def:law}, in the specified
normalized-disc curve topology.

title: Thomason Model Structures in Every Strict Higher Dimension
abstract: We prove the higher-dimensional Thomason model-structure conjecture of Ara and Maltsiniotis. For every \(1\le n\le\infty\), the category of small strict globular n-categories admits a proper combinatorial model structure that is Quillen equivalent to simplicial sets. Its weak equivalences and fibrations are detected by the twice-extended Street nerve \(\mathrm{Ex}^2N_n\), and the Quillen equivalence is given by \(c_n\mathrm{Sd}^2\dashv\mathrm{Ex}^2N_n\). Thus strict higher categories model the homotopy theory of spaces in every positive finite dimension and in dimension ω.

tex.abstract:
We prove the higher-dimensional Thomason model-structure conjecture of
Ara and Maltsiniotis. For every $1\le n\le\infty$, the category of small
strict globular $n$-categories admits a proper combinatorial model structure
that is Quillen equivalent to simplicial sets. Its weak equivalences and
fibrations are detected by the twice-extended Street nerve $\Ex^2N_n$, and
the Quillen equivalence is given by $c_n\Sd^2\dashv\Ex^2N_n$. Thus strict
higher categories model the homotopy theory of spaces in every positive
finite dimension and in dimension $\omega$.
