Relation to the weak-groupoid expansion method

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every $n\in\{1,2,3,\ldots\}\cup\{\infty\}$, the classes
$(C_n,W_n,F_n)$ in \eqref{eq:prescribed-classes} form a proper
combinatorial model structure on $\nCat$. It is cofibrantly generated by
$(L_nI,L_nJ)$, where
\[
 I=\{\partial\Delta[m]\hookrightarrow\Delta[m]:m\ge0\},\qquad
 J=\{\Lambda^k[m]\hookrightarrow\Delta[m]:m\ge1,\ 0\le k\le m\}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 L_n:\sSet_{\KQ}\rightleftarrows(\nCat,C_n,W_n,F_n):R_n
\]
is a Quillen equivalence.

statements.title: Labelled attachments
statements.label: prop:labelled-pushout
statements.text:
Let $A\subset P$ be a full subposet, let $a:\U{A}\to X$ be any strict
functor, and form
\[
 Y=X\amalg_{\U{A}}\U{P}.
\]
Suppose a monotone map $\lambda:P\to[1]$ and a strict functor
$\xi:X\to\Disk{1}$ satisfy
\[
 \xi a=U(\lambda|_A):\U{A}\longrightarrow\Disk{1},
 \qquad \U{[1]}=\Disk{1}.
\]
Write
$P_\epsilon=\lambda^{-1}(\epsilon)$,
$A_\epsilon=A\cap P_\epsilon$, and
$X_\epsilon=\xi^{-1}(\epsilon)$.  Then the induced label
$Y\to\Disk{1}$ has actual full fibers
\begin{equation}
 Y_\epsilon\cong
 X_\epsilon\amalg_{\U{A_\epsilon}}\U{P_\epsilon}.
\end{equation}
Moreover, independently of these labels,
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Ob}Y\cong
 \operatorname{Ob}X\amalg_A P
 \cong\operatorname{Ob}X\amalg(P\setminus A).
\end{equation}
For two such pairs of compatible labels, write
$\bar\lambda_1,\bar\lambda_2:Y\to\Disk{1}$ for the induced labels.
Their $0$-fibers intersect in the $0$-fiber of
$\max\circ(\bar\lambda_1,\bar\lambda_2)$; their $1$-fibers intersect
in the $1$-fiber of $\min\circ(\bar\lambda_1,\bar\lambda_2)$.
Formula~\eqref{eq:pushout-fiber}, using the corresponding maximum or
minimum on both original legs, computes these intersections as well.

statements.title: Sieve and cosieve covers after attachment
statements.label: cor:attachment-covers
statements.text:
With the notation of Proposition~\ref{prop:labelled-pushout}, the
following are canonical identifications of subcategories of $Y$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item Suppose $P_1,P_2$ are sieves of $P$, contain $A$, and cover $P$.
Then the subcategories
\[
 Y_i=X\amalg_{\U{A}}\U{P_i}\quad(i=1,2)
\]
are sieves covering $Y$ on objects, and
\[
 Y_1\cap Y_2
 =X\amalg_{\U{A}}\U{P_1\cap P_2}.
\]
\item Suppose $T_1,T_2$ are cosieves of $P$, cover $P$, satisfy
$A\subset T_1$, and satisfy $A\cap T_2=\varnothing$.  Then
\[
 Y_1=X\amalg_{\U{A}}\U{T_1},\qquad Y_2=\U{T_2}
\]
are cosieves covering $Y$ on objects, and
$Y_1\cap Y_2=\U{T_1\cap T_2}$.
\end{enumerate}
If $A$ itself is a sieve of $P$, the canonical map $X\to Y$ is the
inclusion of a full sieve.

statements.title: Couniversality
statements.label: thm:couniversal
statements.text:
If $i:A\hookrightarrow E$ is a sieve of small posets with a right
adjoint retraction, then $c_n\OrdN(i)$ is a couniversal Thomason
equivalence: for every $a:\U{A}\to X$, the canonical map
\[
 X\longrightarrow X\amalg_{\U{A}}\U{E}
\]
is a Thomason equivalence.  This holds for every finite $n\ge1$ and
for $n=\infty$.

statements.title: The unit on every poset
statements.label: prop:poset-unit
statements.text:
For every small poset $S$, the adjunction unit
\[
 \eta_S:\OrdN S\longrightarrow\Street\U{S}
\]
is a weak homotopy equivalence.  This assertion is natural in $S$
and holds for every finite $n\ge1$ and for $n=\infty$.
statements.section_title: Couniversality and the unit on posets

statements.title: Attachment comparison
statements.label: prop:attachment-comparison
statements.text:
Let $A\subset B$ be a sieve of small posets.  Let $Z$ be its upward
closure, and suppose that $A\hookrightarrow Z$ admits a right adjoint
retraction.  For every functor $a:\U{A}\to X$ in $\nCat$, put
\[
 V_B(X)=X\amalg_{\U{A}}\U{B},\qquad
 P_B(X)=\Street X\amalg_{\Street\U{A}}\Street\U{B}.
\]
The canonical map
\begin{equation}
 \gamma_{B,X}:P_B(X)\longrightarrow\Street V_B(X)
 
\end{equation}
is a simplicial weak equivalence.  The map
$\Street\U{A}\to\Street\U{B}$ is a monomorphism.
The comparison is natural in every functor $f:X\to X'$ under
$\U{A}$.

statements.title: Horn attachments are acyclic
statements.label: cor:horn-acyclic
statements.text:
For every horn inclusion $d\in J$, every pushout of $L_n d$ belongs
to $W_n$.

statements.title: Invariance under attachment
statements.label: cor:attachment-invariance
statements.text:
Let $d\in I\cup J$, write $L_n d$ as $\U{A}\to\U{B}$ using
Lemma~\ref{lem:subdivision-posets}, and let $f:X\to X'$ belong to
$W_n$.  For every $a:\U{A}\to X$, the induced functor
\[
 X\amalg_{\U{A}}\U{B}
 \longrightarrow X'\amalg_{\U{A}}\U{B},
\]
where the second attaching functor is $fa$, belongs to $W_n$.

title: Threshold parallel repetition for finite-dimensional entangled games
abstract: For every finite two-player game with entangled value v < 1, we prove exponential decay for the probability of winning at least a \(v+\delta\) fraction of k independent repetitions, uniformly over all finite-dimensional joint strategies. The result allows arbitrary correlated question distributions and holds for every \(0\lt \delta\lt 1-v\) and k ≥ 1. Its universal rate is proportional to \(\delta^5/(1+\log(|\mathcal A||\mathcal B|))\), where \(\mathcal A,\mathcal B\) are the answer alphabets. For each fixed question distribution, we also obtain an explicit cubic rate in δ.

tex.abstract:
For every finite two-player game with entangled value $v<1$, we prove
exponential decay for the probability of winning at least a $v+\delta$
fraction of $k$ independent repetitions, uniformly over all
finite-dimensional joint strategies. The result allows arbitrary correlated
question distributions and holds for every $0<\delta<1-v$ and $k\ge1$.
Its universal rate is proportional to
$\delta^5/(1+\log(|\mathcal A||\mathcal B|))$, where
$\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ are the answer alphabets. For each fixed question
distribution, we also obtain an explicit cubic rate in $\delta$.
sections: From conditioning to a threshold bound
A cubic bound for a fixed question distribution

statements.title: Threshold parallel repetition
statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There is a universal constant $\kappa_0>0$ such that the following holds.
Let $G$ be any finite two-player one-round game with Boolean acceptance
predicate and entangled value $v=\omega^*(G)<1$. For every
$0<\delta<1-v$, every integer $k\ge1$, and every finite-dimensional
joint strategy for $k$ repetitions,
\begin{equation}
 \Pr\!\left[W_k\ge\lceil(v+\delta)k\rceil\right]
 \le \exp\!\left(-\frac{\kappa_0\delta^5}
                         {1+\log d}\,k\right).
\end{equation}
The same inequality holds for the supremum over those strategies.

statements.title: Conditioning-to-threshold transfer
statements.label: prop:conditioning-to-tail
statements.text:
Let $G$ be a finite two-prover game with nonempty answer alphabets,
$d=|\mathcal A||\mathcal B|$, and $v=\omega^*(G)<1$.
Fix $0<\delta<1-v$ and $0<T\le\delta/4$. Suppose the following holds for
every $k\ge1$, every finite-dimensional strategy for $k$ repetitions,
and every $C\subsetneq[k]$
with $p_C>0$:
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\log(1/p_C)+|C|\log d}{k-|C|}\le T
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \frac{1}{k-|C|}\sum_{i\notin C}\Pr(I_i=1\mid E_C)
 \le v+\delta/4.
\end{equation}
Then, for every $k\ge1$ and every finite-dimensional strategy,
\begin{equation}
 \Pr\bigl(W\ge\lceil(v+\delta)k\rceil\bigr)
 \le \exp\left(-\frac{\delta T}{16(1+\log d)}\,k\right).
\end{equation}
The same bound holds for the supremum over those strategies.
statements.section_title: From conditioning to a threshold bound

statements.title: Song's conditioning estimate, {\cite[Definition~4.3 and Lemma~4.4]{song2026}}
statements.label: prop:song-conditioning
statements.text:
There is a universal constant $B_4\ge1$ with the following property.
Let $G$ be a finite two-player game with entangled value $v<1$, and fix
a finite-dimensional strategy for $k\ge1$ repetitions. For
$C\subsetneq[k]$ with $p_C=\Pr(E_C)>0$, put $m=k-|C|$ and
\[
 \tau=\frac{\log(1/p_C)+|C|\log(|\mathcal A||\mathcal B|)}m.
\]
If $\tau\le1$, then
\begin{equation}
 \frac1m\sum_{i\notin C}\Pr(I_i=1\mid E_C)
 \le v+B_4\tau^{1/4}.
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: From conditioning to a threshold bound

statements.title: Conditioning through support components
statements.label: prop:root-conditioning
statements.text:
Let $G$ be a finite two-prover game with question distribution $\mu$ and
$v=\omega^*(G)$. For any finite-dimensional strategy for $k$ copies and
$C\subsetneq[k]$, suppose that
\[
 E_C=\{I_j=1\text{ for every }j\in C\},\qquad p=\Pr(E_C)>0.
\]
Put $m=k-|C|$ and
$\tau=(|C|\log(|\mathcal A||\mathcal B|)+\log(1/p))/m$.
Then
\begin{equation}
 \frac1m\sum_{i\notin C}\Pr(I_i=1\mid E_C)
 \le v+\sqrt{\frac{\log(1/p)}{2m}}
          +4\sqrt{\kappa_\mu\tau}+2\kappa_\mu\tau.
\end{equation}
The constants are independent of the strategy dimension and of $k$.
statements.section_title: A cubic bound for a fixed question distribution

statements.label: cor:support-threshold
statements.text:
Let $G$ be a finite two-player game with Boolean acceptance predicate,
question distribution $\mu$, and entangled value $v<1$. Put
$d=|\mathcal A||\mathcal B|$, and define $\kappa_\mu$ by
\eqref{eq:root-support-constant}. For every $0<\delta<1-v$, every
$k\ge1$, and every finite-dimensional joint strategy for $k$ repetitions,
\begin{equation}
 \Pr\bigl(W_k\ge\lceil(v+\delta)k\rceil\bigr)
 \le\exp\left(-\frac{\delta^3}
 {16384(1+\kappa_\mu)(1+\log d)}\,k\right).
\end{equation}
The same bound holds for the supremum over those strategies.
statements.section_title: A cubic bound for a fixed question distribution

statements.title: Two-sided error amplification
statements.label: cor:error-amplification
statements.text:
Let $G$ be a finite two-player one-round game in the model above, and
fix $0\le s<c\le1$. Put $\Delta=c-s$, $t=(c+s)/2$, and
$d=|\mathcal A||\mathcal B|$. For an integer $k\ge1$, let $H_k$ sample $k$
independent question pairs from $G$, send each player the entire local
question string, and accept exactly when $W_k\ge\lceil tk\rceil$.
Then
\begin{align*}
 \omega^*(G)\ge c
 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \omega^*(H_k)\ge1-\exp(-\Delta^2k/8),\\
 \omega^*(G)\le s
 &\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \omega^*(H_k)\le
 \exp\!\left(-\frac{\kappa_0(\Delta/2)^5}{1+\log d}\,k\right),
\end{align*}
where $\kappa_0$ is the universal constant in Theorem~\ref{thm:main}.

title: Topological triviality of mu-constant families of surface singularities
abstract: We prove that every holomorphic one-parameter family of isolated hypersurface singularities in ℂ3 with constant Milnor number is topologically right-trivial. This gives a positive answer to the surface case of the μ-constant problem. The trivialization fixes the parameter and the origin section, and preserves the defining functions.

tex.abstract:
We prove that every holomorphic one-parameter family of isolated hypersurface
singularities in $\mathbb C^3$ with constant Milnor number is topologically
right-trivial. This gives a positive answer to the surface case of the
$\mu$-constant problem. The trivialization fixes the parameter and the
origin section, and preserves the defining functions.
sections: Reduction of the numerical assertion to algebraic curves
The nearby Euler characteristic along the boundary
From the numerical invariant to a resolved family
From resolutions to ambient right triviality
The log canonical and double-point cases
Local constructions for the numerical comparison

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $F:(\mathbb C^3\times\Delta,\{0\}\times\Delta)\to(\mathbb C,0)$
be holomorphic.  Suppose that, for every $t\in\Delta$, $f_t(0)=0$,
$f_t$ has an isolated critical point at $0$, and
$\mu(f_t,0)=\mu(f_0,0)$.  After shrinking the disk and the germ
representatives, there is a homeomorphism germ
\[
 \Phi(x,t)=(\phi_t(x),t),\qquad
 \phi_t(0)=0,\quad \phi_0=\mathrm{id},\qquad
 f_t\bigl(\phi_t(x)\bigr)=f_0(x).
\]
Both $\Phi$ and $\Phi^{-1}$ are jointly continuous on neighborhoods
of the origin section over the original disk.

statements.title: Scalar curve reduction
statements.label: prop:scalar-curve-reduction
statements.text:
Assume the following algebraic assertion: for every polynomial family
in three variables with regular coefficients on a smooth complex
algebraic curve $C$, with zero constant and linear terms and constant
positive Milnor number at the origin, the Wahl invariant at a marked
non-log-canonical fiber equals its value on the nearby general fibers.
Then $\beta(X_t,0)$ is constant near $t=0$ in every holomorphic
$\mu$-constant family whose central surface germ is non-log-canonical.
statements.section_title: Reduction of the numerical assertion to algebraic curves

statements.title: The relative log model
statements.label: prop:log-model
statements.text:
Let $C$ be a smooth connected complex algebraic curve with a marked point $0$,
and let $\pi:X\to C$ be a flat projective family of integral normal Gorenstein
surfaces.  Suppose that $X$ is normal and Gorenstein, that a section
$\Gamma\subset X$ contains every fibre singularity, and that $\pi$ is smooth
on $X\setminus\Gamma$.  Then, after shrinking $C$ about $0$ and making a
finite base change from a smooth curve, there is a projective birational
morphism
\[
 h:Y\longrightarrow X
\]
with the following properties.  Here $X$, $C$, $\Gamma$ and $0$ denote the
base-changed objects, and $H$ is the sum, with coefficient one, of all
$h$-exceptional prime divisors dominating $C$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Y$ is normal and $\mathbb Q$-factorial, and $h$ is an isomorphism
      over $X\setminus\Gamma$.
\item For every $c\in C$, the scheme fibre $Y_c$ is a reduced Cartier divisor,
      and $(Y,H+Y_c)$ is divisorial log terminal.
\item $K_Y+H$ is nef over $X$.  Every vertical $h$-exceptional prime divisor
      lies in $Y_0$ and maps to the point $\Gamma\cap X_0$.
\item For $c\ne0$, the surface $Y_c$ is integral and normal, and the divisor
      $H|_{Y_c}$ is reduced as a Weil divisor.  The fibre $Y_0$ has a unique component dominating
      $X_0$; its remaining components are projective surfaces over
      $\Gamma\cap X_0$.
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Support over a non-log-canonical section
statements.label: prop:full-exceptional-boundary
statements.text:
Assume in addition that the surface $X_c$ is not log canonical at
$\Gamma\cap X_c$ for general $c\in C$.  Then $A\le0$, some horizontal coefficient of $A$ is
strictly negative, and
\[
 h^{-1}(\Gamma)=\operatorname{Supp}(-A)
              =\operatorname{Supp}(H)\cup\bigcup_a S_a
\]
as sets.  In particular $B_{S_0}$ is the full reduced exceptional
preimage of $\Gamma\cap X_0$ on $S_0$, and $B_{Y_c}$ has the same property
on every $Y_c$ with $c\ne0$.  Thus
\[
 S_0\setminus\operatorname{Supp}(B_{S_0})
       \simeq X_0\setminus\Gamma,
 \qquad
 Y_c\setminus\operatorname{Supp}(B_{Y_c})
       \simeq X_c\setminus\Gamma\quad(c\ne0).
\]

statements.title: Euler comparison for the log model
statements.label: prop:nearby-euler-comparison
statements.text:
Let $q:Y\to C$ be a projective flat morphism from a normal complex
threefold to a smooth pointed curve $(C,0)$.  Let $H$ be a reduced
divisor with horizontal prime components.  Assume that the Cartier
fiber $Y_0=\sum S$ is reduced, that $(Y,Y_0+H)$ is dlt, and that its
boundary components are $\mathbb Q$-Cartier.  Assume also that
$Y_t\setminus H$ is smooth for all sufficiently small $t\ne0$.
For each component $S$ of $Y_0$, let $B_S$ be the reduced union of its
intersections with the other components of $Y_0+H$, and put
$S^\circ=S\setminus B_S$.  If each local smoothing of an isolated
singularity in $S^\circ$ has Milnor fiber Euler characteristic at
least one, then
\begin{equation}

 \chi_c(Y_t\setminus H)
   =\sum_{S\subset Y_0}\chi_c(S^\circ)+\delta,
 \qquad \delta\ge0,
\end{equation}
for all sufficiently small $t\ne0$.
statements.section_title: The nearby Euler characteristic along the boundary

statements.title: The numerical conclusion of the log model
statements.label: prop:beta-from-log-model
statements.text:
Let $X\to C$, with section $\Gamma$, be the projective family of
Lemma~\ref{lem:compactification}.  Let $h:Y\to X$ be a projective
birational morphism from a normal integral threefold, isomorphic off
$\Gamma$.  Suppose $Y_0=S_0+\sum_a S_a$ is reduced Cartier, $S_0$
maps birationally to $X_0$, and the $S_a$ map to $\Gamma(0)$.  Suppose
that, after shrinking $C$, the other fibres $Y_c$ are normal and map
birationally to $X_c$.

Let $H$ be the reduced horizontal exceptional boundary and set
$L=K_Y+H$, assumed rational Cartier and $h$-nef.  For each component
$S$ of $Y_0$, let $B_S$ be the reduced divisor of its intersections
with the other components of $Y_0+H$.  Assume that $(S,B_S)$ is log
canonical and
\[
 L|_S\sim_{\mathbb Q} K_S+B_S.
\]
For $S_0$, require that $B_{S_0}$ is the full reduced inverse image of
$\Gamma(0)$.  For $c\ne0$, require likewise that the full reduced
inverse image $B_c$ of $\Gamma(c)$ is a divisor, that $(Y_c,B_c)$ is
log canonical, and that
$L|_{Y_c}\sim_{\mathbb Q}K_{Y_c}+B_c$.
If
\[
 (K_{S_a}+B_{S_a})^2=0\qquad\text{for every }a,
\]
then $\beta(X_c,\Gamma(c))=\beta(X_0,\Gamma(0))$ for all remaining
$c\in C$.

statements.title: Constancy of the logarithmic invariant
statements.label: thm:beta-constant
statements.text:
Let $F(x,t)$ be a holomorphic family of isolated hypersurface singularities
in $\mathbb C^3$ with $f_t(0)=0$ and constant positive Milnor number.
If the central normal surface germ $X_0=\{f_0=0\}$ is not log canonical,
then $\beta(X_t,0)=\beta(X_0,0)$ for every sufficiently small $t$.

statements.label: prop:resolved-family
statements.text:
Let $F(x,t)=f_t(x)$ satisfy the hypotheses of the main theorem.  Assume
that $X_0=\{f_0=0\}$ is not log canonical and that $\beta(X_t,0)$ is
constant.  After shrinking the parameter disk and making a finite base
change $t=u^e$, there is a proper modification
\[
 b:N\longrightarrow X'=\{F(x,u^e)=0\}
\]
such that $N\to\Delta_u$ is smooth, $b$ is an isomorphism off the origin
section, and its reduced exceptional divisor $E$ has relative normal
crossings.  The restriction $b_u$ is the minimal semigood resolution,
and $E|_{N_u}$ is its full reduced exceptional divisor.
statements.section_title: From the numerical invariant to a resolved family

statements.title: Whitney regular zero fibers
statements.label: cor:whitney-right
statements.text:
Let $G(x,u)$, with $x\in\mathbb C^n$, be a holomorphic family with
$G(0,u)=0$ and no spatial critical points off the origin section near $(0,0)$. If the pair
\[
 \bigl(\{G=0\}\setminus\{x=0\},\ \{x=0\}\bigr)
\]
satisfies Whitney conditions \textup{(a)} and \textup{(b)}, then $G$ is
ambiently topologically right trivial near that section, with the central
map equal to the identity.
statements.section_title: From resolutions to ambient right triviality

statements.title: Lifts supplied by a resolution
statements.label: prop:resolution-right
statements.section_title: From resolutions to ambient right triviality

statements.label: prop:low-cases
statements.text:
Let $F(x,t)=f_t(x)$ be a holomorphic family in three spatial variables,
with $f_t(0)=0$, an isolated critical point at $0$ in every fiber, and
constant Milnor number.  If either $\operatorname{mult}_0(f_0)=2$ or the
normal surface germ $X_0=\{f_0=0\}$ is log canonical, then $F$ is
topologically right-trivial over a sufficiently small parameter disk.
statements.section_title: The log canonical and double-point cases

statements.title: The local exceptional-square comparison
statements.label: cor:local-exceptional-square
statements.text:
Suppose a projective birational morphism $h:Y\to X$ is a log model
over a smooth curve as in Section~\ref{sec:full-boundary}, except
that $X\to C$ need not be proper.  Assume $X$ and $Y$ are
quasi-projective, all exceptional prime divisors map into the section
$\Gamma\simeq C$, and put
\[
 A=K_Y+H-h^*K_X.
\]
If $Y_0=S_0+\sum_aS_a$ and the nearby fibers are irreducible, then
\[
 (A|_{Y_c})^2=(A|_{S_0})^2+\sum_a(A|_{S_a})^2.
\]
Under the full-boundary, adjunction, and nefness hypotheses of
Proposition~\ref{prop:beta-from-log-model}, the first two squares
are respectively $-\beta(X_c,\Gamma(c))$ and
$-\beta(X_0,\Gamma(0))$, while
\[
 (A|_{S_a})^2=(K_{S_a}+B_{S_a})^2.
\]
Thus vanishing of the extra squares proves constancy of the local
invariant without a projective compactification of $X$.
statements.section_title: Local constructions for the numerical comparison

statements.title: Marked monomial reduction in dimension three
statements.label: prop:marked-monomial-reduction
statements.text:
Let $q:Z\to C$ be a morphism from a smooth quasi-projective complex
threefold to a smooth curve.  Let $0\in C$, write
$Z_0=\sum_i a_iZ_i$, and let $H$ be a reduced divisor with horizontal
components.  Suppose that $(Z_0)_{\mathrm{red}}+H$ is simple normal
crossing, and that away from $0$ the morphism is smooth with relative
simple normal crossing divisor $H$.
After shrinking $C$ about $0$, choose a parameter $\tau$ with no
other zero and an integer $b$ divisible by every $a_i$.  After the
finite base change $s^b=\tau$ and normalization, there is a projective
birational modification whose total space is smooth and whose special
fiber is reduced and simple normal crossing together with the
transformed horizontal marking.  The modification is an isomorphism
on every open set where the original morphism was smooth and the
marking relatively simple normal crossing.
statements.section_title: Local constructions for the numerical comparison

statements.title: A continuous-lift criterion
statements.label: prop:continuous-gradient-lift
statements.text:
Assume that $d_xG\ne0$ off $A$ and that, at every point of $A$,
\begin{equation}

 \frac{|G_u(x,u)|}{\|d_xG(x,u)\|}\longrightarrow0
 \qquad\text{as }(x,u)\longrightarrow A,\quad x\ne0.
\end{equation}
For each $a=1,i$, suppose that $X^*$ carries a smooth real vector field
$v_a=(w_a,a)$ with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $dG(v_a)=0$ and $w_a(x,u)\to0$ on approach to every point of $A$;
\item no trajectory of $v_a$ in $X^*$ has a finite-time endpoint in
      $A$ lying inside the representative, in either time direction.
\end{enumerate}
Then, after shrinking, there is an ambient homeomorphism germ
\[
 H(x,u)=(H_u(x),u),\qquad
 G(H_u(x),u)=G(x,0),\qquad H_u(0)=0,
\]
with $H_0=\mathrm{id}$ and with $H$ and $H^{-1}$ jointly continuous.

statements.title: An explicit Whitney lift
statements.label: cor:gradient-whitney
statements.text:
Suppose that $G$ satisfies the analytic and gradient hypotheses of
Proposition~\ref{prop:continuous-gradient-lift} and that $(X^*,A)$
satisfies the Whitney conditions.  Then $G$ has the trivialization
of that proposition.  The fields on $X^*$ can be chosen to preserve
$\|x\|^2$, and every constant real combination has the same property.

statements.title: Continuous lifts from a resolution
statements.label: cor:gradient-resolution
statements.text:
Suppose that $G$ satisfies the analytic and gradient hypotheses of
Proposition~\ref{prop:continuous-gradient-lift}.  Suppose that there
is a proper holomorphic map $b:M\to\{G=0\}$ over $D$, an
isomorphism away from $A$, such that the composite $q:M\to D$ is
smooth and $E=b^{-1}(A)$ is a relative
normal-crossing divisor.  Then $G$ has the trivialization of that
proposition.  The fields on $X^*$ satisfy the trajectory condition
for every constant real combination.

title: Tracial projection methods and uniform property Gamma
abstract: For a simple, separable, unital, infinite-dimensional, nuclear, stably finite C∗-algebra with traces, real rank zero of the uniform tracial ultrapower of its uniform tracial completion implies uniform property Γ. This answers Problem XXI of Schafhauser, Tikuisis and White affirmatively. Independently, strict comparison implies Jiang–Su absorption for simple, separable, unital, infinite-dimensional nuclear algebras, resolving the unital Toms–Winter conjecture. Under comparison tested on traces of finite target rank, we also obtain uniform property Γ and absorption for simple, separable, nuclear, stably projectionless algebras whose densely finite traces are all bounded and have a nonempty compact normalized base.

tex.abstract:
For a simple, separable, unital, infinite-dimensional, nuclear, stably finite
$C^*$-algebra with traces, real rank zero of the uniform tracial ultrapower
of its uniform tracial completion implies uniform property $\Gamma$.
This answers Problem XXI of Schafhauser, Tikuisis and White affirmatively.
Independently, strict comparison implies Jiang--Su absorption for simple,
separable, unital, infinite-dimensional nuclear algebras, resolving the
unital Toms--Winter conjecture. Under comparison tested on traces of finite
target rank, we also obtain uniform property $\Gamma$ and absorption for
simple, separable, nuclear, stably projectionless algebras whose densely
finite traces are all bounded and have a nonempty compact normalized base.

statements.title: Real rank zero and uniform property $\Gamma$
statements.label: r:thm:main
statements.text:
Let $A$ be a unital, separable, simple, infinite-dimensional, nuclear,
stably finite $C^*$-algebra with $T(A)\ne\varnothing$, and let
$B=\overline A^{T(A)}$. Fix any free ultrafilter $\omega$ on $\N$.
If $B^\omega$ has real rank zero in its quotient $C^*$-norm, then there is
a projection $p\in B^\omega\cap B'$ such that
\[
 \lambda(px)=\tfrac12\lambda(x)
 \qquad(x\in B,\ \lambda\in\Lambda_\omega).
\]
In particular, $A$ has uniform property $\Gamma$.

statements.title: Traces on the completion
statements.label: r:cor:completion-traces
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{r:thm:main}, including real rank zero
of $B^\omega$ in its quotient $C^*$-norm, every tracial state of $B$ is
the designated extension of a unique trace in $T(A)$. Thus restriction
is an affine homeomorphism $T(B)\to T(A)$, with inverse
$\tau\mapsto\bar\tau$. Moreover,
\[
 |\sigma(b)|\le\|b\|_{2,T(A)}
 \qquad(b\in B,\ \sigma\in T(B)),
\]
so every tracial state of $B$ is continuous for the designated uniform
$2$-norm.

statements.title: Finite-set central splitting
statements.label: r:thm:finite
statements.text:
Let $A\subseteq D$ be a unital inclusion of $C^*$-algebras, with $A$ nuclear,
$D$ of real rank zero, and $T(D)\ne\varnothing$. Suppose that for every
$\delta>0$ there is a full projection $g\in D$ with
$\sup_{\tau\in T(D)}\tau(g)<\delta$.
For every finite $K\subseteq\mathcal U(A)$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there is a
projection $P\in D$ such that, for every $x\in K$,
\[
 \sup_{\tau\in T(D)}\|[P,x]\|_{2,\tau}<\varepsilon,
 \qquad
 \sup_{\tau\in T(D)}|\tau(Px)-\tfrac12\tau(x)|<\varepsilon.
\]

statements.title: The direct unital comparison route
statements.label: u:thm:main
statements.text:
Let $A$ be a simple, separable, unital, infinite-dimensional nuclear
$C^*$-algebra with strict comparison in the preceding sense.
Then $A\cong A\otimes\Z$. When $T(A)\ne\varnothing$, the proof constructs
uniform property $\Gamma$ directly.

statements.title: The direct stably projectionless route
statements.label: n:thm:main
statements.text:
Let $A$ be a nonzero simple, separable, nuclear $C^*$-algebra such that
$A\otimes\K$ has no nonzero projections. Suppose that every trace in
$T_{\mathrm{lsc}}(A)$ is bounded on the positive unit ball and that
$T_1(A)$ is nonempty and weak-$*$ compact. Assume that, for
$a,b\in(A\otimes\K)_+$ with $b\ne0$,
\[
 d_\tau(a)<1\quad
 \text{for every }\tau\in T_{\mathrm{lsc}}(A)
 \text{ with }d_\tau(b)=1
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad a\precsim b.
\]
Then $A$ has uniform property $\Gamma$ and $A\cong A\otimes\Z$.

statements.title: Uniform proportional subprojections
statements.label: r:proj:split
statements.text:
Assume that for every $\delta>0$ there is a full projection $g\in D$ with
$\sup_{\tau\in\T(D)}\tau(g)<\delta$.
For every projection $f\in D$, every $s\in[0,1]$, and every $\eps>0$,
there is a projection $e\le f$ such that
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{\tau\in\T(D)}|\tau(e)-s\tau(f)|<\eps.
\end{equation}

statements.title: Splitting finite linear tests
statements.label: r:proj:tests
statements.text:
Under the small-full-projection hypothesis of Proposition~\ref{r:proj:split},
let $q\in D$ be a projection, $s\in[0,1]$, and $\mathcal F\subset D$ a
finite set.  For every $\eps>0$, there is a projection $e\le q$ such that
\begin{equation}
  |\tau(eh)-s\tau(qh)|<\eps
  \qquad(h\in\mathcal F,\ \tau\in\T(D)).
\end{equation}

statements.title: Weighted matrix blocks
statements.label: r:weighted:family
statements.text:
Let \(K\subseteq\U(A)\) be finite and \(0<\eta<1\).
There are contractions \(v_1,\ldots,v_m\in A\) and nonnegative numbers
\(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m\) summing to one, chosen using only
\(K,\eta\), such that the map
\begin{equation}
 \Phi:D\longrightarrow D,\qquad
 \Phi(b)=\sum_{l=1}^m\lambda_l v_lbv_l^*,
\end{equation}
satisfies \eqref{r:eq:diagonal-mass} with \(\mu=\eta^2\).
For every projection \(r\in D\), there is a finite family consisting of
weights \(0<w_j\leq1\), nonzero projections \(q_j\leq r\), integers
\(k_j\geq1\), and rows \(U_j\in M_{1,k_j}(D)\), such that, with
\(p_j=U_jU_j^*\),
\begin{align}
 U_j^*U_j&=1_{k_j}\otimes q_j,\\
 \dist\big(U_j^*xU_j,M_{k_j}(\C)\otimes q_j\big)&<\eta
       &&(x\in K),\\
 \normone{\sum_jw_jp_j-\Phi(r)}{\tau}&\leq\eta^2,
       \\
 \sum_jw_j\normtwo{[x,p_j]}{\tau}^2&\leq6\eta
       &&(x\in K).
\end{align}
The last two estimates hold for every \(\tau\in\T(D)\). The family may
be empty; the base projections \(q_j\) may repeat, and the projections
\(p_j\) need not be mutually orthogonal.
statements.section_title: Nuclear averaging and weighted matrix blocks

statements.title: Castillejos--Evington--Tikuisis--White
statements.label: u:thm:gamma-criterion
statements.text:
Let $A$ be simple, separable, unital and nuclear, with
$T(A)\ne\varnothing$. If $A$ has strict comparison in the
functional formulation and uniform property $\Gamma$, then
\[
 A\cong A\otimes_{\min}\Zalg.
\]

statements.title: Uniform approximation of trace values by ranks
statements.label: u:prop:rank-approximation
statements.text:
Let $A$ be a simple, unital, infinite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra with
$T=T(A)\ne\varnothing$.  For every $b\in A_+$ and $\delta>0$ there
are an integer $L\ge1$ and $v\in M_L(A)_+$ such that
\begin{equation}
 \tau(b)-\delta<d_\tau(v)\le\tau(b)
 \qquad(\tau\in T).
 
\end{equation}
This statement requires neither separability, nuclearity nor strict
comparison.  There is no asserted bound on $L$ independent of $b$ and
$\delta$.

statements.title: Centered symmetries in finite-dimensional commutants
statements.label: u:prop:centered-symmetry
statements.text:
Let $E\subset D$ be a finite-dimensional $C^*$-subalgebra, possibly
nonunital, and let $S\subset D$ be a unital norm-separable
$C^*$-subalgebra.  There is a selfadjoint unitary $r\in D\cap E'$ such
that
\begin{equation}

 \tau(sr)=0\qquad(s\in S,\ \tau\in\Lambda).
\end{equation}

statements.title: Hirshberg--Kirchberg--White, {\cite[Theorem~1.4]{HKW}}
statements.label: u:thm:hkw-approximation
statements.text:
Let $N$ be a nuclear $C^*$-algebra, let $K\subset N$ be finite, and let
$\varepsilon>0$.  There are a finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra $F$ and
completely positive contractive maps
\[
 N\xrightarrow{\psi}F\xrightarrow{\phi}N
\]
such that $\norm{\phi\psi(x)-x}<\varepsilon$ for $x\in K$, and
\[
 \phi=\sum_{i=1}^{M}\beta_i\phi_i,
 \qquad \beta_i\ge0,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^{M}\beta_i=1,
\]
where each $\phi_i:F\to N$ is completely positive, contractive, and of
order zero.  The number $M$ is finite for the chosen approximation;
no bound on $M$ independent of $K$ and $\varepsilon$ is asserted.
statements.section_title: Nuclear averaging and bounded conditional moments

statements.title: An observable with exact coefficient moments
statements.label: u:prop:averaged-observable
statements.text:
Let $E\subset A$ be a finite set of selfadjoint contractions and let
$0<\eta<1$.  There is a selfadjoint $z\in D$ such that, for every
$\tau\in\Lambda$,
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
  \norm{[z,a]}_{2,\tau}^{2}&\le72\eta &&(a\in E),\\
  \tau(bz)&=0,\qquad \tau(bz^2)=\tau(b) &&(b\in A),\\
  \tau(z^4)&\le3.
 \end{aligned}
 
\end{equation}
The construction gives
$z=\sum_{i=1}^M\sqrt{\beta_i}\,r_i$, where the $r_i$ are selfadjoint
unitaries, $\beta_i\ge0$, and $\sum_i\beta_i=1$.  In fact,
$\tau(z^4)\le3-2\sum_i\beta_i^2$.  There is no asserted norm bound on
$z$ independent of $M$.

statements.title: Relative moment estimates
statements.label: u:prop:relative-moments
statements.text:
Let $C\subset D$ be a unital norm-separable $C^*$-subalgebra and fix
$R\geq1$.  There is a selfadjoint element $d\in D\cap C'$ with
$\norm{d}\leq R$ such that, for every $b\in C$ with $\norm{b}\leq1$ and
every $\tau\in\Lambda$,
\begin{equation}

  |\tau(bd)|\leq\frac{3}{R^3},\qquad
  |\tau(b(d^2-1))|\leq\frac{3}{R^2},\qquad
  \tau(d^4)\leq3.
\end{equation}

statements.title: Uniform property Gamma
statements.label: u:thm:uniform-gamma
statements.text:
Let $A$ be a simple, separable, unital, infinite-dimensional nuclear
$C^*$-algebra with nonempty tracial-state space and strict comparison
as in Definition~\ref{u:def:strict-comparison}.  For every integer
$m\geq1$ there exist pairwise orthogonal projections
$p_1,\ldots,p_m\in D\cap A'$ such that
\begin{equation}

  \sum_{i=1}^m p_i=1,
  \qquad
  \tau(ap_i)=\frac{\tau(a)}{m}
  \quad(a\in A,\ \tau\in\Lambda,\ 1\leq i\leq m).
\end{equation}
In particular, $A$ has uniform property $\Gamma$.

statements.label: n:prop:selection
statements.text:
Let $h,z,a\in D$ be positive contractions satisfying $hz=z$ and
$\tau(a)\le\tau(z)$ for all $\tau\in \Lambda$. There is a projection $p\in D$
such that
\[
 hp=p,\qquad \tau(p)=\tau(a)\quad(\tau\in \Lambda).
\]

statements.label: n:prop:models
statements.text:
For a finite set $\mathcal F$ of self-adjoint contractions in $A$ and
$\Delta>0$, there are unital finite-dimensional subalgebras $D_i\subset D$,
self-adjoint contractions $x^{(i)}\in D_i$ for each $x\in\mathcal F$, and
positive weights $w_i$ summing to one, such that
\begin{equation}
 E_i=\sum_{x\in\mathcal F}(x-x^{(i)})^2,
 \qquad \sum_iw_i\tau(E_i)<\Delta\quad(\tau\in \Lambda).
\end{equation}

statements.label: n:prop:split
n:thm:gamma
statements.text:
For every $n\ge2$ there are orthogonal projections $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in
D\cap A'$ summing to $1_D$ such that
\[
 \tau(f_i a)=\frac1n\tau(a)\qquad(a\in A,\ \tau\in \Lambda).
\]
In particular, $A$ has uniform property $\Gamma$.

abstract: For every sufficiently large dimension n, we construct a centrally symmetric convex body whose translative covering density exceeds \(c n\log n\), where c > 0 is absolute. This disproves the existence of a universal linear upper bound and matches the order of Rogers' upper bound.

tex.abstract:
For every sufficiently large dimension $n$, we construct a centrally symmetric
convex body whose translative covering density exceeds $c n\log n$,
where $c>0$ is absolute. This disproves the existence of a universal linear
upper bound and matches the order of Rogers' upper bound.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There are absolute constants $c>0$ and $n_0$ such that, for every integer
$n\ge n_0$, some centrally symmetric convex body $K_n\subset\mathbb R^n$
satisfies
\[
 \theta_T(K_n)>c n\log n.
\]

statements.title: Deterministic localization
statements.label: prop:localization
statements.text:
For all sufficiently large $n$, uniformly for $1\le R\le n^2$, the family
$\mathcal F_n$ has the following properties.  With
$\lambda_0=\log(1+D/a)$,
\begin{equation}
 N_n\le n^{C_1}\exp(\lambda_0n),\qquad
 \log|\mathcal F_n|
       \le\exp\bigl(\lambda_0n+O(\log n)\bigr),
\end{equation}
where $C_1$ and the implicit constant depend only on the fixed parameters.

Let $\mathcal U\subset S^{n-1}$ be any finite set, and put
\[
 K=bB\cap\bigcap_{u\in\mathcal U}\{x:|u\cdot x|\le1\},\qquad
 K^+=(b+3\eta)B\cap
          \bigcap_{u\in\mathcal U}\{x:|u\cdot x|\le1+3\eta\}.
\]
Suppose that $\Lambda$ is any full-rank lattice, $T\subset\mathbb R^n$
is finite, and
\[
 \frac{|T|}{\det\Lambda}\le
       \rho_0:=\frac{R}{2v\omega_na^n}.
\]
If $K+\Lambda+T$ covers $\mathbb R^n$, there is a list
$P=(p_1,\ldots,p_m)\in\mathcal F_n$
such that
\begin{equation}
 B_D\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^{m}(p_j+K^+).
\end{equation}
The constructed list in fact satisfies $|G_P|\ge|B_D|/2$.

For every $P\in\mathcal F_n$ and $y\in G_P$, list all residual vectors
$x_i=y-p_j$ with $|y-p_j|\le b+3\eta$, retaining their indices, and denote
their number by $m_y$.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
 r_--2\eta\le |x_i|\le b+3\eta,\qquad
 m_y\le2C_{\mathrm{loc}}R,\qquad
 \sum_{i=1}^{m_y}w_a(|x_i|)\le2C_{\mathrm{loc}}R,\\
 m_y+\sum_{i=1}^{m_y}w_a(|x_i|)\le4C_{\mathrm{loc}}R.
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}

statements.label: cor:caps-disjoint
statements.text:
With \(\varepsilon=2^{-30}\) and \(a=1+\varepsilon\), caps satisfying
the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:caps} are disjoint whenever their
axes have projective angle greater than \(4\sqrt\varepsilon\), for
all sufficiently large \(n\).

statements.title: Block estimates
statements.label: prop:blocks
statements.text:
Fix constants $C_0\ge1$, $c_0>0$, and $L\ge1$.
There are constants $B_0,K,C\ge1$ and $n_1$, depending only on these
three constants, with the following property.
Let $n\ge n_1$, let $(X,\mu)$ be an atomless finite measure space, and let
$(C_i)_{i\in I}$ be an indexed list of measurable sets with
$0<c_i:=\mu(C_i)<\infty$ and $1\le m:=|I|\le n^2$.
Set
\[
 \bar c_i=\min(c_i,1/2),\qquad s_i=-\log\bar c_i,
\]
and let $d$ be a pseudometric on $I$.  For nonempty $S\subseteq I$, write
\[
 r(S)=\min_{j\in S}\max_{i\in S}d(i,j)^2,
\]
and choose an index $i(S)\in S$ minimizing the uncapped measure $c_i$.
Assume that
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\mu(C_i\cap C_j)}{\sqrt{\bar c_i\bar c_j}}
 \le C_0e^{-c_0d(i,j)^2}\qquad(i,j\in I),
\end{equation}
and that, whenever $r(S)\le B_0\log n$,
\begin{equation}
 \mu\left(\bigcap_{i\in S}C_i\right)
 \ge e^{-L(1+r(S)+\log|S|)}\bar c_{i(S)}.
\end{equation}
Then there is a partition $\mathcal P$ of $I$ and measurable sets
$E_S\subseteq\bigcap_{i\in S}C_i$, $S\in\mathcal P$, of measures
$\lambda_S=\mu(E_S)$ such that
\begin{equation}
 n^{-K}\bar c_{i(S)}\le\lambda_S\le\frac12.
\end{equation}
Writing $q_S=-\log\lambda_S$ and
\[
 w_{ST}=
 \frac{\mu(E_S\cap E_T)}
 {\sqrt{\lambda_S(1+\lambda_S)\lambda_T(1+\lambda_T)}},
\]
we have
\begin{align}
 \sum_{S\in\mathcal P}q_S
 &\le\sum_{i\in I}s_i+\frac{m}{10},
 \\
 \sum_{S\in\mathcal P}\log(1+\lambda_S^{-1})
 &\le C\left(m+\sum_{i\in I}s_i\right),
 \\
 \sum_{S\in\mathcal P}
 \log\left(1+\sum_{T\in\mathcal P\setminus\{S\}}w_{ST}\right)
 &\le C\left(m+\sum_{i\in I}s_i\right).
 
\end{align}

statements.title: Poisson lower tail
statements.label: prop:poisson
statements.text:
Let $\Pi$ be a Poisson process on a finite nonatomic standard Borel
measure space. For each member of a finite nonempty family, take a
finite nonempty labeled list of measurable slots of positive intensity.
Let $Z_\alpha$ count their injective assignments, let $\nu_\alpha$ be
the product of their intensities, and define $D_{\alpha\beta}$ by
\eqref{eq:diagram-definition}. Then $\mathbb{E}Z_\alpha=\nu_\alpha$,
and
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb{P}(Z_\alpha=0\text{ for all }\alpha\in\mathcal A)
 \le\exp\left[-\frac{(\sum_\alpha\nu_\alpha)^2}
                        {2\sum_{\alpha,\beta}D_{\alpha\beta}}\right].
 
\end{equation}
The denominator is positive: the full identity matching in
$D_{\alpha\alpha}$ contributes $\nu_\alpha$.
statements.section_title: Poisson witnesses and their lower tail

statements.title: Witnesses for residual lists
statements.label: cor:witnesses
statements.text:
Fix $A_0>0$. There are constants $A,C_*,H>0$ such that, for all
sufficiently large $n$, the following holds. Let $R\ge1$, and let
$(x_{\alpha i})_{i=1}^{m_\alpha}$, $\alpha\in\mathcal A$, be any
finite nonempty family of deterministic lists satisfying
\[
 1\le m_\alpha\le n^2,\qquad
 r_--3\eta\le |x_{\alpha i}|\le b+3\eta.
\]
Define
\[
 C_{\alpha i}=\{u\in S^{n-1}:|u\cdot x_{\alpha i}|>1+3\eta\},
 \qquad
 s_{\alpha i}=-\log\min\{\mu(C_{\alpha i}),1/2\},
\]
and suppose $m_\alpha+\sum_i s_{\alpha i}\le A_0R$.
For each list there is a nonempty block partition and measurable slots
$E_{\alpha S}\subseteq\bigcap_{i\in S}C_{\alpha i}$, chosen
independently of $\Pi$, with positive intensities at most $1/2$.
Their activities and diagrams satisfy
\begin{equation}
 e^{-AR}\le\nu_\alpha\le1,\qquad
 D_{\alpha\alpha}\le\nu_\alpha^2e^{C_*R}.
 
\end{equation}
For distinct $\alpha,\beta$, if all cross-residual angles exceed
$H\sqrt{\log n/n}$, then
\begin{equation}
 D_{\alpha\beta}\le n^{-3}\nu_\alpha\nu_\beta.
 
\end{equation}
If all those angles exceed $4\sqrt\varepsilon$, then
$D_{\alpha\beta}=0$. A positive injection count for a list implies
that every cap in that list is hit by $\Pi$.

statements.title: Failure probability for one pattern
statements.label: prop:pattern-tail
statements.text:
There are constants $c_0,C_{\mathrm{tail}}>0$ and $n_0$ such that, whenever
$n\ge n_0$ and $1\le R\le c_0n\log n$, every retained pattern
$P\in\mathcal F_n$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:localization} satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P\left(B_D\subseteq\bigcup_{p\in P}(p+K^+)\right)
 \le \exp\left[-\exp\bigl(\gamma n-C_{\mathrm{tail}}\log n\bigr)\right].

\end{equation}
The constants are independent of the pattern, its repetitions, and $R$.
statements.section_title: Many targets for each finite pattern

statements.label: cor:sharp-order
statements.text:
As $n\to\infty$, each of the four quantities
\begin{gather*}
 \sup_{K\in\mathcal K^n}\theta_T(K),\qquad
 \sup_{K\in\mathcal K^n_{\mathrm{sym}}}\theta_T(K),\\
 \sup_{K\in\mathcal K^n}\theta_L(K),\qquad
 \sup_{K\in\mathcal K^n_{\mathrm{sym}}}\theta_L(K)
\end{gather*}
has order $n\log n$, with absolute comparison constants.

statements.label: cor:rational-polytope
statements.text:
With the same $c$ and $n_0$ as in Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, for every
$n\ge n_0$ there is a centrally symmetric polytope
$P_n\subset\mathbb R^n$ with rational vertices such that
\[
 \theta_T(P_n)>c n\log n.
\]

statements.label: prop:rational
statements.text:
The bodies in Theorem~\ref{thm:main} can be chosen in the form
\[
 K=bB\cap\bigcap_{j=1}^m\{x:|u_j\cdot x|\le1\},
 \qquad u_j\in\mathbb Q^n\cap S^{n-1},
\]
with $m<\infty$.

statements.title: Periodization
statements.label: prop:periodization
statements.text:
For every convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$,
\[
 \theta_T(K)=\theta_{\mathrm{per}}(K).
\]
The same infimum is obtained by replacing the centered cube upper density
by centered cube lower density or centered Euclidean-ball lower or upper
density. These are equalities of infima over coverings; the corresponding
statistics of one covering need not agree.

title: Tree Constructions for the l1 Distortion of Binary Edit Distance
abstract: We give two independent constructions of binary words of one length at most d whose ordinary edit-distance metrics require ℓ1 distortion \(\exp(\Omega(\sqrt{\log d\,\log\log d}))\) for every sufficiently large d. We also prove a constant-distortion binary conversion for one prescribed input length. Together with the companion upper embedding theorem, these lower bounds determine the order of logarithmic distortion uniformly over finite alphabets with at least two symbols.

tex.abstract:
We give two independent constructions of binary words of one length at
most $d$ whose ordinary edit-distance metrics require $\ell_1$ distortion
$\exp(\Omega(\sqrt{\log d\,\log\log d}))$ for every sufficiently large $d$.
We also prove a constant-distortion binary conversion for one prescribed
input length. Together with the companion upper embedding theorem, these
lower bounds determine the order of logarithmic distortion uniformly over
finite alphabets with at least two symbols.

statements.title: Binary lower bound
statements.label: thm:binary
statements.text:
There are an absolute constant $c>0$ and an integer $d_0$ such that,
for every integer $d\geq d_0$, there exist an integer $1\leq n\leq d$ and a
finite set $\mathcal W\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$ with $|\mathcal W|\geq2$
satisfying
\[
 c_1(\mathcal W,\ED)
 \geq \exp\!\left(c\sqrt{\log d\,\log\log d}\right).
\]

statements.label: prop:finite-separation

statements.title: Finite obstruction
statements.label: prop:finite-lower
statements.text:
For all sufficiently large $k$, the word image $\{G(x):x\in A\}$,
with ordinary edit distance, has $\ellone$ distortion at least
$C_1^{-1}(k/4)^k$, for an absolute constant $C_1$.

statements.title: Goodness of a fixed shift
statements.label: prop:good-probability
statements.text:
For all sufficiently large $k$, every node $v$ and every fixed
$t\in\T$ with $|t|_{\T}\geq\epsilon$ satisfy
\[
 \Prb[t\text{ is good at }v]\geq9/10,
\]
where probability is over the construction in the subtree below $v$.
Consequently, there exists a realization of the entire tree for which
\begin{equation}
 r_N(X(w),X(w+1/2))\geq\gamma^kN
 \qquad\text{for every }w\in\T^{m^k}.
\end{equation}

statements.title: Uniform upper embedding, companion theorem
statements.label: thm:companion-upper
statements.text:
There are absolute constants $C>0$ and $d_0\geq3$ such that, for every
finite alphabet $\Sigma$ with $|\Sigma|\geq2$ and every integer
$d\geq d_0$, there are an integer $M\geq1$ and one deterministic map
$f:\Sigma^{\leq d}\to\ell_1^M$ satisfying
\[
 \ED(x,y)\leq\|f(x)-f(y)\|_1
 \leq\exp\!\left(C\sqrt{\log d\,\log\log d}\right)\ED(x,y)
 \qquad(x,y\in\Sigma^{\leq d}).
\]
Here $\ell_1^M$ is $\R^M$ with its usual $\ell_1$ norm. The domain
includes the empty word, and $\ED$ is ordinary unit-cost insertion,
deletion and substitution distance. The dimension may depend on
$\Sigma,d$; the constants and threshold do not.

statements.label: cor:matching
statements.text:
There are absolute $c,C>0$ and an integer $d_2$ such that for every
integer $d\geq d_2$ and every finite alphabet $\Sigma$ with
$|\Sigma|\geq2$,
\begin{equation}
 \exp\!\left(c\sqrt{\log d\,\log\log d}\right)
 \leq E_\Sigma(d)\leq
 \exp\!\left(C\sqrt{\log d\,\log\log d}\right).
\end{equation}
The same bounds hold for
$\sup_{\Sigma:\,2\leq|\Sigma|<\infty}E_\Sigma(d)$.

statements.title: Fixed-length binary conversion
statements.label: thm:804
statements.text:
There is an absolute integer $M_0$ such that, for every integer
$M\geq M_0$ and every alphabet $\Gamma$ with $1\leq K=|\Gamma|\leq M$,
there exists a map $c:\Gamma\to\{0,1\}^{P}$ with $P=M^2$ whose
concatenation extension $\enc$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \frac P{804}\ED(x,y)
 \leq\ED(\enc(x),\enc(y))\leq P\ED(x,y)
 \qquad(x,y\in\Gamma^M).
\end{equation}
The encoded words have length $MP=M^3$. More precisely,
\begin{equation}
 r_{MP}(\enc(x),\enc(y))\geq\frac P{402}r_M(x,y)
 \qquad(x,y\in\Gamma^M).
\end{equation}

title: Triangular minimality for planar Coulomb renormalized energy
abstract: We prove the Sandier–Serfaty conjecture: the triangular lattice of covolume one minimizes planar Coulomb renormalized energy over all admissible curl-free fields with a unit uniform background. Combined with Bétermin and Sandier's asymptotic formula, this also proves the Brauchart–Hardin–Saff conjecture for the linear term of optimal ordered-pair logarithmic energy on the unit two-sphere. The proof uses a direct Voronoi-cell comparison with rigorous interval arithmetic.

tex.abstract:
We prove the Sandier--Serfaty conjecture: the triangular lattice of
covolume one minimizes planar Coulomb renormalized energy over all admissible
curl-free fields with a unit uniform background. Combined with B\'etermin and
Sandier's asymptotic formula, this also proves the Brauchart--Hardin--Saff
conjecture for the linear term of optimal ordered-pair logarithmic energy on
the unit two-sphere. The proof uses a direct Voronoi-cell comparison with
rigorous interval arithmetic.

statements.text:

$E\in\mathcal A_1$,
\[
W(E)\geq W(E_\triangle).
\]
The triangular value is finite, and

statements.title: Reduction to square tori
statements.label: red:reduction
statements.text:
Let $C\in\R$.  Suppose that for every integer $n\ge2$ and every
configuration of $n$ distinct points of $T_n$, the mean-zero
potential in \eqref{eq:torus-energy} satisfies
$\mathcal W_n(h)\ge nC$.  Then $W(E)\ge C$ for every
$E\in\mathcal A_1$.  In particular, if these finite-torus bounds
hold with $C=W(E_\triangle)$, then
\[
 \inf_{E\in\mathcal A_1}W(E)=W(E_\triangle).
\]
statements.section_title: From square tori to the full plane

statements.title: Dual identity
statements.label: dual:identity
statements.text:
For compatible periodic Voronoi data on
\(\mathbb T=\R^2/\Gamma\) with \(N\geq1\) distinct sites, lower edge
distance \(d_0>0\), and \(|\mathbb T|=N\), let \(h\) be the mean-zero
potential \eqref{dual:torus-potential}. Let \(I\) be finite or countable,
let \(k_i\geq6\) be integers with repetitions permitted, and let
\(B,D_i\in C^1((0,\infty))\) satisfy
\eqref{dual:radial-origin}--\eqref{dual:radial-sum}. Let \(H\) be the
function supplied by Lemma~\ref{dual:gluing}. Then
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal W_{\mathbb T}(h)
   =\sum_S J(S)+
              \frac12\int_{\mathbb T}|\nabla(h-H)|^2\,\dd x
   \geq\sum_S J(S).
 
\end{equation}
The sum runs over all face--edge incidences in one torus.
No incidence bound or square-torus separation hypothesis is imposed.
statements.section_title: Voronoi sectors and a glued dual potential

statements.title: From sector bounds to energy bounds
statements.label: dual:assembly
statements.text:
Let \(d_0>0\), let \(I\) be finite or countable, let \(k_i\geq6\)
be integers with repetitions permitted, and let
\(B,D_i\in C^1((0,\infty))\) satisfy
\eqref{dual:radial-origin} and \eqref{dual:radial-sum} with
this lower distance \(d_0\). For every sector \eqref{geo:sector} with
\(d\geq d_0\), use these same radial data in \eqref{dual:trial} and
let \(J(S)\) be the functional \eqref{dual:sector-functional}.
Suppose that \(K\leq0\) and \(\lambda,\mu\in\R\) satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \begin{aligned}
 J(S(d,\alpha,\beta))
 &\geq K+\lambda A(S(d,\alpha,\beta))\\
 &\qquad+\mu\theta(S(d,\alpha,\beta)),
 \end{aligned}
 
\end{equation}
for every \(d\geq d_0\), \(|\alpha|,|\beta|<\pi/2\), and
\(\alpha+\beta>0\).

\emph{Compatible tori.}
Let \(\mathbb T=\R^2/\Gamma\) have area \(N\), where \(N\geq1\)
is an integer. Suppose \(N\) distinct sites supply compatible periodic
Voronoi data with lower edge distance \(d_0\) and at most \(6N\)
face--edge sectors. Their mean-zero potential
\eqref{dual:torus-potential} satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal W_{\mathbb T}(h)\geq N(6K+\lambda+2\pi\mu).
\end{equation}

\emph{All square-torus configurations.}
Assume in addition \(d_0\leq d_*=1/(2\sqrt\pi)\). For every
integer \(n\geq2\) and every configuration of \(n\) distinct
points \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\) on \(T_n=\R^2/(\sqrt n\,\Z^2)\), let \(h\)
be the mean-zero solution of
\[
 -\Delta h=2\pi\left(\sum_{i=1}^n\delta_{v_i}-1\right).
\]
Then its puncture-first energy \eqref{eq:torus-energy}, with embedded
and pairwise disjoint punctures, satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal W_n(h)\geq n(6K+\lambda+2\pi\mu).
 
\end{equation}
More generally, if a periodic locally integrable field \(E\) on \(T_n\)
satisfies, distributionally,
\[
 \operatorname{div}E=2\pi\left(\sum_{i=1}^n\delta_{v_i}-1\right),
 \qquad \operatorname{curl}E=0,
\]
then \(E=-\nabla h+c\) for a constant \(c\in\R^2\), and its energy
with the same punctures and counterterm obeys
\[
 \mathcal E_{T_n}(E)=\mathcal W_n(h)+\frac n2|c|^2
                    \geq n(6K+\lambda+2\pi\mu).
\]
The energy identity remains valid after applying the same fixed
orthogonal rotation to both fields.
statements.section_title: Voronoi sectors and a glued dual potential

statements.label: cal:scalar-to-torus
statements.text:
Assume \eqref{cal:scalar-bounds} for the functions and constants just
constructed.  Let $\mathbb T=\R^2/\Gamma$ be a flat torus of area $N$,
where $N\ge1$ is an integer, and let $v_1,\ldots,v_N$ be distinct
sites.  Suppose their full periodic lift gives compatible periodic
Voronoi data with lower edge distance $d_0=b$ and at most $6N$
face-edge sectors.  Let $h$ be the mean-zero potential
\eqref{dual:torus-potential}, with energy
$\mathcal W_{\mathbb T}(h)$ defined by \eqref{dual:torus-energy}.
Then
\[
 \mathcal W_{\mathbb T}(h)\ge NW(E_\triangle).
\]

statements.title: Meaning of the finite assertions

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every system satisfying~\eqref{eq:mixing}, every triple of pairwise
distinct nonzero integers $\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3$, and every
bounded measurable $f_1,f_2,f_3:X\to\C$, the averages
in~\eqref{eq:averages} satisfy
\[
 A_N(x)\longrightarrow\prod_{j=1}^3\int_X f_j\,d\mu
 \quad\text{for almost every }x,
\]
as $N$ tends to infinity through all positive integers. The exceptional
null set may depend on the slopes and the functions.

statements.title: Local estimate with variation in depth
statements.label: thm:local
statements.text:
Fix the primitive distinct integers $b_0=0,b_1,b_2,b_3$ and the
parameters $\delta_0,C_0$. Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite dyadic tree with root
$J$ and largest depth $d$, and let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal T$.
Assign an admissible kernel to every $I\in\mathcal I$.
For each $0\le j\le3$, let $z_{j,s}:J\to\C$, $0\le s\le d$, be
measurable, and partition $\{0,\ldots,d\}$ into $W_j\ge1$
deterministic nonempty consecutive blocks. Suppose that
\[
 \mathcal V_B(z_j)\le W_j^{-1/2}\quad\text{almost everywhere on }J
\]
for each block in the $j$th partition. Extend every input by zero
outside $J$. Then
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{I\in\mathcal I}\abs{I}\,
 \abs{H_I(z_{0,s(I)},z_{1,s(I)},z_{2,s(I)},z_{3,s(I)})}
 \le C_{b,\delta_0,C_0}\abs{J}.
\end{equation}
The constant is independent of the lattice, tree, depth range,
subcollection, kernels, and the four partitions and their sizes.

statements.title: Short-block comparison
statements.label: prop:short-block-b
statements.text:
Let \(2<q<3\).  Let a finite dyadic tree piece have root \(R\), with
internal summation intervals in at most \(K\) consecutive depths and
within the original range of at most \(N\) depths.  Its terminal
intervals, called leaves, partition \(R\) and occur in this depth block
or one depth below it.  In role \(j\), let \(\mathbf z_j\) be a
deterministic Hilbert-space-valued function supported on \(R\), with
\(\|\mathbf z_j\|_{2,L}\le s_j\) on every leaf \(L\).
Suppose scalar randomizations \(z_j^\sigma\) satisfy
\[
 \bigl(\mathbb E_\sigma|z_j^\sigma(y)|^a\bigr)^{1/a}
 \le C_a\|\mathbf z_j(y)\|
\]
for \(a=2,4,8\), with constants independent of the tree and \(K\).
For measurable signs
\(|\epsilon_I(\sigma)|\le1\) and any subcollection of internal intervals,
\[
 \mathbb E_\sigma\left|
 \sum_I |I|\epsilon_I(\sigma)H_I(z_0^\sigma,z_1^\sigma,
                                  z_2^\sigma,z_3^\sigma)\right|
 \le (1+C_N(q))C_{q,b}(1+\log(K+2))^C
       (K+2)^{11(q-2)/(q-1)}|R|\prod_j s_j .
\]
The constant \(C_{q,b}\) may also depend on the fixed moment
bounds \(C_a\) and the kernel bounds.

statements.title: Normalized absorption
statements.label: prop:absorption
statements.text:
For the fixed $q$ chosen above and every sufficiently small
$\tau>0$, there is $A_\tau<\infty$, independent of $N$, such that
the following holds. Suppose a finite rooted dyadic subtree has root
$I_*$, its summation cells lie in at most $N$ consecutive depths,
and its fixed scalar inputs satisfy
\[
 \left(\abs I^{-1}\int_I\abs{f_j}^q\right)^{1/q}\le1
 \quad(0\le j\le3, I\text{ in the subtree}).
\]
Then, for any subset of summation cells and admissible kernels,
\[
 \sum_{I\text{ a summation cell}}\abs I\,\abs{H_I(f_0,f_1,f_2,f_3)}
 \le (A_\tau+\tau C_N(q))\abs{I_*}.
\]

title: Turn-Based Stochastic Mean-Payoff Games in Deterministic Quasipolynomial Time
abstract: We give a uniform deterministic quasipolynomial-time algorithm for finite turn-based stochastic mean-payoff games with signed integer rewards and rational chance-transition probabilities encoded in binary. It computes exactly the vertices of nonnegative value, including value zero, for the expectation of the pathwise liminf mean payoff. The algorithm uses exact rational arithmetic and \(2^{O((\log(L+2))^2)}\) bit operations, where L is the complete binary input length.

title: Two-step monodromy of special quasi-projective varieties
abstract: We give an independent proof that every complex linear representation of the ordinary fundamental group of a connected smooth special complex quasi-projective variety has virtually nilpotent image of class at most two. This conclusion was previously announced by Cao–Deng–Hacon–Păun. We also construct special open surfaces whose general quasi-Albanese fibres are not special.

tex.abstract:
We give an independent proof that every complex linear representation
of the ordinary fundamental group of a connected smooth special complex
quasi-projective variety has virtually nilpotent image of class at most
two. This conclusion was previously announced by
Cao--Deng--Hacon--P\u aun. We also construct special open surfaces whose
general quasi-Albanese fibres are not special.

statements.title: Two-step linear monodromy
statements.label: thm:linear
statements.text:
Let $V$ be a connected smooth special complex quasi-projective variety.
For every positive integer $d$ and every representation
$\rho:\pi_1(V)\to\GL_d(\C)$, the image $\rho(\pi_1(V))$ has a subgroup
of finite index and nilpotency class at most two.

statements.title: Completion under quasi-Albanese exactness
statements.label: thm:completion
statements.text:
Let $V$ be a connected smooth complex quasi-projective variety and let
$a:V\to A=\Alb(V)$ be its algebraic quasi-Albanese map. Suppose $a$ is
dominant, choose a smooth connected general fibre $F$ and a point
$v\in F$, and assume that the sequence of ordinary fundamental groups
\begin{equation}
 \pi_1(F,v)\longrightarrow\Gamma:=\pi_1(V,v)
 \xrightarrow{a_*}\Lambda:=\pi_1(A,a(v))\longrightarrow1
\end{equation}
is exact. Then every canonical rational unipotent quotient of $\Gamma$
has nilpotency class at most two. The full rational unipotent completion
is a finite-dimensional unipotent algebraic group of class at most two.
Every finite-dimensional complex unipotent representation of $\Gamma$
also has image of class at most two.

statements.label: thm:example
statements.text:
Let $E$ be a complex elliptic curve, let $q_1,\ldots,q_n$ be distinct points
of $\PP^1$, where $n\geq3$, and choose points $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ of $E$.
Let
\[
 b:Y=\Bl_{\{(e_i,q_i)\}_{i=1}^n}(E\times\PP^1)
     \longrightarrow E\times\PP^1.
\]
Write $D_i$ for the strict transform of $E\times\{q_i\}$ and put
$D=\sum_iD_i$ and $X=Y\setminus D$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2em]
\item $(Y,D)$ is a smooth projective special pair in the convention of
      \cite[Definitions 2.1--2.9]{CDHP2026}, including every upper model
      in that definition.
\item The morphism $a=(\operatorname{pr}_E\circ b)|_X:X\to E$ is the
      algebraic quasi-Albanese map, after choosing origins. Every
      fibre is connected, and its general fibre is
      $F\simeq\PP^1\setminus\{q_1,\ldots,q_n\}$.
\item The induced map $a_*:\pi_1(X)\to\pi_1(E)$ is an isomorphism.
      Thus $\pi_1(X)\simeq\Z^2$, and the homomorphism
      $\pi_1(F)\to\pi_1(X)$ is trivial.
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Log-Kodaira-zero monodromy
statements.label: cor:log-kodaira-zero
statements.text:
Let $V$ be a connected smooth complex quasi-projective variety with
logarithmic Kodaira dimension $\bar\kappa(V)=0$, and put
$\Gamma=\pi_1(V)$. For every positive integer $d$ and every
representation $\rho:\Gamma\to\GL_d(\C)$, the image $\rho(\Gamma)$ has
a subgroup of finite index and nilpotency class at most two. The full
rational unipotent completion of $\Gamma$ is a finite-dimensional
unipotent algebraic group of class at most two. Every finite-dimensional
complex unipotent representation of $\Gamma$ also has image of class
at most two.

title: Ultraflat real Littlewood polynomials
abstract: For every \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) and every sufficiently large integer N, there is a polynomial of length N with coefficients in \(\{-1,1\}\) whose modulus lies between \((1-\varepsilon)\sqrt N\) and \((1+\varepsilon)\sqrt N\) everywhere on the unit circle. tex.abstract:
For every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ and every sufficiently large integer $N$,
there is a polynomial of length $N$ with coefficients in $\{-1,1\}$ whose
modulus lies between $(1-\varepsilon)\sqrt N$ and
$(1+\varepsilon)\sqrt N$ everywhere on the unit circle. Thus real
Littlewood polynomials can be ultraflat through every sufficiently large
integer length. The signs may be chosen separately at each length.

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ there is an integer $N_0$ such that,
for every integer $N\ge N_0$, there are signs
$\varepsilon_0,\ldots,\varepsilon_{N-1}$ for which
\[
 (1-\varepsilon)\sqrt N
 \le\left|\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\varepsilon_k z^k\right|
 \le(1+\varepsilon)\sqrt N
 \qquad\text{for every }|z|=1.
\]

statements.label: prop:balanced
statements.text:
For every $0<\delta<1/100$, there are an integer $m\ge2$, a real
trigonometric polynomial $F$ on $\T^m$, and $v\in\R^m$ with the
following properties.  Its Fourier support
$\mathcal A\subset\Z^m\setminus\{0\}$ consists of at least two pairs
$\{a,-a\}$, with distinct pairs nonparallel.  If
\[
 c_a=\widehat F(a),\qquad \lambda_a=a\cdot v,\qquad w_a=|\lambda_a|,
\]
then, for an absolute constant $C$,
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
 \norm F_\infty\le1+\delta,\qquad w_a>0,\\
 1-C\delta\le\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}w_a<1,\qquad
 1\le\frac{|c_a|}{\sqrt{w_a}}\le1+C\delta
 \quad(a\in\mathcal A).
 \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
The coefficient ratios in \eqref{eq:balanced} are also at most $2$.
statements.section_title: A real auxiliary function with balanced coefficients

statements.label: prop:waves
statements.text:
There are absolute constants $C>0$ and $\delta_0>0$ with the following
property.  For every $0<\delta<\delta_0$, there are $N_0(\delta)$ and
$K_\delta<\infty$ such that, for every integer $N\ge N_0(\delta)$, there is
a continuous function $B_N:\T\to\C$ satisfying
\begin{align}
 B_N(-t)&=\overline{B_N(t)}, &
 1\le |B_N(t)|&\le 1+C\delta \quad(t\in\T),
 \\
 \sqrt N\,|\widehat B_N(k)|&\le 1+C\sqrt\delta
 &&(0\le k<N),\\
 \sum_{k<0\text{ or }k\ge N}|\widehat B_N(k)|
 &\le K_\delta N^{-1}.
\end{align}
Its Fourier coefficients are real, and its Fourier series converges
absolutely and represents $B_N$.

title: Unbounded Violations of the Square-Root Degree Bound
abstract: We disprove the Gopalan–Servedio square-root conjecture, even up to an arbitrary constant factor. For every real C > 0, there is a nonconstant Boolean function \(f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}\) on a finite sign cube such that \(\displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^n \widehat f(\{i\})\gt C\sqrt{\deg(f)}.\) Here \(\widehat f(\{i\})\) is the linear Fourier coefficient associated with the ith input, and \(\deg(f)\) is the degree of the real multilinear polynomial representing f.

tex.abstract:
We disprove the Gopalan--Servedio square-root conjecture, even up to an
arbitrary constant factor. For every real \(C>0\), there is a nonconstant
Boolean function \(f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}\) on a finite sign cube such that
\[
\sum_{i=1}^n \widehat f(\{i\})>C\sqrt{\deg(f)}.
\]
Here \(\widehat f(\{i\})\) is the linear Fourier coefficient associated with
the \(i\)th input, and \(\deg(f)\) is the degree of the real multilinear
polynomial representing \(f\).
sections: Retaining more variance than the degree cost
A small-width Gaussian calculation for the coarse report

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
For every real \(C>0\), there are a positive integer \(n\) and a
nonconstant Boolean function \(f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}\) such that
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^n\widehat f(\{i\})>C\sqrt{\deg(f)}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \sup_{\substack{n\ge1,\ f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}\\\deg(f)>0}}
 \frac{\sum_i|\widehat f(\{i\})|}{\sqrt{\deg(f)}}=\infty.
\]

statements.title: Amplification criterion
statements.label: prop:amplification
statements.text:
Let \(1\le d<r\) be integers, and let \(\mathcal W\) be a measurable
observation rule on \(r\) real inputs. Suppose:
\begin{enumerate}
\item On any product of finite input alphabets, the indicator of each
output value is a finite linear combination of functions each depending
on at most \(d\) input coordinates.
\item There is an \(\eta>0\) such that, whenever centered variance-one
laws \(Z_j\) converge weakly to a standard normal with uniformly bounded
fourth moments, independent copies satisfy, for all sufficiently large \(j\),
\[
 \Var\!\left(\E\!\left[\sum_{i=1}^r Z_{j,i}\,\middle|\,
                \mathcal W(\mathbf Z_j)\right]\right)\ge d+\eta.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Then finite observations have arbitrarily large retained
variance-to-cell-degree ratios, and Theorem~\ref{thm:main} follows.

statements.title: Amplification from a mean cost advantage
statements.label: thm:mean-cost
statements.text:
Let $q\ge2$, let $\mathcal P:\R^q\to\mathcal L$ be a measurable map
to a finite label set, and let $\ell:\mathcal L\to\{1,\ldots,q\}$.
Suppose that, on every product of finite input alphabets, each cell
indicator for $l$ is a finite linear combination of functions of at
most $\ell(l)$ input coordinates.  Suppose also that every cell has
boundary of standard Gaussian measure zero in $\R^q$.  For independent standard
normals $G_1,\ldots,G_q$, put
\[
 S_G=\sum_{i=1}^qG_i,\qquad
 V=\Var(\E[S_G\mid\mathcal P(G)]),\qquad
 c=\E\ell(\mathcal P(G)).
\]
If $V>c$, then finite observations on sign cubes have arbitrarily
large ratios $v(F)/D$, where $D>0$ is a cell degree bound.
The Boolean conclusion of Theorem~\ref{thm:main} follows by taking the
sign of the final score, without a further averaging step.
All partitions and observations are defined pointwise, including
cells of zero Gaussian probability.

title: Unconditional time lower bounds for Weisfeiler–Leman equivalence
abstract: For every sufficiently large fixed k, deciding whether two n-vertex graphs are k-Weisfeiler–Leman equivalent requires \(n^{\Omega(k)}\) deterministic sequential time in the worst case. The bound holds at every sufficiently large graph order, even for simple connected uncolored graphs of diameter at most two, without a complexity assumption. Inputs are explicit adjacency matrices; the models are multitape Turing machines and sequential logarithmic-word RAMs with fixed polynomial-bit-time instructions. Both joint and separate replacement conventions are covered.

tex.abstract:
For every sufficiently large fixed $k$, deciding whether two
$n$-vertex graphs are $k$-Weisfeiler--Leman equivalent requires
$n^{\Omega(k)}$ deterministic sequential time in the worst case.
The bound holds at every sufficiently large graph order, even for
simple connected uncolored graphs of diameter at most two, without a
complexity assumption. Inputs are explicit adjacency matrices; the models
are multitape Turing machines and sequential logarithmic-word RAMs with
fixed polynomial-bit-time instructions. Both joint and separate replacement
conventions are covered.
sections: Weisfeiler--Leman conventions and the bijective game
A compressed graph representation of arc consistency
Encoding computations by short consistency instances
A language hard at every sufficiently large length
Quantitative transfer and the time lower bound

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
There are absolute constants $c>0$ and $k_0$ with the following
property. For every fixed integer $k\ge k_0$ and every correct
deterministic decider $A$ for $k$-Weisfeiler--Leman equivalence, there
is an integer $n_0=n_0(A,k)$ such that
\[
                     T_A(n)\ge n^{ck}
             \qquad\text{for every integer }n\ge n_0.
\]
This holds for multitape Turing machines and for sequential
random-access machines with $O(\log(n+2))$-bit addresses and words,
boundedly many memory accesses per instruction, and fixed instructions
computable in time polynomial in the word length.
The same bound holds if $A$ is required to decide correctly only on
pairs of simple connected uncolored graphs of diameter at most two,
with $T_A(n)$ maximized over that class. It applies both to the
joint replacement-multiset convention for $k$-dimensional refinement
and to the separate-multiset convention defined below.

statements.title: Compressed consistency reduction
statements.label: comp:reduction
statements.text:
For fixed $r$ and fixed description shape, an instance as above determines
two equally large simple uncolored connected graphs $G^0,G^1$, of
diameter at most two and order
\[
                         O_{r,\mathrm{shape}}(m^6),
\]
such that Duplicator wins the $K$-pair bijective game on $G^0,G^1$ if and
only if the instance has individual-edge arc consistency.
The construction uses the bounded scalar-form data together with the
one-coordinate tables, and enumerates $O_{r,\mathrm{shape}}(m^2)$ blocks
without enumerating all full addresses.
An arbitrary equal number of additional vertices can be added to the two
graphs while preserving the equivalence, connectedness, and diameter
bound.
statements.section_title: A compressed graph representation of arc consistency

statements.title: Circuit simulation
statements.label: circ:simulation
statements.text:
To such a circuit one can associate an individual-edge arc-consistency
instance over $\F_2$, with vector dimensions at most two, that has nonempty
arc-consistent sets if and only if every test gate is false.

If the circuit is specified by gate types indexed by $[m]^r$, connection
schemas with product domains and componentwise partial bijections, and seed
and test requests that are unions of product domains, then the consistency
instance has the same form. A bounded number of gate types, connection
schemas, and product requests gives a bounded number of consistency types and
edge schemas, independently of $m$.
statements.section_title: Encoding computations by short consistency instances

statements.title: Computation reduction
statements.label: circ:computation
statements.text:
Fix such a machine $M$ and an integer $r\geq3$, and put
$d=\lfloor r/3\rfloor$. There is a single effective construction,
depending only on $M$ and $r$, with the following property. For each
$m\geq2$ for which $M$ halts on every length-$m$ input within an integer
bound $T_0(m)$ satisfying
\begin{equation}

 T_0(m)<m^d-1,
 \qquad
 2T_0(m)+m+2<m^{r-d},
\end{equation}
the construction takes $w\in\{0,1\}^m$ to two simple uncolored graphs of
common order $O_{r,M}(m^6)$ such that $M$ accepts $w$
if and only if the two graphs are inequivalent in the $(r+1)$-pebble
bijective game.
Thus they are inequivalent for joint-update $r$-dimensional $\WL$ precisely
when $M$ accepts $w$.

The consistency description used in the construction has
$O_{r,M}(1)$ types and edge schemas, dimensions at most two, and
$O_{r,M}(1)$ one-coordinate tables with $O(m)$ entries each. These tables
can be constructed from $w$ in $O_{r,M}(m^3)$ time without running $M$ on
$w$. For every sufficiently large $m$ satisfying
\eqref{circ:time-space-slack}, the graphs can be padded to any
common order $n\geq m^{20}$ and their adjacency matrices constructed in
$O_{r,M}(n^4)$ multitape time. In particular, for
$m^{20}\leq n<(m+1)^{20}$ the construction time is a polynomial in $m$
of absolute degree, independently of $r$ and $M$.
statements.section_title: Encoding computations by short consistency instances

statements.title: A diagonal language
statements.label: diag:language
statements.text:
For every integer $s\geq 1$ there is a binary language $H_s$ with the following
properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item There is a fixed deterministic one-tape decider $M_s$ and a constant
$C_s$ such that, on every input of length $m\geq 0$, its running time is at
most
\[
                       C_s(m+m^s+2)^{20}.
\]
\item If $D$ is any correct deterministic one-tape decider for $H_s$, then,
for every sufficiently large integer $m$, the worst-case running time of
$D$ on inputs of length $m$ is strictly greater than $m^s$.
\item After their decisions have been recorded, the accepting and rejecting
configurations of $M_s$ may be kept fixed forever.  This gives a stationary
extension of its computation suitable for the local update representation.
\end{enumerate}

title: Uniform Bi-Holder Transport from Weak MTW
abstract: We prove that the weak Ma–Trudinger–Wang condition on a fixed smooth connected compact boundaryless Riemannian manifold of dimension at least two implies a common Hölder estimate for optimal transport maps and their inverses over the entire class of probability densities with fixed positive upper and lower bounds. The maps have homeomorphic representatives, conjugate cut points are allowed, and no density regularity is assumed.

tex.abstract:
We prove that the weak Ma--Trudinger--Wang condition on a fixed smooth
connected compact boundaryless Riemannian manifold of dimension at least
two implies a common H\"older estimate for optimal transport maps and their
inverses over the entire class of probability densities with fixed positive
upper and lower bounds. The maps have homeomorphic representatives, conjugate
cut points are allowed, and no density regularity is assumed.
sections: Jacobi fields and uniform comparison of exponential Jacobians
Sections, scales, and a quantitative separation
Lower jets and the determinant contradiction

statements.title: Uniform bi-H\"older transport
statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Fix $(M,g)$ as above and $0<\lambda\leq\Lambda<\infty$ for which the
following density class is nonempty. There are
$\alpha\in(0,1]$ and $C<\infty$, depending only on
$(M,g),\lambda,\Lambda$, such that the following holds for every pair
of measurable densities satisfying
\[
 \int_M\rho_i\,d\vol=1,\qquad
 \lambda\leq\rho_i\leq\Lambda\quad\vol\text{-almost everywhere},
 \qquad i=0,1.
\]
The almost-everywhere unique optimal map from $\rho_0\vol$ to
$\rho_1\vol$ for the cost $c$ has a homeomorphic representative
$\widetilde T:M\to M$, and
\[
 d(\widetilde T(x),\widetilde T(x'))\leq C d(x,x')^\alpha,
 \qquad
 d(\widetilde T^{-1}(y),\widetilde T^{-1}(y'))
       \leq C d(y,y')^\alpha
\]
for all $x,x',y,y'\in M$.

statements.title: Global supporting property
statements.label: geo:support
statements.text:
For every potential $u$, every $x\in M$, and every
$p\in\partial u(x)$, one has $p\in G_x$ and
\[
 u(x')\geq u(x)+c(x,\exp_xp)-c(x',\exp_xp)
 \qquad(x'\in M).
\]
For each $0<t<1$, $F_t:\Gamma_u\to M$ is a
homeomorphism, $tp\in I(x)$, and its poles are the unique
global minimizers of $Q_tu$.

statements.title: Convex injectivity domains
statements.label: geo:convexity
statements.text: Both $G_x$ and $I(x)$ are convex for every $x\in M$.

statements.title: Convex lifted gap sections
statements.label: geo:sections
statements.text:
For a dual pair $(u,v)$, each set
\[
 \mathcal S_x(r)=\left\{p\in G_x:
      u(x)+\frac{|p|^2}{2}+v(\exp_xp)\leq r\right\}
\]
is compact and convex, including ordinary and conjugate cut
endpoints. If it is nonempty and $r\geq0$, then
\[
 \operatorname{diam}\mathcal S_x(r)^2
 \leq8\left(r+\osc_{p\in\mathcal S_x(r)}v(\exp_xp)\right).
\]

statements.title: Intermediate regularity and pole control
statements.label: geo:intermediate
statements.text:
Let $(u,v)$ be a dual pair and $0<t<1$. Then
$Q_tu=-Q_{1-t}v\in C^{1,1}(M)$, with almost-everywhere bounds
\[
 -\frac{C_g}{1-t}g\leq\Hess Q_tu\leq\frac{C_g}{t}g.
\]
If $(x_t(z),p_t(z))=F_t^{-1}(z)$ and $\Phi_s$ is geodesic
flow on $TM$, then
\[
 (x_t(z),p_t(z))=\Phi_{-t}(z,\grad Q_tu(z)).
\]
In particular, the pole and momentum maps are Lipschitz
with constants depending only on $M,g,t$.
There are also $r_t,b_t>0$, depending only on $M,g,t$,
such that every $z=\exp_x(tp)$, $p\in\partial u(x)$,
satisfies
\[
 u(x')+c_t(x',z)\geq
 u(x)+c_t(x,z)+b_t d(x,x')^2
 \qquad\text{if }d(x,x')<r_t.
\]
All these constants are uniform when $t$ ranges in a
compact subinterval of $(0,1)$.

statements.title: Barycentric configurations
statements.label: spec:outward
statements.text:
Assume weak MTW and the convexity of $G_x$ established in
Corollary~\ref{geo:convexity}.  Fix $\mu\in(0,1)$ and positive constants
$\kappa,L_0$.  Suppose
\[
  p=\sum_{i=1}^N m_i p_i,\qquad
  p_i\in G_x,\quad m_i>0,\quad\sum_i m_i=1,
\]
and for one index $i$ there are $D>0$, a unit vector $e$, and
$t_i>0$ such that
\begin{equation}
  p_i=p+t_i e,\quad h:=p\cdot e>0,\quad
  h^2\ge\kappa D,\quad
  |p_i|^2-|p|^2\le L_0D,\quad m_i\ge\mu.
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
  \sigma_x(p)\ge c\sigma_x(p_i),
\end{equation}
where $c>0$ depends only on $(M,g),\mu,\kappa,L_0$.
statements.section_title: Jacobi fields and uniform comparison of exponential Jacobians

statements.title: The limiting matrix configuration
statements.label: jet:determinants
statements.text:
Fix the center template and the constants of
Lemmas~\ref{sc:excess}, \ref{sc:maximum}, \ref{sc:parameter}, and
\ref{sc:outward}. Choose $K$, then an outer template with curvature
less than $-K$ in the prescribed capped region. For all sufficiently
small scales in the sequence of Lemma~\ref{sc:plateau}, there are
a parameter $b\in[b_-,b_+]$, a pole $x$, center and active logs
$p,p_i\in G_x$, weights $m_i>0$ summing to one, and symmetric
matrices $H,L,V,V_i$ on $T_xM$, with the following properties.
For one selected index $i$,
\begin{gather}
 p=\sum_jm_jp_j,\qquad
 E=\Span\{p_j-p\}=\R e,\qquad |e|=1,\quad
 q=p\cdot e>0,\quad q^2\ge cD, \\
 m_i\ge m_*>0,\qquad p_i=p+d_ie,\quad d_i>0, \\
 L\ge0,\qquad LE=0,\qquad H\le L,\qquad
 H\ge V+c\frac bD\Id-C\frac b{D^2}pp^*,\qquad V>0,
 \\
 V_i\ge m_iL+cK\frac b{D^2}p_ip_i^*,\qquad V_i>0.
 
\end{gather}
The center modified log and the selected outer modified log are
nonconjugate. Let $r$ and $r_i$ denote the reverse logs of these
specified rays, let $y=\exp_xp$, $y_i=\exp_xp_i$, and set
$l=\varphi_c'(v(y))$, $l_i=\varphi_o'(v(y_i))$. The chosen true
limiting branches are also nonconjugate, and
\begin{equation}
 \det V\ge c\,\frac{\sigma_x(p)^2}{\sigma_y(r/l)},
 \qquad
 \det V_i\le C\,\frac{\sigma_x(p_i)^2}{\sigma_{y_i}(r_i/l_i)}.
\end{equation}
Here $c,C,m_*$ are independent of $K$ and the outer template.
The level and norm-increment conclusions of
Lemma~\ref{sc:outward} hold as well.
