title: Virtual compact specialness of hyperbolic one-relator groups
abstract: We prove that every word-hyperbolic one-relator group is virtually compact special. Combined with the work of Kielak–Linton, this resolves Wise's virtual free-by-cyclic conjecture for hyperbolic one-relator groups: every such group is virtually free-by-cyclic, with the free kernel allowed to have infinite rank.

tex.abstract:
We prove that every word-hyperbolic one-relator group is virtually compact
special. Combined with the work of Kielak--Linton, this resolves Wise's
virtual free-by-cyclic conjecture for hyperbolic one-relator groups: every
such group is virtually free-by-cyclic, with the free kernel allowed to have
infinite rank.
sections: A filling criterion and progressive characters
Support and descent for division-ring coefficients
Cyclic closure of the periodic system
Terminal paths and finite-path filling transfer
Filled vertex groups and central panels

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $X$ be finite, let $r\in F(X)$, and suppose that
\[
G=F(X)/\langle\!\langle r\rangle\!\rangle
\]
is word-hyperbolic. Then $G$ is virtually compact special. More precisely, there are a finite-index subgroup $H\leq G$, a finite connected nonpositively curved cube complex $C$, and a finite simplicial graph $\Lambda$ such that
\[
\pi_1(C)\cong H
\quad\text{and}\quad
C\longrightarrow S_\Lambda
\]
is a cubical local isometry to the Salvetti complex of the right-angled Artin group defined by $\Lambda$.

statements.label: thm:ascending-intro
statements.text:
Let $F$ be a finitely generated free group and let $\phi:F\to F$ be injective. If its ascending mapping torus
\[
F*_{\phi}=\langle F,t\mid t^{-1}ft=\phi(f),\ f\in F\rangle
\]
is word-hyperbolic, then it is virtually compact special.

statements.title: Cubulation and quasiconvex hierarchies
statements.label: prop:compact-toolkit

statements.title: Reduction
statements.label: prop:primitive-reduction
statements.text: To prove Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, it suffices to prove that every torsion-free hyperbolic primitive extension group in the two forms of \cite[Section~5]{LintonHyperbolic2026} is VCS.

statements.title: Filling criterion
statements.label: fill:criterion
statements.text:
Let \(G_*\) be a torsion-free hyperbolic group satisfying the following
conditions.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item \(G_*\) is locally indicable, coherent, of type \(F\), and has integral
cohomological dimension at most two.
\item \(G_*\) has a division ring \(D(G_*)\) satisfying the subgroup-field
hypotheses, and the chains of a finite classifying space become acyclic over
\(D(G_*)\).
\item There is a finite malnormal family \(\{D_j\}\) of quasiconvex
hyperbolic virtually compact special subgroups such that arbitrarily deep
peripheral fillings
\[
 G_*\longrightarrow Q_*
\]
are hyperbolic and virtually compact special, and their inherited peripheral
images are hyperbolic and virtually compact special.
\end{enumerate}
In \textup{(iii)}, arbitrarily deep means that the peripheral kernels can
avoid any prescribed finite subset of
\(\bigcup_j(D_j\setminus\{1\})\); the inherited peripheral structure is the
one furnished by relative Dehn filling.

Then a finite-index subgroup of \(G_*\) is an extension of a finite-rank free
group by \(\Z\).  Consequently \(G_*\) is virtually compact special.
statements.section_title: A filling criterion and progressive characters

statements.title: Selective-cover quotient
statements.label: fill:selective
statements.text:
Choose \eqref{fill:cofinite} sufficiently deep.  Let \(H_{\mathrm{given}}\)
be a finite-index preimage in \(G_*\), and let \(\mathcal B\subset\mathcal A\)
be finite.  There is a further finite-index preimage
\(H\le H_{\mathrm{given}}\), normal in \(H_{\mathrm{given}}\), such that,
on retaining all factors indexed by the \(H\)-translates of \(\mathcal B\)
and killing the other factors, the group
\begin{equation}
 P=H/K_-
 
\end{equation}
is hyperbolic and virtually compact special.  The natural map to \(P\)
is injective on \(*_{a\in\mathcal B}R_a\).
statements.section_title: A filling criterion and progressive characters

statements.title: Progressive characters
statements.label: fill:progressive
statements.text:
Let \(J\) be finitely generated with the subgroup-field hypotheses,
and let \(K\lhd J\) satisfy the selective realization property of
Definition~\ref{fill:selective-input}.
Every finite family of rational expressions over \(\Q J\) can,
after restriction of scalars to a finite-index subgroup \(F\),
be realized compatibly in the ordinary Novikov rings for both signs
of a single real character of \(F\).

In particular, if a finite complex of finitely generated free
\(\Q J\)-modules is acyclic over \(D(J)\), then its restriction is
acyclic over both these Novikov rings.  If its degree-zero ordinary
homology is nonzero, the character is nonzero.
statements.section_title: A filling criterion and progressive characters

statements.title: Open Novikov regions for RFRS groups
statements.label: fill:rfrs-novikov
statements.text:
Let \(J\) be virtually RFRS with the subgroup-field hypotheses.
A finite family of bounded complexes of finitely generated free
\(\Q J\)-modules, with polynomial differential matrices and acyclic
extension to \(D(J)\), admits simultaneous ordinary Novikov contractions,
after passage to a finite-index subgroup \(F\), on a nonempty
antipodally invariant open subset of \(\Hom(F,\R)\).
Here the character space has the topology of pointwise convergence.
This property can be imposed after any prescribed further finite-index
restriction.
statements.section_title: A filling criterion and progressive characters

statements.label: asc:vcs
statements.text:
Let $F$ be a free group of finite rank and let $\phi:F\to F$ be injective.
If $J_\phi$ is word-hyperbolic, then $J_\phi$ is virtually compact special.

statements.label: cor:ascending-finite-rank
statements.text:
Let $F$ be a free group of finite rank and let $\phi:F\to F$ be injective.
If $J_\phi$ is word-hyperbolic, it has a finite-index subgroup $H$ fitting
into an exact sequence
\[
 1\longrightarrow F_d\longrightarrow H\longrightarrow\Z
 \longrightarrow1
\]
for some finite $d\geq0$, where $F_d$ is the rank-$d$ free group.
Thus $H\cong F_d\rtimes_\alpha\Z$ for an automorphism $\alpha$ of $F_d$.

statements.title: Restriction to row orbits
statements.label: row:restriction

statements.title: Path inertia
statements.label: row:path-inertia
statements.text:
In \(T\) and \(T_0\), every path with noncyclic pointwise stabilizer
is monotone. For each fixed monotone shape in a fixed absolute level
range, the first homologies of
its stabilizers, indexed modulo \(L\), inject jointly into
\(H_1(L;D_L)\). A path containing an edge has finitely generated free
stabilizer, and a fixed finite shape has finitely many \(G\)-orbits
with nontrivial stabilizer, or finitely many \(L\)-orbits when its
absolute level range is fixed. In particular
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{\gamma\bmod L}\max\{\rk\Stab(\gamma)-1,0\}\leq k-1.
\end{equation}
The same joint-injection statement holds for continuations of any
fixed additional shape inside any subgroup \(U\) of a current path
stabilizer, with the intersection summands indexed by \(U\)-orbits.
It holds after restriction of the actual induced matrices and
double-coset decompositions, not just as a numerical inequality.

statements.title: Period rule
statements.label: row:period-rule
statements.text:
Suppose \(A\leq G\), \(h(A)\neq0\), and
\[
 S=A\cap L,\qquad 0<\beta(S)<\infty.
\]
At every actual level \(\mathscr L\), inclusion induces an isomorphism
\[
 \bigoplus_{\xi\in S\backslash\mathscr L}
 H_1(S\cap X_\xi;D_S)\ \longrightarrow\ H_1(S;D_S).
\]
Both incident edge-level maps to a vertex level are isomorphisms.
Every level sum therefore has dimension \(q_X=\beta(S)\).
The convex hull \(Y\) of the rows with noncyclic \(S\cap X_\xi\)
contains no edge with trivial \(S\)-stabilizer.
If \(A\) is also finitely generated, then \(A\backslash Y\) is finite
and \(A\) is quasiconvex in \(G\).

statements.title: Support and coset descent
statements.label: coeff:support
statements.text:
The following assertions hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If \(S\cap T=\varnothing\), then
\(\mathcal V(S)\cap\mathcal V(T)=0\).
\item There is a \(\Q\)-linear map
\[
 \mathcal F\colon D_J\longrightarrow\Q^J
\]
with \(\mathcal F(1)=\delta_1\), commuting with every right group
translation, such that
\(v\in\mathcal V(S)\) implies
\(\supp\mathcal F(v)\subseteq S\).
\item Let \(A,B\le J\) and \(C=A\cap B\). If \(At\cap Bs\) is empty,
then \(D_A t\cap D_B s=0\). Otherwise, for any \(x\in At\cap Bs\),
\begin{equation}
 D_A t\cap D_B s=D_Cx.
\end{equation}
If, in addition, \(C\) is separable in both \(A\) and \(B\), then
\begin{equation}
 \left(\sum_{g\in J}D_Ag\right)
 \cap
 \left(\sum_{g\in J}D_Bg\right)
 =\sum_{g\in J}D_Cg,
\end{equation}
where each sum denotes its algebraic, finite-support span.
\end{enumerate}
statements.section_title: Support and descent for division-ring coefficients

statements.title: Affiliated positive mean
statements.label: coeff:analytic-mean
statements.text:
Let \(X_n\), \(n\in\Z\), be positive affiliated units in a finite von
Neumann algebra.  Suppose that both \(\{X_n\}\) and \(\{X_n^{-1}\}\)
are tight.  There is a unique positive affiliated unit \(P\) satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \mathfrak M_nF(P,X_n)=\tfrac12\,1.
\end{equation}
The construction is covariant under congruence by affiliated
invertible operators, including affiliated invertible maps between
corners with their restricted traces.

statements.title: Persistence of a rational line
statements.label: gate:rational-persistence
statements.text:
Suppose a bilateral trajectory carries, in \(R_0\), the whole axis
of a loxodromic element \(c\in H_0\) through every finite subwindow
containing position zero. Some nonzero power of \(c\) fixes the
entire trajectory pointwise.

statements.title: The component trees
statements.label: gate:component-tree
statements.text:
Every component of the actual switch graph is a tree.  For a nonisolated
component with stabilizer $A$ and $S=A\cap L$, there is an integer $r\ge2$
such that $S$ is a nested union of rank-$r$ free groups and
\[
 \dim_{D_L}H_1(S;D_L)=r-1.
\]
These approximants and $S$ have injective ambient first-homology maps.
Moreover $A$ is finitely generated, quasiconvex, virtually compact special,
and field-acyclic.

statements.title: Capture by periodic quasiconvex groups
statements.label: gate:capture
statements.text:
Unless $G$ is already virtually compact special by the acylindrical case,
there is an invariant system of actual objects, finite modulo $G$, with
full stabilizers $A$ and kernels $S=A\cap L$, having these properties:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item $h(A)\ne0$; each $A$ is quasiconvex, virtually compact special,
and field-acyclic.
\item Each $S$ is a nested union of finite-rank free approximants of one
constant rank at least two.  Its field first-homology dimension is positive
and finite, and its ambient homology detects every noncyclic subgroup.
\item For representatives of the actual object orbits under $L$, the maps
\[
 \bigoplus H_1(S;D_L)\longrightarrow H_1(L;D_L)
\]
are jointly injective.  Distinct actual object stabilizers intersect in
at most cyclic groups.
\item There is a uniform length such that the pointwise stabilizer of
every longer noncyclically stabilized actual path, in $T_0$ or in the
refined tree $T$, is wholly contained in one of these kernels $S$.
\end{enumerate}

statements.title: Joint injection after a cyclic join
statements.label: close:join-injection
statements.text:
For the new component system the map
\[
 \bigoplus_{i\in L\backslash\mathcal D'}H_1(S'_i;D_L)
       \longrightarrow H_1(L;D_L)
\]
is injective. Consequently a cyclic-join round preserves
admissibility and does not decrease the budget. A round containing a
positive-height cyclic join increases the budget by at least one.
statements.section_title: Cyclic closure of the periodic system

statements.title: Finite strict closure
statements.label: close:strict-system
statements.text:
Iterating cyclic joins stops after finitely many rounds. The final
system is admissible and strictly malnormal: stabilizers of distinct
objects have trivial intersection. Each is the full stabilizer of its
object. For each final object $d$, the union of all actual rows $x$
with $X_x\cap S_d\ne1$ is a connected subtree $Z_d$ with finite
$D_d$-quotient, where $D_d$ is its object stabilizer and $S_d=D_d\cap L$.
statements.section_title: Cyclic closure of the periodic system

statements.title: Folded slot structure and restriction
statements.label: close:folded-slot
statements.text:
Fix a folded vertex $v$ and one slot of incident folded edges $f$.
Let $K_f$ be the image of the endpoint map
$\Gamma_f\to\Gamma_v$. Then $K_f$ is a $Y_f$-cocompact subtree, every
object vertex $d$ of $\Gamma_v$ occurs in exactly one such $K_f$ with
its full stabilizer, and any absent incidence has at most cyclic
stabilizer. For each $H\le Y_v$ the natural map
\begin{equation}
 \bigoplus_{f\bmod H}H_1(H\cap Y_f;D_L)
             \longrightarrow H_1(H;D_L)
\end{equation}
is injective.

statements.title: Strict folded tree
statements.label: close:folding
statements.text:
The quotient $\widehat T$ is a tree with one $L$-orbit at each level,
and every $Z_d$ maps onto a monotone line $\ell_d$. Its row groups and
slot maps have the conclusions of Lemmas~\ref{close:folded-row} and
\ref{close:folded-separation} and
Proposition~\ref{close:folded-slot}. Stabilizers of finite monotone
paths in any fixed height range inject jointly on first field
homology into $L$, over path-orbit representatives.

statements.title: The tail free-product decomposition
statements.label: close:tail-splitting
statements.text:
Let $K$ be the pointwise stabilizer of a positive ray contained in an
old line, starting at an actual free-edge level $w$. An object vertex of $\Gamma_w$ is called full if
its line contains that entire tail. There are finitely many $K$-orbits
of full vertices. With representatives $d_1,\ldots,d_m$, one has
\begin{equation}
 K\cong\Bigl(*_{j=1}^m S_{d_j}\Bigr)*F_r,
 \qquad r<\infty.
\end{equation}
The displayed embeddings of full factors are their actual subgroup
embeddings, up to the usual independent choices of conjugating
basepoint paths.

statements.title: Quasiconvex and virtually compact special end groups
statements.label: close:end-vcs
statements.text:
Each end stabilizer $A_\xi$ is finitely generated, quasiconvex in $G$,
field-acyclic, and virtually compact special. It is torsion-free,
locally indicable, coherent, of type $F$, and of cohomological
dimension at most two.

statements.title: Strict growth at a shared end
statements.label: close:end-growth
statements.text:
Replacing the objects by distinct end stabilizers preserves all
admissibility conditions. If some two distinct old lines share an end
in the chosen orientation, this replacement strictly increases the
budget. Subsequent cyclic closure does not decrease it.

statements.title: Terminal periodic system
statements.label: close:terminal-system
statements.text:
Starting with the system of Proposition~\ref{gate:capture}, finitely
many cyclic-closure and end-enlargement rounds produce an admissible
strict malnormal quasiconvex virtually compact special system
$\{D_d\}$, with $S_d=D_d\cap L$, and a folded tree $\widehat T$ having
all the conclusions of Corollary~\ref{close:folding}. The associated
monotone lines $\ell_d$ of distinct objects share no end. Actual long
noncyclic path stabilizers remain captured, the kernels still detect
all noncyclic subgroups, and their joint homology budget is at most
$k-1$.

statements.title: Unfilled nonparabolic double cosets
statements.label: transfer:unfilled-double-cosets
statements.text:
For fixed exact relative embeddings of $B,C$ in a row $J$, the double
cosets $BgC$ having nonparabolic intersection $B\cap gCg^{-1}$
have representatives in a fixed finite subset of $J$.

statements.title: Simultaneous relative factors
statements.label: transfer:window-splitting
statements.text:
For a sufficiently long monotone folded path \(W\), its pointwise stabilizer \(H\) has a finite relative free-product decomposition
\[
 H=\Bigl(*_{j=1}^m(H\cap S_{d_j})\Bigr)*F_r.
\]
The factors represent exactly the nontrivial peripheral intersections, up to \(H\)-conjugacy. Vertices of the corresponding relative Bass--Serre tree that have nontrivial stabilizer carry injective, equivariant labels by actual objects \(d\). The trivial vertices can be chosen of finite valence.
statements.section_title: Terminal paths and finite-path filling transfer

statements.title: Terminal path bound
statements.label: transfer:terminal-paths
statements.text: There is a length \(n_0\) such that every segment of \(\widehat T\) of length at least \(n_0\) has trivial, cyclic, or parabolic pointwise stabilizer. Moreover there is a uniform bound on the length of a segment fixed by any nontrivial height-zero element lying outside all the \(S_d\).
statements.section_title: Terminal paths and finite-path filling transfer

statements.title: The additional root cyclic
statements.label: transfer:root-cyclic
statements.text: In the root case in which no power of the root cyclic group is claimed by the object system, its maximal cyclic overgroup may be added to the peripheral family. Its nontrivial incidences have finite orbit lists, and the relative embeddings and finite-path conclusions continue to hold with the enlarged induced systems.
statements.section_title: Terminal paths and finite-path filling transfer

statements.title: Finite double-coset representatives
statements.label: transfer:double-cosets
statements.text:
For fixed original exact relative embeddings of $B,C$ in a row,
every double coset in a sufficiently long filling whose intersection
contains an infinite-order loxodromic element has a representative
in the image of a fixed finite original list. The list is independent
of the double coset and of the filling.
statements.section_title: Terminal paths and finite-path filling transfer

statements.title: Exact intersection transfer
statements.label: transfer:exact-intersection
statements.text:
Fix exact relative embeddings \(B,C\hookrightarrow J\) with the full-or-cyclic induced peripheral systems described above, and fix \(g\in J\). There are finitely many compatibility requests of Definition~\ref{transfer:finite-tests}, determined in the original groups, such that every sufficiently long filling satisfying them has
\[
 \bar B\cap\bar g\bar C\bar g^{-1}
 =\overline{B\cap gCg^{-1}}.
\]
The notation \(\bar B\), \(\bar C\) denotes the embedded standalone fillings given by Lemma~\ref{transfer:subgroup-filling}.
statements.section_title: Terminal paths and finite-path filling transfer

statements.title: Finite-path transfer
statements.label: transfer:finite-path-transfer
statements.text:
Fix an integer \(n\). Under the terminal row hypotheses, there is a finite set of original compatibility requests such that every sufficiently long compatible filling has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item The induced row fillings and edge fillings form the quotient graph of groups for \(\bar G\).
\item Every reduced path of length at most \(n\) downstairs with infinite stabilizer lifts, after the permitted changes of Bass--Serre representatives, to an actual reduced path upstairs. Its stabilizer is exactly the image of the actual path stabilizer.
\item Taking \(n\) at least the terminal path bound, the resulting Bass--Serre action is acylindrical: sufficiently long segment stabilizers are finite of uniformly bounded order. Each filled row is hyperbolic and each edge map is quasi-isometric.
\end{enumerate}
Here the ambient filled group is hyperbolic by sufficiently long filling of the original relatively hyperbolic pair: the periodic peripheral reductions are finite-by-cyclic and hence hyperbolic, and the additional cyclic reductions are finite. The conclusion about ambient quasiconvexity is proved separately below.
statements.section_title: Terminal paths and finite-path filling transfer

statements.title: Quasiconvexity from bounded segment stabilizers
statements.label: transfer:ambient-qc
statements.text: Let \(A\) be a hyperbolic group expressed as a finite graph of finitely generated hyperbolic groups. Suppose the edge maps are quasi-isometric embeddings and there is an integer \(n\) such that every length-\(n\) Bass--Serre segment has finite pointwise stabilizer. Then every vertex and edge group is quasiconvex in \(A\). In particular this applies to the filled graph of groups of Theorem~\ref{transfer:finite-path-transfer}.
statements.section_title: Terminal paths and finite-path filling transfer

statements.title: Restriction to one actual level
statements.label: kernel:level-cohomology
statements.text:
For every \(j,\lambda\) as in
Lemma~\ref{kernel:scalar-specialization}, and every vertex or edge level
\(r\) of \(Z_D\), restriction is an isomorphism
\[
 H^1(S_0;\mathbb k_{\lambda^{\chi_j}})
       \longrightarrow
 \prod_{\substack{\xi\text{ at level }r\\\bmod S_0}}
       H^1(M_\xi^0;\mathbb k_{\lambda^{\chi_j}}).
 \tag{K1}
\]
The product on the right is finite.  In particular the group on the
left is finite-dimensional, and restriction to any individual actual
stabilizer is onto.

statements.title: Exact local annihilators
statements.label: kernel:exact-kernel
statements.text:
Each \(V_j\) is finite-dimensional and restriction maps it onto
\(V_{Mj}\) for every actual stabilizer \(M\).  With
\(\ker V_j=\bigcap_{v\in V_j}\ker v\), the subgroup
\[
                     N=\bigcap_j\bigl(S_{\ell j}\cap\ker V_j\bigr)
                     \tag{K2}
\]
is normal in \(D\), has finite index in \(S\), and satisfies
\[
 M\cap N
       =\bigcap_j\left(M_{\ell j}\cap
                         \bigcap_{v\in V_{Mj}}\ker v\right).
                     \tag{K3}
\]
The equality uses no simultaneous surjectivity across different \(j\).

statements.title: The outgoing graph-cover property
statements.label: kernel:graph-cover
statements.text:
Let \(M\) be an incidence group embedded in a free actual row and
represented by its finite Stallings core.  A component \(L_H\) of the
cover determined by \(M^0\) may be required to have arbitrarily large
prescribed girth.  It has a nonempty finite family of connected cyclic
\(\ell\)-covers \(L_{\ell j}\), corresponding to \(M_{\ell j}\).
The component \(L_N\) determined by \(M\cap N\) is exactly the cover
whose fundamental group is the intersection of the covering kernels
and the kernels of every additive first-cohomology class in the
nontrivial deck part of each \(L_{\ell j}\), over the finite field
\(\mathbb k\) with \(\operatorname{char}\mathbb k\ne\ell\).

In particular, if \(e_1,e_2\) are two lifts to \(L_{\ell j}\) of the
same oriented edge of \(L_H\), the pullback to \(L_N\) of
\(e_1^*-e_2^*\) has zero period on every closed path.
All these statements are invariant under the required coset and
conjugation changes.

statements.title: Orders and exact cyclic intersections
statements.label: kernel:orders
statements.text:
For every specified generator \(a\in S\), let \(m_a\) be its order in
\(D/H\).  Its order in \(S/N\) is exactly \(m_a\ell\).  For every
specified pair of actual noncommensurate cyclics, their images in
\(S/N\) have trivial intersection.  Thus the prescribed evenness,
largeness, and divisibility of cyclic orders survive the construction.

statements.title: Simultaneous compatible kernels
statements.label: kernel:construction
statements.text:
For the finite orbit list of periodic peripherals and any added
maximal cyclic peripherals, all the preceding choices can be made
simultaneously and equivariantly.  The resulting \(N_D\unlhd D\)
have finite index in \(S_D\), satisfy every prescribed finite
membership, product, avoidance, girth and cyclic-order requirement,
and give the exact local graph covers of
Corollary~\ref{kernel:graph-cover}.  Specified noncommensurate cyclic
intersections remain exact; commensurate cyclic intersections satisfy
the usual intersection identity in a finite cyclic quotient.

statements.title: Central panel tests
statements.label: fan:central-panels
statements.text:
Fix $K$, a bound $q$ on the number of target link vertices, and a bound
$r$ on the number of prescribed directions at an internal apex.
There is a bound $B$, depending only on these bounds and the fixed
original data, with the following property after suitable kernel
choices.  For every such target list and direction list there is a
partition of the targets into classes, each in one component of $L_N$
and of intrinsic diameter at most $B$, such that every binary
assignment to these classes extends to a central panel.  Its cut germs
are pairwise at angle greater than $K$, and all are at angle greater
than $K$ from the prescribed directions.  The same partition works
for all binary assignments.

There are also fillers: for every occurrence of a link edge there is
a panel cutting that occurrence whose cuts all lie over its one base
edge in $L_H$.  Its cut germs can be required pairwise farther than
$K$.
statements.section_title: Filled vertex groups and central panels

statements.title: Odd inner seeds
statements.label: fan:odd-seeds
statements.text:
A finite pool of central panel systems, chosen at successive fixed
angle scales, can be required to contain, on every satellite arm, a
central tree $W_0$ for which $\tau_0^{W_0}$ has odd total on the arm's
boundary cycle.  The choices and all support bounds are independent
of the sufficiently large individual cycle orders.
statements.section_title: Filled vertex groups and central panels

statements.title: Completed trees and cocycles
statements.label: boundary:completed-trees
statements.text:
The resulting components $W=W_2$ are uniformly quasi-isometrically embedded
trees. Their $W_1$-nodes and switch nodes have distinct projections within a
component. They carry cocycles $\tau_W$ on the full simply connected fan
complex, supported in a uniform neighborhood of $W$. Under group transport
the only ambiguity in these cocycles is a sum of vertex coboundaries at
outer switches. There are finitely many decorated node and edge orbits.

statements.title: Odd outer encounters
statements.label: boundary:outer-odd-seeds
statements.text:
A finite pool of $W_1$-systems contains, on the cycle of every outer apex,
at least one $W_1$ with odd total. The pool and all its required bounds can
be fixed before the final filling depth choices.

statements.title: Boundary separation
statements.label: boundary:separation
statements.text:
There are finitely many systems of completed trees such that every pair of
distinct points of $\partial\bar J$ lies outside the limit set of one of
the trees and has different cocycle colors there.

statements.title: Virtually compact special filled vertices
statements.label: boundary:filled-vertices
statements.text:
For the terminal row and peripheral data constructed in
Sections~\ref{sec:07-transfer}--\ref{sec:09-fans}, one can choose the
height-fiber kernels arbitrarily deep, simultaneously satisfying the
finite-path tests, so that every filled vertex group $\bar J$ is
hyperbolic and virtually compact special.

statements.title: Arbitrarily deep good quotients
statements.label: boundary:good-fillings
statements.text:
Let $G$ be the hyperbolic torsion-free primitive extension group under
consideration, with the terminal finite malnormal quasiconvex virtually
compact special peripheral family constructed in the preceding sections.
For every prescribed sufficiently deep filling-avoidance request, there
is a filling of this family to a hyperbolic virtually compact special
quotient. Its peripheral images are finite-by-cyclic or finite, are
hyperbolic virtually compact special, and have the inherited relative
peripheral structure and filling conclusions.

statements.title: Primitive extensions
statements.label: boundary:primitive-vcs
statements.text:
Every hyperbolic torsion-free primitive extension group of either of
Linton's two forms specified in the introduction is virtually compact
special.

statements.label: cor:free-by-cyclic
statements.text:
Let $G$ be one of the following groups.
\begin{enumerate}
\item A one-relator group
\[
G=F(X)/\langle\!\langle r\rangle\!\rangle,
\]
where $X$ is finite and $r\in F(X)$ is arbitrary, such that either $G$
is word-hyperbolic or $G$ contains no subgroup isomorphic to
$\mathrm{BS}(m,n)$ for any nonzero integers $m,n$.
\item A word-hyperbolic ascending mapping torus
\[
G=\langle F,t\mid t^{-1}ft=\phi(f)\ (f\in F)\rangle,
\]
where $F$ is a free group of finite rank and $\phi:F\to F$ is injective.
\end{enumerate}
There are a finite-index subgroup $H\leq G$, an integer $d\geq0$, an
automorphism $\alpha$ of the rank-$d$ free group $F_d$, and an embedding
\[
H\hookrightarrow F_d\rtimes_\alpha\mathbb Z.
\]
In particular, $G$ is virtually free-by-cyclic: the same $H$ fits into
an exact sequence
\[
1\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow H\longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow1,
\qquad K\text{ free},\quad Q\leq\mathbb Z.
\]
The rank of $K$ may be infinite, and $Q$ may be trivial.

title: Weak Hessian bounds along every geodesic in RCD spaces
abstract: On a full-support \(\mathrm{RCD}(K,N)\) space with \(1\lt N\lt \infty\), we prove that a bounded globally Lipschitz function whose distributional Hessian is bounded above by a bounded continuous function satisfies the corresponding second-derivative inequality along every minimizing geodesic.

tex.abstract:
On a full-support \(\RCD(K,N)\) space with \(1<N<\infty\), we prove
that a bounded globally Lipschitz function whose distributional
Hessian is bounded above by a bounded continuous function satisfies
the corresponding second-derivative inequality along every
minimizing geodesic.
sections: Test functions, approximation and Bochner measures
Bounded changes of measure and the generator domain
From a weak Hessian bound to variable curvature
Localizing the entropy inequality to a prescribed geodesic

statements.title: Weak Hessian bounds along every geodesic
statements.label: weight:every-geodesic
statements.text:
Let \((M,d,m)\) be a full-support \(\RCD(K,N)\) space,
where \(K\in\mathbb R\) and \(1<N<\infty\). Let
\(F\colon M\to\mathbb R\) be bounded and globally Lipschitz,
and let \(G\colon M\to\mathbb R\) be bounded and continuous.
Suppose that for every compactly supported \(g\in\Test(M)\)
and every nonnegative \(h\in\Lip_c(M)\),
\begin{equation}

H_F(\nabla g,\nabla g)(h)
\le\int_M hG\Gamma(g)\dd m.
\end{equation}
Then every constant-speed minimizing geodesic
\(\sigma\colon[0,1]\to M\), of length \(\ell\), satisfies
\begin{equation}

(F\circ\sigma)''\le\ell^2G\circ\sigma
\qquad\text{in distributions on }(0,1).
\end{equation}

statements.title: A distributional Hessian bound changes curvature
statements.label: weight:variable-cd
statements.text:
Let \((M,d,m)\) be a full-support \(\RCD(K,N)\) space,
where \(K\in\mathbb R\) and \(1<N<\infty\).
Let \(F\colon M\to\mathbb R\) be bounded and globally Lipschitz, and let
\(G\colon M\to\mathbb R\) be bounded and continuous. Suppose
that for every compactly supported \(g\in\Test\) and every
nonnegative \(h\in\Lip_c(M)\),
\[
H_F(\nabla g,\nabla g)(h)
\le\int hG\Gamma(g)\dd m.
\]
For every \(\lambda>0\), the measure
\(m_\lambda=e^{\lambda F}m\) satisfies
\(\CD(K-\lambda G,\infty)\). The metric is unchanged.

title: Weak and strong normalization in pure type systems
abstract: We prove that every weakly β-normalizing pure type system is strongly β-normalizing. Both properties quantify over all legal expressions in all valid contexts, and reduction acts inside type annotations. No functionality hypothesis is required. This resolves the β-Barendregt–Geuvers–Klop conjecture.

tex.abstract:
We prove that every weakly $\beta$-normalizing pure type system is strongly
$\beta$-normalizing. Both properties quantify over all legal expressions
in all valid contexts, and reduction acts inside type annotations.
No functionality hypothesis is required. This resolves the
$\beta$-Barendregt--Geuvers--Klop conjecture.
sections: A typed calculus for the forbidden configuration
Relational coding of the diagonal argument
Exclusion and completion of the proof

statements.title: The $\beta$-Barendregt--Geuvers--Klop conjecture
statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
Let $\mathcal P=(\mathcal S,\mathcal A,\mathcal R)$ be any pure type system.
If every legal expression of $\mathcal P$, in every valid context, is weakly
$\beta$-normalizing, then every such expression is strongly
$\beta$-normalizing. No functionality assumption is imposed on
$\mathcal A$ or $\mathcal R$.

Assume system-wide weak normalization and \eqref{obs:forbidden}.

title: Weak mixing of triangular billiards with an irrational angle
abstract: We prove that the unit-speed billiard flow in every nondegenerate Euclidean triangle with at least one angle irrational relative to π is weakly mixing for normalized Liouville measure. Equivalently, the product of the flow with itself is ergodic.

tex.abstract:
We prove that the unit-speed billiard flow in every nondegenerate Euclidean
triangle with at least one angle irrational relative to \(\pi\) is weakly
mixing for normalized Liouville measure. Equivalently, the product of the
flow with itself is ergodic.
sections: The double and its angular coefficients
Localized energy and individual coefficient bounds

statements.label: thm:main
statements.text:
The unit-speed billiard flow in every nondegenerate Euclidean triangle with
at least one angle irrational relative to \(\pi\) is weakly mixing for
normalized Liouville measure.

statements.title: Transverse rigidity
statements.label: prop:rigidity
statements.text:
Let \(M\) be the regular oriented double of a fixed nondegenerate
Euclidean triangle, and let \(\Psi_t\) be its geodesic flow on \(SM\)
with normalized Liouville measure. Suppose \(\lambda\in\R\) and
\(f\in L^\infty(SM)\) satisfy
\[
 f\circ\Psi_t=e^{i\lambda t}f
 \quad\text{in }L^2(SM)\quad\text{for every }t\in\R.
\]
Then \(f\) has square-integrable horizontal weak derivatives and
\[
 Yf=0,\qquad Xf=i\lambda f,\qquad
 \norm{\nabla f}_2^2=\lambda^2\norm{f}_2^2.
\]
statements.section_title: The double and its angular coefficients

statements.label: prop:eigenfunctions
statements.text:
Let \(Q\) be a nondegenerate Euclidean triangle with an angle irrational
relative to \(\pi\). If \(F\in L^2(Q\times S^1,\mu)\) satisfies
\[
 F\circ\Phi_t=e^{i\lambda t}F\quad\text{in }L^2
 \qquad(t\in\R)
\]
for some \(\lambda\in\R\), then \(F\) is constant almost everywhere.
If this constant is nonzero, then \(\lambda=0\).

title: Weak pure infiniteness and O-infinity absorption
abstract: We prove that every complex C∗-algebra in which each positive element is properly infinite is strongly purely infinite. This answers the ordinary-to-strong part of Kirchberg–Rørdam's comparison question. For exact algebras, we also prove that proper infiniteness of one fixed finite amplification of every positive element implies proper infiniteness of each positive element. Consequently, every separable nuclear algebra with this fixed-amplification property absorbs \(\mathcal O_\infty\), without assumptions of unitality or simplicity.

tex.abstract:
We prove that every complex \(C^*\)-algebra in which each positive
element is properly infinite is strongly purely infinite. This answers
the ordinary-to-strong part of Kirchberg--R{\o}rdam's comparison question.
For exact algebras, we also prove that proper infiniteness of one fixed
finite amplification of every positive element implies proper infiniteness
of each positive element. Consequently, every separable nuclear algebra
with this fixed-amplification property absorbs \(\Oinf\), without
assumptions of unitality or simplicity.
sections: Four entries under individual proper infiniteness
Exact localization and removal of amplification

statements.label: thm:individual-to-strong
statements.text:
Let \(C\) be a complex \(C^*\)-algebra satisfying \(\propP\).
For all \(a,b\in C_+\), \(c\in C\), and \(\varepsilon>0\), there are
\(s,t\in C\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \|s^*as-a\|<\varepsilon,\qquad
 \|t^*bt-b\|<\varepsilon,\qquad
 \|s^*ct\|<\varepsilon.
\end{equation}
Consequently \(C\) is strongly purely infinite.

statements.label: thm:exact-infiniteness
statements.text:
Let \(C\) be an exact complex \(C^*\)-algebra.  Suppose that there is
one integer \(n\ge1\) such that \(h^{\oplus n}\) is properly infinite
for every \(h\in C_+\).  Then every positive element of \(C\) is
properly infinite.  Consequently \(C\) is strongly purely infinite.

statements.label: cor:absorption
statements.text:
Let \(A\) be a separable nuclear complex \(C^*\)-algebra.  If there is
one integer \(n\ge1\) such that \(h^{\oplus n}\) is properly infinite
for every \(h\in A_+\), then
\[
 A\cong A\otimes_{\min}\Oinf.
\]

statements.title: Fixed measurements of a graph
statements.label: prop:graph
statements.text:
Let \(C\) be a \(C^*\)-algebra, let \(a,y\in C_+\) be
contractions with \(a\) rich, and let \(c\in\widetilde C\) be a
contraction.  For an integer \(k\ge1\) and fixed positive
\(\gamma_g,\sigma_g\) satisfying \eqref{eq:graph-constants},
there are
\[
 X\in\Her((a-1/8)_+)_+,\qquad
 B_1,\ldots,B_k\in\Her((a-1/8)_+)
\]
with the following property.  For any contractions
\[
 S_i\in\Her((X-\alpha_0)_+),\qquad 1\le i\le k,
\]
one can form a rich positive contraction \(p\in\Her(a)\) such
that, for every representation \(\pi\) of \(C\),
\(\|\pi(a)\|>1/2\) implies \(\|\pi(p)\|=1\).
If a representation \(\pi\) of \(C\) satisfies
\[
 \pi\bigl(y(1-c^*p^2c)y\bigr)=0,\qquad \|\pi(y)\|>s,
\]
then, in that same representation,
\begin{equation}
 \|\pi(X)\|>s,\qquad \pi(B_i)=\pi(S_i)\quad(1\le i\le k).
\end{equation}
The elements \(X,B_1,\ldots,B_k\) are fixed before the
\(S_i\) are chosen.

statements.title: Four entries avoid the fixed measurements
statements.label: prop:four-avoidance
statements.text:
Suppose \(C\) satisfies \(\propP\).  Let \(X\in C_+\) and
\(B_1,B_2,B_3,B_4\in C\).  With
\[
 \alpha_0=\frac1{32}<\alpha=\frac1{16}
 <\beta=\frac18<s=\frac14,\qquad h=\frac12,
\]
there exist contractions \(T_1,\ldots,T_4\) in
\(\Her((X-\alpha_0)_+)\) for which no representation \(\pi\)
of \(C\) satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \|\pi(X)\|>s,\qquad \pi(B_i)=\pi(T_i)\quad(1\le i\le4).
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Four entries under individual proper infiniteness

statements.title: Shrinking under individual proper infiniteness
statements.label: prop:shrinking-P
statements.text:
Suppose \(C\) satisfies \(\propP\).  Let \(a,y\in C\) be positive
contractions and let \(c\in\widetilde C\) be a contraction.  There
are positive contractions \(p_1\in\Her(a)\) and
\(q_1\in\Her(y)\), with \(p_1\) rich, such that for every
representation \(\pi\) of \(C\),
\begin{equation}
 \|\pi(a)\|>1/2\ \Longrightarrow\ \|\pi(p_1)\|=1,
 \qquad
 \|\pi(y)\|>1/2\ \Longrightarrow\ \|\pi(q_1)\|=1,
\end{equation}
and, in the universal bidual,
\begin{equation}
 \|e_{p_1}c e_{q_1}\|<1.
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Four entries under individual proper infiniteness

statements.title: Arbitrarily small support compression
statements.label: prop:iterated-separation
statements.text:
Suppose \(C\) satisfies \(\propP\).  For positive contractions
\(a_*,b_*\in C\), a contraction \(c_*\in C\), and
\(\zeta>0\), there are positive contractions
\(p\in\Her(a_*)\), \(q\in\Her(b_*)\) such that
\[
 \|e_p c_*e_q\|<\zeta
\]
and, for every representation \(\pi\),
\[
 \|\pi(a_*)\|>1/2\ \Longrightarrow\ \|\pi(p)\|=1,
 \qquad
 \|\pi(b_*)\|>1/2\ \Longrightarrow\ \|\pi(q)\|=1.
\]

statements.title: Comparison with bounded coefficients
statements.label: prop:bounded-diagonalization
statements.text:
Suppose \(C\) satisfies \(\propP\).  Let \(a,b\in C_+\) be
contractions and let \(c\in C\).  Given
\[
 0<\delta<1/2,\qquad 0<\rho\le2\delta,\qquad \zeta>0,
\]
there exist \(s,t\in C\) such that
\begin{align}
 \|s^*as-a\|,\ \|t^*bt-b\|&<2\delta+\rho,
 \\
 \|s^*ct\|&<\zeta,\qquad
 \|s\|,\ \|t\|\le\delta^{-1/2}.
 
\end{align}

statements.title: Removing amplification under nuclearity
statements.label: thm:nuclear-to-individual
statements.text:
Let \(C\) be a nuclear complex \(C^*\)-algebra.  Suppose that one
integer \(n\ge1\), fixed for the whole algebra, makes
\(h^{\oplus n}\) properly infinite for every \(h\in C_+\).
Then every positive element of \(C\) is properly infinite.

statements.title: Nuclear avoidance of the fixed measurements
statements.label: prop:nuclear-avoidance
statements.text:
Let \(C\) be nuclear and satisfy \(\propF\) for a fixed \(n\ge1\),
and let \(\ell\) be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:forbidden-tuple}.  For
\(X\in C_+\) and fixed elements
\(B_{j,pq}\in C\), where \(1\le j\le\ell\) and \(1\le p,q\le n\),
there are contractions
\[
 S_{j,pq}\in\Her((X-\alpha_0)_+)
\]
such that no representation \(\pi\) satisfies simultaneously
\begin{equation}
 \|\pi(X)\|>s,\qquad
 \pi(B_{j,pq})=\pi(S_{j,pq})
 \quad(1\le j\le\ell,\ 1\le p,q\le n).
\end{equation}
Here \(\alpha_0=1/32\) and \(s=1/4\), as in
Proposition~\ref{prop:graph}.

statements.title: Uniform gap
statements.label: prop:uniform-gap
statements.text:
There is a constant $\gamma>0$ such that no unital exact $C^*$-algebra
$B$ contains a contraction $v$ with the following property: for every
integer $d\geq1$ and every contraction $D\in M_d(\C)$, there are a unital
representation $\pi:B\to B(H_\pi)$ and an isometry
$J:\C^d\to H_\pi$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \|\pi(v)J-JD\|<\gamma,
 \qquad
 \|\pi(v)^*J-JD^*\|<\gamma.
\end{equation}
The representation and the isometry are allowed to depend on $d$ and
$D$.

statements.title: Uniform perturbation
statements.label: prop:perturbation
statements.text:
Let \(C\) be an exact \(C^*\)-algebra satisfying \propF{} for one
fixed integer \(n\geq1\).  Let \(p,q\in C\) be contractions and
let \(h,k,c\in C_+\) satisfy
\begin{equation}
 p^*ph=h,\qquad qq^*k=k,\qquad
 c^{\oplus n}\precsim h,\qquad c^{\oplus n}\precsim k.
 
\end{equation}
For every \(T\in C\) and every \(\eta,\alpha>0\), there is a
contraction \(y\in C\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \|(T+\eta pyq)_P\|\geq\sigma\eta
 \quad\text{for every }P\in\Prim(C)\text{ with }\|c_P\|\geq\alpha.
 
\end{equation}
If \(h,k\) belong to a hereditary subalgebra
\(\mathcal D\subset C\), then \(y\) may be chosen in \(\mathcal D\).
If, in addition or independently, \(p,q\) are positive and \(pq=0\),
then \(y\) may be chosen selfadjoint.  Both conclusions may be
imposed simultaneously.  The constant \(\sigma\) is independent
of all the data in the Proposition, including \(n\) and the norms
of \(T,h,k,c\).

statements.label: prop:square-zero
statements.text:
Let $C$ be an exact $C^*$-algebra satisfying \propF{} for one fixed
integer $n\geq1$.  Let $K_0\subset\Prim(C)$ be quasi-compact, and let
$\mathcal D\subset C$ be a hereditary subalgebra nonzero at every
point of $K_0$.  There exists $x\in\mathcal D$ such that
\[
 x^2=0,\qquad x_P\ne0\quad(P\in K_0).
\]
statements.section_title: Exact localization and removal of amplification

statements.title: Whole-ideal comparison
statements.label: cor:ideal-comparison
statements.text:
Let $C$ be a $C^*$-algebra satisfying \propP{}.  For every $h\in C_+$,
$c\in\Id(h)_+$, and integer $k\ge1$,
\[
 c^{\oplus k}\precsim h.
\]
If $C$ is exact, Proposition~\ref{prop:perturbation} may be applied
with multiplicity $n=1$, with the same constant $\sigma$ and all its
stated options.
statements.section_title: Exact localization and removal of amplification

statements.title: Direct exact proof
statements.label: prop:direct-strong-infiniteness
statements.text:
Let $C$ be an exact $C^*$-algebra satisfying $\propP$.  For every
$a,b\in C_+$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there are $s,t\in C$ such that
\[
 \|s^*a^2s-a^2\|<\varepsilon,\qquad
 \|t^*b^2t-b^2\|<\varepsilon,\qquad
 \|s^*abt\|<\varepsilon.
\]
Consequently $C$ is strongly purely infinite.

statements.label: thm:totient
statements.text:
For every real $\eps>0$, there are infinitely many positive integers
$n$ such that
\[
 g(n)>n^{1-\eps}.
\]

statements.title: Siegel--Walfisz
statements.label: thm:sw
statements.text:
For fixed $A,C>0$, uniformly for $(a,r)=1$ and
$1\le r\le(\log y)^C$,
\[
 \#\{p\le y:p\equiv a\pmod r\}
 =\frac{\Li(y)}{\varphi(r)}
  +O_{A,C}\!\left(\frac{y}{(\log y)^A}\right).
\]
The constants, which need not be effective, are independent of $y,a,r$.

statements.title: Multiplicative large sieve
statements.label: thm:large-sieve
statements.text:
Let $I$ be a real interval of length $H$, let $a_n$ be complex numbers
supported on $I\cap\Z$, and let $R\ge1$. Then
\[
 \sum_{r\le R}\frac r{\varphi(r)}
 \sum_{\chi\bmod r}^{*}
 \left|\sum_{n\in I\cap\Z}a_n\chi(n)\right|^2
 \ll (H+1+R^2)\sum_n|a_n|^2,
\]
where the asterisk restricts the sum to primitive Dirichlet characters.

statements.title: Harmonic character estimates
statements.label: cor:harmonic-sw
statements.text:
Fix $c,C,B,A>0$. If $\chi$ is nonprincipal modulo $r\le L^B$, then,
uniformly for real $|t|\le L^B$ and intervals
$I\subset[\exp(L^c),x^C]$,
\[
 \sum_{p\in I}\frac{\chi(p)p^{it}}p\ll_{c,C,B,A}L^{-A}.
\]
The same conclusion holds for a nonprincipal character induced from a
smaller modulus.

statements.title: A polynomial for rough integers
statements.label: lem:rough-sieve-polynomial

statements.title: Local transference
statements.label: thm:transference
statements.text:
For every fixed $E>0$ there is $E_{\rm id}>0$, depending only on
$E$ and the fixed data in \Cref{def:prime-groups}, with the following
property.  Assume
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{\Theta\in\R}\norm{\mathcal T(\Theta)}\le L^{-E_{\rm id}}.
\end{equation}
Then, for every sufficiently large fixed $J$, where the lower
bound on $J$ may also depend on $m,C_1$, put
\[
 R=\lceil L^{0.52}\rceil,\qquad N=2R.
\]
For every fixed $\gamma>0$ and $I=[X,2X)$ with
$x^\gamma\le X\le x^{1/\gamma}$, one has
\begin{equation}
 \frac1{|I\cap\Z|}\sum_{n\in I\cap\Z}
 \langle u_n,(\mathcal A\mathcal A^*)^Ru_n\rangle
 \le L^{-EN},
\end{equation}
for all sufficiently large $x$.  Here $u_n$ is one on every
physical state at position $n$ and zero elsewhere.  The threshold
for $x$ may depend on all fixed parameters, including $J,C_2,
\gamma$, and the bound is uniform subject to these parameters
and \Cref{eq:ideal-norm-hypothesis}.  No bound on $\zeta$ is needed
apart from the assumed ideal estimate.

statements.label: cor:transference-pairing
statements.text:
Under the hypotheses and choices of
\Cref{thm:transference}, let $f\in\mathcal H_{\rm ph}$
be supported on positions $I=[X,2X)$ and independent
of the chosen marks, with value $f_n$ at position $n$.
Suppose
\[
 \sup_{n\in I}|f_n|\le\exp(O(\sqrt L)),\qquad
 \norm f,\norm g\le X^{1/2}L^{C_3}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 |\langle f,\mathcal A g\rangle|
       \ll XL^{-E+2C_3}.
\end{equation}
Only the first endpoint must be independent of its
mark list.

statements.title: Construction of the residual ideal operator
statements.label: thm:ideal
statements.text:
Fix $E_{\rm id}>0$ and a fixed frequency exponent $C_4\geq0$.
There are fixed integers $m,J_0$ and a fixed constant $C_1$, depending
only on these parameters, $\ell$, and the prime-group bounds, with the
following property.  For every fixed $J\geq J_0$, there is a family
consisting of the raw pattern
\[
 C_g=\varnothing\quad\hbox{for every }g,\qquad K_0=1,
\]
and signed comparison patterns satisfying
\[
 C_g=\varnothing\ (g\in\mathcal S),\qquad
 |C_g|\leq m\ (g\in\mathcal B),\qquad
 \sum_\nu\sup|K_\nu|\leq L^{C_1},
\]
such that the symmetrized ideal operator of \Cref{sec:transference}
satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{\Theta\in\R,\ |\zeta|\leq L^{C_4}}
 \norm{\mathcal T(\Theta)}_{2\to2}\leq L^{-E_{\rm id}}
\end{equation}
for sufficiently large $x$.  The coefficients and the family are
independent of $\Theta$ and of the individual value of $\zeta$.
Their defining parameters are independent of $J$; $J$ only supplies
the available shared slots.  The threshold for $x$ may depend on $J$.

More precisely, designate $m$ of the first $J$ slots in each big group
as probes, and split the big groups into two blocks. Each comparison
frees nonempty sets $A$ and $B$ of designated probes in the respective
blocks, and its coefficient has the form
\begin{equation}
 -(-1)^{|A|+|B|}\mathcal K_A(D_A,X_A)
                         \mathcal K_B(D_B,X_B).
\end{equation}
Here $D_A,D_B$ are the products of the free labels used to form $D$,
$X_A$ is the product of the target labels in $A$, and $X_B$ the
product of the input labels in $B$.  These coefficients use no
shared labels and none of the last $\ell$ labels.  Each kernel is
a finite sum of products of matched log-cell indicators and pairs of
Dirichlet characters of conductor bounded by a fixed power of $L$.
statements.section_title: Small ideal kernels at every frequency

statements.title: Lifted shift cancellation
statements.label: thm:shift
statements.text:
Fix all the group and endpoint bounds above. Fix $D_0,C>0$ and a fixed
compact interval $[c_\Psi,C_\Psi]\subset(0,\infty)$. Suppose
$0<|k|\leq L^C$ is integral, $xL^{-C}\leq Z\leq xL^C$,
$|a_1|,|a_2|\leq L^C$, and $\Psi$ is supported in that interval with
$\|\Psi^{(j)}\|_\infty\ll_j L^{C(j+1)}$ for every $j\geq0$.
There exists a fixed $B$, depending only on these bounds and $D_0$,
such that \Cref{eq:discrepancy} implies
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{\substack{z>0\\z+k>0}}
 \frac{\Psi(z/Z)}z\,z^{ia_1}(z+k)^{ia_2}
       \overline{F_0(z)}G_0(z+k)W_\ell(z)W_\ell(z+k)
       \ll L^{-D_0}.
\end{equation}
The bound is uniform over the indicated sequences, intervals, characters,
frequencies, and cutoffs. It also holds when the discrepancy-bearing
endpoint or its coefficients have been conjugated.

statements.title: Type II
statements.label: thm:typeii
statements.text:
Fix $D_*>0$, $b_*>0$, and $C>0$, and require
$\eta_*<b_*/4$ in \Cref{eq:typeii-rough-slot}. Let $U,V$ be dyadic
scales satisfying
\[
 UV\asymp x,\qquad x^{b_*}\leq U,V\leq x^{1-b_*}.
\]
Let $\Psi$ be a fixed smooth function with compact support in a fixed
compact subinterval of $(0,\infty)$. Suppose that
$\abs{\alpha_m},\abs{\beta_n}\leq L^C$, and that $\alpha_m=0$ unless
$\Pminus(m)>W$. There is a fixed exponent $B$, depending only on these
data and the fixed group and band constants, such that the discrepancy
hypothesis in \Cref{eq:discrepancy} on $\alpha$ implies
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{\substack{m\asymp U,\ n\asymp V,\ u\geq1\\mn=2u+1}}
      A(u)\Psi(u/x)\alpha_m\beta_n
       \ll xL^{-D_*}.
\end{equation}
Here the sequence to which the discrepancy hypothesis is applied includes
the actual restriction $m\asymp U$ and any additional interval restriction
on $m$. Explicitly, for that restricted sequence one requires
\[
 \left|\sum_{m\in I}\frac{\alpha_m\chi(m)m^{it}}m\right|
       \leq L^{-B}
 \quad\left(I\subset[1,x^2],\quad
       \operatorname{mod}(\chi)\leq L^B,\quad |t|\leq L^B\right).
\]
There is no discrepancy hypothesis on $\beta$. The constants are uniform
over the sequences, scales, and interval restrictions satisfying these
conditions.

statements.title: Candidate mass
statements.label: prop:candidate-mass
statements.text:
Put
\[
 X_A=\sum_u A(u)\Psi(u/x),\quad
 H_Q=\sum_v\frac{a_Q(v)}v,\quad
 H_P=\sum_{r:r_*=1}\frac{W_1(r)}r.
\]
There are constants $C,C_A$ depending only on the early candidate
choices such that, for sufficiently large $x$ after fixing $j_{**}$,
\begin{align}
 0\le A(u)&\le L^C\tau(u_*),
 & A(u)&\le\exp(C\sqrt L)\quad(u\asymp x),\\
 H_P&\sim\exp\left(q\sum_g V_g\right),
 & X_A&\asymp\frac{x}{L}H_QH_P\gg xL^{-C_A}.
 
\end{align}
The comparison constants in \eqref{eq:candidate-mass} can be chosen
independently of $j_{**}\ge j_0$. On the support of
$A(u)\Psi(u/x)$ every prime divisor of $u$ lies in $[L^{20},x^\delta]$.

title: Weil classes and Hodge classes on abelian powers
abstract: We prove the rational Hodge conjecture in every codimension on every self-power of a complex abelian sixfold with an imaginary-quadratic action and a compatible polarization whose rational homological Hermitian form is hyperbolic of signature \((3,3)\). We also prove it in every codimension on every self-power of a complex abelian variety of dimension at most five admitting an imaginary-quadratic action. Both results include nonsimple varieties and special periods with additional endomorphisms. The proof uses the companion theorem on the rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties.
version_note: This version updates citations to revised manuscripts in this collection; see the [previous version](../Weil-classes-and-Hodge-classes-on-abelian-powers-September-30-2026/paper.pdf).

tex.abstract:
We prove the rational Hodge conjecture in every codimension on every
self-power of a complex abelian sixfold with an imaginary-quadratic
action and a compatible polarization whose rational homological Hermitian
form is hyperbolic of signature \((3,3)\). We also prove it in every
codimension on every self-power of a complex abelian variety of dimension
at most five admitting an imaginary-quadratic action. Both results include
nonsimple varieties and special periods with additional endomorphisms.
The proof uses the companion theorem on the rational Hodge conjecture for
CM abelian varieties.

statements.title: Split Weil sixfolds
statements.label: p3ab:split-sixfolds
statements.text:
Let \(E\) be an imaginary quadratic field and let \(A\) be a complex
abelian sixfold with an \(E\)-action.  Suppose a compatible
polarization has hyperbolic rational Hermitian form of signature
\((3,3)\).  Then the rational Hodge conjecture holds in every
codimension on \(A^m\), for every \(m\geq1\).

statements.title: Quadratic actions in dimension at most five
statements.label: p3ab:quadratic-five
statements.text:
Let \(A\) be a complex abelian variety of dimension at most five
admitting an action of an imaginary quadratic field.  The rational
Hodge conjecture holds in every codimension on \(A^m\), for every
\(m\geq1\).

statements.title: A determinant criterion for all powers
statements.label: p3:tensor-criterion
statements.text:
Let $A$ be a complex abelian variety, $H=H^1(A,\Q)$,
$J=\operatorname{Hdg}(H)$, and $R=J^{\mathrm{der}}$.
Suppose the following data exist.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\alph*)}]
\item A rational Hodge summand $H_0\subset H$ has toric Hodge group.
Choose a decomposition of $H_{0,k}$ into CM embedding lines,
with repeated occurrences distinguished, and call this finite list
$\mathcal E_0$.
\item The complement of $H_{0,k}$ is a direct sum of blocks of
nonzero admissible spaces.  In a symplectic or an orthogonal block,
each space is equipped with an admissible isomorphism to a
representative $V_i$ chosen as an actual summand of that block,
with, respectively, an alternating or a
symmetric pair tensor on itself.  A linear block has
$\dim V_i\ge2$, with $V_i$ again an actual summand, and each space is equipped with an admissible
isomorphism to either $V_i$ or $\overline V_i$, paired with
each other as in Lemma~\ref{p3:admissible-operations}.
The pair identifies $\overline V_i$ with $V_i^*(-1)$ as a
Hodge-graded space and with the dual as a group representation.
\item Under these identifications the image of $R_k$ contains
\[
 P=\prod_{i\in I_{\mathrm{Sp}}}\operatorname{Sp}(V_i)
   \times\prod_{i\in I_{\mathrm{SO}}}\operatorname{SO}(V_i)
   \times\prod_{i\in I_{\mathrm{SL}}}\operatorname{SL}(V_i).
\]
Each factor acts by its standard representation on its own copies,
by the dual representation on the opposite copies of a linear
block, and trivially on every other block and on $H_{0,k}$.
The symplectic and orthogonal forms are the inverse pairings.
\item Let $W_1,\ldots,W_s$ be any list, with arbitrary repetitions,
from
\[
 \{V_i:i\in I_{\mathrm{SO}}\}
 \ \cup\
 \{V_i,\overline V_i:i\in I_{\mathrm{SL}}\}.
\]
Whenever there are $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_r\in\mathcal E_0$, again
with arbitrary repetitions, such that
\begin{equation}
 
 \sum_{j=1}^s\epsilon_\gamma(W_j)
 +\sum_{a=1}^r\epsilon_\gamma(\ell_a)=0
 \quad\text{for every }\gamma\in\operatorname{Gal}(k/\Q),
\end{equation}
the line $\bigotimes_{j=1}^sD(W_j)$ is CM-supplied on its
separate tensor slots.  Empty lists are allowed.
\end{enumerate}

Then for every $p\ge0$ every rational balanced tensor in $H^{\otimes 2p}$ is the
class of a rational algebraic cycle on its separate $A$-slots.
The rational Hodge conjecture holds in every codimension of $A^m$
for every $m\ge1$.

Call the data \emph{saturated} if every singleton $D(V_i)$ for
an orthogonal or linear block is CM-supplied, without any balance
condition.  For saturated data and any CM abelian variety $M$,
the induced data on $A\times M$ are saturated.  In particular the
same tensor and Hodge-conjecture conclusions hold for every power of
$A\times M$.

statements.title: Algebraicity of the hyperbolic Weil plane
statements.label: p3sw:weil-plane
statements.text:
Let \(E\) be an imaginary quadratic field.  Let \(A\) be a complex
abelian sixfold with a unital \(E\)-action and a compatible polarization
whose actual homological Hermitian form \(h_E\) is hyperbolic of signature
\((3,3)\).  Then
\[
 \mathcal W_E(A)\ \subset\
 \operatorname{im}\bigl(\CH^3(A)_\Q
                    \longrightarrow H^6(A,\Q)\bigr).
\]
The assertion holds at every compatible period, including nonsimple
varieties and periods with additional endomorphisms.

statements.title: Simultaneous equivariant seeds
statements.label: p3sw:seed
statements.text:
For every integer \(d\geq3\), put \(n=d+1\).  There exist a smooth
nonhyperelliptic genus-three curve \(C\), a point \(p\in C\), and
cyclic subgroups \(G_1,G_2\subset X=\operatorname{Pic}^2(C)\) of
order \(n\), with \(G_1\cap G_2=0\), as follows.  There are cosets
\(\{s_1,\ldots,s_n\}=s_0+G_2\) and
\(\{t_1,\ldots,t_n\}=t_0+G_1\) such that
\begin{equation}
 C_i=t_{s_i}C_p,\qquad \Sigma_j=t_{t_j}\Sigma_p,\qquad
 A=\coprod_{i=1}^n C_i,\qquad \Sigma=\coprod_{j=1}^n\Sigma_j
 
\end{equation}
are disjoint within each of the two indicated unions, and
\begin{equation}
 H^0(X,I_A\otimes H^{\otimes2}\otimes N)
 =
 H^0(X,I_\Sigma\otimes H^{\otimes2}\otimes N)=0
 \quad\text{for every }N\in\widehat X.
 
\end{equation}
statements.section_title: The geometric seed for the Weil-plane theorem

statements.title: The relative kernel and all its base changes
statements.label: p3sw:relative-kernel
statements.text:
For the seed of Proposition \ref{p3sw:seed}, the derived tensor in
\eqref{p3sw:support-kernel-sheaf} is the ordinary coherent sheaf
\(\mathscr I\mathscr J\subset\mathcal O_{X\times M}\).
Both this ideal and its quotient in \(\mathcal O_{X\times M}\) are
flat over \(M\).  Ideal multiplication and both ideal sequences
commute with every base change \(T\to M\).  In particular,
\(\mathscr F\) is \(M\)-flat, and at \(m=(x,N)\) it has the ordinary
fiber
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 \mathscr F_m&=I_{Z_x}\otimes\mathcal M_{x,N},\\
 I_{Z_x}&=I_A I_{\Sigma_x},\qquad
 \Sigma_x=\coprod_jt_{-x}\Sigma_j,\qquad
 \mathcal M_{x,N}=H^{\otimes2}\otimes a(-x)\otimes N^{-1}.
 \end{split}
 
\end{equation}
Moreover \(G=R\pi_*\mathscr F\) has a local finite locally free
model, and for every \(h:T\to M\),
\begin{equation}
 Lh^*G\simeq R\pi_{T,*}(\mathscr F|_{X\times T}).
 
\end{equation}

statements.title: Hochschild--Atiyah trace identity
statements.label: p3sw:hh-triangle
statements.text:
Let \(A\) be a complex abelian variety of dimension \(d\), and let
\(Q\in\operatorname{Perf}(A)\).  Use the raw first-jet class \(a_Q\)
from \eqref{p3sw:hh-eq:jet-extension}, and the left-interior and HKR
conventions \eqref{p3sw:hh-eq:left-action} and
\eqref{p3sw:hh-eq:adjoint-hkr}.  Define
\[
 \operatorname{ob}_Q=\chi_Q\circ\operatorname{HKR}_A:
       HT^2(A)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ext}^2_A(Q,Q).
\]
For \(\alpha=\sum_{a+b=2}\alpha^{a,b}\), this evaluation is
\[
 \operatorname{ob}_Q(\alpha)
       =\sum_{a+b=2}\alpha^{a,b}\mathbin{\lrcorner}
                                      \frac{a_Q^b}{b!}.
\]
On the full group \(\operatorname{Ext}^2_A(Q,Q)\), define
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
 \sigma_Q&=(\sigma_{Q,j})_{0\leq j\leq d-2}:
   \operatorname{Ext}^2_A(Q,Q)
       \longrightarrow H\Omega_{-2}(A)
          =\bigoplus_{j=0}^{d-2}H^{j+2}(A,\Omega_A^j),\\
 \sigma_{Q,j}(v)&=
   \operatorname{Tr}_{Q,\Omega_A^j[j+2]}
        \left(\left(\frac{a_Q^j}{j!}\right)[2]\circ v\right).
\end{split}

\end{equation}
The direct sum is zero if \(d<2\).  Set
\[
 c_Q(\alpha)=\alpha\mathbin{\lrcorner}\operatorname{ch}_H(Q)
       \in H\Omega_{-2}(A).
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \sigma_Q\circ\operatorname{ob}_Q=c_Q.

\end{equation}
More precisely, with
\(\operatorname{ch}_{H,k}(Q)=0\) for \(k\notin[0,d]\), each component
is
\begin{equation}
 \sigma_{Q,j}(\operatorname{ob}_Q(\alpha))
    =\sum_{a+b=2}\alpha^{a,b}\mathbin{\lrcorner}
                          \operatorname{ch}_{H,j+b}(Q)
       \quad\text{in }H^{j+2}(A,\Omega_A^j).

\end{equation}
statements.section_title: Hochschild evaluation and the invariant obstruction space

statements.title: Transport of evaluation and contraction
statements.label: p3sw:hh-transport
statements.text:
For the fixed enhanced Fourier--Mukai equivalence
\(\Phi:\operatorname{Perf}(A)\to\operatorname{Perf}(B)\), there exists an
isomorphism
\[
 \Phi^H_{HH}:H\Omega_{-2}(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}H\Omega_{-2}(B)
\]
depending only on that enhanced equivalence, not on a choice of perfect
complex, such that for every \(Q\in\operatorname{Perf}(A)\),
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
 \Phi_{\mathrm{Ext}}\circ\operatorname{ob}_Q
     &=\operatorname{ob}_{\Phi Q}\circ\Phi^{HT},\\
 \Phi^H_{HH}\circ c_Q&=c_{\Phi Q}\circ\Phi^{HT}.
\end{split}

\end{equation}
Here \(\operatorname{ob}\) and \(c\) have the conventions of
Proposition~\ref{p3sw:hh-triangle}, and \(\Phi_{\mathrm{Ext}}\) is the
induced enhanced map on degree-two Ext.  Consequently
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
 \Phi^{HT}(\ker\operatorname{ob}_Q)
       &=\ker\operatorname{ob}_{\Phi Q},\\
 \Phi^{HT}(\ker c_Q)&=\ker c_{\Phi Q}.
\end{split}

\end{equation}
In particular \(\ker\operatorname{ob}_Q=\ker c_Q\) implies
\(\ker\operatorname{ob}_{\Phi Q}=\ker c_{\Phi Q}\).
statements.section_title: Hochschild evaluation and the invariant obstruction space

statements.label: p3sw:invariant-ext
statements.text:
For the source object \(\mathcal I=I_\Sigma\boxtimes I_A\) and its
canonical \(G_{\mathrm{src}}=G_1\times G_2\) linearization,
\[
 \dim_{\mathbb C}
 \operatorname{Ext}^2_{X^2}(\mathcal I,\mathcal I)^{G_{\mathrm{src}}}
 =6+36+6=48.
\]
This is the invariant subspace of the full derived Ext group.
statements.section_title: Hochschild evaluation and the invariant obstruction space

statements.label: p3sw:invariant-injectivity
statements.text:
For the source \(\mathcal I=I_\Sigma\boxtimes I_A\) with its canonical
\(G_{\mathrm{src}}=G_1\times G_2\)-linearization,
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{im}(o_{\mathcal I})
   =\operatorname{Ext}^2_{X^2}(\mathcal I,\mathcal I)^{G_{\mathrm{src}}},
 \qquad
 \ker(o_{\mathcal I})=\ker(c_{\mathcal I}^2),
\end{equation}
and \(\sigma_{\mathcal I}\) is injective on this full invariant group.

Let \(M=X\times\widehat X\) and use the fixed enhanced equivalence
\[
 \widetilde\Phi=\Phi\circ\bigl((H\boxtimes H)\otimes-\bigr),
 \qquad
 \mathcal G=\widetilde\Phi(\mathcal I)[-3].
\]
Give \(\mathcal G\) the coherent line-translation action from
Proposition~\ref{p3sw:coherent-action}, and denote its underlying
translation group by \(\bar G\simeq G_{\mathrm{src}}\).  Then
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{im}(o_{\mathcal G})
   =\operatorname{Ext}^2_M(\mathcal G,\mathcal G)^{\bar G},
 \qquad
 \ker(o_{\mathcal G})=\ker(c_{\mathcal G}^2),
\end{equation}
and
\[
 \sigma_{\mathcal G}\big|_{
       \operatorname{Ext}^2_M(\mathcal G,\mathcal G)^{\bar G}}
 \quad\text{is injective}.
\]
statements.section_title: Hochschild evaluation and the invariant obstruction space

statements.title: Fixed Clifford identity
statements.label: p3sw:spin-identity
statements.text:
For every algebraic spin element \(g\), one has the exact equality
of rational representations
\begin{equation}

 \rho'_g=e^{p/2}\Lambda\rho(g)e^{-p/2}
       =e^{(p-\Lambda^2\rho(g)p)/2}\Lambda\rho(g).
\end{equation}
The exponentials denote exterior multiplication.  In particular
\[
 [\rho'_g(1)]_0=1,\qquad
 [\rho'_g(1)]_2=\tfrac12\bigl(p-\Lambda^2\rho(g)p\bigr).
\]
statements.section_title: The spin character and the polarized quadratic seed

statements.title: The polarized quadratic seed
statements.label: p3sw:polarized-seed
statements.text:
On the actual sixfold \(M=X\times\widehat X\), define
\[
 \eta(u)(x,N)=\bigl(a^{-1}(N),[-d]a(x)\bigr)
             =\bigl(-\lambda^{-1}(N),[d]\lambda(x)\bigr).
\]
This gives a unital \(K\)-action.  The ample line
\[
 \mathscr L_M=\operatorname{pr}_X^*H^{\otimes d}
          \otimes\operatorname{pr}_{\widehat X}^*(a^{-1})^*H
\]
has a class \(\theta_M=c_{1,\mathrm B}(\mathscr L_M)\) fixed by the
vector images of \(J\) and \(\widetilde L_K\).  The action is of Weil
type \((3,3)\), is compatible with this polarization, and its actual
homological Hermitian form is hyperbolic.

More precisely, the pullback \(f=\eta(u)^*\) on \(V=L\oplus U\) and
its two eigenspaces are
\begin{equation}

 \begin{split}
 f(w,y)&=(d\vartheta y,-\vartheta^{-1}w),\qquad f^2=-d,\\
 W_+&=\operatorname{Ann}(\lambda_+)
       =\{(-u\vartheta y,y):y\in U_K\},\\
 W_-&=\operatorname{Ann}(\lambda_-)
       =\{(u\vartheta y,y):y\in U_K\}.
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
The eigenvalue on \(W_+\) is \(+u\), and that on \(W_-\) is \(-u\).
statements.section_title: The spin character and the polarized quadratic seed

statements.title: Ordered spinor stabilizer
statements.label: p3sw:ordered-stabilizer
statements.text:
Let \(W=W_+\).  Under \(V_K=W\oplus W^*\), the ordered line
stabilizer and the pointwise stabilizer are
\[
 \widetilde L_K
   =\{(g,t)\in GL(W)\times\mathbb G_m:t^2=\det g\},\qquad
 m(g,t)=t^{-1}\Lambda g,\qquad
 J_K=\{(g,1):g\in SL(W)\}.
\]
The characters on \(\lambda_+\) and \(\lambda_-\) are \(t,t^{-1}\).
For \(0\leq j\leq6\),
\begin{equation}

 H^{2j}(M,\Q)^J=
 \begin{cases}
  \Q\theta_M^j,&j\ne3,\\
  \Q\theta_M^3\oplus\mathcal W_K(M),&j=3,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad H^{\mathrm{odd}}(M,\Q)^J=0 .
\end{equation}
The ordered line stabilizer fixes every \(\theta_M^j\) and acts on
the two scalar Weil lines by \(t^2,t^{-2}\).
statements.section_title: The spin character and the polarized quadratic seed

statements.title: The exceptional component of the actual sheaf
statements.label: p3sw:exceptional-character
statements.text:
The normalized character \(\kappa_M\) in
\eqref{p3sw:spin-eq:normalized-character} is a rational
\(J\)-invariant even class, and its degree-six
component has a nonzero rational Weil component:
\[
 (\kappa_M)_3=a_M\theta_M^3+w_M,\qquad
 a_M\in\Q,\quad 0\ne w_M\in\mathcal W_K(M).
\]
statements.section_title: The spin character and the polarized quadratic seed

statements.title: The actual polarized Hodge circle
statements.label: p3sw:hodge-circle
statements.text:
Keep the rational homology of the seed \(M\), the action \(\eta\),
and the Riemann form of \(\mathscr L_M\) fixed.  At every compatible
marked complex structure of Weil type \((3,3)\), every component
\((\kappa_M)_j\) has Hodge type \((j,j)\).
statements.section_title: The spin character and the polarized quadratic seed

statements.label: p3sw:twisted-descent
statements.text:
There are a class \(\alpha\in H^2(Y_0,\mu_r)\), a coherent
\(\alpha\)-twisted sheaf \(\mathcal B\) of rank \(r\) with
\(\det\mathcal B\simeq\mathcal O_{Y_0}\), and an invertible
\(q^*\alpha\)-twisted sheaf \(\mathcal L\) on \(M\), such that
\begin{equation}

 q^*\mathcal B\simeq E\otimes\mathcal L.
\end{equation}
Let \(\mathfrak Y_0\) be the \(\mu_r\)-gerbe of \(\alpha\).  For every
integer \(i\), this isomorphism induces
\begin{equation}

 \operatorname{Ext}^i_{\mathfrak Y_0}(\mathcal B,\mathcal B)
   \simeq\operatorname{Ext}^i_M(E,E)^{\bar G},\qquad
 \operatorname{Ext}^i_0(\mathcal B,\mathcal B)
   \simeq\operatorname{Ext}^i_0(E,E)^{\bar G},
\end{equation}
where the subscript \(0\) denotes the kernel of the perfect trace to
\(H^i(\mathcal O)\).  Put
\[
 \lambda_H=\frac{a_{\det E}}r=\frac{\operatorname{tr}(a_E)}r.
\]
Under the first isomorphism \(\phi\) in degree two, the raw Hodge square
\begin{equation}

\begin{array}{ccc}
 \operatorname{Ext}^2(\mathcal B,\mathcal B)&
       \xrightarrow{\ \phi\ }&\operatorname{Ext}^2(E,E)^{\bar G}\\
 \big\downarrow{\scriptstyle\sigma_{\mathcal B}}&&
       \big\downarrow{\scriptstyle e^{-\lambda_H}\sigma_E}\\
 \mathcal H_{-2}(Y_0)&\xrightarrow{\ q^*\ }&\mathcal H_{-2}(M)
\end{array}
\end{equation}
commutes, both on full Ext and on its trace-free summand.  In particular,
full invariant injectivity for \(E\) makes \(\mathcal B\) semiregular.
By Lemma~\ref{p3sw:descent-duality}, full invariant injectivity for
\(\mathcal G\) is sufficient for this conclusion.

statements.label: p3sw:ordinary-conversion
statements.text:
For the class \(\alpha\) and the semiregular twisted coherent sheaf
\(\mathcal B\) in Proposition~\ref{p3sw:twisted-descent}, put
\(m=r^{12}\) and \(N=6+m-1\).  There exist a holomorphic
\(\mathbb P^{m-1}\)-bundle \(p:Z\to Y\), a determinant-trivial
\(\alpha\)-twisted vector bundle \(Q_0\) of rank \(m\) on \(Y_0\), and
an inverse-twisted tautological line
\(\ell_0=\mathcal O_{\mathbb P(Q_0)}(1)\), with \(Z_0=\mathbb P(Q_0)\).
The ordinary line
\begin{equation}

 H=\omega_{Z/Y}^{-1}=\det T_{Z/Y}
\end{equation}
satisfies \(H|_{Z_0}\simeq\ell_0^m\) and restricts to
\(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^{m-1}}(m)\) on every \(p\)-fiber.  The
normalized Betti class and raw Hodge class
\begin{equation}

 \zeta_{B,s}=\frac{c_1^B(H|_{Z_s})}{m},\qquad
 \zeta_{H,s}=\frac{a_{H|_{Z_s}}}{m},\qquad
 \iota_{Z_s}(\zeta_{H,s})=(2\pi i)\zeta_{B,s}
\end{equation}
have the following properties: \(\zeta_B\) is a horizontal rational
class of type \((1,1)\), and its restriction to every \(p_s\)-fiber
is the normalized hyperplane class.  Every \(Z_s\) and \(p_s\) is
projective algebraic, and \(a\circ p\) has a relative ample line.

The sheaf
\[
 F_0=p_0^*\mathcal B\otimes\ell_0
\]
is ordinary coherent on \(Z_0\), and it is semiregular.  More precisely,
there is a full derived isomorphism
\begin{equation}

 \operatorname{Ext}^2_{Z_0}(F_0,F_0)
       \simeq\operatorname{Ext}^2_{\mathfrak Y_0}(\mathcal B,\mathcal B)
\end{equation}
under which
\begin{equation}

 \sigma_{F_0}(p_0^*v)
       =e^{\zeta_{H,0}}p_0^*\sigma_{\mathcal B}(v).
\end{equation}
If a rational horizontal section
\(\kappa_B=\sum_{k=0}^6\kappa_{B,k}\) specializes to
\(\operatorname{ch}_B(\mathcal B)\) and has type \((k,k)\) in degree
\(2k\), then
\begin{equation}

 A_B=p^*\kappa_B e^{\zeta_B}=\sum_{k=0}^{N}A_{B,k}
\end{equation}
is rational, horizontal, and of type \((k,k)\) in degree \(2k\).
Its raw Hodge section in that degree is the edge of
\((2\pi i)^kA_{B,k}\), and its central value is
\(\operatorname{ch}_{H,k}(F_0)\).  Finally, on every fiber,
\begin{equation}

 p_{s*}^B\bigl(\zeta_{B,s}^{\,m-1}e^{-\zeta_{B,s}}A_B(s)\bigr)
       =\kappa_B(s),
\end{equation}
where \(p_{s*}^B\) is normalized Betti fiber integration.

statements.label: p3sw:projective-germ
statements.text:
Let \(S=(S,0)\) be a smooth complex analytic germ, and let
\(\pi:\mathcal X\to S\) be a proper holomorphic submersion of relative
dimension \(n\), equipped with a holomorphic \(\pi\)-ample line
\(\mathcal L_{\mathcal X}\).  Let \(F_0\) be an ordinary coherent
sheaf on \(X_0\).  For \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), suppose the following
raw semiregularity map is injective:
\begin{equation}

 \begin{split}
 \sigma_{I,0}:\operatorname{Ext}^2_{X_0}(F_0,F_0)&\longrightarrow
       \bigoplus_{k\in I}H^{k+1}(X_0,\Omega_{X_0}^{k-1}),\\
 v&\longmapsto
       \left(\operatorname{Tr}_{F_0,\Omega_{X_0}^{k-1}[k+1]}
       \left(\left(\frac{a_{F_0}^{k-1}}{(k-1)!}\right)[2]\circ v\right)\right)_{k\in I}
 \end{split}
\end{equation}
Suppose there are rational flat sections
\(\beta_{B,k}\) of \(R^{2k}\pi_*\Q\), for \(k\in I\), such that
\[
 \beta_{B,k}(0)=\operatorname{ch}_{B,k}(F_0),\qquad
 \beta_{B,k}\in F^k(R^{2k}\pi_*\C\otimes\mathcal O_S).
\]
The second condition means that the flat de Rham class itself lies in
the indicated Hodge filtration.  Then, after shrinking \(S\), there
is a coherent \(S\)-flat sheaf \(F\) on \(\mathcal X\), with
\(F|_{X_0}\simeq F_0\), for which
\begin{equation}

 \operatorname{ch}_{B,k}(F|_{X_s})=\beta_{B,k}(s)
       \quad(s\text{ near }0,\ k\in I).
\end{equation}
These classes are rational algebraic cycle classes.  No rank,
simplicity, stability, local-freeness, reflexivity, or fixed-support
hypothesis is imposed on \(F_0\).

statements.title: Local algebraicity of the descended character
statements.label: p3sw:local-algebraicity
statements.text:
There is a nonempty analytic neighborhood of the seed in
\(\mathscr D\) on which every component \(\kappa_{B,j}(I)\) is a
rational algebraic cycle class on \(Y_I\).

statements.title: Analytic Hilbert spread
statements.label: p3sw:spread
statements.text:
Let \(\pi:\mathcal X\to S\) be a smooth projective morphism of
relative dimension \(n\) over a smooth quasi-projective complex
variety.  Let \(\nu:T\to S^{\mathrm{an}}\) be holomorphic, where
\(T\) is a connected complex manifold.  Fix \(0\leq c\leq n\)
and a finite-rank rational local subsystem
\[
 \mathbb V\subset\nu^*R^{2c}\pi^{\mathrm{an}}_*\Q.
\]
If every vector of \(\mathbb V_t\) is a rational algebraic
codimension-\(c\) class on \(\mathcal X_{\nu(t)}\) for all \(t\)
in a nonempty analytic open subset of \(T\), then the same is
true for every \(t\in T\).

statements.label: p3sw:endpoint-all-lattices
statements.text:
For the fixed \(K=\Q(u)\) with \(u^2=-d\), \(d\geq3\), let
\(A\) be any complex abelian sixfold with a unital \(K\)-action
and a compatible polarization.  If its actual homological
Hermitian form \(h_A(x,y)=e_A(x,uy)+u e_A(x,y)\) is hyperbolic,
then \(\mathcal W_K(A)\) is a rational algebraic plane.
